title: Data Science vs. Statistics: Two Cultures?
Abstract: Data science, often understood as a broader, task-driven, and computationally-oriented version of statistics, has its roots in the traditional discipline of statistics. This paper advocates for a big-tent view of data analysis, encompassing the evolving approaches to modern data analysis, such as exploratory analysis, machine learning, reproducibility, computation, communication, and the role of theory, within the broader context of statistics. It examines how these trends impact the future of statistics, highlighting promising directions for communication, education, and research.

title: Estimation and Inference of Treatment Effects with $L_2$-Boosting in High-Dimensional Settings
Abstract: Empirical research increasingly deals with large datasets containing numerous control or instrumental variables, necessitating careful variable selection. This paper explores valid inference after post- or orthogonal $L_2$-Boosting is used for variable selection. The authors establish new results for the rate of convergence of iterated post-$L_2$-Boosting and orthogonal $L_2$-Boosting in a high-dimensional setting similar to Lasso, without assuming the beta-min condition. These results are extended to the 2SLS framework for treatment effect analysis. Extensive simulations compare the proposed methods with Lasso, and an empirical application demonstrates their use for estimating the effect of pre-merger bank branch network overlap on acquirer bank stock returns.

title: SenseNet: 3D Objects Database and Tactile Simulator
Abstract: While artificial intelligence research has primarily focused on vision, fueled by high-quality image datasets, this paper advocates for a shift towards sensorimotor systems and tactile feedback to better mimic human intelligence. The authors present SenseNet, a collection of tactile simulators and a large-scale dataset of 3D objects for manipulation. SenseNet aims to accelerate tactile feedback and sensorimotor research, providing new opportunities for machine learning and computational neuroscience communities.

title: ZOOpt: Toolbox for Derivative-Free Optimization
Abstract: ZOOpt (Zeroth Order Optimization) is a derivative-free optimization toolbox that provides efficient solvers for complex functions, including those with many local optima, non-differentiable, and non-continuous functions. Designed for ease of use, ZOOpt offers single-machine parallel optimization using a Python core and multi-machine distributed optimization for time-consuming tasks through the Ray framework. ZOOpt specifically targets optimization problems in machine learning, addressing high-dimensional and noisy problems such as hyper-parameter tuning and direct policy search. It aims to be a ready-to-use tool for real-world machine learning tasks.

title: Towards Building an Intelligent Anti-Malware System: A Deep Learning Approach using Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Malware Classification
Abstract: Effective malware mitigation is a longstanding challenge in information security. This paper explores the potential of deep learning (DL) models for developing an intelligent anti-malware system capable of detecting newly-released malware. By leveraging the Malimg dataset, consisting of malware images processed from binaries, the authors trained three DL models – CNN-SVM, GRU-SVM, and MLP-SVM – for malware family classification. Their empirical findings highlight the GRU-SVM model as the most effective, achieving a predictive accuracy of ~84.92% due to its more sophisticated architecture. The authors propose further exploration of optimal DL-SVM models as the next step in developing an intelligent anti-malware system.

title: Learning Relevant Features of Data with Multi-scale Tensor Networks
Abstract: Inspired by coarse-graining approaches in physics, this paper adapts similar algorithms for data analysis. The resulting algorithms, based on layered tree tensor networks, scale linearly with both the dimension of the input and the training set size. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of these algorithms by classifying MNIST and fashion-MNIST datasets, achieving good results with a smaller number of features by combining unsupervised representation with supervised weights.

title: Neurally Plausible Model of Robot Reaching Inspired by Infant Motor Babbling
Abstract: This paper presents a neurally plausible model of robot reaching inspired by human infant reaching, emphasizing the importance of sensory-motor interaction. The model, based on embodied artificial intelligence, incorporates learning sensory-motor correlations through motor babbling and arm motion planning using spreading activation. Organized in three layers of neural maps representing the same sensory-motor space, the model learns to plan reaching motions with high accuracy and smoothness, as demonstrated through implementation on a humanoid robot.

title: Restricted Boltzmann Machines for Robust and Fast Latent Truth Discovery
Abstract: Latent truth discovery (LTD) aims to uncover the true values of entity attributes despite noisy, conflicting, or incomplete information. While numerous LTD algorithms exist, limited knowledge exists about their overall performance in terms of effectiveness, efficiency, and robustness. This paper proposes LTD-RBM, a novel LTD algorithm based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines, which excels in all three aspects. Extensive experiments on heterogeneous, publicly available datasets demonstrate LTD-RBM's superiority over state-of-the-art LTD techniques.

title: Using Deep Neural Network Approximate Bayesian Network
Abstract: This paper introduces a new method for approximating posterior probabilities of Bayesian Networks using deep neural networks. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate the capability of deep neural networks to learn the joint probability distribution of Bayesian Networks by learning from a few observation and posterior probability distribution pairs with high accuracy. Compared to the traditional likelihood weighting sampling algorithm, this method is faster and achieves higher accuracy for medium-sized Bayesian Networks. The method also benefits from easy parallelization on GPUs. The paper explores the relationship between accuracy and the number of training examples, highlighting the model's saturation with increasing examples. The work contributes to showing how discriminative models like deep neural networks can approximate generative models like Bayesian Networks.

title: Non-invasive biomarkers of fetal brain development reflecting prenatal stress: an integrative multi-scale multi-species perspective on data collection and analysis
Abstract: Prenatal stress (PS) significantly impacts early postnatal behavioral and cognitive development through fetal programming, mediated by its effects on the developing hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic nervous system (ANS). This paper reviews the evidence for PS's effects on fetal programming of the HPA axis and ANS. It proposes a multi-scale, multi-species approach for preclinical and clinical studies to identify early non-invasive biomarkers for these programming effects. This approach aims to identify adverse postnatal brain developmental trajectories, enabling the design of therapeutic interventions. The multiple scales include biomarkers reflecting changes in the brain epigenome, metabolome, microbiome, and ANS activity assessed through fetal heart rate fluctuations. The proposed framework could reveal mechanistic links between maternal stress during pregnancy and physiological changes. These biomarkers could serve as early and non-invasive predictors of neurodevelopmental trajectories influenced by PS. The authors emphasize the need for multi-scale studies across animal models and human cohorts, utilizing machine learning for data synthesis and biomarker identification.

title: Early detection of Crossfire attacks using deep learning
Abstract: Crossfire attacks, designed to disconnect entire geographical areas from the internet, utilize a distributed botnet to generate low-rate benign traffic, congesting selected network links. This paper proposes a framework for early detection of Crossfire attacks during the warm-up period, by monitoring traffic at potential decoy servers. Deep learning methods, including Autoencoder, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Network, are investigated to extract spatiotemporal features for attack detection. The authors report encouraging experimental results.

title: Unstable modes in projection-based reduced-order models: How many can there be, and what do they tell you?
Abstract: Projection methods offer a computationally efficient approach for constructing reduced-order models of large-scale linear dynamical systems. However, these reduced models may not inherit the stability of the original system. This note investigates the number of unstable modes in reduced models generated via orthogonal projection, using theory from iterative methods for linear algebraic systems and eigenvalue problems. Rigorous upper bounds are derived for both continuous- and discrete-time systems. The paper explores the potential of unstable modes in reduced-order models to signal transient growth in the original system.

title: Machine Learning for Building Energy and Indoor Environment: A Perspective
Abstract: Machine learning holds promise for various practical applications, particularly in energy conservation and indoor environment management. This perspective highlights the development and application of machine learning in these fields. The paper addresses the challenge of determining model structure for accurate prediction and proposes the use of an ANN model for predicting indoor culturable fungi concentration, achieving improved accuracy and convenience. Further, an ANN model based on HTS is successfully applied for optimizing building energy systems. This novel method could potentially capture significant attention due to its accuracy and reliability, though further research is needed to assess its feasibility in other fields.

title: Transfer learning for diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on Ultrasound imaging data
Abstract: Classifying ultrasound (US) kidney images for diagnosing congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in children presents a challenge. This study proposes a transfer learning-based method to extract imaging features from US kidney images for improving CAKUT diagnosis. A pre-trained deep learning model (imagenet-caffe-alex) is employed for transfer learning-based feature extraction from 3-channel feature maps computed from US images, including original images, gradient features, and distanced transform features. Support vector machine classifiers are built using transfer learning features, conventional imaging features, and their combination. Experimental results demonstrate that the combination of transfer learning and conventional imaging features achieves the best classification performance for distinguishing CAKUT patients from normal controls based on their US kidney images.

title: Effects of Home Resources and School Environment on Eighth-Grade Mathematics Achievement in Taiwan
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between home resources, school environment, and students' mathematics achievement, drawing from a large body of existing research. The study hypothesizes that students with greater home resources perform better than those with fewer resources, and schools with more socioeconomically advantaged students, located in high-income neighborhoods, and possessing more instructional resources will have better mathematics performance. Focusing on eighth graders in Taiwan, the study explores the variance in mathematics achievement as a function of student and school-level differences.

title: Learning Continuous User Representations through Hybrid Filtering with doc2vec
Abstract: Online ad ecosystem players face challenges in acquiring user data for precise targeting. Audience look-alike modeling offers a potential solution, but model performance depends heavily on data quantity and quality. This paper proposes two novel hybrid filtering techniques using the doc2vec neural probabilistic language model to maximize the predictive performance of look-alike modeling algorithms. The methods are applied to data from a large mobile ad exchange and app metadata from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. The authors model mobile app users through their app usage histories and app descriptions (user2vec), and introduce context awareness by incorporating additional user and app-related metadata (context2vec). The findings demonstrate the superior quality of recommendations from user2vec compared to existing methods, the value of hybrid filtering using doc2vec for look-alike modeling, and the positive impact of context awareness in doc2vec model training.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for List-wise Recommendations
Abstract: Recommender systems play a crucial role in mitigating information overload by suggesting personalized items or services. This paper proposes a novel recommender system capable of continuously improving its strategies during interactions with users. Modeling sequential user-recommender interactions as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), the paper leverages Reinforcement Learning (RL) to automatically learn optimal strategies through trial-and-error recommendations and user feedback. The authors introduce an online user-agent interacting environment simulator for offline pre-training and evaluation of model parameters before online application. They validate the importance of list-wise recommendations during user-agent interactions and develop a novel approach for incorporating them into the proposed framework LIRD. Experimental results on a real-world e-commerce dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Molecular enhanced sampling with autoencoders: On-the-fly collective variable discovery and accelerated free energy landscape exploration
Abstract: Macromolecular and biomolecular folding landscapes often contain high free energy barriers, hindering efficient sampling of configurational space by standard molecular dynamics simulation. Biased sampling can artificially drive simulations along pre-specified collective variables (CVs), but success depends on identifying good CVs related to important collective dynamical motions. This work employs auto-associative artificial neural networks ("autoencoders") to learn nonlinear CVs that are explicit and differentiable functions of atomic coordinates. This approach offers significant speedups in exploring configurational space, enabling simultaneous discovery and acceleration along data-driven CVs. The authors demonstrate the approach in simulations of alanine dipeptide and Trp-cage, providing an open-source and freely-available implementation within OpenMM.

title: Orbital Period Changes in WZ Sagittae
Abstract: This paper presents a long-term study (1961-2017) of eclipse times in the dwarf nova WZ Sagittae, aiming to determine its orbital-period change rate. The study reveals wiggles with a 20-50-year timescale, potentially connected to the 23-year interval between dwarf-nova eruptions. These wiggles dominate the O-C diagram, preventing a precise measurement of the steady orbital-period change rate.

title: A dynamic network model with persistent links and node-specific latent variables, with an application to the interbank market
Abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic network model where two mechanisms control link probability: past link existence and node-specific latent variables (dynamic fitnesses). Assuming a Markov dynamics for both mechanisms, the authors propose an Expectation-Maximization algorithm for model estimation and inference of latent variables. The estimated parameters and fitnesses can be used to forecast future link presence. The methodology is applied to the e-MID interbank network, where the two linkage mechanisms are associated with different trading behaviors – preferential trading and trading driven by node-specific characteristics. Empirical results highlight preferential lending in the interbank market and demonstrate how methods that disregard time-varying network topologies tend to overestimate preferential linkage. |||

title: A Real-time and Registration-free Framework for Dynamic Shape Instantiation
Abstract: Real-time 3D navigation during minimally invasive surgery is crucial, especially when significant tissue movement occurs. To balance image acquisition speed and resolution, only 2D images or low-resolution 3D volumes are currently used in clinical practice. This paper introduces a real-time, registration-free framework for dynamic shape instantiation, applicable to multiple anatomical areas, to create high-resolution 3D organ shapes from a single 2D image during surgery. The method first determines an optimal scan plane using sparse principal component analysis (SPCA) and the pre-operative 3D statistical shape model (SSM) of the anatomy, considering practical constraints. Then, kernel partial least squares regression (KPLSR) is used to learn the relationship between the pre-operative 3D SSM and a synchronized 2D SSM constructed from 2D images obtained at the optimal scan plane. This learned relationship is then applied to new intra-operative 2D images acquired at the same scan plane to predict the high-resolution 3D shape in real-time. A key advantage of this framework is the elimination of the need for extra registration between the pre-operative 3D SSM and the synchronized 2D SSM. Thorough validation was performed on studies involving the liver and right ventricle (RV) of the heart. The derived results (mean accuracy of 2.19mm on patients and computation speed of 1ms) demonstrate the potential clinical value of this method for real-time, high-resolution, dynamic 3D interventional guidance.

title: Theory of Deep Learning III: explaining the non-overfitting puzzle
Abstract: Despite their large overparametrization and capacity to fit random data, deep networks surprisingly do not overfit. This study investigates this phenomenon by demonstrating that the dynamics associated with gradient descent minimization of nonlinear networks, near the asymptotically stable minima of the empirical error, are topologically equivalent to a linear gradient system in a quadratic potential with a degenerate (for square loss) or almost degenerate (for logistic or cross-entropy loss) Hessian. This proposition draws upon the qualitative theory of dynamical systems and is supported by numerical results. Our key propositions extend two properties of gradient descent for linear networks, previously established as essential for their generalization properties, to deep nonlinear networks: 1. Gradient descent implicitly regularizes the model based on the number of iterations, asymptotically converging to the minimum norm solution for suitable initial conditions. This implies that early stopping can effectively prevent overfitting, particularly in regression tasks. 2. For classification tasks, asymptotic convergence to the minimum norm solution leads to convergence towards the maximum margin solution, ensuring good classification error for "low noise" datasets. This property holds for loss functions like the logistic and cross-entropy loss regardless of the initial conditions. The robustness to overparametrization observed here has implications for the robustness of the architecture of deep convolutional networks with respect to the curse of dimensionality.

title: PAC-Bayesian Margin Bounds for Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Recent work has explored the generalization error of deep neural networks using the PAC-Bayesian framework for fully connected layers. This paper extends this approach to the convolutional setting.

title: Deep Learning for Fatigue Estimation on the Basis of Multimodal Human-Machine Interactions
Abstract: This paper proposes a new method to monitor current physical load and accumulated fatigue using objective and subjective characteristics. It was applied to a dataset specifically designed to estimate physical load and fatigue using various statistical and machine learning techniques. Data from peripheral sensors (accelerometer, GPS, gyroscope, magnetometer) and a brain-computing interface (electroencephalography) were collected, integrated, and analyzed using statistical and machine learning methods such as moment analysis, cluster analysis, and principal component analysis. The paper presents and proves hypothesis 1: physical activity can be classified not only by objective parameters but also by subjective parameters. Hypothesis 2, stating that experienced physical load and subsequent restoration can be quantified as fatigue levels with distinctive patterns, is also presented, and potential methods to prove it are demonstrated. Several "physical load" and "fatigue" metrics are proposed. The presented results expand the application of machine learning methods for characterizing complex human activity patterns, allowing for the estimation of actual physical load and fatigue, and providing personalized cautions and advice.

title: Community Detection in Partially Observable Social Networks
Abstract: The discovery of community structures in social networks has garnered significant attention due to its importance in understanding network topology and functions. However, social network data are often collected from partially observable networks with missing nodes and edges. This paper addresses the challenge of detecting overlapping community structures in such incomplete networks, allowing nodes to belong to multiple communities simultaneously. To tackle this problem, the paper introduces KroMFac, a novel framework that performs community detection through regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) based on the Kronecker graph model. From an inferred Kronecker generative parameter matrix, KroMFac first estimates the missing portion of the network. As a key contribution, to enhance community detection accuracy, the framework identifies and selects influential nodes (typically with high degrees) via ranking and adds them to the existing graph. Finally, community structures are unveiled by solving the regularized NMF-aided optimization problem, maximizing the likelihood of the underlying graph. Empirical evaluation using both synthetic and real-world networks shows the superiority of KroMFac over baseline schemes in terms of normalized mutual information (NMI).

title: Towards co-evolution of fitness predictors and Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks have proven to be a powerful tool with numerous practical applications, especially in learning from large labeled datasets. However, achieving optimal learning results requires careful network architecture design. Creating an ideal topology often necessitates extensive experience and knowledge, and there are currently no practical algorithms to aid this process. Utilizing an evolutionary process to develop new network topologies could address this problem. The limiting factor in this case is the speed of evaluating individual network architectures, which involves training on the entire large dataset. This paper proposes a fitness prediction technique to overcome this bottleneck. By using subsets of the original training set for the training process, the results can be used as an approximation of the specimen's fitness. The feasibility of this approach is discussed considering desired fitness predictor features, and the potential of using subsets obtained during the evolutionary process to estimate the fitness of network topologies is analyzed. Finally, conclusions are drawn from experimental results and future work plans are outlined.

title: Compare, Compress and Propagate: Enhancing Neural Architectures with Alignment Factorization for Natural Language Inference
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning architecture for Natural Language Inference (NLI) that enhances representation learning. The architecture compares alignment pairs, compresses them, and then propagates the compressed information to upper layers. Furthermore, factorization layers are employed to efficiently and expressively compress alignment vectors into scalar features, which are then used to augment the base word representations. This approach aims to be conceptually simple, compact, yet powerful. Experiments on three popular benchmarks, SNLI, MultiNLI, and SciTail, demonstrate competitive performance on all. A lightweight parameterization of the model achieves a 3x reduction in parameter size compared to existing state-of-the-art models (ESIM and DIIN) while maintaining competitive performance. Visual analysis reveals that the propagated features are highly interpretable.

title: Parameter-free online learning via model selection
Abstract: This paper presents an efficient algorithmic framework for model selection in online learning, also known as parameter-free online learning. Unlike previous work focusing on highly structured function classes, this framework proposes a generic meta-algorithm that achieves online model selection oracle inequalities under minimal structural assumptions. The framework provides the first computationally efficient parameter-free algorithms that operate in arbitrary Banach spaces under mild smoothness assumptions, while previous results were limited to Hilbert spaces. New oracle inequalities are derived for matrix classes, non-nested convex sets, and  with generic regularizers. These results are further generalized by providing oracle inequalities for arbitrary non-linear classes in the online supervised learning model. All these results are derived through a unified meta-algorithm scheme using a novel "multi-scale" algorithm for prediction with expert advice based on random playout, which may be of independent interest.

title: Towards automated patient data cleaning using deep learning: A feasibility study on the standardization of organ labeling
Abstract: Data cleaning consumes a significant portion of the time spent on data analysis for clinical research projects, particularly in the era of big data and machine learning in medicine where massive volumes of data are generated. This paper presents an initial effort towards automated patient data cleaning using deep learning, focusing on the standardization of organ labeling in radiation therapy. Organs are often labeled inconsistently across different institutions (even within the same institution) and time periods, posing a challenge for clinical research, especially multi-institutional collaborative studies. The paper describes the development of a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically identify and label each organ in CT images with the standardized nomenclature presented by AAPM Task Group 263. The model was tested on CT images of 54 patients with prostate cancer and 100 patients with head and neck cancer who previously received radiation therapy. The model achieved 100% accuracy in detecting organs and assigning standardized labels for the patients tested. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for patient data cleaning, enabling the generation of standardized datasets for effective intra- and interinstitutional collaborative clinical research.

title: PrivySense: $\underline{Pri}$ce $\underline{V}$olatilit$\underline{y}$ based $\underline{Sen}$timent$\underline{s}$ $\underline{E}$stimation from Financial News using Machine Learning
Abstract: As machine learning gains prominence in computer science, sentiment analysis using various textual data is becoming increasingly prevalent. This is particularly pronounced in formulating securities trading strategies, due to the relative ease of implementation and the abundance of research suggesting automated sentiment analysis can be effectively used in trading. The source data for these analyzers covers a wide spectrum, including social media feeds, micro-blogs, real-time news feeds, and ex-post financial data. The underlying technique typically involves supervised learning of sentiment classification, where a classifier is trained on annotated source corpus, and accuracy is measured by assessing its generalization performance on unseen test data. Post-training and model validation, these classifiers are used to execute trading strategies, and the corresponding returns are compared to benchmark returns (e.g., S&P500 returns). This paper introduces a novel technique that utilizes price volatilities to empirically determine sentiment in news data, rather than the traditional reverse approach. It also performs meta-sentiment analysis by evaluating the efficacy of existing sentiment classifiers and exploring the precise definition of sentiment in securities trading context. The paper scrutinizes the efficacy of using human-annotated sentiment classification and the tacit assumptions that introduce subjective bias in existing financial news sentiment classifiers.

title: Learning Structural Weight Uncertainty for Sequential Decision-Making
Abstract: Learning probability distributions on the weights of neural networks (NNs) has recently shown promise in numerous applications. Bayesian methods, such as Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD), provide an elegant framework for reasoning about NN model uncertainty. However, by assuming independent Gaussian priors for individual NN weights, SVGD fails to incorporate prior knowledge about structural information (dependence) among weights. This paper proposes efficient posterior learning of structural weight uncertainty within an SVGD framework by employing matrix variate Gaussian priors on NN parameters. The learned structural uncertainty is then investigated in sequential decision-making problems, including contextual bandits and reinforcement learning. Experiments on various synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the superiority of this model compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Face Synthesis from Visual Attributes via Sketch using Conditional VAEs and GANs
Abstract: Automatic face synthesis from visual attributes is a significant problem in computer vision with wide-ranging applications in law enforcement and entertainment. Deep generative convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been used to synthesize face images from attributes and text descriptions. This paper proposes a different approach by formulating the problem as a stage-wise learning process. It first synthesizes a facial sketch corresponding to the visual attributes and then reconstructs the face image based on this sketch. The proposed Attribute2Sketch2Face framework, based on a combination of deep Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), comprises three stages: (1) Synthesis of facial sketch from attributes using a CVAE architecture, (2) Enhancement of coarse sketches to produce sharper sketches using a GAN-based framework, and (3) Synthesis of face from sketch using another GAN-based network. Extensive experiments and comparisons with recent methods validate the effectiveness of this attribute-based three-stage face synthesis method.

title: Particle Clustering Machine: A Dynamical System Based Approach
Abstract: Identifying clusters from an unlabeled dataset is a fundamental problem in Unsupervised Machine Learning. Existing clustering algorithms typically rely on either the statistical or geometric properties of the dataset. This paper proposes a novel method for clustering data points using dynamical systems theory. By constructing a gradient dynamical system using interaction potential, the paper proves that the asymptotic dynamics of this system determine the cluster centers when the system is initialized at the data points. While many existing heuristic-based clustering techniques suffer from a stochastic nature, the proposed algorithm is deterministic, ensuring consistent outcomes across multiple runs with the same input data. Another advantage is that the number of clusters, often difficult to determine in practice, does not need to be specified beforehand. Simulation results are presented, and comparisons are made with existing methods.

title: Dendritic error backpropagation in deep cortical microcircuits
Abstract: Animal behavior depends on learning to associate sensory stimuli with desired motor commands. Understanding how the brain orchestrates the necessary synaptic modifications across different brain areas has remained a long-standing puzzle. This paper introduces a multi-area neuronal network model in which synaptic plasticity continuously adapts the network towards a global desired output. In this model, synaptic learning is driven by a local dendritic prediction error arising from a failure to predict the top-down input given the bottom-up activities. Such errors occur at apical dendrites of pyramidal neurons where both long-range excitatory feedback and local inhibitory predictions are integrated. When local inhibition fails to match excitatory feedback, an error occurs that triggers plasticity at bottom-up synapses at basal dendrites of the same pyramidal neurons. The paper demonstrates the learning capabilities of the model in various tasks and shows that it approximates the classical error backpropagation algorithm. Furthermore, complementing this cortical circuit with a disinhibitory mechanism enables attention-like stimulus denoising and generation. This framework provides several experimental predictions regarding the function of dendritic integration and cortical microcircuits, aligns with recent observations of cross-area learning, and suggests a biological implementation of deep learning.

title: f-Divergence constrained policy improvement
Abstract: To ensure stability in learning, state-of-the-art generalized policy iteration algorithms augment the policy improvement step with a trust region constraint to bound information loss. The size of this trust region is typically determined by the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, which effectively captures distance and yields closed-form solutions. This paper extends the analysis to a more general class of f-divergences and derives corresponding policy update rules. The generic solution is expressed through the derivative of the convex conjugate function to f and includes the KL solution as a special case. Within the class of f-divergences, the paper focuses on a one-parameter family of  divergences to study the impact of divergence choice on policy improvement. Both known and new policy updates emerge for different values of . The paper demonstrates that each type of policy update comes with a compatible policy evaluation resulting from the chosen f-divergence. Interestingly, mean-squared Bellman error minimization is closely related to policy evaluation with the Pearson  penalty, while KL divergence results in the soft-max policy update and a log-sum-exp critic. Asymptotic analysis of the solutions for different values of is conducted, and the effects of using different divergence functions are demonstrated on a multi-armed bandit problem and common reinforcement learning problems.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Unsupervised Video Summarization with Diversity-Representativeness Reward
Abstract: Video summarization aims to facilitate large-scale video browsing by producing concise and diverse summaries that represent the original videos. This paper formulates video summarization as a sequential decision-making process and develops a deep summarization network (DSN) to summarize videos. DSN predicts a probability for each video frame, indicating its likelihood of being selected, and then takes actions based on these probability distributions to select frames, forming video summaries. To train DSN, the paper proposes an end-to-end reinforcement learning-based framework with a novel reward function that jointly accounts for diversity and representativeness of generated summaries, without relying on labels or user interactions. During training, the reward function judges the diversity and representativeness of the generated summaries, while DSN learns to produce more diverse and representative summaries to earn higher rewards. Since labels are not required, the method is fully unsupervised. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets show that this unsupervised method not only outperforms other state-of-the-art unsupervised methods but is also comparable to or even superior to most published supervised approaches.

title: Characterizing optimal hierarchical policy inference on graphs via non-equilibrium thermodynamics
Abstract: Hierarchies are fundamentally important in both stochastic optimal control and biological control, facilitating desirable computational traits in control algorithms and potentially forming a core principle of sensorimotor and cognitive control systems. However, theoretically justified construction of state-space hierarchies across all spatial resolutions and their evolution through a policy inference process remains a challenge. This paper introduces a formalism for deriving such normative representations of discrete Markov decision processes in the context of graphs. The resulting hierarchies correspond to a hierarchical policy inference algorithm that approximates a discrete gradient flow between state-space trajectory densities generated by the prior and optimal policies.

title: A Deep Belief Network Based Machine Learning System for Risky Host Detection
Abstract: To ensure cyber security in an enterprise, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems are typically implemented to normalize security events from different preventive technologies and flag alerts. Analysts in the security operation center (SOC) investigate these alerts to determine if they are truly malicious. However, the volume of alerts is often overwhelming, with a majority being false positives, exceeding the SOC's capacity to handle all alerts. This necessitates a significant reduction in the false positive rate. While previous research primarily focused on network intrusion detection, this paper focuses on risk detection and proposes an intelligent Deep Belief Network machine learning system. The system leverages alert information, various security logs, and analysts' investigation results in a real enterprise environment to flag hosts with a high likelihood of being compromised. Text mining and graph-based methods are used to generate targets and create features for machine learning. In the experiment, the Deep Belief Network is compared to other machine learning algorithms, including multi-layer neural network, random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression. Results on real enterprise data indicate that the deep belief network machine learning system outperforms other algorithms for this problem and is six times more effective than the current rule-based system. The paper also describes the implementation of the entire system, from data collection, label creation, feature engineering to host score generation, in a real enterprise production environment.

title: Non-negative Matrix Factorization: Robust Extraction of Extended Structures
Abstract: This paper applies the vectorized Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) method to post-processing direct imaging data for exoplanetary systems like circumstellar disks. NMF is an iterative approach that first creates a non-orthogonal and non-negative basis of components using given reference images, then models a target using these components. The constructed model is then rescaled with a factor to compensate for the contribution from a disk. This paper compares NMF with existing methods (classical reference differential imaging and the Karhunen-Loève image projection algorithm) using synthetic circumstellar disks and demonstrates the superiority of NMF. Without the need for prior reference selection, NMF can detect fainter circumstellar disks, better preserve low-order disk morphology, and does not require forward modeling. As an application to a well-known disk example, the paper processes archival Hubble Space Telescope (HST) STIS coronagraphic observations of HD~181327 with different methods and compares them. NMF successfully extracts some circumstellar material inside the primary ring for the first time. In the appendix, the mathematical stability of NMF components during iteration and the linearity of NMF modeling are investigated.

title: A Unified Bayesian Inference Framework for Generalized Linear Models
Abstract: This letter presents a unified Bayesian inference framework for generalized linear models (GLM) that iteratively reduces the GLM problem to a sequence of standard linear model (SLM) problems. This framework provides new perspectives on established GLM algorithms derived from SLM ones and suggests novel extensions for other SLM algorithms. Specific instances elucidated under this framework include the GLM versions of approximate message passing (AMP), vector AMP (VAMP), and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL). It is proven that the resulting GLM version of AMP is equivalent to the well-known generalized approximate message passing (GAMP). Numerical results for 1-bit quantized compressed sensing (CS) demonstrate the effectiveness of this unified framework. |||

title: SBEED: Convergent Reinforcement Learning with Nonlinear Function Approximation
Abstract: Addressing a long-standing challenge in reinforcement learning, this paper tackles the instability issues that arise when function approximation is used to solve the Bellman optimality equation. By reformulating the Bellman equation as a primal-dual optimization problem using Nesterov's smoothing technique and the Legendre-Fenchel transformation, the authors introduce a novel algorithm, Smoothed Bellman Error Embedding. This algorithm, capable of utilizing any differentiable function class, offers the first convergence guarantee for general nonlinear function approximation and analyzes the algorithm's sample complexity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate the algorithm's competitive performance against state-of-the-art baselines in several benchmark control problems.

title: Large-Scale Experiment on the Importance of Social Learning and Unimodality in the Wisdom of the Crowd
Abstract: This study delves into the conditions under which the Wisdom of the Crowd (WoC) phenomenon is enhanced or diminished by exposing individuals to the predictions of their peers. The research presents a novel dataset of unprecedented scale and detail. A key finding highlights the importance of unimodal social information: when individuals observe a clear peak in the distribution of the crowd's predictions, WoC improves, but when no such peak exists, it deteriorates. Furthermore, social learning weights are estimated to identify individuals who are particularly adept at learning from the crowd, enabling potential filtering for improved collective accuracy.

title: Boosting the Actor with Dual Critic
Abstract: This paper introduces a new actor-critic-style algorithm, Dual Actor-Critic (Dual-AC), grounded in the Lagrangian dual form of the Bellman optimality equation. This framework reinterprets the learning process as a two-player game between the actor and a "dual critic" function.  Unlike traditional actor-critic approaches, Dual-AC updates the actor and dual critic cooperatively to optimize the same objective function, providing a more transparent method for learning the critic that is directly linked to the actor's objective. The paper then presents a concrete algorithm using multi-step bootstrapping, path regularization, and a stochastic dual ascent algorithm to effectively solve the resulting minimax optimization problem. Through various benchmarks, the proposed algorithm demonstrates state-of-the-art performances.
label: AI

title: A Stochastic Trust Region Algorithm Based on Careful Step Normalization
Abstract: This paper introduces an algorithm for solving stochastic and finite sum minimization problems. Based on a trust region methodology, the algorithm incorporates normalized steps when stochastic gradient estimates fall within a specified range. The algorithm dynamically decides whether to use normalized steps, offering convergence guarantees similar to traditional stochastic gradient methods under various conditions related to stochastic gradient estimate accuracy and stepsize selection.  Numerical experiments on convex and nonconvex machine learning problems demonstrate the method's potential to outperform traditional stochastic gradient approaches.
label: AI

title: Using abstract elastic membranes to learn about quantum measurements
Abstract: This article presents a popular science version of a research paper exploring an extended version of the quantum formalism as a potential solution to the measurement problem. The original work, by Diederik Aerts and the author, was published in "Ann. Phys. 351 (2014) 975--1025, arXiv:1404.2429."  This accessible explanation aims to introduce the concept to a wider audience.

title: Interstellar communication. VII. Benchmarking inscribed matter probes
Abstract: Building upon previous work that investigated the optimal frequency of interstellar photon communications and benchmarked other particle information carriers, this paper compares the latency and bandwidth of sending probes carrying inscribed matter. The study considers factors such as durability requirements for shielding against dust and radiation, as well as data duplication. Results show that while probes have negligible weight overhead at velocities below 0.2c, they offer significant advantages in terms of energy efficiency per bit and bandwidth compared to classical communication, particularly for long distances (kpc) and low velocities (<0.1c). However, they come at the cost of higher latency.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Interior Tomography for Region-of-Interest Reconstruction
Abstract: Interior tomography for region-of-interest (ROI) imaging offers benefits like reduced detector size and X-ray dose. However, standard analytic reconstruction techniques suffer from severe cupping artifacts caused by null space in the truncated Radon transform. While existing penalized reconstruction methods can address this issue, they involve extensive computations due to iterative reconstruction. Inspired by recent deep learning advancements in low-dose and sparse view CT, this paper proposes a deep learning architecture that removes null space signals from filtered backprojection (FBP) reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate near-perfect reconstruction with a 7-10 dB improvement in PSNR compared to existing methods, achieved with significantly reduced runtime complexity.
label: AI

title: Advanced data mining in field ion microscopy
Abstract: Field ion microscopy (FIM) enables the visualization of individual surface atoms by exploiting the effects of an intense electric field.  While FIM's atomic resolution imaging potential has been limited by a lack of efficient image processing tools, recent advances in imaging and data mining techniques have renewed interest in FIM for materials characterization. This paper, after reviewing existing FIM routines, examines the application of machine learning (ML) approaches for data extraction. The authors explore various supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms, along with advanced image processing techniques, to extract information from large sets of FIM images. The paper discusses the outcomes, limitations, and potential applications of these methods, highlighting the use of energy minimization schemes for improving FIM spatial resolution.

title: Scalable Multi-Domain Dialogue State Tracking
Abstract: Dialogue state tracking (DST), a crucial component of task-oriented dialogue systems, estimates the user's goal at each turn based on the interaction history. Current state-of-the-art approaches rely on deep learning methods and represent dialogue state as a distribution over all possible slot values. This representation becomes problematic when dealing with unbounded or dynamic sets of values. Furthermore, training requires labeled data, hindering model creation for new domains. This paper presents a scalable multi-domain deep learning approach for DST, introducing a novel framework independent of the slot value set. Dialogue state is represented as a distribution over values of interest derived from the dialogue history or knowledge, limiting the candidate set size and addressing the slot scalability issue. Through a slot-independent architecture and transfer learning, the proposed approach enables quick adaptation to new domains.
label: AI

title: Proteomics Analysis of FLT3-ITD Mutation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Using Deep Learning Neural Network
Abstract: Deep Learning can significantly enhance cancer proteomics and genomics. This study aims to identify critical proteins associated with the FLT3-ITD mutation in newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia patients. A Deep Learning network using autoencoders forms a hierarchical model that extracts high-level features without labeled training data. Dimensional reduction narrows down the number of critical proteins from 231 to 20.  The network reveals a strong correlation between FLT3-ITD mutation and the levels of these 20 critical proteins (accuracy 97%, sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%). This study provides a novel approach to determining critical protein pathways in the FLT3-ITD mutation and presents a proof-of-concept for accurately modeling big data in cancer proteomics and genomics.

title: Learning Deep Similarity Models with Focus Ranking for Fabric Image Retrieval
Abstract: Fabric image retrieval is essential for various applications, including clothing search, online shopping, and cloth modeling. Learning pairwise image similarity is crucial for image retrieval tasks. This paper introduces a novel embedding method, termed focus ranking, easily integrated into a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for jointly learning image representations and metrics in the context of fine-grained fabric image retrieval. Focus ranking aims to rank similar examples higher than dissimilar ones by penalizing ranking disorders through minimization of the cost associated with similar samples ranked below dissimilar ones. Training samples are organized into focus ranking units for efficient optimization.  The paper introduces a large-scale fabric image retrieval dataset (FIRD) with 25,000 images of 4,300 fabrics and evaluates the proposed model on this dataset. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model over existing metric embedding models.

title: Quantum Lower Bounds for Tripartite Versions of the Hidden Shift and the Set Equality Problems
Abstract: This paper investigates the quantum query complexity of two tripartite generalizations of the hidden shift and set equality problems, termed the 3-shift-sum and the 3-matching-sum problems. The 3-shift-sum problem involves determining whether a table of 3 x n elements can be circularly shifted to achieve zero column sums. The 3-matching-sum problem allows arbitrary permutation of elements within each row. The paper proves lower bounds of Ω(n^(1/3)) and Ω(√n), respectively, for these problems.  The second lower bound is tight.  The lower bounds are achieved through a novel application of the dual learning graph framework and representation-theoretic tools.
label: AI

title: RedDwarfData: a simplified dataset of StarCraft matches
Abstract: StarCraft, a complex real-time strategy game, presents a compelling testbed for new machine learning and computational intelligence techniques. However, long match durations and the challenge of creating effective training datasets pose obstacles. This paper introduces RedDwarfData, a simplified dataset extracted from the matches published by Robinson and Watson. This dataset comprises thousands of matches processed into frames, enabling temporal studies. RedDwarfData is freely available on GitHub, along with an initial analysis and appraisal of the matches.
label: AI

title: Non-linear motor control by local learning in spiking neural networks
Abstract: Training a spiking neural network with hidden neurons to control nonlinear body dynamics using local, stable, and online rules remains a challenge. This paper introduces a supervised scheme, Feedback-based Online Local Learning Of Weights (FOLLOW), for training a network of heterogeneous spiking neurons with hidden layers to control a two-link arm and reproduce a desired state trajectory. The network learns an inverse model of the nonlinear dynamics, inferring the continuous-time command that produced the trajectory from the input state trajectory. Connection weights are adjusted using a local plasticity rule based on pre-synaptic firing and post-synaptic feedback of the error in the inferred command. The paper explores different network architectures, identifying a differential feedforward structure that minimizes test error. The learned inverse model is then used to generate a continuous-time motor command to control the arm given a desired trajectory.
label: AI

title: Significance of Softmax-based Features in Comparison to Distance Metric Learning-based Features
Abstract: Extracting useful deep features is crucial for many computer vision tasks. Deep features from classification networks have shown promising performance in such tasks. To enhance feature usefulness, end-to-end distance metric learning (DML) has been applied to train the feature extractor directly. However, previous DML studies lacked equitable comparisons between features extracted from DML-based and softmax-based networks. This paper presents objective comparisons between these two approaches using the same network architecture, demonstrating that softmax-based features exhibit competitive or even superior performance compared to state-of-the-art DML features when the dataset size is large. The findings suggest that softmax-based features should be considered when evaluating deep feature performance.
label: AI

title: Learning Deep and Compact Models for Gesture Recognition
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of developing a compact and accurate model for gesture recognition from videos using a deep learning framework. The authors propose a joint 3DCNN-LSTM model that is end-to-end trainable and effectively captures dynamic information in actions. The solution achieves near state-of-the-art accuracy on the ChaLearn dataset with half the model size. The paper further explores knowledge distillation and model compression techniques to achieve a significantly more compact representation. The final model, less than 1 MB in size (one hundredth of the initial model), experiences only a 7% drop in accuracy, making it suitable for real-time gesture recognition on mobile devices.
label: AI

title: The Multilinear Structure of ReLU Networks
Abstract: This paper examines the loss surface of neural networks employing a hinge loss criterion and ReLU or leaky ReLU nonlinearities. These networks define piecewise multilinear forms in parameter space. Through harmonic analysis, the authors demonstrate that all local minima of such networks are non-differentiable, except for those occurring in regions of parameter space with perfectly flat loss surfaces. Non-differentiable minima are not mere technicalities but integral to the problem when analyzing ReLU network loss. Consequently, nonsmooth analysis techniques are required to study these loss surfaces. The paper illustrates the application of these techniques in specific cases.
label: AI

title: Beyond Keywords and Relevance: A Personalized Ad Retrieval Framework in E-Commerce Sponsored Search
Abstract: On most sponsored search platforms, advertisers bid on keywords for their advertisements. Ad retrieval modules rewrite search queries into bidding keywords, using these keywords to select top ads through inverted indexes. This system can prevent retrieval of relevant ads if advertisers do not bid on corresponding keywords. Additionally, most ad retrieval approaches treat rewriting and ad-selection as separate tasks, focusing on relevance between queries and ads.  In e-commerce sponsored search, personalized information like user profiles and click data has become increasingly common, enabling more elements to be used as search signals and retrieval keys. However, this personalization makes it more challenging to measure ads retrieved through different signals. This paper proposes a novel ad retrieval framework for e-commerce sponsored search that goes beyond keywords and relevance.  The framework initializes a hierarchical network representing signals, keys, and ads, incorporating personalized information, using historical ad click data. A model trained on top of this network learns edge weights, and edge selection is used to optimize RPM/CTR. Experimental results on an e-commerce platform demonstrate the framework's effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Objective evaluation metrics for automatic classification of EEG events
Abstract: The evaluation of machine learning algorithms in biomedical fields, particularly for applications involving sequential data, lacks standardization. Commonly used quantitative scalar evaluation metrics like sensitivity and specificity can be misleading depending on the application's needs. Metrics should reflect user requirements while being sensitive enough to guide algorithm development. Feedback from clinicians using automated event detection software in critical care has emphasized a low false alarm rate (typically measured in errors per 24 hours) as the most important criterion for user acceptance. Although a single metric may not be as insightful as performance analysis across various operating conditions, there is a need for a scalar figure of merit. This paper discusses the limitations of existing metrics for seizure detection and proposes new metrics that offer a more balanced view of performance. Using the TUH EEG Corpus, the authors demonstrate these metrics on a seizure detection task. Two promising metrics are Actual Term-Weighted Value (ATWV), a concept borrowed from spoken term detection, and Time-Aligned Event Scoring (TAES), which accounts for temporal alignment between hypothesis and reference annotation. The paper also highlights that state-of-the-art deep learning technology, despite impressive performance, still needs significant improvement to meet strict user acceptance criteria.
label: AI

title: Generation of Bose-Einstein Condensates' Ground State Through Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that both single-component and two-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) ground states can be simulated by deep convolutional neural networks with the same structure. The neural network is trained by inputting the coupling strength in the dimensionless Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GPE) and outputting the ground state wave-function. After training, the neural network generates ground states faster than the imaginary time evolution method, with relative mean-square-error between predicted and original states in the range of 10^-5 to 10^-4. Comparing eigen-energies based on predicted and original states reveals high-precision predictions. Therefore, BEC ground states, continuous wave-functions, can be effectively represented by deep convolutional neural networks. |||

title: Finite-sample risk bounds for maximum likelihood estimation with arbitrary penalties
Abstract: The MDL two-part coding index of resolvability offers a finite-sample upper bound for penalized likelihood estimators within countable models. This bound, however, does not apply to unpenalized maximum likelihood estimation or procedures with extremely small penalties. This paper presents a more general inequality that holds for arbitrary penalties, extending the applicability of the bound. This approach also enables the derivation of exact risk bounds of order 1/n for iid parametric models, improving upon the order (log n)/n resolvability bounds. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of these findings for adaptive estimation.
label: AI

title: Recent Advances in Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) excel at learning features and long-term dependencies from sequential and time-series data. They consist of a stack of non-linear units with at least one connection forming a directed cycle. While a well-trained RNN can model any dynamical system, training them is often hampered by challenges in learning long-term dependencies. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of RNNs, covering their fundamentals and recent advances, along with an introduction to the research challenges in the field. The survey aims to serve both newcomers and professionals in the field of RNNs.
label: AI

title: Application of Convolutional Neural Network to Predict Airfoil Lift Coefficient
Abstract: This study investigates the suitability of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for aerodynamic meta-modeling tasks. The primary goal is to develop a CNN architecture that can handle variable flow conditions and object geometry, while also identifying an effective data preparation process. The study trains multiple CNN structures to learn the lift coefficients of airfoils with varying shapes, Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers, and angles of attack. For comparison, a multi-layered perceptron (MLP) is also trained on the same dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed CNN meta-modeling approach is comparable to MLP in learning capability, and more importantly, the CNN model achieves competitive prediction accuracy with minimal geometric representation constraints.
label: AI

title: Reinforcement Learning with Analogical Similarity to Guide Schema Induction and Attention
Abstract: Research in analogical reasoning suggests that higher-order cognitive functions like abstract reasoning, far transfer, and creativity are rooted in recognizing structural similarities between relational systems. This paper integrates theories of analogy with the computational framework of reinforcement learning (RL). It proposes a new psychological theory that combines analogy and RL, where analogical comparison provides a measure of relational similarity for the RL learning algorithm, and RL provides feedback signals for driving analogical learning. Simulation results support the effectiveness of this combined approach.
label: AI

title: Active Robotic Mapping through Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper proposes an approach for learning agents for active robotic mapping, where the goal is to map the environment as quickly as possible. The agent learns to map efficiently in simulated environments by receiving rewards based on the speed of accurate map construction. Unlike previous work, this approach learns an exploration policy based on a user-specified prior over environment configurations and sensor models, allowing for task-specific specialization. The approach is evaluated in a simulated Disaster Mapping scenario and achieves performance slightly better than a near-optimal myopic exploration scheme, suggesting its potential for more complex problem scenarios.
label: AI

title: Multi-timescale memory dynamics in a reinforcement learning network with attention-gated memory
Abstract: Learning and memory are intricately linked in the brain, and their relationship is central to several recent neural network models. The Attention-Gated MEmory Tagging (AuGMEnT) model, a reinforcement learning network emphasizing biological plausibility of memory dynamics and learning, struggles with hierarchical tasks. These tasks require maintaining higher-level stimuli over long durations while remembering and forgetting lower-level stimuli on shorter timescales. To address this limitation, the paper introduces hybrid AuGMEnT, incorporating both leaky (short-timescale) and non-leaky (long-timescale) memory units. This hybrid architecture allows for exchanging lower-level information while preserving higher-level information, successfully addressing both hierarchical and distractor tasks.
label: AI

title: Corpus specificity in LSA and Word2vec: the role of out-of-domain documents
Abstract: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) and Word2vec are widely used word embedding techniques, but the mechanisms underlying their acquisition of new semantic relations remain unclear. This paper investigates whether the capacity of LSA and Word2vec to identify relevant semantic dimensions increases with corpus size. While intuitively, larger data should lead to better dimension identification, the signal-to-noise ratio might weaken if the corpus expands with topics unrelated to the domain of interest. The paper examines these alternative hypotheses by studying two methods for document elimination: random document removal and removal of documents unrelated to a specific task. The results show that Word2vec effectively utilizes all documents, achieving optimal performance with the entire corpus. Conversely, LSA benefits from corpus specialization (removal of out-of-domain documents) and dimensionality reduction, leading to improved word-representation quality and faster processing. However, specialization without dimensionality reduction significantly reduces LSA's performance on specific tasks. The paper argues that LSA's word-knowledge acquisition might not efficiently leverage higher-order co-occurrences and global relations, unlike Word2vec.
label: AI

title: Kernel Robust Bias-Aware Prediction under Covariate Shift
Abstract: Covariate shift, where training (source) and testing (target) data differ in input space distribution but share the same conditional label distribution, poses a challenging machine learning problem. Robust Bias-Aware (RBA) prediction aims to provide a conditional label distribution that is robust to the worst-case logarithmic loss for the target distribution while matching feature expectation constraints from the source distribution. However, insufficient feature constraints in RBA can lead to high-certainty predictions for the source data while leaving too much uncertainty for target data predictions. This paper extends the representer theorem to the RBA setting, enabling minimization of regularized expected target risk through a reweighted kernel expectation under the source distribution. By employing kernel methods, the paper establishes consistency guarantees and demonstrates improved performance of the RBA classifier compared to competing methods on synthetically biased UCI datasets and datasets with natural covariate shift.

title: Robust Covariate Shift Prediction with General Losses and Feature Views
Abstract: Covariate shift relaxes the commonly assumed independent and identically distributed (IID) assumption by allowing different training and testing input distributions. Traditional methods for addressing covariate shift using importance weighting often exhibit poor theoretical performance guarantees and unreliable predictions with high variance in practice. While recent methods focused on constructing robust predictors for covariate shift learning are limited to minimizing logloss and can be overly conservative in high-dimensional settings. This paper addresses these limitations by robustly minimizing various loss functions, including non-convex ones, under the testing distribution. It also introduces feature-based views to shape the influence of covariate shift according to the relationship between input variables and example labels. These generalizations extend the applicability of robust covariate shift prediction to a wider range of task scenarios, demonstrated through improved performance on classification under covariate shift tasks.
label: AI

title: Discriminative and Geometry Aware Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
Abstract: Domain adaptation (DA) aims to generalize a learning model across training and testing data despite mismatched data distributions. This paper argues that an effective DA method should 1) seek a shared feature subspace where source and target data are aligned in terms of distribution and discriminative (well-separated instances of different classes) and 2) consider the geometric structure of the underlying data manifold for inferring target domain labels. The paper derives three DA models – CDDA, GA-DA, and DGA-DA – to highlight the contributions of Close yet Discriminative DA (CDDA) based on point 1, Geometry Aware DA (GA-DA) based on point 2, and Discriminative and Geometry Aware DA (DGA-DA) implementing both. Using synthetic and real data, the paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art DA methods on 36 image classification DA tasks across six popular benchmarks. The paper provides in-depth analysis of the proposed DA method, quantifying the contribution of each term and visualizing both real and synthetic data to provide further insights.

title: Debiased Machine Learning of Set-Identified Linear Models
Abstract: This paper presents estimation and inference methods for the boundary (support function) of an identified set when covariate selection is based on modern regularized tools. The boundary is characterized using a semiparametric moment equation. Combining Neyman-orthogonality and sample splitting, the paper constructs a root-N consistent, uniformly asymptotically Gaussian estimator for the boundary and proposes a multiplier bootstrap procedure for inference. This result is applied to the partially linear model, the partially linear IV model, and the average partial derivative with an interval-valued outcome.

title: Parallel Active Subspace Decomposition for Scalable and Efficient Tensor Robust Principal Component Analysis
Abstract: Tensor robust principal component analysis (TRPCA) has gained significant attention in various fields. Existing methods, typically relying on tensor nuclear norm minimization, incur high computational cost due to multiple singular value decompositions (SVDs) at each iteration. This paper proposes a scalable and efficient method, Parallel Active Subspace Decomposition (PASD), which divides the unfolding along each mode of the tensor into a columnwise orthonormal matrix (active subspace) and another small-size matrix in parallel. This transformation leads to a nonconvex optimization problem where the scale of nuclear norm minimization is significantly smaller than the original problem. The paper further introduces an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving the reformulated problem, providing rigorous analyses for its convergence and suboptimality. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data show that the PASD algorithm surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in accuracy and is orders of magnitude faster.

title: Estimation and Inference on Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in High-Dimensional Dynamic Panels under Weak Dependence
Abstract: This paper presents estimation and inference methods for conditional average treatment effects (CATE) characterized by a high-dimensional parameter in both homogeneous cross-sectional and unit-heterogeneous dynamic panel data settings. The paper models CATE by interacting the base treatment variable with explanatory variables. The first step involves orthogonalization, where control and unit effects are partially removed from the outcome and base treatment, and the cross-fitted residuals are obtained. This step utilizes a novel generic cross-fitting method designed for weakly dependent time series and panel data, which "leaves out the neighbors" when fitting nuisance components. The method's theoretical foundation is based on Strassen's coupling, enabling the use of any modern machine learning method in the first step if it learns the residuals effectively. Second, an orthogonal (residual) learner of CATE – the Lasso CATE – is constructed by regressing the outcome residual on the vector of interactions of the residualized treatment with explanatory variables. If the complexity of the CATE function is simpler than the first-stage regression, the orthogonal learner converges faster than the single-stage regression-based learner. Third, simultaneous inference on CATE function parameters is performed using debiasing. Ordinary least squares can be used in the last two steps when CATE is low-dimensional. In heterogeneous panel data settings, the unobserved unit heterogeneity is modeled as a weakly sparse deviation from Mundlak's model of correlated unit effects, and L1-penalization is used for estimation. The paper demonstrates the methods by estimating price elasticities of groceries based on scanner data, with results being novel even for the cross-sectional (i.i.d) case.

title: Random Feature-based Online Multi-kernel Learning in Environments with Unknown Dynamics
Abstract: Kernel-based methods are well-established in various nonlinear learning tasks. Most rely on a preselected kernel, which requires task-specific prior information. When such information is unavailable, multi-kernel learning becomes appealing due to its flexibility in choosing kernels from a dictionary. Leveraging the random feature approximation and its orthogonalization-promoting variant, this paper develops a scalable multi-kernel learning scheme (termed Raker) to obtain the nonlinear learning function on the fly, initially for static environments. To further enhance performance in dynamic environments, an adaptive multi-kernel learning scheme (AdaRaker) is introduced. AdaRaker accounts for both data-driven learning of kernel combination and unknown dynamics. Performance is analyzed in terms of static and dynamic regrets. AdaRaker uniquely tracks nonlinear learning functions in environments with unknown dynamics and provides analytic performance guarantees. Synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the novel algorithms.
