title: Context-aware Path Ranking for Knowledge Base Completion
Abstract: Knowledge base (KB) completion aims to infer missing facts from existing ones in a KB. Path ranking (PR) algorithms have gained increasing attention in recent years. PR algorithms enumerate paths between entity pairs in a KB and use these paths as features to train a model for missing fact prediction. Due to their good performance and high model interpretability, several methods have been proposed. However, most existing methods suffer from scalability (high RAM consumption) and feature explosion (training on an exponentially large number of features) problems. This paper proposes a Context-aware Path Ranking (C-PR) algorithm to address these problems by introducing a selective path exploration strategy. C-PR learns global semantics of entities in the KB using word embedding and leverages the knowledge of entity semantics to enumerate contextually relevant paths using bidirectional random walk. Experimental results on three large KBs demonstrate that the path features (fewer in number) discovered by C-PR not only improve predictive performance but also are more interpretable than existing baselines.
label: AI

title: Sheaf-Theoretic Stratification Learning from Geometric and Topological Perspectives
Abstract: This paper explores a sheaf-theoretic interpretation of stratification learning from geometric and topological perspectives. The main result is the construction of stratification learning algorithms framed within a sheaf on a partially ordered set with the Alexandroff topology. It is proven that the resulting decomposition is the unique minimal stratification for which the strata are homogeneous and the given sheaf is constructible. Specifically, when working with the local homology sheaf, the algorithm provides an alternative to the local homology transfer algorithm proposed in Bendich et al. (2012) and the cohomology stratification algorithm presented in Nanda (2017). Furthermore, examples of stratifications based on the geometric techniques of Breiding et al. (2018) are provided, illustrating how the sheaf-theoretic approach can be utilized to study stratifications from both topological and geometric perspectives. This approach also points towards future applications of sheaf theory in the study of topological data analysis by highlighting the utility of the language of sheaf theory in generalizing existing algorithms.
label: AI

title: Enhance Visual Recognition under Adverse Conditions via Deep Networks
Abstract: Visual recognition under adverse conditions is a critical and challenging problem with significant practical value, due to the ubiquitous existence of quality distortions during image acquisition, transmission, or storage. While deep neural networks have been widely used in low-quality image restoration and high-quality image recognition tasks, respectively, few studies have focused on the important problem of recognition from very low-quality images. This paper proposes a deep learning based framework for enhancing the performance of image and video recognition models under adverse conditions, using robust adverse pre-training or its aggressive variant. The robust adverse pre-training algorithms leverage the power of pre-training and generalize conventional unsupervised pre-training and data augmentation methods. A transfer learning approach is further developed to address real-world datasets with unknown adverse conditions. The proposed framework is comprehensively evaluated on multiple image and video recognition benchmarks, achieving significant performance improvements under various single or mixed adverse conditions. Visualization and analysis further contribute to the explainability of the results.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised learning of dynamical and molecular similarity using variance minimization
Abstract: This report presents an unsupervised machine learning method for grouping molecular systems based on similarity in their dynamics or structures using Ward's minimum variance objective function. The minimum variance clustering is first applied to a set of simulated tripeptides using the information theoretic Jensen-Shannon divergence between Markovian transition matrices to gain insight into how point mutations affect protein dynamics. The method is then extended to partition two chemoinformatic datasets according to structural similarity, motivating a train/validation/test split for supervised learning that avoids overfitting.
label: AI

title: GSM-CommSense-based through-the-wall sensing
Abstract: The authors propose a scheme that utilizes channel equalization blocks in telecommunication systems to detect environmental changes, termed "communication-sensing" or CommSense. Building upon initial positive results, they attempted to employ their GSM-based CommSense system for a through-the-wall sensing application. Due to the inherently highly under-determined nature of the system, statistical machine learning techniques were employed to assist in sensing environmental changes during behind-the-wall experiments. The findings revealed that with a limited amount of data per GSM frame of 577 {\\mu}s, a person can be detected across a wall with an accuracy of 77.458%, and a person carrying a weapon can be detected with an accuracy of 95.208%. This article presents details of the experiments and the encouraging results obtained.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Synthesis Learning Enables Segmentation Without Target Modality Ground Truth
Abstract: A lack of generalizability is a key limitation of deep learning-based segmentation. Typically, manual labeling of new training images is required when segmenting organs in different imaging modalities or segmenting abnormal organs from distinct disease cohorts. The manual effort can be reduced if one can reuse manual labels from one modality (e.g., MRI) to train a segmentation network for a new modality (e.g., CT). Previously, two-stage methods using cycle generative adversarial networks (CycleGAN) have been proposed to synthesize training images for a target modality. These methods then trained a segmentation network independently using synthetic images. However, these two independent stages did not leverage the complementary information between synthesis and segmentation. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end synthesis and segmentation network (EssNet) to achieve unpaired MRI to CT image synthesis and CT splenomegaly segmentation simultaneously without using manual labels on CT. The end-to-end EssNet achieved significantly higher median Dice similarity coefficient (0.9188) compared to the two-stage strategy (0.8801), and even higher than canonical multi-atlas segmentation (0.9125) and ResNet method (0.9107), which utilized the CT manual labels.
label: AI

title: Pseudorehearsal in actor-critic agents with neural network function approximation
Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting has a significant negative impact on reinforcement learning. This study investigates how pseudorehearsal can affect the performance of an actor-critic agent with neural-network function approximation. The agent was tested in a pole balancing task, and different pseudorehearsal approaches were compared. The findings suggest that pseudorehearsal can assist learning and reduce forgetting.
label: AI

title: Sim2Real View Invariant Visual Servoing by Recurrent Control
Abstract: Humans demonstrate remarkable proficiency in controlling their limbs and tools from a wide range of viewpoints and angles, even in the presence of optical distortions. In robotics, this ability is referred to as visual servoing: moving a tool or end-point to a desired location primarily using visual feedback. This paper investigates how viewpoint-invariant visual servoing skills can be learned automatically in a robotic manipulation scenario. To achieve this, a deep recurrent controller is trained that can automatically determine which actions move the end-point of a robotic arm to a desired object. The problem the controller must solve is fundamentally ambiguous: under severe variation in viewpoint, determining the actions in a single feedforward operation may be impossible. Therefore, the visual servoing system must utilize its memory of past movements to understand how actions affect robot motion from the current viewpoint, correcting mistakes and gradually moving closer to the target. This capability contrasts with most visual servoing methods, which either assume known dynamics or require a calibration phase. The paper shows how this recurrent controller can be learned using simulated data and a reinforcement learning objective. It then describes how the resulting model can be transferred to a real-world robot by disentangling perception from control and only adapting the visual layers. The adapted model can servo to previously unseen objects from novel viewpoints on a real-world Kuka IIWA robotic arm. For supplementary videos, see: https://fsadeghi.github.io/Sim2RealViewInvariantServo.
label: AI

title: Image Segmentation to Distinguish Between Overlapping Human Chromosomes
Abstract: Visualizing chromosomes is crucial in medicine for medical diagnostics, drug development, and biomedical research. However, chromosomes often overlap, necessitating the identification and differentiation between overlapping chromosomes. A fast and automated segmentation solution would enable scaling of cost-effective medicine and biomedical research. This paper applies neural network-based image segmentation to the problem of distinguishing between partially overlapping DNA chromosomes. A convolutional neural network is customized for this problem. The results achieved intersection over union (IOU) scores of 94.7% for the overlapping region and 88-94% for the non-overlapping chromosome regions.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning with Lung Segmentation and Bone Shadow Exclusion Techniques for Chest X-Ray Analysis of Lung Cancer
Abstract: Recent advancements in computing, machine learning, and especially deep learning for image recognition have yielded meaningful effects for automated detection of various diseases from chest X-ray images (CXRs). This paper demonstrates the efficiency of lung segmentation and bone shadow exclusion techniques for analyzing 2D CXRs using a deep learning approach to assist radiologists in identifying suspicious lesions and nodules in lung cancer patients. Training and validation were performed on the original JSRT dataset (dataset #01), BSE-JSRT dataset (the same JSRT dataset but without clavicle and rib shadows, dataset #02), original JSRT dataset after segmentation (dataset #03), and BSE-JSRT dataset after segmentation (dataset #04). The results highlight the high efficiency and usefulness of the pre-processing techniques even in a simplified configuration. The pre-processed dataset without bones (dataset #02) demonstrates significantly better accuracy and loss results compared to the other pre-processed datasets after lung segmentation (datasets #02 and #03).
label: AI

title: SuperPoint: Self-Supervised Interest Point Detection and Description
Abstract: This paper introduces a self-supervised framework for training interest point detectors and descriptors suitable for a large number of multiple-view geometry problems in computer vision. Unlike patch-based neural networks, the fully-convolutional model operates on full-sized images and jointly computes pixel-level interest point locations and associated descriptors in one forward pass. The paper introduces Homographic Adaptation, a multi-scale, multi-homography approach for boosting interest point detection repeatability and performing cross-domain adaptation (e.g., synthetic-to-real). When trained on the MS-COCO generic image dataset using Homographic Adaptation, the model can repeatedly detect a richer set of interest points than the initial pre-adapted deep model and any other traditional corner detector. The final system achieves state-of-the-art homography estimation results on HPatches compared to LIFT, SIFT, and ORB.
label: AI

title: Improving Generalization Performance by Switching from Adam to SGD
Abstract: Despite superior training outcomes, adaptive optimization methods such as Adam, Adagrad, or RMSprop have been found to generalize poorly compared to Stochastic gradient descent (SGD). These methods tend to perform well during the initial portion of training but are outperformed by SGD at later stages of training. This paper investigates a hybrid strategy that begins training with an adaptive method and switches to SGD when appropriate. Specifically, the authors propose SWATS, a simple strategy that switches from Adam to SGD when a triggering condition is met. The proposed condition relates to the projection of Adam steps on the gradient subspace. By design, the monitoring process for this condition adds minimal overhead and does not increase the number of hyperparameters in the optimizer. Experiments on several standard benchmarks such as ResNet, SENet, DenseNet, and PyramidNet for the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, ResNet on the tiny-ImageNet dataset, and language modeling with recurrent networks on the PTB and WT2 datasets demonstrate that the strategy can close the generalization gap between SGD and Adam on a majority of the tasks.
label: AI

title: MATE robots simplifying my work: benefits and socio-ethical implications
Abstract: With the increasing complexity of modern industrial automatic and robotic systems, operators face a growing burden as they are required to supervise and interact with highly complex systems, typically under challenging and stressful conditions. To address this issue, it is necessary to adopt a responsible approach based on the anthropocentric design methodology, where machines adapt to human capabilities, rather than vice versa. This paper proposes an integrated methodological design approach called MATE, which involves devising complex automatic or robotic solutions that measure the current operator's status, adapt the interaction accordingly, and provide appropriate training to improve the interaction and enhance the operator's skills and expertise. A MATE system aims to be easily usable for all users, adhering to the principles of inclusive design. Using such a MATE system raises several ethical and social implications, which are discussed in this paper. Additionally, the paper presents a discussion about which factors in the organization of companies are critical concerning the introduction of a MATE system.
label: AI

title: Riemann-Theta Boltzmann Machine
Abstract: A general Boltzmann machine with continuous visible and discrete integer-valued hidden states is introduced. Under mild assumptions about the connection matrices, the probability density function of the visible units can be solved analytically, resulting in a novel parametric density function involving a ratio of Riemann-Theta functions. The conditional expectation of a hidden state for given visible states can also be calculated analytically, yielding a derivative of the logarithmic Riemann-Theta function. The conditional expectation can be utilized as an activation function in a feedforward neural network, thereby enhancing the network's modeling capacity. Both the Boltzmann machine and the derived feedforward neural network can be successfully trained using standard gradient- and non-gradient-based optimization techniques.
label: AI

title: Learning to Act Properly: Predicting and Explaining Affordances from Images
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of affordance reasoning in diverse real-world scenes. Affordances relate the agent's actions to their effects when performed on surrounding objects. In this work, the egocentric view of the scene is taken, aiming to reason about action-object affordances that respect both the physical world and social norms. The goal is to teach artificial agents why certain actions should not be taken in specific situations and what would likely happen if those actions were taken. A new dataset, ADE-Affordance, is collected based on ADE20k, containing annotations that enable such rich visual reasoning. The paper proposes a model that utilizes Graph Neural Networks to propagate contextual information from the scene for detailed affordance reasoning about each object. The model is showcased through various ablation studies, highlighting successes and challenges in this complex task.
label: AI

title: Experimental Phase Estimation Enhanced By Machine Learning
Abstract: Phase estimation protocols provide a fundamental benchmark for the field of quantum metrology. Quantum metrology represents one of the most relevant applications of quantum theory, potentially enabling the measurement of unknown physical parameters with improved precision compared to classical strategies. In this context, most theoretical and experimental studies have focused on determining fundamental bounds and achieving them in the asymptotic regime where a large number of resources is employed. However, in most applications, achieving optimal precisions with a limited number of measurements is necessary. Machine learning techniques can be applied as a powerful optimization tool for this purpose. This paper experimentally implements single-photon adaptive phase estimation protocols enhanced by machine learning, demonstrating the capability of reaching optimal precision after a small number of trials. A new approach for Bayesian estimation is introduced, exhibiting the best performances for very low photon numbers (N). Furthermore, the paper studies the resilience to noise of the tested methods, revealing that the optimized Bayesian approach is highly robust in the presence of imperfections. This methodology can be extended to the more general multiparameter case, which represents a paradigmatic scenario for various tasks including imaging or Hamiltonian learning.
label: AI

title: An Ensemble Model with Ranking for Social Dialogue
Abstract: Open-domain social dialogue is a long-standing goal of Artificial Intelligence. This year, the Amazon Alexa Prize challenge was announced for the first time, where real customers rate systems developed by leading universities worldwide. The challenge aims to enable systems to converse "coherently and engagingly with humans on popular topics for 20 minutes". This paper describes the Alexa Prize system developed by the authors (called "Alana"), which consists of an ensemble of bots combining rule-based and machine learning systems and utilizing a contextual ranking mechanism to choose a system response. The ranker was trained on real user feedback received during the competition, addressing the problem of training on noisy and sparse feedback obtained during the competition.
label: AI

title: Differentially Private Federated Learning: A Client Level Perspective
Abstract: Federated learning is a recent advance in privacy protection. In this context, a trusted curator aggregates parameters optimized in a decentralized fashion by multiple clients. The resulting model is then distributed back to all clients, ultimately converging to a joint representative model without explicitly sharing data. However, the protocol is vulnerable to differential attacks, which could originate from any party contributing during federated optimization. In such an attack, a client's contribution during training and information about their dataset is revealed through analyzing the distributed model. This paper tackles this problem and proposes an algorithm for client-sided differential privacy preserving federated optimization. The aim is to hide clients' contributions during training, balancing the trade-off between privacy loss and model performance. Empirical studies suggest that with a sufficiently large number of participating clients, the proposed procedure can maintain client-level differential privacy with only a minor cost in model performance.
label: AI

title: Use of Deep Learning in Modern Recommendation System: A Summary of Recent Works
Abstract: The exponential increase in digital information on the internet, online shops, online music, video, and image libraries, search engines, and recommendation systems have become the most convenient ways to find relevant information quickly. Recent advancements in deep learning have gained significant attention in speech recognition, image processing, and natural language processing. Meanwhile, several recent studies have demonstrated the utility of deep learning in recommendation systems and information retrieval. This review covers recent advancements in recommendation using various deep learning technologies, organized into three parts: Collaborative system, Content-based system, and Hybrid system. The review also discusses the contribution of deep learning integrated recommendation systems in several application domains. The review concludes by discussing the impact of deep learning in recommendation systems in various domains and whether deep learning has shown significant improvement over conventional systems for recommendation. Finally, future directions for research based on the current state of deep learning in recommendation systems are provided.
label: AI

title: Statistical Inference for the Population Landscape via Moment Adjusted Stochastic Gradients
Abstract: Modern statistical inference tasks often require iterative optimization methods to compute the solution. Convergence analysis from an optimization perspective only informs us about how well the solution is approximated numerically but overlooks the sampling nature of the data. In contrast, recognizing the randomness in the data, statisticians are keen to provide uncertainty quantification or confidence for the solution obtained using iterative optimization methods. This paper introduces moment-adjusted stochastic gradient descents, a new stochastic optimization method for statistical inference, making progress in this direction. Non-asymptotic theory is established that characterizes the statistical distribution for certain iterative methods with optimization guarantees. On the statistical front, the theory allows for model mis-specification, with very mild conditions on the data. For optimization, the theory is flexible for both convex and non-convex cases. Notably, the moment-adjusting idea, motivated by "error standardization" in statistics, achieves a similar effect as acceleration in first-order optimization methods used to fit generalized linear models. The paper also demonstrates this acceleration effect in the non-convex setting through numerical experiments. |||
label: AI

title: Ethical Questions in NLP Research: The (Mis)-Use of Forensic Linguistics
Abstract: Forensic linguistics is increasingly used in Natural Language Processing (NLP) with machine learning techniques. However, these applications raise ethical concerns as they often overlook scientific limitations. This trend goes beyond forensic linguistics and affects numerous scientific and data-driven fields, potentially exceeding their legal and scientific bounds. This paper argues that careless implementation can undermine legal due process and violate ethical codes.
label: AI

title: A Distributed Frank-Wolfe Framework for Learning Low-Rank Matrices with the Trace Norm
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of learning high-dimensional, low-rank matrices from large-scale datasets distributed across multiple machines. It introduces DFW-Trace, a distributed Frank-Wolfe algorithm that leverages the low-rank structure of updates for efficient time, memory, and communication usage. DFW-Trace employs a distributed power method to solve the core step. The paper provides theoretical analysis demonstrating sublinear convergence to an optimal solution with minimal power iterations per epoch. Implemented within the Apache Spark framework, DFW-Trace is validated through experiments on synthetic and real data, including ImageNet with high-dimensional features from a deep neural network.
label: AI

title: Learning a Wavelet-like Auto-Encoder to Accelerate Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Accelerating deep neural networks (DNNs) is crucial for enabling mobile devices with limited resources to perform complex tasks like visual recognition. This paper proposes a novel Wavelet-like Auto-Encoder (WAE) for neural network acceleration. The WAE decomposes input images into two low-resolution channels representing low-frequency information (image profiles) and high-frequency information (image details). These channels are then fed into separate classification networks, allowing for efficient and interpretable classification. This framework is compatible with existing convolutional neural networks without structural modifications, providing a general and comprehensive approach for accelerating neural networks.
label: AI

title: Partial Labeled Gastric Tumor Segmentation via patch-based Reiterative Learning
Abstract: Gastric cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, presents challenges in biomedical image analysis due to the difficulty of determining cancer extent. Deep learning has shown promise in biomedical image segmentation but relies heavily on comprehensive annotation, which requires significant resources and expertise. This paper introduces a reiterative learning framework that enables training on partially annotated images, eliminating the need for pre-trained models or further manual annotation. The proposed framework tackles boundary errors using an overlapped region forecast algorithm, achieving high performance on the partial labeled dataset. This approach significantly reduces annotation costs while achieving state-of-the-art results in gastric cancer segmentation.
label: AI

title: Attribute CNNs for Word Spotting in Handwritten Documents
Abstract: Word spotting, a crucial task in document image analysis, has recently seen advancements with the use of AttributeSVMs, which predict a binary attribute representation. This paper proposes a novel approach for learning attribute representations using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Two probabilistic loss functions are derived for binary and real-valued word string embeddings, and two CNN architectures are specifically designed for word spotting, allowing for end-to-end training. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of different word string embeddings and optimization strategies, achieving state-of-the-art results in segmentation-based word spotting across various datasets.
label: AI

title: Differentially Private Distributed Learning for Language Modeling Tasks
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of adapting language models trained on public data to the specific language patterns of users' private data. It introduces a novel distributed fine-tuning technique that significantly improves prediction quality on user data while maintaining performance on general data and minimizing communication costs. The approach outperforms gradient compression methods in terms of communication efficiency, achieving substantial perplexity reduction and keystroke saving rate improvement on informal English texts. This technique is not limited to language modeling and offers good privacy guarantees.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Attentional Reinforcement Learning for Multi-label Image Recognition
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of recognizing multiple labels in images, a fundamental but challenging task in computer vision. It presents a recurrent attention reinforcement learning framework that iteratively identifies attentional and informative regions related to different semantic objects. This approach models long-term dependencies among these regions, capturing semantic label co-occurrence and enhancing multi-label recognition performance. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO benchmarks demonstrate superior performance and efficiency compared to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Fast kNN mode seeking clustering applied to active learning
Abstract: This paper presents a significantly faster algorithm for kNN mode seeking, addressing the limitations of the mean shift algorithm in high-dimensional vector spaces. The algorithm provides uniquely defined modes and generates a multi-scale hierarchy of clusterings without additional computational effort. With time complexity of O(n^1.5), the algorithm is efficient for analyzing large sets of small clusters, making it suitable for handling millions of objects. The algorithm can also be used for active learning, assigning clusters to classes based on modal objects. Experiments with handwritten digits demonstrate the algorithm's feasibility and highlight its advantages over other classification methods.
label: AI

title: Self-Supervised Damage-Avoiding Manipulation Strategy Optimization via Mental Simulation
Abstract: Everyday robotics faces challenges in handling objects autonomously without causing damage. This paper proposes a self-supervised learning approach for damage-minimizing manipulation strategies. The approach involves simulation-based planning of optimal manipulation sequences with respect to potential damage, followed by generalization to new, unseen scenarios using machine learning. This strategy is continuously refined through a self-supervised simulation-in-the-loop optimization cycle. The paper validates the approach on industrial container-unloading and retail shelf-replenishment scenarios.
label: AI

title: In silico generation of novel, drug-like chemical matter using the LSTM neural network
Abstract: This paper explores the use of deep neural networks for generating novel drug-like molecules, providing an alternative to brute-force de novo methods and other machine learning approaches. The proposed method utilizes a long short-term memory (LSTM) network and generates millions of novel, diverse, drug-like molecules with good physicochemical properties and synthetic accessibility. Virtual screening confirms the potential of these molecules to exhibit bioactivity comparable to the ChEMBL set from which they were derived. The molecule generator is written in Python and available on request.
label: AI

title: On the Relation of External and Internal Feature Interactions: A Case Study
Abstract: Detecting feature interactions is crucial for accurate performance prediction in highly configurable systems. Existing methods rely on supervised machine learning, which requires time-consuming performance measurements for training data. This paper proposes a method for reducing the number of required measurements by leveraging static code analysis to identify potentially interacting features. A qualitative case study demonstrates a relation between control-flow feature interactions (detected through static analysis) and performance feature interactions, suggesting potential for exploiting this relation to enhance performance prediction efficiency.
label: AI

title: Incremental Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Continually Changing Environments
Abstract: Continuous appearance shifts, such as changing weather and lighting conditions, can negatively impact the performance of deployed machine learning models. This paper proposes a lifelong, incremental domain adaptation approach that utilizes the continuity of these shifts to improve model robustness. The adversarial approach aligns the model with a series of intermediate domains, progressively diverging from the labelled source domain. Experiments on a traversable-path segmentation task demonstrate improved handling of large appearance changes compared to a direct, single alignment step approach. The method also enables full deployment independence from source training data with minimal performance reduction.
label: AI

title: ADINE: An Adaptive Momentum Method for Stochastic Gradient Descent
Abstract: Polyak's heavy ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient are two popular momentum-based optimization techniques. However, choosing the momentum parameter ($m$) is crucial and typically restricted to values less than 1. This paper introduces a new momentum-based method, ADINE, that relaxes this constraint and allows for adaptive higher momentum. The hypothesis is motivated by experimental observations that higher momentum can efficiently escape saddle points. ADINE prioritizes previous updates by setting $m>1$, leading to faster convergence without compromising generalization error on deep neural networks.
label: AI

title: Finding Competitive Network Architectures Within a Day Using UCT
Abstract: Designing neural network architectures for new datasets is a time-consuming task requiring human expertise. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing the use of Monte Carlo planning with UCT (Upper Confidence Bound applied to Trees) for automated network architecture search. The paper proposes two UCT variations that enable efficient information sharing across different branches of the search tree. Empirical studies demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in finding competitive networks for MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 within a single GPU day. Furthermore, extending the search to five GPU days outperforms human-designed architectures and other methods using similar layer types.
label: AI

title: DeepFuse: A Deep Unsupervised Approach for Exposure Fusion with Extreme Exposure Image Pairs
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning architecture for fusing static multi-exposure images. Existing approaches rely on hand-crafted features, which struggle with varying input conditions and perform poorly for extreme exposure image pairs. The proposed method leverages deep representations known for their robustness and performance in supervised settings. To address the lack of sufficient training data and ground truth for supervision, the paper proposes an unsupervised deep learning framework using a no-reference quality metric as a loss function. The framework uses a novel CNN architecture trained to learn the fusion operation without ground truth images. Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach over existing methods for a variety of natural images.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Structured Prediction for Multivariate Measures
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing structured objects, like sequences, matchings, and trees, which are evaluated using multivariate performance measures like the F-score and alignment error rate (AER). Traditionally, surrogate losses are used for empirical risk minimization, but these approximations can lead to inconsistencies between the learner's objective and desired performance. This paper proposes an adversarial approach where training data is adversarially approximated while optimizing the exact F-score or AER. Structured predictions are derived from solving zero-sum games between a predictor and an adversary, ensuring the adversary matches certain structured properties of the training data. The approach is demonstrated on word alignment and named entity recognition tasks with linear-chain constraints.
label: AI

title: Improvement of Resting-state EEG Analysis Process with Spectrum Weight-Voting based on LES
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive technique for recording brain bioelectric activity, promising applications in fields like human-computer interaction and neuroscience. Analyzing EEG data is challenging due to its complex composition, low amplitude, and signal-to-noise ratio. This paper focuses on using machine learning for classifying schizophrenia phases based on EEG data. It proposes a weight-voting method that leverages sub-band features to obtain weights representing the influence of each frequency band on classification. These weights are then applied to improve classification accuracy. The study reveals the significant role of the low gamma band in distinguishing schizophrenia phases, contributing to psychopathology research.
label: AI

title: Intelligent Power Control for Spectrum Sharing in Cognitive Radios: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of spectrum sharing in a cognitive radio system with a primary user and a secondary user operating non-cooperatively. The primary user employs a predefined power control policy, while the secondary user lacks knowledge about the primary user's transmit power or strategy. To facilitate spectrum sharing, a set of sensor nodes collect received signal strength information. The paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning-based method for the secondary user to intelligently adjust its transmit power, enabling successful data transmission for both users after a few rounds of interaction. Experimental results demonstrate efficient interaction between the users, leading to a goal state where both users can successfully transmit their data.
label: AI

title: Transformation Models in High-Dimensions
Abstract: Transformation models are essential tools in applied statistics and econometrics for achieving homogeneity or normal distribution of errors. This paper investigates transformation models in a high-dimensional setting with a large set of potential covariates. The paper proposes an estimator for the transformation parameter, proving its asymptotic normality using orthogonalized moment conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate the estimator's effectiveness in small samples. The study investigates the validity of the log-transformation for wages using data from the US Current Population Survey.
label: AI

title: Model-Based Clustering of Time-Evolving Networks through Temporal Exponential-Family Random Graph Models
Abstract: Dynamic networks, a general language for describing time-evolving complex systems, are studied using discrete time network models. Detecting community structure in these networks is a fundamental but challenging research question. This paper proposes a novel model-based clustering framework for time-evolving networks using discrete time exponential-family random graph models. A conditional likelihood-based model selection criterion is employed to determine the number of communities. An efficient variational expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm is used to find approximate maximum likelihood estimates of network parameters and mixing proportions. The method demonstrates scalability for large-scale networks and is validated through simulation studies and empirical applications to international trade networks and research collaboration networks. |||
label: AI

title: A Flexible Approach to Automated RNN Architecture Generation
Abstract: Designing neural architectures requires expertise and extensive trial and error. Existing automated architecture search methods produce limited RNN architectures with restricted flexibility and components. This paper introduces a domain-specific language (DSL) for automated architecture search capable of generating novel RNNs with arbitrary depth and width. The DSL allows for the definition of standard architectures like the Gated Recurrent Unit and Long Short Term Memory, as well as the inclusion of non-standard components such as trigonometric curves and layer normalization. The authors explore the novel architectures generated by the RNN DSL for language modeling and machine translation domains using two candidate generation techniques: random search with a ranking function and reinforcement learning. The resulting architectures, while not following human intuition, demonstrate good performance on their targeted tasks, suggesting the space of usable RNN architectures is much larger than previously believed.
label: AI

title: Rhythmic Representations: Learning Periodic Patterns for Scalable Place Recognition at a Sub-Linear Storage Cost
Abstract: Robotic and animal mapping systems share common challenges and characteristics: they must function in diverse environments, enable navigation for finding resources, and be computationally efficient in terms of speed and storage. Unlike robotic mapping systems, the mammalian brain uses a radically different approach for map storage. While robotic systems aim to minimize representational aliasing by solving the data association problem, neurons in the brain intentionally break data association by encoding numerous locations with a single neuron. This paper proposes a novel method based on supervised learning that identifies regularly repeating visual patterns in the environment with co-prime frequencies and an encoding scheme for sub-linear storage growth. To improve robustness in challenging real-world settings while maintaining sub-linear storage growth, multi-exemplar learning and data augmentation techniques are incorporated. Using large benchmark robotic mapping datasets, the authors demonstrate the system's high-performance place recognition with sub-linear storage requirements and characterize the performance-storage growth trade-off. This research marks the first robotic mapping system with sub-linear storage scaling properties and the first large-scale demonstration of one of the proposed memory benefits of these neurons in real-world environments.
label: AI

title: Detection and classification of masses in mammographic images in a multi-kernel approach
Abstract: According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death among adult women globally. While breast cancer occurs in countries with varying levels of social and economic development, mortality rates remain high in developing and underdeveloped countries due to limited access to early detection technologies. Mammography remains the most effective diagnostic technology due to its widespread use and interpretation. This study proposes a method for detecting and classifying mammographic lesions using regions of interest in images. The approach involves decomposing images using multi-resolution wavelets and extracting Zernike moments from each wavelet component, combining texture and shape features for lesion detection and classification. The method was evaluated using 355 images from the IRMA database, achieving a 94.11% accuracy rate using SVM and ELM networks with modified kernels. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, the proposed model combines high accuracy with significantly reduced learning time, saving considerable time in the learning process when new data is received.

title: Revisiting the Master-Slave Architecture in Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Many artificial intelligence tasks require the collaboration of multiple agents. This paper explores deep reinforcement learning for multi-agent domains, revisiting the master-slave architecture to incorporate both decentralized and centralized perspectives within a single framework. This hierarchical structure naturally leverages the advantages of both perspectives, drawing inspiration from real-world systems. The authors highlight three key ingredients for this approach: composed action representation, learnable communication, and independent reasoning. With network designs explicitly facilitating these elements, the proposed method consistently outperforms competing methods in both synthetic experiments and challenging StarCraft micromanagement tasks.
label: AI

title: Block-diagonal Hessian-free Optimization for Training Neural Networks
Abstract: Second-order methods for neural network optimization offer advantages over first-order gradient descent methods, including better scaling to large mini-batch sizes and fewer updates required for convergence. However, their practical application in deep learning is limited by high computational cost and the need for model-dependent algorithmic variations. This paper introduces a variant of the Hessian-free method that utilizes a block-diagonal approximation of the generalized Gauss-Newton matrix. The method computes the curvature approximation matrix only for parameter pairs within the same layer or block of the neural network and performs conjugate gradient updates independently for each block. Experiments on deep autoencoders, deep convolutional networks, and multilayer LSTMs demonstrate superior convergence and generalization compared to the original Hessian-free approach and the Adam method.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical and Interpretable Skill Acquisition in Multi-task Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Learning policies for complex tasks requiring multiple skills presents a significant challenge in reinforcement learning (RL). This paper proposes a novel framework for efficient multi-task reinforcement learning by training agents to employ hierarchical policies that dynamically decide between using previously learned policies or acquiring new skills. This enables continuous skill acquisition during training, where each learned task is associated with a human language description. Agents access previously learned skills through these descriptions, enabling human-interpretable explanations for their choices. To assist the agent in learning the complex temporal dependencies required for the hierarchical policy, a stochastic temporal grammar is provided that modulates the reliance on previously learned skills versus execution of new skills. The approach is validated on Minecraft games designed to test the ability to reuse previously learned skills while simultaneously learning new skills.
label: AI

title: Learning Sight from Sound: Ambient Sound Provides Supervision for Visual Learning
Abstract: Sound conveys crucial information about the objects in our surroundings, such as the crashing of waves or the roar of cars. This work demonstrates that ambient sounds can serve as a supervisory signal for learning visual models. The authors train a convolutional neural network to predict a statistical summary of the sound associated with a video frame. Through this process, the network learns a representation conveying information about objects and scenes. The representation is evaluated on several recognition tasks, demonstrating performance comparable to state-of-the-art unsupervised learning methods. Visualizations reveal that the network learns units selective to objects commonly associated with characteristic sounds. This paper extends an earlier conference paper with additional experiments and discussion.
label: AI

title: FoldingNet: Point Cloud Auto-encoder via Deep Grid Deformation
Abstract: Deep networks that directly process points in a point set, like PointNet, have achieved state-of-the-art results for supervised learning tasks on point clouds, such as classification and segmentation. This work proposes a novel end-to-end deep auto-encoder to address unsupervised learning challenges on point clouds. The encoder incorporates a graph-based enhancement to promote local structures on top of PointNet, while a novel folding-based decoder deforms a canonical 2D grid onto the underlying 3D object surface of a point cloud, achieving low reconstruction errors even for objects with intricate structures. The proposed decoder uses only 7% of the parameters of a fully-connected neural network decoder, yet produces a more discriminative representation that achieves higher linear SVM classification accuracy than the benchmark. The decoder architecture is theoretically capable of reconstructing any arbitrary point cloud from a 2D grid.
label: AI

title: Multi-shot Pedestrian Re-identification via Sequential Decision Making
Abstract: The multi-shot pedestrian re-identification problem, a core challenge in surveillance video analysis, aims to match pedestrian tracks from different cameras. Unlike existing methods that aggregate single-frame features using time series models like recurrent neural networks, this paper proposes an interpretable reinforcement learning-based approach. The method trains an agent to verify pairs of images at each time step, allowing the agent to output a result (same or different) or request additional verification (unsure). This approach implicitly learns the difficulty of image pairs and postpones decisions when insufficient evidence is available. By adjusting the reward for unsure actions, a trade-off between speed and accuracy can be easily managed. In three open benchmarks, the method achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods while using only 3% to 6% of the images. These results highlight the method's advantages in efficiency and performance.
label: AI

title: Probabilistic Learning of Torque Controllers from Kinematic and Force Constraints
Abstract: When learning skills from demonstrations, choosing an appropriate task representation is crucial. This paper proposes a probabilistic approach for simultaneously learning and synthesizing torque control commands that consider task space, joint space, and force constraints. The approach treats the problem by considering multiple torque controllers acting on the robot, with their relevance learned probabilistically from demonstrations. This information is then used to combine the controllers, exploiting the properties of Gaussian distributions, to generate new torque commands that fulfill the task's essential features. The approach is validated in two experimental scenarios using 7-DoF torque-controlled manipulators, with tasks requiring different controllers for proper execution.
label: AI

title: Real-value and confidence prediction of protein backbone dihedral angles through a hybrid method of clustering and deep learning
Abstract: Protein dihedral angles provide detailed information about protein local conformation. Predicted dihedral angles can significantly narrow down the conformational space of the polypeptide chain, aiding protein tertiary structure prediction. However, directly predicting angles from sequence alone is challenging. This study introduces a novel method for predicting real-valued angles by combining clustering and deep learning. The method first generates clusters of angles, each assigned a label, and then applies a deep residual neural network to predict the label posterior probability. Real-valued predictions are then generated by a mixture of the clusters based on their predicted probabilities. The method also estimates the bounds of prediction errors at each residue based on the predicted label probabilities. The proposed method, named RaptorX-Angle, outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods like SPIDER2 in terms of Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The results also demonstrate an approximately linear relationship between the real prediction errors and the estimated bounds, indicating accurate error approximation by the estimated bounds. This research provides a more accurate method for predicting dihedral angles, potentially facilitating protein structure prediction and functional studies.
label: AI

title: DeepPicar: A Low-cost Deep Neural Network-based Autonomous Car
Abstract: This paper introduces DeepPicar, a low-cost autonomous car platform utilizing a deep neural network. DeepPicar is a smaller-scale replica of NVIDIA's DAVE-2 self-driving car, employing a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to produce steering angles from camera images. DeepPicar utilizes the same network architecture (9 layers, 27 million connections, and 250K parameters) and can drive autonomously in real-time using a web camera and a Raspberry Pi 3. Using DeepPicar, the authors analyze the Raspberry Pi 3's capabilities for supporting end-to-end deep learning-based real-time control of autonomous vehicles. A systematic comparison of other contemporary embedded computing platforms using DeepPicar's CNN-based control workload reveals that all tested platforms, including the Pi 3, can support CNN-based real-time control at rates ranging from 20 Hz to 100 Hz. However, shared resource contention remains a significant issue on shared memory-based embedded platforms, potentially causing an 11.6X increase in execution time. The authors evaluate state-of-the-art cache partitioning and memory bandwidth throttling techniques on the Pi 3, concluding that memory bandwidth throttling is an effective solution for addressing this issue.

title: Linear Time Clustering for High Dimensional Mixtures of Gaussian Clouds
Abstract: Clustering mixtures of Gaussian distributions is a fundamental yet challenging problem encountered in various high-dimensional data processing tasks. While recent research on learning Gaussian mixture models has focused on improving separation bounds and generalization, less attention has been paid to computational efficiency. This paper introduces a novel and highly efficient clustering algorithm for n points drawn from a mixture of two arbitrary Gaussian distributions in R^p. The algorithm involves random 1-dimensional projections until a direction is found that achieves a user-specified clustering error e. For a 1-dimensional separation parameter γ satisfying γ = Q^-1(e), the expected number of projections is bounded by o(ln p) when γ ≤ c√(ln{ln{p}}), with c being the separability parameter of the two Gaussians in R^p. Consequently, the expected overall running time of the algorithm is linear in n and quasi-linear in p at o(ln{p})O(np), with sample complexity independent of p. This result contrasts with prior works that provide polynomial, at best quadratic, running time in p and n. The bound on the expected number of 1-dimensional projections is extended to the case of multiple Gaussian components, and the results are generalized to mixture distributions beyond the Gaussian model.

title: Metadynamics for Training Neural Network Model Chemistries: a Competitive Assessment
Abstract: Neural network (NN) model chemistries (MCs) promise to facilitate the accurate exploration of chemical space and simulation of large reactive systems. Enhancing these models by adding layers of physical detail, especially long-range forces, is crucial. However, at short range, these models are data-driven and data-limited. There is limited understanding of how data should be sampled, and randomly chosen "test data" can provide poor information about generality. This manuscript compares two common sampling methods, molecular dynamics (MD) and normal-mode sampling (NMS), and one uncommon alternative, Metadynamics (MetaMD), for preparing training geometries. The authors demonstrate that MD is an inefficient sampling method, with additional samples not improving generality. MetaMD is shown to be easily implemented in any NNMC software package with a cost that scales linearly with the number of atoms in a sample molecule. MetaMD ensures samples reach new regions of chemical space while remaining relevant to chemistry near k_bT. It is a cost-effective tool for addressing generalization issues.

title: Hyperparameters Optimization in Deep Convolutional Neural Network / Bayesian Approach with Gaussian Process Prior
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) are widely used in complex machine learning tasks. However, hyperparameter optimization is a crucial step in developing ConvNet architectures, as accuracy and performance are heavily reliant on these parameters. The architecture is parameterized by a set of hyperparameters, including the number of convolutional and fully connected layers, neurons, dropout probability, and learning rate. Searching for optimal hyperparameter values within the vast hyperparameter space is challenging. While grid search and random search have been proposed, they are inefficient and expensive due to the large number of hyperparameters. This paper explores Sequential model-based Bayesian Optimization as a promising alternative technique to address the challenge of the unknown cost function. A recent study by Snoek on Bayesian Optimization achieved the lowest error report in the CIFAR-10 benchmark using nine convolutional network parameters. This article provides an overview of the mathematical concept behind Bayesian Optimization over a Gaussian prior.
label: AI

title: Fusing Multifaceted Transaction Data for User Modeling and Demographic Prediction
Abstract: Inferring user characteristics, such as demographic attributes, is crucial for many user-centric applications. Demographic data enables personalization, identity security, and other applications. However, this data is sensitive and often difficult to obtain. Previous research has shown that purchase history can be used for multi-task prediction of demographic fields like gender and marital status. This paper presents an embedding-based method to integrate multifaceted sequences of transaction data, along with auxiliary relational tables, for improved user modeling and demographic prediction.
label: AI

title: Discovery of Shifting Patterns in Sequence Classification
Abstract: This paper examines the multi-variate sequence classification problem from a multi-instance learning perspective. Real-world sequential data often exhibits discriminative patterns only at specific time periods. For example, cropland can be identified during its growing season but appears similar to barren land after harvest or before planting. Additionally, even within the same class, discriminative patterns can appear in different periods of sequential data. These shifting patterns can significantly degrade the performance of traditional classification methods without sufficient training data. The authors propose a novel sequence classification method that automatically mines shifting patterns from multi-variate sequences. The method employs a multi-instance learning approach to detect shifting patterns while also modeling temporal relationships within each multi-instance bag using an LSTM model, further improving classification performance. The method is evaluated on two real-world applications: cropland mapping and affective state recognition. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in sequence classification performance and in detecting discriminative shifting patterns.
label: AI

title: Calibrating Noise to Variance in Adaptive Data Analysis
Abstract: Datasets are frequently reused, with subsequent analyses depending on the outcomes of previous analyses. Standard techniques for ensuring generalization and statistical validity do not account for this adaptive dependence. A recent line of work investigates the challenges arising from adaptive data reuse by considering the problem of answering a sequence of "queries" about the data distribution, where each query may depend arbitrarily on answers to previous queries. Strongest results for this problem rely on differential privacy, a strong notion of algorithmic stability that composes well when data is reused. However, differential privacy is a strict notion requiring stability under replacement of an arbitrary data element. The simplest algorithm involves adding Gaussian (or Laplace) noise to distort the empirical answers. Analyzing this technique using differential privacy yields suboptimal accuracy guarantees for queries with low variance. This paper proposes a relaxed notion of stability that also composes adaptively. The authors demonstrate that a simple and natural algorithm based on adding noise scaled to the query's standard deviation provides this notion of stability. This implies an algorithm that can answer statistical queries about the dataset with significantly improved accuracy guarantees for low-variance queries. The only previous approach providing such accuracy guarantees relies on a more involved differentially private median-of-means algorithm, exploiting stronger "group" stability.
label: AI

title: Deep Regression Forests for Age Estimation
Abstract: Age estimation from facial images is typically framed as a nonlinear regression problem. The main challenge lies in the heterogeneous facial feature space with respect to age, due to variations in facial appearance across individuals of the same age and the non-stationary nature of aging patterns. This paper proposes Deep Regression Forests (DRFs), an end-to-end model for age estimation. DRFs connect the split nodes to a fully connected layer of a convolutional neural network (CNN), addressing heterogeneous data by jointly learning input-dependent data partitions at the split nodes and data abstractions at the leaf nodes. This joint learning follows an alternating strategy: first, by fixing the leaf nodes, the split nodes and CNN parameters are optimized using backpropagation; then, by fixing the split nodes, the leaf nodes are optimized by iterating a step-size-free and fast-converging update rule derived from variational bounding. The proposed DRFs are verified on three standard age estimation benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art results on all of them.
label: AI

title: Y-net: 3D intracranial artery segmentation using a convolutional autoencoder
Abstract: Automated segmentation of intracranial arteries on magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) enables quantification of cerebrovascular features, providing tools for understanding aging and pathophysiological adaptations of the cerebrovascular system. Using a convolutional autoencoder (CAE) for segmentation is promising as it leverages the autoencoder structure for effective noise reduction and feature extraction by representing high-dimensional information with low-dimensional latent variables. This report describes an optimized CAE model (Y-net) trained on 49 cases of MRA data to learn a 3D segmentation model of intracranial arteries. The trained model demonstrates superior performance compared to three traditional segmentation methods in both binary classification and visual evaluation. |||

title: On Wasserstein Reinforcement Learning and the Fokker-Planck equation
Abstract: Policy gradient methods often perform better when policy changes are limited to small Kullback-Leibler divergences. We derive policy gradients where policy changes are limited to small Wasserstein distances (or trust regions). This is achieved in both discrete and continuous multi-armed bandit settings with entropy regularization. In the small-step limit with respect to the Wasserstein distance W2, we show that policy dynamics are governed by the Fokker-Planck (heat) equation, consistent with the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto result. This indicates that policies undergo diffusion and advection, concentrating near actions with high rewards. Our findings help clarify the nature of convergence in probability matching and provide justification for empirical practices like Gaussian policy priors and additive gradient noise.
label: AI

title: Approximate Profile Maximum Likelihood
Abstract: We propose an efficient algorithm for approximating the profile maximum likelihood (PML), a maximum likelihood variant that maximizes the probability of observing a sufficient statistic instead of the empirical sample. While PML has desirable theoretical properties, exact computation is challenging. Inspired by observations from exactly solvable cases, we seek an approximate PML solution that intuitively groups comparably frequent symbols into a single symbol. This amounts to lower-bounding a certain matrix permanent by summing over a subgroup of the symmetric group instead of the entire group during computation. Extensive experimentation with the approximate solution reveals that its empirical performance is competitive and sometimes significantly surpasses state-of-the-art performance for various estimation problems.
label: AI

title: Scale-invariant temporal history (SITH): optimal slicing of the past in an uncertain world
Abstract: Both the human brain and any general artificial intelligence (AI) require a representation of the past to predict the future. However, perfectly storing all experiences is impractical. One approach widely used in various applications, including reward prediction in reinforcement learning, is to maintain recently active features of experience in a buffer. Despite its prior successes, we demonstrate that the fixed-length buffer makes Deep Q-learning Networks (DQNs) vulnerable to changes in the scale at which information is learned. To enable learning when relevant temporal scales in the environment are unknown a priori, recent advances in psychology and neuroscience suggest that the brain maintains a compressed representation of the past. We introduce a neurally-plausible, scale-free memory representation called Scale-Invariant Temporal History (SITH) for use with artificial agents. This representation covers an exponentially large period of time by sacrificing temporal accuracy for events further in the past. We demonstrate the utility of this representation by comparing the performance of agents using SITH, buffer, and exponential decay representations in learning to play video games at different complexity levels. In these environments, SITH exhibits superior learning performance by storing information for longer timescales than a fixed-size buffer and representing this information more clearly than a set of exponentially decayed features. Finally, we discuss how the application of SITH, along with other human-inspired models of cognition, could enhance reinforcement and machine learning algorithms in general.
label: AI

title: Machine Learning for Vehicular Networks
Abstract: Emerging vehicular networks are expected to enhance vehicular operation safety, efficiency, and sustainability, paving the way for autonomous driving in the era of the fifth generation (5G) cellular system. Machine learning, a major branch of artificial intelligence, has recently been applied to wireless networks to provide a data-driven approach for solving traditionally challenging problems. This article reviews recent advancements in applying machine learning to vehicular networks, aiming to draw more attention to this emerging field. After a brief overview of core machine learning concepts, we present application examples of machine learning in addressing problems arising in vehicular networks. Finally, we discuss and highlight several open research issues that warrant further investigation.

title: Low-Shot Learning with Imprinted Weights
Abstract: Human vision can instantly recognize novel visual categories after observing just one or a few training examples. We describe how to equip ConvNet classifiers with a similar capability by directly setting the final layer weights from novel training examples during low-shot learning. This process, termed weight imprinting, directly sets weights for a new category based on an appropriately scaled copy of the embedding layer activations for that training example. Weight imprinting serves as a valuable complement to training with stochastic gradient descent, providing immediate good classification performance and an initialization for any future fine-tuning. We demonstrate the connection between this imprinting process and proxy-based embeddings. However, it differs by learning only a single imprinted weight vector for each novel category, unlike embedding methods which rely on nearest-neighbor distances to training instances. Our experiments show that averaging imprinted weights leads to better generalization than using nearest-neighbor instance embeddings.

title: Query-Efficient Black-box Adversarial Examples (superceded)
Abstract: This paper is superseded by "Black-Box Adversarial Attacks with Limited Queries and Information." Current neural network-based image classifiers are vulnerable to adversarial examples, even in black-box settings where the attacker is limited to query access without gradient access. Previous methods, such as substitute networks and coordinate-based finite-difference methods, are either unreliable or query-inefficient, making them impractical for certain problems. We introduce a new method for reliably generating adversarial examples under more restricted, practical black-box threat models. First, we apply natural evolution strategies to perform black-box attacks using two to three orders of magnitude fewer queries than previous methods. Second, we present a new algorithm to perform targeted adversarial attacks in the partial-information setting, where the attacker only has access to a limited number of target classes. Using these techniques, we successfully execute the first targeted adversarial attack against a commercially deployed machine learning system, the Google Cloud Vision API, in the partial information setting.

title: Improved Regularization Techniques for End-to-End Speech Recognition
Abstract: Regularization is crucial for end-to-end speech models, as these models are highly flexible and susceptible to overfitting. Data augmentation and dropout have been essential for improving end-to-end models in other domains. However, their exploration in end-to-end speech models is relatively limited. Therefore, we investigate the effectiveness of both methods for end-to-end trainable, deep speech recognition models. We augment audio data through random perturbations of tempo, pitch, volume, temporal alignment, and by adding random noise. We further investigate the effect of dropout when applied to the inputs of all network layers. Our results show that combining data augmentation and dropout yields a relative performance improvement of over 20% on both the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) and LibriSpeech datasets. Our model performance is also competitive with other end-to-end speech models on both datasets.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Examples: Attacks and Defenses for Deep Learning
Abstract: Deep learning, with its rapid progress and significant successes across a wide range of applications, is increasingly employed in safety-critical environments. However, deep neural networks have recently been found vulnerable to carefully crafted input samples, known as adversarial examples. These examples are imperceptible to humans but can easily deceive deep neural networks during testing or deployment. The vulnerability to adversarial examples poses a major risk for deploying deep neural networks in safety-critical environments. Consequently, attacks and defenses against adversarial examples have garnered significant attention. This paper reviews recent findings on adversarial examples for deep neural networks, summarizes the methods for generating such examples, and proposes a taxonomy of these methods. Within this taxonomy, applications for adversarial examples are investigated. We further elaborate on countermeasures for adversarial examples and explore the challenges and potential solutions.
label: AI

title: Exploring High-Dimensional Structure via Axis-Aligned Decomposition of Linear Projections
Abstract: Two-dimensional embeddings remain the dominant approach for visualizing high-dimensional data. The choice of embeddings ranges from highly non-linear ones, which capture complex relationships but are difficult to interpret quantitatively, to axis-aligned projections, which are easily interpreted but limited to bivariate relationships. Linear projections can be considered a compromise between complexity and interpretability, as they allow explicit axes labels while providing significantly more degrees of freedom compared to axis-aligned projections. However, interpreting the axes directions, which are linear combinations often with many non-trivial components, remains challenging. To address this problem, we introduce a structure-aware decomposition of (multiple) linear projections into sparse sets of axis-aligned projections that jointly capture all the information of the original linear ones. Specifically, we utilize tools from Dempster-Shafer theory to formally define the relevance of a given axis-aligned projection in explaining neighborhood relations displayed in a linear projection. Furthermore, we introduce a new approach for discovering a diverse set of high-quality linear projections and demonstrate that in practice, the information of k linear projections is often jointly encoded in ~k axis-aligned plots. We have integrated these ideas into an interactive visualization system that allows users to jointly browse both linear projections and their axis-aligned representatives. Using several case studies, we show how the resulting plots lead to more intuitive visualizations and new insights.
label: AI

title: On Data-Dependent Random Features for Improved Generalization in Supervised Learning
Abstract: The randomized-feature approach has been successfully employed for large-scale kernel approximation and supervised learning. The distribution from which random features are drawn influences the number of features required to effectively perform a learning task. Recent studies have shown that using data-dependent randomization improves performance in terms of the required number of random features. This paper focuses on the randomized-feature approach in supervised learning for achieving good generalizability. We propose the Energy-based Exploration of Random Features (EERF) algorithm, based on a data-dependent score function that explores the set of possible features and exploits promising regions. We prove that the proposed score function, with high probability, recovers the spectrum of the best fit within the model class. Our empirical results on several benchmark datasets further verify that our method requires fewer random features to achieve a certain generalization error compared to state-of-the-art methods while introducing negligible pre-processing overhead. EERF can be implemented in a few lines of code and requires no additional tuning parameters.
label: AI

title: Improving End-to-End Speech Recognition with Policy Learning
Abstract: Connectionist temporal classification (CTC) is widely used for maximum likelihood learning in end-to-end speech recognition models. However, there is often a discrepancy between the negative maximum likelihood and the performance metric used in speech recognition, such as word error rate (WER). This results in a mismatch between the objective function and metric during training. We show that this problem can be mitigated by jointly training with maximum likelihood and policy gradient. Specifically, policy learning allows us to directly optimize the (otherwise non-differentiable) performance metric. We demonstrate that joint training improves relative performance by 4% to 13% for our end-to-end model compared to the same model learned through maximum likelihood. The model achieves 5.53% WER on the Wall Street Journal dataset and 5.42% and 14.70% on the Librispeech test-clean and test-other sets, respectively.

title: A Reinforcement-Learning Approach to Proactive Caching in Wireless Networks
Abstract: We consider a mobile user accessing content in a dynamic environment, where new content is generated over time (by the user's contacts) and remains relevant to the user for random lifetimes. The user, equipped with a finite-capacity cache memory, randomly accesses the system and requests all relevant content at the time of access. The system incurs an energy cost associated with the number of contents downloaded and the channel quality at that time. Assuming causal knowledge of channel quality, content profile, and user-access behavior, we model the proactive caching problem as a Markov decision process with the goal of minimizing the long-term average energy cost. We first prove the optimality of a threshold-based proactive caching scheme, which dynamically caches or removes appropriate content from the memory, prior to being requested by the user, based on the channel state. The optimal threshold values depend on the system state and are therefore computationally intractable. Therefore, we propose parametric representations for the threshold values and use reinforcement-learning algorithms to find near-optimal parametrizations. Our simulations demonstrate that the proposed schemes significantly outperform classical reactive downloading and perform very close to a genie-aided lower bound.
