title: Deep Neural Networks as 0-1 Mixed Integer Linear Programs: A Feasibility Study
Abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are highly popular today and are the subject of intense investigation. A DNN consists of layers of internal units (or neurons), each computing an affine combination of the outputs from the previous layer, applying a nonlinear operator, and outputting the corresponding value (also known as activation). A commonly used nonlinear operator is the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU), whose output is simply the maximum between its input value and zero. In this (and other similar cases, such as max pooling, where the max operation involves more than one input value), one can model the DNN as a 0-1 Mixed Integer Linear Program (0-1 MILP) where the continuous variables correspond to the output values of each unit and a binary variable is associated with each ReLU to represent its yes/no nature. This paper discusses the peculiarities of this type of 0-1 MILP model and describes an effective bound-tightening technique designed to facilitate its solution. We also present possible applications of the 0-1 MILP model arising in feature visualization and the construction of adversarial examples. Preliminary computational results, investigating (on small DNNs) the computational performance of a state-of-the-art MILP solver when applied to a known test case, namely handwritten digit recognition, are reported.

title: DeepNorm-A Deep Learning Approach to Text Normalization
Abstract: This paper presents a simple yet sophisticated approach to the challenge posed by Sproat and Jaitly (2016) - given a large corpus of written text aligned with its normalized spoken form, train an RNN to learn the correct normalization function. Text normalization for a token appears straightforward without its context. However, considering the context of the token before normalization becomes complex for certain classes. We introduce a novel approach where the prediction of our classification algorithm is utilized by our sequence-to-sequence model to predict the normalized text of the input token. Our approach requires significantly less time to learn and performs well, unlike what has been reported by Google (5 days on their GPU cluster). We have achieved an impressive accuracy of 97.62%, considering the resources employed. Our approach combines the best of both worlds: gradient boosting - state-of-the-art in most classification tasks and sequence-to-sequence learning - state-of-the-art in machine translation. We present our experiments and report results with various parameter settings.

title: Generating and designing DNA with deep generative models
Abstract: We propose generative neural network methods for generating DNA sequences and optimizing them for desired properties. We present three approaches: creating synthetic DNA sequences using a generative adversarial network (GAN); a DNA-based variant of the activation maximization ("deep dream") design method; and a joint procedure combining these two approaches. We demonstrate that these tools capture important structures within the data and, when applied to designing probes for protein binding microarrays, enable the generation of new sequences with properties estimated to be superior to those found in the training data. We believe that these results open the door for applying deep generative models to advance genomics research.
label: AI

title: TensorFlow-Serving: Flexible, High-Performance ML Serving
Abstract: We describe TensorFlow-Serving, a system designed to serve machine learning models within Google, which is also available in the cloud and as open-source software. It is highly flexible in terms of the ML platforms it supports and the ways it integrates with systems that deliver new models and updates from training to serving. Simultaneously, the core code paths surrounding model lookup and inference have been meticulously optimized to avoid performance pitfalls observed in naive implementations. Google utilizes TensorFlow-Serving in numerous production deployments, including a multi-tenant model hosting service called TFS^2.
label: AI

title: Dynamic Boltzmann Machines for Second Order Moments and Generalized Gaussian Distributions
Abstract: Dynamic Boltzmann Machine (DyBM) has proven highly efficient for predicting time-series data. Gaussian DyBM is a DyBM assuming that the predicted data is generated by a Gaussian distribution whose first-order moment (mean) dynamically changes over time, while its second-order moment (variance) remains fixed. However, in many financial applications, this assumption is quite limiting in two aspects. First, even when the data follows a Gaussian distribution, its variance may change over time. Such variance is also related to crucial temporal economic indicators like market volatility. Second, financial time-series data often requires learning datasets generated by the generalized Gaussian distribution with an additional shape parameter essential for approximating heavy-tailed distributions. Addressing these aspects, we show how to extend DyBM, resulting in significant performance improvements in predicting financial time-series data.
label: AI

title: Super-sparse Learning in Similarity Spaces
Abstract: In several applications, input samples are more naturally represented in terms of similarities between each other rather than in terms of feature vectors. In these settings, machine-learning algorithms can become computationally demanding, as they may require matching test samples against a large set of reference prototypes. To mitigate this issue, various approaches have been developed to reduce the number of required reference prototypes. Current reduction approaches select a small subset of representative prototypes in the space induced by the similarity measure and then separately train the classification function on the reduced subset. However, decoupling these two steps may not effectively reduce the number of prototypes without compromising accuracy. We overcome this limitation by jointly learning the classification function along with an optimal set of virtual prototypes, whose number can be either fixed a priori or optimized according to application-specific criteria. Creating a super-sparse set of virtual prototypes provides much sparser solutions, drastically reducing complexity at test time at the expense of slightly increased complexity during training. A smaller set of prototypes also leads to easier-to-interpret decisions. We empirically demonstrate that our approach can reduce up to ten times the complexity of Support Vector Machines, LASSO, and ridge regression at test time, without significantly affecting their classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: Hypothesis Testing for High-Dimensional Multinomials: A Selective Review
Abstract: The statistical analysis of discrete data has been the subject of extensive statistical research dating back to the work of Pearson. This survey reviews some recently developed methods for testing hypotheses about high-dimensional multinomials. Traditional tests like the χ^2 test and the likelihood ratio test can exhibit poor power in the high-dimensional setting. Much of the research in this area has focused on finding tests with asymptotically Normal limits and developing (stringent) conditions under which tests have Normal limits. We argue that this perspective suffers from a significant deficiency: it can exclude many high-dimensional cases when, despite having non-Normal null distributions, carefully designed tests can achieve high power. Finally, we illustrate that adopting a minimax perspective and considering refinements of this perspective can naturally lead to powerful and practical tests.
label: AI

title: Learning a Single Convolutional Super-Resolution Network for Multiple Degradations
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed the unprecedented success of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in single image super-resolution (SISR). However, existing CNN-based SISR methods mostly assume that a low-resolution (LR) image is bicubicly downsampled from a high-resolution (HR) image, inevitably leading to poor performance when the true degradation does not follow this assumption. Moreover, they lack scalability in learning a single model to non-blindly deal with multiple degradations. To address these issues, we propose a general framework with a dimensionality stretching strategy that enables a single convolutional super-resolution network to take two key factors of the SISR degradation process, namely, blur kernel and noise level, as input. Consequently, the super-resolver can handle multiple and even spatially variant degradations, significantly improving practicability. Extensive experimental results on synthetic and real LR images show that the proposed convolutional super-resolution network not only produces favorable results on multiple degradations but is also computationally efficient, providing a highly effective and scalable solution for practical SISR applications.
label: AI

title: Integral Equations and Machine Learning
Abstract: As both light transport simulation and reinforcement learning are governed by the same Fredholm integral equation of the second kind, reinforcement learning techniques may be employed for photorealistic image synthesis. Efficiency can be dramatically improved by guiding light transport paths using an approximate solution of the integral equation learned during rendering. In light of the recent advances in reinforcement learning for playing games, we investigate the representation of an approximate solution of an integral equation by artificial neural networks and derive a loss function for that purpose. The resulting Monte Carlo and quasi-Monte Carlo methods train neural networks with standard information instead of linear information and naturally are capable of generating an arbitrary number of training samples. These methods are demonstrated for applications in light transport simulation.

title: SchNet - a deep learning architecture for molecules and materials
Abstract: Deep learning has led to a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, encompassing web, text and image search, speech recognition, as well as bioinformatics, with growing impact in chemical physics. Machine learning in general and deep learning in particular are ideally suited for representing quantum-mechanical interactions, enabling the modeling of nonlinear potential-energy surfaces or enhancing the exploration of chemical compound space. Here we present the deep learning architecture SchNet, specifically designed to model atomistic systems by utilizing continuous-filter convolutional layers. We demonstrate the capabilities of SchNet by accurately predicting a range of properties across chemical space for molecules and materials where our model learns chemically plausible embeddings of atom types across the periodic table. Finally, we employ SchNet to predict potential-energy surfaces and energy-conserving force fields for molecular dynamics simulations of small molecules and perform an exemplary study of the quantum-mechanical properties of C20-fullerene, which would have been infeasible with regular ab initio molecular dynamics.
label: AI

title: Railway Track Specific Traffic Signal Selection Using Deep Learning
Abstract: With the railway transportation industry actively moving towards automation, accurate location and inventory of wayside track assets like traffic signals, crossings, switches, mileposts, etc., are of paramount importance. The new Positive Train Control (PTC) regulation coming into effect will directly tie many railway safety rules to the location of assets such as mileposts and signals. Newer speed regulations will be enforced based on the location of the train with respect to a wayside asset. Therefore, it is crucial for railroads to maintain an accurate database of the types and locations of these assets. This paper discusses a real-world use case of detecting railway signals from a camera mounted on a moving locomotive and tracking their locations. The camera is engineered to withstand environmental factors on a moving train and provide a consistent steady image at around 30 frames per second. Using advanced image analysis and deep learning techniques, signals are detected in these camera images, and a database of their locations is created. Railway signals differ significantly from road signals in terms of shapes and placement rules with respect to the track. Due to space constraints and traffic densities in urban areas, signals are not placed on the same side of the track, and multiple lines can run in parallel. Therefore, there is a need to associate the detected signal with the specific track on which the train runs. We present a method for associating signals with their respective tracks using a video feed from the front-facing camera mounted on the lead locomotive. A pipeline of track detection, region of interest selection, and signal detection has been implemented, resulting in an overall accuracy of 94.7% on a route covering 150 km with 247 signals.
label: AI

title: Efficient B-mode Ultrasound Image Reconstruction from Sub-sampled RF Data using Deep Learning
Abstract: Portable, three-dimensional, and ultra-fast ultrasound imaging systems increasingly demand the reconstruction of high-quality images from a limited number of radio-frequency (RF) measurements due to receiver (Rx) or transmit (Xmit) event sub-sampling. However, the presence of sidelobe artifacts from RF sub-sampling often leads to blurry images with reduced contrast using the standard beamformer, making them unsuitable for diagnostic purposes. Existing compressed sensing approaches often require either hardware modifications or computationally expensive algorithms, but their quality improvements are limited. To address this problem, we propose a novel deep learning approach that directly interpolates the missing RF data by leveraging redundancy in the Rx-Xmit plane. Our extensive experimental results using sub-sampled RF data from a multi-line acquisition B-mode system confirm that the proposed method effectively reduces the data rate without sacrificing image quality.
label: AI

title: "Zero-Shot" Super-Resolution using Deep Internal Learning
Abstract: Deep Learning has led to a dramatic leap in Super-Resolution (SR) performance in recent years. However, being supervised, these SR methods are restricted to specific training data, where the acquisition of the low-resolution (LR) images from their high-resolution (HR) counterparts is predetermined (e.g., bicubic downscaling), without any distracting artifacts (e.g., sensor noise, image compression, non-ideal PSF, etc.). Real LR images, however, rarely adhere to these restrictions, resulting in poor SR results from state-of-the-art (SotA) methods. This paper introduces "Zero-Shot" SR, which leverages the power of Deep Learning but does not rely on prior training. We exploit the internal recurrence of information inside a single image and train a small image-specific CNN at test time, using examples extracted solely from the input image itself. As such, it can adapt to different settings per image. This allows for SR of real old photos, noisy images, biological data, and other images where the acquisition process is unknown or non-ideal. On such images, our method outperforms SotA CNN-based SR methods as well as previous unsupervised SR methods. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unsupervised CNN-based SR method.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning for Distant Speech Recognition
Abstract:
Deep learning is a rapidly developing field that holds immense promise for achieving advanced artificial intelligence. One of the key goals is to create computers that can understand human speech, a critical step toward building truly intelligent machines. However, despite significant progress in recent decades, natural and reliable human-machine speech interaction remains elusive, particularly when users communicate through a distant microphone in noisy and reverberant environments. These disturbances severely distort the intelligibility of speech signals, making Distant Speech Recognition (DSR) a major challenge in the field. 

This thesis focuses on addressing the DSR scenario and proposes novel techniques, architectures, and algorithms to enhance the robustness of distant-talking acoustic models. The research delves into methodologies for realistic data contamination, particularly emphasizing DNN training using simulated data. It then explores approaches for leveraging speech contexts effectively, introducing original methodologies for both feed-forward and recurrent neural networks. Inspired by the idea that collaboration between different DNNs could be key to mitigating the negative effects of noise and reverberation, the thesis proposes a novel deep learning paradigm called network of deep neural networks. The effectiveness of these original concepts is validated through extensive experimental evaluations using real and simulated data, encompassing various corpora, microphone configurations, environments, noisy conditions, and Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) tasks.
label: AI

title: Spatial As Deep: Spatial CNN for Traffic Scene Understanding
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are typically constructed by stacking convolutional operations in layers. While CNNs demonstrate remarkable proficiency in extracting semantics from raw pixels, their ability to capture spatial relationships between pixels across rows and columns of an image remains largely unexplored. These relationships are crucial for learning semantic objects with strong shape priors but weak appearance coherence, such as traffic lanes, which are often occluded or even absent from the road surface as illustrated in Figure 1 (a). This paper proposes Spatial CNN (SCNN), a generalization of traditional deep layer-by-layer convolutions to slice-by-slice convolutions within feature maps, enabling message passing between pixels across rows and columns within a layer. SCNN is particularly well-suited for long continuous shape structures or large objects with strong spatial relationships but less prominent appearance clues, such as traffic lanes, poles, and walls. We apply SCNN to a newly released, highly challenging traffic lane detection dataset and the Cityscapes dataset. The results demonstrate that SCNN can effectively learn spatial relationships for structure output, significantly enhancing performance. SCNN outperforms the recurrent neural network (RNN) based ReNet and MRF+CNN (MRFNet) in the lane detection dataset by 8.7% and 4.6%, respectively. Notably, SCNN achieved first place in the TuSimple Benchmark Lane Detection Challenge, achieving an accuracy of 96.53%.
label: AI

title: Using Deep learning methods for generation of a personalized list of shuffled songs
Abstract: The shuffle mode, where songs are played in a randomized order determined for all tracks simultaneously, is a common feature in music player systems. However, this mode is not widely utilized by music enthusiasts as it can be too random to match their mood or simply repeat the same list each time. This paper proposes the development of a convolutional deep belief network (CDBN) trained for genre recognition based on audio features extracted from the Million Song Dataset. The learned parameters will then be used to initialize a multi-layer perceptron, which takes extracted features from a user's playlist and metadata as input to classify them into various categories. These categories will be retrospectively shuffled based on metadata, autonomously providing a playlist that effectively plays songs desired by users in normal conditions.
label: AI

title: Nearly Optimal Robust Subspace Tracking
Abstract:
This work delves into the robust subspace tracking (RST) problem and provides one of the first provable guarantees for its solution. The goal of RST is to track sequentially arriving data vectors that reside in a slowly changing low-dimensional subspace, while simultaneously being robust to corruption by additive sparse outliers. This can also be interpreted as a dynamic (time-varying) extension of robust PCA (RPCA), with the minor distinction that RST also requires a short tracking delay. We introduce a recursive projected compressive sensing algorithm called Nearly Optimal RST via ReProCS (ReProCS-NORST) due to its near-optimal tracking delay. We prove that NORST effectively addresses both the RST and dynamic RPCA problems under relaxed standard RPCA assumptions, two simple additional assumptions (slow subspace change and most outlier magnitudes lower bounded), and a few minor assumptions.

Our guarantee demonstrates that NORST enjoys a near-optimal tracking delay of $O(r \log n \log(1/\epsilon))$. The required delay between subspace change times is identical, and its memory complexity is $n$ times this value, making both nearly optimal. Here, $n$ represents the ambient space dimension, $r$ is the subspaces' dimension, and $\epsilon$ is the tracking accuracy. NORST also exhibits the best outlier tolerance compared to all prior RPCA or RST methods, both theoretically and empirically (including real videos), without requiring any specific model for the outlier support generation. This remarkable robustness is achieved through the use of additional assumptions.
label: AI

title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization and Variation Regularization
Abstract: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO) has recently achieved empirical success in various applications within operations research and machine learning, partly attributed to its regularization effect. While the connection between Wasserstein DRO and regularization has been established in several settings, existing results often rely on restrictive assumptions, such as smoothness or convexity, which are not satisfied by many problems. This paper develops a general theory on the variation regularization effect of Wasserstein DRO—a novel form of regularization generalizing total-variation regularization, Lipschitz regularization, and gradient regularization. Our findings encompass possibly non-convex and non-smooth losses and losses on non-Euclidean spaces. Examples include multi-item newsvendor, portfolio selection, linear prediction, neural networks, manifold learning, and intensity estimation for Poisson processes. As an application of this theory of variation regularization, we derive new generalization guarantees for adversarial robust learning.
label: AI

title: Avoiding Synchronization in First-Order Methods for Sparse Convex Optimization
Abstract: Parallel computing has played a pivotal role in accelerating convex optimization methods for big data analytics and large-scale machine learning (ML). However, the scalability of these optimization methods is hindered by the cost of communicating and synchronizing processors in a parallel setting. Iterative ML methods are particularly sensitive to communication cost as they often require communication at every iteration. This work extends well-known techniques from Communication-Avoiding Krylov subspace methods to first-order, block coordinate descent methods for Support Vector Machines and Proximal Least-Squares problems. Our Synchronization-Avoiding (SA) variants reduce the latency cost by a tunable factor of $s$ at the expense of a factor of $s$ increase in flops and bandwidth costs. We demonstrate that the SA-variants are numerically stable and can achieve significant speedups of up to $5.1\times$ on a Cray XC30 supercomputer.
label: AI

title: Study on the Best Uses of Technology in Support of Project-Based Learning
Abstract: Project-Based Learning (PBL) is a teaching method that leverages authentic, real-world projects as the primary driver of student learning experiences. While PBL has proven highly effective, its overall adoption rate remains relatively low, partially due to teachers' unfamiliarity with the best practices for integrating technology into successful implementations. This research study involved a comprehensive survey of supportive technology tools, along with secondary survey research from students and teachers with real-world PBL experience. The objective was to determine which technology tools best support PBL. Overall, the study found that teachers and students largely agree on the importance of technology and the effectiveness of various types of tools. Tools that fostered collaboration between teachers and students were ultimately deemed most effective, but content development and assessment tools were also found to be particularly helpful.
label: AI

title: A Spectral Approach for the Design of Experiments: Design, Analysis and Algorithms
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to construct high-quality space-filling sample designs. First, we propose a new technique to quantify the space-filling property and optimally balance uniformity and randomness in sample designs across arbitrary dimensions. Second, we establish a connection between the proposed metric (defined in the spatial domain) and the objective measure of design performance (defined in the spectral domain). This connection serves as an analytical framework for evaluating the qualitative properties of space-filling designs in general. Leveraging the theoretical insights derived from this spatial-spectral analysis, we introduce the notion of optimal space-filling designs, which we refer to as space-filling spectral designs. Third, we present an efficient estimator to evaluate the space-filling properties of sample designs across arbitrary dimensions and utilize it to develop an optimization framework for generating high-quality space-filling designs. Finally, we conduct a detailed performance comparison across two different applications in 2 to 6 dimensions: a) image reconstruction and b) surrogate modeling on several benchmark optimization functions and an inertial confinement fusion (ICF) simulation code. Our results demonstrate that the proposed spectral designs significantly outperform existing approaches, especially in high dimensions.
label: AI

title: Predicting the dissolution kinetics of silicate glasses using machine learning
Abstract: Predicting the dissolution rates of silicate glasses in aqueous conditions is a complex task as the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, and the dissolution kinetics can depend on numerous intrinsic and extrinsic factors. This study investigates the potential of data-driven models based on machine learning to predict the dissolution rates of various aluminosilicate glasses exposed to a wide range of solution pH values, from acidic to caustic conditions. Four classes of machine learning methods are explored: linear regression, support vector machine regression, random forest, and artificial neural network. Our findings reveal that while linear methods fail to accurately describe the dissolution kinetics, the artificial neural network approach offers excellent predictions due to its inherent ability to handle non-linear data. Overall, we suggest that a more extensive application of machine learning approaches could significantly accelerate the design of novel glasses with tailored properties.
label: AI

title: StackInsights: Cognitive Learning for Hybrid Cloud Readiness
Abstract: Hybrid cloud is an integrated cloud computing environment that combines public cloud, private cloud, and on-premise traditional IT infrastructures. Workload awareness, defined as a comprehensive understanding of each individual workload, is crucial for implementing hybrid cloud. While accurately assessing which workloads are suitable for on-premise deployment versus which workloads can be migrated to a cloud off-premise is critical, the assessment is primarily performed using rule or policy-based approaches. This paper introduces StackInsights, a novel cognitive system for automatically analyzing and predicting the cloud readiness of workloads for an enterprise. Our system leverages critical metrics across the entire stack: 1) infrastructure metrics, 2) data relevance metrics, and 3) application taxonomy, to identify workloads exhibiting characteristics of a) low sensitivity with respect to business security, criticality, and compliance, and b) low response time requirements and access patterns. Since capturing data relevance metrics involves intrusive and in-depth scanning of the content of storage objects, a machine learning model is employed to perform business relevance classification by learning from meta-level metrics harnessed across the stack. In contrast to traditional methods, StackInsights significantly reduces the total time for hybrid cloud readiness assessment by orders of magnitude.
label: AI

title: How well does your sampler really work?
Abstract: We present a new data-driven benchmark system for evaluating the performance of novel MCMC samplers. Inspired by the COCO benchmark in optimization, we view this task as crucial to machine learning and statistics given the rapid development of new samplers. The common hand-crafted examples used to test new samplers are insufficient; we adopt a meta-learning-like approach to generate benchmark examples from a vast corpus of datasets and models. Surrogates of posteriors found in real problems are created using highly flexible density models, including modern neural network-based approaches. We provide new insights into the real effective sample size of various samplers per unit time and the estimation efficiency of the samplers per sample. Additionally, we provide a meta-analysis to assess the predictive utility of various MCMC diagnostics and perform nonparametric regression to combine them.

title: Characterizing Political Fake News in Twitter by its Meta-Data
Abstract: This article presents a preliminary approach to characterizing political fake news on Twitter through the analysis of their meta-data. Our focus is on over 1.5 million tweets collected on the day of Donald Trump's election as the 45th president of the United States of America. We utilize the meta-data embedded within these tweets to identify differences between tweets containing fake news and those that do not. Specifically, our analysis is limited to viral tweets, studying proxies for users' exposure to tweets, characterizing accounts spreading fake news, and examining their polarization. We discovered significant differences in the distribution of followers, the number of URLs in tweets, and the verification status of users.
label: AI

title: Taming Wild High Dimensional Text Data with a Fuzzy Lash
Abstract: The bag of words (BOW) representation transforms a corpus into a matrix whose elements reflect the frequency of words. However, each row in this matrix is a very high-dimensional sparse vector. Dimension reduction (DR) is a popular method for addressing sparsity and high-dimensionality issues. Among various strategies for developing DR methods, Unsupervised Feature Transformation (UFT) is a widely used approach to map all words onto a new basis to represent BOW. The recent surge in text data and its associated challenges suggest that the DR domain still necessitates new perspectives. While a wide range of methods based on the UFT strategy have been developed, the fuzzy approach has not yet been considered for DR based on this strategy. This research investigates the application of fuzzy clustering as a DR method based on the UFT strategy to compress the BOW matrix, providing a lower-dimensional representation of documents instead of the words in a corpus. The quantitative evaluation reveals that fuzzy clustering delivers superior performance and features compared to Principal Components Analysis (PCA) and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), two popular DR methods based on the UFT strategy.
label: AI

title: Using Machine Learning to Enhance Vehicles Traffic in ATN (PRT) Systems
Abstract: This paper explores new techniques to enhance Automated Transit Networks (ATN, previously known as Personal Rapid Transit - PRT) based on Artificial Intelligence tools. The primary focus is on improving the cooperation of autonomous modules that utilize negotiation protocols, following the IoT paradigm. One of the goals is to increase ATN system throughput by optimizing autonomous vehicle cooperation. Machine learning (ML) is employed to refine algorithms designed by human programmers. We leverage "existing controls" corresponding to near-optimal solutions and build refinement models to more accurately correlate a system's dynamics with its performance. A crucial mechanism that heavily influences ATN performance is Empty Vehicle Management (EVM). The algorithms designed by human programmers were used: calling empty vehicles for waiting passengers and balancing based on reallocating empty vehicles to achieve better regularity in their distribution. This paper explores how we can improve these algorithms (and adapt them to current conditions) by employing ML to tailor individual behavioral policies. Utilizing ML techniques was feasible because our algorithm is based on a set of parameters. Various weights and thresholds can be fine-tuned to improve decision-making regarding the movement of empty vehicles across the track.
label: AI

title: Train Once, Test Anywhere: Zero-Shot Learning for Text Classification
Abstract: Zero-shot Learners are models capable of predicting unseen classes. This work proposes a Zero-shot Learning approach for text categorization. Our method involves training a model on a large corpus of sentences to learn the relationship between a sentence and the embedding of its tags. Learning this relationship enables the model to generalize to unseen sentences, tags, and even new datasets, provided they can be represented in the same embedding space. The model learns to predict whether a given sentence is related to a tag or not; unlike other classifiers that learn to classify the sentence as one of the possible classes. We propose three different neural networks for this task and report their accuracy on the test set of the dataset used for training, as well as two other standard datasets for which no retraining was performed. Our results show that our models generalize well across new unseen classes in both cases. While the models do not achieve the accuracy level of state-of-the-art supervised models, they represent a significant step toward general intelligence in natural language processing.

title: Learning a Virtual Codec Based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network to Compress Image
Abstract: While deep convolutional neural networks have proven effective in eliminating coding artifacts caused by coarse quantization in traditional codecs, training any neural network in front of the encoder for gradient back-propagation is challenging. This paper proposes an end-to-end image compression framework based on convolutional neural networks to address the non-differentiability of the quantization function in standard codecs. First, the feature description neural network is utilized to obtain a valid description in the low-dimensional space with respect to the ground-truth image, significantly reducing the amount of image data for storage or transmission. After obtaining a valid image description, standard image codecs like JPEG are leveraged to further compress the image, leading to image distortion and compression artifacts, particularly blocking artifacts, detail missing, blurring, and ringing artifacts. We then employ a post-processing neural network to remove these artifacts. Due to the challenge of directly learning a non-linear function for a standard codec based on convolutional neural networks, we propose learning a virtual codec neural network to approximate the projection from the valid description image to the post-processed compressed image, enabling efficient gradient back-propagation from the post-processing neural network to the feature description neural network during training.  An advanced learning algorithm is proposed to train our deep neural networks for compression.  This method is compatible with standard existing codecs, and our learning strategy can easily be extended to these codecs based on convolutional neural networks. Experimental results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method compared to several state-of-the-art approaches, particularly at very low bit-rates.

title: Toward Secure Edge Networks Taming Device to Device (D2D) Communication in IoT
Abstract: The increasing popularity of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) has created a need for network-based traffic anomaly detection systems capable of identifying misbehaving devices. This work proposes a lightweight technique, IoT-guard, for identifying malicious traffic flows. IoT-guard utilizes semi-supervised learning to distinguish between malicious and benign device behaviors using the network traffic generated by devices. To achieve this, we extracted 39 features from network logs and discarded any features containing redundant information. After feature selection, the Fuzzy C-Mean (FCM) algorithm was trained to obtain clusters that discriminate benign traffic from malicious traffic. We analyzed the feature scores in these clusters and utilized this information to predict the type of new traffic flows. IoT-guard was evaluated using a real-world testbed with over 30 devices. The results demonstrate that IoT-guard achieves high accuracy (98%) in differentiating various types of malicious and benign traffic, with low false positive rates. Moreover, it has a low resource footprint and can operate on OpenWRT-enabled access points and COTS computing boards.

title: Overview of the Wikidata Vandalism Detection Task at WSDM Cup 2017
Abstract: This paper reports on the Wikidata vandalism detection task at the WSDM Cup 2017. The task received five submissions, which are evaluated and compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Unlike previous work, we recast Wikidata vandalism detection as an online learning problem, requiring participant software to predict vandalism in near real-time. The best-performing approach achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.947 at a PR-AUC of 0.458. Notably, this task was organized as a software submission task: to maximize reproducibility and foster future research and development on this task, participants were asked to submit their working software to the TIRA experimentation platform along with the source code for open-source release.

title: An Artificial Neural Network Architecture Based on Context Transformations in Cortical Minicolumns
Abstract: Cortical minicolumns are considered a model of cortical organization. Their function is still a subject of ongoing research and not adequately reflected in the modern architecture of nets used in Artificial Intelligence algorithms. We propose a function for cortical minicolumns and describe it in this article. Moreover, we demonstrate how this proposal enables the construction of a new architecture, not based on convolutional neural networks, test it on MNIST data, and achieve accuracy comparable to Convolutional Neural Networks. We also demonstrate that the proposed architecture possesses the ability to train on a small number of samples. To achieve these results, we equip the minicolumns with the capacity to remember context transformations.
label: AI

title: Noise-tolerant parity learning with one quantum bit
Abstract: Demonstrating quantum advantage with less powerful but more realistic devices is of paramount importance in modern quantum information science. Recently, a significant quantum speedup was achieved in the problem of learning a hidden parity function with noise. However, if all data qubits at the query output are completely depolarized, the algorithm fails. This work presents a quantum parity learning algorithm that exhibits quantum advantage as long as one qubit is provided with non-zero polarization in each query. In this scenario, quantum parity learning naturally becomes deterministic quantum computation with one qubit. The hidden parity function can then be revealed by performing a set of operations that can be interpreted as measuring non-local observables on the auxiliary result qubit with non-zero polarization and each data qubit. We also discuss the source of the quantum advantage in our algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. |||
label: AI

title: NDT: Neual Decision Tree Towards Fully Functioned Neural Graph
Abstract: Traditional neural architectures lack the ability to update variables solely present in conditional branches. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a novel principle involving Dirac symbols and continuous functions to approximate them. This allows gradient calculations for condition-specific variables during back-propagation, creating a fully functional neural graph. Leveraging this principle, the authors propose the Neural Decision Tree (NDT), which utilizes simplified neural networks for decision functions in each branch and complex neural networks for output generation in each leaf. Extensive experiments validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the model's effectiveness.
label: AI

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Resource Allocation Assisted by Cloud Computing
Abstract: Conventional resource allocation optimization problems are often non-convex, making real-time optimal solutions difficult. This leads to performance losses when using Lagrangian relaxation or greedy methods. The paper proposes a machine learning framework for cloud-assisted resource allocation that addresses these challenges. By leveraging historical scenario data, the framework extracts similarities and stores optimal or near-optimal solutions offline. When a new scenario arrives, it is compared to historical scenarios to identify the most similar one, and the corresponding optimal solution is used for resource allocation. An example of beam allocation in multi-user massive MIMO systems showcases the superior performance of the proposed machine learning approach compared to conventional methods.
label: AI

title: Attack and Defense of Dynamic Analysis-Based, Adversarial Neural Malware Classification Models
Abstract: Deep learning-based malware detection systems are susceptible to adversarial attacks, posing a significant threat to their effectiveness. Previous research has focused on adversarial attacks against static analysis-based classifiers. However, static analysis often fails to detect packed or encrypted malware. This work investigates adversarial sample crafting strategies for dynamic analysis, which involves emulation or virtual machine scanning. These strategies operate on sparse, binary inputs, unlike continuous inputs used in image analysis. The paper examines two defensive mechanisms (distillation and ensemble defenses) against adversarial samples and proposes a novel weight decay defense. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these defense strategies in reducing the number of successfully crafted adversarial samples without significantly impacting detection accuracy. The study also finds that increasing the number of hidden layers in neural models enhances robustness to adversarial attacks without necessarily improving classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: Cyberattack Detection in Mobile Cloud Computing: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Mobile cloud applications face security challenges such as data integrity, user confidentiality, and service availability. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for detecting cyberattacks in mobile cloud environments. The framework effectively recognizes diverse cyberattacks and achieves a high accuracy (up to 97.11%) in detection. Comparisons with current machine learning-based approaches further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.
label: AI

title: Parallel Markov Chain Monte Carlo for Bayesian Hierarchical Models with Big Data, in Two Stages
Abstract: The increasing size of big data sets has led to the development of parallel Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. These methods partition data sets by observations. However, for Bayesian nested hierarchical models, a more natural approach is to split the data set by groups, as only a few parameters are common to the entire data set, while most are group-specific. This paper adapts and extends a two-stage Bayesian hierarchical modeling approach for group-based data partitioning. The first stage estimates group-specific parameters independently in parallel. These posteriors are then used as proposal distributions in the second stage, where the target distribution is the full model. Using three-level and four-level models, the paper demonstrates the accuracy and efficiency of the method, showing close agreement with full data analysis while significantly reducing computation time. The advantages over existing parallel MCMC methods are also discussed.
label: AI

title: NSML: A Machine Learning Platform That Enables You to Focus on Your Models
Abstract: Machine learning libraries like TensorFlow and PyTorch simplify model implementation, but researchers still need to perform manual tasks like GPU allocation, training status tracking, and model comparison. This paper proposes a system to automate these tasks and enhance model development. Requirements for the system are derived from an online study group with 25,000 members, including automatic GPU allocation, learning status visualization, model parameter snapshots, hyperparameter modification, and a leaderboard for performance comparison. The paper describes the system architecture and presents a proof-of-concept implementation, NAVER Smart Machine Learning (NSML). Testing confirms the system's efficiency improvements for model development.
label: AI

title: Automatic Music Highlight Extraction using Convolutional Recurrent Attention Networks
Abstract: Music highlights are valuable for music services, but existing methods often rely on low-level signal features. This paper proposes a method for extracting highlights using high-level features from convolutional recurrent attention networks (CRAN). CRAN leverages convolution and recurrent layers with an attention mechanism for sequential learning. The attention mechanism captures significant snippets, enabling differentiation between genres and providing high-level features. CRAN was evaluated on over 32,000 popular tracks in Korea, demonstrating superior performance compared to three baseline methods through quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The effects of attention and sequence information on performance are also analyzed.
label: AI

title: Mitigating Asymmetric Nonlinear Weight Update Effects in Hardware Neural Network based on Analog Resistive Synapse
Abstract: Asymmetric nonlinear weight update poses a challenge for hardware neural networks based on analog resistive synapses, hindering online training capabilities. This paper offers solutions through co-optimization with hardware-applicable deep learning algorithms. By engineering activation functions and introducing a threshold weight update scheme, the undesirable training noise caused by inaccurate weight update is effectively suppressed. The authors successfully trained a two-layer perceptron network online and improved the classification accuracy of the MNIST handwritten digit dataset to 87.8/94.8% using 6-bit/8-bit analog synapses, respectively, despite high asymmetric nonlinearity.
label: AI

title: Travel time tomography with adaptive dictionaries
Abstract: This paper develops a 2D travel time tomography method that regularizes the inversion by modeling groups of slowness pixels, called patches, as sparse linear combinations of atoms from a dictionary. Dictionary learning is incorporated during inversion to adapt dictionaries to specific slowness maps. This patch regularization, referred to as the local model, is integrated into the overall slowness map, known as the global model. The local model considers small-scale variations using a sparsity constraint, while the global model focuses on larger-scale features using an l2 regularization. This locally-sparse travel time tomography (LST) approach enables simultaneous modeling of smooth and discontinuous slowness features. The LST approach is formulated using a maximum a posteriori method and exploits the sparsity of slowness patches through dictionary learning. Comparative results demonstrate the superior performance of LST over smoothness and total variation regularization methods on densely but irregularly sampled synthetic slowness maps.
label: AI

title: Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications
Abstract: The next generation of AI applications will require continuous interaction with the environment and learning from these interactions. This necessitates high performance and flexibility in system design. The paper introduces Ray, a distributed system that addresses these requirements. Ray provides a unified interface for task-parallel and actor-based computations, supported by a single dynamic execution engine. To achieve high performance, Ray utilizes a distributed scheduler and a fault-tolerant store for managing the system's control state. Experimental results demonstrate scaling beyond 1.8 million tasks per second and superior performance compared to existing specialized systems in challenging reinforcement learning applications.
label: AI

title: On reproduction of On the regularization of Wasserstein GANs
Abstract: This report investigates the reproducibility of the paper "On the regularization of Wasserstein GANs" (2018). Five key aspects of the paper's experiments were reproduced: learning speed, stability, robustness against hyperparameters, estimating the Wasserstein distance, and various sampling methods. The report identifies the reproducible aspects and their associated resource costs. All source code for reproduction is publicly available.
label: AI

title: An MPI-Based Python Framework for Distributed Training with Keras
Abstract: This paper presents a lightweight Python framework for distributed training of neural networks using multiple GPUs or CPUs. Built upon the Keras machine learning library, the framework leverages the Message Passing Interface (MPI) protocol for coordinating the training process. The system is well-suited for job submission at supercomputing sites. The paper details the software's features, usage instructions, and performance evaluation on systems of varying sizes using a benchmark problem from high-energy physics research.

title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference

The paper also presents a co-designed training procedure to preserve model accuracy after quantization. The proposed scheme improves the trade-off between accuracy and on-device latency, demonstrating significant improvements even on MobileNets, a family of models known for efficiency. These improvements are showcased in ImageNet classification and COCO detection on popular CPUs.

title: WACSF - Weighted Atom-Centered Symmetry Functions as Descriptors in Machine Learning Potentials
Abstract: This paper introduces weighted atom-centered symmetry functions (wACSFs) as descriptors of a chemical system's geometry for predicting chemical properties such as enthalpies or potential energies using machine learning. wACSFs are based on conventional atom-centered symmetry functions (ACSFs) but address the undesirable scaling issue of ACSFs with increasing element diversity. The results show that wACSFs require a significantly smaller number than ACSFs to achieve comparable spatial resolution and lead to better generalization performance in the machine learning potential. title: A Berkeley View of Systems Challenges for AI
Abstract: With the increasing adoption of computer vision, speech recognition, and machine translation systems, AI has transitioned from research labs to production. These challenges include timely and safe decision-making in unpredictable environments, robustness against sophisticated adversaries, and efficient data processing across organizations and individuals without compromising confidentiality. The paper proposes open research directions in systems, architectures, and security to address these challenges and unlock AI's potential for societal improvement.

title: Hierarchical Text Generation and Planning for Strategic Dialogue

title: Mapping the world population one building at a time

By combining this settlement data with census data, the method generates population maps with ~30 meter resolution for 18 countries. title: Reducing Deep Network Complexity with Fourier Transform Methods

This results in a simpler neuron network, reduced computation load, and the ability to achieve high classification accuracy with fewer training examples.

title: Realistic Traffic Generation for Web Robots

title: Occam's razor is insufficient to infer the preferences of irrational agents

title: Broadcasting Spanning Forests on a Multiple-Access Channel

The input edges are distributed among the processors, with each processor holding a single edge. The underlying broadcast network operates as a multiple-access channel where a broadcast is successful only if exactly one processor broadcasts. Successful broadcasts are delivered to all processors in a single step. However, simultaneous broadcasts from multiple processors lead to interference and prevent any processor from receiving the messages. The study examines the optimality of algorithmic solutions by comparing deterministic and randomized algorithms, as well as adaptive and oblivious ones. title: SenseNet: 3D Objects Database and Tactile Simulator

title: A General Framework for Adversarial Examples with Objectives

title: The Gaussian Noise Model in the Presence of Inter-channel Stimulated Raman Scattering
Abstract: This paper introduces a Gaussian noise (GN) model that accurately accounts for an arbitrary frequency-dependent signal power profile along the link. This enables the evaluation of the impact of inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS) on the optical Kerr nonlinearity. The model also incorporates frequency-dependent fiber attenuation and allows for modeling of transmission systems utilizing hybrid amplification schemes, where distributed Raman amplification is partially applied across the optical spectrum. To include the latter two cases, a set of coupled ordinary differential equations must be numerically solved to obtain the signal power profile, resulting in a semi-analytical model. However, for lumped amplification and negligible variation in fiber attenuation, a simpler and fully analytical model, referred to as the ISRS GN model, is presented. The derived model is accurate to first-order for Gaussian modulated signals and extensively validated by numerical split-step simulations. A maximum deviation of 0.1 dB in nonlinear interference power between simulations and the ISRS GN model is found. The model is applied to a transmission system spanning an optical bandwidth of 10 THz, encompassing the entire C+L band. At optimal launch power, changes of up to 2 dB in nonlinear interference power due to ISRS are reported. Furthermore, the paper benchmarks the ISRS GN model against comparable models published in the literature.

title: Quickest drift change detection in Lévy-type force of mortality model

The approach relies on optimal stopping theory and solving a boundary value problem. The paper includes an extensive numerical analysis related to the construction of Generalized Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. Specifically, the method is applied (after appropriate calibration) to analyze Polish life tables and model the force of mortality in this population, assuming a drift changing over time.

title: An Additive Approximate Gaussian Process Model for Large Spatio-Temporal Data

Based on a hierarchical formulation of the model, the paper leverages the computational advantages of both components to perform efficient Bayesian inference. To demonstrate the inferential and computational benefits of the proposed method, extensive simulation studies are conducted assuming various scenarios of underlying spatio-temporal covariance structure. The proposed method is also applied to analyze large spatio-temporal measurements of ground-level ozone in the Eastern United States.

title: Towards Building an Intelligent Anti-Malware System: A Deep Learning Approach using Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Malware Classification

The paper examines three models: CNN-SVM, GRU-SVM, and MLP-SVM. Empirical evidence shows that GRU-SVM stands out with a predictive accuracy of approximately 84.92%, likely due to its relatively sophisticated architecture. title: Magnetic Field Inspired Contact Angle Hysteresis Drives Floating Polyolefin Rafts

A magnetic field of approximately 0.06 T deforms the water/vapor interface, impacting the interfacial apparent contact angle. This deformation creates a propulsion force, displacing the polymer raft. The velocity of displacement of the rafts' center of mass is measured. The effect is linked to the contact angle hysteresis affected by the magnetic field, enabling changes in the apparent interfacial contact angle. The paper proposes a semi-quantitative model of the process.

title: Transfer of scaled multiple quantum coherence matrices

This block-scaled transfer serves as an alternative to perfect state transfer. Notably, equal scaling of higher-order MQ-coherences matrices is achievable. Additionally, certain states can be transferred to the receiver while preserving their zero-order coherence matrix. The paper presents examples of block-scaled transfer in spin-1/2 communication lines of 6 and 42 nodes with two-qubit senders and receivers.

title: Some Indications on how to Calibrate the Social Force Model of Pedestrian Dynamics

These properties are highly relevant to simulation results, such as the extent and clearance time of a queue, as well as the maximum density and capacity flow. title: A Hierarchical Multivariate Spatio-Temporal Model for Large Clustered Climate data with Annual Cycles

The model components account for spatio-temporal dependence with annual cycles, dependence on covariates, and between responses. The large amount of data is handled by modeling the spatio-temporal dependence using the nearest neighbor Gaussian process. Response multivariate dependencies are described using the linear model of coregionalization, while annual cycles are assessed by a circular representation of time. This approach facilitates imputation of missing values and easy interpolation of climate surfaces at the national level. The motivation behind this model is the characterization of ecoregions across the Italian territory. Ecoregions are broad, discrete, ecologically homogeneous areas with similar climate, physiography, hydrography, vegetation, and wildlife. They provide a geographic framework for interpreting ecological processes, disturbance regimes, vegetation patterns, and dynamics. title: Radially falling test particle approaching an evaporating black hole

Contrary to a previous approach, the study finds that the particle may pass the Schwarzschild radius before the black hole has completely evaporated. Backreaction effects of Hawking radiation on the spacetime metric are not considered, focusing instead on a purely kinematic perspective. The paper emphasizes the importance of selecting an appropriate time coordinate when describing physical processes in the vicinity of the Schwarzschild radius. For a shrinking black hole, the true event horizon is found to be located inside the sphere delimited by the Schwarzschild radius.

title: Microstructure and elevated-temperature mechanical properties of refractory AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr High Entropy Alloy fabricated by powder metallurgy
Abstract: The paper explores new approaches for designing alloy systems with multiprincipal elements, particularly in the field of refractory materials. While most research has focused on arc melting, which suffers from grain coarsening and heterogeneous microstructure due to element segregation during cooling, this study aims to design and fabricate high-entropy alloys using powder metallurgy. The study produces a refractory high-entropy alloy with a composition near AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr through powder metallurgy. The alloy comprises two body-centered cubic (BCC) phases: a disordered BCC phase enriched with Mo, Nb, and Ta, and an ordered BCC phase enriched with Al and Zr. The AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr alloy exhibits a density of 7.46 g/cm3 and a Vickers microhardness of 678 HV. Its compressive yield strength is 2466 MPa at 298 K and 964 MPa at 1273 K. title: Non-invasive biomarkers of fetal brain development reflecting prenatal stress: an integrative multi-scale multi-species perspective on data collection and analysis
Abstract: Prenatal stress (PS) significantly impacts early postnatal behavioral and cognitive development. This phenomenon, known as "fetal programming," is mediated by the effects of the prenatal experience on the developing hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic nervous system (ANS). The HPA axis is a dynamic system regulating homeostasis, particularly the stress response, and is highly sensitive to adverse early life experiences. This paper reviews the evidence for the effects of PS on fetal programming of the HPA axis and the ANS. The authors propose a multi-scale, multi-species approach to designing preclinical and clinical studies to identify early non-invasive biomarkers of these programming effects. Such an approach would identify adverse postnatal brain developmental trajectories, paving the way for therapeutic interventions. The multiple scales include biomarkers reflecting changes in the brain epigenome, metabolome, microbiome, and ANS activity, assessed through advanced non-invasive properties of fetal heart rate fluctuations. This framework has the potential to reveal mechanistic links between maternal stress during pregnancy and changes across these physiological scales. These biomarkers may serve as early and non-invasive predictors of neurodevelopmental trajectories influenced by PS. The paper concludes that studies on PS effects should be conducted on multiple scales, derived from concerted observations in multiple animal models and human cohorts, employing machine learning for data synthesis, identification, and validation of the best non-invasive biomarkers.

title: The simulation of multilayer magnetic films

title: A Systematic Mapping Study on Requirements Engineering in Software Ecosystems

The findings indicate that most SECO-specific research has been conducted on elicitation, analysis, and modeling of requirements. Conversely, requirements selection, prioritization, verification, and traceability have attracted fewer published studies. Similarly, while most SECO research has focused on security, performance, and testability, reliability, safety, maintainability, transparency, and usability have received less attention. The paper provides a review of the academic literature on SECO-related requirements engineering activities, modeling approaches, and quality attributes, placing the source publications within a taxonomy of issues and identifying gaps where further research is needed.

title: Mean-Square Approximation of Iterated Ito and Stratonovich Stochastic Integrals of Multiplicities 1 to 6 from the Taylor-Ito and Taylor-Stratonovich Expansions Using Legendre Polynomials

The considered iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals are part of the stochastic Taylor expansions (Taylor-Ito and Taylor-Stratonovich expansions), making the results applicable to constructing high-order strong numerical methods for Ito stochastic differential equations. The paper derives expansions of iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals of multiplicities 1 to 6 using Legendre polynomials. It also proves the convergence with probability 1 of the mentioned method of generalized multiple Fourier series for iterated Ito stochastic integrals of multiplicities k (k∈ℕ) for the cases of multiple Fourier-Legendre series and multiple trigonometric Fourier series.

title: Learning Continuous User Representations through Hybrid Filtering with doc2vec

First, the paper models mobile app users based on their app usage histories and app descriptions (user2vec). Second, it introduces context awareness to this model by incorporating additional user and app-related metadata during model training (context2vec). The findings reveal three key points: (1) the quality of recommendations provided by user2vec is significantly higher than existing state-of-the-art techniques; (2) user representations generated through hybrid filtering using doc2vec prove to be valuable features in supervised machine learning models for look-alike modeling, representing the first application of hybrid filtering user models using neural probabilistic language models, specifically doc2vec, in look-alike modeling; and (3) incorporating context metadata during doc2vec model training to introduce context awareness positively impacts performance and outperforms directly including the data as features in downstream supervised models.

title: A Priori Error Estimates for Finite Element Approximations to Eigenvalues and Eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami Operator
Abstract: Elliptic partial differential equations on surfaces are fundamental in geometry, relativity theory, phase transitions, materials science, image processing, and other fields. As with SFEM for source problems, spectral approximation faces two types of errors: geometric consistency error due to surface approximation and Galerkin error due to finite element resolution of eigenfunctions. We demonstrate that these two error sources interact for eigenfunction approximations, similar to the source problem. However, the situation differs for eigenvalues, where a unique aspect arises for the geometric consistency error: the degree of geometric error depends on the choice of interpolation points used for constructing the approximate surface. This means that through a careful selection of interpolation points, the geometric consistency term can sometimes converge faster than in the eigenfunction case.

title: A dynamic network model with persistent links and node-specific latent variables, with an application to the interbank market

title: Fluctuations in active membranes

This chapter provides an overview of experimental and theoretical approaches for measuring, analyzing, and modeling active membrane fluctuations. The discussion focuses on the inherent challenge that solely analyzing fluctuations may not suffice to separate active from thermal contributions, as activity can alter the membrane's mechanical properties. It demonstrates how the GENERIC structure arises naturally from a certain symmetry in the Hamiltonian, extending previous work connecting the large-deviation behavior of reversible stochastic processes to the gradient-flow structure of their deterministic limit. Natural examples of application include particle systems with inertia.

title: ScanComplete: Large-Scale Scene Completion and Semantic Segmentation for 3D Scans
Abstract: This paper introduces ScanComplete, a novel data-driven approach for predicting a complete 3D model, along with per-voxel semantic labels, from an incomplete 3D scan of a scene as input. The key contribution of ScanComplete is its ability to handle large scenes with varying spatial extent, managing the cubic growth in data size as scene size increases. This is achieved through a fully-convolutional generative 3D CNN model with filter kernels invariant to the overall scene size. The model can be trained on scene subvolumes but deployed on arbitrarily large scenes at test time. Additionally, a coarse-to-fine inference strategy is proposed to produce high-resolution output while leveraging large input context sizes. Extensive experiments carefully evaluate different model design choices, considering both deterministic and probabilistic models for completion and semantic inference. The results demonstrate that ScanComplete outperforms other methods not only in the size of the environments handled and processing efficiency but also in completion quality and semantic segmentation performance by a significant margin.

title: Neutrino emission from Cooper pairs at finite temperatures
Abstract: This paper provides a brief review of the current understanding of neutrino pair emission through neutral weak currents caused by Cooper pair breaking and formation (PBF) in superfluid baryon matter at thermal equilibrium. The cases of singlet-state pairing with isotropic superfluid gap and spin-triplet pairing with anisotropic gap are analyzed, considering anomalous weak interactions caused by superfluidity. The study reveals that accounting for anomalous weak interactions in both the vector and axial channels is crucial for accurately describing neutrino energy losses through PBF processes. The anomalous contributions lead to almost complete suppression of PBF neutrino emission in spin-singlet superfluids and a significant reduction of PBF neutrino losses in spin-triplet superfluid neutron matter. This significantly slows down the cooling rate of neutron stars with superfluid cores.

title: Unifying Theories of Time with Generalised Reactive Processes
Abstract: Hoare and He's theory of reactive processes provides a unifying foundation for the formal semantics of concurrent and reactive languages. While highly applicable, their theory is limited to models that express event histories as discrete sequences. This paper demonstrates how their theory can be generalized using an abstract trace algebra. This algebra enables the consideration of continuous-time traces, facilitating models of hybrid systems. The paper then uses this algebra to reconstruct the theory of reactive processes in this generic setting and proves characteristic laws for sequential and parallel processes, all of which have been mechanically verified using the Isabelle/HOL proof assistant.

title: Entanglement and teleportation between polarization and wave-like encodings of an optical qubit
Abstract: Light is an essential medium for communication among various quantum information processing and storage devices. Due to their differing physical nature, some of these devices couple more strongly to discrete, and some to continuous degrees of freedom of a quantum optical wave. Therefore, developing a technological capability to interconvert quantum information encoded in these degrees of freedom is desirable. This paper presents the generation and characterization of an entangled state between a dual-rail (polarization-encoded) single-photon qubit and a qubit encoded as a superposition of opposite-amplitude coherent states. The paper further demonstrates the application of this state as a resource for interfacing quantum information between these encodings. In particular, the paper showcases the teleportation of a polarization qubit onto a freely propagating continuous-variable qubit.

title: Asymptotic period of an aperiodic Markov chain
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of asymptotic period for an irreducible and aperiodic, discrete-time Markov chain X on a countable state space and develops the theory leading to its formal definition. The asymptotic period of X equals one minus its period if X is recurrent but may be larger than one if X is transient. X is asymptotically aperiodic if its asymptotic period equals one. The paper presents several sufficient conditions for asymptotic aperiodicity. The asymptotic period of a birth-death process on the nonnegative integers is studied in detail, demonstrating that it is equal to 1, 2, or infinity. Criteria for the occurrence of each value in terms of the 1-step transition probabilities are established.

title: Growing Attributed Networks through Local Processes
Abstract: This paper proposes an attributed network growth model. While it is known that individuals use limited resources to form connections with similar others, we lack an understanding of how local and resource-constrained mechanisms explain the emergence of rich structural properties found in real-world networks. This paper makes three contributions. First, it proposes a parsimonious and accurate model of attributed network growth that jointly explains the emergence of in-degree distributions, local clustering, clustering-degree relationships, and attribute mixing patterns. Second, the model is based on biased random walks and uses local processes to form edges without relying on global network information. Third, the model accounts for various sociological phenomena: bounded rationality, structural constraints, triadic closure, attribute homophily, and preferential attachment. Experiments indicate that the proposed Attributed Random Walk (ARW) model accurately preserves network structure and attribute mixing patterns of six real-world networks. It outperforms eight state-of-the-art models by a statistically significant margin of 2.5-10x.

title: RedDwarfData: a simplified dataset of StarCraft matches

This paper revisits an approximation in this formalism, namely the assumption of a constant Jacobian determinant. The paper demonstrates that this approximation can introduce an error and illustrates it for a harmonic oscillator. Finally, it presents a strategy to prevent this error.

title: Boundary-induced inhomogeneity of particle layers in the solidification of suspensions
Abstract: When a suspension freezes, a compacted particle layer forms at the solidification front, significantly affecting the freezing process. A directional solidification experiment involving monodispersed suspensions in thin samples revealed a connection between the thickness of this layer and the sample depth. This is attributed to an inhomogeneity of particle density induced by the sample plates. A mechanical model relates the layer thickness to the sample depth and enables the selection of a particle density distribution that best fits the data. This distribution involves an influence length of sample plates of about nine particle diameters. These findings clarify the impact of boundaries on suspension freezing and may be useful for modeling polydispersed suspensions, where large particles could act as smooth boundaries for smaller ones.

title: Can winds driven by active galactic nuclei account for the extragalactic gamma-ray and neutrino backgrounds?
Abstract: Observations reveal the widespread presence of fast and powerful winds in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), distinct from relativistic jets. These winds are likely launched from accretion disks and interact strongly with the gas in their host galaxies. This interaction is expected to produce strong shocks that accelerate non-thermal particles to high energies. These winds have been proposed as a source for a significant portion of the observed extragalactic gamma-ray background (EGB) in the GeV-TeV range and the diffuse neutrino background in the PeV range, through the decay of neutral and charged pions generated in inelastic $pp$ collisions between protons accelerated by the forward shock and the ambient gas. However, previous studies did not adequately consider processes like adiabatic losses, which can significantly reduce gamma-ray and neutrino fluxes. This paper evaluates the production of gamma-rays and neutrinos by AGN-driven winds in detail, modeling their hydrodynamic and thermal evolution, including the effects of their two-temperature structure. The study finds that these winds can account for less than $\\sim 30$% of the EGB flux, as exceeding this value would violate the independent upper limit derived from the diffuse isotropic gamma-ray background. If the neutrino spectral index is steep with $\\Gamma\\gtrsim 2.2$, a severe tension with the isotropic gamma-ray background would arise if winds contribute more than $20$% of the IceCube neutrino flux in the $10-100$TeV range. However, at energies $\\gtrsim100$~TeV, the IceCube neutrino flux could still be explained by AGN-driven winds if the spectral index is as small as $\\Gamma\\sim2.0-2.1$. The detectability of gamma-ray point sources also imposes significant constraints on such scenarios. |||

title: Polyp detection inside the capsule endoscopy: an approach for power consumption reduction

While this technology has many advantages over conventional endoscopy, limitations arise due to the use of small-size batteries. The radio transmitter consumes a significant portion of energy, making data reduction a crucial aspect for minimizing power consumption. Compression methods, reduced video resolution, and frame rate reduction have been proposed to address this issue. Our approach focuses on detecting informative frames within the capsule and transmitting only these frames, eliminating the need to send numerous non-informative frames.  We have specifically developed a hardware-friendly algorithm for polyp detection, which utilizes features like positive contrast and customized edges of polyps to identify polyp presence.  This method avoids complex iterative structures, saving power and reducing response time.  Experimental results show an acceptable detection rate.

title: Estimation under group actions: recovering orbits from invariants
Abstract: We investigate a class of orbit recovery problems where we observe independent copies of an unknown element in a p-dimensional space, each linearly acted upon by a random element from a group (such as the cyclic group of order p or the group of 3D rotations) and then corrupted by additive Gaussian noise. We establish matching upper and lower bounds on the number of samples required to recover the group orbit of this unknown element with high probability. These bounds, based on invariant theory, directly relate the statistical difficulty of the estimation problem to the algebraic properties of the group. We also provide computationally efficient procedures for verifying these properties in many cases of interest. This model finds applications in geometric problems in signal processing, computer vision, and structural biology.  Our results are particularly relevant to the reconstruction problem in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a significant practical problem.  For a given problem size, we show that if cryo-EM images are corrupted by noise with variance sigma squared, the number of images required to recover the molecule structure scales as sigma to the power of 6. We demonstrate this bound with a novel algorithm for ab initio reconstruction in cryo-EM, based on invariant features of degree at most 3.  We also discuss how to recover multiple molecular structures from mixed cryo-EM samples.

title: Learning Deep and Compact Models for Gesture Recognition

Our solution achieves near state-of-the-art accuracy on the ChaLearn dataset with only half the model size compared to previous methods.  We further explore knowledge distillation and model compression to achieve an even more compact representation. The final model is less than 1 MB in size, a significant reduction from the initial model, with only a 7% drop in accuracy.  This makes it suitable for real-time gesture recognition on mobile devices.
