title: Potentiality, Actuality and Non-Separability in Quantum and Classical Physics: Res Potentiae in the Macroscopic World
Abstract: To address persistent aporias in quantum mechanics, Kastner, Kauffman, and Epperson have recently proposed a new interpretation of Heisenberg's ontological duality of res extensa and res potentia. In related work, Khrennikov and Aerts, along with their respective associates, have explored the intermediate domain of mesoscopic phenomena where quantum-like behavior can be observed and formalized. This paper generalizes this work to define a third domain, encompassing macroscopic, interactive processes to which quantum concepts, but not quantum formalism, apply. It is shown that these processes follow the non-standard logic proposed in the last century by the Franco-Romanian thinker Stéphane Lupasco. This logical system, rooted in the ontological dualities in nature, describes the evolution of complex processes and emergence at macroscopic levels of reality as chains of interacting actualities and potentialities. Without contradicting the laws of physics, this framework provides new avenues for exploring problems related to life, cognition, and information. The most appropriate formalism for describing this logic is currently under investigation.

title: Mechanisms influencing the formation of the carbonized layer relief on the polymer surface after the ion-plasma treatment modeling
Abstract: This work focuses on modeling processes occurring during ion-plasma treatment of polyurethane, leading to the formation of a specialized carbonized layer on its surface. The mechanisms influencing the formation of wave-like relief in the carbonized layer are examined. The boundary value problem for the heat equation is solved to model the effect of the temperature component. Using the finite element method, the deformation of the polyurethane sample during ion-plasma treatment is calculated. Based on these calculations, conclusions are drawn about the impact of these factors on the formation of wave-like relief in the carbonized layer.

title: Terahertz dynamics of electron-vibron coupling in single molecules with tunable electrostatic potential
Abstract: Understanding electronic and vibronic properties at the individual molecule level provides key insights for future advances in chemistry, nanoelectronics, and quantum information technologies. Single electron tunneling spectroscopy has been employed to study the charging/discharging process in single molecules. However, the obtained information primarily focused on static electronic properties, with indirect access to dynamical properties. This paper reports on terahertz (THz) spectroscopy of single fullerene molecules using a single molecule transistor (SMT) geometry. Time-domain THz autocorrelation measurements yielded THz spectra associated with the THz-induced center-of-mass oscillation of the molecules. The observed peaks are finely split into two, reflecting the difference in the van der Waals potential profile experienced by the molecule on the metal surface when the number of electrons on the molecule fluctuates by one during the single electron tunneling process. This ultrahigh-sensitivity to the electronic/vibronic structures of a single molecule upon adding/removing a single electron was achieved using THz spectroscopy in the SMT geometry. This novel scheme presents a new opportunity for investigating ultrafast THz dynamics of sub-nm scale systems.

title: Coherent control theory and experiment of optical phonons in diamond
Abstract: Coherent control of optical phonons has been experimentally demonstrated in various physical systems. While transient dynamics for optical phonons can be explained by phenomenological models, the coherent control experiment cannot be explained due to quantum interference. This paper proposes a theoretical framework for the generation and detection processes of optical phonons, experimentally confirming the model using the diamond optical phonon through a double-pump-probe type experiment.

title: On the Diversity of Realistic Image Synthesis
Abstract: Numerous image processing tasks can be formulated as translating images between two image domains, such as colorization, super-resolution, and conditional image synthesis. In many of these tasks, an input image may correspond to multiple outputs. However, current approaches exhibit only minor diversity in outputs. This paper introduces a novel approach for synthesizing diverse realistic images corresponding to a semantic layout. A diversity loss objective is introduced, which maximizes the distance between synthesized image pairs and links the input noise to the semantic segments in the synthesized images. This approach not only produces diverse images but also allows users to manipulate the output images by adjusting the noise manually. Experimental results demonstrate that images synthesized using this approach are significantly more diverse than those produced by current methods, and introducing the diversity loss does not degrade the reality of the base networks.

title: Experimental Demonstration of Quantum Tunneling in IBM Quantum Computer
Abstract: Quantum computers hold promise for simulating large quantum systems, a challenging task for classical computers. This work reports the experimental realization of quantum tunneling of a single particle through different types of potential barriers by performing digital quantum simulations using IBM quantum computers. Two and three-qubit systems are considered to visualize the tunneling process and highlight its unique quantum nature. The tunneling and oscillations of the particles in a step-well, double-well, and multi-well potential are observed through experimental results. The proposed quantum circuits and simulation techniques can be extended to observe tunneling phenomena for multi-particle systems in various potentials.

title: A Flexible Approach to Automated RNN Architecture Generation
Abstract: Designing neural architectures demands expert knowledge and extensive trial and error. While automated architecture search simplifies these requirements, existing methods produce recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures limited in flexibility and components. This paper proposes a domain-specific language (DSL) for automated architecture search, capable of generating novel RNNs of arbitrary depth and width. The DSL is flexible enough to define standard architectures like the Gated Recurrent Unit and Long Short Term Memory, allowing the introduction of non-standard RNN components such as trigonometric curves and layer normalization. Using two candidate generation techniques, random search with a ranking function and reinforcement learning, novel architectures produced by the RNN DSL are explored for language modeling and machine translation domains. The resulting architectures deviate from human intuition yet perform well on their targeted tasks, suggesting that the space of usable RNN architectures is far larger than previously assumed.

title: Detection and classification of masses in mammographic images in a multi-kernel approach
Abstract: According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death among adult women globally. While breast cancer occurs indiscriminately across countries with varying levels of social and economic development, mortality rates remain high in developing and underdeveloped countries due to limited access to early detection technologies. Clinically, mammography remains the most effective diagnostic technology due to its widespread use and interpretation. This paper proposes a method for detecting and classifying mammographic lesions using image regions of interest. The proposed method involves decomposing each image using multi-resolution wavelets and extracting Zernike moments from each wavelet component. This approach combines both texture and shape features, applicable to both the detection and classification of mammary lesions. The study utilizes 355 images of fatty breast tissue from the IRMA database, including 233 normal instances (no lesion), 72 benign, and 83 malignant cases. Classification is performed using SVM and ELM networks with modified kernels to optimize accuracy rates, achieving 94.11%. Considering both accuracy rates and training times, the ratio between average percentage accuracy and average training time is calculated in reverse order. The proposed model exhibits a ratio 50 times higher than the best method currently available. This model's ability to combine high accuracy with low learning time significantly reduces learning time for new data, saving hours compared to existing methods.

title: Analysis of supervised and semi-supervised GrowCut applied to segmentation of masses in mammography images
Abstract: Breast cancer is a prevalent malignancy globally. Mammography image analysis is crucial for early detection. Precise tumor segmentation in digital mammograms enhances diagnostic accuracy and reduces misdiagnosis. This study investigates the feasibility of applying GrowCut for tumor segmentation and proposes two semi-supervised GrowCut variations. The study utilizes the Mini-MIAS mammography image database and compares GrowCut to other segmentation techniques, including Region Growing, Active Contours, Random Walks, and Graph Cut. The results demonstrate that GrowCut outperforms other methods in terms of evaluated metrics. Furthermore, the proposed semi-supervised GrowCut variants achieve clinically satisfactory segmentation quality.

title: Network Cache Design under Stationary Requests: Exact Analysis and Poisson Approximation
Abstract: The design of caching algorithms to maximize hit probability is a well-studied area. This paper introduces a utility function associated with each content, reflecting its hit rate or probability. The objective is to maximize the sum of utilities across all contents under stationary and ergodic request processes. While generally non-convex, the problem becomes convex when the inter-request time distribution exhibits a non-increasing hazard rate function. Explicit optimal solutions are provided for specific inter-request time distributions, and a comparison between hit-rate based and hit-probability based optimization is presented. The paper also introduces a reverse engineering approach for LRU implementation under stationary arrivals and proposes decentralized algorithms utilizing limited information. Stability analysis using a discrete time Lyapunov technique (DTLT) reveals that decentralized algorithms solving the hit-rate problem are more robust than their hit-probability counterparts. Based on these findings, lightweight Poisson approximate decentralized and online algorithms are proposed for efficient and accurate hit rate and probability optimization.

title: Temperature of source regions of $^3$He-rich impulsive solar energetic particle events
Abstract: Impulsive solar energetic particle (SEP) events, originating from energy dissipation in small solar flares, exhibit anomalous abundances. This suggests a unique acceleration mechanism, though its details remain unclear. Heavy-ion enhancements indicate a low temperature source plasma, unlike typical flares. This study examines the $^3$He-rich SEP event of November 20, 2012, utilizing Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)/ Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) images to investigate its thermal variation. The event is associated with recurrent coronal jets, and a Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis is conducted to study the temperature evolution and distribution of the source regions. Preliminary results suggest that the temperature of the associated solar source ranges between 1.2 and 3.1 MK.

title: Optical Manipulation of Magnetic Vortex Visualized in situ by 4D Electron Microscopy
Abstract: Understanding the dynamics of topological vortex and antivortex formation in ferromagnetic micro/nanoscale building blocks under external perturbations is critical for magnetic vortex-based information processing and spintronic devices. Prior studies have focused on magnetic vortex-core switching using external magnetic fields, spin-polarized currents, or spin waves, limiting the exploration of novel spin configurations emerging from ground states in ferromagnetic disks. This research presents in situ visualization of femtosecond laser quenching-induced magnetic vortex changes in symmetric ferromagnetic Permalloy disks using Lorentz phase imaging with 4D electron microscopy. Besides switching of magnetic vortex chirality and polarity, a variety of complex magnetic structures are observed, including a multitude of newly created topological magnetic defects (vortex and antivortex) that conserve the topological winding number. This demonstrates the direct impact of topological invariants on magnetization dynamics in ferromagnetic disks. The observed spin configurations exhibit mirror or rotational symmetry due to the geometrical confinement of the disks. Micromagnetic simulations, combined with experimental observations, reveal the underlying magnetization dynamics and formation mechanism of the optically-quenched complex magnetic structures. Their distinct occurrence rates are attributed to their formation-growth energetics and pinning effects at the disk edge. These findings suggest a new paradigm for fast switching of vortex cores through optical quenching, enabling potential applications in magnetic vortex-based information recording and spintronic devices.

title: Learning Sight from Sound: Ambient Sound Provides Supervision for Visual Learning
Abstract: Sounds, such as crashing waves or roaring cars, provide vital information about objects in our environment. This paper demonstrates that ambient sounds can serve as a supervisory signal for learning visual models. A convolutional neural network is trained to predict a statistical summary of the sound associated with a video frame. This process enables the network to learn a representation capturing information about objects and scenes. The representation is evaluated on various recognition tasks, demonstrating performance comparable to other state-of-the-art unsupervised learning methods. Visualizations reveal that the network learns units selectively responsive to objects often associated with characteristic sounds. This work expands on a previous conference paper by Owens et al. (2016) with additional experiments and discussions.

title: Blind High Dynamic Range Quality estimation by disentangling perceptual and noise features in images
Abstract: Assessing the visual quality of High Dynamic Range (HDR) images is a burgeoning research topic, gaining importance with the widespread adoption of HDR technology. This paper proposes a novel convolutional neural network-based model for No Reference Image Quality Assessment (NR-IQA) of HDR data. The model predicts the noise level and location, perceptual influence of image pixels on noise, and perceived quality of a distorted image without relying on a reference image. It extracts numerical values representing the noise present in a distorted image and the perceptual effects observed by a human eye viewing the same image. These measures are extracted sequentially and combined in a mixing function to compute the perceived image quality. The perceptual effects component is trained on a real-world image quality dataset instead of using psychophysical experiment results. The proposed model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance for HDR NR-IQA, achieving results comparable to HDR Full Reference Image Quality Assessment (FR-IQA) algorithms.

title: Model-based curve registration via stochastic approximation EM algorithm
Abstract: Functional data often exhibit both amplitude and phase variation around a common base shape, with phase variation represented by a warping function. Curve registration removes phase variation through curve alignment and inference of warping functions. In the presence of substantial noise, model-based methods are used for simultaneous smoothing and curve registration. However, the nonlinearity of these models can make inference computationally demanding. This paper presents an alternative model-based curve registration method, offering improved computational stability and efficiency compared to existing approaches. The method is applied to analyze elephant seal dive profiles, demonstrating that clustering based on phase variations using predicted warping functions provides more intuitive groupings.
label: AI

title: Positive definite (p.d.) functions vs p.d. distributions
Abstract: This paper provides explicit transforms for Hilbert spaces associated with positive definite functions on the real line and positive definite tempered distributions, including generalizations to non-abelian locally compact groups. Applications to the theory of extensions of positive definite functions and distributions are included. The paper derives explicit representation formulas for positive definite tempered distributions in the sense of L. Schwartz, with applications to Dirac combs and diffraction. Further applications include parallels between Bochner's theorem for continuous positive definite functions and its generalization to Bochner/Schwartz representations for positive definite tempered distributions using tempered positive measures. The transforms clarify the respective reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs), those of N. Aronszajn and L. Schwartz. Additional applications are presented for stationary-increment Gaussian processes.

title: Audio to Body Dynamics
Abstract: This paper presents a method that generates a video of skeleton predictions from an audio recording of violin or piano playing, which can then be used to animate an avatar. The key idea is to create an animation of an avatar that mimics the hand movements of a pianist or violinist based solely on the audio input. While achieving fully detailed and accurate arm and finger motion is an ambitious goal, the possibility of predicting body movement from music alone is uncertain. This paper presents the first result demonstrating that natural body dynamics can be predicted from music. An LSTM network trained on violin and piano recital videos uploaded to the internet is used to predict skeletal points, which are then applied to a rigged avatar to create the animation.

title: Linear Time Clustering for High Dimensional Mixtures of Gaussian Clouds
Abstract: Clustering mixtures of Gaussian distributions is a fundamental and challenging problem encountered in various high-dimensional data processing tasks. While advancements in learning Gaussian mixture models have focused on improving separation bounds and generalization to arbitrary classes of mixture models, computational efficiency has received less attention. This paper proposes a novel and highly efficient clustering algorithm for n points drawn from a mixture of two arbitrary Gaussian distributions in p-dimensional space. The algorithm involves performing random 1-dimensional projections until a direction yielding a user-specified clustering error e is found. For a 1-dimensional separation parameter γ satisfying γ = Q<sup>-1</sup>(e), the expected number of projections is bounded by o(ln p) when γ ≤ c√ln(ln p), where c is the separability parameter of the two Gaussians in p-dimensional space. Consequently, the expected overall running time of the algorithm is linear in n and quasi-linear in p at o(ln p)O(np), and the sample complexity is independent of p. This result contrasts with prior works that provide polynomial, at best quadratic, running times in p and n. The paper shows that the bound on the expected number of 1-dimensional projections extends to the case of three or more Gaussian components and presents a generalization of the results to mixture distributions beyond the Gaussian model.

title: Hyperparameters Optimization in Deep Convolutional Neural Network / Bayesian Approach with Gaussian Process Prior
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) are widely used in complex machine learning tasks. However, hyperparameter optimization is crucial for developing effective ConvNet architectures, as accuracy and performance depend heavily on hyperparameters. These multilayered architectures are parameterized by hyperparameters such as the number of convolutional layers, fully connected dense layers and neurons, dropout probability, and learning rate. Searching for optimal hyperparameter values within the hyperparameter space is challenging, especially for complex hierarchical architectures. Numerous methods have been proposed over the years to explore the hyperparameter space and find the optimal set. Grid search and random search, while widely used, are known to be inefficient and computationally expensive due to the large number of hyperparameters. Sequential model-based Bayesian Optimization emerges as a promising alternative to address the complexity of the unknown cost function. Recent studies on Bayesian Optimization by Snoek, involving nine convolutional network parameters, have achieved the lowest error report in the CIFAR-10 benchmark. This article aims to provide an overview of the mathematical concepts underlying Bayesian Optimization over a Gaussian prior.

title: Equivalences and counterexamples between several definitions of the uniform large deviations principle
Abstract: This paper explores the equivalences between four definitions of uniform large deviations principles and uniform Laplace principles found in the literature. Counterexamples are presented to illustrate the differences between these definitions, and specific conditions are described under which they become equivalent. A fifth definition, called the equicontinuous uniform Laplace principle (EULP), is proposed and proven to be equivalent to Freidlin and Wentzell's definition of a uniform large deviations principle. Sufficient conditions are presented that guarantee a measurable function of an infinite-dimensional Wiener process satisfies an EULP using the variational methods of Budhiraja, Dupuis, and Maroulas. This theory is applied to prove that a family of Hilbert space-valued stochastic equations subject to multiplicative noise satisfies a uniform large deviations principle that is uniform over all initial conditions within bounded subsets of the Hilbert space. This result represents an improvement over previous weak convergence methods, which could only prove uniformity over compact sets.

title: Attentive Memory Networks: Efficient Machine Reading for Conversational Search
Abstract: Recent advancements in conversational systems have revolutionized the search paradigm. Traditionally, users pose queries to search engines, which return answers based on their indices, potentially leveraging external knowledge bases and conditioning responses on previous interactions within the search session. In natural conversations, an additional source of information emerges: earlier utterances can be referred to. Conversational Information Retrieval (IR) systems must keep track of information conveyed by the user during the conversation, even if it is implicit. This paper argues that building a representation of a conversation can be framed as a machine reading task, where an automated system receives a series of statements and must answer questions based solely on those statements, without consulting external knowledge. The paper advocates for the information retrieval community to embrace this task, both as a stand-alone entity and integrated into broader conversational search settings. Focusing on machine reading as a stand-alone task, the paper introduces the Attentive Memory Network (AMN), an end-to-end trainable machine reading algorithm. Its key contribution is efficiency, achieved through a hierarchical input encoder that iterates over the input only once. Speed is critical in conversational search, as delays between conversational turns impact naturalness. The AMN is evaluated on 20 datasets commonly used for assessing machine reading algorithms, demonstrating performance comparable to state-of-the-art models while requiring significantly fewer computations.

title: Fast Quantum Algorithm for Solving Multivariate Quadratic Equations
Abstract: In August 2015, the cryptographic community was shaken by a surprising announcement from the US National Security Agency (NSA) concerning plans to transition to post-quantum algorithms. Since then, post-quantum cryptography has become a topic of paramount importance for standardization bodies. The transition from currently deployed public-key algorithms to post-quantum algorithms has proven challenging in various aspects, particularly in evaluating the quantum-bit security of post-quantum cryptosystems. This question is crucial for standardizing these cryptosystems. This paper investigates the quantum security of solving a system of m Boolean multivariate quadratic equations in n variables (MQb), a central problem in post-quantum cryptography. For n = m, under a natural algebraic assumption, a Las-Vegas quantum algorithm solving MQb is presented, requiring the evaluation of, on average, O(2<sup>0.462n</sup>) quantum gates. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the fastest algorithm for solving MQb.

title: Neutrino Oscillations Within the Induced Gravitational Collapse Paradigm of Long Gamma-Ray Bursts
Abstract: The induced gravitational collapse (IGC) paradigm of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) associated with supernovae (SNe) predicts copious neutrino-antineutrino (νν̄) emission due to the hypercritical accretion process of SN ejecta onto a neutron star (NS) binary companion. Neutrino emission can reach luminosities up to 10<sup>57</sup> MeV s<sup>-1</sup>, with mean neutrino energies of 20 MeV and neutrino densities of 10<sup>31</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup>. Along their path from the vicinity of the NS surface outward, these neutrinos undergo flavor transformations dictated by the neutrino to electron density ratio. This study determines the neutrino and electron densities in the accretion zone and uses them to compute the neutrino flavor evolution. Considering normal and inverted neutrino-mass hierarchies within the two-flavor formalism (ν<sub>e</sub>ν<sub>x</sub>), the final electronic and non-electronic neutrino content is estimated after two oscillation processes: (1) neutrino collective effects due to neutrino self-interactions where the neutrino density dominates, and (2) the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) effect, where the electron density dominates. The study finds that the final neutrino content is composed of approximately 55% (62%) electronic neutrinos (ν<sub>e</sub> + ν̄<sub>e</sub>) for the normal (inverted) neutrino-mass hierarchy. These results represent the first step towards characterizing a novel source of astrophysical MeV neutrinos, in addition to core-collapse SNe, warranting further attention.

title: Towards a More Complete Object-Orientation in Design Grammars
Abstract: The ongoing digital transformation in industry encompasses all stages of the product life cycle. Design decisions and dimensioning during the early conceptual design stages significantly influence the product's life cycle costs (LCC). Automating the conceptual design phase promises substantial LCC gains. Design grammars encode design processes in production systems using rule sequences that automatically create an abstract central product model (central data model) from given requirements. Graph-based design languages utilize the Unified-Modeling-Language (UML) to define product entities (classes) supporting object-oriented inheritance. Graphical rules instantiate classes and iteratively assemble the central model. This paper proposes extending design languages by introducing methods (operations). This enables the use of object-oriented design patterns and interface mechanisms, fully implementing object-oriented principles. A graphical mechanism for modeling method calls is presented, seamlessly integrating into the graph-based design language's graphical rule specification. The object-oriented design grammar facilitates modularization and reusability of engineering knowledge, enhancing the integration of engineering domains and enabling multistakeholder collaboration with access control (information security).

title: Cognitive Database: A Step towards Endowing Relational Databases with Artificial Intelligence Capabilities
Abstract: This paper proposes Cognitive Databases, an approach for transparently enabling Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities within relational databases. A key aspect of the design is to view the structured data source as meaningful unstructured text and then use this text to build an unsupervised neural network model using a Natural Language Processing (NLP) technique called word embedding. This model captures hidden inter-/intra-column relationships between database tokens of different types. Each database token is assigned a vector encoding contextual semantic relationships. The word embedding model is seamlessly integrated into existing SQL query infrastructure, enabling a new class of SQL-based analytics queries called cognitive intelligence (CI) queries. CI queries leverage the model vectors to facilitate complex queries, such as semantic matching, inductive reasoning queries (analogies), predictive queries using entities not present in the database, and more generally, utilizing knowledge from external sources. The unique capabilities of Cognitive Databases are demonstrated using an Apache Spark-based prototype to execute inductive reasoning CI queries over a multi-modal database containing text and images. The authors believe their system exemplifies the use of AI functionality to empower relational databases with capabilities previously difficult to realize in practice.
label: AI

title: Y-net: 3D intracranial artery segmentation using a convolutional autoencoder
Abstract: Automated segmentation of intracranial arteries on magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) facilitates quantification of cerebrovascular features, providing tools for understanding aging and pathophysiological adaptations of the cerebrovascular system. Using a convolutional autoencoder (CAE) for segmentation is promising as it leverages the autoencoder structure for effective noise reduction and feature extraction by representing high-dimensional information with low-dimensional latent variables. This report describes an optimized CAE model (Y-net) trained to learn a 3D segmentation model of intracranial arteries from 49 cases of MRA data. The trained model demonstrates superior performance compared to three traditional segmentation methods in both binary classification and visual evaluation.

title: Simulations of the Solar System's Early Dynamical Evolution with a Self-Gravitating Planetesimal Disk
Abstract: Over the past decade, the Nice model has dramatically reshaped our understanding of the solar system's formation and early evolution. Within this model, a transient period of planet-planet scattering is triggered by gravitational interactions between the giant planets and a massive primordial planetesimal disk, leading to a successful reproduction of the solar system's present-day architecture. Typically, self-gravity of the planetesimal disk is neglected in Nice model realizations due to computational constraints. However, recent analyses have shown that a self-gravitating disk can exhibit distinct dynamic behavior, potentially impacting the solar system's evolutionary path. This work investigates this discrepancy using a large suite of Nice model simulations with and without a self-gravitating planetesimal disk, leveraging the parallel capabilities of graphic processing units. The simulations demonstrate that self-consistent modeling of particle interactions does not lead to significantly different final planetary orbits compared to conventional simulations. Moreover, self-gravitating calculations show similar planetesimal evolution to non-self-gravitating numerical experiments after dynamical instability is triggered, suggesting that the orbital clustering observed in the distant Kuiper belt is unlikely to have a self-gravitational origin.

title: Study of top quark dipole interactions in $t\bar{t}$ production associated with two heavy gauge bosons at the LHC
Abstract: This paper examines the prospects of measuring the strong and weak dipole moments of the top quark at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Measuring these couplings provides a valuable opportunity to probe new physics interactions, as their magnitudes in the Standard Model are quite small. The analyses focus on studying the production cross sections of tν̄WW and tν̄ZZ processes in the same-sign dilepton and four-lepton final states, respectively. Sensitivities to strong and weak top quark dipole interactions at the 95% confidence level for various integrated luminosity scenarios are derived and compared with other studies. Besides using total cross sections, a novel handle based on an angular observable is introduced, showing sensitivity to variations in the top quark strong dipole moments. The paper also investigates the sensitivity of the invariant mass of the system to the strong and weak dipole moments of the top quark. |||

title: SenseNet: 3D Objects Database and Tactile Simulator
Abstract: The majority of artificial intelligence research focused on vision, particularly in the area of biological senses. This focus is partially due to the availability of high-quality datasets for image-based algorithms. However, we believe that concentrating on sensorimotor systems and tactile feedback would lead to algorithms that more closely resemble human intelligence. We present SenseNet, a collection of tactile simulators and a large-scale dataset of 3D objects for manipulation. This dataset was designed for training and researching artificial intelligences (AIs) to interact with their environment through sensorimotor neural systems and tactile feedback. SenseNet aims to replicate the advancements seen in image processing, but within the domain of tactile feedback and sensorimotor research. We hope that SenseNet will provide researchers in both machine learning and computational neuroscience with new opportunities and avenues for exploration.

title: How will the Internet of Things enable Augmented Personalized Health?
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is dramatically changing how we create, consume, and share information. Health enthusiasts and individuals increasingly use IoT technologies to track their sleep, food intake, activity, vital body signals, and other physiological observations. Complementing this trend are IoT systems continuously collecting health-related data from the environment and living spaces. These developments have paved the way for a new generation of healthcare solutions. However, interpreting data to understand an individual's health remains a challenge. This often necessitates considering their clinical history, behavioral information, and social and environmental factors affecting them. Interpreting a patient's progress requires examining their adherence to health objectives, applying relevant clinical knowledge, and assessing desired outcomes. We envision Augmented Personalized Healthcare (APH) to leverage the abundance of relevant data and medical knowledge using Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques. APH aims to enhance human health by offering various stages of augmented health management strategies, including self-monitoring, self-appraisal, self-management, intervention, disease progression tracking, and prediction. kHealth technology, a specific implementation of APH, and its application to Asthma and other diseases, serve as illustrations and discuss alternative technology-assisted health management approaches. The paper also identifies several prominent efforts involving IoT and patient-generated health data (PGHD) in converting multimodal data into actionable information (big data to smart data). The paper discusses the roles of contextualization, abstraction, and personalization in an evidence-based semantic perception approach.
label: AI

title: A General Framework for Adversarial Examples with Objectives
Abstract: Images subtly modified to be misclassified by neural networks, known as adversarial examples, pose a significant technical challenge and concern for various application domains. Most research on adversarial examples focuses solely on ensuring that perturbed images remain similar to the originals. However, real-world applications often require these examples to meet additional objectives, typically enforced through customized modifications of the perturbation process. This paper proposes adversarial generative nets (AGNs), a general methodology to train a generator neural network to generate adversarial examples that satisfy desired objectives. The paper demonstrates AGNs' ability to accommodate a wide range of objectives, including imprecise ones difficult to model, in two application domains. Specifically, it showcases physical adversarial examples—eyeglass frames designed to fool face recognition—with improved robustness, inconspicuousness, and scalability compared to previous approaches, along with a novel attack to deceive a handwritten-digit classifier.

title: Towards Building an Intelligent Anti-Malware System: A Deep Learning Approach using Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Malware Classification
Abstract: Effectively and efficiently mitigating malware is a long-standing endeavor in the information security community. Developing an anti-malware system capable of countering unknown malware is a prolific area of research that could benefit many sectors. We envision an intelligent anti-malware system that leverages the power of deep learning (DL) models. Such models could enable the detection of newly released malware through mathematical generalization. This involves identifying the relationship between a given malware (x) and its corresponding malware family (y), represented by the function f: x ↦ y. To achieve this, we utilized the Malimg dataset, comprising malware images processed from malware binaries. We then trained the following DL models to classify each malware family: CNN-SVM (Tang, 2013), GRU-SVM (Agarap, 2017), and MLP-SVM. Empirical evidence shows that the GRU-SVM model stands out among the DL models, achieving a predictive accuracy of approximately 84.92%. This result aligns with the model's relatively sophisticated architecture design. The exploration of an even more optimal DL-SVM model represents the next step towards engineering an intelligent anti-malware system.

title: Deep Stacked Networks with Residual Polishing for Image Inpainting
Abstract: Deep neural networks have demonstrated promising results in image inpainting, even when dealing with relatively large missing areas. However, most existing inpainting networks introduce undesirable artifacts and noise to the repaired regions. To address this issue, we introduce a novel framework consisting of two stacked convolutional neural networks that inpaint the image and remove artifacts, respectively. The first network considers the global structure of the damaged image and roughly fills the blank area. The second network then modifies the repaired image to eliminate the noise introduced by the first network. This proposed framework divides the problem into two distinct partitions that can be optimized independently, making it applicable to any inpainting algorithm by simply changing the first network. The second stage in our framework, aimed at refining the inpainted images, can be treated as a denoising problem, allowing for the use of various algorithms. Our results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves both visual and quantitative evaluations.

title: Interactive Video Object Segmentation in the Wild
Abstract: This paper presents our system for human-in-the-loop video object segmentation. The core of our system is a method for one-shot video object segmentation. While fast, this method requires an accurate pixel-level segmentation of one (or several) frames as input. As manually annotating such a segmentation is impractical, we propose a deep interactive image segmentation method that can accurately segment objects with only a few clicks. On the GrabCut dataset, our method achieves a 90% IOU with just 3.8 clicks on average, setting a new state-of-the-art. Furthermore, as our method iteratively refines an initial segmentation, it can effectively correct frames where the video object segmentation fails, enabling users to quickly obtain high-quality results even on challenging sequences. Finally, we investigate usage patterns and provide insights into the number of steps users take to annotate frames, the types of corrections they provide, etc., yielding valuable insights for further improving interactive video segmentation.

title: Context aware saliency map generation using semantic segmentation
Abstract: Saliency map detection, a method for identifying important regions within an image, finds applications in various tasks such as image classification and recognition. We propose that context detection plays a crucial role in image saliency detection. This requires extracting high-level features. In this paper, we propose a saliency map based on image context detection using semantic segmentation as a high-level feature. The saliency map derived from semantic information is fused with color and contrast-based saliency maps. The final saliency map is then generated. Simulation results for the Pascal-voc11 image dataset show a 99% accuracy in context detection. Additionally, the final saliency map produced by our proposed method exhibits satisfactory results in detecting salient points.

title: Transfer learning for diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on Ultrasound imaging data
Abstract: Classifying ultrasound (US) kidney images for diagnosing congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in children is a challenging task. Improving existing pattern classification models built upon conventional image features is desirable. This study proposes a transfer learning-based method to extract imaging features from US kidney images to enhance CAKUT diagnosis in children. Specifically, a pre-trained deep learning model (imagenet-caffe-alex) is employed for transfer learning-based feature extraction from 3-channel feature maps computed from US images, including original images, gradient features, and distance transform features. Support vector machine classifiers are then constructed based on various feature sets, including the transfer learning features, conventional imaging features, and their combination. Experimental results have demonstrated that combining transfer learning features with conventional imaging features yields the best classification performance for distinguishing CAKUT patients from normal controls based on their US kidney images.

title: Integrating semi-supervised label propagation and random forests for multi-atlas based hippocampus segmentation
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-atlas based image segmentation method by integrating a semi-supervised label propagation method and a supervised random forests method within a pattern recognition-based label fusion framework. The semi-supervised label propagation method considers local and global image appearances of images to be segmented and segments the images by propagating reliable segmentation results obtained from the supervised random forests method. Notably, the random forests method is used to train a regression model based on image patches of atlas images for each voxel of the images to be segmented. This regression model provides reliable segmentation results to guide the label propagation for segmentation. The proposed method has been compared with state-of-the-art multi-atlas based image segmentation methods for segmenting the hippocampus in MR images. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior segmentation performance.

title: A Unified Method for First and Third Person Action Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a new video classification methodology applicable to both first and third-person videos. The primary idea behind this strategy is to efficiently capture complementary information of appearance and motion by performing two independent streams on the videos. The first stream aims to capture long-term motions from shorter ones by tracking changes in optical flow images over time. These optical flow images are described by pre-trained networks trained on large-scale image datasets. A set of multi-channel time series is obtained by aligning these descriptions. For extracting motion features from these time series, the PoT representation method, combined with a novel pooling operator, is employed due to its various advantages. The second stream extracts appearance features, essential for video classification. The proposed method has been evaluated on both first and third-person datasets, and results indicate that the proposed methodology successfully achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Fractional Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern for Image Retrieval using Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: This paper presents a new texture descriptor named "Fractional Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern" (FLNIP) for content-based image retrieval (CBIR). It is an extension of the Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern (LNIP) [1]. FLNIP calculates the relative intensity difference between a particular pixel and the center pixel of a 3x3 window, taking into account the relationship with adjacent neighbors. In this work, the fractional change in the local neighborhood, involving adjacent neighbors, is first calculated with respect to one of the eight neighbors of the center pixel of a 3x3 window. Next, the fractional change is calculated with respect to the center itself. These two values of fractional change are then compared to generate a binary bit pattern. Both sign and magnitude information are encoded within a single descriptor, as it deals with the relative change in magnitude in the adjacent neighborhood, i.e., comparing the fractional change. This descriptor is applied to four multi-resolution images—one being the raw image and the other three being filtered Gaussian images obtained by applying Gaussian filters of different standard deviations to the raw image—to emphasize the importance of exploring texture information at different resolutions within an image. The four sets of distances obtained between the query and target images are then combined using a genetic algorithm-based approach to improve retrieval performance by minimizing the distance between similar class images. The method's performance for image retrieval was tested on four popular databases. The precision and recall values observed on these databases were compared with recent state-of-the-art local patterns. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvement over many existing methods.

title: A Real-time and Registration-free Framework for Dynamic Shape Instantiation
Abstract: Real-time 3D navigation during minimally invasive procedures is a crucial but challenging task, especially when dealing with substantial tissue motion. To balance image acquisition speed and resolution, only 2D images or low-resolution 3D volumes can be used clinically. This paper proposes a real-time, registration-free framework for dynamic shape instantiation, generalizable to multiple anatomical applications, to instantiate high-resolution 3D shapes of an organ from a single 2D image intra-operatively. First, an approximate optimal scan plane is determined by analyzing the pre-operative 3D statistical shape model (SSM) of the anatomy using sparse principal component analysis (SPCA) and considering practical constraints. Second, kernel partial least squares regression (KPLSR) is employed to learn the relationship between the pre-operative 3D SSM and a synchronized 2D SSM constructed from 2D images obtained at the approximate optimal scan plane. Finally, the derived relationship is applied to the new intra-operative 2D image obtained at the same scan plane to predict the high-resolution 3D shape intra-operatively. A key feature of the proposed framework is that no additional registration between the pre-operative 3D SSM and the synchronized 2D SSM is required. Detailed validation was performed on studies including the liver and right ventricle (RV) of the heart. The derived results (mean accuracy of 2.19mm on patients and computation speed of 1ms) demonstrate its potential clinical value for real-time, high-resolution, dynamic, and 3D interventional guidance.

title: A PDE-based log-agnostic illumination correction algorithm
Abstract: This report presents the results of a partial differential equation (PDE)-based image enhancement algorithm for dynamic range compression and illumination correction in the absence of the logarithmic function. The proposed algorithm combines forward and reverse flows within a PDE-based formulation. The experimental results are compared with algorithms from the literature and indicate comparable performance in most cases.

title: Towards automated patient data cleaning using deep learning: A feasibility study on the standardization of organ labeling
Abstract: Data cleaning consumes about 80% of the time spent on data analysis for clinical research projects. This is a more significant problem in the era of big data and machine learning in medicine, where vast volumes of data are being generated. We report an initial effort towards automated patient data cleaning using deep learning: the standardization of organ labeling in radiation therapy. Organs are often labeled inconsistently across different institutions (sometimes even within the same institution) and at different time periods, posing a problem for clinical research, especially for multi-institutional collaborative clinical research, where acquired patient data is not used effectively. We developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically identify each organ in the CT image and then label it with the standardized nomenclature presented at AAPM Task Group 263. We tested this model on CT images of 54 patients with prostate cancer and 100 patients with head and neck cancer who previously received radiation therapy. The model achieved 100% accuracy in detecting organs and assigning standardized labels for the patients tested. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for patient data cleaning, enabling the generation of standardized datasets for effective intra- and interinstitutional collaborative clinical research.

title: Face Synthesis from Visual Attributes via Sketch using Conditional VAEs and GANs
Abstract: Automatic face synthesis from visual attributes is a crucial problem in computer vision, finding wide applications in law enforcement and entertainment. With the advent of deep generative convolutional neural networks (CNNs), attempts have been made to synthesize face images from attributes and text descriptions. This paper takes a different approach, formulating the original problem as a stage-wise learning problem. We first synthesize the facial sketch corresponding to the visual attributes, followed by reconstructing the face image based on the synthesized sketch. The proposed Attribute2Sketch2Face framework, based on a combination of deep Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), consists of three stages: (1) Synthesis of a facial sketch from attributes using a CVAE architecture, (2) Enhancement of coarse sketches to produce sharper sketches using a GAN-based framework, and (3) Synthesis of a face from the sketch using another GAN-based network. Extensive experiments and comparison with recent methods are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed attribute-based three-stage face synthesis method.

title: Deformable GANs for Pose-based Human Image Generation
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of generating person images conditioned on a given pose. Specifically, given an image of a person and a target pose, we synthesize a new image of that person in the novel pose. To handle pixel-to-pixel misalignments caused by pose differences, we introduce deformable skip connections in the generator of our Generative Adversarial Network. Furthermore, a nearest-neighbor loss is proposed instead of the common L1 and L2 losses to match the details of the generated image with the target image. We test our approach using photos of people in different poses and compare our method with previous work in this area, showcasing state-of-the-art results in two benchmarks. Our method can be applied to the broader field of deformable object generation, provided that the pose of the articulated object can be extracted using a keypoint detector.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Unsupervised Video Summarization with Diversity-Representativeness Reward
Abstract: Video summarization aims to facilitate large-scale video browsing by producing short, concise summaries that are diverse and representative of the original videos. This paper formulates video summarization as a sequential decision-making process and develops a deep summarization network (DSN) to summarize videos. DSN predicts a probability for each video frame, indicating how likely a frame is to be selected, and then takes actions based on these probability distributions to select frames, forming video summaries. To train our DSN, we propose an end-to-end, reinforcement learning-based framework, where we design a novel reward function that jointly considers diversity and representativeness of generated summaries and does not rely on labels or user interactions at all. During training, the reward function judges the diversity and representativeness of the generated summaries, while DSN strives to earn higher rewards by learning to produce more diverse and more representative summaries. Since labels are not required, our method is fully unsupervised. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets show that our unsupervised method not only outperforms other state-of-the-art unsupervised methods but also is comparable to or even superior than most published supervised approaches.

title: Deep Learning Interior Tomography for Region-of-Interest Reconstruction
Abstract: Interior tomography for region-of-interest (ROI) imaging offers advantages such as using a small detector and reducing X-ray radiation dose. However, standard analytic reconstruction suffers from severe cupping artifacts due to the presence of null space in the truncated Radon transform. Existing penalized reconstruction methods may address this problem, but they require extensive computations due to iterative reconstruction. Inspired by recent deep learning approaches to low-dose and sparse view CT, we propose a deep learning architecture that removes null space signals from the FBP reconstruction. Experimental results have shown that the proposed method provides near-perfect reconstruction with about 7-10 dB improvement in PSNR over existing methods despite significantly reduced run-time complexity.

title: ScanComplete: Large-Scale Scene Completion and Semantic Segmentation for 3D Scans
Abstract: We introduce ScanComplete, a novel data-driven approach that takes an incomplete 3D scan of a scene as input and predicts a complete 3D model along with per-voxel semantic labels. Our method's key contribution is its ability to handle large scenes with varying spatial extent, managing the cubic growth in data size as scene size increases. To this end, we devise a fully-convolutional generative 3D CNN model whose filter kernels are invariant to the overall scene size. The model can be trained on scene subvolumes but deployed on arbitrarily large scenes at test time. Additionally, we propose a coarse-to-fine inference strategy to produce high-resolution output while leveraging large input context sizes. In an extensive series of experiments, we carefully evaluate different model design choices, considering both deterministic and probabilistic models for completion and semantic inference. Our results show that we outperform other methods not only in the size of the environments handled and processing efficiency, but also with regard to completion quality and semantic segmentation performance by a significant margin.

title: Learning Deep Similarity Models with Focus Ranking for Fabric Image Retrieval
Abstract: Fabric image retrieval is beneficial for many applications, including clothing searching, online shopping, and cloth modeling. Learning pairwise image similarity is crucial for an image retrieval task. With the resurgence of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), recent works have achieved significant progress through deep representation learning with metric embedding, which brings similar examples closer together in a feature space and dissimilar ones further apart. This paper proposes a novel embedding method termed focus ranking that can be easily integrated into a CNN for jointly learning image representations and metrics in the context of fine-grained fabric image retrieval. Focus ranking aims to rank similar examples higher than all dissimilar ones by penalizing ranking disorders through minimizing the overall cost attributed to similar samples being ranked below dissimilar ones. During the training stage, training samples are organized into focus ranking units for efficient optimization. We construct a large-scale fabric image retrieval dataset (FIRD) with about 25,000 images of 4,300 fabrics and test the proposed model on the FIRD dataset. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model over existing metric embedding models. |||

title: Dense Pooling layers in Fully Convolutional Network for Skin Lesion Segmentation
Abstract: A new class of fully convolutional network with dense pooling layers is proposed for segmenting skin lesion regions in images. The network achieves highly accurate segmentation, surpassing existing algorithms in the field of skin lesion segmentation.

title: A Resilient Image Matching Method with an Affine Invariant Feature Detector and Descriptor
Abstract: Image feature matching is crucial for tasks like 3D object reconstruction and navigation. Existing methods struggle with large viewpoint changes. This paper introduces a novel algorithm that combines an Affine Invariant Feature Detector (AIFD) with a new Affine Invariant Feature Descriptor (AIFDd) to achieve robustness to viewpoint changes. Extensive experiments demonstrate the algorithm's superiority over other state-of-the-art methods in handling viewpoint variations, illumination changes, rotations, and compression.

title: Polyp detection inside the capsule endoscopy: an approach for power consumption reduction
Abstract: Capsule endoscopy, a non-invasive method for diagnosing digestive track issues, faces challenges due to limited battery life. This paper presents a system that detects informative frames within the capsule and transmits only those, reducing data transmission and power consumption. The system utilizes a hardware-friendly polyp detection algorithm based on positive contrast and customized edges, eliminating complex iterative structures for power efficiency. Experimental results show promising polyp detection rates.

title: Estimation under group actions: recovering orbits from invariants
Abstract: This study investigates orbit recovery problems where noisy observations of an unknown element in a multi-dimensional space are acted upon by random elements of a group. Matching upper and lower bounds on the sample size required for accurate orbit recovery are derived based on invariant theory. The findings reveal a connection between the estimation problem's statistical difficulty and the group's algebraic properties. The model is motivated by geometric problems in signal processing, computer vision, and structural biology, and has applications in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). The results demonstrate that the number of cryo-EM images needed to recover the molecule structure scales with the noise variance. A novel algorithm for ab initio reconstruction in cryo-EM, based on invariant features, is presented. The paper also discusses how to recover multiple molecular structures from mixed cryo-EM samples.

title: Exploring the significance of using perceptually relevant image decolorization method for scene classification
Abstract: This paper explores the significance of chrominance information in scene classification. An improved color-to-grayscale image conversion algorithm is proposed that effectively incorporates chrominance information using the Color-to-Gray Structure Similarity Index (C2G-SSIM) and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's superiority over existing methods in terms of perceptual quality and classification accuracy. The effectiveness of incorporating chrominance information in scene classification is further validated using a deep belief network (DBN) based image classification system.

title: Significance of Softmax-based Features in Comparison to Distance Metric Learning-based Features
Abstract: Deep features extracted from classification networks are valuable for many computer vision tasks. This paper compares the performance of features extracted from a distance metric learning (DML) based network and those from a softmax-based network. The results show that softmax-based features are competitive, or even better, than DML features, especially when the dataset size is large. These findings highlight the importance of considering softmax-based features when evaluating deep features.

title: Learning Deep and Compact Models for Gesture Recognition
Abstract: This paper presents a compact and accurate model for gesture recognition from videos using a joint 3DCNN-LSTM framework. The model achieves near state-of-the-art accuracy on the ChaLearn dataset with half the model size. The paper further explores knowledge distillation and model compression techniques to achieve a significantly more compact model that is suitable for real-time gesture recognition on mobile devices.

title: Discriminative and Geometry Aware Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
Abstract: Domain adaptation (DA) aims to generalize a learning model across training and testing data with different distributions. This paper argues that an effective DA method should align data distributions while maintaining discriminative features and account for the data manifold's geometric structure. Three different DA models, CDDA, GA-DA, and DGA-DA, are derived to demonstrate the contributions of close yet discriminative DA, geometry aware DA, and discriminative and geometry aware DA. Experimental results on both synthetic and real data show that the proposed approach consistently outperforms existing DA methods across multiple image classification benchmarks. The paper provides insights into the proposed DA methods through visualization and analysis.

title: Gradient Regularization Improves Accuracy of Discriminative Models
Abstract: Gradient regularization, a technique for regularizing the gradient norm of a neural network's output with respect to its inputs, is shown to consistently improve classification accuracy on vision tasks, especially with limited training data. This paper introduces Jacobian-based regularizers and demonstrates empirically that gradient regularization leads to controlled gradients and improved generalization.

title: Rapid Adaptation with Conditionally Shifted Neurons
Abstract: This paper introduces conditionally shifted neurons, a mechanism that enables artificial neural networks to learn rapid adaptation. This mechanism is implemented within a metalearning framework, where the aim is to replicate human-like learning flexibility. Conditionally shifted neurons modify their activation values using task-specific shifts retrieved from a memory module, which is populated quickly based on limited task experience. The paper demonstrates state-of-the-art results on metalearning benchmarks from the vision and language domains.

title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
Abstract: This paper explores the structure of neural loss functions and their effect on generalization using visualization techniques. A new "filter normalization" method is introduced to visualize loss function curvature. The paper examines how network architecture and training parameters affect the loss landscape and the shape of minimizers.

title: Improved Inception-Residual Convolutional Neural Network for Object Recognition
Abstract: This paper presents a new Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) model called the Inception Recurrent Residual Convolutional Neural Network (IRRCNN). This model leverages the strengths of Recurrent Convolutional Neural Networks (RCNNs), Inception networks, and Residual networks. The IRRCNN architecture significantly improves recognition accuracy compared to existing models, including the Inception-residual network. The model's performance is evaluated on various benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet-200, and CU3D-100. Experimental results demonstrate the IRRCNN's superiority over popular DCNN models, particularly the RCNN. The paper also explores the IRRCNN's performance against its counterparts, the Equivalent Inception Network (EIN) and the Equivalent Inception Residual Network (EIRN), on the CIFAR-100 dataset, achieving substantial improvements in classification accuracy.

title: Handwritten Bangla Character Recognition Using The State-of-Art Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Handwritten Bangla Character Recognition (HBCR) remains a challenging task due to ambiguous characters and cursive handwriting. This paper explores the application of state-of-the-art Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs), including VGG Network, All Convolution Network, Network in Network, Residual Network, FractalNet, and DenseNet, for HBCR. The deep learning approaches excel in extracting feature information, improving recognition accuracy for 2D shapes. The paper systematically evaluates the performance of these DCNN models on a publicly available Bangla handwritten character dataset (CMATERdb), achieving superior recognition accuracy compared to existing methods.

title: Future Frame Prediction for Anomaly Detection -- A New Baseline
Abstract: Existing anomaly detection methods in videos typically focus on minimizing reconstruction errors of training data, which may not guarantee larger errors for abnormal events. This paper proposes a novel anomaly detection framework based on video prediction. The method leverages the difference between a predicted future frame and its ground truth to identify abnormal events. To enhance the quality of future frame predictions for normal events, the paper introduces a motion constraint, along with appearance constraints, to ensure consistent optical flow between predicted frames and ground truth frames. This spatial and motion constraint facilitates anomaly detection by identifying events that deviate from the expected prediction. Experimental results on both a toy dataset and publicly available datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: A Multi-Scale and Multi-Depth Convolutional Neural Network for Remote Sensing Imagery Pan-Sharpening
Abstract: Pan-sharpening is a fundamental task in remote sensing image processing where high-resolution spatial details from panchromatic images are used to enhance the spatial resolution of multi-spectral (MS) images. This paper proposes a multi-scale and multi-depth convolutional neural network (MSDCNN) architecture that incorporates multi-scale feature extraction and residual learning for pan-sharpening. The MSDCNN achieves superior results in both quantitative and visual assessments compared to state-of-the-art methods, generating high-resolution MS images.

title: Siamese LSTM based Fiber Structural Similarity Network (FS2Net) for Rotation Invariant Brain Tractography Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture for segmenting brain fibers, obtained from tractography data, into anatomically meaningful clusters. The architecture combines stacked bidirectional LSTMs and LSTMs with the Siamese network architecture. The network learns structural differences between fibers of different classes, enabling high-accuracy fiber classification. By capturing inter and intra-class structural relationships, the segmentation is robust to relative rotations between test and training data. Extensive experimentation on a large dataset shows state-of-the-art results, even in cases of significant rotations.

title: Efficient Parallel Connected Components Labeling with a Coarse-to-fine Strategy
Abstract: This paper presents a parallel approach to solve connected components on 2D binary images using CUDA. The method accelerates neighborhood exploration by dividing the input image into independent blocks. A coarse-labeling algorithm with row-column connection and label-equivalence list unification is used for initial local labeling. A refinement algorithm merges separated sub-regions from a single component. The block merge stage scans boundary pixels for connectivity instead of processing all pixels. This reduces the length of label-equivalence lists and memory access, improving efficiency. Experimental results show significant performance improvements over other approaches.

title: Sky detection and log illumination refinement for PDE-based hazy image contrast enhancement
Abstract: This report presents a sky detection technique to enhance the performance of a PDE-based hazy image enhancement algorithm. The report also proposes an alternative method that utilizes a function for log illumination refinement to improve de-hazing results while avoiding over-enhancement. The algorithms were tested on benchmark and calibration images and compared with existing methods. Results demonstrate consistent performance and improved color, contrast, and edge visibility compared to other algorithms.

title: Extrapolating Expected Accuracies for Large Multi-Class Problems
Abstract: This paper explores the scalability of multi-class classification with an increasing number of classes. It proposes a method to predict the performance of a classifier on a larger number of classes based on its performance on a subset of classes. The method assumes that classes are sampled identically and independently from a population and that the classifier uses independently learned scoring functions. The expected accuracy when the classifier is trained on k classes is shown to be the (k-1)st moment of a specific distribution that can be estimated from data. The paper presents an unbiased estimation method based on this theory and demonstrates its application in facial recognition.

title: Report: Dynamic Eye Movement Matching and Visualization Tool in Neuro Gesture
Abstract: This research investigates the impact of lecturer gestures on audience attention using eye movement and Electroencephalography (EEG) data. It applies a Time Warp Edit Distance method to measure the similarity of eye movement trajectories, assuming that attentive audiences would look at the same place. Eye movement patterns are clustered based on the similarity metrics. Since a direct metric for "attention" is not available, a visualization tool is used to evaluate the gesture-attention relationship.

title: Learning More Universal Representations for Transfer-Learning
Abstract: A universal representation in computer vision aims to encode all elements of the visual world, regardless of their configuration. While achieving pure universality is difficult, current research focuses on enhancing the universality level of existing representations. This is typically achieved by training Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on diverse datasets, such as ImageNet with additional annotations. However, this approach requires substantial annotated data, which can be a bottleneck. This paper proposes two methods to improve universality while minimizing the need for annotated data. It also introduces a unified framework for these methods based on diversifying the training problem. To align with Atkinson's cognitive study of universal human representations, the paper leverages transfer learning and a new metric to evaluate universality. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is demonstrated on ten target problems, including classification tasks across various visual domains.

title: Geometry Processing of Conventionally Produced Mouse Brain Slice Images
Abstract: Brain mapping research often relies on conventional processing techniques that introduce artifacts, such as tissue tears and loss, during histological preparation. This paper presents a novel method for automatic registration and 3D reconstruction of mouse brain slices in a standardized atlas space. By constructing a virtual 3D mouse brain model from annotated slices of the Allen Reference Atlas (ARA) and re-slicing it to match microscopic images of histological sections, the method aligns the two using geometric contours. Histological artifacts are removed through Constrained Delaunay Triangulation before performing global alignment. Finally, non-linear registration is achieved by solving Laplace's equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. This approach significantly improves upon existing registration techniques, especially for slices with considerable artifacts. As an application, the paper demonstrates counting neurons in different anatomical regions using a dataset of 51 microscopic slices from a single mouse brain. This research contributes significantly to neuroscience by providing tools for analyzing and processing histological data.

title: Eventness: Object Detection on Spectrograms for Temporal Localization of Audio Events
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "Eventness" for audio event detection, analogous to "Objectness" in computer vision. Eventness recognizes that audio events manifest as two-dimensional time-frequency patterns in spectrograms, characterized by unique textures and geometric structures. These patterns are comparable to objects in natural images, although they lack scaling and rotation invariance. This observation allows for framing the detection of monophonic or polyphonic audio events as a visual object detection problem in spectrograms, where partial occlusion and clutter are present. The paper adapts a state-of-the-art visual object detection model to evaluate audio event detection on publicly available datasets. The proposed network achieves comparable results to a baseline and exhibits greater robustness with minority events. The authors anticipate that their concept of Eventness, given large-scale datasets, will contribute significantly to improving audio event detection performance in the audio signal processing community.

title: Adversarial Patch
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for creating universal, robust, and targeted adversarial image patches that can be applied in real-world settings. These patches are universal as they can attack any scene, robust under various transformations, and targeted in that they can manipulate a classifier to output any desired target class. The adversarial patches can be printed, physically added to any scene, photographed, and presented to image classifiers. Even when small, these patches can effectively mislead classifiers, causing them to disregard other elements in the scene and report the chosen target class. The code to reproduce the paper's findings is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Memory-Efficient Deep Salient Object Segmentation Networks on Gridized Superpixels
Abstract: Deep learning has significantly improved the accuracy of computer vision algorithms for pixel-wise labeling tasks, such as semantic segmentation and salient object detection. However, these deep segmentation methods often rely on pre-trained networks with millions of parameters, leading to memory-intensive models. This paper questions the necessity of such resource-demanding networks for salient object segmentation and proposes a memory-efficient network learned from scratch solely on salient object detection datasets. The method encodes images into gridized superpixels, preserving both object boundaries and pixel connectivity rules. This representation enables the use of convolutional neural networks operating on regular grids. By training a memory-efficient network using these encoded images, the authors achieve comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art deep salient object detection methods, but with significantly less memory and faster processing. This makes their approach preferable for applications on memory-constrained devices like mobile phones and IoT devices.

title: Consensus-based Sequence Training for Video Captioning
Abstract: Captioning models are typically trained using cross-entropy loss, but their performance is evaluated using metrics that correlate better with human assessments. While reinforcement learning (RL) can directly optimize these metrics for tasks like captioning, it is computationally expensive and requires specifying a baseline reward at each step. This paper proposes a fast approach to optimize objectives of interest using the REINFORCE algorithm. It demonstrates that RL training can be viewed as a weighted cross-entropy loss by replacing model samples with ground-truth sentences, leading to a fast pre-training algorithm. The paper also suggests using the consensus among ground-truth captions of the same video as the baseline reward, which can be computed efficiently. This combined proposal, called Consensus-based Sequence Training (CST), trains significantly faster than comparable methods and achieves a new state-of-the-art on the MSRVTT video captioning benchmark, improving the CIDEr score from 47.3 to 54.2.

title: Multi-Target, Multi-Camera Tracking by Hierarchical Clustering: Recent Progress on DukeMTMC Project
Abstract: While single-camera tracking has seen significant progress, multi-camera tracking remains challenging. The DukeMTMC dataset, a large-scale multi-camera tracking benchmark, has greatly advanced research in this area. This report briefly introduces a method for the DukeMTMC dataset that employs simple hierarchical clustering combined with well-trained person re-identification features. The results demonstrate that this approach can achieve promising performance on the dataset.
