title: Exploring the Space of Black-box Attacks on Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Black-box attacks on deep neural networks (DNNs) have primarily focused on transferability, where adversarial examples generated for one model can attack others. This paper proposes novel Gradient Estimation black-box attacks that leverage query access to the target model's class probabilities without relying on transferability. The paper further presents strategies to decouple the number of queries needed to generate adversarial samples from the input dimensionality. An iterative variant of the proposed attack achieves close to 100% adversarial success rates for both targeted and untargeted attacks on DNNs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Gradient Estimation attacks outperform transferability-based black-box attacks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, achieving adversarial success rates comparable to white-box attacks. The Gradient Estimation attacks are also successfully applied to a real-world Content Moderation classifier hosted by Clarifai. Furthermore, the paper evaluates these attacks against state-of-the-art defenses, highlighting their effectiveness even against robust defenses.

title: Multi-modal Geolocation Estimation Using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Estimating the location where an image was taken solely based on its contents is a challenging task, even for humans. This is because accurate geolocation relies heavily on contextual information, making it more complex than simply identifying single objects. This paper contributes to image geolocation inferencing research by introducing a novel global meshing strategy using Delaunay triangles, which are shown to be effective in low-volume scenarios compared to state-of-the-art models using quad trees and significantly more training data. The paper also outlines training procedures to overcome data limitations and demonstrates how incorporating additional information, such as time of posting, learned user albuming, and other meta data, can improve geolocation accuracy by up to 11% for country-level locality (750 km) and 3% for city-level locality (25 km).

title: Robust Minutiae Extractor: Integrating Deep Networks and Fingerprint Domain Knowledge
Abstract: This paper introduces MinutiaeNet, a fully automatic minutiae extractor based on deep neural networks with compact feature representation for fast comparison of minutiae sets. The method utilizes two networks: CoarseNet and FineNet. CoarseNet estimates the minutiae score map and orientation using a convolutional neural network and fingerprint domain knowledge, such as enhanced image, orientation field, and segmentation map. FineNet then refines candidate minutiae locations based on the score map. Experimental results on both latent (NIST SD27) and plain (FVC 2004) fingerprint datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of combining fingerprint domain knowledge with deep networks. MinutiaeNet achieves better precision and recall compared to state-of-the-art methods on these datasets. The lack of annotated fingerprint datasets with minutiae ground truth makes this approach valuable for training fingerprint matching algorithms and evaluating fingerprint individuality at scale. The code for MinutiaeNet is available on GitHub.

title: RaspiReader: Open Source Fingerprint Reader
Abstract: This paper introduces RaspiReader, an open-source, easy-to-assemble, spoof-resistant, high-resolution optical fingerprint reader using readily available components. RaspiReader can be built in under an hour for US $175, providing the fingerprint research community with a simple platform for prototyping new ideas involving fingerprint reader hardware. The open-source design encourages the exploration of novel fingerprint spoof detection techniques using both hardware and software. The authors demonstrate one such technique by customizing RaspiReader with two cameras for fingerprint image acquisition. One camera captures high-contrast frustrated total internal reflection (FTIR) fingerprint images, while the other provides direct images of the finger on the platen. Combining information from both image streams enhances spoof detection performance compared to methods relying solely on grayscale FTIR images from commercial optical readers. Fingerprint matching experiments between RaspiReader's FTIR output and images from commercial readers validate RaspiReader's interoperability with existing systems.

title: HACS: Human Action Clips and Segments Dataset for Recognition and Temporal Localization
Abstract: This paper presents HACS (Human Action Clips and Segments), a new large-scale dataset for recognition and temporal localization of human actions collected from web videos. The dataset leverages both consensus and disagreement among visual classifiers to automatically mine candidate short clips from unlabeled videos, which are subsequently validated by human annotators. This results in HACS Clips, a dataset containing 1.5M annotated clips sampled from 504K untrimmed videos. Through a separate process, the authors collect annotations defining action segment boundaries, creating HACS Segments, which includes 139K action segments densely annotated in 50K untrimmed videos across 200 action categories. HACS Clips surpasses existing video benchmarks in the number of labeled examples, making it suitable for large-scale action recognition and spatiotemporal feature learning. Transfer learning experiments on three target datasets show that HACS Clips outperforms Kinetics-600, Moments-In-Time, and Sports1M as a pre-training source. The paper also evaluates state-of-the-art action proposal generation and localization methods on HACS Segments, highlighting the challenges posed by its dense temporal annotations.

title: Zero-Shot Learning via Latent Space Encoding
Abstract: Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) typically relies on a class semantic embedding space to transfer knowledge from seen classes to unseen ones. Successful ZSL hinges on capturing the common semantic characteristics between the visual modality and class semantic modality, such as attributes or word vectors. This paper proposes Latent Space Encoding (LSE), a novel encoder-decoder approach, to connect semantic relations across different modalities. Instead of using projection functions to transfer information, LSE performs interactions through a feature-aware latent space learned implicitly. Different modalities are modeled separately but optimized jointly, with each employing an encoder-decoder framework to learn the latent space. Features referring to the same concept across modalities are enforced to share the same latent codings, generalizing common semantic characteristics with latent representations. The approach is easily extensible to multiple modalities. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets (AwA, CUB, aPY, and ImageNet) demonstrate the superiority of LSE for various ZSL tasks, including traditional ZSL, generalized ZSL, and zero-shot retrieval (ZSR).

title: A model for interpreting social interactions in local image regions
Abstract: Understanding social interactions, such as "hug" or "fight," is a fundamental capability of the human visual system but remains a challenging problem for computer modeling. This paper investigates the visual recognition of social interactions using small but recognizable local regions called "minimal images." The approach relies on two key components: (i) social interactions can be reliably recognized from minimal images, and (ii) recognition involves identifying components and relations within the minimal image, termed "interpretation." The paper presents psychophysics data for minimal images and modeling results for their interpretation. It discusses the integration of minimal configurations in recognizing social interactions within detailed, high-resolution images.

title: Large-Scale 3D Scene Classification With Multi-View Volumetric CNN
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for image classification using a convolutional neural network (CNN) on multi-view image projections. The approach leverages projections of multiple images at multiple depth planes near the reconstructed surface, allowing for the classification of categories whose salient aspect is appearance change under different viewpoints, such as water, trees, and other materials with complex reflection/light response properties. The method does not require boundary labeling in images and works on pixel-level classification with a small context, simplifying training set creation. The paper demonstrates the application on large-scale aerial imagery collections, extending per-pixel classification to create a consistent 2D classification that can fill gaps in non-reconstructible water regions. The method is also applied to classify tree regions. In both cases, training data can be quickly generated using manually created polygons on a map. The CNN, even with a simple network, outperforms state-of-the-art image classification methods, including the Inception-V3 model retrained from a large collection of aerial images.

title: Aircraft Fuselage Defect Detection using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: To ensure the flight safety of aircraft structures, regular maintenance using visual and nondestructive inspection (NDI) methods is crucial. This paper proposes an automatic image-based aircraft defect detection system using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art feature descriptors, concluding that vgg-f DNN as a feature extractor with a linear SVM classifier achieves the best performance. To reduce processing time, the authors propose applying the SURF key point detector to identify defect patch candidates. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of over 96% at around 15 seconds processing time for a high-resolution (20-megapixel) image on a laptop.

title: The Robust Manifold Defense: Adversarial Training using Generative Models
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel attack for finding adversarial examples for image classifiers, exploiting spanners, which are deep neural networks with low-dimensional input spaces and output ranges approximating the set of images of interest. Spanners can be generators of GANs or decoders of VAEs. The attack searches over latent code pairs to find those generating nearby images with different classifier outputs. The authors argue that this approach is stronger than searching over perturbations of real images and demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the accuracy of Defense-GAN to 3%, resolving an open problem from the paper by Athalye et al. Combining this attack with adversarial training yields the most robust known MNIST classifier, significantly improving the state-of-the-art against PGD attacks. The formulation involves solving a min-max problem, where the classifier parameters are optimized by the min player, while the max player runs the attack, searching for adversarial examples in the low-dimensional input space of the spanner. All code and models are available on GitHub.
label: AI

title: Detect-and-Track: Efficient Pose Estimation in Videos
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating and tracking human body keypoints in complex, multi-person video. The proposed approach is lightweight but highly effective, building upon recent advancements in human detection and video understanding. The method operates in two stages: keypoint estimation in frames or short clips, followed by lightweight tracking to generate keypoint predictions linked across the entire video. For frame-level pose estimation, the paper experiments with Mask R-CNN and its proposed 3D extension, which leverages temporal information from small clips to generate more robust frame predictions. Extensive ablative experiments on the PoseTrack benchmark validate the model's design choices. The approach achieves an accuracy of 55.2% on the validation set and 51.8% on the test set using the Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) metric, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the ICCV 2017 PoseTrack keypoint tracking challenge.
label: AI

title: Segmenting Sky Pixels in Images
Abstract: Outdoor scene parsing models often struggle in real-world scenarios due to training on ideal datasets. This discrepancy is particularly noticeable in night-time images, those with varying weather conditions, and scene changes caused by seasonal weather, leading to decreased accuracy in sky classification. This project addresses these challenges by using a state-of-the-art model, RefineNet, with a non-ideal dataset: SkyFinder and a subset from SUN database with Sky objects. The focus is on sky segmentation, the task of differentiating sky from non-sky pixels. The efforts resulted in a 10-15% improvement in average MCR compared to prior methods on the SkyFinder dataset and a nearly 35% improvement in average mIOU compared to an off-the-shelf model. The paper analyzes the trained models based on time of day and weather, demonstrating significant performance advantages over prior methods, despite facing similar challenges.
label: AI

title: Deep Meta Learning for Real-Time Target-Aware Visual Tracking
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel on-line visual tracking framework based on Siamese matching network and meta-learner network, capable of real-time performance. Conventional deep convolutional feature-based discriminative visual tracking algorithms require continuous classifier or correlation filter retraining, involving complex optimization tasks to adapt to changing target object appearances. The proposed algorithm mitigates this complexity by incorporating a meta-learner network, which provides the matching network with new appearance information through target-aware feature space. The parameters for this target-specific feature space are generated instantly through a single forward pass of the meta-learner network. By eliminating the need for continuous optimization, experimental results demonstrate real-time performance while maintaining competitive performance among other state-of-the-art tracking algorithms.
label: AI

title: Brain Tumor Segmentation Based on Refined Fully Convolutional Neural Networks with A Hierarchical Dice Loss
Abstract: Semantic segmentation, a fundamental task in computer vision, provides crucial information for object detection and instance segmentation, enabling artificial intelligence to better understand the real world. Fully convolutional neural networks (FCNNs), renowned for their high accuracy in pixel-wise classification and localization, are widely employed in semantic segmentation. This paper investigates the application of several prominent FCNNs to brain tumor segmentation, comparing their performance and adjusting network architectures for enhanced accuracy, as measured by metrics such as precision, recall, mean of intersection of union (mIoU), and dice score coefficient (DSC). The refinements made to classic FCNNs include the addition of more connections between convolutional layers, expansion of decoders following up-sampling layers, and modification of shallower layer information reuse. In addition to structural modifications, a novel classifier incorporating a hierarchical dice loss is introduced. Inspired by the containment relationship between classes, the loss function transforms multiple classifications into multiple binary classifications to counteract the negative effects of imbalanced datasets. Extensive experiments conducted on both training and testing sets evaluate the refined FCNNs and the new loss function, demonstrating their superior effectiveness over their predecessors.
label: AI

title: Deep Blind Image Inpainting
Abstract: Blind image inpainting, the task of filling in missing information in corrupted image regions, presents a significant challenge. Existing inpainting algorithms typically assume knowledge of the corrupted region locations. Unlike these methods, this paper proposes an efficient blind image inpainting algorithm that directly restores a clear image from a corrupted input. The algorithm draws inspiration from residual learning, aiming to learn the missing information in corrupted regions. However, the direct application of existing residual learning algorithms in image restoration proves ineffective due to the limited information available in corrupted regions. To address this, an encoder-decoder architecture is introduced to capture more useful information, and a robust loss function is developed to handle outliers. The algorithm can predict the missing information in corrupted regions, facilitating clear image restoration. Qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate the algorithm's ability to handle corrupted regions of arbitrary shapes and outperform state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Translation of "Zur Ermittlung eines Objektes aus zwei Perspektiven mit innerer Orientierung" by Erwin Kruppa (1913)
Abstract: Erwin Kruppa's 1913 paper, "Zur Ermittlung eines Objektes aus zwei Perspektiven mit innerer Orientierung", a seminal work in computer vision, presents the first five-point algorithm for relative pose estimation. Kruppa demonstrated that the relative pose between two calibrated images of a rigid object can be computed from five point matches between the images. His work also contributed significantly to the field of camera self-calibration, as outlined in Maybank and Faugeras's 1992 publication. The paper, still highly relevant today, has received over a hundred citations in the last decade, but is not readily available online. To address this, the authors have procured a copy from the German National Library in Frankfurt and provide an English translation alongside the German original. Modern terminology is adapted, and clarifications are provided (highlighted in sans-serif font). For a historical review of geometric computer vision, the reader is referred to Sturm's 2011 survey paper.
label: AI

title: Automatic Image Cropping for Visual Aesthetic Enhancement Using Deep Neural Networks and Cascaded Regression
Abstract: Despite recent advancements, computational visual aesthetics remains a challenging field. Image cropping, the removal of unwanted scene areas, plays a crucial role in enhancing the aesthetic quality of images. However, evaluating the aesthetic appeal of cropped images is subjective and challenging. This paper introduces a novel cascaded cropping regression (CCR) method to perform image cropping by learning from the expertise of professional photographers. The proposed CCR method improves the convergence speed of the cascaded method, which directly uses random-ferns regressors. Additionally, a two-step learning strategy is employed in the CCR method to address the scarcity of labeled cropping data. This involves training a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier on large-scale visual aesthetic datasets and utilizing the trained model to extract features from various image cropping datasets, allowing the CCR method to predict cropping bounding boxes. Experiments conducted on public image cropping datasets demonstrate the method's superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art image cropping methods.
label: AI

title: Domain Adaptation Meets Disentangled Representation Learning and Style Transfer
Abstract: Numerous methods have been proposed to address the domain adaptation problem. However, their success relies on the assumption that information across domains is fully transferable. If this assumption is not met, negative transfer can hinder domain adaptation performance. This paper introduces a new learning network that tackles three tasks simultaneously: domain adaptation, disentangled representation, and style transfer. The learned features are disentangled into common and specific parts. Common parts represent transferable features, suitable for domain adaptation with minimal negative transfer. Conversely, specific parts characterize the unique style of each domain. This allows for the introduction of feature exchange across domains, which not only enhances the transferability of common features but also enables image style transfer. These design features enable the introduction of five training objectives to address the three challenging tasks concurrently. Experimental results demonstrate the architecture's adaptability to both full and partial transfer learning based on a well-learned disentangled representation. Additionally, the trained network exhibits high potential for generating style-transferred images.
label: AI

title: Stratified Transfer Learning for Cross-domain Activity Recognition
Abstract: Activity recognition often faces challenges in acquiring sufficient activity labels, as this process is expensive and time-consuming. Transfer learning addresses this issue by leveraging labeled samples from the source domain to annotate the target domain, which has limited or no labels. Existing approaches primarily focus on learning a global domain shift while neglecting the intra-affinity between classes, hindering algorithm performance. This paper proposes a novel and general cross-domain learning framework that leverages the intra-affinity of classes to facilitate intra-class knowledge transfer. This framework, termed Stratified Transfer Learning (STL), significantly improves classification accuracy for cross-domain activity recognition. STL initially obtains pseudo labels for the target domain using the majority voting technique. Subsequently, it iteratively performs intra-class knowledge transfer to transform both domains into the same subspaces. Finally, the labels of the target domain are obtained via a second annotation. Comprehensive experiments conducted on three large public activity recognition datasets (OPPORTUNITY, PAMAP2, and UCI DSADS) demonstrate that STL significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of classification accuracy (a 7.68% improvement). Additionally, the performance of STL is extensively investigated across varying degrees of similarity and activity levels between domains. The paper also discusses the potential of STL in other pervasive computing applications, providing empirical insights for future research.
label: AI

title: RIDI: Robust IMU Double Integration
Abstract: This paper presents a novel data-driven approach to inertial navigation, learning to estimate trajectories of natural human motions using only an inertial measurement unit (IMU) present in every smartphone. The key observation is that human motions are repetitive and consist of a few major modes (e.g., standing, walking, or turning). The algorithm regresses a velocity vector from the history of linear accelerations and angular velocities, subsequently correcting low-frequency bias in the linear accelerations, which are then integrated twice to estimate positions. Training data with ground-truth motions has been acquired across multiple human subjects and phone placements (e.g., in a bag or a hand). Qualitative and quantitative evaluations demonstrate that the algorithm achieves surprisingly comparable results to full visual inertial navigation. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first paper to integrate sophisticated machine learning techniques with inertial navigation, potentially opening up a new research direction in data-driven inertial navigation. Code and data will be publicly shared to facilitate further research.
label: AI

title: The Internet of Battle Things
Abstract: The future battlefield will be densely populated with diverse entities ("things") – some intelligent and some with limited intelligence – performing a wide range of tasks, including sensing, communicating, acting, and collaborating with each other and human warfighters. This interconnected network is termed the Internet of Battle Things (IoBT). While IoBT is already emerging, it is likely to become a dominant force in warfare in the next 20-30 years. To achieve this vision, significant challenges need to be addressed. One such challenge lies in the need for flexible and adaptive communication among entities to handle rapidly changing situations and military missions. This paper examines this and other major challenges of IoBT and outlines key research directions and approaches for tackling them.
label: AI

title: Human-Centric Data Cleaning [Vision]
Abstract: Data cleaning, the process of detecting and correcting errors in data, relies heavily on human involvement at various stages, such as identifying and repairing errors and validating computed repairs. A vast array of data cleaning algorithms exist, addressing a wide range of data errors (e.g., duplicate detection, integrity constraint violations, missing values, etc.). While many of these algorithms involve human interaction, this interaction is often coupled with the underlying cleaning algorithms. There is currently no end-to-end data cleaning framework that systematically incorporates humans into the cleaning pipeline, regardless of the underlying cleaning algorithms. This paper highlights key challenges that need to be addressed to realize such a framework. It presents a design vision and discusses scenarios motivating the need for a framework to judiciously assist humans in the cleaning process. Finally, it outlines directions for implementing such a framework.
label: AI

title: PuRe: Robust pupil detection for real-time pervasive eye tracking
Abstract: Real-time, accurate, and robust pupil detection is essential for enabling pervasive eye-tracking and its applications, such as gaze-based human-computer interaction, health monitoring, foveated rendering, and advanced driver assistance. However, automated pupil detection proves challenging in real-world scenarios due to a multitude of factors, including rapidly changing illumination and occlusions. This paper introduces Pupil Reconstructor PuRe, a novel method for pupil detection in pervasive scenarios, utilizing edge segment selection and conditional segment combination schemes. The method also includes a confidence measure for the detected pupil. Evaluation on over 316,000 images acquired using four distinct head-mounted eye tracking devices reveals a pupil detection rate improvement of over 10 percentage points compared to state-of-the-art algorithms in the two most challenging datasets (6.46% for all datasets), pushing the boundaries of pupil detection. Furthermore, the evaluation protocol for pupil detection algorithms is advanced by also considering eye images without pupils. In this aspect, PuRe demonstrates improved precision and specificity compared to state-of-the-art algorithms by 25.05% and 10.94% respectively, highlighting the significance of PuRe's confidence measure. PuRe operates in real-time for modern eye trackers (at 120 fps).
label: AI

title: Blind Image Deblurring via Reweighted Graph Total Variation
Abstract: Blind image deblurring, deblurring without knowledge of the blur kernel, is a highly ill-posed problem. It can be solved in two steps: i) estimating a blur kernel from the blurry image, and ii) de-convolving the blurry input using the estimated blur kernel to restore the target image. By interpreting an image patch as a signal on a weighted graph, the paper argues that a skeleton image – a proxy that retains the strong gradients of the target but smooths out the details – can be used for accurate blur kernel estimation and possesses a unique bi-modal edge weight distribution. A reweighted graph total variation (RGTV) prior is designed to efficiently promote bi-modal edge weight distribution given a blurry patch. However, minimizing a blind image deblurring objective with RGTV leads to a non-convex non-differentiable optimization problem. The paper proposes a fast algorithm that solves for the skeleton image and the blur kernel alternately. Finally, with the computed blur kernel, recent non-blind image deblurring algorithms can be applied to restore the target image. Experimental results show that the algorithm can robustly estimate the blur kernel with large kernel sizes, and the reconstructed sharp image is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Use of Generative Adversarial Network for Cross-Domain Change Detection
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of cross-domain change detection from a novel perspective of image-to-image translation. Change detection aims to identify interesting changes between a query image and a reference image of the same scene taken at different times. This task becomes challenging when query and reference images involve different domains (e.g., time of day, weather, season) due to variations in object appearance and limited training examples. This study addresses this issue by leveraging a generative adversarial network (GAN). The key concept is to train a GAN-based image translator using limited training data to map a reference image to a virtual image indistinguishable from query domain images. This allows treating cross-domain change detection as an in-domain image comparison, enabling the use of a vast body of literature on in-domain generic change detectors. Additionally, visual place recognition is considered as a method for mining more appropriate reference images over the space of virtual images. Experiments validate the efficacy of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Texture Synthesis with Recurrent Variational Auto-Encoder
Abstract: A recurrent variational auto-encoder is proposed for texture synthesis. A novel loss function, FLTBNK, is used to train the texture synthesizer. FLTBNK is a rotational and partially color-invariant loss function. Unlike L2 loss, FLTBNK explicitly models the correlation of color intensity between pixels. The texture synthesizer generates neighboring tiles to expand a sample texture, evaluated using various texture patterns from the Describable Textures Dataset (DTD). Quantitative and qualitative experiments are conducted with various loss functions to assess the performance of the proposed FLTBNK loss function. A mini-human subject study is used for qualitative evaluation.
label: AI

title: Large-Scale Object Discovery and Detector Adaptation from Unlabeled Video
Abstract: This paper explores object discovery and detector adaptation based on unlabeled video sequences captured from a mobile platform. A fully automatic approach for object mining from video is proposed, building upon a generic object tracking approach. The method's robustness and generality are demonstrated by applying it to three large video datasets from autonomous driving and mobile robotics scenarios. Based on the object mining results, a novel approach for unsupervised object discovery is introduced, utilizing appearance-based clustering. This approach successfully discovers interesting objects relevant to driving scenarios. Additionally, self-supervised detector adaptation is performed to enhance detection performance on the KITTI dataset for existing categories. The approach has direct relevance for enabling large-scale object learning for autonomous driving.
label: AI

title: Texture Object Segmentation Based on Affine Invariant Texture Detection
Abstract: To address the challenge of segmenting rich texture images, this paper proposes a novel detection method based on the affine invariant principle. Recognizing the similarity between texture areas, the method first applies affine transforms to generate numerous shapes, then utilizes the KLT algorithm to verify similarity. The transforms include rotation, proportional transformation, and perspective deformation to handle diverse situations. An improved LBP method incorporating Canny edge detection is then introduced to manage boundaries during the segmentation process. Furthermore, user-friendly human-computer interaction aids in splitting the matched texture area from the original images.
label: AI

title: Scene-Specific Pedestrian Detection Based on Parallel Vision
Abstract: Pedestrian detection in generic scenes, a specialized type of object detection, has achieved significant progress through training with large amounts of manually labeled data. However, models trained on generic datasets perform poorly when directly applied to specific scenes. Datasets from specific scenes, with unique viewpoints, lighting conditions, and backgrounds, differ considerably from generic datasets. To ensure the effectiveness of generic scene pedestrian detectors in specific scenes, labeled data from those scenes is needed to adapt the models. Manual labeling is time-consuming and expensive, particularly for specific scenes, requiring large amounts of image labeling for each new scene. Additionally, manual pixel-level labeling accuracy varies, and different individuals may provide different labeling information. This paper proposes an ACP-based method that utilizes augmented reality to create virtual worlds representing specific scenes, enabling people to walk within these virtual environments, where their appearances can be captured. This approach addresses the challenges of limited labeled data by providing a virtual environment for data collection. The results demonstrate that data from the virtual world effectively adapts generic pedestrian detectors to specific scenes.
label: AI

title: Combining Weakly and Webly Supervised Learning for Classifying Food Images
Abstract: Food classification from images is a fine-grained classification problem. Manual curation of food images is expensive, time-consuming, and difficult to scale. While web data is freely available, it often contains noise. This paper addresses the problem of classifying food images with minimal data curation. It also tackles the issue of food images from the web often containing multiple co-occurring food types but being weakly labeled with a single label. The paper demonstrates that adding a small number of manually curated samples to a larger uncurated dataset from two web sources increases top-1 classification accuracy from 50.3% to 72.8%. To address weak labels, the deep model is augmented with Weakly Supervised Learning (WSL), resulting in a performance increase to 76.2%. Finally, qualitative results are presented to provide insights into the performance improvements using the proposed ideas.
label: AI

title: Denoising of 3D magnetic resonance images with multi-channel residual learning of convolutional neural network
Abstract: Denoising magnetic resonance (MR) images is crucial for improving image quality. Numerous methods have been proposed in the literature to retrieve noise-free images with good performance. However, state-of-the-art denoising methods require time-consuming optimization processes, and their performance heavily depends on the estimated noise level parameter. This manuscript proposes the idea of denoising MRI Rician noise using a convolutional neural network. The advantage of the proposed methodology is that the learned model can be directly used for denoising without optimization, even without the noise level parameter. Specifically, a ten convolutional layer neural network combined with residual learning and a multi-channel strategy is proposed. Two training methods are investigated: training on a specific noise level and training on a general level, demonstrating the capability of the proposed method. Experimental results on synthetic and real 3D MR data show that the network achieves superior performance compared to other methods in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio and global structural similarity index. Without the noise level parameter, the general noise-applicable model also outperforms other compared methods in two datasets. Furthermore, the trained model exhibits good general applicability.
label: AI

title: Towards Structured Analysis of Broadcast Badminton Videos
Abstract: Sports video data, recorded for nearly every major tournament, remains archived and inaccessible for large-scale data mining and analytics. It can only be viewed sequentially or manually tagged with higher-level labels, which is time-consuming and prone to errors. This work proposes an end-to-end framework for automatic attribute tagging and analysis of sport videos. Utilizing commonly available broadcast videos of matches, unlike previous approaches, it does not rely on special camera setups or additional sensors. The focus is on badminton as the sport of interest. The paper proposes a method to analyze a large corpus of badminton broadcast videos by segmenting the points played, tracking and recognizing the players in each point, and annotating their respective badminton strokes. Performance is evaluated on 10 Olympic matches with 20 players, achieving 95.44% point segmentation accuracy, 97.38% player detection score (mAP@0.5), 97.98% player identification accuracy, and stroke segmentation edit scores of 80.48%. The paper further demonstrates that automatically annotated videos enable gameplay analysis and inference by computing understandable metrics such as player reaction time, speed, and footwork around the court.
label: AI

title: Interpretable Counting for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Questions requiring the counting of various objects in images remain a significant challenge in visual question answering (VQA). Common VQA approaches either classify answers based on fixed-length representations of both the image and question or sum fractional counts estimated from each section of the image. In contrast, this paper treats counting as a sequential decision process, requiring the model to make discrete choices about what to count. Specifically, the model sequentially selects from detected objects and learns interactions between objects that influence subsequent selections. A key feature of this approach is its intuitive and interpretable output, as discrete counts are automatically grounded in the image. Furthermore, the method outperforms state-of-the-art VQA architectures on multiple metrics that evaluate counting. |||
label: AI

title: Aerial Spectral Super-Resolution using Conditional Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Inferring spectral signatures from ground-based natural images has become a popular area of research in applied deep learning. Unlike the spectra of ground-based images, aerial spectral images have low spatial resolution and are susceptible to higher noise interference. This paper proposes a conditional adversarial network to learn an inverse mapping from a trichromatic space to 31 spectral bands within the 400 to 700 nm range. The network is trained on AeroCampus, the first aerial hyperspectral dataset of its kind. AeroCampus contains high spatial resolution color images and low spatial resolution hyperspectral images (HSI). The network is trained using color images synthesized from 31 spectral bands. With a baseline root mean square error of 2.48 on the synthesized RGB test data, the results demonstrate the feasibility of generating spectral signatures in aerial imagery.
label: AI

title: Boundary-sensitive Network for Portrait Segmentation
Abstract: Portrait segmentation presents a unique challenge in semantic segmentation due to its stricter requirement for boundary precision. However, this aspect has not been extensively explored in prior research. This paper introduces a boundary-sensitive deep neural network (BSN) for portrait segmentation. BSN incorporates three novel techniques. Firstly, it proposes an individual boundary-sensitive kernel by dilating the contour line and assigning multi-class labels to boundary pixels. Secondly, it employs a global boundary-sensitive kernel as a position-sensitive prior to further refine the overall shape of the segmentation map. Thirdly, it jointly trains a boundary-sensitive attribute classifier with the segmentation network to enhance the network with semantic boundary shape information. BSN's performance was evaluated on the largest public portrait segmentation dataset, PFCN, and portrait images collected from three popular image segmentation datasets: COCO, COCO-Stuff, and PASCAL VOC. The results demonstrate BSN's superior quantitative and qualitative performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, especially in the boundary area, across all datasets.
label: AI

title: Automated Surgical Skill Assessment in RMIS Training
Abstract: Manual feedback in basic robotic minimally invasive surgery (RMIS) training is time-consuming for expert surgeons and prone to subjectivity. While VR-based training tasks can generate automated score reports, a mechanism for automated feedback during basic surgical tasks in RMIS training is lacking. This study investigates the use of different holistic features derived solely from robot kinematic data for automated skill assessment and proposes a weighted feature fusion technique to improve score prediction performance. Experiments were conducted using the publicly available JIGSAWS dataset, evaluating four types of holistic features: Sequential Motion Texture (SMT), Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), and Approximate Entropy (ApEn). These features were utilized for both skill classification and exact skill score prediction. The study investigated individual feature performance as well as a proposed weighted combination technique. The findings demonstrate that these holistic features outperform all previous Hidden Markov Model (HMM)-based state-of-the-art methods for skill classification on the JIGSAWS dataset. Moreover, the proposed feature fusion strategy significantly enhances performance for skill score predictions, achieving up to 0.61 average Spearman correlation coefficient. This research suggests that holistic features capturing global information from robot kinematic data can effectively evaluate surgeon skill in basic surgical tasks on the da Vinci robot. The presented framework has the potential to enable real-time score feedback during RMIS training.
label: AI

title: Denoising of image gradients and total generalized variation denoising
Abstract: This paper revisits total variation denoising and investigates an augmented model assuming the availability of an image gradient estimate. The study demonstrates that this augmentation improves image reconstruction quality and reveals the resulting model's resemblance to total generalized variation denoising, providing a new perspective on this method. Furthermore, the paper proposes a constraint denoising model and develops a variational denoising model that is essentially parameter-free, where all model parameters are directly estimated from the noisy image. The study explores the application of Chambolle-Pock's primal dual method and the Douglas-Rachford method for the new models. The latter requires solving large discretizations of partial differential equations, which the paper suggests performing inexactly using the preconditioned conjugate gradients method. Preconditioners are derived for this approach. Numerical experiments demonstrate the good denoising properties of the resulting method and the significant improvement in convergence speed due to preconditioning. Finally, the paper analyzes the duality gap of different formulations of the total generalized variation (TGV) denoising problem and derives a simple stopping criterion.
label: AI

title: Evaluation of PPG Biometrics for Authentication in different states
Abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG), a medical biometric trait, is easily acquired by recording blood volume changes using a light-emitting diode and photodiode placed on any part of the body. With the increasing prevalence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and smart homes, PPG recording can be seamlessly integrated with other vital wearable devices. PPG uniquely reflects the hemodynamics and cardiovascular system of each individual. This paper presents a non-fiducial method for PPG-based biometric authentication. As a physiological signal, PPG is susceptible to variations due to physical/mental stress and time. To ensure robustness, these variations cannot be ignored. While previous studies focused solely on single-session data, this paper conducts extensive performance evaluation of PPG biometrics against single-session data, different emotions, physical exercise, and time-lapse using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and Direct Linear Discriminant Analysis (DLDA). Evaluation across different states and datasets resulted in an equal error rate (EER) of 0.5%–6% with an average training time of 45–60 seconds. The CWT/DLDA-based technique outperformed other dimensionality reduction techniques and previous work.
label: AI

title: An Incremental Self-Organizing Architecture for Sensorimotor Learning and Prediction
Abstract: Visuomotor tasks require robots to compensate for inherent temporal delays in their sensorimotor processing systems. Delay compensation becomes crucial in dynamic environments where the visual input continuously changes, such as when interacting with a human demonstrator. To address this, robots need a prediction mechanism that utilizes acquired perceptual experience to estimate potential future motor commands. This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture that learns prototypical visuomotor representations and provides reliable predictions based on visual input. These predictions are used to compensate for delayed motor behavior online. The performance of the proposed method was evaluated through experiments involving a humanoid robot learning and generating visually perceived arm motion trajectories. The accuracy was evaluated based on mean prediction error, and the network's response to novel movement demonstrations was analyzed. Additionally, experiments were conducted with incomplete data sequences to demonstrate the robustness of the architecture in noisy and faulty visual sensor scenarios.
label: AI

title: Training and Testing Object Detectors with Virtual Images
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized computer vision, leading to state-of-the-art models that rely heavily on large labeled datasets. However, collecting and annotating real-world images is labor-intensive and expensive, and it is often inadequate for building datasets with specific characteristics, such as objects occupying small areas and high occlusion levels. This paper proposes a purposeful approach within the framework of Parallel Vision to design artificial scenes and automatically generate virtual images with precise annotations. A virtual dataset called ParallelEye is created, suitable for various computer vision tasks. Training the Deformable Parts Model (DPM) and Faster R-CNN detectors demonstrates that model performance can be significantly enhanced by combining ParallelEye with publicly available real-world datasets during training. Furthermore, the study investigates the potential of using intentionally designed virtual datasets to test trained models from a specific aspect, identifying flaws in the trained models. Experimental results conclude that the proposed virtual dataset is effective for training and testing object detectors.
label: AI

title: Taking Visual Motion Prediction To New Heightfields
Abstract: While the fundamental laws of Newtonian mechanics are well understood, explaining a physical scenario still requires manual modeling using suitable equations and parameter estimation. To leverage the approximation capabilities of artificial intelligence techniques in physics-related contexts, researchers have handcrafted relevant states and trained neural networks to learn state transitions using simulation runs as training data. However, these approaches are ill-suited for complex real-world scenarios where manually authoring relevant state spaces is laborious and challenging. This study explores whether neural networks can implicitly learn the physical states of real-world mechanical processes solely based on visual data, internally modeling non-homogeneous environments and enabling long-term physical extrapolation. The study develops a recurrent neural network architecture for this purpose and characterizes the resulting uncertainties in the form of evolving variance estimates. The setup is evaluated by extrapolating the motion of rolling balls on bowls of varying shapes and orientations, and on arbitrary heightfields, using only images as input. The results demonstrate significant improvements over existing image-based methods in terms of prediction accuracy and scenario complexity, achieving performance comparable to approaches that assume access to internal physical states.
label: AI

title: Simple Methods for Scanner Drift Normalization Validated for Automatic Segmentation of Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging - with data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
Abstract: Scanner drift, a well-known magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) artifact, manifests as gradual signal degradation and scan intensity changes over time. Additionally, hardware and software updates can cause abrupt signal changes. These combined effects pose significant challenges for automatic image analysis methods used in longitudinal studies, leading to increased measurement variation and a risk of bias in estimations, such as volume change for a structure. This paper proposes two distinct approaches for scanner drift normalization and demonstrates their performance in segmenting knee MRI using the fully automatic KneeIQ framework. Validation involved a total of 1975 scans from both high-field and low-field MRI. The results reveal that the Atlas Affine Normalization pre-processing method effectively removes scanner drift effects, ensuring consistent cartilage volume change quantifications with manual expert scores.
label: AI

title: On the Integration of Optical Flow and Action Recognition
Abstract: Most top-performing action recognition methods utilize optical flow as a "black box" input. This paper delves deeper into the combination of optical flow and action recognition, investigating why optical flow is helpful, what constitutes a good flow method for action recognition, and how to further improve it. The study examines the impact of different flow algorithms and input transformations on a state-of-the-art action recognition method. Furthermore, two neural-network flow methods are fine-tuned end-to-end on the widely used UCF101 action recognition dataset. Based on these experiments, the paper presents five key observations: 1) optical flow is beneficial for action recognition due to its appearance invariance, 2) optical flow methods are optimized to minimize end-point-error (EPE), but the current EPE is not strongly correlated with action recognition performance, 3) for the tested flow methods, accuracy at boundaries and small displacements is most correlated with action recognition performance, 4) training optical flow to minimize classification error instead of EPE improves recognition performance, and 5) optical flow learned for action recognition differs from traditional optical flow, especially inside the human body and at the body's boundary. These observations encourage optical flow researchers to explore goals beyond EPE and guide action recognition researchers towards seeking better motion cues, fostering a tighter integration between the optical flow and action recognition communities.
label: AI

title: Detection and Tracking of General Movable Objects in Large 3D Maps
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of detecting and tracking general objects with long-term dynamics observed by a mobile robot navigating a large environment. A key challenge arises from the environment's scale, as the robot can only observe a subset of objects at any given time. The passage of time between object observations in different locations can lead to object movement while the robot is absent. The paper proposes a model for this movement where objects typically move locally, but with a small probability, they undergo longer jumps through what is termed global motion. For filtering, the posterior over local and global movements is decomposed into two interconnected processes. The posterior over global movements and measurement associations is sampled, while local movement is tracked analytically using Kalman filters. This novel filter was evaluated on point cloud data autonomously collected by a mobile robot over an extended period. The results demonstrate the feasibility of tracking jumping objects and the superiority of the proposed probabilistic treatment over previous methods when applied to real-world data. The key to efficient probabilistic tracking in this scenario is focused sampling of the object posteriors.
label: AI

title: The ParallelEye Dataset: Constructing Large-Scale Artificial Scenes for Traffic Vision Research
Abstract: Video image datasets play a crucial role in the design and evaluation of traffic vision algorithms. However, manually collecting and annotating large-scale diversified datasets from real scenes is time-consuming and error-prone. As a result, virtual datasets have emerged as proxies for real datasets. This paper proposes the construction of large-scale artificial scenes for traffic vision research and presents a new virtual dataset called "ParallelEye." The study utilizes street map data to build a 3D scene model of Zhongguancun Area, Beijing. Computer graphics, virtual reality, and rule modeling technologies are employed to synthesize large-scale, realistic virtual urban traffic scenes, ensuring fidelity and geographic alignment with the real world. The Unity3D platform is used to render these artificial scenes and generate accurate ground-truth labels, including semantic/instance segmentation, object bounding box, object tracking, optical flow, and depth. The environmental conditions in the artificial scenes can be fully controlled. This paper presents a viable implementation pipeline for constructing large-scale artificial scenes for traffic vision research. Experimental results demonstrate the pipeline's ability to generate photorealistic virtual datasets with low modeling time and highly accurate labeling.
label: AI

title: Towards dense object tracking in a 2D honeybee hive
Abstract: Detecting and efficiently tracking multiple objects in dense configurations, from human crowds to cells in tissue, is a significant and unsolved problem. Limitations in image analysis have restricted previous studies of dense groups to tracking single or subsets of marked individuals or to coarse-grained group-level dynamics, yielding incomplete information. This paper combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with the model environment of a honeybee hive to automatically recognize all individuals in a dense group from raw image data. The study creates new, adapted individual labeling and utilizes the U-Net segmentation architecture with a loss function dependent on both object identity and orientation. Temporal regularities in the video recording are exploited in a recurrent manner, achieving near human-level performance while reducing the network size by 94% compared to the original U-Net architecture. Given the novel application of CNNs, the study generates extensive problem-specific image data, where labeled examples are produced through a custom interface with Amazon Mechanical Turk. This dataset contains over 375,000 labeled bee instances across 720 video frames at 2 FPS, representing a valuable resource for developing and testing tracking methods. The results show a 96% accuracy in individual detection, with a location error of approximately 7% of a typical body dimension and an orientation error of 12 degrees, approximating the variability of human raters. This research provides an important step towards efficient image-based dense object tracking by enabling the accurate determination of object location and orientation across time-series image data within a single network architecture.
label: AI

title: Deep Hashing with Category Mask for Fast Video Retrieval
Abstract: This paper introduces an end-to-end deep hashing framework with category mask for fast video retrieval. The network is trained in a supervised manner by fully exploiting inter-class diversity and intra-class identity. Classification loss is optimized to maximize inter-class diversity, while intra-pair loss is introduced to learn representative intra-class identity. The study investigates the distribution of binary bits related to categories, discovering a strong correlation between bit effectiveness and data categories. Some bits can degrade the classification performance of certain categories. To address this, a hash code generation scheme with a category mask is designed to filter out bits with negative contributions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art techniques across various evaluation metrics on public datasets.
label: AI

title: Benchmarking Decoupled Neural Interfaces with Synthetic Gradients
Abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are a specific class of learning systems modeled after biological neural functions, with a notable propensity for Hebbian learning, where "neurons that wire together, fire together." However, unlike their natural counterparts, ANNs have a strong and inflexible coupling between their neuronal modules. This coupling or locking imposes a rigid structure on the network, preventing layers from updating their weights until a complete feed-forward and backward pass occurs. While this constraint may have been sufficient in the past, it is no longer feasible in the era of very large-scale machine learning and the increasing desire for parallelization across multiple computing infrastructures. To address this challenge, synthetic gradients (SG) with decoupled neural interfaces (DNI) are introduced as a viable alternative to the backpropagation algorithm. This paper performs a speed benchmark comparing the speed and accuracy capabilities of SG-DNI against a standard neural interface using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). SG-DNI shows promising results, demonstrating not only the ability to capture the learning problem but also a 3-fold speed increase due to its asynchronous learning capabilities.
label: AI

title: SFCN-OPI: Detection and Fine-grained Classification of Nuclei Using Sibling FCN with Objectness Prior Interaction
Abstract: Cell nuclei detection and fine-grained classification are fundamental yet challenging problems in histopathology image analysis. The tiny size of nuclei, significant inter-/intra-class variations, and inferior image quality often lead to limited accuracy and robustness in automated methods. Moreover, existing approaches typically handle these two tasks independently, neglecting their close relatedness. This paper presents a novel method called sibling fully convolutional network with prior objectness interaction (SFCN-OPI) to address both tasks simultaneously and interactively within a unified end-to-end framework. The sibling FCN branches share features in earlier layers while maintaining respective higher layers for specific tasks. Importantly, the detection branch outputs the objectness prior, which dynamically interacts with the fine-grained classification sibling branch during training and testing. This mechanism allows the fine-grained classification to focus on regions with high confidence of nuclei existence and output the conditional probability, which in turn benefits the detection through backpropagation. Extensive experiments on colon cancer histology images validate the effectiveness of SFCN-OPI, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin.
label: AI

title: CSGNet: Neural Shape Parser for Constructive Solid Geometry
Abstract: This paper presents a neural architecture that takes a 2D or 3D shape as input and outputs a program that generates the shape. The instructions in the program are based on constructive solid geometry (CSG) principles, involving Boolean operations on recursively defined shape primitives. Bottom-up techniques for this shape parsing task rely on primitive detection and are inherently slow due to the large search space of potential primitive combinations. In contrast, the proposed model utilizes a recurrent neural network that parses the input shape in a top-down manner, achieving significantly faster execution and producing a compact and easily interpretable sequence of modeling instructions. The model is also more effective as a shape detector compared to existing state-of-the-art detection techniques. The study demonstrates that the network can be trained on novel datasets without ground-truth program annotations using policy gradient techniques.
label: AI

title: A Bidirectional Adaptive Bandwidth Mean Shift Strategy for Clustering
Abstract: The bandwidth of a kernel function is a critical parameter in the mean shift algorithm. This paper proposes a novel adaptive bandwidth strategy with three main contributions: (1) analysis of differences among various adaptive bandwidth strategies, (2) definition of a new mean shift vector based on bidirectional adaptive bandwidth, combining the advantages of different adaptive bandwidth strategies, and (3) introduction of a bidirectional adaptive bandwidth mean shift (BAMS) strategy to enhance the algorithm's ability to escape from local maximum density. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy compared to contemporary adaptive bandwidth mean shift strategies.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Pixel Embedding for Instance Grouping
Abstract: This paper introduces a differentiable, end-to-end trainable framework for solving pixel-level grouping problems, such as instance segmentation, consisting of two novel components. Firstly, the framework regresses pixels into a hyperspherical embedding space, where pixels from the same group exhibit high cosine similarity, while those from different groups have similarity below a specified margin. The paper analyzes the choice of embedding dimension and margin, relating them to theoretical results on the problem of uniformly distributing points on the sphere. Secondly, to group instances, the framework utilizes a variant of mean-shift clustering, implemented as a recurrent neural network parameterized by kernel bandwidth. This recurrent grouping module is differentiable, enjoys convergent dynamics, and probabilistic interpretability. Backpropagating the group-weighted loss through this module enables learning to focus on correcting embedding errors that won't be resolved during subsequent clustering. The framework, while conceptually simple and theoretically rich, is also practically effective and computationally efficient. The paper demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art instance segmentation for object proposal generation and highlights the benefits of grouping loss for classification tasks such as boundary detection and semantic segmentation.
label: AI

title: Beyond saliency: understanding convolutional neural networks from saliency prediction on layer-wise relevance propagation
Abstract: Despite the remarkable achievements of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in numerous computer vision tasks, understanding their underlying mechanisms remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel two-step understanding method, called Salient Relevance (SR) map, aimed at shedding light on how deep CNNs recognize images and learn features from specific areas, referred to as attention areas. The proposed method starts with a layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) step that estimates a pixel-wise relevance map over the input image. Subsequently, a context-aware saliency map, SR map, is constructed from the LRP-generated map, predicting areas close to the foci of attention instead of isolated pixels revealed by LRP. In the human visual system, information from regions is more critical than from individual pixels for recognition. Consequently, the proposed approach closely mimics human recognition. Experimental results using the ILSVRC2012 validation dataset with two well-established deep CNN models, AlexNet and VGG-16, clearly demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies not only key pixels but also attention areas contributing to the underlying neural network's understanding of the given images. This visual interface, SR map, unveils the visual attention of the network and reveals the types of objects the model has learned to recognize after training. The source code is available at https://github.com/Hey1Li/Salient-Relevance-Propagation. |||
