title: Using LIP to Gloss Over Faces in Single-Stage Face Detection Networks
Abstract: This work demonstrates the vulnerability of state-of-the-art single-stage face detectors to adversarial attacks.  Existing methods for generating adversarial perturbations are ineffective against multiple faces, as the perturbation for one face disrupts the perturbation for another. This problem, called Instance Perturbation Interference (IPI), is addressed by analyzing the relationship between the neural network receptive field and adversarial perturbation. The proposed Localized Instance Perturbation (LIP) method confines adversarial perturbation to the Effective Receptive Field (ERF) of a target, significantly outperforming existing methods in attack success rate.
label: AI

title: Collision Selective Visual Neural Network Inspired by LGMD2 Neurons in Juvenile Locusts
Abstract: For autonomous robots operating in dynamic environments alongside humans, swift and reliable collision detection is crucial.  Inspired by biological visual systems, this study focuses on modeling the Lobula Giant Movement Detector 2 (LGMD2) neuron in locusts.  LGMD2 exhibits high firing rates in response to looming dark objects against bright backgrounds, a scenario relevant to ground vehicles and robots. The model incorporates biased ON and OFF pathways to encode brightness increments and decrements separately, achieving selectivity for dark objects.  A biophysical spike frequency adaptation mechanism further refines looming selectivity.  Extensive testing with synthetic and real stimuli, including data from a miniature robot's sensor, demonstrates the model's ability to detect looming dark objects selectively. The model's effectiveness in collision detection is verified through robotic experiments in obstacle-filled environments.  The model also exhibits enhanced collision selectivity to dark approaching objects compared to receding and translating ones.
label: AI

title: Smart, Sparse Contours to Represent and Edit Images
Abstract: This research explores reconstructing images from sparse contour information, demonstrating the ability to achieve high-quality reconstructions with fidelity to the source image from less than 6% of the image pixels. This surpasses existing contour-based methods that require denser input for accurate texture representation and image quality. The generative adversarial network model synthesizes textures and details in areas without input information.  The model's encoded semantic knowledge and sparse input allow contours to serve as an intuitive interface for semantically-aware image manipulation, where local contour edits translate to long-range and coherent changes in pixel space. This enables complex structural modifications, such as altering facial expressions through simple contour edits.  Experiments confirm that both humans and a face recognition system struggle to differentiate between the reconstructed images and the original sources.
label: AI

title: THESEUS: a key space mission concept for Multi-Messenger Astrophysics
Abstract: The detection of the electromagnetic counterpart of the gravitational wave source GW170817 has highlighted the immense value of multi-messenger observations. This field is poised for significant growth in the coming decade.  By 2030, third-generation gravitational wave detectors will achieve sensitivity ten times greater than current instruments. Simultaneously, neutrino detectors are undergoing upgrades to multi-km³ telescopes, including a 10 km³ facility in the Southern hemisphere. This review examines promising high-frequency gravitational wave and neutrino sources likely to be detected over the next two decades. The article emphasizes the role of the Transient High Energy Sky and Early Universe Surveyor (THESEUS) mission concept, proposed to the European Space Agency (ESA) by a large international collaboration.  THESEUS aims to advance early Universe science and play a pivotal role in multi-messenger and time-domain astrophysics, working in synergy with future gravitational wave and neutrino detectors, as well as ground and space-based telescopes. This review expands on the THESEUS white paper (Amati et al. 2017), particularly in light of the discovery of GW170817/GRB170817A.
label: AI

title: Unifying Map and Landmark Based Representations for Visual Navigation
Abstract: This paper presents a unified framework for visual navigation that integrates map-based spatial reasoning, path planning, and landmark-based robust plan execution in noisy environments. The framework is learned from data, leveraging statistical regularities of the world to enable efficient navigation in novel environments using sparse sets of registered images.  The framework consists of three key components: a learned path planner generating path plans, a feature synthesis engine predicting features for locations along the planned path, and a learned goal-driven closed-loop controller following plans based on these synthesized features. The approach is tested in simulated real-world environments, demonstrating performance gains over competitive baseline methods.
label: AI

title: A Deep Learning Interpretable Classifier for Diabetic Retinopathy Disease Grading
Abstract: Deep neural networks excel in image classification tasks, including medical diagnosis, but their lack of interpretability remains a major concern. Despite achieving high statistical confidence, they struggle to provide clear explanations for their results. The vast number of parameters in these models hinders the derivation of interpretable rationale. This paper introduces an interpretable diabetic retinopathy classifier capable of classifying retinal images into disease severity levels and explaining its results by assigning scores to points in the hidden and input spaces, evaluating their contribution to the final classification in a linear manner. The generated visual maps allow experts to compare their knowledge with the model's interpretation.
label: AI

title: Learning Intelligent Dialogs for Bounding Box Annotation
Abstract: This work introduces Intelligent Annotation Dialogs for bounding box annotation, training an agent to automatically select actions for a human annotator to produce a bounding box efficiently. Two actions are considered: box verification, where the annotator confirms a box generated by an object detector, and manual box drawing. The study explores two types of agents: one predicting the probability of positive box verification, and another based on reinforcement learning. The results demonstrate that: 1) agents learn efficient annotation strategies in various scenarios, adapting to image difficulty, desired box quality, and detector strength; 2) annotation dialogs consistently speed up annotation compared to manual drawing alone, box verification alone, and any fixed combination of both; 3) in a realistic scenario with iterative detector retraining, agents develop strategies reflecting the evolving trade-off between verification and drawing as the detector improves.
label: AI

title: AVEID: Automatic Video System for Measuring Engagement In Dementia
Abstract: Engagement in dementia is typically measured using behavior observational scales (BOS), which are time-consuming and labor-intensive to annotate, limiting their scalability. This paper proposes AVEID, a low-cost, user-friendly video-based engagement measurement tool to determine the engagement level of individuals with dementia during digital interaction. The objective behavioral measures computed via AVEID are shown to correlate well with subjective expert impressions for popular BOS, confirming its validity and effectiveness.  AVEID allows for the measurement of engagement across diverse design approaches, facilitating large-scale studies in dementia populations.
label: AI

title: Note on Attacking Object Detectors with Adversarial Stickers
Abstract: Deep learning, while powerful for computer vision tasks, is susceptible to adversarial examples, inputs deliberately designed to mislead deep learning algorithms into mislabeling them. This poses significant risks in safety-critical applications. Recent research has demonstrated the effectiveness of physical adversarial examples under various physical conditions in attacking classifiers. This study shows that state-of-the-art object detection algorithms, while more resistant to traditional adversarial examples, are also vulnerable to physical attacks. The paper presents both static and dynamic test results of an algorithm generating physical adversarial inputs that can deceive the YOLO object detector and successfully attack Faster-RCNN with a high success rate. The algorithm can compress these adversarial inputs into stickers, which when attached to the target object, cause the detector to either mislabel or fail to detect the object a significant percentage of the time. This paper provides a preliminary set of results, with a more comprehensive evaluation on other object detectors and the algorithm's details to be presented in an upcoming publication.
label: AI

title: Siamese Neural Networks for One-shot detection of Railway Track Switches
Abstract: Deep learning methods are widely used to analyze video data by classifying image frames and detecting objects. This paper proposes a novel approach for continuously monitoring railway tracks and detecting critical assets like switches using video feed from a moving locomotive. The technique utilizes Siamese Networks, employing two identical networks to learn the similarity between images.  The Siamese network compares track images to detect significant differences, identifying switches as distinct features and establishing a mapping that distinguishes them from other track anomalies. This method is extendable to detect any abnormalities on the railway track.  Railway transportation, with high-speed trains on guided rails, relies heavily on switches for managing train movements on different tracks.  Accurate switch location and status are crucial for railway operations.  Modern trains utilize high-definition video cameras to continuously record track footage.  By comparing this video feed to benchmark images using a Siamese network, the proposed method enables continuous track monitoring and anomaly highlighting.
label: AI

title: Encoding CNN Activations for Writer Recognition
Abstract: Encoding local features is essential for writer identification and retrieval. While CNN activations have been used for local features, the encoding of these features has received limited attention. This work compares the established VLAD encoding with triangulation embedding, investigates generalized max pooling as an alternative to sum pooling, and explores the impact of decorrelation and Exemplar SVMs. Using these techniques, new performance standards are set on two publicly available datasets (ICDAR13, KHATT).
label: AI

title: Track, then Decide: Category-Agnostic Vision-based Multi-Object Tracking
Abstract: The dominant paradigm for vision-based multi-object tracking is tracking-by-detection, reliant on the availability of reliable detectors for common object categories like cars and pedestrians. However, future mobile systems require the ability to handle complex environments with numerous object categories, making detectors for every object infeasible. This paper proposes a model-free multi-object tracking approach that uses a category-agnostic image segmentation method for object tracking. The efficient segmentation mask-based tracker associates pixel-precise masks generated by the segmentation. This approach leverages semantic information for object classification when available while maintaining the capability to track generic unknown objects.  Experiments demonstrate comparable performance to state-of-the-art tracking-by-detection methods for popular object categories, and also show the ability to discover and robustly track a wide range of other objects.
label: AI

title: Simulating Patho-realistic Ultrasound Images using Deep Generative Networks with Adversarial Learning
Abstract: Ultrasound imaging utilizes the backscattering of waves during their interaction with scatterers in biological tissues. Simulating synthetic ultrasound images is challenging due to the difficulty in accurately modeling factors such as intra-/inter scanline interference, transducer coupling, artifacts, inhomogeneous shadowing, and nonlinear attenuation.  Current approaches solve wave space equations, resulting in high computational costs and slow operation. This paper proposes a generative adversarial network (GAN)-inspired approach for fast simulation of patho-realistic ultrasound images, specifically for intravascular ultrasound (IVUS).  A stage 0 simulation using a pseudo B-mode ultrasound image simulator produces speckle mapping of a digital phantom.  Stage I GAN refines the speckle mapping to preserve tissue-specific intensities, and Stage II GAN further refines the images to generate high-resolution results with patho-realistic speckle profiles. The patho-realism of simulated images is evaluated using a visual Turing test, indicating that humans are unable to distinguish between simulated and real images.  Quantitative analysis of tissue-specific intensity distributions demonstrates the similarity between real and simulated images.
label: AI

title: Exploring Models and Data for Remote Sensing Image Caption Generation
Abstract: The increasing availability of remote sensing images from artificial satellites has driven advancements in scene classification and target detection. However, generating accurate and concise descriptions of the image content remains an open challenge. This paper investigates the use of natural language sentences to describe remote sensing images effectively.  The authors provide annotated instructions specifically tailored for remote sensing images, considering their unique characteristics. To comprehensively exploit the content of these images, a large-scale aerial image dataset is constructed for remote sensing image captioning.  The paper presents a comprehensive review of the proposed dataset, highlighting its potential to advance remote sensing image captioning. Extensive experiments on the dataset demonstrate the ability to fully describe the content of remote sensing images through language descriptions. The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/201528014227051/RSICD_optimal.
label: AI

title: Wolf in Sheep's Clothing - The Downscaling Attack Against Deep Learning Applications
Abstract: This paper examines security risks inherent in the data processing pipeline of common deep learning applications. Deep learning models typically assume fixed scales for their training and input data.  To accommodate a wide range of input data, popular frameworks like Caffe, TensorFlow, and Torch provide data scaling functions to resize inputs to the dimensions used by deep learning models.  Image scaling algorithms aim to preserve visual features after scaling. However, common algorithms are not designed for human-crafted images. Attackers can manipulate scaling outputs to create visually distinct versions from the original input images. The paper presents a downscaling attack that targets the data scaling process in deep learning applications. By carefully crafting input data that mismatches the model's dimensions, attackers can create deceptive effects.  The application consumes manipulated data that differ from those presented to users, enabling evasion and data poisoning attacks through visual inconsistency. The paper provides proof-of-concept attack samples against popular deep learning-based image classification applications and suggests potential mitigation strategies.
label: AI

title: Deep learning for predicting refractive error from retinal fundus images
Abstract: Refractive error, a leading cause of visual impairment, can be corrected by simple interventions like eyeglasses. This study trained a deep learning algorithm to predict refractive error from fundus photographs of participants in the UK Biobank cohort and the AREDS clinical trial, using 45-degree and 30-degree field of view images respectively. The model utilizes an "attention" mechanism to identify features correlated with refractive error. The algorithm's mean absolute error (MAE) in predicting refractive error compared to actual measurements was 0.56 diopters (95% CI: 0.55-0.56) for the UK Biobank dataset and 0.91 diopters (95% CI: 0.89-0.92) for the AREDS dataset.  The baseline MAE obtained by predicting the population mean was 1.81 diopters (95% CI: 1.79-1.84) for UK Biobank and 1.63 (95% CI: 1.60-1.67) for AREDS.  Attention maps revealed that the foveal region was a crucial predictor, with other regions also contributing.  The ability to estimate refractive error with high accuracy from retinal fundus photos is novel and demonstrates the potential of deep learning for making novel predictions from medical images. The feasibility of acquiring fundus photos using mobile phones and inexpensive attachments makes this work particularly relevant in areas lacking access to autorefractors.
label: AI

title: Context-Aware Semantic Inpainting
Abstract: Image inpainting has seen rapid progress due to generative adversarial networks (GANs) capable of synthesizing realistic content. However, most existing GAN-based methods for semantic inpainting employ an auto-encoder architecture with a fully connected layer, limiting their ability to maintain spatial information accurately. Additionally, discriminators in existing GANs struggle to understand high-level semantics within the image context, resulting in semantically inconsistent content. Existing evaluation criteria are biased towards blurry results and fail to adequately capture edge preservation and visual authenticity in the inpainting results. This paper proposes an improved generative adversarial network to address these limitations.  The proposed GAN-based framework utilizes a fully convolutional design for the generator, enhancing spatial structure preservation, and incorporates a joint loss function with a revised perceptual loss to capture high-level semantics within the image context. The paper introduces two novel measures for evaluating image inpainting quality.  Experimental results demonstrate the method's superior performance across various criteria.
label: AI

title: Automatic Estimation of Ice Bottom Surfaces from Radar Imagery
Abstract: Ground-penetrating radar deployed on planes and satellites provides valuable 3D observations of the subsurface structure of polar ice sheets, crucial for understanding and tracking global climate change. However, converting these noisy readings into usable observations is typically done manually, impractical at a continental scale. This paper proposes a computer vision-based technique for extracting 3D ice-bottom surfaces, framing the task as an inference problem on a probabilistic graphical model. The approach first generates a seed surface constrained by a set of criteria, and then refines it using additional sources of evidence through discrete energy minimization. The performance of the tracking algorithm is evaluated on seven topographic sequences (each with over 3000 radar images) collected from the Canadian Arctic Archipelago, with respect to human-labeled ground truth.
label: AI

title: Enhance Visual Recognition under Adverse Conditions via Deep Networks
Abstract: Visual recognition under adverse conditions is a significant challenge with high practical value due to the ubiquitous presence of quality distortions during image acquisition, transmission, or storage. While deep neural networks have been extensively used for low-quality image restoration and high-quality image recognition tasks, few studies have focused on recognition from very low-quality images. This paper proposes a deep learning-based framework to improve the performance of image and video recognition models under adverse conditions, leveraging robust adverse pre-training or its aggressive variant. Robust adverse pre-training algorithms extend conventional unsupervised pre-training and data augmentation methods.  A transfer learning approach is developed to handle real-world datasets with unknown adverse conditions. The framework is comprehensively evaluated on various image and video recognition benchmarks, demonstrating significant performance improvements under diverse adverse conditions. Visualization and analysis provide further explainability to the results.
label: AI

title: An Order Preserving Bilinear Model for Person Detection in Multi-Modal Data
Abstract: This paper introduces a new order-preserving bilinear framework that leverages low-resolution video for person detection in a multi-modal setting using deep neural networks. In this setting, cameras are strategically positioned such that less robust sensors, like geophones monitoring seismic activity, fall within the field of views (FOVs) of cameras. The primary challenge is extracting sufficient information from videos with limited target resolution (less than 40 pixels) while also incorporating information from less discriminative modalities. Unlike existing methods, the bilinear framework preserves spatio-temporal order when computing the vector outer products between feature pairs. Despite the high dimensionality of these outer products, the order-preserving bilinear framework outperforms recent orderless bilinear models and alternative fusion methods. |||
label: AI

title: Adversarial Synthesis Learning Enables Segmentation Without Target Modality Ground Truth
Abstract: Deep learning-based segmentation often lacks generalizability, requiring manual labeling for new modalities or disease cohorts. To address this, we propose EssNet, an end-to-end network that simultaneously synthesizes MRI images into CT images and segments CT splenomegaly without CT labels. EssNet significantly outperforms two-stage methods and achieves comparable performance to multi-atlas segmentation and ResNet, demonstrating its effectiveness in leveraging complementary information between image synthesis and segmentation.
label: AI

title: Sim2Real View Invariant Visual Servoing by Recurrent Control
Abstract: Humans excel at visual servoing, manipulating objects from various viewpoints with remarkable accuracy, even in distorted environments. This paper presents a deep recurrent controller capable of learning viewpoint-invariant visual servoing skills for robotic manipulation. By leveraging past movements, our system addresses the ambiguity inherent in severe viewpoint variations, achieving accurate object manipulation. The model is trained using simulated data and transferred to a real-world robot by adapting visual layers, enabling successful servoing of unseen objects from novel viewpoints on a real Kuka IIWA robotic arm.
label: AI

title: Image Segmentation to Distinguish Between Overlapping Human Chromosomes
Abstract: Accurate and automated chromosome visualization is crucial for medical diagnostics, drug development, and biomedical research. We propose a convolutional neural network tailored for segmenting partially overlapping DNA chromosomes. Our model achieves impressive intersection over union (IOU) scores of 94.7% for overlapping regions and 88-94% for non-overlapping regions, demonstrating its effectiveness in distinguishing overlapping chromosomes.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning with Lung Segmentation and Bone Shadow Exclusion Techniques for Chest X-Ray Analysis of Lung Cancer
Abstract: Deep learning advancements in image recognition have significantly impacted automatic disease detection from chest X-ray images (CXRs). This paper investigates the effectiveness of lung segmentation and bone shadow exclusion techniques in analyzing 2D CXRs using deep learning. Experiments conducted on various pre-processed JSRT datasets demonstrate the high efficiency and usefulness of these techniques, particularly the dataset excluding bones, which achieves superior accuracy and loss results.
label: AI

title: SuperPoint: Self-Supervised Interest Point Detection and Description
Abstract: This paper presents a self-supervised framework for training interest point detectors and descriptors suitable for various multiple-view geometry problems in computer vision. Our fully-convolutional model operates on full-sized images, jointly computing interest point locations and descriptors in a single forward pass. We introduce Homographic Adaptation, a multi-scale, multi-homography approach that enhances detection repeatability and enables cross-domain adaptation. When trained on MS-COCO using Homographic Adaptation, our model surpasses traditional corner detectors and achieves state-of-the-art homography estimation results on HPatches.
label: AI

title: Learning to Act Properly: Predicting and Explaining Affordances from Images
Abstract: This research addresses the problem of affordance reasoning in diverse real-world scenes, considering both the physical world and social norms. We propose a novel dataset, ADE-Affordance, based on ADE20k, which enables rich visual reasoning about action-object affordances. Using Graph Neural Networks, our model propagates contextual information from the scene to perform detailed affordance reasoning about each object. Ablation studies demonstrate the model's successes and challenges in this complex task.
label: AI

title: Learning a Wavelet-like Auto-Encoder to Accelerate Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Accelerating deep neural networks (DNNs) is crucial for enabling resource-constrained mobile systems to perform powerful visual recognition. We propose a Wavelet-like Auto-Encoder (WAE) that decomposes input images into low-resolution channels, integrating it into classification networks for joint training. This approach enables efficient DNN acceleration by preserving low-frequency information for classification while utilizing a lightweight network for high-frequency channel fusion. The WAE is tolerant to existing convolutional neural networks and provides interpretable preservation of key image components for classification.
label: AI

title: Partial Labeled Gastric Tumor Segmentation via patch-based Reiterative Learning
Abstract: Gastric cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, and accurate assessment of cancer extent is crucial for clinical decision-making. This paper presents a reiterative learning framework for training a network on partially annotated biomedical images, achieving superior performance without pre-training or manual annotation. Our overlapped region forecast algorithm eliminates boundary errors in patch-based models, resulting in a mean intersection over union (IOU) of 0.883 and mean accuracy of 91.09% on the partially labeled dataset.
label: AI

title: Attribute CNNs for Word Spotting in Handwritten Documents
Abstract: Word spotting in document image analysis has seen significant progress with the advent of AttributeSVMs. We propose a novel approach for learning attribute representations using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Our approach leverages probabilistic training of CNNs with two distinct loss functions for binary and real-valued word string embeddings. We introduce two specialized CNN architectures designed for word spotting, enabling end-to-end training. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of different word string embeddings and optimization strategies, achieving state-of-the-art results for segmentation-based word spotting on various datasets.
label: AI

title: Accurate 3D Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes from Monocular Image Sequences with Severe Occlusions
Abstract: This paper presents a solution for accurate dense orthographic Non-Rigid Structure from Motion (NRSfM) in scenarios with severe occlusions or inaccurate correspondences. We integrate a shape prior term into a variational optimization framework, allowing for penalization of irregularities in the time-varying structure based on correspondence quality indicators. Our approach assumes the availability of non-occluded views for initial shape prior estimation, effectively addressing the challenge of non-rigid deformations. Experiments on synthetic and real image data demonstrate significant improvements in correspondence establishment and NRSfM performance compared to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Attentional Reinforcement Learning for Multi-label Image Recognition
Abstract: Recognizing multiple labels in images is a fundamental yet challenging task in computer vision. This paper proposes a recurrent attention reinforcement learning framework to iteratively discover informative regions associated with different semantic objects and predict label scores conditioned on these regions. Our method explicitly models long-term dependencies among attentional regions, capturing semantic label co-occurrence and enhancing multi-label recognition. Experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO benchmarks demonstrate superior performance and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Human Action Recognition: Pose-based Attention draws focus to Hands
Abstract: We introduce a novel spatio-temporal attention mechanism for human action recognition that automatically attends to the most relevant hands and discriminative moments within an action. Our recurrent attention model, implemented using Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), is fully differentiable and conditioned on human articulated pose, providing external information for attention distribution extraction. Ablation studies highlight the strengths of this approach, and evaluation on the NTU-RGB+D dataset demonstrates state-of-the-art results.
label: AI

title: Incremental Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Continually Changing Environments
Abstract: Continuous appearance shifts, such as changes in weather and lighting, can negatively impact deployed machine learning models. This work proposes an adversarial approach for lifelong, incremental domain adaptation that leverages unsupervised alignment to a series of intermediate domains. We demonstrate that our incremental approach effectively handles large appearance changes, outperforming single alignment methods. By approximating the source domain feature distribution with a generative adversarial network, the deployment module becomes independent of source training data while maintaining performance.
label: AI

title: Finding Competitive Network Architectures Within a Day Using UCT
Abstract: Designing neural network architectures for new datasets is a laborious task requiring human expertise. We propose a Monte Carlo planning approach combined with two UCT (upper confidence bound applied to trees) derivations for automated network architecture search. Our adapted UCT algorithm incorporates information sharing between search tree branches, enabling the discovery of competitive networks for MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 within a single GPU day. With extended search time, our method outperforms human-designed architectures and competing approaches.
label: AI

title: Light Field Segmentation From Super-pixel Graph Representation
Abstract: Efficient and accurate light field segmentation is crucial in computer vision and graphics. We present a novel graph representation based on light field super-pixels (LFSP) for interactive light field segmentation. LFSP preserves light field redundancy while reducing graph size, enhancing segmentation efficiency. Our graph-cuts based algorithm utilizes this LFSP graph structure, achieving superior accuracy and efficiency compared to existing light field segmentation methods.
label: AI

title: DeepFuse: A Deep Unsupervised Approach for Exposure Fusion with Extreme Exposure Image Pairs
Abstract: We propose a novel deep learning architecture for fusing static multi-exposure images. Existing methods rely on hand-crafted features, which lack robustness and perform poorly for extreme exposure pairs. We address these limitations by introducing an unsupervised deep learning framework utilizing a no-reference quality metric as a loss function. Our architecture learns the fusion operation without ground truth images, fusing low-level features extracted from each image to generate artifact-free, perceptually pleasing results. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our approach over existing state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: On the Diversity of Realistic Image Synthesis
Abstract: Many image processing tasks involve translating images between domains, such as colorization, super resolution, and conditional image synthesis. We introduce a novel approach to synthesize diverse realistic images corresponding to a semantic layout, incorporating a diversity loss objective that maximizes distance between synthesized image pairs. This objective links input noise to semantic segments in the synthesized images, allowing for user-controlled manipulation of output images. Experimental results demonstrate significantly more diverse image synthesis compared to existing approaches while maintaining realistic output.
label: AI

title: Lost in Time: Temporal Analytics for Long-Term Video Surveillance
Abstract: Video surveillance has witnessed significant research in object detection, tracking, and behavior analysis. We propose two schemes for descriptive and predictive analytics on long-term video surveillance data. Our approach generates heatmap and footmap visualizations to describe spatially pooled trajectory patterns. Additionally, we introduce two anomaly prediction approaches: a trajectory-based statistical approach and a time-series based approach. Experiments on one year of data from a single camera demonstrate the ability to uncover insightful scene dynamics and predict anomalies with reasonable accuracy.
label: AI

title: Detection and classification of masses in mammographic images in a multi-kernel approach
Abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related death among women globally. Mammography remains the most effective diagnostic tool, and this paper presents a method for detecting and classifying mammographic lesions using image regions of interest. Our approach utilizes multi-resolution wavelets to decompose images and extracts Zernike moments from each wavelet component. This method combines texture and shape features, enabling both lesion detection and classification. Using the IRMA database, we achieve a classification accuracy of 94.11% with SVM and ELM networks, significantly outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and learning time.
label: AI

title: Analysis of supervised and semi-supervised GrowCut applied to segmentation of masses in mammography images
Abstract: Breast cancer is a common cancer, and mammographic image analysis is crucial for early detection. This paper evaluates the feasibility of applying GrowCut for tumor segmentation and proposes two semi-supervised GrowCut versions. We compare GrowCut performance to other segmentation techniques, including Region Growing, Active Contours, Random Walks, and Graph Cut, using the Mini-MIAS mammography database. Results demonstrate GrowCut's superior performance and the clinical applicability of our semi-supervised GrowCut versions, achieving satisfactory segmentation quality. |||
label: AI

title: LVreID: Person Re-Identification with Long Sequence Videos
Abstract: This paper presents a large-scale video database designed for person re-identification, specifically focusing on long sequences.
label: AI

title: Learning Sight from Sound: Ambient Sound Provides Supervision for Visual Learning
Abstract: This research investigates the use of ambient sound as a supervisory signal for learning visual models. The authors train a convolutional neural network to predict a statistical summary of the sound associated with a video frame, demonstrating that the network learns a representation that conveys information about objects and scenes.  Evaluations show comparable performance to other unsupervised learning methods. The study concludes with visualizations revealing units within the network that are selective to objects often associated with characteristic sounds. This paper expands upon an earlier conference publication with additional experiments and discussion.
label: AI

title: FoldingNet: Point Cloud Auto-encoder via Deep Grid Deformation
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel end-to-end deep auto-encoder for unsupervised learning on point clouds. The encoder utilizes a graph-based enhancement to promote local structures, while the decoder folds a 2D grid onto the 3D object surface of a point cloud, achieving low reconstruction errors even for complex objects. This folding-based decoder uses significantly fewer parameters than traditional fully-connected networks, resulting in a more discriminative representation that surpasses the benchmark in linear SVM classification accuracy.  The decoder structure is theoretically shown to be a general architecture capable of reconstructing any point cloud from a 2D grid.  Code is available at http://www.merl.com/research/license#FoldingNet.
label: AI

title: Audio to Body Dynamics
Abstract: This paper presents a method that takes audio of violin or piano playing as input and outputs a video of skeleton predictions, which are then used to animate an avatar. The main goal is to create realistic hand movements for the avatar, mirroring the movements of a pianist or violinist. The research focuses on predicting natural body dynamics from music, demonstrating for the first time that such prediction is possible. The authors built an LSTM network trained on online videos of violin and piano recitals. The predicted points are then applied to a rigged avatar to generate the animation.
label: AI

title: Multi-shot Pedestrian Re-identification via Sequential Decision Making
Abstract: This paper tackles the multi-shot pedestrian re-identification problem, a fundamental aspect of surveillance video analysis. Unlike existing approaches that rely on time series models, this research proposes an interpretable reinforcement learning-based approach. An agent is trained to verify image pairs, choosing to output a result (same or different) or request additional verification (unsure). This allows the model to implicitly learn the difficulty of image pairs and postpone decisions when insufficient evidence is available. By adjusting the reward for uncertain actions, the system can balance speed and accuracy. The method achieves competitive results on open benchmarks while using significantly fewer images, demonstrating its efficiency and performance.
label: AI

title: Hyperparameters Optimization in Deep Convolutional Neural Network / Bayesian Approach with Gaussian Process Prior
Abstract: This paper delves into the optimization of hyperparameters for convolutional neural network (ConvNet) architectures, highlighting the critical role of hyperparameter selection in achieving high accuracy and performance. The paper explores various methods for searching the hyperparameter space, including grid search and random search, which are often deemed inefficient and expensive. Sequential model-based Bayesian Optimization is presented as a promising alternative for tackling the challenges associated with unknown cost functions. The paper provides an overview of the mathematical concepts behind Bayesian Optimization utilizing a Gaussian prior, drawing inspiration from recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in reducing error rates in benchmark datasets like CIFAR-10.
label: AI

title: Deep Regression Forests for Age Estimation
Abstract: This paper proposes Deep Regression Forests (DRFs) as an end-to-end model for age estimation from facial images, addressing the challenge of heterogeneous facial feature spaces. DRFs combine the strengths of split nodes in decision trees with a fully connected convolutional neural network (CNN) layer, allowing for joint learning of input-dependent data partitions and data abstractions. This joint learning process is achieved through an alternating optimization strategy, iteratively optimizing split nodes, CNN parameters, and leaf nodes.  The proposed DRFs are evaluated on three standard age estimation benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art results across all datasets.
label: AI

title: Y-net: 3D intracranial artery segmentation using a convolutional autoencoder
Abstract: This research presents an optimized convolutional autoencoder (CAE) model, Y-net, for automated segmentation of intracranial arteries on magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) data. The CAE structure leverages its ability to reduce noise and extract features through low-dimensional latent variable representation.  The trained Y-net model demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional segmentation methods in both binary classification and visual evaluation, enabling quantification of cerebrovascular features and advancing understanding of aging and cerebrovascular health.
label: AI

title: Real-time deep hair matting on mobile devices
Abstract: This paper focuses on the application of augmented reality (AR) in the beauty industry, specifically for live virtual try-on of hair color products. The challenge of real-time hair segmentation is addressed by using a modified MobileNet CNN architecture. Instead of requiring large amounts of accurate segmentation data, the system utilizes crowd-sourced hair segmentation data, which is easier to obtain but noisy and coarse. Despite this data quality, the system effectively produces accurate and detailed hair mattes, running at over 30 frames per second on an iPad Pro tablet.
label: AI

title: Low-Shot Learning with Imprinted Weights
Abstract: This paper explores the ability to enable ConvNet classifiers to recognize novel visual categories after seeing only a few training examples, similar to human vision. The authors introduce a process called weight imprinting, which directly sets the final layer weights from new training examples during low-shot learning.  This imprinting process acts as a complement to traditional training with stochastic gradient descent, offering immediate good classification performance and an initialization for future fine-tuning. The paper demonstrates the relationship between imprinting and proxy-based embeddings while highlighting the unique aspect of using only a single imprinted weight vector per category. Experiments show that averaging imprinted weights leads to better generalization compared to using nearest-neighbor instance embeddings.
label: AI

title: Query-Efficient Black-box Adversarial Examples (superceded)
Abstract: This paper presents a new method for generating adversarial examples in the black-box setting with limited queries and information.  The authors use natural evolution strategies to perform black-box attacks with significantly fewer queries than previous methods.  They also introduce a novel algorithm for targeted adversarial attacks under limited information settings. Using these techniques, the paper demonstrates the first successful targeted adversarial attack against a commercially deployed machine learning system, the Google Cloud Vision API, in the partial information setting.
label: AI

title: Real-time 3D Reconstruction on Construction Site using Visual SLAM and UAV
Abstract: This research investigates the application of visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) integrated with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for real-time construction site reconstruction.  The study highlights the advantages of using RGB images for 3D reconstruction in the construction industry due to their low cost, rich texture, and ease of implementation. However, traditional image-based methods often require lengthy acquisition and processing times.  The paper presents a pilot study showcasing the use of visual SLAM and UAVs to overcome these limitations. The system architecture, experimental setup, preliminary results, and potential applications of this approach are discussed.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Examples: Attacks and Defenses for Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper reviews recent findings on adversarial examples for deep neural networks, highlighting their vulnerability to well-designed input samples that can easily deceive these networks.  The authors provide a taxonomy of methods for generating adversarial examples and explore their potential applications. The paper also examines countermeasures against adversarial examples, discussing the challenges and potential solutions in the context of applying deep neural networks in safety-critical environments.
label: AI

title: Automatic Renal Segmentation in DCE-MRI using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a time and memory efficient fully automated segmentation method for renal parenchyma in dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) images, aiding in the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric kidney diseases. The method utilizes a cascaded application of two 3D convolutional neural networks, incorporating spatial and temporal information to learn localization and segmentation tasks.  Evaluations on both normal and abnormal kidneys demonstrate high segmentation accuracy with a mean dice coefficient of 91.4 for normal kidneys and 83.6 for kidneys with hydronephrosis, achieving a runtime in the order of seconds.
label: AI

title: Scale-Space Anisotropic Total Variation for Limited Angle Tomography
Abstract: This paper addresses streak reduction in limited angle tomography. Traditional iterative reweighted total variation (wTV) algorithms struggle to eliminate large streaks due to the scale-dependency of total variation (TV) regularization.  The authors propose the scale-space anisotropic total variation (ssaTV) algorithm with two implementations.  The first utilizes an anisotropic gradient-like operator, while the second employs anisotropic down-sampling and up-sampling operations. Experiments using numerical and clinical data demonstrate that both ssaTV implementations effectively reduce streak artifacts compared to wTV, especially when using multiple scales.
label: AI

title: Bipartite Graph Matching for Keyframe Summary Evaluation
Abstract: This paper examines the evaluation of keyframe summaries, also known as "static storyboards", which are collections of frames designed to summarize video content. The authors review existing methods for matching frames between summaries in the context of graph theory, highlighting the different behaviors of these methods.  Through case studies, the authors recommend a greedy matching algorithm as the most effective for evaluating keyframe summaries.
label: AI

title: ComboGAN: Unrestrained Scalability for Image Domain Translation
Abstract: This paper presents a multi-component image translation model and training scheme that scales linearly with the number of domains, addressing the limitations of existing two-domain models that require a quadratic number of models for scaling. The proposed model offers significant efficiency gains in both resource consumption and training time.  The paper demonstrates the capabilities of the model on datasets of paintings by multiple artists and images from different seasons in the Alps.  The scalability of the model is particularly advantageous, as it requires only a linear number of generator/discriminator pairs compared to the exponential number needed for traditional two-domain models.
label: AI

title: Cross-language Framework for Word Recognition and Spotting of Indic Scripts
Abstract: This paper proposes a cross-language platform for handwritten word recognition and spotting in low-resource scripts, where sufficient training data is often scarce and expensive to collect. The platform utilizes a large dataset from an available script as a source and applies it to recognize and spot text in other scripts with limited data (target scripts).  The research addresses the challenges of handwriting variability and character mapping between scripts.  The proposed Indic cross-language framework leverages zone-wise character mapping for efficient learning, with performance dependent on the similarity between source and target scripts. An entropy-based script similarity score is devised to assess the feasibility of cross-language transcription.  The approach is validated on three Indic scripts, Bangla, Devanagari, and Gurumukhi, with promising results.
label: AI

title: On the Evaluation of Video Keyframe Summaries using User Ground Truth
Abstract: This paper addresses the lack of formalized evaluation methods for keyframe summaries, despite their growing popularity. While user studies are often employed for limited comparisons, they are not feasible for larger-scale studies. The authors propose a discrimination capacity measure as a formal way to quantify improvements over a uniform baseline, assuming the availability of ground truth summaries. Using the VSUMM video collection, they examine various video feature types and frame matching methods, concluding that simple hue histograms are sufficient for comparing keyframe summaries.  A formal protocol for comparison is subsequently proposed for scenarios with available ground truth.
label: AI

title: Learning Fixation Point Strategy for Object Detection and Classification
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel recurrent attentional structure for joint object localization and recognition. The network learns to extract a sequence of local observations with detailed appearance and context information, avoiding the limitations of sliding windows or convolutions on the entire image.  The observations are then fused to complete detection and classification tasks. The authors present a hybrid loss function for end-to-end training, combining stochastic and object-awareness strategies for selecting context and ensuring accurate object localization.  The approach is validated on a real-world dataset, demonstrating precise bounding box prediction and high speed on large images. Experimental results showcase the effectiveness of the method in extracting context, with precision and speed easily adjustable through the number of recurrent steps. The authors plan to open-source the code for their approach. |||
label: AI

title: Comparison of fingerprint authentication algorithms for small imaging sensors
Abstract: The increasing popularity of smartphones has fueled the demand for biometric systems. Fingerprint sensors are widely used in these devices due to their balance between reliability, affordability, and ease of use. While smartphone manufacturers claim high security levels, the small size of these sensors poses challenges for traditional minutiae algorithms. Limited research has addressed this issue, despite the existence of numerous pattern recognition algorithms and commercial solutions. This article explores potential solutions by analyzing the performance of three pattern recognition algorithms.
label: AI

title: End-to-end weakly-supervised semantic alignment
Abstract: Semantic alignment aims to find dense semantic correspondences between two images depicting objects of the same category. This task is challenging due to significant intra-class variation, viewpoint changes, and background clutter. This paper presents three main contributions: 1) an end-to-end trainable convolutional neural network architecture for semantic alignment using weak image-level supervision. This eliminates the need for laborious manual annotation of correspondences during training. 2) A differentiable soft inlier scoring module, inspired by RANSAC, which measures alignment quality based on geometrically consistent correspondences, minimizing the impact of background clutter. 3) Demonstration of state-of-the-art performance on multiple standard benchmarks for semantic alignment.
label: AI

title: Flexible Stereo: Constrained, Non-rigid, Wide-baseline Stereo Vision for Fixed-wing Aerial Platforms
Abstract: This paper proposes a computationally efficient method to estimate the time-varying relative pose between two visual-inertial sensor rigs mounted on flexible wings of a fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The estimated relative poses enable real-time generation of highly accurate depth maps, which can be used for obstacle avoidance during low-altitude flights or landing maneuvers. The approach begins by identifying a wing model by fitting a probability density function to measured deviations from the nominal relative baseline transformation. This prior knowledge is then integrated into an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) alongside relative pose measurements obtained from solving a relative perspective N-point problem (PNP) and linear accelerations and angular velocities measured by the two inertial measurement units (IMU) attached to the cameras. Extensive synthetic experiments demonstrate the framework's ability to estimate highly accurate baseline transformations and depth maps.
label: AI

title: Single Image Deraining using Scale-Aware Multi-Stage Recurrent Network
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of visually removing rain streaks and the veiling effect caused by rain scattering and transmission in a single input rainy image, particularly focusing on heavy rain. The proposed solution utilizes a scale-aware multi-stage convolutional neural network, recognizing that different sizes of rain streaks degrade the scene in different ways. Larger streaks obstruct larger regions and produce more prominent specular highlights compared to smaller, distant streaks. These varying effects are captured in distinct image features and require different treatment. To achieve this, the network employs parallel sub-networks trained to recognize and handle different scales of rain streaks. This novel approach, particularly within the context of rain removal, outperforms existing methods in experiments conducted on both synthetic and real images.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical Cross Network for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Person re-identification (person re-ID) aims to match a target person across different, non-overlapping camera views. This technology is crucial for public safety and has applications in tasks like human retrieval, tracking, and activity analysis. This paper introduces a new network architecture called Hierarchical Cross Network (HCN) for person re-ID. Building on conventional CNNs, HCN incorporates two additional maps, hierarchical cross feature maps, formed by merging layers with different resolutions and semantic levels. These maps enable HCN to effectively uncover semantic features missed by conventional CNNs. To further enhance representation power, the training process is augmented by combining multiple datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over several state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: Tracking objects using 3D object proposals
Abstract: 3D object proposals, regions within a 3D scene likely containing objects of interest, are an effective approach for improving the computational efficiency and accuracy of object detection frameworks. This work proposes a novel online method using previously developed 3D object proposals in RGB-D video sequences to match and track static objects in the scene through shape matching. The method leverages depth images to provide information about scene geometry often overlooked in object matching techniques. This approach takes less than a second to process on a single thread CPU using MATLAB on the UW-RGBD scene dataset, making it suitable for low-power chips in UAVs, quadcopters, and drones.
label: AI

title: MovieGraphs: Towards Understanding Human-Centric Situations from Videos
Abstract: The development of socially intelligent robots requires machines to understand human emotions, motivations, and other behavioral influencers. To facilitate this research, this paper introduces MovieGraphs, a novel dataset providing detailed graph-based annotations of social situations depicted in movie clips. Each graph consists of various node types capturing information about individuals present in the clip, their emotional and physical attributes, relationships (e.g., parent/child), and interactions between them. The interactions are linked to topics providing context and reasons for actions. Time stamps ground most interactions and attributes within the video. Comprehensive analysis of the dataset reveals interesting correlations between different social aspects within scenes and across scenes over time. The paper proposes a method for querying videos and text with graphs, demonstrating: 1) the sufficiency of graph information for summarizing and localizing each scene; 2) the ability of subgraphs to describe situations abstractly and retrieve multiple semantically relevant situations. Additionally, methods for interaction understanding through ordering and reason understanding are presented. MovieGraphs serves as the first benchmark focusing on inferred properties of human-centric situations, opening a path towards the development of socially intelligent AI agents.
label: AI

title: Mining Point Cloud Local Structures by Kernel Correlation and Graph Pooling
Abstract: Semantic learning on 3D point clouds using deep networks presents challenges due to the inherently unordered data structure. While PointNet has shown promising results by directly learning from point sets, it does not fully utilize the local neighborhood of each point, which holds valuable fine-grained structural information for improved semantic learning. This paper presents two new operations to enhance PointNet by efficiently exploiting local structures. The first operation focuses on 3D geometric structures, defining a point-set kernel as a set of learnable 3D points that jointly respond to neighboring data points based on their geometric affinities measured through kernel correlation. The second operation exploits local high-dimensional feature structures through recursive feature aggregation on a nearest-neighbor graph computed from 3D positions. Experiments demonstrate the network's ability to effectively capture local information and achieve robustly better performance on major datasets. The code is available at http://www.merl.com/research/license#KCNet.
label: AI

title: PixelBNN: Augmenting the PixelCNN with batch normalization and the presentation of a fast architecture for retinal vessel segmentation
Abstract: Analysis of retinal fundus images is essential for ophthalmologists in diagnosing, treating, and managing patient care. Accurate fundus and retinal vessel maps enable longitudinal studies using multimedia image registration, disease/condition status measurements, and applications in surgical preparation and biometrics. Segmenting retinal morphology has numerous applications in assessing ophthalmologic and cardiovascular disease pathologies, with early detection being crucial for reducing patient risk. Automated segmentation of vasculature presents challenges due to inconsistencies like noise and variations in hue and brightness, which can significantly degrade fundus image quality. This paper introduces PixelBNN, a highly efficient deep learning method for automating fundus morphology segmentation. The model was trained, tested, and cross-tested on the DRIVE, STARE, and CHASE_DB1 retinal vessel segmentation datasets. Performance was evaluated using G-mean, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and F1-score. The network achieved a significant 8.5 times speed improvement compared to the current state-of-the-art during testing, while maintaining comparable performance despite a 5 to 19 times reduction in information due to image resizing during preprocessing.
label: AI

title: Deformable Classifiers
Abstract: Geometric variations in objects, which do not alter the object class, pose a major challenge for object recognition. These variations can be rigid or non-rigid transformations. This paper proposes a framework for training deformable classifiers by introducing latent transformation variables and computing a transformation of the object image to a reference instantiation based on the classifier output, separately for each class. The classifier outputs for each class, after transformation, are compared to make the final decision. As a byproduct, the classification also provides a transformation of the input object to a reference pose, which can be used for tasks like computing object support. The framework employs a two-step training mechanism, alternating between optimization of latent transformation variables and classifier parameters to minimize the loss function. Multilayer perceptrons, also known as deep networks, are shown to be well-suited for this approach and achieve state-of-the-art results on the rotated MNIST and Google Earth datasets. Competitive results are obtained on MNIST and CIFAR-10 when training on smaller subsets of training data.
label: AI

title: Synthesizing Novel Pairs of Image and Text
Abstract: Generating novel image-text pairs is a problem that combines computer vision and natural language processing. This paper presents strategies for generating novel image-caption pairs based on existing captioning datasets. The model leverages recent advancements in generative adversarial networks and sequence-to-sequence modeling. Generalizations are made to generate paired samples from multiple domains. The paper also explores cycles, including generating from image to text and back to image, and vice versa, and its connection to autoencoders.
label: AI

title: DecideNet: Counting Varying Density Crowds Through Attention Guided Detection and Density Estimation
Abstract: Real-world crowd counting applications encounter significant variations in crowd densities across spatial and temporal domains. Detection-based counting methods excel in low-density scenes but lose reliability in congested areas. Regression-based approaches capture general density information in crowded regions but tend to overestimate counts in low-density areas. Relying solely on either method is insufficient for handling diverse density scenarios. This paper proposes DecideNet (DEteCtIon and Density Estimation Network), a novel end-to-end crowd counting framework that adaptively selects the appropriate counting mode for different locations based on real-time density conditions. DecideNet estimates crowd density by generating separate detection and regression-based density maps. To address density variations, it incorporates an attention module that adaptively assesses the reliability of both estimations. The final crowd counts are obtained using the attention module to adopt suitable estimations from the two density maps. Experimental results show that the method achieves state-of-the-art performance on three challenging crowd counting datasets.
label: AI

title: Objects that Sound
Abstract: This paper aims to create networks capable of embedding audio and visual inputs into a common space suitable for cross-modal retrieval and to localize the object that produces sound in an image given the audio signal. Both objectives are achieved by training from unlabeled video using only audio-visual correspondence (AVC) as the objective function, a form of cross-modal self-supervision from video. The paper presents novel network architectures for cross-modal retrieval and sound source localization in images using the AVC task. Key contributions include: (i) demonstrating that audio and visual embeddings can be learned to enable within-mode (e.g., audio-to-audio) and between-mode retrieval; (ii) exploring various AVC task architectures, including those for the visual stream that ingest a single image, multiple images, or a single image and multi-frame optical flow; (iii) showing that the semantic object producing sound within an image can be localized using only sound without motion or flow information; (iv) providing guidance on avoiding undesirable shortcuts in data preparation.
label: AI

title: End-to-end Recovery of Human Shape and Pose
Abstract: This paper describes Human Mesh Recovery (HMR), an end-to-end framework for reconstructing a full 3D mesh of a human body from a single RGB image. Unlike most current methods that focus on 2D or 3D joint locations, HMR produces a richer and more useful mesh representation parameterized by shape and 3D joint angles. The primary objective is to minimize the reprojection loss of keypoints, allowing the model to be trained using in-the-wild images with only ground truth 2D annotations. However, reprojection loss alone underconstrains the model. This paper addresses this issue by introducing an adversary trained to distinguish real human body parameters from generated ones using a large database of 3D human meshes. HMR can be trained with or without paired 2D-to-3D supervision, bypassing intermediate 2D keypoint detections and inferring 3D pose and shape parameters directly from image pixels. The model runs in real-time given a bounding box containing the person. Results on in-the-wild images demonstrate outperformance compared to previous optimization-based methods that output 3D meshes and show competitive results on tasks like 3D joint location estimation and part segmentation.
label: AI

title: Multi-point Vibration Measurement for Mode Identification of Bridge Structures using Video-based Motion Magnification
Abstract: Image-based vibration mode identification has gained significant attention in civil and construction engineering. A recent video-based motion magnification method was developed to measure and visualize small structure motions, offering potential for low-cost vibration measurement and mode shape identification. While pilot studies on simple rigid body structures have been conducted, its applicability to complex outdoor structures remains unexplored. This paper investigates the capacity of video-based motion magnification in measuring modal frequency and visualizing mode shapes of complex steel bridges. A novel method is introduced to enhance the performance of the motion magnification technique for efficient structure modal analysis. The method was tested in both indoor and outdoor environments for validation. The findings demonstrate that motion magnification is an effective tool for modal analysis of complex bridge structures. The developed method enables simultaneous measurement of mode frequencies for multiple structures and automated visualization of mode shapes for each structure.
label: AI

title: Dynamic Weight Alignment for Temporal Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for improving temporal Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by determining the optimal alignment of weights and inputs using dynamic programming. Conventional CNN convolutions linearly match shared weights to an input window. However, a more optimal alignment might exist. The paper proposes using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to dynamically align weights to the input of the convolutional layer. Dynamic alignment overcomes issues like temporal distortion by finding the minimal distance matching of weights and inputs under constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed architecture is demonstrated on the Unipen online handwritten digit and character datasets, the UCI Spoken Arabic Digit dataset, and the UCI Activities of Daily Life dataset.
label: AI

title: IMU2Face: Real-time Gesture-driven Facial Reenactment
Abstract: This paper presents IMU2Face, a gesture-driven facial reenactment system that combines advancements in facial motion capture and inertial measurement units (IMUs) to control facial expressions in a target video based on intuitive hand gestures. IMUs are widely available, integrated into modern smartphones, smartwatches, and drones for tasks like screen orientation control, step counting, or flight stabilization. Face tracking and reenactment are based on the state-of-the-art real-time Face2Face system. Instead of transferring facial expressions from a source to a target actor, IMU2Face tracks the hand gestures of a source actor and uses their orientation to modify the target actor's expressions.
label: AI

title: Guiding human gaze with convolutional neural networks
Abstract: Human eye fixation patterns are a crucial indicator of areas of interest in images. Manipulating fixation patterns to guide human attention presents an exciting challenge in digital image processing. This paper introduces a new model for manipulating images to control the distribution of human fixations. The state-of-the-art fixation prediction model is used to train a convolutional neural network to transform images to achieve a desired fixation distribution. A carefully designed loss function ensures both perceptual effect and naturalness of the transformed images. The model's effectiveness is evaluated by measuring human fixations for a set of manipulated images. Results show that the model can increase or decrease the probability of fixating on selected objects by an average of 43% and 22%, respectively, highlighting the model's dependency on the semantic content of the manipulated images.
label: AI

title: Multi-modal Face Pose Estimation with Multi-task Manifold Deep Learning
Abstract: Human face pose estimation aims to estimate gazing direction or head postures from 2D images. This information is valuable for tasks like communicative gesture recognition, saliency detection, and more, garnering significant recent attention. However, the task is challenging due to complex backgrounds, varying orientations, and face appearance visibility. Effective face image representation and mapping to poses are crucial. This paper utilizes multi-modal data and proposes a novel face pose estimation method using a deep learning framework called Multi-task Manifold Deep Learning (M^2DL). The framework relies on feature extraction with improved deep neural networks and multi-modal mapping relationships with multi-task learning. Manifold Regularized Convolutional Layers (MRCL) enhance traditional convolutional layers by learning relationships among neuron outputs. The proposed mapping relationship learning method naturally combines different face representation modalities to learn the mapping function from face images to poses, improving the computed mapping model with multiple tasks. Experimental results on three challenging benchmark datasets (DPOSE, HPID, and BKHPD) demonstrate M^2DL's outstanding performance.
label: AI

title: Super-Resolution with Deep Adaptive Image Resampling
Abstract: Deep learning-based methods have recently achieved state-of-the-art performance in Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR). This work revisits more traditional interpolation-based methods, now enhanced with deep learning. The proposed method uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to estimate spatially variant interpolation kernels and adaptively applies these kernels to each image position. The entire model is trained end-to-end. Two approaches are explored to improve results for large upscaling factors, and a recursive extension of the basic model is proposed, achieving performance on par with state-of-the-art methods. The estimated adaptive interpolation kernels are visualized to gain insights into the method's effectiveness. The method is also extended to joint image filtering, again achieving state-of-the-art performance. |||

title: Automatic segmentation method of pelvic floor levator hiatus in ultrasound using a self-normalising neural network
Abstract: This paper proposes a fully automatic method to delineate the levator hiatus in 2D images from 3D ultrasound volumes using a convolutional neural network (CNN). The method employs the scaled exponential linear unit (SELU) as a self-normalising activation function, which is applied for the first time in medical imaging with CNNs.  SELU offers advantages such as parameter-free and mini-batch independence, potentially alleviating memory constraints during training. The proposed method was trained and evaluated on a dataset of 91 images from 35 patients during Valsalva, contraction, and rest, with labels provided by three operators using a leave-one-patient-out cross-validation approach. The results demonstrate a median Dice similarity coefficient of 0.90 with an interquartile range of 0.08, exhibiting performance comparable to the three operators (Williams' index of 1.03) and surpassing a U-Net architecture without batch normalisation. This indicates that the proposed fully automatic method achieved comparable accuracy in segmenting the pelvic floor levator hiatus compared to a previous semi-automatic approach.

title: Automatic Classification of Functional Gait Disorders
Abstract: This article presents a comprehensive study on the automatic classification of functional gait disorders using solely ground reaction force (GRF) measurements. The study aims to investigate the suitability of state-of-the-art GRF parameterization techniques for discriminating functional gait disorders and to establish a baseline performance for automated classification on a large-scale dataset. The utilized database includes GRF measurements from 279 patients with gait disorders (GDs) and 161 healthy controls (N). Patients were manually categorized into four classes based on different functional impairments associated with the "hip", "knee", "ankle", and "calcaneus". Various parameterizations were explored, including GRF parameters, global principal component analysis (PCA)-based representations, and a combined representation applying PCA on GRF parameters. The discriminative power of each parameterization for different classes was investigated using linear discriminant analysis (LDA). Two classification experiments were conducted: (1) distinguishing between healthy and impaired gait (N vs. GD) and (2) multi-class classification between healthy gait and all four GD classes. The experiments revealed promising results and highlighted the impact of factors such as imbalanced class cardinalities and varying numbers of measurement sessions per patient on classification accuracy. The results represent a promising initial step towards automated classification of gait disorders and establish a performance baseline for future advancements in this area.

title: On the Effectiveness of Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Unsupervised learning with generative adversarial networks (GANs) has achieved significant success. Traditional GANs utilize the discriminator as a classifier with the sigmoid cross-entropy loss function. However, this loss function can lead to the vanishing gradients problem during training. To address this issue, this paper proposes Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks (LSGANs), which adopt the least squares loss for both the discriminator and the generator. It is demonstrated that minimizing the objective function of LSGANs results in minimizing the Pearson  $\\chi^2$ divergence.  Furthermore, it is shown that the derived objective function that minimizes the Pearson $\\chi^2$ divergence performs better than the conventional approach of using least squares for classification. LSGANs offer two key advantages over regular GANs:  Firstly, LSGANs produce higher quality images compared to regular GANs. Secondly, LSGANs exhibit greater stability during the learning process. To evaluate image quality, both qualitative and quantitative experiments were conducted, demonstrating that LSGANs generate higher quality images than regular GANs. Additionally, the stability of LSGANs was evaluated in two groups: comparing LSGANs with regular GANs without gradient penalty and comparing LSGANs with gradient penalty (LSGANs-GP) with WGANs with gradient penalty (WGANs-GP). The experimental results indicate that LSGANs-GP successfully train for all the challenging architectures used in WGANs-GP, including the 101-layer ResNet.

title: Space-Filling Curve Indices as Acceleration Structure for Exemplar-Based Inpainting
Abstract: Exemplar-based inpainting reconstructs missing image parts by searching for matching patches within the remaining data. This paper introduces an acceleration structure that leverages a multi-index scheme to significantly speed up this search process, particularly for large datasets. The index scheme combines dimensionality reduction and k-nearest neighbor search on space-filling curves, concepts established in multimedia databases. The proposed method exhibits a theoretical runtime of O(log2 n) per iteration and achieves a speedup factor of up to 660 compared to the original method. This approach is agnostic to most model-based aspects of exemplar-based inpainting, such as the order of patch processing and the cost function used for patch similarity.  Therefore, the acceleration structure can be used with various exemplar-based inpainting algorithms.

title: Video Object Detection with an Aligned Spatial-Temporal Memory
Abstract: This paper introduces Spatial-Temporal Memory Networks (STMN) for video object detection.  At its core, a novel Spatial-Temporal Memory module (STMM) serves as the recurrent computation unit, modeling long-term temporal appearance and motion dynamics. The STMM design enables full integration of pre-trained backbone CNN weights, which is crucial for accurate detection. To address object motion in videos, a novel MatchTrans module is proposed to align spatial-temporal memory across frames. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on the ImageNet VID benchmark dataset, and ablation studies confirm the contribution of different design choices. The code and models are available at http://fanyix.cs.ucdavis.edu/project/stmn/project.html.

title: LSTM Pose Machines
Abstract: Recent advancements in single image human pose estimation have relied on multi-stage Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). While these models excel on static images, their application to videos is computationally demanding and suffers from performance degradation and flicking. These issues stem from the inability to impose sequential geometric consistency, handle severe image quality degradation (e.g., motion blur and occlusion), and capture temporal correlations among video frames. This paper proposes a novel recurrent network to address these challenges. By applying a weight-sharing scheme to the multi-stage CNN, it can be reformulated as a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), decoupling the relationship among network stages and significantly accelerating video processing. This allows for the integration of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units between video frames.  The memory-augmented RNN effectively imposes geometric consistency among frames, handles input quality degradation, and stabilizes sequential outputs. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on two large-scale video pose estimation benchmarks. Insights into the memory cells within the LSTM highlight the benefits of this mechanism for video-based pose estimations.
