title: Visual Explanation by Interpretation: Improving Visual Feedback Capabilities of Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Interpretation and explanation of deep models are crucial for widespread adoption of systems relying on them. This paper presents a novel scheme for both interpretation and explanation, automatically identifying internal features relevant to the set of classes considered by a pre-trained model without requiring additional annotations. The model is interpreted through average visualizations of this reduced set of features. At test time, network predictions are explained by accompanying the predicted class label with supporting visualizations derived from the identified features.  A method is proposed to address artifacts introduced by stridded operations in deconvNet-based visualizations. Additionally, an8Flower, a dataset specifically designed for objective quantitative evaluation of visual explanation methods, is introduced. Experiments on MNIST, ILSVRC12, Fashion144k, and an8Flower datasets show that the proposed method produces detailed explanations with good coverage of relevant features for the classes of interest.

title: Automated flow for compressing convolution neural networks for efficient edge-computation with FPGA
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are the current state-of-the-art for computer vision tasks. However, their large size typically necessitates running them on clusters of CPUs or GPUs, posing significant power and cost challenges for adopting CNNs in IoT applications. Recent research has highlighted the redundancy in CNN structures and the potential for quantization to lower bit-width parameters and activations while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Low bit-width, particularly single bit-width (binary) CNNs, are particularly suitable for mobile applications based on FPGA implementation due to the bitwise logic operations involved.  The transition to lower bit-widths opens avenues for performance optimization and model improvement. This paper presents an automated flow from trained TensorFlow models to FPGA system-on-chip implementation of binarized CNNs. This flow involves quantization of model parameters and activations, generation of network and model in embedded-C, and automatic generation of the FPGA accelerator for binary convolutions. The automated flow is demonstrated through implementation of binarized "YOLOV2" on the low-cost, low-power Cyclone-V FPGA device. Experiments on object detection using binarized YOLOV2 showcase significant performance benefits in terms of model size and inference speed on FPGA compared to CPU and mobile CPU platforms. Furthermore, the entire automated flow from trained models to FPGA synthesis can be completed within one hour.

title: Panoramic Robust PCA for Foreground-Background Separation on Noisy, Free-Motion Camera Video
Abstract: This work introduces a new robust PCA method for foreground-background separation in freely moving camera video with potential dense and sparse corruptions. The proposed method registers video frames and encodes varying perspectives arising from camera motion as missing data in a global model. This formulation enables the algorithm to produce a panoramic background component that automatically stitches together corrupted data from partially overlapping frames to reconstruct the full field of view. The registered video is modeled as the sum of a low-rank component capturing the background, a smooth component capturing the dynamic foreground of the scene, and a sparse component isolating outliers and other sparse corruptions in the video. The low-rank portion of the model is based on a recent low-rank matrix estimator (OptShrink) known for producing superior low-rank subspace estimates. A weighted total variation framework is used to estimate the smooth foreground component, allowing the method to reliably separate the true foreground from sparse corruptions. Extensive numerical experiments on static and moving camera video subject to various dense and sparse corruptions demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of the proposed method compared to existing methods in terms of foreground and background estimation accuracy.

title: Visual Explanations from Hadamard Product in Multimodal Deep Networks
Abstract: Visual explanation of learned representation in models aids in understanding the fundamentals of learning. Previous work on attentional models has used learned weights to visualize attended regions in images or text, confirming their intended mechanism.  Kim et al. (2016) showed that the Hadamard product in multimodal deep networks, known for its joint function in visual question answering tasks, implicitly performs an attentional mechanism for visual inputs. This paper extends this work by demonstrating that the Hadamard product in multimodal deep networks performs attentional mechanisms not only for visual inputs but also for textual inputs simultaneously using a proposed gradient-based visualization technique. The attentional effect of the Hadamard product is visualized for both visual and textual inputs by analyzing the two inputs and the output of the Hadamard product with the proposed method, comparing it to learned attentional weights of a visual question answering model.

title: Attenuation correction for brain PET imaging using deep neural network based on dixon and ZTE MR images
Abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) is a functional imaging modality widely used in neuroscience studies. To obtain meaningful quantitative results from PET images, attenuation correction is necessary during image reconstruction. In PET/MR hybrid systems, PET attenuation is challenging as Magnetic Resonance (MR) images do not directly reflect attenuation coefficients. To address this, this paper presents deep neural network methods to derive continuous attenuation coefficients for brain PET imaging from MR images. Using only Dixon MR images as network input, the existing U-net structure was adopted and analysis on forty patient datasets showed its superiority over other Dixon-based methods. When both Dixon and zero echo time (ZTE) images are available, a modified U-net structure, named GroupU-net, is proposed to efficiently utilize both Dixon and ZTE information through group convolution modules as the network deepens. Quantitative analysis based on fourteen real patient datasets demonstrates that both network approaches outperform standard methods, and the proposed network structure further reduces PET quantification error compared to the U-net structure.

title: clcNet: Improving the Efficiency of Convolutional Neural Network using Channel Local Convolutions
Abstract: Depthwise convolution and grouped convolution have been successfully employed to improve the efficiency of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This paper proposes that these models can be considered as special cases of a generalized convolution operation called channel local convolution (CLC), where an output channel is computed using a subset of input channels. This definition implies computation dependency relations between input and output channels, representable by a channel dependency graph (CDG).  By modifying the CDG of grouped convolution, a new CLC kernel named interlaced grouped convolution (IGC) is created. Stacking IGC and GC kernels results in a convolution block (named CLC Block) for approximating regular convolution. Using the CDG as an analysis tool, the rule for setting the meta-parameters of IGC and GC and the framework for minimizing the computational cost are derived. A new CNN model named clcNet is then constructed using CLC blocks, showing significantly higher computational efficiency and fewer parameters compared to state-of-the-art networks when evaluated on the ImageNet-1K dataset. Source code is available at https://github.com/dqzhang17/clcnet.torch.

title: Super-sparse Learning in Similarity Spaces
Abstract: In numerous applications, input samples are more naturally represented by their similarities to each other rather than feature vectors. In these settings, machine learning algorithms can become computationally demanding, requiring matching test samples against a large set of reference prototypes. To mitigate this issue, different approaches have been developed to reduce the number of reference prototypes. Current reduction approaches select a small subset of representative prototypes in the space induced by the similarity measure and then separately train the classification function on the reduced subset. However, decoupling these steps may not effectively reduce the number of prototypes without compromising accuracy. This limitation is overcome by jointly learning the classification function along with an optimal set of virtual prototypes, whose number can be fixed a priori or optimized according to application-specific criteria. Creating a super-sparse set of virtual prototypes provides much sparser solutions, drastically reducing complexity at test time at the expense of slightly increased complexity during training. A smaller set of prototypes also leads to more easily interpretable decisions. Empirical evidence shows that the proposed approach can reduce the complexity of Support Vector Machines, LASSO, and ridge regression at test time by up to ten times without significantly affecting their classification accuracy.

title: Learning a Single Convolutional Super-Resolution Network for Multiple Degradations
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed the unprecedented success of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in single image super-resolution (SISR). However, existing CNN-based SISR methods largely assume that a low-resolution (LR) image is bicubicly downsampled from a high-resolution (HR) image, leading to poor performance when the true degradation does not follow this assumption. Moreover, these methods lack scalability in learning a single model to non-blindly handle multiple degradations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a general framework with a dimensionality stretching strategy that enables a single convolutional super-resolution network to take two key factors of the SISR degradation process, namely blur kernel and noise level, as input. Consequently, the super-resolver can handle multiple and even spatially variant degradations, significantly improving practicality. Extensive experimental results on synthetic and real LR images show that the proposed convolutional super-resolution network not only produces favorable results on multiple degradations but is also computationally efficient, providing a highly effective and scalable solution for practical SISR applications.

title: Railway Track Specific Traffic Signal Selection Using Deep Learning
Abstract: As the railway transportation industry actively transitions towards automation, accurate location and inventory of wayside track assets like traffic signals, crossings, switches, mileposts, etc., are crucial. The upcoming Positive Train Control (PTC) regulation will tie many railway safety rules directly to the location of assets like mileposts and signals. Newer speed regulations will be enforced based on the train's location relative to wayside assets. Therefore, railroads need an accurate database of asset types and locations. This paper discusses a real-world use case of detecting railway signals from a camera mounted on a moving locomotive and tracking their locations. The camera is designed to withstand environmental factors on a moving train and provide a consistent steady image at approximately 30 frames per second. Advanced image analysis and deep learning techniques are used to detect signals in these camera images and create a database of their locations. Railway signals differ significantly from road signals in terms of shapes and placement rules with respect to the track. Due to space constraints and traffic densities in urban areas, signals may not be placed on the same side of the track, and multiple lines can run in parallel.  Therefore, it is necessary to associate the detected signal with the specific track on which the train runs. This paper presents a method to associate signals with their respective tracks using a video feed from the front-facing camera mounted on the lead locomotive. A pipeline encompassing track detection, region of interest selection, and signal detection has been implemented, achieving an overall accuracy of 94.7% on a 150km route with 247 signals.

title: Efficient B-mode Ultrasound Image Reconstruction from Sub-sampled RF Data using Deep Learning
Abstract: In portable, three-dimensional, and ultra-fast ultrasound imaging systems, there is an increasing demand for reconstructing high-quality images from a limited number of radio-frequency (RF) measurements due to receiver (Rx) or transmit (Xmit) event sub-sampling. However, RF sub-sampling introduces side lobe artifacts, leading to blurry images with reduced contrast, unsuitable for diagnostic purposes. Existing compressed sensing approaches often require hardware modifications or computationally expensive algorithms, but their quality improvements are limited. To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel deep learning approach that directly interpolates missing RF data by leveraging redundancy in the Rx-Xmit plane. Extensive experimental results using sub-sampled RF data from a multi-line acquisition B-mode system confirm that the proposed method effectively reduces the data rate without compromising image quality.

title: "Zero-Shot" Super-Resolution using Deep Internal Learning
Abstract: Deep Learning has dramatically improved Super-Resolution (SR) performance in recent years. However, these supervised SR methods are limited to specific training data where the acquisition of low-resolution (LR) images from their high-resolution (HR) counterparts is predetermined (e.g., bicubic downscaling) without any distracting artifacts (e.g., sensor noise, image compression, non-ideal PSF, etc.). Real LR images rarely adhere to these restrictions, resulting in poor SR results from state-of-the-art (SotA) methods. This paper introduces "Zero-Shot" SR, which harnesses the power of Deep Learning without relying on prior training. It exploits the internal recurrence of information within a single image and trains a small image-specific CNN at test time on examples extracted solely from the input image. This allows the model to adapt to different settings per image. This enables SR of real old photos, noisy images, biological data, and other images where the acquisition process is unknown or non-ideal. On such images, the proposed method outperforms SotA CNN-based SR methods, as well as previous unsupervised SR methods. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unsupervised CNN-based SR method.

title: Spatial As Deep: Spatial CNN for Traffic Scene Understanding
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are typically built by stacking convolutional operations layer-by-layer. While CNNs demonstrate strong capability in extracting semantics from raw pixels, their capacity to capture spatial relationships of pixels across rows and columns of an image is not fully explored. These relationships are crucial for learning semantic objects with strong shape priors but weak appearance coherences, such as traffic lanes, which are often occluded or not even painted on the road surface. This paper proposes Spatial CNN (SCNN), which generalizes traditional deep layer-by-layer convolutions to slice-by-slice convolutions within feature maps, enabling message passing between pixels across rows and columns in a layer.  SCNN is particularly well-suited for long continuous shape structures or large objects with strong spatial relationships but less appearance clues, such as traffic lanes, poles, and walls. SCNN is applied to a newly released challenging traffic lane detection dataset and the Cityscapes dataset.  The results show that SCNN learns spatial relationships for structural output and significantly improves performance. SCNN outperforms the recurrent neural network (RNN)-based ReNet and MRF+CNN (MRFNet) in the lane detection dataset by 8.7% and 4.6%, respectively. Additionally, SCNN won first place in the TuSimple Benchmark Lane Detection Challenge, achieving an accuracy of 96.53%.

title: Nearly Optimal Robust Subspace Tracking
Abstract: This work investigates the robust subspace tracking (RST) problem and presents one of the first two provable guarantees for it. The goal of RST is to sequentially track arriving data vectors lying in a slowly changing low-dimensional subspace while being robust to corruption by additive sparse outliers. It can be interpreted as a dynamic (time-varying) extension of robust PCA (RPCA), with the minor difference that RST requires a short tracking delay. This paper develops a recursive projected compressive sensing algorithm called Nearly Optimal RST via ReProCS (ReProCS-NORST) because its tracking delay is nearly optimal. It is proven that NORST solves both the RST and the dynamic RPCA problems under weakened standard RPCA assumptions, two simple extra assumptions (slow subspace change and most outlier magnitudes lower bounded), and a few minor assumptions. The guarantee demonstrates that NORST enjoys a near-optimal tracking delay of $O(r\n\\log n \\log(1/\\epsilon))$. Its required delay between subspace change times is the same, and its memory complexity is $n$ times this value. Thus, both are nearly optimal. Here, $n$ is the ambient space dimension, $r$ is the subspaces' dimension, and $\\epsilon$ is the tracking accuracy. NORST also exhibits the best outlier tolerance compared to all previous RPCA or RST methods, both theoretically and empirically (including for real videos), without requiring any model on how the outlier support is generated. This is due to the extra assumptions used by NORST.

title: An ILP Solver for Multi-label MRFs with Connectivity Constraints
Abstract: Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulations of Markov random fields (MRFs) models with global connectivity priors were previously investigated in computer vision (e.g., \\cite{globalinter,globalconn}). These works addressed only Linear Programming (LP) relaxations \\cite{globalinter,globalconn} or simplified versions \\cite{graphcutbase} of the problem. This paper explores the ILP of multi-label MRF with exact connectivity priors via a branch-and-cut method, which provably finds globally optimal solutions. The method enforces connectivity priors iteratively using a cutting plane method and provides feasible solutions with a guarantee on sub-optimality even if terminated prematurely. The proposed ILP can be applied as a post-processing method on top of any existing multi-label segmentation approach.  As it provides globally optimal solutions, it can be used offline to generate ground-truth labeling, serving as a quality check for any fast online algorithm. Furthermore, it can generate ground-truth proposals for weakly supervised segmentation.  The power and usefulness of the model are demonstrated through several experiments on the BSDS500 and PASCAL image datasets, as well as on medical images with trained probability maps. |||

title: Learning a Virtual Codec Based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network to Compress Image
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have proven to be effective in eliminating coding artifacts arising from coarse quantization in traditional codecs. However, training a neural network before the encoder presents a challenge due to the difficulty of back-propagating gradients. This paper proposes an end-to-end image compression framework based on convolutional neural networks to address the non-differentiability of the quantization function in standard codecs. The framework utilizes a feature description neural network to generate a compact representation of the image in a low-dimensional space, thereby significantly reducing data for storage or transmission. Subsequently, a standard image codec like JPEG is applied for further compression, introducing distortions and artifacts, including blocking, detail loss, blurring, and ringing. To mitigate these artifacts, a post-processing neural network is employed. Recognizing the difficulty of directly learning a non-linear function for a standard codec using convolutional neural networks, we propose learning a virtual codec neural network to approximate the projection from the compressed image representation to the post-processed compressed image. This enables efficient gradient back-propagation from the post-processing neural network to the feature description neural network during training. Additionally, an advanced learning algorithm is introduced for training the deep neural networks used for compression. Importantly, this approach maintains compatibility with existing standard codecs, and the learning strategy can be readily extended to other codecs based on convolutional neural networks. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art approaches, particularly at very low bit-rates.

title: An Artificial Neural Network Architecture Based on Context Transformations in Cortical Minicolumns
Abstract: Cortical minicolumns are a model of cortical organization, their function is still under investigation and not accurately reflected in modern neural network architectures used in Artificial Intelligence. This paper proposes a new architecture that emulates the function of minicolumns, allowing them to remember context transformations. The architecture is not based on convolutional neural networks and achieves near-CNN accuracy on the MNIST dataset. Additionally, the proposed architecture demonstrates an ability to train on small datasets.

title: SRPGAN: Perceptual Generative Adversarial Network for Single Image Super Resolution
Abstract: Single image super-resolution (SISR) aims to reconstruct a high-resolution image from a single low-resolution image. While convolutional neural network (CNN) based models have achieved significant advancements in SISR, they struggle to recover high-frequency details in high-resolution images. Previous CNN-based models typically rely on pixel-wise losses, such as L2 loss, resulting in images with high peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) but often blurred and lacking high-frequency details, especially at large scaling factors. This paper proposes a super-resolution perceptual generative adversarial network (SRPGAN) framework for SISR tasks. The framework introduces a robust perceptual loss based on the discriminator of the SRPGAN model, combining it with a Charbonnier content loss and adversarial loss. Compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method excels at reconstructing images with sharp edges and rich details. Evaluation on different benchmarks demonstrates superior structural similarity index (SSIM) scores compared to previous CNN-based approaches.

title: Impression Network for Video Object Detection
Abstract: Video object detection presents greater challenges compared to image object detection. Existing methods, such as applying object detectors frame-by-frame, are slow and inaccurate. Defocus and motion blur weaken visual clues, hindering performance on individual frames. Multi-frame feature fusion techniques improve accuracy but significantly impact speed, while feature propagation-based methods improve speed at the cost of accuracy. This paper proposes the Impression Network, which embodies a natural and efficient feature aggregation mechanism, addressing the trade-off between speed and performance. The network establishes an impression feature by iteratively absorbing sparsely extracted frame features, propagating this feature throughout the video to enhance features of low-quality frames. This impression mechanism enables long-range multi-frame feature fusion among sparse keyframes with minimal overhead. The Impression Network significantly improves per-frame detection baseline on ImageNet VID while achieving three times faster performance (20 fps). The proposed framework offers a new perspective on video feature enhancement.

title: Legged Robot State-Estimation Through Combined Forward Kinematic and Preintegrated Contact Factors
Abstract: State-of-the-art robotic perception systems, relying on Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), cameras, and non-linear optimization techniques, are now being deployed as technologies. However, many of these systems heavily depend on vision and often fail when visual tracking is lost due to lighting or insufficient features. This paper introduces a state-estimation technique for legged robots that incorporates both the robot's kinematic model and its contact with the environment. The technique integrates forward kinematic factors and preintegrated contact factors into a factor graph framework, enabling real-time incremental solving. The forward kinematic factor relates the robot's base pose to a contact frame using noisy encoder measurements. The preintegrated contact factor provides odometry measurements of the contact frame while accounting for potential foot slippage. These factors collectively constrain the graph optimization problem, enabling accurate trajectory estimation. The paper evaluates the method using simulated and real sensory IMU and kinematic data from experiments with a Cassie-series robot. Preliminary experiments indicate that incorporating the proposed method alongside IMU measurements reduces drift and improves localization accuracy, suggesting its potential to enable successful recovery from visual tracking loss.

title: Multi-dimensional imaging data recovery via minimizing the partial sum of tubal nuclear norm
Abstract: This paper explores tensor recovery problems within the tensor singular value decomposition (t-SVD) framework, proposing the partial sum of the tubal nuclear norm (PSTNN) of a tensor. The PSTNN serves as a surrogate for the tensor tubal multi-rank. Two PSTNN-based minimization models are developed for two typical tensor recovery problems: tensor completion and tensor principal component analysis. Two algorithms based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) are proposed to solve the PSTNN-based tensor recovery models. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate the superiority of the proposed PSTNN.

title: A Berkeley View of Systems Challenges for AI
Abstract: The commoditization of computer vision, speech recognition, and machine translation systems, coupled with the widespread deployment of learning-based back-end technologies like digital advertising and intelligent infrastructures, has transitioned Artificial Intelligence (AI) from research labs to production. This progress is driven by unprecedented levels of data and computation, advancements in machine learning methodologies, innovations in systems software and architectures, and the broad accessibility of these technologies. The next generation of AI systems promises to further accelerate these developments, profoundly impacting our lives through frequent interactions and decision-making on our behalf, often in highly personalized contexts. However, realizing this potential presents significant challenges. We need AI systems capable of making timely and safe decisions in unpredictable environments, robust against sophisticated adversaries, and capable of processing ever-increasing amounts of data across organizations and individuals without compromising confidentiality. These challenges are exacerbated by the end of Moore's Law, which limits the data storage and processing capacity of these technologies. This paper outlines several open research directions in systems, architectures, and security that can address these challenges and unlock AI's potential for societal improvement.

title: Mapping the world population one building at a time
Abstract: High-resolution datasets of population density accurately mapping sparsely distributed human populations are lacking at a global scale. Population data is typically obtained through censuses and statistical modeling. Recent methods using remotely sensed data have effectively identified urbanized areas. However, achieving high accuracy in estimating population distribution in rural areas remains challenging due to the need for sufficient sensitivity and resolution to detect sparse populations via remote sensing, alongside reliable global-scale performance. This paper presents a machine learning-based computer vision method for creating global population maps from satellite imagery, with a spatial sensitivity corresponding to individual buildings, suitable for global deployment. Combining this settlement data with census data generates population maps with ~30-meter resolution for 18 countries. Validation indicates an average precision and recall of 0.95 and 0.91, respectively, for building identification and a standard error of approximately 2 or less for population estimates. Analysis of the data reveals that 29% of the world's population lives within 36 km of the nearest urban cluster. The resulting high-resolution population datasets have applications in infrastructure planning, vaccination campaign planning, disaster response efforts, and risk analysis, such as high-accuracy flood risk analysis.
label: AI

title: Reducing Deep Network Complexity with Fourier Transform Methods
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing shallow densely connected neuron network architectures, achieving superior performance to convolution-based neural networks (CNNs) with the added advantages of lower computational burden and significantly fewer training examples required for high prediction accuracy (>98%). The proposed method demonstrates significant performance gains over existing state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. By Fourier transforming the inputs, each point in the training sample gains a representational energy encompassing all weighted information from every other point. This input transformation leads to a reduced complexity neuron network, reduced computational load, and eliminates the need for a large number of training examples to achieve high classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: Deep Burst Denoising
Abstract: Noise is an inherent issue in low-light image capture, exacerbated on mobile devices due to their narrow apertures and small sensors. One strategy for mitigating noise in low-light conditions is to increase the camera's shutter time, allowing each photosite to integrate more light and reduce noise variance. However, long exposures have downsides: (a) bright regions can exceed the sensor range, and (b) camera and scene motion can result in blurred images. Another approach for gathering more light is to capture multiple short, noisy frames in a burst and intelligently integrate their content, avoiding the downsides of long exposures. This paper utilizes the burst-capture strategy and implements intelligent integration through a recurrent fully convolutional deep neural network (CNN). The novel multiframe architecture is designed as a simple addition to any single-frame denoising model, handling an arbitrary number of noisy input frames. It achieves state-of-the-art denoising results on a burst dataset, outperforming published multi-frame techniques like VBM4D and FlexISP. The paper further explores other image enhancement applications by integrating content from multiple frames, demonstrating that the DNN architecture generalizes well to image super-resolution.

title: Multi-Attribute Robust Component Analysis for Facial UV Maps
Abstract: Recent advancements in the field of 3D face alignment "in-the-wild," driven by the collection of large-scale 3D face models and the advent of deep learning, have resulted in methods establishing sparse or dense 3D correspondences between 2D facial images and 3D face models. The use of 3D face alignment introduces new challenges and research directions, particularly in the analysis of facial texture images. Notably, texture is no longer affected by warping effects observed with 2D face alignment methods. However, since facial images are often captured under arbitrary recording conditions, significant missing information and outliers are present, arising from self-occlusion or subjects wearing eyeglasses. Given the availability of annotated databases for face analysis tasks, component analysis techniques are needed to address these challenges. This paper proposes a novel component analysis technique suitable for facial UV maps containing missing information and outliers, while incorporating knowledge from various attributes like age and identity. The proposed Multi-Attribute Robust Component Analysis (MA-RCA) is evaluated on tasks like UV completion and age progression, outperforming existing techniques. Furthermore, MA-RCA is shown to provide weak annotations for training deep learning systems for applications like illumination transfer.

title: Semantic Visual Localization
Abstract: Robust visual localization across a wide range of viewing conditions is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Handling challenging cases is not only demanding but also highly relevant in applications such as life-long localization for augmented reality or autonomous robots. This paper presents a novel approach based on a joint 3D geometric and semantic understanding of the world, enabling successful localization under conditions where previous methods failed. The method leverages a generative model for descriptor learning, trained on semantic scene completion as an auxiliary task. The resulting 3D descriptors are robust to missing observations by encoding high-level 3D geometric and semantic information. Experiments on challenging large-scale localization datasets demonstrate reliable localization under extreme viewpoint, illumination, and geometry changes.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for 3D Keypoint Estimation via View Consistency
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel unsupervised domain adaptation technique for 3D keypoint prediction from a single depth scan or image. The key idea is to exploit the consistency of predictions from different views of the same or similar objects. This view consistency provides effective regularization for keypoint prediction on unlabeled instances. Additionally, a geometric alignment term is introduced to regularize predictions in the target domain. The resulting loss function can be efficiently optimized using alternating minimization. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated on real datasets, with experimental results showing superiority over state-of-the-art general-purpose domain adaptation techniques.
label: AI

title: Lightweight Neural Networks
Abstract: Lightweight neural networks are characterized by a majority of their weights having a value of zero, while the remaining weights are either +1 or -1. These universal approximators require approximately 1.1 bits/weight of storage, exhibit fast forward pass execution, and achieve classification accuracies comparable to conventional continuous-weight networks. Their training regimen prioritizes error reduction initially, followed by weight discretization. They ignore insignificant inputs, remove unnecessary weights, and drop unneeded hidden neurons. These networks have been successfully tested on datasets like MNIST, credit card fraud, and credit card defaults, using networks with 2 to 16 hidden layers and up to 4.4 million weights.
label: AI

title: Pre-training Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: Recurrent neural networks with differentiable attention mechanisms have achieved success in generative and classification tasks. This paper demonstrates that the classification performance of such models can be enhanced by guiding a randomly initialized model to attend to salient regions of the input in early training iterations. Furthermore, it shows that if explicit heuristics for guidance are unavailable, a model pretrained on an unsupervised reconstruction task can discover effective attention policies without supervision. The paper highlights that increased efficiency of the attention mechanism itself contributes to these performance improvements. Based on these insights, the paper introduces bootstrapped glimpse mimicking, a simple and theoretically task-general method for more effectively training attention models. The work draws inspiration from and parallels results on human learning of attention.
label: AI

title: Automated Image Analysis Framework for the High-Throughput Determination of Grapevine Berry Sizes Using Conditional Random Fields
Abstract: Berry size is a crucial fruit trait in grapevine breeding. Non-invasive, image-based phenotyping offers a fast and precise method for monitoring grapevine berry size. This study presents an automated image analysis framework for estimating grapevine berry size from images in a high-throughput manner. The framework involves (i) detecting circular structures potentially representing berries and (ii) classifying them into 'berry' or 'non-berry' classes using a conditional random field. The approach utilizes a one-class classification concept, focusing only on the 'berry' class. Classification is performed through an automated active learning approach, eliminating the need for user interaction during the classification process and adapting automatically to varying image conditions, such as illumination or berry color. The framework was tested on three datasets comprising 139 images taken in an experimental vineyard at different grapevine growth stages according to the BBCH scale. The estimated mean berry size from the framework correlates with manually measured berry size with a correlation coefficient of 0.88.
label: AI

title: Fast Hough Transform and approximation properties of dyadic patterns
Abstract: The Hough transform is a popular low-level computer vision algorithm. Its computationally efficient modification, Fast Hough transform (FHT), utilizes special subsets of the image matrix to approximate geometric lines. These subsets, due to their special structure, are called dyadic patterns. This paper investigates various properties of dyadic patterns. Exact upper bounds on approximation error are derived. In the simplest case, this error is shown to be equal to 1/6 log(n) for n x n sized images, confirming a previous conjecture by Goetz et al.
label: AI

title: Transfer Learning for OCRopus Model Training on Early Printed Books
Abstract: This paper presents a method for significantly reducing character error rates in OCR text obtained from OCRopus models trained on early printed books, when only limited amounts of diplomatic transcriptions are available. This is achieved by building upon existing models during training instead of starting from scratch. To address discrepancies between the character sets of the pretrained model and the additional ground truth, the OCRopus code is adapted to allow for alphabet expansion or reduction. The character set now flexibly adds and deletes characters from the pretrained alphabet when an existing model is loaded. Experiments utilize a self-trained mixed model on early Latin prints and two standard OCRopus models on modern English and German Fraktur texts. Evaluation on seven early printed books shows that training from the Latin mixed model reduces the average error rate by 43% and 26%, respectively, compared to training from scratch with 60 and 150 lines of ground truth, respectively. Additionally, the study demonstrates that even building upon mixed models trained on data unrelated to the newly added training and test data can lead to significantly improved recognition results.
label: AI

title: The exploding gradient problem demystified - definition, prevalence, impact, origin, tradeoffs, and solutions
Abstract: While techniques like Adam, batch normalization, and more recently, SeLU nonlinearities are believed to "solve" the exploding gradient problem, this paper shows that this is not generally true. In a range of popular MLP architectures, exploding gradients persist, limiting the depth to which networks can be effectively trained, both theoretically and practically. The paper explains the occurrence of exploding gradients and highlights the "collapsing domain problem," which can arise in architectures that avoid exploding gradients. ResNets, with significantly lower gradients, can circumvent the exploding gradient problem, enabling effective training of much deeper networks. This is attributed to the Pythagorean equation. Recognizing that any neural network is a residual network, the paper introduces the "residual trick," which reveals that introducing skip connections simplifies the network mathematically. This simplification may be the primary reason for their success.
label: AI

title: CoDraw: Collaborative Drawing as a Testbed for Grounded Goal-driven Communication
Abstract:
This work proposes a goal-driven collaborative task that combines language, perception, and action, specifically developing a collaborative image-drawing game called CoDraw. The game is set in a virtual world containing movable clip art objects. Two players participate: a Teller and a Drawer. The Teller observes an abstract scene with multiple clip art pieces in a semantically meaningful configuration, while the Drawer attempts to reconstruct the scene on an empty canvas using available clip art pieces. The two players communicate using natural language. The CoDraw dataset of ~10K dialogs containing ~138K messages exchanged between human players is collected. The paper defines protocols and metrics to evaluate learned agents in this testbed, highlighting the need for a novel "crosstalk" evaluation condition that pairs agents trained independently on disjoint subsets of the training data. Models for the task are presented and benchmarked using both fully automated evaluation and live gameplay with humans.

title: Visual Based Navigation of Mobile Robots
Abstract: We have developed an algorithm that creates a complete map of the traversable area for a personal assistant robot using only monocular vision. Our approach leverages multiple images captured by a simple webcam to enable obstacle detection and avoidance.  We utilize Simple Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC) for segmentation, reducing memory and computational costs.  The map is generated through a robust and fast inverse perspective mapping and occupancy grid technique, suitable for indoor navigation.
label: AI

title: AI2-THOR: An Interactive 3D Environment for Visual AI
Abstract: A novel framework for visual AI research, called The House of Interactions (THOR), is presented at http://ai2thor.allenai.org. AI2-THOR provides near photorealistic 3D indoor scenes where AI agents can navigate and interact with objects to complete tasks. This platform facilitates research in various areas, including deep reinforcement learning, imitation learning, learning by interaction, planning, visual question answering, unsupervised representation learning, object detection and segmentation, and learning models of cognition. The ultimate goal of AI2-THOR is to drive advancements in visual intelligence by enabling the development of visually intelligent models.
label: AI

title: RAN4IQA: Restorative Adversarial Nets for No-Reference Image Quality Assessment
Abstract: Drawing inspiration from the free-energy brain theory, which suggests that the human visual system strives to reduce uncertainty and enhance perceptual details when encountering distorted images, we introduce Restorative Adversarial Network (RAN).  This GAN-based model is designed for no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA).  RAN mimics the human visual process by incorporating a restorator, a discriminator, and an evaluator. The restorator restores and reconstructs distorted image patches, while the discriminator differentiates between reconstructed patches and pristine distortion-free patches.  Post-restoration, we observe a monotonic relationship between the perceptual distance of the restored and distorted patches and the distortion level. Based on this observation, we define Gain of Restoration (GoR). The evaluator extracts feature representations from the distorted and restored patches to measure GoR and predicts the perceptual score. Ultimately, the quality score of an input image is determined by a weighted sum of the patch scores. Experimental results on Waterloo Exploration, LIVE, and TID2013 demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization ability of RAN compared to existing state-of-the-art NR-IQA models.
label: AI

title: Real Time Visualization of Dynamic Magnetic Fields with a Nanomagnetic FerroLens
Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in nanomagnetism and the development of innovative nanomagnetic materials and devices have unlocked new avenues for research and applications previously inaccessible.  We propose a novel research field and application for nanomagnetism, focusing on the visualization of dynamic magnetic fields in real-time, termed Nano Magnetic Vision. A novel methodology, technique, and apparatus were developed and prototyped to demonstrate and validate this new application. As a practical demonstration, we chose to visualize the dynamic magnetic field of a transmitting antenna.  This application yielded unprecedented high-resolution photographs and real-time color video showcasing the actual dynamic magnetic field within a transmitting radio antenna rod for the first time. The antenna rod is powered by six hundred volts, orthogonal pulses. This unipolar signal operates in the very low frequency (VLF) range. The signal, combined with the extremely short electrical length of the rod, generates a relatively strong fluctuating magnetic field, analogous to the transmitted signal, along and inside the antenna. This field is induced into a ferrolens and becomes visible in real-time within the normal human eyes frequency spectrum. We named the new observation apparatus the SPIONs Superparamagnetic Ferrolens Microscope (SSFM), a powerful passive scientific observation tool with significant potential for future applications.

title: Deep CNN ensembles and suggestive annotations for infant brain MRI segmentation
Abstract: Precise 3D segmentation of infant brain tissues is crucial for comprehensive volumetric studies and quantitative analysis of early brain development. However, achieving accurate segmentation presents significant challenges, especially for 6-month infant brains, due to poor image quality and intrinsic difficulties associated with infant brain MRI. These difficulties include the isointense contrast between white and gray matter and the severe partial volume effect due to small brain sizes. This study addresses these challenges by employing an ensemble of semi-dense fully convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that utilize T1-weighted and T2-weighted MR images as input. We demonstrate a strong correlation between ensemble agreement and segmentation errors. This enables our method to provide measures that can guide local user corrections.  To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first ensemble of 3D CNNs for suggesting annotations within images.  Furthermore, inspired by the recent success of dense networks, we introduce a novel architecture, SemiDenseNet, which directly connects all convolutional layers to the end of the network.  Our architecture facilitates efficient gradient propagation during training while limiting the number of parameters, requiring one order of magnitude fewer parameters than popular medical image segmentation networks, such as 3D U-Net.  Another contribution of our work is the investigation of the impact of early or late fusions of multiple image modalities on the performance of deep architectures. We evaluated our method using the public data of the MICCAI iSEG-2017 Challenge on 6-month infant brain MRI segmentation and achieved very competitive results among 21 teams, ranking first or second in most metrics.

title: A Performance Evaluation of Local Features for Image Based 3D Reconstruction
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive and comparative evaluation of state-of-the-art local features for image-based 3D reconstruction. The evaluated local features include recent developments leveraging powerful machine learning techniques and meticulously crafted handcrafted features. For a comprehensive evaluation, we chose to include both float type features and binary ones.  Two datasets were utilized in our evaluation.  The first dataset comprises various scene types with groundtruth 3D points, containing images of different scenes captured at fixed positions. This dataset enables quantitative performance evaluation of different local features in controlled image capturing scenarios.  The second dataset consists of Internet-scale image sets of several landmarks with numerous unrelated images. This dataset is used for qualitative performance evaluation of different local features in free image collection scenarios.  Our experimental results indicate that binary features are effective in reconstructing scenes from controlled image sequences with significantly reduced processing time compared to float type features. However, for large-scale image sets with many distracting images, float type features exhibit a clear advantage over binary ones.
label: AI

title: Image Super-resolution via Feature-augmented Random Forest
Abstract: Recent random-forest (RF)-based image super-resolution approaches inherit properties from dictionary-learning-based algorithms, but the effectiveness of these properties in RF is often overlooked in the literature.  This paper proposes a novel feature-augmented random forest (FARF) for image super-resolution, which augments conventional gradient-based features with gradient magnitudes. Different feature recipes are formulated at different stages within an RF. Our method offers several advantages.  First, the dictionary-learning-based features are enhanced by incorporating gradient magnitudes, as these non-linear gradient magnitudes exhibit highly discriminative properties. Second, generalized locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) is employed to replace principal component analysis (PCA) for feature dimensionality reduction, and original high-dimensional features are used for the leaf-nodes' regressors instead of compressed ones.  This allows regressors to benefit from higher-dimensional features.  This original-compressed coupled feature sets scheme unifies the unsupervised LSH evaluation for both image super-resolution and content-based image retrieval (CBIR).  Finally, we introduce a generalized weighted ridge regression (GWRR) model for the leaf-nodes' regressors.  Experimental results on various public benchmark datasets demonstrate that our FARF method achieves an average gain of approximately 0.3 dB compared to traditional RF-based methods.  Moreover, a fine-tuned FARF model can match or even outperform some recent state-of-the-art deep-learning-based algorithms.
label: AI

title: Pointwise Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep learning with 3D data, such as reconstructed point clouds and CAD models, has gained significant research interest recently.  However, the potential of utilizing point clouds with convolutional neural networks has not been fully explored. This paper presents a convolutional neural network for semantic segmentation and object recognition with 3D point clouds. At the heart of our network is pointwise convolution, a novel convolution operator applicable to each point within a point cloud. Our fully convolutional network design, while remarkably simple to implement, achieves competitive accuracy in both semantic segmentation and object recognition tasks.
label: AI

title: Robust Estimation of Similarity Transformation for Visual Object Tracking
Abstract: Most existing correlation filter-based tracking approaches estimate simple axis-aligned bounding boxes, and very few are capable of recovering the underlying similarity transformation. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel correlation filter-based tracker that incorporates a robust estimation of similarity transformation for large displacements.  To efficiently search within this large 4-DoF space in real-time, we decompose the problem into two 2-DoF sub-problems and apply an efficient Block Coordinates Descent solver to optimize the estimation result.  Specifically, we employ an efficient phase correlation scheme to simultaneously handle scale and rotation changes in log-polar coordinates. Additionally, a variant of the correlation filter is used to individually predict translational motion. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed tracker achieves highly promising prediction performance compared to state-of-the-art visual object tracking methods while retaining the advantages of high efficiency and simplicity inherent in conventional correlation filter-based tracking methods.
label: AI

title: Adaptive kNN using Expected Accuracy for Classification of Geo-Spatial Data
Abstract: The k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) classification approach, despite its conceptual simplicity, is widely applied due to its effectiveness in practical applications. However, using a global constant k does not always yield an optimal solution, especially for datasets with irregular density distributions of data points. This paper proposes an adaptive kNN classifier where k is dynamically chosen for each instance (point) to be classified, aiming to maximize the expected accuracy of classification. We define the expected accuracy as the accuracy of a set of structurally similar observations. An arbitrary similarity function can be used to identify these observations.  We introduce and evaluate different similarity functions. For evaluation, we utilize five distinct classification tasks based on geospatial data, each comprising (tens of) thousands of items.  Our results demonstrate that the presented expected accuracy measures serve as a good estimator for kNN performance, and the proposed adaptive kNN classifier outperforms common kNN and previously introduced adaptive kNN algorithms.  Furthermore, we show that the range of considered k can be significantly reduced to accelerate the algorithm without compromising classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: SEE: Towards Semi-Supervised End-to-End Scene Text Recognition
Abstract: Detecting and recognizing text in natural scene images is a challenging task that remains unsolved. In recent years, several new systems have been proposed that aim to address at least one of the two sub-tasks (text detection and text recognition).  This paper presents SEE, a step towards semi-supervised neural networks for scene text detection and recognition, capable of end-to-end optimization.  Unlike existing systems, which often rely on multiple deep neural networks and pre-processing steps, we propose a single deep neural network that learns to detect and recognize text from natural images in a semi-supervised manner.  SEE integrates and jointly learns a spatial transformer network, capable of learning to detect text regions within an image, and a text recognition network that processes the identified text regions to recognize their textual content. We outline the concept behind our novel approach and demonstrate its feasibility through a series of experiments on standard benchmark datasets, achieving competitive results.
label: AI

title: Semi-Automatic Algorithm for Breast MRI Lesion Segmentation Using Marker-Controlled Watershed Transformation
Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an effective imaging modality for identifying and localizing breast lesions in women.  Accurate and precise lesion segmentation using a computer-aided-diagnosis (CAD) system is a crucial step in evaluating tumor volume and quantifying tumor characteristics.  However, this task is challenging due to the complex shape, topological structure, and high variance in intensity distribution of breast lesions across patients.  This paper introduces a novel marker-controlled watershed transformation-based approach that utilizes the brightest pixels within a region of interest (defined by experts) as markers to address this challenge and enable accurate lesion segmentation in breast MRI. The proposed approach was evaluated on 106 lesions, including 64 malignant and 42 benign cases. Segmentation results were quantified by comparing them to ground truth labels using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Jaccard index (JI) metrics. The proposed method achieved an average Dice coefficient of 0.7808$\\pm$0.1729 and Jaccard index of 0.6704$\\pm$0.2167. These results highlight the potential of the proposed method for future work related to the segmentation and classification of benign and malignant breast lesions.

title: Learning Compact Recurrent Neural Networks with Block-Term Tensor Decomposition
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are powerful tools for sequence modeling. However, when dealing with high-dimensional inputs, training RNNs becomes computationally expensive due to the large number of model parameters. This hinders RNNs from effectively solving many important computer vision tasks, such as Action Recognition in Videos and Image Captioning. To overcome this limitation, we propose a compact and flexible structure, namely Block-Term tensor decomposition, which significantly reduces the number of parameters in RNNs and improves their training efficiency. Compared to alternative low-rank approximations, such as tensor-train RNN (TT-RNN), our method, Block-Term RNN (BT-RNN), is not only more concise (when using the same rank) but also capable of achieving a better approximation to the original RNNs with significantly fewer parameters. On three challenging tasks, including Action Recognition in Videos, Image Captioning, and Image Generation, BT-RNN outperforms TT-RNN and the standard RNN in terms of both prediction accuracy and convergence rate. Specifically, BT-LSTM utilizes 17,388 times fewer parameters than the standard LSTM while achieving a 15.6\\% accuracy improvement in the Action Recognition task on the UCF11 dataset.

title: Multi-appearance Segmentation and Extended 0-1 Program for Dense Small Object Tracking
Abstract: To address the challenge of fast multi-object tracking for dense small objects in cluster backgrounds, we explore track-oriented multi-hypothesis tracking (TOMHT) with a focus on batch optimization. Employing an autocorrelation-based motion score test and a staged hypotheses merging approach, we construct a homologous hypothesis generation and management method. A novel one-to-many constraint is proposed and implemented to address track exclusions during complex occlusions.  Furthermore, to enhance performance, we develop a multi-appearance segmentation for detection that leverages tree-like topological information and utilizes one threshold for each object.  Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of our methods, showcasing the speed and performance advantages of our tracker.
label: AI

title: Detection and Attention: Diagnosing Pulmonary Lung Cancer from CT by Imitating Physicians
Abstract: This paper presents a novel and efficient method for building a Computer-Aided Diagnoses (CAD) system for lung nodule detection using Computed Tomography (CT).  This task is treated as an Object Detection on Video (VID) problem by mimicking the way a radiologist interprets CT scans. A lung nodule detector is trained to automatically learn nodule features from still images to detect lung nodule candidates with both high recall and accuracy. Unlike previous work, which employed 3-dimensional information surrounding the nodule to reduce false positives, we propose two simple yet effective methods, Multi-slice propagation (MSP) and Motionless-guide suppression (MLGS). These methods analyze sequence information from CT scans to reduce false negatives and suppress false positives. We evaluated our method on the open-source LUNA16 dataset, which includes 888 CT scans, and achieved a state-of-the-art result (Free-Response Receiver Operating Characteristic score of 0.892) with a detection speed (end-to-end within 20 seconds per patient on a single NVidia GTX 1080) significantly faster than existing methods.

title: Learning Binary Residual Representations for Domain-specific Video Streaming
Abstract: We investigate domain-specific video streaming, specifically targeting a scenario where videos streamed from a server to a client are all within the same domain and must be compressed to a small size for low-latency transmission.  Several popular video streaming services, such as the video game streaming services of GeForce Now and Twitch, fall into this category.  While conventional video compression standards like H.264 are commonly used for this task, we hypothesize that leveraging the property that videos are all within the same domain can lead to improved video quality. Based on this hypothesis, we propose a novel video compression pipeline.  We first apply H.264 to compress domain-specific videos.  Then, we train a novel binary autoencoder to encode the remaining domain-specific residual information frame-by-frame into binary representations. These binary representations are compressed and transmitted to the client along with the H.264 stream.  In our experiments, we demonstrate that our pipeline consistently outperforms standard H.264 compression across several benchmark datasets while using the same channel bandwidth.

title: Learning to Navigate by Growing Deep Networks
Abstract: Adaptability is essential for autonomy. Intuitively, for high-dimensional learning problems, such as navigating based on vision, internal models with greater complexity allow for more accurate encoding of available information. However, most learning methods rely on models with fixed structure and complexity. This paper presents a self-supervised framework for robots to learn to navigate without any prior knowledge of the environment by incrementally building the structure of a deep network as new data becomes available. Our framework captures images from a monocular camera and self-labels the images to continuously train and predict actions from a computationally efficient adaptive deep architecture based on Autoencoders (AE) in a self-supervised manner. The deep architecture, named Reinforced Adaptive Denoising Autoencoders (RA-DAE), utilizes reinforcement learning to dynamically modify the network structure by adding or removing neurons.  Experiments conducted in simulation and real-world indoor and outdoor environments assess the potential of self-supervised navigation.  RA-DAE exhibits superior performance compared to equivalent non-adaptive deep learning alternatives and can continuously expand its knowledge, balancing past and present information.

title: Extreme 3D Face Reconstruction: Seeing Through Occlusions
Abstract: Existing single view, 3D face reconstruction methods can produce incredibly detailed 3D results, but typically only for near frontal, unobstructed viewpoints.  We describe a system designed to generate detailed 3D reconstructions of faces viewed under extreme conditions, including out-of-plane rotations and occlusions.  Inspired by the concept of bump mapping, we propose a layered approach that decouples the estimation of global shape from its mid-level details (e.g., wrinkles).  We first estimate a coarse 3D face shape, which serves as a foundation, and then separately layer this foundation with details represented by a bump map. We demonstrate how a deep convolutional encoder-decoder can be used to estimate these bump maps.  Furthermore, we show how this approach naturally extends to generate plausible details for occluded facial regions.  We extensively tested our approach and its components, quantitatively demonstrating the invariance of our estimated facial details.  Additionally, we provide numerous qualitative examples showcasing that our method produces detailed 3D face shapes in viewing conditions where existing state-of-the-art methods often fail.

title: Weakly Supervised Action Localization by Sparse Temporal Pooling Network
Abstract: We propose a weakly supervised temporal action localization algorithm for untrimmed videos using convolutional neural networks. Our algorithm learns from video-level class labels and predicts temporal intervals of human actions without requiring temporal localization annotations.  Our network is designed to identify a sparse subset of key segments associated with target actions in a video using an attention module and fuse these key segments through adaptive temporal pooling. Our loss function comprises two terms: one that minimizes video-level action classification error and another that enforces the sparsity of segment selection. At inference time, we extract and score temporal proposals using temporal class activations and class-agnostic attentions to estimate the time intervals corresponding to target actions. The proposed algorithm achieves state-of-the-art results on the THUMOS14 dataset and outstanding performance on ActivityNet1.3 despite its weak supervision.
label: AI

title: MentorNet: Learning Data-Driven Curriculum for Very Deep Neural Networks on Corrupted Labels
Abstract: Recent deep networks are capable of memorizing the entire dataset even when the labels are completely random.  To address overfitting on corrupted labels, we propose a novel technique that involves learning another neural network, called MentorNet, to supervise the training of the base deep network, namely StudentNet.  During training, MentorNet provides a curriculum (sample weighting scheme) for StudentNet to prioritize samples with likely correct labels.  Unlike existing curricula, which are typically predefined by human experts, MentorNet learns a data-driven curriculum dynamically with StudentNet.  Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the generalization performance of deep networks trained on corrupted training data.   Notably, to the best of our knowledge, we achieve the best-published result on WebVision, a large benchmark containing 2.2 million images with real-world noisy labels. The code is available at https://github.com/google/mentornet |||

title: Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: A fully automated deep learning approach for bone age assessment is presented, utilizing U-Net, ResNet-50, and custom VGG-style neural networks trained end-to-end on the Pediatric Bone Age Challenge dataset. The study investigates the importance of specific hand bones for automated bone age analysis and evaluates the method's performance across skeletal development stages. The proposed approach outperforms other common methods for bone age assessment.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Histopathology Image Synthesis
Abstract: An unsupervised method for synthesizing large histopathology image datasets suitable for supervised training is proposed. The pipeline generates initial synthetic images with paired nuclei segmentation masks, refines them using a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), and trains a task-specific CNN. The synthetic images are realistic, representative, and challenging for training task-specific CNNs. The method significantly outperforms supervised methods for nucleus segmentation in the absence of supervised data and shows improved performance even when supervised data is available.

title: Learning Low-shot facial representations via 2D warping
Abstract: This work focuses on investigating the impact of the 2D warping module on one-shot face recognition.

title: Real-time Egocentric Gesture Recognition on Mobile Head Mounted Displays
Abstract: This paper presents a real-time egocentric hand gesture detection and localization system for mobile VR HMDs. Contributions include a novel mixed-reality data collection tool for automatic annotation, a large-scale egocentric hand gesture dataset, and a neural network that achieves high precision on gesture recognition across 8 classes.
label: AI

title: Multidimensional Data Tensor Sensing for RF Tomographic Imaging
Abstract: A novel tensor sensing approach for highly accurate estimation of real-world three-dimensional spaces is proposed. The approach utilizes a transform-based tensor model to formulate a tensor sensing problem and employs a fast alternating minimization algorithm (Alt-Min) to solve it. Evaluation on IKEA 3D data demonstrates significant improvement in recovery error and convergence speed compared to prior tensor-based compressed sensing.
label: AI

title: Rethinking Spatiotemporal Feature Learning: Speed-Accuracy Trade-offs in Video Classification
Abstract: This paper addresses challenges in video analysis, particularly spatial feature representation, temporal information representation, and model complexity. The study investigates the use of 3D CNNs and explores the replacement of 3D convolutions with low-cost 2D convolutions to achieve a balance between speed and accuracy. The results show that temporal representation learning on high-level semantic features is more beneficial, leading to an effective and efficient video classification system that performs well on various benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Self-Supervised Relative Depth Learning for Urban Scene Understanding
Abstract: A deep network trained with fully automatic supervision to predict relative scene depth from single images is presented. This network, trained using simple videos of cars moving through a scene, exhibits improved performance in downstream tasks like semantic segmentation, road segmentation, and monocular depth estimation. The method outperforms other automatically supervised methods and even surpasses supervised pre-training with ImageNet for monocular depth estimation.
label: AI

title: MaskLab: Instance Segmentation by Refining Object Detection with Semantic and Direction Features
Abstract: MaskLab, a model for instance segmentation that simultaneously solves object detection and semantic segmentation, is proposed. The model generates box detection, semantic segmentation, and direction prediction outputs. By combining semantic and direction prediction within each region of interest, MaskLab effectively distinguishes between objects of different semantic classes and separates instances of the same class. The model shows comparable performance to other state-of-the-art models on the COCO instance segmentation benchmark.
label: AI

title: Symbol detection in online handwritten graphics using Faster R-CNN
Abstract: The Faster R-CNN object detection algorithm is evaluated as a general method for symbol detection in handwritten graphics, including diagrams and mathematical expressions. The study analyzes different configurations of the algorithm and addresses challenges related to the handwritten nature of the data. Evaluation on publicly available datasets demonstrates that Faster R-CNN can be effectively used for symbol detection in handwritten graphics.
label: AI

title: GMM-Based Synthetic Samples for Classification of Hyperspectral Images With Limited Training Data
Abstract: A method for enriching the feature matrix with synthetically generated sample points to address the challenge of multi-class classification in hyperspectral remote sensing with limited training data is proposed. Synthetic data is sampled from a GMM fitted to each class of the limited training data, effectively replacing missing training samples. The approach demonstrates significant improvement in classification performance on two hyperspectral datasets.
label: AI

title: Mathematics of Deep Learning
Abstract: This tutorial provides a mathematical justification for several properties of deep networks, including global optimality, geometric stability, and invariance of learned representations, contributing to the understanding of the success of deep learning systems.
label: AI

title: Regularization and Optimization strategies in Deep Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: This article explores theoretical concepts and mathematical formulations of regularization and optimization strategies commonly used in ConvNet architectures. The focus is on addressing limitations of ConvNets, such as high computational cost, slow convergence, and overfitting, and how these techniques enhance network expressiveness.
label: AI

title: An Enhanced Hybrid MobileNet
Abstract: A novel architecture to improve the MobileNet for image recognition on mobile and embedded devices is proposed. The architecture utilizes a depth multiplier and combines it with either Fractional Max Pooling or max pooling, reducing computational cost and increasing accuracy compared to the original MobileNet.
label: AI

title: UV-GAN: Adversarial Facial UV Map Completion for Pose-invariant Face Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a framework for training a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) to complete facial UV maps extracted from in-the-wild images. The framework utilizes a meticulously designed architecture that combines local and global adversarial DCNNs to learn an identity-preserving UV completion model. By attaching the completed UV to the fitted mesh and generating instances of arbitrary poses, the method improves pose variations for training deep face recognition models and minimizes pose discrepancy during testing, leading to better performance.
label: AI

title: Learning Disentangling and Fusing Networks for Face Completion Under Structured Occlusions
Abstract: A jointly disentangling and fusing Generative Adversarial Network (DF-GAN) for generative face completion under structured occlusions is proposed. The method treats face completion and corruption as disentangling and fusing processes of clean faces and occlusions. DF-GAN learns transformations between three domains (occluded faces, clean faces, and occlusions) using unpaired data and allows for simulating structure occlusions by modifying latent representations. The method demonstrates effectiveness for face completion under structured occlusions in Meshface verification.
label: AI

title: Stochastic Low-Rank Bandits
Abstract: LowRankElim, an algorithm for finding the maximum entry of a stochastic low-rank matrix from sequential observations, is proposed. The algorithm identifies a class of non-negative matrices for which the maximum entry can be found efficiently and derives a regret bound that depends on problem-specific constants but not on the matrix dimensions.
label: AI

title: The Effectiveness of Data Augmentation in Image Classification using Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper explores and compares multiple data augmentation techniques for image classification, including traditional transformations, GAN-based image generation, and neural augmentation. The study investigates the effectiveness of each technique on a constrained subset of the ImageNet dataset, highlighting successes and shortcomings.
label: AI

title: Transfer Adversarial Hashing for Hamming Space Retrieval
Abstract: Transfer Adversarial Hashing (TAH), a hybrid deep architecture for transfer retrieval in large-scale image retrieval, is presented. TAH incorporates a pairwise t-distribution cross-entropy loss to learn concentrated hash codes and an adversarial network to align data distributions between source and target domains. This method generates compact transfer hash codes for efficient retrieval in both source and target domains, achieving state-of-the-art performance on standard datasets.
label: AI

title: Deep Quaternion Networks
Abstract: This work explores the benefits of using hyper-complex numbers, specifically quaternions, in deep learning. The paper reviews quaternion convolutions, develops a novel quaternion weight initialization scheme, and proposes algorithms for quaternion batch-normalization. These components are tested in classification and segmentation models, demonstrating improved convergence compared to real-valued and complex-valued networks, particularly for segmentation.
label: AI

title: Low-dose spectral CT reconstruction using L0 image gradient and tensor dictionary
Abstract: An improved tensor dictionary learning method (L0TDL) for low-dose spectral CT reconstruction is proposed, incorporating an image gradient L0-norm constraint to enhance edge information preservation. L0TDL utilizes the similarity of spectral CT images and emphasizes spatial sparsity. The method demonstrates superior performance compared to other competing methods in both numerical simulations and real mouse studies. |||
label: AI

title: Fusing Multiple Multiband Images
Abstract: We propose a method for fusing multiple multiband images of the same scene, using a maximum-likelihood estimator for the endmember abundance matrix. To improve robustness and address potential ill-posedness, we incorporate a vector total-variation penalty term with nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints on the endmember abundances. This regularization leverages the prior knowledge that natural images are mostly composed of piecewise smooth regions, facilitating the exploitation of spatial information. By utilizing the circular convolution theorem and fast Fourier transform, the computational complexity of our algorithm is significantly reduced. Experiments on real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art fusion algorithms, particularly when fusing more than two multiband images.
label: AI

title: Im2Pano3D: Extrapolating 360 Structure and Semantics Beyond the Field of View
Abstract: Im2Pano3D is a convolutional neural network that generates a dense 3D structure and semantic label probability distribution for a full 360° panoramic view of an indoor scene, given only a partial observation (≤50%) in the form of an RGB-D image. The network leverages strong contextual priors learned from large-scale synthetic and real-world indoor scenes. To simplify 3D structure prediction, we parameterize surfaces with their plane equations and train the model to predict these parameters directly. We utilize multiple loss functions to ensure both pixel-level accuracy and global context consistency. Experiments demonstrate that Im2Pano3D achieves significant performance improvements over alternative approaches, predicting semantics and 3D structure with over 56% pixel accuracy and less than 0.52 meters average distance error.
label: AI

title: Face-from-Depth for Head Pose Estimation on Depth Images
Abstract: We introduce a complete framework for head and shoulder pose estimation using only depth images, aiming to provide reliable solutions for people monitoring and behavior understanding, particularly in scenarios with unstable or poor illumination conditions. Our framework includes a head detection and localization module, creating an end-to-end system. The core element is a Convolutional Neural Network, called POSEidon+, which takes three types of images as input and outputs the 3D angles of the pose. Additionally, a Face-from-Depth component based on a Deterministic Conditional GAN generates a face from the corresponding depth image, enhancing system performance. We evaluate our framework on two public datasets, Biwi Kinect Head Pose and ICT-3DHP, and a new challenging dataset, Pandora, inspired by automotive setups. Results demonstrate that our method surpasses several state-of-the-art approaches using both intensity and depth input data, operating in real-time at over 30 frames per second.
label: AI

title: Camera Calibration for Daylight Specular-Point Locus
