Abstract: This paper presents a new camera calibration method for identifying a straight-line locus in a special color feature space, traversed by daylight illuminants and approximately followed by specular points. This calibration enables the recovery of the illuminant color in a scene using the calibrated camera. We prove theoretically that any candidate specular points, under a daylight illuminant for a specific camera, must lie on a straight line in log-chromaticity space when using a geometric-mean denominator. This holds under the assumptions of daylight illuminants being approximated by Planckians and camera sensors being narrowband or spectrally sharpened. We demonstrate how to calibrate a camera to discover this locus. The identified curve finds applications in illuminant detection and image re-lighting for displaying images under lighting with different color temperatures.
label: AI

title: Fingerprint Spoof Buster
Abstract: This study focuses on developing accurate, generalizable, and efficient algorithms for detecting fingerprint spoof attacks, which can compromise the security of fingerprint recognition systems. We propose a deep convolutional neural network approach utilizing local patches centered and aligned using fingerprint minutiae. Experiments on three public-domain LivDet datasets (2011, 2013, and 2015) demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracies in fingerprint spoof detection for intra-sensor, cross-material, cross-sensor, and cross-dataset testing scenarios. For instance, our approach achieves 99.03% average accuracy on LivDet 2015, surpassing the 95.51% achieved by the LivDet 2015 competition winners. Additionally, we present two new fingerprint presentation attack datasets containing over 20,000 images, using two fingerprint readers and over 12 different spoof fabrication materials. Furthermore, we introduce a graphical user interface, Fingerprint Spoof Buster, that allows operators to visually examine the local regions of the fingerprint identified as live or spoof, providing more insight than traditional approaches that rely on a single score.
label: AI

title: Image Registration for the Alignment of Digitized Historical Documents
Abstract: This paper explores the suitability of different registration algorithms for hyperspectral historical image registration applications. After evaluating various algorithms, we choose an intensity-based registration algorithm with a curved transformation model. We select cubic B-splines for the transformation model due to their ability to handle non-rigid deformations in hyperspectral images. From a number of similarity measures, we identified residual complexity and localized mutual information as being well-suited for our application. Both measures demonstrate acceptable performance in handling various challenges, such as capture range, non-stationary and spatially varying intensity distortions, and multi-modality that occur in our application.
label: AI

title: Learning a Complete Image Indexing Pipeline
Abstract: A complete image indexing system for large-scale applications consists of two components: an inverted file index for restricting search to a relevant subset and an approximate distance computation mechanism for rapidly scanning these lists. While recent advancements in supervised deep learning have improved the latter component, the former remains reliant on unsupervised clustering in the literature. In this work, we propose the first system that learns both components within a unified neural framework of structured binary encoding.
label: AI

title: Data Distillation: Towards Omni-Supervised Learning
Abstract: We delve into omni-supervised learning, a specific regime of semi-supervised learning that leverages all available labeled data along with internet-scale unlabeled data. Omni-supervised learning is lower-bounded by performance on existing labeled datasets, presenting the potential to surpass state-of-the-art fully supervised methods. We introduce data distillation, a method that ensembles predictions from multiple transformations of unlabeled data using a single model, to automatically generate new training annotations. We argue that visual recognition models have recently attained sufficient accuracy to enable the application of classic self-training ideas to challenging real-world data. Our experimental results demonstrate that data distillation surpasses the performance of using solely labeled data from the COCO dataset for human keypoint detection and general object detection.
label: AI

title: 3D Object Classification via Spherical Projections
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for classifying 3D objects by projecting them onto a spherical domain centered around their barycenter and developing a neural network to classify the spherical projection. We introduce two complementary projections: one capturing depth variations of a 3D object and the other capturing contour information viewed from different angles. Spherical projections combine the advantages of both image-based and 3D-based classification methods. Specifically, they are locally planar, enabling the use of massive image datasets (e.g., ImageNet) for pre-training, and similar to voxel-based methods, encoding complete 3D object information in a single neural network. Our network design fully leverages these benefits. Experimental results on ModelNet40 and ShapeNetCore demonstrate that our method outperforms prior approaches.
label: AI

title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks for Emoji Synthesis with Word Embedding Manipulation
Abstract: Emojis, ubiquitous in modern digital communication, contribute to nuanced and subtle emotional expression beyond plain text. This paper presents a novel application of deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (DC-GANs) with an optimized training procedure for generating realistic emojis. We show that incorporating word embeddings conditioned on Google's word2vec model into the network enables the generator to synthesize emojis virtually indistinguishable from real ones.
label: AI

title: Deception Detection in Videos
Abstract: We present a system for automated deception detection in real-life courtroom trial videos using various modalities like vision, audio, and text. On the vision side, our system utilizes classifiers trained on low-level video features to predict human micro-expressions, which are then used as features for deception prediction. Surprisingly, IDT (Improved Dense Trajectory) features, commonly employed for action recognition, also excel at predicting deception in videos. We fuse the scores of classifiers trained on IDT features and high-level micro-expressions to enhance performance. MFCC (Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients) features from the audio domain further improve performance, while transcript information proves less beneficial for our system. Using various classifiers, our automated system achieves an AUC of 0.877 (10-fold cross-validation) when evaluated on subjects outside the training set, outperforming state-of-the-art methods that rely on human annotations of micro-expressions by 5%. Combining with human annotations of micro-expressions further elevates our AUC to 0.922. We also present results from a user study analyzing average human performance on this task, the modalities they use for deception detection, and their performance when only one modality is accessible. Our project page can be found at [https://doubaibai.github.io/DARE/](https://doubaibai.github.io/DARE/).
label: AI

title: Logo Synthesis and Manipulation with Clustered Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Designing a logo for a new brand is a lengthy and iterative process involving a designer and a client. We explore the potential of machine learning to automate the creative task of the designer. For this purpose, we build a dataset, LLD, of 600k+ logos crawled from the web. Training Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for logo synthesis on this multi-modal data poses challenges and often results in mode collapse for existing methods. We propose utilizing synthetic labels obtained through clustering to disentangle and stabilize GAN training. This allows us to generate a diverse range of plausible logos and demonstrate latent space exploration techniques for interactive logo design. Furthermore, we validate our clustered GAN training on CIFAR-10, achieving state-of-the-art Inception scores when using synthetic labels derived from clustering the features of an ImageNet classifier. GANs can effectively handle multi-modal data using synthetic labels achieved through clustering, highlighting the creative potential of these techniques for logo synthesis and manipulation. Our dataset and models will be made publicly available at [https://data.vision.ee.ethz.ch/cvl/lld/](https://data.vision.ee.ethz.ch/cvl/lld/).
label: AI

title: Review. Machine learning techniques for traffic sign detection
Abstract: An automatic road sign detection system localizes road signs from images captured by a vehicle's on-board camera, assisting drivers in safe navigation. Most existing algorithms include a preprocessing step, feature extraction, and detection step. This paper categorizes road sign detection methods into two groups: general machine learning and neural networks. This review addresses the challenges associated with automatic road sign detection, provides an overview of popular methods developed to tackle the problem, and compares their features.
label: AI

title: Decision-Based Adversarial Attacks: Reliable Attacks Against Black-Box Machine Learning Models
Abstract: Many machine learning algorithms are susceptible to imperceptible input perturbations, known as adversarial perturbations. The risk these perturbations pose to real-world applications has been unclear, as most methods for generating them require detailed model information (gradient-based attacks) or confidence scores (score-based attacks), which are often unavailable in real-world scenarios. Transfer-based attacks, relying on cumbersome substitute models and access to training data, are commonly used but vulnerable to defenses. This paper emphasizes the importance of attacks that solely rely on the final model decision. These decision-based attacks are applicable to real-world black-box models (e.g., autonomous cars), require less knowledge and are easier to apply than transfer-based attacks, and are more robust to simple defenses than gradient- or score-based attacks. Previous attacks in this category were limited to simple models or datasets. We introduce the Boundary Attack, a decision-based attack that starts with a large adversarial perturbation and reduces it while maintaining adversarial properties. This attack is conceptually simple, requires minimal hyperparameter tuning, does not rely on substitute models, and is competitive with the best gradient-based attacks in standard computer vision tasks like ImageNet. We apply the attack to two black-box algorithms from Clarifai.com. The Boundary Attack, and the class of decision-based attacks in general, opens new avenues for studying machine learning model robustness and raises concerns regarding the safety of deployed machine learning systems. An implementation of the attack is available as part of Foolbox at [https://github.com/bethgelab/foolbox](https://github.com/bethgelab/foolbox).
label: AI

title: 3D Face Reconstruction with Region Based Best Fit Blending Using Mobile Phone for Virtual Reality Based Social Media
Abstract: The use of virtual reality (VR) is rapidly increasing, prompting researchers to develop VR-based social media platforms. For this purpose, it's crucial to have user avatars that resemble them and are easily generated by accessible devices like mobile phones. This paper proposes a novel method for recreating a 3D human face model from a phone camera image or video data, focusing more on model shape than texture for facial recognition. We detect 68 facial feature points and use them to divide the face into four regions. For each region, we find the best-fitting models and morph them together to find the best-fitting models for each area. These are then combined and further morphed to restore the original facial proportions. We also present a method for texturing the resulting model, using the aforementioned feature points to generate a texture for the final model.
label: AI

title: Benchmarking Single Image Dehazing and Beyond
Abstract: We present a comprehensive study and evaluation of existing single image dehazing algorithms using a new large-scale benchmark, REalistic Single Image DEhazing (RESIDE), containing both synthetic and real-world hazy images. RESIDE highlights diverse data sources and image contents, and is divided into five subsets, each serving distinct training or evaluation purposes. We provide a rich variety of dehazing algorithm evaluation criteria, including full-reference metrics, no-reference metrics, subjective evaluation, and novel task-driven evaluation. Experiments on RESIDE shed light on the comparisons and limitations of state-of-the-art dehazing algorithms, suggesting promising future directions.
label: AI

title: Direction-aware Spatial Context Features for Shadow Detection
Abstract: Shadow detection, a fundamental and challenging task, requires understanding global image semantics and handling diverse backgrounds around shadows. This paper presents a novel network for shadow detection by analyzing image context in a direction-aware manner. To achieve this, we formulate a direction-aware attention mechanism within a spatial recurrent neural network (RNN) by introducing attention weights during the aggregation of spatial context features in the RNN. By learning these weights through training, we recover direction-aware spatial context (DSC) for detecting shadows. This design is integrated into the DSC module and embedded in a CNN to learn DSC features at different levels. We also employ a weighted cross entropy loss to enhance training effectiveness. We evaluate our network using two common shadow detection benchmark datasets, and results show that our network outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 97% accuracy and a 38% reduction in balance error rate.
label: AI

title: Deep learning enhanced mobile-phone microscopy
Abstract: Mobile phones have enabled the creation of field-portable, cost-effective imaging and sensing technologies that approach laboratory-grade instrument performance. However, the optical imaging interfaces of mobile phones are not designed for microscopy and introduce spatial and spectral distortions when imaging microscopic specimens. This paper reports on the use of deep learning to correct these distortions introduced by mobile-phone-based microscopes. This allows the production of high-resolution, denoised, and color-corrected images, matching the performance of benchtop microscopes with high-end objective lenses and extending their limited depth-of-field. After training a convolutional neural network, we successfully imaged various samples, including blood smears, histopathology tissue sections, and parasites. The recorded images were highly compressed for easy storage and transmission in telemedicine applications. This method is applicable to other low-cost, aberrated imaging systems, potentially offering alternatives to costly and bulky microscopes. Additionally, it provides a framework for standardizing optical images for clinical and biomedical applications.
label: AI

title: A vision based system for underwater docking
Abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) have been deployed for underwater exploration. However, their potential is limited by their on-board battery energy and data storage capacity. This problem has been addressed using docking systems for underwater recharging and data transfer for AUVs. This paper proposes a vision-based framework for underwater docking following these systems. The framework consists of two modules: (i) a detection module that provides location information on underwater docking stations in 2D images captured by an on-board camera, and (ii) a pose estimation module that recovers the relative 3D position and orientation between docking stations and AUVs from the 2D images. To ensure robust and credible detection of docking stations, we propose a convolutional neural network called Docking Neural Network (DoNN). For accurate pose estimation, a perspective-n-point algorithm is integrated into our framework. We collected a dataset of 2D images, named Underwater Docking Images Dataset (UDID), in an experimental water pool to evaluate our framework in underwater docking tasks. To our knowledge, UDID is the first publicly available underwater docking dataset. Experiments first evaluate the performance of the proposed detection module on UDID and its deformed variations. Next, we assess the accuracy of the pose estimation module through ground experiments, as obtaining true relative position and orientation underwater is not feasible. Finally, we examine the pose estimation module through underwater experiments in our experimental water pool. Experimental results show that our framework effectively and successfully detects docking stations and estimates their relative pose compared to state-of-the-art baseline systems.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning for Reliable Mobile Edge Analytics in Intelligent Transportation Systems
Abstract: Intelligent transportation systems (ITSs) will be a key component of future smart cities. However, realizing their full potential requires ultra-low latency and reliable data analytics solutions capable of combining heterogeneous data streams from the ITS network and its environment in real-time. Conventional cloud-centric data processing techniques cannot provide these capabilities due to their high communication and computing latency. Edge-centric solutions tailored to the unique ITS environment are necessary. This paper introduces an edge analytics architecture for ITSs where data is processed at the vehicle or roadside smart sensor level to overcome ITS latency and reliability challenges. With the increasing capability of passengers' mobile devices and intra-vehicle processors, a distributed edge computing architecture can leverage deep learning techniques for reliable mobile sensing in ITSs. This paper investigates ITS mobile edge analytics challenges related to heterogeneous data, autonomous control, vehicular platoon control, and cyber-physical security, and proposes various deep learning solutions for these challenges. These solutions will enable ITS edge analytics by empowering ITS devices with powerful computer vision and signal processing capabilities. Preliminary results demonstrate that the proposed edge analytics architecture, coupled with the power of deep learning algorithms, can provide a reliable, secure, and truly smart transportation environment. |||
label: AI

title: 200x Low-dose PET Reconstruction using Deep Learning
Abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is widely used in various clinical applications, including cancer diagnosis, heart disease, and neurological disorders. The use of radioactive tracers in PET imaging raises concerns due to the risk of radiation exposure. To minimize this risk, efforts have been made to reduce the amount of radiotracer usage. However, lower doses result in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and loss of information, both of which significantly affect clinical diagnosis. Additionally, the ill-conditioning of low-dose PET image reconstruction makes it a challenging problem for iterative reconstruction algorithms. Previous methods proposed are often complicated and slow, and they still cannot produce satisfactory results at significantly low doses. This paper proposes a deep learning method to address this issue using an encoder-decoder residual deep network with concatenate skip connections. Experiments show that the proposed method can reconstruct low-dose PET images to a standard-dose quality with only a two-hundredth dose. Various cost functions for training the model are explored. A multi-slice input strategy is introduced to provide the network with more structural information and make it more robust to noise. Evaluation on ultra-low-dose clinical data demonstrates that the proposed method achieves better results than state-of-the-art methods and reconstructs images with comparable quality using only 0.5% of the original regular dose.
label: AI

title: Im2Flow: Motion Hallucination from Static Images for Action Recognition
Abstract: Existing methods for recognizing actions in static images rely solely on visual appearances, including objects, scenes, and body poses, to differentiate action classes. However, these models lack information about the rich dynamic structure and motions that define human activity. This paper proposes an approach that hallucinates the unobserved future motion implied by a single snapshot to enhance static-image action recognition. The key idea is to learn a prior over short-term dynamics from thousands of unlabeled videos, infer the anticipated optical flow on novel static images, and then train discriminative models that exploit both streams of information. The main contributions are twofold: First, an encoder-decoder convolutional neural network and a novel optical flow encoding are devised to translate a static image into an accurate flow map. Second, the paper demonstrates the power of hallucinated flow for recognition, successfully transferring the learned motion into a standard two-stream network for activity recognition. Experiments conducted on seven datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach. Not only does it achieve state-of-the-art accuracy for dense optical flow prediction, but it also consistently improves the recognition of actions and dynamic scenes.
label: AI

title: Learning Compressible 360° Video Isomers
Abstract: Standard video encoders developed for conventional narrow field-of-view video are often applied to 360° video, with reasonable results. However, this approach commits arbitrarily to a projection of the spherical frames, leading to some orientations of a 360° video being more compressible than others once projected. This paper introduces a novel approach to predict the sphere rotation that will yield the maximal compression rate. Given video clips in their original encoding, a convolutional neural network learns the association between a clip's visual content and its compressibility at different rotations of a cubemap projection. When presented with a new video, this learning-based approach efficiently infers the most compressible direction in one shot, eliminating the need for repeated rendering and compression of the source video. Validation on thousands of video clips and multiple popular video codecs reveals that this untapped dimension of 360° compression offers substantial potential: "good" rotations are typically 8-10% more compressible than "bad" ones, and the learning approach can reliably predict them 82% of the time.
label: AI

title: Character-Based Handwritten Text Transcription with Attention Networks
Abstract: This paper explores handwritten text recognition (HTR) using attentional encoder-decoder networks trained on sequences of characters, rather than words. Experiments are conducted on lines of text from popular handwriting datasets, comparing different activation functions for the attention mechanism used to align image pixels and target characters. Results show that softmax attention focuses heavily on individual characters, while sigmoid attention focuses on multiple characters at each step of the decoding process. When the sequence alignment is one-to-one, softmax attention learns a more precise alignment at each step of the decoding, while the alignment generated by sigmoid attention is much less precise. When a linear function is used to obtain attention weights, the model predicts a character by considering the entire sequence of characters and performs poorly due to the lack of a precise alignment between the source and target. Future research may investigate HTR in natural scene images, as the model can transcribe handwritten text without requiring segmentation or bounding boxes of text in images.
label: AI

title: Deep metric learning for multi-labelled radiographs
Abstract: Many radiological studies reveal the presence of multiple co-existing abnormalities, each represented by a distinct visual pattern. This paper addresses the problem of learning a distance metric for plain radiographs that captures a notion of "radiological similarity": two chest radiographs are considered similar if they share similar abnormalities. Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNs) are employed to learn a low-dimensional embedding for radiographs equipped with the desired metric. Two loss functions are proposed to handle multi-labeled images and potentially noisy labels. A large-scale study involving over 745,000 chest radiographs, whose labels were automatically extracted from free-text radiological reports using a natural language processing system, is conducted. Using 4,500 validated exams, the paper demonstrates that the methodology performs satisfactorily on clustering and image retrieval tasks. Notably, the learned metric successfully separates normal exams from those containing radiological abnormalities.
label: AI

title: Investigating the Impact of Data Volume and Domain Similarity on Transfer Learning Applications
Abstract: Transfer learning enables practitioners to recognize and apply knowledge gained from previous tasks (source task) to new tasks or domains (target task) that share commonalities. The performance of transfer learning models is significantly influenced by: (a) the size of the target dataset, and (b) the similarity in distribution between source and target domains. This paper investigates the impact of target dataset size and source/target domain similarity on model performance through a series of experiments. The findings indicate that more data consistently improves model performance, with performance increasing linearly with the log of data size until data saturation is reached. When source/target domains differ, more data is required, and fine tuning yields better performance than feature extraction. Conversely, when source/target domains are similar and data size is small, fine tuning and feature extraction provide equivalent performance. This research aims to inspire further exploration of the significance of data in developing more accurate statistical models by providing a quantitative investigation into the effects of data volume and domain similarity in transfer learning.
label: AI

title: Training Ensembles to Detect Adversarial Examples
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel ensemble method for detecting and classifying adversarial examples generated by state-of-the-art attacks, including DeepFool and C&W. The method trains the members of an ensemble to have low classification error on random benign examples while simultaneously minimizing agreement on examples outside the training distribution. Evaluation is conducted on both MNIST and CIFAR-10, against oblivious and both white- and black-box adversaries.
label: AI

title: Eye In-Painting with Exemplar Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: This paper presents Exemplar GANs (ExGANs), a novel approach to in-painting that preserves and accounts for the identity of the object to be removed or changed at inference time. ExGANs are a type of conditional GAN that leverage exemplar information to produce high-quality, personalized in-painting results. Exemplar information is utilized in the form of a reference image of the region to be in-painted, or a perceptual code describing that object. Unlike previous conditional GAN formulations, this extra information can be inserted at multiple points within the adversarial network, enhancing its descriptive power. The paper demonstrates that ExGANs can produce photo-realistic personalized in-painting results that are both perceptually and semantically plausible by applying them to the task of closed-to-open eye in-painting in natural pictures. A new benchmark dataset is also introduced for the task of eye in-painting for future comparisons.
label: AI

title: StrassenNets: Deep Learning with a Multiplication Budget
Abstract: A significant portion of the arithmetic operations required to evaluate deep neural networks (DNNs) involves matrix multiplications, present in both convolutional and fully connected layers. This paper presents an end-to-end learning approach for creating low-cost approximations of matrix multiplications in DNN layers by casting matrix multiplications as 2-layer sum-product networks (SPNs) (arithmetic circuits) and learning their (ternary) edge weights from data. SPNs effectively disentangle multiplication and addition operations, enabling the imposition of a budget on the number of multiplication operations. Combining this method with knowledge distillation and applying it to image classification DNNs (trained on ImageNet) and language modeling DNNs (using LSTMs), the paper achieves a first-of-a-kind reduction in the number of multiplications (over 99.5%) while maintaining the predictive performance of the full-precision models. Furthermore, it demonstrates that the proposed framework can rediscover Strassen's matrix multiplication algorithm, learning to multiply 2 × 2 matrices using only 7 multiplications instead of 8.
label: AI

title: MINOS: Multimodal Indoor Simulator for Navigation in Complex Environments
Abstract: This paper introduces MINOS, a simulator designed to support the development of multisensory models for goal-directed navigation in complex indoor environments. The simulator leverages large datasets of complex 3D environments and offers flexible configuration of multimodal sensor suites. MINOS is used to benchmark deep-learning-based navigation methods, analyze the influence of environmental complexity on navigation performance, and conduct a controlled study of multimodality in sensorimotor learning. Experiments reveal that current deep reinforcement learning approaches struggle in large, realistic environments. However, the experiments also indicate that multimodality is beneficial in learning to navigate cluttered scenes. MINOS is released open-source to the research community at http://minosworld.org. A video showcasing MINOS is available at https://youtu.be/c0mL9K64q84.
label: AI

title: Depth-Based 3D Hand Pose Estimation: From Current Achievements to Future Goals
Abstract: This paper explores two key questions: What is the current state of 3D hand pose estimation from depth images? And what are the next challenges that need to be addressed? Following the successful Hands In the Million Challenge (HIM2017), the paper investigates the top 10 state-of-the-art methods on three tasks: single frame 3D pose estimation, 3D hand tracking, and hand pose estimation during object interaction. The performance of different CNN structures is analyzed with regard to hand shape, joint visibility, viewpoint, and articulation distributions. Findings include: (1) Isolated 3D hand pose estimation achieves low mean errors (10 mm) in the viewpoint range of [70, 120] degrees, but it is far from solved for extreme viewpoints; (2) 3D volumetric representations outperform 2D CNNs, better capturing the spatial structure of the depth data; (3) Discriminative methods still generalize poorly to unseen hand shapes; (4) While joint occlusions pose a challenge for most methods, explicit modeling of structure constraints can significantly narrow the gap between errors on visible and occluded joints.
label: AI

title: Feature Mapping for Learning Fast and Accurate 3D Pose Inference from Synthetic Images
Abstract: This paper proposes a simple and efficient method for leveraging synthetic images during the training of a deep network to predict 3D pose from an image. The ability to use synthetic images for training is highly valuable, as it is easy to create a virtually infinite training set while capturing and annotating real images can be cumbersome. However, synthetic images don't perfectly resemble real images, leading to suboptimal performance when used for training. Recent research has shown that for exemplar-based approaches, it's possible to learn a mapping from exemplar representations of real images to exemplar representations of synthetic images. This paper demonstrates that this approach is more general and that a network can be applied after the mapping to infer 3D pose: At runtime, given a real image of the target object, the features for the image are first computed, mapped to the feature space of synthetic images, and finally used as input to another network that predicts the 3D pose. This network can be trained effectively using synthetic images, resulting in strong performance in practice. Inference is faster and more accurate compared to exemplar-based approaches. The approach is demonstrated on the LINEMOD dataset for 3D object pose estimation from color images and the NYU dataset for 3D hand pose estimation from depth maps. Results show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both datasets.
label: AI

title: Learning Modality-Invariant Representations for Speech and Images
Abstract: This paper explores the unsupervised learning of a semantic embedding space for co-occurring sensory inputs. Specifically, it focuses on learning a semantic vector space for both spoken and handwritten digits using the TIDIGITs and MNIST datasets. Existing techniques encode image and audio/textual inputs directly to semantic embeddings. In contrast, this approach maps an input to the mean and log variance vectors of a diagonal Gaussian, from which sample semantic embeddings are drawn. The loss function encourages semantic similarity between co-occurring inputs while including a regularization term borrowed from variational autoencoders (VAEs) that drives the posterior distributions over embeddings to be unit Gaussian. This regularization term filters out modality information while preserving semantic information. The paper speculates that this technique might be broadly applicable to other areas of cross-modality/domain information retrieval and transfer learning.
label: AI

title: DeepConfig: Automating Data Center Network Topologies Management with Machine Learning
Abstract: Recent years have seen the development of numerous techniques to enhance the performance and efficiency of data center networks. While these techniques provide high accuracy, they are often designed using heuristics that leverage domain-specific properties of the workload or hardware. This vision paper argues that many data center networking techniques, such as routing, topology augmentation, and energy savings, with diverse goals actually share design and architectural similarities. It presents a design for developing general intermediate representations of network topologies using deep learning, suitable for solving classes of data center problems. A framework, DeepConfig, is developed to simplify the process of configuring and training deep learning agents that utilize the intermediate representation to learn different tasks. To illustrate the effectiveness of this approach, a DeepConfig-Agent is configured, implemented, and evaluated for the data center topology augmentation problem. Initial results show promising performance, with DeepConfig performing comparably to the optimal solution.
label: AI

title: Generalized Zero-Shot Learning via Synthesized Examples
Abstract: This paper presents a generative framework for generalized zero-shot learning where the training and test classes are not necessarily disjoint. Built upon a variational autoencoder-based architecture, consisting of a probabilistic encoder and a probabilistic conditional decoder, the model can generate novel exemplars from seen/unseen classes, given their respective class attributes. These exemplars can then be used to train any off-the-shelf classification model. A key aspect of the encoder-decoder architecture is a feedback-driven mechanism where a discriminator (a multivariate regressor) learns to map the generated exemplars to the corresponding class attribute vectors, improving the generator. The model's ability to generate and leverage examples from unseen classes to train the classification model naturally helps mitigate the bias towards predicting seen classes in generalized zero-shot learning settings. Through comprehensive experiments, the model outperforms several state-of-the-art methods on various benchmark datasets for both standard and generalized zero-shot learning.
label: AI

title: Using a single RGB frame for real time 3D hand pose estimation in the wild
Abstract: This paper presents a method for real-time estimation of the full 3D pose of one or more human hands using a single commodity RGB camera. Recent advancements in this area have shown impressive progress using RGBD input. However, since the introduction of RGBD sensors, progress for monocular color input has been limited. This paper leverages the latest deep learning advancements, combining them with generative hand pose estimation techniques, to achieve real-time monocular 3D hand pose estimation in unrestricted scenarios. Given an RGB image and camera calibration information, a state-of-the-art detector localizes hands. A crop of a hand in the image is then input to the pretrained network of OpenPose for hands to estimate the 2D location of hand joints. Finally, non-linear least-squares minimization fits a 3D model of the hand to the estimated 2D joint positions, recovering the 3D hand pose. Extensive experimental results provide comparisons to the state-of-the-art and qualitative assessments of the method in real-world settings.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Feature Learning for Audio Analysis
Abstract: Identifying acoustic events from a continuously streaming audio source is crucial for many applications, including environmental monitoring for basic research. In this scenario, different event classes and the features that distinguish them are unknown. Therefore, this paper presents an unsupervised feature learning method for exploring audio data, incorporating two novel contributions: First, an audio frame predictor based on a convolutional LSTM autoencoder is demonstrated for unsupervised feature extraction. Second, a new training method for autoencoders is presented, which amplifies event similarities to generate distinct features. Compared to standard approaches, features extracted from the audio frame predictor trained using this novel method show a 13% improvement in results when used with a classifier and a 36% improvement when used for clustering.
label: AI

title: Error Correction for Dense Semantic Image Labeling
Abstract: Pixelwise semantic image labeling is an important but challenging task with numerous applications. Common approaches involve either training deep networks on vast amounts of images to directly infer labels or using probabilistic graphical models to jointly model input (images) and output (labels) dependencies. However, the former approaches fail to capture the structure of output labels, which is crucial for dense labeling performance, while the latter rely on carefully hand-designed priors requiring costly parameter tuning via optimization techniques, leading to long inference times. To address these limitations, this paper explores a method for obtaining dense semantic pixel labels given both the input image and an initial estimate of the output labels. A parallel architecture is proposed that: 1) exploits context information through a LabelPropagation network to propagate correct labels from nearby pixels to improve object boundaries, 2) uses a LabelReplacement network to directly replace potentially erroneous initial labels with new ones, and 3) combines the different intermediate results via a Fusion network to obtain the final per-pixel label. Experimental validation on two datasets for semantic segmentation and face parsing tasks shows improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses of the generated results are provided.
label: AI

title: Identifying the Mislabeled Training Samples of ECG Signals using Machine Learning
Abstract: The classification accuracy of electrocardiogram signals is often affected by various factors, with mislabeled training samples being a major issue. To mitigate this negative effect, this paper introduces a cross-validation method for identifying mislabeled samples. The method leverages the cooperative advantages of different classifiers to act as a filter for the training samples. The filter removes mislabeled training samples and retains correctly labeled ones with the help of 10-fold cross-validation. This process results in a new training set provided to the final classifiers to achieve higher classification accuracies. The paper numerically demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method using the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database.
label: AI

title: NestedNet: Learning Nested Sparse Structures in Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed increasing demand for compact deep architectures to remove unnecessary redundancy and improve inference speed. While many recent works focus on reducing redundancy by eliminating unnecessary weight parameters, applying a single deep architecture for multiple devices with different resources is not feasible. When a new device or condition requires a new deep architecture, it is necessary to construct and train a new network from scratch. This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework, called a nested sparse network, which utilizes an n-in-1-type nested structure within a neural network. A nested sparse network comprises multiple levels of networks, each with a different sparsity ratio, and higher-level networks share parameters with lower-level networks to enable stable nested learning. The proposed framework realizes a resource-aware versatile architecture, enabling the same network to meet diverse resource requirements. Furthermore, the nested network can learn different forms of knowledge in its internal networks at various levels, enabling multiple tasks using a single network, such as coarse-to-fine hierarchical classification. Efficient weight connection learning, channel and layer scheduling strategies are proposed for training the nested sparse network. Evaluation across multiple tasks, including adaptive deep compression, knowledge distillation, and learning class hierarchy, demonstrates that nested sparse networks perform competitively but more efficiently compared to existing methods. |||
label: AI

title: Deep convolutional neural networks for brain image analysis on magnetic resonance imaging: a review
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have revolutionized computer vision tasks, including object recognition, detection, and segmentation. They have also proven valuable in medical image analysis, specifically in lesion segmentation, anatomical segmentation, and classification. This comprehensive literature review explores the application of CNN techniques in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis. The focus is on analyzing different CNN architectures, examining state-of-the-art pre-processing, data-preparation, and post-processing strategies, and condensing the results obtained using public datasets. The review aims to provide a detailed reference for researchers exploring deep CNN applications in brain MRI analysis and presents a perspective on future research directions in this field.
label: AI

title: Domain Adaptation Using Adversarial Learning for Autonomous Navigation
Abstract: Autonomous navigation has become a popular machine learning application, with significant advancements driven by deep learning. However, traditional outdoor autonomous navigation relies heavily on expensive sensors or extensive real labeled data, which is challenging to acquire and often inaccurate. This study proposes a novel method to train an autonomous navigation model using a simulator and an inexpensive monocular camera. To effectively leverage the simulator, the proposed method utilizes domain adaptation with adversarial learning. This includes implementing a dilated residual block in the generator, cycle loss, and style loss to enhance the adversarial learning performance for effective domain adaptation. The method is theoretically analyzed and empirically evaluated on outdoor courses with various intersections using a commercial radio-controlled car. The results demonstrate that the model learns a favorable navigation model by generating images with realistic textures. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to apply domain adaptation with adversarial learning for autonomous navigation in real outdoor environments. The proposed method has potential applications in precise image generation and other robotic tasks.
label: AI

title: Learning Surrogate Models of Document Image Quality Metrics for Automated Document Image Processing
Abstract: Computing document image quality metrics often relies on the availability of a ground truth image, limiting its applicability in scenarios where ground truth images are unavailable, such as hyperparameter optimization of image processing algorithms. This paper proposes using surrogate models to learn the behavior of a given document quality metric using existing datasets with ground truth images. The trained surrogate model can predict metric values for unseen document images without requiring access to ground truth images. The effectiveness of the surrogate model is empirically evaluated on the Document Image Binarization Competition (DIBCO) and Handwritten Document Image Binarization Competition (H-DIBCO) datasets.
label: AI

title: Can We Teach Computers to Understand Art? Domain Adaptation for Enhancing Deep Networks Capacity to De-Abstract Art
Abstract: Humans possess an exceptional ability to comprehend a natural scene at a single glance, a capacity explored by artists through abstract representations. Computer vision solutions have achieved human-level performance in many visual recognition tasks. This paper focuses on the problem of recognizing the genre (subject) in digitized paintings using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), addressing the challenges presented by abstract and artistic representations of scenes. The study begins by establishing a baseline performance by training a CNN from scratch. It then analyzes aspects hindering CNNs' recognition capabilities, particularly artistic abstraction, and tests various domain adaptation methods to enhance subject recognition. The evaluation is performed on a database of 80,000 annotated digitized paintings, supplemented with artistic photographs to simulate artistic representations. Interestingly, the most effective domain adaptation method is not neural style transfer. The paper concludes with an experiment-based assessment of the level of abstraction CNNs can achieve.
label: AI

title: The Effectiveness of Data Augmentation for Detection of Gastrointestinal Diseases from Endoscopical Images
Abstract: The lack of large public databases of medical pathologies, due to privacy concerns, poses a significant challenge for applying deep learning techniques in this field. This article investigates the use of data augmentation techniques to address this data deficiency, focusing on the recent Kvasir dataset of endoscopic images of gastrointestinal diseases. The dataset comprises 4,000 labeled and verified images covering common pathologies at different anatomical landmarks: Z-line, pylorus, and cecum. The study demonstrates how data augmentation techniques can significantly improve classification performance, both in terms of precision and recall, compared to previous approaches.
label: AI

title: FHEDN: A based on context modeling Feature Hierarchy Encoder-Decoder Network for face detection
Abstract: Objects captured by outdoor surveillance cameras or access control systems are often small, blurry, occluded, and present diverse poses due to weather conditions, camera pose, and range. This makes face detection for face recognition systems in public security applications particularly challenging. This paper proposes a novel context modeling structure called Feature Hierarchy Encoder-Decoder Network for face detection (FHEDN) to address this challenge. FHEDN can detect small, blurry, and occluded faces hierarchically from the end to the beginning, similar to encoder-decoder networks, within a single network. The proposed network consists of multiple context modeling and prediction modules specifically designed for detecting small, blurry, occluded, and diverse pose faces. The study analyzes the influence of training set distribution, default box scale, and receipt field size on detection performance during implementation. Experimental results on WIDER FACE and FDDB benchmarks demonstrate the promising performance of the network.
label: AI

title: A practical guide and software for analysing pairwise comparison experiments
Abstract: Common strategies for capturing subjective judgments from humans involve constructing a unidimensional relative measurement scale to represent order preferences or judgments about objects or conditions. This information is typically gathered through direct scoring using Likert or cardinal scales or by comparative judgments in pairs or sets. Pairwise comparisons are gaining popularity due to their simplicity; however, they require non-trivial data analysis to aggregate comparison ranks into a quality scale and analyze the results effectively. This paper explains the process of translating pairwise comparison data into a measurement scale, highlighting the benefits and limitations of scaling methods. It introduces a publicly available software in Matlab that enhances existing scaling methods by incorporating outlier analysis, methods for computing confidence intervals and statistical testing, and a prior that reduces estimation error when the number of observers is low. The examples primarily focus on image quality assessment.
label: AI

title: Parallel Mapper
Abstract: Mapper construction has emerged as a powerful and effective topological data analysis tool in the last decade, approximating and generalizing other topological summaries like the Reeb graph, contour tree, split, and joint trees. This paper investigates the parallel analysis of Mapper construction. A provably correct parallel algorithm for executing Mapper on multiple processors is presented, along with performance results comparing this approach to a reference sequential Mapper implementation. The performance experiments demonstrate the efficiency of the parallel Mapper method.
label: AI

title: Sketch Layer Separation in Multi-Spectral Historical Document Images
Abstract: High-resolution imaging has opened new avenues for investigating the material composition and structure of cultural treasures. While various analytical techniques exist, a significant diagnostic gap remains in the range of available research capabilities for works on paper. Old master drawings often involve multi-step processes with various materials, resulting in overlapping layers that make subjacent strata difficult to differentiate. Separating these stratified layers using imaging methods can provide insights into artistic work processes and answer questions about the object, its attribution, or potential forgeries. This paper explores the use of multi- or hyperspectral technology for layer separation, which records the characteristic signatures of the material's reflectance. This approach allows for accurate layer separation, as demonstrated through mock replicas, and enables the visualization of concealed red chalk under ink. Unlike RGB-sensor-based imaging, this technique minimizes the risk of damage to artworks by using combinations of defined spectra for lightning and image capturing. The results suggest that the technique can be applied to a broader range of objects and contribute to diagnostic research on cultural treasures.
label: AI

title: Quantifying Translation-Invariance in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: A fundamental challenge in object recognition lies in developing image representations invariant to common transformations like translation, rotation, and small deformations. Various hypotheses exist regarding the source of translation invariance in CNNs, including the increasing receptive field size of neurons in successive convolution layers and the pooling operation. This study introduces a simple tool, the translation-sensitivity map, to visualize and quantify translation invariance in different architectures. The results surprisingly show that architectural choices like the number of pooling layers and convolution filter size have only a secondary effect on translation invariance. The analysis identifies data augmentation as the most critical factor in achieving translation-invariant image representations using CNNs.
label: AI

title: An Architecture Combining Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Image Classification
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) resemble "ordinary" neural networks, consisting of hidden layers of neurons with "learnable" parameters. These neurons receive inputs, perform a dot product, and apply a non-linearity. The entire network represents a mapping between raw image pixels and their class scores. Traditionally, the Softmax function acts as the classifier in the final layer of the network. However, recent studies have challenged this norm, exploring the use of linear support vector machines (SVMs) in artificial neural network architectures. Inspired by previous work, this project further investigates this concept. Empirical data indicates that the CNN-SVM model achieves a test accuracy of ~99.04% using the MNIST dataset, while the CNN-Softmax achieves ~99.23%. Both models were also tested on the Fashion-MNIST dataset, a more challenging image classification dataset than MNIST. The CNN-SVM reached a test accuracy of ~90.72%, while the CNN-Softmax achieved ~91.86%. The results suggest that further improvements could be achieved by employing data preprocessing techniques and utilizing a more sophisticated base CNN model.
label: AI

title: Dynamics Transfer GAN: Generating Video by Transferring Arbitrary Temporal Dynamics from a Source Video to a Single Target Image
Abstract: This paper introduces Dynamics Transfer GAN, a novel method for generating video sequences based on generative adversarial learning. The spatial constructs of a generated video sequence are derived from the target image, while the dynamics are imported from a source video sequence with arbitrary motion and imposed onto the target image. To preserve the spatial construct of the target image, the appearance of the source video sequence is suppressed, extracting only the dynamics before imposition. This is achieved through the proposed appearance-suppressed dynamics feature. Spatial and temporal consistencies in the generated video sequence are validated using two discriminator networks: one verifies the fidelity of the generated frame appearance, and the other verifies the dynamic consistency of the generated video sequence. Experimental results confirm the quality of the video sequences generated by Dynamics Transfer GAN, successfully transferring arbitrary dynamics from the source video sequence onto a target image. The experiments also show that Dynamics Transfer GAN maintains the spatial constructs (appearance) of the target image while generating spatially and temporally consistent video sequences.
label: AI

title: 3D Facial Expression Reconstruction using Cascaded Regression
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel model fitting algorithm for reconstructing 3D facial expressions from a single image. Reconstructing face expressions from a single image is a challenging task in computer vision. Existing state-of-the-art methods fit the input image to a 3D Morphable Model (3DMM), requiring the solution of a stochastic problem and struggling with expression and pose variations. To overcome this, the proposed method adopts a 3D face expression model and utilizes a combined feature robust to scale, rotation, and different lighting conditions. The method employs a cascaded regression framework to estimate 3DMM parameters, using detected 2D landmarks to initialize the 3D shape and mapping matrices. In each iteration, residues between current 3DMM parameters and the ground truth are estimated and used to update the 3D shapes. The mapping matrices are also calculated based on the updated shapes and 2D landmarks. HOG features of local patches and displacements between 3D landmark projections and 2D landmarks are exploited. Compared to existing methods, the proposed method is robust to expression and pose changes and can reconstruct higher fidelity 3D face shapes.
label: AI

title: Unified presentation of four fundamental inequalities
Abstract: This paper suggests a unified presentation for teaching fundamental constants to graduate students, introducing four lower limits to observed phenomena. The reduced Planck constant (hbar) represents the lowest classically definable action. The inverse of the invariant speed (s) corresponds to the lowest observable slowness. The Planck time (tP) represents the lowest observable time scale. The Boltzmann constant (k) determines the lowest coherent degree of freedom. The paper revisits Einstein's criterion on fluctuations in small thermal systems and demonstrates its far-reaching implications, such as showing relationships between critical exponents. Each of these four fundamental limits is involved in an inequality, marking a horizon in the perceived universe. This compact presentation addresses difficulties encountered when defining the epistemological status of these constants and emphasizes their role in shaping our intuitive understanding of the universe.
label: AI

title: Geometry Guided Adversarial Facial Expression Synthesis
Abstract: Facial expression synthesis has gained significant attention in computer graphics and pattern recognition, finding applications in face animation and recognition. However, the high-level semantic presence of large and non-linear face geometry variations poses a challenge. This paper proposes a Geometry-Guided Generative Adversarial Network (G2-GAN) for photo-realistic and identity-preserving facial expression synthesis. Facial geometry (fiducial points) is employed as a controllable condition to guide facial texture synthesis with specific expressions. A pair of generative adversarial subnetworks are jointly trained for opposite tasks: expression removal and expression synthesis. These paired networks form a mapping cycle between neutral expressions and arbitrary expressions, facilitating other applications like face transfer and expression-invariant face recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the method can generate visually compelling results on various facial expression synthesis databases. An expression-invariant face recognition experiment further highlights the advantages of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Single-Shot Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation From Monocular RGB
Abstract: This paper introduces a new single-shot method for multi-person 3D pose estimation in general scenes from a monocular RGB camera. The approach leverages novel occlusion-robust pose-maps (ORPM) that enable full body pose inference even under strong partial occlusions by other people and objects in the scene. ORPM outputs a fixed number of maps encoding the 3D joint locations of all people in the scene. Body part associations allow for inferring 3D pose for an arbitrary number of people without explicit bounding box prediction. To train the approach, the study introduces MuCo-3DHP, the first large-scale training dataset showcasing real images of sophisticated multi-person interactions and occlusions. A large corpus of multi-person images is synthesized by compositing images of individual people (with ground truth from multi-view performance capture). The method is evaluated on the challenging 3D annotated multi-person test set MuPoTs-3D, achieving state-of-the-art performance. To encourage further research in multi-person 3D pose estimation, the new datasets and associated code are made publicly available.
label: AI

title: SPP-Net: Deep Absolute Pose Regression with Synthetic Views
Abstract: Image-based localization is a crucial problem in computer vision due to its broad applicability in robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous systems. Extensive literature describes methods for geometrically registering a 2D image with a 3D model. Recently, methods based on deep (and convolutional) feedforward networks (CNNs) have gained popularity for pose regression. However, these CNN-based methods are less accurate than geometry-based methods despite their speed and memory efficiency. This work presents a deep neural network architecture based on sparse feature descriptors to estimate the absolute pose of an image. Using sparse feature descriptors offers two main advantages: first, the network is significantly smaller than CNNs used for this task, making it more efficient and scalable. Second, sparse features enable data augmentation with synthetic viewpoints, resulting in substantial improvements in generalization performance for unseen poses. The proposed method aims to combine the strengths of feature-based localization and CNN-based pose regression to achieve state-of-the-art performance in absolute pose estimation. A detailed analysis of the architecture and rigorous evaluation on existing datasets support the method's effectiveness.
label: AI

title: CycleGAN Face-off
Abstract: Face-off is an interesting case of style transfer where the facial expressions and attributes of one person can be fully transformed onto another face. This project investigates an unsupervised training process that requires only two unaligned video sequences from each person and automatically learns shared attributes to extract. The project explores various improvements for adversarial training, specifically CycleGAN, to capture details in facial expressions and head poses, generating transformation videos with higher consistency and stability.
label: AI

title: Deep Koalarization: Image Colorization using CNNs and Inception-ResNet-v2
Abstract: This paper reviews recent approaches to colorizing grayscale images using deep learning methods. Building on these approaches, the paper proposes a model that combines a deep Convolutional Neural Network trained from scratch with high-level features extracted from the Inception-ResNet-v2 pre-trained model. The fully convolutional architecture of the encoder-decoder model enables processing images of any size and aspect ratio. In addition to presenting training results, the paper assesses the "public acceptance" of the generated images through a user study. Finally, the paper showcases a carousel of applications on different image types, such as historical photographs.
label: AI

title: NAG: Network for Adversary Generation
Abstract: Adversarial perturbations pose a significant threat to the deployment of machine learning systems. Recent studies have demonstrated the existence of image-agnostic perturbations that can fool classifiers across most natural images. Existing methods rely on optimization approaches that solve for a fooling objective with an imperceptibility constraint to craft perturbations. However, these methods generate one perturbation at a time, representing a single instance from the manifold of adversarial perturbations. To build robust models, exploring this manifold is crucial. This paper presents, for the first time, a generative approach to model the distribution of adversarial perturbations. The proposed model's architecture is inspired by GANs and is trained using fooling and diversity objectives. The trained generator network aims to capture the distribution of adversarial perturbations for a given classifier, readily generating a wide variety of such perturbations. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that perturbations generated by the model achieve state-of-the-art fooling rates, exhibit wide variety, and deliver excellent cross-model generalizability. This work is a significant step toward understanding the complex manifolds of adversarial perturbations. |||
label: AI

title: Visual aesthetic analysis using deep neural network: model and techniques to increase accuracy without transfer learning
Abstract: We trained a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) from scratch for visual aesthetic analysis in images, and we discuss techniques we used to improve accuracy.  We avoided using pretrained weights, a common transfer learning approach, and trained a model from scratch, achieving 78.7% accuracy on the AVA2 dataset, close to the best models available (85.6%). We also show that accuracy increases to 81.48% when we increase the training set by increments of 10% of the entire AVA dataset, demonstrating that our algorithm improves with more data.
label: AI

title: Noise Level Estimation for Overcomplete Dictionary Learning Based on Tight Asymptotic Bounds
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating Gaussian noise level from trained dictionaries during the update stage. We provide rigorous statistical analysis on the eigenvalue distributions of a sample covariance matrix.  We then propose an interval-bounded estimator for noise variance in high-dimensional settings.  Using the boundness and asymptotic behavior of the noise eigenvalue spectrum, we develop an effective estimation method for the noise level.  Our method is guaranteed to perform well both theoretically and empirically.  Analysis and experimental results show that our proposed algorithm can reliably infer true noise levels and outperforms existing methods.
label: AI

title: A Deep Recurrent Framework for Cleaning Motion Capture Data
Abstract: We present a deep, bidirectional, recurrent framework for cleaning noisy and incomplete motion capture data.  Our approach exploits temporal coherence and joint correlations to infer adaptive filters for each joint in each frame.  A single model can be trained to denoise a heterogeneous mix of action types under substantial amounts of noise.  We use a second bidirectional network to pre-process signals containing both noise and gaps, synthesizing missing frames from surrounding context.  This approach handles a wide variety of noise types and long gaps, does not require knowledge of the noise distribution, and operates in a streaming setting.  We validate our approach through extensive evaluations on noise in joint angles and positions, showing that it outperforms various alternatives.
label: AI

title: Peephole: Predicting Network Performance Before Training
Abstract: The pursuit of performant networks has been a major driving force behind advancements in deep learning in recent years. While this is rewarding, improving network design has always been a challenging task.  The large design space combined with the tremendous cost of network training poses a major obstacle to this endeavor.  In this work, we propose a new approach to this problem: predicting network performance before training based on its architecture.  We develop a unified way to encode individual layers into vectors and combine them into an integrated description using an LSTM.  Leveraging the recurrent network's strong expressive power, this method reliably predicts the performance of various network architectures.  Our empirical studies show that the method achieved accurate predictions and produced consistent rankings across datasets, a key desideratum in performance prediction.
label: AI

title: Geometry-Aware Learning of Maps for Camera Localization
Abstract: Maps are crucial components in image-based camera localization and visual SLAM systems. They are used to establish geometric constraints between images, correct drift in relative pose estimation, and relocalize cameras after lost tracking.  The exact definitions of maps are often application-specific and hand-crafted for different scenarios (e.g., 3D landmarks, lines, planes, bags of visual words). We propose representing maps as a deep neural network called MapNet, which enables learning a data-driven map representation.  Unlike prior work on learning maps, MapNet uses cheap and ubiquitous sensory inputs like visual odometry and GPS, in addition to images, and fuses them together for camera localization.  Geometric constraints expressed by these inputs, traditionally used in bundle adjustment or pose-graph optimization, are formulated as loss terms during MapNet training and are also used during inference.  This directly improves localization accuracy and allows us to update MapNet (i.e., maps) in a self-supervised manner using additional unlabeled video sequences from the scene.  We also propose a novel parameterization for camera rotation better suited for deep-learning-based camera pose regression.  Experimental results on both the indoor 7-Scenes dataset and the outdoor Oxford RobotCar dataset show significant performance improvements over prior work.  The MapNet project webpage is https://goo.gl/mRB3Au.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Joint Matrix Decomposition for Data Integration with Heterogeneous Noise
Abstract: Matrix decomposition is a popular and fundamental approach in machine learning and data mining. It has been successfully applied to various fields.  Most matrix decomposition methods focus on decomposing a data matrix from a single source.  However, data often comes from different sources with heterogeneous noise.  A few matrix decomposition methods have been extended to integrate and discover patterns in such multi-view data.  However, few methods explicitly consider the heterogeneity of noise in such multi-view data for data integration.  We propose a joint matrix decomposition framework (BJMD), which models the heterogeneity of noise using a Gaussian distribution in a Bayesian framework.  We develop two algorithms to solve this model: one is a variational Bayesian inference algorithm, which makes full use of the posterior distribution; the other is a maximum a posterior algorithm, which is more scalable and can be easily parallelized.  Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that BJMD, considering the heterogeneity of noise, is superior or competitive to the state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Fine-Grained Object Recognition and Zero-Shot Learning in Remote Sensing Imagery
Abstract: Fine-grained object recognition, which aims to identify the type of an object among a large number of subcategories, is an emerging application with the increasing resolution of image data, which exposes new details.  Traditional fully supervised algorithms fail to handle this problem, where there is low between-class variance and high within-class variance for the classes of interest with small sample sizes. We study an even more extreme scenario, zero-shot learning (ZSL), where no training examples exist for some of the classes.  ZSL aims to build a recognition model for new, unseen categories by relating them to seen classes that were previously learned. We establish this relation by learning a compatibility function between image features extracted via a convolutional neural network and auxiliary information describing the semantics of the classes of interest by using training samples from the seen classes. We then show how knowledge transfer can be performed for the unseen classes by maximizing this function during inference. We introduce a new dataset containing 40 different types of street trees in 1-foot spatial resolution aerial data and evaluate the performance of this model with manually annotated attributes, a natural language model, and a scientific taxonomy as auxiliary information.  The experiments show that the proposed model achieves 14.3% recognition accuracy for the classes with no training examples, which is significantly better than a random guess accuracy of 6.3% for 16 test classes and three other ZSL algorithms.
label: AI

title: IQA: Visual Question Answering in Interactive Environments
Abstract: We introduce Interactive Question Answering (IQA), the task of answering questions that require an autonomous agent to interact with a dynamic visual environment.  IQA presents the agent with a scene and a question, such as: "Are there any apples in the fridge?" The agent must navigate the scene, acquire visual understanding of scene elements, interact with objects (e.g., open refrigerators), and plan a series of actions conditioned on the question.  Popular reinforcement learning approaches with a single controller perform poorly on IQA due to the large and diverse state space. We propose the Hierarchical Interactive Memory Network (HIMN), consisting of a factorized set of controllers, allowing the system to operate at multiple levels of temporal abstraction.  To evaluate HIMN, we introduce IQUAD V1, a new dataset built upon AI2-THOR, a simulated photo-realistic environment of configurable indoor scenes with interactive objects (code and dataset available at https://github.com/danielgordon10/thor-iqa-cvpr-2018). IQUAD V1 has 75,000 questions, each paired with a unique scene configuration. Our experiments show that our proposed model outperforms popular single controller-based methods on IQUAD V1. For sample questions and results, please view our video: https://youtu.be/pXd3C-1jr98.
label: AI

title: Sim-to-Real Transfer of Accurate Grasping with Eye-In-Hand Observations and Continuous Control
Abstract: In the context of deep learning for robotics, we show an effective method for training a real robot to grasp a tiny sphere (1.37 cm in diameter) with an original combination of system design choices.  We decompose the end-to-end system into a vision module and a closed-loop controller module, which both use target object segmentation as their common interface.  The vision module extracts information from the robot end-effector camera in the form of a binary segmentation mask of the target. We train it to achieve effective domain transfer by composing real background images with simulated images of the target.  The controller module takes as input the binary segmentation mask and is thus agnostic to visual discrepancies between simulated and real environments.  We train our closed-loop controller in simulation using imitation learning and show that it is robust to discrepancies between the dynamic model of the simulated and real robot.  When combined with eye-in-hand observations, we achieve a 90% success rate in grasping a tiny sphere with a real robot.  The controller can generalize to unseen scenarios where the target is moving and even learns to recover from failures.
