title: Transformational Sparse Coding
Abstract: A fundamental problem faced by object recognition systems is that objects and their features can appear in different locations, scales, and orientations.  Current deep learning methods attempt to achieve invariance to local translations via pooling, discarding the locations of features in the process.  Other approaches explicitly learn transformed versions of the same feature, leading to representations that quickly explode in size. Instead of discarding the rich and useful information about feature transformations to achieve invariance, we argue that models should learn object features conjointly with their transformations to achieve equivariance.  We propose a new model of unsupervised learning based on sparse coding that can learn object features jointly with their affine transformations directly from images.  Results based on learning from natural images indicate that our approach matches the reconstruction quality of traditional sparse coding but with significantly fewer degrees of freedom while simultaneously learning transformations from data.  These results open the door to scaling up unsupervised learning to allow deep feature + transformation learning in a manner consistent with the ventral + dorsal stream architecture of the primate visual cortex.
label: AI

title: Estimation of the mechanical properties of the eye through the study of its vibrational modes
Abstract: Measuring the eye's mechanical properties in vivo and with minimally invasive techniques can be key to individualized solutions for a number of eye pathologies. The development of such techniques relies largely on computational modeling of the eyeball and optimally requires the synergistic interplay between experimentation and numerical simulation.  In Astrophysics and Geophysics, the remote measurement of structural properties of the systems in their realm is performed on the basis of (helio-)seismic techniques.  As a biomechanical system, the eyeball possesses normal vibrational modes encompassing rich information about its structure and mechanical properties.  However, an integral analysis of the eyeball's vibrational modes has not yet been performed.  Here, we develop a new finite difference method to compute both the spheroidal and, especially, the toroidal eigenfrequencies of the human eye.  Using this numerical model, we show that the vibrational eigenfrequencies of the human eye fall in the interval 100 Hz - 10 MHz.  We find that compressible vibrational modes may release a trace on high-frequency changes in intraocular pressure, while incompressible normal modes could be registered by analyzing the scattering pattern that the motions of the vitreous humor leave on the retina.  Existing contact lenses with embedded devices operating at high sampling frequency could be used to register the microfluctuations of the eyeball shape we obtain.  We advance that an inverse problem to obtain the mechanical properties of a given eye (e.g., Young's modulus, Poisson ratio) by measuring its normal frequencies is doable.  These measurements can be done using non-invasive techniques, opening very interesting perspectives to estimate the mechanical properties of eyes in vivo.  Future research might relate various ocular pathologies with anomalies in the measured vibrational frequencies of the eye.
label: AI

title: Basic Thresholding Classification
Abstract: In this thesis, we propose a lightweight sparsity-based algorithm, Basic Thresholding Classifier (BTC), for classification applications (such as face identification, hyper-spectral image classification, etc.) which is capable of identifying test samples extremely rapidly and performing high classification accuracy.  Originally BTC is a linear classifier that works based on the assumption that the samples of the classes of a given dataset are linearly separable.  However, in practice, those samples may not be linearly separable.  In this context, we also propose another algorithm, Kernel Basic Thresholding Classifier (KBTC), which is a non-linear kernel version of the BTC algorithm.  KBTC can achieve promising results, especially when the given samples are linearly non-separable.  For both proposals, we introduce sufficient identification conditions (SICs) under which BTC and KBTC can identify any test sample in the range space of a given dictionary.  By using SICs, we develop parameter estimation procedures that do not require any cross-validation.  Both BTC and KBTC algorithms provide efficient classifier fusion schemes in which individual classifier outputs are combined to produce better classification results.  For instance, for the application of face identification, this is done by combining the residuals having different random projectors.  For spatial applications, such as hyper-spectral image classification, the fusion is carried out by incorporating the spatial information, in which the output residual maps are filtered using a smoothing filter.  Numerical results on publicly available face and hyper-spectral datasets show that our proposal outperforms well-known support vector machines (SVM)-based techniques, multinomial logistic regression (MLR)-based methods, and sparsity-based approaches like $l_1$-minimization and simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP).

title: Class Rectification Hard Mining for Imbalanced Deep Learning
Abstract: Recognizing detailed facial or clothing attributes in images of people is a challenging task for computer vision, especially when the training data are both very large scale and extremely imbalanced among different attribute classes.  To address this problem, we formulate a novel scheme for batch incremental hard sample mining of minority attribute classes from imbalanced large-scale training data.  We develop an end-to-end deep learning framework capable of avoiding the dominant effect of majority classes by discovering sparsely sampled boundaries of minority classes.  This is made possible by introducing a Class Rectification Loss (CRL) regularizing algorithm. We demonstrate the advantages and scalability of CRL over existing state-of-the-art attribute recognition and imbalanced data learning models on two large-scale imbalanced benchmark datasets: the CelebA facial attribute dataset and the X-Domain clothing attribute dataset.

title: Minimal Solvers for Monocular Rolling Shutter Compensation under Ackermann Motion
Abstract: Modern automotive vehicles are often equipped with a budget commercial rolling shutter camera.  These devices often produce distorted images due to the inter-row delay of the camera while capturing the image. Recent methods for monocular rolling shutter motion compensation utilize blur kernel and the straightness property of line segments.  However, these methods are limited to handling rotational motion and are not fast enough to operate in real time.  In this paper, we propose a minimal solver for rolling shutter motion compensation that assumes a known vertical direction of the camera.  Thanks to the Ackermann motion model of vehicles, which consists of only two motion parameters, and two parameters for the simplified depth assumption that leads to a 4-line algorithm.  The proposed minimal solver estimates the rolling shutter camera motion efficiently and accurately.  Extensive experiments on real and simulated datasets demonstrate the benefits of our approach in terms of qualitative and quantitative results.
label: AI

title: Combining Deep Universal Features, Semantic Attributes, and Hierarchical Classification for Zero-Shot Learning
Abstract: We address zero-shot (ZS) learning, building upon prior work in hierarchical classification by combining it with approaches based on semantic attribute estimation.  For both non-novel and novel image classes, we compare multiple formulations of the problem, starting with deep universal features in each case. We investigate the effect of using different posterior probabilities as inputs to the hierarchical classifier, comparing the performances of posteriors derived from distances to SVM classifier boundaries with those of posteriors based on semantic attribute estimation.  Using a dataset consisting of 150 object classes from the ImageNet ILSVRC2012 dataset, we find that the hierarchical classification method that maximizes expected reward for non-novel classes differs from the method that maximizes expected reward for novel classes.  We also show that using input posteriors based on semantic attributes improves the expected reward for novel classes.
label: AI

title: Weaving Multi-scale Context for Single Shot Detector
Abstract: Aggregating context information from multiple scales has been proven effective for improving the accuracy of Single Shot Detectors (SSDs) on object detection.  However, existing multi-scale context fusion techniques are computationally expensive, which unfavorably diminishes the advantageous speed of SSD.  In this work, we propose a novel network topology, called WeaveNet, that can efficiently fuse multi-scale information and boost detection accuracy with negligible extra cost.  The proposed WeaveNet iteratively weaves context information from adjacent scales together to enable more sophisticated context reasoning while maintaining fast speed.  Built by stacking lightweight blocks, WeaveNet is easy to train without requiring batch normalization and can be further accelerated by our proposed architecture simplification.  Experimental results on PASCAL VOC 2007 and PASCAL VOC 2012 benchmarks show significant performance boost brought by WeaveNet.  For 320x320 input of batch size = 8, WeaveNet reaches 79.5% mAP on PASCAL VOC 2007 test in 101 fps with only 4 fps extra cost and further improves to 79.7% mAP with more iterations.
label: AI

title: Wild Patterns: Ten Years After the Rise of Adversarial Machine Learning
Abstract: Learning-based pattern classifiers, including deep networks, have shown impressive performance in several application domains, ranging from computer vision to cybersecurity.  However, it has also been shown that adversarial input perturbations carefully crafted either at training or at test time can easily subvert their predictions.  The vulnerability of machine learning to such wild patterns (also referred to as adversarial examples), along with the design of suitable countermeasures, has been investigated in the research field of adversarial machine learning.  In this work, we provide a thorough overview of the evolution of this research area over the last ten years and beyond, starting from pioneering, earlier work on the security of non-deep learning algorithms up to more recent work aimed to understand the security properties of deep learning algorithms in the context of computer vision and cybersecurity tasks.  We report interesting connections between these apparently different lines of work, highlighting common misconceptions related to the security evaluation of machine learning algorithms. We review the main threat models and attacks defined to this end and discuss the main limitations of current work, along with the corresponding future challenges towards the design of more secure learning algorithms.
label: AI

title: Simultaneous Hand Pose and Skeleton Bone-Lengths Estimation from a Single Depth Image
Abstract: Articulated hand pose estimation is a challenging task for human-computer interaction. The state-of-the-art hand pose estimation algorithms work only with one or a few subjects for which they have been calibrated or trained.  Particularly, the hybrid methods based on learning followed by model fitting or model-based deep learning do not explicitly consider varying hand shapes and sizes.  In this work, we introduce a novel hybrid algorithm for estimating the 3D hand pose as well as bone lengths of the hand skeleton at the same time from a single depth image. The proposed CNN architecture learns hand pose parameters and scale parameters associated with the bone lengths simultaneously. Subsequently, a new hybrid forward kinematics layer employs both parameters to estimate 3D joint positions of the hand.  For end-to-end training, we combine three public datasets, NYU, ICVL, and MSRA-2015, into one unified format to achieve large variation in hand shapes and sizes.  Among hybrid methods, our method shows improved accuracy over the state-of-the-art on the combined dataset and the ICVL dataset that contains multiple subjects.  Also, our algorithm is demonstrated to work well with unseen images.
label: AI

title: Image Inpainting for High-Resolution Textures using CNN Texture Synthesis
Abstract: Deep neural networks have been successfully applied to problems such as image segmentation, image super-resolution, coloration, and image inpainting.  In this work, we propose the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image inpainting of large regions in high-resolution textures.  Due to limited computational resources, processing high-resolution images with neural networks is still an open problem. Existing methods separate inpainting of global structure and the transfer of details, which leads to blurry results and loss of global coherence in the detail transfer step.  Based on advances in texture synthesis using CNNs, we propose patch-based image inpainting by a CNN that is able to optimize for global as well as detail texture statistics.  Our method is capable of filling large inpainting regions, oftentimes exceeding the quality of comparable methods for high-resolution images.  For reference patch look-up, we propose to use the same summary statistics that are used in the inpainting process.

title: An Integrated Platform for Live 3D Human Reconstruction and Motion Capturing
Abstract: The latest developments in 3D capturing, processing, and rendering provide means to unlock novel 3D application pathways.  The main elements of an integrated platform, which target tele-immersion and future 3D applications, are described in this paper, addressing the tasks of real-time capturing, robust 3D human shape/appearance reconstruction, and skeleton-based motion tracking.  More specifically, initially, the details of a multiple RGB-depth (RGB-D) capturing system are given, along with a novel sensors' calibration method.  A robust, fast reconstruction method from multiple RGB-D streams is then proposed, based on an enhanced variation of the volumetric Fourier transform-based method, parallelized on the Graphics Processing Unit, and accompanied with an appropriate texture-mapping algorithm.  On top of that, given the lack of relevant objective evaluation methods, a novel framework is proposed for the quantitative evaluation of real-time 3D reconstruction systems.  Finally, a generic, multiple depth stream-based method for accurate real-time human skeleton tracking is proposed.  Detailed experimental results with multi-Kinect2 datasets verify the validity of our arguments and the effectiveness of the proposed system and methodologies. |||

title: A Frequency Domain Neural Network for Fast Image Super-resolution
Abstract: This paper introduces a frequency domain neural network for image super-resolution. The network uses the convolution theorem to represent spatial domain convolutions as products in the frequency domain. Non-linearity, traditionally achieved through rectifier units, is also represented as a convolution in the frequency domain. This approach results in a computationally efficient network for testing and allows all parameters to be learned. Training is done using backpropagation, and complex numbers are avoided by using the Hartley transform instead of the Fourier transform. This network has potential applications in other computer vision and image processing tasks that utilize frequency domain representations. The paper presents results on super-resolution and compares the performance of the proposed network with existing methods. Experimental findings demonstrate that the network is significantly faster than alternative approaches, achieving a speed-up of one to two orders of magnitude with negligible performance degradation.
label: AI

title: Variational models for joint subsampling and reconstruction of turbulence-degraded images
Abstract: Turbulence-degraded image frames suffer from both turbulent deformations and time-varying blurs. To address this issue, we propose a multi-frame reconstruction scheme that recovers a latent image from a sequence of observed images. Existing methods typically rely on registering each frame to a reference image, allowing for the estimation of geometric turbulent deformations and subsequent image sharpening. However, a high-quality reference image is often unavailable due to the distortion inherent in turbulence-degraded frames. This poses a challenge for accurate estimation of geometric deformations and frame fusion. Additionally, not all frames in the sequence are equally useful, making frame selection crucial. In this work, we present a variational model that jointly subsamples frames and extracts a clear image. Through iterative minimization of an energy functional, a high-quality image and an optimal subsample are simultaneously obtained. The energy functional includes a fidelity term measuring the discrepancy between the extracted image and subsampled frames, as well as regularization terms for the extracted image and the subsample. We explore different choices of fidelity and regularization terms. By carefully selecting frames and extracting the image, the quality of the reconstructed image can be significantly improved. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our proposed model. Furthermore, the extracted subsamples and images can be incorporated into existing algorithms to further enhance results.
label: AI

title: Direct and Real-Time Cardiovascular Risk Prediction
Abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden, measured using low-dose chest CT, is a reliable predictor of cardiovascular events. We propose an automated method for CAC quantification, eliminating the need for intermediate CAC segmentation. Our method first uses a convolutional neural network (ConvNet) to determine a bounding box around the heart for localization. Subsequently, a dedicated ConvNet analyzes axial slices within the bounding box to estimate CAC quantity through regression. We validated our method using a dataset of 1,546 baseline CT scans from the National Lung Screening Trial, where CAC was manually identified. The method achieved a high interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.98 between manual reference and automatically obtained Agatston scores. Stratifying subjects into five cardiovascular risk categories resulted in an accuracy of 85% and a Cohen's linearly weighted κ of 0.90. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of real-time CAC burden quantification in chest CT without requiring CAC segmentation.
label: AI

title: Defense against Adversarial Attacks Using High-Level Representation Guided Denoiser
Abstract: Neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial examples, posing a security risk in sensitive applications. We propose a high-level representation guided denoiser (HGD) as a defense mechanism for image classification. Standard denoisers suffer from error amplification, where small residual adversarial noise is magnified, leading to incorrect classifications. HGD addresses this issue by using a loss function based on the difference between the target model's outputs activated by the clean image and the denoised image. Compared to ensemble adversarial training, the current state-of-the-art defense for large images, HGD offers several advantages. First, HGD enhances the target model's robustness against both white-box and black-box adversarial attacks. Second, HGD can be trained on a small subset of images and generalizes well to other images and unseen classes. Third, HGD can be transferred to defend models other than the one guiding it. In the NIPS competition on defense against adversarial attacks, our HGD solution achieved first place, outperforming other models by a significant margin.
label: AI

title: 3D Surface-to-Structure Translation using Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: We present a system that estimates internal body structures from 3D surface models using deep convolutional neural networks trained on CT (computed tomography) images of the human body. Traditionally, internal structures are visualized using CT or MRI scanners. However, assuming a non-zero mutual information between the external body shape and its internal structure, we propose using a 3D surface model to infer an approximate internal structure based on a database of MRI and CT images. This suggests the possibility of identifying potential diseases and their locations within a person's body solely through 3D surface scanning. As a first prototype, we developed a system for estimating internal body structures from surface models using Visible Human Project DICOM CT Datasets from the University of Iowa Magnetic Resonance Research Facility.

title: Learning 2D Gabor Filters by Infinite Kernel Learning Regression
Abstract: Gabor functions have widespread applications in image processing and computer vision. This paper proves that 2D Gabor functions are translation-invariant positive-definite kernels and proposes a novel formulation for image representation using Gabor functions, based on infinite kernel learning regression. This formulation leads to a support vector expansion of an image based on a mixture of Gabor functions. However, this representation includes all Gabor functions at all support vector pixels. Applying LASSO to this support vector expansion results in a sparse representation where each Gabor function is positioned at a small set of pixels. As an application, we introduce a method for learning a dataset-specific set of Gabor filters, which can be subsequently used for feature extraction. Our experiments show that using these learned Gabor filters improves the recognition accuracy of a recently introduced face recognition algorithm.
label: AI

title: $l_1$-$l_2$ Regularization of Split Feasibility Problems
Abstract: Numerous problems in signal processing, imaging, statistical learning, data mining, and computer vision can be formulated as optimization problems involving the minimization of a sum of convex functions, potentially non-differentiable and composed with linear operators. These problems can be transformed into split feasibility problems (SFP), as shown in [reference]. Each function typically represents either a data fidelity term or a regularization term enforcing specific properties on the solution, as detailed in [reference]. This paper focuses on split feasibility problems, which can be viewed as a generalization of Q-Lasso, an extension of the well-known Lasso of Tibshirani [reference]. Q represents a closed convex subset of a Euclidean m-space, interpreted as the set of errors within a given tolerance level when linear measurements are used to recover a signal/image via Lasso. Inspired by recent works [reference], we explore nonconvex regularization of SFP and propose three split algorithms for solving this general case. The first algorithm is based on the DC (difference of convex) algorithm (DCA) introduced by Pham Dinh Tao. The second algorithm is the well-known forward-backward algorithm. The third algorithm utilizes a method introduced by Mine and Fukushima. It is noteworthy that the SFP model encompasses a range of applied problems in signal/image processing, particularly optimization problems for intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) treatment planning, as demonstrated in [reference].
label: AI

title: Shape from Shading through Shape Evolution
Abstract: This paper tackles the shape-from-shading problem by training deep networks with synthetic images. Unlike conventional approaches that combine deep learning and synthetic imagery, our method does not require any external shape dataset to generate synthetic images. Our approach comprises two synergistic processes: the evolution of complex shapes from simple primitives and the training of a deep network for shape-from-shading. The evolution process generates improved shapes guided by the network training, while the training process benefits from the evolved shapes. We demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on a shape-from-shading benchmark.
label: AI

title: Compact Hash Code Learning with Binary Deep Neural Network
Abstract: Learning compact binary codes for image retrieval using deep neural networks has gained significant attention recently. However, training deep hashing networks is challenging due to the binary constraints imposed on hash codes. This paper proposes deep network models and learning algorithms for learning binary hash codes given image representations under both unsupervised and supervised settings. Our network design incorporates a hidden layer that directly outputs the binary codes. This design overcomes a challenging problem faced in previous works: optimizing non-smooth objective functions due to binarization. Additionally, we propose incorporating independence and balance properties in both direct and strict forms into the learning schemes. We also include a similarity preserving property in our objective functions. The resulting optimizations involving binary, independence, and balance constraints are challenging to solve. To address this difficulty, we propose learning the networks using alternating optimization with careful relaxation. Moreover, leveraging the powerful capacity of convolutional neural networks, we present an end-to-end architecture that jointly learns to extract visual features and generate binary hash codes. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed methods outperform or achieve comparable performance to the state-of-the-art.
label: AI

title: CycleGAN, a Master of Steganography
Abstract: CycleGAN (Zhu et al. 2017) is a recent successful approach for learning a transformation between two image distributions. Through a series of experiments, we uncover an intriguing property of the model: CycleGAN learns to "hide" information about a source image within the generated images using a nearly imperceptible, high-frequency signal. This technique allows the generator to recover the original sample and satisfy the cyclic consistency requirement, while maintaining the realism of the generated image. We establish a connection between this phenomenon and adversarial attacks by viewing CycleGAN's training process as training a generator of adversarial examples. Our analysis reveals that the cyclic consistency loss makes CycleGAN particularly vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
label: AI

title: OneDataShare: A Vision for Cloud-hosted Data Transfer Scheduling and Optimization as a Service
Abstract: Fast, reliable, and efficient data transmission across wide-area networks is a major bottleneck for data-intensive cloud applications. This paper introduces OneDataShare, designed to address the challenges associated with effective cloud-based data transfers involving varying file sizes and incompatible transfer end-points. OneDataShare aims to achieve high-speed data communication, interoperability between multiple transfer protocols, and accurate delivery time estimation for advance planning. These capabilities maximize user-profit through improved and faster data analysis for business intelligence. The paper elaborates on the desirable features of OneDataShare as a cloud-hosted data transfer scheduling and optimization service and its alignment with the vision of harnessing the power of the cloud and distributed computing. Experimental evaluation and comparison with existing real-life file transfer services demonstrate that OneDataShare achieves a 6.5 times greater transfer throughput.
label: AI

title: Dense Optical Flow based Change Detection Network Robust to Difference of Camera Viewpoints
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for detecting scene changes from a pair of images captured with different camera viewpoints using a dense optical flow-based change detection network. When camera poses are fixed or known, as in surveillance or satellite cameras, pixel correspondence between images captured at different times can be established. This allows for comparatively accurate scene change detection by modeling the scene's appearance. However, for cameras mounted on moving objects, such as ground or aerial vehicles, spatial correspondence between images captured at different times needs to be considered. Accurate estimation of camera pose or a 3D model of the scene can be challenging due to scene changes or limited imagery. To address this issue, we propose a change detection convolutional neural network that utilizes dense optical flow between input images to improve robustness to differences in camera viewpoints. Our evaluation based on the panoramic change detection dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art change detection algorithms.
label: AI

title: Chaining Identity Mapping Modules for Image Denoising
Abstract: We propose a fully-convolutional network model called Chain of Identity Mapping Modules (CIMM) for image denoising. The CIMM structure exhibits two key features essential for noise removal. First, each residual unit employs identity mappings as skip connections and receives pre-activated input to preserve the gradient magnitude propagated in both forward and backward directions. Second, by using dilated kernels for the convolution layers in the residual branch (within an identity mapping module), each neuron in the last convolution layer can observe the full receptive field of the first layer. After training on the BSD400 dataset, our network demonstrates significantly higher numerical accuracy and improved visual image quality compared to state-of-the-art methods when evaluated on conventional benchmark images and the BSD68 dataset.
label: AI

title: Exploiting Modern Hardware for High-Dimensional Nearest Neighbor Search
Abstract: Numerous multimedia information retrieval or machine learning problems require efficient high-dimensional nearest neighbor search techniques. For instance, multimedia objects, such as images, music, or videos, can be represented by high-dimensional feature vectors. Finding similar multimedia objects translates to finding objects with similar feature vectors. With the widespread use of social networks, large-scale multimedia databases, and machine learning applications, the need for efficient nearest neighbor search approaches is increasingly evident. This thesis builds upon product quantization, an efficient nearest neighbor search technique that compresses high-dimensional vectors into short codes. This enables the storage of large databases entirely in RAM, facilitating low response times. We propose several contributions that exploit the capabilities of modern CPUs, particularly SIMD and the cache hierarchy, to further reduce response times offered by product quantization.
label: AI

title: Representations of Sound in Deep Learning of Audio Features from Music
Abstract: The work of a single musician, group, or composer can exhibit significant variation in musical style. Different stylistic elements, including performance medium, rhythm, harmony, and texture, are typically explored and developed throughout an artist's career. However, at the perceptual level, the work of individual composers often possesses a discernible character. Experienced listeners can often identify the composer or performer based on subtle clues in the music. This paper suggests that a convolutional network can learn these subtle clues or features given an appropriate representation of the music. We apply a deep convolutional neural network to a large audio dataset and empirically evaluate its performance on audio classification tasks. Our trained network demonstrates accurate performance on these tasks when presented with 5-second examples of music obtained through simple transformations of the raw audio waveform. Notably, the spectral representation of music obtained by applying a logarithmically spaced filter bank, mirroring the early stages of auditory signal transduction in mammals, proves to be particularly effective. The most successful representation for facilitating discrimination was obtained via a random matrix transform (RMT). Networks based on logarithmic filter banks and RMT achieved correct composer identification (out of 31 possibilities) in 68% and 84% of cases, respectively.
label: AI

title: Audio-Visual Sentiment Analysis for Learning Emotional Arcs in Movies
Abstract: Stories possess tremendous power, not only for entertainment but also for activating our interests and mobilizing our actions. The resonance of a story with its audience may be partially reflected in the emotional journey it takes them on. This paper utilizes machine learning methods to construct emotional arcs in movies, calculate families of arcs, and demonstrate the ability of certain arcs to predict audience engagement. The system is applied to Hollywood films and high-quality shorts found online. We begin by employing deep convolutional neural networks for audio and visual sentiment analysis. These models are trained on both new and existing large-scale datasets, enabling the computation of separate audio and visual emotional arcs. We then crowdsource annotations for 30-second video clips extracted from highs and lows in the arcs to assess the micro-level precision of the system. Precision is measured in terms of agreement in polarity between the system's predictions and annotators' ratings. These annotations are also used to combine the audio and visual predictions. Next, we examine macro-level characterizations of movies by investigating the existence of "universal shapes" of emotional arcs. Specifically, we develop a clustering approach to identify distinct classes of emotional arcs. Finally, we demonstrate on a sample corpus of short web videos that certain emotional arcs are statistically significant predictors of the number of comments a video receives. These results suggest that the emotional arcs learned by our approach effectively represent macroscopic aspects of a video story that drive audience engagement. This machine understanding could be used to predict audience reactions to video stories, ultimately enhancing our storytelling abilities and communication with one another.
label: AI

title: Deep Texture and Structure Aware Filtering Network for Image Smoothing
Abstract: Image smoothing is a fundamental task in computer vision, aiming to preserve salient structures while removing insignificant textures. This paper addresses the shortcomings of existing image smoothing methods, which struggle to distinguish textures and structures with similar low-level appearances. While deep learning approaches have begun exploring structure preservation through image smoothing, current work does not adequately address textures. To address this gap, we generate a large dataset by blending natural textures with clean structure-only images. We then build a texture prediction network (TPN) that predicts the location and magnitude of textures. By combining the TPN with a semantic structure prediction network (SPN), we create a texture and structure aware filtering network (TSAFN) capable of identifying textures to remove ("texture-awareness") and structures to preserve ("structure-awareness"). The proposed model is simple to understand and implement and demonstrates excellent performance on real-world images as well as our generated dataset.
label: AI

title: Network Analysis for Explanation
Abstract: Safety-critical systems require explainability in artificial intelligence. This paper analyzes a trained network to extract features that primarily contribute to the inference. Based on this analysis, we develop a simple solution for generating explanations of the inference processes.
label: AI

title: An End to End Deep Neural Network for Iris Segmentation in Unconstraint Scenarios
Abstract: With the increasing imaging and processing capabilities of today's mobile devices, user authentication using iris biometrics has become feasible. However, as acquisition conditions become more unconstrained and image quality typically lower than dedicated iris acquisition systems, accurate segmentation of iris regions is crucial for these devices. This work proposes an end-to-end Fully Convolutional Deep Neural Network (FCDNN) design to perform iris segmentation for lower-quality iris images. The network design process is explained in detail, and the resulting network is trained and tuned using several large public iris datasets. We provide a set of methods to generate and augment suitable lower-quality iris images from high-quality public databases. The network is initially trained on Near InfraRed (NIR) images and subsequently fine-tuned on additional datasets derived from visible images. Comprehensive inter-database comparisons are provided along with results from experiments detailing the effects of different network tunings. Finally, the proposed model is compared to SegNet-basic, and a near-optimal tuning of the network is compared to a selection of other state-of-the-art iris segmentation algorithms. The results show very promising performance from the optimized Deep Neural Networks design when compared to state-of-the-art techniques applied to the same lower-quality datasets.
label: AI

title: Multi-Scale Video Frame-Synthesis Network with Transitive Consistency Loss
Abstract: Traditional approaches to interpolate/extrapolate frames in a video sequence rely on accurate pixel correspondences between images, typically using optical flow. Their results depend on the accuracy of optical flow estimation and can produce significant artifacts when flow estimation fails. Recent methods using auto-encoders have shown impressive progress, but they are usually trained for specific interpolation/extrapolation settings and lack flexibility. To address these limitations, we propose a unified network that parameterizes the interest frame position, allowing inference of interpolated/extrapolated frames within the same framework. To achieve this, we introduce a transitive consistency loss to better regularize the network. We adopt a multi-scale structure for the network, enabling parameter sharing across multiple layers. Our approach avoids expensive global optimization required by optical flow methods and is efficient and flexible for video interpolation/extrapolation applications. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods. |||
label: AI

title: Learned Perceptual Image Enhancement
Abstract: Minimizing a loss function between enhanced and reference images is the traditional method for learning an image enhancement pipeline. While L1 and L2 losses are widely used, they may not produce perceptually appealing results. This paper proposes a novel approach that adds a learned no-reference image quality metric to the loss function, significantly enhancing the enhancement operators. This metric is implemented using a CNN trained on a large-scale dataset labeled with human aesthetic preferences. This perceptual loss allows for back-propagation during training, simultaneously optimizing for similarity to a reference image and perceptual quality. Importantly, the perceptual loss only affects training parameters, not inference time complexity. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this loss for tuning various operators, including local tone mapping and dehazing.
label: AI

title: MoDL: Model Based Deep Learning Architecture for Inverse Problems
Abstract: A model-based image reconstruction framework incorporating a CNN-based regularization prior is presented. This framework offers a systematic way to derive deep architectures for inverse problems with arbitrary structures. Explicitly accounting for the forward model allows for smaller networks with fewer parameters, reducing the need for training data and time. End-to-end training ensures that CNN weights are customized to the forward model, leading to improved performance compared to pre-trained denoisers. The framework distinguishes itself by sharing network weights across iterations and channels. Experiments show that decoupling the number of iterations from network complexity offers advantages like reduced training data requirements, lower overfitting risk, and significantly smaller memory footprints. Data-consistency is enforced by employing numerical optimization blocks like the conjugate gradients algorithm, resulting in faster convergence compared to proximal gradient methods. Faster convergence translates to improved performance, especially when limited GPU memory restricts the number of iterations.
label: AI

title: Per-Pixel Feedback for improving Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Semantic segmentation, the task of assigning labels to each pixel in an image, has seen significant advancements due to deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). However, the lack of transparency in DCNNs hinders understanding their inner workings. This paper investigates DCNNs for semantic segmentation, specifically focusing on the importance of global image information for pixel labeling. Based on experiments with discriminative regions and fixation modeling, new training loss functions are proposed for fine-tuning DCNN models. This training regime demonstrates performance improvements for the DeepLab Large FOV (VGG-16) segmentation model on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset. However, further testing across different models and datasets is needed to conclusively evaluate the benefits of the proposed loss functions.
label: AI

title: Self-supervised Multi-level Face Model Learning for Monocular Reconstruction at over 250 Hz
Abstract: Reconstructing dense 3D models of face geometry and appearance from a single image presents significant challenges due to its ill-posed nature. Many approaches rely on strong priors, like parametric face models learned from limited 3D scan data. However, these priors restrict the generalization of the diverse range of facial geometry, skin reflectance, and illumination. This paper introduces a novel approach that jointly learns a regressor for face shape, expression, reflectance, and illumination alongside a parametric face model. This multi-level face model combines the advantages of 3D Morphable Models for regularization with the generalization capabilities of a learned corrective space. The model is trained end-to-end on real-world images without dense annotations by fusing a convolutional encoder with a differentiable expert-designed renderer and a self-supervised training loss, all defined at multiple detail levels. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, this approach delivers superior reconstruction quality, better generalizes to real-world faces, and achieves a high processing speed of over 250 Hz.
label: AI

title: Stochastic reconstruction of an oolitic limestone by generative adversarial networks
Abstract: Stochastic image reconstruction, a crucial aspect of modern digital rock physics and materials analysis, aims to generate numerous representative samples of material micro-structures for upscaling, numerical computation of effective properties, and uncertainty quantification. This paper presents a method for three-dimensional stochastic image reconstruction based on generative adversarial neural networks (GANs). GANs offer an unsupervised learning framework that does not require prior inference of the probability distribution associated with the training data. Utilizing a fully convolutional neural network enables fast sampling of large volumetric images. The proposed GAN-based workflow involving network training and image generation is applied to an oolitic Ketton limestone micro-CT dataset. Minkowski functionals, effective permeability, and velocity distributions of simulated flow within the acquired images are compared with the synthetic reconstructions generated by the deep neural network. While the results show that GANs facilitate fast and accurate reconstruction of the evaluated image dataset, several open questions and challenges remain in the evaluation of generative network-based methods.
label: AI

title: Stacked Denoising Autoencoders and Transfer Learning for Immunogold Particles Detection and Recognition
Abstract: This paper presents a system for detecting immunogold particles and a Transfer Learning (TL) framework for recognizing them. Immunogold particles are a high-magnification method for selectively localizing biological molecules at the subcellular level, visible only through Electron Microscopy. The number of immunogold particles in cell walls provides insight into their composition, serving as a tool to analyze plant quality. Quantifying these particles requires laborious manual labeling of images containing hundreds of particles. The proposed system aims to alleviate this manual task. For particle detection, a LoG filter coupled with a SDA is used. To enhance recognition, the applicability of TL settings for immunogold recognition is explored. TL reuses a source problem's learning model on other datasets (target problems) containing particles of different sizes. The proposed system was developed for a specific problem on maize cells, namely determining the composition of cell wall ingrowths in endosperm transfer cells. This novel dataset, along with the code for reproducing the experiments, is made publicly available. The LoG detector alone achieved over 84% accuracy with the F-measure. TL-based immunogold recognition also showed superior performance compared to baseline models, increasing accuracy rates by 10%.
label: AI

title: Hybrid eye center localization using cascaded regression and hand-crafted model fitting
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel cascaded regressor for eye center detection. Unlike previous methods that rely solely on advanced features or powerful regressors, this approach utilizes an existing facial feature alignment method for more accurate eye detection. Robustness is enhanced by employing both advanced features and powerful regression machinery. Instead of directly using regression results, a robust circle fitting post-processing step is introduced to further refine localization accuracy. The cascaded regressor can be trained without manually annotated data using a simple hand-crafted method for eye center localization. Evaluation on the BioID, GI4E, and TalkingFace datasets demonstrates state-of-the-art performance. The manually trained regressor achieves an accuracy of 95.07% (BioID), 99.27% (GI4E), and 95.68% (TalkingFace) at an average normalized error of e < 0.05. The automatically trained regressor achieves comparable results, with accuracies of 93.9% (BioID), 99.27% (GI4E), and 95.46% (TalkingFace).
label: AI

title: On Usage of Autoencoders and Siamese Networks for Online Handwritten Signature Verification
Abstract: This paper presents a novel writer-independent global feature extraction framework for automatic signature verification, aiming to create robust systems for distinguishing genuine and forged signatures. The method utilizes an autoencoder to model the sample space into a fixed-length latent space and a Siamese Network to classify fixed-length samples obtained from the autoencoder based on reference samples, identifying them as "Genuine" or "Forged." The application of Attention Mechanism and Downsampling significantly improved the framework's accuracy. Evaluation on the SigWiComp2013 Japanese and GPDSsyntheticOnLineOffLineSignature datasets demonstrates the framework's effectiveness. An EER of 8.65% was achieved on the SigWiComp2013 Japanese dataset, representing a 1.2% improvement over the best-reported result. On the GPDSsyntheticOnLineOffLineSignature dataset, average EERs of 0.13%, 0.12%, 0.21%, and 0.25% were achieved for 150, 300, 1000, and 2000 test subjects, respectively, indicating significant improvement over the best-reported results. The framework's neural network-based approach, involving simple consecutive matrix multiplications, leads to a lower computational cost compared to conventional methods like DTW and allows for concurrent use on devices like GPU, TPU, etc.
label: AI

title: Exploring the Landscape of Spatial Robustness
Abstract: Research on adversarial robustness has primarily focused on perturbations bound in p-norms. However, state-of-the-art models remain vulnerable to more natural classes of perturbations like translations and rotations. This work investigates the vulnerability of neural network-based classifiers to rotations and translations. While data augmentation offers limited robustness, robust optimization and test-time input aggregation techniques are employed to significantly enhance robustness. Unlike the p-norm case, first-order methods cannot reliably find worst-case perturbations for spatial robustness, highlighting the need for further research in this distinct setting.
label: AI

title: Super-FAN: Integrated facial landmark localization and super-resolution of real-world low resolution faces in arbitrary poses with GANs
Abstract: This paper tackles two challenging tasks: improving the quality of low-resolution facial images and accurately locating facial landmarks on such images. To achieve this, five key contributions are made: (a) Super-FAN, the first end-to-end system addressing both tasks simultaneously, is introduced. It integrates a sub-network for face alignment through heatmap regression into a GAN-based super-resolution algorithm, optimizing a novel heatmap loss. (b) The benefits of joint training are illustrated through improved results on a wider range of facial poses and real-world images. (c) A new residual-based architecture is proposed, improving face super-resolution. (d) Significant improvements over the state-of-the-art are demonstrated for both face super-resolution and alignment. (e) The first good results on real-world low-resolution images are presented qualitatively.
label: AI

title: On the Duality Between Retinex and Image Dehazing
Abstract: Image dehazing focuses on removing visibility loss caused by fog in outdoor images. Retinex, a color vision model mimicking the Human Visual System's ability to discount varying illuminations, has been widely explored for image enhancement. This paper demonstrates a simple linear relationship connecting these seemingly unrelated problems. Most Retinex-based algorithms increase image brightness, making them suitable for dehazing by directly applying Retinex to an inverted hazy image. The paper provides theoretical proof that Retinex on inverted intensities solves the image dehazing problem. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative results show that various Retinex implementations can be transformed into effective image dehazing algorithms, competing with more complex methods and overcoming key challenges in this domain.
label: AI

title: End-to-end Learning of Deterministic Decision Trees
Abstract: Conventional decision trees offer interpretability, low computational footprint, and the ability to learn from limited data. However, they lack the end-to-end trainability and ability to learn optimal features from scratch, which are key strengths of deep learning. While previous work has addressed this, it compromised decision trees' advantage of routing samples through a small subset of nodes. This paper introduces a fully probabilistic model and Expectation-Maximization training scheme for decision trees, transitioning to determinism at test time through deterministic annealing. An analysis of learned oblique split parameters on image datasets shows the potential for training Neural Networks at each split node. This work presents the first end-to-end learning scheme for deterministic decision trees, achieving results comparable or superior to standard oblique decision tree algorithms.
label: AI

title: Using Rule-Based Labels for Weak Supervised Learning: A ChemNet for Transferable Chemical Property Prediction
Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved human-level accuracy in image and speech recognition tasks with access to large datasets. However, data in chemistry is inherently small and fragmented. This work proposes an approach using rule-based knowledge to train ChemNet, a transferable and generalizable DNN for chemical property prediction. ChemNet learns in a weak-supervised manner from large unlabeled chemical databases. When coupled with transfer learning for predicting other smaller datasets, ChemNet's accuracy surpasses contemporary DNN models trained using conventional supervised learning. Notably, the pre-training approach is equally effective on CNN (Chemception) and RNN (SMILES2vec) models, demonstrating its architecture-agnostic nature and effectiveness across data modalities. Pre-trained ChemNet, incorporating chemistry domain knowledge, enables the development of generalizable neural networks for accurate prediction of novel chemical properties.
label: AI

title: Incremental Learning in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks Using Partial Network Sharing
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural network (DCNN)-based supervised learning is a widely used approach for large-scale image classification. However, retraining these networks for new, previously unseen data requires significant computational time and energy. Additionally, previously seen training samples may not be available during retraining. This paper proposes an efficient training methodology and incrementally growing DCNN to learn new tasks while retaining knowledge from previous tasks. Inspired by transfer learning techniques, the proposed methodology avoids forgetting previously learned tasks. An updated network for learning new classes is formed using previously learned convolutional layers (shared from the initial part of the base network) and additional newly added convolutional kernels in later layers. The "clone-and-branch" technique allows the network to learn new tasks sequentially without performance degradation in old tasks. Evaluation on several recognition applications shows that the proposed approach achieves classification accuracy comparable to regular incremental learning, while offering energy efficiency, reduced storage requirements, memory access, and training time.
label: AI

title: AdaComp : Adaptive Residual Gradient Compression for Data-Parallel Distributed Training
Abstract: Highly distributed training of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) on future compute platforms (offering 100 TeraOps/s of computational capacity) is expected to be severely communication constrained. To address this limitation, novel gradient compression techniques are needed that are computationally efficient, applicable to diverse DNN layers, and adaptable to variations in network architectures and hyperparameters. This paper introduces AdaComp, an Adaptive Residual Gradient Compression scheme. AdaComp utilizes localized selection of gradient residues and automatically tunes the compression rate based on local activity. The method demonstrates excellent results on a wide range of state-of-the-art Deep Learning models across domains (vision, speech, language), datasets (MNIST, CIFAR10, ImageNet, BN50, Shakespeare), optimizers (SGD with momentum, Adam), and network parameters. Exploiting both sparsity and quantization, AdaComp achieves end-to-end compression rates of ~200X for fully-connected and recurrent layers, and ~40X for convolutional layers, without compromising model accuracy.
label: AI

title: Creating Capsule Wardrobes from Fashion Images
Abstract: This paper proposes an automated method for creating capsule wardrobes. Given a set of candidate garments and accessories, the algorithm aims to assemble a minimal set that provides maximum mix-and-match outfit options. This task is formulated as a subset selection problem. To enable efficient subset selection across all outfit combinations, submodular objective functions are developed to capture visual compatibility, versatility, and user-specific preferences. Since adding garments to a capsule expands its outfit possibilities, an iterative approach is devised for near-optimal submodular function maximization. An unsupervised method is presented to learn visual compatibility from real-world full body outfit photos, which translates well to cleaner catalog photos and outperforms existing methods. Results on thousands of pieces from popular fashion websites demonstrate the potential of automatic capsule creation to mimic the expertise of skilled fashionistas in assembling flexible wardrobes while being significantly more scalable.
label: AI

title: Using SVDD in SimpleMKL for 3D-Shapes Filtering
Abstract: This paper proposes the adaptation of Support Vector Data Description (SVDD) to the multiple kernel case (MK-SVDD), based on SimpleMKL. Additionally, a variant called Slim-MK-SVDD is introduced, capable of generating a tighter frontier around the data. For comparison, equivalent methods are developed for One-Class SVM, known to be similar to SVDD for certain kernel shapes. These algorithms are illustrated in the context of 3D-shapes filtering and outlier detection. In the 3D-shapes problem, the goal is to select sub-categories of 3D-shapes, each learned using the proposed algorithm to create a filter. For outlier detection, the algorithms are applied for both unsupervised and supervised cases.
label: AI

title: Disentangled Person Image Generation
Abstract: Generating novel and realistic person images is a challenging task due to the complex interplay of image factors like foreground, background, and pose information. This work presents a two-stage reconstruction pipeline that learns a disentangled representation of these factors and generates novel person images simultaneously. First, a multi-branched reconstruction network disentangles and encodes the factors into embedding features, which are then recombined to reconstruct the input image. Second, three mapping functions are learned adversarially to map Gaussian noise to the learned embedding feature space for each factor. This framework enables manipulation of the foreground, background, and pose of the input image, as well as the generation of targeted manipulations through sampling new embedding features. Experiments on Market-1501 and Deepfashion datasets demonstrate that the model generates realistic person images with new elements and manipulates generated factors, interpolating in-between states. Experiments on Market-1501 also show the model's benefits for the person re-identification task.
label: AI

title: In-Place Activated BatchNorm for Memory-Optimized Training of DNNs
Abstract: This paper presents In-Place Activated Batch Normalization (InPlace-ABN), a novel approach to drastically reduce the training memory footprint of modern deep neural networks in a computationally efficient way. InPlace-ABN substitutes the conventional BatchNorm + Activation layer sequence with a single plugin layer, avoiding invasive framework changes and offering straightforward applicability for existing deep learning frameworks. Memory savings of up to 50% are achieved by dropping intermediate results and recovering required information during the backward pass through the inversion of stored forward results, with only a minor increase (0.8-2%) in computation time. The paper demonstrates how frequently used checkpointing approaches can be made computationally as efficient as InPlace-ABN. Experiments on image classification show on-par results with state-of-the-art approaches on ImageNet-1k. For the memory-demanding task of semantic segmentation, the paper reports results for COCO-Stuff, Cityscapes, and Mapillary Vistas, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the latter without additional training data but in a single-scale and -model scenario.
label: AI

title: Solving internal covariate shift in deep learning with linked neurons
Abstract: This work proposes a novel solution to the problem of internal covariate shift and dying neurons using the concept of linked neurons. Neuron linkage is defined through two constraints: first, all neuron activations within a linkage must share the same operating point, meaning they share input weights. Second, neurons are linked only if at least one member of the linkage has a non-zero gradient in regard to the activation function's input, ensuring non-flat and non-zero operation for at least one member. This simple change has profound implications for network learning dynamics. The paper explores the consequences of this proposal, showing that linked neurons implicitly solve internal covariate shift. As a result, arbitrarily large networks can be trained without architectural or algorithmic tricks, eliminating the need for re-normalization schemes like Batch Normalization and halving training time. It also eliminates the need for standardized input data. Results show that linked neurons effectively solve these problems and offer a competitive alternative to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating promising results. |||
