title: Consistent Multiple Graph Matching with Multi-layer Random Walks Synchronization
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of finding corresponding elements across multiple graphs with complex structures, while maintaining consistency in the matching process.  The authors propose a novel framework that represents each graph pair as a multi-layer structure and jointly considers all matching pairs.  Their approach utilizes a robust multiple graph matching method based on multi-layer random walks, synchronizing the movement of random walkers to identify consistent matching candidates.  Extensive experiments demonstrate the method's robust and accurate performance compared to existing multiple graph matching algorithms.
label: AI

title: Maximum Classifier Discrepancy for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
Abstract: This work introduces a novel approach for unsupervised domain adaptation, addressing limitations in adversarial learning methods.  Existing methods train domain classifiers to distinguish source and target features, leading to ambiguous feature generation near class boundaries and difficulty in matching feature distributions across domains.  The proposed method tackles these issues by aligning source and target distributions using task-specific decision boundaries.  It maximizes the discrepancy between classifier outputs to identify target samples far from the source support, and a feature generator learns to produce target features close to the support to minimize the discrepancy.  The method achieves superior performance on image classification and semantic segmentation datasets.
label: AI

title: Learning Random Fourier Features by Hybrid Constrained Optimization
Abstract: This paper proposes a teacher-learner framework for efficient kernel embedding, addressing the computational bottleneck in the testing phase of kernel embedding algorithms.  The framework leverages high-precision embeddings as the "teacher" to transfer data information to computation-efficient kernel embeddings, the "learner."  The authors propose a novel constrained variational expectation maximization (CVEM) approach, employing the alternate direction method of multipliers (ADMM) over a nonconvex domain in the maximization step.  Two specific formulations, masked and blocked Computation-Efficient RFF (CERF), are presented based on Random Fourier Features (RFF), using a random binary mask or a block structure on the transformation matrix.  Empirical studies demonstrate CERF's significant performance improvement over RFF for kernel methods, meeting specific arithmetic operation requirements and suitability for structured matrix multiplication in Fastfood-type algorithms.
label: AI

title: Broadcasting Convolutional Network for Visual Relational Reasoning
Abstract: This paper introduces the Broadcasting Convolutional Network (BCN) for extracting key object features from an entire input image and understanding their relationship with local features.  BCN is a simple module that collects effective spatial features, embeds location information, and broadcasts it across the feature maps.  The authors further propose the Multi-Relational Network (multiRN), which enhances the Relation Network (RN) by integrating the BCN module.  multiRN extends the "pairwise relations" concept in conventional RNs to "multiwise relations," allowing each object to be related with multiple objects at once, resulting in O(n) complexity for n objects, a substantial computational gain over RNs' O(n^2) complexity.  Experiments demonstrate multiRN's state-of-the-art performance on the CLEVR dataset, highlighting the effectiveness of BCN in relation reasoning problems.
label: AI

title: TV-GAN: Generative Adversarial Network Based Thermal to Visible Face Recognition
Abstract: This work addresses the challenge of face recognition using thermal camera images, which are captured in non-light environments.  Due to the limited availability of thermal imagery data compared to visible light domain (VLD) data, directly applying VLD-trained face recognition models to thermal images yields unsatisfactory results.  The authors propose a Thermal-to-Visible Generative Adversarial Network (TV-GAN) to transform thermal face images into their VLD counterparts while preserving identity information sufficient for VLD face recognition models.  Unlike previous methods, TV-GAN utilizes an explicit closed-set face recognition loss to regularize the discriminator network training, conveying identity information to the generator network through gradient loss.  Experiments demonstrate that this additional regularization enhances identity preservation during thermal image translation, leading to improved recognition performance.
label: AI

title: Take it in your stride: Do we need striding in CNNs?
Abstract: This paper provides a novel mathematical perspective on the role of the striding operator in convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which is commonly used to reduce receptive field overlap and spatial dimensions.  While striding offers clear heuristic benefits in parameter reduction, its mathematical role in CNN learning has remained unclear.  The authors demonstrate theoretically that a CNN incorporating striding can always be represented as an equivalent non-striding CNN with more filters and smaller size.  This equivalence reveals striding as a mechanism for parameter sharing among channels, reducing training complexity.  The framework provides a new mathematical perspective on striding, facilitating future theoretical analysis of CNNs.
label: AI

title: CNNs are Globally Optimal Given Multi-Layer Support
Abstract: This paper explores a novel strategy for accelerating CNN training by employing an alternation strategy between weights and support.  The authors replace the ReLU nonlinearity with positive hard-thresholding, reinterpreting it as a binary state vector.  This allows the entire CNN to become linear when the multi-layer support is known, and under certain conditions, a global optima can be found through local descent.  The alternation strategy leads to significantly faster convergence rates, desirable theoretical properties, and state-of-the-art results on large-scale datasets like ImageNet and other benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Examples that Fool Detectors
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the existence of adversarial examples for object detectors, specifically Faster RCNN and YOLO, which can be maliciously used to create security hazards in environments with smart vehicles.  The construction of adversarial examples for detectors differs significantly from that for classifiers, and the structure of detectors, requiring bounding box search and imprecise estimation, makes it likely that adversarial patterns are disrupted.  The authors show that their adversarial examples generalize well across digital sequences despite requiring large perturbations and also produce physically adversarial objects.
label: AI

title: Stacked Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks for Jointly Learning Shadow Detection and Shadow Removal
Abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-task framework for jointly learning shadow detection and removal, addressing the limitations of existing single-task approaches.  The proposed framework utilizes a STacked Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (ST-CGAN) composed of two stacked CGANs, each with a generator and a discriminator.  The first generator produces a shadow detection mask from a shadow image, and the second generator generates a shadow-free image from the shadow image and its predicted mask.  The discriminators model higher-level relationships and global scene characteristics for the detected shadow region and reconstruction, respectively.  The stacked paradigm offers a novel approach compared to multi-branch versions, enabling mutual benefit from both tasks.  The framework is evaluated on a newly constructed large-scale benchmark and shows consistent advantages over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: CURE-TSR: Challenging Unreal and Real Environments for Traffic Sign Recognition
Abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of traffic sign recognition algorithms under challenging conditions, highlighting the limitations of existing datasets in size and coverage.  The authors introduce the Challenging Unreal and Real Environments for Traffic Sign Recognition (CURE-TSR) dataset, containing over two million images based on real-world and simulator data.  Performance benchmarking of existing solutions in real-world scenarios reveals that challenging conditions significantly impact baseline methods, particularly those involving loss or displacement of spatial information.  The paper also explores the effectiveness of data augmentation, demonstrating that combining simulator and real-world data enhances average recognition performance.  The CURE-TSR dataset is publicly available.
label: AI

title: A Novel Model for Arbitration between Planning and Habitual Control Systems
Abstract: This paper proposes a general architecture for decision making and control, integrating both habitual action selection and deliberate planning systems.  Humans rely on multiple systems for these processes, where habitual systems use previously rewarded actions while deliberate systems use internal models to plan.  The proposed architecture includes an arbitrator that controls which subsystem is used based on the situation.  The system is implemented for a target-reaching task with a simulated robotic arm, incorporating a supervised internal model and deep reinforcement learning.  Through varying task conditions, the paper demonstrates the system's ability to learn kinematics without prior knowledge, adapt to changes in environmental reward and kinematics, and operate under occluded vision.  Comparison with exclusive deliberate planning and habitual control models showcases the benefits of this integrated approach, enabling fast decisions in reliable situations and optimized performance in changing environments.
label: AI

title: High performance ultra-low-precision convolutions on mobile devices
Abstract: This paper addresses the computational constraints of mobile deep learning, particularly for real-time computer vision workloads running on older consumer phones.  The authors provide an open-source implementation and analysis of ultra-low-precision (<4 bit precision) implementations of core deep learning primitives for ARMv7 devices, achieving speedups of 4x-20x compared to float32 and int8 baselines.  The paper focuses on the state-of-the-art for ultra-low-precision deep learning on ARMv7 devices, showcasing the potential for significant performance gains on resource-constrained mobile platforms.
label: AI

title: Tomographic Reconstruction using Global Statistical Prior
Abstract: This paper proposes a global prior for improving both speed and quality in tomographic reconstruction within a compressive sensing framework.  To compensate for limited measurements, the authors leverage information from templates, which are pre-reconstructed structurally similar images.  Previous work has utilized patch-based dictionary priors.  This paper introduces a global prior by constructing an eigenspace from a set of representative 2D templates, guiding the iterative reconstruction of a similar slice from sparse acquisition data.  Experiments demonstrate that using an appropriate global prior leads to faster and more accurate reconstruction compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Deep Regionlets for Object Detection
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel object detection framework called "Deep Regionlets," bridging deep neural networks and conventional detection schema for accurate generic object detection.  The framework incorporates regionlets, which model object deformation and aspect ratios, into an end-to-end trainable deep learning architecture.  It consists of a region selection network and a deep regionlet learning module.  The region selection network guides feature learning region selection based on detection bounding box proposals, while the regionlet learning module focuses on local feature selection and transformation to mitigate local variations.  Deep Regionlets enable non-rectangular region selection and utilize a "gating network" for soft regionlet selection and pooling.  End-to-end training eliminates the need for additional efforts.  Ablation studies and experiments on PASCAL VOC and Microsoft COCO datasets show that Deep Regionlets outperform state-of-the-art algorithms like RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN, even without segmentation labels.
label: AI

title: Controllable Top-down Feature Transformer
Abstract: This paper investigates the intrinsic transformation of feature maps across convolutional network layers with explicit top-down control.  The authors develop a top-down feature transformer (TFT) that accounts for hidden layer transformation while maintaining consistency across layers, capturing underlying feature transformation processes independent of specific training images.  TFT provides insights into CNN internal feature representation and transformation under top-down processes.  The paper demonstrates TFT's significant advantage over data-driven approaches in building data-independent spatial transformations and highlights its applicability in data augmentation and image style transfer.
label: AI

title: SGAN: An Alternative Training of Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes an alternative training process called SGAN for Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), addressing the challenges associated with their training.  GANs have proven successful in data synthesis but are notorious for being difficult to train, requiring time-consuming and human-involved development.  SGAN involves training multiple "local" adversarial network pairs independently, allowing a "global" supervising pair to be trained against them.  This aims to improve mode coverage and prevent the global pair from getting trapped in unsatisfactory local minima or facing oscillations.  The global pair never affects the local ones, ensuring stability.  Experiments demonstrate SGAN's superiority over standard training in mitigating mode collapse, achieving stability during convergence, and surprisingly, accelerating convergence speed.
label: AI

title: Generative Adversarial Perturbations
Abstract: This paper proposes novel generative models for creating adversarial examples, subtly perturbed images resembling natural images but designed to fool pre-trained models.  The authors introduce trainable deep neural networks for generating image-agnostic and image-dependent adversarial perturbations for both targeted and non-targeted attacks.  The proposed architectures achieve impressive results in fooling classification and semantic segmentation models, eliminating the need for task-specific hand-crafted attack methods.  Extensive experiments on high-resolution datasets like ImageNet and Cityscapes demonstrate that the perturbations achieve high fooling rates with minimal perturbation norms and are faster than current iterative methods during inference.
label: AI

title: Burst Denoising with Kernel Prediction Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a technique for jointly denoising bursts of images captured from a handheld camera.  The authors propose a convolutional neural network architecture for predicting spatially varying kernels that align and denoise frames.  The approach includes a synthetic data generation method based on a realistic noise formation model and an optimization guided by an annealed loss function to avoid local minima.  The model achieves state-of-the-art performance across various noise levels on both real and synthetic data.
label: AI

title: From Lifestyle Vlogs to Everyday Interactions
Abstract: This work addresses the lack of good training data for understanding basic human interactions, such as getting out of bed or opening a refrigerator.  Previous efforts have focused on explicit data collection, starting with action labels and searching for tagged videos.  This paper proposes an implicit approach, starting with a large collection of interaction-rich video data from Internet Lifestyle Vlogs and subsequently annotating and analyzing it.  This approach allows for greater scale and diversity in actions and actors, exposing biases present in explicitly gathered data.  The paper analyzes the central component of interaction, hands, and benchmarks two tasks: identifying semantic object contact at the video level and non-semantic contact state at the frame level.  It also demonstrates future prediction of hand movements.
label: AI

title: Joint 3D Proposal Generation and Object Detection from View Aggregation
Abstract: This paper introduces AVOD, an Aggregate View Object Detection network for autonomous driving scenarios.  The neural network architecture uses LIDAR point clouds and RGB images to generate shared features for a region proposal network (RPN) and a second stage detector network.  The RPN utilizes a novel architecture for multimodal feature fusion on high-resolution feature maps to generate reliable 3D object proposals for multiple object classes in road scenes.  The second stage detector network performs accurate 3D bounding box regression and category classification to predict the extent, orientation, and classification of objects.  The proposed architecture achieves state-of-the-art results on the KITTI 3D object detection benchmark while running in real time with low memory footprint, making it suitable for deployment in autonomous vehicles. |||
label: AI

title: Stretching Domain Adaptation: How far is too far?
Abstract: Deep learning has made significant progress in visual recognition, but it often requires extensive annotated data. Unsupervised domain adaptation offers an alternative, reducing the need for labeled data. However, prior domain adaptation evaluations have been limited to relatively similar datasets. This work introduces a new dataset suite to comprehensively evaluate cross-modality domain adaptation problems. We evaluate several state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets and our new suite, pushing the limits of unsupervised domain adaptation. We also propose a new domain adaptation network, Deep MagNet, which effectively transfers knowledge for cross-modality domain adaptation. Deep MagNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on two benchmark datasets and demonstrates consistent improvements on our proposed dataset suite.
label: AI

title: ObamaNet: Photo-realistic lip-sync from text
Abstract: ObamaNet is the first architecture capable of generating synchronized audio and photo-realistic lip-sync videos from any new text. Unlike other lip-sync approaches, ObamaNet relies solely on fully trainable neural modules, eliminating the need for traditional computer graphics methods. The architecture employs three main modules: a Char2Wav-based text-to-speech network, a time-delayed LSTM for generating mouth-keypoints synchronized with the audio, and a Pix2Pix-based network for generating video frames conditioned on the keypoints.
label: AI

title: Pose-Normalized Image Generation for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Person Re-identification (re-id) faces challenges due to the lack of cross-view paired training data and the need to learn discriminative identity-sensitive and view-invariant features in the presence of large pose variations. We propose a novel deep person image generation model, termed pose-normalization GAN (PN-GAN), to address these challenges. PN-GAN synthesizes realistic person images conditioned on pose, facilitating the learning of deep re-id features that are free from pose variations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this new feature both independently and in combination with features learned from original images. Notably, our model exhibits strong transferability to new re-id datasets without requiring any training data for fine-tuning, paving the way for truly scalable re-id models.
label: AI

title: Beyond the Pixel-Wise Loss for Topology-Aware Delineation
Abstract: Delineating curvilinear structures is a crucial task in Computer Vision with numerous practical applications. While Deep Learning has led to advancements in automatic delineation, existing approaches primarily focus on optimizing deep architectures while relying on traditional pixel-wise losses like binary cross-entropy. We argue that pixel-wise losses are inadequate for this problem due to their inability to reflect the topological impact of prediction errors. We propose a novel loss term that considers the higher-order topological features of linear structures. Additionally, we introduce a refinement pipeline that iteratively applies the same model to enhance delineations at each step, maintaining a constant model complexity and parameter count. Our new loss term and refinement pipeline, when combined with the standard pixel-wise loss, significantly improve the quality of predicted delineations, sometimes doubling the accuracy compared to using binary cross-entropy alone. We demonstrate the superiority of our approach on diverse data, from microscopy to aerial images.
label: AI

title: Learning to Write Stylized Chinese Characters by Reading a Handful of Examples
Abstract: Automatically generating stylized Chinese characters is an attractive yet challenging task due to its wide applicability. We present a novel framework, Style-Aware Variational Auto-Encoder (SA-VAE), for flexible Chinese character generation. Our approach disentangles latent features into content-related and style-related components, capturing the distinct characteristics of a character. To address the complex shapes and structures, we incorporate structure information as prior knowledge into our framework to guide the generation process. SA-VAE exhibits a powerful one-shot/low-shot generalization ability, inferring the style component from a single or few examples of characters with unseen styles. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to learn to write new-style Chinese characters from limited examples. Extensive experiments demonstrate SA-VAE's effectiveness in generating diverse stylized Chinese characters by combining feature vectors corresponding to different contents and styles, showcasing its significant potential in real-world applications.
label: AI

title: Detecting Curve Text in the Wild: New Dataset and New Solution
Abstract: Scene text detection has progressed significantly, transitioning from axis-aligned rectangles to rotated rectangles and finally to quadrangles. However, current datasets contain limited curve text, which is prevalent in scene images like signboards and product names. To address the challenge of reading curve text in real-world scenarios, we introduce CTW1500, a new curve text dataset containing over 10k text annotations in 1,500 images. Based on CTW1500, we propose a novel polygon-based curve text detector (CTD) that directly detects curve text without relying on empirical combinations. By seamlessly integrating the recurrent transverse and longitudinal offset connection (TLOC), our method becomes end-to-end trainable, learning the inherent connection among position offsets. This allows CTD to explore contextual information rather than predicting points independently, resulting in smoother and more accurate detection. We further introduce two post-processing methods, non-polygon suppress (NPS) and polygonal non-maximum suppression (PNMS), to further enhance detection accuracy. Our approach is designed for universal applicability and can be trained with rectangular or quadrilateral bounding boxes without additional effort. Experimental results on CTW-1500 demonstrate our method's superiority over state-of-the-art methods even with a lightweight backbone. Evaluated on curve or non-curve subsets, CTD + TLOC consistently achieves the best results. Code is available at https://github.com/Yuliang-Liu/Curve-Text-Detector.
label: AI

title: Guided Labeling using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks, has become a powerful tool in computer vision. However, the need for large, manually labeled datasets limits its applicability to various areas. We propose a simple and efficient method, called guided labeling, for automatically determining which samples from an unlabeled dataset should be labeled. By employing this procedure, we significantly reduce the number of samples requiring manual labeling compared to random selection.
label: AI

title: Separating Reflection and Transmission Images in the Wild
Abstract: Reflections from common semi-reflectors, such as glass windows, can hinder the performance of computer vision algorithms. Existing methods effectively remove reflections from synthetic data and controlled scenarios but rely on strong assumptions and fail to generalize well to real-world images. We challenge the misconception that polarization information readily addresses this challenge in real-world images. We present a deep learning approach to separate the reflected and transmitted components of recorded irradiance, explicitly utilizing the polarization properties of light. To train our model, we introduce an accurate synthetic data generation pipeline that simulates realistic reflections, including those generated by curved and non-ideal surfaces, non-static scenes, and high-dynamic-range scenes.
label: AI

title: Automatic Segmentation and Overall Survival Prediction in Gliomas using Fully Convolutional Neural Network and Texture Analysis
Abstract: This paper proposes a fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) for segmenting gliomas from Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI). A fully automatic, voxel-based classification is achieved by training a 23-layer deep FCNN on 2-D slices extracted from patient volumes. The network was trained on slices from 130 patients and validated on 50 patients. For survival prediction, texture and shape-based features were extracted from T1 post-contrast volume to train an XGBoost regressor. On the BraTS 2017 validation set, our scheme achieved a mean whole tumor, tumor core, and active Dice score of 0.83, 0.69, and 0.69, respectively. We also achieved an accuracy of 52% for overall survival prediction.
label: AI

title: Attacking Visual Language Grounding with Adversarial Examples: A Case Study on Neural Image Captioning
Abstract: Visual language grounding is extensively studied in modern neural image captioning systems, typically employing an encoder-decoder framework with a convolutional neural network (CNN) for image feature extraction and a recurrent neural network (RNN) for caption generation. To investigate the robustness of language grounding to adversarial perturbations in machine vision and perception, we introduce Show-and-Fool, a novel algorithm for crafting adversarial examples in neural image captioning. Show-and-Fool provides two evaluation approaches: assessing whether systems can be misled into outputting random captions or keywords. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that our algorithm successfully generates visually similar adversarial examples with randomly targeted captions or keywords, showcasing high transferability to other image captioning systems. This reveals new robustness implications for neural image captioning and provides insights into visual language grounding.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Multi-Domain Image Translation with Domain-Specific Encoders/Decoders
Abstract: Unsupervised Image-to-Image Translation has achieved remarkable progress. However, current approaches primarily focus on one model with two domains, leading to substantial training time and model parameter costs ($O(n^2)$ complexity) when enabling free transfer between n domains. To address this issue, we introduce Domain-Bank, a novel and unified framework consisting of a global shared auto-encoder and n domain-specific encoders/decoders, assuming a universal shared-latent space. This approach reduces complexity to $O(n)$ in model parameters and significantly reduces training time. Despite its high efficiency, Domain-Bank delivers comparable or even better image translation results than state-of-the-art methods on various challenging tasks, including face image translation, fashion-clothes translation, and painting style translation. We also apply Domain-Bank to domain adaptation and achieve state-of-the-art performance on digit benchmark datasets. Moreover, the explicit representation of domain-specific decoders and the universal shared-latent space enable incremental learning by adding new domain encoders/decoders. Linear combination of different domain representations is also achieved by fusing corresponding decoders.
label: AI

title: Saliency Preservation in Low-Resolution Grayscale Images
Abstract: Visual salience detection, a fundamental mechanism in nature, has evolved over 500 million years. In contrast, many state-of-the-art computational saliency models are complex and inefficient. Most saliency models process high-resolution color (HC) images. However, insights into the evolutionary origins of visual salience suggest that achromatic low-resolution vision is crucial for its speed and efficiency. Previous studies have shown that low-resolution color and high-resolution grayscale images preserve saliency information. However, the preservation of saliency in low-resolution grayscale (LG) images has not been investigated. This study explores the biological and computational rationale for LG and demonstrates, through human eye-tracking and computational modeling experiments, that saliency information is preserved in LG images. We further demonstrate significant speedups in model training and detection times when using LG images. We conclude by advocating for LG images for fast and efficient salience detection.
label: AI

title: Learning Semantic Concepts and Order for Image and Sentence Matching
Abstract: Image and sentence matching has made significant progress, but challenges remain due to the large visual-semantic discrepancy. This arises from the fact that pixel-level image representations often lack the high-level semantic information present in their matched sentences. We propose a semantic-enhanced image and sentence matching model to address this issue. Our model improves image representation by learning semantic concepts and organizing them in a correct semantic order. Given an image, we first use a multi-regional multi-label CNN to predict its semantic concepts, including objects, properties, actions, etc. Recognizing that different semantic concept orders lead to diverse semantic meanings, we employ a context-gated sentence generation scheme for semantic order learning. This scheme leverages both the image global context containing concept relations as a reference and the groundtruth semantic order in the matched sentence as supervision. After obtaining the improved image representation, we learn the sentence representation with a conventional LSTM and then jointly perform image and sentence matching and sentence generation for model learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our learned semantic concepts and order, achieving state-of-the-art results on two public benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: AdaBatch: Adaptive Batch Sizes for Training Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Training deep neural networks with Stochastic Gradient Descent or its variants requires careful tuning of both learning rate and batch size. While smaller batch sizes generally lead to faster convergence in training epochs, larger batch sizes offer greater parallelism and better computational efficiency. We introduce a novel training approach that adaptively increases batch size during the training process instead of statically choosing a single batch size for all epochs. Our method achieves the convergence rate of small batch sizes while attaining performance comparable to large batch sizes. We analyze our approach using the standard AlexNet, ResNet, and VGG networks on popular CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet datasets. Our results demonstrate that learning with adaptive batch sizes can improve performance by factors of up to 6.25 on 4 NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPUs, while changing accuracy by less than 1% relative to training with fixed batch sizes.
label: AI

title: Towards Recovery of Conditional Vectors from Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs) enable the generation of samples conditioned on specific external information. The ability to recover latent and conditional vectors from a cGAN holds significant potential in various applications, from image manipulation for entertainment to neural network diagnosis for security purposes. This work demonstrates the feasibility of recovering both latent and conditional vectors from generated images given the generator of a cGAN. This recovery is non-trivial due to the often multi-layered non-linearity of deep neural networks. We further investigate the impact of this recovery on real natural images. Our findings reveal a gap between the recovery performance on generated and real images, which we attribute to the difference in data distributions. Experiments evaluating the recovered conditional vectors and reconstructed images from these vectors demonstrate promising results both quantitatively and qualitatively.
label: AI

title: Deep Anticipation: Light Weight Intelligent Mobile Sensing in IoT by Recurrent Architecture
Abstract: The burgeoning IoT era is shaping the future of mobile services. Advanced communication technology facilitates heterogeneous connectivity where mobile devices broadcast information to everything. Mobile applications like robotics and vehicles connecting to the cloud and surroundings transition from short-range on-board sensor perception to long-range mobile-sensing perception. However, mobile sensing perception introduces new challenges in efficiently analyzing and intelligently interpreting the deluge of IoT data in mission-critical services. This article models these challenges as latency, packet loss, and measurement noise, which significantly deteriorate the reliability and quality of IoT data. We propose a novel architecture leveraging recurrent neural networks (RNN) and Kalman filtering to anticipate motions and interactions between objects. The core idea is to learn environmental dynamics through recurrent networks. To enhance the robustness of IoT communication, we integrate Kalman filtering, implementing a prediction and correction step. This architecture learns to develop a biased belief between prediction and measurement in various situations. We evaluate our approach using synthetic and real-world datasets with noise simulating the challenges of IoT communications. Our method brings a new level of IoT intelligence, exhibiting a lightweight design compared to other state-of-the-art convolutional recurrent architectures, making it ideal for resource-limited mobile applications.
label: AI

title: What's in my closet?: Image classification using fuzzy logic
Abstract: A fuzzy system was developed in MATLAB to classify clothing items as dresses, shirts, or pants from a series of input images. The system was initialized using high-contrast vector images of each clothing item as the state closest to a direct solution. Nine additional user-input images (three of each item) were utilized to determine the characteristic function of each item and recognize patterns. Mamdani inference systems were employed for edge location and identification of characteristic regions of interest for each clothing item. Based on these non-dimensional trends, a second Mamdani fuzzy inference system was used to classify each image as containing a shirt, a dress, or a pair of pants. The paper outlines the fuzzy inference system and image processing techniques used to create this image pattern recognition system.
label: AI

title: Learning to Forecast Videos of Human Activity with Multi-granularity Models and Adaptive Rendering
Abstract: We present an approach for forecasting video of complex human activity involving multiple people. Direct pixel-level prediction is too simplistic for handling the appearance variability in complex activities. Hence, we introduce novel intermediate representations. Our architecture combines a hierarchical temporal model for predicting human poses and encoder-decoder convolutional neural networks for rendering target appearances. Our hierarchical model captures interactions among people by adopting a dynamic group-based interaction mechanism. Our appearance rendering network encodes the targets' appearances by learning adaptive appearance filters using a fully convolutional network. These filters are then placed in encoder-decoder neural networks to complete the rendering process. We demonstrate that our model generates videos superior to state-of-the-art methods and effectively handles complex human activity scenarios in video forecasting.
label: AI

title: Recognizing Plans by Learning Embeddings from Observed Action Distributions
Abstract: Recent advancements in visual activity recognition have opened possibilities for applications like automated video surveillance. Effective approaches for such problems require the ability to recognize agent plans from video information. While traditional plan recognition algorithms rely on sophisticated planning domain models, a promising recent direction involves learning approximated (or shallow) domain models directly from observed activity sequences. However, these approaches require observed action sequences as input. In many cases, especially when processing raw data, there is significant uncertainty about the specific action at any given time point. The most we can expect in such cases is probabilistic information about the action. The input will then be sequences of these observed action distributions. This work addresses the problem of constructing a data interface that enables a plan recognition module to directly handle such observation distributions. This interface acts as a bridge between the low-level perception module and the high-level plan recognition module. We propose two approaches. The first involves resampling the distribution sequences to single action sequences, allowing us to learn an action affinity model based on learned action (word) embeddings for plan recognition. The second approach directly learns action distribution embeddings using our proposed Distr2vec (distribution to vector) model to construct an affinity model for plan recognition.
label: AI

title: Learning Latent Super-Events to Detect Multiple Activities in Videos
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of learning latent super-events from activity videos and demonstrates its benefits for activity detection in continuous videos. A super-event is defined as a set of multiple events occurring together in videos with a particular temporal organization, contrasting with the concept of sub-events. Real-world videos often contain multiple activities and are rarely segmented (e.g., surveillance videos). Learning latent super-events enables the model to capture the temporal relationships between events in videos. We design temporal structure filters that allow the model to focus on specific sub-intervals of videos and use them with a soft attention mechanism to learn representations of latent super-events. Super-event representations are combined with per-frame or per-segment CNNs to provide frame-level annotations. Our approach is fully differentiable, enabling end-to-end learning of latent super-event representations jointly with the activity detector. Experiments with multiple public video datasets confirm that the concept of latent super-event learning significantly improves activity detection, advancing the state-of-the-art. |||
label: AI

title: Blind Image Deblurring Using Row-Column Sparse Representations
Abstract: Blind image deblurring, where the blur kernel is unknown, is a challenging problem with significant practical implications for imaging devices like cellphone cameras. Existing methods struggle with large motions. This paper presents a novel technique called Blind Image Deblurring using Row-Column Sparsity (BD-RCS) to address this limitation. BD-RCS models the outer product of kernel and image coefficients in specific transformation domains as a rank-one matrix and recovers it through rank minimization. The core contribution is solving two new optimization problems involving row and column sparsity to automatically determine the blur kernel and image support sequentially. Subsequently, the kernel and image are recovered using singular value decomposition (SVD). Experimental results on linear motion deblurring demonstrate that BD-RCS achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly for large motion blur, both visually and quantitatively.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Visual Recognition using Semantics-Preserving Adversarial Embedding Networks
Abstract: We introduce Semantics-Preserving Adversarial Embedding Network (SP-AEN), a novel framework for zero-shot visual recognition (ZSL) where both test images and their classes are unseen during training. SP-AEN tackles the "semantic loss" problem prevalent in embedding-based ZSL, where discarding non-discriminative semantics during training can hinder recognition of unseen classes. SP-AEN prevents semantic loss by introducing an independent visual-to-semantic space embedder that disentangles the semantic space into two subspaces for classification and reconstruction. Adversarial learning of these subspaces allows SP-AEN to transfer semantics from the reconstructive subspace to the discriminative one, improving zero-shot recognition of unseen classes. Unlike prior works, SP-AEN not only enhances classification but also generates photo-realistic images, highlighting the effectiveness of semantic preservation. Evaluated on popular benchmarks CUB, AWA, SUN, and aPY, SP-AEN significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art methods by an absolute performance difference of 12.2%, 9.3%, 4.0%, and 3.6% in terms of harmonic mean values.
label: AI

title: iPose: Instance-Aware 6D Pose Estimation of Partly Occluded Objects
Abstract: This work addresses the problem of 6D pose estimation for known rigid objects from single input images, specifically when the objects are partially occluded. While RGB-D-based methods handle moderate occlusion, there are no effective solutions for RGB inputs when dealing with partly occluded objects. This paper presents the first deep learning-based system that estimates accurate poses for partially occluded objects from both RGB-D and RGB input. The key innovation is a new instance-aware pipeline that decomposes 6D object pose estimation into a sequence of simpler steps. First, an instance segmentation network localizes all known objects in the image, removing clutter and occluders. Second, an encoder-decoder network maps pixels to 3D object surface positions, termed object coordinates, eliminating object appearance. Finally, geometric optimization predicts the 6D pose. The results demonstrate significant outperformance compared to state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation of partially occluded objects, for both RGB and RGB-D input.
label: AI

title: Co-domain Embedding using Deep Quadruplet Networks for Unseen Traffic Sign Recognition
Abstract: Visual recognition has achieved significant advancements due to large supervised datasets. However, acquiring such datasets is often challenging, especially for intelligent transportation applications like traffic sign recognition. For example, models trained with data from one country may not generalize well to another without extensive data. This paper proposes a novel feature embedding scheme for unseen class classification when the representative class template is given. Traffic signs, unlike other objects, have official images. The proposed method utilizes a co-domain embedding using a quadruple relationship from real and synthetic domains. The quadruplet network fully exploits pairwise similarity relationships among samples from different domains. Validation on three datasets with experiments involving one-shot classification and feature generalization demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms competing approaches on both seen and unseen classes.
label: AI

title: Population-based Respiratory 4D Motion Atlas Construction and its Application for VR Simulations of Liver Punctures
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) training simulators for liver needle insertion in the hepatic area of breathing virtual patients currently require 4D data acquisitions as a prerequisite. This involves constructing a population-based breathing virtual patient 4D atlas followed by warping the mean atlas motion to mitigate the need for a dose-relevant or expensive 4D data set for a new static 3D patient. The breakthrough contribution of this work lies in the construction and reuse of population-based learned 4D motion models, offering a significant improvement in efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Grounding Referring Expressions in Images by Variational Context
Abstract: Referential expression grounding in images involves localizing or linking phrases like "largest elephant standing behind baby elephant" to specific objects within an image. This is a challenging vision-language task requiring not only object localization but also multimodal comprehension of context – visual attributes (e.g., "largest", "baby") and relationships (e.g., "behind") – to distinguish the referent from other objects, especially those of the same category. Existing methods simplify this task by modeling pairwise region relationships through multiple instance learning, neglecting the complexity of modeling multiple image regions. This paper presents a variational Bayesian approach, Variational Context, to address complex context modeling in referring expression grounding. The model exploits the reciprocal relation between the referent and context, reducing the search space of context and leading to improved referent localization. A novel cue-specific language-vision embedding network learns this reciprocity model end-to-end. The model is extended to the unsupervised setting where no referent annotation is available. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvement over state-of-the-art methods in both supervised and unsupervised settings.
label: AI

title: Deep Gradient Compression: Reducing the Communication Bandwidth for Distributed Training
Abstract: Large-scale distributed training relies heavily on communication bandwidth for gradient exchange, limiting scalability and requiring expensive high-bandwidth network infrastructure. This limitation is amplified in federated learning where mobile devices experience higher latency, lower throughput, and intermittent connections. This paper identifies that 99.9% of gradient exchange in distributed SGD is redundant and proposes Deep Gradient Compression (DGC) to drastically reduce communication bandwidth. DGC employs four methods – momentum correction, local gradient clipping, momentum factor masking, and warm-up training – to preserve accuracy during compression. The effectiveness of Deep Gradient Compression is demonstrated in image classification, speech recognition, and language modeling on datasets like Cifar10, ImageNet, Penn Treebank, and Librispeech Corpus. It achieves a compression ratio from 270x to 600x without sacrificing accuracy, reducing the gradient size of ResNet-50 from 97MB to 0.35MB and for DeepSpeech from 488MB to 0.74MB. This enables large-scale distributed training on cost-effective commodity 1Gbps Ethernet and facilitates federated learning. Code is available at: https://github.com/synxlin/deep-gradient-compression.
label: AI

title: Structured Set Matching Networks for One-Shot Part Labeling
Abstract: Diagrams serve as effective testbeds for visual and textual reasoning due to their ability to depict complex phenomena. However, understanding diagrams using traditional natural image understanding approaches requires extensive diagram training datasets, which are difficult to acquire. This can be addressed as a matching problem between labeled diagrams, images, or both. This problem is challenging due to the ambiguity introduced by the lack of significant color and texture, requiring global reasoning instead of relying on local cues. This paper focuses on one-shot part labeling, labeling multiple parts of an object in a target image given a single source image of that category. The Structured Set Matching Network (SSMN), a structured prediction model incorporating convolutional neural networks, is introduced to handle this set-to-set matching problem. SSMN utilizes global normalization to maximize local match scores between corresponding elements and a global consistency score among all matched elements, while enforcing a matching constraint between the two sets. The SSMN significantly outperforms strong baselines on three label transfer scenarios: diagram-to-diagram, evaluated on a new diagram dataset of over 200 categories; image-to-image, evaluated on a dataset built on top of the Pascal Part Dataset; and image-to-diagram, evaluated on transferring labels across these datasets.
label: AI

title: Factoring Shape, Pose, and Layout from the 2D Image of a 3D Scene
Abstract: This paper explores recovering 3D structure from a single 2D image of a scene using a concise set of factors: a layout representing the enclosing surfaces and a set of objects represented in terms of shape and pose. A convolutional neural network-based approach is proposed to predict this representation, benchmarked on a large dataset of indoor scenes. The experiments evaluate various practical design questions, demonstrate the feasibility of inferring this representation, and quantify and qualitatively highlight its advantages compared to alternative representations.
label: AI

title: On-Chip Communication Network for Efficient Training of Deep Convolutional Networks on Heterogeneous Manycore Systems
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown remarkable success in diverse application domains, including computer vision, speech recognition, and natural language processing. However, with the increasing size of datasets and the complexity of neural network architectures, designing high-performance and energy-efficient computing hardware for training CNNs is crucial. This paper addresses the problem of designing specialized CPU-GPU based heterogeneous manycore systems for energy-efficient CNN training. The traditional on-chip communication infrastructures used in conventional CPU-GPU platforms struggle to handle both CPU and GPU communication requirements efficiently. To address this issue, the paper analyzes the on-chip traffic patterns arising from the computational processes associated with training two deep CNN architectures, LeNet and CDBNet, for image classification. Utilizing this knowledge, a hybrid Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture, incorporating both wireline and wireless links, is designed to improve the performance of CPU-GPU based heterogeneous manycore platforms running the mentioned CNN training workloads. The proposed NoC achieves a 1.8x reduction in network latency and a 2.2x improvement in network throughput for training CNNs compared to a highly-optimized wireline mesh NoC. These network-level improvements translate into a 25% reduction in full-system energy-delay-product (EDP) for the considered CNN workloads. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid NoC for heterogeneous manycore architectures in significantly accelerating CNN training while maintaining energy efficiency.
label: AI

title: R-FCN-3000 at 30fps: Decoupling Detection and Classification
Abstract: R-FCN-3000 is a large-scale real-time object detector that decouples objectness detection and classification. The detection score for a region of interest (RoI) is calculated by multiplying the objectness score with the fine-grained classification score. This approach modifies the R-FCN architecture by sharing position-sensitive filters across object classes for localization. These filters are not required for fine-grained classification. R-FCN-3000 achieves an mAP of 34.9% on the ImageNet detection dataset, outperforming YOLO-9000 by 18% while processing 30 images per second. The objectness learned by R-FCN-3000 generalizes to novel classes, with performance increasing with the number of training object classes, supporting the hypothesis of a universal objectness detector. Code will be made available.
label: AI

title: Towards Practical Verification of Machine Learning: The Case of Computer Vision Systems
Abstract: The increasing use of machine learning (ML) techniques in security- and safety-critical domains, like autonomous systems and medical diagnosis, underscores the importance of ensuring correct behavior of ML systems, especially for different corner cases. This paper proposes a generic framework for evaluating the security and robustness of ML systems using real-world safety properties. VeriVis, a scalable methodology for verifying diverse safety properties of state-of-the-art computer vision systems with blackbox access, is designed, implemented, and evaluated. VeriVis leverages input space reduction techniques for efficient verification of various safety properties. It identifies thousands of safety violations in fifteen state-of-the-art computer vision systems, including ten Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) like Inception-v3 and Nvidia's Dave self-driving system, and five commercial third-party vision APIs like Google Vision and Clarifai, for twelve different safety properties. VeriVis successfully verifies local safety properties for an average of 31.7% of the test images. It detects up to 64.8x more violations than existing gradient-based methods, which cannot guarantee the absence of violations. Retraining using the detected safety violations reduces the average number of violations by up to 60.2%.
label: AI

title: Tech Report: A Fast Multiscale Spatial Regularization for Sparse Hyperspectral Unmixing
Abstract: Sparse hyperspectral unmixing from large spectral libraries is used to overcome limitations of endmember extraction algorithms in various applications. This strategy often results in ill-posed inverse problems that can benefit from spatial regularization strategies. Existing spatial regularization methods improve problem conditioning and promote piecewise smooth solutions but lead to large nonsmooth optimization problems. Efficiently incorporating spatial context in the unmixing problem remains a challenge, crucial for many real-world applications. This paper presents a novel multiscale spatial regularization approach for sparse unmixing. The method utilizes a signal-adaptive spatial multiscale decomposition based on superpixels, decomposing the unmixing problem into two simpler problems: one in the approximation domain and another in the original domain. Simulation results using both synthetic and real data show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art Total Variation-based algorithms while maintaining a computational time comparable to their unregularized counterparts.
label: AI

title: Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks for Dynamic MR Image Reconstruction
Abstract: Accelerating data acquisition in dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) presents a challenging ill-posed inverse problem that has attracted attention from signal processing and machine learning communities. The key to addressing this problem lies in exploiting the temporal correlation of the MR sequence to resolve aliasing artifacts. Traditionally, this has led to non-convex optimization problems solved using iterative algorithms. Recently, deep learning-based approaches have gained popularity due to their ability to solve general inversion problems. This work proposes a unique convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) architecture for reconstructing high-quality cardiac MR images from highly undersampled k-space data. The architecture exploits both temporal dependencies in the sequences and the iterative nature of traditional optimization algorithms. Notably, it embeds the structure of traditional iterative algorithms, efficiently modeling the recurrence of iterative reconstruction stages using recurrent hidden connections. Additionally, spatiotemporal dependencies are learned simultaneously through bidirectional recurrent hidden connections across time sequences. The proposed algorithm effectively learns both temporal dependency and the iterative reconstruction process with a minimal number of parameters, outperforming current MR reconstruction methods in computational complexity, reconstruction accuracy, and speed.
label: AI

title: OLÉ: Orthogonal Low-rank Embedding, A Plug and Play Geometric Loss for Deep Learning
Abstract: Deep neural networks trained using a softmax layer and the cross-entropy loss are widely used for image classification. However, this does not inherently enforce intra-class similarity or inter-class margin of the learned deep representations. Various solutions, like pairwise or triplet losses, have been proposed to address these goals simultaneously. However, these solutions require selecting pairs or triplets, adding computational burden for computing and learning many combinations. This paper introduces a plug-and-play loss term for deep networks that explicitly reduces intra-class variance and enforces inter-class margin simultaneously, in a simple and elegant geometric manner. For each class, the deep features are collapsed into a learned linear subspace, or union of them, and inter-class subspaces are pushed to be as orthogonal as possible. The proposed Orthogonal Low-rank Embedding (OL'E) does not necessitate crafting pairs or triplets for training, working standalone as a classification loss. It is the first reported deep metric learning framework of its kind. The improved margin between features of different classes leads to better generalization, higher discriminative power, and increased robustness in resulting deep networks. The paper demonstrates improved classification performance in general object recognition by integrating the proposed loss term into existing off-the-shelf architectures. The advantage of the proposed loss is particularly evident in the small data/model scenario, significantly advancing the state-of-the-art on the Stanford STL-10 benchmark.
label: AI

title: Automated Pruning for Deep Neural Network Compression
Abstract: This work presents a method to enhance the pruning step of the current state-of-the-art methodology for compressing neural networks. The novelty lies in the differentiability of the proposed pruning technique, enabling pruning to be performed during the backpropagation phase of network training. This facilitates end-to-end learning and significantly reduces training time. The technique utilizes a family of differentiable pruning functions and a new regularizer designed specifically for enforcing pruning. Experimental results show that joint optimization of both thresholds and network weights leads to a higher compression rate, reducing the number of weights in the pruned network by an additional 14% to 33% compared to the current state-of-the-art. Notably, this is the first study to analyze the generalization capabilities of features extracted by a pruned network in transfer learning tasks. The results demonstrate that representations learned using the proposed pruning methodology maintain the same effectiveness and generality as those learned by the corresponding non-compressed network on various recognition tasks.
label: AI

title: IEOPF: An Active Contour Model for Image Segmentation with Inhomogeneities Estimated by Orthogonal Primary Functions
Abstract: Image segmentation remains a challenge, particularly when intensities of the objects of interest overlap due to intensity inhomogeneity, also known as bias field. To segment images with intensity inhomogeneities, this paper proposes a bias correction embedded level set model where Inhomogeneities are Estimated by Orthogonal Primary Functions (IEOPF). The proposed model estimates the smoothly varying bias using a linear combination of orthogonal primary functions. An inhomogeneous intensity clustering energy is then defined, and membership functions of the clusters described by the level set function are introduced to rewrite the energy as a data term of the proposed model. Similar to popular level set methods, a regularization term and an arc length term are also included to regularize and smooth the level set function, respectively. The proposed model is extended to multichannel and multiphase patterns for segmenting colorful images and images with multiple objects, respectively. Extensive testing on synthetic and real images, including the BrainWeb and IBSR datasets, demonstrates the advantages of the proposed model in terms of bias correction and segmentation accuracy.

title: Recognizing Gender from Human Facial Regions using Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: Gender recognition from facial images has gained significant importance. Existing research focuses on feature extraction to obtain gender-specific information from facial images. However, analyzing and fusing features from different facial regions can improve gender identification. This paper proposes a new approach for identifying gender from frontal facial images, robust to background, illumination, intensity, and facial expressions. The framework first divides the frontal face image into distinct regions based on facial landmark points obtained using the Chehra model by Asthana et al. The model provides 49 landmark points covering various facial regions, such as forehead, left eye, right eye, and lips. The image is then segmented into facial regions using these landmarks, and features are extracted from each region. Compass LBP, a variant of LBP features, is employed to extract discriminative gender-specific information. A Support Vector Machine based classifier computes probability scores from each region. Finally, these scores are combined using a genetic algorithm-based learning to enhance overall classification accuracy. Experiments conducted on popular face image datasets, such as Adience, cFERET, LFW, CUFS, and CUFSF, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches.

title: Flexible on-chip mode-division switching with a new mode converter design
Abstract: Optical-fiber multimode communications have seen significant advancements, with recent efforts focusing on on-chip communication for realizing mode-division multiplexing (MDM). However, the lack of mode converters that can freely perform mode conversions between different waveguide modes has limited the development of flexible on-chip mode-division switching communication. This paper presents the first demonstration of a mode converter capable of converting an arbitrary waveguide mode into any other mode through phase tuning. Based on this converter, two flexible on-chip mode-division switching architectures are proposed. This architecture is compatible with wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) and enables further scaling of on-chip communication bandwidth. This demonstration highlights the potential of mode-divisional switching for realizing fully flexible, dense, on-chip optical networks.

title: On Deterministic Sampling Patterns for Robust Low-Rank Matrix Completion
Abstract: This letter investigates deterministic sampling patterns for completing low-rank matrices corrupted with sparse noise, also known as robust matrix completion. The recent results on deterministic sampling patterns in the absence of noise are extended based on geometric analysis on the Grassmannian manifold. A special case where each column contains a specific number of noisy entries is considered, where probabilistic analysis proves highly efficient. Furthermore, assuming the rank of the original matrix is unknown, the paper provides an analysis to determine if the rank of a valid completion is indeed the actual rank of the data corrupted with sparse noise by verifying certain conditions. |||

title: Empirically Analyzing the Effect of Dataset Biases on Deep Face Recognition Systems
Abstract: It is unclear what biases are present in modern face datasets due to the lack of annotation. Consequently, overall recognition rates offer limited insight into the generalization capabilities of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs). We aim to empirically investigate the influence of various dataset biases on the generalization performance of DCNNs. Using synthetically generated face images, we examine the face recognition rate as a function of interpretable parameters like face pose and lighting. Our approach allows for detailed observations and comparisons of generalization performance across different DCNN architectures. Our experiments revealed: 1) Dataset bias significantly impacts the generalization performance of DCNNs. 2) DCNNs can surprisingly generalize well to unseen illumination conditions and substantial sampling gaps in pose variations. 3) Our methodology demonstrates that the VGG-16 architecture surpasses AlexNet in face recognition tasks due to its superior ability to generalize to unseen face poses, despite having significantly more parameters. 4) We identify a major limitation of current DCNN architectures – their difficulty in generalizing when different identities do not share the same pose variation. 5) Our findings on synthetic data are applicable to real-world data. Our face image generator is publicly available, enabling the research community to benchmark other DCNN architectures.

title: Deep Learning for automatic sale receipt understanding
Abstract: Data analytics are now essential for companies. Analyzing scanned documents presents additional challenges due to paper damage and scanning quality. This work focuses on the automatic understanding of sales receipts in an industrial context, providing access to crucial and accurate consumption statistics. Given a smartphone-captured image, this work primarily focuses on the initial steps of a comprehensive toolchain aimed at extracting essential information like the store brand, purchased products, and corresponding prices with the highest possible confidence. To achieve this high confidence level, even with imperfect scanning, we propose a double-check processing toolchain utilizing Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) and more traditional image and text processing methods. The originality of this work lies in this double-check processing and the combined use of DCNNs for diverse applications and text analysis.

title: Deep learning for semantic segmentation of remote sensing images with rich spectral content
Abstract: The rapid advancements in remote sensing acquisition techniques necessitate scalable and improved processing tools to handle the increasing data volume and complexity. Deep Learning, a popular technique in remote sensing, is gaining significant interest but relies heavily on the quality of training data. This paper presents recent Deep Learning approaches for fine or coarse land cover semantic segmentation estimation. Various 2D architectures are tested, and a new 3D model is introduced to jointly process the spatial and spectral dimensions of the data. This network set enables the comparison of different spectral fusion schemes. Additionally, we assess the use of "noisy ground truth" (outdated and low spatial resolution labels) for training and testing the networks.

title: Manifold-valued Image Generation with Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets
Abstract: Generative modeling of natural images is a fundamental machine learning problem. However, few modern generative models, including Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets (WGANs), have been studied on manifold-valued images, which are common in real-world applications. To bridge this gap, this paper first formulates the problem of generating manifold-valued images and explores three typical instances: hue-saturation-value (HSV) color image generation, chromaticity-brightness (CB) color image generation, and diffusion-tensor (DT) image generation. For the proposed generative modeling problem, we then introduce a theorem of optimal transport to derive a new Wasserstein distance of data distributions on complete manifolds, allowing us to achieve a tractable objective under the WGAN framework. We recommend three benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 HSV/CB color images, ImageNet HSV/CB color images, and UCL DT image datasets. We experimentally demonstrate that the proposed manifold-aware WGAN model generates more plausible manifold-valued images than its competitors on these three datasets.

title: O-CNN: Octree-based Convolutional Neural Networks for 3D Shape Analysis
Abstract: We present O-CNN, an Octree-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for 3D shape analysis. Built on the octree representation of 3D shapes, our method utilizes the average normal vectors of a 3D model sampled in the finest leaf octants as input and performs 3D CNN operations on the octants occupied by the 3D shape surface. We design a novel octree data structure to efficiently store the octant information and CNN features in the graphics memory, executing the entire O-CNN training and evaluation on the GPU. O-CNN supports various CNN structures and works with 3D shapes in different representations. By restricting computations to the octants occupied by 3D surfaces, the memory and computational costs of O-CNN grow quadratically as the depth of the octree increases, making 3D CNN feasible for high-resolution 3D models. We compare the performance of O-CNN with other existing 3D CNN solutions and demonstrate its efficiency and efficacy in three shape analysis tasks: object classification, shape retrieval, and shape segmentation.

title: Successive Embedding and Classification Loss for Aerial Image Classification
Abstract: Deep neural networks can effectively classify aerial images automatically but are prone to overfitting to the training data. It is crucial for trained neural networks to be robust to variations between training and test environments. To address the overfitting problem in aerial image classification, we consider the neural network as successive transformations of an input image into embedded feature representations and ultimately into a semantic class label. We train neural networks to optimize image representations in the embedded space in addition to optimizing the final classification score. We demonstrate that networks trained with this dual embedding and classification loss outperform networks solely trained with classification loss. We also study placing the embedding loss on different network layers and discover that moving the embedding loss from the commonly used feature space to the classifier space, the space just before softmax nonlinearization, leads to the best classification performance for aerial images. Visualizations of the network's embedded representations reveal that the embedding loss encourages greater separation between target class clusters for both training and testing partitions of two aerial image classification benchmark datasets: MSTAR and AID. Our code is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Cooperative Training of Deep Aggregation Networks for RGB-D Action Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep neural network training paradigm that leverages the conjoint information in multiple heterogeneous sources. Specifically, in an RGB-D based action recognition task, it cooperatively trains a single convolutional neural network (named c-ConvNet) on both RGB visual features and depth features, deeply aggregating the two types of features for action recognition. Unlike conventional ConvNets, which learn deep separable features for homogeneous modality-based classification with only one softmax loss function, c-ConvNet enhances the discriminative power of the deeply learned features and mitigates the undesired modality discrepancy by jointly optimizing a ranking loss and a softmax loss for both homogeneous and heterogeneous modalities. The ranking loss comprises intra-modality and cross-modality triplet losses, reducing both intra-modality and cross-modality feature variations. Moreover, the correlations between RGB and depth data are embedded in the c-ConvNet and can be retrieved by either modality, contributing to recognition even when only one modality is available. The proposed method was extensively evaluated on two large RGB-D action recognition datasets, ChaLearn LAP IsoGD and NTU RGB+D datasets, and one small dataset, SYSU 3D HOI, achieving state-of-the-art results.

title: Fully Automatic Segmentation of Lumbar Vertebrae from CT Images using Cascaded 3D Fully Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a method to address the challenging problem of segmenting lumbar vertebrae from CT images acquired with varying fields of view. Our method is based on cascaded 3D Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs), comprising a localization FCN and a segmentation FCN. Specifically, in the first step, we train a regression 3D FCN (named "LocalizationNet") to locate the bounding box of the lumbar region. Subsequently, a 3D U-net like FCN (named "SegmentationNet") is developed and trained to perform a pixel-wise multi-class segmentation, mapping a cropped lumbar region volumetric data to its volume-wise labels. Evaluated on publicly available datasets, our method achieved an average Dice coefficient of 95.77 ± 0.81% and an average symmetric surface distance of 0.37 ± 0.06 mm.

title: Adversarial Attribute-Image Person Re-identification
Abstract: While attributes have been widely used for person re-identification (Re-ID), which aims to match images of the same person across different camera views, they are typically employed as extra features or for multi-task learning to assist the image-image matching task. However, finding a set of person images based on a given attribute description, a practical need in many surveillance applications, remains a rarely investigated cross-modality matching problem in person Re-ID. In this work, we present this challenge and formulate this task as a joint space learning problem. By incorporating an attribute-guided attention mechanism for images and a semantic consistent adversary strategy for attributes, each modality (images and attributes) effectively learns semantically correlated concepts under the guidance of the other. We conducted extensive experiments on three attribute datasets and demonstrated that the proposed joint space learning method is the most effective approach for the attribute-image cross-modality person Re-ID problem so far.

title: Multimodal Storytelling via Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
Abstract: Deriving event storylines is an effective summarization method for succinctly organizing extensive information, significantly alleviating information overload. The key challenge lies in the lack of a widely recognized definition of storyline metric. Previous studies have developed various approaches based on different assumptions about user interests. While these works can extract interesting patterns, their assumptions do not guarantee that the derived patterns align with user preferences. Additionally, their reliance on single-modality sources misses cross-modality information. This paper proposes a method, multimodal imitation learning via generative adversarial networks (MIL-GAN), to directly model user interests as reflected in various data. Specifically, the proposed model addresses the critical challenge by imitating users' demonstrated storylines. Our proposed model learns the reward patterns given user-provided storylines and then applies the learned policy to unseen data. The proposed approach demonstrates its capability of acquiring user implicit intent and outperforming competing methods significantly, as confirmed by a user study.

title: 4DFAB: A Large Scale 4D Facial Expression Database for Biometric Applications
Abstract: The remarkable progress witnessed in numerous computer vision applications, including automatic face analysis, is made possible by significant efforts in collecting and annotating large-scale visual databases. To this end, we propose 4DFAB, a new large-scale database of dynamic high-resolution 3D faces (over 1,800,000 3D meshes). 4DFAB contains recordings of 180 subjects captured in four different sessions spanning over a five-year period. It includes 4D videos of subjects displaying both spontaneous and posed facial behaviors. The database can be used for both face and facial expression recognition, as well as behavioral biometrics. It can also be utilized to learn powerful blendshapes for parameterizing facial behavior. In this paper, we conduct several experiments and demonstrate the database's usefulness for various applications. The database will be made publicly available for research purposes.

title: Zone-based Keyword Spotting in Bangla and Devanagari Documents
Abstract: This paper presents a word spotting system in text lines for offline Indic scripts such as Bangla (Bengali) and Devanagari. Recently, the zone-wise recognition method was shown to improve word recognition performance compared to conventional full word recognition systems in Indic scripts. Inspired by this idea, we consider the zone segmentation approach and utilize middle zone information to enhance traditional word spotting performance. To avoid the problem of zone segmentation using heuristic approaches, we propose an HMM-based approach to segment upper and lower zone components from text line images. Candidate keywords are searched from a line without segmenting characters or words. Additionally, we propose a novel feature combining foreground and background information of text line images for keyword spotting by character filler models. Notably, using both foreground and background information significantly improves performance compared to using either individually. Pyramid Histogram of Oriented Gradient (PHOG) features are used in our word spotting framework. Experiments indicate that the proposed zone-segmentation-based system outperforms traditional word spotting approaches.

title: AI Oriented Large-Scale Video Management for Smart City: Technologies, Standards and Beyond
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved significant success in various computer vision tasks. Intelligent video analysis, broadly applicable to video surveillance in numerous smart city applications, can also be driven by these powerful deep learning engines. However, practically facilitating deep neural network models in large-scale video analysis presents unprecedented challenges for large-scale video data management. Deep feature coding, instead of video coding, offers a practical solution for handling large-scale video surveillance data. To enable interoperability in the context of deep feature coding, standardization is urgent and crucial. However, due to the explosion of deep learning algorithms and the particularity of feature coding, numerous problems remain in the standardization process. This paper envisions the future deep feature coding standard for AI-oriented large-scale video management, discussing existing techniques, standards, and potential solutions for these open problems.
