title: Human activity recognition from mobile inertial sensors using recurrence plots
Abstract: Inertial sensors are now prevalent in most mobile devices, and these devices are used by people throughout their daily activities. This paper presents an approach for human activity recognition based on inertial sensors, employing recurrence plots (RP) and visual descriptors. The proposed approach pipeline involves computing RPs from sensor data, extracting visual features from RPs, and using them in a machine learning protocol. As RPs generate texture visual patterns, we transform the problem of sensor data classification into a texture classification problem. Experiments for classifying human activities based on accelerometer data demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves the highest accuracies, outperforming time- and frequency-domain features extracted directly from sensor data. The best results are obtained when using RGB RPs, where each RGB channel corresponds to the RP of an independent accelerometer axis.

title: Beyond Grand Theft Auto V for Training, Testing and Enhancing Deep Learning in Self Driving Cars
Abstract: As an initial assessment, over 480,000 labeled virtual images of normal highway driving were generated in Grand Theft Auto V's virtual environment. Using these images, a CNN was trained to detect following distance to cars/objects ahead, lane markings, and driving angle (angular heading relative to lane centerline) – all variables essential for basic autonomous driving. Encouraging results were obtained when tested on over 50,000 labeled virtual images from substantially different GTA-V driving environments. This initial assessment begins to define both the range and scope of labeled images needed for training and testing, establishing the boundaries and limitations of trained networks. The efficacy and flexibility of a "GTA-V"-like virtual environment are expected to provide an efficient, well-defined foundation for training and testing Convolutional Neural Networks for safe driving. Additionally, this paper describes the Princeton Virtual Environment (PVE) for the training, testing, and enhancement of safe driving AI, which is being developed using the video-game engine Unity. PVE is being developed to recreate rare but critical corner cases that can be used for retraining and enhancing machine learning models and understanding the limitations of current self-driving models. The Florida Tesla crash is being used as an initial reference.

title: Visual to Sound: Generating Natural Sound for Videos in the Wild
Abstract: Vision and sound, two of the five traditional human senses (sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch), are fundamental sources through which humans understand the world. Often correlated during natural events, these two modalities combine to jointly affect human perception. This paper addresses the task of generating sound based on visual input. Such capabilities could enable applications in virtual reality (automatically generating sound for virtual scenes) or provide enhanced accessibility to images or videos for people with visual impairments. As a first step in this direction, we apply learning-based methods to generate raw waveform samples from input video frames. We evaluate our models on a dataset of videos containing a variety of sounds (ambient sounds and sounds from people/animals). Our experiments demonstrate that the generated sounds are fairly realistic and exhibit good temporal synchronization with the visual inputs.

title: A Generative Adversarial Approach for Zero-Shot Learning from Noisy Texts
Abstract: Most existing zero-shot learning methods approach the problem as a visual semantic embedding one. Leveraging the demonstrated capability of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate images, we propose using GANs to imagine unseen categories from text descriptions and thereby recognize novel classes with no examples being seen. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective generative model that takes as input noisy text descriptions about an unseen class (e.g., Wikipedia articles) and generates synthesized visual features for this class. With added pseudo data, zero-shot learning is naturally converted into a traditional classification problem. Additionally, to maintain the inter-class discrimination of the generated features, we propose a visual pivot regularization as explicit supervision. Unlike previous methods that use complex engineered regularizers, our approach effectively suppresses noise without requiring additional regularization. Empirically, we show that our method consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art on the largest available benchmarks for Text-based Zero-shot Learning.

title: A+D Net: Training a Shadow Detector with Adversarial Shadow Attenuation
Abstract: We propose a novel GAN-based framework for detecting shadows in images, where a shadow detection network (D-Net) is trained alongside a shadow attenuation network (A-Net) that generates adversarial training examples. A-Net modifies the original training images constrained by a simplified physical shadow model, focusing on fooling D-Net's shadow predictions. Thus, it effectively augments the training data for D-Net with challenging cases. D-Net is trained to predict shadows in both original images and generated images from A-Net. Our experimental results show that the additional training data from A-Net significantly improves D-Net's shadow detection accuracy. Our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the most challenging shadow detection benchmark (SBU) and also achieves state-of-the-art results on a cross-dataset task, testing on UCF. Furthermore, the proposed method achieves accurate real-time shadow detection at 45 frames per second.

title: 3D Semantic Trajectory Reconstruction from 3D Pixel Continuum
Abstract: This paper presents a method for reconstructing dense semantic trajectory streams of human interactions in 3D from synchronized multiple videos. Interactions inherently introduce self-occlusion and illumination/appearance/shape changes, leading to fragmented trajectory reconstruction with noisy and coarse semantic labels. Our hypothesis is that among multiple views, a set of views exists that can confidently recognize the visual semantic label of a 3D trajectory. We introduce a new representation called the 3D semantic map – a probability distribution over the semantic labels per trajectory. We construct the 3D semantic map by reasoning about visibility and 2D recognition confidence based on view-pooling, i.e., finding the view that best represents the semantics of the trajectory. Using the 3D semantic map, we precisely infer all trajectory labels jointly by considering the affinity between long-range trajectories through estimating their local rigid transformations. This inference quantitatively outperforms baseline approaches in terms of predictive validity, representation robustness, and affinity effectiveness. We demonstrate that our algorithm can robustly compute the semantic labels of a large-scale trajectory set involving real-world human interactions with objects, scenes, and people.

title: Long-Term Visual Object Tracking Benchmark
Abstract: We propose a new long video dataset (called Track Long and Prosper – TLP) and benchmark for single object tracking. The dataset comprises 50 HD videos from real-world scenarios, spanning over 400 minutes (676K frames), making it more than 20 times larger in average duration per sequence and more than 8 times larger in terms of total covered duration compared to existing generic datasets for visual tracking. The proposed dataset provides a suitable means to assess long-term tracking performance and train better deep learning architectures (avoiding/reducing augmentation, which may not reflect real-world behavior). We benchmark the dataset on 17 state-of-the-art trackers and rank them according to tracking accuracy and run time speeds. We present a thorough qualitative and quantitative evaluation highlighting the importance of the long-term aspect of tracking. Our most interesting observations are: (a) existing short sequence benchmarks fail to capture the inherent differences in tracking algorithms, which become more pronounced when tracking on long sequences; and (b) the accuracy of trackers drops sharply on challenging long sequences, suggesting a potential need for research efforts in the direction of long-term tracking. |||

title: Self-supervised Learning of Motion Capture
Abstract: Current state-of-the-art motion capture solutions rely on optimization techniques, seeking to adjust the parameters of a 3D human model to match video measurements. However, these methods are susceptible to local minima, hindering their effectiveness without clean backgrounds, manual initialization, or multiple cameras. This paper proposes a learning-based motion capture model for single-camera input, eschewing direct optimization of mesh and skeleton parameters. Instead, the model optimizes neural network weights that predict 3D shape and skeleton configurations from monocular RGB video. Trained with a combination of synthetic data and self-supervision through differentiable rendering of keypoints, dense 3D mesh motion, and human-background segmentation, the model seamlessly integrates supervised learning and test-time optimization. Supervised learning ensures accurate initialization, while self-supervision enables unsupervised adaptation to test data, resulting in superior performance compared to fixed models. The proposed model demonstrates continuous improvement with experience, converging to low-error solutions where optimization methods falter.

title: Examining Cooperation in Visual Dialog Models
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel blackbox intervention method for visual dialog models, designed to assess the contribution of individual linguistic or visual components. Structured or randomized interventions are used to selectively impair specific components, while changes in task performance are monitored. We replicate a state-of-the-art visual dialog model and demonstrate that our methodology unveils surprising insights, namely the minimal contributions of both dialog and image information to task performance. The presented intervention method serves as a sanity check for the strength and robustness of each component within visual dialog systems.

title: Learning by Asking Questions
Abstract: We introduce "learning-by-asking" (LBA), an interactive learning framework for the development and testing of intelligent visual systems. We explore LBA in the context of Visual Question Answering (VQA), where most questions are unseen during training and the learner must actively seek answers. This approach more closely mimics natural learning and offers potential for greater data efficiency than the traditional VQA setting. We present a model that performs LBA on the CLEVR dataset, demonstrating its ability to autonomously discover an easy-to-hard curriculum during interactive learning from an oracle. The generated LBA data consistently matches or surpasses the CLEVR training data while being more sample efficient. Furthermore, our model's questions generalize to state-of-the-art VQA models and novel test-time distributions.

title: Iterative Deep Learning for Network Topology Extraction
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of estimating the topology of filamentary networks, such as retinal vessels and road networks. Building upon a global model for dense semantic pixel classification, we design a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that predicts the local connectivity between a central pixel and its bordering points. By iteratively applying this local connectivity prediction across the image, we infer the global network topology, emulating the human process of tracing a complex network with a fingertip. Extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations are conducted on two datasets: DRIVE for retinal veins and arteries, and Massachusetts Roads for road networks. Our approach consistently surpasses strong baseline methods in both tasks.

title: Why my photos look sideways or upside down? Detecting Canonical Orientation of Images using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Image orientation detection demands high-level scene understanding. Humans rely on object recognition and contextual scene information to correctly orient images. Existing image orientation detection methods primarily employ low-level vision features, with limited incorporation of semantic cues. The vast semantic content in images poses a significant challenge, creating a semantic gap between current methods and human behavior. Existing methods also exhibit highly discrepant detection rates due to dataset variations and limited test image diversity. This work leverages the power of deep learning, adapting pre-trained convolutional neural networks using the largest training dataset to date for image orientation detection. Extensive evaluations on various public datasets demonstrate our model's remarkable generalization capabilities, accurately orienting a wide range of unconstrained images. It significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving accuracy comparable to humans.

title: Robust 3D Action Recognition through Sampling Local Appearances and Global Distributions
Abstract: 3D action recognition plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction and intelligent surveillance. However, recognizing similar actions remains challenging due to limitations in existing methods for capturing motion and shape cues from noisy depth data. This paper proposes a novel two-layer Bag-of-Visual-Words (BoVW) model that effectively suppresses noise and jointly encodes motion and shape cues. Background clutter is removed using a depth data-specific background modeling method. Robust and distinctive spatial-temporal interest points (STIPs) are then generated using both motion and shape cues, yielding motion-based STIPs and shape-based STIPs. The first layer of our model employs a multi-scale 3D local steering kernel (M3DLSK) descriptor to characterize the local appearance of cuboids surrounding motion-based STIPs. In the second layer, a spatial-temporal vector (STV) descriptor describes the spatial-temporal distributions of shape-based STIPs. The BoVW model combines motion and shape cues to form a fused action representation. Our model outperforms conventional STIP detection and description methods. Thorough experiments validate the effectiveness of our model in distinguishing similar actions and its robustness to background clutter, partial occlusions, and pepper noise.

title: A Generalized Motion Pattern and FCN based approach for retinal fluid detection and segmentation
Abstract: SD-OCT (Spectral Domain Optical Coherence Tomography) is a non-invasive cross-sectional imaging modality used for diagnosing macular defects. Efficient detection and segmentation of abnormalities in OCT scans, serving as biomarkers, aid in analyzing disease progression and advising appropriate treatment. This paper proposes a fully automated Generalized Motion Pattern (GMP) based segmentation method utilizing a cascade of fully convolutional networks for detecting and segmenting retinal fluids from SD-OCT scans. Traditional segmentation methods rely on domain knowledge-based feature extraction, while our proposed method leverages GMP derived by inducing motion in an image to suppress the background. This parallelizable method effectively handles inter-scanner variability. Our method achieves mean Dice scores of 0.61, 0.70, and 0.73 for segmentation, and mean AUC scores of 0.85, 0.84, and 0.87 for detection of the three fluid types: IRF, SRF, and PDE, respectively.

title: Connecting Pixels to Privacy and Utility: Automatic Redaction of Private Information in Images
Abstract: Images inherently convey a broad spectrum of personal information. Sharing these images on social media platforms leaks this private information, violating the privacy of individuals depicted. This paper focuses on automated approaches to redact such private information, safeguarding individual privacy. A user study reveals that obfuscating image regions associated with private information effectively protects privacy while maintaining image utility. Varying the size of these regions enables customizable privacy-utility trade-offs. Our findings advocate for a "redaction by segmentation" paradigm. We introduce the first substantial dataset of "in-the-wild" private images, annotated with pixel and instance level labels across diverse privacy classes. We further present the first model for automatic redaction of a broad range of private information.

title: SOT for MOT
Abstract: This paper presents a robust tracker to solve the multiple object tracking (MOT) problem within the tracking-by-detection framework. As the first contribution, we innovatively integrate single object tracking (SOT) algorithms with multiple object tracking algorithms. Our results demonstrate that SOT effectively reduces the number of false negatives, regardless of detection quality. Another contribution lies in showcasing the efficient and accurate association of detections belonging to the same object using a deep learning-based appearance model. This appearance model plays a pivotal role in our MOT algorithm for associating detections into long trajectories, and in our SOT algorithm for identifying new detections missed by the detector. The deep neural network-based model ensures robustness, enabling data association across diverse scenes. Comprehensive experiments on the challenging MOT16 benchmark demonstrate our tracker's state-of-the-art performance using both public and private detections.

title: GANerated Hands for Real-time 3D Hand Tracking from Monocular RGB
Abstract: We tackle the highly challenging problem of real-time 3D hand tracking from monocular RGB sequences. Our tracking method integrates a convolutional neural network with a kinematic 3D hand model, ensuring robust generalization to unseen data, resilience to occlusions and varying viewpoints, and anatomically plausible and temporally smooth hand motions. For training our CNN, we propose a novel approach for synthetic data generation based on a geometrically consistent image-to-image translation network. This network translates synthetic images into "real" images, aligning their statistical distribution with real-world hand images. Training this translation network combines an adversarial loss, a cycle-consistency loss, and a geometric consistency loss to preserve geometric properties during translation. Our hand tracking system outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on challenging RGB-only footage.

title: CNN based Learning using Reflection and Retinex Models for Intrinsic Image Decomposition
Abstract: Traditional intrinsic image decomposition methods rely on priors about scene characteristics, while recent deep learning approaches treat the process as a black box, neglecting well-established image formation principles. Consequently, while deep learning methods excel in quantitative benchmarks, traditional methods retain dominance in achieving high qualitative results. This paper aims to exploit the best of both worlds by proposing a method that (1) leverages deep learning capabilities, (2) incorporates a physics-based reflection model to guide the learning process, and (3) utilizes traditional methods to extract intrinsic images by exploiting reflectance and shading gradient information. The proposed model is computationally efficient and integrates all intrinsic components. For training, object-centered large-scale datasets with intrinsic ground-truth images are created. Evaluation results demonstrate the model's superior performance compared to existing methods. Visual inspection reveals the image formation loss function enhances color reproduction, and the use of gradient information produces sharper edges. Datasets, models, and higher resolution images are available at https://ivi.fnwi.uva.nl/cv/retinet.

title: Learning for Disparity Estimation through Feature Constancy
Abstract: Stereo matching algorithms typically involve four steps: matching cost calculation, matching cost aggregation, disparity calculation, and disparity refinement. Existing CNN-based methods utilize CNNs for only portions of these steps or employ different networks for each step, hindering the pursuit of an optimal overall solution. This paper proposes a network architecture that integrates all steps of stereo matching. The network comprises three parts: (1) multi-scale shared feature calculation, (2) initial disparity estimation using shared features for matching cost calculation, aggregation, and disparity calculation, and (3) disparity refinement using initial disparity and shared features to calculate feature constancy, a measure of correspondence correctness. The proposed method, evaluated on the Scene Flow and KITTI datasets, achieves state-of-the-art performance on the KITTI 2012 and KITTI 2015 benchmarks while maintaining a fast execution time.

title: Towards Faster Training of Global Covariance Pooling Networks by Iterative Matrix Square Root Normalization
Abstract: Global covariance pooling in convolutional neural networks has significantly outperformed classical first-order pooling. Recent research has highlighted the central role of matrix square root normalization in achieving state-of-the-art performance. However, existing methods heavily rely on eigendecomposition (EIG) or singular value decomposition (SVD), leading to inefficient training due to limited GPU support for these operations. This paper proposes an iterative matrix square root normalization method for fast end-to-end training of global covariance pooling networks. Our core innovation is a meta-layer designed with a loop-embedded directed graph structure. The meta-layer comprises three consecutive nonlinear structured layers performing pre-normalization, coupled matrix iteration, and post-compensation. Compared to EIG or SVD-based methods, our method is significantly faster, involving only matrix multiplications suitable for GPU parallelization. Furthermore, the proposed network with ResNet architecture converges in fewer epochs, further accelerating training. On the large-scale ImageNet benchmark, we achieve competitive performance surpassing existing counterparts. By fine-tuning our ImageNet pre-trained models, we establish state-of-the-art results on three challenging fine-grained benchmarks. The source code and network models are available at http://www.peihuali.org/iSQRT-COV.

title: Wasserstein Divergence for GANs
Abstract: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have achieved remarkable success in numerous computer vision domains. Among these, the family of Wasserstein GANs (WGANs) stands out as state-of-the-art due to their theoretical contributions and competitive qualitative performance. However, approximating the $k$-Lipschitz constraint required by the Wasserstein-1 metric (W-met) poses a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel Wasserstein divergence (W-div), a relaxed version of W-met that does not require the $k$-Lipschitz constraint. As a concrete application, we introduce a Wasserstein divergence objective for GANs (WGAN-div), enabling faithful approximation of W-div through optimization. Under various settings, including progressive growing training, we demonstrate the stability of WGAN-div due to its theoretical and practical advantages over WGANs. We further analyze the quantitative and visual performance of WGAN-div on standard image synthesis benchmarks, showcasing its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Learning to detect chest radiographs containing lung nodules using visual attention networks
Abstract: Machine learning approaches hold great promise for automated lung nodule detection in chest radiographs. However, training these algorithms demands vast amounts of manually annotated images, which are difficult to obtain. Weak labels indicating the likelihood of pulmonary nodules in radiographs are typically easier to acquire at scale by parsing historical free-text radiological reports associated with the radiographs. Using a repository of over 700,000 chest radiographs, this study demonstrates the potential for achieving promising nodule detection performance using weak labels via convolutional neural networks for radiograph classification. We propose two network architectures for classifying images likely to contain pulmonary nodules, leveraging both weak labels and manually-delineated bounding boxes when available. Annotated nodules are incorporated during training to provide a visual attention mechanism that informs the model about its localization performance. The first architecture extracts saliency maps from high-level convolutional layers and compares the estimated nodule position with ground truth, back-propagating a corresponding localization error alongside the softmax classification error. The second approach employs a recurrent attention model that learns to observe a sequence of smaller image portions through reinforcement learning. When a nodule annotation is available at training time, the reward function is modified to penalize exploration of image portions away from the nodule. Our empirical results highlight the potential advantages of these architectures over competing methodologies.
label: AI

title: Feature Generating Networks for Zero-Shot Learning
Abstract: Existing state-of-the-art approaches struggle to achieve satisfactory results for the challenging generalized zero-shot learning task due to the extreme training data imbalance between seen and unseen classes. To circumvent the need for labeled examples of unseen classes, we propose a novel generative adversarial network (GAN) that synthesizes CNN features conditioned on class-level semantic information, offering a direct shortcut from a semantic descriptor to a class-conditional feature distribution. Our proposed approach, combining a Wasserstein GAN with a classification loss, effectively generates discriminative CNN features for training softmax classifiers or any multimodal embedding method. Our experimental results demonstrate a significant accuracy boost over the state of the art on five challenging datasets—CUB, FLO, SUN, AWA, and ImageNet—in both zero-shot learning and generalized zero-shot learning settings.
label: AI

title: Face Translation between Images and Videos using Identity-aware CycleGAN
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel problem of unpaired face translation between images and videos, applicable to facial video prediction and enhancement. This problem presents two major technical challenges: (1) designing a robust translation model between static images and dynamic videos, and (2) preserving facial identity during image-video translation. To address these challenges, we generalize the state-of-the-art image-to-image translation network (Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks) to the image-to-video/video-to-image translation context, employing an image-video translation model and an identity preservation model. Specifically, we apply the advanced Wasserstein GAN technique to image-video translation for improved convergence and introduce a face verificator to ensure identity preservation. Experiments on standard image/video face datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model, both qualitatively and quantitatively.
label: AI

title: Leaf Identification Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have gained widespread popularity, particularly in computer vision, due to their exceptional performance on various tasks, such as image classification. This paper proposes a nine-layer CNN for leaf identification using the renowned Flavia and Foliage datasets. Supervised learning of deep CNNs typically requires extensive training datasets. However, the used datasets contain limited examples per plant species. To prevent overfitting, we apply data augmentation and transfer learning techniques. The trained CNNs achieve recognition rates exceeding 99% on the Flavia and Foliage datasets, slightly surpassing existing methods for leaf classification.
label: AI

title: FSSD: Feature Fusion Single Shot Multibox Detector
Abstract: SSD (Single Shot Multibox Detector) is a prominent object detection algorithm known for its high accuracy and speed. However, SSD's feature pyramid detection method hinders effective fusion of features from different scales. This paper proposes FSSD (Feature Fusion Single Shot Multibox Detector), an enhanced SSD featuring a novel and lightweight feature fusion module that significantly improves performance with minimal speed reduction. The feature fusion module concatenates features from different layers with varying scales, followed by down-sampling blocks to generate a new feature pyramid that feeds into multibox detectors for final detection results. On the Pascal VOC 2007 test, our network achieves an 82.7 mAP (mean average precision) at a speed of 65.8 FPS (frames per second) with an input size of 300x300 using a single Nvidia 1080Ti GPU. Our results on COCO also outperform conventional SSD by a significant margin. FSSD surpasses many state-of-the-art object detection algorithms in both accuracy and speed. Code is available at https://github.com/lzx1413/CAFFE_SSD/tree/fssd.
label: AI

title: Composite Quantization
Abstract: This paper investigates the compact coding approach to approximate nearest neighbor search. We introduce a composite quantization framework, utilizing the composition of multiple ($M$) elements, each selected from a different dictionary, to accurately approximate a $D$-dimensional vector. This framework achieves accurate search while representing the data vector with a short code composed of indices of the selected elements. Our key contribution lies in introducing a near-orthogonality constraint, ensuring search efficiency by reducing the distance computation cost to $O(M)$ from $O(D)$ using a distance table lookup scheme. This approach is termed near-orthogonal composite quantization. We theoretically justify the equivalence between near-orthogonal composite quantization and minimizing an upper bound of a function formed by jointly considering the quantization error and search cost according to a generalized triangle inequality. Empirical evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of our approach over several benchmark datasets. We further showcase superior performances in three applications: combination with inverted multi-index, quantizing the query for mobile search, and inner-product similarity search.
label: AI

title: Enhanced Characterness for Text Detection in the Wild
Abstract: Text spotting, the process of identifying text in images, presents a unique challenge as text can appear in a variety of forms and locations. Accurately detecting text opens up exciting possibilities for enhancing numerous computer vision applications. This paper proposes a novel language-agnostic text detection method that leverages edge-enhanced Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSERs) in natural scenes by defining strong characterness measures. Our approach demonstrates that a simple combination of characterness cues effectively rejects non-text regions. The identified regions undergo further refinement to eliminate neighboring non-textual regions. Comprehensive evaluation of the proposed scheme reveals its superior or comparable generalization performance compared to traditional methods for this task.
label: AI

title: Object Classification using Ensemble of Local and Deep Features
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce an ensemble approach for object classification that combines local and deep features. Our research investigates the effectiveness of feature representation capabilities across various layers of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Extensive experiments on object classification demonstrate that the representation capabilities of features from deep networks can be enhanced by incorporating information captured from local features. We also discover that features extracted from different deep convolutional networks encode distinct characteristic information. Our findings challenge conventional practices and highlight the potential of intermediate layers in deep networks to augment the classification capabilities of features derived from fully connected layers.
label: AI

title: Deep Sampling Networks
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved impressive image up-sampling performance. However, CNN-based methods often rely heavily on traditional interpolations (e.g., bicubic) to reconstruct high-resolution results. This paper introduces a novel deep sampling network (DSN) for down-sampling and up-sampling without relying on any cheap interpolation. Our approach involves two key components: a down-sampling subnetwork and an up-sampling subnetwork. The down-sampling subnetwork is trained without supervision, enabling it to preserve more information and produce visually enhanced low-resolution images. The up-sampling subnetwork learns a sub-pixel residual with dense connections to accelerate convergence and improve performance. DSN's down-sampling subnetwork can be utilized to generate photo-realistic low-resolution images and replace traditional down-sampling methods in image processing. The co-training DSN, empowered by the robust down-sampling process, achieves state-of-the-art performance for image super-resolution. Furthermore, DSN exhibits compatibility with existing image codecs, paving the way for enhanced image compression.
label: AI

title: Deep Visual Perception for Dynamic Walking on Discrete Terrain
Abstract: Dynamic bipedal walking on discrete terrain, such as stepping stones, poses a significant challenge that necessitates feedback controllers to ensure safety-critical constraints. Effective constraint enforcement in real-world experiments hinges on fast and accurate perception for foothold detection and estimation. This work presents a deep visual perception model designed to accurately estimate the step length of the next step, providing crucial input to the feedback controller for enabling vision-in-the-loop dynamic walking on discrete terrain. A custom convolutional neural network architecture is developed and trained to predict the step length to the next foothold using a sampled image preview of the upcoming terrain at foot impact. Notably, visual input is provided only at the beginning of each step, proving sufficient for dynamically stepping onto discrete footholds. Extensive numerical studies confirm the robot's ability to autonomously walk successfully for over 100 steps without failure on a discrete terrain with footholds randomly positioned within a step length range of 45-85 centimeters.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Diffuse Optical Tomography
Abstract: Diffuse optical tomography (DOT) has emerged as a promising alternative imaging modality for breast cancer detection due to its excellent contrast to hemoglobin oxidization level. However, the inherent complexity of non-linear photon scattering physics and the ill-posed nature of the problem pose significant challenges, making conventional reconstruction algorithms susceptible to variations in imaging parameters, such as boundary conditions. To address this, we propose a novel deep learning approach that effectively learns non-linear photon scattering physics and achieves accurate three-dimensional (3D) distribution of optical anomalies. Unlike traditional black-box deep learning approaches, our deep network is designed to invert the Lippman-Schwinger integral equation, leveraging the recent mathematical theory of deep convolutional framelets. Demonstrating its clinical relevance, we applied the method to our prototype DOT system. Our results show that the deep neural network, trained solely on simulation data, can accurately recover the location of anomalies within biomimetic phantoms and live animals without requiring exogenous contrast agents.
label: AI

title: Towards Realistic Face Photo-Sketch Synthesis via Composition-Aided GANs
Abstract: Face photo-sketch synthesis, the task of generating a facial sketch or photo based on a given photo or sketch, has wide-ranging applications in digital entertainment and law enforcement. Achieving precise depictions of face photos or sketches remains a significant challenge due to the constraints on structural realism and textural consistency. While existing methods have yielded impressive results, they often produce blurred effects and substantial deformation across various facial components, leading to an unrealistic feel in the synthesized images. To address this challenge, we propose utilizing facial composition information to facilitate the synthesis of face sketches or photos. Specifically, we introduce a novel composition-aided generative adversarial network (CA-GAN) for face photo-sketch synthesis. CA-GAN leverages paired inputs, including a face photo or sketch and its corresponding pixel-wise face labels, for generating a sketch or photo. Moreover, to focus training on hard-generated components and delicate facial structures, we propose a compositional reconstruction loss. Finally, we employ stacked CA-GANs (SCA-GANs) to further rectify defects and add compelling details. Experimental results demonstrate the capabilities of our method in generating visually comfortable and identity-preserving face sketches or photos across a wide range of challenging data. Our method achieves state-of-the-art quality, significantly reducing the best previous Frechet Inception distance (FID). Additionally, we showcase the proposed method's remarkable generalization ability. Our code and results are publicly available at: https://fei-hdu.github.io/ca-gan/.
label: AI

title: Data Dropout in Arbitrary Basis for Deep Network Regularization
Abstract: A critical challenge in training deep networks with high capacity lies in ensuring their robust performance when presented with novel inputs beyond the training dataset. Dropout, a widely used regularization technique, effectively enhances network generalization by randomly setting a subset of data elements and extracted features to zero during training. This paper presents a new randomized regularization technique, termed Generalized Dropout, that randomly withholds a portion of the data without necessarily disabling neurons or data elements. Our proposed method, of which conventional dropout is a special case, performs random data dropout in an arbitrary basis. We further present a framework for efficient application of this technique to convolutional neural networks. Numerical experiments demonstrate the notable performance gains achieved by the proposed technique. Generalized Dropout provides new insights into the concept of dropout, showcasing the potential for achieving different performance improvements by employing different basis matrices. This work opens up new avenues for research into optimal basis matrix selection for maximizing performance gains.
label: AI

title: Improving Object Detection from Scratch via Gated Feature Reuse
Abstract: This paper introduces a simple and parameter-efficient drop-in module, termed GFR (Gated Feature Reuse), designed for one-stage object detectors like SSD when learning from scratch (i.e., without pre-trained models). Our module exhibits two primary advantages. First, we introduce a novel gate-controlled prediction strategy enabled by Squeeze-and-Excitation to adaptively enhance or attenuate supervision at different scales based on the input object size. This allows our model to effectively detect objects of diverse sizes. Second, we propose a feature-pyramids structure to integrate rich spatial and semantic features into a single prediction layer, strengthening feature representation and reducing the number of parameters to learn. We apply the proposed structure to DSOD and SSD detection frameworks and evaluate performance on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and COCO datasets. GFR-DSOD, with fewer model parameters, surpasses the baseline DSOD by 1.4%, 1.1%, 1.7%, and 0.6%, respectively. GFR-SSD also outperforms the original SSD and SSD with dense prediction by 3.6% and 2.8% on the VOC 2007 dataset. Code is available at: https://github.com/szq0214/GFR-DSOD.
label: AI

title: A GRU-based Encoder-Decoder Approach with Attention for Online Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
Abstract: This study presents a novel end-to-end approach based on the encoder-decoder framework with an attention mechanism for online handwritten mathematical expression recognition (OHMER). The input two-dimensional ink trajectory information of handwritten expressions is first encoded using a gated recurrent unit-based recurrent neural network (GRU-RNN). Subsequently, the decoder is also implemented using GRU-RNN with a coverage-based attention model. The proposed approach concurrently accomplishes symbol recognition and structural analysis to output a character sequence in LaTeX format. Validated on the CROHME 2014 competition task, our approach significantly surpasses the state-of-the-art, achieving an expression recognition accuracy of 52.43% by utilizing only the official training dataset. Additionally, the alignments between the input trajectories of handwritten expressions and the output LaTeX sequences are visualized through the attention mechanism, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Drone Monitoring
Abstract: This work proposes a drone monitoring system that integrates deep-learning-based detection and tracking modules. The primary challenge in adopting deep learning methods for drone detection stems from the limited availability of training drone images. To address this issue, we develop a model-based drone augmentation technique that automatically generates drone images with bounding box labels indicating the drone's location. For tracking small flying drones, we leverage the residual information between consecutive image frames. Finally, we present an integrated detection and tracking system that outperforms the performance of each individual module containing only detection or tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that even with training on synthetic data, the proposed system performs well on real-world drone images with complex backgrounds. The USC drone detection and tracking dataset, featuring user-labeled bounding boxes, is publicly available.
label: AI

title: Visual Explanation by High-Level Abduction: On Answer-Set Programming Driven Reasoning about Moving Objects
Abstract: We propose a hybrid architecture for systematically computing robust visual explanations encompassing hypothesis formation, belief revision, and default reasoning with video data. The architecture comprises two tightly integrated synergistic components: (1) (functional) answer set programming based abductive reasoning with space-time tracklets as native entities; and (2) a visual processing pipeline for detection-based object tracking and motion analysis. We present the formal framework, its general implementation as a (declarative) method in answer set programming, and an example application and evaluation based on two diverse video datasets: the MOTChallenge benchmark developed by the vision community and a recently developed Movie Dataset.
label: AI

title: Avaliação da doença de Alzheimer pela análise multiespectral de imagens DW-MR por redes RBF como alternativa aos mapas ADC
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease, the most common cause of dementia, poses a significant diagnostic challenge, particularly in the early stages, as accurate diagnosis often requires invasive techniques. This work focuses on the classification and analysis of multispectral synthetic images composed of diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance brain volumes to evaluate the area of cerebrospinal fluid and its correlation with the progression of Alzheimer's disease. A 1.5 T MR imaging system was used to acquire all the images presented. The classification methods employed are based on multilayer perceptrons and radial basis function network classifiers. Assuming that the classes of interest can be separated by hyperquadrics, a polynomial network of degree 2 is utilized to classify the original volumes, generating a ground-truth volume. The classification results enhance the usual analysis by providing a map of apparent diffusion coefficients.
label: AI

title: Semi-Global Stereo Matching with Surface Orientation Priors
Abstract: Semi-Global Matching (SGM) is a widely used and efficient stereo matching technique. While it performs well on textured scenes, it struggles with untextured slanted surfaces due to its fronto-parallel smoothness assumption. To address this issue, we propose a simple extension, termed SGM-P, which utilizes precomputed surface orientation priors. These priors favor different surface slants in various 2D image regions or 3D scene regions and can be derived through various methods. This paper evaluates plane orientation priors derived from stereo matching at a coarser resolution, demonstrating that these priors can significantly enhance performance for challenging weakly-textured scenes. We also explore surface normal priors derived from Manhattan-world assumptions and analyze the potential performance gains using oracle priors derived from ground-truth data. SGM-P introduces a minimal computational overhead to SGM, making it an attractive alternative to more complex methods employing higher-order smoothness terms.
label: AI

title: Dialectical Multispectral Classification of Diffusion-Weighted Magnetic Resonance Images as an Alternative to Apparent Diffusion Coefficients Maps to Perform Anatomical Analysis
Abstract: Multispectral image analysis is a promising field of research with applications in diverse areas, including medical imaging and satellite monitoring. A significant number of current analysis methods rely on parametric statistics. Alternatively, some methods in Computational Intelligence draw inspiration from biology and other sciences. We propose that Philosophy can also serve as a valuable source of inspiration. This work introduces the Objective Dialectical Method (ODM): a classification method rooted in the Philosophy of Praxis. ODM plays a crucial role in assembling evolvable mathematical tools for analyzing multispectral images. In the case study described in this paper, multispectral images are composed of diffusion-weighted (DW) magnetic resonance (MR) images. The results are compared to ground-truth images generated by polynomial networks using a morphological similarity index. The classification results improve the conventional analysis of the apparent diffusion coefficient map. Our findings demonstrate the ability to distinguish gray and white matter in DW-MR multispectral analysis, indicating that DW-MR images can provide anatomical information.
label: AI

title: Avaliação do método dialético na quantização de imagens multiespectrais
Abstract: Unsupervised classification plays a vital role in the analysis of multispectral images, facilitating the extraction of a priori knowledge from images. Algorithms such as k-means and fuzzy c-means have long been employed for this task. Computational Intelligence has proven to be a valuable field for building classifiers optimized based on the quality of class grouping and vector quantization evaluation. Numerous studies have highlighted the inspirational role of Philosophy, particularly the Dialectical Method, in constructing novel computational methods. This paper presents an evaluation of four methods based on Dialectics: the Objective Dialectical Classifier and the Dialectical Optimization Method adapted to create a version of k-means with optimal quality indices. Each method is presented in two versions: a canonical version and another version obtained by applying the Principle of Maximum Entropy. These methods were compared to k-means, fuzzy c-means, and Kohonen's self-organizing maps. The results revealed that the Dialectics-based methods exhibit robustness to noise, and quantization can achieve results comparable to those obtained with the Kohonen map, considered an optimal quantizer.
label: AI

title: Triagem virtual de imagens de imuno-histoquímica usando redes neurais artificiais e espectro de padrões
Abstract: The importance of organizing medical images based on their nature, application, and relevance is steadily increasing. Moreover, pre-selecting medical images can significantly accelerate the analysis process performed by pathologists. This work proposes an image classifier to integrate a CBIR (Content-Based Image Retrieval) selection system. The classifier is based on pattern spectra and neural networks. Feature selection is accomplished using pattern spectra and principal component analysis, while image classification relies on multilayer perceptrons and a combination of self-organizing maps and learning vector quantization. These methods were applied to content selection for immunohistochemical images of placenta and newborn lungs. Results demonstrate that this approach can achieve reasonable classification performance.
label: AI

title: Fuzzy-Based Dialectical Non-Supervised Image Classification and Clustering
Abstract: The materialist dialectical method is a philosophical investigative approach used to analyze aspects of reality. These aspects are viewed as complex processes composed of basic units called poles, which interact with each other. Dialectics has experienced considerable progress in the 19th century with Hegel's dialectics and, in the 20th century, with the works of Marx, Engels, and Gramsci in Philosophy and Economics. The movement of poles through their contradictions is considered a dynamic process with intertwined phases of evolution and revolutionary crisis. To construct a computational process based on dialectics, the interaction between poles can be modeled using fuzzy membership functions. Based on this assumption, we introduce the Objective Dialectical Classifier (ODC), an unsupervised map for classification rooted in materialist dialectics and designed as an extension of the fuzzy c-means classifier. As a case study, we employed ODC to classify 181 magnetic resonance synthetic multispectral images composed of proton density, $T_1$- and $T_2$-weighted synthetic brain images. Comparing ODC to k-means, fuzzy c-means, and Kohonen's self-organized maps, using image fidelity indexes as estimates of quantization distortion, we demonstrated that ODC achieves nearly the same quantization performance as optimal unsupervised classifiers like Kohonen's self-organized maps.
label: AI

title: A semi-supervised fuzzy GrowCut algorithm to segment and classify regions of interest of mammographic images
Abstract: According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most prevalent form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women globally, making it the most fatal form of cancer. Mammographic image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, considering shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders. However, mammogram segmentation is a challenging process due to its high dependency on the types of mammary tissues. This work presents a novel semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on modifications to the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of interest is selected by a specialist. Our proposal utilizes fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut algorithm, enabling the estimation of the uncertainty of a pixel being part of the object or background. The proposed method significantly reduces the expert effort required for initializing seed points in GrowCut to achieve accurate segmentation, eliminating the need for background seed selection. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the simulated annealing optimization method, eliminating the need for human intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of the segmented regions. To validate our proposal, we developed an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. We employed Zernike moments to extract segmented image features. This analysis utilized 685 mammograms from the IRMA breast cancer database, focusing on fat and fibroid tissues. Results indicate that the proposed technique achieved a classification rate of 91.28% for fat tissues, demonstrating the feasibility of our approach.
label: AI

title: Multimodal Visual Concept Learning with Weakly Supervised Techniques
Abstract: Despite the abundance of video data accompanied by descriptive texts, effectively exploiting the information contained in natural language to automatically recognize video concepts remains a challenge. To address this, this paper utilizes textual cues as means of supervision, introducing two weakly supervised techniques that extend the Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) framework: the Fuzzy Sets Multiple Instance Learning (FSMIL) and the Probabilistic Labels Multiple Instance Learning (PLMIL). FSMIL encodes the spatio-temporal imprecision of linguistic descriptions using Fuzzy Sets, while PLMIL models different interpretations of each description's semantics with Probabilistic Labels, both formulated through a convex optimization algorithm. Additionally, we introduce a novel technique for extracting weak labels in the presence of complex semantics, involving semantic similarity computations. We evaluate our methods on two distinct problems, namely face and action recognition, in the challenging and realistic setting of movies accompanied by their screenplays, contained in the COGNIMUSE database. Our results show that, on both tasks, our method significantly outperforms a state-of-the-art weakly supervised approach, as well as other baselines.
label: AI

title: Gradient Descent Learns One-hidden-layer CNN: Don't be Afraid of Spurious Local Minima
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of learning a one-hidden-layer neural network with a non-overlapping convolutional layer and ReLU activation, i.e., $f(\mathbf{Z}, \mathbf{w}, \mathbf{a}) = \sum_j a_j\sigma(\mathbf{w}^T\mathbf{Z}_j)$, where both the convolutional weights $\mathbf{w}$ and the output weights $\mathbf{a}$ are parameters to be learned. When the labels are the outputs from a teacher network of the same architecture with fixed weights $(\mathbf{w}^*, \mathbf{a}^*)$, we prove that with Gaussian input $\mathbf{Z}$, there exists a spurious local minimizer. Surprisingly, in the presence of this spurious local minimizer, gradient descent with weight normalization from randomly initialized weights can still be proven to recover the true parameters with constant probability. This probability can be boosted to 1 with multiple restarts. We also show that with constant probability, the same procedure could converge to the spurious local minimum, highlighting its non-trivial role in the dynamics of gradient descent. Furthermore, a quantitative analysis reveals that the gradient descent dynamics exhibits two phases: it initially progresses slowly but converges much faster after several iterations. |||
label: AI

title: SenseNet: 3D Objects Database and Tactile Simulator
Abstract: The majority of artificial intelligence research focused on vision, propelled by the availability of high-quality image datasets. We propose that focusing on sensorimotor systems and tactile feedback will lead to algorithms that better mimic human intelligence.  We present SenseNet, a collection of tactile simulators and a large-scale dataset of 3D objects designed for manipulation. SenseNet aims to accelerate tactile feedback and sensorimotor research, providing new opportunities for researchers in machine learning and computational neuroscience.
label: AI

title: How will the Internet of Things enable Augmented Personalized Health?
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming how we interact with information, particularly in healthcare.  IoT devices track our sleep, food intake, activity, and vital signs, while environmental sensors collect additional health-related data. This abundance of information opens up new avenues for healthcare solutions.  However, understanding an individual's health requires integrating clinical records, behavioral patterns, and social and environmental factors.  Augmented Personalized Healthcare (APH), leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI), addresses this challenge by combining various data sources and medical knowledge to enhance health management.  kHealth technology, an APH implementation, provides examples for technology-assisted health management in areas like asthma.  This approach emphasizes the conversion of multimodal data into actionable insights ("big data to smart data"), highlighting the role of contextualization, abstraction, and personalization.
label: AI

title: Users Constraints in Itemset Mining
Abstract: Discovering significant itemsets is a fundamental problem in data mining.  Constraint programming provides a flexible approach to addressing data mining tasks, allowing users to easily express and efficiently answer queries with constraints on items.  However, practical applications often require constraints on the dataset itself, such as specifying a particular itemset within a specific portion of the data. This paper introduces a general constraint programming model capable of handling any type of query on items or the dataset for itemset mining.
label: AI

title: Towards Building an Intelligent Anti-Malware System: A Deep Learning Approach using Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Malware Classification
Abstract: Developing an anti-malware system capable of counteracting unknown malware is a critical endeavor in information security.  We propose an intelligent anti-malware system powered by deep learning (DL) models.  These models can detect newly released malware through mathematical generalization, identifying the relationship between malware and its corresponding family. Using the Malimg dataset, we trained three DL models: CNN-SVM, GRU-SVM, and MLP-SVM.  Empirical results demonstrate that the GRU-SVM model, with its sophisticated architecture, achieves a predictive accuracy of approximately 84.92%.  Further exploration of optimal DL-SVM models represents the next step in the development of this intelligent anti-malware system.
label: AI

title: Neurally Plausible Model of Robot Reaching Inspired by Infant Motor Babbling
Abstract: This paper presents a neurally plausible model of robot reaching inspired by human infant reaching, grounded in embodied artificial intelligence.  The model combines learning sensory-motor correlations through motor babbling with arm motion planning using spreading activation.  Organized in three layers of neural maps representing the same sensory-motor space, the model is trained through motor babbling, shaping the structure and connections within and between the maps.  An implementation of the model is investigated using a simple reaching task on a humanoid robot, demonstrating successful learning of reaching motions with high accuracy and smoothness.
label: AI

title: Game-theoretic Network Centrality: A Review
Abstract: Game-theoretic centrality is a flexible and sophisticated approach to identifying the most important nodes in a network.  It draws on cooperative game theory and network theory, treating nodes as players in a cooperative game where coalition values are determined by graph-theoretic properties.  Using cooperative game theory solution concepts, the centrality of each node can be measured based on its contribution to the network's overall value.  This paper reviews game-theoretic network centrality measures, organizing them into two categories: those focused on node connectivity and those focused on synergies achieved by nodes in groups.  Algorithms and complexity are discussed for each centrality measure.
label: AI

title: Learning Continuous User Representations through Hybrid Filtering with doc2vec
Abstract: Online ad platforms struggle to acquire the necessary user data for precise targeting.  Audience look-alike modeling offers a potential solution, but model performance depends heavily on data quantity and quality.  To improve the predictive performance of look-alike modeling algorithms, we propose two novel hybrid filtering techniques utilizing the doc2vec neural probabilistic language model.  These techniques are applied to data from a large mobile ad exchange and app metadata from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.  First, we model mobile app users based on their app usage history and app descriptions (user2vec).  Second, we introduce context awareness to the model by incorporating additional user and app-related metadata during training (context2vec). Our findings reveal that: (1) user2vec provides higher-quality recommendations than existing techniques; (2) user representations generated by hybrid filtering using doc2vec serve as valuable features in supervised machine learning models for look-alike modeling, representing the first application of hybrid filtering user models using neural probabilistic language models in this domain; and (3) incorporating context metadata during doc2vec model training enhances performance compared to directly including the data as features in downstream models.
label: AI

title: Dynamic Interference Steering in Heterogeneous Cellular Networks
Abstract: With the proliferation of wireless communication technologies, interference has emerged as a significant impediment to network performance.  Effective interference management (IM) is crucial for accommodating the increasing number of subscribers and diverse services.  While numerous IM schemes exist, they all come with costs. Balancing the benefits and costs of each IM scheme requires adapting its operating parameters to different network deployments and dynamic channel conditions.  We propose a novel IM scheme, dynamic interference steering (DIS), which recognizes that interference can be steered rather than solely suppressed or mitigated. DIS leverages both channel state information (CSI) and data from the interfering signal to generate a signal that modifies the spatial characteristics of the original interference, partially or fully canceling it at the victim receiver.  By intelligently adjusting the steering signal strength, DIS optimizes interference direction to balance the transmitter's power allocation between interference steering and desired signal transmission.  Simulation results demonstrate that DIS enhances users' spectral efficiency by making better use of transmit power.

title: Compare, Compress and Propagate: Enhancing Neural Architectures with Alignment Factorization for Natural Language Inference
Abstract: This paper introduces a new deep learning architecture for Natural Language Inference (NLI).  First, we propose a new architecture where alignment pairs are compared, compressed, and then propagated to upper layers for enhanced representation learning. Second, we incorporate factorization layers for efficient and expressive compression of alignment vectors into scalar features, which augment the base word representations.  Our approach is designed to be conceptually simple, compact, and powerful.  Experiments on three popular benchmarks, SNLI, MultiNLI, and SciTail, demonstrate competitive performance. A lightweight parameterization of our model achieves a significant reduction in parameter size compared to existing state-of-the-art models, while maintaining competitive performance.  Visual analysis shows that our propagated features are highly interpretable.
label: AI

title: Learning Structural Weight Uncertainty for Sequential Decision-Making
Abstract: Learning probability distributions over the weights of neural networks (NNs) has proven beneficial in many applications.  Bayesian methods, such as Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD), offer a framework for reasoning about NN model uncertainty. However, by assuming independent Gaussian priors for individual NN weights, SVGD fails to incorporate the structural information (dependence) often present among weights.  We propose an efficient posterior learning method for structural weight uncertainty within an SVGD framework, employing matrix variate Gaussian priors on NN parameters.  We investigate the learned structural uncertainty in sequential decision-making problems, including contextual bandits and reinforcement learning. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the superiority of our model compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: f-Divergence constrained policy improvement
Abstract: To ensure stability during learning, state-of-the-art generalized policy iteration algorithms incorporate a trust region constraint in the policy improvement step, limiting information loss.  The size of the trust region is typically determined by the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, which offers a good notion of distance and yields closed-form solutions. This paper explores a more general class of f-divergences and derives corresponding policy update rules. The generic solution is expressed through the derivative of the convex conjugate function to f, encompassing the KL solution as a special case. Within the class of f-divergences, we focus on a one-parameter family of α-divergences to analyze the impact of divergence choice on policy improvement.  Previously known and new policy updates emerge for different α values.  We demonstrate that each type of policy update has a compatible policy evaluation stemming from the chosen f-divergence. Interestingly, mean-squared Bellman error minimization is closely related to policy evaluation with the Pearson χ²-divergence penalty, while the KL divergence results in the soft-max policy update and a log-sum-exp critic.  Asymptotic analysis of solutions for different α values is performed, showcasing the effects of using different divergence functions on a multi-armed bandit problem and common reinforcement learning problems.
label: AI

title: The Astrobiology of the Anthropocene
Abstract: Human influence on the biosphere has been evident since the advent of agriculture, with some stratigraphers suggesting that modern civilization marks a geological epoch transition. The study of the Anthropocene as a geological epoch, and its implications for the future of energy-intensive civilizations, is an emerging transdisciplinary field where astrobiology can play a significant role.  Habitability research on Earth, Mars, and exoplanets examines extreme cases relevant to understanding climate change as a planetary process.  Energy-intensive civilizations will also face thermodynamic limits to growth, providing constraints for estimating the longevity of human civilization and guiding the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.  We recommend pursuing mission concepts like LUVOIR, HabEx, and OST to advance our understanding of the future evolution of life on Earth and the potential evolution of technological, energy-intensive life elsewhere in the universe.
label: AI

title: Characterizing optimal hierarchical policy inference on graphs via non-equilibrium thermodynamics
Abstract: Hierarchies are fundamental in both stochastic optimal control and biological control.  Their ability to facilitate desirable computational traits in control algorithms and the potential for them to form a core principle in sensorimotor and cognitive control systems make them of particular interest.  However, a theoretically justified construction of state-space hierarchies across all spatial resolutions and their evolution through a policy inference process remains elusive.  This paper introduces a formalism for deriving such normative representations of discrete Markov decision processes in the context of graphs. The resulting hierarchies correspond to a hierarchical policy inference algorithm that approximates a discrete gradient flow between state-space trajectory densities generated by the prior and optimal policies.
label: AI

title: A Deep Belief Network Based Machine Learning System for Risky Host Detection
Abstract: To ensure cybersecurity within an enterprise, SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) systems are typically deployed to normalize security events from various preventive technologies and generate alerts.  Security Operation Center (SOC) analysts investigate these alerts to determine their malicious nature.  However, the volume of alerts is often overwhelming, with a high false positive rate exceeding the SOC's capacity to handle all alerts.  A critical need exists to minimize the false positive rate. While most previous research focused on network intrusion detection, we concentrate on risk detection and propose an intelligent Deep Belief Network machine learning system.  This system leverages alert information, security logs, and analysts' investigation results from a real enterprise environment to identify hosts with a high likelihood of compromise. Text mining and graph-based methods are employed to generate targets and create features for machine learning.  In experiments, Deep Belief Network outperforms other machine learning algorithms, including multi-layer neural network, random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression, on real enterprise data.  This system proves six times more effective than current rule-based systems.  We have implemented the entire system, from data collection, label creation, and feature engineering to host score generation, within a real enterprise production environment.

title: Principles of Neuromorphic Photonics
Abstract: In a world awash with information, the ability to process vast amounts of data has become essential.  The demand for data will only continue to grow as smart gadgets proliferate and become increasingly integrated into our lives.  Next-generation industries in artificial intelligence services and high-performance computing currently rely on microelectronic platforms.  These data-intensive enterprises require continual hardware improvements, but they face a stark reality: conventional one-size-fits-all solutions offered by digital electronics can no longer meet this need as Moore's Law, interconnection density, and the von Neumann architecture reach their limits.  With its superior speed and reconfigurability, analog photonics offers a potential solution.  However, complex applications of analog photonics remain largely unexplored due to the lack of a robust photonic integration industry.  Recent advancements in commercially manufacturable photonic chips promise to achieve economies of scale previously enjoyed solely by microelectronics.  The scientific community is bridging the gap between photonic device physics and neural networks, giving rise to the field of neuromorphic photonics.  This article reviews recent progress in integrated neuromorphic photonics, providing an overview of neuromorphic computing, discussing associated technology platforms, and comparing their performance metrics.  Photonic neural network approaches and challenges for integrated neuromorphic photonic processors are explored, along with an in-depth description of photonic neurons and a candidate interconnection architecture. The article concludes with a future outlook for neuro-inspired photonic processing.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Interior Tomography for Region-of-Interest Reconstruction
Abstract: Interior tomography for region-of-interest (ROI) imaging offers advantages in terms of using a small detector and reducing X-ray radiation dose.  However, standard analytic reconstruction suffers from severe cupping artifacts due to the null space in the truncated Radon transform.  Existing penalized reconstruction methods can address this issue, but they require extensive computations due to iterative reconstruction.  Inspired by recent deep learning approaches to low-dose and sparse view CT, we propose a deep learning architecture that removes null space signals from the FBP reconstruction.  Experimental results show that our method provides near-perfect reconstruction with significant improvement in PSNR over existing methods, while significantly reducing runtime complexity.
label: AI

title: RedDwarfData: a simplified dataset of StarCraft matches
Abstract: StarCraft is a compelling arena for testing new machine learning and computational intelligence techniques.  However, StarCraft matches are lengthy, and creating a good training dataset can be challenging.  Analyzing match logs to extract key characteristics can be time-consuming and subject to bias depending on the chosen methods.  This paper presents a simplified dataset, RedDwarfData, extracted from matches published by Robinson and Watson, containing thousands of matches processed into frames for temporal analysis.  The dataset is available on GitHub under a free license. An initial analysis and appraisal of these matches are also provided.
label: AI

title: Significance of Softmax-based Features in Comparison to Distance Metric Learning-based Features
Abstract: Extracting useful deep features is crucial for many computer vision tasks.  Deep features extracted from classification networks have proven successful in these tasks.  To obtain even more useful features, end-to-end distance metric learning (DML) has been applied to train the feature extractor directly.  However, equitable comparisons between features extracted from DML-based networks and those from softmax-based networks were lacking.  This paper provides objective comparisons between these two approaches under the same network architecture, demonstrating that softmax-based features perform competitively, or even better, than state-of-the-art DML features when the dataset size (number of training samples per class) is large.  These results suggest that softmax-based features should be considered when evaluating the performance of deep features.

title: 9.5 Hypotheses on the Informational Structure of Life which are Multi-scale, Human-readable, Provocative, Coherent, Plausible, Falsifiable, and Actionable
Abstract: This document presents a framework for a zero-parameter Unified Theory of Life, aiming to address the accelerating de-calibration of fluid human brains by compelling digitized signals.  Human sensory systems must be provided with data of the same quality as that used to train algorithmic intelligences.  The framework consists of ten hypotheses, encompassing humanity's current problem-space and a possible solution space.  The hypotheses are: H1.0 Stably evolving distributions must balance themselves between narrowing and broadening; H2.0 Stabilization and homeostasis are fragile in multiple ways; H3.0 Representing spacetime requires micro-timing and mega-assumptions; H4.0 When in doubt, ping!; H5.0 Mediated communication becomes infected with pinging; H6.0 If scaling and incentives are the problems, then entropy and affection are the solutions; H7.0 "Paleo everything but violence" provides sensorimotor nutrition; H8.0 Humans evolved to resonate ecstatically; H9.0 Symmetric spinal health syndrome; H9.5 Helping the irresistible force beat the immovable object.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Analogical Similarity to Guide Schema Induction and Attention
Abstract: Research in analogical reasoning suggests that higher-order cognitive functions, such as abstract reasoning, far transfer, and creativity, are based on recognizing structural similarities among relational systems.  This paper integrates theories of analogy with the computational framework of reinforcement learning (RL).  We propose a psychology theory that combines analogy and RL, where analogical comparison provides the RL learning algorithm with a measure of relational similarity, and RL provides feedback signals that drive analogical learning.  Simulation results support the effectiveness of this approach. |||

title: Corpus specificity in LSA and Word2vec: the role of out-of-domain documents
Abstract: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) and Word2vec are popular word embedding techniques, but the exact mechanisms by which they learn new semantic relationships between words remain unclear. This study investigates whether LSA and Word2vec's ability to identify relevant semantic dimensions increases with corpus size.  It examines two hypotheses:  one suggesting that larger datasets improve dimension identification, and another proposing that increasing corpus size with irrelevant topics can reduce signal-to-noise ratio. The study analyzes two methods of document elimination: random removal versus removal of documents unrelated to a specific task. Results show that Word2vec benefits from using the entire corpus, achieving optimal performance with all documents. Conversely, LSA's performance improves with specialized training sets (removing out-of-domain documents) and dimensionality reduction,  resulting in faster processing times. However, specialization without dimensionality reduction significantly reduces LSA's performance on specific tasks. From a cognitive modeling perspective, the study suggests that LSA's word knowledge acquisition might not efficiently leverage higher-order co-occurrences and global relationships, unlike Word2vec.
