title: Kernel Robust Bias-Aware Prediction under Covariate Shift
Abstract: Covariate shift occurs when training and testing data differ in input space distribution but share the same conditional label distribution, presenting a challenge for machine learning. Robust Bias-Aware (RBA) prediction aims to find the conditional label distribution that is robust to the worst-case logarithmic loss for the target distribution while satisfying feature expectation constraints from the source distribution. However, insufficient feature constraints can lead to high-certainty predictions for the source data, while leaving target data predictions uncertain. To address this issue, the study extends the representer theorem to the RBA setting, allowing the minimization of regularized expected target risk through a reweighted kernel expectation under the source distribution.  By applying kernel methods, the study establishes consistency guarantees and demonstrates superior performance of the RBA classifier compared to existing methods on both synthetically biased UCI datasets and datasets exhibiting natural covariate shift.
label: AI

title: Toward Continual Learning for Conversational Agents
Abstract: End-to-end neural conversation models have achieved significant advancements in reducing hand-crafted features and errors associated with traditional complex system architectures. However, they typically require vast amounts of data due to their lack of modularity. Previous studies have employed hybrid approaches with knowledge-based components to address this challenge, either by extracting domain-specific information or by augmenting data to encompass more diverse patterns.  This study proposes a different approach, leveraging recent advancements in continual learning for neural models.  Specifically, it adopts a domain-independent neural conversational model and introduces a novel neural continual learning algorithm that allows a conversational agent to acquire skills across various tasks in a data-efficient manner.  This is the first study to apply continual learning to conversation systems. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through conversational skill transfer from both synthetic and human-human dialogs to human-computer conversations in a customer support domain.
label: AI

title: Automated Conjecturing VII: The Graph Brain Project & Big Mathematics
Abstract: The Graph Brain Project explores a model for future mathematical research, leveraging automated mathematical discovery software, databases, large-scale collaboration, and systematic investigation. The project began with the development of software capable of generating invariant-relation and property-relation conjectures in various mathematical fields, producing conjectures that are not implied by existing published theorems. This study proposes a new approach to advancing existing mathematical research goals by utilizing automated mathematical discovery software, advocating for the initiation and harnessing of large-scale collaborative mathematics. The study envisions mathematical research labs similar to those in other sciences, along with new avenues for funding, student training opportunities, and more efficient utilization of published mathematical research. The experiment in graph theory serves as a model that can be replicated in other areas of mathematical research. The study emphasizes "Big Mathematics," a concept advocating for large-scale, systematic, and collaborative research on existing mathematical problems.  It explores the potential outcomes of systematically combining skills, tools, and results.
label: AI

title: What do we need to build explainable AI systems for the medical domain?
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) demonstrate remarkable practical success in various application domains, including autonomous driving, speech recognition, and recommender systems. Deep learning approaches, trained on massive datasets or using reinforcement learning methods, have even surpassed human performance in visual tasks, notably in playing games like Atari and mastering Go.  Despite these achievements, the "black-box" nature of such models poses a significant challenge.  While the underlying mathematical principles are understood, these models lack an explicit declarative knowledge representation, hindering the generation of underlying explanatory structures.  This necessitates systems that enable transparent, understandable, and explainable decisions.  The study highlights the increasing importance of legal and privacy aspects, with the new European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) making black-box approaches difficult to employ in business. While not prohibiting automatic learning methods, the regulation requires the ability to trace results upon request.  The paper outlines research topics within the emerging field of explainable-AI, focusing on medical applications, which present unique challenges due to the use of distributed, heterogeneous, and complex data sources. The study concentrates on three data sources: images, *omics data, and text. It argues that research in explainable-AI can facilitate the implementation of AI/ML in the medical domain, specifically enhancing transparency and trust.
label: AI

title: Rating Protocol Design for Extortion and Cooperation in the Crowdsourcing Contest Dilemma
Abstract: Crowdsourcing has emerged as a paradigm for harnessing human intelligence and activity to solve a wide range of tasks. However, strategic workers may exploit the crowdsourcing contest dilemma game by free-riding and engaging in malicious activities. This necessitates effective incentive mechanisms to overcome the inefficiency of socially undesirable equilibria. Existing incentive mechanisms are often ineffective in encouraging cooperation in crowdsourcing competitions due to the heterogeneity of workers competing against each other on platforms with imperfect monitoring. This study addresses these limitations by developing a novel game-theoretic design of rating protocols that integrate binary rating labels with differential pricing.  This approach aims to maximize the requester's utility by deterring selfish workers and promoting cooperation. By quantifying necessary and sufficient conditions for sustainable social norms, the study formulates the problem of maximizing the requester's revenue among all sustainable rating protocols. It provides design guidelines for optimal rating protocols and develops a low-complexity algorithm to select optimal design parameters related to differential punishments and pricing schemes. Simulation results demonstrate the impact of intrinsic parameters on design parameters and the performance gains achieved by the proposed rating protocol.
label: AI

title: Report: Dynamic Eye Movement Matching and Visualization Tool in Neuro Gesture
Abstract: Inferring audience attention during lectures involving gestures poses a significant challenge. Eye movement and Electroencephalography (EEG) data provide valuable insights into attention levels.  Under the assumption that attentive individuals focus on the same location simultaneously, this study applies the "Time Warp Edit Distance" method to calculate the similarity of eye movement trajectories among audience members.  The study further clusters audience eye movement patterns based on pairwise similarity metrics. Due to the absence of a direct "attention" ground truth, visual assessment becomes crucial for evaluating the gesture-attention relationship.  Consequently, the study implements a visualization tool to facilitate this assessment.
label: AI

title: Learning More Universal Representations for Transfer-Learning
Abstract: A universal representation encodes all elements of the visual world (objects, scenes) in any configuration (scale, context).  While perfect universality is not expected, research aims to improve universality levels starting from existing representations.  Current state-of-the-art approaches involve learning CNN-based representations on diversified training problems (e.g., modified ImageNet with annotated data). While effective, this requires significant effort in acquiring annotated data. This study proposes two methods to enhance universality while minimizing the need for annotated data.  It introduces a unified framework for these methods based on training problem diversification.  Drawing inspiration from Atkinson's cognitive study on universal human representations, the study employs a transfer-learning scheme and a new metric for evaluating universality.  The study demonstrates the benefits of these methods on 10 target problems related to classification tasks and various visual domains.
label: AI

title: Scalable Entity Resolution Using Probabilistic Signatures on Parallel Databases
Abstract: Accurate and efficient entity resolution is an open challenge, particularly relevant for intelligence organizations that collect large datasets from diverse sources with varying quality and standards.  Starting from a first-principles formulation of entity resolution, this study presents a novel Entity Resolution algorithm that introduces a data-driven blocking and record-linkage technique based on the probabilistic identification of entity signatures in data.  The scalability and accuracy of the proposed algorithm are evaluated using benchmark datasets, demonstrating state-of-the-art results.  The algorithm can be readily implemented on modern parallel databases, enabling easy deployment in large-scale industrial applications.
label: AI

title: The information bottleneck and geometric clustering
Abstract: The information bottleneck (IB) approach to clustering uses a joint distribution $P\\!\\left(X,Y\\right)$ and maps data $X$ to cluster labels $T$ that retain maximum information about $Y$ (Tishby et al., 1999). This objective results in an algorithm that clusters data points based on the similarity of their conditional distributions $P\\!\\left(Y\\mid X\\right)$.  In contrast, classic "geometric clustering" algorithms, such as $k$-means and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs), cluster observed data points $\\left\\{ \\mathbf{x}_{i}\\right\\} _{i=1:N}$ based on their geometric (typically Euclidean) distance from one another.  This study demonstrates how to use the deterministic information bottleneck (DIB) (Strouse and Schwab, 2017), a variation of IB, to perform geometric clustering by selecting cluster labels that preserve information about data point location on a smoothed dataset.  It introduces a novel method for choosing the number of clusters, based on identifying solutions where the tradeoff between the number of clusters used and spatial information preserved is strongest. The study applies this approach to various simple clustering problems, showing that DIB with the model selection procedure recovers the generative cluster labels.  Furthermore, it demonstrates that in specific limits of model parameters, clustering with DIB and IB is equivalent to $k$-means and EM fitting of a GMM with hard and soft assignments, respectively. Thus, clustering with (D)IB generalizes and provides an information-theoretic perspective on these classic algorithms.
label: AI

title: PyPhi: A toolbox for integrated information theory
Abstract: Integrated information theory provides a mathematical framework for characterizing the cause-effect structure of a physical system.  This study introduces PyPhi, a Python software package that implements this framework for causal analysis and unveils the full cause-effect structure of discrete dynamical systems of binary elements.  The software allows users to easily study these structures, serves as an up-to-date reference implementation of integrated information theory formalisms, and has been applied in research on complexity, emergence, and specific biological questions.  The study first provides an overview of the main algorithm and demonstrates PyPhi's functionality through an example system analysis.  It then delves into details regarding the algorithm's design and implementation. PyPhi can be installed with Python's package manager using the command 'pip install pyphi' on Linux and macOS systems with Python 3.4 or higher. The software is open-source and licensed under the GPLv3, with source code hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/wmayner/pyphi. Comprehensive and continuously updated documentation is available at https://pyphi.readthedocs.io/. The pyphi-users mailing list can be joined at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/pyphi-users.  A web-based graphical interface is accessible at http://integratedinformationtheory.org/calculate.html.

title: An empirical evaluation for the intrusion detection features based on machine learning and feature selection methods
Abstract: Despite significant advancements in information technology, particularly the internet, computer networks, and global information exchange, which have positively impacted all areas of daily life, these technologies have also contributed to the development of penetration and intrusion, posing significant risks to the security of information organizations, government agencies, and resulting in substantial economic losses.  Many protection techniques have been developed, such as firewalls and intrusion detection systems (IDS). IDS utilizes software and/or hardware techniques to detect malicious activities in computer systems.  Two types of anomalies are used in IDS to identify intrusive activities that deviate from normal user behavior. Misuse detection relies on a knowledge base containing all known attack techniques, identifying intrusions by researching this base.  Artificial intelligence techniques have been introduced to enhance the performance of these systems.  IDS plays a crucial role in identifying unauthorized access attempts to compromise confidentiality, integrity, or availability of computer networks. This study investigates the Intrusion Detection (ID) problem using three machine learning algorithms: BayesNet algorithm, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machine (SVM).  The algorithms are applied to a real-world, Management Information Based (MIB) dataset collected from a real-life environment.  To improve detection accuracy, the study employs a set of feature selection approaches: Infogain (IG), ReleifF (RF), and Genetic Search (GS). Experiments show that the three feature selection methods enhance classification performance.  GS combined with BayesNet, MLP, and SVM yields high accuracy rates, with BayesNet achieving a 99.9% accuracy rate with GS.
label: AI

title: An Online Ride-Sharing Path Planning Strategy for Public Vehicle Systems
Abstract: Public vehicle (PV) systems, as efficient traffic management platforms, are envisioned as a promising solution for addressing traffic congestion and pollution in future smart cities.  PV systems provide online/dynamic peer-to-peer ride-sharing services, aiming to serve a sufficient number of customers with the minimum number of vehicles and lowest possible cost.  Online ride-sharing scheduling strategy is a key component of PV systems. This study proposes an efficient path planning strategy that focuses on a limited potential search area for each vehicle by filtering out requests that violate passenger service quality levels, reducing global search to local search.  The study analyzes the performance of the proposed solution, including the reduction ratio of computational complexity. Simulations based on the Manhattan taxi dataset demonstrate a 22% reduction in computing time compared to the exhaustive search method, while maintaining the same service quality performance.
label: AI

title: First Draft on the xInf Model for Universal Physical Computation and Reverse Engineering of Natural Intelligence
Abstract: Turing Machines are theoretically universal computing machines.  The debate regarding whether Turing Machines can simulate conscious mind behaviors in the materialistic universe has generated three primary hypotheses: (A) Can; (B) Cannot; (C) Super-Turing machines can. Since Turing Machines and other theoretical computing models are abstract objects, while behaviors are real observables, this debate involves at least three distinct fields: physics, computer engineering, and experimental neuroscience. The languages used in these fields are highly heterogeneous and not easily interpretable by each other, hindering the development of partial agreements.  This study aims to establish a common language that can facilitate communication across these fields.  It proposes a theoretical model for analyzing how theoretical computing machines would physically run in physical time, termed the xInf. This model is Turing-complete in theory and, depending on the properties of physical time, can be either Turing-equivalent or Super-Turing in the physical universe.  The xInf model is demonstrated to be a suitable universal language for translating across physics, computer engineering, and neuroscience.  The study concludes by proposing a conjecture that there exists a Minimal Complete Set of rules in the xInf model that enables the construction of a physical machine using inorganic materials capable of passing the Turing Test in physical time.  The conjecture cannot be verified or falsified using paper-based finite-order logic, requiring physical time itself, i.e., an evolutionary competition, to determine the conclusion.
label: AI

title: RLlib: Abstractions for Distributed Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms involve deeply nested highly irregular computation patterns, each exhibiting opportunities for distributed computation.  This study advocates for distributing RL components in a composable manner by adapting algorithms for top-down hierarchical control, thereby encapsulating parallelism and resource requirements within short-running compute tasks.  The study demonstrates the benefits of this principle through RLlib, a library that provides scalable software primitives for RL.  These primitives enable the implementation of a wide range of algorithms with high performance, scalability, and substantial code reuse.  RLlib is available at https://rllib.io/.

title: HACS: Human Action Clips and Segments Dataset for Recognition and Temporal Localization
Abstract: This study presents HACS (Human Action Clips and Segments), a new large-scale dataset for recognizing and temporally localizing human actions collected from web videos. The dataset utilizes both consensus and disagreement among visual classifiers to automatically mine candidate short clips from unlabeled videos, which are subsequently validated by human annotators. The resulting dataset is named HACS Clips. Through a separate process, the study also collects annotations defining action segment boundaries, resulting in the HACS Segments dataset.  Overall, HACS Clips comprises 1.5 million annotated clips sampled from 504,000 untrimmed videos, and HACS Segments contains 139,000 action segments densely annotated in 50,000 untrimmed videos spanning 200 action categories.  HACS Clips provides more labeled examples than any existing video benchmark, making it a large-scale action recognition benchmark and an excellent source for spatiotemporal feature learning.  Transfer learning experiments on three target datasets show that HACS Clips outperforms Kinetics-600, Moments-In-Time, and Sports1M as a pretraining source.  The study evaluates state-of-the-art action proposal generation and action localization methods on HACS Segments, highlighting the new challenges posed by its dense temporal annotations.
label: AI

title: Building Robust Deep Neural Networks for Road Sign Detection
Abstract: Deep Neural Networks are designed to generalize beyond the training set by employing techniques such as regularization, early stopping, and dropout. However, considerations for making them more resilient to adversarial examples are often neglected. As deep neural networks become more prevalent in mission-critical and real-time systems, malicious actors are beginning to attack them by intentionally causing misclassification. This can have catastrophic consequences in scenarios where the classification of a deep neural network leads to fatal machine decisions.  This study uses the GTSRB dataset to craft adversarial samples using the Fast Gradient Sign Method and Jacobian Saliency Method.  These crafted adversarial samples are then used to attack another Deep Convolutional Neural Network, and the attacked network is made more resilient to adversarial attacks by employing Defensive Distillation and Adversarial Training, enhancing its robustness.
label: AI

title: Who is Smarter? Intelligence Measure of Learning-based Cognitive Radios
Abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) is considered a key enabling technology for dynamic spectrum access, improving spectrum efficiency. While the CR concept was initially conceived with the core idea of cognitive capabilities, research on measuring these capabilities and intelligence remains largely unexplored.  Deriving intelligence measures for CR can not only lead to the development of new CR technologies but also enable better network configuration by integrating CRs with varying cognitive capabilities.  This study proposes a data-driven methodology to quantitatively measure the intelligence factors of CRs with learning capabilities.  The approach involves conducting various tests on CRs in different spectrum environments under varying settings, obtaining performance data on different metrics.  Factor analysis is then applied to the performance data to identify and quantify the intelligence factors and cognitive capabilities of the CR.  The study presents a case study consisting of 144 different types of CRs, varying in learning-based dynamic spectrum access strategies, number of sensors, sensing accuracy, processing speed, and algorithmic complexity.  Five intelligence factors are identified for the CRs through data analysis.  The study demonstrates that these factors align well with the nature of the tested CRs, validating the proposed intelligence measure methodology.
label: AI

title: A model for interpreting social interactions in local image regions
Abstract: Understanding social interactions (e.g., "hug" or "fight") is a fundamental and essential capability of the human visual system but remains a challenging and open problem for modeling.  This study investigates visual recognition of social interactions, focusing on small but recognizable local regions.  The approach relies on two key components: (i) reliable recognition of social interactions from reduced images ("minimal images"), and (ii) interaction recognition based on identifying components and relationships within the minimal image ("interpretation").  The study presents psychophysics data for minimal images and modeling results for their interpretation.  It discusses the integration of minimal configurations for recognizing social interactions in detailed, high-resolution images.
label: AI

title: A Real-Time Autonomous Highway Accident Detection Model Based on Big Data Processing and Computational Intelligence
Abstract: Due to increasing urban populations and growing numbers of motor vehicles, traffic congestion is becoming a major problem of the 21st century.  Accidents are a significant contributor to congestion, leading to casualties, losses for those involved, and wasted time for others caught in traffic.  Early accident detection can save lives, facilitate faster road openings, minimize wasted time and resources, and enhance efficiency.  This study proposes a preliminary real-time autonomous accident detection system based on computational intelligence techniques.  Istanbul City traffic flow data for 2015 from various sensor locations is populated using big data processing methodologies. The extracted features are then fed into a nearest neighbor model, a regression tree, and a feed-forward neural network model to predict the possibility of an accident.  While the number of false alarms outpaces real accident cases, the results indicate that the system can still provide useful information for status verification and early response to potential accidents.
label: AI

title: REDBEE: A Visual-Inertial Drone System for Real-Time Moving Object Detection
Abstract: Real-time motion detection from moving cameras is crucial for aerial surveillance and monitoring. Current drone-based techniques rely on sending video data back to ground stations, leading to delays and potential data corruption. To address these limitations, this paper proposes REDBEE, a visual-inertial drone system that enables real-time motion detection with high accuracy on limited computing power. REDBEE leverages inertial-aided dual-plane homography estimation to overcome parallax challenges and probabilistic modeling based on spatial, temporal, and entropy consistency to filter dynamic background noise. Experiments demonstrate REDBEE's superior performance in detecting moving targets compared to existing real-time onboard detection systems.
label: AI

title: Matching model of flow table for networked big data
Abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) offers a promising solution for intelligent big data networking, where adaptive data transmission is crucial. This paper focuses on optimizing the matching strategy in SDN switches' flow tables. A classification approach is employed to analyze packet structures using a tuple-space lookup mechanism. The proposed F-OpenFlow model classifies packets based on specific fields, enhancing flow table utilization and matching efficiency for networked big data. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of F-OpenFlow in improving performance.
label: AI

title: The Age of Information in Multihop Networks
Abstract: Minimizing the age of information in multihop networks, such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems, is essential for timely updates. This paper investigates strategies to minimize the age of a single information flow in interference-free multihop networks. Under preemption and exponentially distributed packet transmission times, the preemptive Last-Generated, First-Served (LGFS) policy is proven to minimize age processes across all nodes compared to any other causal policy. For New-Better-than-Used (NBU) distributions, the non-preemptive LGFS policy is shown to be within a constant age gap from the optimal average age. However, numerical results indicate that preemptive LGFS can deviate significantly from the optimal for some NBU distributions. When preemption is prohibited and packet transmission times are arbitrary, the non-preemptive LGFS policy minimizes age processes across all nodes among work-conserving policies. These findings hold under general conditions, including arbitrary packet generation and arrival times.
label: AI

title: A Random Block-Coordinate Douglas-Rachford Splitting Method with Low Computational Complexity for Binary Logistic Regression
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for sparse logistic regression based on a stochastic version of the Douglas-Rachford splitting method. The algorithm utilizes a mini-batch approach for efficient training set traversal, enabling block coordinate updates of variables. Leveraging the proximity operator of the logistic loss, expressed with the generalized Lambert W function, the proposed method demonstrates superior efficiency compared to stochastic gradient-like methods. Experiments conducted on standard datasets validate the effectiveness of the approach.
label: AI

title: Brain Tumor Segmentation Based on Refined Fully Convolutional Neural Networks with A Hierarchical Dice Loss
Abstract: Semantic segmentation, a fundamental task in computer vision, provides crucial information for object detection and instance segmentation, aiding artificial intelligence in understanding the real world. This paper explores the application of fully convolutional neural networks (FCNNs) for brain tumor segmentation, comparing different architectures and proposing modifications for improved performance. Enhancements include additional connections between convolutional layers, enlarged decoders after upsampling layers, and refined information reuse from shallower layers. A new classifier incorporating a hierarchical dice loss is also introduced, addressing data imbalance challenges. Extensive experiments on training and testing sets validate the effectiveness of the refined FCNNs and the hierarchical dice loss, demonstrating superior results compared to previous approaches.
label: AI

title: A total uncertainty measure for D numbers based on belief intervals
Abstract: The theory of D numbers, a generalization of Dempster-Shafer theory, provides a framework for uncertainty reasoning. This paper addresses the challenge of measuring the uncertainty of knowledge represented by D numbers. Inspired by distance-based uncertainty measures for Dempster-Shafer theory, a total uncertainty measure is proposed based on belief intervals. This measure captures discord, non-specificity, and non-exclusiveness in D numbers. The paper also presents basic properties of this measure, including range, monotonicity, and generalized set consistency.
label: AI

title: Null Dynamical State Models of Human Cognitive Dysfunction
Abstract: This paper explores the "hard problem" in artificial intelligence, investigating how symbol manipulation in programs leads to semantic experiences and qualia. The paper focuses on a new class of human semantic symbols that arise during unexpected environmental changes, rendering pre-learned programs ineffective and causing surprise, confusion, and even dysfunction. This state is then linked to the natural response of learning machines encountering novel inputs outside their training set, resulting in null outputs and lack of response. Further exploration focuses on learning machines trained to execute multiple functions with environmental data dictating program elements. Drastic changes in these inputs can lead to inoperative programs, allowing for the modeling of human cognitive symbols like attachment and grief based on specific environmental dependencies. The approach connects known machine states with human qualia, providing new insights into the hard problem of artificial intelligence.
label: AI

title: Kernel Regression with Sparse Metric Learning
Abstract: Kernel regression is a non-parametric fitting technique widely used for function learning. This paper proposes a novel kernel regression method, called KR_SML, incorporating sparse metric learning. The method utilizes a mixed (2,1)-norm regularization on the metric matrix to learn a Mahalanobis distance metric. This approach enables simultaneous dimensionality reduction and improved prediction results. KR_SML is evaluated on 19 datasets for regression, demonstrating its effectiveness. Additionally, the method is applied to forecasting short-term traffic flows and compared to other kernel regression methods. Experimental results highlight KR_SML's competitive performance.
label: AI

title: Android Malware Detection using Deep Learning on API Method Sequences
Abstract: Android's widespread adoption has made it a target for malicious apps, necessitating robust malware detection solutions. This paper introduces MalDozer, an automatic Android malware detection and family attribution framework based on deep learning techniques. MalDozer utilizes sequence classification by analyzing the raw sequence of API method calls within an app. It automatically extracts malicious and benign patterns from actual samples to detect malware. MalDozer can be deployed across servers, mobile devices, and even IoT devices. Evaluation on multiple datasets, ranging from 1K to 33K malware apps and 38K benign apps, demonstrates MalDozer's high accuracy with an F1-Score of 96%-99% and a false positive rate of 0.06%-2%.
label: AI

title: Network-Scale Traffic Modeling and Forecasting with Graphical Lasso and Neural Networks
Abstract: Short-term traffic flow forecasting is crucial for intelligent transportation systems (ITS). This paper explores network-scale modeling and forecasting of short-term traffic flows. It introduces single-link and multi-link models for traffic flow forecasting and proposes four prediction models by combining these models with single-task and multi-task learning. The multi-link model with multi-task learning improves both efficiency and prediction accuracy. Additionally, a novel multi-link single-task approach combining graphical lasso (GL) with neural network (NN) is presented. GL utilizes L1 regularization to build a sparse graphical model based on the sparse inverse covariance matrix. Gaussian process regression (GPR), a classic regression algorithm in Bayesian machine learning, is also applied to traffic flow forecasting. Extensive experiments compare the proposed approaches, highlighting their effectiveness and potential for accurate short-term traffic flow forecasting.
label: AI

title: The Internet of Battle Things
Abstract: The future battlefield is envisioned as the Internet of Battle Things (IoBT), where diverse intelligent entities interact and collaborate with each other and human warfighters. This paper explores the major challenges of IoBT, focusing on the need for flexible and adaptive communications among these entities. Other challenges discussed include the need for scalable and secure infrastructure, robust decision-making processes, and efficient human-machine collaboration. The paper outlines key research directions and approaches to address these challenges, emphasizing the importance of developing new technologies and strategies for a successful IoBT implementation.
label: AI

title: How do you Command an Army of Intelligent Things?
Abstract: The increasing integration of intelligent things, such as robots and agents, into the workforce poses significant challenges for management and organization. This paper examines these issues within the context of warfare, where Command and Control (C2) is crucial for managing military operations. The paper explores how human and intelligent entities can contribute effectively to C2, ensuring decision-makers have the necessary information and utilize it effectively. Challenges for managing mixed human-thing organizations are highlighted, including the need for things to explain their actions, build trust, and negotiate with humans. Both things and humans face limitations in anticipating and coping with the unexpected, requiring innovative solutions to navigate these challenges.
label: AI

title: Traffic Flow Forecasting Using a Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Network Predictor
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel spatio-temporal Bayesian network predictor for traffic flow forecasting. Unlike existing methods, this approach incorporates all available spatial and temporal information within a transportation network. Pearson correlation coefficient is used to rank input variables, and a best-first strategy selects a subset as cause nodes in a Bayesian network. A Gaussian Mixture Model is applied to describe the relationship between input and output nodes. Traffic flow forecasting is performed based on the Minimum Mean Square Error (M.M.S.E.) criterion. Experiments using urban vehicular flow data from Beijing demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed spatio-temporal Bayesian network predictor.
label: AI

title: Optimal Weighting for Exam Composition
Abstract: Designing exams that accurately assess student abilities is a significant challenge for instructors. Traditional exam design relies on fixed question weights based on subjective difficulty estimates. This paper introduces a novel framework using machine learning algorithms to optimize exam question weights based on overall class grades as a proxy for true ability. The approach demonstrates significant error reduction compared to standard weighting schemes and provides insights into the characteristics of effective and ineffective exam questions, informing the design of improved evaluation methods.
label: AI

title: How Intelligent is your Intelligent Robot?
Abstract: This paper investigates the concept of embodied intelligence in robots and compares it to animal intelligence. It proposes a framework for understanding intelligence as a combination of four distinct types: cognitive, social, emotional, and physical. These types are represented diagrammatically as axes in a star diagram, allowing for qualitative comparisons between animal and robot intelligence. The analysis reveals a chronic intelligence deficit in robots and explores potential avenues for quantifying these four types of intelligence.
label: AI

title: Predicting Rich Drug-Drug Interactions via Biomedical Knowledge Graphs and Text Jointly Embedding
Abstract: Predicting drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is a crucial area of research in clinical pharmacology. While big data offers new opportunities for DDI discovery, the vast amount of noisy data necessitates sophisticated approaches. This paper presents PRD, a novel framework for predicting multiple DDI labels by leveraging graph embedding. PRD utilizes a large-scale drug knowledge graph generated from diverse sources and embeds it with biomedical text into a shared low-dimensional space. Learned embeddings are then used for efficient DDI prediction through a link prediction process. Experiments on real-world datasets validate PRD's effectiveness, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Whatever Does Not Kill Deep Reinforcement Learning, Makes It Stronger
Abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been shown to be vulnerable to policy manipulation attacks via adversarial perturbations. This paper investigates the robustness and resilience of deep RL to training-time and test-time attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that Deep Q-Network (DQN) agents can recover and adapt to noncontiguous training-time attacks by adjusting their policies. The study also reveals that policies trained under adversarial perturbations exhibit greater robustness against test-time attacks.  The paper compares the performance of ε-greedy and parameter-space noise exploration methods in terms of resilience and robustness against adversarial perturbations.
label: AI

title: Towards Collaborative Conceptual Exploration
Abstract: Collaborative interactive learning environments are crucial in domains with high knowledge distribution. This paper presents a mathematical characterization of a collaborative learning group, a consortium, based on closure systems of attribute sets and attribute exploration algorithms. The paper introduces local experts for subdomains, capable of refuting or accepting queries within their respective closure systems. A consortial expert is then constructed, enabling collective responses to queries. The paper explores techniques for handling falsely accepted implications and combining counterexamples, providing initial insights into the decidability of consortium-based exploration. Applications in knowledge acquisition and collaborative ontology learning are highlighted.
label: AI

title: Multi-Objective Vehicle Routing Problem Applied to Large Scale Post Office Deliveries
Abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) in combinatorial optimization is a complex area with diverse optimization techniques, but real-world benchmarks for testing algorithms are limited. This paper presents an extensible real-world mail delivery benchmark for the VRP, embedded in a planar graph in 2D Euclidean space. The multi-objective problem involves up to 25 vehicles and 30,000 deliveries per day, modeling a generic day of mail delivery. The benchmark allows for comparing and validating optimization algorithms for routing problems and can be extended to model various scenarios.
label: AI

title: Interpretable Counting for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Visual question answering (VQA) faces significant challenges in counting objects within images. Existing VQA approaches rely on fixed-length representations or fractional counts from image sections. This paper proposes a novel approach that treats counting as a sequential decision process, forcing the model to make discrete object selections. The model learns interactions between objects to influence subsequent selections, resulting in intuitive and interpretable outputs. This method surpasses state-of-the-art architectures for VQA on multiple counting-related metrics.
label: AI

title: Obtaining Accurate Probabilistic Causal Inference by Post-Processing Calibration
Abstract: Accurately determining causal relationships from observational data is crucial in many scientific fields. This paper proposes a novel framework for deriving calibrated probabilities of causal connections, which are essential for guiding further research. The framework utilizes three components: (1) an approximate method to generate initial probability estimates, (2) a calibration training set containing known causal relationships, and (3) a calibration method for generating calibrated probabilities based on the initial estimates and training set.  A new calibration method based on a shallow neural network is introduced. Experiments on simulated data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the calibration, precision, and recall of causal edge predictions.
label: AI

title: Letter-Based Speech Recognition with Gated ConvNets
Abstract: Letter-based acoustic models trained in an end-to-end manner have gained traction in speech recognition, offering advantages over traditional phone-based approaches. This paper presents a letter-based speech recognition system utilizing a ConvNet acoustic model, incorporating Gated Linear Units and high dropout. The ConvNet maps audio sequences to their corresponding letter transcriptions via CTC or ASG. This system achieves performance comparable to the best existing letter-based systems on the WSJ benchmark and nears state-of-the-art performance on LibriSpeech.
label: AI

title: Rank Pruning for Dominance Queries in CP-Nets
Abstract: Conditional preference networks (CP-nets) graphically represent individual preferences over discrete variables. This paper introduces a novel method for quantifying preference for any outcome based on a CP-net representation. These preference values facilitate reasoning about user preferences, including ordering outcomes and improving the efficiency of outcome dominance testing. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method compared to existing techniques for enhancing dominance testing efficiency, even for CP-nets expressing indifference between variable values.
label: AI

title: Inverse Classification for Comparison-based Interpretability in Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of explaining classifier predictions in post-hoc interpretability when no information is available about the classifier or the processed data. It proposes an instance-based approach that identifies minimal changes needed to alter a prediction. Given a data point, the method finds a close neighbor classified differently, incorporating a sparsity constraint. This principle is implemented using observation generation in the Growing Spheres algorithm. Experimental results illustrate the relevance of this approach for gaining knowledge about the classifier.
label: AI

title: Taking Visual Motion Prediction To New Heightfields
Abstract: Despite the well-understood laws of Newtonian mechanics, modeling physical scenarios often requires manual equation development and parameter estimation. To leverage the approximation capabilities of AI in physics-related contexts, researchers have previously used neural networks to learn state transitions from simulation data. However, these approaches are not suitable for complex real-world scenarios. This work investigates whether neural networks can implicitly learn the physical states of real-world mechanical processes solely from visual data.  A recurrent neural network architecture is developed to model non-homogeneous environments and enable long-term physical extrapolation. The setup is evaluated on scenarios involving rolling balls on bowls of varying shapes and orientations, and on arbitrary heightfields, demonstrating significant improvements over existing methods in terms of accuracy and scenario complexity.
label: AI

title: Intelligent Device Discovery in the Internet of Things - Enabling the Robot Society
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, connecting billions of smart devices. To enable autonomous device discovery and service generation, a new Social-Aware and Distributed (SAND) scheme is proposed for efficient device discovery. SAND utilizes a novel device ranking criteria based on degree, social relationship diversity, clustering coefficient, and betweenness. This allows discovery requests to traverse critical devices at major network intersections, quickly reaching the desired target device. SAND facilitates self-organized computing groups, enabling autonomous social connections between IoT devices and the creation of novel applications and services.
label: AI

title: CSGNet: Neural Shape Parser for Constructive Solid Geometry
Abstract: This paper presents a neural architecture that takes a 2D or 3D shape as input and outputs a program that generates the shape. The program instructions are based on constructive solid geometry principles, utilizing boolean operations on recursively defined shape primitives. The proposed model uses a recurrent neural network for top-down shape parsing, offering significant speed advantages over bottom-up approaches. The model also surpasses existing state-of-the-art shape detection techniques and can be trained on novel datasets without ground-truth program annotations using policy gradient techniques.
label: AI

title: Learning and Transferring IDs Representation in E-commerce
Abstract: E-commerce relies heavily on machine intelligence techniques, particularly the representation of IDs like user, item, product, store, brand, and category IDs. Traditional encoding methods suffer from sparsity issues and cannot capture relationships between IDs. This paper proposes an embedding-based framework to learn and transfer ID representations. By leveraging item ID sequences from interactive sessions and structural connections between IDs, all types of IDs are embedded into a low-dimensional semantic space. These representations are utilized in four scenarios: (i) measuring item similarity, (ii) transferring from seen to unseen items, (iii) transferring across different domains, and (iv) transferring across different tasks. The approach is evaluated in the Hema App and demonstrates its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Federated Control with Hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a framework that combines hierarchical and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning to solve coordination problems among multiple agents using a semi-decentralized model. The framework introduces a meta-controller that guides communication between agent pairs, allowing agents to focus on communication with only one other agent at a time. This hierarchical decomposition enables efficient exploration and learning of policies that identify globally optimal solutions, even as the number of collaborating agents increases. Initial experimental results on a simulated distributed scheduling problem are promising.
label: AI

title: Fair Forests: Regularized Tree Induction to Minimize Model Bias
Abstract: Fairness in machine learning outputs has become a growing concern. This paper addresses the lack of fair decision tree and fair random forest algorithms, which are widely popular due to their interpretability, non-linearity, and ease of use. The paper proposes a new technique for inducing fair decision trees, called "Fair Forest." Fair Forest retains the benefits of tree-based approaches while providing improved accuracy and fairness compared to other alternatives, for both group fairness and individual fairness.  The paper also introduces new fairness measures that can handle multinomial and continuous attributes as well as regression problems. Finally, it presents a more robust evaluation procedure that considers the entire dataset instead of focusing solely on a specific protected attribute.
label: AI

title: Learning Intelligent Dialogs for Bounding Box Annotation
Abstract: This paper introduces Intelligent Annotation Dialogs for bounding box annotation. An agent is trained to automatically select a sequence of actions for a human annotator, aiming to minimize annotation time. The actions considered are box verification and manual box drawing. Two types of agents are explored: one based on predicting the probability of positive box verification, and the other based on reinforcement learning. The study demonstrates that (1) the agents learn efficient annotation strategies, adapting to image difficulty, desired box quality, and detector strength; (2) the resulting annotation dialogs accelerate annotation compared to manual drawing or verification alone; and (3) in a realistic scenario with iterative detector retraining, the agents evolve strategies that reflect the shifting trade-off between verification and drawing as the detector improves.
label: AI

title: Variable selection for Gaussian processes via sensitivity analysis of the posterior predictive distribution
Abstract: Variable selection for Gaussian process models is often performed using automatic relevance determination, which relies on the inverse length-scale parameter for variable relevance. This approach has limitations that prevent the selection of optimal input variables in terms of predictive performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes two novel variable selection methods that utilize predictions from a full model in the vicinity of training points. These methods rank variables based on their predictive relevance. Empirical results on synthetic and real-world data demonstrate improved variable selection compared to automatic relevance determination, in terms of variability and predictive performance.
label: AI

title: Improvements to Inference Compilation for Probabilistic Programming in Large-Scale Scientific Simulators
Abstract: Bayesian inference in probabilistic models implicitly defined by stochastic generative models of data presents challenges due to intractable likelihoods and non-differentiability. This paper extends previous work in "inference compilation," combining probabilistic programming and deep learning methods, to large-scale scientific simulators. A C++ based probabilistic programming library called CPProb is introduced. The successful application of CPProb with SHERPA, a large code-base in particle physics, highlights the technical innovations achieved and planned for this library.
label: AI

title: A Deep Policy Inference Q-Network for Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract: This paper introduces DPIQN, a deep policy inference Q-network for multi-agent systems with controllable agents, collaborators, and opponents. To address the challenge of modeling agents with varying strategies, DPIQN utilizes "policy features" learned from raw observations of collaborators and opponents by inferring their policies. These features are incorporated into DPIQN's deep Q-network, improving Q-value prediction for controllable agents.  An enhanced version, deep recurrent policy inference Q-network (DRPIQN), is proposed for handling partial observability.  Both DPIQN and DRPIQN are trained using an adaptive procedure that focuses on learning policy features and Q-values at different training phases. Experiments in a soccer game setting demonstrate the superior performance of DPIQN and DRPIQN compared to baseline models, particularly in competitive and collaborative scenarios with dynamically changing policies.
label: AI

title: Multiagent-based Participatory Urban Simulation through Inverse Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Multiagent-based participatory simulations are used in urban planning, utilizing the combination of domain knowledge and local knowledge. However, generating realistic agents for specific social phenomena poses a challenge. This paper introduces Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) to address this issue. IRL, successful in robotics, psychology, and machine learning, offers new possibilities for modeling human behavior. The paper discusses the potential and challenges associated with this new approach.
label: AI

title: Multi-task learning of time series and its application to the travel demand
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of modeling and predicting temporal events in the context of intelligent transportation systems. A multi-task learning framework is proposed to leverage information shared between different events. A support vector regression model is developed for joint learning of mutually dependent time series, extending previous work on classification to time series. The paper discusses the relatedness of observed time series, deploying dynamic time warping distance to identify groups of similar series. A common latent representation is inferred to align multiple time series, considering both time and scale warping. The models are tested on travel demand prediction in Nancy's public transport system, highlighting the benefits of multi-task learning.
label: AI

title: Reachable Set Computation and Safety Verification for Neural Networks with ReLU Activations
Abstract: Neural networks have gained widespread use in addressing complex real-world problems.  This paper focuses on ensuring the safety of neural networks, particularly for safety-critical applications, by addressing the output reachable set computation and safety verification problems for a class of neural networks using ReLU activation functions. A layer-by-layer approach is developed to compute the output reachable set, formulated as a set of manipulations for a union of polyhedra, which can be efficiently implemented using polyhedron computation tools. Based on these results, safety verification is performed by checking the intersection of unsafe regions with the computed output reachable set. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Geometrical Insights for Implicit Generative Modeling
Abstract: Learning algorithms for implicit generative models optimize various criteria to measure the difference between the data distribution and the implicit model distribution. This paper examines the geometries induced by these distances on the space of probability measures, revealing interesting differences. Notably, approximate global convergence guarantees are established for the 1-Wasserstein distance, even when the parametric generator has a nonconvex parametrization.
label: AI

title: Bit-Vector Model Counting using Statistical Estimation
Abstract: Approximate model counting for bit-vector SMT formulas, a generalization of #SAT, has numerous applications in probabilistic inference and quantitative information-flow security. This paper proposes an approach inspired by statistical estimation to continually refine a probabilistic estimate of the model count for a formula, maximizing information gained from each XOR-streamlined query. The approach is implemented as a wrapper around an SMT or SAT solver. Experimental results show faster performance compared to previous approaches using simpler refinement strategies. This technique also extends to floating-point constraints, demonstrated by an application to a vulnerability in differential privacy mechanisms.
label: AI

title: Towards an unanimous international regulatory body for responsible use of Artificial Intelligence [UIRB-AI]
Abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) present significant challenges for policymakers and legal frameworks. This paper examines the societal impact of AI, emphasizing the need for an Unanimous International Regulatory Body for AI (UIRB-AI). The paper explores the benefits and drawbacks of such an organization and proposes novel policies for its structure and operation. It aims to promote a win-win situation for everyone in society by fostering responsible AI development and deployment. |||

title: Context-aware Path Ranking for Knowledge Base Completion
Abstract: Knowledge base (KB) completion aims to infer missing facts from existing ones in a KB. Path ranking (PR) algorithms have gained significant attention in recent years as a method for KB completion. PR algorithms enumerate paths between entity pairs in a KB and use these paths as features to train a model for predicting missing facts. Due to their strong performance and high model interpretability, several PR methods have been proposed. However, most existing methods face scalability (high RAM consumption) and feature explosion (training on an exponentially large number of features) problems. This paper introduces a Context-aware Path Ranking (C-PR) algorithm to address these challenges by implementing a selective path exploration strategy. C-PR learns the global semantics of entities in the KB using word embedding and leverages this knowledge to enumerate contextually relevant paths using bidirectional random walk. Experimental results on three large KBs demonstrate that the path features (fewer in number) discovered by C-PR not only improve predictive performance but are also more interpretable than existing baselines.
label: AI

title: Pseudorehearsal in actor-critic agents with neural network function approximation
Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting poses a significant challenge in reinforcement learning. This study investigates the impact of pseudorehearsal on the performance of an actor-critic agent using neural-network function approximation. The agent was evaluated in a pole balancing task, and different pseudorehearsal approaches were compared. The results show that pseudorehearsal can effectively assist learning and mitigate forgetting.
label: AI

title: Tracking Cyber Adversaries with Adaptive Indicators of Compromise
Abstract: After a security breach, a forensics investigation often reveals network and host indicators of compromise (IOCs) that can be used to detect future attacks. However, adversaries constantly adapt their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), rendering existing IOCs ineffective. This paper addresses the problem of "Tracking the Known" (TTK) by proposing a framework for keeping IOCs, specifically regular expressions (regexes), up-to-date with a dynamic adversary. The framework employs a data-driven approach to self-adapt a model based on its own detection capabilities, enabling automated, cyclic tracking of the adversary. Initial experiments demonstrate that the true positive rate (TPR) of the adaptive solution degrades less significantly over time compared to a naive approach, suggesting that self-updating the model facilitates continued detection of adversaries. While the false positive rate (FPR) increases over time for the adaptive solution, the overall detection performance, measured by the area under the curve (AUC), remains comparable to the naive solution. This result implies that self-updating the model is beneficial for continuous detection of evolving adversaries.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning with Lung Segmentation and Bone Shadow Exclusion Techniques for Chest X-Ray Analysis of Lung Cancer
Abstract: Advances in computing, machine learning, and particularly deep learning have significantly impacted automatic disease detection from chest X-ray images (CXRs). This study explores the efficiency of lung segmentation and bone shadow exclusion techniques for analyzing 2D CXRs using deep learning, aiming to assist radiologists in identifying suspicious lesions and nodules in lung cancer patients. The training and validation were conducted on four datasets: the original JSRT dataset (#01), the BSE-JSRT dataset (JSRT without clavicle and rib shadows, #02), the original JSRT dataset after segmentation (#03), and the BSE-JSRT dataset after segmentation (#04). The results demonstrate the effectiveness and usefulness of the pre-processing techniques, even in a simplified configuration. Notably, the pre-processed dataset without bones (#02) exhibits significantly better accuracy and loss results compared to the other pre-processed datasets after lung segmentation (#02 and #03).
label: AI

title: An Ensemble Model with Ranking for Social Dialogue
Abstract: Open-domain social dialogue is a long-standing goal in artificial intelligence. The Amazon Alexa Prize challenge, where real customers rate systems developed by universities worldwide, presents an opportunity to advance this area. The goal of the challenge is to develop systems capable of engaging in coherent and engaging conversations with humans on popular topics for 20 minutes. This paper describes the Alexa Prize system "Alana," which combines rule-based and machine learning systems into an ensemble of bots. A contextual ranking mechanism is used to select a system response, which was trained on real user feedback received during the competition. The paper addresses the challenges of training a ranker on the noisy and sparse feedback obtained during the competition.
label: AI

title: Partial Labeled Gastric Tumor Segmentation via patch-based Reiterative Learning
Abstract: Gastric cancer is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally, and determining the extent of the cancer is a major hurdle in biomedical image analysis. This task is clinically significant and typically requires extensive microscopic assessment by pathologists. Recent advances in deep learning have achieved promising results in biomedical image segmentation, but rely on comprehensive annotation, which is labor-intensive due to the meticulous manual annotation required by pathologists. This paper presents a reiterative learning framework for training a network on partially annotated biomedical images, achieving superior performance without pre-trained models or further manual annotation. The proposed approach eliminates boundary errors associated with patch-based models through an overlapped region forecast algorithm. These techniques resulted in a mean intersection over union coefficient (IOU) of 0.883 and a mean accuracy of 91.09% on the partially labeled dataset, leading to victory in the 2017 China Big Data & Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competitions.
label: AI

title: Self-Supervised Damage-Avoiding Manipulation Strategy Optimization via Mental Simulation
Abstract: Everyday robotics face the challenge of autonomous product handling in applications such as logistics and retail, where unintended object motion during manipulation can cause damage. Traditionally, most approaches prioritize minimizing physical interaction with goods. This paper proposes a self-supervised learning approach that accounts for unintended object motion and learns damage-minimizing manipulation strategies. The approach involves a simulation-based planning method for generating an optimal manipulation sequence considering potential damage. These planned sequences are then generalized to new, unseen scenes using machine learning. The learned manipulation strategy is continuously refined in a self-supervised, simulation-in-the-loop optimization cycle during load-free periods, known as mental simulation. This strategy can be deployed in near-real time in an anytime fashion. The approach is validated in an industrial container-unloading scenario and a retail shelf-replenishment scenario.
label: AI

title: Intelligent Power Control for Spectrum Sharing in Cognitive Radios: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: This paper investigates spectrum sharing in a cognitive radio system consisting of a primary user and a secondary user operating in a non-cooperative manner. The primary user is assumed to update its transmit power based on a pre-defined power control policy. The secondary user lacks knowledge of the primary user's transmit power or power control strategy. The goal is to develop a learning-based power control method for the secondary user to share the common spectrum with the primary user. To assist the secondary user, sensor nodes are deployed to collect received signal strength information at various locations. The paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning-based method that enables the secondary user to intelligently adjust its transmit power. Through interaction with the primary user, both users can successfully transmit their data with the required quality of service. Experimental results demonstrate that the secondary user can efficiently interact with the primary user to reach a goal state (where both users can successfully transmit data) from any initial state within a few steps.
label: AI

title: Analysis of supervised and semi-supervised GrowCut applied to segmentation of masses in mammography images
Abstract: Breast cancer is a prevalent form of cancer worldwide, and mammography image analysis remains the most effective diagnostic method for early detection. Accurate tumor segmentation in digital mammography images is crucial for improving diagnosis capabilities and avoiding misdiagnosis. This paper evaluates the feasibility of using GrowCut for segmenting tumor regions and proposes two semi-supervised versions of GrowCut. The analysis was conducted using images from the Mini-MIAS mammography image database, comparing GrowCut segmentation to other techniques such as Region Growing, Active Contours, Random Walks, and Graph Cut. Experiments indicate that GrowCut consistently achieves better results for the analyzed metrics compared to other methods. Moreover, the proposed semi-supervised versions of GrowCut exhibit clinically satisfactory segmentation quality.
label: AI

title: Revisiting the Master-Slave Architecture in Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Many tasks in artificial intelligence require the collaboration of multiple agents. This paper explores deep reinforcement learning for multi-agent domains, revisiting the master-slave architecture to integrate both decentralized and centralized perspectives within a single framework. This hierarchical structure leverages the advantages of both perspectives. The paper highlights three key ingredients: composed action representation, learnable communication, and independent reasoning. By incorporating these elements into network designs, the proposed approach consistently outperforms competing methods in both synthetic experiments and challenging StarCraft micromanagement tasks.
label: AI

title: Block-diagonal Hessian-free Optimization for Training Neural Networks
Abstract: Second-order methods for neural network optimization offer advantages over first-order gradient descent methods, including better scaling to large mini-batch sizes and fewer updates required for convergence. However, their practical application in deep learning is limited due to high computational cost and the need for model-dependent algorithmic variations. This paper introduces a variant of the Hessian-free method that leverages a block-diagonal approximation of the generalized Gauss-Newton matrix. This method computes the curvature approximation matrix only for pairs of parameters within the same layer or block of the neural network, performing conjugate gradient updates independently for each block. Experiments on deep autoencoders, deep convolutional networks, and multilayer LSTMs demonstrate improved convergence and generalization compared to the original Hessian-free approach and the Adam method.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical and Interpretable Skill Acquisition in Multi-task Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Learning policies for complex tasks requiring multiple skills is a significant challenge in reinforcement learning (RL). This paper proposes a novel framework for efficient multi-task reinforcement learning that trains agents to employ hierarchical policies. These policies decide when to use previously learned policies and when to acquire new skills, enabling agents to continuously learn new skills during training. Each learned task is associated with a human language description, providing human-interpretable descriptions of the agent's choices. To assist the agent in learning complex temporal dependencies required for hierarchical policies, a stochastic temporal grammar is introduced to modulate when to rely on previous skills and when to execute new skills. The approach is validated on Minecraft games designed to test the ability to reuse previously learned skills while simultaneously acquiring new ones.

title: Probabilistic Learning of Torque Controllers from Kinematic and Force Constraints
Abstract: When learning skills from demonstrations, selecting the appropriate task representation (operational or configuration space) is often necessary. This paper proposes a probabilistic approach for simultaneously learning and synthesizing torque control commands that consider task space, joint space, and force constraints. Different torque controllers are considered, and their relevance is learned probabilistically from demonstrations. This information is used to combine controllers by exploiting the properties of Gaussian distributions, generating torque commands that satisfy the task's key features. The approach is validated in two experimental scenarios using 7-DoF torque-controlled manipulators, demonstrating the effectiveness of using different controllers for complex tasks.

title: Cognitive Database: A Step towards Endowing Relational Databases with Artificial Intelligence Capabilities
Abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Databases, a novel approach for seamlessly integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities into relational databases. The design involves viewing structured data as meaningful unstructured text and using this text to build an unsupervised neural network model using word embedding. This model captures hidden relationships between database tokens. For each token, the model includes a vector encoding contextual semantic relationships. The word embedding model is integrated into existing SQL query infrastructure, enabling a new class of SQL-based analytics queries called cognitive intelligence (CI) queries. CI queries leverage the model vectors to enable complex queries such as semantic matching, inductive reasoning (analogies), predictive queries using entities not present in the database, and utilizing external knowledge. The paper demonstrates the unique capabilities of Cognitive Databases using an Apache Spark-based prototype for executing inductive reasoning CI queries on a multi-modal database containing text and images. The system exemplifies using AI functionality to enhance relational databases with capabilities previously difficult to implement.

title: Scale-invariant temporal history (SITH): optimal slicing of the past in an uncertain world
Abstract: Both the human brain and any general artificial intelligence (AI) require a representation of the past to predict the future. However, storing all experiences perfectly is not feasible. Many applications, including reward prediction in reinforcement learning, use a buffer to retain recently active features of experience. While this approach has been successful, this paper demonstrates that fixed-length buffers make Deep Q-learning Networks (DQNs) vulnerable to changes in the scale over which information is learned. To address this, the paper draws inspiration from psychology and neuroscience, suggesting that the brain maintains a compressed representation of the past. The paper introduces a neurally-plausible, scale-free memory representation called Scale-Invariant Temporal History (SITH) for use with artificial agents. This representation covers a vast period of time by sacrificing temporal accuracy for events further in the past. The utility of SITH is demonstrated by comparing the performance of agents using SITH, buffer, and exponential decay representations in learning to play video games of varying complexity. SITH exhibits better learning performance by storing information for longer timescales than a fixed-size buffer and representing this information more clearly than a set of exponentially decayed features. The paper concludes by discussing how SITH, along with other human-inspired cognitive models, could improve reinforcement and machine learning algorithms.

title: Machine Learning for Vehicular Networks
Abstract: Vehicular networks are expected to enhance safety, sustainability, and efficiency in daily vehicular operations, paving the way for autonomous driving in the 5G era. Machine learning, a crucial branch of artificial intelligence, has been applied to wireless networks, providing a data-driven approach to solving traditionally challenging problems. This article reviews recent advances in applying machine learning to vehicular networks, highlighting its potential in this emerging field. After a brief overview of machine learning concepts, the paper presents application examples of machine learning in addressing problems within vehicular networks. Finally, the paper discusses and emphasizes open research questions requiring further investigation.

title: On Data-Dependent Random Features for Improved Generalization in Supervised Learning
Abstract: The randomized-feature approach has proven effective in large-scale kernel approximation and supervised learning. The distribution from which random features are drawn influences the number of features required for efficient learning. Recent research has shown that data-dependent randomization improves performance in terms of required random features. This paper focuses on the randomized-feature approach in supervised learning for achieving good generalizability. It introduces the Energy-based Exploration of Random Features (EERF) algorithm, which employs a data-dependent score function to explore potential features and exploit promising regions. The paper proves that the proposed score function, with high probability, recovers the spectrum of the best fit within the model class. Empirical results on several benchmark datasets validate that EERF requires fewer random features to achieve a specific generalization error compared to state-of-the-art methods, while introducing negligible pre-processing overhead. EERF is easy to implement and requires no additional tuning parameters.

title: Column Generation for Interaction Coverage in Combinatorial Software Testing
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel column generation framework for combinatorial software testing, combining mathematical programming and constraint programming in a hybrid decomposition to generate covering arrays. This approach allows generating parameterized test cases with coverage guarantees between parameter interactions of a given application. Compared to exhaustive testing, combinatorial test case generation significantly reduces the number of tests required. The proposed column generation algorithm is generic and can handle mixed coverage arrays over heterogeneous alphabets. The algorithm is implemented as a cloud service and was recognized as one of the top five winners in Oracle's company-wide cloud application challenge. This service assists software developers from various product teams in their testing efforts while exposing declarative constraint models and hybrid optimization techniques to a broader audience.

title: The NarrativeQA Reading Comprehension Challenge
Abstract: Reading comprehension (RC) requires integrating information and reasoning about events, entities, and their relationships across an entire document, unlike information retrieval. Question answering is commonly used to assess RC abilities in both artificial agents and children learning to read. However, existing RC datasets and tasks primarily rely on superficial information (e.g., local context similarity or global term frequency), failing to test the essential integrative aspect of RC. To encourage progress in deeper language comprehension, this paper presents a new dataset and set of tasks where readers must answer questions about stories by reading entire books or movie scripts. These tasks are designed to require understanding the underlying narrative rather than shallow pattern matching or salience. While humans solve these tasks easily, standard RC models struggle. The paper provides an analysis of the dataset and the challenges it presents.

title: The Merits of Sharing a Ride
Abstract: The culture of sharing over ownership is rapidly increasing, particularly in transportation. Ride-sharing concepts like carpooling and ridesharing have gained popularity. Real-time passenger matching is essential for the efficiency of any ridesharing system. This paper models ridesharing as an online matching problem on general graphs, assuming passengers use shared taxis instead of private cars. It proposes an optimization algorithm to solve this problem, calculating the optimal waiting time for passengers upon arrival. This leads to a matching solution that minimizes overall overheads while maximizing partnerships. To evaluate the algorithm's behavior, real-life NYC taxi data was used. The results demonstrate a significant reduction in overall overheads. |||

title: Any-gram Kernels for Sentence Classification: A Sentiment Analysis Case Study
Abstract: Any-gram kernels offer a flexible and efficient method for utilizing bag-of-n-gram features in text-based learning tasks. These kernels are also compatible with word embeddings, allowing for the consideration of word similarities.  We propose a new approach to any-gram kernels that is independent of tree kernels and achieves greater efficiency. Additionally, we propose a more effective way to leverage word embeddings compared to the original any-gram formulation.  When applied to sentiment classification, our new approach demonstrates significantly improved performance.

title: Mining Smart Card Data for Travelers' Mini Activities
Abstract: In the domain of public transport modeling and simulation, we tackle the problem of discrepancies between simulated and observed transit trips. We identify a weakness in current travel demand modeling processes, where generated trips tend to be overly optimistic and fail to reflect real passenger choices. We introduce the concept of "mini activities" that travelers engage in during trips, which can explain these discrepancies. We propose extracting these mini activities from smart card data and integrating them into simulated trips. Our approach utilizes two sources of information: trip history and trip planner recommendations. For a given travel demand, we construct a Markov chain over the trip collection and apply the Monte Carlo Markov Chain algorithm to integrate mini activities in a way that aligns selected characteristics with desired distributions. Our method is tested in various settings using passenger trip data from Nancy, France. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial reduction in the mismatch between simulated and observed trips.
