title: Safe Policy Improvement with Baseline Bootstrapping
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of Safe Policy Improvement (SPI) in Batch Reinforcement Learning (Batch RL), aiming to train a policy from a fixed dataset, without direct access to the true environment, that guarantees performance at least as good as the baseline policy used to collect the data. Our approach, called SPI with Baseline Bootstrapping (SPIBB), draws inspiration from the "knows-what-it-knows" paradigm by bootstrapping the trained policy with the baseline when uncertainty is high. Our first algorithm, $\Pi_b$-SPIBB, comes with theoretical SPI guarantees. We also implement a variant, $\Pi_{\leq b}$-SPIBB, that proves even more efficient in practice. We evaluate our algorithms in a motivational stochastic gridworld domain and further demonstrate, through randomly generated MDPs, the superiority of SPIBB over existing algorithms in terms of both safety and mean performance. Finally, we implement a model-free version of SPIBB and showcase its benefits on a navigation task using a deep RL implementation called SPIBB-DQN. To the best of our knowledge, SPIBB-DQN is the first RL algorithm utilizing a neural network representation capable of efficient and reliable training from batch data, without any interaction with the environment.

title: Large-Scale Vandalism Detection with Linear Classifiers - The Conkerberry Vandalism Detector at WSDM Cup 2017
Abstract: Many modern artificial intelligence systems rely on knowledge bases to enrich the information they process.  These knowledge bases are often difficult to obtain and are therefore crowdsourced, making them readily available for edits and additions from internet users.  However, they can be vulnerable to vandalism, where individuals introduce inaccurate or offensive information.  This poses a significant challenge for systems that rely on these knowledge bases, as they require reliable information to make accurate inferences.  Wikidata, a prominent knowledge base, has taken steps to combat vandalism by challenging participants in the WSDM Cup 2017 to build a model for detecting untrustworthy edits.  This paper presents the second-place solution, demonstrating that simple linear classification can achieve competitive performance. Our approach achieves an AU ROC of 0.938 on the test data, surpassing other approaches while also being significantly faster. The solution is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Continual Prediction of Notification Attendance with Classical and Deep Network Approaches
Abstract: We explore the potential of mobile usage patterns to predict, at the moment of posting, whether a notification will be clicked within the next 10 minutes. Our analysis utilizes a dataset comprising detailed mobile phone usage logs from 279 users who received 446,268 notifications from various apps over a five-week period.  Beyond employing traditional gradient-boosted trees, we demonstrate the feasibility of making continual predictions using a recurrent neural network (RNN). Both approaches achieve a similar AUC of approximately 0.7 on unseen users, with a possible operation point of 50% sensitivity and 80% specificity when considering all notification types (a 40% increase compared to a probabilistic baseline). These findings enable automatic, intelligent handling of mobile phone notifications without requiring user feedback or personalization. Furthermore, they highlight the ability to forgo feature extraction by employing RNNs for continual predictions directly on mobile usage logs. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that leverages mobile sensor data for continual, context-aware predictions of interruptibility using deep neural networks.

title: Heinrich Behmann's Contributions to Second-Order Quantifier Elimination from the View of Computational Logic
Abstract: For relational monadic formulas (the Löwenheim class), second-order quantifier elimination, closely related to the computation of uniform interpolants, projection, and forgetting (operations currently receiving significant attention in knowledge processing), always succeeds. The decidability proof for this class, originally established by Heinrich Behmann in 1922, explicitly proceeds through elimination using equivalence-preserving formula rewriting. This paper provides a detailed reconstruction of Behmann's results, discussing related issues relevant in the context of modern approaches to second-order quantifier elimination in computational logic. Additionally, we offer an extensive documentation of Behmann's bequest, including letters and manuscripts related to second-order quantifier elimination, providing a commented register and English abstracts of the German sources with a focus on technical material. In the late 1920s, Behmann attempted to develop an elimination-based decision method for formulas with predicates of arity greater than one.  His manuscripts and correspondence with Wilhelm Ackermann reveal technical aspects that remain relevant today and offer insights into the genesis of Ackermann's landmark paper "Untersuchungen über das Eliminationsproblem der mathematischen Logik" from 1935, which laid the foundation for the two prevailing modern approaches to second-order quantifier elimination.

title: Electrifying the Urban Taxi Fleet: A Data-driven Approach
Abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven approach for electrifying the urban taxi fleet. Leveraging real-time vehicle trajectory data gathered from 39,053 taxis in Beijing, we conduct time-series simulations to gain insights into both the configuration of an electric taxi fleet and dispatching strategies. Our simulation framework accurately models electric vehicle charging behavior considering factors such as time window, charging demand, and availability of unoccupied chargers. It further incorporates a centralized and intelligent fleet dispatching platform capable of handling taxi service requests and coordinating electric taxis' recharging in real-time. To address the challenges of limited driving range and long battery-recharging time on operational efficiency, the dispatching platform integrates information from customers, taxi drivers, and charging stations. It adopts a rule-based approach to achieve multiple objectives, including minimizing taxi customers' average waiting time, maximizing the taxi demand fill rate, and ensuring income equity among taxi drivers.  While this study focuses on a specific type of fleet in one city, the methodological framework is readily applicable to other cities and fleet types with similar data availability.

title: Learning Representations from Road Network for End-to-End Urban Growth Simulation
Abstract: Experience has shown that urban growth is heavily reliant on transportation networks. In megacities, these networks significantly influence population movement and housing development.  Therefore, transportation network data is crucial for accurate urban growth prediction systems. Previous research has utilized manually derived distance-based features based on road networks to build models for urban growth. However, the manual feature engineering process is often non-generic and laborious.  This paper proposes a method to integrate road network data into an existing rule-based end-to-end framework without requiring manual feature engineering. Our approach utilizes recurrent neural networks to represent road networks in a structured manner that can be seamlessly integrated into the previously proposed end-to-end framework.  This integration significantly enhances the performance of the existing rule-based framework, resulting in improvements in the Figure of Merit, Producer's accuracy, User's accuracy, and overall accuracy.

title: MovieGraphs: Towards Understanding Human-Centric Situations from Videos
Abstract: The growing interest in artificial intelligence for building socially intelligent robots necessitates machines capable of "reading" human emotions, motivations, and other factors that influence behavior. To advance this goal, we introduce a novel dataset called MovieGraphs, which provides detailed, graph-based annotations of social situations depicted in movie clips.  Each graph comprises multiple node types, capturing the individuals present in the clip, their emotional and physical attributes, their relationships (e.g., parent/child), and their interactions. Most interactions are associated with topics that provide further details, and reasons that explain motivations for actions.  Additionally, most interactions and many attributes are grounded in the video with time stamps. We conduct a thorough analysis of our dataset, revealing interesting common-sense correlations between different social aspects of scenes and across scenes over time.  We propose a method for querying videos and text with graphs, demonstrating that: 1) our graphs contain rich and sufficient information to summarize and localize each scene; and 2) subgraphs enable us to describe situations at an abstract level and retrieve multiple semantically relevant situations. We also propose methods for understanding interactions through ordering and reasoning. MovieGraphs is the first benchmark specifically focused on inferred properties of human-centric situations, opening exciting avenues for the development of socially-intelligent AI agents.

title: Game-Theoretic Electric Vehicle Charging Management Resilient to Non-Ideal User Behavior
Abstract: This paper examines an electric vehicle (EV) charging competition among EV aggregators that coordinate EV charging, considering potential non-ideal actions of the aggregators.  In the coordinated EV charging strategy presented, each aggregator determines EV charging start times and energy profiles to minimize overall charging costs while accounting for the actions of neighboring aggregators. The competitive interactions among aggregators are modeled using a two-stage non-cooperative game.  We then analyze the game under prospect theory to examine the impact of non-ideal actions, where aggregators subjectively evaluate their opponents' actions when selecting EV charging start times.  Our findings demonstrate that non-cooperative interactions among aggregators lead to a subgame perfect $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium, regardless of whether aggregators exhibit ideal or non-ideal actions. A case study highlights the significant resilience of the coordinated EV charging strategy's benefits, in terms of energy cost savings and peak-to-average ratio reductions, to non-ideal actions of the aggregators.

title: Towards the Augmented Pathologist: Challenges of Explainable-AI in Digital Pathology
Abstract: Digital pathology stands as a promising field within diagnostic medicine and a hot topic for fundamental research.  It transcends the simple digitization of histopathological slides, offering a powerful tool for advancing medical knowledge and care.  By integrating diverse data sources, including images, patient records, and omics data, and leveraging advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning, digital pathology makes novel information accessible and quantifiable to human experts, surpassing the limitations of current medical settings. The overarching goal is to achieve a level of usable intelligence capable of understanding data in the context of application tasks, ensuring that machine decisions are transparent, interpretable, and explainable.  Building an "augmented pathologist" requires an integrated approach: while machine learning algorithms often require vast training datasets, human experts typically work with limited data points.  Interestingly, humans can learn from these few examples and effortlessly interpret complex patterns.  Therefore, the ultimate objective is to combine the capabilities of artificial and human intelligence, finding a balance that enables what neither could achieve alone. This has the potential to elevate the quality of education, diagnosis, prognosis, and prediction of cancer and other diseases. This paper identifies several research challenges that require concerted and integrated efforts to pave the way towards the augmented pathologist.

title: Parallel Complexity of Forward and Backward Propagation
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that forward and backward propagation can be formulated as the solution to lower and upper triangular systems of equations. For standard feedforward (FNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), these triangular systems are always block bi-diagonal, while for a general computation graph (directed acyclic graph), they may exhibit a more complex triangular sparsity pattern. We discuss direct and iterative parallel algorithms that can be applied to solve these systems, interpreting them as different approaches to model parallelism. Furthermore, we show that for FNNs and RNNs with $k$ layers and $\tau$ time steps, backward propagation can be parallelized in O($\log k$) and O($\log k \log \tau$) steps, respectively.  Finally, we outline a generalization of this technique using Jacobians that potentially enables the handling of arbitrary layers.

title: ES Is More Than Just a Traditional Finite-Difference Approximator
Abstract: An evolution strategy (ES) variant, based on a simplification of a natural evolution strategy, has garnered recent attention due to its surprisingly strong performance in challenging deep reinforcement learning domains. This ES seeks neural network parameters by generating perturbations to the current parameter set, evaluating their performance, and moving in the direction of higher reward.  Its resemblance to a traditional finite-difference approximation of the reward gradient can lead to confusion. However, this ES optimizes for a different gradient than just reward; it optimizes for the average reward of the entire population, seeking parameters robust to perturbation. This distinction can steer ES toward distinct areas of the search space compared to gradient descent, potentially leading to networks with different properties.  This unique robustness-seeking property and its optimization implications are demonstrated in several domains, including humanoid locomotion, where networks trained with policy gradient-based reinforcement learning exhibit significantly less robustness to parameter perturbation compared to ES-based policies solving the same task.  While the implications of such robustness and robustness-seeking remain a subject of further investigation, this work primarily highlights these differences and their potential significance.

title: Safe Mutations for Deep and Recurrent Neural Networks through Output Gradients
Abstract: Neuroevolution, the process of evolving neural networks, has a proven track record across various domains, from reinforcement learning to artificial life. However, its application to large, deep neural networks is uncommon. A primary reason is that while random mutation generally works well in low dimensions, a random perturbation of thousands or millions of weights is likely to disrupt existing functionality, providing no learning signal even if some individual weight changes were beneficial. This paper proposes a solution by introducing a family of safe mutation (SM) operators that aim, within the mutation operator itself, to find a degree of change that minimally alters network behavior while facilitating exploration. Importantly, these SM operators do not require additional interactions with the environment. The most effective SM variant capitalizes on the intriguing opportunity to scale the degree of mutation of each individual weight according to the network's output sensitivity to that weight. This requires computing the gradient of outputs with respect to the weights (instead of the gradient of error, as in conventional deep learning). This safe mutation through gradients (SM-G) operator dramatically enhances the ability of a simple genetic algorithm-based neuroevolution method to find solutions in high-dimensional domains that require deep and/or recurrent neural networks (which tend to be particularly susceptible to mutation). These domains include tasks that involve processing raw pixels. By improving the ability to evolve deep neural networks, this new safer approach to mutation expands the scope of domains amenable to neuroevolution.

title: Improving Exploration in Evolution Strategies for Deep Reinforcement Learning via a Population of Novelty-Seeking Agents
Abstract: Evolution strategies (ES) are a family of black-box optimization algorithms that can train deep neural networks with comparable effectiveness to Q-learning and policy gradient methods on challenging deep reinforcement learning (RL) problems. However, ES offers significantly faster training times (e.g., hours vs. days) due to its superior parallelizability. Many RL problems require directed exploration, particularly when reward functions are sparse or deceptive (containing local optima).  The challenge lies in promoting such exploration within ES. This paper demonstrates that algorithms designed to encourage directed exploration in small-scale evolved neural networks through populations of exploring agents, specifically novelty search (NS) and quality diversity (QD) algorithms, can be effectively hybridized with ES to enhance its performance on sparse or deceptive deep RL tasks while retaining scalability. Our experiments confirm that the resulting new algorithms, NS-ES and two QD algorithms, NSR-ES and NSRA-ES, effectively avoid local optima encountered by ES, achieving superior performance on Atari and simulated robots learning to navigate a deceptive trap. This paper introduces a family of fast, scalable algorithms for reinforcement learning capable of directed exploration. It also adds this new family of exploration algorithms to the RL toolbox, raising the intriguing possibility that analogous algorithms with multiple simultaneous exploration paths might also synergize well with existing RL algorithms beyond ES.

title: Nonparametric Inference for Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
Abstract: Our goal is to learn low-dimensional and highly interpretable latent representations. The Gaussian Process Latent Variable Model (GP-LVM) possesses these characteristics, offering complementary strengths and weaknesses to the Variational Autoencoder (VAE). The GP-LVM provides interpretable low-dimensional latent representations, while the VAE excels in handling large datasets and utilizing non-Gaussian likelihoods.  This paper proposes a novel approach that combines the benefits of both models.  We introduce a new approximate inference scheme inspired by the GP-LVM and the VAE.  Our experimental results demonstrate that this approximation allows for an arbitrarily large generative bottleneck (Z) in the VAE without compromising the interpretability of the representation. This enables reconstruction quality to be unlimited by Z while simultaneously allowing for the use of a low-dimensional space for both ancestral sampling and reasoning about the embedded data.

title: 'Indifference' methods for managing agent rewards
Abstract: "Indifference" refers to a class of methods used to control reward-based agents. Indifference techniques aim to achieve one or more of three distinct goals: rewards dependent on specific events (without motivating the agent to manipulate the probability of those events), effective disbelief (where agents behave as if certain events could never happen), and seamless transition between reward functions (with the agent acting as if the change is unanticipated). This paper presents several methods for achieving these goals in the Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) setting, detailing their uses, strengths, and requirements. These control methods function even when the agent's reward implications are not fully understood.

title: Automated flow for compressing convolution neural networks for efficient edge-computation with FPGA
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are the current state-of-the-art for computer vision tasks. Their large size typically necessitates execution on clusters of CPUs or GPUs. However, power requirements and cost budgets can hinder the adoption of CNNs for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Recent research highlights that CNNs exhibit significant redundancy in their structure and can be quantized to lower bit-width parameters and activations while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Low bit-width and particularly single bit-width (binary) CNNs are well-suited for mobile applications based on FPGA implementation due to the bitwise logic operations involved. Furthermore, the transition to lower bit-widths opens up new avenues for performance optimizations and model improvements. This paper presents an automated flow from trained TensorFlow models to FPGA system-on-chip implementation of binarized CNNs. This flow involves quantization of model parameters and activations, generation of network and model in embedded-C, followed by automatic generation of the FPGA accelerator for binary convolutions.  We demonstrate the automated flow through the implementation of binarized "YOLOV2" on the low-cost, low-power Cyclone-V FPGA device. Experiments on object detection using binarized YOLOV2 demonstrate significant performance gains in terms of model size and inference speed on FPGA compared to CPU and mobile CPU platforms. Moreover, the entire automated flow from trained models to FPGA synthesis can be completed within one hour.

title: Visual Explanations from Hadamard Product in Multimodal Deep Networks
Abstract: Visualizing the learned representations of models provides valuable insights into the underlying principles of learning.  Attentional models in prior works have utilized learned weights to visualize attended regions within images or text, confirming their intended mechanism. Kim et al. (2016) demonstrated that the Hadamard product in multimodal deep networks, commonly used in visual question answering tasks, implicitly performs an attentional mechanism for visual inputs. This work extends their findings to show that the Hadamard product in multimodal deep networks performs attentional mechanisms for both visual and textual inputs simultaneously using a proposed gradient-based visualization technique.  The attentional effect of the Hadamard product is visualized for both visual and textual inputs by analyzing the two inputs and the output of the Hadamard product using the proposed method.  These results are compared with the learned attentional weights of a visual question answering model.

title: Towards a Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Tower Line Wars
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed significant breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, particularly in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), with notable successes in playing and winning advanced computer games.  Anticipation is growing that DRL will play a pivotal role when the first AI surpasses human capabilities in complex game strategies required to defeat professional Real-Time Strategy (RTS) players. To enable this advancement, a game environment tailored to AI research, especially DRL, is necessary.  While existing game environments exist, they often fall short: some are overly simplistic (e.g., Atari 2600), while others are excessively complex (e.g., Starcraft II from Blizzard Entertainment). We propose a game environment that bridges this gap, specifically targeting DRL algorithm research.  The environment is a variant of Tower Line Wars from Warcraft III, Blizzard Entertainment.  As a proof of concept demonstrating the environment's suitability for DRL algorithms, we propose and apply a Deep Q-Reinforcement architecture. This architecture simplifies the state space, making it compatible with Q-learning and enhancing performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods.  Our experiments show that the proposed architecture learns to play the environment effectively, achieving a 33% improvement over standard Deep Q-learning, thus validating the usefulness of the game environment. |||

title: Organic Visualization of Document Evolution
Abstract: Recent advancements in data collection have provided access to fine-grained records of document writing processes, down to the keystroke level. This has opened new avenues for research into the evolution of document creation. To leverage this data effectively, we propose a data structure capable of capturing a document's detailed history and an intuitive visualization that acts as an interface for accessing this information. Through a pilot study involving student-written documents at a public university, we evaluate a proof-of-concept implementation of our system. Our findings are encouraging, revealing insights into common writing strategies, local editing patterns, and the hierarchical structure of the final text.

title: SchNet - a deep learning architecture for molecules and materials
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized artificial intelligence, impacting fields ranging from web and text search to speech recognition and bioinformatics. Its influence is also growing in chemical physics. Machine learning, particularly deep learning, is well-suited for representing quantum-mechanical interactions, enabling the modeling of nonlinear potential-energy surfaces and enhanced exploration of chemical compound space. We introduce SchNet, a deep learning architecture specifically designed to model atomistic systems by utilizing continuous-filter convolutional layers. SchNet demonstrates remarkable accuracy in predicting various properties across chemical space for molecules and materials, learning chemically plausible embeddings of atom types across the periodic table. Moreover, we utilize SchNet to predict potential-energy surfaces and energy-conserving force fields for molecular dynamics simulations of small molecules, conducting an exemplary study of the quantum-mechanical properties of C20-fullerene. This study would be infeasible with traditional ab initio molecular dynamics methods.

title: Efficient B-mode Ultrasound Image Reconstruction from Sub-sampled RF Data using Deep Learning
Abstract: The demand for high-quality ultrasound imaging in portable, three-dimensional, and ultra-fast systems is increasing. However, limited radio-frequency (RF) measurements due to sub-sampling of receiver (Rx) or transmit (Xmit) events pose a challenge, resulting in sidelobe artifacts and blurry images with reduced contrast. While compressed sensing approaches offer solutions, they often require hardware modifications or computationally expensive algorithms, yielding limited quality improvements. To address this, we propose a novel deep learning approach that directly interpolates missing RF data by leveraging redundancy in the Rx-Xmit plane. Extensive experimental results using sub-sampled RF data from a multi-line acquisition B-mode system demonstrate that our method effectively reduces data rate without compromising image quality.

title: Deep Learning for Distant Speech Recognition
Abstract: Deep learning is a cutting-edge technology widely recognized as a promising path towards achieving higher levels of artificial intelligence. One of its notable achievements is the development of computers capable of understanding speech, a crucial step towards intelligent machines. Despite significant efforts over the past decades, natural and robust human-machine speech interaction remains elusive, especially when users interact with distant microphones in noisy and reverberant environments. These disturbances severely impair the intelligibility of speech signals, making Distant Speech Recognition (DSR) a major challenge in the field. This thesis addresses the DSR scenario and presents novel techniques, architectures, and algorithms to enhance the robustness of distant-talking acoustic models. We delve into methodologies for realistic data contamination, focusing on DNN training with simulated data. We then explore approaches for better leveraging speech contexts, proposing original methods for both feed-forward and recurrent neural networks. Finally, inspired by the notion that cooperation across different DNNs could be the key to mitigating the detrimental effects of noise and reverberation, we propose a novel deep learning paradigm called network of deep neural networks. The analysis of these original concepts is grounded in extensive experimental validations conducted on both real and simulated data, considering various corpora, microphone configurations, environments, noisy conditions, and Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) tasks.

title: A Spectral Approach for the Design of Experiments: Design, Analysis and Algorithms
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing high-quality space-filling sample designs. We introduce a new technique to quantify the space-filling property, enabling optimal trade-off between uniformity and randomness in designs across arbitrary dimensions. We establish a connection between our proposed metric (defined in the spatial domain) and the objective measure of design performance (defined in the spectral domain). This connection serves as an analytic framework for evaluating the qualitative properties of space-filling designs in general. Leveraging insights from this spatial-spectral analysis, we derive the notion of optimal space-filling designs, termed space-filling spectral designs. Furthermore, we propose an efficient estimator to evaluate the space-filling properties of sample designs in arbitrary dimensions and utilize it to develop an optimization framework for generating high-quality space-filling designs. We conduct a detailed performance comparison on two diverse applications in 2 to 6 dimensions: image reconstruction and surrogate modeling on benchmark optimization functions and an inertial confinement fusion (ICF) simulation code. Our results demonstrate that the proposed spectral designs significantly outperform existing approaches, particularly in higher dimensions.

title: StackInsights: Cognitive Learning for Hybrid Cloud Readiness
Abstract: Hybrid cloud is an integrated cloud computing environment combining public cloud, private cloud, and on-premise traditional IT infrastructures. Workload awareness, encompassing a comprehensive understanding of each individual workload, is crucial for effective hybrid cloud implementation. While accurately assessing workload suitability for on-premise deployment versus cloud migration is critical, traditional methods often rely on rule or policy-based approaches. This paper introduces StackInsights, a novel cognitive system designed to automatically analyze and predict the cloud readiness of workloads for an enterprise. Our system leverages critical metrics across the entire stack: infrastructure metrics, data relevance metrics, and application taxonomy. These metrics enable the identification of workloads with characteristics such as low sensitivity to business security, criticality, and compliance, as well as low response time requirements and access patterns. Since data relevance metrics require intrusive and in-depth scanning of storage object content, a machine learning model is employed to perform business relevance classification by learning from meta-level metrics across the stack. Compared to traditional methods, StackInsights significantly reduces the total time for hybrid cloud readiness assessment by orders of magnitude.

title: Using Machine Learning to Enhance Vehicles Traffic in ATN (PRT) Systems
Abstract: This paper explores new techniques to enhance Automated Transit Networks (ATN, previously known as Personal Rapid Transit - PRT) using Artificial Intelligence tools. The primary focus is on improving cooperation among autonomous modules using negotiation protocols within the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm. One key objective is to increase ATN system throughput by optimizing autonomous vehicle collaboration. Machine learning (ML) is utilized to refine algorithms designed by human programmers, leveraging "existing controls" representing near-optimal solutions. We construct refinement models to more accurately correlate a system's dynamics with its performance. A pivotal mechanism influencing ATN performance is Empty Vehicle Management (EVM). Human-programmed algorithms are employed, including calling empty vehicles for waiting passengers and balancing based on reallocation of empty vehicles to achieve better regularity in their distribution. This paper investigates how ML can be applied to improve these algorithms, tailoring individual behavioral policies to current conditions. The use of ML is possible due to the algorithmic reliance on a set of parameters, including weights and thresholds that can be tuned to enhance decision-making regarding the movement of empty vehicles across the track.
label: AI

title: Train Once, Test Anywhere: Zero-Shot Learning for Text Classification
Abstract: Zero-shot Learners are models capable of predicting unseen classes. This work proposes a Zero-shot Learning approach for text categorization. Our method involves training a model on a large corpus of sentences to learn the relationship between a sentence and its corresponding tag embedding. This learned relationship enables the model to generalize to unseen sentences, tags, and even new datasets, provided they can be mapped to the same embedding space. The model learns to predict whether a given sentence is related to a tag or not, unlike other classifiers that classify sentences into predefined classes. We propose three distinct neural networks for this task and report their accuracy on the test set used for training, as well as two other standard datasets without retraining. Our results demonstrate that our models effectively generalize across new, unseen classes in both cases. Although the models do not achieve the accuracy of state-of-the-art supervised models, they represent a significant step towards general intelligence in natural language processing.

title: An Artificial Neural Network Architecture Based on Context Transformations in Cortical Minicolumns
Abstract: Cortical minicolumns are considered a fundamental unit of cortical organization. Their function remains an area of ongoing research and is not adequately reflected in the architecture of modern artificial intelligence algorithms. We propose a function for cortical minicolumns and describe its implications. This proposal allows for the construction of a novel architecture, distinct from convolutional neural networks, which we test on the MNIST dataset, achieving accuracy comparable to convolutional neural networks. We also demonstrate that the proposed architecture possesses the ability to train on a small number of samples. These results are achieved by enabling minicolumns to remember contextual transformations.

title: Odessa Scientific School of Researchers Of Variable Stars: From V.P.Tsesevich (1907-1983) to Our Days
Abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of the life and contributions of Vladimir Platonovich Tsesevich (11.11.1907 - 28.10.1983), a leading figure in Odessa's astronomy community from 1944 to 1983. The paper highlights the research directions and key achievements of the scientific school he founded, focusing on the study of variable stars. This research encompasses a wide range of variability types, including "magnetic" and "non-magnetic" cataclysmic variables, symbiotic, X-ray, and other interacting binaries, classical eclipsers, "extreme direct impactors," and pulsating variables ranging from DSct and RR to C and RV, and ultimately to SR and M. Improved algorithms and programs have been developed for statistically optimal phenomenological and physical modeling. These studies in Odessa were deeply inspired by Vladimir Platonovich Tsesevich, a meticulous scientist, brilliant educator, thorough author, engaging popularizer, persevering organizer, and cheerful joker – a true professor and teacher. He was fondly known as "the Poet of the Starry Heavens."

title: Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications
Abstract: The next generation of AI applications will continuously interact with their environment and learn from these interactions. This presents new and demanding system requirements in terms of performance and flexibility. This paper addresses these requirements by introducing Ray, a distributed system specifically designed to meet them. Ray implements a unified interface that can express both task-parallel and actor-based computations, supported by a single dynamic execution engine. To address performance requirements, Ray employs a distributed scheduler and a distributed and fault-tolerant store to manage the system's control state. Our experiments demonstrate scaling beyond 1.8 million tasks per second and superior performance compared to existing specialized systems for several challenging reinforcement learning applications.
label: AI

title: Morphology dictates a robot's ability to ground crowd-proposed language
Abstract: As robots increasingly operate in close proximity to humans, ensuring their decisions and actions align with human values becomes essential. This necessitates robots understanding the true intentions behind human-issued commands. This paper defines a safe robot as one that receives a natural-language command from humans, considers an action in response, and accurately predicts how humans would judge that action if executed in reality. Our contribution is twofold: Firstly, we introduce a web platform allowing human users to propose commands to simulated robots. The robots receive and act upon these commands, and users then provide positive and/or negative reinforcement. Secondly, we train a critic for each robot to predict the crowd's response to a crowd-proposed command. We demonstrate that robot morphology plays a role in how language is grounded: the critics show that two of the robots used in the experiment achieve lower prediction errors than the others. Therefore, according to our definition, these two robots are safer as they ground the proposed commands more accurately.
label: AI

title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
Abstract: The rising popularity of intelligent mobile devices and the demanding computational cost of deep learning-based models necessitate efficient and accurate on-device inference schemes. We propose a quantization scheme that enables inference using solely integer arithmetic, which can be implemented more efficiently than floating-point inference on widely available integer-only hardware. We also co-design a training procedure to preserve end-to-end model accuracy after quantization. As a result, our quantization scheme improves the trade-off between accuracy and on-device latency. These improvements are significant even for MobileNets, a model family renowned for its run-time efficiency, and are demonstrated in ImageNet classification and COCO detection on popular CPUs.
label: AI

title: A Berkeley View of Systems Challenges for AI
Abstract: With the increasing commoditization of computer vision, speech recognition, and machine translation systems, coupled with the widespread deployment of learning-based back-end technologies such as digital advertising and intelligent infrastructures, AI (Artificial Intelligence) has transitioned from research labs to production. These advancements are driven by unprecedented levels of data and computation, methodological advances in machine learning, innovations in systems software and architectures, and the broad accessibility of these technologies. The next generation of AI systems promises to accelerate these developments and increasingly impact our lives through frequent interactions and decision-making (often mission-critical) on our behalf, often in highly personalized contexts. Realizing this promise, however, presents formidable challenges. Notably, we require AI systems that make timely and safe decisions in unpredictable environments, exhibit robustness against sophisticated adversaries, and can process ever-increasing amounts of data across organizations and individuals without compromising confidentiality. These challenges will be exacerbated by the end of Moore's Law, which will constrain the amount of data these technologies can store and process. This paper proposes several open research directions in systems, architectures, and security to address these challenges and help unlock AI's potential to improve lives and society.
label: AI

title: Occam's razor is insufficient to infer the preferences of irrational agents
Abstract: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) aims to infer human rewards or preferences from observed behavior. As human planning systematically deviates from rationality, various approaches have been attempted to account for specific human shortcomings. However, the general problem of inferring the reward function of an agent with unknown rationality has received limited attention. Unlike the well-known ambiguity problems in IRL, this problem is practically relevant but cannot be resolved by observing the agent's policy in sufficient environments. This paper demonstrates (1) that a No Free Lunch result implies it is impossible to uniquely decompose a policy into a planning algorithm and reward function, and (2) that even with a reasonable simplicity prior/Occam's razor on the set of decompositions, we cannot distinguish between the true decomposition and others that lead to high regret. To address this, we need simple "normative" assumptions, which cannot be derived solely from observations.
label: AI

title: Deep Burst Denoising
Abstract: Noise is an inherent challenge in low-light image capture, particularly exacerbated on mobile devices due to their narrow apertures and small sensors. One strategy to mitigate noise in low-light situations is to increase the camera's shutter time, allowing each photosite to integrate more light and reduce noise variance. However, long exposures have two downsides: (a) bright regions can exceed the sensor range, and (b) camera and scene motion can result in blurred images. Another approach to gathering more light is capturing multiple short (noisy) frames in a "burst" and intelligently integrating their content, avoiding the aforementioned downsides. This paper utilizes the burst-capture strategy and implements intelligent integration via a recurrent fully convolutional deep neural net (CNN). We design our novel, multiframe architecture to be a simple addition to any single frame denoising model, capable of handling an arbitrary number of noisy input frames. Our results demonstrate state-of-the-art denoising performance on our burst dataset, surpassing the best published multi-frame techniques, such as VBM4D and FlexISP. Finally, we explore other image enhancement applications by integrating content from multiple frames and showcase the generalizability of our DNN architecture to image super-resolution.
label: AI

title: Sentiment Predictability for Stocks
Abstract: This work presents our findings and experiments on stock-market prediction using various textual sentiment analysis tools, such as mood analysis and event extraction, along with prediction models, including LSTMs and specific convolutional architectures.

title: Side-channel based intrusion detection for industrial control systems
Abstract: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are facing increasing scrutiny due to their historically subpar security. While manufacturers are taking steps to address this, the large installed base of legacy systems cannot be easily updated with state-of-the-art security measures. This paper proposes a system that utilizes electromagnetic side-channel measurements to detect behavioral changes in software running on ICS. To demonstrate the feasibility of this method, we show that it is possible to profile and distinguish between even small changes in programs on Siemens S7-317 PLCs, using techniques from cryptographic side-channel analysis.
label: AI

title: Information Processing by Networks of Quantum Decision Makers
Abstract: This paper proposes a model of a multi-agent society of decision-makers who make decisions based on two criteria: the utility of the prospects and the attractiveness of the considered prospects. This model is a generalization of quantum decision theory, previously developed for single decision-makers making one-step decisions. The generalization encompasses two primary aspects. First, it considers multiple decision-makers simultaneously, interacting with each other through information exchange. Second, it addresses a multistep procedure where agents exchange information repeatedly. Multiple decision-makers exchanging information and forming judgments using quantum rules create a type of quantum information network where collective decisions evolve over time as a result of information exchange. In addition to characterizing collective decisions in human societies, such networks can describe dynamic processes in artificial quantum intelligence composed of multiple parts or in a cluster of quantum computers. The practical applicability of the theory is illustrated through the dynamic disjunction effect, for which three quantitative predictions are made: (i) the probabilistic behavior of decision-makers in the initial stage of the process is described; (ii) the decrease in the difference between initial prospect probabilities and related utility factors is proven; and (iii) the existence of a common consensus after multiple information exchanges is predicted. The predicted numerical values align well with empirical data.
label: AI

title: Lightweight Neural Networks
Abstract: Most weights in a Lightweight Neural Network have a value of zero, while the remaining weights are either +1 or -1. These universal approximators require approximately 1.1 bits/weight of storage, exhibit a fast forward pass, and achieve classification accuracies comparable to conventional continuous-weight networks. Their training regimen initially focuses on error reduction but later emphasizes weight discretization. They ignore insignificant inputs, remove unnecessary weights, and discard unneeded hidden neurons. We have successfully tested them on the MNIST, credit card fraud, and credit card defaults datasets using networks with 2 to 16 hidden layers and up to 4.4 million weights. |||
label: AI

title: Pre-training Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: Recurrent neural networks with differentiable attention mechanisms have achieved success in generative and classification tasks. This work demonstrates that the classification performance of these models can be enhanced by guiding a randomly initialized model to focus on salient input regions during the early training iterations. Moreover, when explicit guidance heuristics are unavailable, a model pretrained on an unsupervised reconstruction task can learn effective attention policies without supervision. The study reveals that increased efficiency in the attention mechanism itself contributes to these performance improvements. Building on these insights, this work introduces bootstrapped glimpse mimicking, a simple, theoretically task-general method for more effective training of attention models. The research draws inspiration from and parallels results on human attention learning.
label: AI

title: Avoiding Echo-Responses in a Retrieval-Based Conversation System
Abstract: Retrieval-based conversational systems often prioritize responses that are semantically similar or even identical to the given conversation context. While the system's objective is to find the most suitable response, this tendency leads to low-quality outputs. This challenge is referred to as the echoing problem. To mitigate this, the paper utilizes a hard negative mining approach during the training stage. The evaluation shows that the resulting model reduces echoing and achieves better performance in terms of Average Precision and Recall@N metrics compared to models trained without this approach.
label: AI

title: CoDraw: Collaborative Drawing as a Testbed for Grounded Goal-driven Communication
Abstract: This research proposes a goal-driven collaborative task that combines language, perception, and action. Specifically, the paper develops a Collaborative image-Drawing game, called CoDraw, played by two agents. The game takes place in a virtual world with movable clip art objects, involving a Teller and a Drawer. The Teller observes an abstract scene with multiple clip art pieces arranged in a semantically meaningful configuration, while the Drawer attempts to recreate the scene on an empty canvas using available clip art pieces. Both players communicate using natural language. The paper introduces the CoDraw dataset, comprising ~10K dialogs containing ~138K messages exchanged between human players. The research defines protocols and metrics for evaluating learned agents in this testbed, highlighting the need for a novel "crosstalk" evaluation condition that pairs agents trained independently on disjoint subsets of the training data. The paper presents models for this task and benchmarks them through fully automated evaluation and live gameplay with humans.
label: AI

title: Inverse Reinforce Learning with Nonparametric Behavior Clustering
Abstract: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) involves learning a single reward function for a Markov Decision Process (MDP) without defining the reward function explicitly, given demonstrations generated by humans or experts. However, assuming that human behaviors can be explained by a single reward function is often unrealistic due to inherent inconsistency. Additionally, demonstrations may be collected from multiple users and aggregated to infer and predict user behavior. This paper introduces the Non-parametric Behavior Clustering IRL algorithm to simultaneously cluster demonstrations and learn multiple reward functions from demonstrations potentially generated from more than one behavior. The method is iterative, alternating between clustering demonstrations into different behavior clusters and inversely learning the reward functions until convergence. It leverages Expectation-Maximization formulation and non-parametric clustering within the IRL setting. To enhance computational efficiency, the paper eliminates the need to completely solve multiple IRL problems for multiple clusters during iteration steps and introduces a resampling technique to avoid generating excessive unlikely clusters. The convergence and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated by learning multiple driver behaviors from demonstrations generated in a grid-world environment and continuous trajectories collected from autonomous robot cars using the Gazebo robot simulator.
label: AI

title: What Can This Robot Do? Learning from Appearance and Experiments
Abstract: When interacting with an unknown robot, how can an autonomous agent determine its capabilities? The robot's appearance can provide clues about its physical and cognitive abilities. Seeing a humanoid robot might raise questions about its ability to kick balls, climb stairs, or recognize faces. This paper proposes an approach to enable the learner to build a model of the robot's performance at a task based on its appearance and refine it through experimentation. Beyond the robot's inherent capabilities, extrinsic factors can influence its performance at a task. The learner can identify potential factors based on the robot's appearance and prior task knowledge, assuming a subset of these factors are controllable. The approach selects values for controllable factors to generate the most informative experiments for testing the robot. Additionally, a metric is introduced to determine if a factor should be incorporated into the model. The paper presents results on modeling a humanoid robot at the task of kicking a ball. It demonstrates that actively selecting values for controllable factors, even in noisy experiments, leads to faster learning of the robot's model for the task. Furthermore, starting from a minimal set of factors, the metric identifies relevant factors to include in the model. Finally, the paper shows that the refined model better represents the robot's performance at the task.
label: AI

title: AI2-THOR: An Interactive 3D Environment for Visual AI
Abstract: The paper introduces The House Of inteRactions (THOR), a framework for visual AI research, available at http://ai2thor.allenai.org. AI2-THOR consists of photorealistic 3D indoor scenes where AI agents can navigate and interact with objects to perform tasks. This framework facilitates research in diverse domains including but not limited to deep reinforcement learning, imitation learning, learning by interaction, planning, visual question answering, unsupervised representation learning, object detection and segmentation, and learning models of cognition. The goal of AI2-THOR is to enable the development of visually intelligent models and advance research in this field.
label: AI

title: Three IQs of AI Systems and their Testing Methods
Abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has brought about the artificial intelligence threat theory and the challenge of evaluating the intelligence level of intelligent products. Both issues necessitate a quantitative method for evaluating intelligence levels in various systems, including human intelligence. This paper proposes General IQ, Service IQ, and Value IQ evaluation methods for intelligence systems, based on the standard intelligence system and extended Von Neumann architecture, depending on different evaluation purposes. General IQ aims to address whether artificial intelligence can surpass human intelligence, placing intelligence systems on an equal footing for unified evaluation. Service IQ and Value IQ are used to determine how intelligent products can better serve humans, reflecting the intelligence and required cost of each intelligence system as a product in the process of serving humans.
label: AI

title: An SDN hybrid architecture for vehicular networks: Application to Intelligent Transport System
Abstract: Vehicular networks are a cornerstone of an Intelligent Transportation System (ITS). They are expected to provide ubiquitous network connectivity to moving vehicles while supporting various ITS services, some with stringent latency and reliability requirements. Two vehicular networking technologies are envisioned to support the full range of ITS services: DSRC (Dedicated Short Range Communication) for direct vehicle-to-vehicle/Road Side Units (RSU) communication and cellular technologies. Existing approaches often divide ITS services based on their requirements, assigning each service to a single network. Multi-path routing, load balancing, or path splitting for enhanced ITS service quality of experience often assume separate control of networks. This paper proposes a hybrid network architecture under the umbrella of SDN (Software Defined Networking) that enables joint control of networks providing connectivity to multi-homed vehicles and explores the opportunities arising from this architecture. The paper demonstrates that beyond the flexibility and fine-grained programmability of SDN, it paves the way for effective network control algorithms essential for supporting ITS services, particularly those with stringent QoS requirements. It also highlights how these algorithms can benefit from environmental or contextual information, such as traffic density and planned trajectories, easily collected by data providers and accessible through the cloud.
label: AI

title: Constraint and Mathematical Programming Models for Integrated Port Container Terminal Operations
Abstract: This paper examines the integrated problem of quay crane assignment, quay crane scheduling, yard location assignment, and vehicle dispatching operations at a container terminal. The primary objective is to minimize vessel turnover times and maximize terminal throughput, key economic drivers in terminal operations. Due to computational complexities, these problems are not optimized jointly in existing work. This paper revisits this limitation and proposes Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) and Constraint Programming (CP) models for the integrated problem under realistic assumptions. Experimental results show that the MIP formulation can only solve small instances, while the CP model finds optimal solutions within reasonable timeframes for realistic instances derived from actual container terminal operations.
label: AI

title: A Bayesian Clearing Mechanism for Combinatorial Auctions
Abstract: This paper frames the problem of combinatorial auction design within a Bayesian framework to incorporate prior information into the auction process and minimize the number of rounds needed to reach convergence. The research develops a generative model of agent valuations and market prices, making clearing prices the maximum a posteriori estimates given observed agent valuations. This generative model serves as the foundation for an auction process that iterates between refining estimates of agent valuations and calculating candidate clearing prices. The auction is implemented using assumed density filtering for valuation estimation and expectation maximization for price computation. An empirical evaluation across various valuation domains demonstrates that the proposed Bayesian auction mechanism is highly competitive against the combinatorial clock auction in terms of rounds to convergence, even under the most favorable price increment choices for the baseline.
label: AI

title: Proximodistal Exploration in Motor Learning as an Emergent Property of Optimization
Abstract: During sensorimotor development, infants harness the complexity of their high-dimensional bodies by utilizing patterns of freezing and freeing degrees of freedom. For instance, when learning to reach, infants free degrees of freedom in their arm proximodistally, progressing from joints closer to the body to those further away. This paper computationally formulates and studies the hypothesis that such patterns can emerge spontaneously as a result of a family of stochastic optimization processes, specifically evolution strategies with covariance-matrix adaptation, without an innate encoding of a maturational schedule. Simulated experiments with an arm demonstrate how a computational learner progressively acquires reaching skills through adaptive exploration, resulting in the spontaneous emergence of a proximodistal organization, denoted PDFF (ProximoDistal Freezing and Freeing of degrees of freedom). The paper also compares this emergent organization across different arm morphologies, from human-like to unnatural, to investigate the effect of kinematic structures on PDFF emergence. Keywords: human motor learning; proximo-distal exploration; stochastic optimization; modelling; evolution strategies; cross-entropy methods; policy search; morphology.
label: AI

title: Intrinsic Point of Interest Discovery from Trajectory Data
Abstract: This paper presents a framework for intrinsic point of interest discovery from trajectory databases. Intrinsic points of interest are regions in a geospatial area inherently defined by the spatial and temporal aspects of trajectory data. These regions can vary in size, shape, and resolution. Any trajectory database exhibits such points of interest, making them intrinsic compared to extrinsic POI definitions that require trajectory metadata, external knowledge about the region, or application-specific information. Spatial and temporal aspects are inherent qualities of any trajectory database, making the framework applicable to data from any domain and resolution. The framework is developed based on recent advancements in the consistency of nonparametric hierarchical density estimators, enabling formal statistical inference and evaluation of intrinsic points of interest. Comparisons of POIs uncovered by the framework in synthetic truth data to thousands of parameter settings for common POI discovery methods show a marked improvement in fidelity without requiring manual parameter tuning.
label: AI

title: Learning to Attend via Word-Aspect Associative Fusion for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
Abstract: Aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) aims to predict the polarity of a given document with respect to a specific aspect entity. While neural network architectures have excelled in predicting overall sentence polarity, aspect-specific sentiment analysis remains an open problem. This paper proposes a novel method for integrating aspect information into a neural model by modeling word-aspect relationships. The novel model, Aspect Fusion LSTM (AF-LSTM), learns to attend based on associative relationships between sentence words and the aspect, allowing it to adapt and focus on relevant words given an aspect term. This addresses shortcomings of other state-of-the-art models that rely on naive concatenations to model word-aspect similarity. Instead, AF-LSTM employs circular convolution and circular correlation to model similarity between the aspect and words, seamlessly integrating this within a differentiable neural attention framework. The model is end-to-end differentiable and closely related to convolution-correlation (holographic) memories. The proposed neural model achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, outperforming ATAE-LSTM by 4%-5% on average across multiple datasets.
label: AI

title: Relation Extraction : A Survey
Abstract: The advent of the internet has led to a massive generation of digital text in the form of news articles, research publications, blogs, question-answering forums, and social media. Extracting information automatically from these documents is crucial as essential information remains hidden within them. This extracted information can improve access and knowledge management within large text corpora, benefiting applications such as Question Answering and Information Retrieval. Entities like persons and organizations form the most basic unit of information. Entity occurrences in a sentence are often linked through well-defined relations, e.g., occurrences of person and organization in a sentence might be linked through relations such as "employed at." Relation Extraction (RE) automates the identification of such relations. This paper surveys significant supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised RE techniques, covering Open Information Extraction (OIE) and Distant Supervision paradigms. It concludes by discussing recent trends in RE techniques and potential future research directions. This survey benefits three types of readers: newcomers who want a quick introduction to RE, researchers seeking to understand RE evolution and future directions, and practitioners seeking the most effective RE technique for various settings.
label: AI

title: Rasa: Open Source Language Understanding and Dialogue Management
Abstract: The paper introduces a pair of open-source Python libraries, Rasa NLU and Rasa Core, for building conversational software. Their goal is to make machine-learning based dialogue management and language understanding accessible to non-specialist software developers. The libraries prioritize ease of use and bootstrapping from minimal or no initial training data. Both packages are extensively documented and include a comprehensive suite of tests. The code is available at https://github.com/RasaHQ/.
label: AI

title: X-SRAM: Enabling In-Memory Boolean Computations in CMOS Static Random Access Memories
Abstract: Silicon-based Static Random Access Memories (SRAM) and digital Boolean logic have been the mainstay of modern computing platforms. Despite significant advancements in scaling the ubiquitous metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor, the underlying von-Neumann computing architecture has remained unchanged. The limited throughput and energy efficiency of state-of-the-art computing systems are largely attributed to the well-known von-Neumann bottleneck. The energy and throughput inefficiency of von-Neumann machines has become more pronounced due to the current emphasis on data-intensive applications like artificial intelligence and machine learning. A potential approach to mitigating the overhead associated with the von-Neumann bottleneck is to enable in-memory Boolean computations. This manuscript presents an augmented version of conventional SRAM bit-cells, called the X-SRAM, capable of performing in-memory, vector Boolean computations in addition to standard memory storage operations. The paper proposes at least six different schemes for enabling in-memory vector computations, including NAND, NOR, IMP (implication), and XOR logic gates, considering different bit-cell topologies: the 8T cell and the 8+T Differential cell. Additionally, a novel "read-compute-store" scheme is introduced, where the computed Boolean function can be directly stored in memory without requiring data latching or a subsequent write operation. The feasibility of these proposed schemes has been verified using predictive transistor models and Monte-Carlo variation analysis.
label: AI

title: Learning Binary Residual Representations for Domain-specific Video Streaming
Abstract: This paper focuses on domain-specific video streaming, targeting a streaming setting where all videos streamed from a server to a client are within the same domain and must be compressed for low-latency transmission. Several popular video streaming services, such as GeForce Now and Twitch, fall into this category. While conventional video compression standards like H.264 are commonly used, the paper hypothesizes that leveraging the domain-specific nature of videos can improve video quality. Based on this hypothesis, a novel video compression pipeline is proposed. The pipeline first compresses domain-specific videos using H.264. Then, a novel binary autoencoder is trained to encode the remaining domain-specific residual information frame-by-frame into binary representations. These binary representations are compressed and transmitted to the client alongside the H.264 stream. Experiments show that this pipeline consistently outperforms standard H.264 compression across several benchmark datasets while utilizing the same channel bandwidth.
label: AI

title: Reasoning in Systems with Elements that Randomly Switch Characteristics
Abstract: This paper investigates the issue of probability stability in reasoning about complex systems with structural uncertainty. Typically, propositions are viewed as probability functions on an abstract random graph, implicitly assuming stable node properties. However, what if some nodes change their characteristics? This scenario cannot be addressed by static or dynamic set abstractions when these changes occur at regular intervals. The paper proposes the use of sets with changing elements, where modular forms are introduced to account for one type of change. An expression for the dependence of the mean on the probability of switching elements is determined. The system is also analyzed from the perspective of decision-making between different hypotheses. Such sets are expected to be useful in complex system queries and survey analysis.
label: AI

title: Reconfigurable Hardware Accelerators: Opportunities, Trends, and Challenges
Abstract: With the emergence of big data applications in Machine Learning, Speech Recognition, Artificial Intelligence, and DNA Sequencing in recent years, computer architecture research communities face the explosive scale of data explosion. To achieve high efficiency in data-intensive computing, studies of heterogeneous accelerators, focusing on the latest applications, have become a hot topic in computer architecture. Heterogeneous accelerator implementation currently relies primarily on computing units like Application-specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). Among these heterogeneous architectures, FPGA-based reconfigurable accelerators offer two key advantages: First, the FPGA architecture contains a large number of reconfigurable circuits, fulfilling the requirements for high performance and low power consumption during specific application execution. Second, the reconfigurable architectures employed in FPGAs enable rapid prototyping of systems and offer excellent customizability and reconfigurability. Recent years have seen a surge of accelerating works based on FPGA or other reconfigurable architectures in top-tier computer architecture conferences. This survey reviews the latest high-level research products of reconfigurable accelerator architectures and algorithm applications. It compares key research issues and domains, analyzing and highlighting the advantages, disadvantages, and challenges of reconfigurable accelerators. Finally, the paper provides a future development trend outlook for accelerator architectures, aiming to serve as a reference for computer architecture researchers.
label: AI

title: Review of Design of Speech Recognition and Text Analytics based Digital Banking Customer Interface and Future Directions of Technology Adoption
Abstract: Banking is a leading adopter of cutting-edge information technologies. Since its modern era began with paper-based accounting maintained in branches, the adoption of computerized systems enabled centralized processing in data centers and improved customer experience through a more accessible and efficient system. The latest evolution involves incorporating natural language processing and speech recognition into the user interface between humans and the system, along with the use of machine learning and advanced analytics for backend processing. This paper reviews technological adoption progress in the field and assesses the maturity level of solutions involving less-studied or low-resource languages like Hindi and other Indian regional languages. It includes an analysis based on a prototype developed by the authors. Future directions in this field are also highlighted. |||
label: AI

title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Marketing
Abstract: Learning customer preferences from observed behavior is a crucial area of research in marketing. Traditional structural models often assume forward-looking customers or firms maximizing their utility, estimating it using stochastic optimal control methods. This research proposes an alternative approach based on Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) for studying dynamic consumer demand. The authors develop a version of Maximum Entropy IRL, leading to a highly tractable model formulation requiring low-dimensional convex optimization for optimal parameter search. Simulations demonstrate that observational noise for identical customers can be mistakenly interpreted as consumer heterogeneity.
label: AI

title: Multi-focus Attention Network for Efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in learning various tasks to human levels. However, unlike human perception, current DRL models directly connect low-level sensory input to state-action values, failing to exploit relationships between entities within the input. This leads to a need for vast experience samples for learning. This paper introduces a Multi-focus Attention Network (MANet) that mimics human spatial abstraction, dividing the sensory input into multiple entities (partial states) and attending to them simultaneously. Parallel attention layers focus on relevant partial states for solving the task, improving state-action value estimation. Experiments show that MANet achieves higher scores with significantly less experience samples compared to Deep Q-network and single attention models. Additionally, MANet is extended to an attentive communication model for multi-agent cooperative tasks, demonstrating a 20% faster learning rate than state-of-the-art models.

title: Consideration on Example 2 of "An Algorithm of General Fuzzy InferenceWith The Reductive Property"
Abstract: This paper examines the correctness of fuzzy reasoning algorithms, specifically addressing the following: (1) confirming results from a 2007 paper based on a 1988 paper, (2) identifying an error in a specific example presented in a paper by He Ying-Si, Quan Hai-Jin, and Deng Hui-Wen, and (3) correcting the mistakes found and providing a calculation example of FMT.

title: Deception Detection in Videos
Abstract: This research presents a system for covert automated deception detection in real-life courtroom trial videos, investigating the role of different modalities (vision, audio, text). The vision component utilizes classifiers trained on low-level video features to predict human micro-expressions, which are then used for deception prediction. Surprisingly, IDT (Improved Dense Trajectory) features, commonly employed for action recognition, also effectively predict deception in videos. The system fuses the scores of classifiers trained on IDT features and high-level micro-expressions for improved performance. MFCC (Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients) features from the audio domain further enhance performance, while transcript information proves less beneficial. Using various classifiers, the automated system achieves an AUC of 0.877 (10-fold cross-validation) on unseen subjects, outperforming state-of-the-art methods using human micro-expression annotations by 5%. Combining human annotations with the system improves AUC to 0.922. A user study investigates human performance on deception detection, the modalities utilized, and performance with limited modalities. The project page can be found at https://doubaibai.github.io/DARE/.
