title: Co-domain Embedding using Deep Quadruplet Networks for Unseen Traffic Sign Recognition
Abstract: While recent advances in visual recognition have been driven by large supervised datasets, acquiring such data for specialized domains like traffic sign recognition is often challenging. This paper proposes a novel feature embedding scheme for classifying unseen classes in traffic sign recognition, leveraging official images as class templates. The proposed method utilizes a quadruple relationship between real and synthetic domains, exploiting pairwise similarities among samples. This approach demonstrates improved performance compared to competing methods for both seen and unseen classes, highlighting its potential for cross-domain traffic sign recognition.

title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
Abstract: Chess, a widely studied domain in artificial intelligence, relies on sophisticated search techniques, domain-specific adaptations, and handcrafted evaluation functions refined by human experts. This paper introduces AlphaZero, a generalized algorithm inspired by AlphaGo Zero's success in Go. AlphaZero, starting from random play with no domain knowledge beyond the game rules, achieved superhuman performance in chess, shogi (Japanese chess), and Go within 24 hours, convincingly defeating world-champion programs in each case. This demonstrates the power of tabula rasa reinforcement learning for achieving superhuman performance in diverse challenging domains.

title: Neural Cross-Lingual Entity Linking
Abstract: Entity Linking (EL) faces challenges in effectively using contextual information to disambiguate mentions to Wikipedia entries. This problem is exacerbated in cross-lingual EL, where mentions in non-English documents are linked to entries in the English Wikipedia. This paper proposes a neural EL model that trains fine-grained similarities and dissimilarities between query and candidate documents from multiple perspectives. The model combines convolution and tensor networks to capture complex relationships. The English-trained system is surprisingly effective for zero-shot learning in other languages using multilingual embeddings. The model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in English and cross-lingual settings, including Spanish and Chinese TAC 2015 datasets.

title: Autonomous development and learning in artificial intelligence and robotics: Scaling up deep learning to human--like learning
Abstract: Autonomous lifelong development and learning are key human capabilities that differentiate humans from current deep learning systems. This paper examines crucial ingredients from other branches of artificial intelligence that contribute to autonomous learning: curiosity and intrinsic motivation, social learning, and embodied interaction. These mechanisms guide exploration and goal selection, offering promising perspectives for integrating them with deep learning. Deep learning (DL) has made significant advancements but still falls short of human learning. This paper highlights fundamental differences between DL systems and human learning, focusing on autonomous development and learning, which are under-discussed in existing literature. Humans learn autonomously, setting their own goals and exploring skills driven by intrinsic motivation and social interaction. This process is incremental, online, and progressive, involving a curriculum of learning where skills are built upon each other. Human learning occurs in the physical world through embodied experimentation, constrained by energy, time, and computational resources. Developmental and Cognitive Robotics, informed by developmental psychology and neuroscience, has made significant progress in computational models of autonomous learning.
label: AI

title: Memory-based Combination PUFs for Device Authentication in Embedded Systems
Abstract: Embedded systems are crucial for the growth of the Internet-of-Things (IoT) in diverse application domains. However, their increasing network connectivity and access to sensitive information raise security and privacy concerns. Counterfeit components further complicate the issue. Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) offer a promising security primitive, particularly memory-based PUFs due to their minimal hardware requirements. Existing memory-based PUFs rely on a single memory technology, making them vulnerable to attacks. This paper proposes a new combination PUF that intelligently combines SRAM and DRAM technologies to address these shortcomings. The combination PUF exhibits high entropy, supports a large number of challenge-response pairs, and is intrinsically reconfigurable. Implemented using a Terasic TR4-230 FPGA board and commercially available SRAMs and DRAMs, the proposed design demonstrates significant improvements over existing PUFs in resisting attacks and achieving high robustness across temperature and aging tests.
label: AI

title: Human Perception of Performance
Abstract: Humans regularly assess the performance of others, distinguishing success from failure and influencing outcomes in fields ranging from science to education and sports. However, in many contexts, the specific metrics driving human evaluation remain unclear. This research examines a massive dataset of player evaluations by human judges to investigate human perception of performance in soccer, the world's most popular sport. Machine learning is used to create an artificial judge that accurately replicates human evaluation, revealing biases toward various contextual features. By analyzing the structure of the artificial judge, we uncover the aspects of player behavior that capture the attention of human judges, demonstrating that human evaluation relies on a "noticeability heuristic" where only feature values significantly deviating from the norm are considered to rate an individual's performance.
label: AI

title: Determinism in the Certification of UNSAT Proofs
Abstract: The pursuit of increased trustworthiness in SAT solvers is an active area of research utilizing various methods. Some approaches involve obtaining a proof from provers and then verifying it, typically by replicating the search based on the proof's information. However, this certification process itself requires another non-trivial proof search, diminishing the level of trust we can place in it. Attempts to address this issue employ certifiers verified by proof assistants like Isabelle/HOL and Coq. Our approach differs, relying on an extremely simplified certifier. This certifier enjoys a high level of trust but is very inefficient. This paper explores this approach and concludes that by placing certain restrictions on the formats, one can largely eliminate the need for search and, in principle, certify proofs of arbitrary size.
label: AI

title: An All-Memristor Deep Spiking Neural Computing System: A Step Towards Realizing the Low Power,Stochastic Brain
Abstract: Deep Analog Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) excel at complex classification tasks with remarkably high accuracy. However, they rely on massive amounts of power for calculations, obscuring the accuracy benefits. The biological brain, significantly more powerful and energy-efficient, suggests a conceptual mismatch. Considering the energy-efficient spike-based communication of biological neurons and their non-deterministic behavior, incorporating these effects into Deep Artificial Neural Networks could lead to a more realistic neuron model. This work proposes harnessing the inherent stochasticity of nanoscale resistive devices to emulate the functionality of a spiking neuron, integrating it into deep stochastic Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). We propose algorithmic modifications to convert an ANN to an SNN while supporting the stochastic activation function offered by these devices. We devise circuit architectures incorporating stochastic memristive neurons and memristive crossbars for synaptic weight functionality. The proposed All Memristor deep stochastic SNN is tested for image classification, demonstrating only a 1% accuracy degradation compared to the ANN baseline after incorporating circuit and device non-idealities. The network exhibits robustness to variations and consumes approximately 6.4 times less energy than its CMOS counterpart.
label: AI

title: Learning to Fuse Music Genres with Generative Adversarial Dual Learning
Abstract: FusionGAN introduces a novel genre fusion framework for music generation, integrating the strengths of generative adversarial networks and dual learning. The proposed method features a dual learning extension that effectively merges the styles of different domains. To efficiently quantify the difference among diverse domains and mitigate the vanishing gradient issue, FusionGAN utilizes a Wasserstein-based metric to approximate the distance between the target domain and existing domains. Leveraging this Wasserstein distance, a new domain is created by combining the patterns of existing domains through adversarial learning. Experimental results on public music datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in merging two genres.
label: AI

title: Multimodal Storytelling via Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning
Abstract: Deriving event storylines offers an effective summarization method for concisely organizing vast information, alleviating the burden of information overload. However, a widely recognized storyline metric remains elusive. Previous research has developed various approaches based on different assumptions about user interests. While these studies can extract interesting patterns, their assumptions do not guarantee that the derived patterns align with user preferences. Additionally, their reliance on single-modality sources overlooks cross-modality information. This paper proposes a method, multimodal imitation learning via generative adversarial networks (MIL-GAN), to directly model user interests as reflected in various data. Specifically, the proposed model addresses the challenge by imitating users' demonstrated storylines. The model is designed to learn reward patterns from user-provided storylines and subsequently applies the learned policy to unseen data. The proposed approach is shown to be capable of acquiring implicit user intent and significantly outperforming competing methods, as verified by a user study.
label: AI

title: AI Oriented Large-Scale Video Management for Smart City: Technologies, Standards and Beyond
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success across various tasks in computer vision. Intelligent video analysis, widely applicable to video surveillance in numerous smart city applications, can also be propelled by these powerful deep learning engines. To practically integrate deep neural network models into large-scale video analysis, unprecedented challenges exist in managing large-scale video data. Deep feature coding, rather than video coding, provides a practical solution for handling large-scale video surveillance data. To enable interoperability within the context of deep feature coding, standardization is crucial. However, the rapid evolution of deep learning algorithms and the unique characteristics of feature coding present numerous challenges for standardization. This paper envisions the future deep feature coding standard for AI-oriented large-scale video management, discussing existing techniques, standards, and possible solutions for these open problems.
label: AI

title: Examining Cooperation in Visual Dialog Models
Abstract: This work proposes a blackbox intervention method for visual dialog models, aiming to assess the contribution of individual linguistic or visual components. We conduct structured or randomized interventions that aim to impair specific components of the model and observe changes in task performance. We replicate a state-of-the-art visual dialog model and demonstrate that our methodology yields surprising insights. Notably, both dialog and image information have minimal contributions to task performance. The intervention method presented here can serve as a sanity check for the strength and robustness of each component in visual dialog systems.
label: AI

title: Learning User Intent from Action Sequences on Interactive Systems
Abstract: Interactive systems have become ubiquitous on the web and in mobile applications, with increasing user participation. Applications across marketing domains can now be accessed via mobile or web platforms, enabling users to directly perform actions and achieve desired outcomes. User actions on a system can be representative of a specific intent. Learning this intent from user actions can provide valuable insights into user behavior on a system. This paper presents models for optimizing interactive systems by learning and analyzing user intent through their actions. We propose a four-phased model that utilizes sequential time-series of interaction actions using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based sequence learning system to construct a model for intent recognition. Our system then provides objective-specific maximization followed by analysis and contrasting methods to identify areas for improvement in the interaction system. We discuss deployment scenarios for such a system and present evaluation results on an online marketplace using user clickstream data.
label: AI

title: An Equivalence of Fully Connected Layer and Convolutional Layer
Abstract: This article demonstrates that convolutional operations can be converted to matrix multiplication, mirroring the calculation process of fully connected layers. This insight is helpful for beginners in neural networks to understand the underlying workings of fully connected and convolutional layers. For clarity and readability, we focus on the linear case, which can be easily extended to the non-linear case by introducing a non-linear encapsulation to the values, denoted as  $\\sigma(x)$ represented as $x^{\\prime}$.
label: AI

title: Learning by Asking Questions
Abstract: This paper introduces an interactive learning framework for the development and testing of intelligent visual systems called learning-by-asking (LBA). We explore LBA in the context of the Visual Question Answering (VQA) task. LBA differs from standard VQA training in that most questions are not observed during training time, and the learner must actively ask questions it seeks answers to. This more closely mimics natural learning and has the potential to be more data-efficient than the traditional VQA setting. We present a model that performs LBA on the CLEVR dataset and show that it automatically discovers an easy-to-hard curriculum when learning interactively from an oracle. Our LBA-generated data consistently matches or outperforms the CLEVR training data and exhibits greater sample efficiency. Additionally, our model asks questions that generalize to state-of-the-art VQA models and to novel test-time distributions.
label: AI

title: On the Real-time Vehicle Placement Problem
Abstract: Motivated by ride-sharing platforms' efforts to minimize rider wait times, this paper introduces a novel problem of placing vehicles to fulfill real-time pickup requests in a spatially and temporally dynamic environment. The real-time nature of this problem distinguishes it from other placement and scheduling problems, as it requires not only real-time placement decisions but also handling real-time request dynamics influenced by human mobility patterns. We utilize a dataset of ten million ride requests from four major US cities to demonstrate significant self-similarity in the requests. We then propose distributed online learning algorithms for the real-time vehicle placement problem and bound their expected performance under this observed self-similarity.
label: AI

title: A path to AI
Abstract: To develop a safe system replicating and potentially surpassing human-level intelligence, three fundamental modules are proposed: objective, agent, and perception. The objective module ensures the system acts in humanity's best interest, not against it. It comprises two components: a network of machine learning agents to address value alignment and a distributed ledger to mitigate existential threats. The agent module expands on the Dyna concept and leverages insights from sociology to build the missing link of artificial general intelligence—a world simulator. The perception module estimates the state of the world, benefiting from existing machine learning algorithms enhanced by a new paradigm in hardware design—a quantum computer. This paper outlines a potential approach for constructing such a system, analyzing the current state-of-the-art and proposing alternative research directions rather than concrete, industry-ready solutions.
label: AI

title: Robust 3D Action Recognition through Sampling Local Appearances and Global Distributions
Abstract: 3D action recognition has broad applications in human-computer interaction and intelligent surveillance. However, recognizing similar actions remains challenging as existing literature fails to effectively capture motion and shape cues from noisy depth data. This paper proposes a novel two-layer Bag-of-Visual-Words (BoVW) model to suppress noise disturbances and jointly encode both motion and shape cues. First, background clutter is removed using a background modeling method specifically designed for depth data. Subsequently, motion and shape cues are combined to generate robust and distinctive spatial-temporal interest points (STIPs): motion-based STIPs and shape-based STIPs. In the first layer of our model, a multi-scale 3D local steering kernel (M3DLSK) descriptor is proposed to describe local appearances of cuboids around motion-based STIPs. In the second layer, a spatial-temporal vector (STV) descriptor is introduced to describe the spatial-temporal distributions of shape-based STIPs. Utilizing the BoVW model, motion and shape cues are combined to form a fused action representation. Our model demonstrates favorable performance compared to common STIP detection and description methods. Comprehensive experiments verify the effectiveness of our model in distinguishing similar actions and its robustness to background clutter, partial occlusions, and pepper noise.
label: AI

title: Specifying and Computing Causes for Query Answers in Databases via Database Repairs and Repair Programs
Abstract: A correspondence between database tuples as causes for query answers in databases and tuple-based repairs of inconsistent databases with respect to denial constraints has already been established. This work utilizes answer-set programs that specify repairs of databases as a foundation for solving computational and reasoning problems related to causes. We introduce causes at the attribute level by appealing to both null-based and attribute-based repair semantics. The corresponding repair programs are presented and serve as a basis for computation and reasoning about attribute-level causes. These programs are extended to handle causality under integrity constraints.
label: AI

title: Mining Supervisor Evaluation and Peer Feedback in Performance Appraisals
Abstract: Performance appraisal (PA) is an important HR process for periodically measuring and evaluating every employee's performance against organizational goals. A PA process involves purposeful, multi-step, multi-modal communication between employees, supervisors, and peers, encompassing self-appraisal, supervisor assessment, and peer feedback. Analyzing the structured data and text generated during PA is crucial for assessing the quality of appraisals and tracking actual improvements. This paper applies text mining techniques to extract insights from PA text. Initially, we perform sentence classification to identify strengths, weaknesses, and suggestions for improvement found in supervisor assessments and then utilize clustering to discover broad categories among them. Subsequently, we employ multi-class multi-label classification techniques to match supervisor assessments to predefined broad perspectives on performance. Finally, we propose a short-text summarization technique to generate a summary of peer feedback comments for a given employee and compare it with manual summaries. All techniques are illustrated using a real-life dataset of supervisor assessment and peer feedback text generated during the PA of 4528 employees in a large multinational IT company.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Relation Extraction using Markov Logic Networks
Abstract: The task of end-to-end relation extraction comprises two sub-tasks: i) identifying entity mentions along with their types and ii) recognizing semantic relations among the entity mention pairs. %Identifying entity mentions along with their types and recognizing semantic relations among the entity mentions, are two very important problems in Information Extraction. It has been shown that for better performance, it is necessary to address these two sub-tasks jointly. We propose an approach for simultaneously extracting entity mentions and relations in a sentence using inference in Markov Logic Networks (MLN). We learn three different classifiers: i) local entity classifier, ii) local relation classifier, and iii) "pipeline" relation classifier that utilizes predictions from the local entity classifier. Predictions from these classifiers may be inconsistent with each other. We represent these predictions along with some domain knowledge using weighted first-order logic rules in an MLN and perform joint inference over the MLN to obtain a global output with minimal inconsistencies. Experiments on the ACE (Automatic Content Extraction) 2004 dataset demonstrate that our approach of joint extraction using MLNs outperforms baselines of individual classifiers. Our end-to-end relation extraction performance surpasses 2 out of 3 previous results reported on the ACE 2004 dataset.
label: AI

title: Learning Multi-Level Hierarchies with Hindsight
Abstract: Hierarchical agents have the potential to solve sequential decision-making tasks with greater sample efficiency than their non-hierarchical counterparts because hierarchical agents can break down tasks into sets of subtasks that only require short sequences of decisions. To realize this potential of faster learning, hierarchical agents need to be able to learn their multiple levels of policies in parallel so that these simpler subproblems can be solved simultaneously. Yet, learning multiple levels of policies in parallel is hard because it is inherently unstable: changes in a policy at one level of the hierarchy may cause changes in the transition and reward functions at higher levels in the hierarchy, making it difficult to jointly learn multiple levels of policies. In this paper, we introduce a new Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) framework, Hierarchical Actor-Critic (HAC), that can overcome the instability issues that arise when agents try to jointly learn multiple levels of policies. The main idea behind HAC is to train each level of the hierarchy independently of the lower levels by training each level as if the lower level policies are already optimal. We demonstrate experimentally in both grid world and simulated robotics domains that our approach can significantly accelerate learning relative to other non-hierarchical and hierarchical methods. Indeed, our framework is the first to successfully learn 3-level hierarchies in parallel in tasks with continuous state and action spaces.
label: AI

title: V2X Content Distribution Based on Batched Network Coding with Distributed Scheduling
Abstract: Content distribution is an application in intelligent transportation systems to assist vehicles in acquiring information, such as digital maps and entertainment materials. This paper considers content distribution from a single roadside infrastructure unit to a group of vehicles passing by. To combat the short connection time and lossy channel quality, the downloaded contents need to be further shared among vehicles after the initial broadcasting phase. To this end, we propose a joint infrastructure-to-vehicle (I2V) and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication scheme based on batched sparse (BATS) coding to minimize traffic overhead and reduce the total transmission delay. In the I2V phase, the roadside unit (RSU) encodes the original large-size file into a number of batches in a rateless manner, each containing a fixed number of coded packets, and sequentially broadcasts them during the I2V connection time. In the V2V phase, vehicles perform network-coded cooperative sharing by re-encoding the received packets. We propose a utility-based distributed algorithm to efficiently schedule the V2V cooperative transmissions, thereby reducing the transmission delay. A closed-form expression for the expected rank distribution of the proposed content distribution scheme is derived, which is used to design the optimal BATS code. The performance of the proposed content distribution scheme is evaluated through extensive simulations considering multi-lane roads and realistic vehicular traffic settings, demonstrating significant performance improvements over existing content distribution protocols.
label: AI

title: SERKET: An Architecture for Connecting Stochastic Models to Realize a Large-Scale Cognitive Model
Abstract: To achieve human-like robot intelligence, a large-scale cognitive architecture is required for robots to understand their environment through the various sensors they are equipped with. This paper introduces a novel framework called Serket that facilitates the construction of a large-scale generative model and its inference by connecting sub-modules, allowing robots to acquire diverse capabilities through interactions with their environments and others. We propose that large-scale cognitive models can be constructed by hierarchically connecting smaller, fundamental models while maintaining their programmatic independence. Moreover, connected modules are interdependent, and parameters need to be optimized as a whole. Traditionally, equations for parameter estimation have to be derived and implemented based on the models. However, deriving and implementing these equations for a larger-scale model becomes more challenging. To address these problems, this paper proposes a method for parameter estimation by communicating minimal parameters between various modules while preserving their programmatic independence. Consequently, Serket simplifies the construction of large-scale models and facilitates parameter estimation through module connections. Experimental results demonstrate that models can be constructed by connecting modules, parameters can be optimized collectively, and these results are comparable to the original models we have proposed.
label: AI

title: A text-independent speaker verification model: A comparative analysis
Abstract: The most pressing challenge in voice biometrics lies in selecting the most efficient speaker recognition technique. Each individual's voice is unique, and factors like physical differences in vocal organs, accent, and pronunciation contribute to the problem's complexity. This paper explores various methods available in each block of the speaker recognition process, aiming to identify the most effective techniques for achieving precise results. We analyze results on text-independent corpora. We utilize MFCC (Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient), LPCC (linear predictive cepstral coefficient), and PLP (perceptual linear prediction) algorithms for feature extraction; PCA (Principal Component Analysis) and tSNE for dimensionality reduction; and SVM (Support Vector Machine), feedforward, nearest neighbor, and decision tree algorithms for the classification block in the speaker recognition system. We comparatively analyze each block to determine the best technique. |||
label: AI

title: A Deeper Look at Experience Replay
Abstract: Experience replay is widely used in deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, but its utility is often overlooked. We show that a large memory buffer can negatively affect performance and propose a simple O(1) method to mitigate this issue. Our method is evaluated in simple grid worlds and challenging Atari games.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Diffuse Optical Tomography
Abstract: Diffuse optical tomography (DOT) is a promising technique for breast cancer detection due to its sensitivity to hemoglobin oxidization levels. However, traditional reconstruction algorithms are sensitive to imaging parameters. We propose a novel deep learning approach that leverages recent mathematical theory to accurately reconstruct 3D optical anomalies. Our method is trained on simulation data and successfully recovers anomaly locations in both phantoms and live animals without the use of contrast agents.

title: Proceedings of the Fifth Workshop on Proof eXchange for Theorem Proving
Abstract: This volume of EPTCS presents the proceedings of the Fifth Workshop on Proof Exchange for Theorem Proving (PxTP 2017). The workshop fosters collaboration among researchers working on communication, integration, and cooperation between reasoning systems and formalisms, with a focus on proofs. Recent advancements in computer-aided reasoning have led to the development of powerful deduction tools that can handle increasingly complex problems. This workshop aims to promote further collaboration by exploring theoretical formalisms and practical tools for exchanging problems, proofs, and models.
label: AI

title: In folly ripe. In reason rotten. Putting machine theology to rest
Abstract: Computation has profoundly transformed the world, with its algorithmic embodiment resembling a digital theology. While algorithmic computation can mimic creative aspects of life, it remains closed to meaning. AI, in its historical development, has not truly achieved artificial intelligence but rather automated tasks associated with intelligence. This has led to the machine's hypostatized role as a deterministic reality producer, including the reality of the human creators. Deep learning, as the latest form of this deterministic theology, claims more than it actually achieves in terms of data processing. We suggest a new understanding of complexity and a distinction between artificial reactiveness and living anticipatory nature as responses to the challenges posed by machine theology.
label: AI

title: Always Lurking: Understanding and Mitigating Bias in Online Human Trafficking Detection
Abstract: Web-based human trafficking is difficult to detect due to its latent nature and dispersion among escort advertisements. Intelligent systems can help allocate investigative resources and combat this widespread social problem. We present a trafficking detection pipeline architecture that assigns a normalized score to escort advertisements, indicating the risk of trafficking activities. Our research, conducted within the DARPA Memex program, analyzes multi-institutional data and systems, and addresses potential bias in the algorithm. We demonstrate that while automatic trafficking detection is beneficial, it necessitates de-biasing measures for responsible deployment. Our system is currently used by over 200 law enforcement agencies to investigate leads.
label: AI

title: Visual Explanation by High-Level Abduction: On Answer-Set Programming Driven Reasoning about Moving Objects
Abstract: We propose a hybrid architecture for robust visual explanation encompassing hypothesis formation, belief revision, and default reasoning with video data. Our architecture integrates answer set programming based abductive reasoning with a visual processing pipeline for object tracking and motion analysis. The formal framework is implemented in answer set programming, and its efficacy is demonstrated through applications on two video datasets: the MOTChallenge benchmark and a Movie Dataset.

title: The Complexity of Satisfiability in Non-Iterated and Iterated Probabilistic Logics
Abstract: We investigate the complexity of satisfiability in probabilistic logics (PL and PPL) with respect to the complexity of the underlying logic L. We obtain complexity bounds for satisfiability parameterized by the complexity of satisfiability of conjunctions of positive and negative formulas without probabilistic or classical operators. Our results provide tight complexity bounds for PL and PPL when L is classical propositional logic or justification logic.

title: Dialectical Multispectral Classification of Diffusion-Weighted Magnetic Resonance Images as an Alternative to Apparent Diffusion Coefficients Maps to Perform Anatomical Analysis
Abstract: Multispectral image analysis is a promising field with applications in medical imaging and satellite monitoring. We propose the Objective Dialectical Method (ODM), a classification method inspired by the Philosophy of Praxis, for analyzing multispectral images. ODM utilizes evolvable mathematical tools to analyze diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance (MR) images. Results are compared to ground-truth images generated by polynomial networks, demonstrating the ability of ODM to distinguish gray and white matter in DW-MR images.

title: Avaliação do método dialético na quantização de imagens multiespectrais
Abstract: Unsupervised classification plays a vital role in multispectral image analysis, assisting in extracting a priori knowledge. We present an evaluation of four methods based on Dialectics: the Objective Dialectical Classifier and the Dialectical Optimization Method adapted to k-means. These methods are compared to existing algorithms like k-means, fuzzy c-means, and Kohonen's self-organizing maps. Our findings show that Dialectics-based methods exhibit robustness to noise and achieve comparable quantization performance to Kohonen's map, considered an optimal quantizer.

title: Fuzzy-Based Dialectical Non-Supervised Image Classification and Clustering
Abstract: The materialist dialectical method is a philosophical framework for analyzing reality as complex processes composed of interacting poles. We introduce the Objective Dialectical Classifier (ODC), a non-supervised map for classification inspired by materialist dialectics. ODC extends the fuzzy c-means classifier and is evaluated on a dataset of synthetic multispectral brain images. Comparison with other classification methods, including k-means, fuzzy c-means, and Kohonen's self-organized maps, demonstrates ODC's ability to achieve quantization performance comparable to optimal non-supervised classifiers.

title: A semi-supervised fuzzy GrowCut algorithm to segment and classify regions of interest of mammographic images
Abstract: Breast cancer is a major health concern for women worldwide. Mammographic image segmentation is crucial for analyzing and diagnosing breast lesions. We present a semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the GrowCut algorithm, utilizing fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to improve accuracy. Our method reduces the need for expert intervention in seed point selection and provides an automatic point selection process based on simulated annealing. The algorithm is compared to state-of-the-art segmentation techniques and evaluated on an image classifier using Zernike moments extracted from segmented images. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in segmenting fat and fibroid tissues with a high classification rate.

title: Reconstruction of Electrical Impedance Tomography Using Fish School Search, Non-Blind Search, and Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a non-invasive imaging technique that utilizes evolutionary computation and swarm intelligence to solve inverse problems. We introduce a method for EIT image reconstruction based on Fish School Search (FSS) and Non-Blind Search (NBS). Our method is evaluated on numerical phantoms with varying electrical conductivity configurations. Results show that both FSS and FSS-NBS exhibit faster convergence compared to genetic algorithms.

title: Gradient Descent Learns One-hidden-layer CNN: Don't be Afraid of Spurious Local Minima
Abstract: We analyze the problem of learning a one-hidden-layer neural network with non-overlapping convolutional layers and ReLU activation. We prove the existence of a spurious local minimizer when the labels are generated by a teacher network with fixed weights. Despite the presence of this spurious local minimizer, gradient descent with weight normalization can recover the true parameters with high probability. We further demonstrate that the local minimizer plays a non-trivial role in the gradient descent dynamics, exhibiting a two-phase convergence behavior: slow initial convergence followed by rapid acceleration.

title: Sentiment Classification using Images and Label Embeddings
Abstract: We investigate the contribution of image data to sentiment analysis. Our analysis compares models utilizing only image data, only text data, and a combination of both. We assess the impact of images on sentiment classification and their potential for generalizing to unknown sentiments.

title: Evaluation of Alzheimer's Disease by Analysis of MR Images using Multilayer Perceptrons and Kohonen SOM Classifiers as an Alternative to the ADC Maps
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease is challenging to diagnose without invasive techniques, especially in the early stages. We present a method for image analysis and classification of multispectral brain images composed of diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance (MR) images to evaluate cerebrospinal fluid area and Alzheimer's disease progression. We use multilayer perceptrons and Kohonen Self-Organized Map classifiers and assume that classes of interest can be separated by hyperquadrics. title: Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Graph Coloring
Abstract: This Random Walks project explores the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method for graph coloring. We present plots of the cost function by varying parameters like the number of colors and average node degree. The results are obtained using a simulated annealing scheme where the temperature parameter in the MCMC is progressively lowered.

title: Will humans even write code in 2040 and what would that mean for extreme heterogeneity in computing?
Abstract: Programming trends suggest a future where machines will write most of their own code, driven by advancements in machine learning, AI, natural language processing, and code generation technologies. The extreme heterogeneity may drive the creation of this technology, facilitating efficient programming for diverse devices.

title: Data-Driven Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Curbside Parking Demand: A Case-Study in Seattle
Abstract: Curbside parking management is crucial for mitigating urban congestion. We present a data-driven study of the spatio-temporal characteristics of curbside parking demand in Seattle. We utilize a Gaussian mixture model to identify zones with similar spatial parking demand and introduce a metric for assessing temporal consistency. Our findings provide insights into where and when to implement performance-based pricing policies and target information and incentives to drivers.
label: AI

title: From knowledge-based to data-driven modeling of fuzzy rule-based systems: A critical reflection
Abstract: This paper examines the shift in fuzzy logic from a knowledge-based to a data-driven approach for designing fuzzy rule-based systems. The classical rule-based paradigm is better suited to knowledge-based design, while data-driven modeling poses challenges. We discuss the limitations of the flat structure of rule bases and the local nature of fuzzy rules in handling complex dependencies between variables. This motivates alternative approaches for fuzzy systems modeling, where functional dependencies can be represented more flexibly and compactly using hierarchical structures.

title: PFAx: Predictable Feature Analysis to Perform Control
Abstract: Predictable Feature Analysis (PFA) is a dimensionality reduction algorithm that extracts predictable features from high-dimensional input signals. We extend PFA by incorporating supplementary information to enhance prediction quality. PFAx, the extended PFA, extracts features from the main input signal that are most predictable based on themselves and the supplementary information. PFAx provides insight into how supplementary information affects prediction quality and can even be used to generate supplementary information that achieves a desired outcome for the main signal. We apply this framework to a reinforcement learning setting, demonstrating the feasibility of locally optimizing an agent's state to reach a goal. We are developing a follow-up paper that explores global optimization using this method. |||

title: Artificial intelligence in peer review: How can evolutionary computation support journal editors?
Abstract: The increasing volume of manuscripts submitted for publication highlights the shortcomings of peer review, such as extended review times. Editorial strategies, sets of guidelines designed to streamline the process and reduce editors' workloads, are considered trade secrets by publishing houses and remain undisclosed. Editors in smaller publishing groups, seeking to enhance the effectiveness of their strategies, are forced to rely on iterative trial-and-error methods. This research demonstrates that Cartesian Genetic Programming, a nature-inspired evolutionary algorithm, can significantly improve editorial strategies. The artificially evolved strategy reduced the duration of the peer review process by 30%, without expanding the pool of reviewers, when compared to a typical human-developed strategy. While evolutionary computation has traditionally been employed in technological or biological domains, these findings showcase the potential of genetic programs to optimize real-world social systems, which are inherently more complex and challenging to understand and manage than physical systems.

title: MAgent: A Many-Agent Reinforcement Learning Platform for Artificial Collective Intelligence
Abstract: MAgent is a platform designed to facilitate research and development in the realm of many-agent reinforcement learning. Unlike previous research platforms focused on single or multi-agent reinforcement learning, MAgent specializes in supporting tasks that involve hundreds to millions of agents. Through the interactions within a population of agents, it enables not only the study of learning algorithms for optimal agent policies but also, more importantly, the observation and comprehension of individual agent behaviors and emergent social phenomena, including communication languages, leadership structures, and altruistic behavior. MAgent exhibits high scalability, accommodating up to one million agents on a single GPU server. It also provides flexible configurations for AI researchers to customize their environments and agents. This demonstration presents three environments developed on MAgent, showcasing the emergence of collective intelligence through learning from scratch.

title: Interactive Reinforcement Learning for Object Grounding via Self-Talking
Abstract: Humans are adept at identifying a specific visual object within a complex scene through a series of natural language interactions. Effective communication necessitates active engagement and adaptation from both parties. This paper introduces an interactive training method to enhance natural language conversation systems for visual grounding tasks. During interactive training, both agents are reinforced by guidance from a shared reward function. This parameterized reward function also cooperatively updates itself through interactions, contributing to task completion. The method is evaluated on the GuessWhat?! visual grounding task, resulting in a significant improvement in task success rate. However, language drifting issues are observed during training, leading to the proposal of reward engineering to enhance the interpretability of generated conversations. These results highlight the need for semantic-relevant metrics beyond task success rate when evaluating goal-ended visual conversation tasks.

title: Recurrent Neural Network Language Models for Open Vocabulary Event-Level Cyber Anomaly Detection
Abstract: Automated analysis methods are essential tools for monitoring and defending networks to protect the sensitive or confidential data they host. This research introduces a flexible, powerful, and unsupervised approach to detecting anomalous behavior in computer and network logs, effectively eliminating the need for domain-dependent feature engineering commonly employed by existing methods. By treating system logs as sequences of interleaved "sentences" (event log lines) for training online unsupervised neural network language models, this approach provides an adaptive model of normal network behavior. The effectiveness of both standard and bidirectional recurrent neural network language models in detecting malicious activity within network log data is compared. Furthermore, a tiered recurrent architecture is introduced to provide context by modeling sequences of users' actions over time. Compared to Isolation Forest and Principal Components Analysis, two popular anomaly detection algorithms, this approach demonstrates superior performance on the Los Alamos National Laboratory Cyber Security dataset. Notably, the best-performing character-based model achieves a test set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.98, highlighting the strong fine-grained anomaly detection capabilities of this method for open vocabulary logging sources.

title: Compatibility Family Learning for Item Recommendation and Generation
Abstract: Compatibility between items, such as clothes and shoes, is a significant factor in customer purchasing decisions. However, learning "compatibility" presents challenges due to its broader scope compared to similarity, its asymmetric nature, and the limited availability of compatible and incompatible item pairs. This paper proposes an end-to-end trainable system to embed each item into a latent vector and project a query item into K compatible prototypes within the same space. These prototypes reflect the broader notions of compatibility, and both the embedding and prototypes are referred to as "Compatibility Family." A novel Projected Compatibility Distance (PCD) function, differentiable and ensuring diversity, is introduced in this learned space. The PCD function aims to ensure at least one prototype is close to a compatible item, while none of the prototypes are close to an incompatible item. The system is evaluated on a toy dataset, two Amazon product datasets, and the Polyvore outfit dataset, consistently achieving state-of-the-art performance. Additionally, the visualization of candidate compatible prototypes is demonstrated using a Metric-regularized Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (MrCGAN), where the input is a projected prototype and the output is a generated image of a compatible item. Human evaluators preferred the generated images from MrCGAN significantly, with roughly twice the number of votes compared to images generated by CGANs directly conditioned on query items.
label: AI

title: Explainable AI: Beware of Inmates Running the Asylum Or: How I Learnt to Stop Worrying and Love the Social and Behavioural Sciences
Abstract: Alan Cooper, in his seminal book "The Inmates are Running the Asylum," argues that a key reason for software's frequent poor design from a user perspective is the dominance of programmers in design decisions, rather than interaction designers. As a result, programmers design software for themselves instead of their target audience, a phenomenon Cooper refers to as "the inmates running the asylum." This paper contends that explainable AI faces a similar risk. While the resurgence of explainable AI is positive, this paper argues that most AI researchers are developing explanatory agents for themselves rather than for their intended users. However, explainable AI is more likely to succeed if researchers and practitioners integrate, implement, and improve models from the vast and valuable research in philosophy, psychology, and cognitive science, focusing evaluation on people rather than technology. A brief review of the literature reveals significant potential to incorporate more findings from the social and behavioral sciences into explainable AI. Several key results from these fields relevant to explainable AI are presented.
label: AI

title: State Estimation For An Agonistic-Antagonistic Muscle System
Abstract: Research in assistive technology, rehabilitation, and prosthetics necessitates understanding human-machine interaction, where human muscular properties play a crucial role. This paper investigates a nonlinear agonistic-antagonistic muscle system based on the Hill muscle model. To understand the characteristics of the muscle model, the problem of estimating state variables and activation signals of the dual muscle system is considered. This work accounts for parameter uncertainty and unknown inputs in the estimation problem, presenting three observers: a high-gain observer, a sliding mode observer, and an adaptive sliding mode observer. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the convergence of all three observers. To facilitate numerical simulations, a backstepping controller is employed to guide the muscle system toward tracking a desired trajectory. Numerical simulations indicate that the three observers are comparable and provide reliable estimates in both noise-free and noisy environments. These proposed schemes can serve as frameworks for estimating complex multi-muscle systems, potentially leading to intelligent exercise machines for adaptive training and rehabilitation, as well as adaptive prosthetics and exoskeletons.
label: AI

title: Visual Features for Context-Aware Speech Recognition
Abstract: Automatic transcriptions of consumer-generated multimedia content, such as YouTube videos, still exhibit high word error rates. This data typically spans a broad domain, is recorded under challenging conditions with inexpensive hardware, focuses on the visual modality, and may have undergone post-processing or editing. This paper builds upon previous work adapting the acoustic model of a DNN-based speech recognition system to an RNN language model, demonstrating how both can be adapted to the objects and scenes automatically detectable in the video. The focus is on a corpus of "how-to" videos from the web, where the presence of an object (e.g., "car") or a detected scene (e.g., "kitchen") can be used to condition both models on the "context" of the recording, thereby reducing perplexity and improving transcription. Significant improvements are achieved in both cases, and the respective reductions in word error rate are compared and analyzed. These findings have implications for any speech processing task where "context" information is available, such as robotics, human-machine interaction, or indexing large audio-visual archives. Ultimately, this research aims to bridge the gap between the "video-to-text" and "speech-to-text" communities.
label: AI

title: Intelligent EHRs: Predicting Procedure Codes From Diagnosis Codes
Abstract: To submit a claim to insurance companies, doctors must code a patient encounter with both the diagnosis (ICDs) and procedures performed (CPTs) in an Electronic Health Record (EHR). Identifying and applying relevant procedure codes is a laborious and time-consuming process, requiring doctors to choose from approximately 13,000 procedure codes without predefined one-to-one mapping. This paper proposes a state-of-the-art deep learning method for automated and intelligent coding of procedures (CPTs) based on the diagnosis codes (ICDs) entered by the doctor. Specifically, the learning problem is framed as a multi-label classification problem, leveraging distributed representation to learn the input mapping of high-dimensional sparse ICDs codes. The final model, trained on 2.3 million claims, surpasses existing rule-based, probabilistic, and association-rule mining based methods, achieving a recall of 90@3.
label: AI

title: Novel Exploration Techniques (NETs) for Malaria Policy Interventions
Abstract: Decision-making under uncertainty is a daunting task, particularly for problems with significant complexity. Healthcare policymakers worldwide face challenges under restrictive constraints, with limited tools to aid in data-driven decisions. This research frames the process of finding an optimal malaria policy as a stochastic multi-armed bandit problem, implementing three agent-based strategies to explore the policy space. A Gaussian Process regression is applied to the findings of each agent, both for comparison and to account for stochastic results from simulating the spread of malaria in a fixed population. The generated policy spaces are compared with published results, providing a direct reference against human expert decisions for the same simulated population. This novel approach offers a powerful resource for policymakers, serving as a platform readily extensible to encompass future, more nuanced policy spaces.

title: The mind as a computational system
Abstract: This document excerpts an essay written as part of a graduate school application in Computer Science (with a focus on Artificial Intelligence) in 1986. The essay's full title was "Some Topics in Philosophy and Computer Science." Though not accepted by any of the schools that received it, the author pursued a career as a theoretical physicist. This text, unchanged from 1985 and preserving the original typesetting as much as possible, is made available now in memory of Jerry Fodor, whose writings significantly influenced the author at the time (despite occasional disagreements).

title: Don't Just Assume; Look and Answer: Overcoming Priors for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Numerous studies have revealed that current Visual Question Answering (VQA) models heavily rely on superficial correlations within training data and lack sufficient image grounding. To encourage the development of models focusing on image grounding, this paper proposes a new setting for VQA where, for each question type, train and test sets have different prior distributions of answers. Specifically, new splits of the VQA v1 and VQA v2 datasets, termed Visual Question Answering under Changing Priors (VQA-CP v1 and VQA-CP v2 respectively), are introduced. First, the performance of several existing VQA models is evaluated in this new setting, demonstrating a significant performance decline compared to the original VQA setting. Second, a novel Grounded Visual Question Answering model (GVQA) is proposed, incorporating inductive biases and architectural restrictions designed to prevent "cheating" by primarily relying on priors in the training data. GVQA explicitly disentangles the recognition of visual concepts present in the image from the identification of plausible answer spaces for a given question, enabling more robust generalization across different answer distributions. GVQA is built upon an existing VQA model - Stacked Attention Networks (SAN). Experiments demonstrate that GVQA significantly outperforms SAN on both VQA-CP v1 and VQA-CP v2 datasets. Interestingly, it also surpasses more powerful VQA models like Multimodal Compact Bilinear Pooling (MCB) in several cases. GVQA offers complementary strengths to SAN when trained and evaluated on the original VQA v1 and VQA v2 datasets. Furthermore, GVQA is more transparent and interpretable than existing VQA models.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Cross-modal Hashing
Abstract: Cross-modal hashing aims to map heterogeneous multimedia data into a shared Hamming space, enabling fast and flexible retrieval across different modalities. Unsupervised cross-modal hashing is more flexible and applicable than supervised methods, as it avoids intensive labeling efforts. However, existing unsupervised methods learn hashing functions by preserving inter and intra correlations, neglecting the underlying manifold structure across different modalities, which is crucial for capturing meaningful nearest neighbors for cross-modal retrieval. To address this, this paper proposes an Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Cross-modal Hashing approach (UGACH), leveraging GAN's unsupervised representation learning capabilities to exploit the underlying manifold structure of cross-modal data. The key contributions are: (1) A generative adversarial network is proposed to model cross-modal hashing in an unsupervised manner. In UGACH, given data of one modality, the generative model attempts to fit the distribution over the manifold structure and selects informative data of another modality to challenge the discriminative model. The discriminative model learns to distinguish generated data from true positive data sampled from a correlation graph, improving retrieval accuracy. These two models are trained adversarially, enhancing each other and promoting hashing function learning. (2) A correlation graph-based approach is introduced to capture the underlying manifold structure across different modalities, ensuring data from different modalities but within the same manifold exhibit smaller Hamming distances, thereby improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments compared with six state-of-the-art methods validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: A Novel Brain Decoding Method: a Correlation Network Framework for Revealing Brain Connections
Abstract: Brain decoding is a prominent area in cognitive science, focusing on reconstructing perceptual images from brain activities. Analyzing the correlations of collected data from human brain activities and representing activity patterns are two key challenges in brain decoding based on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) signals. However, existing correlation analysis methods primarily focus on the strength information of voxels, revealing functional connectivity in the cerebral cortex, often neglecting the structural information that implies intracortical or intrinsic connections - structural connectivity. Consequently, the effective connectivity inferred by these methods is relatively unilateral. This research proposes a correlation network (CorrNet) framework that can be flexibly combined with diverse pattern representation models. The CorrNet framework introduces topological correlation to unveil structural information, leading to richer correlations that contribute to specifying the underlying effective connectivity. The CorrNet framework is also integrated with a linear support vector machine (SVM) and a dynamic evolving spike neuron network (SNN) for pattern representation separately, offering a novel approach for decoding cognitive activity patterns. Experimental results validate the reliability and robustness of the CorrNet framework, demonstrating significant improvements in brain decoding compared to comparable methods.
label: AI

title: A double competitive strategy based learning automata algorithm
Abstract: Learning Automata (LA) are recognized as one of the most powerful tools in reinforcement learning. The family of estimator algorithms has been proposed to enhance the convergence rate of LA, achieving significant progress. However, these estimators perform poorly in estimating the reward probabilities of actions during the initial stages of the LA learning process. This leads to an excessive addition of rewards to the probabilities of non-optimal actions, necessitating a large number of extra iterations to compensate for these incorrect rewards. To accelerate convergence, this paper proposes a new P-model absorbing learning automaton employing a double competitive strategy for updating the action probability vector. This strategy allows for immediate correction of incorrect rewards. The proposed Double Competitive Algorithm overcomes the limitations of existing estimator algorithms. A refined analysis is presented to demonstrate the epsilon-optimality of the proposed scheme. Extensive experimental results in benchmark environments showcase that the proposed learning automata outperform both the classic LA SE_RI and the currently fastest LA DGCPA*.

title: InclusiveFaceNet: Improving Face Attribute Detection with Race and Gender Diversity
Abstract: This research presents an approach to face attribute detection that maintains or improves attribute detection accuracy across gender and race subgroups by incorporating demographic information before learning the attribute detection task. The system, termed InclusiveFaceNet, detects face attributes by transferring race and gender representations learned from a separate dataset of public race and gender identities. Utilizing learned demographic representations while withholding demographic inference from the downstream face attribute detection task safeguards potential users' demographic privacy while achieving some of the best reported results to date on attribute detection using the Faces of the World and CelebA datasets.
label: AI

title: Modeling the Multiple Sclerosis Brain Disease Using Agents: What Works and What Doesn't?
Abstract: The human brain, one of the most complex living structures in the known universe, comprises billions of neurons and synapses. Its intrinsic complexity makes it a challenging task to accurately represent its structure and functionality. Numerous studies have been conducted to model brain disease, structure, and functionality, with some employing Agent-based approaches including multiagent-based simulation models and brain complex networks. While these models have been developed using agent-based computing, none, to our knowledge, have utilized Agent-Oriented Software Engineering (AOSE) methodologies in developing the brain or disease model. This is problematic as models developed without due process can miss important requirements. AOSE uniquely merges concepts from multiagent systems, agent-based modeling, artificial intelligence, and distributed systems. It incorporates tested software engineering principles across various phases of model development, including analysis, design, implementation, and testing. This paper applies three different AOSE methodologies (GAIA, TROPOS, and MASE) to model the Multiple Sclerosis brain disease. After developing the models, Exploratory Agent-based Modeling (EABM) is employed to develop an actual model replicating previous results as proof of concept. This study aims to demonstrate and explore the viability and effectiveness of AOSE methodologies in developing complex brain structure and cognitive process models. Key findings include the demonstration that AOSE methodologies can be significantly helpful in modeling various complex living systems, particularly the human brain.
label: AI

title: New Techniques for Inferring L-Systems Using Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: Lindenmayer systems (L-systems) are a formal grammar system that iteratively rewrites all symbols of a string, in parallel. When visualized with a graphical interpretation, the images exhibit self-similar shapes frequently observed in nature. L-systems have proven particularly successful as a concise, reusable technique for simulating plants. The L-system inference problem involves finding an L-system to simulate a given plant. This process is currently primarily performed by experts, limited by the availability of experts, the complexity solvable by humans, and time constraints. This paper introduces the Plant Model Inference Tool (PMIT), which infers deterministic context-free L-systems from an initial sequence of strings generated by the system using a genetic algorithm. PMIT can infer more complex systems than existing approaches. While existing approaches are limited to L-systems with a total sum of 20 combined symbols in the productions, PMIT can infer almost all tested L-systems with a total sum of 140 symbols. This was validated using a test bed of 28 previously developed L-system models, in addition to models created artificially by bootstrapping larger models.
label: AI

title: Audio Cover Song Identification using Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cover song identification using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Previous studies primarily extract feature vectors characterizing the cover song relationship from a pair of songs, using them to compute the (dis)similarity between the two songs. Recognizing the existence of a meaningful pattern between cover songs that can be learned, this research reformulates the cover song identification problem within a machine learning framework. A CNN is constructed using a cross-similarity matrix generated from a pair of songs as input. A dataset composed of cover song pairs and non-cover song pairs is built, serving as positive and negative training samples, respectively. The trained CNN outputs the probability of a cover song relationship given a cross-similarity matrix generated from any two pieces of music, identifying cover songs through probability-based ranking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves performance better than or comparable to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Budget-Aware Activity Detection with A Recurrent Policy Network
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenging problem of efficient temporal activity detection in untrimmed long videos. While recent research has focused on enhancing detection accuracy, the inference time for processing each video can range from seconds to minutes, hindering real-world applications. This research introduces a budget-aware framework that learns to perform activity detection by intelligently selecting a small subset of frames based on a specified time budget. This problem is formulated as a Markov decision process, employing a recurrent network to model the frame selection policy. A recurrent policy gradient-based approach is derived to approximate the gradient of the non-decomposable and non-differentiable objective defined in this problem. Through extensive experiments, the proposed framework achieves competitive detection accuracy while significantly reducing computation time, enabling the detection of multiple activities within a mere 0.35 seconds for each untrimmed long video. |||

title: Deep Neural Networks for Multiple Speaker Detection and Localization
Abstract: Neural networks can be used for simultaneous sound source detection and localization in human-robot interaction, offering an advantage over traditional signal processing methods due to their reduced reliance on strict environmental assumptions. Existing neural network approaches primarily focus on single sound source localization, limiting their applicability to multiple source scenarios. This paper presents a likelihood-based encoding of the network output that enables the detection of an arbitrary number of sound sources. Additionally, it investigates the use of sub-band cross-correlation information as features for enhanced localization in sound mixtures, exploring three different network architectures. Experiments using real data recorded from a robot demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly surpass the performance of popular spatial spectrum-based approaches.
label: AI

title: Embodied Question Answering
Abstract: Embodied Question Answering (EmbodiedQA), a novel AI task, challenges an agent to answer questions by navigating a 3D environment, gathering information through first-person vision, and providing a response. This task necessitates a multifaceted set of AI skills, including active perception, language understanding, goal-driven navigation, commonsense reasoning, and grounding language into actions. This work introduces environments, end-to-end-trained reinforcement learning agents, and evaluation protocols specifically designed for EmbodiedQA.
label: AI

title: Calculating Semantic Similarity between Academic Articles using Topic Event and Ontology
Abstract: Determining semantic similarity between academic documents is crucial for tasks such as plagiarism detection, automatic technical surveys, and semantic search. While existing research primarily focuses on semantic similarity at the concept, sentence, and short text fragment levels, document-level semantic matching remains reliant on surface-level statistical information, neglecting article structures and global semantic meanings. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a novel method for document-level semantic similarity assessment in academic literature. The approach represents academic articles using topic events that integrate multiple information profiles, such as research purposes, methodologies, and domains, to comprehensively describe the research work. Similarity between topic events is calculated based on domain ontology to derive semantic similarity between articles. Experiments demonstrate the significant performance improvement of this method compared to state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: Collaborative Filtering with Social Exposure: A Modular Approach to Social Recommendation
Abstract: This paper explores the use of social information to enhance recommendations, addressing the limitations of existing social recommender systems that assume shared preferences among social friends. Inspired by causal process-based recommendations that model user exposures to items, this work proposes a novel approach, SERec, to integrate social exposure into collaborative filtering. SERec assumes that users gain product information from their online friends, rather than sharing identical preferences, providing a more realistic and less restrictive model. Two methods, social regularization and social boosting, are presented to implement SERec, each employing different approaches to construct social exposures. Experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance of these methods compared to state-of-the-art techniques for top-N recommendations. Further analysis compares the robustness and scalability of the two proposed methods.
label: AI

title: ConvNets and ImageNet Beyond Accuracy: Understanding Mistakes and Uncovering Biases
Abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning for image classification, driven by ConvNets and Imagenet, have shown marked slowdowns in performance improvements, alongside concerns about neural network robustness to adversarial examples and potential biases. This work investigates these issues from the end-user perspective using human subject studies and explanations. The study reveals that the accuracy and robustness of ConvNets measured on Imagenet are significantly underestimated. It demonstrates that explanations can mitigate the impact of misclassified adversarial examples from the end-user perspective. Finally, it introduces a novel tool for uncovering undesirable biases learned by a model. These contributions highlight the value of explanations in enhancing our understanding of ConvNets' predictions and designing more reliable models.
label: AI

title: Learning to Learn from Weak Supervision by Full Supervision
Abstract: This paper presents a method for training neural networks using a combination of weakly labeled and truly labeled data. The approach involves training two neural networks: a target network (the learner) and a confidence network (the meta-learner). The target network is optimized for a specific task using a large set of weakly annotated unlabeled data. Gradient updates to the target network are controlled using scores provided by the confidence network, which is trained on a smaller amount of supervised data. This method prevents noisy labels from negatively impacting the quality of the target network model.
label: AI

title: Learning to Compose Skills
Abstract: This work introduces a differentiable framework capable of learning various compositions of simple policies, termed skills. Recursive composition of skills creates hierarchies that exhibit complex behavior. Skill networks are trained to generate skill-state embeddings that serve as input to a trainable composition function, which outputs a policy for the overall task. Experiments on an environment encompassing multiple collect and evade tasks demonstrate the framework's ability to rapidly build complex skills from simpler ones. Moreover, the learned composition function exhibits transfer to unseen combinations of skills, enabling zero-shot generalizations.
label: AI

title: Enabling Embodied Analogies in Intelligent Music Systems
Abstract: This methodology focuses on cross-modal machine learning, leveraging multidisciplinary tools and methods from diverse fields, including music, systematic musicology, dance, motion capture, human-computer interaction, computational linguistics, and audio signal processing. The key tasks include: (1) adapting wisdom-of-the-crowd approaches to embodiment in music and dance performances to create a dataset of music and lyrics encompassing a range of emotions; (2) employing audio/language-informed machine learning techniques to automatically identify the emotional content of the music and lyrics; and (3) integrating motion capture data from a Vicon system and dancers performing to the music.
label: AI

title: Transferring Autonomous Driving Knowledge on Simulated and Real Intersections
Abstract: Autonomous vehicle intersection handling is treated as a reinforcement learning problem within a transfer learning setting. This paper investigates the ability of a network trained on one type of intersection to generalize to other intersections. It is observed that a network trained solely on one intersection generally fails to generalize to different intersections. However, a network pre-trained on one intersection and fine-tuned on another exhibits improved performance on the new task compared to isolated training. This network also retains knowledge of the prior task, although some forgetting occurs. Finally, the benefits of fine-tuning are demonstrated when transferring simulated intersection handling knowledge to a real autonomous vehicle.
label: AI

title: Improving Latent User Models in Online Social Media
Abstract: Modern social platforms are characterized by abundant user-behavior data associated with the publication, sharing, and consumption of textual content. Users interact with content and each other within a complex and dynamic social environment while evolving over time. Effectively characterizing users and predicting their future behavior in such a setting necessitates overcoming several challenges. Content heterogeneity and temporal inconsistency of behavior data result in severe sparsity at the user level. This paper proposes a novel mutual-enhancement framework to simultaneously partition and learn latent activity profiles of users. A flexible user partitioning approach is introduced to effectively discover rare behaviors and address user-level sparsity. The framework is evaluated extensively on massive datasets from real-world platforms, including Q&A networks and interactive online courses (MOOCs). Results indicate significant gains over state-of-the-art behavior models (15% avg) across various tasks, with further magnified gains for users with limited interaction data. The algorithms are amenable to parallelization, scale linearly with dataset size, and offer flexibility to model diverse aspects of user behavior.
label: AI

title: Knowledge Graph Embedding with Iterative Guidance from Soft Rules
Abstract: Embedding knowledge graphs (KGs) into continuous vector spaces is a prominent area of research. Integrating such an embedding model with logic rules has garnered increasing attention. Most previous attempts involved a one-time injection of logic rules, neglecting the interactive nature between embedding learning and logical inference. They primarily focused on hard rules, which always hold true and require extensive manual effort for creation or validation. This paper introduces Rule-Guided Embedding (RUGE), a novel paradigm of KG embedding with iterative guidance from soft rules. RUGE enables an embedding model to simultaneously learn from 1) labeled triples directly observed in a given KG; 2) unlabeled triples with labels predicted iteratively; and 3) soft rules with varying confidence levels extracted automatically from the KG. The learning process iteratively queries rules for soft labels for unlabeled triples, incorporating newly labeled triples to update the embedding model. This iterative procedure enhances the transfer of knowledge embodied in logic rules into the learned embeddings. RUGE is evaluated for link prediction on Freebase and YAGO. Experimental results demonstrate that: 1) with rule knowledge injected iteratively, RUGE achieves significant and consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines; and 2) despite their uncertainties, automatically extracted soft rules significantly benefit KG embedding, even those with moderate confidence levels. The code and data used for this paper are available at https://github.com/iieir-km/RUGE.

title: Variational Deep Q Network
Abstract: This framework directly addresses the probability distribution of the value function parameters in Deep Q Network (DQN), employing powerful variational inference subroutines to approximate the posterior of the parameters. The equivalence between the proposed surrogate objective and variational inference loss is established. This new algorithm achieves efficient exploration and performs well on large-scale chain Markov Decision Process (MDP).
