title: Comparing Deep Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Methods in Continuous Control
Abstract: Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Strategy are two prominent approaches for addressing complex control problems. Both have dedicated communities actively developing advancements in their respective domains, leading to cutting-edge techniques for continuous control tasks. This paper formulates parallelized versions of the Proximal Policy Optimization method and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient method within the context of Deep Reinforcement Learning. A comprehensive comparison is conducted between state-of-the-art techniques from both camps for continuous control, including evolutionary methods and Deep Reinforcement Learning methods. The results reveal that there is no consistent winner.
label: AI

title: Embedded Real-Time Fall Detection Using Deep Learning For Elderly Care
Abstract: This paper presents a real-time embedded fall detection system using a DVS (Dynamic Vision Sensor), a novel application for traditional fall detection. It includes a dataset for fall detection using the DVS, as well as a DVS-TN (DVS-Temporal Network). The first contribution is the creation of the DVS Falls Dataset, enabling the network to recognize a wider range of falls than existing datasets while addressing privacy concerns through the use of DVS. Secondly, the paper introduces DVS-TN: an optimized deep learning network for fall detection using DVS. Finally, a fall detection system that operates in real-time on low-computing hardware is implemented and tested on the DVS Falls Dataset, encompassing various fall scenarios. The approach achieves a 95.5% F1-score and operates at 31.25 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson TX1 board.
label: AI

title: Improved Learning in Evolution Strategies via Sparser Inter-Agent Network Topologies
Abstract: This work draws inspiration from the literature on human collective intelligence to improve deep learning. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms often utilize a network of processors for parameter sharing. Existing approaches implicitly employ fully-connected networks, where all processors are connected. However, the scientific literature on human collective intelligence suggests that complete networks may not always be the most effective for distributed search through complex spaces. This study demonstrates that alternative network topologies can enhance deep neural network training. It is found that sparser networks learn higher rewards faster, leading to learning improvements at lower communication costs.
label: AI

title: Towards Data Quality Assessment in Online Advertising
Abstract: In online advertising, the goal is to match advertisers with the most relevant users to optimize campaign performance. Multiple data sources provided by advertisers or third-party data providers are utilized to select users based on advertiser targeting criteria. This paper presents a framework for assessing the quality of these data sources at scale. The framework efficiently evaluates the similarity of a specific data source categorization to the ground truth, particularly when the ground truth is accessible only in aggregate form, and user-level information is anonymized or unavailable due to privacy concerns. The paper proposes several methodologies within this framework, presents preliminary assessment results, and evaluates their comparative performance. Additionally, two use cases are presented: targeting specific user categories and forecasting desirable audiences for online advertising campaigns with pre-defined targeting criteria.
label: AI

title: Learnings Options End-to-End for Continuous Action Tasks
Abstract: This paper presents new results on learning temporally extended actions for continuous tasks using the options framework (Sutton et al. [1999b], Precup [2000]). To achieve this, the option-critic architecture (Bacon et al. [2017]) is employed with a deliberation cost and trained using proximal policy optimization (Schulman et al. [2017]) instead of vanilla policy gradient. Results on Mujoco domains are promising, but raise questions about when a specific option should be used, an issue directly related to the use of initiation sets.
label: AI

title: A Semantic Loss Function for Deep Learning with Symbolic Knowledge
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for integrating symbolic knowledge into deep learning. From first principles, a semantic loss function is derived that bridges between neural output vectors and logical constraints. This loss function captures the neural network's proximity to satisfying constraints on its output. Experimental evaluation demonstrates its effectiveness in guiding the learner to achieve (near-)state-of-the-art results on semi-supervised multi-class classification. Furthermore, it significantly improves the neural network's ability to predict structured objects, such as rankings and paths. These discrete concepts are notoriously difficult to learn and benefit from a tight integration of deep learning and symbolic reasoning methods.
label: AI

title: Predicting Depression Severity by Multi-Modal Feature Engineering and Fusion
Abstract: This paper presents preliminary research exploring whether patient vocal acoustic, linguistic, and facial patterns can predict clinical ratings of depression severity, as measured by the Patient Health Questionnaire depression scale (PHQ-8). A multi-modal fusion model is proposed that combines audio, video, and text features. Training on the AVEC 2017 dataset, the proposed model outperforms single-modality prediction models and surpasses the dataset baseline with a significant margin.
label: AI

title: Video Captioning via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Video captioning involves automatically generating a textual description of the actions depicted in a video. While previous work (e.g., sequence-to-sequence models) has shown promising results in summarizing short videos, generating detailed captions for videos containing multiple fine-grained actions remains challenging. This paper tackles this challenge by proposing a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for video captioning. A high-level Manager module learns to design sub-goals, while a low-level Worker module recognizes the primitive actions needed to fulfill the sub-goal. This compositional framework, which reinforces video captioning at different levels, significantly outperforms all baseline methods on a newly introduced large-scale dataset for fine-grained video captioning. Notably, the non-ensemble model achieves state-of-the-art results on the widely used MSR-VTT dataset. |||
label: AI

title: A Novel Image-centric Approach Towards Direct Volume Rendering
Abstract: Generating transfer functions (TFs) is a fundamental task in direct volume rendering (DVR). A TF maps voxels to color and opacity values, revealing internal structures. Existing TF tools are complex and unintuitive for users, who are often medical professionals rather than computer scientists. We propose a novel image-centric method for TF generation that allows users to directly manipulate volume data to create DVRs, simplifying the process. Our method focuses on presenting only the most informative volume slices for selection, further streamlining user interaction. The selected parts are then classified using our novel sparse nonparametric support vector machine classifier, which combines both local and near-global distributional information of the training data. The resulting voxel classes are mapped to aesthetically pleasing and distinguishable color and opacity values using harmonic colors. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets and a detailed user survey demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.
label: AI

title: Generalized Grounding Graphs: A Probabilistic Framework for Understanding Grounded Commands
Abstract: Robots in many task domains need to interpret and act upon natural language commands given by humans, which often refer to the robot's physical surroundings. This interpretation is known as the symbol grounding problem, grounded semantics, or grounded language acquisition. This problem is challenging because people use diverse vocabulary and grammar, and robots have substantial uncertainty about their surroundings, making it difficult to link language elements to specific aspects of the environment. While symbolic models capture linguistic structure, they haven't scaled successfully to handle diverse language from untrained users. Existing statistical approaches can better handle diversity, but lack the ability to model complex linguistic structure, limiting their accuracy. Recent hybrid approaches have addressed scaling and complexity limitations, but haven't effectively linked linguistic and perceptual features. Our framework, called Generalized Grounding Graphs (G^3), addresses these issues by defining a probabilistic graphical model dynamically according to the linguistic parse structure of a natural language command. This approach effectively scales, handles linguistic diversity, and enables the system to associate command parts with specific objects, places, and events in the external world. We demonstrate that robots can learn word meanings and use them to robustly follow natural language commands from untrained users. We showcase our approach with both mobility and mobile manipulation commands, involving various semi-autonomous robotic platforms, including a wheelchair, a micro-air vehicle, a forklift, and the Willow Garage PR2.

title: Happiness Pursuit: Personality Learning in a Society of Agents
Abstract: Modeling personality is a challenging problem with applications in computer games, virtual assistants, online shopping, and education. Numerous techniques have been explored, from neural networks to computational cognitive architectures. However, most approaches rely on examples with hand-crafted features and scenarios. We propose a novel approach to learning personality by training agents using a Deep Q-Network (DQN) model on rewards based on psychoanalysis, against hand-coded AI in the game of Pong. This process resulted in four agents, each with its own distinct personality. We then define the happiness of an agent, which can be seen as a measure of alignment with its objective function, and analyze it when agents play against both hand-coded AI and each other. We found that agents achieving higher happiness during testing against hand-coded AI exhibited lower happiness when competing against each other. This suggests that higher happiness in testing may be a sign of overfitting to the hand-coded AI, leading to worse performance against agents with different personalities.

title: Embedding Words as Distributions with a Bayesian Skip-gram Model
Abstract: We introduce a method for embedding words as probability densities in a low-dimensional space. Unlike standard word embedding methods that assume a fixed word embedding across the entire text collection, our Bayesian model generates a word-specific prior density for each occurrence of a word. Intuitively, this prior density encodes the distribution of potential "meanings" for each word. These prior densities are conceptually similar to Gaussian embeddings. However, unlike Gaussian embeddings, our model can also obtain context-specific densities, encoding uncertainty about the sense of a word given its context. These densities correspond to posterior distributions within our model and have many potential applications. For instance, we demonstrate their direct use in the lexical substitution task. We describe an effective estimation method based on the variational autoencoding framework and show that our embeddings achieve competitive results on standard benchmarks.

title: HoME: a Household Multimodal Environment
Abstract: We introduce HoME: a Household Multimodal Environment for artificial agents to learn from vision, audio, semantics, physics, and interaction with objects and other agents, all within a realistic context. HoME integrates over 45,000 diverse 3D house layouts based on the SUNCG dataset, a scale that may facilitate learning, generalization, and transfer. HoME is an open-source, OpenAI Gym-compatible platform extensible to tasks in reinforcement learning, language grounding, sound-based navigation, robotics, multi-agent learning, and more. Our hope is that HoME will better enable artificial agents to learn as humans do: in an interactive, multimodal, and richly contextualized setting.
label: AI

title: Now Playing: Continuous low-power music recognition
Abstract: Existing music recognition applications require a connection to a server for recognition. We present a low-power music recognizer that runs entirely on a mobile device and automatically recognizes music without user interaction. To minimize battery consumption, a small music detector runs continuously on the mobile device's DSP chip, waking up the main application processor only when it's confident that music is present. Once activated, the recognizer on the application processor receives a few seconds of audio, which is fingerprinted and compared to the stored fingerprints in the on-device fingerprint database of tens of thousands of songs. Our presented system, Now Playing, has an average daily battery usage of less than 1%, respects user privacy by running entirely on-device, and can passively recognize a wide range of music.

title: Intelligent Traffic Light Control Using Distributed Multi-agent Q Learning
Abstract: The combination of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), known as AI-powered Internet of Things (AIoT), is capable of processing vast amounts of data generated from numerous devices and handling complex problems in social infrastructures. As AI and IoT technologies mature, we propose applying AIoT technologies to traffic light control, a crucial component of intelligent transportation systems, to enhance the efficiency of smart city road systems. Specifically, various sensors, including surveillance cameras, provide real-time information for intelligent traffic light control systems to monitor both motorized and non-motorized traffic conditions. We introduce an intelligent traffic light control solution using distributed multi-agent Q-learning, considering traffic information at neighboring intersections as well as local motorized and non-motorized traffic, to improve the overall performance of the entire control system. Our solution, utilizing the proposed multi-agent Q-learning algorithm, aims to optimize both motorized and non-motorized traffic. Additionally, we incorporated numerous real-world constraints/rules for traffic light control into the learning algorithm, facilitating the deployment of our solution in real operational scenarios. Numerical simulations were conducted on a real-world map using real-world traffic data. The simulation results demonstrate that our proposed solution outperforms existing solutions in terms of vehicle and pedestrian queue lengths, waiting time at intersections, and various other key performance metrics.
label: AI

title: Extreme Dimension Reduction for Handling Covariate Shift
Abstract: In the covariate shift learning scenario, the training and test covariate distributions differ, causing a predictor's average loss over the training and test distributions to diverge. This work investigates the potential of extreme dimension reduction, i.e., to very low dimensions, in improving the performance of importance weighting methods for handling covariate shift. These methods struggle in high dimensions due to potentially high train/test covariate divergence and the inability to accurately estimate the required density ratios. We first formulate and solve a problem that optimizes a combination of predictive utility and train/test divergence within linear subspaces. Applying this approach to simulated and real data, we show that extreme dimension reduction sometimes helps, but not always, due to a bias introduced by the dimension reduction process.

title: NPC: Neighbors Progressive Competition Algorithm for Classification of Imbalanced Data Sets
Abstract: Learning from numerous real-world datasets is often hampered by the class imbalance problem. A dataset is imbalanced when one class (the majority class) has significantly more samples than the other class (the minority class). Such datasets cause typical machine learning algorithms to perform poorly on the classification task. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach called Neighbors Progressive Competition (NPC) for classifying imbalanced datasets. While inspired by weighted k-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) algorithms, NPC has key differences. Unlike k-NN, NPC doesn't limit its decision criteria to a fixed number of nearest neighbors. Instead, NPC progressively considers more neighbors of the query sample in its decision-making until the sum of grades for one class significantly outweighs the other classes. Furthermore, NPC uses a novel method for grading training samples to compensate for the imbalance issue. These grades are calculated using both local and global information. In short, this paper introduces an entirely new classifier for effectively handling the imbalance issue without any manually set parameters or expert knowledge. Experimental results compare the proposed approach with five representative algorithms applied to fifteen imbalanced datasets, illustrating the algorithm's effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for De-Novo Drug Design
Abstract: We propose a novel computational strategy for de novo design of molecules with desired properties called ReLeaSE (Reinforcement Learning for Structural Evolution). Based on deep and reinforcement learning approaches, ReLeaSE integrates two deep neural networks - generative and predictive - that are trained separately but employed jointly to generate novel targeted chemical libraries. ReLeaSE uses a simple representation of molecules as SMILES strings. Generative models are trained with stack-augmented memory networks to produce chemically feasible SMILES strings, while predictive models are derived to forecast the desired properties of the de novo generated compounds. In the first phase of the method, generative and predictive models are trained separately using a supervised learning algorithm. In the second phase, both models are trained jointly with the reinforcement learning approach to bias the generation of new chemical structures towards those with the desired physical and/or biological properties. In the proof-of-concept study, we have employed the ReLeaSE method to design chemical libraries biased towards structural complexity or towards compounds with either maximal, minimal, or specific ranges of physical properties such as melting point or hydrophobicity, as well as to develop novel putative inhibitors of JAK2. The approach proposed herein can find a general use for generating targeted chemical libraries of novel compounds optimized for either a single desired property or multiple properties.

title: Saliency Weighted Convolutional Features for Instance Search
Abstract: This work explores attention models to weigh the contribution of local convolutional representations for the instance search task. We present a retrieval framework based on bags of local convolutional features (BLCF) that benefits from saliency weighting to build an efficient image representation. The use of human visual attention models (saliency) allows for significant improvements in retrieval performance without the need for region analysis or spatial verification, and without requiring any feature fine-tuning. We investigate the impact of different saliency models, finding that higher performance on saliency benchmarks doesn't necessarily equate to improved performance when used in instance search tasks. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art on the challenging INSTRE benchmark by a large margin, and provides similar performance on the Oxford and Paris benchmarks compared to more complex methods that use off-the-shelf representations. The source code used in this project is available at https://imatge-upc.github.io/salbow/.

title: Efficient exploration with Double Uncertain Value Networks
Abstract: This paper studies directed exploration for reinforcement learning agents by tracking uncertainty about the value of each available action. We identify two sources of uncertainty relevant for exploration. The first originates from limited data (parametric uncertainty), while the second stems from the distribution of returns (return uncertainty). We identify methods to learn these distributions with deep neural networks, where we estimate parametric uncertainty with Bayesian drop-out, while return uncertainty is propagated through the Bellman equation as a Gaussian distribution. We then identify that both can be jointly estimated in one network, which we call the Double Uncertain Value Network. The policy is directly derived from the learned distributions based on Thompson sampling. Experimental results show that both types of uncertainty can vastly improve learning in domains with a strong exploration challenge.
label: AI

title: Leveraging Conversation Structure on Social Media to Identify Potentially Influential Users
Abstract: Social networks often have a community providing feedback on comments, allowing identification of opinion leaders and users whose positions are unwelcome. Other platforms lack such tools. Assessing the community's reactions to published content is a non-trivial problem. This work proposes a novel approach using Abstract Argumentation Frameworks and machine learning to describe interactions between users. Our experiments provide evidence that modeling the flow of a conversation with AAF primitives can support the identification of users who produce consistently appreciated content without directly modeling the content itself.
label: AI

title: Representation Learning for Scale-free Networks
Abstract: Network embedding aims to learn low-dimensional representations of vertices in a network while preserving the network's structure and inherent properties. Existing network embedding works primarily focus on preserving microscopic structure, such as first- and second-order proximity of vertices, largely ignoring the macroscopic scale-free property. The scale-free property reflects the fact that vertex degrees follow a heavy-tailed distribution (i.e., only a few vertices have high degrees), which is a critical property of real-world networks, such as social networks. This paper studies the problem of learning representations for scale-free networks. We first theoretically analyze the difficulty of embedding and reconstructing a scale-free network in the Euclidean space, by converting our problem to the sphere packing problem. Then, we propose the "degree penalty" principle for designing scale-free property preserving network embedding algorithms: punishing the proximity between high-degree vertices. We introduce two implementations of our principle using spectral techniques and a skip-gram model, respectively. Extensive experiments on six datasets show that our algorithms are able to not only reconstruct heavy-tailed distributed degree distribution but also outperform state-of-the-art embedding models in various network mining tasks, such as vertex classification and link prediction.

title: RoboJam: A Musical Mixture Density Network for Collaborative Touchscreen Interaction
Abstract: RoboJam is a machine-learning system for generating music that assists users of a touchscreen music app by performing responses to their short improvisations. This system uses a recurrent artificial neural network to generate sequences of touchscreen interactions and absolute timings, rather than high-level musical notes. To achieve this, RoboJam's network employs a mixture density layer to predict appropriate touch interaction locations in space and time. This paper describes the design and implementation of RoboJam's network and its integration into a touchscreen music app. A preliminary evaluation analyzes the system in terms of training, musical generation, and user interaction.
label: AI

title: PSIque: Next Sequence Prediction of Satellite Images using a Convolutional Sequence-to-Sequence Network
Abstract: Predicting unseen weather phenomena is a critical issue for disaster management. This paper proposes a model using a convolutional sequence-to-sequence autoencoder to predict undiscovered weather situations from previous satellite images. We also introduce a symmetric skip connection between encoder and decoder modules to produce more comprehensive image predictions. To evaluate our model's performance, we conducted experiments for each proposed model to predict future satellite images from historical satellite images. A specific combination of skip connection and sequence-to-sequence autoencoder was able to generate the closest prediction to the ground truth image.
label: AI

title: TensorFlow Distributions
Abstract: The TensorFlow Distributions library implements a vision of probability theory adapted to the modern deep-learning paradigm of end-to-end differentiable computation. Built on two basic abstractions, it offers flexible building blocks for probabilistic computation. Distributions provide fast, numerically stable methods for generating samples and computing statistics, e.g., log density. Bijectors provide composable volume-tracking transformations with automatic caching. Together, these enable modular construction of high-dimensional distributions and transformations not possible with previous libraries (e.g., pixelCNNs, autoregressive flows, and reversible residual networks). They are the workhorse behind deep probabilistic programming systems like Edward and empower fast black-box inference in probabilistic models built on deep-network components. TensorFlow Distributions has proven an important part of the TensorFlow toolkit within Google and the broader deep learning community.
label: AI

title: Intent-Aware Contextual Recommendation System
Abstract: Recommender systems take inputs from user history, use an internal ranking algorithm to generate results, and potentially optimize this ranking based on feedback. However, recommender systems are often unaware of the user's actual intent and simply provide recommendations dynamically without fully understanding the user's thought process. An intelligent recommender system is beneficial not only for the user but also for businesses seeking to understand user tendencies. Discovering user tendencies or intents is a challenging problem. To address this challenge, we aimed to create an intelligent system that tracks user activity on a web application and determines the user's intent in each session. We devised a method to encode user activity across sessions, then represented the information seen by the user in a high-dimensional format, which is reduced to lower dimensions using tensor factorization techniques. Intent awareness (or scoring) is addressed at this stage. Finally, combining user activity data with contextual information provides a recommendation score. The final recommendations are then ranked using filtering and collaborative recommendation techniques to show the top-k recommendations to the user. The system also incorporates feedback, informing the model to update the various weights in the recommender system. Our overall model aims to combine both frequency-based and context-based recommendation systems and quantify user intent to provide better recommendations. We conducted experiments on real-world timestamped user activity data, in the context of recommending reports to users of a business analytics tool, and the results surpass the baselines. We also fine-tuned certain aspects of our model to achieve optimized results.
label: AI

title: A reinforcement learning algorithm for building collaboration in multi-agent systems
Abstract: This paper presents a proof-of-concept study demonstrating the viability of building collaboration among multiple agents using a standard Q-learning algorithm embedded in particle swarm optimization. Collaboration is formulated to be achieved through a degree of competition, where agents are expected to balance their actions in a way that prevents any of them from drifting away from the team or intruding on fellow neighbors' territories. Particles are equipped with a Q-learning algorithm for self-training, learning how to act as members of a swarm and how to produce collaborative/collective behaviors. The generated results support the algorithmic structures, suggesting that substantive collaboration can be built through the proposed learning algorithm.
label: AI

title: Wisdom of the crowd from unsupervised dimension reduction
Abstract: The wisdom of the crowd, the collective intelligence derived from responses of multiple human or machine individuals to the same questions, can be more accurate than each individual and improve social decision-making and prediction accuracy. This can also integrate multiple programs or datasets, each as an individual, for the same predictive questions. Crowd wisdom estimates each individual's independent error level arising from their limited knowledge and finds the crowd consensus that minimizes the overall error. However, previous studies have merely built isolated, problem-specific models with limited generalizability, mainly for binary (yes/no) responses. This paper shows, through simulation and real-world data, that the crowd wisdom problem is analogous to one-dimensional unsupervised dimension reduction in machine learning. This provides a natural class of crowd wisdom solutions, such as principal component analysis and Isomap, which can handle both binary and continuous responses, like confidence levels, and consequently can be more accurate than existing solutions. They can even outperform supervised-learning-based collective intelligence that is calibrated on historical performance of individuals, e.g., penalized linear regression and random forest. This study unifies crowd wisdom and unsupervised dimension reduction, introducing a broad range of highly-performing and widely-applicable crowd wisdom methods. As the costs for data acquisition and processing rapidly decrease, this study will promote and guide crowd wisdom applications in the social and natural sciences, including data fusion, meta-analysis, crowd-sourcing, and committee decision making. |||

title: Physics Informed Deep Learning (Part II): Data-driven Discovery of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are neural networks trained to solve supervised learning tasks while adhering to physical laws described by nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). This second part of a two-part treatise focuses on data-driven PDE discovery.  We introduce two primary algorithmic classes, continuous time and discrete time models, depending on whether the data is spatially and temporally scattered or arranged in fixed temporal snapshots. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach using various benchmark problems in mathematical physics, encompassing conservation laws, incompressible fluid flow, and nonlinear shallow-water wave propagation.
label: AI

title: FearNet: Brain-Inspired Model for Incremental Learning
Abstract: Incremental class learning involves sequentially learning classes in bursts of examples from the same class. This violates the assumptions underlying standard deep neural network training methods, leading to catastrophic forgetting. While iCaRL is arguably the best method for incremental class learning, it requires storing training examples for each class, making it difficult to scale. We propose FearNet for incremental class learning, a generative model that is memory efficient by not storing previous examples. FearNet utilizes a brain-inspired dual-memory system, where new memories are consolidated from a recent memory network (inspired by the mammalian hippocampal complex) to a long-term storage network (inspired by the medial prefrontal cortex).  This memory consolidation is inspired by sleep-related mechanisms. FearNet also incorporates a module inspired by the basolateral amygdala to determine which memory system is used for recall.  FearNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on image (CIFAR-100, CUB-200) and audio classification (AudioSet) benchmarks.

title: Physics Informed Deep Learning (Part I): Data-driven Solutions of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are neural networks trained to solve supervised learning tasks while respecting any given law of physics described by general nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). This two-part treatise presents our developments in solving two primary classes of problems: data-driven solution and data-driven discovery of PDEs. We develop two distinct classes of algorithms, continuous time and discrete time models, based on the nature and arrangement of the available data. The resulting neural networks form a novel class of data-efficient universal function approximators that inherently encode any underlying physical laws as prior information. This first part demonstrates how these networks can be used to infer solutions to PDEs and obtain physics-informed surrogate models fully differentiable with respect to all input coordinates and free parameters.
label: AI

title: A Recursive Bayesian Approach To Describe Retinal Vasculature Geometry
Abstract: Demographic studies indicate that changes in retinal vasculature geometry, particularly vessel width, are associated with the incidence or progression of eye-related and systemic diseases.  Traditionally, width estimation from fundus images has relied on intensity profiles between vessel edges. However, factors such as pathologies, central light reflex, and local illumination levels can significantly influence intensity profiles. In this study, we introduce three information sources for width estimation: probability profiles of vessel interior, centerline, and edge locations generated by a deep network. These probability profiles provide direct access to vessel geometry and are used in likelihood calculations for a Bayesian method, particle filtering. We also introduce a geometric model capable of handling non-ideal conditions in the probability profiles.  Experiments on the REVIEW dataset yielded consistent estimates of vessel width, even in cases where one of the vessel edges is difficult to identify. Moreover, our results suggest that the method outperforms human observers in locating the edges of low-contrast vessels.
label: AI

title: La production de nitrites lors de la dénitrification des eaux usées par biofiltration - Stratégie de contrôle et de réduction des concentrations résiduelles
Abstract: The increasing popularity of post-denitrification processes in wastewater treatment plants in the greater Paris area has led to a resurgence of nitrite in the Seine river. Controlling nitrite production during post-denitrification has become a critical technical challenge. Research within the MOCOPEE program (www.mocopee.com) investigates the underlying mechanisms behind nitrite production during wastewater denitrification and develops technical tools (measurement and control solutions) to facilitate on-site nitrite reduction. Prior studies have revealed that typical methanol dosage strategies result in varying carbon-to-nitrogen ratios in the reactor, leading to unstable nitrite concentrations in the effluent. The possibility of adding a model-free control to the existing classical dosage strategy has been tested using the SimBio model, which simulates wastewater biofilter behavior.  The corresponding "intelligent" feedback loop, which utilizes effluent nitrite concentrations, compensates for the classical strategy only when necessary. Simulation results demonstrate a clear improvement in average nitrite concentration level and stability in the effluent without a significant increase in methanol usage.

title: Backprop as Functor: A compositional perspective on supervised learning
Abstract: A supervised learning algorithm searches over a set of functions $A \to B$ parameterized by a space $P$ to find the best approximation to an ideal function $f \colon A \to B$. This is achieved by using examples $(a,f(a)) \in A \times B$ and updating the parameter according to a specific rule.  We define a category where these update rules can be composed and show that gradient descent—with respect to a fixed step size and an error function satisfying a certain property—defines a monoidal functor from a category of parameterized functions to this category of update rules. This provides a structural perspective on backpropagation and a broad generalization of neural networks.
label: AI

title: Role of Deep LSTM Neural Networks And WiFi Networks in Support of Occupancy Prediction in Smart Buildings
Abstract: Knowing the number of occupants in a building and their location is essential for smart building services. Commercial, industrial, and residential buildings often incorporate systems for occupancy determination. However, relatively simple sensor technology and control algorithms limit the effectiveness of smart building services. In this paper, we propose replacing sensor technology with time series models that can predict the number of occupants at a specific location and time.  We utilize readily available Wi-Fi datasets for smart building services and train Auto Regression Integrating Moving Average (ARIMA) models and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) time series models.  As a use case scenario for smart building services, these models allow forecasting the number of people at a given time and location in 15, 30, and 60-minute time intervals at both the building and Access Point (AP) levels.  For LSTM, we construct models in two ways: a separate model for each time scale and a combined model for all three time scales. Our experiments demonstrate that the LSTM combined model reduces computational resources with respect to the number of neurons by 74.48% at the AP level and 67.13% at the building level. Moreover, the root mean square error (RMSE) was reduced by 88.2%-93.4% for LSTM compared to ARIMA for the building-level models and by 80.9%-87% for the AP level models.

title: Meteorology-Aware Multi-Goal Path Planning for Large-Scale Inspection Missions with Long-Endurance Solar-Powered Aircraft
Abstract: Solar-powered aircraft offer significantly increased flight endurance compared to conventional aircraft, making them promising candidates for large-scale aerial inspection missions. However, their structural fragility necessitates the avoidance of adverse weather conditions through appropriate path planning methods. This paper introduces MetPASS, the Meteorology-aware Path Planning and Analysis Software for Solar-powered UAVs. MetPASS is the first path planning framework in the literature to consider all aspects influencing the safety and performance of solar-powered flight. It avoids environmental risks (thunderstorms, rain, wind, wind gusts, and humidity) and exploits advantageous regions (high sun radiation or tailwind). It also avoids system risks such as low battery state of charge and returns safe paths through cluttered terrain. MetPASS imports weather data from global meteorological models, propagates the aircraft state through an energetic system model, and combines both into a cost function. A combination of dynamic programming techniques and an A*-search algorithm with a custom heuristic is leveraged to plan globally optimal paths in station-keeping, point-to-point, or multi-goal aerial inspection missions with coverage guarantees. A full software implementation, including a GUI, is provided.  The planning methods are verified using three missions of ETH Zurich's AtlantikSolar UAV: an 81-hour continuous solar-powered station-keeping flight, a 4000km Atlantic crossing from Newfoundland to Portugal, and two multi-glacier aerial inspection missions above the Arctic Ocean performed near Greenland in summer 2017.

title: Classification of entities via their descriptive sentences
Abstract: Hypernym identification of open-domain entities is crucial for taxonomy construction and numerous higher-level applications. Existing methods suffer from either low precision or low recall. To mitigate this challenge, we adopt a classification-based approach. We pre-define a concept taxonomy and classify an entity to one of its leaf concepts based on the entity's name and description information. A convolutional neural network classifier and a K-means clustering module are employed for classification.  We applied this system to 2.1 million Baidu Baike entities, successfully identifying 1.1 million with a precision of 99.36%.

title: Crossmodal Attentive Skill Learner
Abstract: This paper introduces the Crossmodal Attentive Skill Learner (CASL), integrated with the recently introduced Asynchronous Advantage Option-Critic (A2OC) architecture [Harb et al., 2017] to enable hierarchical reinforcement learning across multiple sensory inputs. We provide concrete examples where the approach not only improves performance in a single task but also accelerates transfer to new tasks.  We demonstrate that the attention mechanism anticipates and identifies useful latent features while filtering irrelevant sensor modalities during execution.  We modify the Arcade Learning Environment [Bellemare et al., 2013] to support audio queries and conduct evaluations of crossmodal learning in the Atari 2600 game Amidar. Building on the recent work of Babaeizadeh et al. [2017], we open-source a fast hybrid CPU-GPU implementation of CASL.

title: The Price of Quota-based Diversity in Assignment Problems
Abstract: We introduce and analyze an extension to the matching problem on a weighted bipartite graph: Assignment with Type Constraints. The two parts of the graph are partitioned into subsets called types and blocks; we seek a matching with the largest sum of weights under the constraint that there is a pre-specified cap on the number of vertices matched in every type-block pair. Our primary motivation stems from Singapore's public housing program, which accounts for over 70% of its residential real estate. To promote ethnic diversity within its housing projects, Singapore imposes ethnicity quotas: each new housing development comprises blocks of flats, and each ethnicity-based group in the population must not own more than a certain percentage of flats in a block. Other domains utilizing similar hard capacity constraints include matching prospective students to schools or medical residents to hospitals. Limiting agents' choices for ensuring diversity in this manner naturally entails some welfare loss.  One of our goals is to study the trade-off between diversity and social welfare in such settings. We first show that, while the classic assignment program is polynomial-time computable, adding diversity constraints makes it computationally intractable; however, we identify a $\tfrac{1}{2}$-approximation algorithm, as well as reasonable assumptions on the weights that permit polynomial-time algorithms. Next, we provide two upper bounds on the price of diversity—a measure of the loss in welfare incurred by imposing diversity constraints—as functions of natural problem parameters. We conclude the paper with simulations based on publicly available data from two diversity-constrained allocation problems—Singapore Public Housing and Chicago School Choice—which shed light on how the constrained maximization as well as lottery-based variants perform in practice.
label: AI

title: Learning to Rank based on Analogical Reasoning
Abstract: Object ranking or "learning to rank" is an important problem in preference learning. Based on training data in the form of a set of rankings of objects represented as feature vectors, the goal is to learn a ranking function that predicts a linear order of any new set of objects. In this paper, we propose a new approach to object ranking based on principles of analogical reasoning.  More specifically, our inference pattern is formalized in terms of so-called analogical proportions and can be summarized as follows: Given objects $A,B,C,D$, if object $A$ is known to be preferred to $B$, and $C$ relates to $D$ as $A$ relates to $B$, then $C$ is (supposedly) preferred to $D$. Our method applies this pattern as a main building block and combines it with ideas and techniques from instance-based learning and rank aggregation. Based on initial experimental results for datasets from various domains (sports, education, tourism, etc.), we conclude that our approach is highly competitive. It appears to be particularly interesting in situations where the objects come from different subdomains, requiring a type of knowledge transfer.
label: AI

title: Visualisation and 'diagnostic classifiers' reveal how recurrent and recursive neural networks process hierarchical structure
Abstract: We investigate how neural networks can learn and process languages with hierarchical, compositional semantics. To this end, we define the artificial task of processing nested arithmetic expressions and study whether different types of neural networks can learn to compute their meaning.  We find that recursive neural networks can discover a generalizing solution to this problem, and we visualize this solution by breaking it down into three steps: project, sum, and squash. As a next step, we investigate recurrent neural networks and show that a gated recurrent unit, which processes its input incrementally, also performs very well on this task. To understand what the recurrent network encodes, visualization techniques alone are insufficient. Therefore, we develop an approach where we formulate and test multiple hypotheses on the information encoded and processed by the network.  For each hypothesis, we derive predictions about features of the hidden state representations at each time step and train "diagnostic classifiers" to test those predictions.  Our results indicate that the networks follow a strategy similar to our hypothesized "cumulative strategy," which explains the high accuracy of the network on novel expressions, the generalization to longer expressions than seen in training, and the mild deterioration with increasing length. This, in turn, shows that diagnostic classifiers can be a useful technique for opening up the black box of neural networks.  We argue that diagnostic classification, unlike most visualization techniques, scales up from small networks in a toy domain to larger and deeper recurrent networks dealing with real-life data, and may therefore contribute to a better understanding of the internal dynamics of current state-of-the-art models in natural language processing.
label: AI

title: Hyper-dimensional computing for a visual question-answering system that is trainable end-to-end
Abstract: This work proposes a system for visual question answering. Our architecture consists of two parts. The first part creates the logical knowledge base given the image.  The second part evaluates questions against the knowledge base. Unlike previous work, the knowledge base is represented using hyper-dimensional computing. This choice has the advantage that all operations in the system, namely creating the knowledge base and evaluating questions against it, are differentiable, making the system easily trainable in an end-to-end fashion.
label: AI

title: Gradual Tuning: a better way of Fine Tuning the parameters of a Deep Neural Network
Abstract: This paper presents an alternative strategy for fine-tuning the parameters of a network called Gradual Tuning. Once trained on a first task, the network is fine-tuned on a second task by modifying a progressively larger set of the network's parameters.  We test Gradual Tuning on different transfer learning tasks, using networks of varying sizes trained with different regularization techniques.  The results show that, compared to usual fine-tuning, our approach significantly reduces catastrophic forgetting of the initial task while retaining comparable or even better performance on the new task.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical Policy Search via Return-Weighted Density Estimation
Abstract: Learning an optimal policy from a multi-modal reward function is a challenging problem in reinforcement learning (RL). Hierarchical RL (HRL) tackles this problem by learning a hierarchical policy, where multiple option policies are in charge of different strategies corresponding to modes of a reward function, and a gating policy selects the best option for a given context. Although HRL has shown promise, current state-of-the-art methods struggle to perform well in complex real-world problems due to the difficulty of identifying reward function modes. This paper proposes a novel method called hierarchical policy search via return-weighted density estimation (HPSDE), which can efficiently identify modes through density estimation with return-weighted importance sampling. Our proposed method finds option policies corresponding to the modes of the return function and automatically determines the number and location of option policies, significantly reducing the burden of hyperparameter tuning.  Through experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed HPSDE successfully learns option policies corresponding to modes of the return function and can be successfully applied to a challenging motion planning problem of a redundant robotic manipulator.

title: Digital Encyclopedia of Scientific Results
Abstract: This study presents a vision for how technology can enhance research efficiency. We propose a new clean-slate design that prioritizes the correctness and up-to-dateness of scientific results, is more open to new ideas, and better utilizes research efforts worldwide by providing personalized interfaces for each researcher. The key idea is to reveal the structure and connections of the problems solved in scientific studies. We will build the system with a primary focus on the solved problems themselves, treating studies as just one presentation form. By utilizing artificial intelligence and machine learning on the network of solved problems, we could coordinate individual research activities on a large scale never seen before.
label: AI

title: Intelligent Notification Systems: A Survey of the State of the Art and Research Challenges
Abstract: Notifications offer a unique mechanism for enhancing the effectiveness of real-time information delivery systems. However, notifications that demand users' attention at inopportune moments are more likely to have adverse effects and may become disruptive rather than beneficial to users. To address these challenges, various intelligent notification mechanisms based on monitoring and learning user behavior have been proposed. The goal of such mechanisms is to maximize user receptivity to the delivered information by automatically inferring the optimal time and context for sending a specific type of information. This article provides an overview of the current state of the art in the area of intelligent notification mechanisms that rely on awareness of user context and preferences.  Specifically, we first present a survey of studies focusing on understanding and modeling user interruptibility and receptivity to notifications from desktops and mobile devices. Then, we discuss the existing challenges and opportunities in developing mechanisms for intelligent notification systems in various application scenarios.
label: AI

title: QCBA: Improving Rule Classifiers Learned from Quantitative Data by Recovering Information Lost by Discretisation
Abstract: Prediscretization of numerical attributes, a requirement for certain rule learning algorithms, can introduce inefficiencies. This paper describes new rule tuning steps that aim to recover lost information during discretization and new pruning techniques that may further reduce the size of rule models and improve their accuracy.  The proposed QCBA method was initially developed to post-process quantitative attributes in models generated by the Classification based on associations (CBA) algorithm but can also be applied to the results of other rule learning approaches. We demonstrate its effectiveness on the post-processing of models generated by five association rule classification algorithms (CBA, CMAR, CPAR, IDS, SBRL) and two first-order logic rule learners (FOIL2 and PRM). Benchmarks on 22 datasets from the UCI repository show a smaller size and the overall best predictive performance for FOIL2+QCBA compared to all seven baselines. Post-optimized CBA models exhibit better predictive performance compared to the state-of-the-art rule learner CORELS in this benchmark. The article includes an ablation study for the individual post-processing steps and a scalability analysis on the KDD'99 Anomaly detection dataset.
label: AI

title: One-Shot Reinforcement Learning for Robot Navigation with Interactive Replay
Abstract: Model-free reinforcement learning algorithms have recently demonstrated the ability to solve challenging problems by learning from extensive interaction with the environment.  A significant challenge in transferring this success to the robotics domain is that real-world interaction is costly, while training on limited experience is prone to overfitting. We present a method for learning to navigate to a fixed goal in a known environment on a mobile robot.  The robot leverages an interactive world model built from a single traversal of the environment, a pre-trained visual feature encoder, and stochastic environmental augmentation to demonstrate successful zero-shot transfer under real-world environmental variations without fine-tuning. |||

title: Learning to cluster in order to transfer across domains and tasks
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for transfer learning across domains and tasks by framing it as a clustering problem. The key idea is that, in addition to features, we can transfer similarity information, which is sufficient to learn a similarity function and clustering network for both domain adaptation and cross-task transfer learning.  We begin by converting categorical information into pairwise constraints, which simply indicate whether two instances belong to the same class. This similarity is category-agnostic and can be learned from source domain data using a similarity network. We propose two novel approaches for transfer learning using this similarity function. First, for unsupervised domain adaptation, we introduce a new loss function to regularize classification with a constrained clustering loss, leading to a clustering network that uses the transferred similarity metric to generate training inputs. Second, for cross-task learning (unsupervised clustering with unseen categories), we propose a framework for reconstructing and estimating the number of semantic clusters, again using the clustering network. As the similarity network is noisy, the key is to use a robust clustering algorithm. We demonstrate that our formulation is more robust than alternative constrained and unconstrained clustering approaches. Using this method, we achieve state-of-the-art results for the challenging cross-task problem on Omniglot and ImageNet, demonstrating the ability to reconstruct semantic clusters with high accuracy. We further evaluate cross-domain transfer performance using images from the Office-31 and SVHN-MNIST tasks and present top accuracy on both datasets. Notably, our approach does not explicitly address domain discrepancy. However, combining it with a domain adaptation loss yields further improvement.
label: AI

title: Homomorphic Parameter Compression for Distributed Deep Learning Training
Abstract: Distributed training of deep neural networks has gained significant attention, with major approaches including implementations on multiple GPUs and clusters. Parallelization can dramatically improve the efficiency of training deep and complex models with large-scale data. However, a fundamental challenge hindering the speedup of DNN training is the trade-off between computation and communication time. Increasing the number of worker nodes reduces computation time but simultaneously increases communication overhead under limited network bandwidth, particularly in commodity hardware environments. To alleviate this trade-off, we propose the concept of homomorphic parameter compression, which compresses parameters with minimal expense and trains the DNN using the compressed representation. While the specific method remains to be discovered, we demonstrate a high probability that homomorphism can reduce communication overhead due to minimal compression and decompression times. We also provide theoretical speedup estimates for homomorphic compression.
label: AI

title: Machine Learning based Intelligent Cognitive Network using Fog Computing
Abstract: This paper proposes a Cognitive Radio Network (CRN) based on artificial intelligence for more efficient distribution of limited radio spectrum resources. The CRN framework utilizes fog computing with different machine learning techniques to analyze time-sensitive signal data close to the signal source. Depending on the computational capabilities of the fog nodes, different features and machine learning techniques are selected to optimize spectrum allocation. Furthermore, the computing nodes send periodic signal summaries, which are much smaller than the original signal, to the cloud for dynamically updating the overall system spectrum source allocation strategies. By leveraging fog computing, the system becomes more adaptive to the local environment and robust to spectrum changes. As most signal data is processed at the fog level, it further strengthens system security by reducing the communication burden of the communication network.
label: AI

title: Tensor Completion Algorithms in Big Data Analytics
Abstract: Tensor completion addresses the problem of filling in missing or unobserved entries in partially observed tensors. Given the multidimensional nature of tensors in representing complex datasets, tensor completion algorithms and their applications have gained widespread attention and success in areas such as data mining, computer vision, signal processing, and neuroscience. This survey provides a modern overview of recent advancements in tensor completion algorithms from the perspective of big data analytics, characterized by diverse variety, large volume, and high velocity. We classify these advancements from four perspectives: general tensor completion algorithms, tensor completion with auxiliary information (variety), scalable tensor completion algorithms (volume), and dynamic tensor completion algorithms (velocity). Additionally, we identify several tensor completion applications in real-world data-driven problems and present common experimental frameworks prevalent in the literature. Our objective is to summarize these popular methods and introduce them to researchers and practitioners, promoting future research and applications. We conclude with a discussion of key challenges and promising research directions in this community for future exploration.
label: AI

title: Big Data Analytics, Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence in Next-Generation Wireless Networks
Abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are evolving into highly complex systems due to diverse service requirements and heterogeneity in applications, devices, and networks. Mobile network operators (MNOs) need to optimize the use of available resources, such as power, spectrum, and infrastructure. Traditional networking approaches, including reactive, centrally managed, one-size-fits-all approaches and conventional data analysis tools with limited capability (space and time), are no longer sufficient to address the complexities of future networks in terms of cost-effective operation and optimization. A novel paradigm of proactive, self-aware, self-adaptive, and predictive networking is urgently needed. MNOs have access to vast amounts of data, especially from the network and subscribers. Systematic exploitation of big data significantly contributes to creating a smart, intelligent network, enabling cost-effective operation and optimization. In this context, we propose a data-driven next-generation wireless network model where MNOs utilize advanced data analytics for their networks. We discuss data sources and compelling drivers for adopting data analytics and the role of machine learning and artificial intelligence in making the network intelligent by enabling self-awareness, self-adaptation, proactive, and prescriptive capabilities. We present a set of network design and optimization schemes based on data analytics. The paper concludes with a discussion of challenges and benefits of adopting big data analytics and artificial intelligence in next-generation communication systems.
label: AI

title: Risk-sensitive Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Semi- and Non-Parametric Methods
Abstract: The literature on Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) typically assumes that humans act to minimize the expected value of a cost function, implying risk neutrality. However, in practice, humans often exhibit significant risk aversion. To bridge this gap, this paper aims to develop a framework for risk-sensitive IRL to explicitly account for human risk sensitivity. We propose a flexible class of models based on coherent risk measures, allowing us to capture a spectrum of risk preferences from risk-neutral to worst-case. We present efficient non-parametric algorithms based on linear programming and semi-parametric algorithms based on maximum likelihood for inferring a human's underlying risk measure and cost function in diverse static and dynamic decision-making settings. We demonstrate the approach using a simulated driving game with ten human participants. Our method effectively infers and mimics a wide range of qualitatively different driving styles, from highly risk-averse to risk-neutral, in a data-efficient manner. Comparisons of the Risk-Sensitive (RS) IRL approach with a risk-neutral model show that the RS-IRL framework more accurately captures observed participant behavior both qualitatively and quantitatively, particularly in scenarios with potential catastrophic outcomes, such as collisions.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Generative Adversarial Networks for Proximal Learning and Automated Compressive Image Recovery
Abstract: Recovering images from undersampled linear measurements typically poses an ill-posed linear inverse problem requiring appropriate statistical priors. Designing effective priors is challenging due to limited training and testing overhead in real-time tasks and the need to retrieve visually "plausible" and physically "feasible" images with minimal hallucination. To address these challenges, we propose a cascaded network architecture that unrolls the proximal gradient iterations by integrating benefits from generative residual networks (ResNet) into proximal operator modeling. A combination of pixel-wise and perceptual costs is then employed to train the proximals. The overall architecture resembles back-and-forth projection onto the intersection of feasible and plausible images. Extensive computational experiments are conducted for a global task of reconstructing MR images of pediatric patients and a more local task of superresolving CelebA faces, providing valuable insights into designing efficient architectures. Our observations suggest that for MRI reconstruction, a recurrent ResNet with a single residual block effectively learns the proximal. This simple architecture significantly outperforms alternative deep ResNet architectures by 2dB SNR and conventional compressed-sensing MRI by 4dB SNR with 100x faster inference. For image superresolution, our preliminary results indicate that modeling the denoising proximal requires deep ResNets.
label: AI

title: AI Safety Gridworlds
Abstract: This work presents a suite of reinforcement learning environments illustrating various safety properties of intelligent agents. These problems include safe interruptibility, avoiding side effects, absent supervisor, reward gaming, safe exploration, as well as robustness to self-modification, distributional shift, and adversaries. To measure compliance with intended safe behavior, we equip each environment with a hidden performance function. This allows us to categorize AI safety problems into robustness and specification problems, depending on whether the performance function aligns with the observed reward function. We evaluate A2C and Rainbow, two recent deep reinforcement learning agents, on our environments and demonstrate that they are unable to solve them satisfactorily.
label: AI

title: Distilling a Neural Network Into a Soft Decision Tree
Abstract: Deep neural networks have proven to be highly effective for classification tasks. They excel when the input data is high-dimensional, the relationship between input and output is complex, and the number of labeled training examples is large. However, explaining why a learned network makes a specific classification decision on a particular test case remains challenging due to their reliance on distributed hierarchical representations. If we could translate the knowledge acquired by the neural network into a model based on hierarchical decisions, explaining a particular decision would be much easier. We describe a method for using a trained neural network to create a type of soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from the training data.
label: AI

title: GazeGAN - Unpaired Adversarial Image Generation for Gaze Estimation
Abstract: Recent research has demonstrated the ability to estimate gaze on mobile devices by performing inference on the image from the phone's front-facing camera without requiring specialized hardware. While this offers significant potential applications in human-computer interaction, medical diagnosis, and accessibility (e.g., hands-free gaze input for patients with motor disorders), current methods are limited by their reliance on data collection from real users, which is a tedious, expensive, and difficult-to-scale process across devices. Some attempts to synthesize eye region data using 3D models, simulating various head poses and camera settings, lack realism. This paper improves upon a recently suggested method and proposes a generative adversarial framework to generate a large dataset of high-resolution, colorful images with high diversity (e.g., in subjects, head pose, camera settings) and realism while preserving the accuracy of gaze labels. The proposed approach operates on extended regions of the eye and even completes missing image parts. Using this rich synthesized dataset, and without using any additional training data from real users, we demonstrate improvements over state-of-the-art for estimating 2D gaze position on mobile devices. We further demonstrate cross-device generalization of model performance and improved robustness to diverse head pose, blur, and distance.
label: AI

title: How linguistic descriptions of data can help to the teaching-learning process in higher education, case of study: artificial intelligence
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence is a central topic in the computer science curriculum. Since 2011, a project-based learning methodology based on computer games has been designed and implemented in the artificial intelligence course at the University of the Bio-Bio. The project focuses on developing software-controlled agents (bots) programmed using heuristic algorithms covered during the course. This methodology delivers effective learning results, but several challenges have been encountered during implementation. This paper explores how linguistic descriptions of data can provide students and teachers with technical and personalized feedback on learned algorithms. It proposes an algorithm behavior profile and a new Turing test for computer game bots based on linguistic modeling of complex phenomena to address these challenges. To demonstrate and explore the possibilities of this new technology, a web platform has been designed and implemented by one of the authors. Its integration into the assessment process enhances the teaching-learning process.
label: AI

title: Table-to-text Generation by Structure-aware Seq2seq Learning
Abstract: Table-to-text generation aims to generate a description for a factual table, which can be viewed as a set of field-value records. To encode both the content and structure of a table, we propose a novel structure-aware seq2seq architecture consisting of a field-gating encoder and a description generator with dual attention. During encoding, we update the cell memory of the LSTM unit using a field gate and its corresponding field value to incorporate field information into the table representation. In the decoding phase, we introduce a dual attention mechanism, including word-level attention and field-level attention, to model the semantic relevance between the generated description and the table. We conduct experiments on the WIKIBIO dataset, which contains over 700k biographies and corresponding infoboxes from Wikipedia. Attention visualizations and case studies demonstrate that our model can generate coherent and informative descriptions based on a comprehensive understanding of both the content and structure of a table. Automatic evaluations show that our model significantly outperforms baselines. The code for this work is available at https://github.com/tyliupku/wiki2bio.
label: AI

title: Classifier Selection with Permutation Tests
Abstract: This work presents a content-based recommender system for machine learning classifier algorithms. Given a new dataset, it recommends the classifier most likely to perform best based on classifier performance on similar known datasets. Similarity is measured using a dataset characterization that includes several state-of-the-art metrics considering physical structure, statistics, and information theory. A novel aspect of this work is the use of a robust approach based on permutation tests to directly assess whether a given learning algorithm can exploit attributes in a dataset to predict class labels and compare it to the more commonly used F-score metric for evaluating classifier performance. To evaluate our approach, we conducted extensive experimentation involving 8 of the main machine learning classification methods with varying configurations and 65 binary datasets, resulting in over 2331 experiments. Our results demonstrate that utilizing information from the permutation test significantly improves the quality of recommendations.
label: AI

title: Production Ready Chatbots: Generate if not Retrieve
Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid model that combines a neural conversational model and a rule-based graph dialogue system to assist users in scheduling reminders through a chat conversation. The graph-based system offers high precision and grammatically accurate responses but has low recall. The neural conversation model can handle a variety of requests, generating responses word by word instead of using canned responses. The hybrid system exhibits significant improvements over the existing baseline system of rule-based approach and addresses complex queries using a domain-restricted neural model. Restricting the conversation topic and combining the graph-based retrieval system with a neural generative model make the final system robust enough for real-world application.
label: AI

title: Butterfly Effect: Bidirectional Control of Classification Performance by Small Additive Perturbation
Abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm for controlling classification results by generating a small additive perturbation without modifying the classifier network. Our work draws inspiration from existing research on generating adversarial perturbations that degrade classification performance. In contrast to existing methods, our work aims to generate perturbations that enhance overall classification performance. To solve this performance enhancement problem, we introduce a novel perturbation generation network (PGN) influenced by the adversarial learning strategy. In our problem, information from a large external dataset is summarized by a small additive perturbation, which helps improve the performance of the classifier trained with the target dataset. Besides this performance enhancement problem, we demonstrate that the proposed PGN can be adapted to solve the classical adversarial problem without using information about the target classifier. The aforementioned characteristics of our method are validated through extensive experiments on publicly available visual datasets.
label: AI

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Sepsis Treatment
Abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality in intensive care units and incurs billions in hospital costs annually. Treating a septic patient is highly challenging due to individual patient responses to medical interventions and the lack of a universally agreed-upon treatment for sepsis. This work proposes an approach to deduce treatment policies for septic patients using continuous state-space models and deep reinforcement learning. Our model learns clinically interpretable treatment policies that resemble physicians' treatment policies in significant aspects. The learned policies could assist intensive care clinicians in medical decision making and improve patient survival likelihood.
label: AI

title: Memory Aware Synapses: Learning what (not) to forget
Abstract: Humans can learn in a continuous manner, where old, rarely used knowledge can be overwritten by new incoming information while important, frequently used knowledge is protected from erasure. In artificial learning systems, lifelong learning has primarily focused on accumulating knowledge across tasks and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. This paper argues that, given limited model capacity and unlimited new information to be learned, knowledge preservation or erasure should be selective. Inspired by neuroplasticity, we propose a novel lifelong learning approach called Memory Aware Synapses (MAS). MAS computes the importance of neural network parameters in an unsupervised and online manner. Upon receiving a new sample, MAS accumulates an importance measure for each network parameter based on the sensitivity of the predicted output function to changes in that parameter. When learning a new task, changes to important parameters can be penalized, effectively preventing the overwriting of important knowledge related to previous tasks. Furthermore, we demonstrate an interesting connection between a local version of our method and Hebb's rule, a model for the learning process in the brain. We test our method on a sequence of object recognition tasks and the challenging problem of learning an embedding for predicting <subject, predicate, object> triplets. We show state-of-the-art performance and, for the first time, the ability to adapt parameter importance based on unlabeled data, aligning with the network's needs (not) to forget, which can vary depending on test conditions.
label: AI

title: Code Completion with Neural Attention and Pointer Networks
Abstract: Intelligent code completion has become a crucial research task to accelerate modern software development. To facilitate effective code completion for dynamically-typed programming languages, we employ neural language models trained on large codebases and develop a tailored attention mechanism for code completion. However, standard neural language models, even with an attention mechanism, cannot accurately predict out-of-vocabulary (OoV) words, limiting code completion performance. This paper, inspired by the prevalence of locally repeated terms in program source code and the recently proposed pointer copy mechanism, proposes a pointer mixture network for better predicting OoV words in code completion. Based on the context, the pointer mixture network learns to either generate a within-vocabulary word through an RNN component or regenerate an OoV word from local context through a pointer component. Experiments on two benchmarked datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our attention mechanism and pointer mixture network for code completion.
label: AI

title: Computational intelligence for qualitative coaching diagnostics: Automated assessment of tennis swings to improve performance and safety
Abstract: Coaching technology, wearables, and exergames can provide quantitative feedback based on measured activity, but there is limited evidence of qualitative feedback to aid technique improvement. To achieve personalized qualitative feedback, we developed a proof-of-concept prototype combining kinesiology and computational intelligence, which could help improve tennis swing technique using three-dimensional tennis motion data acquired from multi-camera video. Expert data labeling relied on virtual 3D stick figure replay. Diverse assessment criteria for novice to intermediate skill levels and configurable coaching scenarios, matched with a variety of tennis swings (22 backhands and 21 forehands), included good technique and common errors. A set of selected coaching rules was transferred to adaptive assessment modules capable of learning from data, evolving their internal structures, and producing autonomous personalized feedback, including verbal cues over virtual camera 3D replay and an end-of-session progress report. The prototype demonstrated autonomous assessment on future data based on learning from prior examples, aligned with skill level, flexible coaching scenarios, and coaching rules. The generated intuitive diagnostic feedback consisted of elements of safety and performance for tennis swing technique, where each swing sample was compared with the expert. For safety aspects of the relative swing width, the prototype showed improved assessment...
