title: HP-GAN: Probabilistic 3D human motion prediction via GAN
Abstract: Predicting and understanding human motion dynamics has numerous applications, including motion synthesis, augmented reality, security, and autonomous vehicles. Due to the recent success of generative adversarial networks (GANs), there has been significant interest in probabilistic estimation and synthetic data generation using deep neural network architectures and learning algorithms. This paper proposes a novel sequence-to-sequence model for probabilistic human motion prediction, trained with a modified version of improved Wasserstein generative adversarial networks (WGAN-GP), where we use a custom loss function designed for human motion prediction. Our model, called HP-GAN, learns a probability density function of future human poses conditioned on previous poses. It predicts multiple sequences of possible future human poses, each from the same input sequence but a different vector z drawn from a random distribution. Furthermore, to quantify the quality of non-deterministic predictions, we simultaneously train a motion-quality-assessment model that learns the probability that a given skeleton sequence represents real human motion. We test our algorithm on two of the largest skeleton datasets: NTURGB-D and Human3.6M. We train our model on both single and multiple action types. Its predictive power for long-term motion estimation is demonstrated by generating multiple plausible futures of more than 30 frames from just 10 frames of input. We show that most sequences generated from the same input have probabilities greater than 50% of being judged as a real human sequence. We will release all the code used in this paper on Github.|||

title: Pulsar Candidate Identification with Artificial Intelligence Techniques
Abstract: Discovering pulsars is a crucial research area in radio astronomy. The surge in data volume and rate generated by instruments like China's Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) necessitates the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for automatic pulsar candidate identification. This task aims to separate potential pulsar candidates from noise and radio frequency interferences. However, the performance of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) for pulsar identification is hindered by limited training samples and class imbalance. To overcome these challenges, we propose a framework combining deep convolution generative adversarial networks (DCGAN) with support vector machines (SVM). DCGAN generates samples and learns features, while SVM acts as a classifier. This framework addresses class imbalance and learns discriminative features, leading to improved accuracy in automatic pulsar candidate selection. Experiments on two pulsar datasets validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our approach.
label: AI

title: An Introduction to Deep Visual Explanation
Abstract: Deep learning has significantly impacted complex supervised learning problems, often being incorporated into various AI tasks. However, the lack of explainability and debuggability in deep learning poses a significant challenge, especially when unexpected results can affect human lives. To address this issue, we present a preliminary framework called "deep visual explanation" (DVE). DVE focuses on understanding the development and performance of deep neural networks through visualization techniques. By leveraging visual representation, we aim to identify and expose hypotheses about the performance behavior of learned deep models. In this work, we demonstrate DVE using image classification examples and various initial deep model configurations. Through careful instrumentation and visualization, we showcase classification outcomes and highlight the potential of DVE for interpretability.
label: AI

title: Quantum Artificial Life in an IBM Quantum Computer
Abstract: This paper presents the first experimental realization of a quantum artificial life algorithm on a quantum computer. Our quantum biomimetic protocol encodes the fundamental behaviors of living systems, including self-replication, mutation, interaction, and death, into the IBM ibmqx4 cloud quantum computer. We observe that entanglement propagates across generations, with genuine quantum information features inherited through genealogical networks. Experimental data aligns with the ideal model with high accuracy, demonstrating the proof-of-concept for quantum artificial life. This opens the door for exploring more complex quantum artificial life models on future generations of quantum computers. This research advances the fields of quantum biomimetics, quantum machine learning, and quantum artificial intelligence.
label: AI

title: A general unified framework for interval pairwise comparison matrices
Abstract: Interval Pairwise Comparison Matrices are widely used to represent uncertain preferences in decision-making. Existing approaches include multiplicative and fuzzy interval matrices. This paper proposes a unified framework for Interval Pairwise Comparison Matrices based on Abelian linearly ordered groups. This framework generalizes consistency conditions and provides inclusion relationships between different matrix types. We introduce a distance metric for intervals and a mean concept defined on real continuous Abelian linearly ordered groups to derive a consistency index and an indeterminacy index. This allows us to compare inconsistency and indeterminacy of various Interval Pairwise Comparison Matrices, such as multiplicative, additive, and fuzzy, on a single Cartesian coordinate system.
label: AI

title: MAVOT: Memory-Augmented Video Object Tracking
Abstract: We present a one-shot learning approach for video object tracking that requires observing the target object only once. The proposed algorithm utilizes an external memory to store and remember evolving features of the foreground object and background over time during tracking. By retrieving and updating relevant memory in each tracking frame, our model maintains a long-term memory of the object, effectively handling challenging scenarios like occlusion, motion changes, and large-scale variations. Our experiments on the ImageNet ILSVRC2015 video detection dataset and the VOT-2016 benchmark demonstrate the performance of our Memory-Augmented Video Object Tracking (MAVOT) model. The one-shot property and design simplicity make MAVOT an attractive approach in visual tracking, achieving good performance on the VOT-2016 benchmark and ranking among the top 5 performers in accuracy and robustness.
label: AI

title: Pedagogical learning
Abstract: Machine learning typically assumes independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) training data, implying a lack of information about the data's helpfulness for learning. However, cognitive science research suggests that humans, when acting as teachers, deliberately select informative examples to aid learning. This more informative data leads to faster learning. Interestingly, this effect is more prominent when learners are aware of the pedagogical nature of the data. We call this "pedagogical learning," where the learner assumes the evidence comes from a helpful teacher. This work explores pedagogical learning in machine learning algorithms. We conducted a behavioral study to understand how humans teach regular expressions using example strings, revealing that teachers' examples possess powerful clustering structure that facilitates learning. Subsequently, we develop a teaching model and demonstrate its potential to enhance learner performance.
label: AI

title: Improved Neural Text Attribute Transfer with Non-parallel Data
Abstract: Text attribute transfer using non-parallel data requires techniques capable of disentangling content and linguistic attributes. This work proposes several improvements to existing approaches, enabling the encoder-decoder framework to handle text attribute transfer from non-parallel data. Experiments on the sentiment transfer task using two datasets show that our method outperforms a strong baseline in two of the three evaluation metrics.
label: AI

title: Generative Adversarial Network for Abstractive Text Summarization
Abstract: This paper proposes an adversarial process for abstractive text summarization, employing a generative model G and a discriminative model D. The generator G, acting as a reinforcement learning agent, takes raw text as input and predicts the abstractive summarization. The discriminator D distinguishes between generated summaries and ground truth summaries. Extensive experiments on the CNN/Daily Mail dataset demonstrate that our model achieves competitive ROUGE scores with state-of-the-art methods. Qualitatively, our model generates more abstractive, readable, and diverse summaries.
label: AI

title: A Big Data Analysis Framework Using Apache Spark and Deep Learning
Abstract: With the rise of Big Data, frameworks like Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark have become popular, particularly in industries. Effective big data analysis is crucial for solving AI problems. While Apache Spark's MLlib library supports various machine learning algorithms, its efficiency for computationally expensive tasks like deep learning remains limited. This paper proposes a novel framework combining the distributed computation capabilities of Apache Spark and the advanced machine learning architecture of a deep multi-layer perceptron (MLP), using the Cascade Learning concept. Empirical analysis on two real-world datasets shows promising results, demonstrating the framework's effectiveness and superiority over traditional big data analysis methods.
label: AI

title: Generalizing Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with Neural Networks
Abstract: We present a general-purpose method for training Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) kernels parameterized by deep neural networks, enabling faster convergence and mixing to their target distribution. This method generalizes Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and is trained to maximize expected squared jumped distance, a proxy for mixing speed. We demonstrate significant empirical improvements on challenging distributions, achieving a 106x improvement in effective sample size in one case and mixing when standard HMC fails in another. Additionally, we showcase quantitative and qualitative gains on a real-world task: latent-variable generative modeling. We release an open source TensorFlow implementation of the algorithm.
label: AI

title: An Energy Efficient Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio Wireless Sensor Networks
Abstract: Cognitive radio wireless sensor networks play a crucial role in communicating spectrum information to the fusion center in a cooperative spectrum sensing environment. Battery-operated sensors need energy-efficient strategies for transmitting binary information about spectrum availability. Intelligent decision-making through proper routing can be a solution. This paper introduces an energy-efficient routing protocol and compares its performance with existing systems in terms of energy consumption. The proposed protocol considers both uniform and non-uniform clustering strategies, proving to be an energy-efficient method for communication.
label: AI

title: Complex Structure Leads to Overfitting: A Structure Regularization Decoding Method for Natural Language Processing
Abstract: Recent structured prediction systems focus on increasing structural dependencies within the model. However, complex structures can lead to high overfitting risks. To control structure-based overfitting, we propose structure regularization decoding (SR decoding). The decoding of the complex structure model is regularized by an additionally trained simple structure model. We theoretically analyze the relationship between structural complexity and overfitting risk, showing that complex structure models are prone to structure-based overfitting. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our method improves the performance of complex structure models by reducing overfitting. On sequence labeling tasks, our method significantly enhances the performance of complex neural network models, achieving a maximum F1 error rate reduction of 36.4% for the third-order model. Our method also benefits the parsing task, yielding a maximum UAS improvement of 5.5% for the tri-sibling model. These results are competitive with or better than state-of-the-art results.
label: AI

title: D numbers theory based game-theoretic framework in adversarial decision making under fuzzy environment
Abstract: Adversarial decision making involves decision problems where the outcome is influenced by the actions of others. Representing alternatives' evaluations and finding optimal alternatives are crucial aspects. This study develops a general framework for solving adversarial decision making problems under uncertainty. By combining fuzzy set theory, game theory, and D numbers theory (DNT), we present a DNT-based game-theoretic framework for adversarial decision making under fuzzy environments. Within this framework, fuzzy set theory models uncertain evaluations, DNT accounts for non-exclusiveness among fuzzy evaluations, and game theory considers the conflict of interests among decision makers. An illustrative application showcases the effectiveness of the proposed model. This work provides an effective framework for adversarial decision making under fuzzy environments and further strengthens DNT as a generalization of Dempster-Shafer theory for uncertainty reasoning.
label: AI

title: Echo State Transfer Learning for Data Correlation Aware Resource Allocation in Wireless Virtual Reality
Abstract: This paper investigates data correlation-aware resource management for a network of wireless virtual reality (VR) users communicating over cloud-based small cell networks (SCNs). In this model, small base stations (SBSs) with limited computational resources act as VR control centers, collecting tracking information from VR users over the uplink and sending it back over the downlink. VR users may exchange or request correlated data, such as panoramic images and tracking data. This spatial data correlation can be leveraged for resource allocation, reducing traffic load in both uplink and downlink. We formulate the VR resource allocation problem as a non-cooperative game, jointly optimizing computational and spectrum resources while considering data correlation. To solve this game, we propose a transfer learning algorithm based on echo state networks (ESNs). Unlike conventional reinforcement learning algorithms, our algorithm efficiently transfers learned utility information across time, enabling rapid adaptation to dynamic environments caused by factors like content changes or data correlation. Simulation results show that our algorithm achieves up to 16.7% and 18.2% gains in delay compared to Q-learning with and without data correlation. Our algorithm also exhibits faster convergence than Q-learning while guaranteeing low delays.
label: AI

title: Cascade Attribute Learning Network
Abstract: We introduce the cascade attribute learning network (CALNet), which learns attributes separately for a control task and assembles them together. Our contributions are two-fold: first, we propose attribute learning in reinforcement learning (RL). Traditionally, attributes were modeled using constraint functions or terms in the objective function, making transfer challenging. Attribute learning, however, models task properties as modules within the policy network. Second, we propose using novel cascading compensative networks in CALNet to learn and assemble attributes. CALNet allows for zero-shot learning of unseen tasks by separately learning all their attributes and assembling the corresponding modules. We validate our model's capacity on a diverse set of control problems with attributes in time, position, velocity, and acceleration phases.
label: AI

title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Planning: A Survey
Abstract: Cooperative multi-agent planning (MAP) is a relatively new research field combining technologies, algorithms, and techniques from the Artificial Intelligence Planning and Multi-Agent Systems communities. While planning has typically been a single-agent task, MAP generalizes this concept by considering multiple intelligent agents working cooperatively to achieve a common goal. This paper reviews the most relevant approaches to MAP, focusing on solvers that participated in the 2015 Competition of Distributed and Multi-Agent Planning. We classify these solvers based on their key features and relative performance.
label: AI

title: Interactive Robot Learning of Gestures, Language and Affordances
Abstract: Human-robot collaboration, a growing field in robotics and AI research, aims to enable effective teamwork between humans and robots. However, human teams often outperform human-robot teams due to their ability to communicate goals effectively using language and observe each other's actions, leveraging shared motor repertoires and sensorimotor resources. This paper proposes a model for cognitive robots that combines knowledge acquired from interacting with the environment (affordance exploration) with probabilistic observation of another agent's actions. Our model integrates learning robot affordances and word descriptions with statistical recognition of human gestures using vision sensors. We discuss theoretical motivations, possible implementations, and initial results demonstrating that a humanoid robot, after acquiring environmental knowledge, can generalize this knowledge to observe a human partner performing the same actions.
label: AI

title: Ethical Challenges in Data-Driven Dialogue Systems
Abstract: Dialogue systems, increasingly prevalent in human-machine interaction, are increasingly using conversation strategies learned from large datasets. However, this data-driven training process can lead to biased or offensive conversations. This paper highlights potential ethical issues arising in dialogue system research, including implicit biases in data-driven systems, adversarial examples, privacy violations, safety concerns, considerations for reinforcement learning systems, and reproducibility issues. We suggest areas for further investigation stemming from these issues, aiming to promote research leading to robust, safe, and ethically sound dialogue systems.
label: AI

title: A Compression-Inspired Framework for Macro Discovery
Abstract: This paper explores how a reinforcement learning agent tasked with solving a set of related Markov decision processes can leverage past experience to accelerate learning on novel, but related, tasks. One approach is to identify recurring patterns in trajectories obtained from successful policies. We propose a three-step framework: 1) generating candidate open-loop macros by compressing trajectories from near-optimal policies; 2) evaluating the value of each macro; and 3) selecting a maximally diverse subset of macros spanning the space of policies required for solving the task set. Our experiments demonstrate that augmenting the agent's original action set with these identified macros enables faster learning of optimal policies in unseen but similar MDPs.
label: AI

title: Action Branching Architectures for Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Discrete-action algorithms have been crucial for recent deep reinforcement learning successes. However, applying these algorithms to high-dimensional action tasks presents challenges due to the combinatorial increase in the number of possible actions with action dimensions. This problem is further exacerbated for continuous-action tasks requiring fine control. This paper introduces a novel neural architecture featuring a shared decision module followed by multiple network branches, one for each action dimension. This approach achieves a linear increase in the number of network outputs with the number of degrees of freedom by allowing independence for each action dimension. To illustrate this, we present a novel agent, Branching Dueling Q-Network (BDQ), as a branching variant of Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (Dueling DDQN). We evaluate BDQ's performance on challenging continuous control tasks. Empirical results demonstrate that our agent scales well to environments with increasing action dimensionality, highlighting the significance of the shared decision module in coordinating distributed action branches. Furthermore, BDQ performs competitively against the state-of-the-art continuous control algorithm, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG). |||
label: AI

title: Automated Algorithm Selection on Continuous Black-Box Problems By Combining Exploratory Landscape Analysis and Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a method for automatically selecting the best optimization algorithm for a given problem based on the problem's landscape. The authors leverage existing work on Exploratory Landscape Analysis features and apply them to the COCO platform's algorithm performance data. They build an algorithm selection model that outperforms the best single solver in the portfolio by requiring less than half the resources to solve a problem. This efficiency gain comes with the added benefit of deeper insights into problem characteristics and algorithm properties. The model's ability to select the most suitable algorithm for unseen problems based on a small function evaluation sample makes it particularly useful for practical applications, as such samples can also be repurposed for initializing evolutionary optimization algorithms, further minimizing the cost of feature evaluation.
label: AI

title: Technology Aware Training in Memristive Neuromorphic Systems based on non-ideal Synaptic Crossbars
Abstract: Advances in neuromorphic computing have led to intense research into hardware implementations of neural networks, utilizing memristive technologies like oxide-based devices, spintronics, and phase change materials. However, non-idealities in crossbar implementations of synaptic arrays can significantly degrade neural network performance, imposing constraints on feasible crossbar sizes. This study analyzes the impact of various non-idealities, including source resistance, neuron resistance, and chip-to-chip device variations, on the classification accuracy of fully connected networks (FCNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The findings reveal that non-ideal crossbars can lead to a significant reduction in accuracy (up to 59.84% for FCNs and 62.4% for CNNs), severely limiting crossbar size. To address this challenge, the authors propose a technology-aware training algorithm that incorporates mathematical models of the non-idealities into the standard training algorithm. The proposed methodology successfully recovers a significant portion of the ideal accuracy (within 1.9% for FCNs and 1.5% for CNNs), potentially enabling the use of significantly larger crossbar arrays (784x500 for FCNs and 4096x512 for CNNs) with minimal or no accuracy trade-off.
label: AI

title: Exploring Approximations for Floating-Point Arithmetic using UppSAT
Abstract: This paper presents UppSAT, a novel implementation of a systematic approximation refinement framework for solving floating-point constraints obtained from software verification. UppSAT acts as an abstract SMT solver, using an approximation and a decision procedure (implemented in an off-the-shelf SMT solver) to produce an approximating SMT solver. It features a library of predefined approximation components that can be combined and extended to define new encodings, orderings, and solving strategies, facilitating flexible exploration of new approximations. The authors explore various approximations of floating-point arithmetic, emphasizing that approximations are compositions of an encoding into a target theory, a precision ordering, and strategies for model reconstruction and precision refinement. They present encodings of floating-point arithmetic into reduced precision floating-point arithmetic, real-arithmetic, and fixed-point arithmetic (encoded in the theory of bit-vectors). The paper concludes with an experimental evaluation comparing the advantages and disadvantages of approximating solvers obtained by combining different encodings and decision procedures based on state-of-the-art SMT solvers for floating-point, real, and bit-vector arithmetic.
label: AI

title: Improvised Comedy as a Turing Test
Abstract: This paper explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in improvisational theatre, challenging the traditional paradigm where human actors make their scene partners "shine." The authors trained an AI to perform live shows alongside human actors for human audiences. Over 30 performances to nearly 3,000 people, they refined theatrical games incorporating both human and AI actors, some adversarial. They developed scene structures engaging audience participants and a complete show structure designed to subject the audience to a Turing test, observing their suspension of disbelief, which is considered crucial for human/non-human theatre co-creation.
label: AI

title: Server, server in the cloud. Who is the fairest in the crowd?
Abstract: This paper investigates how machine learning, particularly neural networks, are changing the way attractiveness is perceived and its impact on culture. The authors analyze the behavior of two convolutional neural network architectures in classifying facial attractiveness in a large database of celebrity faces. They discuss the difficulty of detecting attractiveness robustly even for the most advanced classification systems, contrasting it with readily definable facial features. Based on experimental observations, they explore approaches to identify factors influencing machine evaluation of human features and address the potential for bias in both data selection and network architectures, encompassing various levels throughout the process. The paper aims to outline the novel condition of "slippages" produced by platform-level machine learning systems making judgments in domains traditionally considered dependent on high-level human intelligence.
label: AI

title: fpgaConvNet: A Toolflow for Mapping Diverse Convolutional Neural Networks on Embedded FPGAs
Abstract: This paper presents fpgaConvNet, an end-to-end framework for mapping Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), addressing the challenge of optimizing ConvNets for diverse performance requirements in embedded AI systems. The framework employs an automated design methodology based on the Synchronous Dataflow (SDF) paradigm and defines a set of SDF transformations for efficient architectural design space exploration. By selectively optimizing for throughput, latency, or multiobjective criteria, fpgaConvNet efficiently generates hardware designs from high-level ConvNet specifications, tailored to the desired performance metric. The framework produces designs that outperform highly optimized embedded GPU designs by up to 6.65x for the same power constraints in embedded environments.
label: AI

title: Identification of Strong Edges in AMP Chain Graphs
Abstract: The essential graph, a distinguished member of a Markov equivalence class of AMP chain graphs, may not necessarily contain strong or invariant directed or undirected edges shared by every member of the equivalence class. This paper develops a procedure for identifying strong edges within an essential graph. The authors demonstrate how this procedure can be used to bound causal effects when the true chain graph is unknown.
label: AI

title: Safer Classification by Synthesis
Abstract: This paper addresses the vulnerability of discriminative deep neural networks to adversarial examples and out-of-distribution examples. The authors demonstrate that conventional discriminative methods can be easily fooled into providing incorrect labels with high confidence for out-of-distribution examples. They propose a generative approach as a remedy, introducing a method for classification using generative models. During training, a generative model is learned for each class, and at test time, each generator is queried for its most similar generation for a given example. The class corresponding to the most similar generation is then selected. This general approach, applicable to expressive models like GANs and VAEs, allows the model to "know when it does not know" at test time, providing resilience against out-of-distribution examples while maintaining competitive performance on standard examples.
label: AI

title: Temporal Relational Reasoning in Videos
Abstract: Temporal relational reasoning, the ability to link meaningful transformations of objects or entities over time, is fundamental to intelligent species. This paper introduces the Temporal Relation Network (TRN), an effective and interpretable network module designed to learn and reason about temporal dependencies between video frames at multiple time scales. The authors evaluate TRN-equipped networks on activity recognition tasks using three video datasets: Something-Something, Jester, and Charades, which rely heavily on temporal relational reasoning. The results demonstrate that TRN significantly enhances convolutional neural networks' ability to discover temporal relations in videos. TRN-equipped networks accurately predict human-object interactions in the Something-Something dataset, identify gestures in the Jester dataset with competitive performance, and outperform two-stream and 3D convolution networks in recognizing daily activities in the Charades dataset. Further analysis reveals that the models learn intuitive and interpretable visual common sense knowledge from videos.
label: AI

title: MagNet and "Efficient Defenses Against Adversarial Attacks" are Not Robust to Adversarial Examples
Abstract: This paper challenges the effectiveness of two recent defenses against adversarial examples: MagNet and "Efficient Defenses...". The authors demonstrate the ability to construct adversarial examples that defeat these defenses with only a slight increase in distortion.
label: AI

title: From Monte Carlo to Las Vegas: Improving Restricted Boltzmann Machine Training Through Stopping Sets
Abstract: This paper proposes a Las Vegas transformation of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimators for Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), termed Markov Chain Las Vegas (MCLV). MCLV provides statistical guarantees in exchange for random running times, utilizing a stopping set built from the training data and a maximum number of Markov chain steps K (MCLV-K). The authors present a MCLV-K gradient estimator (LVS-K) for RBMs and explore its correspondence and differences with Contrastive Divergence (CD-K), demonstrating that LVS-K significantly outperforms CD-K in training RBMs on the MNIST dataset. These results suggest that MCLV holds promise for learning generative models.
label: AI

title: Identifying user habits through data mining on call data records
Abstract: This paper proposes a framework for identifying patterns and regularities in anonymized Call Data Records (CDR) pertaining to mobile operator subscribers. The authors address the challenge of automatically extracting meaningful information from the data using an unsupervised cluster analysis approach, without relying on prior knowledge of the applicative context. The mined clusters provide insights into user habits and enable the creation of characterizing profiles. Two implementations are presented: the first utilizes LD-ABCD, a novel system for cluster and knowledge discovery that retrieves clusters and automatically discovers the most appropriate dissimilarity measure for each cluster, and the second employs PROCLUS, a well-known subclustering algorithm. The dataset analyzed features limited characteristics, prompting the authors to generate additional fields describing implicit information hidden within the data. Finally, the paper introduces an effective graphical representation of the data mining results, facilitating easy understanding and practical applications by analysts.
label: AI

title: Building Machines that Learn and Think for Themselves: Commentary on Lake et al., Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 2017
Abstract: While agreeing with Lake et al. on the importance of model-based reasoning for building humanlike intelligence, this paper advocates for an approach centered on autonomy. The authors believe that agents capable of building and exploiting their own internal models with minimal human intervention have the greatest potential for success in tackling real-world complexity, particularly in domains where pre-existing formal models are unavailable. The paper surveys examples of progress in developing autonomous agents with humanlike abilities and highlights outstanding challenges.
label: AI

title: Allocation Problems in Ride-Sharing Platforms: Online Matching with Offline Reusable Resources
Abstract: This paper introduces Online Matching with (offline) Reusable Resources under Known Adversarial Distributions (OM-RR-KAD), a new model for bipartite matching markets where resources on the offline side are reusable, unlike disposable resources in traditional online bipartite matching markets. The model addresses scenarios where resources become available again after being matched. The authors demonstrate the model's tractability by presenting an LP-based adaptive algorithm achieving an online competitive ratio of 1/2 - eps for any given eps greater than 0. They also prove that no non-adaptive algorithm can achieve a ratio of 1/2 + o(1) based on the same benchmark LP. A data-driven analysis on a massive open dataset shows that the model is robust enough to capture the application of taxi dispatching services and ride-sharing systems. The paper concludes with the presentation of heuristics that perform well in practice.
label: AI

title: A correlational analysis of multiagent sensorimotor interactions: clustering autonomous and controllable entities
Abstract: This paper explores the potential of sensorimotor interactions for developing Theory of Mind (ToM) abilities in synthetic agents. The authors propose a dual-arm robotic setup for probing ToM and discuss extracting measures from sensorimotor interaction data (based on correlation analysis) to distinguish between self and other, and between other/inanimate and other/active with intentions. They address the limitations of current cognitive architectures in acquiring ToM abilities from sensorimotor interactions, highlighting the need for both bottom-up development from reactive agent interaction behaviors and top-down optimization of social behavior and cooperation.
label: AI

title: Few-shot Learning by Exploiting Visual Concepts within CNNs
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are driving advancements in computer vision, but they face challenges in achieving ideal machine intelligence. One challenge lies in their complexity and lack of interpretability, and another is the need for large amounts of annotated data, which can be difficult to obtain. This paper addresses these limitations by developing novel, flexible, and interpretable models for few-shot learning. The authors utilize the concept of visual concepts (VCs), represented by feature vectors within CNNs, to encode objects. They adapt VC learning to the few-shot setting and identify two key properties of feature encoding using VCs: category sensitivity and spatial pattern. Based on these properties, they present two intuitive models for few-shot learning. Experiments demonstrate that these models achieve competitive performance while offering greater flexibility and interpretability than alternative state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods. The paper concludes that VCs expose CNNs' inherent capability for few-shot learning.
label: AI

title: Approximate Inference-based Motion Planning by Learning and Exploiting Low-Dimensional Latent Variable Models
Abstract: This paper presents an efficient framework for generating motion plans for robots with high degrees of freedom, such as humanoid robots. The challenge of high dimensionality in the robot's configuration space often hinders the use of traditional motion planning algorithms. To address this, the authors employ two key concepts: first, the Gaussian process latent variable model (GP-LVM) for low-dimensional representation of the original configuration space, and second, an approximate inference algorithm that exploits the duality between control and estimation to explore the decision space and compute high-quality motion trajectories. By integrating GP-LVM and this duality, a fully probabilistic generative model is constructed, transforming the high-dimensional motion planning problem into a tractable inference problem. The motion trajectory is computed using an approximate inference algorithm based on a variant of the particle filter. The resulting motions are visualized in a supplemental video.
label: AI

title: GraphGAN: Graph Representation Learning with Generative Adversarial Nets
Abstract: The goal of graph representation learning is to embed each vertex in a graph into a low-dimensional vector space. Existing methods fall into two categories: generative models that learn the underlying connectivity distribution in the graph, and discriminative models that predict edge existence probability between vertex pairs. This paper introduces GraphGAN, a novel graph representation learning framework that unifies these two classes of methods. GraphGAN implements a game-theoretical minimax game between a generative model and a discriminative model. The generative model aims to fit the underlying true connectivity distribution for a given vertex and generates "fake" samples to deceive the discriminative model, while the discriminative model attempts to detect whether the sampled vertex is from ground truth or generated by the generative model. This competition between the models iteratively enhances their performance. The authors propose a novel graph softmax to address the limitations of traditional softmax functions, satisfying desirable properties of normalization, graph structure awareness, and computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that GraphGAN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in various applications, including link prediction, node classification, and recommendation.
label: AI

title: Decomposition Strategies for Constructive Preference Elicitation
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of constructive preference elicitation, which involves learning user preferences over large decision problems with combinatorial spaces of possible outcomes. In this setting, configurations are synthesized on-the-fly by solving a constrained optimization problem, and preferences are learned iteratively through user interaction. The authors explore the use of Coactive Learning, a suitable method for learning preferences in constructive scenarios, where the user provides feedback in the form of improvements to suggested configurations. To reduce the cognitive burden of this interaction for problems with many decision variables and constraints, they propose a decomposition technique relying on inference and feedback over partial configurations. This significantly reduces the cognitive load and can potentially be exponentially less computationally demanding than full configuration inference. The paper discusses the theoretical implications of this approach and presents promising empirical results on one synthetic and two realistic constructive problems.
label: AI

title: The Stochastic Firefighter Problem
Abstract: The dynamics of infectious disease spread are crucial for determining risk and developing containment strategies. This paper studies sequential vaccination of individuals in networks. The authors extend the deterministic Firefighter problem, where a fire spreads through a graph, to a probabilistic setting where infection is stochastic. They develop a simple policy that optimally vaccinates neighbors of infected nodes on regular trees and general graphs for sufficiently large budgets. The paper derives methods for calculating upper and lower bounds on the expected number of infected individuals and estimates the budget required for containment in expectation, providing explicit calculations for trees, d-dimensional grids, and Erdős-Rényi graphs. Finally, the authors construct a state-dependent budget allocation strategy and demonstrate its superiority over constant budget allocation on real networks following a first-order acquaintance vaccination policy. |||
label: AI

title: An influence-based fast preceding questionnaire model for elderly assessments
Abstract: To enhance the efficiency of elderly assessments, this paper proposes an influence-based fast preceding questionnaire model (FPQM). This model optimizes questionnaires by reordering attributes, allowing the prediction of low-ranking attribute values from high-ranking ones. This reduces the number of attributes needed without redesigning the questionnaires. The FPQM employs a new function based on probability theory to calculate attribute influence, leading to reordering and reduction algorithms. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through a practical application in an elderly-care company, resulting in a 90.56% reduction in attributes with a prediction accuracy of 98.39%. Compared to methods like Expert Knowledge, Rough Set, and C4.5, FPQM achieves superior performance and can be applied to other questionnaires.
label: AI

title: Hypergraph $p$-Laplacian: A Differential Geometry View
Abstract: The graph Laplacian plays a crucial role in processing relational data and has analogies with the Laplacian in differential geometry. This paper generalizes this analogy to the hypergraph setting by introducing a novel hypergraph $p$-Laplacian. This generalization allows the analysis of hypergraphs, where edges can connect any number of nodes, unlike existing two-node graph Laplacians. The paper further proposes a semi-supervised learning method based on the hypergraph $p$-Laplacian, formalized as an analogue to the Dirichlet problem, which frequently appears in physics. It explores theoretical connections to the normalized hypergraph cut and proposes a corresponding cut for the hypergraph $p$-Laplacian. The proposed $p$-Laplacian surpasses standard hypergraph Laplacians in experiments on hypergraph semi-supervised learning and normalized cut settings.
label: AI

title: Multiagent Simple Temporal Problem: The Arc-Consistency Approach
Abstract: The Simple Temporal Problem (STP), a fundamental temporal reasoning problem, has been extended to the Multiagent Simple Temporal Problem (MaSTP). This paper presents a novel approach based on enforcing arc-consistency (AC) on the input (multiagent) simple temporal network. It demonstrates that the AC-based approach is sufficient for solving both STP and MaSTP and provides efficient algorithms for them. Since this approach does not impose new constraints between agents, it preserves agent privacy and surpasses existing MaSTP approaches. Empirical evaluations on diverse benchmark datasets show that the AC-based algorithms for STP and MaSTP are significantly more efficient than existing methods.
label: AI

title: Dilated FCN for Multi-Agent 2D/3D Medical Image Registration
Abstract: 2D/3D image registration, the alignment of a 3D volume with 2D X-ray images, is a challenging problem due to its ill-posed nature and various artifacts in 2D X-ray images. This paper proposes a multi-agent system with an auto-attention mechanism for robust and efficient 2D/3D image registration. Each agent is trained with a dilated Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) to perform registration in a Markov Decision Process (MDP) by observing local regions. The final action is then taken based on proposals from multiple agents, weighted by their corresponding confidence levels. This paper makes three key contributions. First, it formulates 2D/3D registration as an MDP with well-defined observations, actions, and rewards related to X-ray imaging systems. Second, to address artifacts in 2D X-ray images, multiple local agents are employed efficiently via FCN-based structures, and an auto-attention mechanism prioritizes proposals from regions with reliable visual cues. Third, a dilated FCN-based training mechanism significantly reduces the degrees of freedom in the registration environment simulation, drastically improving training efficiency compared to standard CNN-based methods. The proposed method demonstrates high robustness on spine cone beam Computed Tomography data with low signal-to-noise ratios and data from minimally invasive spine surgery with severe artifacts and occlusions due to metal screws and guide wires. It outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including single agent-based and optimization-based approaches, by a significant margin.
label: AI

title: Asymmetric Action Abstractions for Multi-Unit Control in Adversarial Real-Time Games
Abstract: Action abstractions limit the number of legal actions during search in multi-unit real-time adversarial games, enabling algorithms to focus on promising actions. Optimal strategies from un-abstracted spaces are guaranteed to be no worse than those derived from action-abstracted spaces. However, real-time constraints and state space size limit the derivation of good strategies in un-abstracted spaces for large-scale games. This paper introduces search algorithms utilizing an action abstraction scheme called asymmetric abstraction. This approach retains the theoretical advantage of un-abstracted spaces while allowing the derivation of effective strategies even in large-scale games. Empirical results on combat scenarios in a real-time strategy game demonstrate that these algorithms significantly outperform state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: Robust Stackelberg Equilibria in Extensive-Form Games and Extension to Limited Lookahead
Abstract: Stackelberg equilibria have gained prominence as a solution concept in computational game theory, particularly in practical problems like security settings. However, uncertainty regarding the opponent's model is prevalent. This paper is the first to investigate Stackelberg equilibria under uncertainty in extensive-form games, a broad class of games. It introduces robust Stackelberg equilibria, addressing uncertainty about opponent payoffs and limited lookahead. The paper develops a new mixed-integer program for the deterministic limited-lookahead setting and extends it to the robust setting for Stackelberg equilibrium under both unlimited and limited lookahead by the opponent. It demonstrates that for interval uncertainty about opponent payoffs (or node evaluations in the case of limited lookahead), robust Stackelberg equilibria can be computed using a mixed-integer program with the same asymptotic size as the deterministic setting.
label: AI

title: Deterministic Policy Optimization by Combining Pathwise and Score Function Estimators for Discrete Action Spaces
Abstract: Policy optimization methods have shown great promise in solving complex reinforcement and imitation learning tasks. While model-free methods are widely applicable, they often require extensive samples to optimize complex policies. Model-based methods enhance sample efficiency but at the cost of poor generalization, requiring carefully handcrafted models of the system dynamics for each task. Hybrid methods successfully balance applicability and sample complexity, but they have been limited to continuous action spaces. This paper presents a new hybrid method based on approximating dynamics as an expectation over the next state under the current policy. This relaxation leads to a novel hybrid policy gradient estimator, combining score function and pathwise derivative estimators, applicable to discrete action spaces. The method demonstrates significant gains in sample complexity, ranging from 1.7 to 25 times, when learning parameterized policies on Cart Pole, Acrobot, Mountain Car, and Hand Mass. Its applicability extends to both discrete and continuous action spaces, unlike competing pathwise methods restricted to the latter.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Relational Networks
Abstract: This paper focuses on learning to solve tasks requiring a chain of interdependent relational inference steps, such as answering complex questions about object relationships or solving puzzles with mutually constraining elements. It introduces the recurrent relational network, a general-purpose module operating on a graph representation of objects. As a generalization of Santoro et al. [2017]'s relational network, it enhances any neural network model with the ability to perform multi-step relational reasoning. The recurrent relational network achieves state-of-the-art results on the bAbI textual question-answering dataset, consistently solving all 20 tasks. However, as bAbI is not particularly challenging from a relational reasoning perspective, the paper introduces Pretty-CLEVR, a new diagnostic dataset for relational reasoning. The Pretty-CLEVR setup allows varying the question to control the number of relational reasoning steps required to obtain the answer. Using Pretty-CLEVR, the paper probes the limitations of multi-layer perceptrons, relational, and recurrent relational networks. Finally, it demonstrates how recurrent relational networks can learn to solve Sudoku puzzles from supervised training data, a challenging task requiring numerous relational reasoning steps. It achieves state-of-the-art results among comparable methods, solving 96.6% of the hardest Sudoku puzzles.
label: AI

title: Toward Foraging for Understanding of StarCraft Agents: An Empirical Study
Abstract: Assessing and understanding intelligent agents is a difficult task for users lacking an AI background. Explainable AI is emerging to address this problem, but little is known about how users would navigate the information provided by an explanation system. To inform the development of Explainable AI systems, this study used Information Foraging Theory to investigate how experienced users navigated the StarCraft domain to assess an agent. The results showed that participants encountered difficult foraging problems. These problems led them to miss important events, reluctantly ignore actions they did not want to ignore, and face high cognitive, navigation, and information costs to access the information they needed.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Adaptation with Domain Separation Networks for Robust Speech Recognition
Abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation of speech signals aims to adapt a well-trained source-domain acoustic model to unlabeled target-domain data. This is achieved by adversarial training of deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models to learn an intermediate deep representation that is both senone-discriminative and domain-invariant. Specifically, the DNN is trained to jointly optimize the primary task of senone classification and the secondary task of domain classification with adversarial objective functions. This work goes beyond learning a domain-invariant feature (the shared component between domains) by characterizing the difference between source and target domain distributions. It explicitly models the private component of each domain through a private component extractor DNN, trained to be orthogonal to the shared component, implicitly increasing the domain-invariance of the shared component. A reconstructor DNN reconstructs the original speech feature from the private and shared components, acting as a regularization. This domain separation framework applied to unsupervised environment adaptation achieved an 11.08% relative WER reduction compared to gradient reversal layer training, a representative adversarial training method, for automatic speech recognition on the CHiME-3 dataset.
label: AI

title: Relating Input Concepts to Convolutional Neural Network Decisions
Abstract: Many current methods for interpreting convolutional neural networks (CNNs) use visualization techniques and words to highlight concepts of the input seemingly relevant to the CNN's decision. These methods hypothesize that the recognition of these concepts plays a crucial role in the CNN's decision, but the nature of this relationship remains unexplored. To address this gap, this paper examines the quality of a concept's recognition by a CNN and its association with CNN decisions. The study considers a CNN trained for scene recognition on the ADE20k dataset. It uses a novel approach to find and score the strength of minimally distributed representations of input concepts (defined by objects in scene images) across late-stage feature maps. Subsequent analysis finds evidence that concept recognition impacts decision-making. Strong recognition of concepts frequently occurring in few scenes indicates correct decisions, while recognizing concepts common to many scenes can mislead the network.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning for Physical Processes: Incorporating Prior Scientific Knowledge
Abstract: This paper explores the use of Deep Learning methods for modeling complex phenomena, such as those occurring in natural physical processes. With the vast amount of data gathered on these phenomena, the data-intensive paradigm could challenge traditional approaches in fields like mathematics and physics. However, despite significant successes in various application domains, the machine learning field is not yet equipped to handle the complexity of such problems. Using Sea Surface Temperature Prediction as an example application, this paper shows how general background knowledge from physics can guide the design of efficient Deep Learning models. To motivate this approach and assess its generality, a formal link is established between the solution of a class of differential equations underlying a large family of physical phenomena and the proposed model. Experiments and comparisons with baselines, including a state-of-the-art numerical approach, are provided.
label: AI

title: Quantifying Performance of Bipedal Standing with Multi-channel EMG
Abstract: Spinal cord stimulation has enabled individuals with motor complete spinal cord injury (SCI) to stand independently and regain some lost autonomic function. Quantifying the quality of bipedal standing under spinal stimulation is essential for spinal rehabilitation therapies and strategies combining spinal stimulation with rehabilitative robots (like exoskeletons) in real-time feedback. To study the potential of automated electromyography (EMG) analysis in SCI, this research evaluated the standing quality of paralyzed patients undergoing electrical spinal cord stimulation using video and multi-channel surface EMG recordings during therapy sessions. The quality of standing under different stimulation settings was quantified manually by experienced clinicians. By correlating features of the recorded EMG activity with expert evaluations, the research shows that multi-channel EMG recording provides accurate, fast, and robust estimation for the quality of bipedal standing in spinally stimulated SCI patients. Moreover, the analysis demonstrates that the total number of EMG channels needed for effective standing quality prediction can be reduced while maintaining high estimation accuracy, providing greater flexibility for rehabilitation robotic systems to incorporate EMG recordings.

title: Constructive Preference Elicitation over Hybrid Combinatorial Spaces
Abstract: Preference elicitation involves suggesting a highly preferred configuration to a decision-maker. Preferences are typically learned by querying the user for choice feedback over pairs or sets of objects. In its constructive variant, new objects are synthesized "from scratch" by maximizing an estimate of the user's utility over a combinatorial (potentially infinite) space of candidates. Most existing elicitation techniques fail in the constructive setting due to reliance on exhaustive enumeration of candidates. A previous solution explicitly designed for constructive tasks lacks formal performance guarantees and can be expensive or inapplicable in problems with non-Boolean attributes. This paper proposes the Choice Perceptron, a Perceptron-like algorithm for learning user preferences from set-wise choice feedback over constructive domains and hybrid Boolean-numeric feature spaces. It provides a theoretical analysis of the attained regret, holding for a large class of query selection strategies, and devises a heuristic strategy to optimize regret in practice. Finally, the paper demonstrates its effectiveness through empirical evaluation against existing competitors on constructive scenarios of increasing complexity.
label: AI

title: Evaluation of bioinspired algorithms for the solution of the job scheduling problem
Abstract: This research utilizes bio-inspired metaheuristics, such as artificial immune systems and ant colony algorithms, which are based on characteristics and behaviors of living things that are interesting in computer science. The paper presents an evaluation of bio-inspired solutions for the combinatorial optimization problem known as Job Shop Scheduling or work planning. In simple terms, the objective is to find a configuration or job stream that minimizes the execution time in machine settings. The performance of the algorithms was characterized and evaluated using reference instances of the job shop scheduling problem, comparing the quality of the solutions obtained with respect to the best known solution of the most effective methods. The solutions were evaluated in two aspects: firstly, in relation to the quality of solutions, taking the makespan as a reference, and secondly, in relation to performance, taking the number of evaluations performed by the algorithm to obtain the best solution.
label: AI

title: Hidden Tree Markov Networks: Deep and Wide Learning for Structured Data
Abstract: This paper introduces the Hidden Tree Markov Network (HTN), a neuro-probabilistic hybrid fusing the representation power of generative models for trees with the incremental and discriminative learning capabilities of neural networks. It proposes a modular architecture where multiple generative models of limited complexity are trained to learn structural feature detectors whose outputs are then combined and integrated by neural layers at a later stage. This makes the model both deep, due to the unfolding of generative models on input structures, and wide, given the potentially large number of generative modules trained in parallel. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art syntactic kernels as well as generative kernels built on the same probabilistic model as the HTN.
label: AI

title: JamBot: Music Theory Aware Chord Based Generation of Polyphonic Music with LSTMs
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for generating polyphonic music based on LSTMs. Music generation occurs in two steps. First, a chord LSTM predicts a chord progression based on a chord embedding. A second LSTM then generates polyphonic music from the predicted chord progression. The generated music sounds pleasing and harmonic, with minimal dissonant notes, and exhibits clear long-term structure similar to what a musician might play during a jam session. The paper demonstrates the musical theory sensibility of this approach by evaluating the learned chord embeddings. Surprisingly, the simple model managed to extract the circle of fifths, an important tool in music theory, from the dataset.
label: AI

title: Transferring Agent Behaviors from Videos via Motion GANs
Abstract: A significant bottleneck in developing general reinforcement learning agents is determining rewards that lead to desirable behaviors under various circumstances. This paper introduces a general mechanism for automatically specifying meaningful behaviors from raw pixels. Specifically, it trains a generative adversarial network to produce short sub-goals represented through motion templates. The paper demonstrates that this approach generates visually meaningful behaviors in unknown environments with novel agents and describes how these motions can be used to train reinforcement learning agents.
label: AI

title: Fullie and Wiselie: A Dual-Stream Recurrent Convolutional Attention Model for Activity Recognition
Abstract: Multimodal features play a crucial role in wearable sensor-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR). Selecting the most salient features adaptively is a promising way to maximize the effectiveness of multimodal sensor data. In this regard, the paper proposes the "collect fully and select wisely (Fullie and Wiselie)" principle and a dual-stream recurrent convolutional attention model, Recurrent Attention and Activity Frame (RAAF), to enhance recognition performance. The model first collects modality features and the relations between each pair of features to generate activity frames, then introduces an attention mechanism to select the most prominent regions from these frames. The selected frames maximize the utilization of valid features while effectively reducing the number of features to be computed. The paper further analyzes the hyper-parameters, accuracy, interpretability, and annotation dependency of the proposed model based on extensive experiments. Results show that RAAF achieves competitive performance on two benchmarked datasets and works effectively in real-life scenarios.
label: AI

title: A Study on Modeling of Inputting Electrical Power of Ultra High Power Electric Furnace by using Fuzzy Rule and Regression Model
Abstract: This paper proposes a method to input electrical model parameters affecting the melting process of high ultra-power (UHP) electric furnaces using fuzzy rules and a regression model. The effectiveness of this method is verified through simulation experiments.
label: AI

title: Cross Temporal Recurrent Networks for Ranking Question Answer Pairs
Abstract: Temporal gates, key components in modern recurrent neural encoders, finely tune recursive composition over time. In models like LSTMs, these gates regulate information retention and discarding, influencing representations and mitigating vanishing gradients. This work explores the concept of learning temporal gates for question-answer pairs, jointly influencing their representations. Our approach leverages 1D convolutional layers to learn these gates, subsequently cross-applying them across the question and answer for joint learning. Empirically, this simple gate sharing achieves competitive performance across multiple benchmarks. Intuitively, our network learns representations aware of each other's memory, akin to pairwise temporal gating. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on two community-based QA datasets and competitive results on one factoid-based QA dataset.
label: AI

title: Delay Aware Intelligent Transient Stability Assessment System
Abstract: Transient stability assessment is crucial for power system design and operation. Advanced synchrophasor measurement techniques have ushered in the era of machine learning for stability assessment. However, existing research often assumes negligible data transmission delays. This paper focuses on the impact of communication delay on synchrophasor-based stability assessment and proposes a delay-aware intelligent system to address this challenge. By leveraging an ensemble of multiple LSTMs, the system can make early assessments with incomplete system variable measurements, achieving significantly shorter response times compared to existing methods. Numerous case studies demonstrate the system's superiority, providing accurate assessments with a response time one-third less than state-of-the-art methodologies. Notably, simulations indicate that noise in the measurements has minimal impact on assessment performance, highlighting the robustness of the proposed system.
label: AI

title: Generating Thematic Chinese Poetry using Conditional Variational Autoencoders with Hybrid Decoders
Abstract: Computer poetry generation is the initial step towards computer writing.  Writing necessitates a theme, yet current sequence-to-sequence models with attention often generate thematically inconsistent poems. We introduce a novel conditional variational autoencoder featuring a hybrid decoder, combining deconvolutional neural networks with general recurrent neural networks, to fully learn topic information via latent variables. This approach significantly improves the relevance of generated poems by representing each line in a context-sensitive and holistic manner, strongly tied to the given keyword and learned topic. A proposed augmented word2vec model further enhances rhythm and symmetry. Tests reveal that the generated poems are mostly satisfying, adhering to regulated rules and consistent themes, with 73.42% receiving an Overall score of at least 3 (out of 5).
label: AI

title: Groupwise Maximin Fair Allocation of Indivisible Goods
Abstract: Fair allocation of indivisible goods among agents is a well-studied problem with maximin share (MMS) as a prominent fairness concept, defining a threshold for fairness. MMS guarantees an agent a minimum utility when partitioning goods into bundles, with other agents picking adversarially. An allocation is deemed fair if every agent receives a bundle valued at least as high as their MMS. While MMS offers a natural fairness benchmark, it has limitations, particularly in ruling out unsatisfactory allocations. Motivated by these drawbacks, this paper introduces a stronger fairness notion: groupwise maximin share guarantee (GMMS). GMMS necessitates achieving the MMS guarantee not only for the grand bundle but also for all agent subgroups, thus strengthening MMS and providing ex-post fairness. We show that GMMS allocations exist in specific settings and establish the existence of approximate GMMS allocations under additive valuations, developing a polynomial-time algorithm to find them. Additionally, a scale of fairness is established, demonstrating that GMMS implies approximate envy-freeness. Empirical results demonstrate the existence of GMMS allocations in a large set of randomly generated instances. For the same instances, our algorithm achieves an approximation factor exceeding the established worst-case bound.
label: AI

title: Asking the Difficult Questions: Goal-Oriented Visual Question Generation via Intermediate Rewards
Abstract: Despite significant progress in vision-and-language tasks, developing methods for asking intelligent, goal-oriented questions about images remains a challenging problem. To address this, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning framework incorporating three novel intermediate rewards: goal-achieved, progressive, and informativeness. These rewards encourage the generation of concise questions that uncover valuable information towards the overall goal. By directly optimizing for questions that efficiently contribute to the goal, we mitigate the tendency of existing methods to produce lengthy, unhelpful queries. We evaluate our model on the GuessWhat?! dataset and demonstrate that the resulting questions significantly improve a standard Guesser's ability to identify a specific object in an image.
label: AI

title: Are You Talking to Me? Reasoned Visual Dialog Generation through Adversarial Learning
Abstract: The Visual Dialogue task necessitates an agent engaging in image-related conversations with humans. It extends Visual Question Answering by requiring the agent to answer questions in the context of the ongoing dialogue. The key challenge lies in maintaining consistent, natural dialogue while accurately answering questions. We introduce a novel approach combining Reinforcement Learning and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate more human-like responses. The GAN mitigates the scarcity of training data and the tendency of typical MLE-based approaches to generate overly concise answers. Critically, the GAN is tightly integrated into the attention mechanism that generates human-interpretable reasons for each answer. The discriminative model of the GAN assesses whether a candidate answer is human-generated given the provided reason, driving the generative model to produce high-quality, well-supported answers. This method achieves state-of-the-art results on the primary benchmark.
label: AI

title: On the Distortion of Voting with Multiple Representative Candidates
Abstract: We investigate positional voting rules where candidates and voters reside in a common metric space, with cardinal preferences naturally defined by distances in this space. In positional voting, each candidate receives a score from each ballot based on their rank order, with the highest total score winning. The cost of a candidate is their sum of distances to all voters, and the distortion of an election is the ratio between the cost of the elected candidate and the optimal candidate. We focus on the case where candidates represent the population, drawn independently from the voter population, and analyze the expected distortion of positional voting rules. Our key finding is a clear and tight characterization of positional voting rules exhibiting constant expected distortion (independent of the number of candidates and the metric space). This result implies constant expected distortion for Borda Count and elections where each voter approves a constant fraction of candidates. Conversely, we obtain super-constant expected distortion for Plurality, Veto, and approving a constant number of candidates. These results contrast with previous findings on voting with metric preferences. When candidates are chosen adversarially, all aforementioned voting rules have distortion linear in the number of candidates or voters. The representative candidate model allows us to differentiate voting rules that appear equally poor in worst-case scenarios.
label: AI

title: Posterior Sampling for Large Scale Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: We present a practical non-episodic PSRL algorithm that, unlike recent state-of-the-art PSRL algorithms, employs a deterministic, model-independent episode switching schedule. Our algorithm, termed deterministic schedule PSRL (DS-PSRL), is efficient in terms of time, sample, and space complexity. Under mild assumptions, we prove a Bayesian regret bound, applicable more generally to multiple parameters and continuous state-action problems. Comparisons with state-of-the-art PSRL algorithms on standard discrete and continuous problems from the literature showcase our algorithm's performance. Finally, we demonstrate how the assumptions of our algorithm satisfy a sensible parametrization for a broad class of problems in sequential recommendations.
label: AI

title: Science Driven Innovations Powering Mobile Product: Cloud AI vs. Device AI Solutions on Smart Device
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surging popularity of mobile devices like iPhones, driven by the convenience they offer. Rich user profiling and behavioral data from diverse sources (per-app, app-interaction, system-interaction levels) enable the delivery of enhanced services like recommendation and advertisement targeting. This further boosts revenue through a deeper understanding of user behavior and improved user engagement. To delight customers, intelligent personal assistants like Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Google Now are highly desirable, providing real-time audio, video, and image recognition, natural language understanding, user-friendly interfaces, personalized recommendations, and effective advertisement targeting. This paper presents research efforts conducted on mobile devices to deliver smarter and more convenient services. Leveraging statistics, big data science, machine learning, deep learning, user modeling, and marketing techniques, these efforts aim to significantly enhance user growth, engagement, and satisfaction on mobile devices. The new features are developed on both cloud and device sides, working harmoniously to improve existing services and increase user happiness. Case studies illustrate the system and algorithmic design of these features, demonstrating how science-driven innovation delivers better technology services and drives business revenue. These research efforts have clear scientific contributions, published in top venues, and play increasingly important roles in mobile AI products.
label: AI

title: SPARE: Spiking Networks Acceleration Using CMOS ROM-Embedded RAM as an In-Memory-Computation Primitive
Abstract: Despite the immense success of artificial intelligence, hardware systems running these algorithms consume significantly more energy compared to the human brain, mainly due to extensive data movements between memory units and computation cores. Spiking neural networks (SNNs), built using biologically plausible neuron and synaptic models, have emerged as a power-efficient alternative for designing cognitive applications. These algorithms involve various lookup-table (LUT)-based function evaluations, such as high-order polynomials and transcendental functions for solving complex neuro-synaptic models, which typically require additional storage. To address this, we propose SPARE - an in-memory, distributed processing architecture built on ROM-embedded RAM technology for accelerating SNNs. ROM-embedded RAMs enable the storage of LUTs within a typical memory array without additional area overhead. Our proposed architecture consists of a 2-D array of Processing Elements (PEs). Since most computations are performed locally within each PE, unnecessary data transfers are minimized, mitigating the von-Neumann bottleneck. We evaluate SPARE for two ROM-Embedded RAM structures: CMOS-based ROM-Embedded SRAMs (R-SRAMs) and STT-MRAM-based ROM-Embedded MRAMs (R-MRAMs). We analyze trade-offs in energy, area, and performance for using these technologies on various image classification benchmarks. Moreover, we leverage the additional storage density to implement complex neuro-synaptic functionalities. This enhances the architecture's utility by providing implementation of any neuron/synaptic behavior as needed by the application. Our results show up to 1.75x, 1.95x, and 1.95x improvement in energy, iso-storage area, and iso-area performance, respectively, by using neural network accelerators built on ROM-embedded RAM primitives.
label: AI

title: What's up with Privacy?: User Preferences and Privacy Concerns in Intelligent Personal Assistants
Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have empowered individuals to rely on automated systems for various purposes. Prominent examples include voice-enabled systems like Amazon Echo and Google Home, known as Intelligent Personal Assistants (IPAs). Despite growing concerns about privacy and ethical implications, IPA users seem to continue using these systems. This study aims to investigate user privacy concerns and their coping mechanisms while using IPAs. By analyzing online reviews and survey responses, this paper provides insights into detected markers related to user interests and privacy challenges. These insights reveal a generally positive perception of IPAs in daily life, regardless of privacy concerns. However, a significant percentage of users express privacy concerns and take actions to address them. While some users initially expressed no privacy concerns, their concerns increased upon learning about the "always listening" feature of these devices.
label: AI

title: SquishedNets: Squishing SqueezeNet further for edge device scenarios via deep evolutionary synthesis
Abstract: Deep neural networks have demonstrably outperformed other machine learning methods across a wide range of applications. However, their high computational and memory demands pose a significant challenge for widespread deployment on edge devices like mobile phones and consumer devices. Recent research has focused on developing smaller deep neural network architectures more suitable for edge devices, with SqueezeNet (4.8MB model size) being a notable example. This study explores the utility of combining architectural modifications and an evolutionary synthesis strategy for synthesizing even smaller deep neural architectures based on the SqueezeNet v1.1 macroarchitecture, specifically for applications with fewer target classes. Architectural modifications are first implemented in SqueezeNet v1.1 to accommodate a 10-class ImageNet-10 dataset. Subsequently, an evolutionary synthesis strategy is leveraged to synthesize more efficient deep neural networks based on this modified macroarchitecture. The resulting SquishedNets exhibit model sizes ranging from 2.4MB to 0.95MB (~5.17X smaller than SqueezeNet v1.1, or 253X smaller than AlexNet). Despite their reduced size, SquishedNets achieve accuracies ranging from 81.2% to 77% and processing speeds of 156 images/sec to 256 images/sec on an Nvidia Jetson TX1 embedded chip. These preliminary findings suggest that combining architectural modifications and an evolutionary synthesis strategy can be a valuable tool for producing compact deep neural network architectures well-suited for edge device scenarios.

title: A generalised framework for detailed classification of swimming paths inside the Morris Water Maze
Abstract: The Morris Water Maze is a widely used tool in behavioral neuroscience for studying spatial learning in rodents. Over time, various methods for analyzing rodent data collected in this task have been proposed. These methods range from classical performance measurements (escape latency, rodent speed, quadrant preference) to more sophisticated categorization techniques that classify animal swimming paths into behavioral classes known as strategies. Classification techniques provide additional insights into actual animal behaviors but are limited by their reliance on machine learning expertise. We previously demonstrated that animals implement diverse strategies, and classifying whole trajectories can lead to the loss of important information. This work introduces a generalized and robust classification methodology that employs majority voting to enhance classification performance and eliminate the need for manual tuning. Based on this framework, we have developed a comprehensive software capable of performing the full analysis described in this paper. The software provides a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) for entering trajectory data, segmenting and labeling it, and generating reports and figures of the results.
