title: Malicious URL Detection using Machine Learning: A Survey
Abstract: Malicious URLs pose a significant cybersecurity threat, hosting malicious content that can lead to financial losses, data theft, and malware infections. Traditional blacklisting methods are ineffective against newly generated URLs. Machine learning has emerged as a promising approach for malicious URL detection. This article provides a comprehensive survey of malicious URL detection techniques using machine learning. It formally defines the task, categorizes existing literature, and reviews contributions across different dimensions (feature representation, algorithm design, etc.). The survey aims to inform machine learning researchers, engineers, cybersecurity professionals, and practitioners about the state-of-the-art and facilitate their own research and applications. It also discusses practical system design issues, open research challenges, and future research directions.

title: Leveraging SDN to Monitor Critical Infrastricture Networks in a Smarter Way
Abstract: Industrial Control Systems (ICSes) in critical infrastructures rely on communication networks to exchange vital data. To enhance cybersecurity in these systems, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSes) are recommended for monitoring data traffic. The placement of IDSes is crucial to monitor as many traffic streams as possible. This is particularly important in ICS networks, where traffic is confined to geographically distributed and largely autonomous subnetworks. This paper proposes a methodology and software architecture that leverage spare bandwidth in over-provisioned ICS networks to forward traffic stream replicas to a single IDS at an arbitrary location. It utilizes Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and considers the stability of ICS network topology and predictable bandwidth needs. The approach fulfills strict requirements for packet loss, ensuring functional and security integrity. The methodology is evaluated on real-world network topologies.

title: How will the Internet of Things enable Augmented Personalized Health?
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming healthcare by enabling data collection from individuals and their environment. This data can be used to develop new healthcare solutions, but interpreting it to understand an individual's health is challenging. It requires integrating clinical records, behavioral information, social and environmental factors, adherence to health objectives, and clinical knowledge. Augmented Personalized Healthcare (APH) leverages AI to exploit this vast data and medical knowledge, enabling personalized health management strategies. The paper discusses APH's application to Asthma and other diseases, illustrating technology-assisted health management. It also identifies prominent IoT and patient-generated health data (PGHD) efforts focused on converting multimodal data into actionable information. The roles of Contextualization, Abstraction, and Personalization in an evidence-based semantic perception approach are discussed.

title: Geometric optics for Rayleigh wavetrains in d-dimensional nonlinear elasticity
Abstract: Rayleigh waves are surface waves that propagate at the boundary of an elastic solid. This paper addresses the long-standing question of whether a leading term approximation to the solution of the Rayleigh wave equation is close to the exact solution. The paper proves a positive answer for Rayleigh wavetrains in any space dimension. The case of Rayleigh pulses in two dimensions was previously addressed by Coulombel and Williams. For highly oscillatory Rayleigh wavetrains, high-order approximate solutions are constructed, consisting of the leading term and correctors. Error analysis demonstrates that for small wavelengths, the leading term is close to the exact solution in the L-infinity norm on a fixed time interval. The error analysis can be applied to other wave types where high-order approximations can be constructed.

title: Dynamic Load-Balancing Vertical Control for Large-Scale Software-Defined Internet of Things
Abstract: The increasing popularity of the Internet of Things (IoT) highlights the need for efficient network flow management to optimize performance. Traditional IoT architecture limits current traffic management technologies, preventing differentiated services for large-scale IoT. Software-defined Internet of Things (SD-IoT) is a new paradigm that separates control and data planes, enabling centralized logic control. This paper presents a general framework for SD-IoT consisting of SD-IoT controllers and SD-IoT switches. Controllers use resource pooling technology for centralized network control, while switches integrate with gateway functions for data access and forwarding. The SD-IoT controller pool is designed as a vertical control architecture with main and base control layers. The paper proposes dynamic balancing algorithms for both main and base controllers, based on election mechanisms and balanced delay, respectively. Experimental results show that these algorithms effectively ensure message consistency and workload balancing.
label: AI

title: Distributed Laser Charging: A Wireless Power Transfer Approach
Abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) holds promise for providing convenient and continuous energy supply to electronics. However, existing WPT technologies struggle to deliver Watt-level power over meter-level distances, limiting their application to IoT and mobile devices. Distributed laser charging (DLC) emerges as a potential solution, offering WPT with similar accessibility to Wi-Fi communications. This paper presents a multi-module DLC system model, explaining its physical fundamentals and mathematical formulas. The model enables evaluation of power conversion/transmission for individual modules, considering laser wavelength, transmission attenuation, and photovoltaic-cell (PV-cell) temperature. Based on linear approximation of electricity-to-laser and laser-to-electricity power conversion, the paper derives the maximum power transmission efficiency in closed form. It demonstrates the variation of efficiency with supply power, laser wavelength, transmission distance, and PV-cell temperature. Similar to maximizing information capacity in wireless information transfer (WIT), maximizing power transmission efficiency is crucial for WPT. This study provides theoretical insights and practical guidelines for DLC system design.

title: The Age of Information in Multihop Networks
Abstract: Information updates in multihop networks, such as IoT and intelligent transportation systems, are crucial. This paper focuses on minimizing the age of a single information flow in interference-free multihop networks. When preemption is allowed and packet transmission times are exponentially distributed, the paper proves that a preemptive Last-Generated, First-Served (LGFS) policy minimizes the age processes across all nodes compared to any other causal policy. For New-Better-than-Used (NBU) distributions, the non-preemptive LGFS policy is shown to be within a constant age gap from the optimal average age. However, numerical results indicate that the preemptive LGFS policy may deviate significantly from the optimal for some NBU distributions. When preemption is prohibited and packet transmission times are arbitrarily distributed, the non-preemptive LGFS policy minimizes age processes across all nodes among work-conserving policies. These results hold under general conditions, including arbitrary packet generation and arrival times, and for minimizing age processes in stochastic ordering and non-decreasing functionals.

title: An improved sieve of Eratosthenes
Abstract: This paper presents an improved Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm that requires O(N^(1/3)(log N)^(2/3)) space and O(N log N) time to find all primes up to N. This improvement over traditional versions, which take O(sqrt(N)) space and linear time in N, enables efficient prime finding in subintervals of length Omega(N^(1/3) (log N)^(2/3)). The approach is based on Diophantine approximation and Voronoi's work on the Dirichlet divisor problem. Unlike previous methods, this sieve can also be used for integer factorization, not just prime generation.

title: Android Malware Detection using Deep Learning on API Method Sequences
Abstract: Android's popularity extends beyond mobile devices to the Internet of Things (IoT), making it a prime target for malicious apps. This necessitates robust malware detection solutions. This paper proposes MalDozer, an automatic Android malware detection and family attribution framework that leverages deep learning for sequence classification. MalDozer analyzes the raw sequence of an app's API method calls to learn malicious and benign patterns, enabling malware detection. It can be deployed on servers, mobile devices, and even IoT devices. Evaluation on multiple Android malware datasets shows that MalDozer accurately detects malware and attributes them to their families, achieving an F1-Score of 96%-99% and a false positive rate of 0.06%-2%.

title: Smart Fog: Fog Computing Framework for Unsupervised Clustering Analytics in Wearable Internet of Things
Abstract: The increasing use of wearables in smart telehealth generates heterogeneous medical big data, requiring efficient processing. This paper proposes and evaluates the use of low-resource machine learning on Fog devices for smart healthcare. Traditional telecare systems rely on cloud processing for physiological data analysis. The proposed architecture employs Intel Edison and Raspberry Pi as Fog computers for unsupervised machine learning big data analysis. Validation studies on real-world pathological speech data from Parkinson's disease (PD) patients demonstrate the potential of Fog-based machine learning for analyzing physiological data obtained from smartwatches. This approach could be beneficial for other wearable IoT applications in smart telehealth scenarios, moving machine learning from cloud backend to edge computing devices.

title: The Internet of Battle Things
Abstract: Future battlefields will be densely populated with various entities ("things"), some intelligent and others less so, performing sensing, communication, action, and collaboration. This vision of the Internet of Battle Things (IoBT) presents significant challenges, particularly in communication flexibility and adaptability. This paper explores these challenges, outlining key research directions and approaches for overcoming them.

title: How do you Command an Army of Intelligent Things?
Abstract: Within a decade, we will need to manage a growing number of intelligent things, including robots and agents. This interconnected workforce of humans and intelligent things presents challenges in organizational management, especially in the demanding context of warfare. This paper examines Command and Control (C2) in mixed human-thing organizations, highlighting the need for effective human and machine collaboration. It emphasizes the importance of providing decision-makers with necessary information and ensuring its effective utilization for C2 functions. The paper discusses challenges faced by commanders in managing such organizations, including the need for human capabilities in areas where things are lacking, such as explanation, trust building, bonding, understanding personal agendas, emotions, and politics.

title: Learning-Based Computation Offloading for IoT Devices with Energy Harvesting
Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices can leverage mobile-edge computing (MEC) and energy harvesting (EH) to enhance performance and extend battery life for computationally intensive applications. This paper investigates computation offloading for IoT devices with EH in wireless networks with multiple MEC devices (base stations, access points) having varying resources and communication capabilities. A reinforcement learning based computation offloading framework is proposed, where an IoT device chooses the MEC device and offloading rate based on battery level, previous bandwidth, and predicted harvested energy. "Hotbooting" Q-learning and fast deep Q-network (DQN) based offloading schemes are introduced, allowing the IoT device to achieve optimal performance without complete knowledge of MEC models, energy consumption, and computation latency. The proposed schemes achieve optimal offloading policies after sufficient learning time and provide performance bounds under typical MEC scenarios. Simulations using wireless power transfer for ambient radio-frequency energy harvesting demonstrate that the fast DQN-based scheme outperforms benchmark Q-learning, reducing energy consumption, computation delay, task drop ratio, and improving overall utility in dynamic MEC environments.

title: COOJA Network Simulator: Exploring the Infinite Possible Ways to Compute the Performance Metrics of IOT Based Smart Devices to Understand the Working of IOT Based Compression & Routing Protocols
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the Internet of Things (IoT), exploring its core concepts and underlying technologies. It highlights the integration of physical systems and human interaction within a networked environment. The paper delves into key protocols like 6LoWPAN (IPV6 Low Power Personal Area Networks) for efficient IPV6 address utilization and RPL routing protocol for low-power devices. The functionality of these protocols is further illustrated using the Contiki OS-based COOJA Network simulator, showcasing real-time simulations of routing and compression processes.

title: Intelligent Device Discovery in the Internet of Things - Enabling the Robot Society
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, connecting billions of smart devices across various locations and times, fostering a diverse range of applications and interactions between humans and objects. The paper addresses the challenge of enabling autonomous device discovery in this heterogeneous and pervasive landscape. To achieve fast, scalable, and efficient discovery, the authors propose a Social-Aware and Distributed (SAND) scheme. SAND utilizes a novel device ranking criteria that considers factors like degree, social relationship diversity, clustering coefficient, and betweenness. This ranking system allows discovery requests to navigate strategically through key devices at network intersections, minimizing the number of intermediate devices required to reach the desired target. SAND paves the way for IoT devices to establish social connections, form self-organized computing groups, and collaborate on novel applications and services, ultimately paving the path towards a robot society.

title: A ReRAM Physically Unclonable Function (ReRAM PUF)-based Approach to Enhance Authentication Security in Software Defined Wireless Networks
Abstract: The surge in interconnected wireless devices in Internet of Things (IoT) networks necessitates a new approach to data flow management under software defined wireless networking (SDWN). The limited resources and centralized control within SDWN pose significant security challenges. Authentication between controllers and forwarding devices is a key concern due to the large-scale and heterogeneous nature of IoT networks. Existing authentication protocols based on public key infrastructure (PKI) are inadequate due to cost, vulnerability, and key management complexities. This paper proposes a novel security protocol leveraging physical unclonable functions (PUFs), a hardware-based security mechanism, to enhance authentication in SDWNs. The protocol employs digital PUFs derived from the inherent randomness of Resistive Random Access Memory (ReRAM) materials commonly found in IoT devices, enabling secure authentication and access control. These PUFs utilize a multi-state approach to mitigate environmental variations, reducing potential errors in challenge-response pairs. The paper also introduces a PUF-based PKI protocol to secure controllers within SDWNs, and the performance of ReRAM-based PUFs is validated through experimental results.

title: A topological interpretation of three Leibnizian principles within the functional extensions
Abstract: This paper provides a precise logico-mathematical formulation of three philosophical principles associated with Leibniz: the Identity of Indiscernibles, Possibility as Consistency, and the Transfer Principle. These principles are interpreted within the framework of Functional Extensions, mathematical structures generalizing compactifications, completions, and elementary extensions of models. Within this framework, the principles are represented as topological or algebraic properties: a property of separation, a property of compactness, and a property of directness, respectively. The paper concludes that while these Leibnizian principles can be fulfilled in pairs, they cannot be fulfilled all three together.

title: WiBall: A Time-Reversal Focusing Ball Method for Indoor Tracking
Abstract: The increasing popularity of indoor tracking applications in the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the development of WiBall, a calibration-free indoor tracking system that can operate effectively in non-line-of-sight scenarios. Leveraging the time-reversal focusing effect of radio signals, WiBall achieves high accuracy in moving distance estimation by exploiting a stationary and location-independent property. Combining this with direction estimation based on inertial measurement units and location correction using floorplan constraints, WiBall demonstrates decimeter-level accuracy in tracking moving objects across different environments. Its ability to accommodate a large number of users with a single device pair makes it a cost-effective and scalable solution, promising a wide range of future indoor tracking applications.

title: Squeezed Convolutional Variational AutoEncoder for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Edge Device Industrial Internet of Things
Abstract: This paper proposes a Squeezed Convolutional Variational AutoEncoder (SCVAE) for anomaly detection in time series data within the context of Edge Computing in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). The SCVAE model is evaluated using labeled time series data from UCI datasets, providing precise performance metrics. Real-world data is also utilized for indirect model performance comparison. The paper further demonstrates the benefits of applying Fire Modules from SqueezeNet, showcasing reduced model size and inference times while maintaining similar performance levels.

title: The stability and rapid exponential stabilization of heat equation in non-cylindrical domain
Abstract: This paper investigates the stability and stabilizability of the heat equation in non-cylindrical domains. It reveals that for a specific class of initial values, the system exhibits polynomial stability rather than exponential stability. The paper explores the rapid exponential stabilization of the system through the application of the backstepping method.

title: Incentive Mechanism Design for Wireless Energy Harvesting-Based Internet of Things
Abstract: Radio frequency energy harvesting (RFEH) presents a promising solution for wirelessly charging low-power Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The future IoT landscape will require not only traditional data access points (DAPs) for data collection but also energy access points (EAPs) to ensure sustainable operation of IoT devices. This paper addresses the challenge of incentivizing EAPs to charge IoT devices associated with DAPs operated by different entities. The authors analyze a practical scenario with asymmetric information, where the DAP lacks knowledge of EAP channel conditions and energy costs. They extend existing Stackelberg game-based approaches to incorporate asymmetric information, defining and maximizing the expected utility of the DAP. To address asymmetric information more efficiently, a contract theory-based framework is developed, deriving the optimal contract to maximize DAP utility and social welfare. Simulation results demonstrate the significant performance degradation of the Stackelberg game-based framework due to information asymmetry, while the proposed contract theory-based approach using asymmetric information outperforms the complete information scenario. This highlights the critical role of market structure, allowing EAPs to optimize received power with full freedom, in determining system performance.

title: Causal perturbative QED and infra-red states
Abstract: At the classical level, the electromagnetic field can be accurately described at spatial infinity. title: Energy Efficient Resource Allocation in Machine-to-Machine Communications with Multiple Access and Energy Harvesting for IoT
Abstract: This paper examines energy-efficient resource allocation for machine-to-machine (M2M) enabled cellular networks with non-linear energy harvesting, focusing on two multiple access strategies: non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and time division multiple access (TDMA). The goal is to minimize total network energy consumption through joint power control and time allocation, considering circuit power consumption. For both NOMA and TDMA, the paper demonstrates that it is optimal for each machine type communication device (MTCD) to transmit with the minimum throughput, and that energy consumption for each MTCD is a convex function with respect to allocated transmission time. Based on these optimal conditions, the original optimization problem for NOMA is transformed into an equivalent problem, solved suboptimally using an iterative power control and time allocation algorithm. An appropriate variable transformation also transforms the original optimization problem for TDMA into a tractable problem, allowing for iterative solutions. Numerical results confirm the theoretical findings, demonstrating that NOMA consumes less total energy than TDMA in low circuit power regimes for MTCDs, while TDMA achieves better network energy efficiency than NOMA in high circuit power regimes.

title: An Amateur Drone Surveillance System Based on Cognitive Internet of Things
Abstract: Drones, also known as mini-unmanned aerial vehicles, have gained immense popularity due to their diverse applications in communication, photography, agriculture, surveillance, and public services. It provides a comprehensive overview of current research in this domain, proposing a vision, named Dragnet, that adapts the emerging cognitive Internet of Things framework for amateur drone surveillance. The paper delves into the key enabling techniques for Dragnet, highlighting technical challenges and open issues. It also presents a case study on the detection and classification of authorized and unauthorized amateur drones, focusing on scenarios where only authorized drones are permitted to fly, such as during significant events.

title: Practical Synchronization Waveform for Massive Machine-Type-Communications

This comment addresses practical considerations not covered in the original paper, including obtaining frequency error information from the waveform, refining timing estimation, and adjusting waveform parameters to meet various spectral requirements. These issues are crucial for practical implementation of the proposed synchronization waveform.

title: IoT based Platform as a Service for Provisioning of Concurrent Applications
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has witnessed explosive growth, with an estimated 20 billion devices projected to be connected by 2020. This paper proposes an IoT-based Cloud to leverage the PaaS model, providing a platform to host concurrent applications for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This model uniquely allocates network interfaces to specific containers, enabling seamless communication among processes and supporting the diverse requirements of IoT applications.

title: Optimal Dynamic Sensor Subset Selection for Tracking a Time-Varying Stochastic Process
Abstract: Motivated by the Internet-of-things and sensor networks for cyberphysical systems, this paper addresses the problem of dynamic sensor activation for tracking time-varying processes. The tradeoff between energy efficiency, decreasing with the number of active sensors, and fidelity, increasing with active sensors, is investigated. The paper examines the minimization of time-averaged mean-squared error over an infinite horizon, constrained by the mean number of active sensors. The proposed methods combine Gibbs sampling, stochastic approximation for learning, and modifications to consensus algorithms to create high-performance, energy-efficient tracking mechanisms with active sensor selection. Three scenarios are considered: centralized tracking of an i.i.d. process, distributed tracking of an i.i.d. process, and finally, distributed tracking of a Markov chain. The challenge in the i.i.d. case lies in learning the process distribution parameterized by a known or unknown parameter. Key theoretical results prove that the proposed algorithms converge to local optima for the two i.i.d. process cases, with numerical results suggesting that global optimality is achieved. The proposed distributed tracking algorithm for a Markov chain, based on Kalman-consensus filtering and stochastic approximation, demonstrates comparable error performance to a centralized Kalman filter.

title: Adversarial Networks for Prostate Cancer Detection
Abstract: The large number of trainable parameters in deep neural networks makes them inherently data-hungry, posing challenges for medical imaging, where data scarcity is common. This paper proposes employing adversarial training for segmentation networks to mitigate these issues. The research focuses on segmenting aggressive prostate cancer using challenging MRI images from 152 patients, demonstrating the proposed scheme's superiority over the current standard in terms of detection sensitivity and Dice score for aggressive prostate cancer. Notably, the gains achieved are particularly pronounced in the small dataset limit.

title: Learning to Segment Every Thing
Abstract: Most object instance segmentation methods require all training examples to be labeled with segmentation masks. This requirement makes annotation expensive for new categories, limiting instance segmentation models to a small number of well-annotated classes. This paper proposes a novel partially supervised training paradigm, along with a weight transfer function, to train instance segmentation models on a large set of categories with box annotations but only a small fraction of mask annotations. This approach allows Mask R-CNN to detect and segment 3000 visual concepts using box annotations from the Visual Genome dataset and mask annotations from the 80 classes in the COCO dataset. Evaluation on the COCO dataset demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach, paving the way for instance segmentation models with broader comprehension of the visual world.

title: Towards Information-Centric Networking (ICN) Naming for Internet of Things (IoT):The Case of Smart Campus
Abstract: Information-Centric Networking (ICN), specifically Name Data Networking (NDN), is a name-based (content-based) networking approach that treats named content as a "first-class citizen," making it an ideal candidate for the future internet. NDN's striking features, such as named-data self-secured content, name-based forwarding, in-network caching, and mobility support, align well with the Internet of Things (IoT) environment, aiming to facilitate communication among smart devices and integrate all internet-based smart applications. However, IoT poses challenges for network architecture, requiring support for heterogeneous devices and scalability. IoT may rely on names and addresses of billions of devices and must efficiently manage the massive data generated every second. This paper focuses on the smart campus application of IoT, which has gained significant attention due to its diverse benefits. To design NDN for IoT, a sophisticated naming scheme is crucial, motivating this work. The paper examines NDN-IoT smart campus (in terms of connected devices and content) and identifies the lack of a suitable naming and addressing mechanism. Consequently, it proposes an NDN-based Hybrid Naming Scheme (NDN-HNS) for IoT-based Smart Campus (IoTSC).

title: An Efficient Fog-Assisted Unstable Sensor Detection Scheme with Privacy Preserved
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a prominent topic in both research and industry. The future IoT envisions an enormous number of sensors constantly collecting physical information to enable control centers to make informed decisions and enhance quality of service (QoS). However, faulty sensors can generate inaccurate data, compromising decision-making. To guarantee QoS, the system must be able to detect faulty sensors and eliminate the impact of inaccurate data. While various faulty sensor detection mechanisms have been developed for wireless sensor networks (WSNs), some are only suitable for WSNs, while others impose a communication burden on the control center. This paper proposes an efficient faulty sensor detection scheme for general IoT applications, leveraging fog computing to reduce the computational and communication load on the control center. To maintain sensor data privacy, the Paillier Cryptosystem is employed in fog computing, with batch verification techniques ensuring efficient authentication. Performance analysis demonstrates the scheme's ability to conserve communication resources for the control center, achieve a high true positive ratio while maintaining an acceptable false positive ratio, withstand security attacks, and preserve data privacy.

title: A Novel Approach for Security Situational Awareness in the Internet of Things
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) comprises diverse heterogeneous devices and faces numerous security threats. Modeling the security of IoT remains a significant challenge. The SCPN computes all possible attack paths, dynamically considering antagonistic behavior of both attackers and defenders based on Game Theory. Two attack scenarios in a smart home environment are used to demonstrate the model's effectiveness. The proposed model can generate a macroscopic trend curve of the security situation. Analysis shows the model's capabilities in identifying vulnerable devices, potential attack paths, and mitigating attack impact. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to establish a dynamic SSA model for complex IoT-based smart environments.

title: Bars in dark matter-dominated dwarf galaxy discs
Abstract: This paper investigates the shape and kinematics of simulated dwarf galaxy discs using the APOSTLE suite of ΛCDM cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. The study reveals that a significant fraction of these gas-rich, star-forming discs exhibit weak bars in their stellar component, despite being dark matter-dominated systems. The bar pattern shape and orientation reflect the ellipticity of the dark matter potential, with its rotation locked to the slow figure rotation of the triaxial dark halo. The bar-like nature of the potential induces non-circular motions in the gas component, including strong bisymmetric flows observable as m=3 harmonic perturbations in the HI line-of-sight velocity fields. Similar bisymmetric flows are observed in many galaxies from the THINGS and LITTLE THINGS surveys, although their amplitudes are typically weaker than those simulated. The results indicate that bar-like patterns can emerge even in the absence of dominant baryons, and they are sufficiently common to warrant consideration when analyzing the gas kinematics of dwarf galaxy discs.

title: Scalable Object Detection for Stylized Objects
Abstract: Recent advancements in convolutional neural networks and monolithic model architectures have enabled state-of-the-art object detection models to reliably and accurately scale to thousands of classes. However, scaling to tens of thousands, millions, or billions of unique objects poses significant challenges. Furthermore, bounding box-trained end-to-end models require extensive training data, making annotation labor-intensive. While hierarchical approaches can sometimes scale to thousands of classes, clean image annotations quickly become unmanageable. This paper presents a two-layer object detection method for brand logos and other stylized objects, where prototypical images exist, enabling scaling to large numbers of unique classes. The first layer, a CNN from the Single Shot Multibox Detector family, learns to propose regions where stylized objects are likely to appear. The contents of these proposed bounding boxes are then compared against an image index optimized for retrieval tasks. The proposed architecture scales to a large number of object classes, allows for the continuous addition of new classes without retraining, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on stylized object detection tasks like logo recognition.

title: Antenna Current Optimization and Realizations for Far-Field Pattern Shaping
Abstract: Shaping the far-field radiation pattern of small antennas is a challenging task, and realizing non-dipole radiation from small to intermediate-sized antennas is difficult. This paper examines the antenna bandwidth cost associated with such constraints and, in some cases, designs antennas that approach the theoretical limits. Far-field shaping is particularly relevant for Internet-of-things (IoT) and Wi-Fi applications, as spatial filtering can mitigate package loss through reduced mutual interference, improving power efficiency. Even careful far-field shaping of smaller antennas can lead to a significant reduction in the best achievable bandwidth. Therefore, understanding the constraints that small antennas can accommodate is crucial. The paper defines a power front-to-back ratio and a related beam-shaping constraint that can be used in optimization for the minimum Q-factor. The research demonstrates that this non-convex Q-factor optimization can be solved using the semi-definite relaxation technique. It further shows that certain optimized non-standard radiation patterns can be realized using a multi-position feeding strategy with a moderate loss of Q-factor (Qantenna ≤ 1.61Qoptimal).

title: Designing Secure Ethereum Smart Contracts: A Finite State Machine Based Approach

These vulnerabilities pose a serious concern as contracts often handle valuable financial assets, and contract bugs are inherently unfixable. To assist developers in creating more secure smart contracts, this paper introduces FSolidM, a framework rooted in rigorous semantics for designing contracts as Finite State Machines (FSMs). The research presents a tool for creating FSMs on a user-friendly graphical interface and for automatically generating Ethereum contracts. Additionally, it introduces a set of design patterns implemented as plugins that developers can easily incorporate into their contracts to enhance security and functionality.

title: A Manifesto for Future Generation Cloud Computing: Research Directions for the Next Decade
Abstract: Cloud computing has revolutionized the computer science landscape over the past decade, establishing computing as the fifth utility. It has garnered significant attention from academia, industry, and government bodies, becoming the backbone of the modern economy by offering subscription-based services following a pay-as-you-go model. This has led to several positive outcomes, including shorter establishment times for startups, scalable global enterprise applications, improved cost-to-value association for scientific and high-performance computing applications, and various invocation/execution models for pervasive and ubiquitous applications. Recent technological advancements and paradigms like serverless computing, software-defined networking, the Internet of Things, and processing at the network edge create new opportunities for cloud computing. However, they also pose significant challenges, demanding new approaches, research strategies, and reevaluation of existing models addressing issues like scalability, elasticity, reliability, security, sustainability, and application models. This manifesto addresses these challenges by identifying major open issues, emerging trends, and impact areas in cloud computing. It proposes research directions for the next decade, contributing to the realization of Future Generation Cloud Computing. |||

title: Engineering Resilient Collective Adaptive Systems by Self-Stabilisation
Abstract: Collective adaptive systems, a new class of networked computational systems, are particularly suited for applications such as smart cities, complex sensor networks, and the Internet of Things. These systems are characterized by large scale, heterogeneous communication models, and the need for self-adaptiveness to handle unforeseen changes in operating conditions. This paper presents a methodology that combines formal theory and computer simulation to address the challenge of engineering reusable pieces of distributed behavior in these systems. The methodology utilizes field calculus, a computational model that captures the notion of aggregate network-level computation.  It leverages a field calculus fragment that generates self-stabilizing behavior, guaranteeing a correct and stable final state despite transient perturbations. The methodology also investigates the impact of different implementations of building blocks with provably equivalent functional properties on system performance using simulation. This work sheds light on identifying core building blocks of collective behavior and selecting implementations that optimize system performance while maintaining overall system functionality and resilience.

title: A novel JXTA-based architecture for implementing heterogenous Networks of Things
Abstract: This paper introduces EmbJXTAChord, a novel peer-to-peer (P2P) architecture designed for developing IoT applications over heterogeneous networks. EmbJXTAChord integrates features from JXTA, EXI, and CoAP, providing capabilities like distributed and fault-tolerant resource discovery, transparent routing over subnetworks, and application protocol independence from the transport protocol. It supports various communication technologies, including TCP/HTTP, Bluetooth RFCOMM, and 6LoWPAN, enabling connectivity with a wide range of IoT devices. The architecture also includes security features such as secure peergroups and group encryption for both unicast and multicast communication. EmbJXTAChord incorporates jxCOAP-E, a new CoAP implementation that leverages EmbJXTAChord's transport mechanisms, providing a RESTful service architecture for peer-to-peer networks. Unlike traditional CoAP, jxCOAP-E offers a distributed and fault-tolerant service discovery mechanism and support for secure multicast communications. This paper presents EmbJXTAChord, discusses its design challenges, and compares its experimental performance with state-of-the-art solutions.

title: Backscatter Communications for the Internet of Things: A Stochastic Geometry Approach
Abstract: Inspired by recent advancements in the Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Power Transfer (WPT), this paper investigates a network architecture consisting of power beacons (PBs) and passive backscatter nodes (BNs). PBs transmit a continuous sinusoidal wave, and BNs reflect a portion of this signal while harvesting the remaining energy for their operation. A BN harvests energy from multiple nearby PBs and modulates its information bits on the composite CW through backscatter modulation. The analysis accounts for the double fading channel and its dependence on the spatial distribution of BNs and PBs. Utilizing stochastic geometry, the paper derives expressions for coverage probability and capacity, which are dependent on system parameters. The study reveals that coverage probability decreases with an increase in BN density while network capacity improves. The paper further compares the performance of this network with a regular powered network and shows that for high PB densities, the coverage probability of the former network approaches that of the latter.

title: Evaluating the Performance of eMTC and NB-IoT for Smart City Applications

The paper also presents a model for analytically evaluating latency and the maximum number of devices in a network. Furthermore, the main functionalities of both technologies are implemented and simulated in the NS-3 network simulator to assess end-to-end latency and maximum device capacity. Numerical results demonstrate that both technologies can achieve a battery life of 8 years in low-coverage scenarios. The comparison reveals that eMTC consumes less energy than NB-IoT for certain coverage conditions and data lengths. Moreover, eMTC supports a greater number of devices than NB-IoT while offering significantly lower latency.

title: Spin-order-induced multiferroicity in LiCuFe2(VO4)3 and disorder effects in NaCuFe2(VO4)3
Abstract: Mixed spin chain compounds, ACuFe2(VO4)3 (A = Li, Na), exhibit magnetically ordered states at TN ~ 11 K (Li) or ~ 9 K (Na) and undergo further transformations in magnetic order at T* ~ 7 K (Li) or ~ 5 K (Na). These transformations are evident in magnetic susceptibility and specific heat measurements. While NaCuFe2(VO4)3 shows no anomalies in its dielectric properties, LiCuFe2(VO4)3 exhibits a step-like feature preceding a sharp peak in permittivity at TN. These findings suggest the presence of spin-order-induced ferroelectricity in the Li compound and its absence in the Na compound. However, Mössbauer spectroscopy analysis reveals a similar wide distribution of hyperfine fields between T* and TN for both compounds. First-principles calculations also yield similar magnetic exchange interaction parameters for both compounds. These observations point to the crucial role of alkali metal mobility within the crystal structure in explaining the improper multiferroicity in one compound and its absence in the other.

title: Long-term observations of pulsars in the globular clusters 47 Tucanae and M15
Abstract: Multi-decade observing campaigns of the globular clusters 47 Tucanae and M15 have yielded numerous discoveries. In M15, the relativistic spin precession effect in PSR B2127+11C has been studied using full-Stokes observations.  These observations allow for modeling the precession effect and constraining the system geometry. The findings indicate that the pulsar's visible beam is moving away from our line of sight, potentially making it undetectable in the near future. title: Securing Heterogeneous IoT with Intelligent DDoS Attack Behavior Learning
Abstract: The rapid growth of diverse Internet of Things (IoT) services and devices poses significant challenges for network connectivity, computation, and security. title: Remedies against the Vocabulary Gap in Information Retrieval
Abstract: Search engines heavily rely on term-based approaches that represent queries and documents as bags of words, ignoring grammar and word order while retaining word frequency counts. While effective, term-based approaches assume that documents containing the exact query terms are highly relevant regardless of semantics and that documents without query terms are irrelevant. However, this assumption can lead to a vocabulary gap, where queries and documents use different words to describe the same concepts. This dissertation addresses the problem of alleviating the effect of this vocabulary gap by proposing methods to formulate effective queries from complex textual structures and latent vector space models that circumvent the vocabulary gap in information retrieval.

title: Increasing altruistic and cooperative behaviour with simple moral nudges

title: D-SLATS: Distributed Simultaneous Localization and Time Synchronization
Abstract: Recent years have seen a dramatic rise in Internet of Things (IoT) devices, leading to a pressing need to coordinate their actions across both time and space. Our methods are evaluated on a custom Ultra-Wideband communication testbed and a quadrotor, representing a network of both static and mobile nodes. title: On Time-of-Arrival Estimation in NB-IoT Systems
Abstract: We delve into the estimation of time-of-arrival (ToA) for the first arrival path in narrowband Internet-of-Things (NB-IoT) systems. The limited bandwidth of 180 KHz used in NB-IoT results in a wide main lobe for the time-domain auto-correlation function (ACF) of the transmitted NB positioning reference signal (NPRS). Neglecting this characteristic can degrade ToA estimation performance for two reasons. Firstly, in multi-path channel environments, NPRS signals corresponding to different received paths overlap, leading to superimposed cross-correlations. Secondly, the measured peak-to-average-power-ratio (PAPR) used for detecting NPRS presence becomes inaccurate. Therefore, we propose a space-alternating generalized expectation-maximization (SAGE) based method to jointly estimate the number of channel taps, channel coefficients, and corresponding delays in NB-IoT systems, considering the imperfect ACF of NPRS. This method utilizes only the time-domain cross-correlations between the received signal and the transmitted NPRS, offering low complexity. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method's ToA estimation performance approaches that of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for a single-path channel, significantly outperforming traditional ToA estimators based on signal-to-noise (SNR) or power thresholds.

title: An extension of orthogonality relations based on norm derivatives

We explore its key properties and demonstrate a characterization of inner product spaces via the functional ${\\rho}_{\\lambda}$. Furthermore, we investigate a class of linear mappings that preserve this new form of orthogonality. Specifically, we show that any linear mapping preserving ${\\rho}_{\\lambda}$-orthogonality must be a similarity, meaning a scalar multiple of an isometry.

title: Multi-agent based IoT smart waste monitoring and collection architecture
Abstract: Solid waste management poses a significant challenge in urban areas, particularly with the rapid growth in population. Effective waste management systems are crucial for environmental health and resident well-being. This paper proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) architecture for real-time waste monitoring and collection, aiming to improve and optimize waste collection in a city. We employ the Netlogo Multiagent platform to simulate real-time monitoring and facilitate smart waste management decisions. The waste filling level in bins and truck collection process are abstracted into a multiagent model, with citizen involvement through payment for waste collection services. Waste level data is updated and recorded continuously, providing information to decision algorithms to determine optimal vehicle routes for waste collection to distributed bins within the city. Through several simulation cases and validated results, our proposed solution delivers substantial benefits to all waste stakeholders by enabling more efficient waste collection processes.

title: Graphene oxide dielectric permittivity at GHz and its applications for wireless humidity sensing
Abstract: Graphene oxide's relative dielectric permittivity, encompassing both its real and imaginary components, has been measured at GHz frequencies under varying humidity conditions. Our findings demonstrate that the relative dielectric permittivity increases with rising humidity due to water absorption. This electrical property of graphene oxide serves as the foundation for a battery-free wireless radio-frequency identification (RFID) humidity sensor. We achieve this by coating a printed graphene antenna with a graphene oxide layer. The resonance frequency and backscattering phase of this graphene oxide/graphene antenna exhibit sensitivity to the surrounding humidity, detectable by the RFID reader. This enables batteryless wireless monitoring of local humidity with digital identification, allowing attachment to any location or item. This innovation paves the way for cost-effective and efficient sensors for Internet of Things applications.

title: Optimal Auction For Edge Computing Resource Management in Mobile Blockchain Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Blockchain technology, with its public ledger of transactions, has found applications in diverse areas such as Bitcoin, smart grids, and the Internet of Things (IoT). However, its use in mobile environments remains limited due to the computationally and energy-intensive nature of the mining process on mobile devices. Edge computing, offered by Edge Computing Service Providers, presents a viable solution for offloading mining tasks from mobile devices, known as miners, in the mobile blockchain environment. Nevertheless, a mechanism for edge resource allocation that maximizes revenue for the Edge Computing Service Provider while ensuring incentive compatibility and individual rationality is still an open challenge. This paper proposes an optimal auction based on deep learning for edge resource allocation. We develop a multi-layer neural network architecture based on an analytical solution of the optimal auction. The neural networks first perform monotone transformations of the miners' bids. They then calculate allocation and conditional payment rules for the miners. Using valuations of the miners as training data, we adjust neural network parameters to optimize the loss function, which represents the expected, negated revenue of the Edge Computing Service Provider. Our experimental results validate the benefits of deep learning in deriving the optimal auction for mobile blockchain, achieving high revenue.

title: Towards Developing Network forensic mechanism for Botnet Activities in the IoT based on Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of interconnected everyday objects, referred to as things, enhanced with basic computing capabilities. Recently, the IoT has faced various botnet activities. Given the history of botnets causing significant security risks and financial damage, existing network forensic techniques struggle to identify and track current sophisticated botnet methods. This limitation stems from the reliance of commercial tools on signature-based approaches, which fail to detect novel botnet forms. While literature explores the application of Machine Learning (ML) techniques to train and validate models for identifying such attacks, they often produce high false alarm rates and face challenges in investigating botnet tracks. This paper investigates the role of ML techniques in developing a Network forensic mechanism based on network flow identifiers capable of tracking suspicious botnet activities. Using the UNSW-NB15 dataset, our experimental results reveal that ML techniques utilizing flow identifiers effectively and efficiently detect botnet attacks and their associated tracks.

title: Multi-Player Bandits Revisited
Abstract: Multi-player Multi-Armed Bandits (MAB) have garnered significant attention in the literature, motivated by applications in Cognitive Radio systems. Driven by such applications, we introduce multiple levels of feedback for multi-player MAB algorithms. Most existing work assumes the availability of sensing information to the algorithm. Under this assumption, we improve the state-of-the-art lower bound for the regret of any decentralized algorithms and present two algorithms, RandTopM and MCTopM, that demonstrate superior empirical performance compared to existing algorithms. We provide strong theoretical guarantees for these algorithms, including a notion of asymptotic optimality in terms of the number of selections of bad arms. We then introduce a promising heuristic, called Selfish, that can operate without sensing information, crucial for emerging applications in Internet of Things networks. We analyze the empirical performance of this algorithm and provide initial theoretical insights into its behavior.

title: Underlay Control Signaling for Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency IoT Communications
Abstract: Future mobile networks aim to not only enhance traditional link quality and data rates for mobile broadband (MBB) links, but also develop new control channels to meet the demands of delay-sensitive use cases. Specifically, the need for ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) for numerous internet of things (IoT) users is increasingly emphasized. This paper presents a novel spread spectrum waveform design for transmitting control signals to establish URLLC communications. These control signals are transmitted over spectral resources allocated to MBB communications in the network, but at a level that minimally affects data channels. The proposed waveform, although a direct sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) technique, is designed to leverage symbol synchronization available to OFDM broadband communications within the network. This enables straightforward synchronization with the rest of the network. The proposed DSSS method can transmit single and multiple bits within each OFDM time frame, effectively serving numerous user equipment (UE) nodes simultaneously.

title: Beyond Profiling: Scaling Profiling Data Usage to Multiple Applications
Abstract: Profiling techniques are extensively utilized at different levels of the computing stack to achieve various goals. One prominent objective is to enhance the efficiency of software execution on a specific hardware platform, where efficiency encompasses criteria such as power consumption, performance, and resource requirements. Researchers, both in academia and industry, have introduced numerous techniques for gathering and utilizing profiling data. However, a persistent challenge remains: optimizing the execution of application A on machine 1. This paper extends this criteria by exploring the potential of using profiling information from application A on machine 1 to improve the efficiency of application B on the same machine. This implies that as machine 1 executes more applications, it progressively becomes more efficient and capable. We present a generalized method for leveraging profiling information gathered from executing programs within a limited corpus of applications to enhance the performance of software outside this corpus. As a proof of concept, we apply our technique to the specific problem of selecting the most efficient last-level-cache for executing an application. We achieved a reduction of an average of 19% in last-level-cache blocks for selected programs from the PARSEC benchmark suite, observing only an average 2.8% increase in the rate of last-level cache misses.

title: Analysis of a Stratified Kraichnan Flow
Abstract:
We consider the stochastic convection-diffusion equation
  \[
  \partial_t u(t\,,{\bf x}) =\nu\Delta u(t\,,{\bf x}) +
  V(t\,,x_1)\partial_{x_2}u(t\,,{\bf x}),
  \] for $t>0$ and ${\bf x}=(x_1\,,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, subject to $\theta_0$
being a smooth initial profile. The velocity field $V$ is assumed to be
centered Gaussian with covariance structure
  \[
  \text{Cov}[V(t\,,a)\,,V(s\,,b)]= \delta_0(t-s)\rho(a-b)\qquad\text{for all
  $s,t\ge0$ and $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$},
  \] where $\rho$ is a continuous and bounded positive-definite function on
$\mathbb{R}$.
  We establish a general existence/uniqueness/regularity theorem, accompanied by a probabilistic representation of the solution, expressing $u$ as an expectation functional of an exogenous infinite-dimensional Brownian motion. We leverage this probabilistic representation to investigate the It\^o/Walsh solution, when it exists, and relate it to the Stratonovich solution, which is proven to exist for all $\nu>0$.
  Our a priori estimates imply the physically-natural fact that, in general, the solution dissipates. Moreover, we often observe that
  \begin{equation}
  P\left\{\sup_{|x_1|\leq m}\sup_{x_2\in\mathbb{R}} |u(t\,,{\bf x})|
  = O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt t}\right)\qquad\text{as $t\to\infty$}
  \right\}=1\qquad\text{for all $m>0$},
  \end{equation} with the $O(1/\sqrt t)$ rate demonstrated to be unimprovable.
  Our flexible probabilistic representation allows us to analyze the solution in two physically-relevant regimes: as $t\to\infty$ and as $\nu\to
0$. Our analysis, among other insights, leads to a "macroscopic multifractal
analysis" of the decay rate in the above equation in terms of the reciprocal
of the Prandtl (or Schmidt) number, valid in a number of simple yet physically-relevant cases.

title: Strategies for Conceptual Change in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Human beings possess a remarkable capacity for creative behavior, characterized by their ability to respond to problems in novel, surprising, and useful ways. Transformational creativity, a specific form of creativity, is driven by a transformation of the actor's conceptual space, the representational system used to interpret their environment. This report focuses on methods for adapting systems of learned representations as they transition from performing one task to another. We present an experimental comparison of various strategies for adapting learned features and evaluate their effectiveness in terms of training time and their ability to handle limited training data availability. Our findings demonstrate, among other insights, that across handwritten digits, natural images, and classical music, adaptive strategies consistently outperform a baseline method that starts learning from scratch.
label: AI

title: Machine Learning Approach to RF Transmitter Identification
Abstract: The widespread adoption of wireless devices, including mobile phones, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and Wi-Fi networks, has led to significant congestion in the electromagnetic spectrum. To address security threats posed by rogue or unknown transmitters, it is crucial to identify RF transmitters not by the data content of transmissions but by their intrinsic physical characteristics. RF waveforms present a unique challenge due to the extremely high data rates involved and the potentially large number of transmitters present in a given location. These factors necessitate rapid fingerprinting and identification methods that go beyond traditional hand-engineered approaches. This study investigates the application of machine learning (ML) strategies to address classification and identification problems, employing wavelets to reduce the required data volume. We evaluate four different ML strategies: deep neural nets (DNN), convolutional neural nets (CNN), support vector machines (SVM), and multi-stage training (MST) using accelerated Levenberg-Marquardt (A-LM) updates. The wavelet-preconditioned A-LM MST method emerges as the most accurate approach, achieving 100% classification accuracy for transmitters, as validated using data from 12 distinct transmitters. We discuss strategies for extending MST to accommodate a much larger number of transmitters.

title: Linearly Constrained Kalman Filter For Linear Discrete State-Space Models
Abstract: For linear discrete state-space (LDSS) models, under specific conditions, the linear least mean squares filter estimate adopts a convenient recursive predictor/corrector format, known as the Kalman filter (KF). This paper introduces the general form of the linearly constrained KF (LCKF) for LDSS models, encompassing the linearly constrained minimum variance estimator (LCMVE). This extension provides access to the extensive literature on LCMVE in the deterministic framework, which can be transposed to the stochastic framework. Consequently, LCKF can offer alternative solutions to $H_{\\infty }$ filters and unbiased finite impulse response filters for robustly enhancing the KF, whose performance is susceptible to misspecified noise or uncertainties in the system matrices.
label: AI

title: Optimal Checkpointing for Secure Intermittently-Powered IoT Devices
Abstract: Energy harvesting emerges as a promising solution for powering Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, the intermittent nature of these energy sources prevents guaranteed forward progress in program execution. Prior work has advocated for checkpointing intermediate states to off-chip non-volatile memory (NVM). While encrypting checkpoints addresses security concerns, it significantly increases checkpointing overheads. This paper proposes a novel online checkpointing policy that strategically determines checkpointing moments to minimize application completion time while ensuring security. Compared to state-of-the-art checkpointing schemes that neglect the overheads of encrypted checkpoints, our approach improves execution time by up to 1.4x.
label: AI

title: RF Wireless Power Transfer: Regreening Future Networks
Abstract: Green radio communication is a rapidly evolving field, driven by the predicted tripling of the overall footprint of information and communication technology (ICT) services between 2007 and 2020. Within this research line, energy harvesting (EH) and wireless power transfer (WPT) networks stand out as promising approaches. This paper provides an overview of recent trends in future green networks, focusing on EH and WPT platforms. By rethinking the application of radio frequency (RF)-WPT, we introduce a novel concept, green RF-WTP. This concept explores the potential of current technologies such as small-cell, millimeter (mm)-wave, and Internet of Things (IoT) networks, discussing challenges and promising combinations to address the question of how to re-green future networks.

title: Deep Learning-Based Dynamic Watermarking for Secure Signal Authentication in the Internet of Things
Abstract: Securing the Internet of Things (IoT) is a crucial step towards accelerating the deployment of its applications and services. The functionality of IoT devices hinges on the reliability of their message transmission. Cyber attacks, including data injection, eavesdropping, and man-in-the-middle threats, pose significant security challenges. Protecting IoT devices against such attacks requires considering their limited computational power and the need for low-latency operations. This paper introduces a novel deep learning method for dynamic watermarking of IoT signals to detect cyber attacks. The proposed learning framework, based on a long short-term memory (LSTM) structure, enables IoT devices to extract a set of stochastic features from their generated signals and dynamically watermark these features into the signal. This approach empowers the IoT's cloud center, responsible for collecting signals from IoT devices, to effectively authenticate the reliability of the signals. Moreover, this method prevents complex attack scenarios such as eavesdropping, where cyber attackers collect data from IoT devices aiming to break the watermarking algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that, with an attack detection delay under 1 second, messages can be transmitted from IoT devices with near 100% reliability.

title: Semiflat Orbifold Projections
Abstract: We compute the semiflat positive cone $K_0^{+SF}(A_\\theta^\\sigma)$ of the $K_0$-group of the irrational rotation orbifold $A_\\theta^\\sigma$ under the noncommutative Fourier transform $\\sigma$ and demonstrate that it is determined by classes of positive trace and the vanishing of two topological invariants. The semiflat orbifold projections are 3-dimensional and fall into three basic topological genera: $(2,0,0)$, $(1,1,2)$, $(0,0,2)$. (A projection is considered semiflat when it has the form $h + \\sigma(h)$ where $h$ is a flip-invariant projection such that $h\\sigma(h)=0$.) Among other findings, we show that every number in $(0,1) \\cap (2\\mathbb Z + 2\\mathbb Z\\theta)$ represents the trace of a semiflat projection in $A_\\theta$. The noncommutative Fourier transform is the order 4 automorphism $\\sigma: V \\to U \\to V^{-1}$ (and the flip is $\\sigma^2$:\n$U \\to U^{-1},\\ V \\to V^{-1}$), where $U,V$ are the canonical unitary generators of the rotation algebra $A_\\theta$ satisfying $VU = e^{2\\pi i\\theta}\nUV$.

title: Categorical formal punctured neighborhood of infinity, I
Abstract:
This paper introduces and examines the formal punctured neighborhood of infinity, both within the algebro-geometric and DG categorical frameworks. For a smooth algebraic variety $X$ over a field of characteristic zero, one can take its smooth compactification $\bar{X}\supset X,$ and subsequently consider the DG category of perfect complexes on the formal punctured neighborhood of the infinity locus $\bar{X}-X.$ Interestingly, the result proves independent of $\bar{X}$ (up to a quasi-equivalence), and we denote this DG category by $\operatorname{Perf}(\hat{X}_{\infty}).$
  We demonstrate that this construction can be achieved purely DG categorically (and therefore also $A_{\infty}$-categorically). For any smooth DG category $\mathcal{B},$ we construct the DG category $\operatorname{Perf}_{top}(\hat{\mathcal{B}}_{\infty}),$ termed the category of perfect complexes on the formal punctured neighborhood of infinity of $\mathcal{B}.$
  This construction bears a close resemblance to the algebraic version of a Calkin algebra: endomorphisms of an infinite-dimensional vector space modulo endomorphisms of finite rank. We prove that the DG categorical construction is compatible with its algebro-geometric counterpart.
  We explore numerous examples. Notably, for the algebra of rational functions on a smooth complete connected curve $C$, we obtain the algebra of adeles $\mathbb{A}_C,$ and for $\mathcal{B}=D^b_{coh}(Y)$ where $Y$ is a proper singular scheme, we arrive at the category $D_{sg}(Y)^{op}$ -- the opposite category of Orlov's category of singularities. We further discuss the relationship with the works of Tate \cite{Ta} and Arbarello, de Concini, and Kac \cite{ACK}.

title: Analysis of the Communication Traffic for Blockchain Synchronization of IoT Devices
Abstract: Blockchain technology stands out as uniquely suited to support a massive number of transactions and smart contracts within the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, thanks to its decentralized accounting mechanism. In a blockchain network, the states of accounts are stored and updated by validator nodes, interconnected in a peer-to-peer fashion. IoT devices are characterized by relatively low computing capabilities and power consumption, along with sporadic and low-bandwidth wireless connectivity. An IoT device connects to one or more validator nodes to observe or modify the state of accounts. To interact with the most recent state of accounts, a device must synchronize with the blockchain copy stored by the validator nodes. This work outlines general architectures and synchronization protocols that enable synchronization of IoT endpoints to the blockchain, with varying communication costs and security levels. We model and analytically characterize the traffic generated by the synchronization protocols, and investigate the trade-off between power consumption and synchronization through numerical simulations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to rigorously model the role of wireless connectivity in blockchain-powered IoT systems. |||
