title: Providing Privacy, Safety, and Security in IoT-Based Transactive Energy Systems using Distributed Ledgers
Abstract: Power grids are evolving rapidly with the rise of renewable energy and advanced battery technologies. This shift towards sustainability and efficiency brings challenges as the complexity of power systems increases. Decentralized Internet of Things (IoT) solutions are emerging to address these challenges by creating transactive microgrids that connect local communities. In a transactive microgrid, "prosumers" (consumers with energy generation and storage capabilities) can trade energy, reducing the strain on the main grid. However, ensuring security, safety, and privacy in this decentralized and transactive energy system is a major obstacle. On one hand, prosumers' personal information needs protection from trading partners and system operators. On the other hand, the system itself needs protection against careless or malicious trading that could destabilize the entire grid. This paper introduces Privacy-preserving Energy Transactions (PETra), a secure and safe solution for transactive microgrids that enables energy trading without compromising consumer privacy. PETra leverages distributed ledgers, like blockchains, to provide anonymity for communication, bidding, and trading.
label: AI

title: PlaTIBART: a Platform for Transactive IoT Blockchain Applications with Repeatable Testing
Abstract: The increasing popularity of blockchain-enabled IoT applications necessitates the development of robust software patterns, middleware concepts, and testing practices to ensure high quality and productivity. IoT and blockchain technologies offer distinct design goals, concepts, and practices that must be integrated, including the distributed actor model and fault tolerance from IoT, and transactive information integrity over untrustworthy sources from blockchain. Due to their emerging nature, both IoT and blockchain lack standardized patterns and practices for developing combined applications. This paper introduces PlaTIBART, a platform for transactive IoT blockchain applications with repeatable testing. PlaTIBART combines the Actor pattern, a common computational model in IoT, with a custom Domain Specific Language (DSL) and test network management tools. The paper demonstrates how PlaTIBART has been used to develop, test, and analyze fault-tolerant IoT blockchain applications.
label: AI

title: Microservices: Granularity vs. Performance
Abstract: Microservice Architectures (MA) hold the potential to enhance the agility of software development. In an era where businesses demand software applications to adapt to emerging requirements, especially for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, the question of microservice granularity and its impact on application latency arises. This paper simulates two approaches to microservice deployment: one with microservices in a single container and the other with microservices partitioned across separate containers. The results indicate a negligible increase in service latency for the multiple container deployment compared to the single container deployment.
label: AI

title: Non-cocompact Group Actions and $π_1$-Semistability at Infinity
Abstract: A finitely presented 1-ended group $G$ possesses a {\\it semistable fundamental group at infinity} if $G$ acts geometrically on a simply connected and locally compact ANR $Y$ with the property that any two proper rays in $Y$ are properly homotopic. This property of $Y$ reflects a concept of connectivity at infinity stronger than "1-ended" and is inherent to $G$, independent of choices. It plays a fundamental role in the homotopical study of finitely presented groups. While many important classes of groups have been shown to have semistable fundamental groups at infinity, the question of whether every $G$ possesses this property has remained open for nearly forty years. This paper tackles this problem by considering a proper {\\it but non-cocompact} action of a group $J$ on such a $Y$. Typically, $J$ would be a subgroup of infinite index in the geometrically acting over-group $G$; for example, $J$ could be infinite cyclic or another subgroup with known semistability properties. The semistability property of $G$ is divided into a $J$-part and a "perpendicular to $J$" part, and the paper analyzes how these two parts interact. This analysis leads to a proof (presented in a companion paper) that a class of groups previously considered potential counter examples do, in fact, possess the semistability property.
label: AI

title: Generalized Sparse and Low-Rank Optimization for Ultra-Dense Networks
Abstract: Ultra-dense network (UDN) is a promising technology for evolving wireless networks to meet the diverse performance requirements of 5G networks. With abundant access points, each equipped with communication, computation, and storage resources, UDN offers unprecedented benefits, including significant improvement in network spectral and energy efficiency, greatly reduced latency for enabling novel mobile applications, and the ability to provide massive access for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, these advantages come with formidable research challenges. Efficient and innovative methodologies are needed to design and operate such complex networks with various types of resources. This motivates the recent introduction of highly structured and generalizable models for network optimization. This article presents some recently proposed large-scale sparse and low-rank frameworks for optimizing UDNs, supported by various motivating applications. It focuses on algorithmic approaches for handling nonconvex objective functions and constraints, as well as computational scalability.
label: AI

title: Designing a Framework for Smart IoT Adaptations
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) involves connecting multiple devices that coordinate to provide a specific service. IoT environments are complex, dynamic, rapidly changing, and resource-constrained. Consequently, proactively adapting devices to align with contextual fluctuations becomes a critical concern. To propose suitable configurations, it is necessary to sense information from devices, analyze the data, and reconfigure them accordingly. When applied to environmental services, a fleet of devices can monitor environmental indicators and control them to propose optimal solutions or prevent risks such as resource overconsumption (e.g., water and energy). This paper describes a methodology for designing a framework for monitoring and multi-instantiation of fleets of connected objects. The methodology first identifies the particularities of the fleet, then specifies the connected object as a Dynamic Software Product Line (DSPL), capable of readjusting while running.
label: AI

title: Correctness of the Chord Protocol
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) can be viewed as a collaboration of various heterogeneous devices with limited performance capabilities, all participating in the same system. By their nature, these devices can be highly distributed. The core of any IoT system is its discovery and control service. The Chord protocol, one of the earliest, simplest, and most popular distributed protocols, can be used as the backbone of the discovery and control services in an IoT system. This paper proves the correctness of the Chord protocol using the logic of time and knowledge. The analysis considers Chord actions that maintain ring topology, assuming that nodes are not allowed to fail or leave.
label: AI

title: Spontaneous mass generation suggests small dimension of the SM group U(1)xSU(2)xSU(3)
Abstract: The underlying reasons for the gauge symmetry of the Standard Model, U(1)xSU(2)xSU(3), remain unclear. One noticeable feature is the low dimensionality of all its subgroups. Under certain conditions, it is possible to provide a negative answer to the question: "Why not larger groups like SU(15), or for that matter, SP(26) or E7?". Recent observations suggest that fermions charged under large groups acquire significantly larger dynamical masses, all other factors being equal at a high, e.g., GUT scale, compared to ordinary quarks. If such multicharged fermions exist, they are too heavy to be observed today (and have either decayed early on if coupled to the rest of the Standard Model, or become relic dark matter if uncoupled). Their mass scale is governed by strong antiscreening of the running coupling for those larger groups (with an appropriately small number of flavors) along with scaling properties of the Dyson-Schwinger equation for the fermion mass. Assuming only a few flavors to avoid disrupting antiscreening, the generated fermion mass grows exponentially with the number of colors as M(N_c) ~ exp(N_c) for scales well below the GUT scale. Large groups would already be strongly coupled near the GUT scale, resulting in correspondingly large masses for fermions charged thereunder.
label: AI

title: ROMANO: A Novel Overlay Lightweight Communication Protocol for Unified Control and Sensing of a Network of Robots
Abstract: This paper introduces the Robotic Overlay coMmunicAtioN prOtocol (ROMANO), a lightweight, application layer overlay communication protocol designed for a unified sensing and control abstraction of a network of heterogeneous robots, primarily consisting of low-power, low-compute-capable robots. ROMANO is built to work in conjunction with the well-known MQ Telemetry Transport for Sensor Nodes (MQTT-SN) protocol, a lightweight publish-subscribe communication protocol for the Internet of Things, and leverages its "topics" concept to designate the addition and deletion of communication endpoints by modifying the subscriptions of topics at each device. The paper presents a portable implementation of ROMANO for low-power IEEE 802.15.4 (Zigbee) radios, deployed on a small testbed of commercially available, low-power, and low-compute-capable robots called Pololu 3pi robots. Through a comprehensive analysis of the protocol on the real testbed, using throughput as a measure, the paper demonstrates that ROMANO can guarantee a message delivery ratio exceeding 99.5% for a message generation rate up to 200 messages per second. Single hop delays in ROMANO are as low as 20ms with linear dependency on the number of connected robots. These delay figures align with typical delays in 802.15.4 networks, indicating that ROMANO does not introduce additional delays. Finally, the paper implements four different multi-robot applications to showcase the scalability, adaptability, ease of integration, and reliability of ROMANO.
label: AI

title: Enabling Community Health Care with Microservices
Abstract: Microservice architectures (MA) are composed of loosely coupled, coarse-grained services that prioritize resilience and autonomy, enabling the development of more scalable applications. These architectures are more tolerant of changing user and enterprise demands, adapting to emerging technologies and their associated influences on human interaction and behavior. This article examines microservices within the Internet of Things (IoT) through the lens of agency, and using an example in the community healthcare domain, explores how a complex application scenario (both in terms of software and hardware interactions) might be modeled.
label: AI

title: Towards In-Transit Analytics for Industry 4.0
Abstract: Industry 4.0, or Digital Manufacturing, envisions interconnected services to facilitate innovation in the manufacturing sector. A fundamental requirement for innovation is the ability to visualize manufacturing data to discover new insights for gaining a competitive advantage. This article describes the enabling technologies that facilitate In-Transit Analytics, a necessary precursor for Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) visualization.
label: AI

title: Heterogeneous Networked Data Recovery from Compressive Measurements Using a Copula Prior
Abstract: Large-scale data collection through wireless sensor networks and internet-of-things technology poses significant challenges due to limitations in transmission, computation, and energy resources of the associated wireless devices. Compressive data gathering based on compressed sensing has proven to be a suitable solution to this problem. Existing designs leverage spatiotemporal correlations among data collected by a specific sensing modality. However, many applications, such as environmental monitoring, involve collecting heterogeneous data that are intrinsically correlated. This study proposes leveraging the correlation from multiple heterogeneous signals when recovering data from compressive measurements. To this end, the study introduces a novel recovery algorithm, built upon belief-propagation principles, that utilizes correlated information from multiple heterogeneous signals. The proposed algorithm employs the statistical model of copula functions to efficiently capture the statistical dependencies among diverse sensor data. Experiments using heterogeneous air-pollution sensor measurements demonstrate that the proposed design provides significant performance improvements compared to state-of-the-art compressive data gathering and recovery schemes that utilize classical compressed sensing, compressed sensing with side information, and distributed compressed sensing.
label: AI

title: Towards an Understanding of Microservices
Abstract: Microservices architectures represent a departure from traditional Service Oriented Architecture (SOA). Influenced by Domain Driven Design (DDD), microservices architectures aim to assist business analysts and enterprise architects in developing scalable applications that embody flexibility for new functionalities as businesses evolve, such as scenarios in the Internet of Things (IoT) domain. This article compares microservices architecture with SOA and identifies key characteristics that will aid application designers in selecting the most appropriate approach.
label: AI

title: A Load Balancing Algorithm for Resource Allocation in IEEE 802.15.4e Networks
Abstract: The recently established IETF 6TiSCH working group combines the high reliability and low-energy consumption of IEEE 802.15.4e Time Slotted Channel Hopping with IPv6 for industrial Internet of Things. This paper proposes a distributed link scheduling algorithm, called Local Voting, for 6TiSCH networks that adapts the schedule to network conditions. The algorithm aims to equalize the link load (defined as the ratio of the queue length over the number of allocated cells) through cell reallocation. Local Voting calculates the number of cells to be added or released by the 6TiSCH Operation Sublayer (6top). Compared to a representative algorithm from the literature, Local Voting provides both high reliability and low end-to-end latency while consuming significantly less energy. Its performance has been evaluated and compared to the On-the-fly algorithm in the 6TiSCH simulator by modeling an industrial environment with 50 sensors.
label: AI

title: Getting Virtualized Wireless Sensor Networks IaaS Ready for PaaS
Abstract: Recent advancements in sensor hardware and software have led to the emergence of architectures for virtualized Wireless Sensor Networks (vWSNs). Through node- and network-level virtualization, vWSNs can be offered as Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), facilitating the realization of the true potential of the Internet-of-Things (IoT). Cloud computing provides elastic provisioning of large-scale infrastructures to multiple concurrent users, where Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) interacts with IaaS to efficiently host and execute applications over these infrastructures. Integrating IoT with cloud computing potentially enables rapid application and service provisioning in an efficient, scalable, and robust manner. However, interactions between vWSNs and PaaS remain largely unexplored. Existing vWSN IaaS are not yet ready for PaaS integration. This paper proposes a vWSN IaaS architecture that is prepared for interactions with PaaS. The proposed architecture builds upon previous works and is rooted in the fundamental differences between traditional IaaS and vWSN IaaS. A prototype was built using Java Sunspot as the WSN toolkit and preliminary performance measurements were conducted.
label: AI

title: A Proof Technique for Skewness of Graphs
Abstract: The skewness of a graph G is the minimum number of edges in G whose removal results in a planar graph. By appropriately introducing a weight to each edge of a graph, this paper determines, among other things, the skewness of the generalized Petersen graph P(4k, k) for odd k at least 9. This provides an answer to the conjecture raised in [3].
label: AI

title: Relational Marginal Problems: Theory and Estimation
Abstract: In the propositional setting, the marginal problem involves finding a (maximum-entropy) distribution that exhibits certain given marginals. This paper investigates this problem in a relational setting and makes the following contributions. Firstly, it compares two distinct notions of relational marginals. Secondly, the paper demonstrates a duality between the resulting relational marginal problems and the maximum likelihood estimation of parameters in relational models, generalizing a well-known duality from the propositional setting. Thirdly, by leveraging the relational marginal formulation, the paper presents a statistically sound method for learning the parameters of relational models, applicable in situations where the number of constants differs between training and test data. Additionally, based on a relational generalization of marginal polytopes, the paper characterizes cases where standard estimators based on the number of true groundings of features need adjustments and quantitatively assesses the implications of these adjustments. Fourthly, the paper proves bounds on expected errors of the estimated parameters, enabling lower bounds on, among other things, the effective sample size of relational training data.
label: AI

title: Device Activity and Embedded Information Bit Detection Using AMP in Massive MIMO
Abstract: Future cellular networks will support a massive number of devices due to emerging technologies like the Internet of Things and sensor networks. Enhanced by machine type communication (MTC), billions of low-power, low-complexity devices are projected to receive service from cellular networks. Unlike traditional networks designed for human-driven traffic, future networks must handle MTC-based systems exhibiting sparse traffic properties, operating with small packets and encompassing a large number of devices. Such a system requires smarter control signaling schemes for efficient resource utilization. This work considers a grant-free random access cellular network and proposes an approach that jointly detects user activity and single information bit per packet. Inspired by approximate message passing (AMP), the proposed approach demonstrates superior performance compared to the original AMP method. Furthermore, numerical analysis reveals that the performance of the proposed approach scales with the number of devices, making it suitable for user detection in cellular networks with a massive number of devices.
label: AI

title: A Streaming Accelerator for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks with Image and Feature Decomposition for Resource-limited System Applications
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in modern artificial intelligence (AI) and smart vision systems. However, their performance is limited by computation latency, throughput, and energy efficiency in resource-constrained scenarios, such as mobile devices, the internet of things (IoT), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and so on. This paper proposes a hardware streaming architecture to accelerate convolution and pooling computations for state-of-the-art deep CNNs. It is optimized for energy efficiency by maximizing local data reuse to reduce off-chip DRAM data access. Additionally, image and feature decomposition techniques are introduced to optimize memory access patterns for arbitrary image sizes and numbers of features within limited on-chip SRAM capacity. A prototype accelerator was implemented in TSMC 65 nm CMOS technology with a 2.3 mm x 0.8 mm core area, achieving a peak throughput of 144 GOPS and a peak energy efficiency of 0.8 TOPS/W.
label: AI

title: Sensor Fusion for Public Space Utilization Monitoring in a Smart City
Abstract: Understanding public space utilization is crucial for urban developers to assess the efficiency of space occupancy and improve existing or future infrastructure. In a smart cities approach, implementing public space monitoring with Internet of Things (IoT) sensors appears to be a viable solution. However, selecting appropriate sensors is often a challenging problem, often linked to scalability, coverage, energy consumption, accuracy, and privacy. To maximize the value of low-cost sensors while considering these design factors, this paper proposes data processing modules for capturing public space utilization using a Renewable Wireless Sensor Network (RWSN) platform equipped with pyroelectric infrared (PIR) and analog sound sensors. The paper first proposes a calibration process to eliminate false alarms from the PIR sensor due to weather and environmental impacts. It then demonstrates how sound sensor data can be processed to provide various insights into public space. Finally, the paper fuses data from both sensors and studies a particular public space utilization based on one month of data to unveil its usage patterns. |||
label: AI

title: Diffusion Based Molecular Communication: Principle, Key Technologies, and Challenges
Abstract: Molecular communication (MC) is a communication technology that uses biochemical molecules as information carriers to connect nano-devices. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the basic principles of diffusion-based MC and its key technologies. The state-of-the-art advancements in diffusion-based MC are discussed and compared, including the system model, performance analysis, information coding, and modulation techniques. Multi-hop nano-networks based on diffusion MC are also explored. Given the breadth of this research field, open issues and challenges are presented to stimulate future research, including the development of channel models, information theory, self-organizing nano-networks, and biochemical applications.
label: AI

title: Detection of Unauthorized IoT Devices Using Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: Security experts have identified various risks posed by Internet of Things (IoT) devices to organizations. The widespread adoption of IoT devices, their diversity, standardization obstacles, and inherent mobility require an intelligent mechanism to automatically detect suspicious IoT devices connected to organizational networks. This research uses Random Forest, a supervised machine learning algorithm, to identify IoT device types from a whitelist by analyzing features extracted from network traffic data. The study collected and manually labeled network traffic data from 17 distinct IoT devices, representing nine device types. The classification of 20 consecutive sessions using majority rule enabled the accurate detection of unknown IoT device types not on the whitelist in 96% of test cases (on average). Whitelisted device types were correctly classified in 99% of cases. Some IoT device types were identified more quickly than others (e.g., sockets and thermostats were detected within five TCP sessions). Perfect detection of unauthorized devices was achieved after analyzing 110 consecutive sessions, while perfect classification of whitelisted types required 346 sessions, with 110 of them achieving 99.49% accuracy. Further experiments demonstrated the successful applicability of classifiers trained in one location and tested in another. The paper also discusses the resilience of this machine learning-based IoT whitelisting method against adversarial attacks.
label: AI

title: A direct proof of Tychonoff's theorem
Abstract: Proofs of Tychonoff's theorem often appear to rely on seemingly magical techniques like ultrafilters, nets, or maximal families with the finite intersection property. While these methods provide elegant proofs, they may not be the most intuitive approach for someone with a standard open set topology background. This paper presents a direct and simple proof of Tychonoff's theorem, directly from the open cover definition of compactness.
label: AI

title: StarSpace: Embed All The Things!
Abstract: StarSpace is a general-purpose neural embedding model that can solve various problems such as labeling tasks like text classification, ranking tasks like information retrieval/web search and recommendation, embedding of multi-relational graphs, and learning word, sentence, or document level embeddings. The model works by embedding entities comprised of discrete features and comparing them against each other, learning similarities dependent on the task. Empirical results across multiple tasks show that StarSpace is highly competitive with existing methods while also being generally applicable to new cases where those methods are not.
label: AI

title: The Internet-of-Things Meets Business Process Management: A Manifesto
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to a network of connected devices collecting and exchanging data over the Internet. These devices can be artificial or natural and interact as autonomous agents forming a complex system. Business Process Management (BPM) is used to analyze, discover, design, implement, execute, monitor, and evolve collaborative business processes within and across organizations. While IoT and BPM have been treated as separate fields in research and practice, this paper argues that the management of IoT applications can significantly benefit from BPM concepts, methods, and technologies. Conversely, IoT presents challenges that require enhancements and extensions to existing BPM technologies. This paper explores the potential for combining these two paradigms and discusses the emerging challenges.
label: AI

title: Physical properties and H-ionizing-photon production rates of extreme nearby star-forming regions
Abstract: Measurements of the galaxy UV luminosity function at redshifts greater than 6 suggest that young stars in low-mass star-forming galaxies produced the majority of hydrogen-ionizing photons needed to reionize the intergalactic medium (IGM) by redshift 6. However, the dominance of star-forming galaxies in cosmic reionization depends on their stellar populations and interstellar medium properties, which determine the production rate of H-ionizing photons, ξion∗, and the fraction escaping into the IGM. Given the difficulty of constraining the physical properties of galaxies at redshifts greater than 6 with current observatories, this study focuses on a sample of ten nearby galaxies exhibiting comparable UV spectral features. The Beagle tool models the UV-to-optical photometry and UV/optical emission lines of these local "analogues" of high-redshift galaxies. The analysis finds that a relatively simple yet fully self-consistent physical model can successfully reproduce the observed observables. The galaxies studied span a wide range of metallicities and are characterized by high ionization parameters, low dust attenuation, and very young stellar populations. The study derives a new diagnostic for the production rate of H-ionizing photons per unit UV luminosity, ξion∗, based on the equivalent width of the bright [OIII] λ4959,5007 doublet. This diagnostic does not require measurements of H-recombination lines. This new diagnostic can be used to estimate ξion∗ from future direct measurements of the [OIII] λ4959,5007 line using JWST/NIRSpec (out to redshift 9.5) and by exploiting the contamination by Hβ + [OIII] λ4959,5007 in photometric observations of distant galaxies, for instance, from existing Spitzer/IRAC data and future data from JWST/NIRCam.
label: AI

title: Collaborative Reuse of Streaming Dataflows in IoT Applications
Abstract: Distributed Stream Processing Systems (DSPS) like Apache Storm and Spark Streaming enable the creation of continuous dataflows that execute persistently over data streams. They are used in Internet of Things (IoT) applications to analyze sensor data from smart city cyber-infrastructure and make active utility management decisions. As the ecosystem of IoT applications leveraging shared urban sensor streams grows, applications perform duplicate pre-processing and analytics tasks. This offers the opportunity to collaboratively reuse the outputs of overlapping dataflows, improving resource efficiency. This paper proposes dataflow reuse algorithms that, given a submitted dataflow, identify reusable tasks and streams from a collection of running dataflows to form a merged dataflow. Similar algorithms for unmerging dataflows when they are removed are also proposed. These algorithms are implemented for Apache Storm DSPS and validated for performance and resource savings using 35 synthetic dataflows based on public OPMW workflows with diverse arrival and departure distributions and 21 real IoT dataflows from RIoTBench.
label: AI

title: The relation between specific baryon angular momentum and mass for a sample of nearby low-mass galaxies with resolved HI kinematics
Abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between specific baryon angular momentum jb and baryon mass Mb for a sample of nearby late-type galaxies with resolved HI kinematics. The study nearly doubles the number of galaxies with Mb ≤ 1010 M⊙ used to investigate the jb-Mb relation. The majority of galaxies in the sample have their baryon mass dominated by their gas content, providing jb and Mb measurements relatively unaffected by uncertainties arising from the stellar mass-to-light ratio. Measured HI surface density radial profiles, combined with optical and rotation curve data from the literature, are used to derive a best-fit relation given by jb = qMbα, where α = 0.62 ± 0.02 and log10q = -3.35 ± 0.25. This result is consistent with the jb ∝ Mb2/3 relation theoretically expected and also observed by Obreschkow & Glazebrook (2014) for their full sample of THINGS spiral galaxies. However, this result differs from their steeper relation found for subsets with fixed bulge fraction. The 30 arcsec spatial resolution of the HI imaging used in this study is significantly lower than that of the THINGS imaging used by Obreschkow & Glazebrook (2014), but the results presented here demonstrate no significant systematic errors due to the lower resolution imaging.
label: AI

title: A tetrachotomy for expansions of the real ordered additive group
Abstract: Let ℛ be an expansion of the ordered real additive group. When ℛ is o-minimal, it is known that either ℛ defines an ordered field isomorphic to (ℝ,<,+,⋅) on some open subinterval I ⊆ ℝ, or ℛ is a reduct of an ordered vector space. ℛ is considered field-type if it satisfies the former condition. This paper proves a more general result for arbitrary expansions of (ℝ,<,+). Specifically, it shows that for expansions that do not define dense ω-orders (referred to as type A expansions), an appropriate version of Zilber's principle holds. As a consequence, in a type A expansion that is not field-type, every continuous definable function [0,1]m → ℝn is locally affine outside a nowhere dense set.
label: AI

title: Reshaping Mobile Crowd Sensing using Cross Validation to Improve Data Credibility
Abstract: Data credibility is a crucial concern in mobile crowd sensing (MCS) and, more generally, people-centric Internet of Things (IoT). While previous work has focused on incentive mechanism design and data mining to address this issue, this paper leverages the power of crowds itself. It proposes a cross-validation approach where a validating crowd verifies the data credibility of the original sensing crowd. The verification result reshapes the original sensing dataset into a more credible posterior belief of the ground truth. Following this approach, the paper designs a specific cross-validation mechanism that integrates four sampling techniques with a privacy-aware competency-adaptive push (PACAP) algorithm. This mechanism is applicable to time-sensitive and quality-critical MCS applications. It functions as a lightweight "plug-in" without requiring the redesign of a new MCS system, making it easier to adopt in practice. The results demonstrate that the proposed mechanism significantly improves data credibility by reinforcing obscure truths and scavenging hidden truths.
label: AI

title: Extremal $k$-forcing sets in oriented graphs
Abstract: This paper examines the k-forcing number for oriented graphs, generalizing both the zero forcing number for directed graphs and the k-forcing number for simple graphs. Given a simple graph G, the maximum (minimum) oriented k-forcing number, denoted MOFk(G) (mofk(G)), is introduced. This represents the largest (smallest) k-forcing number among all possible orientations of G. These new concepts are compared to existing graph invariants. The paper shows that, among other things, mof(G) equals the path covering number of G, while MOFk(G) is greater than or equal to the independence number of G, with equality holding if G is a tree or if k is at least the maximum degree of G. title: Uncertainty measurement with belief entropy on interference effect in Quantum-Like Bayesian Networks

This special network considers interference, which is potentially an efficient way to describe the underlying mechanism. title: Survey and Systematization of Secure Device Pairing

This taxonomy enables meaningful comparison and analysis of SDP schemes for the first time. The analysis of existing SDP schemes using this model reveals common systemic security weaknesses, highlighting priority areas for future SDP research, such as incorporating privacy requirements into the design of SDP schemes. title: NarrowBand IoT Data Transmission Procedures for Massive Machine Type Communications

title: A Traffic Model for Machine-Type Communications Using Spatial Point Processes

For multi-band RF signals, a specialized variant called non-uniform wavelet bandpass sampling (NUWBS) is introduced, further enhancing sensitivity and reducing hardware complexity. Simulations demonstrate that NUWBS approaches the theoretical performance limits of sparse signal recovery using the l1-norm. title: Distributed Real-Time HVAC Control for Cost-Efficient Commercial Buildings under Smart Grid Environment

title: Analysis of Information Delivery Dynamics in Cognitive Sensor Networks Using Epidemic Models

title: Recursion for the smallest eigenvalue density of $β$-Wishart-Laguerre ensemble
Abstract: The smallest eigenvalue statistics of Wishart-Laguerre ensembles hold significance in various fields, often expressed in terms of determinants or Pfaffians. For real matrices, Edelman provided an efficient recurrence scheme to calculate the smallest eigenvalue density without relying on determinants. This approach was recently extended to complex matrices. The paper compares these results with earlier expressions involving hypergeometric functions, providing an effective method for explicit evaluation. Exact evaluations for large matrix dimensions and alpha values allow comparison with Tracy-Widom density and large deviation results. The paper examines the argument that the "no-signalling" condition can be seen as a generalization of Einstein's principle for irreducible statistical theories like quantum mechanics. It then argues that information causality can be viewed as a further generalization of the Einsteinian principle for communication theories. While mean-field models of actin polymerization have successfully elucidated the nucleotide profile and mechanisms of accessory proteins, they require numerical solutions of high-dimensional nonlinear ODEs. The Brooks-Carlsson model simplifies dimensionality to 11 by truncating a set of recursion equations, but it remains nonlinear and lacks an analytical solution, hindering dynamic understanding. This paper proposes two model reduction schemes, taking advantage of the fast timescales of the hydrolysis states at filament tips, to achieve low dimensionality and linearity. An exact solution of the resulting linear equations is provided, shedding light on the dynamics of the full Brooks-Carlsson model and highlighting the relative ordering of timescales for various collective processes. The analysis also explains unusual dependencies of the steady-state behavior on initial conditions.

title: Throughput Enhancement of Multicarrier Cognitive M2M Networks: Universal-Filtered OFDM Systems
Abstract: This paper investigates throughput enhancement in a cognitive radio network consisting of a primary cellular system and a secondary cognitive machine-to-machine (M2M) system, employing universal-filtered orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (UF-OFDM) modulation. The downlink transmission capacity of the cognitive M2M system is maximized while limiting interference to primary users (PUs) below a specified threshold under a total transmit power budget of the secondary base station (SBS). The performance of UF-OFDM based CR is compared to OFDM and filter bank multicarrier (FBMC) based CR systems. A near-optimal resource allocation method separating subband and power allocation is proposed, simplifying the solution of the original combinatorial problem. Numerical results show that for given interference thresholds and transmit power limits, the UF-OFDM based CR system exhibits intermediate performance in terms of achievable capacity compared to OFDM and FBMC based CR systems. Notably, UF-OFDM performs equally well as FBMC for certain degrees of PU robustness. Moreover, the percentage rate-gain of the UF-OFDM based CR system significantly increases when employing UF-OFDM modulation with lower sidelobe ripple. The proposed throughput enhancement method, despite its reduced computational complexity, achieves near-optimal performance.

title: Big Data Model Simulation on a Graph Database for Surveillance in Wireless Multimedia Sensor Networks
Abstract: Sensors are ubiquitous in modern life, integrated into devices like mobile phones, surveillance cameras, smart televisions, refrigerators, and blood pressure monitors. These sensors often form networks, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), which comprises millions of interconnected sensors. Advancements in wireless communication technologies have led to the growing importance of multimedia sensors and their networks within the IoT. Numerous studies have explored wireless multimedia sensor networks for various applications, including fire detection, city surveillance, and early warning systems. These applications involve long-term data collection and real-time data flow, generating massive amounts of big data. This study proposes a big database model based on the graph database model for handling data generated by wireless multimedia sensor networks. A simulator is introduced to generate synthetic data and store and query big data using a graph model as a big database. The performance of well-known graph-based NoSQL databases (Neo4j and OrientDB) and a relational database (MySQL) is evaluated through query experiments on the implemented simulator. Results demonstrate the efficiency and scalability of these database systems for surveillance in wireless multimedia sensor networks.

title: IoT Data Analytics Using Deep Learning
Abstract: Deep learning, a popular machine learning approach, has made significant progress in traditional machine learning domains. Internet of Things (IoT) and Smart City deployments generate vast amounts of time-series sensor data requiring analysis. This paper explores the application of deep learning to these domains, specifically utilizing Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting events with long intervals and delays in time series. LSTM networks, capable of maintaining long-term memory, employ stacked LSTM hidden layers to learn high-level temporal features without the need for fine-tuning or preprocessing. The proposed LSTM-Gauss-NBayes method constructs a LSTM recurrent neural network structure using a normal time series training set to build a prediction model. Predicted errors from the prediction model are then used to construct a Gaussian naive Bayes model for detecting anomalies in the original sample. The effectiveness and robustness of LSTM-Gauss-NBayes are demonstrated using three real-world datasets with varying degrees of time dependence, highlighting its potential for anomaly detection in IoT and Smart City environments.

title: Privacy Guidelines for Internet of Things: A Cheat Sheet

title: The Dark Side(-Channel) of Mobile Devices: A Survey on Network Traffic Analysis
Abstract: Mobile devices, such as smartphones and tablets, have become indispensable elements of daily life for billions of people globally. They are used for a wide range of tasks, from traditional communication to advanced applications in finance, gaming, and shopping. This extensive usage results in significant network traffic, contributing a substantial portion of overall Internet traffic. As a result, the research community has focused on security and privacy issues related to mobile device network traffic, which can be analyzed to obtain valuable information for various purposes, including device security, network optimization, and user profiling. This paper reviews the state-of-the-art in network traffic analysis targeting mobile devices. A systematic classification is presented based on three criteria: the analysis goal, the point of network traffic capture, and the targeted mobile platforms. The review considers capture points such as Wi-Fi Access Points, software simulations, and real mobile devices or emulators. For the surveyed works, analysis techniques, validation methods, and achieved results are reviewed and compared. Possible countermeasures, challenges, and future research directions in mobile traffic analysis and emerging domains, such as the Internet of Things, are discussed. This comprehensive survey serves as a valuable reference for researchers and practitioners in this field.

title: The sign clusters of the massless Gaussian free field percolate on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \geqslant 3$ (and more)
Abstract: This paper investigates the percolation phase transition for level sets of the Gaussian free field on $\\mathbb{Z}^d$, where $d\\geqslant 3$. It proves that the corresponding critical parameter $h_*(d)$ is strictly positive for all $d\\geqslant3$, resolving an open question from arXiv:1202.5172. This result implies that the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field percolate on $\\mathbb{Z}^d$ for all $d\\geqslant 3$. The construction of an infinite cluster above a small positive level $h$ involves random interlacements at level $u>0$, a random subset of $\\mathbb{Z}^d$ with desired percolative properties introduced in arXiv:0704.2560. The paper also utilizes a Dynkin-type isomorphism theorem relating random interlacements to the Gaussian free field (arXiv:1111.4818) and a recent coupling of these objects (arXiv:1402.0298) lifted to a continuous metric graph structure over $\\mathbb{Z}^d$.

title: Givers & Receivers perceive handover tasks differently: Implications for Human-Robot collaborative system design
Abstract: This research investigates human-human joint-action in repetitive handover tasks using a bottle handover task as a case study. Both objective and subjective measures are used for evaluation. Subjective evaluation incorporates a psychological perspective, highlighting the differences in how individuals perceive joint-action depending on their role (giver or receiver). This comprehensive approach provides a systematic methodology for analyzing similar tasks. Combining the results of all three analyses, the research offers insights into the science of joint-action for short-cycle repetitive tasks and its implications for designing human-robot collaborative systems.

title: Addendum to: Summary Information for Reasoning About Hierarchical Plans
Abstract:
Hierarchically structured agent plans are crucial for efficient planning and action. They also contribute to the creation of richer classical plans, including not only primitive actions but also abstract actions representing hierarchical structures. A critical step in this process is deriving precondition and effect summaries from a given plan hierarchy. This paper presents mechanisms for deriving these summaries for more pragmatic and conventional hierarchies than previously explored. Formal definitions for preconditions and effects of hierarchical plans are provided, along with data structures and algorithms for automatically deriving this information. The properties of the presented algorithms are analyzed, and their integration with a classical planner for obtaining abstract plans is described.

title: A differential Least Squares Deconvolution method for high precision spectroscopy of stars and exoplanets I. Application to obliquity measurements of HARPS observations of HD189733b
Abstract: High-precision measurements of stellar spectroscopic line profiles and their temporal variations offer valuable insights into stellar photospheric physics (stellar activity) and can be used to characterize exoplanets through the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect or reflected light. This paper introduces a novel method called differential Least Squares Deconvolution (dLSD) for measuring subtle changes in the mean line profile of a spectrum. dLSD determines the convolution function (kernel) necessary to transform a high signal-to-noise ratio template of the star into each observed spectrum. Unlike similar techniques, it requires no assumptions about the template spectrum, eliminating the need for a line-list or cross-correlation mask. The efficacy of dLSD is demonstrated by applying it to star-planet obliquity measurements of the exoplanet HD183799 during its transit. The method's ability to perform at least as well as other techniques, coupled with its model-independent nature, enables the detection of light reflected by an exoplanet.

title: Internet of Tangible Things (IoTT): Challenges and Opportunities for Tangible Interaction with IoT

This disconnect diminishes the user experience and risks isolating users in digital bubbles. Tangible interaction has the potential to bridge this gap, offering a more intuitive and engaging user experience. This paper explores the potential benefits and challenges of tangible interaction in the context of the IoT, introducing the concept of the "Internet of Tangible Things." After analyzing the current challenges for human-computer interaction in the IoT, the paper summarizes trends in tangible interaction and identifies eight properties that could be leveraged to design novel interactions with IoT objects. title: Gaussian elements of a semicontent algebra
Abstract: The relationship between a univariate polynomial possessing locally principal content and the content function behaving as a homomorphism (the Gaussian property) has been extensively studied. The framework of the Ohm-Rush content function is employed for this purpose. The correspondence is particularly strong in situations where the base ring is approximately Gorenstein or the target ring element is regular.

title: Real Time Analytics: Algorithms and Systems
Abstract: Velocity is one of the four Vs commonly used to characterize Big Data. Forrester aptly described this characteristic in Q3 2014: "The high velocity, white-water flow of data from innumerable real-time data sources such as market data, Internet of Things, mobile, sensors, click-stream, and even transactions remain largely unnavigated by most firms. The opportunity to leverage streaming analytics has never been greater." Streaming analytics finds extensive application in diverse domains such as healthcare, e-commerce, financial services, telecommunications, energy and utilities, manufacturing, government, and transportation. Key use cases include real-time visualization of business metrics, enabling highly personalized experiences, and expediting responses during emergencies. This tutorial provides a comprehensive overview of streaming analytics, encompassing its applications, algorithms, and platforms. It traces the evolution of the field over the past decade and discusses the current challenges posed by the other three Vs: Volume, Variety, and Veracity, in the context of Big Data streaming analytics. title: When is a dynamical system mean sensitive?
Abstract: This article investigates the conditions under which a topological dynamical system exhibits mean sensitivity and those under which it does not. Notably, it shows that every uniquely ergodic, mixing system with positive entropy is mean sensitive. Conversely, an example is provided of a transitive system that is cofinitely sensitive or Devaney chaotic with positive entropy but fails to be mean sensitive. The theoretical and practical implications of these findings are explored through several applications. The article provides a negative answer to an open question regarding equicontinuity/sensitivity dichotomies raised by Tu. It introduces and presents results for locally mean equicontinuous systems. Furthermore, it demonstrates that mean sensitivity of the induced hyperspace does not necessarily imply mean sensitivity of the phase space.

title: Asymptotic Behavior of Conjunctive Boolean Networks Over Weakly Connected Digraphs
Abstract: A conjunctive Boolean network (CBN) is a finite state dynamical system where variables take binary values and the update rule for each variable is a Boolean function consisting solely of logical AND operations. This paper delves into the asymptotic behavior of CBNs by analyzing their periodic orbits. When the underlying digraph is strongly connected, the periodic orbits of the associated CBN are well-understood, exhibiting a one-to-one correspondence with binary necklaces of a specific length determined by the graph's loop number. This paper characterizes the periodic orbits of CBNs over arbitrary weakly connected digraphs. It introduces a novel graphical approach, termed "system reduction," which transforms the underlying digraph into a special weakly connected digraph whose strongly connected components are all cycles. The paper demonstrates that the reduced system uniquely determines the asymptotic behavior of the original system. Moreover, it provides a constructive method for computing the periodic orbit of the reduced system, which the original system will eventually enter for any given initial condition.

title: The $L^p$ Dirichlet boundary problem for second order Elliptic Systems with rough coefficients
Abstract: Given a domain above a Lipschitz graph, this paper establishes solvability results for strongly elliptic second-order systems in divergence form, allowing for lower-order (drift) terms and $L^p$-boundary data for $p$ near 2 (specifically, within an interval of the form $\\big(2-\\varepsilon,\\frac{2(n-1)}{n-2}+\\varepsilon\\big)$ for a small $\\varepsilon>0$). The primary novelty of this result lies in the relaxed requirements on the coefficients of the operator. Unlike previous works that assumed constant coefficients or very high regularity, this paper demonstrates solvability under a natural Carleson condition, previously observed in the scalar case. A noteworthy example of a system amenable to this result is the Lamé system for isotropic inhomogeneous materials. The paper shows that the result applies to isotropic materials with a Poisson ratio $\\nu<0.396$. Dealing with genuine systems introduces significant challenges not encountered in the scalar case. These challenges include the absence of a maximum principle for general elliptic systems and the potential inapplicability of the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory. Despite these obstacles, the paper successfully establishes estimates for the square-function and the nontangential maximal operator for the solutions of the elliptic system. These estimates serve as alternative tools for proving $L^p$ solvability results for $p$ near 2.

title: A Novel Neural Network Model Specified for Representing Logical Relations
Abstract: As computers handle increasingly complex tasks in dynamic environments, the need for artificial intelligence (AI) with the ability to automatically judge and decide based on numerous specific conditions becomes paramount. Artificial neural networks (ANNs), inspired by the human brain, are promising candidates for this task. However, most current numeric ANNs struggle to effectively represent logical relations due to their reliance on functional approximation based ratios. Researchers have been actively pursuing novel neural network models designed to represent logical relations. This work proposes a novel neural network model specifically designed for representing logical relations. It introduces new neuron types and multiple link types, including inhibitory links alongside excitatory links. Unlike existing numeric ANNs, inhibitory links connect to excitatory links instead of neurons, conditionally inhibiting the connected excitatory links to ensure accurate representation of logical relations. The model can simulate the operations of Boolean logic gates and construct complex logical relations with simpler neural network structures compared to recent works in this area. This work provides insights into enabling neural networks to represent logical relations more directly and efficiently. The model could serve as a complement to current numeric ANNs for addressing logical issues and expanding the application areas of ANNs.

title: Implementing an Edge-Fog-Cloud architecture for stream data management
Abstract: The Internet of Moving Things (IoMT) necessitates support for a comprehensive data life cycle process, ranging from sorting, cleaning, and monitoring data streams to more intricate tasks like querying, aggregation, and analytics. Current solutions for stream data management in IoMT have primarily focused on specific aspects of the data life cycle process, with a particular emphasis on sensor networks. This paper tackles this challenge by developing a streaming data life cycle process that incorporates an edge/fog/cloud architecture crucial for handling heterogeneous, streaming, and geographically dispersed IoMT devices. It proposes a three-tier architecture to enable instant intra-layer communication, establishing a real-time stream data flow for immediate response to data life cycle tasks within the system. Communication and process are therefore central to the design of this stream data management solution for IoMT. The paper describes and evaluates a prototype implementation using real-time transit data feeds. Preliminary results highlight the advantages of executing data life cycle tasks in reducing the volume of redundant data streams that should not be transported to the cloud.

title: Capturing the Connections: Unboxing Internet of Things Devices

title: An Analysis of the Twitter Discussion on the 2016 Austrian Presidential Elections
Abstract: This paper presents a systematic analysis of the Twitter discussion surrounding the 2016 Austrian presidential elections. It examines a dataset consisting of 343,645 Twitter messages related to the election, utilizing methods from network science, sentiment analysis, and bot detection. Key findings include: a) the election winner (Alexander Van der Bellen) enjoyed significantly greater popularity and influence on Twitter than his opponent; b) Van der Bellen's Twitter followers actively participated in the spread of misinformation about him; c) a clear polarization existed in terms of the sentiments expressed by Twitter followers of the two presidential candidates; d) the in-degree and out-degree distributions of the underlying communication network exhibited heavy tails; and e) compared to other recent events such as the 2016 Brexit referendum or the 2016 US presidential elections, a significantly smaller number of bots participated in the Twitter discussion on the 2016 Austrian presidential election.

title: Advances in Security in Computing and Communications

It serves as a valuable resource for researchers, engineers, practitioners, graduate students, and doctoral students working in the domains of cryptography, network security, and security and privacy issues in the Internet of Things. title: Self-Synchronization in Duty-cycled Internet of Things (IoT) Applications
Abstract: In recent years, networks of low-power devices have gained popularity. These devices, typically wireless, interact to form large networks such as Machine to Machine (M2M) networks, the Internet of Things (IoT), Wearable Computing, and Wireless Sensor Networks. A major challenge in this field is to ensure robust communication between elements while maintaining energy efficiency across the network. This paper introduces an extended and improved emergent broadcast slot (EBS) scheme that facilitates collaborative communication for robust communication and energy efficiency. In the EBS, nodes' communication units remain in sleep mode and wake up only for communication. The EBS scheme is fully decentralized, enabling nodes to coordinate their wake-up windows in a partially overlapped manner within each duty cycle to avoid message collisions. The paper demonstrates the theoretical convergence behavior of the scheme, which is corroborated through real testbed experimentation.

title: How Often Should CSI be Updated for Massive MIMO Systems with Massive Connectivity?
Abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems require support for massive connectivity in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT). The overhead of channel state information (CSI) acquisition becomes a bottleneck in system performance due to the increasing number of users. This paper proposes an intermittent estimation scheme to alleviate the burden of channel estimation and maximize sum capacity. The scheme leverages the temporal correlation of MIMO channels and analyzes the impact of CSI age on the downlink transmission rate using linear precoders. It shows that the CSI updating interval should follow a quasi-periodic distribution, achieving a trade-off between CSI estimation accuracy and CSI acquisition overhead by optimizing the CSI updating frequency for each user. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed intermittent scheme offers significant capacity gains over the conventional continuous estimation scheme.

title: Bandit Convex Optimization for Scalable and Dynamic IoT Management
Abstract: This paper addresses online convex optimization involving both time-varying loss functions and time-varying constraints. The learner does not have full access to the loss functions, only receiving function values (bandit feedback) at queried points. Constraints are revealed after decisions are made, allowing for instantaneous violations but requiring long-term satisfaction. This setting aligns well with emerging online network tasks such as fog computing in the Internet of Things (IoT), where online decisions must adapt to changing user preferences (loss functions) and unpredictable resource availability (constraints). Tailored for human-in-the-loop systems with challenging loss function modeling, the paper develops a family of bandit online saddle-point (BanSaP) schemes. BanSaP adaptively adjusts online operations based on bandit feedback (potentially from multiple sources) regarding loss functions and the changing environment. Performance is assessed using: i) dynamic regret, generalizing the widely used static regret, and ii) fit, quantifying accumulated constraint violations. BanSaP is shown to achieve sub-linear dynamic regret and fit simultaneously, provided that the best dynamic solutions vary slowly over time. Numerical tests on fog computation offloading tasks demonstrate that BanSaP offers competitive performance compared to existing approaches based on gradient feedback.

title: Expressive Stream Reasoning with Laser
Abstract: An increasing number of use cases require the timely extraction of non-trivial knowledge from semantically annotated data streams, particularly on the web and for the Internet of Things (IoT). This extraction often necessitates expressive reasoning, posing computational challenges for large streams. This paper proposes Laser, a novel reasoner supporting a pragmatic, non-trivial fragment of the logic LARS, which extends Answer Set Programming (ASP) for streams. At its core, Laser implements a novel evaluation procedure that annotates formulas to avoid redundant computations at multiple time points. This procedure, combined with a judicious implementation of the LARS operators, significantly improves runtimes compared to other state-of-the-art systems like C-SPARQL and CQELS, or an implementation of LARS running on the ASP solver Clingo. This enables the application of expressive logic-based reasoning to large streams, expanding the range of stream reasoning use cases.

title: Digital Forensic Approaches for Amazon Alexa Ecosystem
Abstract: Internet of Things devices such as the Amazon Echo are undeniably valuable sources of potential digital evidence due to their ubiquitous use and always-on mode of operation, effectively acting as a "black box" of human life. The Amazon Echo plays a central role in the cloud-based intelligent virtual assistant Alexa, developed by Amazon Lab126. The Alexa-enabled wireless smart speaker serves as the gateway for all voice commands submitted to Alexa. Furthermore, the IVA interacts with a multitude of compatible IoT devices and third-party applications leveraging cloud resources. Understanding the complex cloud ecosystem that enables ubiquitous use of Alexa is paramount for supporting digital investigations when necessary. This paper discusses methods for digital forensics pertaining to the IVA Alexa ecosystem. The primary contribution of this paper lies in its novel and efficient approach of combining cloud-native forensics with client-side forensics to support practical digital investigations. Based on a deep understanding of the targeted ecosystem, the paper proposes a proof-of-concept tool, CIFT, that supports identification, acquisition, and analysis of both native artifacts from the cloud and client-centric artifacts from local devices.

title: The Internet of Hackable Things

title: Baryon Asymmetry and Gravitational Waves from Pseudoscalar Inflation
Abstract: In models of inflation driven by an axion-like pseudoscalar field (the inflaton, $a$), a coupling to the standard model hypercharge via a Chern-Simons-type interaction, $L \subset a/(4\Lambda) F\tilde{F}$, can occur. This coupling results in explosive gauge field production during inflation, particularly during its final stage, leading to intriguing phenomenological consequences. Firstly, the primordial hypermagnetic field exhibits maximal helicity, enabling the generation of non-zero baryon number via the standard model chiral anomaly around the time of electroweak symmetry breaking. Secondly, gauge field production during inflation feeds back into the primordial tensor power spectrum, leaving an imprint on the stochastic background of gravitational waves (GWs). This paper focuses on the correlation between these two phenomena. Working within the approximation of instant reheating, it (1) updates the investigation of baryogenesis via hypermagnetic fields from pseudoscalar inflation and (2) examines the corresponding implications for the GW spectrum. The paper finds that successful baryogenesis requires a suppression scale $\Lambda$ of around $\Lambda \sim 3 \times 10^{17}$ GeV, corresponding to a relatively weakly coupled axion. The gauge field production at the end of inflation is typically accompanied by a peak in the GW spectrum at frequencies in the MHz range or above. While detecting such a peak is beyond the capabilities of current technology, it could serve as a smoking-gun signal for baryogenesis from pseudoscalar inflation in the future. Conversely, models that do produce an observable GW signal suffer from the overproduction of baryon number unless the reheating temperature is lower than the electroweak scale.

title: About Extensions of the Extremal Principle

title: Actor-Relational Database Systems: A Manifesto

title: Spacetime and Physical Equivalence

title: Effects of Feedback on the One-sided Secrecy of Two-way Wiretap through Multiple Transmissions

The gap between these bounds is explored using binary input two-way wiretap channels, and the secrecy capacity regions are established for the XOR channel. title: Achieving both positive secrecy rates of the users in two-way wiretap channel by individual secrecy
Abstract: This paper examines the individual secrecy of two-way wiretap channels, where the messages of two legitimate users are separately secured against an eavesdropper. An achievable secrecy rate region is derived for the general two-way wiretap channel with individual secrecy, demonstrating that this region is larger than that with joint secrecy for deterministic channels. The paper also presents outer bounds on the secrecy capacity region for general and specific classes of two-way wiretap channels. The gap between these bounds is explored for binary input and degraded Gaussian two-way wiretap channels, and the secrecy capacity regions are established for the XOR channel and the degraded Gaussian two-way wiretap channel. Notably, the secure sum-rate of the degraded Gaussian two-way wiretap channel under individual secrecy is shown to be strictly larger than under joint secrecy.

title: Contagious disruptions and complexity traps in economic development

It identifies a poverty trap where frequent disruptions lead agents to produce simpler, less valuable goods, perpetuating these disruptions. Escaping this trap requires investing in buffers against disruptions, which rise and fall as the economy produces more complex goods. This finding suggests why "big push" policies might fail and highlights the importance of reliability and gradual technological complexity increases.

title: Realistic Indoor Path Loss Modeling for Regular WiFi Operations in India
Abstract: Indoor wireless communication using Wi-Fi is becoming crucial for the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud robotics in both developed and developing countries. title: Computation Rate Maximization for Wireless Powered Mobile Edge Computing
Abstract: Integrating mobile edge computing (MEC) and wireless power transfer (WPT) is a promising technique to enhance computation capabilities for self-sustainable Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This paper investigates a wireless powered multiuser MEC system where a multi-antenna access point (AP) equipped with an MEC server transmits wireless power to charge multiple users for mobile computing. Using a time-division multiple access (TDMA) protocol, the paper optimizes the system to maximize the weighted sum of computation rates across users by jointly optimizing the energy transmit beamformer, task partition for local computing and offloading, and time allocation among users. The optimal solution is derived in a semi-closed form using convex optimization techniques. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed design over alternative benchmark schemes.

title: RDV: An Alternative To Proof-of-Work And A Real Decentralized Consensus For Blockchain
Abstract: Blockchains, decentralized ledgers recording all transactions, require decentralized consensus mechanisms to ensure reliability and prevent double-spending. Bitcoin uses proof-of-work (PoW), a computationally intensive consensus mechanism, but its high latency and energy consumption pose challenges. This paper introduces an alternative consensus mechanism, RDV (Register, Deposit, Vote), based on a distributed voting process. RDV eliminates the mining process, making it suitable for low-energy devices and the Internet of Things (IoT), offering a potentially more efficient and environmentally friendly approach.

title: Forensic Investigation of P2P Cloud Storage: BitTorrent Sync as a Case Study
Abstract: Cloud computing is a vital technology for the Internet of Things (IoT) and effective evidence collection. This paper examines data remnants left behind by BitTorrent Sync version 2.0, a popular cloud storage and synchronization service. The study found that artifacts related to installation, uninstallation, login, logout, and file synchronization can be recovered from mobile and computer devices running various operating systems. These findings highlight the potential of BitTorrent Sync data for IoT forensics and present a forensically sound investigation methodology for this service.

title: Stable processes, self-similarity and the unit ball
Abstract: This review article delves into the classical identities for isotropic stable processes in one and higher dimensions, drawing connections between Riesz potential theory and the theory of self-similar Markov processes. It re-examines classical identities related to the unit ball and explores recent extensions by combining elements from these two theoretical perspectives. The author emphasizes path decompositions, particularly the Lamperti-Kiu decomposition and the Riesz-Bogdan-Zak transformation. The proofs presented are a mix of known results, existing proofs with novel methods, and entirely new proofs. The paper assumes basic familiarity with Lévy processes and includes reminders of standard material.

title: Be Careful What You Backpropagate: A Case For Linear Output Activations & Gradient Boosting
Abstract: This paper argues that saturating output activation functions, such as softmax, hinder learning performance in various standard classification tasks. It debunks the common belief that softmax's benefit stems from normalization and demonstrates that normalization actually degrades performance. The true advantage lies in the exponentiation of error gradients, leading to exponential gradient boosting, which accelerates convergence and improves generalization. This claim is supported by faster convergence and better performance on tasks like image classification (CIFAR-10 and ImageNet) and semantic segmentation (PASCAL VOC 2012). In the latter case, the proposed method significantly reduces training time compared to standard softmax activation while achieving slightly better performance.

title: Automation of Feature Engineering for IoT Analytics
Abstract: This paper proposes an approach for automating interpretable feature selection for Internet of Things Analytics (IoTA) using machine learning (ML) techniques. The authors recognize that feature selection is a time-consuming and skill-demanding task in IoTA development. The paper demonstrates an automated feature selection method that does not compromise decision-making accuracy, reducing project completion time and resource costs. The approach leverages pattern recognition principles and state-of-the-art (SoA) ML techniques. Experiments using three datasets showcase the effectiveness of the automation, achieving a significant reduction in feature selection time without sacrificing accuracy. Comparisons with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) further validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Subdifferential Stability Analysis for Convex Optimization Problems via Multiplier Sets
Abstract: This paper explores differential stability of convex programming problems in Hausdorff locally convex topological vector spaces. The authors derive formulas for computing or estimating the subdifferential and singular subdifferential of the optimal value function using suitable multiplier sets.

title: Geospatial Semantics
Abstract: Geospatial semantics is a multifaceted field encompassing various research areas. This chapter provides a systematic review of existing geospatial semantic research, focusing on understanding the meaning of geographic entities and their cognitive and digital counterparts. It examines six major research areas: semantic interoperability, digital gazetteers, geographic information retrieval, geospatial Semantic Web, place semantics, and cognitive geographic concepts. The availability of big geo data, especially unstructured text data on the web, and advancements in natural language processing methods are enabling new research directions within geospatial semantics.

title: Wextractor: Follow-up of the evolution of prices in web pages
Abstract: Extracting prices from web pages is crucial for e-commerce activities like buying a product when it falls below a certain threshold. This paper presents Wextractor, a novel web data extraction system consisting of an extraction method and a web app for listing retrieved prices. Wextractor prioritizes usability, requiring users to only identify the pages of interest, while the system automatically extracts the price from the page.

title: Observing IoT Resources over ICN
Abstract: The Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) is a lightweight protocol for RESTful applications on constrained devices, commonly used in the Internet of Things. CoAP observe, an extension to CoAP, enables clients to observe resources through a publish/subscribe mechanism. This paper explores the use of Information-Centric Networking (ICN) within a network provider's domain to enhance CoAP services. The authors present the design and implementation of CoAP observe over ICN, demonstrating how ICN benefits both network providers and CoAP applications without requiring the latter to be aware of ICN's existence. ICN simplifies state management, implementation at CoAP endpoints, and reduces communication overhead in the network.

title: CoAP over ICN
Abstract: The Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) is a specialized Web transfer protocol for resource-oriented applications on constrained devices, commonly found in the Internet of Things. This paper investigates how Information-Centric Networking (ICN), deployed within a network provider's domain that connects CoAP endpoints, can enhance CoAP services. The authors present different CoAP-specific communication scenarios and discuss how ICN benefits both network providers and CoAP applications without requiring the latter to be aware of ICN's existence.  Specifically, ICN reduces state management complexity, simplifies implementation at CoAP endpoints, and lowers communication overhead in the network. |||
