title: Proactive Population-Risk Based Defense Against Denial of Cyber-Physical Service Attacks
Abstract: While the Internet of Things (IoT) holds great promise for improving areas such as energy efficiency, healthcare, and transportation, it is highly vulnerable to cyberattacks. Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks overwhelm a server's bandwidth, but many IoT devices are part of cyber-physical systems (CPS). This means they can be used to launch "physical" Denial-of-Service attacks (PDoS) by overloading the "physical bandwidth" of a CPS. This paper quantifies the population-based risk to a group of IoT devices targeted by malware for a PDoS attack. To model bot recruitment, the paper extends a traditional game-theoretic concept and creates a "Poisson signaling game". It then analyzes two different mechanisms (legal and economic) for deterring botnet recruitment. The findings indicate that defenders can limit botnet activity and that legislating a minimum security level has a limited effect, while incentivizing active defense can significantly reduce botnet activity. This work provides a quantitative foundation for designing proactive defenses against PDoS attacks.

title: Guided-Processing Outperforms Duty-Cycling for Energy-Efficient Systems
Abstract: Energy efficiency is highly desirable for sensing systems in the Internet of Things (IoT). A common approach to achieving low-power systems is duty-cycling, where components are periodically turned off to meet an energy budget. However, this paper demonstrates that duty-cycling is not necessarily optimal for energy efficiency and proposes "guided-processing" as a fundamentally superior alternative. Guided-processing offers explicit modeling of performance uncertainties in system internals, a realistic resource consumption model, and a key insight into its superiority over duty-cycling. The paper also presents a generalization from the cascade structure to a more general graph-based one. When applied to optimize a large-scale audio sensing system with a practical detection application, empirical results show that guided-processing significantly improves detection performance (up to 1.7x and 4x reduction in false-alarm and miss rate, respectively) for the same energy consumption compared to duty-cycling.

title: Feature-Sharing in Cascade Detection Systems with Multiple Applications
Abstract: Traditional distributed detection systems are typically designed for a single target application. However, with the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm, next-generation systems are expected to serve as a shared infrastructure for multiple applications. This paper proposes a modular, cascade design for resource-efficient, multi-task detection systems. Two classes of applications are considered: a primary and a secondary application. The primary application has universal features that can be shared with other applications to reduce the overall feature extraction cost, while the secondary application does not. In this setting, the two applications can collaborate via feature sharing. The paper provides a method to optimize the operation of the multi-application cascade system based on an accurate resource consumption model. It also incorporates the inherent uncertainties in feature models. For evaluation, the twin-comparison argument is used, demonstrating that with the optimal feature sharing strategy, a system can achieve 9x resource savings and 1.43x improvement in detection performance.

title: Peeling property and asymptotic symmetries with a cosmological constant
Abstract: This paper establishes two key properties in an asymptotically (anti-)de Sitter spacetime, using direct computations in the physical spacetime without relying on spacetime compactification. Firstly, the peeling property of the Weyl spinor is guaranteed. In the presence of Maxwell fields, the peeling properties of both Weyl and Maxwell spinors hold if the leading order term of the spin coefficient ρ, when expanded as inverse powers of r (where r is the usual spherical radial coordinate, and r→∞ is null infinity, ℐ), has a coefficient of -1. Secondly, in the absence of gravitational radiation (a conformally flat ℐ), the group of asymptotic symmetries is trivial, with no room for supertranslations.

title: Middleware Technologies for Cloud of Things - a survey
Abstract: The next wave of communication and applications rely on the new services provided by the Internet of Things (IoT), which is becoming a critical aspect of the future of humans and machines. IoT services offer a key solution for creating smart environments in homes, buildings, and cities. However, the massive number of connected things and objects, with a high growth rate, presents several challenges, including management, aggregation, and storage of the large amount of data generated. To address these challenges, cloud computing has emerged as Cloud of Things (CoT), providing virtually unlimited cloud services to enhance large-scale IoT platforms. The design and implementation of a CoT platform involve several factors, with heterogeneity of different objects being one of the most important and challenging problems. This paper focuses on middleware technologies for CoT as a solution to address this heterogeneity. It presents the main features and characteristics of middlewares, examines different architecture styles and service domains, and highlights several middlewares suitable for CoT-based platforms. Finally, the paper discusses current challenges and issues in the design of CoT-based middlewares.

title: A sub-mW IoT-endnode for always-on visual monitoring and smart triggering
Abstract: This paper presents a fully programmable Internet of Things (IoT) visual sensing node designed for sub-mW power consumption in always-on monitoring scenarios. The system features a spatial-contrast 128x64 binary pixel imager with focal-plane processing. Operating at its lowest power mode (10 μW at 10 fps), the sensor provides the number of changed pixels as output. This information is used by a dedicated camera interface, implemented on a low-power FPGA, to wake up an ultra-low-power parallel processing unit for extracting context-aware visual information. The smart sensor is evaluated in three always-on visual triggering application scenarios. Triggering accuracy comparable to RGB image sensors is achieved under nominal lighting conditions, while consuming an average power between 193 μW and 277 μW depending on context activity. The digital sub-system is extremely flexible due to a fully programmable digital signal processing engine, yet achieves 19x lower power consumption compared to MCU-based cameras with significantly lower on-board computing capabilities.

title: Internet of Things-aided Smart Grid: Technologies, Architectures, Applications, Prototypes, and Future Research Directions
Abstract: Traditional power grids are undergoing a transformation into Smart Grids (SGs) to address the challenges of unidirectional information flow, energy wastage, growing energy demand, and reliability and security concerns in the existing power system. SGs offer bidirectional energy flow between service providers and consumers, encompassing power generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization systems. SGs utilize various devices for monitoring, analysis, and control of the grid, deployed at power plants, distribution centers, and consumer premises in vast numbers. Consequently, an SG requires connectivity, automation, and tracking of these devices. This is achieved through the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT). IoT enables SG systems to support various network functions throughout the generation, transmission, distribution, and consumption of energy by incorporating IoT devices (such as sensors, actuators, and smart meters) and providing connectivity, automation, and tracking for these devices. This paper offers a comprehensive survey of IoT-aided SG systems, covering existing architectures, applications, and prototypes. It also highlights open issues, challenges, and future research directions for IoT-aided SG systems.

title: Intelligent Personal Assistant with Knowledge Navigation
Abstract: An Intelligent Personal Agent (IPA) aims to assist users in obtaining information from reliable sources by utilizing knowledge navigation techniques and saving time in finding the best content. The agent is also responsible for responding to chat-based queries using a Conversation Corpus. This paper explores different methods for optimal query generation. To enhance user experience, the agent accepts input through text (keyboard), voice (speech recognition), and server (Facebook), providing output responses using the same method. Unlike existing chatbots that reply by modifying the input, this agent provides responses based on multiple SRT files. The model learns using a human dialogs dataset and is designed to respond in a human-like manner. Queries about famous things (places, people, and words) can be answered using web scraping, enabling the bot to have knowledge navigation features. The agent learns from its past experiences, supporting semi-supervised learning.

title: Energy-Efficient Low-Power Circuit Techniques for Wireless Energy and Data Transfer in IoT Sensor Nodes
Abstract: This paper presents techniques and examples to reduce power consumption and enhance energy efficiency in autonomous Wireless Sensor Nodes (WSNs) for the Internet of Things. The focus is on the RF Energy Harvester (RFEH), data receiver, and transmitter, all of which significantly impact device cost, lifetime, and functionality. Co-design of the antenna and electronics is explored to boost the power conversion efficiency of the RF-DC converter. As a proof of concept, a charge pump rectifier is designed and its measurement results are presented. To further enhance the rectifier output voltage, a DC-DC converter incorporating maximum power point tracking is designed. A prototype circuit is presented that accommodates an input power level range of 1 μW to 1 mW and offers peak efficiencies of 76.3% and 82% at 1 μW and 1 mW, respectively. The co-design principle is also applied to the receiver side, optimizing the antenna-electronics interface. It is shown how this technique improves the noise figure of the Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) without compromising power consumption. As a low-power alternative to narrow-band wireless transmission, sub-GHz ultra-wideband is proposed. A novel low-power sub-GHz Ultra-Wide-Bandwidth (UWB) transmitter consuming only 0.28 mW is designed as a proof of concept. Its working principle is verified through circuit simulations and measurements. The low-power nature of the transmitter and receiver principles, combined with the power-efficient RF-DC converter, pave the way for continuous operation of a WSN.

title: SIT: A Lightweight Encryption Algorithm for Secure Internet of Things
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT), a promising technology for the future, is expected to connect billions of devices. This increased communication is anticipated to generate a massive amount of data, raising concerns about data security. Devices in the IoT architecture are typically small and low-powered. Conventional encryption algorithms are generally computationally expensive due to their complexity and require numerous rounds for encryption, wasting the limited energy of these gadgets. Less complex algorithms, however, may compromise the desired integrity. This paper proposes a lightweight encryption algorithm named Secure IoT (SIT), a 64-bit block cipher requiring a 64-bit key to encrypt data. The algorithm's architecture combines features of Feistel and a uniform substitution-permutation network. Simulations show that the algorithm provides substantial security in just five encryption rounds. The algorithm is implemented in hardware on a low-cost 8-bit microcontroller, and the results of code size, memory utilization, and encryption/decryption execution cycles are compared with benchmark encryption algorithms. The MATLAB code for relevant simulations is available online at https://goo.gl/Uw7E0W.

title: Stochastic Optimization from Distributed, Streaming Data in Rate-limited Networks
Abstract: Motivated by machine learning applications in networks of sensors, Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, and autonomous agents, this paper proposes techniques for distributed stochastic convex learning from high-rate data streams. The setup involves a network of nodes, each receiving a data stream at a constant rate, that collaboratively solve a stochastic convex optimization problem over rate-limited communication links. Two algorithms are presented and analyzed: distributed stochastic approximation mirror descent (D-SAMD) and accelerated distributed stochastic approximation mirror descent (AD-SAMD). These algorithms are based on two stochastic variants of mirror descent and involve nodes collaborating through approximate averaging of local, noisy subgradients using distributed consensus. The main contributions are (i) bounds on the convergence rates of D-SAMD and AD-SAMD in terms of the number of nodes, network topology, and ratio of data streaming and communication rates, and (ii) sufficient conditions for order-optimum convergence of these algorithms. The findings show that for sufficiently well-connected networks, distributed learning schemes can achieve order-optimum convergence even with a low communication rate. Moreover, accelerated methods significantly expand the regime where order-optimum convergence is achieved, unlike the centralized setting where accelerated methods typically offer only modest improvements. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms is demonstrated through numerical experiments.

title: Reliable Energy-Efficient Routing Algorithm for Vehicle-Assisted Wireless Ad-Hoc Networks
Abstract: This paper investigates the design of optimal routing paths in a moving vehicles environment within the context of the Internet of Things (IoT). The paper proposes a three-step optimal routing path algorithm for reliable and energy-efficient communications. Results show that the assistance of moving vehicles can significantly reduce total energy consumption. The paper also analyzes the impact of path loss, maximum transmit power constraints, QoS requirements, etc., on optimal routing path design and energy consumption.

title: Small Loop Transfer Spaces with Respect to Subgroups of Fundamental Groups
Abstract: Let H be a subgroup of π1(X,x0). This paper extends the concept of X being an SLT space to H-SLT space at x0. Firstly, it is shown that the fibers of the endpoint projection pH:˜XH→X are topological groups when X is H-SLT space at x0 and H is a normal subgroup. The paper also demonstrates that under these conditions, the concepts of homotopically path Hausdorff relative to H and homotopically Hausdorff relative to H coincide. Additionally, among other findings, the paper proves that the endpoint projection map pH has the unique path lifting property if and only if H is a closed normal subgroup of π1qtop(X,x0) when X is SLT at x0. Secondly, the paper presents conditions under which the whisker topology agrees with the quotient of the compact-open topology on ˜XH. title: A Novel Hybrid Quicksort Algorithm Vectorized using AVX-512 on Intel Skylake
Abstract:
Modern CPUs, featuring hierarchical memory and SIMD/vectorization capabilities, offer significant potential for efficient algorithm implementations. The introduction of AVX-512 has spurred the search for sorting algorithms optimized for this architecture. This paper presents a novel two-part hybrid sorting algorithm based on Quicksort. The core partitioning operation utilizes a new algorithm, while small partitions are sorted using a branch-free Bitonic-based sort. This approach demonstrates how classical algorithms can be adapted and enhanced through the AVX-512 extension. Performance evaluations on an Intel Xeon Skylake processor demonstrate significant speedups over reference libraries, with a 4x speedup over GNU C++ sort and a 1.4x speedup over Intel IPP.  ||| 
This research examines the relationship between the radius (r) and attachment number (a) of tetravalent graphs with half-arc-transitive automorphism groups. Despite advancements in the study of strongly interacting matter, the region of high baryonic densities and low temperatures remains difficult to access experimentally. The model exhibits chiral symmetry breaking at high densities through the formation of a Dual Chiral Density Wave (DCDW) condensate, leading to electromagnetic interactions described by axion electrodynamics and a dissipationless Hall current. |||

Forwarding data by name has been considered essential for an information-centric redesign of the Internet, aiming to improve content access, dissemination, and storage. The Named Data Networking (NDN) and Content-Centric Networking (CCNx) architectures are leading examples of this approach. However, name-based forwarding introduces significant storage and communication complexities compared to address-based solutions. Additionally, algorithms used in NDN and CCNx have limitations. This paper introduces the Addressable Data Networking (ADN) architecture as an alternative, particularly attractive for large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) deployments due to its reduced storage and processing requirements at relaying nodes. ADN allows things and data to be denoted by names, similar to NDN and CCNx, but utilizes an address-based forwarding plane and an information plane that seamlessly maps names to addresses without involving end-user applications. Mission-critical data dissemination in massive Internet of Things (IoT) networks requires stringent message transfer delay constraints. Due to the limited power and communication range of IoT devices, data often relies on multiple device-to-device (D2D) links for transmission. This creates challenges in maximizing network transmission capacity while minimizing multi-hop delay to support mission-critical applications. Balancing the tradeoff between conflicting objectives like spatial frequency reuse, transmission quality, and packet progress is crucial. This paper utilizes a stochastic geometry approach to quantify the performance of multi-hop massive IoT networks under different packet forwarding schemes, considering spatial frequency reuse and transmission quality. A comprehensive performance metric is developed to optimize the system for optimal performance. The results can guide the selection of forwarding schemes and tuning of the carrier sensing threshold to meet specific delay constraints and transmission quality requirements. |||

Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering, a quantum correlation intermediate between entanglement and Bell nonlocality, is linked to measurement incompatibility. TrustShadow leverages ARM TrustZone technology to partition resources into secure and normal worlds, creating a trusted execution environment for security-critical applications within the secure world. This paper investigates positioning using observed-time-difference-of-arrival (OTDOA) for devices deployed in Long-Term-Evolution (LTE) based narrow-band Internet-of-things (NB-IoT) systems. Due to the low-cost analog circuits and low-sampling rate (1.92 MHz or lower) of NB-IoT devices, a low-complexity ToA detector is designed. The EM-SIC algorithm consists of two stages for ToA detection. In the first stage, coarse ToA estimates are obtained after a predefined number of EM-SIC iterations. In the second stage, a low-pass filter is used to interpolate correlations at a low sampling rate to a higher rate (30.72 MHz), improving ToA resolution. Only correlations within a small search window centered at the coarse ToA estimates are upsampled. With at least three detected cells, OTDOA and cell site locations are used to estimate the NB-IoT device's position. Numerical simulations demonstrate the robustness of the EM-SIC based ToA detector against impairments like inter-cell interference, fading-channel, and residual FO. J. Kigami laid the foundation for analysis on fractals by constructing a Laplacian-like operator on fractal graphs. The Sierpinski gasket is a well-known example. This operator is obtained through a weak formulation based on Dirichlet forms, built inductively on a sequence of graphs converging towards the domain. These Dirichlet forms enable the derivation of energy forms on the fractal domain. However, the Laplacian's construction is not straightforward for all fractal domains. While it is naturally obtained for domains like the Sierpinski gasket, Dirichlet forms only depend on the topology, not the geometry. Therefore, for domains with the same topology as a line segment but different geometry, a method for incorporating this specific geometry is needed. This paper explores this issue using the graph of the Weierstrass function, where more sophisticated energy forms are introduced through normalization constants that account for both topology and geometry. The focus then shifts to investigating the relationship between energy forms and geometry using fractal curves, specifically the Sierpinski arrowhead curve, whose limit is the Sierpinski gasket. The paper raises the question of whether the Laplacian obtained for this curve is the same as for the triangle, suggesting a worthy area for further investigation. |||

title: Clarifying Trust in Social Internet of Things
Abstract: A social approach can enhance the Internet of Things (IoT) by managing numerous interconnected objects. These objects function autonomously, seeking and providing information and services to users. Establishing trust between objects significantly improves node interaction efficiency in a social IoT, mitigating uncertainty and risk. However, existing trust models have limitations. This paper proposes a comprehensive trust model tailored for social IoT, encompassing elements such as trustor, trustee, goal, trustworthiness evaluation, decision, action, result, and context. Building on this model, the paper clarifies the concept of trust in social IoT through five aspects: mutuality of trustor and trustee, inferential transfer of trust, transitivity of trust, trustworthiness update, and trustworthiness influenced by a dynamic environment. Simulations utilizing real-world social network connectivities evaluate the performance of a social IoT operating with the proposed trust model. The model's validity is further confirmed using an experimental IoT network.

title: PIANO: Proximity-based User Authentication on Voice-Powered Internet-of-Things Devices
Abstract: Voice interaction is anticipated to become a prevalent method for humans to engage with Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This paper proposes a proximity-based user authentication method, dubbed PIANO, for access control on voice-powered IoT devices. PIANO leverages the built-in speaker, microphone, and Bluetooth commonly found in these devices. It assumes a user carries a personal voice-powered device (e.g., smartphone, smartwatch, or smartglass) serving as their identity. When another voice-powered IoT device requires authentication, PIANO estimates the distance between the devices by transmitting and detecting acoustic signals. Access is granted if the estimated distance remains below a user-defined threshold. A proof-of-concept prototype of PIANO was implemented. Theoretical and empirical evaluations demonstrate that PIANO is secure, reliable, customizable, and efficient.

title: Compile-Time Extensions to Hybrid ODEs
Abstract: Reachability analysis for hybrid systems is an active field of research, leading to the development of many promising prototype tools. These tools typically allow users to express hybrid systems as automata with associated ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for each state, alongside rules for transitions between states. Significant effort is invested in developing, verifying, and correctly implementing these tools. Expanding their scope of applicability is highly desirable. This paper demonstrates how compile-time transformations can be used to extend the basic hybrid ODE formalism traditionally supported in reachability tools such as SpaceEx or Flow*. The extension supports certain types of partial derivatives and equational constraints. These extensions facilitate, among other things, expressing the Euler-Lagrangian equation and capturing practically relevant constraints frequently encountered in mechanical systems. Achieving this level of expressiveness requires utilizing binding time analysis (BTA), program differentiation, symbolic Gaussian elimination, and abstract interpretation using interval analysis. Except for BTA, the other components are readily available or can be easily integrated into most reachability tools. Therefore, this paper focuses on presenting both the declarative and algorithmic specifications for the BTA phase and establishing the soundness of the algorithmic specifications with respect to the declarative one.

title: Weakly-Supervised Spatial Context Networks
Abstract: This research investigates the potential of spatial context as a self-supervisory signal for learning visual representations. Specifically, it proposes spatial context networks that learn to predict a representation of one image patch from another within the same image, conditioned on their real-valued relative spatial offset. Unlike auto-encoders, which aim to encode and reconstruct original image patches, this network aims to encode and reconstruct intermediate representations of spatially offset patches, learning a spatially conditioned contextual representation. The paper demonstrates the importance of focusing on object-centric patches by testing performance with various patch selection mechanisms. It also shows that using object proposal as a patch selection mechanism leads to the greatest performance improvement. Furthermore, unlike auto-encoders, context encoders, or other unsupervised feature learning methods, this research illustrates that contextual supervision (with pre-trained model initialization) can enhance the performance of existing pre-trained models. The spatial context networks are built upon standard VGG_19 and CNN_M architectures, demonstrating improvements (without additional explicit supervision) over the original ImageNet pre-trained VGG_19 and CNN_M models in object categorization and detection on VOC2007.

The paper comprehensively characterizes one-dimensional bounded solutions of this problem and demonstrates that if u is a bounded solution with ρ := sup_{R^N}u verifying f(ρ) = 0, then u is necessarily one-dimensional.

title: Using Aesthetic Judgements to Distinguish between Humans and Computers

Initial analysis suggests that Aesthetic CAPTCHAs theoretically offer advantages over other schemes in terms of satisfying the full range of CAPTCHA requirements. More broadly, employing human aesthetic judgment introduces a potential new dimension to the future design of Turing tests.

title: Market Crashes as Critical Phenomena? Explanation, Idealization, and Universality in Econophysics

It is naturally construed as a "minimal model" in the sense of Batterman and Rice (2014), yet it provides a causal explanation of market crashes, aligning with Woodward's interventionist account of causation (2003).

title: Is Time Travel Too Strange to Be Possible? Determinism and Indeterminism on Closed Timelike Curves
Abstract: General relativity's Einstein equations have solutions that exhibit closed timelike curves (CTCs), where time loops back on itself, leading to exotic consequences. To maintain consistency in time travel narratives, specific constraints must be met, preventing seemingly ordinary and plausible processes. This, along with other "unphysical" features, has motivated many authors to exclude solutions with CTCs from consideration, often by proposing a chronology protection law. This contribution investigates the nature of one particular class of exotic consequences of CTCs, namely those involving unexpected cases of indeterminism or determinism. Indeterminism arises even within the framework of deterministic physical theories when CTCs do not intersect spacelike hypersurfaces outside of a limited CTC region (such hypersurfaces fail to be Cauchy surfaces). Conversely, a specific type of determinism seems to emerge when an indeterministic theory is applied on a CTC: things cannot deviate from their pre-existing state. The paper argues that, upon further consideration, both this indeterminism and determinism on CTCs have parallels in other familiar areas of physics. CTC-indeterminism resembles the epistemological indeterminism known from statistical physics, while the "fixedness" characteristic of CTC-determinism is prevalent in physics. Therefore, CTC-determinism and CTC-indeterminism do not provide compelling grounds for rejecting CTCs as conceptually inadmissible.

title: Threat analysis of IoT networks Using Artificial Neural Network Intrusion Detection System

A multi-level perceptron, a type of supervised ANN, is trained using internet packet traces and then assessed for its ability to thwart Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS/DoS) attacks. The paper focuses on classifying normal and threat patterns on an IoT Network. The ANN procedure is validated against a simulated IoT network. Experimental results demonstrate 99.4% accuracy, successfully detecting various DDoS/DoS attacks.

title: Modulation in the Air: Backscatter Communication over Ambient OFDM Carrier
Abstract: Ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) enables radio-frequency (RF) powered backscatter devices (BDs) (e.g., sensors, tags) to modulate their information bits over ambient RF carriers in an over-the-air manner. This technology, also known as "modulation in the air," has emerged as a promising solution for achieving green communications in future Internet-of-Things scenarios. This paper investigates an AmBC system that leverages ambient orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulated signals in the air. It first models such an AmBC system from a spread-spectrum communication perspective, leading to the proposal of a novel joint design for BD waveform and receiver detector. The BD symbol period is designed to be generally an integer multiple of the OFDM symbol period. The waveform for BD bit '0' maintains the same state within a BD symbol period, while the waveform for BD bit '1' undergoes a state transition in the middle of each OFDM symbol period within a BD symbol period. In the receiver detector design, a test statistic is constructed that cancels out direct-link interference by exploiting the repeating structure of the ambient OFDM signals due to the use of cyclic prefix. For systems with a single-antenna receiver, the maximum-likelihood detector is proposed for recovering BD bits, with the optimal threshold derived in closed-form expression. For systems with a multi-antenna receiver, a new test statistic is proposed, and the optimal detector is derived. Moreover, practical timing synchronization algorithms are presented, and the paper analyzes the impact of various system parameters on system performance. Finally, extensive numerical results demonstrate that the proposed transceiver design significantly improves system bit-error-rate (BER) performance and operating range, achieving a substantially higher data rate compared to conventional designs.

title: Random Access Analysis for Massive IoT Networks under A New Spatio-Temporal Model: A Stochastic Geometry Approach
Abstract: The emergence of massive Internet of Things (mIoT) has presented an opportunity to build powerful and ubiquitous connections, but it also introduces a multitude of new challenges. Cellular networks are potential solutions due to their high scalability, reliability, and efficiency. The Random Access CHannel (RACH) procedure is the initial step in establishing connections between IoT devices and Base Stations (BSs) in cellular-based mIoT networks. Modelling the interactions between the static properties of the physical layer network and the dynamic properties of queues evolving in each IoT device poses significant challenges. To address this, the paper proposes a novel traffic-aware spatio-temporal model to analyze RACH in cellular-based mIoT networks. The physical layer network is modelled and analyzed using stochastic geometry in the spatial domain, while queue evolution is analyzed using probability theory in the time domain. For performance evaluation, exact expressions are derived for the preamble transmission success probabilities of a randomly chosen IoT device with different RACH schemes in each time slot, providing insights into the effectiveness of each scheme. The derived analytical results are verified through realistic simulations capturing the evolution of packets in each IoT device. This mathematical model and analytical framework can be applied to assess the performance of other types of RACH schemes in cellular-based networks by simply integrating their preamble transmission principles.

title: Rethinking probabilistic prediction in the wake of the 2016 U.S. presidential election
Abstract: Many statisticians and citizens perceive the outcome of the recent US presidential election as a failure of data-driven methods on a grand scale. This impression has sparked debate and discussion about how election predictions went awry - were the polls inaccurate, the models flawed, or did we misinterpret the probabilities? Conversely, it also raises the question of how the predictions were correct - perhaps the analyses were sound, even if the predictions were wrong, as probabilistic forecasting inherently involves uncertainty. This paper analyzes the election outcome in relation to a core set of effectiveness principles. Regardless of whether and how the election predictions were right or wrong, the paper argues that they were ineffective in conveying the extent to which the data was informative about the outcome and the level of uncertainty associated with making these assessments. The analysis highlights the shortcomings of the classical interpretations of probability and its communication to consumers in the form of predictions. An alternative approach, based on the concept of validity, is presented, offering two immediate insights for predictive inference. First, the predictions are more conservative, arguably more realistic, and come with certain guarantees on the probability of an erroneous prediction. Second, this approach easily and naturally reflects the (possibly substantial) uncertainty about the model by outputting plausibilities instead of probabilities. Had these simple steps been taken by popular prediction outlets, the election outcome may not have been as shocking.

title: Emergence of Time in a Participatory Universe
Abstract: After acknowledging the measurement problem, physicists typically assume the problem originates from the measurement process. Since classical probabilities also collapse when updating information, quantum state collapse doesn't appear to be unique. This paper argues that the problem actually stems from the unitary evolution part of quantum theory. Instead of asking "what happens during measurement?", the question should be "what is time?". After discussing the challenges associated with time evolution in quantum theory, the paper proposes a new approach to interpreting time, arguing how it would emerge from the non-commutativity of quantum theory, assuming participatory realism. Its relation to the familiar mechanical or unitary notion of time is discussed. The subjectivity associated with the increasingly popular epistemic interpretations of quantum theory makes it seem like a cure that's worse than the disease. This paper aims to reintroduce objectivity into quantum physics without resorting to many-worlds or similar interpretations.

title: Drift-Free Fabry-Perot-Cavity-based Optical Refractometry -- Accurate Expressions for Assessments of Gas Refractivity and Density
Abstract: Recent advances in Fabry-Perot cavity-based optical refractometry (OR), FPC-OR, utilizing proposed novel methodologies based on drift-free Dual FPC-OR (DF-DFPC-OR), have significantly mitigated previous challenges associated with FPC-OR, particularly drifts of the cavity spacer. This has opened up new possibilities for accurate characterization of gases. However, to leverage these techniques for highly accurate assessments, general and explicit expressions are needed for how gas density, ρ_n, relates to gas refractivity, n-1, and how the latter depends on the change in frequency of laser light following cavity evacuation, Δν_l. This paper provides such relations, properly accounting for the influence of all conceivable phenomena and higher-order (non-linear) contributions to the assessment of these entities under drift-free conditions. The relative contributions of each phenomenon to measurements of gas refractivity and density are individually evaluated. The paper demonstrates, among other findings, that the influence of cavity deformation is greater for an open cavity (placed in a compartment where gas is introduced) than a closed one. If not accounted for appropriately, under standard pressure and temperature conditions, it can contribute to the accuracy of the technique by up to a few times 10^-3 when using an open cavity, while it can be an order of magnitude smaller, around 10^-4, for a well-designed closed cavity. Additionally, it shows that non-linearities from dispersion are smaller when relocking is employed compared to when it is not used. The derived expressions can serve as a foundation for assessing refractivity or gas density, and changes therein, in future realizations of OR, allowing them to fully benefit from the extraordinary power of DF-DFPC-OR.

title: A Neural Networks Approach to Predicting How Things Might Have Turned Out Had I Mustered the Nerve to Ask Barry Cottonfield to the Junior Prom Back in 1997
Abstract: This research utilizes a feed-forward artificial neural network with back-propagation through a single hidden layer to predict Barry Cottonfield's likely response to the author's invitation to the "Once Upon a Daydream" junior prom at Conard High School gymnasium in 1997. To examine the network's ability to generalize to such a situation beyond specific training scenarios, an L2 regularization term is incorporated into the cost function, and performance is evaluated across a range of regularization strengths. Additionally, the network's nonsensical decision-making strategies are examined when Barry is recently engaged in a fight with his sister, Janice. To simulate Barry's inability to learn efficiently from significant mistakes (documented by his algebra teacher), a simple quadratic form is chosen for the cost function, ensuring that the weight update magnitude is not necessarily correlated with the magnitude of the output error. Network performance on test data indicates an 87.2% chance of a "Yes" response from Barry given specific environmental input parameters. The most effective method of question delivery is found to be Secret Note rather than Verbal Speech. Mild evidence suggests that wearing a burgundy mini-dress might have been beneficial. The network performs comparably for all values of regularization strength, implying that noise in a high school hallway during passing time does not significantly impact the outcome. The paper discusses potential biases inherent in the output, implications for the functionality of real biological networks, and future directions. title: High Efficiency Power Side-Channel Attack Immunity using Noise Injection in Attenuated Signature Domain
Abstract: The advancement of technology in recent decades has led to the widespread availability of miniaturized sensors and internet-connected things (IoT), making the security of electronic devices a top priority. Side-channel attack (SCA) is a prominent method for compromising the security of encryption systems by exploiting information leaked from physical devices. Correlational power attack (CPA) is an efficient power side-channel attack technique that analyzes the correlation between estimated and measured supply current traces to extract the secret key. Existing countermeasures to power attacks primarily focus on reducing the SNR of leaked data or introducing significant overhead using techniques like power balancing. This paper presents an attenuated signature AES (AS-AES) that resists SCA with minimal noise current overhead. AS-AES utilizes a shunt low-drop-out (LDO) regulator to suppress the AES current signature by 400x in the supply current traces. The shunt LDO has been fabricated and validated in 130 nm CMOS technology. System-level implementation of AS-AES, along with noise injection, demonstrates that the system remains secure even after 50K encryptions, with a 10x reduction in power overhead compared to noise addition alone.

title: On pointwise periodicity in tilings, cellular automata and subshifts

title: How brains are built: Principles of computational neuroscience
Abstract: Nobel laureate Richard Feynman famously stated, "If I cannot build it, I do not understand it." By this metric, we have a decent understanding of physics, a lesser understanding of chemistry, and almost no understanding of biology. When we fully grasp a phenomenon, we can specify its entire sequence of events, causes, and effects with such completeness that it becomes possible to fully simulate it, with all its internal mechanisms intact. Achieving this level of understanding is rare. It equates to constructing a complete design for a machine that could serve as a stand-in for the thing being studied. To understand a phenomenon sufficiently to fully simulate it is to understand it computationally. Computation does not refer to computers per se. Instead, it refers to the underlying principles and methods that make them work. As Turing Award recipient Edsger Dijkstra said, computational science "is no more about computers than astronomy is about telescopes." Computational science is the study of the hidden rules underlying complex phenomena, from physics to psychology. Computational neuroscience, therefore, aims to understand brains well enough to simulate their functions, thereby encompassing the twin goals of science and engineering: deeply understanding the inner workings of our brains and being able to construct simulacra of them. Just as simple robots today replace human physical abilities in settings ranging from factories to hospitals, brain engineering will construct substitutes for our mental abilities, potentially even enabling us to repair our brains when they malfunction.

title: Painless Breakups -- Efficient Demixing of Low Rank Matrices
Abstract: Consider a sum of linear measurements of s different rank-r matrices of the form y = ∑_{k=1}^{s} A_k (X_k). This paper presents two computationally efficient algorithms based on hard thresholding to solve this low-rank demixing problem. The paper proves that, under suitable conditions, these algorithms are guaranteed to converge to the correct solution at a linear rate. It discusses applications in the context of quantum tomography and the Internet of Things. Numerical simulations demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed algorithms. |||

Abstract: This paper challenges the notion of Newtonian backreaction affecting the expansion of the universe, a concept proposed by Racz et al. (2017). title: A Contract-based Incentive Mechanism for Energy Harvesting-based Internet of Things

The paper also formulates a novel peer offloading game among SBSs, analyzing its equilibrium and efficiency loss in terms of the price of anarchy. title: The Goldman-Turaev Lie bialgebra in genus zero and the Kashiwara-Vergne problem

The main result of this paper shows that constructing an expansion for which the full bracket and cobracket coincide with their lowest degree parts is essentially equivalent to solving the KV problem. This equivalence is established by demonstrating that the Turaev cobracket can be expressed in terms of the double bracket and the non-commutative divergence cocycle, key components of the KV theory. title: Jump detection in Besov spaces via a new BBM formula. Applications to Aviles-Giga type functionals

It is shown that $BV^q(\Omega)$ contains both $BV(\Omega) \cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ and $W^{1/q,q}(\Omega)$. title: Designing Privacy-aware Internet of Things Applications

title: Performance Analysis of Mixed-ADC Massive MIMO Systems over Rician Fading Channels

The authors explore the use of low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) to reduce cost and power consumption. However, the practical implementation of this architecture requires complex signal processing to compensate for the quantization errors caused by low-resolution ADCs. To address this, the authors propose a mixed-ADC architecture that includes a few high-resolution ADCs for low-complexity transceiver algorithms. Unlike previous studies over Rayleigh fading channels, this work analyzes the performance of mixed-ADC massive MIMO systems over the more general Rician fading channel, relevant for 5G scenarios like Internet of Things (IoT). Novel closed-form approximate expressions for uplink achievable rate are derived for both perfect and imperfect channel state information (CSI). The results show that the achievable rate converges to a fixed value with increasing Rician K-factor. The authors also derive the power-scaling law, demonstrating that user transmit power can be scaled down proportionally to the inverse of the number of base station (BS) antennas for both perfect and imperfect CSI. Finally, the paper reveals a tradeoff between achievable rate and energy efficiency with respect to key system parameters, and numerical results demonstrate the energy-rate trade-off advantage of the mixed-ADC architecture compared to ideal infinite-resolution and low-resolution ADC architectures.

title: Anomaly Detection and Redundancy Elimination of Big Sensor Data in Internet of Things

title: Performance Optimization of Network Coding Based Communication and Reliable Storage in Internet of Things

The paper also examines the optimal storage allocation problem in network coding-based distributed cloud storage, aiming to find the most reliable allocation of data components across multiple data centers. A polynomial-time optimal storage allocation (OSA) scheme is proposed to solve this problem. Both theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate the significant improvement in storage reliability achieved by the OSA scheme.

title: Dynamic Intention-Aware Recommendation System

title: Enriques surfaces with normal K3-like coverings

The paper also develops a general theory of Zariski singularities in arbitrary dimensions, connects it to the theory of height-one group schemes actions and restricted Lie algebras, and investigates conditions for the local freeness of tangent sheaves. title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Privacy-Preserving Mobile Analytics

The privacy benefits of this approach are evaluated based on the information exposed to the cloud service, while the local inference cost of different layers on a modern handset is also assessed. The evaluation shows that Siamese fine-tuning significantly reduces the amount of potentially sensitive information in personal data, achieving a balance between utility, privacy, and performance.

title: Localization in Long-range Ultra Narrow Band IoT Networks using RSSI

title: Functions that Emerge through End-to-End Reinforcement Learning - The Direction for Artificial General Intelligence -

title: The Ohm-Rush content function II. Noetherian rings, valuation domains, and base change

title: Arithmetic properties of coefficients of power series expansion of $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(1-x^{2^{n}}\right)^{t}$ (with an Appendix by Andrzej Schinzel)
Abstract: The generating function for the Prouhet-Thue-Morse sequence is $F(x)=\prod_{n=0}^{\infty}(1-x^{2^{n}})$. When $t$ is a positive integer, the sequence $(f_{n}(t))_{n\in N}$ is the Cauchy convolution of $t$ copies of the Prouhet-Thue-Morse sequence. For negative integers $t$, the $n$-th term of the sequence $(f_{n}(t))_{n\in N}$ counts the number of representations of the number $n$ as a sum of powers of 2, where each summand can have one of $-t$ colors. This paper presents a characterization of the solutions to the equations $f_{n}(2^k)=0$ (where $k$ is a non-negative integer) and $f_{n}(3)=0$. title: A quantum dynamic belief decision making model
Abstract: The sure thing principle and the law of total probability are fundamental principles in classical probability theory. A disjunction fallacy violates these principles. This paper proposes a new quantum dynamic belief decision-making model based on quantum dynamic modeling and Dempster-Shafer (D-S) evidence theory to address this issue and model real human decision-making processes. Techniques from quantum mathematics are incorporated. The model separates belief and action as distinct parts of the decision-making process. Belief uncertainty is represented by a superposition of states, while action uncertainty is represented by an extra uncertainty state. The entanglement between beliefs and actions leads to an interference effect. Basic probability assignment (BPA) for decisions is generated through quantum dynamic modeling. Then, BPA for the extra uncertain state and an entanglement degree defined by Deng entropy are used to measure the interference effect. Compared to existing models, the proposed model has fewer free parameters. A classical categorization decision-making experiment illustrates the model's effectiveness.

title: Building Interoperable and Cross-Domain Semantic Web of Things Applications
Abstract: The Web of Things (WoT) is rapidly gaining popularity, attracting the interest of technologists, scientists, industrial players, system integrators, and solution providers. The success of the WoT hinges on its ability to create relatively easy-to-build ecosystems, inheriting this trait from the web and enabling end-to-end solution development. Connecting physical devices like sensors, RFID tags, or any device capable of sending data over the internet using web technologies in the WoT is practically automatic. The shared data within the WoT can be used to develop smarter solutions offering business services in the form of IoT applications. This chapter reviews the major challenges of the WoT, focusing on those that require combining heterogeneous IoT data to design smarter services and applications and benefit from data interoperability. Semantic web technologies help address these challenges by achieving the following objectives: 1) semantically annotating and unifying heterogeneous data, 2) enriching semantic WoT datasets with external knowledge graphs, and 3) providing data analysis through reasoning mechanisms to infer meaningful information. To overcome the challenge of creating interoperable semantics-based IoT applications, the Machine-to-Machine Measurement (M3) semantic engine was designed. M3 semantically annotates WoT data, builds the logic for smarter services, and deduces meaningful knowledge by linking it to external knowledge graphs accessible on the web. M3 assists application and business developers in designing interoperable Semantic Web of Things applications. title: Secure and Reconfigurable Network Design for Critical Information Dissemination in the Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT)

title: When IoT Keeps People in the Loop: A Path Towards a New Global Utility

title: Examples of sharp asymptotic profiles of singular solutions to an elliptic equation with a sign-changing non-linearity
Abstract:
The first two authors [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) {bf 114}(1):1--34, 2017] classified the behavior near zero for all positive solutions of the perturbed elliptic equation with a critical Hardy--Sobolev growth 
  $$-\Delta u=|x|^{-s} u^{2^{\star(s)-1}} -\mu u^q \hbox{ in }B\setminus\{0\},$$
where $B$ denotes the open unit ball centered at $0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq 3$, $s\in (0,2)$, $2^{\star(s)}:=2(n-s)/(n-2)$, $\mu>0$ and $q>1$. For $q\in (1,2^{\star}-1)$ with $2^{\star}=2n/(n-2)$, it was shown in the op. cit. that the positive solutions with a non-removable singularity at $0$ could exhibit up to three different singular profiles, although their existence was left open. In this paper, we settle this question for all three singular profiles in the maximal possible range. As an important novelty for $\mu>0$, we prove that for every $q\in (2^{\star(s)} -1,2^{\star}-1)$ there exist infinitely many positive solutions satisfying $|x|^{s/(q-2^{\star(s)}+1)}u(x)\to \mu^{-1/(q-2^{\star(s)}+1)}$ as $|x|\to 0$, using a dynamical system approach. Moreover, we show that there exists a positive singular solution with $\liminf_{|x|\to 0} |x|^{(n-2)/2} u(x)=0$ and  $\limsup_{|x|\to 0} |x|^{(n-2)/2} u(x)\in (0,\infty)$ if (and only if) $q\in (2^{\star}-2,2^{\star}-1)$.

title: Higgs Pair Production as a Signal of Enhanced Yukawa Couplings

After considering constraints from electroweak precision measurements, Higgs coupling strength measurements, and unitarity and perturbativity bounds, an interesting region of parameter space is identified that leads to enhanced Yukawa couplings as well as enhanced di-Higgs gluon fusion production within the LHC reach. The paper encourages dedicated searches based on differential distributions as a novel way to indirectly probe enhanced Higgs couplings to light fermions.

title: SAFFRON: A Semi-Automated Framework for Software Requirements Prioritization
Abstract: Due to the dynamic nature of current software development methods, changes in requirements are embraced and given due consideration. To address this issue, this paper presents a Semi-Automated Framework for soFtware Requirements priOritizatioN (SAFFRON). SAFFRON predicts appropriate stakeholder ratings for a particular requirement, reducing human interactions. Initially, item-item collaborative filtering is used to estimate the similarity between new and previously elicited requirements. Based on this similarity, stakeholders most likely to rate requirements are identified. Afterward, collaborative filtering based on a latent factor model is used to predict the ratings of those stakeholders. The proposed approach is implemented and tested on the RALIC dataset. The results demonstrate consistent correlation, similar to state-of-the-art approaches, with the ground truth. Abstract: This paper presents a Gaussian noise (GN) model that accurately accounts for an arbitrary frequency-dependent signal power profile along the link. This allows for the evaluation of the impact of inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS) on the optical Kerr nonlinearity. Additionally, the model considers frequency-dependent fiber attenuation and can be applied to transmission systems employing hybrid amplification schemes where distributed Raman amplification is partially applied across the optical spectrum. To include the latter two cases, a set of coupled ordinary differential equations must be numerically solved to obtain the signal power profile, resulting in a semi-analytical model. However, for lumped amplification and negligible variation in fiber attenuation, a less complex and fully analytical model, referred to as the ISRS GN model, is presented. This model is exact to first order for Gaussian modulated signals and extensively validated by numerical split-step simulations. A maximum deviation of 0.1 dB in nonlinear interference power between simulations and the ISRS GN model is observed. The model is applied to a transmission system occupying an optical bandwidth of 10 THz, representing the entire C+L band. title: Quickest drift change detection in Lévy-type force of mortality model

The approach relies on optimal stopping theory and solving a boundary value problem. The paper is supplemented by extensive numerical analysis related to the construction of the Generalized Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. title: On Operator Valued Measures

The paper defines the integrability of a positive quantum random variable with respect to a POVM. Emphasis is placed on the structure of POVMs, and positive operator-valued versions of the Lebesgue decomposition theorem and Johnson's atomic and nonatomic decomposition theorem are developed. Beyond these generalizations, connections are established between absolute continuity and the "cleanness" relation defined on POVMs, as well as to the concept of atomic and nonatomic measures.

title: What drives the Quasar Main Sequence?

This allows for the construction of a quasar main sequence analogous to the stellar property-driven HR diagram (Sulentic et al. 2001). This paper aims to identify the main driver behind EV1 among the fundamental (theoretically motivated) parameters of an active nucleus (Eddington ratio, black hole mass, accretion rate, spin, and viewing angle). Assuming that both H$\beta$ and FeII emission originate from the Broad Line Region represented as a constant density cloud in a plane-parallel geometry, the effect of changing Eddington ratio on the R$_{\mathrm{FeII}}$ - T$_{\mathrm{BBB}}$ trends with varying mean hydrogen densities is examined. title: Pull and Push&Pull in Random Evolving Graphs
Abstract: The Push, Pull, and Push&Pull algorithms are well-studied rumor spreading protocols. In all three, initially, one node of a graph is informed. In the Push setting, each round, every informed node chooses a neighbor uniformly at random and informs it if it is not already informed. In the Pull setting, each round, each uninformed node chooses a neighbor uniformly at random and asks it for the rumor; if the asked neighbor is informed, the asking node is also informed. Push&Pull combines Push and Pull: In each round, each node picks a neighbor uniformly at random. If at least one of them knows the rumor, both know it after the round. Clementi et al. considered Push in scenarios where the underlying graph changes each round. In one setting they investigated, the underlying graph is a newly sampled Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ each round. They show that if $p\geq 1/n$, with probability $1-o(1)$ (as $n\rightarrow \infty$), the number of rounds needed until all nodes are informed is $\mathcal{O}(\ln(n))$. Doerr and Kostrygin introduced a general framework to analyze rumor spreading algorithms; using this framework, for $a>0$ and $p=a/n$, they improved the previous results in the described setting: The expected number of rounds needed by Push was determined to be $\log_{2-e^{-a}}(n)+1/(1-e^{-a})\ln(n)+\mathcal{O}(1)$; large deviation bounds were also obtained. Using their framework, this paper investigates Pull and Push&Pull in that setting: It is proven that the expected number of rounds needed by Pull to inform all nodes is $\log_{2-e^{-a}}(n)+1/a \ln(n)+\mathcal{O}(1)$. Let $\gamma:= 2(1-e^{-a})-(1-e^{-a})^2/a$; the paper proves that the expected number of rounds needed by Push&Pull is $\log_{1+\gamma}(n)+1/a\ln(n)+\mathcal{O}(1)$; as a byproduct, large deviation bounds are also obtained.

title: Symmetric double bubbles in the Grushin plane
Abstract: This paper addresses the double bubble problem for the anisotropic Grushin perimeter $P_\alpha$, $\alpha\geq 0$, and the Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb R^2$, in the case of two equal volumes. It is assumed that the contact interface between the bubbles lies on either the vertical or the horizontal axis. Since no regularity theory is available in this setting, in both cases, the existence of minimizers is first proven via the direct method using symmetrization arguments. Then, the minimizers are characterized in terms of the given area by first variation techniques. Angles at which minimal boundaries intersect satisfy the standard 120-degree rule up to a suitable change of coordinates. While for $\alpha=0$ the Grushin perimeter reduces to the Euclidean one, and both minimizers coincide with the symmetric double bubble found in [Foisy et al., Pacific J. Math. (1993)], for $\alpha=1$ vertical interface minimizers have Grushin perimeter strictly greater than horizontal interface minimizers. As the latter ones are obtained by translating and dilating the Grushin isoperimetric set found in [Monti Morbidelli, J. Geom. Anal. (2004)], it is conjectured that they solve the double bubble problem without any assumptions on the contact interface.

title: Estimation of Gaussian quantum states
Abstract:

This bound determines the ultimate precision with which parameters encoded into quantum states can be estimated. The paper includes expressions for mixed states, for the case when the Williamson decomposition of the covariance matrix is known, expressions in terms of infinite series, and expressions for pure states. It also discusses problematic behavior when some modes are pure and presents a method that allows the use of expressions defined only for mixed states to compute QFIM for states with any number of pure modes.

title: Magnetic Field Inspired Contact Angle Hysteresis Drives Floating Polyolefin Rafts
Abstract: Floating polymer rafts, composed of polyolefin, can be displaced by a steady magnetic field. This phenomenon is attributed to the interplay of gravitational deformation of the water-vapor interface, contact angle hysteresis, and the diamagnetic properties of the supporting liquid.  The magnetic field, approximately 0.06 T, deforms the water-vapor interface, influencing the apparent contact angle at the interface.  This deformation produces a propulsive force, leading to the displacement of the polymer raft.  The velocity of the raft's center of mass was measured.  The effect is linked to the magnetic field's impact on contact angle hysteresis, enabling a change in the apparent interfacial contact angle.  A semi-quantitative model of this process is proposed.

title: Deep Stacked Networks with Residual Polishing for Image Inpainting
Abstract: Deep neural networks have proven effective in image inpainting, even when handling large missing areas. However, many inpainting networks introduce undesirable artifacts and noise into the repaired regions. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework composed of two stacked convolutional neural networks. The first network focuses on the global structure of the damaged image and roughly fills the missing area. Subsequently, the second network refines the repaired image to remove noise introduced by the first network. This framework effectively separates the problem into two distinct optimization tasks, making it adaptable to various inpainting algorithms by modifying the first network. The second stage, aimed at polishing the inpainted images, can be viewed as a denoising problem, enabling the use of a wide range of denoising algorithms. Our findings demonstrate significant improvements in both visual and quantitative evaluations using the proposed framework.

We have investigated the concentration profiles of group-III atoms for various growth parameters using two exchange Kinetic Models. Based on these models, we have identified critical growth temperature and growth rate regions for producing structures exhibiting less than 10% segregation of group-III atoms.

title: PolicySpace: a modeling platform
Abstract: Public Policy involves proposing changes to existing practices, exploring alternatives, and promoting new habits. Citizens and institutions respond to these proposals by accepting, rejecting, or adapting them. This paper introduces PolicySpace, a modeling platform designed to simulate public policies within an empirical, spatially defined environment utilizing data from 46 metropolitan regions in Brazil. We provide a detailed description of the model's foundation, its agents and markets, the tax system, parameterization, and operational procedures. Finally, we validate the model and demonstrate its application in fiscal analysis. Our results highlight the significance of tax transfer rules for improving urban quality of life.

title: Non-invasive biomarkers of fetal brain development reflecting prenatal stress: an integrative multi-scale multi-species perspective on data collection and analysis
Abstract: Prenatal stress (PS) significantly impacts early postnatal behavioral and cognitive development. This phenomenon, known as "fetal programming," is mediated by the effects of prenatal experiences on the developing hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic nervous system (ANS). The HPA axis, a dynamic system regulating homeostasis, particularly the stress response, is highly susceptible to adverse early life experiences. This review examines the evidence for the effects of PS on fetal programming of the HPA axis and the ANS. We propose a multi-scale, multi-species approach for devising preclinical and clinical studies aimed at identifying early, non-invasive biomarkers of these programming effects. This approach would enable the identification of adverse postnatal brain developmental trajectories, a crucial step in developing therapeutic interventions. The multiple scales encompass biomarkers reflecting changes in the brain epigenome, metabolome, microbiome, and ANS activity, measured using advanced non-invasive techniques analyzing fetal heart rate fluctuations. The proposed framework has the potential to reveal mechanistic links between maternal stress during pregnancy and changes across these physiological scales. These biomarkers may serve as early and non-invasive predictors of neurodevelopmental trajectories influenced by PS.  We conclude that studies investigating the effects of PS should be conducted across multiple scales, integrating concerted observations from multiple animal models and human cohorts in an interactive and iterative manner, employing machine learning for data synthesis, identification, and validation of optimal non-invasive biomarkers.

title: Deterministic Computations on a PRAM with Static Processor and Memory Faults
Abstract: We investigate the operation of a Parallel Random Access Machine (PRAM) with faulty processors and memory cells. The faults considered are static, meaning that the operational/faulty status of PRAM components remains unchanged once the machine starts operating.  We develop a deterministic simulation of a fully operational PRAM on a similar faulty machine with constant fractions of faults among processors and memory cells. The simulating PRAM employs n processors and m memory cells, simulating a PRAM with n processors and a constant fraction of m memory cells. The simulation unfolds in two phases: preprocessing followed by step-by-step simulation.  Preprocessing is completed in time O((m/n + log n) log n). The step-by-step simulation component incurs a slowdown of O(log m).

title: Mean-Square Approximation of Iterated Ito and Stratonovich Stochastic Integrals of Multiplicities 1 to 6 from the Taylor-Ito and Taylor-Stratonovich Expansions Using Legendre Polynomials
Abstract: This article delves into the practical aspects of expansions and mean-square approximations of specific iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals of multiplicities 1 to 6. These integrals are based on components of the multidimensional Wiener process and utilize the method of generalized multiple Fourier series. Specifically, we employ multiple Fourier-Legendre series converging in the norm sense of the space L2([t, T]k) (k=1,...,6) for approximating iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals.  The considered iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals form part of stochastic Taylor expansions (Taylor-Ito and Taylor-Stratonovich expansions). Therefore, the results of this article are valuable for constructing high-order strong numerical methods for Ito stochastic differential equations.  Expansions of iterated Ito and Stratonovich stochastic integrals of multiplicities 1 to 6 using Legendre polynomials are derived. The convergence with probability 1 of the mentioned method of generalized multiple Fourier series is proven for iterated Ito stochastic integrals of multiplicities k (k∈ℕ) in cases involving multiple Fourier-Legendre series and multiple trigonometric Fourier series.

title: Vector disformal transformation of cosmological perturbations
Abstract: We examine disformal transformations of cosmological perturbations mediated by vector fields within theories invariant under U(1) gauge transformations.  Three types of vector disformal transformations are considered: (i) transformations by a single timelike vector; (ii) transformations by a single spacelike vector; and (iii) transformations by three spacelike vectors. Our analysis reveals that transformations of type (i) do not affect either curvature perturbation or gravitational waves. Type (ii) transformations do not alter curvature perturbation but influence gravitational waves, while type (iii) transformations modify both curvature perturbation and gravitational waves. Consequently, coupling matter fields to the metric after disformal transformations of type (ii) or (iii) may have observable consequences.  While the recent multi-messenger observation of binary neutron stars has precisely identified a proper disformal frame at the present epoch, the findings of this paper could aid in distinguishing disformal frames in the early universe.

title: Manipulating lightcone fluctuations in an analogue cosmic string
Abstract: We investigate flight time fluctuations in an anisotropic medium inspired by a cosmic string with a fluctuating effective refractive index caused by fluctuating vacuum electric fields. These fluctuations are analogous to lightcone fluctuations arising from fluctuating spacetime metrics when gravity is quantized. This medium can be realized as a metamaterial mimicking a cosmic string through transformation optics. For probe light near the analogous string, the flight time variance is ν times greater than in a normal homogeneous and isotropic medium, where ν is a parameter characterizing the deficit angle of the cosmic string's spacetime. The parameter ν, always greater than unity for a real cosmic string, is determined by the dielectric properties of the metamaterial in the case of an analogous string. Thus, the flight time fluctuations of probe light can be manipulated by altering the electric permittivity and magnetic permeability of the analogous medium. We propose that it is potentially feasible to fabricate a metamaterial mimicking a cosmic string with a large ν in a laboratory setting, enabling the observation of a significant flight time variance.

title: Emotion-Based Crowd Simulation Model Based on Physical Strength Consumption for Emergency Scenarios
Abstract: The modeling and simulation of traffic flow and crowd movement, two phenomena involving interactions between pedestrians and cars in various situations, are gaining increasing attention. Crowd simulation is particularly crucial for understanding mobility and transportation patterns. This paper introduces an emotion-based crowd simulation model incorporating physical strength consumption. Drawing inspiration from the "devoted actor" theory, individual movements in our model are determined by considering the influence of physical strength consumption and panic emotions.  Physical strength consumption is calculated using a physics-based numerical method.  Based on the James-Lange theory, panic levels are estimated using an enhanced emotional contagion model that leverages the inherent relationship between physical strength consumption and panic. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method integrating physical strength consumption into an emotion-based crowd simulation model by exploiting the relationship between physical strength consumption and emotion.  We demonstrate the model's performance on diverse scenarios and compare the resulting behaviors with real-world video sequences. Our approach effectively predicts changes in physical strength consumption and panic levels of individuals in emergency situations.

The complete system admits an SU(2|1) covariant separation into the center-of-mass sector and the quotient. Explicit expressions for the classical and quantum SU(2|1) generators in both sectors and the entire system are derived. We determine the relevant energy spectra, degeneracies, and sets of physical states.

title: A Unified Method for First and Third Person Action Recognition

These images are described using pre-trained networks trained on extensive image datasets. Multi-channel time series are obtained by aligning these descriptions.  The PoT representation method, along with a novel pooling operator, is employed for extracting motion features from these time series, leveraging its advantages. The second stream extracts appearance features, crucial for video classification. title: Fractional Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern for Image Retrieval using Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: This paper introduces a new texture descriptor called "Fractional Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern" (FLNIP) for content-based image retrieval (CBIR). It expands upon the Local Neighborhood Intensity Pattern (LNIP). FLNIP calculates the relative intensity difference between a particular pixel and the center pixel of a 3x3 window by considering the relationship with adjacent neighbors. The fractional change in the local neighborhood, including adjacent neighbors, is initially calculated with respect to one of the eight neighbors of the center pixel of a 3x3 window. Subsequently, the fractional change is calculated with respect to the center pixel itself.  These two fractional change values are then compared to generate a binary bit pattern. Both sign and magnitude information are encoded within a single descriptor, reflecting the relative change in magnitude in the adjacent neighborhood through the comparison of fractional change. The descriptor is applied to four multi-resolution images: the raw image and three filtered Gaussian images obtained by applying Gaussian filters with varying standard deviations to the raw image. This approach highlights the importance of exploring texture information at different resolutions within an image. The four sets of distances obtained between the query and target image are combined using a genetic algorithm-based approach to enhance retrieval performance by minimizing the distance between similar class images.  The method's performance was evaluated on four popular databases for image retrieval. Precision and recall values observed on these databases were compared with recent state-of-the-art local patterns. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvement over many existing methods.

title: Radiation Forces and the Abraham-Minkowski Problem
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable advancements in radiation optics. This mini-review aims to highlight key developments in radiation pressure physics, specifically focusing on the relevance of recent experiments to the classic Abraham-Minkowski problem.  This problem centers on determining the "correct" expression for electromagnetic momentum density in continuous matter.  We observe that authors often overinterpret the significance of their experimental findings in relation to the momentum problem.  Many of these experiments lack the ability to distinguish between Abraham and Minkowski energy-momentum tensors, as they can be readily explained using force expressions common to both frameworks.  Moreover, we emphasize the inherent ambiguity in applying formal conservation principles to the radiation field within a dielectric medium.  This ambiguity arises because the electromagnetic field in matter represents a subsystem that requires supplementation by the mechanical subsystem to form a closed system. Finally, we offer insights into the connection between macroscopic electrodynamics and the Casimir effect, suggesting a limit for the magnitudes of cutoff parameters in quantum field theory related to surface tension in conventional hydromechanics.

title: First-principles study of the effects of electron-phonon coupling on the thermoelectric properties: a case study of SiGe compound
Abstract: The thermoelectric community generally assumes that the lattice thermal conductivity of a material is independent of its electronic properties. However, this assumption is questionable, as electron-phonon coupling can influence both carrier and phonon transport, affecting thermoelectric properties. Using SiGe compound as a model system, we provide an accurate prediction of carrier relaxation time by considering scattering from all phonon modes, contrasting with the simplified deformation potential theory.  Our findings indicate that the carrier relaxation time remains relatively consistent with varying concentration. However, this is not the case for phonon transport, where electron-phonon coupling significantly reduces lattice thermal conductivity at higher carrier concentrations.  Consequently, the figure-of-merit of the SiGe compound is notably enhanced at optimized carrier concentration, particularly at elevated temperatures.

title: Abrupt transitions in collaborative social networks

title: APEx: Accuracy-Aware Differentially Private Data Exploration
Abstract: Organizations are increasingly opening their sensitive datasets for exploration by external data scientists. title: Threat Modeling Data Analysis in Socio-technical Systems
Abstract: Our decision-making processes are becoming increasingly data-driven, relying on data from diverse sources and technologies. title: Demographics and discussion influence views on algorithmic fairness

title: Density-aware Dynamic Mobile Networks: Opportunities and Challenges

title: Secure Network Code for Adaptive and Active Attacks with No-Randomness in Intermediate Nodes

For this class of symbols, pre-learned programs become inoperative, making syntactical programs an unlikely source of experienced qualia. Second, we model the dysfunctional human response to a radically altered environment as the natural response of any learning machine facing novel inputs far outside its previous training set. In such situations, learning machines are unable to extract information from their input and typically enter a dynamical state characterized by null outputs and a lack of response. This state immediately predicts and explains the characteristics of human semantic experiences in similar circumstances. In the third stage, we consider learning machines trained to implement multiple functions in simple sequential programs using environmental data to specify subroutine names, control flow instructions, memory calls, and so on. Drastic changes in any of these environmental inputs can again lead to inoperative programs. By examining changes specific to people or locations, we can model human cognitive symbols featuring these dependencies, such as attachment and grief. This implies that the ordering of entangled states in all finite dimensions may not be preserved under trace-preserving LOCC.

Our results show that increasing the number of interactions in the network tends to suppress average non-Markovianity. This suggests that tree networks optimize this quantity among random networks.

title: The Jets of AGN as giant co-axial cables
