title: Robust Contextual Bandit via the Capped-$\ell_{2}$ norm
Abstract: This paper considers the actor-critic contextual bandit for mobile health (mHealth) interventions. State-of-the-art decision-making methods in mHealth generally assume that the noise in the dynamic system follows a Gaussian distribution. These methods use least-square-based algorithms to estimate the expected reward, which are susceptible to outliers. To address the issue of outliers, this study proposes a novel robust actor-critic contextual bandit method for mHealth interventions. In the critic updating, the capped-$\\ell_{2}$ norm is used to measure the approximation error, which prevents outliers from dominating the objective. A set of weights is achieved from the critic updating, which provides a weighted objective for the actor updating. This gives the badly noised sample in the critic updating with zero weights for the actor updating. As a result, the robustness of both actor-critic updating is enhanced. There is a key parameter in the capped-$\\ell_{2}$ norm. This study provides a reliable method to properly set it using one of the most fundamental definitions of outliers in statistics. Extensive experiment results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve almost identical results compared to state-of-the-art methods on datasets without outliers and dramatically outperforms them on datasets noised by outliers.

title: How 5G (and concomitant technologies) will revolutionize healthcare
Abstract: This paper argues that 5G and concomitant emerging technologies (such as IoT, big data, artificial intelligence, and machine learning) will transform global healthcare systems in the near future. The optimism around 5G-enabled healthcare stems from a confluence of significant technical pushes already at play: apart from the availability of high-throughput low-latency wireless connectivity, other significant factors include the democratization of computing through cloud computing; the democratization of AI and cognitive computing (e.g., IBM Watson); and the commoditization of data through crowdsourcing and digital exhaust. These technologies together can finally crack a dysfunctional healthcare system that has largely been impervious to technological innovations. The study highlights the persistent deficiencies of the current healthcare system and demonstrates how the 5G-enabled healthcare revolution can address these deficiencies. It also highlights open technical research challenges and potential pitfalls that may hinder the development of such a 5G-enabled health revolution.

title: Multi-task Neural Networks for Personalized Pain Recognition from Physiological Signals
Abstract: Pain is a complex and subjective experience that poses several measurement challenges. While self-report by the patient is considered the gold standard of pain assessment, this approach fails when patients cannot verbally communicate pain intensity or lack normal mental abilities. This paper presents a pain intensity measurement method based on physiological signals. Specifically, a multi-task learning approach based on neural networks is implemented that accounts for individual differences in pain responses while still leveraging data from across the population. The method is tested on a dataset containing multi-modal physiological responses to nociceptive pain.

title: Identifying Growth-Patterns in Children by Applying Cluster analysis to Electronic Medical Records
Abstract:
Obesity is a leading health concern in the United States. Researchers and health care providers are interested in understanding factors affecting obesity and detecting the likelihood of obesity as early as possible. This study aims to recognize children at higher risk of obesity by identifying distinct growth patterns in them. This is achieved using clustering methods, which group together children who share similar body measurements over time. The measurements characterizing children within the same cluster are plotted as a function of age. These plots are referred to as growth-pattern curves. The study shows that distinct growth-pattern curves are associated with different clusters and can be used to separate children into the topmost (heaviest), middle, or bottom-most cluster based on early growth measurements.

title: Effects of ultrasound waves intensity on the removal of Congo red color from the textile industry wastewater by Fe3O4@TiO2 core-shell nanospheres
Abstract: Textile industry dyes pollute water, impacting its quality and hindering water treatment efficiency. These dyes pose health risks due to reactions with disinfectants, producing harmful byproducts. Iron oxide nanoparticles are effective for removing pollutants from water. To enhance their stability and dispersion, iron oxide-titanium oxide nanospheres were synthesized via coprecipitation. These nanospheres, ranging from 5 to 10 nm in size, exhibited high purity, as confirmed by TEM and XRD analysis. The absorption rate of Congo red was evaluated under ultrasonic conditions, revealing a direct correlation between ultrasonic power and absorption capacity, reaching 100% at powers exceeding 30 watts.

title: An Exploratory Study of Health Habit Formation Through Gamification
Abstract: Promoting healthy habits is crucial for maintaining and improving health, reducing disease risks, and managing chronic illnesses. Gamification techniques, incorporating elements like badges, leaderboards, and health-related challenges, hold promise in motivating and engaging users in adopting healthier behaviors. This exploratory study investigated the influence of game mechanics and dynamics on habit formation using a mobile application. Results indicate varying levels of user engagement based on the presence of gamification elements, highlighting the value of incorporating game elements into the user experience.

title: Constrained Community Detection in Social Networks
Abstract: Community detection in networks involves identifying densely connected sub-networks, a core aspect of many network analyses. Modularity optimization, maximizing the difference between edges within groups (communities) and expected random distribution, is a common paradigm. While the modularity objective function incorporates network topology, incorporating constraints or external information remains largely unexplored. This study imposes a penalty function on the modularity objective function to regulate community composition. Applying this methodology to a network of hospitals, it identifies health care communities (HCCs) with a minimum threshold of cardiac defibrillator surgeries. This restriction allows meaningful comparisons in cardiac care among HCCs by standardizing cardiac care distribution across the hospital network.

title: Group-driven Reinforcement Learning for Personalized mHealth Intervention
Abstract: The widespread adoption of smartphones and wearable devices makes mobile health (mHealth) technologies promising for improving health outcomes. Current decision-making methods in mHealth rely on assumptions of either complete user homogeneity or heterogeneity. This paper proposes a novel group-driven reinforcement learning (RL) method for mHealth, aiming to share information among similar users to enhance learned RL policies. Users are grouped based on trajectory information similarity using K-means clustering, and a shared RL policy is learned for each group. Extensive experimentation demonstrates that this method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art RL methods in mHealth.

title: Medication non adherence: finding solutions through design thinking approach
Abstract: Medication non-adherence is a major health concern, affecting approximately 50% of patients and leading to complications, mortality, and increased healthcare costs. This problem is particularly acute for chronic illnesses requiring lifelong medication, such as organ transplantation. Non-adherence to immunosuppressant medications is linked to rejection episodes and graft loss in transplant patients. This article explores factors influencing non-compliance in transplant patients, including patient characteristics, illness factors, and therapeutic regimen aspects. Using a user-centered design thinking approach, hypotheses are formulated, and strategies for enhancing adherence through mobile technology and gamification techniques are discussed.

title: Infection-acquired versus vaccine-acquired immunity in an SIRWS model
Abstract: Despite high vaccination coverage, pertussis re-emergence poses a public health concern in many countries. One hypothesis for this re-emergence is waning immunity. This study investigates the interplay between infection and immunity, exploring the impact of differing durations of infection-acquired and vaccine-acquired immunity on disease patterns and prevalence. The model demonstrates that vaccination can induce cyclic behavior, and its effectiveness in reducing infection prevalence increases with both the durations of infection-acquired and vaccine-acquired immunity. Increasing vaccination coverage, while potentially increasing overall transmission, consistently reduces the prevalence of primary infections, leading to longer interepidemic periods and higher peak infection rates. These findings highlight the importance of understanding the duration of protection and its influence by infection prevalence in optimizing vaccination strategies.

title: DM-PhyClus: A Bayesian phylogenetic algorithm for infectious disease transmission cluster inference
Abstract: Traditional phylogenetic clustering methods rely on arbitrary cutpoints applied to phylogenetic estimates. While Bayesian and bootstrap-based approaches often lead to similar estimates, they may produce conflicting confidence measures for clusters. This study introduces a new Bayesian phylogenetic clustering algorithm, DM-PhyClus, which identifies sets of sequences resulting from rapid transmission chains, providing easily interpretable clusters without relying on ad hoc distance or confidence requirements. Simulations demonstrate that DM-PhyClus outperforms conventional clustering methods and the Gap procedure in cluster recovery. Applying DM-PhyClus to HIV-1 sequences, the resulting clusters align with previous analysis conclusions. By eliminating the need for cutpoints and producing sensible cluster configurations, DM-PhyClus facilitates transmission cluster detection, enhancing public health strategies to combat infectious diseases like HIV-1.

title: TensorFlow Estimators: Managing Simplicity vs. Flexibility in High-Level Machine Learning Frameworks
Abstract: This paper introduces a framework for specifying, training, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models, aiming to simplify cutting-edge machine learning for practitioners and facilitate its implementation in production environments. Recognizing the rapid evolution of deep learning, the framework focuses on user-defined model code with abstractions guiding the development of production-ready models. A unifying Estimator interface enables the development of downstream infrastructure, like distributed training and hyperparameter tuning, independent of the model implementation. Balancing flexibility and simplicity, the framework offers APIs at different abstraction levels, providing readily available common model architectures and utilities for faster experimentation. To enhance flexibility and usability across diverse problems, these canned Estimators are parameterized using feature columns, a declarative specification for interpreting input data. The paper discusses the framework's impact on code health, maintainability, and development speed based on real-world research and production experiences.

title: Evidence from web-based dietary search patterns to the role of B12 deficiency in chronic pain

title: LIKWID Monitoring Stack: A flexible framework enabling job specific performance monitoring for the masses

title: Hashtag Healthcare: From Tweets to Mental Health Journals Using Deep Transfer Learning

title: A glass-box interactive machine learning approach for solving NP-hard problems with the human-in-the-loop

While big data benefits aML, health informatics often faces limited datasets, where aML struggles due to insufficient training samples and computational complexity. title: Retrofitting Distributional Embeddings to Knowledge Graphs with Functional Relations

Functional Retrofitting, a framework presented in this paper, overcomes these limitations by explicitly modeling pairwise relations. This framework incorporates various pairwise penalty functions previously developed for knowledge graph completion, allowing for encoding, learning, and extracting information about relation semantics. Linear and neural instantiations of the framework are presented. Functional Retrofitting significantly outperforms existing retrofitting methods on complex knowledge graphs while maintaining accuracy on simpler graphs. The framework's utility is demonstrated by predicting new drug-disease treatment pairs in a large, complex health knowledge graph.

title: Automatic Crack Detection in Built Infrastructure Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

title: Hitomi X-ray studies of Giant Radio Pulses from the Crab pulsar
Abstract: To search for giant X-ray pulses correlated with giant radio pulses (GRPs) from the Crab pulsar, a simultaneous observation was conducted using the X-ray satellite Hitomi (2-300 keV band) and the Kashima NICT radio observatory (1.4-1.7 GHz band). The timing performance of Hitomi met the requirements, and approximately 1,000 and 100 GRPs were observed at the main and inter-pulse phases, respectively. No apparent correlation was found between giant radio pulses and X-ray emission at either phase. Variations were within the 2-sigma fluctuations of X-ray fluxes at pulse peaks, with 3-sigma upper limits of main- or inter-pulse GRPs variations being 22% or 80% of peak flux in a 0.20 phase width. These values increased to 25% or 110% when the phase width was restricted to 0.03. Upper limits from Hitomi, particularly in the 4.5-10 keV and 70-300 keV bands, were obtained for the first time, consistent with previous reports. The upper limits of main- and inter-pulse GRPs in the 0.20 phase width were approximately 2.4 and 9.3 × 10^{-11} erg cm^{-2}. No significant variability in pulse profiles suggests that GRPs originated from a localized area within the magnetosphere, and the number of photon-emitting particles temporarily increased. However, the results do not statistically rule out variations correlated with GRPs, as potential X-ray enhancement could occur due to a >0.02% brightening of the pulse-peak flux under such conditions.

title: A signature-based machine learning model for bipolar disorder and borderline personality disorder

title: Criticality in the brain: A synthesis of neurobiology, models and cognition

title: Autoencoder-augmented Neuroevolution for Visual Doom Playing

title: Catching Zika Fever: Application of Crowdsourcing and Machine Learning for Tracking Health Misinformation on Twitter

title: Modification of Symmetric Cryptography with Combining Affine Chiper and Caesar Chiper which Dynamic Nature in Matrix of Chiper Transposition by Applying Flow Pattern in the Planting Rice
Abstract: Classical cryptography, a method of disguising information before the advent of computers, relies on encoding to protect data. This paper describes a modification of classical algorithms to enhance the difficulty of cryptanalysis and protect undisclosed messages. The approach combines three types of classical algorithms: affine cipher, Caesar cipher, and transposition cipher. The affine cipher and Caesar cipher are made dynamic by looping them as many times as the initial key, enabling variations based on key value. The results of the affine and Caesar ciphers are then combined within the transposition cipher matrix, utilizing a pattern inspired by rice cultivation paths. Ciphertext retrieval employs the reverse pattern of rice planting paths. Finally, the resulting digits are converted into binary digits, scrambling 5 characters into 80-digit bits. This intricate process significantly hinders cryptanalysis and increases the time required to decrypt the information.

title: Proactive Defense Against Physical Denial of Service Attacks using Poisson Signaling Games

This makes them susceptible to "physical" denial-of-service attacks (PDoS), where IoT devices overload the "physical bandwidth" of a CPS. This paper quantifies the population-based risk to a group of IoT devices targeted by malware for a PDoS attack. We develop a "Poisson signaling game," a signaling game with an unknown number of receivers with varying abilities to detect deception, to model bot recruitment. Using a version of this game, we analyze two mechanisms (legal and economic) to deter botnet recruitment. Equilibrium results indicate that defenders can limit botnet activity. Legislating minimum security levels has a limited effect, while incentivizing active defense can significantly reduce botnet activity. This work provides a quantitative foundation for proactive PDoS defense.

title: Spectral analysis of the blood flow in the foot microvascular bed during thermal testing in patients with diabetes mellitus

title: A Robust Interrupted Time Series Model for Analyzing Complex Healthcare Intervention Data
Abstract: Current health policy emphasizes the use of evidence-based care delivery services to improve patient quality and safety outcomes. Interrupted time series (ITS) is a robust quasi-experimental design that can infer the effectiveness of an intervention while accounting for data dependency. Existing standardized ITS analysis methods fail to model changes in variation and correlation following the intervention, a key limitation as variability and dependency can be influenced by the intervention. Additionally, current methodology assumes a pre-specified interruption time point with an instantaneous effect or removes data for which the intervention's effect is not fully realized. This paper introduces a novel "Robust-ITS" model that addresses these limitations. The Robust-ITS model performs formal inference on (a) identifying the change point, (b) differences in pre- and post-intervention correlation, (c) differences in outcome variance pre- and post-intervention, and (d) differences in the mean pre- and post-intervention. We illustrate the proposed method by analyzing patient satisfaction data from a hospital that implemented a new nursing care delivery model. title: Stein-like Estimators for Causal Mediation Analysis in Randomized Trials
Abstract: Causal mediation analysis aims to estimate the natural direct and indirect effects of treatments under specific assumptions. Traditional mediation analysis using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) relies on the absence of unmeasured causes of the mediator and outcome. When this assumption cannot be justified, Instrumental Variables (IV) estimators can be used to produce an asymptotically unbiased estimator of the mediator-outcome link. However, even with valid instruments, bias removal comes at the cost of variance inflation for standard IV procedures like Two-Stage Least Squares (TSLS). A Semi-Parametric Stein-Like (SPSL) estimator has been proposed, offering a balance between the unbiasedness of TSLS and the relatively small variance of OLS. Additionally, the SPSL's shrinkage parameter can be directly estimated from the data. This paper demonstrates how this Stein-like estimator can be implemented in the context of estimating natural direct and natural indirect effects of treatments in randomized controlled trials. The performance of competing methods is studied through a simulation study, varying both the strength of hidden confounding and the strength of the instruments. Abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the complex chemical cross-talk between microbes and the host is essential for elucidating the role of the gut microbiota in health and disease.  This study presents NJS16, a literature-curated interspecies network of the human gut microbiota, encompassing 570 microbial species, 3 human cell types, and over 4,400 small-molecule transport and macromolecule degradation events.  A mathematical approach is developed to elucidate representative microbial and metabolic features of the gut microbial community in a given population.  Applying this strategy to microbiome data from type 2 diabetes patients reveals a context-specific infrastructure of the gut microbial ecosystem, key microbial entities with substantial metabolic influence, and frequently-produced metabolic compounds indicative of relevant community metabolic processes.  NJS16 provides a foundation for integrative investigations of microbial activities at the community level within the human gut.

title: A Field Study of On-Calendar Visualizations
Abstract: Feedback tools enable individuals to monitor personal data, such as pedometer counts, blood pressure readings, or electricity consumption, to improve health, sustainability practices, or well-being.  However, deriving meaningful insights from these data can be challenging.  This research integrates quantitative feedback data within a personal digital calendar, aiming to make the data more accessible and comprehensible.  An eight-week field study of an on-calendar visualization tool demonstrates that a personal calendar can provide rich context for reasoning about feedback data, enabling the identification and analysis of patterns and anomalies.  A model of the behavior feedback process is derived, extending existing technology adoption models, and potential barriers to ongoing use of feedback tools are discussed.

title: Estimating the prevalence of infectious diseases from under-reported age-dependent compulsorily notification databases
Abstract: Reporting of notifiable diseases to public health authorities is often incomplete, with reported fractions ranging from 9% to 99%, primarily due to factors like unrecognized disease or failures in reporting processes.  This study proposes a method to estimate the full prevalence of infectious diseases, accounting for incomplete notification of incidence and allowing for the estimation of non-notified infections.  The method is illustrated using the case of hepatitis C in Brazil.  Application of the model to hepatitis C data in Brazil resulted in estimates for notified cases, non-notified cases, and total prevalence of infections.  The proposed model is considered useful for estimating the true magnitude of endemic states of infectious diseases, particularly for underreported conditions, and can be extended to other areas such as underreported crime incidence.

title: A context-aware e-bike system to reduce pollution inhalation while cycling

title: Beyond Volume: The Impact of Complex Healthcare Data on the Machine Learning Pipeline
Abstract: Healthcare has transitioned from a paper-based paradigm to a digital age characterized by an abundance of data from electronic health records, digitized imaging, and public health datasets. However, deriving accurate and informative insights requires a deep understanding of the data beyond simply executing machine learning models.  This chapter highlights the complexities of healthcare data, focusing on challenges encountered throughout the machine learning pipeline.  The discussion covers data preprocessing, model building, and model output interpretation, addressing data attributes unique to the healthcare domain and their implications for the efficiency of machine learning techniques.

title: Feature Extraction for Machine Learning Based Crackle Detection in Lung Sounds from a Health Survey
Abstract: While innovative solutions for recording and viewing sounds from a stethoscope have become readily available, the need for automated detection of abnormal lung sounds remains.  Current methods often rely on small, non-diverse datasets, limiting their accuracy.  This research proposes a machine learning approach for detecting crackles in lung sounds recorded using a stethoscope in a large health survey.  The method is trained and evaluated using a dataset of 209 files with crackles classified by expert listeners.  The analysis pipeline utilizes features extracted from small windows in audio files, and various feature extraction methods and classifiers are evaluated.  The approach achieves a precision of 86% and recall of 84% for classifying crackles in audio windows, exceeding the accuracy of health personnel.  The low-dimensional feature vector makes the SVM classifier fast and efficient, allowing for rapid training and classification.  The model can be utilized to train health personnel or integrated into smartphone applications for Bluetooth stethoscopes.

title: Bayesian multi-parameter evidence synthesis to inform decision-making: a case study in hormone-refractory metastatic prostate cancer
Abstract: Health technology assessments rely on complex cost-effectiveness models requiring numerous input parameters.  When relevant estimates are unavailable, model simplification may be necessary.  Multi-parameter evidence synthesis allows for the combination of data from diverse sources, providing estimates essential for clinical decision-making.  This study demonstrates the use of bivariate meta-analysis (BVMA) to predict unreported estimates of treatment effects, enabling the implementation of multi-state Markov models that would otherwise require simplification.  The example of docetaxel in metastatic hormone-refractory prostate cancer illustrates how BVMA can be used to predict the effect on progression-free survival (PFS), facilitating the use of a three-state Markov model.  The comparison of the two-state and three-state models reveals a significant difference in incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, highlighting the value of the three-state model in distinguishing patients who progressed from those who did not.  This study emphasizes the importance of advanced meta-analytic techniques in obtaining relevant parameter estimates for accurate modeling of natural history and preventing valuable clinical data from being discarded.

title: Investigations of Auditory Filters Based Excitation Patterns for Assessment of Noise Induced Hearing Loss
Abstract: Noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL), a major preventable occupational health issue, has been extensively studied.  The excitation pattern (EP) is used to estimate movements of the basilar membrane (BM) in the cochlea, providing insights into NIHL.  This study employs two auditory filters, DRNL and ROEX, to create two EPs: the velocity EP and the loudness EP.  Two noise hazard metrics based on these EPs are proposed to assess hazardous levels caused by different noise types.  Simulations using Gaussian noise and pure-tone noise evaluate the performance of the developed EPs and noise metrics.  The results indicate that both EPs reflect BM responses to various noise types, highlighting their potential application in NIHL assessment. |||

title: Fast and Accurate Likelihood Ratio Based Biometric Comparison in the Encrypted Domain
Abstract: Biometric verification is increasingly vulnerable to privacy breaches as it can reveal sensitive information like gender, ethnicity, and health conditions. This paper proposes a new secure biometric verification approach that balances efficiency and accuracy while ensuring security against adversaries. The system uses elliptic curve-based homomorphic ElGamal encryption for efficient verification in the encrypted domain and a log-likelihood ratio classifier for accurate classification. A two-party secure protocol ensures that no private information is disclosed during the verification process. Initial tests demonstrate high accuracy within milliseconds.

title: Targeted Learning with Daily EHR Data
Abstract: Electronic health records (EHR) offer a cost-effective means to conduct cohort studies on the effects of multiple time-point interventions. However, analyzing EHR data at granular levels poses computational challenges. Current guidelines recommend using small intervals, but their practical impact remains unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by developing a scalable targeted learning approach that allows for analyzing large-scale EHR data at daily intervals. Specifically, the study maps daily EHR data into four datasets using different time intervals (90, 30, 15, and 5 days) and applies a longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) approach to estimate the effects of dynamic treatment rules. To overcome computational challenges, a novel "long-format TMLE" implementation is proposed, leveraging machine learning software like xgboost and h2o for efficient nuisance parameter estimation.

title: Learning Bundled Care Opportunities from Electronic Medical Records
Abstract: The fee-for-service healthcare model encourages independent management of patient conditions, leading to negative consequences. This study proposes a data-driven framework to infer clusters of health conditions based on shared clinical workflows in an electronic medical record (EMR) system. Using data from a large medical center, the framework identified four condition clusters: fetal abnormalities, late pregnancies, prostate problems, and chronic diseases. These clusters were validated as plausible for bundled care by healthcare experts. The study suggests that EMR data can be used to identify potential areas for bundled care, requiring further refinement and evaluation.

title: A Data-Driven Analysis of the Influence of Care Coordination on Trauma Outcome
Abstract: This study investigated the relationship between care coordination patterns and length of stay (LOS) for trauma patients. A spectral co-clustering methodology was applied to identify patient groups and their corresponding care coordination patterns, represented as interaction networks among healthcare professionals. Three distinct care coordination patterns were identified, each associated with a specific patient group. The group with the shortest LOS exhibited a care coordination pattern involving fewer operational areas but with a higher density of collaborations. The other two groups, with longer LOS, had larger networks with fewer collaborations. The findings suggest that specific care coordination patterns are associated with different LOS durations, highlighting the importance of understanding and optimizing care coordination for improved patient outcomes.

title: When Will AI Exceed Human Performance? Evidence from AI Experts

The survey also reveals a 50% likelihood of AI surpassing human capabilities in all tasks within 45 years and automating all human jobs within 120 years. Asian respondents anticipate these milestones occurring earlier than North Americans. These findings provide valuable insights for researchers and policymakers to anticipate and manage the transformative impact of AI.

title: Improving institutional memory on challenges and methods for estimation of pig herd antimicrobial exposure based on data from the Danish Veterinary Medicines Statistics Program (VetStat)

The selection of challenges and solutions was based on consensus among researchers working with VetStat data. While quantitative data quality evaluations were not performed, the paper clarifies how VetStat data can be used to estimate antimicrobial exposure at the herd level by suggesting uniform methods for data extraction and editing, ensuring reliable and comparable estimates for research purposes.

title: Patchnet: Interpretable Neural Networks for Image Classification
Abstract: Understanding how complex machine learning models make classification decisions is crucial for their acceptance in sensitive domains like healthcare. The paper mathematically analyzes this trade-off, demonstrating PatchNet's ability to generate sharp visual heatmap representations of learned features. PatchNet is applied to the classification of benign/malignant skin lesions from the ISBI-ISIC 2017 melanoma classification challenge, and its features are quantitatively compared with those selected by domain experts.

title: The pulse of the city through Twitter: relationships between land use and spatiotemporal demographics
Abstract: Social network data offer insights into urban dynamics. This study utilizes Twitter data to analyze city activity patterns throughout the day. Users were grouped by city zone and time slot to understand the daily dynamics and its relationship with land use. The study compared daytime and nighttime activity in each zone to identify zones with increased activity during specific time slots. Typical Twitter activity profiles were generated based on predominant land use, revealing how land uses linked to activities are activated at different rates. A multiple regression analysis determined the influence of land uses on different time slots (morning, afternoon, evening, and night) through their changing coefficients. The findings show that activity tends to decrease throughout the day for most land uses but remains constant in parks and increases in retail and residential zones. These results highlight the value of social network data for understanding the link between land use and urban dynamics.

The framework obtains estimates of current incidence from online data and incorporates them into traditional epidemiological models, improving prediction accuracy. The study demonstrates that the proposed framework outperforms alternative approaches, particularly for delays of four weeks or more.

title: Accretion Dynamics on Wet Granular Materials
Abstract: Wet granular aggregates are commonly used in construction materials, food, and healthcare products. The physical mechanisms governing the mixing of dry grains with a wet substrate remain poorly understood and difficult to control. This paper experimentally investigates the accretion of dry grains on a wet granular substrate by measuring the growth dynamics of the wet aggregate. The study shows that the aggregate is fully saturated and its cohesion is ensured by capillary depression at the air-liquid interface. The growth dynamics exhibit two regimes: a viscous regime where growth is limited by capillary-driven liquid flow and a capture regime where capture probability depends on liquid availability at the saturated interface. A model that rationalizes the observations and captures both dynamics is proposed, based on the evolution of capture probability with hydrostatic depression.

title: Individualized Risk Prognosis for Critical Care Patients: A Multi-task Gaussian Process Model
Abstract: This paper presents a novel, data-driven real-time risk score for assessing the clinical acuity of ward patients based on temporal lab tests and vital signs, facilitating timely intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. The proposed score is individualized, clustering patients based on static covariates into subcohorts and learning a separate temporal, non-stationary multi-task Gaussian Process (GP) model for each subcohort. Experiments on a heterogeneous cohort of 6,094 patients demonstrate that the risk score significantly outperforms existing technologies, such as the Rothman index and MEWS, in terms of timeliness, true positive rate (TPR), and positive predictive value (PPV). The score increases the area under the curve (AUC) by 20% and 38% compared to Rothman index and MEWS, respectively, and can predict ICU admissions up to 8 hours before clinicians with a PPV of 35% and a TPR of 50%. The score also enables efficient discharge decisions for stable patients, optimizing hospital resource utilization.

title: Cybernetic Health
Abstract: Future health ecosystems require integrating emerging data technology with a focus on preventive medicine. Cybernetics offers a framework for harnessing the full potential of data to address the spectrum of healthcare needs, from acute to chronic conditions. Actionable cybernetic navigation tools can empower optimal health decisions by quantifying lifestyle and environmental data. This data-to-decisions transformation leverages intuitive event analysis to provide semantic abstraction of dynamic living systems. Preventive health systems within the cybernetic model rely on a flow of components: personalized models predict health status using continuous sensing and data streams, tailored recommendations are generated based on predictions, and persuasive technology facilitates targeted interventions to enact these recommendations.

title: Balanced Policy Evaluation and Learning
Abstract: Evaluating and learning personalized decision policies from observational data is challenging, particularly when only the outcome of the enacted decision is available and the historical policy is unknown. Existing approaches using inverse propensity weighting often reject data points with decisions inconsistent with the new policy, leading to high variance estimates and ineffective learning. This paper proposes a new, balance-based approach that optimizes weights to align weighted data with the target policy, minimizing worst-case or posterior conditional mean square error. The policy learner is formulated as a two-level optimization problem over policies and weights. The study demonstrates that this approach significantly outperforms existing methods in evaluation and learning, supported by extensive theoretical consistency guarantees and regret bounds.

title: BAMHealthCloud: A Biometric Authentication and Data Management System for Healthcare Data in Cloud
Abstract: Advancements in healthcare technology and population growth have increased security threats to sensitive patient data. The healthcare data management system, consisting of diverse data formats, presents challenges for managing big and unstructured data. A cloud-based healthcare management system can offer an effective solution, but security remains a major concern. Biometric authentication emerges as a suitable security mechanism, overcoming limitations of traditional token-based methods. This paper introduces BAMHealthCloud, a cloud-based healthcare data management system incorporating biometric authentication for enhanced data security. The system was developed after a detailed case study of the healthcare sector in a developing country. Signature samples for authentication were trained using Resilient Backpropagation neural networks on a Hadoop MapReduce framework. Rigorous experiments demonstrate significant performance improvements, achieving a 9x speedup, an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 0.12, a sensitivity of 0.98, and a specificity of 0.95 compared to existing approaches.

title: I Probe, Therefore I Am: Designing a Virtual Journalist with Human Emotions

The aim is to demonstrate the feasibility of creating a humanoid conversational agent capable of engaging in natural interactions with users. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations showed the technical feasibility of the system but revealed limitations in its ability to engage users in a natural and emotionally engaging manner. The paper argues that naturalness should not always be the primary goal and suggests that deliberately suppressing naturalness in virtual human interactions can yield more desirable results.

title: Visualizing reacting single atoms in chemical reactions, advancing the frontiers of materials research
Abstract: Heterogeneous gas and solid catalyst reactions occur at the atomic level. Understanding and controlling these reactions is crucial for developing improved processes and materials. This instrument combines controlled operating temperatures and a continuous gas environment with full AC STEM capabilities, enabling real-time in-situ analysis and visualization of single atoms and clusters in nanoparticle catalysis. ESTEM imaging and analysis in controlled gas and temperature environments provide unique insights into catalytic reaction pathways, potentially involving metastable intermediate states. This approach offers benefits including new knowledge and more environmentally friendly technologies for healthcare, renewable energy, and chemical and energy industries.

title: Learning from Clinical Judgments: Semi-Markov-Modulated Marked Hawkes Processes for Risk Prognosis
Abstract: Critically ill patients in regular wards are vulnerable to unanticipated adverse events requiring urgent transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU). This paper proposes a novel continuous-time probabilistic model for analyzing the temporal sequence of physiological data from monitored patients. The model captures "informatively sampled" episodes, representing clinicians' decisions on when to observe a patient's vital signs and lab tests, using a marked Hawkes process modulated by latent clinical states. Observable physiological data is modeled as a switching multi-task Gaussian process. The model also incorporates "informatively censored" episodes by representing latent clinical states as an absorbing semi-Markov jump process. Model parameters are learned from offline patient episodes in electronic health records using an EM-based algorithm. Experiments on a cohort of patients demonstrate that risk prognosis based on this model significantly outperforms existing medical risk scores and machine learning algorithms.

title: Adapting a General Purpose Social Robot for Paediatric Rehabilitation through In-situ Design

The process is explored through the development of the humanoid social robot NAO as a rehabilitation aid for children with cerebral palsy. The paper presents and evaluates the design process, achieved outcomes, and preliminary results from clinical testing. The In-situ design methodology is crucial for the rapid and successful deployment of SARs in clinical settings.

title: An Open-Data Analysis of Heterogeneities in Lung Cancer Premature Mortality Rate and Associated Factors among Toronto Neighborhoods

Neighborhoods were clustered into three classes to assess the influence of heterogeneity. The study found that in the most severe class, two additional factors related to dwellings were involved, increasing the observation's deviance from 48.1% to 80%. The identified factors can assist governments in improving public health policies.

title: Discovery and visualization of structural biomarkers from MRI using transport-based morphometry
Abstract: Brain diseases are often associated with subtle, diffuse, or complex tissue changes that may be difficult to detect, even with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Current computer-assisted approaches rely on pre-specified features, limiting their ability to capture a wide range of physical changes. This paper presents transport-based morphometry (TBM), a technique for automated pattern analysis that determines the relationship between brain structure and observable phenotypes without requiring a priori features. TBM is an image transformation that maps brain images losslessly to a domain where they become more separable. The technique is validated on structural brain images of healthy older adults, demonstrating its ability to discover characteristic changes of aging and highlight potential mechanisms by which aerobic fitness may mediate brain health. TBM is a generative approach that can visualize physically meaningful shifts in tissue distribution through inverse transformation. The proposed framework is a powerful tool for elucidating genotype-structural-behavioral associations in various diseases. |||

title: Wearable Health Monitoring Using Capacitive Voltage-Mode Human Body Communication
Abstract: The rapid miniaturization and cost reduction of computing devices, coupled with the availability of wearable and implantable sensors, has led to the development of human Body Area Networks (BANs). These networks, comprised of interconnected sensors and computing devices, hold significant promise for wearable health monitoring applications. The collected data from these sensors can be transmitted and analyzed to assess a person's health. Traditionally, devices within a BAN are connected wirelessly (WBAN), which suffers from energy inefficiency due to the high-energy consumption of wireless transmission. Human Body Communication (HBC) offers a more energy-efficient alternative, utilizing the human body as the communication medium. This approach promises orders of magnitude better energy efficiency and built-in security compared to WBAN. This paper demonstrates a health monitoring device and system constructed using Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) sensors and components, capable of collecting data from physiological sensors and transmitting it through intra-body HBC to a hub device worn on the body or via HBC-based human-machine interaction to an HBC-capable machine. The system design constraints and signal transfer characteristics for the implemented HBC-based wearable health monitoring system have been measured and analyzed, revealing reliable connectivity with over 8x power savings compared to Bluetooth low energy (BTLE).

title: ShortFuse: Biomedical Time Series Representations in the Presence of Structured Information
Abstract: In healthcare applications, temporal variables encoding movement, health status, and longitudinal patient evolution are often accompanied by rich structured information such as demographics, diagnostics, and medical exam data. However, current methods do not jointly optimize over structured covariates and time series in the feature extraction process. This paper introduces ShortFuse, a method that enhances the accuracy of deep learning models for time series by explicitly modeling temporal interactions and dependencies with structured covariates. ShortFuse introduces hybrid convolutional and LSTM cells that incorporate covariates via weights shared across the temporal domain. ShortFuse outperforms competing models by 3% on two biomedical applications, forecasting osteoarthritis-related cartilage degeneration and predicting surgical outcomes for cerebral palsy patients, matching or exceeding the accuracy of models that utilize features engineered by domain experts.

title: PerfWeb: How to Violate Web Privacy with Hardware Performance Events
Abstract: Browser history reveals highly sensitive information about users, such as financial status, health conditions, or political views. Private browsing modes and anonymity networks are essential tools for preserving the privacy of regular users, particularly whistleblowers and dissidents. This study demonstrates how a malicious application can infer opened websites from Google Chrome in Incognito mode and from Tor Browser by exploiting hardware performance events (HPEs). The analysis utilizes advanced Machine Learning techniques, including k-th Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, and Convolutional Neural Networks, to examine the browsers' microarchitectural footprint. The study profiled 40 different websites, including 30 of the top Alexa sites and 10 whistleblowing portals, on two machines featuring Intel and ARM processors. By monitoring retired instructions, cache accesses, and bus cycles for at most 5 seconds, the researchers managed to classify the selected websites with a success rate of up to 86.3%. The findings suggest that hardware performance events can compromise the privacy of web users. Mitigation strategies that impede these attacks while permitting legitimate use of HPEs are proposed.

title: Using Facebook Ads Audiences for Global Lifestyle Disease Surveillance: Promises and Limitations
Abstract: Millions of users reveal their interests on Facebook daily, which are then monetized through targeted advertisement marketing campaigns. Despite its potential, the study found that, for modeling prevalence of health conditions across countries, differences in interest audiences are only weakly indicative of corresponding prevalence rates. However, within countries, the approach provides insights into trends of health awareness across demographic groups. Finally, the study provides a temporal error analysis to expose the potential pitfalls of using Facebook's Marketing API as a black box.

title: HuGaDB: Human Gait Database for Activity Recognition from Wearable Inertial Sensor Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a human gait data collection for analysis and activity recognition, consisting of continuous recordings of combined activities, including walking, running, taking stairs up and down, sitting down, and so on. Additionally, two electromyography sensors were used on the quadriceps (front thigh) to measure muscle activity. This database can be used for activity recognition, studying how activities are performed, and analyzing how the parts of the legs move relative to each other. Therefore, the data can be used for healthcare-related studies, such as walking rehabilitation or Parkinson's disease recognition; in virtual reality and gaming for simulating humanoid motion; or for humanoid robotics to model humanoid walking. This dataset is the first of its kind to provide detailed data about human gait. The database is available free of charge at https://github.com/romanchereshnev/HuGaDB.

title: Optimal stopping and a non-zero-sum Dynkin game in discrete time with risk measures induced by BSDEs

The agents' payoffs are assessed by g-expectations, potentially with different drivers for each player. Using results from the first part combined with ideas from S. Hamadène and J. Zhang, a Nash equilibrium point of this game is constructed through a recursive procedure. The findings are applicable to a standard Lipschitz driver g without any additional assumptions, except for those ensuring the monotonicity of the corresponding g-expectation.

title: Skin lesion detection based on an ensemble of deep convolutional neural network
Abstract: Skin cancer is a significant public health problem, with over 5 million newly diagnosed cases in the United States annually. To achieve the highest classification accuracy, the outputs of the softmax layers of four different neural architectures are fused. For aggregation, the individual accuracies of the networks are weighted by the confidence values provided by their final softmax layers. title: A generalized approach to model the spectra and radiation dose rate of solar particle events on the surface of Mars
Abstract: Future human missions to Mars necessitate the study of the surface radiation environment during extreme and elevated conditions. Long-term exposure to Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs), modulated by solar activity, contributes significantly to radiation on the Martian surface. Intense solar energetic particle (SEP) events, however, can induce acute health effects. These events can significantly enhance radiation levels and should be detected promptly to prevent severe damage to humans and equipment. The energetic particle environment on the Martian surface differs significantly from that in deep space due to the influence of the Martian atmosphere. Depending on the intensity and shape of the original solar particle spectra and particle types, the surface spectra can induce entirely different radiation effects. To provide immediate and accurate alerts while avoiding unnecessary ones, it is crucial to model and understand the atmospheric effect on incoming SEPs, including both protons and helium ions. This paper presents a generalized approach to quickly model the surface response of any given incoming proton/helium ion spectra, applying it to a set of historical large solar events. The findings provide insights into the variety of surface radiation environments that may arise during SEP events. Based on the statistical study of over 30 significant solar events, an empirical model is developed for estimating the surface dose rate directly from the intensities of a power-law SEP spectra.

title: Measuring Social Media Activity of Scientific Literature: An Exhaustive Comparison of Scopus and Novel Altmetrics Big Data
Abstract: This paper analyzes social media activity across 15 broad scientific disciplines indexed in the Scopus database, using Altmetric.com data. The study investigates the presence of Altmetric.com data in the Scopus database, both overall and across disciplines. The correlation between bibliometric and altmetric indices is examined using Spearman correlation. A zero-truncated negative binomial model is employed to determine the association of various factors with increasing or decreasing citations. Finally, the effectiveness of altmetric indices in identifying publications with high citation impact is evaluated using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) - a receiver operating characteristic application. The findings indicate a rapid increase in the presence of Altmetric.com data in the Scopus database, rising from 10.19% in 2011 to 20.46% in 2015. A zero-truncated negative binomial model was implemented to measure the contribution of different bibliometric and altmetric factors to citation counts. Blog count emerged as the most significant factor, increasing the number of citations by 38.6% in the field of Health Professions and Nursing, followed by Twitter count, increasing citations by 8% in the field of Physics and Astronomy. Interestingly, both Blog count and Twitter count consistently showed a positive increase in the number of citations across all fields. While a weak positive correlation existed between bibliometric and altmetric indices, the results demonstrate that altmetric indices can effectively discriminate highly cited publications, with an encouraging AUC= 0.725 between highly cited publications and total altmetric count. Overall, the findings suggest that altmetrics can better distinguish highly cited publications.

title: Detecting Gamification in Breast Cancer Apps: an automatic methodology for screening purposes

title: Connected Health in Multiple Sclerosis: a mobile applications review

title: Machine Learning with World Knowledge: The Position and Survey
Abstract: Machine learning has become pervasive in various domains, impacting applications such as knowledge discovery and data mining, natural language processing, information retrieval, computer vision, social and health informatics, and ubiquitous computing. Two crucial problems in machine learning are feature generation and label acquisition for machine learning. Labeling large amounts of data for each domain-specific problem can be time-consuming and expensive, posing a significant obstacle to realistic learning protocols in applications. This paper discusses how to leverage existing general-purpose world knowledge to enhance machine learning processes, enriching features or reducing labeling efforts. The comparison of world knowledge with domain-specific knowledge is presented, followed by an introduction of three key problems in utilizing world knowledge in learning processes: explicit and implicit feature representation, inference for knowledge linking and disambiguation, and learning with direct or indirect supervision. Finally, future directions for this research topic are explored.

title: People on Drugs: Credibility of User Statements in Health Communities
Abstract: Online health communities are valuable resources for patients and physicians. However, user-generated content is often plagued by inaccuracies and misinformation. This paper proposes a method for automatically establishing the credibility of user-generated medical statements and the trustworthiness of their authors by exploiting linguistic cues and distant supervision from expert sources. A probabilistic graphical model is introduced that jointly learns user trustworthiness, statement credibility, and language objectivity. This methodology is applied to the task of extracting rare or unknown side-effects of medical drugs - a problem where large-scale non-expert data can complement expert medical knowledge. The study demonstrates that this method can reliably extract side-effects and filter out false statements, while identifying trustworthy users likely to contribute valuable medical information.

title: Status Updates Over Unreliable Multiaccess Channels
Abstract: Applications such as environmental sensing, health and activity sensing, are supported by networks of devices (nodes) that send periodic packet transmissions over the wireless channel to a sink node. This paper examines simple abstractions that capture commonalities in such networks: (a) nodes send periodically sensed information that is temporal and must be delivered promptly, (b) they share a multiple access channel, and (c) channels between nodes and the sink are unreliable (packets may be received in error) and differ in quality. The study considers scheduled access and slotted ALOHA-like random access. Under scheduled access, nodes take turns and receive feedback on successful packet reception by the sink. During their turn, nodes can transmit multiple times to compensate for channel uncertainty. For slotted ALOHA-like access, each node attempts transmission in every slot with a certain probability. The study derives the age of information (AoI), a timeliness metric, for these access mechanisms, and determines conditions that optimize AoI at the sink. The case of symmetric updating, where updates from different nodes must have the same AoI, is also analyzed. The findings show that ALOHA-like access, while simple, results in AoI that is worse by a factor of about 2e, compared to scheduled access.

title: Light pollution offshore: zenithal sky glow measurements in the Mediterranean coastal waters
Abstract: Light pollution is a global phenomenon whose consequences for the natural environment and human health are being intensively studied. Most published studies address light pollution inland. However, coastal waters are spaces of high environmental interest due to their biodiversity richness and economic significance. The elevated population density in coastal regions is accompanied by correspondingly large emissions of artificial light at night, whose role as an environmental stressor is increasingly being recognized. The marine surface environment provides an unobstructed stage for measuring the dependence of skyglow on the distance to light-polluting sources and validating (or rejecting) atmospheric light propagation models. This work presents a proof-of-concept of a gimbal measurement system for zenithal skyglow measurements on board both small boats and large vessels under actual navigation conditions. The results obtained in the summer of 2016 along two measurement routes in the Mediterranean waters offshore Barcelona, traveling 9 and 31.7 km away from the coast, are reported. The atmospheric conditions in both routes differed from those assumed for the calculation of recently published models of anthropogenic sky brightness. The results from the first route, conducted under conditions closer to theoretical predictions, approach them better. The results from the second route, conducted under a clearer atmosphere, showed systematic differences attributable to two expected phenomena, which are a consequence of the smaller aerosol content: the reduction of anthropogenic sky glow at short distances from the sources and the slower decay rate of brightness with distance, which gives rise to a relative excess of brightness at large distances from the coastline.

title: DeepDeath: Learning to Predict the Underlying Cause of Death with Big Data
Abstract: Multiple cause-of-death data provides valuable information for enhancing health standards by predicting health-related trajectories in societies with large populations. This data is often available in vast quantities across US states and requires Big Data techniques to uncover complex hidden patterns. This study designs two different classes of models suitable for large-scale analysis of mortality data: a Hadoop-based ensemble of random forests trained over N-grams and DeepDeath, a deep classifier based on the recurrent neural network (RNN). Both classes are applied to mortality data provided by the National Center for Health Statistics, demonstrating that while both perform significantly better than the random classifier, the deep model utilizing long short-term memory networks (LSTMs) surpasses the N-gram-based models and can learn the temporal aspect of the data without the need for building ad-hoc, expert-driven features.

title: An Ensemble Approach to Predicting the Impact of Vaccination on Rotavirus Disease in Niger
Abstract: Recently developed vaccines offer a new method for controlling rotavirus in sub-Saharan Africa. Models for the transmission dynamics of rotavirus are crucial for estimating the current burden from imperfect surveillance and assessing the potential effects of vaccine intervention strategies. This study examines rotavirus infection in the Maradi area of southern Niger using hospital surveillance data collected by Epicentre over two years. Additionally, a cluster survey of households in the region provides estimates of the proportion of children with diarrhea who consulted a health structure. Model fit and future projections are necessarily specific to a given model; therefore, where competing models exist for the underlying epidemiology, an ensemble approach can account for uncertainty. This study compares results across several variants of Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered (SIR) compartmental models to quantify the impact of modeling assumptions on estimates. Model-specific parameters are estimated through Bayesian inference using Markov chain Monte Carlo. Bayesian model averaging is then used to generate ensemble estimates of the current dynamics, including estimates of R0, the burden of infection in the region, and the impact of vaccination on both short-term dynamics and long-term reduction of rotavirus incidence under varying levels of coverage. The ensemble of models predicts that the current burden of severe rotavirus disease is 2.9 to 4.1% of the population each year, and a 2-dose vaccine schedule achieving 70% coverage could reduce burden by 37-43%.

title: A Rural Lens on a Research Agenda for Intelligent Infrastructure
Abstract: A National Agenda for Intelligent Infrastructure is incomplete without explicit consideration of the needs of rural communities. While the American population has urbanized, the United States relies on rural communities for agriculture, fishing, forestry, manufacturing, and mining. Approximately 20% of the US population lives in rural areas, with a skew towards aging adults. Additionally, nearly 25% of Veterans reside in rural America. Yet, when intelligent infrastructure is envisioned, it is often done so with implicit or explicit bias towards cities. This brief describes the unique opportunities for rural communities and offers an inclusive vision of intelligent infrastructure research. The study argues for coordinated actions to ensure that rural Americans are not left behind in the digital revolution. These technological platforms and applications, supported by appropriate policy, will address key issues in transportation, energy, agriculture, public safety, and health. The study concludes that, rather than a set of needs, the rural United States presents a set of exciting possibilities for novel innovation that benefits not only those living there but also the American economy more broadly.

title: Safety and Security for Intelligent Infrastructure
Abstract: Smart computing devices, with powerful sensors and internet connectivity, are increasingly being embedded into all new forms of infrastructure, from hospitals to roads to factories. These devices are part of the Internet of Things (IoT), and the economic value of their widespread deployment is estimated to be trillions of dollars, with billions of devices deployed. For example, "smart meters" for electricity utilities have been rolled out across North America due to clear economic benefits, including reduced meter reading costs, more precise outage and diagnostic information, and increased benefits from predicting and balancing electric loads. With residential solar collection, smart meters allow individuals to sell power back to the grid, providing economic incentives for conservation. Similarly, smart water meters facilitate water conservation during droughts. These infrastructure upgrades, while infrequent (with smart meters expected to be in service for 20-30 years), justify their significant cost due to long-term benefits. One such benefit is the realization of unforeseen savings in the future when new analytic techniques are applied to the collected data. Similar benefits accrue to any infrastructure that embeds increased sensing and actuation capabilities via IoT devices, including roads and traffic control, energy and water management in buildings, and public health monitoring. |||

title: City-Scale Intelligent Systems and Platforms
Abstract: Urban areas are rapidly expanding, with 54% of the global population currently residing in cities, a number expected to reach 66% by 2050. Megacities, with populations exceeding 10 million, are particularly prominent, with 12% of the global population currently living in 28 megacities, and this number is projected to grow to at least 40 by 2030. This rapid urbanization necessitates massive investments in urban infrastructure, including roads, buildings, and utility networks.  The scale of this infrastructure development, combined with the need to renew aging urban infrastructure, represents a significant financial undertaking, potentially reaching tens of trillions of dollars in the coming decades. These investments must be carefully managed to balance factors such as environmental impact, energy consumption, maintenance costs, and the well-being and productivity of city residents. The challenge of ensuring cost-effective and sustainable management of these expanding urban areas has led to the concept of "Smart Cities," which utilize science and data-driven approaches to design, retrofit, and operate urban environments.

title: Robust Inference under the Beta Regression Model with Application to Health Care Studies
Abstract: Data involving rates, percentages, or proportions frequently arise in numerous disciplines like medical biology, healthcare, and psychology. This study focuses on developing a robust inference procedure for the beta regression model, specifically designed to analyze response variables that fall within the range of (0, 1) while accounting for related explanatory variables.  The issue of robustness in relation to the beta regression model has largely been overlooked in existing literature. Traditional inference methods based on maximum likelihood estimation are highly susceptible to the influence of outliers in the data, leading to inaccurate and unreliable inferences in the presence of data contamination. This paper introduces a robust minimum density power divergence estimator and a class of robust Wald-type tests for the beta regression model. These methods are supported by theoretical analyses of their asymptotic properties and robustness through influence function analysis. The effectiveness of these estimators and tests is validated through extensive simulations and real-world applications in healthcare and psychology. While the primary focus is on beta regression models with fixed dispersion parameters, the study also explores potential extensions to variable dispersion beta regression models.

title: Improving fitness: Mapping research priorities against societal needs on obesity
Abstract: Science policy is increasingly focused on tackling societal challenges and grand challenges. This shift demands new evaluation tools that assess not only the knowledge production aspect of research programs and organizations but also their alignment with societal needs. This paper presents an exploratory investigation into the relationship between scientific supply and societal needs in the context of the grand challenge of obesity, an emerging health problem with significant societal costs. The study proposes a novel approach using topic modeling to: (a) analyze scientific publications to identify existing research priorities; (b) analyze records of questions posed in the European Parliament to capture societal concerns; and (c) compare these two datasets to highlight potential misalignments between scientific outputs and societal needs. This method, while primarily a technical exercise, demonstrates the potential for such mapping techniques to inform strategic planning and evaluation in funding agencies.

title: Estimating and interpreting secondary attack risk: Binomial considered harmful
Abstract: The household secondary attack risk (SAR), often referred to as the secondary attack rate or secondary infection risk, represents the probability of infectious contact from an infected household member (A) to a given household member (B). Infectious contact is defined as a contact sufficient to infect individual B if they are susceptible. Estimating SAR is crucial for understanding and controlling the transmission of infectious diseases.  While SAR is commonly estimated using binomial models such as logistic regression, these models implicitly assume that all secondary infections within a household are attributable to the primary case. This simplification can lead to inaccurate estimates, particularly when multiple generations of transmission are possible. This paper demonstrates that the proportion of susceptible household members infected can be substantially larger than the true SAR, even when SAR is small. This bias arises from the neglect of multiple generations of transmission within households. As a result, binomial estimates of SAR are biased upward, and their confidence intervals have poor coverage probabilities, even when adjusted for clustering. To address these issues, the paper advocates for the use of longitudinal chain binomial models or pairwise survival analysis, which account for multiple generations of transmission, ongoing external infection risk, and incomplete follow-up. These methods provide more accurate point and interval estimates of SAR.  The practical implications of these findings are illustrated using an analysis of household surveillance data collected during the 2009 influenza A (H1N1) pandemic.

title: Fuzzy Approach Topic Discovery in Health and Medical Corpora
Abstract: The abundance of medical documents and electronic health records (EHRs) in textual format poses a significant challenge for data processing and retrieval of relevant information. The need to automatically access the vast reservoir of health and medical knowledge has been a longstanding research focus. Recent years have witnessed the development of powerful methods for automated text processing. Topic modeling, a popular approach for information retrieval based on theme discovery within health and medical corpora, continues to require further advancements. This research introduces Fuzzy Latent Semantic Analysis (FLSA), a novel topic modeling approach that utilizes fuzzy logic. FLSA addresses the redundancy issue inherent in health and medical corpora and provides a new method for estimating the number of topics. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that FLSA outperforms Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), the most widely used topic model, in terms of performance and features.

title: A mean score method for sensitivity analysis to departures from the missing at random assumption in randomised trials
Abstract: Most analyses of randomized trials with incomplete outcomes rely on untestable assumptions and should be subjected to sensitivity analyses. However, methods for conducting sensitivity analyses are not widely adopted. This paper proposes a mean score approach for exploring global sensitivity to departures from missing at random (MAR) or other assumptions related to incomplete outcome data in randomized trials. The approach focuses on a single outcome analyzed under a generalized linear model and introduces sensitivity parameters that measure the degree of departure from MAR within a pattern mixture model. The sensitivity parameters are defined by the user and can be interpreted relatively easily, making them suitable for elicitation from subject matter experts.  The method offers several advantages: it is computationally efficient and non-stochastic, and its point estimate, standard error, and confidence interval perfectly align with standard methods when specific values of the sensitivity parameters are used. The method is illustrated using data from a mental health trial.

title: Wireless Sensor Network based System for the Prevention of Hospital Acquired Infections
Abstract: Hospital-acquired infections pose a significant threat to the health and well-being of both patients and medical staff within clinical units. A substantial portion of these infections arise from medical personnel who come into contact with contaminated individuals, surfaces, or equipment and subsequently interact with patients without adhering to proper hygiene protocols. This paper presents ongoing efforts in the development of a wireless sensor network-based cyber-physical system designed to prevent hospital infections by promoting compliance with established hygiene guidelines. The system, currently being developed with European Union funding, integrates a network of sensors for monitoring clinical workflows and environmental conditions, a workflow engine that manages workflow instances, and monitoring software that provides real-time information in case of infection risk detection. The paper uses the example of a general practitioner's office to illustrate the types of sensors deployed and their positioning within the monitored environment. By leveraging the information collected by the sensors, the system can proactively identify infection risks and take immediate action to prevent the spread of infections.

title: Proactive Population-Risk Based Defense Against Denial of Cyber-Physical Service Attacks
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) holds tremendous potential to enhance areas such as energy efficiency, healthcare, and transportation. However, it also presents significant vulnerability to cyberattacks, particularly distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, which overwhelm server bandwidth. Many IoT devices are integrated into cyber-physical systems (CPS), making them susceptible to "physical" denial-of-service (PDoS) attacks, where IoT devices flood the "physical bandwidth" of a CPS. This paper quantifies the population-based risk to a group of IoT devices targeted by malware for a PDoS attack. To model bot recruitment, the study extends traditional game-theoretic concepts, introducing a "Poisson signaling game." It then analyzes two distinct mechanisms (legal and economic) for deterring botnet recruitment. The findings reveal that: 1) defenders can effectively limit botnet activity and 2) legislating minimum security standards has limited impact, whereas incentivizing active defense can significantly reduce botnet activity. This research provides a quantitative foundation for developing proactive defenses against PDoS attacks.

title: A System for Accessible Artificial Intelligence

The paper discusses how genetic programming can facilitate this endeavor and highlights specific examples where genetic programming has automated machine learning analyses in previous projects.

title: Nonparametric Cusum Charts for Angular Data with Applications in Health Science and Astrophysics
Abstract: This paper introduces non-parametric rotation invariant CUSUMs (cumulative sum charts) suitable for detecting changes in the mean direction and the concentration parameter of angular data. The properties of these CUSUMs are illustrated through theoretical calculations, Monte Carlo simulations, and applications to sequentially observed angular data from health science and astrophysics.

title: Quantifying Mental Health from Social Media with Neural User Embeddings
Abstract: Mental illnesses affect a substantial portion of the global population. However, traditional methods for estimating and characterizing the prevalence of mental health conditions are time-consuming and expensive, often resulting in outdated estimates. Automated approaches that leverage social media content provide a potential means for near real-time, large-scale estimations. This paper proposes a novel model for automated mental health status quantification that incorporates user embeddings. This model builds upon recent research exploring representation learning methods that induce embeddings based on social media post histories. These embeddings capture latent characteristics of individuals and encode a soft notion of homophily. The paper investigates whether user embeddings learned from Twitter post histories encode information that correlates with mental health statuses. The study evaluated embeddings for users known to be affected by depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and for a set of demographically matched control users. The findings demonstrate that the user embeddings capture similarities between users with respect to mental health conditions and are predictive of mental health status.

title: Illinois Accelerator Research Center
Abstract: The Illinois Accelerator Research Center (IARC) is a new accelerator development program located at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. title: Modeling the impact of rain on population exposed to air pollution

However, a notable reduction in air pollutant concentrations has been observed during the rainy season. Recent research has focused on understanding the mechanisms by which rain removes air pollutants. These studies have consistently demonstrated the effectiveness of rain in purifying the environment. title: Word Affect Intensities
Abstract: Words often convey affect, encompassing emotions, feelings, and attitudes. Furthermore, different words can convey affect to varying degrees (intensities).  While existing manually created lexicons for basic emotions (such as anger and fear) only provide coarse categories of affect association, automatic lexicons of affect offer finer degrees of association but tend to lack accuracy compared to human-created lexicons. This paper presents, for the first time, a manually created affect intensity lexicon with real-valued intensity scores for four basic emotions: anger, fear, joy, and sadness. The dataset, known as the NRC Affect Intensity Lexicon (AIL), includes entries for approximately 6,000 English words.  AIL was created using best-worst scaling (BWS), a technique that improves annotation consistency and generates reliable fine-grained scores. The paper compares the entries in AIL with those in the NRC VAD Lexicon, which contains valence, arousal, and dominance (VAD) scores for 20,000 English words. The analysis reveals that, on average, anger, fear, and sadness words have similar VAD scores, although sadness words tend to have slightly lower dominance scores than fear and anger words. The Affect Intensity Lexicon has numerous applications in automatic emotion analysis across various domains, including commerce, education, intelligence, and public health. AIL also serves as a valuable resource for developing natural language generation systems.
