The p-DLA is compared to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), a popular machine learning algorithm, and simulation studies demonstrate the impressive performance of the sparse memory predictive approach, which excels in knowledge discovery and information prediction with minimal resources. The proposed approach proves to be competitive with established AI techniques like LSTM.
label: AI

title: Sparsity enabled cluster reduced-order models for control
Abstract: Characterizing and controlling nonlinear, multi-scale phenomena is crucial in science and engineering. Cluster-based reduced-order modeling (CROM) exploits the low-dimensional dynamics of complex systems by building a data-driven discretization of the Perron-Frobenius operator, resulting in a probabilistic model for ensembles of trajectories. CROM embeds nonlinear dynamics within a linear framework and allows for uncertainty management through data assimilation. However, the high dimensionality of CROM computations limits its real-time implementation for prediction and control. This paper introduces sparsity-enabled CROM, which addresses this challenge by identifying a minimal subset of critical measurements for efficient model learning.  Leveraging compressive measurements, the approach faithfully captures the cluster geometry and preserves probabilistic dynamics.  Furthermore, optimized sensor locations are identified to outperform random measurements for specific applications. These sparsity-enabled sensing strategies significantly reduce the burden of data acquisition and processing, facilitating low-latency in-time estimation and control. The effectiveness of this unsupervised learning approach is illustrated across three high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems from fluids with increasing complexity, including a flow control application.  Sparsity-enabled CROM is a crucial facilitator for real-time implementation in high-dimensional systems where full-state information may be inaccessible.
label: AI

title: Digital Advertising Traffic Operation: Machine Learning for Process Discovery
Abstract: Effective Web Advertising Traffic Operation requires managing the day-to-day trafficking, pacing, and optimization of digital and paid social campaigns. Data analysts in this domain must provide quick answers and communicate effectively with process managers, visually highlighting process problems. To address growing customer service complaints, weaknesses in the process itself need to be identified and communicated. Process Mining for CRM data enables the identification of unwanted loops and delays in the process. This paper proposes a process discovery method based on machine learning techniques that automatically detects variations and identifies problems at a glance, allowing for timely corrective measures.
label: AI

title: Deep Neural Networks to Enable Real-time Multimessenger Astrophysics
Abstract: Gravitational wave astronomy has revolutionized scientific discovery. To further enhance this emerging field, there is a pressing need to improve the speed and depth of gravitational wave algorithms. Deep Filtering, a highly scalable method for end-to-end time-series signal processing, is introduced in this paper. This method employs two deep convolutional neural networks, designed for classification and regression, to rapidly detect and estimate parameters of signals in noisy time-series data streams. A novel training scheme with gradually increasing noise levels and a transfer learning procedure between the two networks are presented. The application of this method for detecting and estimating parameters of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers demonstrates its effectiveness. Results show that Deep Filtering significantly outperforms conventional machine learning techniques and achieves performance comparable to matched-filtering while being several orders of magnitude faster, enabling real-time processing of raw big data with minimal resources. Importantly, Deep Filtering expands the range of detectable gravitational wave signals with ground-based detectors. This framework leverages advancements in artificial intelligence algorithms and hardware architectures, such as deep-learning-optimized GPUs, to facilitate real-time searches for gravitational wave sources and their electromagnetic and astro-particle counterparts.
label: AI

title: Counterfactual Prediction with Deep Instrumental Variables Networks
Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is largely driven by the success of deep learning architectures, which map observables to outputs through multiple layers of latent representations. These deep learning algorithms excel in unstructured prediction and can be combined within AI systems to solve complex automated reasoning problems. This paper presents a recipe for combining machine learning (ML) algorithms to determine causal effects in the presence of instrumental variables – sources of treatment randomization conditionally independent from the response. The proposed Deep IV framework resolves into two prediction tasks solved by deep neural nets: a first-stage network for treatment prediction and a second-stage network with a loss function involving integration over the conditional treatment distribution.  While imposing specific structure on the stochastic gradient descent routine used for training, Deep IV remains general enough to leverage off-the-shelf ML capabilities and minimize algorithm customization. The paper outlines methods for obtaining out-of-sample causal validation to avoid overfitting and introduces schemes for both Bayesian and frequentist inference: the former via a novel adaptation of dropout training and the latter via a data splitting routine.
label: AI

title: PrASP Report
Abstract: This technical report describes the usage, syntax, semantics, and core algorithms of the probabilistic inductive logic programming framework PrASP.  PrASP is a research software that integrates non-monotonic reasoning based on Answer Set Programming (ASP), probabilistic inference, and parameter learning. Unlike traditional probabilistic (inductive) logic programming approaches, PrASP imposes minimal restrictions on probabilistic logic programs. It supports both ASP and First-Order Logic syntax and allows for annotating formulas with point probabilities as well as interval probabilities.  A variety of configurable inference algorithms can be combined in a pipeline-like fashion to address a wide range of use cases.
label: AI

title: Automatic Data Deformation Analysis on Evolving Folksonomy Driven Environment
Abstract: The Folksodriven framework empowers data scientists to define an ontology environment for effectively searching for predictive patterns and building predictive models.  It achieves this by providing abstractions that isolate parameters of the predictive modeling process, including pattern searching and feature set design. This paper explores ontologies based on folksonomies, introducing a new concept structure called "Folksodriven" to represent them. The studies on the transformational regulation of Folksodriven tags are crucial for adaptive folksonomies classifications in evolving environments used by Intelligent Systems for knowledge sharing. Folksodriven tags categorize salient data points, enabling machine-learning systems to "featurize" the data.
label: AI

title: Investor Experiences and Financial Market Dynamics
Abstract: This research investigates the impact of macro-financial shocks on investor behavior and market dynamics.  Recent evidence on experience effects suggests that personally experienced outcomes have a long-lasting influence on investor beliefs and investment, with notable differences across generations.  The paper formalizes experience-based learning within an overlapping generations (OLG) model where diverse cross-cohort experiences generate persistent heterogeneity in beliefs, portfolio choices, and trading activity. The model establishes a novel link between investor demographics and the dependence of prices on past dividends, while also replicating known features of asset prices, such as excess volatility and return predictability. Furthermore, the model generates new implications for the cross-section of asset holdings, trade volume, and investors' heterogeneous responses to recent financial crises, which are shown to be consistent with empirical data.
label: AI

title: A Joint Speaker-Listener-Reinforcer Model for Referring Expressions
Abstract: Referring expressions, natural language constructions used to identify specific objects within a scene, are the focus of this paper. It proposes a unified framework for the tasks of referring expression comprehension and generation.  This framework consists of three modules: speaker, listener, and reinforcer. The speaker generates referring expressions, the listener comprehends them, and the reinforcer introduces a reward function to guide the sampling of more discriminative expressions. The listener-speaker modules are trained jointly in an end-to-end learning framework, allowing them to be aware of each other during learning while benefiting from the discriminative reinforcer's feedback.  This unified framework and training achieve state-of-the-art results for both comprehension and generation on three referring expression datasets.
label: AI

title: Feedback Networks
Abstract: Current state-of-the-art learning models in computer vision rely on learning successive representations followed by a decision layer, typically implemented through feedforward multilayer neural networks like ConvNets. This paper proposes an alternative feedback-based approach where the representation is formed iteratively based on feedback received from previous iteration's output. It demonstrates several fundamental advantages of the feedback-based approach over feedforward methods, including the ability to make early predictions at query time, a natural output conforming to hierarchical structures in the label space, and a new foundation for Curriculum Learning. The paper observes that feedback networks develop a distinct representation compared to their feedforward counterparts, aligning with these advantages. It introduces a general feedback-based learning architecture that achieves comparable or better results than existing feedforward networks while incorporating the aforementioned advantages. The paper also investigates several mechanisms within feedback architectures, such as skip connections in time, and design choices, such as feedback length. This study offers new perspectives on developing more natural and practical learning models.
label: AI

title: Smart Content Recognition from Images Using a Mixture of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: With the rapid growth of the Internet, web content has become vast.  While most websites are publicly accessible, not all web content is appropriate for all users, particularly children. Pornographic images, for instance, should be restricted to specific age groups. Additionally, such content is often considered NSFW (Not Safe For Work) and should be avoided by employees during work hours. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successfully applied to various computer vision problems. This paper proposes a mixture of CNNs for adult content recognition. Unlike other approaches, the proposed method utilizes a weighted sum of multiple deep neural network models. The weights of each CNN model are determined as a linear regression problem using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). Experimental results demonstrate that this model outperforms both single CNN models and the average sum of CNN models in adult content recognition.
label: AI

title: Double Coupled Canonical Polyadic Decomposition for Joint Blind Source Separation
Abstract: Joint Blind Source Separation (J-BSS) is an emerging data-driven technique for multi-set data fusion. This paper addresses J-BSS from a tensorial perspective.  By using second-order multi-set statistics in J-BSS, a specific double coupled canonical polyadic decomposition (DC-CPD) problem is formulated. An algebraic DC-CPD algorithm based on a coupled rank-1 detection mapping is proposed. This algorithm transforms a potentially underdetermined DC-CPD into a set of overdetermined CPDs, which can be solved algebraically using a generalized eigenvalue decomposition scheme.  The algorithm is deterministic and returns the exact solution in the noiseless case.  For noisy cases, it serves as an effective initialization for optimization-based DC-CPD algorithms. Additionally, the paper derives deterministic and generic uniqueness conditions for DC-CPD, which are shown to be more relaxed than those for standard CPD. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of DC-CPD over standard CPD-based BSS methods and existing J-BSS methods in terms of uniqueness and accuracy.
label: AI

title: Adaptive Lambda Least-Squares Temporal Difference Learning
Abstract: Temporal Difference (TD) learning, specifically TD($\lambda$), is a fundamental algorithm in reinforcement learning.  However, setting the $\lambda$ parameter, which controls the timescale of TD updates, is typically left to the practitioner. This paper formalizes the $\lambda$ selection problem as a bias-variance trade-off, where the optimal $\lambda$ minimizes the Mean Squared Value Error (MSVE).  The paper proposes applying Leave-One-Trajectory-Out Cross-Validation (LOTO-CV) to search the space of $\lambda$ values. While computationally expensive, LOTO-CV can be efficiently implemented for Least Squares TD (LSTD) to automatically tune $\lambda$ and apply function optimization methods for efficient search. The resulting algorithm, ALLSTD, is parameter-free and experimental results show that it significantly outperforms the naive LOTO-CV implementation in terms of computational speed while achieving comparable performance.
label: AI

title: Automatic Discoveries of Physical and Semantic Concepts via Association Priors of Neuron Groups
Abstract: The recent success of deep neural networks relies largely on supervised training, where complex patterns of input samples are associated with neurons in the final layer, forming representations of concepts.  Despite their success, the properties of these associated complex patterns remain unclear. This paper analyzes how neurons are associated with concepts in supervised networks and hypothesizes that with proper priors to regulate learning, neural networks can automatically associate neurons in intermediate layers with concepts aligned with real-world concepts. This hypothesis is validated by training networks only with labels that associate concepts with top-level neurons, a plausible scenario for unsupervised learning.  The paper develops a prior to verify the hypothesis and experimentally finds that the proposed prior helps neural networks automatically learn both basic physical concepts at lower layers (e.g., rotation of filters) and highly semantic concepts at higher layers (e.g., fine-grained categories of an entry-level category).
label: AI

title: Community-based Outlier Detection for Edge-attributed Graphs
Abstract: The study of networks has emerged across diverse disciplines as a means of analyzing complex relationship data. While graph analysis tasks like graph query processing, link analysis, and influence propagation have received significant attention, recent work has focused on outlier detection for information network data. While various outlier types have been studied for graph data, anomaly detection from edge-attributed graphs remains under-explored. This paper introduces a method for detecting novel outlier graph nodes by considering both node and edge data simultaneously to identify anomalies. The problem is modeled as a community detection task, where outliers form a distinct community. The proposed method uses a probabilistic graph model (Hidden Markov Random Field) to jointly model nodes and edges in the network and compute Holistic Community Outliers (HCOutliers). This model is particularly suitable for heterogeneous graphs with multiple edges/relationships between nodes.  The EM (Expectation Maximization) algorithm is used to learn model parameters and infer hidden community labels.  Experimental results on synthetic datasets and the DBLP dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for finding novel outliers from networks.
label: AI

title: Data driven estimation of Laplace-Beltrami operator
Abstract: Approximations of Laplace-Beltrami operators on manifolds using graph Laplacians have become popular tools in data analysis and machine learning. These discretized operators typically depend on bandwidth parameters, whose tuning remains a theoretical and practical challenge.  This paper addresses this problem for the unnormalized graph Laplacian by establishing an oracle inequality that provides a foundation for data-driven bandwidth selection. The approach relies on recent results by Lacour and Massart on Lepski's method.
label: AI

title: Curiosity-Aware Bargaining
Abstract: Opponent modeling involves modeling the strategy or preferences of an agent based on its provided data. In automated negotiation, this can provide a significant advantage, potentially hindering casual agents from participating in the bargaining process.  This paper defines "curious" agents as those driven by a desire to negotiate in order to gather information and improve their opponent models. While curiosity-based rationality and curiosity-robust protocols have not been explored in automated negotiation, this paper leverages mechanism design to propose three extensions to the standard bargaining protocol that limit information leakage. These extensions are supported by an enhanced rationality model that considers exchanged information, and they are theoretically analyzed and experimentally evaluated. |||
label: AI

title: Automatic labeling of molecular biomarkers of whole slide immunohistochemistry images using fully convolutional networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based method for automatically quantifying biomarkers in multi-stained tissue samples. The method uses a fully convolutional network (FCN) that takes an RGB image of a tissue as input and outputs a map of different biomarkers. The FCN relies on a convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies each cell based on the biomarker it expresses. The CNN is trained on a dataset of manually labeled cell images, achieving an accuracy of 92% on a test set. The trained CNN is then integrated into the FCN to generate a biomarker map for the entire tissue slide. Evaluation on manually labeled whole slide images shows that the proposed method performs comparably to manual labeling by humans, with an average F-score of 0.96.
label: AI

title: Permuted and Augmented Stick-Breaking Bayesian Multinomial Regression
Abstract: A new permuted and augmented stick-breaking (paSB) construction is proposed for modeling categorical response variables in multinomial regression. The paSB construction maps observed categories to randomly permuted latent sticks, transforming multinomial regression into a regression analysis of stick-specific binary variables. This allows the use of arbitrary cross-entropy-loss binary classifiers for Bayesian multinomial modeling. The paper introduces Bayesian multinomial softplus regression and Bayesian multinomial SVM, leveraging covariate-dependent softplus functions. These models offer probability estimates, uncertainty quantification, robustness, and nonlinear classification capabilities. Example results demonstrate their attractive properties and performance.
label: AI

title: Action Recognition Based on Joint Trajectory Maps with Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for applying convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) to human action recognition using 3D skeleton sequences. The proposed method converts spatio-temporal information from the sequences into three 2D images, called Joint Trajectory Maps (JTMs), which encode joint trajectories and dynamics into color distribution. ConvNets are then used to learn discriminative features from these JTMs for action recognition. This approach enables fine-tuning existing ConvNets models without retraining them. The three JTMs provide complementary information from different orthogonal planes, and their scores are fused for improved recognition performance. Evaluation on four public benchmark datasets demonstrates state-of-the-art results.
label: AI

title: Automatically generating features for learning program analysis heuristics
Abstract: This paper introduces a technique for automatically generating features for data-driven program analyses. The technique leverages existing codebases to learn heuristics for efficient abstraction, reducing the manual effort required for feature design. The approach involves reducing and abstracting program-query pairs to a few lines of code, ensuring that the analysis maintains similar behavior for both the original and the reduced programs. Each reduced program serves as a boolean feature for program-query pairs. Experimental evaluation on real-world program analyses shows that the automatically generated features achieve comparable performance to manually crafted features.
label: AI

title: Sparse Learning with Semi-Proximal-Based Strictly Contractive Peaceman-Rachford Splitting Method
Abstract: This paper introduces a stochastic version of the Semi-Proximal-Based Strictly Contractive Peaceman-Rachford Splitting Method (SPB-SPRSM) for solving splitting problems, a common type of convex optimization problem in machine learning. The proposed Stochastic SPB-SPRSM algorithm utilizes subsets of samples (even a single sample) at each iteration, making it more flexible than Stochastic ADMM and other ADMM-based algorithms. The paper proves an ergodic convergence rate of O(1/√t) for the algorithm, demonstrating its theoretical efficiency. The algorithm also preserves the advantage of SPRSM-based methods over ADMM, exhibiting faster convergence in practical applications.
label: AI

title: The Neural Hawkes Process: A Neurally Self-Modulating Multivariate Point Process
Abstract: This paper presents a neurally self-modulating multivariate point process for modeling streams of discrete events in continuous time. The model utilizes a continuous-time LSTM to evolve the intensities of multiple event types, allowing past events to influence future event intensities in a complex and realistic manner. This generative model achieves competitive likelihood and predictive accuracy on real and synthetic datasets, including under missing-data conditions. The model exhibits desirable qualitative properties and offers insights into the dynamic relationships between events.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Logo Detection with Data Expansion by Synthesising Context
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for training logo detection models using synthetically generated training images to address the challenge of limited labelled data. The method generates Synthetic Context Logo (SCL) images, which introduce background clutter and improve model robustness. For evaluation, a new logo detection dataset, TopLogo-10, is introduced, containing logos from the top 10 most popular clothing/wearable brands. Extensive comparisons demonstrate the superiority of the SCL model over state-of-the-art alternatives on real-world logo detection datasets, FlickrLogo-32 and TopLogo-10.
label: AI

title: Communication-efficient Distributed Estimation and Inference for Transelliptical Graphical Models
Abstract: This paper proposes communication-efficient distributed estimation and inference methods for the transelliptical graphical model, a semiparametric extension of the elliptical distribution for high-dimensional data. The proposed method distributes data across worker machines, estimates the latent precision matrix locally, and then aggregates the debiased local estimators on a master machine. The aggregated estimator achieves the same statistical rate as a centralized estimator, provided the number of machines satisfies certain conditions. This algorithm and theory can be applied to Gaussian graphical models, Gaussian copula graphical models, and elliptical graphical models, as they are special cases of the transelliptical model. Experiments on synthetic data support the theoretical findings.
label: AI

title: Symmetry, Saddle Points, and Global Optimization Landscape of Nonconvex Matrix Factorization
Abstract: This paper presents a general theory for analyzing the landscape of nonconvex optimization problems with underlying symmetric structures, focusing on low-rank matrix factorization, phase retrieval, and deep linear neural networks. The theory characterizes the stationary points and null space of Hessian matrices using invariant groups. By applying the theory to low-rank matrix factorization, the paper identifies all stationary points, dividing the parameter space into regions corresponding to strict saddle points, global minima, and regions with large gradient magnitudes. This global landscape analysis provides strong convergence guarantees for popular iterative algorithms with arbitrary initial solutions.
label: AI

title: Generalized Intersection Kernel
Abstract: This paper introduces the generalized intersection (GInt) kernel and the normalized generalized min-max (NGMM) kernel, extensions of the min-max kernel for data with both negative and positive entries. Extensive empirical classification studies on 40 datasets from the UCI repository demonstrate the performance of the GInt kernel, which is tuning-free. The NGMM kernel, interpreted as an asymmetrically transformed version of the GInt kernel, consistently outperforms the GInt kernel. The NGMM kernel can be efficiently linearized using generalized consistent weighted sampling (GCWS), and its discrete nature enables approximate near neighbor search.
label: AI

title: Using Big Data to Enhance the Bosch Production Line Performance: A Kaggle Challenge
Abstract: This paper describes the approach used to solve the Bosch production line performance challenge on Kaggle.com. The goal was to maximize production yield by predicting internal failures in products at the Bosch assembly line using data science methods. By analyzing data from tests and measurements made on components, the team developed a model that predicts which parts are most likely to fail. This allows for the creation of a smarter failure detection system, enabling the salvage of potentially failing parts, reducing operating costs, and increasing profit margins.
label: AI

title: Motifs in Temporal Networks
Abstract: This paper examines the role of network motifs in temporal networks, which contain timestamped links between nodes. The authors introduce the concept of a temporal network motif as an elementary unit of temporal networks and develop a general methodology for counting these motifs. They define temporal network motifs as induced subgraphs on sequences of temporal edges, design fast algorithms for counting them, and prove their runtime complexity. These algorithms achieve significant speedup compared to baseline methods. Analysis of various networks shows that networks from different domains have distinct motif counts, while networks from the same domain exhibit similar motif counts. Additionally, the occurrence of different motifs at different time scales provides further insights into the structure and function of temporal networks.
label: AI

title: A hybrid approach to supervised machine learning for algorithmic melody composition
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for composing monophonic melodies similar in style to a given sample of melodies annotated with phrases. The algorithm combines parametric Markov models of higher order with a contour concept of phrases. The work builds upon a master's thesis by Thayabaran Kathiresan (2015) and improves upon the pure Markov model by incorporating musically relevant context, such as count and planned melody contour. An online listening test confirms that this enhancement significantly improves the results.
label: AI

title: Deep neural heart rate variability analysis
Abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of blood tests for early cardiovascular disease detection and explores the potential of heart rate variability analysis using deep learning. The authors introduce a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines a layer of biological neuron models of cardiac dynamics with a feed-forward neural network. The model is evaluated on ECG data from patients with coronary artery disease and chest pain, demonstrating significantly better performance compared to traditional heart rate variability predictors. The model also approaches or even surpasses the performance of clinical blood tests, using only 60 seconds of inter-beat intervals.
label: AI

title: Quantum Clustering and Gaussian Mixtures
Abstract: This paper proposes a quantum-inspired method for clustering, drawing inspiration from quantum interference phenomena in physics. Instead of directly modeling class distributions using Gaussian distributions, the proposed method models class wave functions, whose magnitude squares represent the class Gaussian distributions. These class wave functions are then mixed to create a mixture wave function, and the final mixture distribution is obtained by taking the magnitude square of the mixture wave function. This approach introduces quantum class interference effects not present in the traditional Gaussian mixture model. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance in estimating distribution parameters, exhibiting higher accuracy, reduced fluctuations, and robustness to deviations from Gaussian assumptions. The paper illustrates the method with an example application in color segmentation.
label: AI

title: Are inequities in self-efficacy a systemic feature of physics education?
Abstract: This paper examines the evidence of physics instruction negatively impacting female students' self-efficacy, their belief in their ability to learn and do physics. The harm is problematic as self-efficacy is crucial for student learning and persistence. Building upon previous research by Nissen and Shemwell (2016), which found a gender difference in self-efficacy states in a single college physics course, this paper analyzes a large dataset of student experiences from 33 secondary schools. The results confirm the existence of a significant gender difference in self-efficacy states specifically in high school physics courses, not observed in other courses. This consistency across different settings suggests a systemic issue within physics instruction that undermines female students' confidence in their abilities.
label: AI

title: A comparison of Hake's g and Cohen's d for analyzing gains on concept inventories
Abstract: This paper investigates the implications of choosing between two common methods for analyzing shifts in concept inventories: Hake's gain (g) and Cohen's d. Hake's gain is widely used in physics education research, while Cohen's d is prevalent in broader education research. The analysis uses data from the Learning Assistant Supported Student Outcomes (LASSO) database, comprising test scores from over 4,500 students on concept inventories in physics, chemistry, biology, and math. The results show that the two methods lead to different conclusions about student learning and equity, with Hake's gain exhibiting a bias favoring high pretest populations. The paper recommends using caution when interpreting findings based on Hake's gain and suggests using Cohen's d for more accurate and unbiased assessments of student learning and equity.
label: AI

title: A Unified Approach to Analyzing Asynchronous Coordinate Descent and Tatonnement
Abstract: This paper examines asynchrony in iterative processes, focusing on gradient descent and tatonnement, a fundamental price dynamic in economics. The paper explores asynchronous variants of gradient descent, particularly coordinate descent, and provides new analyses of cyclic coordinate descent, parallel asynchronous stochastic coordinate descent, and a general worst-case parallel asynchronous coordinate descent. The analyses utilize a common amortized framework, with new ideas introduced to address the challenges of asynchronous actions in the stochastic case. The paper shows that the proposed framework can also be applied to asynchronous versions of tatonnement, demonstrating its convergence towards market equilibrium for Fisher markets with CES or Leontief utilities.
label: AI

title: High-dimensional Filtering using Nested Sequential Monte Carlo
Abstract: This paper proposes nested sequential Monte Carlo (NSMC), a methodology that generalizes the Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework for Bayesian filtering. NSMC allows for approximate, properly weighted samples from the SMC proposal distribution, resulting in a correct SMC algorithm. This enables the exact approximation of the locally optimal proposal, extending the applicability of SMC to a broader class of models. NSMC demonstrates improved accuracy over other state-of-the-art methods on spatio-temporal state space models, showcasing its effectiveness in high-dimensional settings.
label: AI

title: Learning Visual N-Grams from Web Data
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of training real-world image recognition systems with tens of thousands of classes using webly supervised data, where images are associated with user comments instead of traditional labels. The authors develop visual n-gram models, which are feed-forward convolutional networks trained using novel loss functions inspired by n-gram models in language modeling. These models can predict phrases relevant to the content of an image and have applications in phrase prediction, phrase-based image retrieval, image-caption association, and zero-shot transfer. The paper demonstrates the advantages of visual n-gram models in webly supervised image recognition settings. |||
label: AI

title: The interplay between system identification and machine learning
Abstract: Learning from examples is a fundamental challenge in scientific and engineering domains. This task involves reconstructing a function from a limited set of noisy data points. Regularization techniques in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHSs) are widely used to address this challenge, yielding powerful estimators such as regularization networks.  Recent advancements have demonstrated the statistical consistency of these kernel-based approaches.  Simultaneously, various system identification methods have been developed, but their interaction with machine learning remains relatively weak.  One reason for this gap is that the RKHSs commonly used in machine learning do not incorporate information inherent to dynamic systems, such as bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability.  Furthermore, the assumption of independent data, prevalent in machine learning, is often unrealistic in system identification. This paper bridges the gap between system identification and machine learning by introducing RKHSs specifically designed for dynamic systems. These spaces contain functionals over system input spaces, allowing for the interpretation of system identification as learning from examples.  Both in linear and nonlinear settings, this perspective facilitates the derivation of conditions for RKHS stability, ensuring the presence of only BIBO stable systems or predictors within the space.  This framework also enables the design of novel kernels tailored for system identification.  Moreover, the paper proves the convergence of the regularized estimator towards the optimal predictor under conditions typically encountered in dynamic systems.
label: AI

title: Linear Learning with Sparse Data
Abstract: Linear predictors are particularly useful when working with high-dimensional, sparse data. One common technique for training linear predictors is the Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent (ASGD) algorithm. This paper presents an efficient implementation of ASGD that avoids dense vector operations. Additionally, a translation-invariant extension of this algorithm, called Centered Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent (CASGD), is described.
label: AI

title: From Virtual to Real World Visual Perception using Domain Adaptation -- The DPM as Example
Abstract: Supervised learning typically outperforms unsupervised learning in terms of classifier accuracy. This highlights the importance of training data with annotations. When addressing visual perception tasks, such as object localization within images, the training of classifiers often becomes a practical bottleneck. This is due to the requirement of manually labeling object examples with bounding boxes in thousands of images.  The complexity of the model, in terms of its number of parameters, further necessitates a larger number of annotated examples.  Human oracles perform this annotation task, which inherently introduces inaccuracies and errors in the ground truth due to the complexity and ambiguity involved. As a solution, virtual worlds have been proposed as a means for automatically collecting annotations with high precision.  However, since models trained on virtual data need to function in the real world, domain adaptation (DA) is still required.  This chapter examines the DA of a deformable part-based model (DPM) as an illustrative case of virtual-to-real-world DA.  Vehicle detection for driver assistance is used as a use case, utilizing publicly available virtual-world data.  The study investigates factors such as the impact of virtual-vs-real data on the domain gap with respect to dominant object appearance, as well as the role of photorealism in the virtual world.
label: AI

title: Modeling documents with Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a method for learning distributed representations of natural language documents using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The proposed model is based on the Energy-Based GAN but utilizes a Denoising Autoencoder as the discriminator network. Document representations are extracted from the discriminator's hidden layer and evaluated both quantitatively and qualitatively.
label: AI

title: Deep Semi-Supervised Learning with Linguistically Motivated Sequence Labeling Task Hierarchies
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel Neural Network algorithm for semi-supervised learning in sequence labeling tasks organized within a linguistically motivated hierarchy. The hierarchical relationship is exploited to regularize the representations of supervised tasks by backpropagating the error from the unsupervised task through the supervised tasks.  The architecture features a neural network where lower layers are supervised by junior downstream tasks and the final layer is an auxiliary unsupervised task.  The proposed architecture demonstrates improvements of up to two percentage points in F1 score for Chunking compared to a plausible baseline.
label: AI

title: Sequence-to-point learning with neural networks for nonintrusive load monitoring
Abstract: Energy disaggregation, also known as nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM), is a single-channel blind source separation problem that aims to decompose the total electricity consumption measured at the main circuit into appliance-specific readings.  This problem is inherently challenging due to its unidentifiability. Recent approaches have demonstrated the potential of incorporating domain knowledge into the model to address the identifiability issue. Deep neural networks have shown promise for these problems, but sliding windows are often needed to handle the long sequences encountered in signal processing, raising questions about combining predictions from different windows. This paper proposes a sequence-to-point learning approach where the input is a window of the mains signal and the output is a single point of the target appliance.  Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed to train the model. Interestingly, the study demonstrates that CNNs can inherently learn the signatures of target appliances, which are automatically incorporated into the model to reduce the identifiability issue.  The proposed neural network approaches are applied to real-world household energy data, achieving state-of-the-art performance with improvements of 84% and 92% in two standard error measures.
label: AI

title: Selecting Bases in Spectral learning of Predictive State Representations via Model Entropy
Abstract: Predictive State Representations (PSRs) are powerful techniques for modeling dynamical systems, representing a state as a vector of predictions about future observable events (tests).  A fundamental challenge in PSRs is the learning of the underlying system's PSR model. Spectral methods have emerged as a successful approach to this challenge by treating the learning problem as the task of computing a singular value decomposition (SVD) over a submatrix of a special type of matrix called the Hankel matrix.  Under the assumptions that the submatrix rows and columns are sufficient (which typically requires a very large number and often fails in practice) and the matrix entries can be accurately estimated, spectral learning of PSRs has been shown to be statistically consistent, with learned parameters converging to the true parameters. However, in practice, computational limitations restrict the use of a finite set of rows or columns for spectral learning.  Since different column selections lead to variations in model accuracy, this paper proposes an approach called basis selection for choosing the set of columns. This selection is guided by the concept of model entropy, which measures the accuracy of the learned model.  Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning and Hierarchal Generative Models
Abstract: Deep learning is considered highly efficient for data generated from hierarchical generative models. Examples of such models include wavelet scattering networks, functions of compositional structure, and deep rendering models.  However, for all these models, it is either not rigorously known that they can be learned efficiently, or it is not known that "deep algorithms" are essential for learning them. This paper proposes a simple family of "generative hierarchical models" that can be learned efficiently and where "deep" algorithms are necessary for learning.  The definition of "deep" algorithms in this context is based on the empirical observation that deep networks inherently utilize correlations between features.  Formally, the paper shows that in a semi-supervised setting, given access to low-order moments of the labeled data and all the unlabeled data, it is information theoretically impossible to perform classification.  Simultaneously, there exists an efficient algorithm that, given all labeled and unlabeled data, perfectly labels all unlabeled data with high probability.  The proof utilizes and strengthens the fact that Belief Propagation does not admit a good approximation in terms of linear functions.
label: AI

title: Linking the Neural Machine Translation and the Prediction of Organic Chemistry Reactions
Abstract: Determining the main product of a chemical reaction is a crucial problem in organic chemistry. This paper presents a method for applying a neural machine translation model to predict organic chemical reactions.  To translate "reactants and reagents" into "products," a gated recurrent unit (GRU)-based sequence-to-sequence model and a parser to generate input tokens from reaction SMILES strings are constructed. Training sets are composed of reactions from patent databases and reactions manually generated based on elementary reactions described in a standard organic chemistry textbook by Wade.  The trained models are evaluated using examples and problems from the textbook.  The prediction process does not require manual encoding of rules (e.g., SMARTS transformations) to predict products, relying solely on sufficient training reaction sets to learn new reaction types.
label: AI

title: Geometric descent method for convex composite minimization
Abstract: This paper extends the geometric descent method recently proposed by Bubeck, Lee, and Singh to address nonsmooth and strongly convex composite problems.  The proposed algorithm, dubbed Geometric Proximal Gradient Method (GeoPG), is proven to converge with a linear rate of $(1-1/\\sqrt{\\kappa})$, achieving the optimal rate among first-order methods, where $\\kappa$ is the problem's condition number. Numerical results on linear regression and logistic regression with elastic net regularization show that GeoPG outperforms Nesterov's accelerated proximal gradient method, particularly for ill-conditioned problems.
label: AI

title: Meta-Unsupervised-Learning: A supervised approach to unsupervised learning
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm for unsupervised learning that reduces unsupervised learning to supervised learning.  Specifically, the subjectivity inherent in unsupervised decision-making is mitigated by leveraging knowledge acquired from prior, potentially heterogeneous, supervised learning tasks.  The versatility of this framework is demonstrated through comprehensive expositions and detailed experiments on various unsupervised problems, including (a) clustering, (b) outlier detection, and (c) similarity prediction, under a unified umbrella of meta-unsupervised-learning.  The paper also provides rigorous PAC-agnostic bounds to establish the theoretical foundations of the framework, showing that this framing of meta-clustering circumvents Kleinberg's impossibility theorem for clustering.
label: AI

title: A Basic Recurrent Neural Network Model
Abstract: This paper presents a model of a basic recurrent neural network (bRNN) that incorporates a separate linear term with a slightly "stable" fixed matrix to guarantee bounded solutions and fast dynamic response.  A state space viewpoint is formulated, and the constrained optimization Lagrange Multiplier (CLM) technique and the vector Calculus of Variations (CoV) are adapted to derive the (stochastic) gradient descent.  This approach avoids the commonly used re-application of the circular chain-rule and identifies error back-propagation with the co-state backward dynamic equations.  The paper asserts that this bRNN can effectively perform regression tracking of time series.  Moreover, the "vanishing and exploding" gradients are explicitly quantified and explained through co-state dynamics and update laws.  The adapted CoV framework can also integrate new loss functions in the network on any variable and for varied goals, such as supervised learning on outputs and unsupervised learning on internal (hidden) states.
label: AI

title: Automated capture and delivery of assistive task guidance with an eyewear computer: The GlaciAR system
Abstract: This paper describes and evaluates a mixed reality system designed to augment users in task guidance applications by combining automated and unsupervised information collection with minimally invasive video guides.  The system, called GlaciAR (Glass-enabled Contextual Interactions for Augmented Reality), is self-contained and operates by extracting contextual interactions from observing users performing actions.  GlaciAR is capable of: i) automatically determining moments of relevance based on a head motion attention model, ii) automatically generating video guidance information, iii) triggering these video guides based on object detection, iv) learning without supervision by observing multiple users, and v) operating fully on-board a current eyewear computer (Google Glass).  The paper details the components of GlaciAR and provides evaluations of how users can utilize the system to achieve three tasks.  This work represents a first step towards the development of systems that scale up the challenging authoring problem in guidance systems, enhancing people's natural abilities through minimally invasive visual guidance.
label: AI

title: A Deep Learning Approach To Multiple Kernel Fusion
Abstract: Kernel fusion is a widely used and effective approach for combining multiple features that capture different aspects of data.  Traditional methods for Multiple Kernel Learning (MKL) aim to learn the parameters for combining kernels through complex optimization procedures.  This paper proposes an alternative approach that creates dense embeddings for data using kernel similarities and employs a deep neural network architecture for fusing these embeddings.  To enhance the effectiveness of this network, the paper introduces kernel dropout regularization coupled with the use of an expanded set of composition kernels.  Experimental results on a real-world activity recognition dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture in fusing kernels, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
label: AI

title: Signal to noise in matching markets
Abstract: In many matching markets, one side "applies" to the other, and these applications are often costly and time-consuming (e.g., students applying to college).  Intuitively, simplifying the application process should benefit both sides of the market. Applicants could submit more applications, and recipients would have a larger pool of applicants to choose from.  However, this paper proposes and analyzes a simple model to understand scenarios where both sides of the market suffer from increased application numbers.  The main insights of the paper are derived from quantifying the signal-to-noise tradeoff in random matchings, as applications provide a signal of the applicants' preferences. When applications are costly, the signal is stronger, as the act of applying itself is meaningful. Therefore, more applications could potentially yield better matches, but fewer applications create stronger signals for the receiving side to learn true preferences.  The paper derives analytical characterizations of the expected quality of stable matchings in a simple utility model where applicants have an overall quality but also synergy with specific potential partners.  The results show how reducing application costs without introducing an effective signaling mechanism can lead to inefficiencies for both sides of the market.
label: AI

title: Here's My Point: Joint Pointer Architecture for Argument Mining
Abstract: One of the primary goals in automated argumentation mining is to uncover the argument structure present in argumentative text.  To determine this structure, it is crucial to understand how different individual components of the overall argument are linked.  The prevailing consensus in this field is that argument components form a hierarchy of persuasion, manifested as a tree structure. This work presents the first neural network-based approach to argumentation mining, focusing on two tasks: extracting links between argument components and classifying types of argument components. To address this problem, the paper proposes a joint model based on a Pointer Network architecture.  Pointer Networks are well-suited for this task due to: 1) their ability to account for the sequential nature of argument components, 2) their inherent enforcement of properties of the tree structure in argument relations, and 3) the applicability of hidden representations to auxiliary tasks.  To expand on the contribution of the original Pointer Network model, the paper constructs a joint model that simultaneously attempts to learn the type of argument component while predicting links between components.  The proposed joint model achieves state-of-the-art results on two separate evaluation corpora, significantly outperforming a regular Pointer Network model.  The findings indicate that optimizing for both tasks and adding a fully connected layer before recurrent neural network input is crucial for achieving high performance.
label: AI

title: ggRandomForests: Exploring Random Forest Survival
Abstract: Random Forest (RF) is a non-parametric statistical method requiring no distributional assumptions on the relationship between covariates and the response. RF is a robust, nonlinear technique that optimizes predictive accuracy by fitting an ensemble of trees to stabilize model estimates.  Random Survival Forests (RSF) extend Breiman's RF techniques to enable efficient nonparametric analysis of time-to-event data. The randomForestSRC package provides a unified treatment of Breiman's random forest for survival, regression, and classification problems.  The predictive accuracy of RF makes it an attractive alternative to parametric models.  However, the complexity and interpretability of the forest can hinder wider application of the method. This paper introduces the ggRandomForests package, tools for visually understanding random forest models grown in R using the randomForestSRC package.  The ggRandomForests package is designed to extract intermediate data objects from randomForestSRC objects and generate figures using the ggplot2 graphics package.  This document serves as a tutorial for building random forests for survival with the randomForestSRC package and using ggRandomForests to investigate the forest's construction.  The analysis of the Primary Biliary Cirrhosis of the liver data from a clinical trial at the Mayo Clinic demonstrates the power of using Random Forest methods for both prediction and information retrieval, especially in time-to-event data settings.
label: AI

title: Efficient iterative policy optimization
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of finding a good policy when the number of policy updates is limited. This is achieved by approximating the expected policy reward as a sequence of concave lower bounds, which can be efficiently maximized, significantly reducing the number of policy updates required for good performance.  The paper also extends existing methods to negative rewards, enabling the use of control variates.
label: AI

title: Partial Membership Latent Dirichlet Allocation
Abstract: Topic models (e.g., pLSA, LDA, sLDA) have been widely used for segmenting imagery.  However, these models are restricted to crisp segmentation, forcing a visual word (an image patch) to belong to only one topic.  Many images contain regions that cannot be assigned a crisp categorical label (e.g., transition regions between fog and ground or sand and water). In these cases, a visual word is best represented with partial memberships across multiple topics. To address this, the paper presents a partial membership latent Dirichlet allocation (PM-LDA) model and an associated parameter estimation algorithm.  This model is suitable for imagery where a visual word may be a mixture of multiple topics.  Experimental results on visual and sonar imagery demonstrate that PM-LDA can produce both crisp and soft semantic image segmentations, a capability lacking in previous topic modeling methods.
label: AI

title: Optimal bandwidth estimation for a fast manifold learning algorithm to detect circular structure in high-dimensional data
Abstract: This paper provides a method for inferring the existence of topological circularity in high-dimensional datasets in $\\mathbb{R}^d$ from its projection in $\\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained through a fast manifold learning map.  This map is a function of the high-dimensional dataset $\\mathbb{X}$ and a specific choice of a positive real $\\sigma$, known as the bandwidth parameter.  Simultaneously, the paper provides a way to estimate the optimal bandwidth for fast manifold learning in this setting by minimizing these functions of bandwidth.  The paper also presents limit theorems to characterize the behavior of the proposed functions of bandwidth. |||
label: AI

title: Bayesian Optimization with Shape Constraints
Abstract: Bayesian optimization typically makes minimal assumptions about the objective function. However, incorporating shape constraints can be beneficial in applications like hyperparameter tuning and decision analysis. This paper proposes a methodology for integrating shape constraints into the Bayesian optimization framework, demonstrating positive results from simple applications. This suggests that Bayesian optimization with shape constraints is a promising area for further research.
label: AI

title: Joint Network Coding and Machine Learning for Error-prone Wireless Broadcast
Abstract: Reliable data broadcasting to multiple receivers over lossy wireless channels is challenging due to varying link conditions. Automatic Repeat-reQuest (ARQ) retransmission schemes are bandwidth-inefficient due to data duplication. Network coding (NC) offers improved bandwidth efficiency by combining lost packets for retransmission but faces challenges in determining which packets to combine due to disrupted feedback. This paper proposes a novel data encoding scheme at the transmitter by integrating network coding and machine learning (NCML). NCML leverages historical feedback signals to train a classifier that predicts the states of transmitted packets based on corrupted feedback, enabling effective data mixing. Extensive simulations confirm the efficiency of this approach, achieving a 90% average accuracy in classifying packet states and significant bandwidth gains compared to ARQ and NC schemes across different transmission terrains, power levels, and distances.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised domain adaptation in brain lesion segmentation with adversarial networks
Abstract: Despite significant advances in automatic segmentation systems using machine learning, their performance degrades when applied to new data differing from the training data, such as variations in imaging protocols. Manually annotating new data is impractical. This work explores unsupervised domain adaptation using adversarial neural networks to train a segmentation method that is more invariant to data differences, requiring no test domain annotations. The method learns domain-invariant features by counteracting an adversarial network that attempts to classify the data domain based on segmentation network activations. Additionally, a multi-connected domain discriminator is proposed for enhanced adversarial training. Evaluation on two MR databases of subjects with traumatic brain injuries, acquired using different scanners and protocols, demonstrates segmentation accuracies close to the upper bound of supervised domain adaptation.
label: AI

title: Improving Blind Steganalysis in Spatial Domain using a Criterion to Choose the Appropriate Steganalyzer between CNN and SRM+EC
Abstract: Current state-of-the-art image steganalysis approaches typically rely on classifiers trained with features extracted by rich image models. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) embody both feature extraction and classification, previous studies have explored CNN-based steganalyzers. This work proposes a criterion for selecting either CNN or SRM+EC (Spatial Rich Models and Ensemble Classifier) for a given image, achieving detection capabilities superior to either method alone. The approach is evaluated using S-UNIWARD, MiPOD, and HILL steganographic algorithms and demonstrates improved detection capabilities compared to individual methods, particularly in blind steganalysis scenarios.
label: AI

title: MARTA GANs: Unsupervised Representation Learning for Remote Sensing Image Classification
Abstract: Supervised learning using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is often challenging for remotely sensed image classification due to limited labeled data availability. This paper proposes an unsupervised model called MARTA GANs (Multiple-Layer Feature-Matching Generative Adversarial Networks) to learn representations from unlabeled data. MARTA GANs consists of a generative model (G) and a discriminative model (D), treating D as a feature extractor.  A fusion layer is used to combine mid-level and global features, enabling G to produce realistic images and D to learn better representations from the training data provided by G. Classification results on two remote sensing image databases show significant performance improvements compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: The Pessimistic Limits and Possibilities of Margin-based Losses in Semi-supervised Learning
Abstract: This paper investigates the potential for semi-supervised learning to improve linear classifiers with convex margin-based surrogate losses.  It is shown that for decreasing losses, no semi-supervised approach can guarantee an improvement over the supervised classifier. However, for increasing losses, safe improvements are demonstrably achievable.
label: AI

title: Multi-Party Privacy-Preserving Record Linkage using Bloom Filters
Abstract: Privacy-preserving record linkage (PPRL) aims to identify records from different sources that refer to the same real-world entity without revealing sensitive information. While most PPRL techniques focus on two sources, many real-world applications require linking data from multiple sources. This paper proposes a solution for multi-party PPRL using Bloom filter encoding and distributed secure summation. The protocol efficiently identifies matching record sets with a similarity above a given threshold while ensuring privacy under the semi-honest adversary model. Evaluation on a large voter registration database demonstrates the scalability, linkage quality, and privacy of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: The Predictron: End-To-End Learning and Planning
Abstract: A key challenge in artificial intelligence is developing effective models for planning. This paper introduces the predictron architecture, a fully abstract model represented by a Markov reward process. The predictron can be rolled forward multiple planning steps, accumulating internal rewards and values at different planning depths. It is trained end-to-end to accurately approximate the true value function. Applied to procedurally generated random mazes and a pool game simulator, the predictron demonstrates significantly more accurate predictions compared to conventional deep neural network architectures.
label: AI

title: Provable learning of Noisy-or Networks
Abstract: Many machine learning applications utilize latent variable models to explain data structure, where visible variables are explained as a probabilistic function of hidden variables.  Finding maximum likelihood parameters is NP-hard, even for simple settings. Recent years have seen the development of efficient algorithms for models with linear structures like topic models, mixture models, and hidden Markov models. These algorithms leverage matrix or tensor decomposition and make assumptions about model parameters.  However, tensor decomposition becomes less effective with nonlinearities in latent variable models. This paper explores applying tensor decomposition for learning single-layer noisy-OR networks, demonstrating its applicability for models with nonlinearities. The key novelty lies in analyzing tensor decomposition in the presence of systematic error, requiring a re-evaluation of all steps.  The analysis assumes network parameters are drawn from a probability distribution but suggests wider applicability.
label: AI

title: Automatic Composition and Optimization of Multicomponent Predictive Systems With an Extended Auto-WEKA
Abstract: Composition and parameterization of multicomponent predictive systems (MCPSs) consisting of data transformation chains is a challenging task. Auto-WEKA automates algorithm selection and hyperparameter (CASH) optimization. This paper extends CASH and Auto-WEKA to support MCPSs, including preprocessing steps for classification and regression tasks. The optimization problem involves searching for MCPS solutions represented by parameterized Petri nets. Extensive experiments examine the impact of a significantly expanded search space, using three optimization strategies to compose MCPSs for 21 datasets. The diversity of MCPSs demonstrates the feasibility and benefit of fully and automatically exploiting data cleaning and preprocessing techniques. Results on seven real chemical production datasets highlight the potential impact on predictive model development, maintenance, and scalability.
label: AI

title: Clustering with Confidence: Finding Clusters with Statistical Guarantees
Abstract: Clustering is a widely used unsupervised learning method for finding data structure. However, the resulting clusters lack guarantees on robustness, and slight changes in the data or stochastic components in the clustering algorithm can lead to different clusters. This paper proposes a technique for quantifying clustering solution instability and identifying robust "core clusters," defined as clusters where the co-occurrence probability of each data item is at least 1-alpha. The approach links the core clustering problem to finding the largest maximal cliques in a graph and can be applied to both clustering and classification algorithms. Evaluation on simulated and real datasets demonstrates the robustness of the obtained clusters.
label: AI

title: Semantic Perceptual Image Compression using Deep Convolution Networks
Abstract: Improving the visual quality of lossy image and video compression has been a significant challenge. Recent advances in computing power and large training datasets have spurred the application of deep learning CNNs to image recognition and processing tasks. This paper presents a CNN tailored to semantic image understanding for achieving higher visual quality in lossy compression. A slight increase in encoder complexity allows for the use of a standard JPEG decoder. Unlike object detection techniques, this model identifies objects in a single pass without object position labeling.  The architecture generates a map highlighting semantically-salient regions for higher quality encoding compared to background regions. Experiments on the Kodak PhotoCD and MIT Saliency Benchmark datasets demonstrate improved visual quality for the same compressed size.
label: AI

title: A Hybrid Both Filter and Wrapper Feature Selection Method for Microarray Classification
Abstract: Gene expression data is widely used in disease analysis and cancer diagnosis, but its high dimensionality poses challenges for microarray classification. Feature selection is crucial for pre-treatment, reducing computational time and cost while improving accuracy. This study combines information gain as a filter approach and improved binary particle swarm optimization as a wrapper approach for feature selection. The selected gene subsets are then evaluated for their classification performance. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively selects fewer genes while achieving better classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: Reproducible Pattern Recognition Research: The Case of Optimistic SSL
Abstract: This paper discusses the approach and trade-offs involved in making a paper on a conceptual topic in pattern recognition research fully reproducible. It defines reproducibility, outlines the tools used, describes the analysis setup, presents examples of alternative analyses enabled by the code, and provides insights on reproducibility in research.
label: AI

title: A Sparse Nonlinear Classifier Design Using AUC Optimization
Abstract: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is a crucial performance measure for imbalanced datasets. Maximizing AUC performance is a key research problem, and using a max-margin surrogate loss function approximates AUC optimization as a pairwise rankSVM learning problem. While batch learning methods for the kernelized version suffer from scalability and may not result in sparse classifiers, online learning algorithms have gained interest. However, the AUC performance of nonlinear classifiers designed using online methods often falls short of batch learning methods. This paper proposes a scalable algorithm for maximizing AUC performance by greedily adding basis functions to the classifier model, leading to sparse classifiers with faster inference. Experimental results demonstrate that the achieved sparsity can be significantly lower than Kernel RankSVM without significantly affecting AUC performance.
label: AI

title: ASAP: Asynchronous Approximate Data-Parallel Computation
Abstract: Emerging workloads like graph processing and machine learning involve approximations due to data scale and stochastic algorithms. These workloads are often distributed using bulk-synchronous processing (BSP) or other synchronous paradigms, but synchronization overheads are significant. Asynchronous and stale data processing are used to improve performance, but this can lead to reduced accuracy. This paper presents ASAP, a model providing asynchronous and approximate processing semantics for data-parallel computation. ASAP uses NOTIFY-ACK semantics for fine-grained worker synchronization and stochastic reduce for approximate but guaranteed convergence. Results show that ASAP reduces synchronization costs, providing 2-10X speedups in convergence and up to 10X network cost savings for distributed machine learning applications, while providing strong convergence guarantees.
label: AI

title: Concentration Inequalities for Random Sets
Abstract: In a large population where individuals are colored red with probability p, this paper investigates the imbalance in a finite sub-population. The imbalance is defined as the difference between the number of reds in the sub-population and p times its size. High-probability upper bounds (tail-bounds) on this imbalance are presented. To facilitate this, a new measure called the "UI dimension" is introduced, quantifying the richness of a set-family.  Three simple rules for upper-bounding the UI dimension are provided.  The upper bounds on the sub-population imbalance depend on its size and the UI dimension of its support. Connections to known concepts from machine learning, including the VC dimension and Rademacher complexity, are explored.
label: AI

title: Monte Carlo Sort for unreliable human comparisons
Abstract: Sorting algorithms have been extensively studied for decades, typically relying on pairwise comparisons. However, sorting lists based on subjective or complex judgments is a common task in areas such as marketing research, recruiting, and sporting tournaments.  This paper develops a novel sorting algorithm where each comparison reflects a subjective human judgment.  The algorithm incorporates a finite error rate for each judgment and prioritizes the most informative comparisons to minimize human input.  The Discrete Adiabatic Monte Carlo approach leverages gradual information acquisition by tracking plausible hypotheses, which are updated after each comparison.
label: AI

title: Rank-One NMF-Based Initialization for NMF and Relative Error Bounds under a Geometric Assumption
Abstract: This paper proposes a geometric assumption for nonnegative data matrices, enabling deterministic and probabilistic upper bounds on the relative error of nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF). The proposed algorithm first uses the geometric assumption for exact clustering of data matrix columns and then employs several rank-one NMFs for final decomposition.  Evaluation on data matrices generated from a statistical model demonstrates comparable relative errors to classical NMF algorithms but with significantly faster speeds.  Applications to face image and hyperspectral imaging datasets showcase the algorithm's effectiveness as an initialization for other NMF algorithms at low computational cost.  Further analysis on face and text datasets demonstrates improved clustering performance when combined with classical NMF algorithms.

title: Theory-guided Data Science: A New Paradigm for Scientific Discovery from Data
Abstract: While data science models have proven successful in commercial domains, their application in scientific problems involving complex physical phenomena has been limited.  Theory-guided data science (TGDS) is an emerging paradigm that aims to leverage scientific knowledge for enhancing data science models in scientific discovery. The vision of TGDS is to introduce scientific consistency for learning generalizable models and to produce interpretable models that advance scientific understanding. TGDS has gained prominence in disciplines such as turbulence modeling, material discovery, and climate science. This paper provides a formal conceptualization of TGDS and presents a taxonomy of research themes. It describes various approaches for integrating domain knowledge and highlights promising avenues for realizing the full potential of theory-guided data science. |||

title: Distributed Real-Time Sentiment Analysis for Big Data Social Streams
Abstract: The rise of big data has led to the emergence of data-centric systems that continuously process high-velocity data streams. Real-time analytics on stream data has become a prominent research area, aiming to provide immediate insights into ongoing events with minimal delay. The primary challenge in real-time stream data processing lies in the impossibility of storing all data instances. Consequently, online analytical algorithms are employed to analyze the data on the fly. To enable efficient real-time analytics, data pre-processing is crucial, ensuring that only a concise summary of the stream is stored in the main memory. Additionally, the high data arrival rate necessitates rapid processing times for each data instance to avoid data loss. Furthermore, the learning algorithm must deliver high analytical accuracy. Sentinel, a distributed system written in Java, addresses this challenge by distributing both the processing and learning tasks. Built upon Apache Storm, a distributed computing platform, Sentinel utilizes the Vertical Hoeffding Tree, a parallel decision tree-learning algorithm derived from VFDT, enabling parallel classification in distributed environments. Sentinel also leverages SpaceSaving to maintain a summary of the data stream, storing it in a synopsis data structure. The effectiveness of Sentinel is demonstrated through its application on the Twitter Public Stream API, and the results are analyzed.

title: Robust LSTM-Autoencoders for Face De-Occlusion in the Wild
Abstract: Face recognition technology has advanced significantly in recent years. However, recognizing partially occluded faces remains a significant challenge for existing face recognizers, hindering their applicability in real-world surveillance and security applications. While extensive research has focused on developing face de-occlusion methods, most existing methods only perform well under constrained conditions, such as when all faces belong to a predefined closed set. This paper proposes a robust LSTM-Autoencoders (RLA) model to effectively restore partially occluded faces even in challenging real-world scenarios. The RLA model comprises two LSTM components: one for occlusion-robust face encoding and another for recurrent occlusion removal. The multi-scale spatial LSTM encoder reads facial patches of various scales sequentially to generate a latent representation, achieving occlusion-robustness by mitigating the influence of occlusion on specific patches. The LSTM decoder, featuring a dual channel architecture, reconstructs the entire face and simultaneously detects occlusion. Leveraging the capabilities of LSTM, the decoder breaks down the face de-occlusion task into restoring the occluded part step by step. Moreover, to minimize identity information loss and guarantee face recognition accuracy on recovered faces, an identity-preserving adversarial training scheme is introduced to further enhance RLA. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real datasets containing faces with occlusion clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RLA in removing diverse types of facial occlusion at various locations. The proposed method also significantly outperforms other de-occlusion methods in promoting recognition performance on partially-occluded faces.

title: Learning Non-Lambertian Object Intrinsics across ShapeNet Categories
Abstract: The problem of recovering diffuse albedo, shading, and specular highlights from a single image of a non-Lambertian object is addressed. A large-scale object intrinsics database, built upon existing 3D models from the ShapeNet database, is utilized. Rendered with realistic environment maps, millions of synthetic images of objects and their corresponding albedo, shading, and specular ground-truth images are used to train an encoder-decoder convolutional neural network (CNN). Once trained, the network can decompose an image into the product of albedo and shading components, along with an additive specular component. The CNN achieves accurate and sharp results in this classic inverse problem of computer vision, attributed to skip layer connections at corresponding resolutions from the encoder to the decoder. Benchmarked on the ShapeNet and MIT intrinsics datasets, the proposed model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin. The CNN is trained and tested on different object categories. Surprisingly, the intrinsics CNN exhibits strong generalization capabilities across categories. Analysis indicates that feature learning at the encoder stage plays a crucial role in developing a universal representation across categories. The synthetic data trained model is applied to images and videos downloaded from the internet, demonstrating robust and realistic intrinsics results. High-quality non-Lambertian intrinsics have potential applications in various areas, including image-based albedo and specular editing.

title: End-to-End Data Visualization by Metric Learning and Coordinate Transformation
Abstract: This paper introduces a deep nonlinear metric learning framework for data visualization on image datasets. The Triangular Similarity is proposed and proven to be equivalent to the Cosine Similarity in measuring the similarity between data pairs. Based on this novel similarity, a geometrically motivated loss function, the triangular loss, is developed for optimizing a metric learning system composed of two identical convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The deep nonlinear system can be effectively trained using a hybrid algorithm based on the conventional backpropagation algorithm. Interestingly, leveraging classical manifold learning theories, the proposed system offers two different views to visualize the outputs. The second view provides improved classification results compared to state-of-the-art methods in visualizable spaces.

title: Steerable CNNs
Abstract: The invariance and equivariance properties of a representation are crucial for success in numerous vision tasks. This paper presents Steerable Convolutional Neural Networks, an efficient and flexible class of equivariant convolutional networks. Steerable CNNs achieve state-of-the-art results on the CIFAR image classification benchmark. The mathematical theory of steerable representations reveals a type system where any steerable representation is a composition of elementary feature types, each associated with a specific type of symmetry. The parameter cost of a steerable filter bank is shown to depend on the types of input and output features, enabling the construction of CNNs that utilize parameters effectively.
