title: Physically-Based Rendering for Indoor Scene Understanding Using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Indoor scene understanding is central to applications such as robot navigation and human companion assistance. In recent years, data-driven deep neural networks have outperformed traditional approaches due to their representation learning capabilities. One bottleneck in training for better representations is the need for a substantial amount of available per-pixel ground truth data, which is essential for core scene understanding tasks like semantic segmentation, normal prediction, and object edge detection. To address this challenge, several works have proposed using synthetic data. However, a systematic study of how such synthetic data is generated is lacking. This work introduces a large-scale synthetic dataset with 400K physically-based rendered images from 45K realistic 3D indoor scenes. We investigate the effects of rendering methods and scene lighting on training for three computer vision tasks: surface normal prediction, semantic segmentation, and object boundary detection. This study provides insights into best practices for training with synthetic data (more realistic rendering is beneficial) and shows that pretraining with our new synthetic dataset can improve results beyond the current state-of-the-art on all three tasks.
label: AI

title: A Context-aware Attention Network for Interactive Question Answering
Abstract: Neural network-based sequence-to-sequence models within an encoder-decoder framework have been successfully applied to solve Question Answering (QA) problems, predicting answers from statements and questions. However, nearly all previous models have failed to consider detailed context information and unknown states, where systems lack sufficient information to answer given questions. These scenarios with incomplete or ambiguous information are prevalent in the setting of Interactive Question Answering (IQA). To address this challenge, we develop a novel model employing context-dependent word-level attention for more accurate statement representations and question-guided sentence-level attention for enhanced context modeling. We also generate unique IQA datasets to test our model, which will be made publicly available. Through these attention mechanisms, our model accurately determines when it can output an answer or when it requires generating a supplementary question for additional input, depending on different contexts. When available, user feedback is encoded and directly applied to update sentence-level attention to infer an answer. Extensive experiments on QA and IQA datasets quantitatively demonstrate the effectiveness of our model, showing significant improvement over state-of-the-art conventional QA models.
label: AI

title: Statistical Distances and Their Role in Robustness
Abstract: Statistical distances, divergences, and similar quantities have a long history and play a fundamental role in statistics, machine learning, and associated scientific disciplines. However, within the statistical literature, this extensive role has often been relegated to the background, with other aspects of statistical problems being viewed as more central, interesting, or important. The behind-the-scenes role of statistical distances is evident in estimation, where we frequently use estimators based on minimizing a distance, explicitly or implicitly, but rarely investigate how the properties of a distance determine the properties of the estimators. Distances are also prominent in goodness-of-fit, but the typical question we ask is "how powerful is this method against a set of interesting alternatives" rather than "what aspect of the distance between the hypothetical model and the alternative are we measuring?" This paper focuses on describing the statistical properties of some of the distance measures we have found to be most important and visible. We illustrate the robust nature of Neyman's chi-squared and the non-robust nature of Pearson's chi-squared statistics and discuss the concept of discretization robustness.
label: AI

title: Efficient Action Detection in Untrimmed Videos via Multi-Task Learning
Abstract: This paper investigates the joint learning of action recognition and temporal localization in long, untrimmed videos. We utilize a multi-task learning framework that performs the three highly related steps of action proposal, action recognition, and action localization refinement in parallel, rather than the standard sequential pipeline that performs these steps in order. We develop a novel temporal actionness regression module that estimates the proportion of a clip containing action. We use it for temporal localization but it could have other applications, such as video retrieval, surveillance, summarization, etc. We also introduce random shear augmentation during training to simulate viewpoint change. We evaluate our framework on three popular video benchmarks. Results demonstrate that our joint model is efficient in terms of storage and computation since we do not need to compute and cache dense trajectory features, and it is several times faster than its sequential ConvNets counterpart. Despite being more efficient, our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy.
label: AI

title: Microstructure Representation and Reconstruction of Heterogeneous Materials via Deep Belief Network for Computational Material Design
Abstract: Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) aims to accelerate the optimal design of complex material systems by integrating material science and design automation. For tractable ICME, it is necessary that (1) a structural feature space be identified to allow reconstruction of new designs, and (2) the reconstruction process be property-preserving. Most existing structural presentation schemes rely on the designer's understanding of specific material systems to identify geometric and statistical features, which can be biased and insufficient for reconstructing physically meaningful microstructures of complex material systems. In this paper, we develop a feature learning mechanism based on convolutional deep belief networks to automate a two-way conversion between microstructures and their lower-dimensional feature representations, achieving a 1000-fold dimension reduction from the microstructure space. The proposed model is applied to a wide spectrum of heterogeneous material systems with distinct microstructural features, including Ti-6Al-4V alloy, Pb63-Sn37 alloy, Fontainebleau sandstone, and spherical colloids, to produce material reconstructions that closely resemble the original samples in terms of 2-point correlation functions and mean critical fracture strength. This capability is not achievable by existing synthesis methods that rely on the Markovian assumption of material microstructures.
label: AI

title: Detecting Unusual Input-Output Associations in Multivariate Conditional Data
Abstract: Despite significant advancements in outlier detection research in recent years, the majority of existing methods are designed solely to detect unconditional outliers, which correspond to unusual data patterns expressed in the joint space of all data attributes. Such methods are not applicable when seeking to detect conditional outliers that reflect unusual responses associated with a given context or condition. This work focuses on multivariate conditional outlier detection, a specialized type of conditional outlier detection problem where data instances consist of multi-dimensional input (context) and output (responses) pairs. We present a novel outlier detection framework that identifies abnormal input-output associations in data using a decomposable conditional probabilistic model learned from all data instances. Since components of this model can vary in quality, we combine them using weights reflecting their reliability in outlier assessment. We study two methods for calculating component weights: global, which relies on all data, and local, which relies only on instances similar to the target instance. Experimental results on data from various domains demonstrate the ability of our framework to successfully identify multivariate conditional outliers.
label: AI

title: Top-down Visual Saliency Guided by Captions
Abstract: Neural image/video captioning models can generate accurate descriptions, but their internal process of mapping regions to words is a black box, making it difficult to explain. Top-down neural saliency methods can identify important regions given a high-level semantic task, such as object classification, but cannot use a natural language sentence as the top-down input for the task. In this paper, we propose Caption-Guided Visual Saliency to expose the region-to-word mapping in modern encoder-decoder networks and demonstrate that it is learned implicitly from caption training data without any pixel-level annotations. Our approach can produce spatial or spatiotemporal heatmaps for both predicted captions and for arbitrary query sentences. It recovers saliency without the overhead of introducing explicit attention layers and can be used to analyze various existing model architectures and improve their design. Evaluation on large-scale video and image datasets shows that our approach achieves comparable captioning performance with existing methods while providing more accurate saliency heatmaps. Our code is available at visionlearninggroup.github.io/caption-guided-saliency/.
label: AI

title: Distributed Dictionary Learning
Abstract: This paper investigates distributed Dictionary Learning (DL) problems where the learning task is distributed across a multi-agent network with time-varying (nonsymmetric) connectivity. This formulation is relevant in big-data scenarios where massive amounts of data are collected or stored in different locations, making it impractical to aggregate and/or process all data in a fusion center due to resource limitations, communication overhead, or privacy concerns. We develop a general distributed algorithmic framework for the (nonconvex) DL problem and establish its asymptotic convergence. The new method relies on Successive Convex Approximation (SCA) techniques coupled with i) a gradient tracking mechanism instrumental for locally estimating the missing global information, and ii) a consensus step, as a mechanism to distribute computations among the agents. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first distributed algorithm with provable convergence for the DL problem and, more generally, bi-convex optimization problems over (time-varying) directed graphs.
label: AI

title: Loss is its own Reward: Self-Supervision for Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Reinforcement learning optimizes policies for expected cumulative reward. Is this narrow form of supervision necessary? Reward is often delayed and sparse for many tasks, making it a difficult and impoverished signal for end-to-end optimization. To augment reward, we consider a range of self-supervised tasks that incorporate states, actions, and successors to provide auxiliary losses. These losses offer ubiquitous and instantaneous supervision for representation learning, even in the absence of reward. While current results show that learning from reward alone is feasible, pure reinforcement learning methods are constrained by computational and data efficiency issues that can be addressed by auxiliary losses. Self-supervised pre-training and joint optimization improve the data efficiency and policy returns of end-to-end reinforcement learning. |||
label: AI

title: Stacking machine learning classifiers to identify Higgs bosons at the LHC
Abstract: Machine learning algorithms are widely used to classify signal and background events in particle physics. This paper compares the performance of stacked generalization against two state-of-the-art algorithms: a deep neural network (DNN) and a scalable machine learning system for tree boosting. The comparison is performed in the context of discovering a new neutral Higgs boson and the Standard Model Higgs to tau leptons channel at the 8 TeV LHC. Results indicate that stacking three algorithms performs approximately 16% worse than DNN but requires significantly less computation. However, stacking outperforms boosted decision trees. Moreover, using stacked classifiers in a multivariate statistical analysis (MVA) significantly enhances statistical significance compared to cut-and-count in both Higgs processes. This suggests that combining an ensemble of simpler and faster ML algorithms with MVA tools is a more effective approach than building complex state-of-the-art algorithms for cut-and-count analysis.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Decision Process for Cost-Efficient Dynamic Ranking via Crowdsourcing
Abstract: Rank aggregation based on pairwise comparisons over a set of items has numerous applications. While many rank aggregation algorithms have been developed, an important question remains: how to efficiently collect a large amount of high-quality pairwise comparisons for ranking purposes. Crowdsourcing services offer a solution by employing a crowd of workers to conduct pairwise comparisons with small monetary rewards. However, worker reliability and pair ambiguity vary, necessitating an efficient allocation of the limited budget for comparisons. This paper models the active sampling problem in crowdsourced ranking as a Bayesian Markov decision process. The model dynamically selects item pairs and workers to optimize ranking accuracy under a budget constraint. A computationally efficient sampling policy based on knowledge gradient and a moment matching technique for posterior approximation are developed. Experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate that the proposed policy achieves high ranking accuracy with lower labeling cost.
label: AI

title: Learning Motion Patterns in Videos
Abstract: Determining whether an object is in motion, independent of camera motion, remains a challenging problem. This paper tackles this challenge by learning motion patterns in videos. The core of the approach is a fully convolutional network trained entirely on synthetic video sequences with ground-truth optical flow and motion segmentation. This encoder-decoder architecture first learns a coarse representation of optical flow field features, then refines it iteratively to generate motion labels at the original high-resolution. Further improvement is achieved through an objectness map and a conditional random field, addressing errors in optical flow and focusing on moving "things" rather than "stuff." The output label of each pixel indicates whether it has undergone independent motion, regardless of camera motion. The paper demonstrates the benefits of this learning framework on the moving object segmentation task, achieving state-of-the-art results on the DAVIS benchmark dataset and the Berkeley motion segmentation database.
label: AI

title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
Abstract: The current mainstream approach to training natural language systems involves exposing them to large amounts of text. However, this passive learning method is inadequate for developing interactive machines like conversational agents. This paper proposes a framework for language learning based on multi-agent communication. The learning process is studied in the context of referential games, where a sender and a receiver observe a pair of images. The sender identifies a target image and communicates its selection to the receiver using a fixed vocabulary. The receiver must then identify the target based on the message. Through this communication process, agents develop their own language interactively. The paper demonstrates that two networks with simple configurations are capable of learning to coordinate in the referential game. Further exploration investigates modifications to the game environment to align the "word meanings" induced in the game with intuitive semantic properties of the images. Additionally, a simple strategy for grounding the agents' code into natural language is presented. These advancements are crucial steps towards developing machines capable of productive communication with humans.
label: AI

title: A Unified Framework for Tumor Proliferation Score Prediction in Breast Histopathology
Abstract: This paper presents a unified framework for predicting tumor proliferation scores from breast histopathology whole slide images. The framework offers a fully automated solution for predicting both a molecular data-based and a mitosis counting-based tumor proliferation score. It integrates three modules: an image processing component for handling whole slide images, a deep learning-based mitosis detection network, and a proliferation scores prediction module. The system achieved a quadratic weighted Cohen's kappa of 0.567 in mitosis counting-based score prediction and an F1-score of 0.652 in mitosis detection. On Spearman's correlation coefficient, evaluating predictive accuracy on the molecular data-based score, the system achieved 0.6171. This approach won first place in all three tasks of the Tumor Proliferation Assessment Challenge 2016, a MICCAI grand challenge.
label: AI

title: Collaborative Filtering with User-Item Co-Autoregressive Models
Abstract: Deep neural networks have shown potential in collaborative filtering (CF). However, existing neural approaches are either user-based or item-based, failing to explicitly leverage all underlying information. This paper proposes CF-UIcA, a neural co-autoregressive model for CF tasks, which exploits the structural correlation in both user and item domains. The co-autoregression allows for incorporating extra desired properties for different tasks. Additionally, an efficient stochastic learning algorithm is developed to handle large-scale datasets. CF-UIcA is evaluated on two popular benchmarks, MovieLens 1M and Netflix, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both rating prediction and top-N recommendation tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Robust Classification of Graph-Based Data
Abstract: This paper proposes a graph-based classification method for semi-supervised learning with Euclidean data and classification with graph data. The manifold learning technique is based on a convex optimization problem involving a convex quadratic regularization term and a concave quadratic loss function with a carefully chosen trade-off parameter to maintain convexity. Empirically, the concave loss function enhances robustness in the presence of noisy labels. Additionally, the loss function is more similar to a classification loss, unlike several other methods that treat graph-based classification problems as regression problems.
label: AI

title: A Survey of Deep Network Solutions for Learning Control in Robotics: From Reinforcement to Imitation
Abstract: Deep learning techniques have been widely applied, achieving state-of-the-art results in various fields. This survey focuses on deep learning solutions for learning control policies in robotics applications. The discussion centers around the two main paradigms for learning control with deep networks: deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and imitation learning. For DRL, the survey starts with traditional reinforcement learning algorithms, showing their extension to the deep context and effective mechanisms that can be integrated with DRL algorithms. Representative works utilizing DRL to solve navigation and manipulation tasks in robotics are then introduced. The survey then addresses the challenge of the reality gap, focusing on transferring DRL policies trained in simulation to real-world scenarios, and summarizes robotics simulation platforms for DRL research. For imitation learning, the survey explores its three main categories: behavior cloning, inverse reinforcement learning, and generative adversarial imitation learning, discussing their formulations and robotics applications. Finally, the survey discusses open challenges and research frontiers in this field.

title: Nanoindenting the Chelyabinsk meteorite to learn about impact deflection effects in asteroids
Abstract: The Chelyabinsk meteorite is a highly shocked, low-porosity, ordinary chondrite, likely similar to S- or Q-type asteroids. Nanoindentation experiments on this meteorite provide key data for understanding the physical properties of near-Earth asteroids. Tests at different length scales reveal information about the local mechanical properties of the minerals comprising the meteorite, including reduced Young's modulus, hardness, elastic recovery, and fracture toughness. These tests also provide insights into the potential for deflecting threatening asteroids using kinetic projectiles. The findings reveal that differences in mechanical properties between regions of the meteorite, affecting impact efficiency, are not due to compositional variations. A low mean particle size, attributed to repetitive shock, can increase hardness, while low porosity promotes higher momentum multiplication. Momentum multiplication, the ratio of the target's momentum change to the projectile's momentum, indicates impact efficiency. The light-colored lithology materials in the Chelyabinsk meteorite exhibit higher momentum multiplication values compared to other regions. Additionally, a low fracture toughness in the shock-melt veins of Chelyabinsk promotes material ejection after impact, further enhancing momentum multiplication. These findings are relevant to the growing interest in asteroid deflection missions, such as the Asteroid Impact and Deflection Assessment mission, a collaboration between the European Space Agency and NASA.
label: AI

title: An Empirical Study of Language CNN for Image Captioning
Abstract: Language models based on recurrent neural networks have dominated recent image caption generation tasks. This paper introduces a Language CNN model suitable for statistical language modeling tasks, achieving competitive performance in image captioning. Unlike previous models that predict the next word based on the previous word and hidden state, the Language CNN utilizes all previous words, allowing it to model long-range dependencies critical for image captioning. The effectiveness of this approach is validated on two datasets, MS COCO and Flickr30K. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms vanilla recurrent neural network-based language models and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: A deep learning approach for predicting the quality of online health expert question-answering services
Abstract: Currently, health consumers are increasingly seeking health-related information online, offering convenient and cost-effective access to healthcare. Online health expert question-answering (HQA) services are prevalent, as consumers prefer answers from professional physicians. However, the quality of these answers can vary, making it crucial to predict answer quality via machine learning. Predicting HQA answer quality presents challenges due to data sparsity in short text answers and the lack of community features like best answers and user votes. This paper addresses these problems by defining HQA answer quality prediction as a classification task. First, based on HQA service characteristics and medical expert feedback, a standard for evaluating HQA service answer quality is established. Novel non-textual features, including surface linguistic features and social features, are then proposed based on HQA service characteristics. Finally, a deep belief network (DBN)-based HQA answer quality prediction framework is proposed to predict answer quality by learning high-level hidden semantic representations from physicians' answers. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework overcomes the problem of sparse textual features in short text answers and effectively identifies high-quality answers.
label: AI

title: Robust Learning with Kernel Mean p-Power Error Loss
Abstract: Correntropy is a second-order statistical measure in kernel space, successfully applied in robust learning and signal processing. This paper defines a nonsecond-order statistical measure in kernel space, called the kernel mean-p power error (KMPE), which includes the correntropic loss (CLoss) as a special case. The paper presents basic properties of KMPE and applies it to extreme learning machine (ELM) and principal component analysis (PCA), developing two robust learning algorithms: ELM-KMPE and PCA-KMPE. Experimental results on synthetic and benchmark data show that the developed algorithms consistently outperform existing methods.
label: AI

title: Personalized Video Recommendation Using Rich Contents from Videos
Abstract: Video recommendation has become essential for helping users navigate massive video libraries and discover relevant content. Existing video recommender systems rely on user-video interactions and single specific content features. However, their performance deteriorates significantly when specific content features are unavailable. Recognizing the abundance of rich content (e.g., text, audio, motion) within videos, this paper explores how to utilize this information to overcome limitations caused by the absence of specific features. Specifically, a novel general framework named collaborative embedding regression (CER) is proposed. This framework integrates arbitrary single content features with user-video interactions to effectively recommend videos in both in-matrix and out-of-matrix scenarios. Extensive experiments on two real-world large-scale datasets demonstrate that CER outperforms existing recommender models with any single content feature and is more time-efficient. Furthermore, a priority-based late fusion (PRI) method is proposed to leverage the benefits of integrating multiple content features. Experimental results show that PRI improves the baseline performance and outperforms existing fusion methods.
label: AI

title: Supernova 1604, Kepler's supernova, and its remnant
Abstract: Supernova 1604 is the last Galactic supernova with documented historical records. Johannes Kepler's name is associated with it due to his detailed account of observations made by himself and European colleagues. This supernova was likely a Type Ia supernova, exploding 350 pc to 750 pc above the Galactic plane. Its remnant, known as Kepler's supernova remnant, shows clear evidence of interaction with nitrogen-rich material in the north/northwest part of the remnant. Given its height above the Galactic plane, this material must have originated from mass loss from the supernova progenitor system. The combination of a Type Ia supernova and the presence of circumstellar material makes Kepler's supernova remnant a unique object for studying the origin of Type Ia supernovae. Evidence suggests that the progenitor binary system of supernova 1604 consisted of a carbon-oxygen white dwarf and an evolved companion star, likely in the (post) asymptotic giant branch of its evolution. However, a challenge remains: the companion star should have survived the explosion, but no trace has been found despite extensive searches.
label: AI

title: CLEVR: A Diagnostic Dataset for Compositional Language and Elementary Visual Reasoning
Abstract: Building artificial intelligence systems capable of reasoning and answering questions about visual data requires diagnostic tests to evaluate progress and identify shortcomings. While existing benchmarks for visual question answering can be helpful, they exhibit strong biases that models can exploit to answer questions correctly without true reasoning. These biases conflate multiple sources of error, making it difficult to pinpoint specific model weaknesses. This paper presents a diagnostic dataset that tests a range of visual reasoning abilities. It minimizes biases and includes detailed annotations describing the reasoning required for each question. The dataset is used to analyze various modern visual reasoning systems, offering novel insights into their capabilities and limitations.
label: AI

title: Beyond Skip Connections: Top-Down Modulation for Object Detection
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed tremendous progress in object detection, primarily driven by deeper feedforward networks. However, detecting challenging object categories like bottles and remotes requires fine detail representation beyond coarse, semantic representations. These fine details are often lost in early convolutional layers. This paper proposes a solution for incorporating finer details from lower layers into the detection architecture. While skip connections have been proposed to combine high-level and low-level features, selecting the right features from low-level layers requires top-down contextual information. Inspired by the human visual pathway, this paper introduces top-down modulations as a method for incorporating fine details into the detection framework. The approach supplements the standard bottom-up, feedforward ConvNet with a top-down modulation (TDM) network connected using lateral connections. These connections modulate lower layer filters, while the top-down network handles the selection and integration of contextual information and low-level features. The proposed TDM architecture significantly improves performance on the COCO testdev benchmark, achieving 28.6 AP for VGG16, 35.2 AP for ResNet101, and 37.3 for InceptionResNetv2 network without using any additional techniques like multi-scale or iterative box refinement.
label: AI

title: Center-Focusing Multi-task CNN with Injected Features for Classification of Glioma Nuclear Images
Abstract: Classifying the shapes and attributes of glioma cell nuclei is crucial for diagnosis and understanding the disease. This paper investigates automated classification of glioma nuclear shapes and visual attributes using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on pathology images of automatically segmented nuclei. Three methods are proposed to enhance the performance of a previously developed semi-supervised CNN. First, a method is proposed that allows the CNN to focus on the most important part of an image – the center containing the nucleus. Second, pre-extracted VGG features are injected (concatenated) into an intermediate layer of the semi-supervised CNN, enabling the CNN to learn complementary features during training. Third, the losses of the two groups of target classes (nuclear shapes and attributes) are separated into a single-label loss and a multi-label loss, incorporating prior knowledge of inter-label exclusiveness. On a dataset of 2078 images, the combined proposed methods reduced the error rate of attribute and shape classification by 21.54% and 15.07%, respectively, compared to the existing state-of-the-art method on the same dataset.
label: AI

title: Temporal Feature Selection on Networked Time Series
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of learning discriminative features (i.e., segments) from networked time series data considering the linked information among time series. For instance, social network users can be considered social sensors continuously generating social signals (tweets) represented as a time series. Discriminative segments are often referred to as shapelets in a time series. Extracting shapelets for time series classification has been extensively studied, but existing works assume independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) time series, limiting their application to social networked time series analysis where user actions can be correlated with their social affiliations. This paper proposes a new Network Regularized Least Squares (NetRLS) feature selection model that combines typical time series data and user network data for analysis. Experiments on real-world networked time series data from Twitter and DBLP demonstrate the performance of the proposed method. NetRLS outperforms LTS, the state-of-the-art time series feature selection approach, on real-world data.
label: AI

title: Two decades of local binary patterns: A survey
Abstract: Texture is a significant characteristic for various types of images. Recent years have witnessed the development of highly discriminative and computationally efficient local texture descriptors based on local binary patterns (LBP), leading to significant progress in applying texture methods to different problems and applications. This progress has blurred the distinction between texture descriptors and more generic image or video descriptors. Numerous variants of LBP have been developed to improve its robustness, discriminative power, and applicability to different problems. This chapter surveys the most recent and important variants of LBP in 2D, spatiotemporal, 3D, and 4D domains. Interesting new developments of LBP in 1D signal analysis are also considered. Finally, some future research challenges are presented.
label: AI

title: Machine learning and multivariate goodness of fit
Abstract: Multivariate goodness-of-fit and two-sample tests are crucial components of many nuclear and particle physics analyses. While several powerful methods exist for low-dimensional feature spaces, their power rapidly diminishes as dimensionality increases and data becomes sparse. Machine learning classifiers offer a powerful tool for reducing highly multivariate problems into univariate ones, enabling the application of commonly used tests like chi-squared or Kolmogorov-Smirnov. This paper explores the application of both traditional and machine-learning-based tests to several example problems, investigating how the power of each approach depends on dimensionality. A pedagogical discussion is provided on the suitability of traditional versus machine-learning-based tests for different problems, along with guidelines for properly employing the machine-learning-based approach. |||
label: AI

title: SCDV : Sparse Composite Document Vectors using soft clustering over distributional representations
Abstract: Sparse Composite Document Vectors (SCDV) offer a novel approach to document representation that addresses limitations of existing distributional paragraph vector methods. SCDV clusters word embeddings to capture diverse semantic contexts, then chains them to create document topic vectors that can express complex, multi-topic documents. Through extensive experiments on multi-class and multi-label classification tasks, SCDV surpasses the previous state-of-the-art method, NTSG. Additionally, SCDV demonstrates strong performance on heterogeneous tasks like Topic Coherence, context-sensitive Learning, and Information Retrieval. Furthermore, SCDV significantly reduces training and prediction times compared to other representation methods. SCDV provides the best of both worlds, achieving improved performance with lower time and space complexity.
label: AI

title: Action-Driven Object Detection with Top-Down Visual Attentions
Abstract: A novel "action-driven" object detection mechanism, leveraging a "top-down" visual attention model, is presented in this paper. This approach deviates from the dominant "bottom-up" paradigm that relies on "passive" scoring of class-agnostic proposals. The attention model, conditioned on an image region, provides sequential actions that guide the detection process towards the target object. Each action is weak individually, but the ensemble of sequential actions accurately converges the bounding box to the object's boundary. The AttentionNet, a convolutional neural network, drives the detection process without requiring any modules for object proposals or post-bounding-box regression. Evaluation on the PASCAL VOC series and ILSVRC CLS-LOC dataset demonstrates state-of-the-art performance compared to major bottom-up detection methods, particularly excelling in precise localization.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Perceptual Rewards for Imitation Learning
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of reward function design and exploration time in real-world reinforcement learning (RL) by proposing a method for learning perceptual reward functions from demonstrations. The method leverages the abstraction power of deep models to identify key intermediate steps in a task and automatically select discriminative features for recognizing these steps. By utilizing features from a pre-trained deep model, the method avoids explicit sub-goal specification. The learned reward functions can then guide RL agents to perform tasks in real-world settings. Qualitative results on two real-world tasks and quantitative comparisons with human-designed reward functions demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. Notably, the method enables learning a real-world door opening skill using a real robot, even with demonstrations provided by humans using their own hands. These results represent the first demonstration of learning complex robotic manipulation skills directly from human video demonstrations without supervised labels.
label: AI

title: Classification and Learning-to-rank Approaches for Cross-Device Matching at CIKM Cup 2016
Abstract: This paper presents two methods for cross-device matching in online advertising. The first method treats the matching problem as a binary classification task and utilizes ensemble learning techniques. The second method defines matching as a ranking task and employs learning-to-rank algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of both methods, with the ranking-based approach outperforming the classification-based approach for the task.
label: AI

title: Multivariate Industrial Time Series with Cyber-Attack Simulation: Fault Detection Using an LSTM-based Predictive Data Model
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for monitoring and detecting faults in industrial multivariate time series data using an LSTM neural network. The approach is validated using a Modelica model of a real gasoil plant, where faults are introduced and labeled. An LSTM architecture with a forecasting error threshold is used to achieve precision and recall quality metrics, considering the dependence of these metrics on the threshold level. A mechanism for filtering faults outside of the plant operator's field of interest is also introduced.
label: AI

title: Inferring the location of authors from words in their texts
Abstract: This paper presents a series of experiments exploring the use of positionally annotated microblog posts to learn location-indicating words for locating blog texts and their authors. A Gaussian distribution model is used to represent the locational qualities of words, introducing the concept of "placeness" to describe how locational words are. Experiments show that modeling word distributions with multiple locations, filtering words with high placeness based on local context, and aggregating locational information into a centroid for each text yield the most useful results. The study focuses on data in the Swedish language.
label: AI

title: LWE from Non-commutative Group Rings
Abstract: The Ring Learning-With-Errors (LWE) problem, whose security relies on hard ideal lattice problems, has proven to be a versatile cryptographic primitive. However, recent advancements in algorithms for the principal ideal SVP problem and attempts to generalize the attack to non-principal ideals pose security concerns. This work investigates the LWE problem on group rings and introduces cryptographic schemes based on this new primitive. By utilizing non-commutative groups, the proposal overcomes the weakness associated with principal ideal lattices, offering improved security compared to ring-LWE while maintaining efficiency. The paper demonstrates how to construct public key encryption schemes from dihedral group rings, highlighting the potential for enhanced security in lattice-based cryptography.
label: AI

title: Enhancing Observability in Distribution Grids using Smart Meter Data
Abstract: Observability challenges in distribution grids, due to limited metering infrastructure, can be addressed by utilizing smart meter data to infer grid state. This work proposes a coupled formulation of the power flow problem (CPF) that leverages the variability of injections at metered buses, the controllability of solar inverters, and the relative time-invariance of conventional loads. By solving non-linear power flow equations jointly over consecutive time instants, the method estimates the grid state. An observability criterion for radial networks is established, relating the locations of metered and non-metered buses to local observability. To account for noisy smart meter readings, a coupled power system state estimation (CPSSE) problem is developed. Both CPF and CPSSE tasks are solved using augmented semi-definite program relaxations, and the approach is numerically validated using synthetic and real solar generation and load data on the IEEE 34-bus benchmark feeder.

title: Partially blind domain adaptation for age prediction from DNA methylation data
Abstract: The abundance of biological and medical data presents opportunities for machine learning applications in healthcare, but also presents challenges due to the large number of correlated features and data heterogeneity. This paper focuses on epigenetic research, particularly the analysis of DNA methylation data. An adaptive model is proposed for feature selection, which performs feature selection individually for each test sample based on the input data distribution. The method can be viewed as partially blind domain adaptation. The model is applied to age prediction based on DNA methylation data from various tissues, demonstrating improvement over standard models that do not account for heterogeneity. The adaptive approach shows significant performance gains on tissue types not included in the training data.

title: Supervised Learning for Optimal Power Flow as a Real-Time Proxy
Abstract: This paper investigates the use of supervised learning algorithms to efficiently approximate the cost of Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow (ACOPF) for long-term and medium-term planning in power networks. The proposed approximation module, called a proxy, predicts short-term decision outcomes without requiring full simulation and optimization. The method achieves fast and accurate approximation of OPF cost with less than 1% error on average, while being significantly faster than exact computation. The efficiency of the approach is demonstrated on test cases such as IEEE-RTS96.
label: AI

title: Deep Motion Features for Visual Tracking
Abstract: This paper explores the impact of deep motion features in a tracking-by-detection framework for robust visual tracking. Deep RGB features extracted from convolutional neural networks capture appearance information, while motion cues provide complementary and discriminative information. This work demonstrates that hand-crafted, deep RGB, and deep motion features contain complementary information, and proposes a novel approach for fusing appearance information with deep motion features for visual tracking. Comprehensive experiments show that this fusion approach outperforms standard methods relying on appearance information alone.

title: WoCE: a framework for clustering ensemble by exploiting the wisdom of Crowds theory
Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for unsupervised and semi-supervised cluster ensemble, inspired by the Wisdom of Crowds (WOC) theory. The WOC theory states that collective decisions by a group can outperform individual decisions under specific conditions. The framework incorporates four conditions from the WOC theory: diversity, independency, decentralization, and aggregation. A novel mapping system removes feature correlation, a new mechanism generates high-quality individual clustering results, and a uniformity metric evaluates diversity. A weighted evidence accumulation clustering method is proposed for final aggregation without thresholding. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Detecting Unexpected Obstacles for Self-Driving Cars: Fusing Deep Learning and Geometric Modeling
Abstract: Detecting small road hazards, such as lost cargo, is crucial for self-driving cars. This paper addresses this challenging problem with a vision system that leverages appearance, contextual, and geometric cues. A novel deep learning-based obstacle detection framework is proposed, utilizing a variant of a fully convolutional network to predict pixel-wise semantic labeling of free-space, on-road unexpected obstacles, and background. Geometric cues are exploited using a state-of-the-art detection approach that predicts obstacles from stereo images. A principled Bayesian framework fuses semantic and stereo-based detection results, employing the mid-level Stixel representation for compact and robust obstacle description. Evaluation on the Lost and Found dataset, containing challenging scenes with obstacles as small as 5 cm, demonstrates significant improvement over the state-of-the-art, with relative performance gains of up to 50%. The system operates at 22 Hz on a self-driving platform.

title: RIDS: Robust Identification of Sparse Gene Regulatory Networks from Perturbation Experiments
Abstract: Reconstructing the causal network in a complex dynamical system is essential in various fields, including biology and economics. This paper focuses on inferring gene regulation networks (GRNs) from perturbation or gene deletion experiments. To address the costliness of such experiments, the Robust IDentification of Sparse networks (RIDS) method is developed. RIDS reconstructs the GRN from a small number of perturbation experiments by translating gene expression data into steady state conditions of the system's nonlinear interaction dynamics. A sparse optimization criterion extracts the parameters of the underlying weighted network, even with limited experimental data. Analytical results show that under certain conditions, the GRN can be perfectly reconstructed with a scalable number of experiments. Evaluation on synthetic and experimental data demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, requiring significantly fewer experiments. RIDS infers the directionality of GRN links, allowing for the inference of empirical GRNs without relying on pre-defined transcription factor lists.

title: Dictionary Learning Based Sparse Channel Representation and Estimation for FDD Massive MIMO Systems
Abstract: This paper addresses uplink and downlink channel estimation in FDD Massive MIMO systems by utilizing sparse recovery and compressive sensing algorithms. This approach improves estimation accuracy and reduces pilot symbol count, assuming channel sparsity under a suitable basis/dictionary. While previous works employed predefined basis/dictionaries, this paper introduces a dictionary learning-based channel model where the dictionary is learned from comprehensive channel measurements. The learned dictionary adapts to cell characteristics, enabling more efficient and robust channel representation, which further enhances estimation performance. The paper extends the dictionary learning approach to a joint uplink/downlink learning framework by exploiting the reciprocity of AOA/AOD between uplink and downlink transmissions. A joint channel estimation algorithm is proposed that combines uplink and downlink training signals for more accurate channel estimation. This approach reduces downlink training overhead, a bottleneck in FDD Massive MIMO systems, by leveraging information from simpler uplink training.

title: Wide-Slice Residual Networks for Food Recognition
Abstract: Food diary applications present significant challenges for computer vision and pattern recognition algorithms, particularly in the area of image food recognition. This paper proposes a novel deep learning scheme specifically designed to handle the structure of food. Inspired by residual deep networks, the scheme employs a slice convolution block to capture vertical food layers. Outputs from residual blocks are combined with sliced convolution to produce classification scores for food categories. Evaluation on three benchmark datasets demonstrates that the proposed architecture outperforms existing approaches, achieving a top-1 accuracy of 90.27% on the Food-101 dataset.

title: Neuro-symbolic EDA-based Optimisation using ILP-enhanced DBNs
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for solving discrete optimization problems using the estimation of distribution (EDA) approach, combining deep belief networks (DBN) and inductive logic programming (ILP). DBNs learn the structure of progressively better feasible solutions, while ILP incorporates domain-based background knowledge about solution goodness. ILP is integrated into the EDA process to enhance sampling efficiency and incorporate domain knowledge. The proposed Neuro-symbolic EDA uses an ILP engine to construct a model of good solutions based on domain knowledge, introducing logical ILP features as Boolean features in the DBN's last hidden layer. This integration requires modifications to DBN training and sampling, ensuring that generated samples are consistent with the logical model. The approach is demonstrated on two optimization problems: predicting optimal depth-of-win in the KRK endgame and jobshop scheduling. Results show that the ILP-assisted DBN generates samples with a higher proportion of good solutions and more near-optimal samples compared to DBNs without ILP features. These findings suggest the potential of incorporating complex domain knowledge into deep models for EDA-based procedures.
label: AI

title: Exploring the Design Space of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks at Large Scale
Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved superior accuracy in various machine learning problems. However, there is no single optimal CNN/DNN architecture for all tasks, and the "right" architecture varies based on the specific application. This dissertation develops a methodology for systematic exploration of the CNN design space, comprising four key themes: judicious benchmark selection, rapid CNN training, CNN design space definition and description, and CNN architecture design space exploration. These themes, combined, provide an effective methodology for discovering optimal CNN architectures tailored to practical applications.

title: Deeply Aggregated Alternating Minimization for Image Restoration
Abstract: Regularization-based image restoration, utilizing guidance signals from different domains, is a prominent research area in computer vision and image processing. This paper presents a general framework called Deeply Aggregated Alternating Minimization (DeepAM) for image restoration. Deep neural networks are trained to enhance two steps in the conventional AM algorithm: proximal mapping and ?-continuation. These steps are learned end-to-end from large datasets, allowing CNNs to act as priors or regularizers within the AM algorithm. Deep aggregation-based learning of the regularizer demonstrates superior performance compared to recent data-driven approaches and nonlocal methods. The framework's flexibility and effectiveness are showcased in various image restoration tasks, including single image denoising, RGB-NIR restoration, and depth super-resolution.

title: Parallelized Tensor Train Learning of Polynomial Classifiers
Abstract: Polynomial classifiers are well-established methods in pattern classification due to their ability to generate complex decision surfaces. However, multivariate polynomials become impractical for high-dimensional problems. This paper overcomes this limitation by employing the tensor train format to represent a polynomial classifier. Based on the tensor train structure, two learning algorithms are proposed, involving optimization problems with low computational complexity. The methods incorporate regularization to prevent overfitting and parallelization to handle large training sets. The efficiency and efficacy of the tensor-based polynomial classifier are demonstrated on the USPS and MNIST datasets. |||

title: Randomized Clustered Nystrom for Large-Scale Kernel Machines
Abstract: The Nystrom method is widely used for low-rank approximation of kernel matrices, a common task in machine learning. The approximation's quality hinges on the number of landmark points chosen and their selection method. This paper introduces a novel algorithm that optimizes the Nystrom low-approximation when the landmark points surpass the target rank. Additionally, it proposes a randomized algorithm for selecting landmark points, making it scalable to large datasets. This method clusters data points in low-dimensional projections, leading to significant computational savings for high-dimensional data. Theoretical analysis clarifies the tradeoffs between accuracy and efficiency of this approach, while extensive experiments demonstrate its strong performance and efficiency.

title: ICON: an adaptation of infinite HMMs for time traces with drift
Abstract: Bayesian nonparametric methods have revolutionized areas within data science. One such method, the infinite hidden Markov model (iHMM), extends the popular HMM and is particularly promising for single molecule data analysis. Unlike HMM, iHMM learns all parameters and the number of states without needing model selection steps. However, common features in single molecule time traces, such as drift, can lead to over-interpretation of drift and spurious states. This paper introduces an adaptation of the iHMM that accounts for drift originating from individual or multiple traces. This fully Bayesian method integrates iHMM with a continuous control process for drift, learning all model quantities including state numbers. The key advantage is that all traces, regardless of drift, can be analyzed uniformly, eliminating manual trace selection and pre-processing for drift removal.

title: An introduction to infinite HMMs for single molecule data analysis
Abstract: The hidden Markov model (HMM) is a cornerstone of single molecule data analysis and has become a ubiquitous tool in time series analysis. This paper introduces a powerful generalization of the HMM: the infinite hidden Markov model (iHMM). iHMMs analyze sequential data without requiring a predefined number of states, unlike the traditional HMM. While the current iHMM literature is primarily aimed at statistics audiences, its broad applicability extends far beyond machine learning and data science. This paper explains the core concepts of iHMM, emphasizing its implementation and providing details about freely available code. A companion article will delve into an important extension of the iHMM for handling complexities such as drift.

title: Random Walk Models of Network Formation and Sequential Monte Carlo Methods for Graphs
Abstract: This paper introduces a class of generative network models that construct edges by connecting the starting and terminal vertices of a random walk on the network graph. Within statistical network models, this class uniquely allows the location of a new edge to depend explicitly on the graph structure, while remaining statistically and computationally tractable. In the limit of infinite walk length, the model converges to an extension of the preferential attachment model, revealing that preferential attachment is an approximation of this model. Theoretical properties, including the limiting degree sequence, are analyzed. If the complete history of the graph is available, parameters can be estimated through maximum likelihood. When only the final graph is available, its history can be imputed using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). The paper develops a class of sequential Monte Carlo algorithms that are more broadly applicable to sequential network models and may be of independent interest. The model parameters can be recovered from a single graph generated by the model. Applications to data highlight the role of the random walk length as a length scale for interactions within the graph.

title: The OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. Eclipsing Binaries in the Magellanic System
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive catalog of eclipsing binaries in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, based on data from the OGLE survey. The catalog contains 48,605 systems, with 40,204 belonging to the LMC and 8,401 to the SMC. Among these, 16,374 binaries are newly identified. The paper provides time-series photometry for the selected objects, obtained during the fourth phase of the OGLE project. The catalog was constructed using a two-step machine learning procedure based on the Random Forest algorithm.

title: Asynchronous Temporal Fields for Action Recognition
Abstract: Actions are more than just physical movements and trajectories; they are performed with purpose and intention. Understanding videos comprehensively necessitates going beyond appearance modeling and delving into the sequence of activities and the higher-level intentions behind them. This paper proposes a fully-connected temporal conditional random field (CRF) model for reasoning about different aspects of activities, including objects, actions, and intentions, with potentials predicted by a deep network. End-to-end training of such structured models poses a challenge: inference and learning require mini-batches of whole videos, leading to small mini-batches with high data correlation, hindering the backpropagation algorithm. To address this, the paper presents an asynchronous variational inference method that enables efficient end-to-end training. This method achieves a classification mean average precision (mAP) of 22.4% on the Charades benchmark, surpassing the state-of-the-art (17.2% mAP) and offering similar gains for temporal localization.
label: AI

title: Learning Features by Watching Objects Move
Abstract: This paper presents a novel and intuitive approach to unsupervised feature learning. Drawing inspiration from the human visual system, the research investigates the potential of using low-level motion-based grouping cues to learn effective visual representations. Unsupervised motion-based segmentation on videos is employed to obtain segments, which serve as "pseudo ground truth" for training a convolutional network to segment objects from a single frame. Given the significant role of motion in human visual system development, this straightforward approach aims to surpass the effectiveness of cleverly designed "pretext" tasks explored in the literature. Experimental results confirm this hypothesis, demonstrating that this method significantly outperforms previous unsupervised approaches for transfer learning on object detection, particularly when training data is limited.

title: Semantic Jitter: Dense Supervision for Visual Comparisons via Synthetic Images
Abstract: Distinguishing subtle differences in visual attributes is valuable, but learning to make visual comparisons remains challenging. The number of possible comparisons grows quadratically with the number of training images, and acquiring images sufficiently spanning the space of fine-grained differences is limited. To overcome this sparsity problem, this paper proposes using synthetically generated images. By building upon a state-of-the-art image generation engine, the research samples pairs of training images exhibiting minor modifications to specific attributes. Augmenting real training image pairs with these synthetic examples, attribute ranking models are trained to predict the relative strength of an attribute in novel real image pairs. Results on face and fashion image datasets demonstrate the promise of leveraging imperfect image generators to counter sample sparsity in learning to rank.
label: AI

title: Computing Human-Understandable Strategies
Abstract: Algorithms for equilibrium computation typically disregard the need for human interpretability of the computed strategies. For instance, strategies for high-performing poker agents are often represented as massive binary files. In many situations, we desire strategies that humans can readily implement, considering their computational limitations and limited memory capacity. This paper focuses on poker games with arbitrary private information distributions. A large training set of game instances and solutions is created by randomly selecting information probabilities, and algorithms are developed to learn from these instances for effective performance in games with unseen information distributions. The research identifies several new fundamental poker strategy rules that are easily implementable by humans.

title: Randomized Learning of the Second-Moment Matrix of a Smooth Function
Abstract: Consider an open set in n-dimensional Euclidean space, equipped with a probability measure. An important characteristic of a smooth function on this set is its second-moment matrix, which captures the function's variation in different directions. The span of the leading eigenvectors of this matrix defines an active subspace, containing directions where the function changes most significantly, crucial for ridge approximation. This paper proposes a simple algorithm for estimating the second-moment matrix from random point evaluations of the function, without imposing any structural assumptions. Theoretical guarantees for this algorithm are established using technical tools previously employed in covariance matrix estimation from partial measurements.

title: Computationally Discovered Potentiating Role of Glycans on NMDA Receptors
Abstract: N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) are glycoproteins in the brain crucial for learning and memory. However, the impact of glycosylation on the structure and dynamics of NMDARs remains largely unknown. This paper uses extensive molecular dynamics simulations of GluN1 and GluN2B ligand binding domains (LBDs) of NMDARs to investigate these effects. Simulations predict that intra-domain interactions involving the glycan attached to residue GluN1-N440 stabilize closed-clamshell conformations of the GluN1 LBD. The glycan on GluN2B-N688 shows a similar, though weaker, effect. Based on these findings and assuming the transferability of LBD simulation results to the full receptor, the paper predicts that glycans at GluN1-N440 might play a potentiator role in NMDARs. To validate this prediction, electrophysiological analysis of full-length NMDARs with a glycosylation-preventing GluN1-N440Q mutation is performed, revealing an increase in the glycine EC50 value. Overall, these results suggest an intramolecular potentiating role of glycans on NMDA receptors.

title: Handwritten Signature Verification Using Hand-Worn Devices
Abstract: Online signature verification technologies, commonly found in banks and post offices, rely on dedicated digital devices like tablets or smart pens for capturing, analyzing, and verifying signatures. This paper proposes a novel approach to online signature verification that leverages the increasing availability of hand-worn devices like smartwatches or fitness trackers. The method uses known genuine and forged signatures recorded using the motion sensors of a hand-worn device to train a machine learning classifier. Given an unknown signature and a claimed identity, the classifier determines whether the signature is genuine or forged. Validation of this method was performed on 1,980 recordings of genuine and forged signatures from 66 subjects, resulting in a high accuracy (0.98 AUC and 0.05 EER) in distinguishing between genuine and forged signatures.

title: Hybrid Transactional Replication: State-Machine and Deferred-Update Replication Combined
Abstract: This paper introduces Hybrid Transactional Replication (HTR), a novel replication scheme for highly dependable services. It combines two replication schemes: transactions are executed either optimistically by a single service replica in deferred update mode (DU) or deterministically by all replicas in state machine mode (SM), based on an oracle's decision. The DU mode allows for parallelism, taking advantage of multicore hardware. In contrast, the SM mode ensures abort-free execution, making it suitable for irreversible operations and transactions with high contention. For flexibility, transactions can be discarded or retried on demand. The paper formally proves that this increased flexibility does not compromise client guarantees: HTR satisfies strong consistency guarantees similar to those provided by other popular transactional replication schemes like Deferred Update Replication. HTR-enabled Paxos STM, an object-based distributed transactional memory system, was developed and thoroughly evaluated under various workloads. The benefits of using a novel oracle, which relies on machine learning techniques for automatic adaptation to changing conditions, are demonstrated. In tests, the ML-based oracle provides up to 50% improvement in throughput compared to using DU-only or SM-only oracles. This approach is inspired by a well-known algorithm used in the context of the multi-armed bandit problem.

title: Simple Black-Box Adversarial Perturbations for Deep Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks are powerful and popular learning models that achieve state-of-the-art performance in pattern recognition across various domains, including computer vision, speech, and language processing. However, these networks are vulnerable to carefully crafted adversarial perturbations that can force misclassification of inputs. Adversarial examples enable adversaries to subvert expected system behavior, leading to undesired consequences and posing security risks when deployed in real-world applications. This paper focuses on deep convolutional neural networks and demonstrates that adversaries can easily create adversarial examples without any knowledge of the target network's internal workings. These attacks treat the network as an oracle (black-box) and only require observing the network's output on probed inputs. The first attack involves adding perturbation to a randomly selected pixel or a small set of pixels. This attack's effectiveness is further enhanced by constructing a small set of pixels for perturbation using a greedy local-search approach. The proposed attacks naturally extend to a stronger notion of misclassification. Extensive experimental results show that even these simple attacks can expose vulnerabilities in deep neural networks. The simplicity and effectiveness of these schemes make them valuable tools for evaluating the robustness of networks.

title: Photo-Quality Evaluation based on Computational Aesthetics: Review of Feature Extraction Techniques
Abstract: Researchers have attempted to model the aesthetic quality of photographs by analyzing low-level and high-level features, drawing inspiration from art theory, psychology, and marketing. This literature review aims to comprehensively describe each feature extraction measure employed in this process. The review categorizes each feature based on its implementation complexity, considering real-world applications and integration into mobile apps and digital cameras. The paper also discusses machine learning results and identifies unexplored research areas for future work.

title: Corralling a Band of Bandit Algorithms
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of combining multiple bandit algorithms, which are online learning algorithms with partial feedback. The goal is to create a master algorithm that performs as well as the best base algorithm if run individually. The main challenge is that when run with a master, base algorithms receive less feedback, making it crucial to avoid starving a base algorithm that might initially perform poorly but ultimately outperform others given enough feedback. To address this, the paper proposes a version of Online Mirror Descent with a specialized mirror map and a sophisticated learning rate scheme. This approach achieves a more delicate balance between exploiting and exploring base algorithms compared to previous work, resulting in improved regret bounds. These findings are applicable to various settings, including multi-armed bandits, contextual bandits, and convex bandits. The paper presents two main applications: creating an algorithm with worst-case robustness while performing better in easier environments and creating an algorithm that works simultaneously under different environmental assumptions, such as different priors or loss structures.

title: A Knowledge-Assisted Visual Malware Analysis System: Design, Validation, and Reflection of KAMAS
Abstract: IT-security experts engage in behavior-based malware analysis to learn about previously unknown malicious software (malware) or malware families. This process involves identifying and categorizing suspicious patterns from vast collections of execution traces. Existing systems fail to meet the analysts' needs: they lack visual access for complex data structures, provide inadequate visual representations for IT-security experts, lack workflow-specific interaction techniques, and struggle to externalize knowledge as rules for analysis sharing with colleagues. To bridge this gap, the paper presents KAMAS, a knowledge-assisted visualization system for behavior-based malware analysis. KAMAS aids malware analysts with visual analytics and knowledge externalization methods for the analysis process. This design study details the design, implementation, and evaluation of the prototype. KAMAS was validated through expert reviews, a user study with domain experts, and focus group meetings with industry analysts. The study discusses the insights gained, advantages, and disadvantages of the applied visualization methods.

title: A recurrent neural network without chaos
Abstract: This paper introduces an exceptionally simple gated recurrent neural network (RNN) that achieves performance comparable to well-known gated architectures like LSTMs and GRUs on the word-level language modeling task. Notably, this model exhibits simple, predictable, and non-chaotic dynamics, a stark contrast to more standard gated architectures whose underlying dynamical systems exhibit chaotic behavior.

title: An extended Perona-Malik model based on probabilistic models
Abstract: The Perona-Malik model has been highly successful in image restoration from noisy input. This paper reinterprets the Perona-Malik model within the framework of Gaussian scale mixtures and derives several model extensions. The paper shows that applying the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to Gaussian scale mixtures leads to the lagged-diffusivity algorithm for computing stationary points of the Perona-Malik diffusion equations. Additionally, the paper demonstrates how mean field approximations to these Gaussian scale mixtures lead to a modified lagged-diffusivity algorithm that better captures uncertainties in the restoration. As this modification can be computationally demanding, relaxations to the mean field objective are proposed to make the algorithm feasible. Numerical experiments show that this modified lagged-diffusivity algorithm often performs better at restoring textured areas and fuzzy edges compared to the unmodified algorithm. As a second application of the Gaussian scale mixture framework, the paper demonstrates how an efficient sampling procedure can be obtained for the probabilistic model, enabling the computation of conditional mean and other expectations. Again, the resulting algorithm closely resembles the lagged-diffusivity algorithm. Finally, the paper shows that a probabilistic version of the Mumford-Shah segmentation model can be obtained within the same framework using a discrete edge-prior.

title: Crowd collectiveness measure via graph-based node clique learning
Abstract: Collective motions in crowd systems have attracted significant attention in recent years. This paper proposes a novel node clique learning method to quantify the collectiveness of a crowd system. This graph-based method investigates the influence of one node on others. Each node is represented by a set of nodes known as a clique, which is determined by spreading information from this node to other nodes in the graph. Only nodes with sufficient information are selected as part of the node's clique. The motion coherence between two nodes is defined by comparing their node cliques. The collectiveness of a node and the overall crowd system are defined based on node coherence. Self-driven particle (SDP) model and a crowd motion database are used to test the proposed method's ability to measure collectiveness. |||

title: Few-Shot Object Recognition from Machine-Labeled Web Images
Abstract: This work proposes an abstraction memory framework for few-shot learning, leveraging machine-labeled image annotations. The framework utilizes a large-scale external memory bank, with image features serving as keys and label embeddings as values. When presented with few-shot examples, the model retrieves visually similar data from the memory bank and transfers relevant information to an abstraction memory. LSTM controllers and attention mechanisms ensure the data transferred to the abstraction memory is relevant to the query. Experimental results on ImageNet demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model, achieving performance comparable to models trained with human-labeled data.

title: Domain specialization: a post-training domain adaptation for Neural Machine Translation
Abstract: Domain adaptation is a key aspect of Machine Translation, especially in Computer Assisted Translation (CAT) workflows. This paper explores a novel approach to domain adaptation called "specialization," which shows promising results in terms of learning speed and adaptation accuracy.

title: Neural Machine Translation from Simplified Translations
Abstract: This paper introduces simplified translations as a technique to enhance the learning capabilities of deep neural machine translation models. Preliminary experiments demonstrate that simplified translations, compared to target references, reduce translation complexity in a bi-text while maintaining the same meaning. The simplified bi-text is then used to train an NMT model, which outperforms the model trained on the reference data. Further improvements are achieved by combining reference and automatic translations in training. The approach is evaluated on English-to-French and English-to-German translation tasks, showing promising results.

title: Boosting Neural Machine Translation
Abstract: Training efficiency is a significant challenge in Neural Machine Translation (NMT) due to the large data requirements and extensive training iterations needed for state-of-the-art performance. This paper proposes data boosting and bootstrapping methods to improve training efficiency without modifying the neural network. Inspired by human learning processes, these methods prioritize learning "difficult" concepts, resulting in accuracy improvements of up to 1.63 BLEU and a 20% reduction in training time.

title: Monte Carlo sampling for stochastic weight functions
Abstract: This paper introduces a rigorous Monte Carlo algorithm for situations where the weight determining the acceptance probability in a trial move fluctuates. The algorithm ensures that points in state space are visited with a probability proportional to their average weight. This approach has the potential to transform the methodology of high-throughput experiments and noisy dataset analysis.

title: Active and Continuous Exploration with Deep Neural Networks and Expected Model Output Changes
Abstract: This paper proposes a continuous active learning and exploration method for visual recognition systems. The algorithm actively selects relevant unlabeled examples for annotation, either from known or undiscovered classes. title: A real-time framework for visual feedback of articulatory data using statistical shape models
Abstract: This paper presents an open-source framework for real-time visualization of electromagnetic articulography (EMA) data. The framework features a modular structure and anatomically accurate tongue and palate models derived using multilinear subspace learning.

title: Cross-Modal Manifold Learning for Cross-modal Retrieval
Abstract: This paper introduces a scalable algorithm for cross-modal similarity-preserving retrieval in a learned manifold space. Unlike existing approaches that compromise between global and local geometries, this algorithm preserves both simultaneously during manifold alignment. Global topologies are maintained by recovering underlying mapping functions, while inter- and intra-modality affinity matrices are computed to reinforce the data skeleton using perturbed minimum spanning trees and maximize affinity among similar cross-modal instances. The algorithm demonstrates superior performance over comparative methods in classification and regression tasks on two multimodal image datasets, highlighting its potential for improving computer-assisted diagnosis systems.

title: X-ray In-Depth Decomposition: Revealing The Latent Structures
Abstract: This paper explores the use of deep learning for decomposing conventional X-ray images into multiple sub-volume components. The goal is to improve the interpretation of hidden and obscured anatomy in X-ray images, reducing the need for high radiation doses and multiple imaging perspectives. title: Transfer Learning based Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization Algorithms
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of tracking the varying Pareto-optimal front in dynamic multiobjective optimization problems (DMOPs), where optimization objectives change over time. This approach leverages transfer learning to reuse past experience and speed up the evolutionary process, benefiting any population-based multiobjective algorithm without significant modifications. title: Hierarchical Partitioning of the Output Space in Multi-label Data
Abstract: This paper presents HOMER (Hierarchy of Multi-label Classifiers), a multi-label learning algorithm that decomposes complex tasks into simpler sub-tasks. title: On Random Weights for Texture Generation in One Layer Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper explores the effectiveness of one-layer convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with random filters in generating natural textures. Theoretical analysis reveals that these architectures, paired with an energy function, can preserve and modulate frequency coefficients, resulting in similar image generation capabilities for random and pretrained weights. title: A Convex Program for Mixed Linear Regression with a Recovery Guarantee for Well-Separated Data
Abstract: This paper introduces a convex approach for mixed linear regression using a second-order cone program based on L1 minimization. The approach assigns an estimate regression coefficient to each data point, which can then be clustered. The paper proves that under certain conditions, this approach can exactly recover all mixture components in the noiseless setting. The method is demonstrated on real and synthetic data using iteratively reweighted least squares.
