title: Separation of Concerns in Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper introduces a framework for solving a single-agent task using multiple agents, each specializing in different aspects of the task. This approach offers two key advantages: 1) it allows for training specialized agents on distinct parts of the task, and 2) it presents a novel method for knowledge transfer by transferring trained agents. The framework generalizes the traditional hierarchical decomposition, where a single agent maintains control until its specific subtask is resolved. Empirical experiments on two domains illustrate the efficacy of this framework.
label: AI

title: On the Potential of Simple Framewise Approaches to Piano Transcription
Abstract: This paper delves into the limitations of simple approaches to piano transcription, focusing on an in-depth analysis of neural network-based framewise transcription. A systematic comparison of different popular input representations for transcription systems is conducted to identify those most suitable for use with neural networks. Leveraging recent advancements in training techniques and novel regularizers, coupled with hyper-parameter tuning, this paper demonstrates that a simple bottom-up frame-wise processing can achieve a piano transcriber that surpasses the current published state-of-the-art on the publicly available MAPS dataset without complex post-processing steps. This simple approach is proposed as a new baseline for this dataset, encouraging future transcription research to build upon and improve upon it.
label: AI

title: Coupling Adaptive Batch Sizes with Learning Rates
Abstract: Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent and its variants have become standard for large-scale empirical risk minimization, commonly employed in the training of neural networks. These methods typically utilize a constant batch size determined through empirical inspection. However, the batch size significantly influences the stochastic optimization algorithm's behavior, as it dictates the variance of gradient estimates. This variance also fluctuates throughout the optimization process, often requiring a (manually tuned) decreasing learning rate schedule to ensure stability and convergence when using a constant batch size. This paper proposes a practical method for dynamically adapting the batch size. The method estimates the variance of stochastic gradients and adjusts the batch size to decrease the variance proportionally to the objective function's value, eliminating the need for the aforementioned learning rate decrease. Unlike recent related works, this algorithm couples the batch size to the learning rate, directly reflecting the known relationship between the two. On popular image classification benchmarks, this batch size adaptation leads to faster optimization convergence while simplifying learning rate tuning. A TensorFlow implementation is readily available.
label: AI

title: A Fully Convolutional Deep Auditory Model for Musical Chord Recognition
Abstract: Chord recognition systems rely on robust feature extraction pipelines. While these pipelines are traditionally hand-crafted, recent advancements in end-to-end machine learning have inspired researchers to explore data-driven methods for such tasks. This paper presents a chord recognition system that utilizes a fully convolutional deep auditory model for feature extraction. The extracted features are then processed by a Conditional Random Field, which decodes the final chord sequence. Both processing stages are trained automatically, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in parameter optimization. This paper demonstrates that the learned auditory system extracts musically interpretable features and that the proposed chord recognition system achieves results comparable to or exceeding those of state-of-the-art algorithms.
label: AI

title: Towards End-to-End Audio-Sheet-Music Retrieval
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the feasibility of learning to retrieve short snippets of sheet music (images) when given a short query excerpt of music (audio), and vice versa, without relying on symbolic representation of music or scores. This capability would be highly valuable in numerous content-based musical retrieval scenarios. The approach is based on Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis (DCCA), which learns correlated latent spaces enabling cross-modality retrieval in both directions. Initial experiments using relatively simple monophonic music show promising results.
label: AI

title: Feature Learning for Chord Recognition: The Deep Chroma Extractor
Abstract: This paper explores frame-level audio feature learning for chord recognition using artificial neural networks. It argues that chroma vectors potentially hold sufficient information to model the harmonic content of audio for chord recognition but that standard chroma extractors produce overly noisy features. Consequently, the paper proposes a learned chroma feature extractor based on artificial neural networks. This extractor is trained to compute chroma features that encode harmonic information crucial for chord recognition while being robust to irrelevant interferences. This is achieved by feeding the network an audio spectrum with context instead of a single frame as input, enabling the network to learn to selectively compensate for noise and resolve harmonic ambiguities. The resulting features are compared to hand-crafted ones using a simple linear frame-wise classifier for chord recognition on various datasets. Results demonstrate that the learned feature extractor generates superior chroma vectors for chord recognition.
label: AI

title: Reflectance Adaptive Filtering Improves Intrinsic Image Estimation
Abstract: Separating an image into reflectance and shading layers poses a challenge for learning approaches due to the lack of a large corpus of precise and realistic ground truth decompositions. The Intrinsic Images in the Wild (IIW) dataset offers a sparse set of relative human reflectance judgments, serving as a standard benchmark for intrinsic images. Several methods utilize IIW to learn statistical dependencies between images and their reflectance layer. While learning plays a crucial role in achieving high performance, this paper shows that a standard signal processing technique matches the performance of current state-of-the-art methods. It proposes a loss function for CNN learning of dense reflectance predictions. The findings demonstrate that a simple pixel-wise decision, without any context or prior knowledge, provides a strong baseline on IIW, surpassed by only two other approaches. The paper then develops a joint bilateral filtering method that incorporates strong prior knowledge about reflectance constancy. This filtering operation can be applied to any intrinsic image algorithm, improving several previous results and establishing a new state-of-the-art on IIW. These results suggest that the impact of learning-based approaches might have been overestimated. Explicit prior knowledge remains at least as essential in achieving high performance in intrinsic image decompositions.
label: AI

title: Graphical RNN Models
Abstract: Many time series are generated by a set of entities that interact with one another over time. This paper introduces a broad, flexible framework for learning from multiple inter-dependent time series generated by such entities. The framework explicitly models the entities and their interactions over time by building upon the capabilities of Recurrent Neural Networks while offering various ways to incorporate domain knowledge/constraints into the model architecture. The application of this approach to weather prediction showcases its capabilities, demonstrating gains over strong baselines.
label: AI

title: Expectation Propagation performs a smoothed gradient descent
Abstract: Bayesian inference is a popular method for constructing learning algorithms but faces the challenge that its central object, the posterior probability distribution, is often uncomputable. Expectation Propagation (EP) (Minka (2001)) is a widely used algorithm that addresses this issue by computing a parametric approximation (e.g., Gaussian) to the posterior density. While empirically known to quickly compute fine approximations, EP remains poorly understood, hindering its adoption by a broader community. This paper aims to shed intuitive light on EP by relating it to other better-understood methods. It establishes a connection between EP and using gradient descent to compute the Laplace approximation of a target probability distribution. The paper shows that EP is precisely equivalent to performing gradient descent on a smoothed energy landscape – the original energy landscape convoluted with a smoothing kernel. This also connects EP to algorithms that compute the Gaussian approximation minimizing the reverse KL divergence to the target distribution, a link previously conjectured but not rigorously proven. These findings can help practitioners gain a better understanding of how EP operates and may lead to new results concerning this significant method.
label: AI

title: Towards Score Following in Sheet Music Images
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of matching short music audio snippets to their corresponding pixel location in images of sheet music. It presents a system that simultaneously learns to read notes, listens to music, and matches the currently played music to its corresponding notes in the sheet. The system consists of an end-to-end multi-modal convolutional neural network that takes as input images of sheet music and spectrograms of the respective audio snippets. It learns to predict, for a given unseen audio snippet (covering approximately one bar of music), the corresponding position in the respective score line. The results suggest that utilizing (deep) neural networks, proven to be powerful image processing models, makes working with sheet music feasible and a promising future research direction.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Message Passing For Graphical Models
Abstract: Bayesian inference on structured models typically relies on the ability to infer posterior distributions of underlying hidden variables. However, inference in implicit models or complex posterior distributions presents significant challenges. Generative adversarial networks (GANs), a popular tool for learning implicit models, learn parameters of generators by fooling discriminators. GANs are typically viewed as models themselves and not understood in the context of inference. Current techniques rely on inefficient global discrimination of joint distributions for learning or only consider discriminating a single output variable. This paper overcomes these limitations by treating GANs as a basis for likelihood-free inference in generative models and generalizes them to Bayesian posterior inference over factor graphs. It proposes local learning rules based on message passing that minimize a global divergence criterion involving cooperating local adversaries to circumvent explicit likelihood evaluations. This approach enables model composition and yields a unified inference and learning framework for adversarial learning. The framework separates model specification and inference, facilitating richly structured models within the Directed Acyclic Graphs family, including components like intractable likelihoods, non-differentiable models, simulators, and generally cumbersome models. A key insight is that Bayesian inference on structured models can be performed solely with sampling and discrimination when using nonparametric variational families, without access to explicit distributions. As a byproduct, the paper discusses the link to likelihood maximization. These approaches hold promise for probabilistic modelers and expand the range of current probabilistic programming applications.

title: Optimal structure and parameter learning of Ising models
Abstract: Reconstructing the structure and parameters of an Ising model from binary samples is a problem of practical significance in various fields, ranging from statistical physics and computational biology to image processing and machine learning. The research community has shifted its focus towards developing universal reconstruction algorithms that are computationally efficient and require minimal expensive data. This paper introduces a new method, Interaction Screening, which accurately estimates model parameters using local optimization problems. The algorithm demonstrably achieves perfect graph structure recovery with an information-theoretically optimal number of samples, particularly in the low-temperature regime known for its difficulty in learning. The efficacy of Interaction Screening is assessed through extensive numerical tests on synthetic Ising models of diverse topologies with different interaction types, as well as on real data generated by a D-Wave quantum computer. This study reveals that Interaction Screening is an exact, tractable, and optimal technique that universally solves the inverse Ising problem.
label: AI

title: Graph-based semi-supervised learning for relational networks
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of semi-supervised learning in relational networks, networks where nodes represent entities and links represent the relationships or interactions between them. This problem is often conflated with graph-based semi-supervised learning (GSSL), as both represent data as a graph and predict missing class labels of nodes. However, not all graphs are created equal. In GSSL, a graph is constructed, often from independent data, based on similarity, resulting in edges connecting instances with the same class label. Conversely, relational networks can be more heterogeneous, and edges do not always indicate similarity. For instance, links might occur more frequently between nodes with different class labels (link-heterogeneity) instead of nodes with the same class label. Additionally, nodes with the same class label might not exhibit the same connectivity type across the entire network (class-heterogeneity), e.g., in a sexual interaction network, links between opposite genders may be observed in some parts of the graph, while links between the same genders may occur in others. Performing classification in networks with different types of heterogeneity presents a challenging task, further complicated by the absence of prior knowledge about the type or level of heterogeneity. This paper presents two scalable approaches for graph-based semi-supervised learning applicable to the more general case of relational networks. These approaches are demonstrated on synthetic and real-world networks exhibiting diverse link patterns within and between classes. Compared to state-of-the-art approaches, the proposed methods achieve better classification performance without prior knowledge of class interactions. In particular, the two-step label propagation algorithm consistently delivers good accuracy and operates on networks with over 1.6 million nodes and 30 million edges in approximately 12 seconds.
label: AI

title: Improving Neural Network Generalization by Combining Parallel Circuits with Dropout
Abstract: To address the lengthy training times of neural networks, Parallel Circuits (PCs), a biologically inspired architecture, was proposed. Previous work has shown that while this approach achieves significant speed gains, it fails to maintain generalization performance. Motivated by the way Dropout prevents node co-adaptation, this paper suggests an improvement by extending Dropout to the PC architecture. The paper provides insights into this combination, including various fusion approaches. Experiments reveal promising results, showing improved error rates in most cases while retaining the speed advantage of the PC approach.
label: AI

title: Learning through Dialogue Interactions by Asking Questions
Abstract: An effective dialogue agent should possess the ability to engage with users by both responding to questions and asking questions, and importantly, learn from both interaction types. This paper explores this direction by designing a simulator and a set of synthetic tasks in the movie domain that facilitate such interactions between a learner and a teacher. It investigates how a learner can benefit from asking questions in both offline and online reinforcement learning settings, demonstrating improved learner performance when asking questions. Real experiments using Mechanical Turk validate the approach. This work represents a first step towards developing end-to-end learned interactive dialogue agents.
label: AI

title: What have we learned about the sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays via neutrino astronomy?
Abstract: Observations of TeV--PeV-energy cosmic neutrinos by the IceCube observatory suggest that extragalactic cosmic-ray sources should have an optical depth greater than $\\sim$0.01 and contribute to more than 10\\% of the observed bulk of cosmic rays at 10 PeV. If the spectrum of cosmic rays from these extragalactic sources extends well beyond 1 EeV, the neutrino flux indicates that extragalactic cosmic-ray protons dominate the observed total cosmic-ray flux at 1 EeV. Among known powerful astronomical objects, including gamma-ray bursters (GRBs), only flat-spectrum radio quasars could (barely) satisfy these conditions. However, the null detection of neutrinos with energies significantly exceeding PeV excludes the possibility that radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and/or GRBs, popular source candidates discussed in the literature, are the origins of the highest-energy cosmic rays ($\\sim100 {\\rm EeV}$) if they are mainly composed of protons. Their origins must be objects that have evolved on timescales comparable to or slower than the star formation rate. These considerations indicate that none of the known extragalactic astronomical objects can simultaneously be a source of both PeV- and trans-EeV-energy cosmic rays. Due to the stringent limits on EeV-energy neutrino fluxes, a significant portion of the parameter space for the AGN and new-born pulsar models is starting to appear unfavorable, even for scenarios involving mixed and heavy cosmic-ray compositions at the highest energies.
label: AI

title: Dynamical Kinds and their Discovery
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the possibility of classifying causal systems into kinds that share a common structure without first constructing an explicit dynamical model or using prior knowledge of the system dynamics. The algorithmic ability to determine whether arbitrary systems are governed by causal relations of the same form offers significant practical applications in the development and validation of dynamical models. It is also theoretically interesting as a crucial stage in the scientific inference of laws from empirical data. The presented algorithm is based on the dynamical symmetry approach to dynamical kinds. A dynamical symmetry with respect to time is an intervention on one or more variables of a system that commutes with the system's time evolution. A dynamical kind is a class of systems sharing a set of dynamical symmetries. The algorithm presented classifies deterministic, time-dependent causal systems by directly comparing their exhibited symmetries. Using simulated, noisy data from a variety of nonlinear systems, the paper shows that this algorithm correctly sorts systems into dynamical kinds. It is robust under significant sampling error, immune to violations of normality in sampling error, and fails gracefully with increasing dynamical similarity. The algorithm demonstrated is the first to address this aspect of automated scientific discovery.
label: AI

title: Music Generation with Deep Learning
Abstract: The application of deep learning to solve problems in literary arts has become a recent trend garnering significant attention. Automated music generation has also been an active area of research. This project focuses on music generation using raw audio files in the frequency domain, relying on various LSTM architectures. Fully connected and convolutional layers are employed alongside LSTMs to capture rich features in the frequency domain, enhancing the quality of the generated music. The work centers on unconstrained music generation and does not utilize information about musical structure (notes or chords) to assist learning. The music generated from different architectures is compared using blindfold tests. Training models directly on raw audio provides a means to tap into the vast amount of mp3 files available online without requiring manual effort to create structured MIDI files. Furthermore, not all audio files can be represented with MIDI files, making the study of these models an intriguing prospect for the future of such models.

title: Deep Learning the Quantum Phase Transitions in Random Electron Systems: Applications to Three Dimensions
Abstract: Three-dimensional random electron systems exhibit a variety of quantum phases, including band gap insulators, Anderson insulators, topological insulators, Weyl semimetals, and diffusive metals.  We utilize a multilayered convolutional neural network to classify eigenfunctions according to their phase, leveraging an image recognition algorithm similar to our previous work on two-dimensional quantum phase transitions.  Our approach successfully characterizes various models: the Anderson model for localization-delocalization transitions, the Wilson-Dirac model for topological insulators, and the layered Chern insulator model for Weyl semimetals.  This method also provides a solution for situations where traditional transfer matrix approaches are not applicable.
label: AI

title: Tinkering Under the Hood: Interactive Zero-Shot Learning with Net Surgery
Abstract: A novel approach to visual net surgery is presented, allowing for the reconfiguration of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to recognize new concepts without requiring additional training data.  Unlike previous approaches that rely on linguistic cues for zero-shot learning, we exploit the pictorial language representation implicitly learned by the CNN to generalize to unseen classes.  This is achieved through visualization techniques that reveal activation patterns and relationships between CNN filters.  We then introduce a "pictorial language classifier" (PLC) which reconfigures specific CNN neurons into a part model.  These PLCs demonstrate robustness in weakly supervised scenarios, enabling the labeling of unlabeled concepts for visual classes present in the training data.  For example, a PLC built on a CNN trained for ImageNet classification successfully localizes humans in Graz-02 and determines the pose of birds in PASCAL-VOC without requiring extra labeled data or retraining.  Furthermore, we demonstrate interactive zero-shot learning using PLCs, showcasing their ability to detect visual classes in MS-COCO that were absent from the ImageNet training set.
label: AI

title: Semi-Supervised Phone Classification using Deep Neural Networks and Stochastic Graph-Based Entropic Regularization
Abstract: This paper presents a semi-supervised learning framework based on graph regularization for deep neural networks.  It utilizes a graph-based entropic regularizer to favor smooth solutions over a graph induced by the data.  A computationally efficient, stochastic graph-regularization technique is introduced, employing mini-batches that are consistent with the graph structure while maintaining sufficient stochasticity for the convergence of stochastic gradient descent methods.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method on the TIMIT speech corpus, achieving significant improvements in frame-level phone classification accuracy when the fraction of labeled data is low.  The proposed approach is general and scalable to large datasets, offering comparable performance to other methods in fully labeled scenarios.
label: AI

title: Efficient Distributed Semi-Supervised Learning using Stochastic Regularization over Affinity Graphs
Abstract: A computationally efficient, stochastic graph-regularization technique is presented for semi-supervised training of deep neural networks in parallel or distributed settings.  This technique leverages synthesized partitions of an affinity graph to create mini-batches consistent with the graph structure while preserving enough stochasticity for convergence of stochastic gradient descent.  This approach allows for the decomposition of a graph-based semi-supervised loss function into a sum over objectives, enabling data parallelism for scalable training of machine learning models.  Empirical results indicate that this method significantly improves classification accuracy compared to fully supervised training when the fraction of labeled data is low.  In parallel settings, it achieves significant speed-up in terms of wall-clock time to convergence.  The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated on a speech corpus using both sequential and distributed-memory semi-supervised DNN training.
label: AI

title: Learning binary or real-valued time-series via spike-timing dependent plasticity
Abstract: The dynamic Boltzmann machine (DyBM), a model of a spiking neural network, exhibits key properties of spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP), a learning rule that refines the Hebbian rule.  This paper relaxes constraints in the DyBM to enhance its computational and learning capabilities.  It demonstrates that DyBM learning can be viewed as logistic regression for binary-valued time-series and introduces the Gaussian DyBM, enabling learning of real-valued data.  The Gaussian DyBM extends the vector autoregressive (VAR) model by incorporating additional explanatory variables, representing eligibility traces and capturing long-term dependency in the time-series.  Numerical experiments reveal significant improvements in predictive accuracy of the Gaussian DyBM compared to the VAR model.
label: AI

title: Projected Regression Methods for Inverting Fredholm Integrals: Formalism and Application to Analytical Continuation
Abstract: This paper presents a machine learning approach for inverting Fredholm integrals of the first kind, offering a natural regularization mechanism for ill-conditioned inverse problems and facilitating the efficient and stable handling of constraints.  The approach leverages the stability of the forward problem to construct a large database of outputs corresponding to physically meaningful inputs.  Machine learning is applied to this database to generate a regression function of controlled complexity, providing approximate solutions for unseen inputs.  These approximate solutions are then projected onto the subspace of functions satisfying relevant constraints, and uncertainty estimates are derived.  The approach is illustrated using the analytical continuation problem in quantum many-body physics, where it demonstrates competitive performance with the Maximum Entropy method for low input noise and superior robustness to increased input noise.  This methodology is expected to be effective for any ill-conditioned inversion problem where the forward problem can be efficiently solved.
label: AI

title: Deep learning is effective for the classification of OCT images of normal versus Age-related Macular Degeneration
Abstract: The advent of Electronic Medical Records (EMR) with large electronic imaging databases, coupled with advancements in deep neural networks and machine learning, presents a unique opportunity for automating image analysis.  This study investigates the application of deep learning to distinguish normal Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images from images of patients with Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD).  The study utilized an automated extraction of an OCT imaging database linked to clinical endpoints from the EMR.  A deep neural network was trained to classify images as normal or AMD.  The results demonstrate high accuracy in image classification: 92.78% area under the receiver operator curve (auROC) at the image level, 93.83% auROC at the macula level, and 97.45% auROC at the patient level.  These findings suggest the potential for deep learning to enhance automated screening and computer-aided diagnosis tools using OCT.
label: AI

title: A Data-Driven Compressive Sensing Framework Tailored For Energy-Efficient Wearable Sensing
Abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) is a promising technology for energy-efficient wireless sensors in long-term health monitoring.  However, conventional model-driven CS frameworks struggle with limited compression ratios and reconstruction quality when dealing with physiological signals due to inaccurate models and the neglect of individual variability.  This paper introduces a data-driven CS framework that learns signal characteristics and personalized features from individual recordings of physiological signals, enhancing CS performance with a minimized number of measurements.  This improvement is achieved through a co-training approach that optimizes the sensing matrix and dictionary for improved restricted isometry property and signal sparsity, respectively.  Experimental results using ECG signals demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a compression ratio of 10x while reducing the isometry constant of trained sensing matrices by 86% compared to random matrices and improving the overall reconstructed signal-to-noise ratio by 15 dB over conventional model-driven approaches.
label: AI

title: Collaborative creativity with Monte-Carlo Tree Search and Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This research explores a collaborative drawing environment where an autonomous agent sketches images while allowing user intervention in its trajectory.  Monte Carlo Tree Search is combined with image classifiers, including both shallow models (e.g., multinomial logistic regression) and deep Convolutional Neural Networks (e.g., LeNet, Inception v3).  Results show that the agent produces a limited variety of recognizable images when using shallow models, but generates a more diverse range of images with deeper models.  While the agent remains confident in achieving its objective, these images appear as unrecognizable noise to humans.  This aligns with recent research highlighting the susceptibility of deep neural networks to being fooled, and the paper discusses potential solutions and future directions for this research.
label: AI

title: Robust Local Scaling using Conditional Quantiles of Graph Similarities
Abstract: Spectral analysis of neighborhood graphs is a widely used technique in exploratory data analysis, spanning applications from machine learning to social sciences.  This paper proposes a quantile analysis approach for robust neighborhood graph construction, addressing the sensitivity of traditional methods to parameter choices, noise, and varying data densities.  An auto-encoding neural network infers conditional quantiles of a similarity function, providing robust estimates of local scales for neighborhood graph construction.  This approach is highly resilient to noise and outliers, and unlike existing methods, does not require extensive parameter tuning.  The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated in spectral clustering and single-example label propagation tasks, where it outperforms existing locally scaled graph construction approaches.
label: AI

title: Interpretable Semantic Textual Similarity: Finding and explaining differences between sentences
Abstract: User acceptance of artificial intelligence agents may depend on their ability to explain their reasoning, necessitating an interpretability layer to facilitate user understanding of their behavior.  This paper focuses on adding an interpretable layer to Semantic Textual Similarity (STS), a measure of semantic equivalence between sentences.  The interpretability layer is formalized as the alignment between pairs of segments across the two sentences, where the relation between segments is labeled with a relation type and a similarity score.  A publicly available dataset of sentence pairs annotated with this formalization is presented, along with a system trained on this dataset to explain similarities and differences in the form of graded and typed segment alignments.  Evaluation results show that the system outperforms an informed baseline, demonstrating the feasibility of the dataset and task.  User studies provide preliminary evidence that the system's output can be used to automatically produce natural language explanations, improving user performance compared to scenarios without explanations.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Optimization for Machine Learning : A Practical Guidebook
Abstract: The engineering of machine learning systems is a rapidly evolving field, relying on a diverse collection of tools and best practices.  This guidebook aims to provide a valuable resource for machine learning practitioners seeking to leverage Bayesian optimization techniques.  Four example machine learning problems are presented, showcasing the benefits of Bayesian optimization in common machine learning applications using open source machine learning libraries.

title: Constraint Selection in Metric Learning
Abstract: Many machine learning algorithms rely on metrics or distances to compare individuals.  While the Euclidean distance is commonly used, learning a parametric distance like the Mahalanobis metric can be more efficient.  This paper introduces a simple approach to improve the accuracy and scalability of iterative metric learning algorithms by employing a loss-dependent weighted selection of constraints prior to the algorithm.  This method utilizes a dedicated loss function and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and time complexity.  Experimental results on real-world and large datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.
label: AI

title: The More You Know: Using Knowledge Graphs for Image Classification
Abstract: One of the key distinctions between humans and modern learning-based computer vision algorithms is the ability to acquire knowledge about the world and apply it to visual reasoning.  Humans can learn about object characteristics and relationships between them to acquire a diverse set of visual concepts, often with limited examples.  This paper explores the incorporation of structured prior knowledge in the form of knowledge graphs to enhance image classification performance.  Building on recent work on end-to-end learning on graphs, the Graph Search Neural Network is introduced as a method for efficiently incorporating large knowledge graphs into a vision classification pipeline.  Experiments demonstrate that this approach outperforms standard neural network baselines for multi-label classification.
label: AI

title: Uncovering the Dynamics of Crowdlearning and the Value of Knowledge
Abstract: Crowdlearning, where users learn from and contribute knowledge on online platforms, has gained popularity in the Web and social media.  This paper presents a probabilistic modeling framework for crowdlearning that analyzes the evolution of a user's expertise over time, leveraging assessments from other users.  The model captures both off-site and on-site learning, as well as knowledge forgetting.  A scalable estimation method is developed to fit model parameters from millions of recorded learning and contributing events.  The model's effectiveness is demonstrated by tracing the activity of 25,000 users on Stack Overflow over a 4.5-year period.  Findings reveal that answers with high knowledge value are rare, and both newbies and experts acquire less knowledge than mid-level users.  Prolific learners tend to be proficient contributors, posting answers with high knowledge value.
label: AI

title: Fast-AT: Fast Automatic Thumbnail Generation using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Fast-AT is a deep neural network-based automatic thumbnail generation system.  It utilizes a fully convolutional deep neural network to learn specific filters for thumbnails of different sizes and aspect ratios, selecting the appropriate filter based on the target thumbnail dimensions.  Unlike previous methods that rely on saliency, Fast-AT directly addresses the problem, eliminating the need for region search on the saliency map.  The model generalizes to thumbnails of various sizes, including those with extreme aspect ratios, and can generate thumbnails in real time.  A dataset of over 70,000 thumbnail annotations was collected for training Fast-AT, which demonstrates competitive results compared to existing techniques.
label: AI

title: Anomaly Detection Using the Knowledge-based Temporal Abstraction Method
Abstract: The rapid growth in stored time-oriented data necessitates the development of new methods for handling, processing, and interpreting large amounts of temporal data.  Anomaly detection in time-oriented data is a critical aspect of this processing.  This paper proposes a framework that integrates the Knowledge-Based Temporal Abstraction (KBTA) method with temporal pattern mining for anomaly detection.  The approach applies temporal pattern mining to a dataset of basic temporal abstraction databases to extract patterns representing normal behavior.  These patterns are then analyzed to identify abnormal time periods characterized by a significantly small number of normal patterns.  The framework is demonstrated using a dataset collected from a real server.
label: AI

title: Deep Function Machines: Generalized Neural Networks for Topological Layer Expression
Abstract: This paper introduces a generalization of deep neural networks called deep function machines (DFMs), which operate on vector spaces of arbitrary (potentially infinite) dimension.  The paper demonstrates that a family of DFMs are invariant to the dimension of input data, meaning that the model's parameterization is not directly dependent on the quality of the input.  This generalization leads to a new theory of universal approximation of bounded non-linear operators between function spaces.  The authors suggest that DFMs provide a flexible framework for designing new neural network layer types with topological considerations.  Finally, a novel architecture, RippLeNet, for resolution invariant computer vision is introduced, achieving state-of-the-art invariance empirically.

title: Quantum Monte Carlo simulation of a particular class of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians in quantum annealing
Abstract: Quantum annealing is a generic solver for optimization problems that utilizes fictitious quantum fluctuation.  Classical computer simulations of quantum annealing often employ quantum Monte Carlo simulation via the Suzuki-Trotter decomposition.  However, the negative sign problem can arise in simulating quantum annealing with complex driver Hamiltonians, as they belong to a class of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians.  This paper proposes an alternative approach to avoid the negative sign problem for a specific class of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians.  The method's validity is demonstrated by applying it to a simple problem involving anti-ferromagnetic XX interaction, a typical instance of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians.
label: AI

title: An Improved Deterministic Rescaling for Linear Programming Algorithms
Abstract: The perceptron algorithm for linear programming, rooted in machine learning, has been employed since the 1950s.  While not a polynomial-time algorithm, its simplicity and robustness make it practically useful.  In 2004, Dunagan and Vempala demonstrated that randomized rescaling transforms the perceptron method into a polynomial-time algorithm, followed by a deterministic rescaling approach by Pe~{n}a and Soheili.  This paper presents a deterministic rescaling for the perceptron algorithm that improves upon previous rescaling methods by enabling earlier rescaling, leading to a faster running time for the rescaled perceptron algorithm.  The same rescaling methods are shown to yield a polynomial-time algorithm based on the multiplicative weights update method, highlighting a connection to an area of significant recent interest in theoretical computer science.  |||

title: Beam Search for Learning a Deep Convolutional Neural Network of 3D Shapes
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to 3D shape recognition by formulating CNN learning as a beam search optimization problem. The goal is to find the optimal CNN architecture, including the number of layers, nodes, and their connectivity, as well as the optimal parameters. The beam search efficiently explores candidate CNNs by transferring parameters from parent to child networks. Experiments on the 3D ModelNet dataset demonstrate that this approach yields a CNN with superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Detect, Replace, Refine: Deep Structured Prediction For Pixel Wise Labeling
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of pixel-wise image labeling by proposing a novel architecture that decomposes the label improvement task into three steps: detection, replacement, and refinement. The architecture identifies incorrect labels, replaces them with new ones, and refines the renewed labels by predicting residual corrections. The proposed approach is evaluated in the challenging task of dense disparity estimation (stereo matching) and achieves state-of-the-art results on three different datasets, surpassing previous methods by a significant margin.

title: Encapsulating models and approximate inference programs in probabilistic modules
Abstract: This paper introduces the probabilistic module interface, which provides a platform-agnostic abstraction barrier between complex probabilistic models and their host inference systems. This interface allows the encapsulation of latent variables and custom stochastic approximate inference machinery, providing a stochastic generalization of standard simulation and density interfaces. The paper demonstrates that sound approximate inference algorithms can be constructed for networks of probabilistic modules using learned stochastic inference networks, MCMC, and SMC approximate inference programs.

title: Incorporating Language Level Information into Acoustic Models
Abstract: This paper presents a novel class of Deep Recurrent Neural Networks, called Recurrent Deep Language Networks (RDLNs), which incorporate language-level information into acoustic models for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). The paper explores different variants of RDLNs, including various context information processing methods and techniques for incorporating language-level information. RDLNs offer a potential approach to fine-tuning the entire ASR system during the acoustic modeling process.

title: On convergence rates of game theoretic reinforcement learning algorithms
Abstract: This paper focuses on multi-player discrete games where players aim to maximize their utility functions without complete knowledge of each other's actions, action sets, or utility function structures. The authors propose a reinforcement learning algorithm that converges to the set of action profiles with maximal stochastic potential with probability one, quantifying the convergence rate. The algorithm's performance is validated through case studies in the smart grid and cybersecurity domains.

title: Network cross-validation by edge sampling
Abstract: This paper proposes a new resampling strategy for network data, addressing the challenge of applying cross-validation to network analysis. The approach involves splitting node pairs instead of individual nodes, preserving the network structure. The paper provides theoretical justification and demonstrates how this method can be applied to various network model selection and parameter tuning tasks. Numerical results on simulated and real-world networks demonstrate the effectiveness of this cross-validation approach.

title: Virtual Breathalyzer
Abstract: This research presents a novel approach for detecting intoxication using motion differences captured by wearable sensors. The problem is formalized as a supervised machine learning task, both as a binary classification (drunk or sober) and a regression (breath alcohol content level). Data collected from 30 subjects using wearable devices and validated against a breathalyzer show that the proposed system can successfully detect intoxication with high accuracy (0.95 AUC, 0.05 FPR, 1.0 TPR). This system can be used to analyze the gait of individuals and alert them or connected cars about potential drunk driving situations.

title: VAST : The Virtual Acoustic Space Traveler Dataset
Abstract: This paper introduces a new paradigm for sound source localization called Virtual Acoustic Space Traveling (VAST), along with a novel dataset for this purpose. VAST overcomes the limitations of existing methods by learning a mapping from audio features to desired audio properties using a massive dataset of simulated room impulse responses. This virtual dataset is designed to be maximally representative of potential audio scenes while remaining compact. The paper demonstrates that mappings learned virtually on this dataset generalize to real data, overcoming challenges faced by traditional binaural sound localization methods.
label: AI

title: Real-time interactive sequence generation and control with Recurrent Neural Network ensembles
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for real-time continuous control and steering of sequence generation using an ensemble of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). By dynamically altering the mixture weights of the models, users can interact with the generation process in real-time. The paper demonstrates this method using character-based LSTM networks and a gestural interface, enabling users to "conduct" the generation of text.

title: IEDC: An Integrated Approach for Overlapping and Non-overlapping Community Detection
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for general community detection in social network analysis, addressing the challenge of handling both overlapping and non-overlapping community structures. The proposed framework utilizes a primary node-based criterion that considers both internal and external association degrees. The evaluation through simulations and real network datasets shows that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms based on well-known evaluation criteria.

title: Stable Memory Allocation in the Hippocampus: Fundamental Limits and Neural Realization
Abstract: This paper investigates the role of the hippocampus as a memory allocator in the brain, drawing on Valiant's neuroidal model. The authors formulate the requirements for a stable memory allocator (SMA) mathematically, introducing the concept of capacity based on the probability of erroneous allocation. They prove fundamental limits for the capacity and error probability of SMA and provide an example of a stable memory allocator implementable via neuroidal circuits. Theoretical bounds and simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of neural SMA functions.

title: Harmonic Networks: Deep Translation and Rotation Equivariance
Abstract: This paper addresses the lack of rotational equivariance in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by introducing Harmonic Networks (H-Nets). H-Nets replace regular CNN filters with circular harmonics, achieving equivariance to patch-wise translation and 360-rotation. This approach utilizes a rich, parameter-efficient, and computationally efficient representation, encoding complicated rotational invariants in deep feature maps. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of H-Nets on rotated-MNIST and other benchmark challenges, achieving state-of-the-art results.
label: AI

title: Predicting Process Behaviour using Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper explores the application of deep learning with recurrent neural networks for predicting the next event in a business process. The approach, inspired by research in natural language processing, offers a novel method for process prediction that surpasses state-of-the-art precision compared to methods relying on explicit process models. The approach is evaluated on two real datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Retrieving sinusoids from nonuniformly sampled data using recursive formulation
Abstract: This paper presents a heuristic procedure for decomposing 1-D signals into a sparse set of sinusoids (SSS), combining novel recursive formulation of sinusoid (RFS) and regression with predictive least-squares (LS). The procedure estimates both the cardinality and parameters of SSS by optimizing RFS parameters of near-optimal sinusoids using Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) optimization. The algorithm can identify RFS parameters of a sinusoid from a data sequence containing only a fraction of its cycle, detect linear trends, and reconstruct under-sampled sinusoids. The parsimonious nature of the obtained models makes this method suitable for machine learning and intelligent systems requiring signal analysis and representation.

title: Scalable Group Level Probabilistic Sparse Factor Analysis
Abstract: This paper proposes a probabilistic sparse factor analysis (psFA) model for extracting neural representations from fMRI data. psFA incorporates spatially sparse maps, component pruning using automatic relevance determination (ARD), and subject-specific heteroscedastic spatial noise modeling. The model identifies sparse components and provides a natural way to handle parameter uncertainties. The variational Bayesian framework facilitates the extension to more complex noise models.

title: Permutation-equivariant neural networks applied to dynamics prediction
Abstract: This paper explores permutation-invariant neural network layers in analogy to convolutional layers, which inherently capture translation-invariant operations. The permutation layer proposed in this paper is capable of learning to predict the motion of a variable number of interacting hard discs in 2D. This layer generalizes to different numbers of objects, analogous to the way convolutional layers generalize to different image sizes.
label: AI

title: Astronomical image reconstruction with convolutional neural networks
Abstract: This paper investigates the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image reconstruction in astronomy, offering a computationally efficient and interpretable alternative to traditional optimization-based methods. The approach leverages the fixed complexity per pixel in the prediction step, resulting in linear complexity. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this method is both computationally efficient and competitive with other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Mining Compatible/Incompatible Entities from Question and Answering via Yes/No Answer Classification using Distant Label Expansion
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of extracting compatible and incompatible products from yes/no questions in Product Community Question Answering (PCQA). The proposed approach leverages a two-stage framework: Complementary Entity (product) Recognition (CER) followed by polarity identification. CER is performed using an existing unsupervised method, while polarity identification utilizes a distant PU-learning method combined with a binary classifier. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through experiments on four products.
label: AI

title: Sparse Factorization Layers for Neural Networks with Limited Supervision
Abstract: This paper proposes two novel network layers based on dictionary learning: a sparse factorization layer and a convolutional sparse factorization layer. These layers can be integrated into existing CNNs and trained end-to-end, allowing for semi-supervised learning. Experiments show that networks with these layers outperform classical CNNs when supervised data are limited, demonstrating performance improvements in certain tasks compared to CNNs without sparse factorization layers.

title: Interactive Preference Learning of Utility Functions for Multi-Objective Optimization
Abstract:
This paper proposes a generative model for scalar-valued utility functions to capture human preferences in multi-objective optimization settings. The model enables performance tuning for practical machine learning systems, addressing the challenge of optimizing for multiple metrics. An interactive active learning system is outlined, which refines the understanding of stakeholder preferences using binary preference queries.

title: Fast Stability Scanning for Future Grid Scenario Analysis
Abstract: Future grid scenario analysis necessitates a departure from traditional power system planning, which typically analyzes only a limited number of critical conditions. To account for the inter-seasonal variability in renewable generation within a future grid scenario, computationally intensive time-series analysis is required. This paper proposes a planning framework for rapid stability scanning of future grid scenarios using a novel feature selection algorithm and a self-adaptive PSO-k-means clustering algorithm. To accelerate computation, stability analysis is performed only on a small number of representative cluster centroids instead of the entire set of operating conditions. A simplified model of the Australian National Electricity Market with significant renewable energy penetration is used as a case study for small-signal stability and steady-state voltage stability scanning. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared to exhaustive time series scanning, the proposed framework reduces computational burden by up to ten times while maintaining an acceptable level of accuracy.
label: AI

title: Disentangling Space and Time in Video with Hierarchical Variational Auto-encoders
Abstract: Video data encompasses various forms of feature information, including object identity information, which remains relatively static across multiple video frames, and object pose and style information, which continuously evolves from frame to frame. Existing models often conflate these two types of representations by mapping them to a shared feature space. This paper proposes a probabilistic approach for learning separable representations of object identity and pose information using unsupervised video data. The approach leverages a deep generative model with a factored prior distribution that encodes properties of temporal invariances in the hidden feature set. Learning is achieved through variational inference. The paper presents results of learning identity and pose information on datasets of moving characters and rotating 3D objects. Experimental results demonstrate the model's success in factoring its representation and achieving improved performance in transfer learning tasks.
label: AI

title: Identification of Cancer Patient Subgroups via Smoothed Shortest Path Graph Kernel
Abstract: Characterizing patient somatic mutations through next-generation sequencing technologies offers opportunities for refining cancer subtypes. However, mutation catalogues reveal that only a small subset of genes are frequently altered in patients. Conversely, different genomic alterations can perturb the same pathways. This paper proposes a novel clustering procedure that quantifies patient similarities based on their mutational profiles on pathways using a novel graph kernel. Each KEGG pathway is represented as an undirected graph. For each patient, vertex labels are assigned based on their altered genes. The smoothed shortest path graph kernel (smSPK) evaluates each patient pair by comparing their vertex-labeled pathway graphs. The clustering procedure involves two steps: first, the smSPK kernel matrix derived for each pathway is input to the kernel k-means algorithm, and each pathway is evaluated individually. Subsequently, only successful pathways are combined into a single kernel input for kernel k-means to stratify patients. Evaluation on simulated data showed that smSPK clusters patients with up to 88% accuracy. Finally, to identify ovarian cancer patient subgroups, the methodology is applied to the Cancer Genome Atlas ovarian data, encompassing 481 patients. The identified subgroups are evaluated through survival analysis. Grouping patients into four clusters reveals significant differences in their survival times (p-value ≤ 0.005).
label: AI

title: Improving Neural Language Models with a Continuous Cache
Abstract: This paper presents an extension to neural network language models that adapts their prediction to recent history. The proposed model, a simplified version of memory-augmented networks, stores past hidden activations as memory and accesses them through a dot product with the current hidden activation. This mechanism is highly efficient and scalable to very large memory sizes. The paper also draws a connection between the use of external memory in neural networks and cache models used with count-based language models. The approach is demonstrated on several language model datasets and shows significantly better performance than recent memory-augmented networks.
label: AI

title: On the Convergence of Asynchronous Parallel Iteration with Unbounded Delays
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed the emergence of asynchronous parallel (async-parallel) iterative algorithms due to the increasing prevalence of problems involving extremely large-scale data and a vast number of decision variables. Asynchrony introduces outdated information into iterate computations. The delay, which represents the age of outdated information, is defined as the number of updates since its creation. Most recent works prove convergence under the assumption of a finite maximum delay and set their stepsize parameters accordingly. However, the maximum delay is often unknown in practice. This paper presents a convergence analysis of an async-parallel method from a probabilistic perspective, allowing for large, unbounded delays. An explicit formula for the stepsize that guarantees convergence is provided, depending on the statistics of delays. With p+1 identical processors, empirical measurements demonstrate that delays closely follow the Poisson distribution with parameter p, aligning with the theoretical model, allowing for appropriate stepsize settings. Simulations on both convex and nonconvex optimization problems validate the analysis and reveal that the existing maximum-delay-induced stepsize is overly conservative, often slowing down algorithm convergence.
label: AI

title: Modeling cognitive deficits following neurodegenerative diseases and traumatic brain injuries with deep convolutional neural networks
Abstract: Accurately diagnosing and assessing neurodegenerative diseases and traumatic brain injuries (TBI) remain significant challenges. Both conditions lead to cognitive and functional deficits due to focal axonal swellings (FAS), but the limited ability to assess damaged neurons at a cellular level in vivo hinders prognosis. This paper utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as a model of cognition to simulate the effects of neurodegenerative diseases and TBI. Biophysically relevant statistical data on FAS is used to functionally damage connections in CNNs. Energy constraints on the brain are incorporated by pruning the CNNs to reduce over-engineering. Qualitatively, the paper demonstrates that damage leads to human-like mistakes. Quantitative assessments of accuracy variations due to different types and levels of damage are also provided. The deficit resulting from a fixed amount of damage varies significantly depending on which connections are randomly injured, offering insight into the difficulty of predicting impairments. Despite the inherent subjectivity in interpreting cognitive deficits from complex systems like the human brain, the paper provides valuable insights and a quantitative framework for disorders involving FAS.
label: AI

title: User Model-Based Intent-Aware Metrics for Multilingual Search Evaluation
Abstract: Despite the growing importance of multilingual aspects in web search, no appropriate offline metrics for evaluating its quality have been proposed. Personal language preferences can be viewed as query intents, translating the multilingual search problem into a task of search diversification. The standard intent-aware approach could be adapted to build a diversified metric for multilingual search based on classical information retrieval (IR) metrics like ERR. The intent-aware approach estimates user satisfaction under a user behavior model. However, this paper demonstrates that the underlying user behavior models are unrealistic in the multilingual case, and the resulting intent-aware metrics do not accurately estimate user satisfaction. A novel approach to build intent-aware user behavior models is developed, overcoming these limitations and converting to quality metrics that better correlate with standard online metrics of user satisfaction.
label: AI

title: Inferring object rankings based on noisy pairwise comparisons from multiple annotators
Abstract: Ranking a set of objects involves establishing an order that facilitates comparisons between any pair of objects within the set. In the absence of a ground truth of ranked orders, researchers often rely on obtaining judgments from multiple annotators, followed by inferring the ground truth based on the collective knowledge of the crowd. However, aggregation is often ad-hoc and involves imposing stringent assumptions in inferring the ground truth (e.g., majority vote). This paper proposes Expectation-Maximization (EM)-based algorithms that utilize judgments from multiple annotators and object attributes to infer the latent ground truth. The algorithm learns the relationship between the latent ground truth and object attributes, as well as annotator-specific probabilities of flipping, a metric for assessing annotator quality. The EM algorithm is extended to allow for a variable probability of flipping based on the pair of objects at hand. The algorithms are tested on two datasets with synthetic annotations to investigate the impact of annotator quality and quantity on the inferred ground truth. Results are also obtained on two other datasets with annotations from machine/human annotators, and output trends are interpreted based on data characteristics.
label: AI

title: Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel generative model called Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (SGAN), trained to invert the hierarchical representations of a bottom-up discriminative network. The model comprises a top-down stack of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), each learned to generate lower-level representations conditioned on higher-level representations. A representation discriminator is introduced at each feature hierarchy to encourage the representation manifold of the generator to align with that of the bottom-up discriminative network, leveraging powerful discriminative representations to guide the generative model. Additionally, a conditional loss is introduced to promote the use of conditional information from the layer above, along with a novel entropy loss that maximizes a variational lower bound on the conditional entropy of generator outputs. Each stack is first trained independently, followed by end-to-end training of the entire model. Unlike the original GAN, which uses a single noise vector to represent all variations, SGAN decomposes variations into multiple levels and gradually resolves uncertainties in the top-down generative process. Through visual inspection, Inception scores, and visual Turing tests, the paper demonstrates that SGAN generates images of significantly higher quality than GANs without stacking.
label: AI

title: Defensive Player Classification in the National Basketball Association
Abstract: The National Basketball Association (NBA) has significantly expanded its data gathering efforts and invested heavily in new technologies to collect advanced performance metrics on players. This expanded dataset enables analysts to utilize unique performance metrics in models for estimating and classifying player performance. Instead of grouping players based on physical attributes and positions played, analysts can now group players who exhibit similar playing styles based on these tracked metrics. Existing methods for player classification typically rely on offensive metrics for clustering. While attempts have been made to classify players using past defensive metrics, the lack of quality metrics has yielded limited results. The classifications presented in this paper utilize newly introduced defensive metrics to identify different defensive positions for each player. Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), which can identify the optimal number of clusters without prior knowledge of category counts, are applied to the model. The model presented identifies five distinct defensive player types.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning for Lane Keeping Assist
Abstract: Reinforcement learning is considered a powerful AI paradigm capable of teaching machines through interaction with the environment and learning from mistakes. However, its application in automotive settings has not yet been fully realized. Recent interest in the topic has been revived by the ability of deep learning algorithms to learn effective representations of the environment. Inspired by Google DeepMind's successful demonstrations of learning for games, ranging from Breakout to Go, this paper proposes different methods for autonomous driving using deep reinforcement learning. This approach is particularly relevant due to the difficulty of formulating autonomous driving as a supervised learning problem, given its strong interaction with the environment, including other vehicles, pedestrians, and roadworks. As this is a relatively new research area for autonomous driving, two main categories of algorithms are formulated: 1) Discrete actions category and 2) Continuous actions category. For the discrete actions category, the Deep Q-Network Algorithm (DQN) is employed, while the Deep Deterministic Actor Critic Algorithm (DDAC) is utilized for the continuous actions category. The paper further investigates the performance of these two categories on an open-source car simulator for racing called TORCS (The Open Racing Car Simulator). Simulation results demonstrate the learning of autonomous maneuvering in scenarios involving complex road curvatures and simple interactions with other vehicles. Finally, the effect of restricted conditions imposed on the car during the learning phase on the convergence time for completing the learning phase is explained.
label: AI

title: Fast Patch-based Style Transfer of Arbitrary Style
Abstract: Artistic style transfer is an image synthesis problem where the content of an image is reproduced with the style of another. Recent studies have shown that visually appealing style transfer can be achieved using the hidden activations of a pretrained convolutional neural network. However, existing methods either employ (i) an optimization procedure that works for any style image but is computationally expensive or (ii) an efficient feedforward network that allows only a limited number of trained styles. This paper proposes a simpler optimization objective based on local matching that combines content structure and style textures within a single layer of the pretrained network. The paper demonstrates that this objective exhibits desirable properties, including a simpler optimization landscape, intuitive parameter tuning, and consistent frame-by-frame performance on video. Furthermore, an inverse network is trained using 80,000 natural images and 80,000 paintings to approximate the result of the optimization. This results in a procedure for artistic style transfer that is efficient while allowing for arbitrary content and style images.
label: AI

title: How do people explore virtual environments?
Abstract: Understanding how people explore immersive virtual environments is crucial for various applications, including designing virtual reality (VR) content, developing new compression algorithms, and learning computational models of saliency or visual attention. While recent research has focused on modeling saliency in desktop viewing conditions, VR significantly differs due to viewing behavior governed by stereoscopic vision and the complex interaction of head orientation, gaze, and other kinematic constraints. To enhance our understanding of viewing behavior and saliency in VR, this paper captures and analyzes gaze and head orientation data from 169 users exploring stereoscopic, static omni-directional panoramas, resulting in a total of 1980 head and gaze trajectories across three viewing conditions. A thorough analysis of the data reveals several important insights, including the existence of a particular fixation bias. This bias is then used to adapt existing saliency predictors to immersive VR conditions. The paper further explores other applications of the data and analysis, such as automatic alignment of VR video cuts, panorama thumbnails, panorama video synopsis, and saliency-based compression.
label: AI

title: Incorporating Human Domain Knowledge into Large Scale Cost Function Learning
Abstract: Recent advancements have demonstrated the capability of Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (FCN) to model cost functions for motion planning in the context of learning driving preferences solely based on demonstration data from human drivers. While pure learning from demonstrations within the framework of Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) is a promising approach, incorporating well-informed human priors into the learning process can further enhance its effectiveness. This paper achieves this by pretraining a model to regress to a manual cost function and refining it based on Maximum Entropy Deep Inverse Reinforcement Learning. By injecting prior knowledge as pretraining for the network, the paper achieves higher robustness, more visually distinct obstacle boundaries, and the ability to capture instances of obstacles that elude models trained purely on demonstration data. Furthermore, by leveraging these human priors, the resulting model can more accurately handle corner cases that are sparsely observed in the demonstration data, such as stairs, slopes, and underpasses.
label: AI

title: Towards Adaptive Training of Agent-based Sparring Partners for Fighter Pilots
Abstract: A key requirement for current artificial decision-makers is their ability to adapt well to unexpected situations. This paper addresses the scenario where an AI for aerial dogfighting, with tunable parameters governing its behavior, must optimize behavior with respect to an objective function evaluated and learned through simulations. Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian Process surrogate is employed as the method for investigating the objective function. A key benefit is that during optimization, the Gaussian Process learns a global estimate of the true objective function, with predicted outcomes and a statistical measure of confidence in areas not yet explored. Modeling the objective function is crucial for understanding possible outcomes within the decision space, which is essential for training and providing feedback to human pilots. However, standard Bayesian optimization does not consistently perform well or provide an accurate Gaussian Process surrogate function for highly volatile objective functions. The paper addresses these problems by introducing a novel sampling technique called Hybrid Repeat/Multi-point Sampling. This technique enables the AI to learn optimal behaviors in highly uncertain environments. Importantly, it not only improves the reliability of optimization but also creates a better model of the entire objective surface. This improved model equips the agent to more accurately and efficiently predict performance in unexplored scenarios.
label: AI

title: Learning physical descriptors for materials science by compressed sensing
Abstract: The availability of big data in materials science opens up new avenues for analyzing material properties and functions, facilitating scientific understanding. Discovering structure within these data that is not directly visible through standard tools and exploiting scientific information requires new and dedicated methodologies based on approaches from statistical learning, compressed sensing, and other recent methods from applied mathematics, computer science, statistics, signal processing, and information science. This paper explains and demonstrates a compressed-sensing-based methodology for feature selection, specifically for discovering physical descriptors, i.e., physical parameters that describe the material and its properties of interest, and associated equations that explicitly and quantitatively describe those relevant properties. As a showcase application and proof of concept, the paper describes how to build a physical model for the quantitative prediction of the crystal structure of binary compound semiconductors.
label: AI

title: An equation-of-state-meter of QCD transition from deep learning
Abstract: Supervised learning with a deep convolutional neural network is used to identify the QCD equation of state (EoS) employed in relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions from the simulated final-state particle spectra ρ(pT, Φ). High-level correlations of ρ(pT, Φ) learned by the neural network act as an effective "EoS-meter" in detecting the nature of the QCD transition. The EoS-meter is model-independent and insensitive to other simulation inputs, especially the initial conditions. Therefore, it provides a powerful direct connection between heavy-ion collision observables and the bulk properties of QCD.
label: AI

title: Neuro-symbolic representation learning on biological knowledge graphs
Abstract: Biological data and knowledge bases increasingly rely on Semantic Web technologies and the use of knowledge graphs for data integration, retrieval, and federated queries. In recent years, feature learning methods applicable to graph-structured data have become available but have not been widely applied and evaluated on structured biological knowledge. This paper develops a novel method for feature learning on biological knowledge graphs. The method combines symbolic methods, particularly knowledge representation using symbolic logic and automated reasoning, with neural networks to generate embeddings of nodes that encode related information within knowledge graphs. Through the use of symbolic logic, these embeddings contain both explicit and implicit information. These embeddings are applied to the prediction of edges in the knowledge graph, representing problems of function prediction, finding candidate genes of diseases, protein-protein interactions, or drug target relations. The method demonstrates performance that matches and sometimes outperforms traditional approaches based on manually crafted features. This method can be applied to any biological knowledge graph, opening up the increasing amount of Semantic Web-based knowledge bases in biology for use in machine learning and data analytics. The method is available at https://github.com/bio-ontology-research-group/walking-rdf-and-owl.
