title: Gradient Coding
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel coding theoretic framework for mitigating stragglers in distributed learning.  The authors show how data block replication and coding across gradients can provide tolerance to failures and stragglers for Synchronous Gradient Descent.  The scheme is implemented in Python using MPI and evaluated on Amazon EC2, demonstrating improved running time and generalization error compared to baseline approaches.

title: Improved prediction accuracy for disease risk mapping using Gaussian Process stacked generalisation
Abstract: Maps of infectious disease, charting spatial variations in infection, endemicity, and health burden, provide crucial evidence for global health planning.  Modern disease mapping efforts employ statistical modeling to account for uncertainties in measurements and spatial interpolation.  Gaussian process regression, a common approach, combines a mean function utilizing predictive power of multiple variables and a covariance function for spatio-temporal shrinkage. While many techniques have been developed to improve covariance function flexibility, mean function models remain typically restricted to simple linear terms.  For infectious diseases, driven by complex interactions, improved mean function modeling can significantly enhance predictive power.  This paper introduces an ensemble approach based on stacked generalization, allowing multiple, non-linear algorithmic mean functions to be jointly embedded within the Gaussian process framework.  Applied to mapping Plasmodium falciparum prevalence data in Sub-Saharan Africa, the generalized ensemble approach outperforms individual methods.

title: Towards an Automated Image De-fencing Algorithm Using Sparsity
Abstract: This position paper proposes an automatic de-fencing algorithm for images of dynamic scenes, addressing the limitations of conventional methods.  The problem is divided into three tasks: automatic fence detection, motion estimation, and data fusion from multiple video frames.  Fence detection utilizes Gabor filters and a machine learning method, while fence removal is framed as an optimization problem modeled by degraded observations. The inverse problem is solved using the split Bregman technique, assuming total variation of the de-fenced image as the regularization constraint.

title: Hebbian Plasticity for Improving Perceptual Decisions
Abstract: Shibata et al. reported that humans could learn to repeatedly evoke a stimulus-associated functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) activity pattern in visual areas V1/V2, achieving visual perceptual learning without stimulus presentation. This paper challenges the attribution of visual improvements to neuroplasticity in adult V1/V2, proposing a Hebbian learning interpretation of these data. The authors argue that the observed improvements result from enhanced perceptual decisions rather than plastic changes in V1/V2.

title: Generalized Deep Image to Image Regression
Abstract: This paper introduces a Deep Convolutional Neural Network architecture, the Recursively Branched Deconvolutional Network (RBDN), serving as a generic image-to-image regressor that can be trained end-to-end without additional machinery. The RBDN develops a multi-context image representation early on through recursive branching with parameter sharing and learnable upsampling.  This representation undergoes a highly non-linear locality preserving transformation through a series of convolutions/deconvolutions without spatial downsampling. The fully convolutional RBDN architecture can handle variable image sizes during inference. Qualitative and quantitative results on three tasks, relighting, denoising, and colorization, demonstrate comparable performance to state-of-the-art methods when used off-the-shelf without post-processing or task-specific modifications. |||

title: Real-time eSports Match Result Prediction
Abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for predicting the winning team in Dota 2 matches, by integrating both pre-match player data and real-time match features. The authors use logistic regression, a novel Attribute Sequence Model, and combinations thereof as prediction models. Their experiments on a dataset of 78,362 matches show that incorporating more pre-match features increases accuracy from 58.69% to 71.49%, and the use of real-time features achieves up to 93.73% accuracy when predicting at the 40th minute.

title: StackGAN: Text to Photo-realistic Image Synthesis with Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Generating high-quality images from text descriptions is a challenging task in computer vision with numerous applications. Existing text-to-image methods can capture the overall meaning of descriptions but lack fine details and vivid object representations. This paper introduces StackGAN, a novel stacked generative adversarial network that generates 256x256 photo-realistic images conditioned on text descriptions. The proposed approach decomposes the complex task into manageable sub-problems through a sketch-refinement process. A Stage-I GAN creates a basic sketch of the object based on the text description, followed by a Stage-II GAN that refines the sketch into a high-resolution image with realistic details. To enhance image diversity and training stability, the authors introduce a Conditioning Augmentation technique that promotes smoothness in the latent conditioning manifold. Extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of StackGAN in generating photo-realistic images conditioned on text descriptions.

title: Active Learning for Speech Recognition: the Power of Gradients
Abstract: In speech recognition, labeling audio clips can be costly, and not all data is equally valuable. Active learning aims to minimize annotation costs by selecting the most informative samples for labeling. While confidence scores and likelihood-based active learning methods have proven effective, gradient-based methods remain less understood. This work investigates the Expected Gradient Length (EGL) approach for active learning in end-to-end speech recognition. The authors justify EGL from a variance reduction perspective and demonstrate that it identifies novel samples uncorrelated with confidence scores. Experimental results show that EGL can reduce word errors by 11% or, alternatively, reduce the number of samples required for labeling by 50% compared to random sampling.

title: Optimal Generalized Decision Trees via Integer Programming
Abstract: Decision trees have been widely used for predictive modeling due to their interpretability and effectiveness with categorical features. However, they can be prone to overfitting and lose interpretability when allowed to grow excessively. This paper proposes a mixed integer programming formulation to construct optimal decision trees of a predetermined size. The approach considers the unique structure of categorical features, enabling combinatorial decisions at each node based on subsets of feature values. It can also handle numerical features through thresholding. Experiments show that small trees can achieve high accuracy using moderately sized training sets, and the resulting optimization problems are tractable with modern solvers.

title: Finding Better Active Learners for Faster Literature Reviews
Abstract: Literature reviews are often time-consuming and tedious. This paper presents FASTREAD, a novel technique for accelerating the review of large document corpora, based on state-of-the-art active learning methods from evidence-based medicine and legal electronic discovery. FASTREAD was evaluated using datasets from existing software engineering literature reviews. Compared to manual methods, FASTREAD allows researchers to identify 95% of relevant studies after reviewing significantly fewer papers. Compared to other automatic methods, it requires 20-50% fewer reviews while finding the same number of relevant primary studies in a systematic literature review.

title: Automatic Lymphocyte Detection in H&E Images with Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Automatic lymphocyte detection in H&E images is crucial for numerous tissue image analysis algorithms. Accurate and robust automated lymphocyte detection is essential in both computer science and clinical studies. Existing approaches typically rely on traditional image processing or classic machine learning methods. Recent advances in deep learning have revolutionized computer image interpretation, becoming a superior solution for various pattern recognition problems. This work proposes a new deep neural network model that extends the fully convolutional network by incorporating ideas from recent techniques, such as shortcut links. The authors also design a new training scheme that leverages prior knowledge about lymphocytes, efficiently utilizing limited free-form annotations from pathologists while supporting efficient fine-tuning. This model has the potential for self-improvement by learning from errors collected during real applications. Experiments demonstrate the model's effectiveness in detecting lymphocytes in images with varying staining conditions and tissue types.

title: #HashtagWars: Learning a Sense of Humor
Abstract: This paper introduces a new dataset for computational humor, specifically for comparative humor ranking, which aims to move beyond the binary approach of traditional humor detection. The dataset comprises humorous tweets responding to a given hashtag. The authors describe the motivation and collection process, including details of their semi-automated data collection system. Initial experiments using unsupervised and supervised approaches are presented. The best supervised system achieved 63.7% accuracy, suggesting that humor ranking is a more challenging task than typical humor detection tasks. Initial results indicate that a character-level model is more suitable for this task than a token-level model, likely due to the prevalence of puns that can be better captured by a character-level representation.

title: Towards deep learning with spiking neurons in energy based models with contrastive Hebbian plasticity
Abstract: Error back-propagation in multi-layer neural networks (deep learning) has been remarkably successful in supervised and reinforcement learning tasks. However, deep learning as a model for brain function has been questioned due to its reliance on non-local plasticity rules. To address this issue, energy-based models with local contrastive Hebbian learning were proposed and tested on a classification task using networks of rate neurons. This paper extends this work by implementing and testing such a model with networks of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. Preliminary results suggest that it is possible to learn a non-linear regression task with hidden layers, spiking neurons, and a local synaptic plasticity rule.

title: DeepCancer: Detecting Cancer through Gene Expressions via Deep Generative Learning
Abstract: Transcriptional profiling using microarrays to obtain gene expressions has been employed to facilitate cancer diagnosis. This paper proposes a deep generative machine learning architecture called DeepCancer that learns features from unlabeled microarray data. These models are used in conjunction with conventional classifiers to categorize tissue samples as cancerous or non-cancerous. The proposed model was tested on two different clinical datasets. Evaluation results demonstrate that DeepCancer achieves high precision while effectively controlling false positive and false negative rates.

title: Low-Rank Inducing Norms with Optimality Interpretations
Abstract: Optimization problems with rank constraints arise in various fields, including control, machine learning, and image analysis. Due to the non-convex nature of rank constraints, these problems are often solved approximately using convex relaxations. Nuclear norm regularization is a common convexifying technique for such problems. This paper introduces a family of low-rank inducing norms and regularizers, which includes the nuclear norm as a special case. A posteriori guarantees for solving underlying rank-constrained optimization problems using these convex relaxations are provided. The performance of these low-rank inducing norms is evaluated on three matrix completion problems. The nuclear norm heuristic is outperformed by convex relaxations based on other low-rank inducing norms in all cases. For two of the problems, low-rank inducing norms successfully recover the partially unknown matrix, while the nuclear norm fails. These low-rank inducing norms are representable as semi-definite programs and have cheaply computable proximal mappings, enabling the efficient solution of large-scale problems using first-order methods.

title: Square Hellinger Subadditivity for Bayesian Networks and its Applications to Identity Testing
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that the square Hellinger distance between two Bayesian networks on the same directed graph is subadditive with respect to the graph's neighborhoods. Specifically, for two Bayesian networks on the same directed acyclic graph, the square Hellinger distance between their probability distributions is upper bounded by the sum of the square Hellinger distances between the marginals on each node and its parents in the graph. Importantly, this bound does not depend on the conditionals but only on the marginals. A similar inequality is derived for more general Markov Random Fields. As an application, the paper shows that distinguishing whether two Bayesian networks on the same (but potentially unknown) DAG are equal or have a total variation distance greater than a given threshold can be achieved with a sample complexity of  $\\tilde{O}(|\\Sigma|^{3/4(d+1)} \\cdot n/\\epsilon^2)$, where $d$ is the maximum in-degree of the DAG and $\\Sigma$ is the domain of each variable. If the networks are defined on potentially different and unknown trees, the sample complexity increases to $\\tilde{O}(|\\Sigma|^{4.5} n/\\epsilon^2)$, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. For product distributions over $\\{0,1\\}^n$ where one distribution is known, the sample complexity becomes $O(\\sqrt{n}/\\epsilon^2)$, which is optimal up to constant factors.

title: Testing Bayesian Networks
Abstract: This paper initiates a systematic investigation of testing high-dimensional structured distributions, focusing specifically on Bayesian networks, the prototypical family of directed graphical models. A Bayesian network is defined by a directed acyclic graph where each node represents a random variable. The value at a node is conditionally independent of all other non-descendant nodes given its parents. The paper examines the properties of identity testing and closeness testing for Bayesian networks. The main contribution is the development of the first non-trivial efficient testing algorithms for these problems, along with corresponding information-theoretic lower bounds. For a wide range of parameter settings, the proposed algorithms have a sample complexity sublinear in the dimension and are sample-optimal up to constant factors.

title: Optimal mean-based algorithms for trace reconstruction
Abstract: In the trace reconstruction problem (deletion channel), an unknown n-bit source string is to be recovered from noisy traces, where each bit is independently deleted with probability $\\delta$. The goal is to minimize the number of traces and running time required to reconstruct the original string.  Previous work by Holenstein et al. introduced an algorithm with a sample and time complexity of $\\exp(\\tilde{O}(n^{1/2}))$ for any fixed deletion rate $0 < \\delta < 1$. This algorithm is considered "mean-based" as it relies solely on empirical means of individual bits in the traces. Holenstein et al. also proved a lower bound, demonstrating that any mean-based algorithm must use at least $n^{\\tilde{\\Omega}(\\log\nn)}$ samples. This paper improves both the upper and lower bounds for mean-based trace reconstruction. For any constant deletion rate, a mean-based algorithm is provided with a sample and time complexity of $\\exp(O(n^{1/3}))$.  Furthermore, it is proven that any mean-based algorithm requires at least $\\exp(\\Omega(n^{1/3}))$ traces. These matching bounds are extended to subconstant deletion rates $\\delta$ and $\\rho := 1-\\delta$. When $(\\log^3 n)/n \\ll \\delta \\leq 1/2$, the bound is $\\exp(-\\Theta(\\delta n)^{1/3})$, and when $1/\\sqrt{n} \\ll \\rho \\leq 1/2$, the bound is $\\exp(-\\Theta(n/\\rho)^{1/3})$. The proofs involve estimates for the maxima of Littlewood polynomials on complex disks. These techniques can also be applied to trace reconstruction with random insertions and bit-flips in addition to deletions. A surprising result is found: for deletion probabilities $\\delta > 1/2$, insertions can actually improve trace reconstruction.

title: Testing Ising Models
Abstract: Given samples from an unknown multivariate distribution, can we distinguish between the distribution being the product of its marginals and it being far from every product distribution? Similarly, can we distinguish between the distribution being equal to a given distribution and the two distributions being far from each other? These problems of testing independence and goodness-of-fit have received significant attention in statistics, information theory, and theoretical computer science, with sample-optimal algorithms known for certain parameter regimes. However, it is also known that these problems become intractable in high dimensions, requiring exponential sample complexity.  Motivated by the exponential lower bounds for general distributions and the prevalence of Markov Random Fields (MRFs) in high-dimensional distribution modeling, this paper investigates distribution testing on structured multivariate distributions, focusing on the prototypical example of MRFs: the Ising Model. It is demonstrated that in this structured setting, the curse of dimensionality can be avoided, obtaining sample and time-efficient testers for independence and goodness-of-fit. One of the key technical challenges addressed is bounding the variance of functions of the Ising model.

title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
Abstract: Feature pyramids are a fundamental component in recognition systems for detecting objects at various scales. However, recent deep learning object detectors have avoided pyramid representations due to their computational and memory intensiveness. This paper leverages the inherent multi-scale, pyramidal hierarchy of deep convolutional networks to construct feature pyramids with minimal extra cost. A top-down architecture with lateral connections is developed for building high-level semantic feature maps at all scales. This architecture, called a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), significantly improves performance as a generic feature extractor across various applications. Using FPN within a basic Faster R-CNN system, the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art single-model results on the COCO detection benchmark without relying on complex techniques, surpassing all existing single-model entries, including those from the COCO 2016 challenge winners. Furthermore, the method can run at 5 FPS on a GPU, making it a practical and accurate solution for multi-scale object detection. The code will be made publicly available.

title: Robust mixture of experts modeling using the skew $t$ distribution
Abstract: Mixture of Experts (MoE) is a popular framework in statistics and machine learning for modeling data heterogeneity in regression, classification, and clustering. MoE for continuous data is typically based on the normal distribution. However, it is known that the normal distribution is unsuitable for data with asymmetric behavior, heavy tails, and atypical observations. This paper introduces a new robust non-normal mixture of experts modeling using the skew $t$ distribution. The proposed skew $t$ mixture of experts, named STMoE, addresses the limitations of normal mixtures of experts by handling skewed, heavy-tailed, and noisy data. An expectation conditional maximization (ECM) algorithm is developed for estimating model parameters by monotonically maximizing the observed data log-likelihood. The paper describes how STMoE can be used for prediction and model-based clustering of regression data. Numerical experiments on simulated data demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed model in fitting non-linear regression functions and performing model-based clustering. STMoE is then applied to real-world data on tone perception in musical data analysis and temperature anomalies in climate change data analysis. The obtained results confirm the model's usefulness for practical data analysis applications.

title: SimTensor: A synthetic tensor data generator
Abstract: SimTensor is a multi-platform, open-source software for generating artificial tensor data (with CP/PARAFAC or Tucker structure) for reproducible research on tensor factorization algorithms. SimTensor, a standalone MATLAB-based application, provides a wide range of facilities for generating tensor data with various configurations. It features a user-friendly graphical interface that allows users to easily generate tensors with complex settings. SimTensor can export generated data to universal formats such as CSV and HDF5, which can be imported into a variety of programming languages. Its most innovative feature is the ability to generate temporal tensors with periodic waves, seasonal effects, and streaming structure. It can also apply constraints such as non-negativity and different types of sparsity to the data. SimTensor further provides the capability to simulate various change-points and inject different types of anomalies. The source code and binary versions of SimTensor are available for download at http://www.simtensor.org.

title: Phase transitions in Restricted Boltzmann Machines with generic priors
Abstract: This paper examines Generalised Restricted Boltzmann Machines with generic priors for units and weights, interpolating between Boolean and Gaussian variables. A complete analysis of the replica symmetric phase diagram for these systems, which can be viewed as Generalised Hopfield models, is presented. The paper highlights the role of the retrieval phase in both inference and learning processes, demonstrating its robustness for a wide range of weight and unit priors beyond the standard Hopfield scenario. Furthermore, it shows how the paramagnetic phase boundary is directly related to the optimal size of the training set required for good generalization in a teacher-student scenario of unsupervised learning.
label: AI

title: Boundary-aware Instance Segmentation
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of instance-level semantic segmentation, which aims to jointly detect, segment, and classify individual objects within an image. Existing methods typically propose candidate objects, often as bounding boxes, and directly predict a binary mask within each proposal. This approach is limited as it cannot recover from errors in the object candidate generation process, such as overly small or shifted boxes. The paper introduces a novel object segment representation based on the distance transform of the object masks. An object mask network (OMN) is designed with a new residual-deconvolution architecture that infers this representation and decodes it into the final binary object mask. This enables the prediction of masks that extend beyond the bounding box boundaries, making them robust to inaccurate object candidates. The OMN is integrated into a Multitask Network Cascade framework, and the resulting boundary-aware instance segmentation (BAIS) network is trained end-to-end. Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate the benefits of this approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in both object proposal generation and instance segmentation.

title: Advancing Bayesian Optimization: The Mixed-Global-Local (MGL) Kernel and Length-Scale Cool Down
Abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) has emerged as a central method for solving expensive black-box optimization problems. While much research has focused on the choice of acquisition function, this paper focuses on online length-scale adaptation and the selection of kernel function. Instead of relying on maximum likelihood estimation on past data for hyperparameter selection, the authors propose using the acquisition function to adaptively adjust hyperparameters more robustly and with a focus on future optimization progress.  A specific kernel function is introduced that incorporates non-stationarity and local anisotropy, implicitly integrating the efficiency of local convex optimization with global Bayesian optimization. Comparisons with state-of-the-art BO methods highlight the efficiency of these mechanisms on global optimization benchmarks. |||

title: Low-rank matrix recovery via rank one tight frame measurements
Abstract: Reconstructing a low-rank matrix from incomplete linear measurements is a fundamental problem in various fields, including machine learning, quantum state tomography, and phase retrieval. This paper examines a specific scenario where the measurements are taken with respect to rank-one matrices constructed from elements of a random tight frame.  The authors propose a convex optimization approach and demonstrate its robustness against noise in the measurements and stability in the presence of approximately low-rank matrices. This is achieved by establishing a version of the null space property for the corresponding measurement map.
label: AI

title: Following Gaze Across Views
Abstract: Following a person's gaze in videos is crucial for understanding human behavior and actions. This paper presents a novel approach for tracking gaze across multiple views by predicting the gaze direction of a specific person throughout a scene. The authors introduce a new dataset called VideoGaze, which serves as a benchmark for training and evaluating gaze prediction models. The proposed model estimates a gaze location density in a second view given a person in a first view and a second view of the same scene. The model is trained end-to-end, solving sub-problems related to saliency, gaze pose, and geometric relationships between views. Experiments indicate that the proposed approach outperforms standard baselines and produces plausible results in everyday scenarios.
label: AI

title: Clipper: A Low-Latency Online Prediction Serving System
Abstract: Machine learning is increasingly deployed in applications demanding real-time, accurate, and robust predictions under heavy query loads. However, most existing machine learning frameworks and systems focus primarily on model training rather than deployment. This paper introduces Clipper, a general-purpose low-latency prediction serving system that bridges the gap between end-user applications and various machine learning frameworks. Clipper's modular architecture simplifies model deployment across different frameworks and applications. By incorporating caching, batching, and adaptive model selection techniques, Clipper significantly reduces prediction latency and improves prediction throughput, accuracy, and robustness without modifying the underlying machine learning frameworks. Evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate Clipper's effectiveness in meeting the stringent latency, accuracy, and throughput requirements of online serving applications.  A comparison with TensorFlow Serving highlights Clipper's ability to achieve comparable performance while enabling model composition and online learning for enhanced accuracy and robustness.

title: Bayesian forecasting of electoral outcomes with new parties' competition
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology for forecasting electoral outcomes by combining a fundamental model and a model-based aggregation of polls. The fundamental model adopts a Bayesian hierarchical structure that integrates data from provincial, regional, and national levels. A Bayesian strategy is employed to fuse the fundamental model with information from recent polls. The resulting model can be continuously updated as new information, such as poll results, becomes available. This methodology is particularly suitable for electoral scenarios involving new political parties, but remains general enough to accommodate other electoral situations. The paper illustrates the method's advantages using the 2015 Spanish Congressional Election, where two new parties garnered 30% of the votes.  Comparative analysis with alternative models demonstrates the proposed model's superior predictive performance, including hybrid models combining fundamental and poll models. Notably, the model accurately predicts the seat distribution among political parties.
label: AI

title: Towards a cognitive MAC layer: Predicting the MAC-level performance in Dynamic WSN using Machine learning
Abstract: Predictable network performance is paramount in various low-power wireless sensor network applications. This paper utilizes machine learning as an effective technique for real-time characterization of communication performance observed at the MAC layer. The proposed approach adopts a data-driven methodology comprising three steps: extensive data collection through experiments, offline modeling, and trace-driven performance evaluation. Analysis reveals that a neural network prediction model exhibits the best performance.
label: AI

title: Measuring Adverse Drug Effects on Multimorbity using Tractable Bayesian Networks
Abstract: Managing patients with multiple chronic conditions often leads to polypharmacy, the prescription of multiple medications. However, the long-term effects of specific drug combinations and their interactions with various diseases remain largely unknown.  This paper investigates the potential adverse effects of medications on the progression of multimorbidity using models learned from primary care data. These models represent diseases and prescriptions using state-of-the-art tractable Bayesian networks, enabling efficient computation of complex queries.  Results confirm that certain prescriptions can have unintended negative consequences on the development of cardiovascular multimorbidity.  Furthermore, medication treatments for one disease group can impact diseases in other groups.
label: AI

title: ActionFlowNet: Learning Motion Representation for Action Recognition
Abstract: Despite recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for visual recognition tasks, state-of-the-art action recognition systems still rely on handcrafted motion features, such as optical flow, for optimal performance.  This paper proposes a multitask learning model called ActionFlowNet, which trains a single-stream network directly from raw pixels to simultaneously estimate optical flow and recognize actions using CNNs. The model effectively captures both appearance and motion information within a single framework. The authors also investigate the impact of optical flow quality on action recognition accuracy. ActionFlowNet significantly improves action recognition accuracy by a substantial margin of 31% compared to CNN-based models trained without external large-scale data or optical flow input.  Even without pre-training on large external labeled datasets, the model effectively leverages motion information to achieve competitive recognition accuracy compared to models trained on large datasets like ImageNet and Sport-1M.

title: Robust mixture of experts modeling using the $t$ distribution
Abstract: Mixture of Experts (MoE) is a widely used framework for modeling heterogeneity in data for regression, classification, and clustering.  While MoE typically employs normal experts based on the Gaussian distribution for regression and clustering of continuous data, this approach proves inadequate for data sets containing groups of observations with heavy tails or atypical values. This paper introduces a robust MoE model based on the t-distribution to address these challenges. The proposed t-MoE (TMoE) model effectively handles heavy-tailed and noisy data. The authors develop a dedicated expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for parameter estimation, monotonically maximizing the observed data log-likelihood. The paper describes how the model can be used in prediction and model-based clustering of regression data. Validation on simulated data demonstrates TMoE's effectiveness and robustness in modeling nonlinear regression functions and performing model-based clustering.  Real-world applications involving tone perception in musical data analysis and temperature anomalies in climate change data further showcase TMoE's practicality.
label: AI

title: Automatic Model Based Dataset Generation for Fast and Accurate Crop and Weeds Detection
Abstract: Selective weeding is a critical challenge in agricultural robotics.  Farm robots must accurately detect plants and distinguish between crops and weeds to successfully perform this task. Many promising state-of-the-art approaches rely on appearance-based models trained on large annotated datasets. However, creating such datasets with pixel-level annotations is extremely time-consuming, hindering the practicality of data-driven techniques. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a novel and effective approach that minimizes human intervention in training detection and classification algorithms. The idea is to procedurally generate large synthetic training datasets by randomizing key features of the target environment, including crop and weed species, soil type, and light conditions. By tuning model parameters and leveraging real-world textures, the approach generates realistic views of an artificial agricultural scenario without manual effort. This generated data can be used directly to train the model or supplement real-world images.  The proposed methodology is validated using a deep learning-based image segmentation architecture as a testbed.  Comparison of classification results obtained using real and synthetic training data confirms the effectiveness and potential of this approach.
label: AI

title: Georges Lemaître: Life, Science and Legacy
Abstract: This paper celebrates the remarkable life, scientific contributions, and legacy of Abb'e Georges Lemaître, a Belgian cleric and physicist who developed the fireworks model for the origin of the universe. Lemaître passed away half a century ago, just three days after learning about the discovery of the cosmic microwave background by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson. Despite his grave illness from leukemia, Lemaître lucidly praised this news, which confirmed the explosive genesis of our universe.
label: AI

title: BaTFLED: Bayesian Tensor Factorization Linked to External Data
Abstract: Most machine learning algorithms are designed to predict single responses or vectors of responses. However, many types of responses are naturally organized as matrices or higher-order tensor objects exhibiting shared characteristics across different modes. This paper introduces BaTFLED (Bayesian Tensor Factorization Linked to External Data), a novel machine learning algorithm for predicting values in a three-dimensional response tensor using input features for each dimension. BaTFLED employs a probabilistic Bayesian framework to learn projection matrices mapping input features for each mode into latent representations that multiply to form the response tensor. The model utilizes a Tucker decomposition to capture interaction weights between latent factors for each mode in a small core tensor. Sparsity-inducing priors on the projection matrices and core tensor facilitate feature selection and model regularization.  The paper demonstrates that BaTFLED significantly outperforms elastic net and neural network models on cold-start tasks from simulated data with a three-mode structure. Additionally, the model is applied to predict dose-response curves in a panel of breast cancer cell lines treated with drug compounds, as part of a Dialogue for Reverse Engineering Assessments and Methods (DREAM) challenge.
label: AI

title: Mathematical modelling of the electric sense of fish: the role of multi-frequency measurements and movement
Abstract: Understanding active electrolocation in weakly electric fish remains a challenging problem. This paper proposes a mathematical formulation of this problem using partial differential equations. This formulation enables the development of two algorithms: one for localizing a target using the multi-frequency aspect of the electric signal, and another for identifying the target's shape. Shape recognition is designed from a machine learning perspective, leveraging both the multi-frequency setup and the fish's movement around its prey. The paper presents numerical simulations for computing the electric field emitted and sensed by the fish, which serve as input for the two algorithms.
label: AI

title: Vertical stratification of forest canopy for segmentation of under-story trees within small-footprint airborne LiDAR point clouds
Abstract: Airborne LiDAR point clouds representing forests contain 3D data that can be used to derive vertical stand structure, including understory layers. This paper presents a tree segmentation approach for multi-story stands, stratifying the point cloud into canopy layers and segmenting individual tree crowns within each layer using a digital surface model-based segmentation method. The novel aspect of this approach lies in the stratification procedure, which separates the point cloud into an overstory and multiple understory tree canopy layers by analyzing vertical distributions of LiDAR points within overlapping locales. This procedure does not rely on prior assumptions about tree crown shape and size and can be used independently of the segmentation method to vertically stratify tree crowns in forest canopies. The proposed approach was applied to the University of Kentucky Robinson Forest, a natural deciduous forest with complex and highly variable terrain and vegetation structure. Segmentation results indicate that using the stratification procedure significantly improved understory tree detection (from 46% to 68%) at the cost of introducing a fair number of over-segmented understory trees (increased from 1% to 16%), while minimally affecting the overall segmentation quality of overstory trees. Analysis of vertical canopy stratification revealed suboptimal point density in understory canopy layers for accurate tree segmentation, suggesting that denser LiDAR point clouds would further enhance understory tree segmentation. The paper concludes that the segmentation approach is applicable to various forest types, as evidenced by correlations between the results and forest structure.

title: Improved Stereo Matching with Constant Highway Networks and Reflective Confidence Learning
Abstract: This paper presents an improved three-step pipeline for stereo matching, introducing multiple novelties at each stage. A new highway network architecture is proposed for computing matching costs at each possible disparity, based on multilevel weighted residual shortcuts. The model is trained with a hybrid loss function that supports multilevel comparison of image patches. A novel post-processing step employs a second deep convolutional neural network for pooling global information from multiple disparities. This network outputs both the image disparity map, replacing the conventional "winner takes all" strategy, and a confidence score for the prediction. The confidence score is achieved by training the network with a new technique called the reflective loss. Finally, the learned confidence is used to improve outlier detection in the refinement step. The proposed pipeline achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the largest and most competitive stereo benchmarks, demonstrating that the learned confidence outperforms all existing alternatives.

title: EgoCap: Egocentric Marker-less Motion Capture with Two Fisheye Cameras (Extended Abstract)
Abstract: Marker-based and marker-less optical skeletal motion capture methods rely on an outside-in arrangement of cameras placed around a scene, with viewpoints converging on the center. These methods often create discomfort due to the need for marker suits and have severely restricted recording volumes, typically confined to indoor scenes with controlled backgrounds. This paper proposes a novel method for real-time, marker-less, and egocentric motion capture, estimating the full-body skeleton pose from a lightweight stereo pair of fisheye cameras attached to a helmet or virtual reality headset. The method combines the strengths of a new generative pose estimation framework for fisheye views with a ConvNet-based body-part detector trained on a new automatically annotated and augmented dataset. The proposed inside-in method captures full-body motion in general indoor and outdoor scenes, including crowded environments.
label: AI

title: p-DLA: A Predictive System Model for Onshore Oil and Gas Pipeline Dataset Classification and Monitoring - Part 1
Abstract: The rise in militant activity and rogue behavior in oil and gas regions worldwide has led to an increase in oil pipeline disturbances, resulting in substantial losses for multinational operators and the countries hosting these facilities. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence-based predictive monitoring system for mitigating these disturbances. The system uses a highly sparse predictive Deviant Learning Algorithm (p-DLA) designed to synthesize a sequence of memory predictive clusters for monitoring, control, and decision-making. The p-DLA is compared with a popular machine learning algorithm, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), based on a temporal version of standard feed-forward back-propagation trained artificial neural networks (ANNs). Simulation studies demonstrate the impressive performance and effectiveness of the sparse memory predictive approach, which favors the sub-synthesis of a highly compressed and low-dimensional knowledge discovery and information prediction scheme. The results highlight the proposed approach's competitiveness with established AI methods like LSTM.

title: Super-Resolution Reconstruction of Electrical Impedance Tomography Images
Abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) systems are gaining popularity due to their advantages over competing systems. However, EIT produces images with very low resolution, and its non-uniform sampling characteristic hinders the direct application of traditional image super-resolution techniques. This paper proposes a resampling-based super-resolution method for improving EIT image quality. Preliminary results indicate that the proposed technique can substantially enhance EIT image resolution, making it more competitive with other technologies.
label: AI

title: A Unified Tensor-based Active Appearance Face Model
Abstract: Appearance variations pose significant challenges in face image analysis. To address this, this paper presents a Unified Tensor-based Active Appearance Model (UT-AAM) for jointly modeling the geometry and texture information of 2D faces. For each type of face information, shape and texture, a unified tensor model is constructed, capturing all relevant appearance variations. This contrasts with the variation-specific models of traditional tensor AAMs.  A strategy for handling self-occluded faces is proposed to obtain consistent shape and texture representations of pose-varied faces, ensuring unification across pose variations. UT-AAM is also capable of constructing the model from incomplete training datasets using tensor completion methods. The paper employs an effective cascaded-regression-based method for UT-AAM fitting. These advancements enhance UT-AAM's practical utility. The authors demonstrate UT-AAM's improvement in training facial landmark detectors by synthesizing a large number of virtual samples. Experimental results using the Multi-PIE and 300-W face datasets highlight the proposed approach's merits.

title: A Joint Speaker-Listener-Reinforcer Model for Referring Expressions
Abstract: Referring expressions are natural language constructions used to identify specific objects within a scene. This paper presents a unified framework for referring expression comprehension and generation. The model comprises three modules: speaker, listener, and reinforcer. The speaker generates referring expressions, the listener comprehends them, and the reinforcer introduces a reward function to guide the sampling of more discriminative expressions. The listener and speaker modules are trained jointly in an end-to-end learning framework, enabling inter-module awareness during learning and benefiting from the discriminative reinforcer's feedback. The paper demonstrates that this unified framework and training strategy achieve state-of-the-art results for both comprehension and generation on three referring expression datasets.  Further information is available on the project and demo page: https://vision.cs.unc.edu/refer.

title: Feedback Networks
Abstract: Currently, the most successful learning models in computer vision are based on learning successive representations followed by a decision layer, often implemented through feedforward multilayer neural networks, such as ConvNets, where each layer forms one of these successive representations. This paper explores an alternative approach: feedback-based learning, where the representation is formed iteratively based on feedback from previous iterations. The authors establish that a feedback-based approach offers fundamental advantages over feedforward methods: enabling early predictions during query time, naturally conforming to hierarchical structures in the label space (e.g., a taxonomy), and providing a new basis for Curriculum Learning. They observe that feedback networks develop significantly different representations compared to their feedforward counterparts, aligning with these advantages. The paper proposes a general feedback-based learning architecture achieving results comparable to or better than existing feedforward networks while incorporating the aforementioned advantages.  The authors also investigate various mechanisms in feedback architectures (e.g., skip connections in time) and design choices (e.g., feedback length). This study offers new perspectives on developing more natural and practical learning models. |||

title: Smart Content Recognition from Images Using a Mixture of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: The proliferation of internet content has made it readily accessible from various locations, including workplaces, homes, and schools. However, not all content is suitable for all users, particularly children. Pornographic images, for instance, should be restricted to specific age groups and are considered NSFW (not safe for work) in professional environments. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated success in computer vision tasks. Building upon this success, we propose a novel approach for adult content recognition based on a weighted combination of multiple deep neural network models. Unlike existing methods, our approach utilizes a weighted sum of various CNN models, with weights determined through a linear regression problem using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). Experimental results show that our proposed model outperforms both single CNN models and the average sum of CNN models in adult content recognition.
label: AI

title: Paving the Way to Smart Micro Energy Internet: Concepts, Design Principles, and Engineering Practices
Abstract: The energy internet, a promising future energy infrastructure, holds the potential to enhance energy efficiency and improve operational flexibility. Similar to microgrids, the micro energy internet focuses on the distribution level and demand side. This paper introduces the concepts and design principles of a smart micro energy internet capable of accommodating microgrids, distributed poly-generation systems, energy storage facilities, and associated energy distribution infrastructure. The dispatch and control system of the smart micro energy internet plays a crucial role in managing external disturbances, striving to achieve a satisfactory operating point while adhering to multiple criteria such as safety, economy, and environmental protection. To realize the vision of a smart micro energy internet, we investigate an engineering game theory-based energy management system with self-approaching-optimum capabilities. Based on the proposed concepts, design principles, and energy management system, this paper presents a prototype of China's first conceptual solar-based smart micro energy internet, established at Qinghai University.

title: Automatic labeling of molecular biomarkers of whole slide immunohistochemistry images using fully convolutional networks
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of quantifying biomarkers in multi-stained tissues, leveraging color and spatial information. We propose a deep learning-based method that automatically localizes and quantifies cells expressing biomarkers within a whole slide image. Our deep learning network utilizes a fully convolutional network (FCN) that takes the true RGB color image of a tissue as input and outputs a map of the different biomarkers. The FCN relies on a convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies each cell based on the biomarker it expresses. This study employed images of immunohistochemistry (IHC) stained slides, with over 4,500 RGB images of cells manually labeled according to the expressing biomarkers. These labeled cell images were used to train the CNN, achieving an accuracy of 92% on a test set. The trained CNN was then extended to an FCN that generates a map of all biomarkers in the whole slide image acquired by the scanner. To evaluate our method, we manually labeled all nuclei expressing different biomarkers in two whole slide images, using these as the ground truth. Our proposed method for immunohistochemical analysis demonstrates comparable performance to manual labeling by humans, with an average F-score of 0.96.

title: Shape Estimation from Defocus Cue for Microscopy Images via Belief Propagation
Abstract: The increasing significance of 3D shape estimation in microscopic or close-range imaging stems from the ability to utilize the 3D information for various applications. Due to the limited depth of field at such small distances, the defocus blur induced in images provides valuable information about the object's 3D shape. The task of "shape from defocus" (SFD) involves estimating high-quality 3D shape estimates from images with depth-dependent defocus blur. While SFD research is well-established, existing approaches have primarily focused on objects with bulk or coarse shape variations. However, microscopic objects often exhibit fine and detailed structures, which have not been adequately addressed in most methods. Furthermore, the increasing data volumes associated with microscopy applications necessitate efficient SFD methods. This work explores the potential of the Belief Propagation (BP) approach to address these concerns for SFD. BP is known for its efficiency in combinatorial optimization and has been empirically proven to provide high-quality solutions in low-level vision problems such as image restoration and stereo disparity estimation. To leverage the efficiency of BP in SFD, we assume local space-invariance of the defocus blur, allowing for straightforward BP application. Despite this assumption, BP's ability to yield high-quality solutions using non-convex priors results in plausible shape estimates in the presence of fine structures on objects under microscopy imaging.
label: AI

title: Action Recognition Based on Joint Trajectory Maps with Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) have recently shown promising performance in many computer vision tasks, particularly image-based recognition. However, effectively applying ConvNets to sequence-based data remains an open problem. This paper proposes an effective yet simple method to represent spatio-temporal information carried in 3D skeleton sequences as three 2D images. This representation, referred to as Joint Trajectory Maps (JTM), encodes joint trajectories and their dynamics into color distribution within the images. ConvNets are then employed to learn discriminative features for human action recognition. This image-based representation allows for fine-tuning existing ConvNets models for classifying skeleton sequences without retraining from scratch. The three JTMs, generated in three orthogonal planes, provide complementary information. The final recognition is further enhanced through multi-score fusion of the three JTMs. The proposed method was evaluated on four public benchmark datasets: the large NTU RGB+D Dataset, MSRC-12 Kinect Gesture Dataset (MSRC-12), G3D Dataset, and UTD Multimodal Human Action Dataset (UTD-MHAD). It achieved state-of-the-art results.

title: Analysis of the noise in back-projection light field acquisition and its optimization
Abstract: Light field reconstruction from images captured through focal plane sweeping can achieve high lateral resolution comparable to modern camera sensors, surpassing the capabilities of conventional micro-lenslet-based light field capture systems. However, severe defocus noise and low depth resolution limit its applications. This paper analyzes the defocus noise and depth resolution in focal plane sweeping-based light field reconstruction, proposing a method to reduce defocus noise and enhance depth resolution. Numerical and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Rotation equivariant vector field networks
Abstract: In many computer vision tasks, we expect specific output behavior with respect to rotations of the input image. Explicitly encoding this relationship, rather than treating it as any other variation, reduces problem complexity and the size of the required model. This paper introduces Rotation Equivariant Vector Field Networks (RotEqNet), a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture that encodes rotation equivariance, invariance, and covariance. Each convolutional filter is applied at multiple orientations, resulting in a vector field representing the magnitude and angle of the highest scoring orientation at each spatial location. We develop a modified convolution operator based on this representation to create deep architectures. We evaluate RotEqNet on various problems requiring different responses to input rotations, including image classification, biomedical image segmentation, orientation estimation, and patch matching. In all cases, RotEqNet demonstrates exceptionally compact models in terms of parameter count and provides results comparable to networks orders of magnitude larger.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Logo Detection with Data Expansion by Synthesising Context
Abstract: Logo detection in unconstrained images presents challenges, particularly when only very sparse labelled training images are available due to high labelling costs. This work describes a model training image synthesizing method that significantly improves logo detection performance, even when only a handful (e.g., 10) of labelled training images captured in realistic contexts are available. This method avoids the need for extensive manual labelling. Specifically, we design a novel algorithm for generating Synthetic Context Logo (SCL) training images to enhance model robustness against unknown background clutters, resulting in superior logo detection performance. To benchmark model performance, we introduce a new logo detection dataset, TopLogo-10, consisting of top 10 most popular clothing/wearable brandname logos captured in rich visual contexts. Extensive comparisons highlight the advantages of our proposed SCL model over state-of-the-art alternatives for logo detection using two real-world logo benchmark datasets: FlickrLogo-32 and our new TopLogo-10.

title: Generalized Intersection Kernel
Abstract: Building upon the recent work on the "generalized min-max" (GMM) kernel, this study introduces the "generalized intersection" (GInt) kernel and the related "normalized generalized min-max" (NGMM) kernel. In computer vision, the (histogram) intersection kernel has been widely used, and the GInt kernel generalizes it to data with both negative and positive entries. An extensive empirical classification study on 40 datasets from the UCI repository demonstrates the effectiveness of this (tuning-free) GInt kernel. The empirical results also show that the NGMM kernel typically outperforms the GInt kernel. Interestingly, the NGMM kernel can be interpreted as the "asymmetrically transformed" version of the GInt kernel, based on the concept of "asymmetric hashing." Similar to the GMM kernel, the NGMM kernel can be efficiently linearized through methods like generalized consistent weighted sampling (GCWS), as empirically validated in our study. The discrete nature of hashed values also provides a scheme for approximate near neighbor search.

title: Increasing the Efficiency of 6-DoF Visual Localization Using Multi-Modal Sensory Data
Abstract: Localization is essential for mobile robot autonomy and human-robot interaction. Vision-based localization offers accuracy and flexibility but incurs a high computational burden, limiting its application on resource-constrained platforms. This paper addresses the problem of performing real-time localization in large-scale 3D point cloud maps of ever-growing size. While most systems using multi-modal information reduce localization time by employing side-channel information coarsely (e.g., WiFi for rough prior position estimation), we propose interweaving the map with rich sensory data. This multi-modal approach achieves two key goals simultaneously: harnessing additional sensory data for real-time localization in a vast area and enabling rough localization for devices without cameras. Our approach leverages a localization policy based on a sequential Monte Carlo estimator. The localizer utilizes this policy to attempt point-matching only in nodes where success is likely, significantly improving localization efficiency. The proposed multi-modal localization system was extensively evaluated in a large museum building. Results show that our multi-modal approach not only enhances localization accuracy but also significantly reduces computational time.

title: Quantum Clustering and Gaussian Mixtures
Abstract: The mixture of Gaussian distributions, a soft version of k-means, is considered a state-of-the-art clustering algorithm. It is widely used in computer vision for selecting classes, such as color, texture, and shapes. In this algorithm, each class is represented by a Gaussian distribution defined by its mean and covariance. The data is described by a weighted sum of these Gaussian distributions. We propose a novel method inspired by quantum interference in physics. Instead of modeling each class distribution directly, we model a class wave function such that its magnitude square is the class Gaussian distribution. We then mix the class wave functions to create the mixture wave function. The final mixture distribution is the magnitude square of the mixture wave function. Consequently, we observe quantum class interference phenomena not present in the Gaussian mixture model. Our results show that the quantum method outperforms the Gaussian mixture method in all aspects of estimation. It provides more accurate estimates of all distribution parameters with significantly less fluctuation and is more robust to data deviations from the Gaussian assumptions. We illustrate our method through an example application: color segmentation.
label: AI

title: Learning Visual N-Grams from Web Data
Abstract: Real-world image recognition systems need to recognize tens of thousands of classes encompassing a vast array of visual concepts. The traditional approach of annotating thousands of images per class for training is impractical in such a scenario, prompting the use of webly supervised data. This paper investigates the training of image recognition systems using large numbers of images and associated user comments. Specifically, we develop visual n-gram models that can predict arbitrary phrases relevant to the content of an image. Our visual n-gram models are feed-forward convolutional networks trained using new loss functions inspired by n-gram models commonly used in language modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our models in phrase prediction, phrase-based image retrieval, relating images and captions, and zero-shot transfer.
label: AI

title: From Virtual to Real World Visual Perception using Domain Adaptation -- The DPM as Example
Abstract: Supervised learning generally produces more accurate classifiers than unsupervised learning, highlighting the preference for training data with annotations. However, when addressing visual perception challenges like localizing specific object classes within an image, learning the involved classifiers poses a practical bottleneck. This is due to the need to frame object examples with bounding boxes in thousands of images. Moreover, the complexity of the model, in terms of its parameter count, necessitates more annotated examples. This annotation task, performed by human oracles, is inherently cumbersome and prone to inaccuracies and errors in the annotations (ground truth). As an alternative, we have pioneered the use of virtual worlds for collecting annotations automatically and with high precision. However, since the models learned with virtual data must operate in the real world, domain adaptation (DA) is still necessary. This chapter revisits the DA of a deformable part-based model (DPM) as an exemplifying case of virtual-to-real-world DA. We address the challenge of vehicle detection for driver assistance, using different publicly available virtual-world data. In doing so, we investigate questions such as how the domain gap behaves due to virtual-vs-real data with respect to dominant object appearance per domain, as well as the role of photo-realism in the virtual world.
label: AI

title: Cosmic particles
Abstract: For over a century, we have investigated cosmic particles originating from the Universe, aiming to understand their nature, origin, and acceleration mechanisms. Cosmic rays have yielded impressive results, giving rise to particle physics and expanding our understanding of the Universe across a wide range of energies. This contribution provides an overview of the most recent findings. This field remains highly active, with new experiments and instruments opening new perspectives for research at the intersection of astrophysics and particle physics.
label: AI

title: Meta-Unsupervised-Learning: A supervised approach to unsupervised learning
Abstract: We introduce a novel paradigm for unsupervised learning, effectively reducing it to supervised learning. Specifically, we mitigate the subjectivity in unsupervised decision-making by leveraging knowledge acquired from prior, potentially heterogeneous, supervised learning tasks. The versatility of our framework is demonstrated through comprehensive expositions and detailed experiments on several unsupervised problems, including (a) clustering, (b) outlier detection, and (c) similarity prediction under a common umbrella of meta-unsupervised-learning. We also provide rigorous PAC-agnostic bounds to establish the theoretical foundations of our framework and show that our framing of meta-clustering circumvents Kleinberg's impossibility theorem for clustering.
label: AI

title: Partial Membership Latent Dirichlet Allocation
Abstract: Topic models (e.g., pLSA, LDA, sLDA) have been extensively used for image segmentation. However, these models are restricted to crisp segmentation, requiring each visual word (image patch) to belong to only one topic. Many images, however, contain regions that cannot be assigned a crisp categorical label (e.g., transitions between a foggy sky and the ground or between sand and water at a beach). In these cases, a visual word is best represented with partial memberships across multiple topics. To address this, we present a partial membership latent Dirichlet allocation (PM-LDA) model and an associated parameter estimation algorithm. This model is particularly useful for imagery where a visual word may be a mixture of multiple topics. Experimental results on visual and sonar imagery demonstrate that PM-LDA can produce both crisp and soft semantic image segmentations, a capability lacking in previous topic modeling methods.

title: Fast color transfer from multiple images
Abstract: Color transfer between images effectively utilizes image statistics information. We present a novel approach for local color transfer between images based on simple statistics and locally linear embedding. A sketching interface is proposed for quick and easy specification of color correspondences between the target and source image. Users can specify correspondences of local regions using scribes, which more accurately transfers the target color to the source image while smoothly preserving boundaries and exhibiting more natural output results. Our algorithm is not limited to one-to-one image color transfer and can utilize multiple target images to transfer color to different regions in the source image. Additionally, our algorithm does not require choosing the same color style and image size between source and target images. We propose sub-sampling to reduce the computational load. Compared to other approaches, our algorithm excels in color blending in input data. It preserves other color details in the source image. Various experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in specifying correspondences of local color regions in source and target images, reflecting user intent and generating more realistic and natural visual effect results.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised domain adaptation in brain lesion segmentation with adversarial networks
Abstract: Significant advancements have been made in building accurate automatic segmentation systems for various biomedical applications using machine learning. However, the performance of these systems often degrades when applied to new data that differs from the training data, for instance, due to variations in imaging protocols. Manually annotating new data for each test domain is not a viable solution. This work investigates unsupervised domain adaptation using adversarial neural networks to train a segmentation method more invariant to differences in input data without requiring any annotations on the test domain. Specifically, we learn domain-invariant features by training the segmentation network to counter an adversarial network that attempts to classify the domain of input data based on the segmentation network's activations. Furthermore, we propose a multi-connected domain discriminator for improved adversarial training. Our system is evaluated using two MR databases of subjects with traumatic brain injuries, acquired using different scanners and imaging protocols. Using our unsupervised approach, we achieve segmentation accuracies close to the upper bound of supervised domain adaptation.

title: MARTA GANs: Unsupervised Representation Learning for Remote Sensing Image Classification
Abstract: With the development of deep learning, supervised learning has become prevalent in classifying remotely sensed images using convolutional networks (CNNs). However, the limited availability of labeled data often hinders supervised learning. Therefore, we propose an unsupervised model called multiple-layer feature-matching generative adversarial networks (MARTA GANs) to learn a representation using only unlabeled data. MARTA GANs comprises a generative model (G) and a discriminative model (D). We treat (D) as a feature extractor. To accommodate the complex characteristics of remote sensing data, we use a fusion layer to merge mid-level and global features. (G) can generate numerous images similar to the training data, enabling (D) to learn better representations of remotely sensed images using the training data provided by (G). The classification results on two widely used remote sensing image databases show that our proposed method significantly enhances classification performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Semantic Video Segmentation by Gated Recurrent Flow Propagation
Abstract: Semantic video segmentation presents challenges due to the vast amount of data that requires processing and labeling to construct accurate models. This paper presents a deep, end-to-end trainable methodology for video segmentation capable of leveraging information present in unlabeled data to improve semantic estimates. Our model combines a convolutional architecture and a spatio-temporal transformer recurrent layer that can temporally propagate labeling information using optical flow, adaptively gated based on locally estimated uncertainty. The flow, recognition, and gated temporal propagation modules can be trained jointly, end-to-end. The temporal, gated recurrent flow propagation component of our model can be integrated into any static semantic segmentation architecture, transforming it into a weakly supervised video processing system. Our extensive experiments on the challenging CityScapes and Camvid datasets, utilizing multiple deep architectures, indicate that the resulting model can leverage unlabeled temporal frames, alongside labeled ones, to improve both video segmentation accuracy and the consistency of its temporal labeling without additional annotation costs and with minimal extra computation. |||

title: FastMask: Segment Multi-scale Object Candidates in One Shot
Abstract: Objects appear to change in size depending on their position within natural images. This phenomenon poses a challenge for methods designed for object-centric tasks, such as object proposal, as they need to be robust to variations in object scale. This paper presents FastMask, a novel segment proposal framework that leverages hierarchical features in deep convolutional neural networks to segment objects of varying scales in a single step. FastMask divides the segment proposal network into three functional components: body, neck, and head. Additionally, the paper proposes a weight-shared residual neck module and a scale-tolerant attentional head module for efficient one-shot inference.  Evaluated on the MS COCO benchmark, FastMask outperforms all existing segment proposal methods in terms of average recall while being 2-5 times faster.  Furthermore, with a slight trade-off in accuracy, FastMask can segment objects in near real-time (approximately 13 frames per second) with 800x600 resolution images, highlighting its potential for practical applications. The implementation is available at https://github.com/voidrank/FastMask.
