title: Accelerated Convolutions for Efficient Multi-Scale Time to Contact Computation in Julia
Abstract: Convolutions are essential in applied mathematics, physics, and engineering. Their mathematical elegance enables efficient computation of common tasks like numerical differentiation on large datasets. Efficient convolution computation is crucial for real-time applications in artificial intelligence, particularly in machine vision, where convolutions need to be calculated continuously and efficiently on tens to hundreds of kilobytes per second. This paper investigates the use of convolutions in fundamental machine vision applications. It presents an accelerated n-dimensional convolution package implemented in the high-performance computing language Julia and demonstrates its effectiveness in solving the time-to-contact problem for machine vision. Results are evaluated against synthetically generated videos and assessed quantitatively using mean squared error from the ground truth. The package achieves over an order of magnitude reduction in compute time and allocated memory for comparable machine vision applications. The code is packaged and integrated into the official Julia Package Manager for use in various other scenarios.
label: AI

title: Multivariate mixture model for myocardium segmentation combining multi-source images
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for simultaneous segmentation of multi-source images utilizing the multivariate mixture model (MvMM) and maximum of log-likelihood (LL) framework. Segmentation is treated as a texture classification procedure, and the MvMM is employed to model the joint intensity distribution of the images. Specifically, the method is applied to myocardial segmentation by combining complementary texture information from multi-sequence (MS) cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images. Considering the presence of inter-image mis-registration and intra-image misalignment of slices in the MS CMR images, the MvMM is formulated with transformations embedded into the LL framework and optimized simultaneously with the segmentation parameters. The proposed method effectively corrects inter- and intra-image misalignment by registering each slice of the MS CMR to a virtual common space. It also delineates the indistinguishable boundaries of myocardium containing pathologies. Results demonstrate statistically significant improvement in segmentation performance compared to conventional approaches that can only segment each image independently. The proposed method exhibits superior robustness in incongruent data, where some images may not fully cover the region of interest, and full coverage can only be reconstructed by combining images from multiple sources.
label: AI

title: Symbolic Representation and Classification of Logos
Abstract: This paper introduces a model for logo classification based on symbolic representation of features. The proposed model leverages global features of logo images, such as color, texture, and shape features, for classification. Logo images are broadly categorized into three classes: logos containing only text, logos with only a symbol, and logos with both text and a symbol. Within each class, similar-looking logo images are clustered using the K-means clustering algorithm. Intra-cluster variations present in each cluster corresponding to each class are then preserved using symbolic interval data. Thus, reference logo images are represented in the form of interval data. A sample logo image is then classified using a suitable symbolic classifier. For experimentation, a relatively large dataset of color logo images (5044 logos) is created. The classification results are validated using accuracy, precision, recall, F-measure, and time. To assess the efficacy of the proposed model, comparative analyses are conducted against other models. Results indicate that the proposed model outperforms other models in terms of time and F-measure.
label: AI

title: Superpixel Segmentation Using Gaussian Mixture Model
Abstract: Superpixel segmentation algorithms partition an image into perceptually coherent atomic regions by assigning each pixel a superpixel label. These algorithms are widely used as a preprocessing step in computer vision tasks, as they significantly reduce the number of entries for subsequent algorithms. This work proposes an alternative superpixel segmentation method based on the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) by assuming that each superpixel corresponds to a Gaussian distribution. It is assumed that each pixel is generated by first randomly selecting a distribution from several Gaussian distributions related to that pixel, and then the pixel is drawn from the selected distribution. Based on this assumption, each pixel is supposed to be drawn from a mixture of Gaussian distributions with unknown parameters (GMM). An algorithm based on the expectation-maximization method is applied to estimate the unknown parameters. Once the unknown parameters are obtained, the superpixel label of a pixel is determined by a posterior probability. The success of applying GMM to superpixel segmentation depends on the two main differences between traditional GMM-based clustering and the proposed one: data points in this model may be non-identically distributed, and an approach to control the shape of the estimated Gaussian functions by adjusting their covariance matrices is presented. The method exhibits linear complexity with respect to the number of pixels. The proposed algorithm is inherently parallel and can achieve faster speed by adding simple OpenMP directives to the implementation. Experimental results indicate that the algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art superpixel algorithms in accuracy and presents a competitive performance in computational efficiency.
label: AI

title: An FFT-based Synchronization Approach to Recognize Human Behaviors using STN-LFP Signal
Abstract: Classifying human behavior is crucial for developing closed-loop Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) systems, which may reduce the power consumption and side effects of existing systems. Recent studies have shown that Local Field Potential (LFP) signals from both Subthalamic Nuclei (STN) of the brain can be used to recognize human behavior. Since the DBS leads implanted in each STN can collect three bipolar signals, selecting a suitable pair of LFPs that achieves optimal recognition performance remains an open problem. Considering the presence of synchronized aggregate activity in the basal ganglia, this paper presents an FFT-based synchronization approach to automatically select a relevant pair of LFPs. This pair is then used together with an SVM-based MKL classifier for behavior recognition purposes. Experiments on five subjects demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach compared to other methods employed for behavior classification.
label: AI

title: Semantic Perceptual Image Compression using Deep Convolution Networks
Abstract: Improving the visual quality of lossy image and video compression has long been a significant problem. Recent advances in computing power combined with the availability of large training datasets have increased interest in applying deep learning convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to address image recognition and image processing tasks. This paper presents a powerful CNN tailored to the specific task of semantic image understanding to achieve higher visual quality in lossy compression. A modest increase in complexity is incorporated into the encoder, allowing a standard, off-the-shelf JPEG decoder to be used. While JPEG encoding may be optimized for generic images, the process is ultimately unaware of the specific content of the image being compressed. This technique makes JPEG content-aware by designing and training a model to identify multiple semantic regions in a given image. Unlike object detection techniques, this model does not require labeling of object positions and can identify objects in a single pass.  The paper presents a new CNN architecture specifically for image compression, which generates a map highlighting semantically-salient regions so they can be encoded at higher quality compared to background regions. By adding a complete set of features for every class and taking a threshold over the sum of all feature activations, a map is generated highlighting semantically-salient regions for higher-quality encoding compared to background regions. Experiments on the Kodak PhotoCD dataset and the MIT Saliency Benchmark dataset demonstrate that the algorithm achieves higher visual quality for the same compressed size.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Nonparametric Models for Synchronous Brain-Computer Interfaces
Abstract: A brain-computer interface (BCI) is a system aiming to establish a non-muscular communication path for individuals suffering from neurodegenerative diseases. Many BCI systems utilize the phenomenon of event-related synchronization and desynchronization of brain waves as a primary feature for classifying different cognitive tasks. However, the temporal dynamics of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals contain additional information that can be incorporated into the inference engine to improve BCI performance. This information about signal dynamics has previously been exploited in BCIs using generative and discriminative methods. In particular, hidden Markov models (HMMs) have been used in previous work. These methods have the drawback that model parameters, such as the number of hidden states and the number of Gaussian mixtures, need to be fixed a priori. This paper proposes a Bayesian nonparametric model for brain signal classification that does not require a priori selection of the number of hidden states and the number of Gaussian mixtures of an HMM. Results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other methods based on HMM, as well as the winning algorithm of the BCI competition IV.
label: AI

title: Theory-guided Data Science: A New Paradigm for Scientific Discovery from Data
Abstract: Data science models, despite their success in various commercial domains, have limited applicability in scientific problems involving complex physical phenomena. Theory-guided data science (TGDS) is an emerging paradigm that aims to leverage the wealth of scientific knowledge for enhancing the effectiveness of data science models in enabling scientific discovery. The overarching vision of TGDS is to introduce scientific consistency as an essential component for learning generalizable models.  Furthermore, by producing scientifically interpretable models, TGDS aims to advance scientific understanding by discovering novel domain insights. Indeed, the TGDS paradigm has started gaining prominence in several scientific disciplines, including turbulence modeling, material discovery, quantum chemistry, biomedical science, biomarker discovery, climate science, and hydrology. This paper formally conceptualizes the TGDS paradigm and presents a taxonomy of research themes in TGDS.  It describes various approaches for integrating domain knowledge in different research themes using illustrative examples from diverse disciplines. The paper also highlights promising avenues for novel research to realize the full potential of theory-guided data science.
label: AI

title: Robust LSTM-Autoencoders for Face De-Occlusion in the Wild
Abstract: Face recognition techniques have advanced significantly in recent years. However, recognizing faces with partial occlusion remains a challenge for existing face recognizers, a crucial aspect in real-world applications involving surveillance and security. While extensive research has been dedicated to developing face de-occlusion methods, most perform well only under constrained conditions, such as all faces belonging to a pre-defined closed set. This paper proposes a robust LSTM-Autoencoders (RLA) model to effectively restore partially occluded faces even in unconstrained environments. The RLA model consists of two LSTM components: one for occlusion-robust face encoding and the other for recurrent occlusion removal. The first component, named multi-scale spatial LSTM encoder, reads facial patches of various scales sequentially to output a latent representation. Occlusion-robustness is achieved because the influence of occlusion is only upon some of the patches. Receiving the representation learned by the encoder, the LSTM decoder with a dual channel architecture reconstructs the overall face and detects occlusion simultaneously. By utilizing LSTM, the decoder breaks down the task of face de-occlusion into restoring the occluded part step by step. Furthermore, to minimize identity information loss and guarantee face recognition accuracy over recovered faces, an identity-preserving adversarial training scheme is introduced to further improve RLA. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real datasets of faces with occlusion clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RLA in removing different types of facial occlusion at various locations. The proposed method also provides significantly larger performance gain than other de-occlusion methods in promoting recognition performance over partially-occluded faces.
label: AI

title: Learning Non-Lambertian Object Intrinsics across ShapeNet Categories
Abstract: The non-Lambertian object intrinsic problem of recovering diffuse albedo, shading, and specular highlights from a single image of an object is considered.  A large-scale object intrinsics database is built based on existing 3D models in the ShapeNet database. Rendered with realistic environment maps, millions of synthetic images of objects and their corresponding albedo, shading, and specular ground-truth images are used to train an encoder-decoder CNN. Once trained, the network can decompose an image into the product of albedo and shading components, along with an additive specular component. The CNN delivers accurate and sharp results in this classical inverse problem of computer vision, with sharp details attributed to skip layer connections at corresponding resolutions from the encoder to the decoder. Benchmarked on the ShapeNet and MIT intrinsics datasets, the model consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art by a significant margin. The CNN is trained and tested on different object categories.  Surprisingly, from a CNN classification perspective, the intrinsics CNN generalizes very well across categories. Analysis shows that feature learning at the encoder stage is more crucial for developing a universal representation across categories.  The synthetic data-trained model is applied to images and videos downloaded from the internet, and robust and realistic intrinsics results are observed.  High-quality non-Lambertian intrinsics could enable many interesting applications, such as image-based albedo and specular editing.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Data Visualization by Metric Learning and Coordinate Transformation
Abstract: This paper presents a deep nonlinear metric learning framework for data visualization on an image dataset. The Triangular Similarity is proposed and its equivalence to the Cosine Similarity in measuring a data pair is proven. Based on this novel similarity, a geometrically motivated loss function, the triangular loss, is developed for optimizing a metric learning system comprising two identical CNNs. It is shown that this deep nonlinear system can be efficiently trained using a hybrid algorithm based on the conventional backpropagation algorithm.  Interestingly, drawing on classical manifold learning theories, the proposed system offers two different views to visualize the outputs. The second view provides better classification results than state-of-the-art methods in the visualizable spaces.
label: AI

title: Steerable CNNs
Abstract: The invariance and equivariance properties of a representation are crucial for success in many vision tasks. This paper presents Steerable Convolutional Neural Networks, an efficient and flexible class of equivariant convolutional networks. Steerable CNNs achieve state-of-the-art results on the CIFAR image classification benchmark. The mathematical theory of steerable representations reveals a type system where any steerable representation is a composition of elementary feature types, each associated with a particular kind of symmetry. This paper shows how the parameter cost of a steerable filter bank depends on the types of the input and output features, and demonstrates how to use this knowledge to construct CNNs that utilize parameters effectively.
label: AI

title: An Automated CNN Recommendation System for Image Classification Tasks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are widely used in practical applications for image classification tasks. However, designing CNN models is highly specialized and challenging for ordinary users. Even for CNN experts, selecting an optimal model for a specific task may require significant time (training many different models). To address this problem, an automated CNN recommendation system for image classification tasks is proposed.  The system accurately evaluates the complexity of the classification task and the classification ability of the CNN model. Based on the evaluation results, the system recommends the optimal CNN model that perfectly matches the task. The recommendation process is fast as it does not require any model training. Experimental results confirm that the evaluation methods are highly accurate and reliable.
label: AI

title: Signature of Geometric Centroids for 3D Local Shape Description and Partial Shape Matching
Abstract: Depth scans acquired from different views may contain nuisances such as noise, occlusion, and varying point density. A novel Signature of Geometric Centroids descriptor is proposed, supporting direct shape matching on the scans without requiring any preprocessing like scan denoising or conversion into a mesh.  First, the descriptor is constructed by voxelizing the local shape within a uniquely defined local reference frame and concatenating geometric centroid and point density features extracted from each voxel.  Second, two descriptors are compared by employing only corresponding voxels that are both non-empty, enabling matching of incomplete local shapes, such as those close to the scan boundary.  Third, a descriptor saliency measure is proposed and computed from a descriptor-graph to improve shape matching performance.  The descriptor's robustness and effectiveness for shape matching are demonstrated by comparing it with three state-of-the-art descriptors and applying it to object/scene reconstruction and 3D object recognition.
label: AI

title: Extracting Sub-Exposure Images from a Single Capture Through Fourier-based Optical Modulation
Abstract: Pixel-wise optical coding of images during exposure time enables the extraction of sub-exposure images from a single capture. This capability has various applications, including high-speed imaging, high-dynamic-range imaging, and compressed sensing. This paper presents a sub-exposure image extraction method where the exposure coding pattern is inspired by the frequency division multiplexing idea from communication systems. The coding masks modulate sub-exposure images in such a way that they are placed in non-overlapping regions in the Fourier domain. The sub-exposure image extraction process involves digital filtering of the captured signal with appropriate band-pass filters. The prototype imaging system incorporates a Liquid Crystal over Silicon (LCoS) based spatial light modulator synchronized with a camera for pixel-wise exposure coding.
label: AI

title: Image-Text Multi-Modal Representation Learning by Adversarial Backpropagation
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for image-text multi-modal representation learning. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this work is the first approach to applying adversarial learning concepts to multi-modal learning without exploiting image-text pair information to learn multi-modal features.  In contrast to most previous methods that use image-text pair information for multi-modal embedding, this method only uses category information. This paper demonstrates that multi-modal features can be achieved without image-text pair information, and the method achieves a more similar distribution with image and text in the multi-modal feature space compared to other methods that utilize image-text pair information.  Furthermore, the multi-modal feature exhibits universal semantic information, even though it was trained for category prediction. The model is end-to-end backpropagation, intuitive, and easily extended to other multi-modal learning work.
label: AI

title: Globally Optimal Object Tracking with Fully Convolutional Networks
Abstract: Tracking is a fundamental but challenging task in computer vision and pattern recognition.  The main difficulties in tracking are appearance variation and occlusion. Most traditional tracking methods set the parameters or templates to track target objects in advance and require modification accordingly. This paper proposes a new and robust tracking method using a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) to obtain an object probability map and Dynamic Programming (DP) to find the globally optimal path through all frames of a video. The proposed method addresses the object appearance variation problem using an FCN and handles occlusion through DP. The method is effective in tracking various single objects through video frames.
label: AI

title: YOLO9000: Better, Faster, Stronger
Abstract: This paper introduces YOLO9000, a state-of-the-art, real-time object detection system capable of detecting over 9000 object categories. First, various improvements to the YOLO detection method are proposed, both novel and drawn from prior work. The improved model, YOLOv2, achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard detection tasks like PASCAL VOC and COCO. At 67 FPS, YOLOv2 achieves 76.8 mAP on VOC 2007.  At 40 FPS, YOLOv2 achieves 78.6 mAP, surpassing state-of-the-art methods like Faster RCNN with ResNet and SSD while running significantly faster.  Finally, a method for joint training on object detection and classification is proposed. Using this method, YOLO9000 is trained simultaneously on the COCO detection dataset and the ImageNet classification dataset.  This joint training allows YOLO9000 to predict detections for object classes without labeled detection data.  The approach is validated on the ImageNet detection task. YOLO9000 achieves 19.7 mAP on the ImageNet detection validation set despite having detection data for only 44 of the 200 classes. On the 156 classes not in COCO, YOLO9000 achieves 16.0 mAP.  YOLO can detect more than just 200 classes; it predicts detections for over 9000 different object categories.  Moreover, it runs in real-time.
label: AI

title: A Fixed-Point Model for Pancreas Segmentation in Abdominal CT Scans
Abstract: Deep neural networks have been widely adopted for automatic organ segmentation from abdominal CT scans. However, the segmentation accuracy of some small organs (e.g., the pancreas) is sometimes unsatisfactory, potentially due to deep networks being easily disrupted by the complex and variable background regions that occupy a significant portion of the input volume.  This paper formulates this problem into a fixed-point model that uses a predicted segmentation mask to shrink the input region. This is motivated by the fact that a smaller input region often leads to more accurate segmentation.  During the training process, the ground-truth annotation is used to generate accurate input regions and optimize network weights. In the testing stage, the network parameters are fixed, and the segmentation results are updated iteratively.  The approach is evaluated on the NIH pancreas segmentation dataset and outperforms the state-of-the-art by more than 4%, measured by the average Dice-Sørensen Coefficient (DSC). Additionally, a DSC of 62.43% is reported in the worst case, guaranteeing the reliability of the approach in clinical applications. |||

title: PixelCNN Models with Auxiliary Variables for Natural Image Modeling
Abstract: We propose a novel image generation model based on the PixelCNN architecture, incorporating auxiliary variables to enhance image quality. Our model utilizes two types of auxiliary variables: quantized grayscale images and multi-resolution image pyramids. These auxiliary variables help overcome the limitations of existing PixelCNN models, such as their focus on low-level details and computationally expensive sampling. Our experimental results demonstrate that our model generates more realistic images compared to state-of-the-art models.
label: AI

title: Joint denoising and distortion correction of atomic scale scanning transmission electron microscopy images
Abstract: Modern electron microscopes provide images at atomic resolution, allowing for the precise analysis of material properties. However, specimen movements introduce distortions in the images, making it challenging to accurately locate atomic centers. We propose a Bayesian method to address this issue, jointly estimating image distortions and reconstructing the underlying atomic grid using suitable bump functions. Our method utilizes a trust region approach to solve the resulting highly non-convex minimization problem. We have validated our approach using variational techniques and evaluated its performance on both synthetic and real experimental data.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Video Segmentation via Spatio-Temporally Nonlocal Appearance Learning
Abstract: Video object segmentation faces significant challenges due to factors such as rapid motion, cluttered backgrounds, and object appearance variation. Existing methods often rely on information from consecutive frames, neglecting the valuable long-term nonlocal information. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel approach that mines long-term spatio-temporal nonlocal appearance information for unsupervised video segmentation. Our algorithm leverages the reoccurrence of region appearance in a video, generating superpixels to represent foreground and background and updating their appearance based on long-term nonlocal counterparts. We then formulate a spatio-temporal graphical model with label consistency potentials, optimizing it to generate the final segmentation. Extensive evaluations on SegTrack and Youtube-Objects datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: EgoReID: Cross-view Self-Identification and Human Re-identification in Egocentric and Surveillance Videos
Abstract: Human identification remains a challenging task due to variations in visual features across different viewpoints, lighting conditions, and occlusions. Existing research primarily focuses on re-identification across similar viewpoints. However, with the growing popularity of egocentric and top-view vision, re-identification between these drastically different views presents new opportunities. This paper proposes a CRF-based method for re-identification across egocentric and top-view videos. Our approach identifies the cameraman in the top-view video and re-identifies individuals in the egocentric video by matching them to identities in the top-view video. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across various video recordings.
label: AI

title: UDBMS: Road to Unification for Multi-model Data Management
Abstract: Traditional database systems rely on a single data model for data organization, storage, and manipulation. This paper envisions a new approach for managing multiple data models against a single integrated backend. This approach enables the support of diverse models, such as semi-structured, graph, and relational models, providing a unified platform for both well-structured and NoSQL data. This integration reduces complexities related to integration, migration, development, maintenance, and operations. We propose a UDBMS (Unified Database Management System) with features like unified data model, flexible schema, unified query processing, unified index structure, and cross-model transaction guarantees. We outline our vision and discuss the research challenges that need to be addressed.
label: AI

title: Correlation Preserving Sparse Coding Over Multi-level Dictionaries for Image Denoising
Abstract: We introduce a novel image denoising method based on correlation preserving sparse coding. Our approach addresses limitations in dictionary-driven denoising methods caused by unstable and unreliable correlations among basis sets. We employ two effective regularized strategies: a graph-based regularizer for preserving global similarity correlations and a robust locality-constrained coding for preserving spatial neighborhood information. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both PSNR and subjective visual quality.
label: AI

title: Blind restoration for non-uniform aerial images using non-local Retinex model and shearlet-based higher-order regularization
Abstract: Aerial images are often degraded by space-varying motion blur and uneven illumination. We propose a novel patch-wise restoration approach to recover high-quality aerial images from degraded versions. Our method leverages the observation that blurring is influenced by illumination conditions. We utilize a non-local Retinex model to estimate the reflectance component from the degraded image, followed by illumination correction. We then alleviate non-uniform blurring and transform it to a uniform distribution, facilitating subsequent deblurring. For constructing the multi-scale sparsified regularizer, we improve the discrete shearlet transform to better represent anisotropic image features. Additionally, we introduce a new adaptive variant of total generalized variation for structure-preserving regularization. These complementary regularizers are integrated into an objective function, and the final deblurred image is extracted using a fast alternating direction scheme. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm, effectively removing both illumination and motion blur while recovering abundant details of aerial scenes with top-level quality.
label: AI

title: Active Learning and Proofreading for Delineation of Curvilinear Structures
Abstract: Many state-of-the-art delineation methods rely on supervised machine learning, requiring manually annotated training data. We present a generic approach to address the limitations of these methods by considering the influence of misclassification on delineation. Our approach identifies critical parts of linear structures that should be annotated first for effective classifier training in an Active Learning context. Similarly, we identify regions of the resulting reconstruction that require priority verification for near-perfect results in a proofreading context. By focusing human attention on potential classification errors, we reduce the required supervision. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on microscopy images depicting blood vessels and neurons.
label: AI

title: Validation, comparison, and combination of algorithms for automatic detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography images: the LUNA16 challenge
Abstract: Automatic detection of pulmonary nodules in thoracic CT scans has been an active area of research. We introduce the LUNA16 challenge, an objective evaluation framework for automatic nodule detection algorithms using the largest publicly available chest CT scan database. Participants develop their algorithms and submit predictions on 888 CT scans in two tracks: complete nodule detection and false positive reduction. This paper outlines the LUNA16 setup and presents the challenge results. We observed that leading solutions employed convolutional networks and utilized the provided set of nodule candidates. Combining these solutions achieved excellent sensitivity with fewer than 1.0 false positives per scan. Our observer study with expert readers revealed that the best system detected nodules missed by experts who initially annotated the LIDC-IDRI data. We released this set of additional nodules for further development of CAD systems.
label: AI

title: Two-stream convolutional neural network for accurate RGB-D fingertip detection using depth and edge information
Abstract: Accurate fingertip detection in depth images is crucial for human-computer interaction. We present a novel two-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for RGB-D fingertip detection. Our approach extracts edge images from depth images using random forests and combines this edge information with depth information within our CNN structure. We investigated various fusion approaches and propose a slow fusion strategy as a promising solution. Our real-time algorithm outperforms existing methods on the HandNet dataset with an average 3D error of 9.9mm and shows comparable accuracy on the NYU hand dataset.

title: Understanding Non-optical Remote-sensed Images: Needs, Challenges and Ways Forward
Abstract: Non-optical remote-sensed images are becoming increasingly important in disaster management, crime prevention, and precision agriculture. With the rise of small satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles equipped with radar and hyperspectral image sensors, there will be an abundance of non-optical data. Real-time understanding of this data is crucial for sustainable development goals. This article discusses the challenges and needs for image understanding in the non-optical domain, exploring existing approaches and outlining the path towards a reliable real-time system.
label: AI

title: EnhanceNet: Single Image Super-Resolution Through Automated Texture Synthesis
Abstract: Single image super-resolution aims to infer a high-resolution image from a single low-resolution input. Traditional performance metrics, like PSNR, correlate poorly with human perception. We propose a novel approach that combines automated texture synthesis with a perceptual loss, focusing on creating realistic textures instead of pixel-accurate reproduction. Our method utilizes feed-forward fully convolutional neural networks in an adversarial training setting, achieving significant improvements in image quality at high magnification ratios. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding state-of-the-art results in both quantitative and qualitative benchmarks.
label: AI

title: DARN: a Deep Adversial Residual Network for Intrinsic Image Decomposition
Abstract: We present a new deep supervised learning method for intrinsic image decomposition, separating a single image into its albedo and shading components. Our approach utilizes a fully convolutional neural network that estimates absolute albedo and shading jointly. Our solution relies on a deep sequence of residual blocks and a perceptually-motivated metric based on adversarially trained discriminators. Unlike traditional methods, our approach is fully data-driven and does not require physical priors or geometric information. Compared to recent deep learning techniques, we simplify the architecture and constrain it to generate valid and reversible decompositions. We enhance quantitative metrics to account for non scale-invariant quantities. Our architecture is trained and demonstrated on the MPI Sintel dataset, showing reduced overfitting and generalizability to other data. Results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing deep algorithms in both qualitative and quantitative aspects.
label: AI

title: Automatic Interpretation of Unordered Point Cloud Data for UAV Navigation in Construction
Abstract: This work focuses on developing a data processing system for automatic waypoint generation for UAV navigation during inspections of structures like buildings and bridges. The input includes data from two orthogonally mounted 2D laser scanners and an IMU. We have developed algorithms for data processing, divided into three major groups: data registration and filtering for 3D model generation, surface and obstacle detection for monitoring tasks, and waypoint generation for flight path planning. Experiments on different datasets demonstrate the system's ability to reconstruct a 3D point cloud of the structure, extract surfaces and objects, and generate waypoints for inspection tasks.
label: AI

title: Understanding Image and Text Simultaneously: a Dual Vision-Language Machine Comprehension Task
Abstract: We introduce a novel multi-modal task for computer systems, presented as a vision-language comprehension challenge: identifying the most suitable text description for a scene from multiple similar options. This task requires understanding beyond keyword recognition, demanding alignment between representations of both modalities to achieve a visually-grounded understanding of linguistic elements and their dependencies. We introduce an effective mechanism for generating decoys from image captions, resulting in a large-scale machine comprehension dataset based on COCO images and captions. We provide human evaluation results and present baseline and competitive learning approaches to illustrate the task's utility in advancing image and language comprehension. We demonstrate that multi-task learning settings show a positive correlation between performance on this task and end-to-end image captioning.
label: AI

title: Learning from Simulated and Unsupervised Images through Adversarial Training
Abstract: Recent progress in computer graphics has made it possible to train models using synthetic images, potentially eliminating the need for expensive annotations. However, a gap between synthetic and real image distributions can hinder performance. To bridge this gap, we propose Simulated+Unsupervised (S+U) learning, where the goal is to learn a model that improves the realism of a simulator's output using unlabeled real data while preserving annotations. Our method utilizes an adversarial network similar to GANs, but with synthetic images as inputs. We introduce modifications to the standard GAN algorithm to preserve annotations, prevent artifacts, and stabilize training. These modifications include self-regularization, a local adversarial loss, and discriminator updates using a history of refined images. This enables the generation of highly realistic images, validated qualitatively and through a user study. We evaluate the generated images by training models for gaze and hand pose estimation, demonstrating significant improvement over using synthetic images and achieving state-of-the-art results on the MPIIGaze dataset without labeled real data.
label: AI

title: First-Person Activity Forecasting with Online Inverse Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: We address the problem of incrementally modeling and forecasting long-term goals of a first-person camera wearer. Unlike prior work in trajectory forecasting, our algorithm, DARKO, reasons about semantic states (e.g., picking up an object) and future goal states far in space and time. DARKO learns and forecasts from visual observations of the user's daily behaviors via an Online Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) approach. Unlike classical IRL, which operates in batch settings, DARKO discovers states, transitions, rewards, and goals from streaming data. We show that DARKO forecasts goals better than competing methods in both noisy and ideal settings, demonstrating its theoretical and empirical no-regret property.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Examples Detection in Deep Networks with Convolutional Filter Statistics
Abstract: Deep learning has significantly improved visual recognition, but recent research has revealed adversarial examples that can negatively impact performance. This paper focuses on detecting adversarial examples by analyzing their distribution compared to normal examples. Instead of training a deep neural network for detection, we propose a simpler approach based on statistics from convolutional layer outputs. A cascade classifier is designed to efficiently detect adversarial examples. Importantly, the classifier trained on one adversarial generating mechanism can successfully detect examples from different mechanisms. The non-subdifferentiable nature of the classifier makes it difficult for adversaries to attack using gradient information. After detecting adversarial examples, we show that many can be recovered by applying a simple average filter. These findings provide insights into the classification mechanisms within deep convolutional neural networks.
label: AI

title: Set2Model Networks: Learning Discriminatively To Learn Generative Models
Abstract: We present a new "learning-to-learn" approach for rapid concept learning from small-to-medium sized training sets, specifically designed for web-initialized image retrieval. Our approach utilizes a deep architecture (Set2Model network) that maps sets of examples to simple generative probabilistic models, such as Gaussians or mixtures of Gaussians, in the space of high-dimensional descriptors. The embedding parameters into the descriptor space are trained end-to-end using meta-learning. The novelty of our approach lies in the derivation of the backprop process through mixture model fitting, making the likelihood of the resulting models differentiable. While meta-learning is discriminative, a trained Set2Model network performs generative learning of models in the descriptor space, facilitating learning in scenarios with no negative examples or polysemous concepts. We demonstrate that Set2Model networks excel at picking visual concepts from raw Internet image search outputs compared to strong baselines.
label: AI

title: MultiNet: Real-time Joint Semantic Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
Abstract: While most semantic reasoning approaches focus on improving performance, this paper emphasizes the importance of computational efficiency for real-time applications like autonomous driving. We present an approach for joint classification, detection, and semantic segmentation using a unified architecture with a shared encoder for all three tasks. Our approach is simple, trainable end-to-end, and demonstrates exceptional performance on the challenging KITTI dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in road segmentation. It is also highly efficient, taking less than 100ms to complete all tasks.
label: AI

title: Hardware for Machine Learning: Challenges and Opportunities
Abstract: Machine learning is crucial for extracting useful information from massive amounts of sensor data collected daily. While some applications focus on analyzing data to identify trends, others require immediate action based on the data. Local embedded processing near the sensor is often preferred over cloud-based processing due to privacy, latency, and bandwidth limitations. However, sensors face constraints on energy consumption, cost, throughput, and accuracy. Furthermore, flexibility is needed to adapt processing for different applications and environments. Machine learning often involves transforming input data into higher-dimensional spaces, which increases data movement and energy consumption. This paper explores strategies to address these challenges at various levels of hardware design, ranging from architecture and algorithms to circuits and advanced technologies.
label: AI

title: Re-evaluating Automatic Metrics for Image Captioning
Abstract: Image captioning, the task of generating natural language descriptions from images, has gained significant attention in recent years. Evaluating image captioning approaches automatically is becoming increasingly important. This paper provides a thorough evaluation of existing image captioning metrics through carefully designed experiments. It also explores the use of Word Mover's Distance (WMD) for image captioning. The findings highlight differences and similarities between metrics and their robustness based on extensive correlation, accuracy, and distraction evaluations. Results demonstrate that WMD offers significant advantages over other metrics.
label: AI

title: A Revisit of Hashing Algorithms for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
Abstract: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) is a fundamental problem in machine learning and data mining. While numerous hashing algorithms have been proposed to solve this problem, their evaluations haven't been comprehensive enough. This paper revisits the problem of search with a hash index, analyzing the pros and cons of two popular search procedures. It proposes a simple but effective two-level index structure and compares eleven popular hashing algorithms. Surprisingly, random-projection-based Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) emerged as the best performer, contradicting claims made by other hashing papers. Despite its simplicity, the capability of random-projection-based LSH has been underestimated. For reproducibility, the code used in this paper is publicly available on GitHub, serving as a testing platform for fair comparisons between different hashing algorithms.
label: AI

title: Handwriting recognition using Cohort of LSTM and lexicon verification with extremely large lexicon
Abstract: State-of-the-art handwriting recognition methods rely on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks (RNN), achieving impressive character recognition performance. However, lexicon-driven decoding processes, which integrate dictionaries, are limited to hundreds of thousands of words, hindering language coverage and overall recognition performance. This article proposes an alternative to lexicon-driven decoding based on lexicon verification and an original cascade architecture. The cascade consists of numerous complementary networks extracted from a single training cohort, making the learning process efficient. This approach achieves new state-of-the-art word recognition performance on the Rimes and IAM databases. Dealing with a gigantic lexicon of 3 million words, the method demonstrates interesting performance with a fast decision stage.
label: AI

title: Deep Blind Compressed Sensing
Abstract: This research addresses the challenge of extracting deeply learned features directly from compressive measurements. Unlike existing deep learning tools, which require the full signal or preprocessing, this work demonstrates that better results can be obtained by learning directly from the compressed domain. The study extends the framework of deep matrix factorization combined with blind compressed sensing, hence the term deep blind compressed sensing. Simulation experiments on imaging via single pixel camera, under-sampled biomedical signals, and compressive hyperspectral imaging showcase the superiority of deep blind compressed sensing.
label: AI

title: Physically-Based Rendering for Indoor Scene Understanding Using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Indoor scene understanding is crucial for applications such as robot navigation and human companion assistance. Data-driven deep neural networks have surpassed traditional approaches due to their representation learning capabilities. However, training for better representations requires a significant amount of per-pixel ground truth data, which is a bottleneck for core scene understanding tasks like semantic segmentation, normal prediction, and object edge detection. To address this issue, several studies have proposed using synthetic data. This work introduces a large-scale synthetic dataset with 400K physically-based rendered images from 45K realistic 3D indoor scenes. The research examines the impact of rendering methods and scene lighting on training for three computer vision tasks: surface normal prediction, semantic segmentation, and object boundary detection. This study provides insights into best practices for training with synthetic data, highlighting the benefits of realistic rendering. Results show that pretraining with this new synthetic dataset can surpass current state-of-the-art results on all three tasks.
label: AI

title: Probabilistic graphical model based approach for water mapping using GaoFen-2 (GF-2) high resolution imagery and Landsat 8 time series
Abstract: This paper evaluates the potential of Gaofen-2 (GF-2) high-resolution multispectral sensor (MS) and panchromatic (PAN) imagery for water mapping. Challenges in water mapping on high-resolution data include misclassification between water and shadows or low-reflectance objects due to spectral similarity and the difficulty of detecting small water bodies smaller than the spatial resolution of the MS image. To address the confusion between water and low-reflectance objects, Landsat 8 time series with two shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands are incorporated, as water exhibits strong absorption in SWIR. The probabilistic graphical model (PGM) is employed to integrate these multi-sensor, multi-resolution datasets, with conditional probability distributions based on object size. Results from SVM classification on PCA-fused and MS data, thresholding on the PAN image, and water index methods on the Landsat data are compared. The confusion matrices indicate that the PGM method achieves the best performance with the highest overall accuracy. Additionally, small rivers can be extracted by weighting the PAN result in PGM. A post-classification procedure further excludes misclassification in shadow and water-land boundary regions, improving producer's, user's, and overall accuracy.
label: AI

title: Efficient Action Detection in Untrimmed Videos via Multi-Task Learning
Abstract: This paper explores joint learning of action recognition and temporal localization in long, untrimmed videos. A multi-task learning framework is employed, performing action proposal, action recognition, and action localization refinement in parallel instead of the standard sequential pipeline. A novel temporal actionness regression module is developed to estimate the proportion of a clip containing action, enabling temporal localization and other applications such as video retrieval, surveillance, and summarization. Random shear augmentation is introduced during training to simulate viewpoint change. Evaluation on three popular video benchmarks demonstrates the efficiency and accuracy of the joint model. Compared to sequential ConvNets, the joint model requires less storage and computation, eliminating the need for dense trajectory features. Despite its efficiency, the joint model surpasses state-of-the-art methods in accuracy.
label: AI

title: SE-Sync: A Certifiably Correct Algorithm for Synchronization over the Special Euclidean Group
Abstract: Many important geometric estimation problems involve synchronization over the special Euclidean group: estimating the values of poses based on relative measurements between them. This problem is typically formulated as a nonconvex maximum-likelihood estimation that is computationally challenging. This paper presents an algorithm that efficiently recovers certifiably globally optimal solutions for special Euclidean synchronization in a non-adversarial noise regime. The algorithm leverages a semidefinite relaxation of the maximum-likelihood estimation, whose minimizer provides an exact maximum-likelihood estimate as long as the noise level remains below a critical threshold. Moreover, the algorithm can verify exactness a posteriori, certifying the optimality of the recovered estimate. A specialized optimization scheme is developed to solve large-scale instances of this relaxation by exploiting its low-rank, geometric, and graph-theoretic structure, reducing it to an equivalent optimization problem on a low-dimensional Riemannian manifold. A truncated-Newton trust-region method is used to efficiently solve this reduction. Combining this fast optimization approach with a simple rounding procedure results in the algorithm SE-Sync. Evaluation on simulated and real-world pose-graph SLAM datasets demonstrates that SE-Sync recovers certifiably globally optimal solutions for noise levels exceeding typical robotics and computer vision applications, and does so significantly faster than current state-of-the-art techniques.
label: AI

title: Automatic Identification of Scenedesmus Polymorphic Microalgae from Microscopic Images
Abstract: Microalgae counting is used to measure biomass quantity. Traditionally, this is performed manually using a Neubauer chamber and expert criterion, leading to potential errors. This paper presents a methodology for automatic identification of Scenedesmus microalgae, used in methane production and the food industry, applied to images captured by a digital microscope. The use of contrast adaptive histogram equalization for pre-processing and active contours for segmentation is described. Statistical features, such as Histogram of Oriented Gradients, Hu and Zernike moments, and texture features, including Haralick and Local Binary Patterns descriptors, are used for algae characterization. Scenedesmus algae form coenobia consisting of 1, 2, 4, and 8 cells, and the amount of algae in each coenobium helps determine the amount of lipids, proteins, and other substances in a given sample. Classification of coenobia achieves accuracies of 98.63% with Support Vector Machine (SVM) and 97.32% with Artificial Neural Network (ANN), making this methodology a viable alternative to traditional algae counting techniques. The database used in this paper is publicly available for download.
label: AI

title: Top-down Visual Saliency Guided by Captions
Abstract: Neural image/video captioning models generate accurate descriptions, but their internal region-to-word mapping process remains a black box. Top-down neural saliency methods can identify important regions for tasks like object classification but cannot utilize natural language sentences as input. This paper proposes Caption-Guided Visual Saliency to expose the region-to-word mapping in encoder-decoder networks, demonstrating that it is learned implicitly from caption training data without explicit pixel-level annotations. This approach generates spatial or spatiotemporal heatmaps for both predicted captions and arbitrary query sentences, recovering saliency without requiring additional attention layers. It can analyze various model architectures and improve their design. Evaluation on large-scale video and image datasets shows comparable captioning performance with existing methods while providing more accurate saliency heatmaps. The code is available at visionlearninggroup.github.io/caption-guided-saliency/.
label: AI

title: Survey of Promising Technologies for 5G Networks
Abstract: As an enhancement to cellular networks, the future-generation 5G network promises ultra-high-speed technology. This proposed network incorporates advanced technologies to deliver exceptional services. This study recommends new architectures and service management schemes for various emerging technologies in 5G, addressing issues related to data traffic capacity, high data rate, and reliability for ensuring QoS. Cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT), and software-defined networking (SDN) are key enabling technologies for the 5G network. Cloud-based services provide cost-effective and flexible solutions for information and communications technology, reducing infrastructure management costs. SDN offers a promising architecture that decouples control planes and data planes, supporting programmability, adaptability, and flexibility in evolving network architectures. IoT combines cloud computing and SDN to achieve higher productivity for evolving technologies in 5G by facilitating interaction between the physical and human world. This study provides a vision on comprehensive works related to enabling technologies for next-generation mobile systems and networks, with a focus on 5G mobile communications.
label: AI

title: Learning Motion Patterns in Videos
Abstract: Determining whether an object is in motion, independent of camera motion, is a challenging problem. This research addresses this task by learning motion patterns in videos. The core of the approach is a fully convolutional network trained entirely on synthetic video sequences, their ground-truth optical flow, and motion segmentation. This encoder-decoder architecture first learns a coarse representation of optical flow field features and then refines it iteratively to produce motion labels at the original high resolution. Further improvement is achieved using an objectness map and a conditional random field, addressing errors in optical flow and focusing on moving objects rather than static elements. The output label of each pixel indicates whether it has undergone independent motion. The benefits of this learning framework are demonstrated on the moving object segmentation task, where the goal is to segment all objects in motion. The approach outperforms the top method on the DAVIS benchmark dataset, comprising real-world sequences, by 5.6%. Evaluation on the Berkeley motion segmentation database also achieves state-of-the-art results.
label: AI

title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
Abstract: The current mainstream approach for training natural language systems involves exposing them to large amounts of text. This passive learning approach is problematic for developing interactive machines like conversational agents. This paper proposes a framework for language learning based on multi-agent communication, studying this learning in the context of referential games. In these games, a sender and a receiver see a pair of images. The sender is informed about the target image and can send a message from a fixed vocabulary to the receiver. The receiver must rely on this message to identify the target image. Through this process, the agents develop their own language interactively to communicate effectively. The research demonstrates that two networks with simple configurations can learn to coordinate in the referential game. Furthermore, the study explores modifications to the game environment to make the "word meanings" induced in the game better reflect intuitive semantic properties of the images. Additionally, a simple strategy for grounding the agents' code into natural language is presented. These steps are crucial for developing machines that can communicate productively with humans.
label: AI

title: A Unified Framework for Tumor Proliferation Score Prediction in Breast Histopathology
Abstract: This paper presents a unified framework to predict tumor proliferation scores from breast histopathology whole slide images. The system offers a fully automated solution for predicting both a molecular data-based and a mitosis counting-based tumor proliferation score. The framework integrates three modules, each fine-tuned for optimal performance: an image processing component for handling whole slide images, a deep learning-based mitosis detection network, and a proliferation score prediction module. The system achieved a 0.567 quadratic weighted Cohen's kappa in mitosis counting-based score prediction and a 0.652 F1-score in mitosis detection. On Spearman's correlation coefficient, evaluating predictive accuracy for the molecular data-based score, the system obtained 0.6171. This approach won first place in all three tasks of the Tumor Proliferation Assessment Challenge 2016, a MICCAI grand challenge.
label: AI

title: Trilaminar Multiway Reconstruction Tree for Efficient Large Scale Structure from Motion
Abstract: Accuracy and efficiency are crucial in large-scale incremental Structure from Motion (SfM). This paper proposes a unified framework for dividing the image set into clusters suitable for reconstruction and finding multiple reliable and stable starting points. Image partitioning occurs in two steps: First, small image groups are selected at locations with high image density. Second, all images are clustered based on their optimal reconstruction paths to these image groups. This ensures that the scene is reconstructed from dense areas to sparse areas, reducing error accumulation when image overlap is weak. For faster speed, images outside the selected group in each cluster are further divided to achieve greater parallelism. Experiments demonstrate significant speedup, higher accuracy, and better completeness achieved by this method.
label: AI

title: Stochastic Multidimensional Scaling
Abstract: Multidimensional scaling (MDS) is a popular dimensionality reduction technique used for network visualization and cooperative localization. However, the traditional stress minimization formulation of MDS requires batch optimization algorithms, limiting scalability to large-sized problems. This paper presents an alternative stochastic stress minimization framework amenable to incremental and distributed solutions. A novel linear-complexity stochastic optimization algorithm is proposed, proven to be convergent and easy to implement. The algorithm's applicability to localization and visualization tasks is explored. Extensive tests on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy.
label: AI

title: An Empirical Study of Language CNN for Image Captioning
Abstract: Language Models based on recurrent neural networks have dominated recent image caption generation tasks. This paper introduces a Language CNN model suitable for statistical language modeling tasks, achieving competitive performance in image captioning. Unlike previous models that predict the next word based on one previous word and hidden state, the language CNN receives all previous words as input, modeling long-range dependencies crucial for image captioning. The effectiveness of this approach is validated on two datasets, MS COCO and Flickr30K. Extensive experimental results show that this method outperforms vanilla recurrent neural network-based language models and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Relieving Core Routers from Dynamic Routing with off-the-shelf Equipment and Protocols
Abstract: To achieve traffic engineering goals, current backbone networks utilize expensive and sophisticated equipment running distributed algorithms for dynamic multi-path routing. This paper proposes a simpler approach where the backbone implements many pre-computed paths, and most adaptation to traffic engineering goals occurs at the network edge. In line with Software Defined Networking, edge adaptation is driven by a logically centralized controller that leverages available paths to adapt traffic load balancing based on current demands and network status. Two algorithms are presented to support this vision. The first algorithm selects sets of paths capable of supporting future load balancing needs and adaptation to network faults. As the total number of required paths is crucial and their continuous availability necessitates numerous FIB entries in core routers, the second algorithm aggregates these paths into a reduced number of trees. This algorithm surpasses previously proposed algorithms for path aggregation. The study shows that off-the-shelf equipment supporting simple protocols can implement routing with these trees, demonstrating that simplicity in the core can be achieved by using only trivially available protocols and their basic implementations.
label: AI

title: Image biomarker standardisation initiative
Abstract: The image biomarker standardization initiative (IBSI) is an independent international collaboration dedicated to standardizing the extraction of image biomarkers from acquired imaging for high-throughput quantitative image analysis (radiomics). Reproducibility and validation are major challenges in this field, partly due to the lack of consensus-based guidelines and definitions for translating acquired imaging into high-throughput image biomarkers. The IBSI aims to address these challenges by providing image biomarker nomenclature and definitions, benchmark datasets, benchmark values for verifying image processing and biomarker calculations, reporting guidelines, and promoting high-throughput image analysis. |||

title: Temporal Tessellation: A Unified Approach for Video Analysis
Abstract: This paper proposes a general approach for video understanding, inspired by semantic transfer techniques that have proven successful in 2D image analysis. The method treats a video as a sequence of clips, each with its own semantics, which can be natural language captions or other labels depending on the task. By finding correspondences between clips in a test video and reference videos with known semantics, the method transfers the reference semantics to the test video. Two matching methods are presented, both designed to ensure that reference clips resemble test clips and that the semantics of selected reference clips are consistent and temporally coherent. The method is applied to various tasks, including video captioning, summarization, temporal action detection, and sound prediction, and outperforms the state of the art in most cases. Notably, it is the only known single method successfully applied to such a diverse range of tasks.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Place Discovery for Visual Place Classification
Abstract: This study examines the use of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) in visual place classification for robotic mapping and localization. The challenge lies in partitioning the robot's workspace into places to optimize the performance of DCNN classifiers.  Addressing the chicken-and-egg problem of requiring predefined place classes to train a DCNN classifier, the study proposes several unsupervised strategies for discovering place classes, namely "time cue," "location cue," "time-appearance cue," and "location-appearance cue."  These methods are evaluated using the publicly available University of Michigan North Campus Long-Term (NCLT) Dataset.
label: AI

title: A Statistical Approach to Continuous Self-Calibrating Eye Gaze Tracking for Head-Mounted Virtual Reality Systems
Abstract: This work introduces a novel, automatic eye gaze tracking scheme inspired by smooth pursuit eye motion during mobile gaming or virtual reality content consumption. The algorithm continuously calibrates an eye tracking system for a head-mounted display, eliminating the need for explicit calibration and automatically compensating for small headset movements relative to the head. By finding correspondences between corneal motion and screen space motion, the algorithm generates Gaussian Process Regression models that provide a continuous mapping from corneal position to screen space position. The accuracy achieved is comparable to that of explicit calibration methods.
label: AI

title: CLEVR: A Diagnostic Dataset for Compositional Language and Elementary Visual Reasoning
Abstract: Developing artificial intelligence systems capable of reasoning and answering questions about visual data requires diagnostic tests to evaluate progress and identify weaknesses. While existing benchmarks for visual question answering can be helpful, they suffer from biases that models can exploit to answer questions without true reasoning, and they conflate multiple sources of error, hindering the identification of specific model weaknesses. This paper introduces a diagnostic dataset designed to test a range of visual reasoning abilities. It minimizes biases and provides detailed annotations describing the type of reasoning required for each question.  The dataset is used to analyze various modern visual reasoning systems, revealing novel insights into their capabilities and limitations.
label: AI

title: Beyond Skip Connections: Top-Down Modulation for Object Detection
Abstract: Recent advancements in object detection have focused on deeper feedforward networks, achieving significant progress. However, detecting certain object categories, such as bottles and remotes, requires representations of fine details, not just coarse, semantic representations.  As such, a method is proposed to incorporate finer details from lower layers into the detection architecture. While skip connections have been used to combine high-level and low-level features, the paper argues that selecting the right features from lower levels necessitates top-down contextual information. Inspired by the human visual pathway, the proposed method supplements the standard bottom-up, feedforward ConvNet with a top-down modulation (TDM) network, connected using lateral connections. These connections modulate lower layer filters, while the top-down network handles the selection and integration of contextual information and low-level features. The TDM architecture significantly improves performance on the COCO testdev benchmark, achieving notable accuracy gains for various network architectures without requiring additional techniques.
label: AI

title: From Images to 3D Shape Attributes
Abstract: This paper investigates properties of 3D shape that can be determined from a single image. It defines 3D shape attributes, generic properties capturing curvature, contact, and occupied space, and aims to infer these attributes and a low-dimensional 3D shape embedding from a single image.  A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is trained to perform this task, starting with synthetic images to control the influence of cues and nuisance parameters.  The research then transitions to real images, introducing a large-scale image dataset of sculptures. The CNN trained on the sculpture dataset demonstrates the following: (i) the specific regions of the imaged sculpture used to infer 3D shape attributes; (ii) the ability of the shape embedding to match previously unseen sculptures regardless of viewpoint; and (iii) the generalization of 3D attributes to images of other object classes.
label: AI

title: Center-Focusing Multi-task CNN with Injected Features for Classification of Glioma Nuclear Images
Abstract: Classifying the various shapes and attributes of glioma cell nuclei is crucial for diagnosis and understanding the disease. This study investigates automated classification of glioma nuclear shapes and visual attributes using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on pathology images of automatically segmented nuclei.  Three methods are proposed to enhance the performance of a previously developed semi-supervised CNN: (1) focusing the CNN on the image center containing the nucleus, (2) injecting pre-extracted VGG features into an intermediate layer of the CNN, and (3) separating the losses of the two target class groups (nuclear shapes and attributes) into single-label and multi-label losses.  On a dataset of 2078 images, the combined methods reduce the error rate of attribute and shape classification by 21.54% and 15.07%, respectively, compared to the previous state-of-the-art method.
label: AI

title: Two decades of local binary patterns: A survey
Abstract: Texture is a crucial characteristic for various image types. Recent advancements in local binary patterns (LBP)-based descriptors have led to significant progress in applying texture methods to diverse problems and applications.  This chapter surveys the latest and most important LBP variants in 2D, spatiotemporal, 3D, and 4D domains, highlighting new developments in 1D signal analysis.  Finally, the chapter outlines future research challenges in the field.
label: AI

title: Video Stream Retrieval of Unseen Queries using Semantic Memory
Abstract: Retrieval of live, user-broadcast video streams presents an increasingly relevant and under-addressed challenge. The online nature of the problem necessitates temporal evaluation, while the unpredictable scope of potential queries motivates an approach accommodating arbitrary search queries.  To address the breadth of possible queries, a no-example approach is adopted, using a query's semantic relatedness to pre-trained concept classifiers.  To adapt to shifting video content, memory pooling and memory welling methods are proposed, prioritizing recent information over past content. The paper identifies two stream retrieval tasks: instantaneous retrieval at any given time and continuous retrieval over an extended duration, and proposes methods for evaluating them.  Three large-scale video datasets are adapted for stream retrieval, and results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed search methods for both stream retrieval tasks and traditional, non-streaming video tasks.
label: AI

title: Local Sparse Approximation for Image Restoration with Adaptive Block Size Selection
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of image restoration (denoising and inpainting) using sparse approximation of local image blocks. Local image blocks are extracted by sliding square windows over the image. An adaptive block size selection procedure is proposed for local sparse approximation, influencing the global recovery of the underlying image. The adaptive local block selection aims to minimize the mean square error (MMSE) in the recovered image. This framework results in a clustered image based on the selected block size, with each cluster restored separately using sparse approximation. The proposed framework achieves results comparable to recently developed image restoration techniques.
label: AI

title: Action-Driven Object Detection with Top-Down Visual Attentions
Abstract: A prevalent paradigm for deep learning-based object detection relies on a "bottom-up" approach using "passive" scoring of class-agnostic proposals. While efficient, these approaches lack holistic analysis of scene-level context.  This paper presents an "action-driven" detection mechanism using a "top-down" visual attention model. The model localizes an object by taking sequential actions guided by the attention model. The attention model, conditioned on an image region, provides actions to approach a target object.  While individual actions are weak, an ensemble of sequential actions accurately converges a bounding box to the target object boundary.  The attention model, referred to as AttentionNet, is composed of a convolutional neural network.  The detection procedure solely utilizes actions from a single AttentionNet without relying on object proposals or post bounding-box regression.  Evaluations on the PASCAL VOC series and ILSVRC CLS-LOC dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance compared to bottom-up detection methods, particularly excelling in elaborate localization.
label: AI

title: Dynamic Action Recognition: A convolutional neural network model for temporally organized joint location data
Abstract: Recognizing human actions in a video is a challenging task with applications in various fields. Existing work has primarily used images from 2D or 3D cameras, with limited use of the idea that human actions are easily identified by joint movement in 3D space.  This paper proposes a CNN model that predicts human activity using joint data. The use of joint data representation offers lower dimensionality than image or video representations, resulting in a simpler and faster model than RNN models.  The developed six-layer convolutional network reduces each input feature vector to a one-dimensional binary vector, providing the predicted activity. The model achieves an accuracy of up to 87% in recognizing activities, using joint data from the Cornell Activity Datasets.
label: AI

title: Efficient Optical flow and Stereo Vision for Velocity Estimation and Obstacle Avoidance on an Autonomous Pocket Drone
Abstract: Miniature Micro Aerial Vehicles (MAVs) are well-suited for indoor flight, but autonomous navigation poses challenges due to hardware limitations. This paper presents a highly efficient computer vision algorithm called Edge-FS for determining velocity and depth. The algorithm runs at 20 Hz on a 4 g stereo camera with an embedded STM32F4 microprocessor, using feature histograms to calculate optical flow and stereo disparity.  Stereo-based distance estimates are used to scale the optical flow, retrieving the drone's velocity. The velocity and depth measurements enable fully autonomous flight of a 40 g pocket drone, relying solely on on-board sensors. The method allows the MAV to control its velocity and avoid obstacles.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Perceptual Rewards for Imitation Learning
Abstract: Reward function design and exploration time are significant obstacles to deploying reinforcement learning (RL) agents in real-world settings. Designing reward functions often requires extensive hand engineering and additional sensors for measuring task success.  Furthermore, many tasks involve multiple implicit intermediate steps that must be executed sequentially.  To address these challenges, the paper proposes leveraging the abstraction power of intermediate visual representations learned by deep models to rapidly infer perceptual reward functions from limited demonstrations. The presented method identifies key intermediate task steps from a small number of demonstration sequences and automatically identifies the most discriminative features for recognizing these steps.  The method utilizes features from a pre-trained deep model without requiring explicit sub-goal specification.  The resulting reward functions can be used by an RL agent to learn the task in real-world settings.  Evaluations on real-world tasks demonstrate qualitative results and quantitative comparisons to human-designed reward functions.  The method is also shown to learn a real-world door opening skill using a real robot, even with a human demonstration provided using their own hand. These findings represent the first results demonstrating that complex robotic manipulation skills can be learned directly from a human demonstration video without supervised labels.
label: AI

title: Deep Motion Features for Visual Tracking
Abstract: Robust visual tracking is a challenging computer vision problem with numerous real-world applications. Most existing approaches employ hand-crafted appearance features, such as HOG or Color Names. While deep RGB features extracted from convolutional neural networks have proven successful for tracking, they only capture appearance information.  Motion cues provide discriminative and complementary information that can enhance tracking performance. Deep motion features have been successfully applied to action recognition and video classification tasks, typically learned by training a CNN on optical flow images extracted from large labeled video datasets.  This paper investigates the impact of deep motion features within a tracking-by-detection framework.  The study demonstrates that hand-crafted, deep RGB, and deep motion features contain complementary information. The paper proposes fusing appearance information with deep motion features for visual tracking, representing the first approach to combine these features for this purpose.  Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the fusion approach outperforms standard methods relying solely on appearance information.
label: AI

title: Detecting Unexpected Obstacles for Self-Driving Cars: Fusing Deep Learning and Geometric Modeling
Abstract: Detecting small road hazards, such as lost cargo, is crucial for self-driving cars. This paper tackles this challenging problem with a vision system that leverages appearance, contextual, and geometric cues.  To utilize appearance and contextual cues, a deep learning-based obstacle detection framework is proposed, employing a variant of a fully convolutional network to predict pixel-wise semantic labeling of free-space, on-road unexpected obstacles, and background.
