Geometric cues are exploited using a state-of-the-art detection approach that predicts obstacles from stereo input images via model-based statistical hypothesis tests.  A Bayesian framework is presented to fuse the semantic and stereo-based detection results, using the mid-level Stixel representation to describe obstacles in a flexible, compact, and robust manner.  The system is evaluated on the Lost and Found dataset, featuring challenging scenes with obstacles as small as 5 cm in height.  The results demonstrate significant improvements over the state-of-the-art, with relative performance gains of up to 50%.  The system achieves a detection rate exceeding 90% for distances up to 50 m, operating at 22 Hz on a self-driving platform.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Pedestrian Collision Warning System based on a Convolutional Neural Network with Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Traditional pedestrian collision warning systems sometimes generate false alarms, even in situations where there is no danger, such as when pedestrians are walking on the sidewalk. These false alarms can hinder driver focus.  This paper proposes a novel framework for an end-to-end pedestrian collision warning system based on a convolutional neural network. Semantic segmentation information is used to train the CNN, minimizing two loss functions: cross-entropy and Euclidean losses.  The method demonstrates effectiveness in reducing false alarms and improving warning accuracy compared to a traditional histogram of oriented gradients (HoG)-based system.
label: AI

title: Wide-Slice Residual Networks for Food Recognition
Abstract: Food diary applications represent a lucrative market. These applications, based on image food recognition, present new challenges for computer vision and pattern recognition algorithms.  Recent work has focused on either hand-crafted representations or learning these representations using deep neural networks.  Despite the success of deep neural network approaches, they generally utilize off-the-shelf architectures for food dish classification, limiting the architectures' adaptation to the specific problem.  This paper introduces a new deep scheme designed to handle food structure.  Inspired by the success of residual deep networks, the proposed scheme employs a slice convolution block to capture vertical food layers.  Outputs from deep residual blocks are combined with sliced convolution to produce the classification score for specific food categories.  Evaluations on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed solution compared to existing approaches.
label: AI

title: Automatic Generation of Grounded Visual Questions
Abstract: This paper proposes the first model capable of generating visually grounded questions with diverse types for a single image.  Visual question generation is an emerging field that aims to generate natural language questions based on visual input.  However, it currently lacks automatic methods for generating meaningful questions with varying types for the same visual input.  This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a model that automatically generates visually grounded questions with diverse types.  The model takes as input both images and captions generated by a dense caption model, samples the most probable question types, and generates the questions sequentially.  Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that the model outperforms the strongest baseline in terms of both correctness and diversity.
label: AI

title: 3D Human Pose Estimation = 2D Pose Estimation + Matching
Abstract: This paper explores 3D human pose estimation from a single RGB image. While many approaches attempt to directly predict 3D pose from image measurements, this paper explores a simple architecture that reasons through intermediate 2D pose predictions.  The approach is based on two key observations: (1) deep neural networks have revolutionized 2D pose estimation, achieving accurate predictions even for poses with self-occlusions; and (2) large datasets of 3D motion capture (mocap) data are readily available, enabling the lifting of predicted 2D poses to 3D through simple memorization methods.  The resulting architecture is straightforward to implement using off-the-shelf 2D pose estimation systems and 3D mocap libraries. Notably, the study demonstrates that these methods outperform most state-of-the-art 3D pose estimation systems, which typically regress 3D pose directly from 2D measurements. |||
label: AI

title: Exploring the Design Space of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks at Large Scale
Abstract:
Recent research has shown that deep neural networks (DNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) significantly outperform previous solutions in numerous machine learning problems.  However, no single CNN/DNN architecture is optimal for all problems. Instead, the most effective architecture varies depending on the application. Due to the vast design space of CNNs, containing billions of possible architectures, this dissertation develops a methodology for systematically exploring this space. This methodology consists of four key elements: 

1.  Strategic selection of benchmarks and metrics.
2.  Efficient training of CNN models.
3.  Defining and describing the CNN design space.
4.  Exploring the design space of CNN architectures.

These themes together form a robust methodology for identifying the most suitable CNN architectures for practical applications.
label: AI

title: Deeply Aggregated Alternating Minimization for Image Restoration
Abstract: Image restoration using regularization techniques remains an active research area in computer vision and image processing. These techniques often utilize a guidance signal from different modalities as an additional input. This work introduces a general framework for image restoration called Deeply Aggregated Alternating Minimization (DeepAM). DeepAM proposes training a deep neural network to advance two steps in the conventional Alternating Minimization (AM) algorithm: proximal mapping and continuation.  Both steps are learned from a large dataset in an end-to-end manner. This framework enables convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to function as a prior or regularizer within the AM algorithm.  The learned regularizer through deep aggregation surpasses recent data-driven approaches and nonlocal methods. The framework's flexibility and effectiveness are demonstrated in various image restoration tasks, including single image denoising, RGB-NIR restoration, and depth super-resolution.
label: AI

title: Efficiently Computing Piecewise Flat Embeddings for Data Clustering and Image Segmentation
Abstract: Image segmentation, a critical area of computer vision with widespread applications, benefits from a technique called Piecewise Flat Embeddings (PFE). PFE transforms image pixel data into a lower-dimensional representation where similar pixels are clustered together and dissimilar pixels are separated. While PFE has shown promise, its original formulation is computationally prohibitive for large images. This paper presents two improvements to accelerate PFE computation. First, it reformulates parts of the algorithm to enable parallelization of linear algebra operations. Second, it proposes using an iterative linear solver (preconditioned conjugate gradient) to efficiently solve a linear least-squares problem within the algorithm's inner loop. These computational enhancements, demonstrated on a publicly available image database, result in a significant order of magnitude speedup without compromising segmentation performance. This advancement makes PFE more practical for large datasets and applicable not only to image segmentation but also to general data clustering problems.
label: AI

title: High Performance Software in Multidimensional Reduction Methods for Image Processing with Application to Ancient Manuscripts
Abstract: Multispectral imaging is a powerful technique for enhancing the readability of faded text, whether due to intentional erasure or the passage of time. While individual wavelengths often suffice to read text, image enhancement is sometimes necessary to maximize readability. This paper evaluates and compares a comprehensive set of dimensionality reduction methods for image processing. Fifteen dimensionality reduction methods were assessed using two different manuscripts, both subjectively (through expert opinion) and objectively (using the Davies-Bouldin and Dunn indexes). The study found that Canonical Variates Analysis (CVA), previously used to enhance multispectral images, outperformed all other tested methods. However, specific circumstances might favor alternative approaches. CVA, being a supervised clustering technique, requires significantly more user time and effort than unsupervised techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA). If PCA results are sufficient for text readability, the additional effort for CVA may not be justified. To facilitate comparisons, a CVA method was implemented in the C programming language using the GNU Scientific Library (GSL) and OpenCV computer vision library.
label: AI

title: Exploring Structure for Long-Term Tracking of Multiple Objects in Sports Videos
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for tracking multiple objects, even when they experience long-term occlusion and abrupt motion, by leveraging structural relations. The method employs a model-free approach that relies solely on annotations provided in the first video frame for online tracking of all objects, without any knowledge from future frames.  A probabilistic Attributed Relational Graph (ARG) is initialized from the first frame and incrementally updated throughout the video. The proposed approach uses structural information not only to evaluate the scene but also to generate new tracking hypotheses, thereby enabling the generation of relevant object candidates to improve or recover lost tracks.  Evaluated on table tennis, volleyball, and the ACASVA dataset, the method demonstrates robustness, flexibility, and outperformance compared to other state-of-the-art methods in sports videos exhibiting structural patterns.
label: AI

title: Binary Distance Transform to Improve Feature Extraction
Abstract: Various methods have been developed for texture recognition over the years. However, texture datasets can be challenging to classify due to artifacts such as varying scale, illumination, and noise.  This paper proposes using binary distance transform on the original dataset to enhance texture representation and consequently improve recognition. Texture images, typically grayscale, undergo binarization prior to the distance transform. The resulting images are then combined with the original texture to augment the information content.  The approach was evaluated on four datasets.  For example, on the Outex dataset, the proposed method significantly outperformed the traditional approach, achieving up to a 10% improvement in classification rates. These results demonstrate the importance of this approach for improving texture recognition.
label: AI

title: Fractal Descriptors of Texture Images Based on the Triangular Prism Dimension
Abstract: This work introduces a novel descriptor for texture images based on fractal geometry and its application to image analysis. The descriptors are derived by estimating the triangular prism fractal dimension at different scales using a weighted exponential parameter, followed by dimensionality reduction using the Karhunen-Loève transform. The effectiveness of these descriptors is evaluated on two well-known texture datasets, Brodatz and Vistex, for both classification and image retrieval. The method is also tested for its invariance to rotations and Gaussian noise. The results demonstrate superior performance compared to other classical and state-of-the-art descriptors in the literature, highlighting the strength of triangular descriptors for these tasks and suggesting their potential in practical applications of image analysis based on texture features.
label: AI

title: Feature Encoding in Band-limited Distributed Surveillance Systems
Abstract: Distributed surveillance systems have gained popularity due to increasing security concerns. However, transmitting high-dimensional data in bandwidth-limited distributed systems presents a significant challenge. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a novel probabilistic algorithm based on the divergence between the probability distributions of visual features. The algorithm effectively reduces dimensionality, saving network bandwidth in distributed wireless smart camera networks. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments on two surveillance recognition tasks.
label: AI

title: Asynchronous Temporal Fields for Action Recognition
Abstract: Actions are more than just movements and trajectories; they are contextualized within a larger purpose.  For instance, we cook to eat and hold a cup to drink.  A complete understanding of videos requires going beyond appearance modeling and reasoning about the sequence of activities and higher-level constructs like intentions. This paper proposes a fully-connected temporal CRF model for reasoning about various aspects of activities, including objects, actions, and intentions, where potentials are predicted by a deep network.  Training such structured models end-to-end poses challenges, as inference and learning require mini-batches of whole videos, resulting in high correlation between data points and potential breakdown of the backpropagation algorithm. To overcome this, the paper presents an asynchronous variational inference method that allows efficient end-to-end training. The proposed method achieves a classification mAP of 22.4% on the Charades benchmark, outperforming the state-of-the-art (17.2% mAP) and offering similar improvements in temporal localization.
label: AI

title: Learning Features by Watching Objects Move
Abstract: This paper presents a novel and intuitive approach to unsupervised feature learning inspired by the human visual system.  It investigates whether low-level motion-based grouping cues can be used to learn effective visual representations. Unsupervised motion-based segmentation on videos is utilized to obtain segments, which serve as "pseudo ground truth" to train a convolutional network to segment objects from a single frame. The approach is based on the idea that motion plays a crucial role in visual system development, aiming to be more effective than "pretext" tasks commonly explored in unsupervised learning.  Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, with the learned representation significantly outperforming previous unsupervised methods in object detection, particularly when training data is scarce.
label: AI

title: Semantic Jitter: Dense Supervision for Visual Comparisons via Synthetic Images
Abstract: Learning to distinguish subtle differences in attributes is valuable, yet challenging. The number of possible comparisons grows quadratically with the number of training images, and access to images spanning the space of fine-grained visual differences is limited. This paper proposes addressing the sparsity of supervision problem by synthesizing training images.  Building upon a state-of-the-art image generation engine, it samples pairs of training images exhibiting slight modifications of individual attributes. By augmenting real training image pairs with these synthetic examples, attribute ranking models are trained to predict the relative strength of an attribute in novel pairs of real images.  Results on datasets of faces and fashion images demonstrate the promising potential of bootstrapping imperfect image generators to counteract sample sparsity in learning to rank.
label: AI

title: Large-Scale Image Retrieval with Attentive Deep Local Features
Abstract: This paper introduces DELF (DEep Local Feature), an attentive local feature descriptor suitable for large-scale image retrieval. The new feature is based on convolutional neural networks trained only with image-level annotations on a landmark image dataset. To identify semantically useful local features for image retrieval, an attention mechanism is proposed for keypoint selection, sharing most network layers with the descriptor. This framework acts as a drop-in replacement for other keypoint detectors and descriptors, facilitating more accurate feature matching and geometric verification. The system provides reliable confidence scores to reject false positives, making it robust against queries lacking a correct match in the database. To evaluate DELF, a new large-scale dataset, Google-Landmarks, is introduced, presenting challenges such as background clutter, partial occlusion, multiple landmarks, and objects at varying scales. DELF outperforms the state-of-the-art global and local descriptors in the large-scale setting by significant margins. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/tensorflow/models/tree/master/research/delf.
label: AI

title: Handwritten Signature Verification Using Hand-Worn Devices
Abstract: Online signature verification technologies, typically used in banks and post offices, rely on dedicated digital devices like tablets or smart pens for signature capture, analysis, and verification. This paper presents a novel method for online signature verification that utilizes increasingly available hand-worn devices, such as smartwatches or fitness trackers, instead of specialized hardware. The method uses a set of known genuine and forged signatures recorded using the motion sensors of a hand-worn device to train a machine learning classifier. Given an unknown signature and a claimed identity, the classifier determines whether the signature is genuine or forged. Validation was performed on 1980 recordings of genuine and forged signatures from 66 subjects. The method achieved a high degree of accuracy (0.98 AUC and 0.05 EER) in distinguishing between genuine and forged signatures.
label: AI

title: Simple Black-Box Adversarial Perturbations for Deep Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks are powerful and popular learning models achieving state-of-the-art performance in various pattern recognition tasks across computer vision, speech, and language processing. However, these networks are susceptible to carefully crafted adversarial perturbations that force misclassification of inputs. Adversarial examples enable adversaries to subvert system behavior, posing security risks when deployed in real-world scenarios. This work focuses on deep convolutional neural networks and demonstrates the ease with which adversaries can craft adversarial examples even without internal knowledge of the target network.  Attacks treat the network as a black box, only assuming that the network's output can be observed for probed inputs. The first attack simply adds perturbation to a randomly selected pixel or a small set of pixels. This is further enhanced by strategically selecting a small set of pixels to perturb using greedy local search. The proposed attacks naturally extend to a stronger notion of misclassification. Extensive experimental results illustrate the vulnerability of deep neural networks even to these elementary attacks. The simplicity and effectiveness of these schemes highlight their potential as a litmus test for designing robust networks.
label: AI

title: Photo-Quality Evaluation based on Computational Aesthetics: Review of Feature Extraction Techniques
Abstract: Researchers strive to model the aesthetic quality of photographs using both low-level and high-level features, drawing inspiration from art theory, psychology, and marketing. This literature review provides a taxonomy of each feature extraction measure by its implementation complexity, considering real-world applications and integration in mobile apps and digital cameras. The review also discusses machine learning results and identifies unexplored research areas for future work.
label: AI

title: An extended Perona-Malik model based on probabilistic models
Abstract: The Perona-Malik model has been successful in restoring images from noisy input. This paper reinterprets the Perona-Malik model in the language of Gaussian scale mixtures and derives extensions. It demonstrates that the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm applied to Gaussian scale mixtures leads to the lagged-diffusivity algorithm for computing stationary points of the Perona-Malik diffusion equations. Additionally, it shows how mean field approximations to these Gaussian scale mixtures lead to a modified lagged-diffusivity algorithm that better captures restoration uncertainties. Due to computational challenges with this modification, relaxations to the mean field objective are proposed to improve feasibility. Numerical experiments show that this modified algorithm often performs better in restoring textured areas and fuzzy edges compared to the unmodified algorithm. As a second application, the paper demonstrates the efficient sampling procedure for the probabilistic model within this framework, enabling the computation of conditional mean and other expectations. This resulting algorithm closely resembles the lagged-diffusivity algorithm. Finally, the paper shows that a probabilistic version of the Mumford-Shah segmentation model can be obtained within the same framework with a discrete edge-prior.
label: AI

title: Crowd collectiveness measure via graph-based node clique learning
Abstract: Collective motions of crowd systems have attracted significant attention in recent years. This paper proposes a node clique learning method to measure the collectiveness of a crowd system. This graph-based method investigates the influence of one node on others. A node is represented by a clique, a set of nodes obtained by spreading information from the node to others in the graph. Only nodes with sufficient information are selected as part of the node's clique. Motion coherence between two nodes is defined by comparing their node cliques. The collectiveness of a node and the overall crowd system are defined by the coherence between nodes. Self-driven particle (SDP) models and crowd motion databases are used to test the proposed method's ability to measure collectiveness.
label: AI

title: Few-Shot Object Recognition from Machine-Labeled Web Images
Abstract: With the tremendous progress of Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) in object recognition, reliable machine-labeled annotations are readily available through predictions from off-the-shelf ConvNets. This paper presents an abstraction memory-based framework for few-shot learning using machine-labeled image annotations. The method utilizes large-scale machine-annotated datasets (e.g., OpenImages) as an external memory bank. Information in the bank is stored in memory slots with a key-value format, where image features serve as keys and label embeddings as values. When queried by few-shot examples, the model selects visually similar data from the external memory bank and writes useful information obtained from related external data into another memory bank, called the abstraction memory. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) controllers and attention mechanisms are employed to ensure the data written to the abstraction memory is correlated with the query example. This abstraction memory concentrates information from the external memory bank, making few-shot recognition effective. Experiments demonstrate the model's ability to learn few-shot object recognition on clean human-labeled data from the ImageNet dataset. The results show that machine-labeled image annotations serve as effective and abundant resources for object recognition on novel categories. The proposed model with machine-labeled annotations achieves high performance, with a gap of only 1% compared to the performance using human-labeled annotations.
label: AI

title: Active and Continuous Exploration with Deep Neural Networks and Expected Model Output Changes
Abstract: The demands on visual recognition systems extend beyond the complexity offered by current large-scale image datasets like ImageNet. Therefore, curious and continuously learning algorithms are needed to actively acquire knowledge about semantic concepts present in unlabeled data. This paper presents an approach for performing continuous active learning and exploration where the algorithm actively selects relevant batches of unlabeled examples for annotation. These examples can belong to either known or undiscovered classes. The algorithm is based on a new generalization of the Expected Model Output Change principle for deep architectures, tailored specifically to deep neural networks. Efficient active selection techniques are provided through easy-to-implement approximations. Empirical experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms currently used heuristics.
label: AI

title: Cross-Modal Manifold Learning for Cross-modal Retrieval
Abstract: This paper introduces a scalable algorithm for cross-modal similarity preserving retrieval in a learned manifold space. Unlike existing approaches that compromise between preserving global and local geometries, the proposed technique respects both simultaneously during manifold alignment. Global topologies are maintained by recovering underlying mapping functions in the joint manifold space using partially corresponding instances. Inter- and intra-modality affinity matrices are then computed to reinforce the original data skeleton using perturbed minimum spanning tree (pMST) and maximize affinity among similar cross-modal instances, respectively. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on two multimodal image datasets (coronary atherosclerosis histology and brain MRI) for two applications: classification and regression.  The results demonstrate the superiority of this technique over comparative methods and its feasibility for improving computer-assisted diagnosis systems. This approach enables aggregating and interpreting disease-specific complementary information across modalities to make final decisions.
label: AI

title: X-ray In-Depth Decomposition: Revealing The Latent Structures
Abstract: X-ray radiography is a widely used imaging technique for diagnosing and guiding procedures. However, interpreting obscured anatomical features in X-ray images can be challenging and often requires high radiation doses and multiple perspectives. This study proposes a deep learning approach to decompose conventional X-ray images into multiple independent sub-volumes, enabling a better understanding of hidden anatomy. Despite the complexity of this task, the study shows promising results, paving the way for further advancements in this field.
label: AI

title: On Random Weights for Texture Generation in One Layer Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successfully used to model natural textures, even with just a single layer of random filters. This paper investigates why such simple CNNs are effective in generating textures. It theoretically demonstrates that one-layer CNNs, without a non-linearity, can preserve and modulate frequency coefficients, resulting in similar image generation capabilities with both random and pretrained weights. The paper further explores the impact of adding a ReLu non-linearity, showing that it can limit the variability of generated images.
label: AI

title: Dual Deep Network for Visual Tracking
Abstract: Visual tracking involves identifying and localizing a target object in a video sequence. This paper proposes a dual network architecture that leverages features across different layers of a deep model to improve tracking performance. The approach utilizes high-level features for semantic context and low-level features for discriminative appearance, enhancing feature representation. Geometric contours are highlighted by integrating an edge detector with hierarchical feature maps. To ensure robustness, the dual network is trained with random patches, enforcing focus on the target object. The network updates online based on the similarity between consecutive frames, further improving accuracy.  Additionally, prior maps are incorporated to provide target context using independent component analysis (ICA) with a reference algorithm. This results in improved tracking performance, outperforming current state-of-the-art methods on two large-scale benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: An Empirical Study of Adequate Vision Span for Attention-Based Neural Machine Translation
Abstract: Attention mechanisms are crucial for high-performance neural machine translation models. However, they can be computationally expensive due to the computation of score functions for all encoder states at each decoding step. This paper proposes a novel attention framework that dynamically reduces redundant score computation by introducing a "vision span" concept. This vision span defines a window of encoder states considered by the attention model at each step. The study shows that the average window size can be significantly reduced without significant loss in accuracy, highlighting the potential for efficient attention models in machine translation.
label: AI

title: Parsing Images of Overlapping Organisms with Deep Singling-Out Networks
Abstract: Parsing biological images with overlapping articulated organisms (e.g., worms or larvae) presents a significant challenge. This study proposes a novel approach that separates the tasks of individual object shape estimation and disentangling object groups. A deep feed-forward singling-out network (SON) is trained to map local image patches to vectorial descriptors that are sensitive to object characteristics but invariant to surrounding elements. Using SON-descriptors, the approach matches local patches to a gallery of isolated elements, generating hypotheses about the shape of the central object. Image-level optimization then selects a subset of these hypotheses to parse the whole image and disentangle the organism groups. This approach offers advantages over existing methods by avoiding stochastic search in high-dimensional configuration space and numerous rendering operations during testing. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach on microscopy images of various model organisms, showcasing its applicability to parsing crowded articulated objects.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Deep Structural Networks for Mammographic Mass Segmentation
Abstract: Mammographic mass segmentation is crucial for breast cancer diagnosis, identifying morphological features and regions of interest. This paper proposes an end-to-end network for mammogram segmentation, integrating a fully convolutional network (FCN) for potential function modeling and a conditional random field (CRF) for structural learning. The FCN is combined with position priori to account for varying mass distribution. Adversarial training is used to prevent overfitting on small datasets. The network's performance is further enhanced by fusing four models with different convolutional kernels. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed network, combined with adversarial training, achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance.
label: AI

title: Deep Multi-instance Networks with Sparse Label Assignment for Whole Mammogram Classification
Abstract: Mammogram classification plays a key role in computer-aided breast cancer diagnosis. Traditional methods require laborious manual annotation of training data and specialized models for annotation detection. This paper proposes end-to-end trained deep multi-instance networks for whole mammogram classification, eliminating the need for costly annotation. The study explores three different schemes for constructing deep multi-instance networks, demonstrating their robustness compared to previous methods that rely on segmentation and detection annotations.  The results highlight the potential of deep multi-instance networks for efficient and accurate mammogram classification.
label: AI

title: Learning a No-Reference Quality Metric for Single-Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: While numerous single-image super-resolution algorithms exist, evaluating their performance based on visual perception remains a challenge. This paper addresses this gap by conducting human subject studies and proposing a no-reference metric learned from perceptual scores. The metric utilizes three types of low-level statistical features in spatial and frequency domains to quantify artifacts in super-resolved images. A two-stage regression model is then trained to predict image quality scores without relying on ground-truth images. Extensive experiments confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed metric in assessing super-resolution image quality based on human perception.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning on Lie Groups for Skeleton-based Action Recognition
Abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition is a popular 3D classification problem. Existing state-of-the-art methods represent motion sequences as high-dimensional trajectories on a Lie group, followed by shallow learning of Lie group features. This paper proposes a deep network architecture that incorporates the Lie group structure to learn more appropriate features for action recognition. The network includes rotation mapping layers to transform input features, rotation pooling layers to reduce dimensionality, and a logarithm mapping layer to project manifold data onto a tangent space. The proposed network significantly outperforms existing shallow and conventional deep learning methods on standard 3D action recognition datasets, highlighting the benefits of incorporating the Lie group structure into deep learning models.
label: AI

title: 3D Shape Induction from 2D Views of Multiple Objects
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of inferring a distribution over 3D structures from 2D views of multiple objects taken from unknown viewpoints. The proposed "projective generative adversarial networks" (PrGANs) train a deep generative model of 3D shapes, ensuring that their projections match the distributions of input 2D views. The addition of a projection module allows for 3D shape distribution inference without requiring 3D information or annotations during training. The study demonstrates that PrGANs produce 3D shapes comparable in quality to those generated by GANs trained on 3D data. The disentangled representation of 2D shapes into geometry and viewpoint leads to a generative model of 2D shapes, enabling unsupervised prediction of 3D, viewpoint, and novel views from an input image.
label: AI

title: Joint Spatial-Angular Sparse Coding for dMRI with Separable Dictionaries
Abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) enables the reconstruction of neuronal fibers in the brain by measuring water diffusion along different directions in q-space. High angular resolution diffusion imaging (HARDI) provides better fiber orientation estimates but requires longer scan times due to the increased number of samples. This paper proposes a joint spatial-angular representation of dMRI to achieve sparser representations and accelerate dMRI acquisition. The study presents adaptations of sparse coding algorithms to efficiently solve large-scale problems by exploiting spatial-angular separability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significantly sparser representations of HARDI than current state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: EgoTransfer: Transferring Motion Across Egocentric and Exocentric Domains using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Mirror neurons, observed in the primary motor cortex of primates, fire both when an individual performs an action and when they observe the same action performed by another. This study explores the transfer of motion information between egocentric and exocentric perspectives, a crucial step towards building intelligent systems with human-like learning abilities. The researchers train models that predict motion in one view based on observations from the other view. Linear and non-linear models are evaluated on their ability to retrieve motion features across perspectives, demonstrating successful motion information transfer between egocentric and exocentric views.
label: AI

title: The Dem@Care Experiments and Datasets: a Technical Report
Abstract: The Dem@Care project aims to develop a comprehensive system providing personalized health services for individuals with dementia, medical professionals, and caregivers. The system utilizes multi-sensor data analysis and intelligent decision-making mechanisms to monitor lifestyle, environment, and health parameters, providing accurate representation of an individual's status and personalized feedback. The project has conducted data collection activities to facilitate technical development and evaluation, adhering to ethical guidelines and ensuring participant privacy. This report outlines the project's main objectives, ethical principles, and the datasets created.
label: AI

title: Learning to predict where to look in interactive environments using deep recurrent q-learning
Abstract: Bottom-Up (BU) saliency models struggle in complex interactive environments where humans are actively engaged in tasks. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to highlight task-relevant locations in input frames. A soft attention mechanism is integrated with a Deep Q-Network (DQN) model to train an RL agent to play a game and focus on pertinent visual input. Evaluations on Atari 2600 games show that the soft attention-based model outperforms bottom-up saliency models like Itti-Kochs saliency and GBVS, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting fixation locations during task-based interactions.
label: AI

title: Microscopic Muscle Image Enhancement
Abstract: Muscle fiber specimen images captured by optical microscopes often suffer from blur or out-of-focus issues. This paper presents a robust image enhancement algorithm specifically designed for muscle images. The proposed framework employs a novel spatially non-uniform blind deblurring approach that automatically detects and corrects degraded regions. Ring artifacts are addressed, and a kernel propagation strategy is implemented to accelerate the algorithm and handle the non-uniformity of blur kernels in muscle images. Experiments demonstrate the framework's effectiveness on muscle images obtained with advanced optical microscopes, providing computationally efficient and parameter-free enhancement.
label: AI

title: A Fusion Method Based on Decision Reliability Ratio for Finger Vein Verification
Abstract: Finger vein verification has made significant progress but lacks a perfect algorithm. While algorithms with similar overall accuracy may exhibit different misclassification patterns, this complementation can be exploited for fusion to enhance precision. This paper introduces a decision reliability ratio to quantify the confidence of individual algorithms. The Maximum Decision Reliability Ratio (MDRR) fusion method, incorporating weighted voting, is proposed. Experiments on a dataset of 1000 fingers demonstrate the effectiveness of MDRR, achieving higher accuracy than original individual classifiers and traditional fusion methods.
label: AI

title: SonoNet: Real-Time Detection and Localisation of Fetal Standard Scan Planes in Freehand Ultrasound
Abstract: Identifying and interpreting fetal standard scan planes during ultrasound examinations is a complex task requiring extensive training. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network-based method for automatic detection of 13 fetal standard views in freehand 2D ultrasound data, providing localization of fetal structures through bounding boxes. The network leverages weak supervision based on image-level labels, enabling real-time operation and optimal localization. Results demonstrate the method's effectiveness in real-time annotation, retrospective frame retrieval, and localization on a large and challenging dataset. The method achieves high accuracy in both real-time detection and retrospective frame retrieval tasks, showcasing its potential for assisting both experienced and inexperienced operators.
label: AI

title: Building Efficient Query Engines in a High-Level Language
Abstract: Abstraction without regret aims to use high-level programming languages for systems development without sacrificing performance. This paper presents LegoBase, a query engine written in Scala that achieves both high productivity and performance through generative programming.  LegoBase compiles high-level Scala code into specialized C code, enabling efficient implementation of various optimizations. The study demonstrates that powerful abstractions are essential for handling optimization complexity, shielding developers from compiler internals and decoupling optimizations. Evaluation using the TPC-H benchmark shows that LegoBase significantly outperforms commercial databases and existing query compilers while requiring minimal code development, making it a practical approach for building high-performance query engines.
label: AI

title: On the crucial impact of the coupling projector-backprojector in iterative tomographic reconstruction
Abstract: The performance of iterative reconstruction algorithms for X-ray tomography heavily depends on the accuracy and speed of the forward and backprojector operators. This study investigates the overlooked aspect of "coupling projector-backprojector," examining the impact of mathematical affinity between forward and backprojection implementations. Experiments demonstrate that reconstruction quality and algorithm convergence are significantly influenced by the matching between these operators. This finding highlights the importance of considering this coupling in the design of iterative reconstruction algorithms.
label: AI

title: Video Propagation Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a technique for propagating information forward through video data, enabling the transfer of structured information like semantic labels based on video content. The "Video Propagation Network" processes video frames adaptively and propagates information forward without access to future frames. It combines a temporal bilateral network for adaptive filtering with a spatial network for feature refinement, achieving increased performance compared to previous task-specific methods. The approach is tested on video object segmentation, semantic video segmentation, and a color propagation regression task, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness in various video-based applications. |||
label: AI

title: A Study of Lagrangean Decompositions and Dual Ascent Solvers for Graph Matching
Abstract: We propose a novel approach to address the quadratic assignment problem (QAP), also known as graph matching in computer vision. This approach builds upon the existing framework of dual ascent optimization for Lagrange decomposition. We introduce several novel Lagrangean relaxations of the graph matching problem, each with its corresponding algorithm, all of which operate within a unified dual ascent framework. Our comprehensive empirical analysis provides valuable theoretical insights and demonstrates the superior performance of our proposed approach, establishing it as a state-of-the-art any-time solver for the QAP. This improvement is particularly evident in dealing with large-scale sparse problem instances, involving over 500 graph nodes each.
label: AI

title: A Dual Ascent Framework for Lagrangean Decomposition of Combinatorial Problems
Abstract: We introduce a general dual ascent framework for Lagrangean decomposition of combinatorial problems, expanding upon the efficiency of existing dual ascent methods for various problems. Our proposed algorithm, applicable across multiple problem types, is parametrized to optimize performance for specific scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on graph matching and multicut problems, surpassing existing state-of-the-art solvers, including subgradient optimization methods and off-the-shelf linear programming solvers.
label: AI

title: A Message Passing Algorithm for the Minimum Cost Multicut Problem
Abstract: We propose a novel dual decomposition and linear program relaxation of the NP-hard minimum cost multicut problem. Unlike traditional polyhedral relaxations, our approach enables efficient optimization through message passing.  Similar to other polyhedral relaxations, our approach can be effectively tightened using cutting planes. We introduce an algorithm that iteratively alternates between message passing and efficient separation of cycle- and odd-wheel inequalities. This algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms based on linear programming, including those implemented within leading commercial software, as demonstrated in experiments with large instances of the problem derived from computer vision, biomedical image analysis, and data mining applications.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Pixel-Level Domain Adaptation with Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Training modern machine learning algorithms necessitates large, well-annotated image datasets, which are often prohibitively expensive to acquire. Synthesizing data offers an attractive alternative, with the advantage of automatic ground-truth annotation generation. However, models trained solely on rendered images often fail to generalize to real images. Previous work addressed this limitation through unsupervised domain adaptation algorithms, aiming to map representations between domains or extract domain-invariant features. We propose a novel approach that learns a pixel-space transformation between domains in an unsupervised manner. Our generative adversarial network (GAN)-based method adapts source-domain images to appear as if drawn from the target domain. This approach not only produces realistic samples but also significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in various unsupervised domain adaptation scenarios. Notably, the adaptation process generalizes to object classes unseen during training.
label: AI

title: SymbioCity: Smart Cities for Smarter Networks
Abstract: The "Smart City" (SC) concept aims to integrate cutting-edge ICT solutions into the infrastructure of future cities, offering enhanced services to citizens while reducing management costs across financial, social, and environmental domains. Within this framework, communication technologies serve as the backbone for SC services, providing the infrastructure for collecting and processing data. This paper proposes a new vision, "SymbioCity", where technology and SC services are designed to enhance each other in a symbiotic manner. This paradigm suggests that SC services can improve the performance of the communication systems that provide them with data. We present illustrative examples of this symbiotic ecosystem and substantiate our proposition with a proof-of-concept case study. This study demonstrates how the traffic monitoring service provided by the London Smart City initiative can be used to predict user density within a zone and optimize cellular service in that area.
label: AI

title: Deep Residual Hashing
Abstract: Hashing aims to generate compact similarity-preserving code words well-suited for large-scale image retrieval tasks. Most existing hashing methods involve a two-stage process, first encoding images as a vector of hand-crafted features and then performing separate binarization to generate hash codes. This two-stage process can result in sub-optimal encoding. This paper introduces Deep Residual Hashing (DRH), the first deep architecture for supervised hashing through residual learning, enabling simultaneous end-to-end representation learning and hash coding. DRH incorporates four key components: (1) a sub-network with multiple stacked residual blocks; (2) a hashing layer for binarization; (3) a supervised retrieval loss function based on neighborhood component analysis for similarity-preserving embedding; and (4) hashing-related losses and regularizations to control quantization error and enhance hash coding quality. We present extensive experimental results on a large public chest X-ray image database with co-morbidities, demonstrating substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: The VQA-Machine: Learning How to Use Existing Vision Algorithms to Answer New Questions
Abstract: The Visual Question Answering (VQA) challenge poses a unique challenge due to the unpredictable nature of questions. Answering these questions demands a wide range of image operations, from detection and counting to segmentation and reconstruction. Training a model to accurately perform even one of these operations using {image, question, answer} tuples would be challenging, and attempting to achieve all of them with limited training data seems ambitious. We propose a more general and scalable approach that leverages the existing proficiency of off-the-shelf algorithms for these operations. Our method learns how to utilize these external algorithms to achieve its goal, drawing inspiration from the Neural Turing Machine concept. The core of our approach is a novel co-attention model. Additionally, our method generates human-readable explanations for its decisions and can be trained end-to-end without requiring ground truth reasons. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on two publicly available datasets, Visual Genome and VQA, achieving state-of-the-art results in both cases.
label: AI

title: Output Constraint Transfer for Kernelized Correlation Filter in Tracking
Abstract: Kernelized Correlation Filter (KCF) is a state-of-the-art object tracker. However, it does not accurately model the distribution of correlation response during tracking, potentially leading to drifting problems, particularly when targets undergo significant appearance changes due to occlusion, camera shaking, or deformation. This paper introduces Output Constraint Transfer (OCT), a method that mitigates drifting by modeling the distribution of correlation response within a Bayesian optimization framework. OCT leverages the assumption that the correlation response to the target image follows a Gaussian distribution, using this information to select training samples and reduce model uncertainty. OCT is grounded in a novel theory that transfers data distribution to a constraint on the optimized variable, resulting in an efficient framework for calculating correlation filters. Extensive experiments on a widely used tracking benchmark show that OCT significantly enhances KCF and surpasses other state-of-the-art trackers. To encourage further development, the source code is available at https://github.com/bczhangbczhang/OCT-KCF.
label: AI

title: Learning Residual Images for Face Attribute Manipulation
Abstract: Face attributes are intriguing due to their detailed description of human faces. Unlike existing attribute prediction research, we address the inverse and more challenging problem of face attribute manipulation, aiming to modify a face image according to a given attribute value. Instead of manipulating the entire image, we propose learning the corresponding residual image, defined as the difference between images before and after manipulation. This approach allows for efficient manipulation with minimal pixel modification. Our framework is based on the Generative Adversarial Network, consisting of two image transformation networks and a discriminative network. The transformation networks handle attribute manipulation and its dual operation, while the discriminative network distinguishes generated images from real images. We employ dual learning, enabling transformation networks to learn from each other. Experiments demonstrate that residual images can be effectively learned and used for attribute manipulations, with generated images preserving most details in attribute-irrelevant areas.
label: AI

title: Medical Image Synthesis with Context-Aware Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is essential for various clinical applications, including radiotherapy treatment planning and PET attenuation correction. However, CT acquisition exposes patients to radiation, potentially causing side effects. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in contrast, is much safer and radiation-free. This has prompted researchers to explore methods for estimating CT images from corresponding MR images of the same subject, particularly for radiotherapy planning. This paper presents a data-driven approach to address this challenge. We train a fully convolutional network to generate CT images from MR images. To better model the nonlinear relationship between MRI and CT and produce more realistic images, we incorporate adversarial training and an image gradient difference loss function. We further enhance the network with an AutoContext Model, implementing a context-aware generative adversarial network. Experimental results demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of our method for predicting CT images from MRI images, surpassing three state-of-the-art methods under comparison.
label: AI

title: FusionNet: A deep fully residual convolutional neural network for image segmentation in connectomics
Abstract: Electron microscopic connectomics aims to map comprehensive brain connectivity by using high-throughput, nano-scale microscopy. A major challenge in connectomics research is developing scalable image analysis algorithms that require minimal user intervention. Deep learning has emerged as a promising solution for this challenge, due to its exceptional performance in image classification tasks. This paper introduces FusionNet, a novel deep neural network architecture for automatic segmentation of neuronal structures in connectomics data. FusionNet leverages recent advancements in machine learning, such as semantic segmentation and residual neural networks, incorporating summation-based skip connections to enable a deeper network architecture for more accurate segmentation. We demonstrate the performance of our approach by comparing it to state-of-the-art electron microscopy (EM) segmentation methods from the ISBI EM segmentation challenge. Additionally, we present segmentation results on two distinct tasks, cell membrane and cell body segmentation, and conduct a statistical analysis of cell morphology.
label: AI

title: Machine Reading with Background Knowledge
Abstract: Intelligent systems capable of automatically understanding natural language text are crucial for numerous artificial intelligence applications, including mobile phone voice assistants, computer vision, and robotics. Language understanding often involves integrating new information into a previously acquired world view. However, many machine reading systems rely solely on text to infer meaning. This paper explores a different approach: machine reading methods that utilize background knowledge to facilitate language understanding. To this end, we introduce two methods. The first method addresses prepositional phrase attachment ambiguity by incorporating background knowledge within a semi-supervised machine learning algorithm that learns from both labeled and unlabeled data. This approach achieves state-of-the-art results on two datasets, outperforming strong baselines. The second method extracts relationships from compound nouns. Our knowledge-aware method for compound noun analysis accurately extracts relationships and significantly outperforms a baseline that does not utilize background knowledge.
label: AI

title: Mirrored Light Field Video Camera Adapter
Abstract: This paper proposes the design of a custom mirror-based light field camera adapter, characterized by its low cost, simple construction, and accessibility. Mirrors of varying shapes and orientations reflect the scene into an upwards-facing camera, creating an array of virtual cameras with overlapping fields of view at specific depths, delivering light fields at video frame rates. We describe the design, construction, decoding, and calibration processes of our mirror-based light field camera adapter, preparing it for open-source release to benefit the robotic vision community.
label: AI

title: Fast, Dense Feature SDM on an iPhone
Abstract: This paper presents a method for enabling dense SDM to run at over 90 FPS on a mobile device. Our contributions are two-fold. Inspired by the FFT, we propose a Sparse Compositional Regression (SCR) framework, which significantly accelerates computations compared to classical dense regressors. Secondly, we introduce Binary Approximated SIFT (BASIFT) features, a computationally efficient approximation to SIFT, a commonly used feature with SDM. We demonstrate the performance of our algorithm on an iPhone 7, achieving accuracy comparable to SDM.
label: AI

title: A Stochastic Large Deformation Model for Computational Anatomy
Abstract: In the study of human organ shapes using computational anatomy, variations arise from inter-subject anatomical differences, disease-specific effects, and measurement noise. This paper introduces a stochastic model for incorporating random variations into the Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping (LDDMM) framework. By accounting for randomness in a setup tailored to the geometric properties of LDDMM, we formulate the template estimation problem for landmarks with noise and present two methods for efficiently estimating the parameters of the noise fields from a given dataset. One method directly approximates the time evolution of the variance of each landmark using a finite set of differential equations, while the other relies on an Expectation-Maximization algorithm. In the second method, data likelihood evaluation is achieved without registering the landmarks by applying bridge sampling using a stochastically perturbed version of the large deformation gradient flow algorithm. The method and estimation algorithms are validated experimentally on synthetic examples and shape data of human corpora callosa.
label: AI

title: Towards a Deep Learning Framework for Unconstrained Face Detection
Abstract: Robust face detection is a crucial pre-processing step for supporting facial expression analysis, facial landmarking, face recognition, pose estimation, 3D facial model building, and other applications. Despite decades of research, face detection remains challenging due to the numerous variations in face images encountered in real-world scenarios. This paper introduces a novel approach, Multiple Scale Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (MS-FRCNN), for robustly detecting human facial regions from images captured under various challenging conditions, such as large occlusions, extremely low resolutions, facial expressions, strong illumination variations, etc. The proposed approach is benchmarked on two challenging face detection databases, the Wider Face database and the Face Detection Dataset and Benchmark (FDDB), and compared against recent face detection methods, including Two-stage CNN, Multi-scale Cascade CNN, Faceness, Aggregate Channel Features, HeadHunter, Multi-view Face Detection, Cascade CNN, etc. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach consistently achieves highly competitive results, outperforming other recent face detection methods.
label: AI

title: Visual Compiler: Synthesizing a Scene-Specific Pedestrian Detector and Pose Estimator
Abstract: We introduce the concept of a Visual Compiler, which generates a scene-specific pedestrian detector and pose estimator without requiring any pedestrian observations. Given a single image and auxiliary scene information, including camera parameters and geometric layout, the Visual Compiler first infers geometrically and photometrically accurate images of humans in that scene using computer graphics rendering. These renders are then used to learn a scene-and-region specific spatially-varying fully convolutional neural network for simultaneous detection, pose estimation, and segmentation of pedestrians. We demonstrate that in scenarios where real human annotated data is scarce or unavailable, our data generation strategy provides an effective solution for bootstrapping human detection and pose estimation. Experimental results show that our approach surpasses off-the-shelf state-of-the-art pedestrian detectors and pose estimators trained on real data.
label: AI

title: CSVideoNet: A Real-time End-to-end Learning Framework for High-frame-rate Video Compressive Sensing
Abstract: This paper tackles the real-time encoding-decoding problem for high-frame-rate video compressive sensing (CS). Unlike previous works that rely on iterative optimization-based reconstruction, we propose a non-iterative model, named "CSVideoNet". CSVideoNet directly learns the inverse mapping of CS and reconstructs the original input in a single forward propagation. To address the limitations of existing CS cameras, we introduce a multi-rate CNN and a synthesizing RNN to improve the trade-off between compression ratio (CR) and spatial-temporal resolution of the reconstructed videos. Experimental results show that CSVideoNet significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. Without pre/post-processing, we achieve 25dB PSNR recovery quality at 100x CR, with a frame rate of 125 fps on a Titan X GPU. Due to the feedforward and high-data-concurrency nature of CSVideoNet, it leverages GPU acceleration to achieve a three-order-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional iterative-based approaches. The source code is available at https://github.com/PSCLab-ASU/CSVideoNet.
label: AI

title: Coupling Adaptive Batch Sizes with Learning Rates
Abstract: Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent and its variants have become standard for large-scale empirical risk minimization, such as neural network training. These methods typically employ a constant batch size determined through empirical inspection. However, the batch size significantly influences the behavior of the stochastic optimization algorithm, impacting the variance of gradient estimates. This variance also changes throughout the optimization process, and using a constant batch size often necessitates manual tuning of a decreasing learning rate schedule to ensure stability and convergence. We propose a practical method for dynamic batch size adaptation. Our algorithm estimates the variance of stochastic gradients and adapts the batch size to decrease the variance proportionally to the objective function value, eliminating the need for a learning rate decrease. Unlike recent related work, our algorithm couples the batch size with the learning rate, reflecting the known relationship between the two. On popular image classification benchmarks, our batch size adaptation leads to faster optimization convergence while simplifying learning rate tuning. A TensorFlow implementation is available.
label: AI

title: SceneNet RGB-D: 5M Photorealistic Images of Synthetic Indoor Trajectories with Ground Truth
Abstract: We introduce SceneNet RGB-D, expanding upon the previous work of SceneNet to enable large-scale photorealistic rendering of indoor scene trajectories. It provides pixel-perfect ground truth for scene understanding problems, such as semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, object detection, and geometric computer vision problems like optical flow, depth estimation, camera pose estimation, and 3D reconstruction. Random sampling allows for virtually unlimited scene configurations, and we provide a set of 5M rendered RGB-D images from over 15K trajectories in synthetic layouts with randomized but physically simulated object poses. Each layout also features random lighting, camera trajectories, and textures. The dataset's scale is well-suited for pre-training data-driven computer vision techniques from scratch with RGB-D inputs, previously limited by relatively small labelled datasets in NYUv2 and SUN RGB-D. Additionally, it provides a basis for investigating 3D scene labelling tasks by offering perfect camera poses and depth data as a proxy for a SLAM system. The dataset is hosted at http://robotvault.bitbucket.io/scenenet-rgbd.html. |||
label: AI

title: Beyond Holistic Object Recognition: Enriching Image Understanding with Part States
Abstract: Inferring rich semantic descriptions of objects at part level is crucial for high-level vision tasks such as human-object interaction, image captioning, and robotic manipulation. Building upon previous work on part localization, this paper tackles the problem of inferring the semantic meaning conveyed by an object part in still images. The paper proposes a novel approach that tokenizes the semantic space as a discrete set of part states. This modeling of part state is spatially localized, allowing the part state inference problem to be formulated as a pixel-wise annotation problem. An iterative part-state inference neural network is specifically designed for this task, offering both efficiency in time and accuracy in performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in predicting the semantic states of parts and simultaneously correcting localization errors, benefiting various visual understanding applications. The paper also introduces a new part state dataset containing rich part-level semantic annotations.
label: AI

title: Reflectance Adaptive Filtering Improves Intrinsic Image Estimation
Abstract: Separating an image into its reflectance and shading layers is a challenging task for learning approaches due to the lack of large datasets containing precise and realistic ground truth decompositions. The Intrinsic Images in the Wild (IIW) dataset offers a sparse set of relative human reflectance judgments, serving as a standard benchmark for intrinsic images. Several methods utilize IIW to learn statistical dependencies between images and their reflectance layer. While learning is crucial for achieving high performance, this paper demonstrates that a standard signal processing technique can achieve comparable performance to current state-of-the-art methods. The paper proposes a loss function for CNN learning of dense reflectance predictions. The results show that a simple pixel-wise decision, without any context or prior knowledge, is sufficient to provide a strong baseline on IIW, surpassing all but two other approaches. Building upon this, the paper develops a joint bilateral filtering method that incorporates strong prior knowledge about reflectance constancy. This filtering operation can be applied to any intrinsic image algorithm, leading to improvements in several previous results and achieving a new state-of-the-art on IIW. These findings suggest that the impact of learning-based approaches might have been overestimated, highlighting the continued importance of explicit prior knowledge for high performance in intrinsic image decompositions.
label: AI

title: Towards Score Following in Sheet Music Images
Abstract: This paper presents a system for matching short music audio snippets to their corresponding pixel locations in images of sheet music. The system simultaneously learns to read notes, listen to music, and match the currently played music to its corresponding notes in the sheet. It consists of an end-to-end multi-modal convolutional neural network that takes as input images of sheet music and spectrograms of the respective audio snippets. The network learns to predict, for a given unseen audio snippet (covering approximately one bar of music), the corresponding position in the respective score line. The results suggest that the use of deep neural networks, known for their power in image processing, makes working with sheet music feasible and opens promising avenues for future research.
label: AI

title: Objective Micro-Facial Movement Detection Using FACS-Based Regions and Baseline Evaluation
Abstract: Micro-facial expressions, subtle movements that can signal emotional deception, are challenging to detect for both humans and machines. This paper proposes an individualized baseline micro-movement detection method using a 3D Histogram of Oriented Gradients (3D HOG) temporal difference method. The method defines a face template consisting of 26 regions based on the Facial Action Coding System (FACS). Temporal features are extracted from each region using 3D HOG. The Chi-square distance is then employed to identify subtle facial motion in the local regions. Finally, an automatic peak detector is used to detect micro-movements exceeding a newly proposed adaptive baseline threshold. The performance of the method is evaluated on two FACS coded datasets: SAMM and CASME II. This objective method focuses on the movement of the 26 face regions. When compared to the ground truth, the method achieves an AUC of 0.7512 and 0.7261 on SAMM and CASME II, respectively. The results demonstrate that 3D HOG outperforms state-of-the-art feature representations, such as Local Binary Patterns in Three Orthogonal Planes and Histograms of Oriented Optical Flow, for micro-movement detection.
label: AI

title: A Multilinear Tongue Model Derived from Speech Related MRI Data of the Human Vocal Tract
Abstract: This paper presents a multilinear statistical model of the human tongue that captures anatomical and tongue pose-related shape variations separately. The model is derived from 3D magnetic resonance imaging data of 11 speakers sustaining speech-related vocal tract configurations. Extraction is performed using a minimally supervised method that leverages an image segmentation approach and a template fitting technique. Additionally, the method incorporates image denoising to handle potentially corrupt data, palate surface information reconstruction to address palatal tongue contacts, and a bootstrap strategy to refine the obtained shapes. Evaluation concludes that limiting the degrees of freedom for anatomical and speech-related variations to 5 and 4, respectively, results in a model that can reliably register unknown data while avoiding overfitting effects. The model can be used to generate plausible tongue animation by tracking sparse motion capture data.
label: AI

title: Development of a Real-time Colorectal Tumor Classification System for Narrow-band Imaging zoom-videoendoscopy
Abstract: Colorectal endoscopy, essential for the early detection and treatment of colorectal cancer, is widely used worldwide. A computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system that provides objective measures to endoscopists during colorectal endoscopic examinations would be highly beneficial. This study presents a newly developed CAD system that offers real-time objective measures. The system captures the video stream from an endoscopic system and transmits it to a desktop computer. The captured video stream is then classified by a pretrained classifier, and the results are displayed on a monitor. Experimental results demonstrate the system's efficient operation in actual endoscopic examinations, highlighting its medical significance.
label: AI

title: Design of Image Matched Non-Separable Wavelet using Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: Image-matched nonseparable wavelets have potential applications in areas like image classification, segmentation, compressive sensing, and more. This paper introduces a novel design methodology utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to design two-channel nonseparable wavelets matched to a given image. The design is proposed on a quincunx lattice. The CNN's loss function is set up to minimize the total squared error between the given input image and the reconstructed image at the output of the CNN, resulting in perfect reconstruction at the end of training. Simulation results are presented on some standard images.
label: AI

title: Cloud Dictionary: Sparse Coding and Modeling for Point Clouds
Abstract: With the advent of range sensors like LIDAR and time-of-flight cameras, 3D point cloud scans have become ubiquitous in computer vision applications, notably gesture recognition and autonomous driving. Parsimony-based algorithms have proven successful on images and videos where data points are sampled on a regular Cartesian grid. This paper proposes an adaptation of these techniques to irregularly sampled signals by employing continuous dictionaries. An example application in the form of point cloud denoising is presented.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Image Captioner: Describing Images with Spatial-Invariant Transformation and Attention Filtering
Abstract: Image captioning, also known as image description, has made significant advancements in recent years thanks to the development of recurrent neural networks for modeling sequential data and the power of the attention mechanism in automatically identifying salient information. However, most existing paradigms face limitations in their invariance to images with different scaling, rotation, etc., and the effective integration of standalone attention into a holistic end-to-end system. This paper proposes a novel image captioning architecture, termed Recurrent Image Captioner (RIC), which enables visual encoder and language decoder to cooperate coherently in a recurrent manner. Specifically, the paper equips the CNN-based visual encoder with a differentiable layer to facilitate spatially invariant transformation of visual signals. Furthermore, an attention filter module (differentiable) is deployed between encoder and decoder to dynamically determine salient visual parts. The paper also utilizes bidirectional LSTM to preprocess sentences for generating better textual representations. Moreover, variational inference is employed to optimize the entire architecture. Extensive experimental results on three benchmark datasets (Flickr8k, Flickr30k, and MS COCO) demonstrate the superiority of the proposed architecture compared to most state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Regressing Robust and Discriminative 3D Morphable Models with a very Deep Neural Network
Abstract: The 3D shapes of faces are known to be discriminative. However, they are rarely used for face recognition and typically under controlled viewing conditions. This paper argues that this is due to a significant but often overlooked problem with existing methods for single-view 3D face reconstruction: when applied in real-world scenarios, their 3D estimates are either unstable and change for different photos of the same subject or over-regularized and generic. In response, the paper describes a robust method for regressing discriminative 3D morphable face models (3DMM). A convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to regress 3DMM shape and texture parameters directly from an input photo. The paper addresses the shortage of training data required for this purpose by offering a method for generating a vast number of labeled examples. The 3D estimates produced by the CNN surpass state-of-the-art accuracy on the MICC dataset. When coupled with a 3D-3D face matching pipeline, the paper presents the first competitive face recognition results on the LFW, YTF, and IJB-A benchmarks using 3D face shapes as representations, rather than the opaque deep feature vectors used by other modern systems.
label: AI

title: Tinkering Under the Hood: Interactive Zero-Shot Learning with Net Surgery
Abstract: This paper explores the task of visual net surgery, where a CNN can be reconfigured without additional data to recognize novel concepts that may be omitted from the training set. While most prior work utilizes linguistic cues for this "zero-shot" learning, this paper uses a pictorial language representation of the training set, implicitly learned by a CNN, to generalize to new classes. The paper introduces a set of visualization techniques that reveal the activation patterns and relationships between groups of CNN filters. It demonstrates that knowledge of pictorial languages can be used to rewire certain CNN neurons into a part model, called a pictorial language classifier (PLC). The paper highlights the robustness of simple PLCs by applying them in a weakly supervised manner: labeling unlabeled concepts for visual classes present in the training data. Specifically, the paper shows that a PLC built on top of a CNN trained for ImageNet classification can localize humans in Graz-02 and determine the pose of birds in PASCAL-VOC without additional labeled data or training. The paper then applies PLCs in an interactive zero-shot manner, demonstrating that pictorial languages are expressive enough to detect a set of visual classes in MS-COCO that never appear in the ImageNet training set.
label: AI

title: Deep learning is effective for the classification of OCT images of normal versus Age-related Macular Degeneration
Abstract: The advent of Electronic Medical Records (EMR) with large electronic imaging databases, combined with advances in deep neural networks and machine learning, has presented a unique opportunity for achieving milestones in automated image analysis. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the most commonly obtained imaging modality in ophthalmology, representing a dense and rich dataset when combined with labels derived from the EMR. This study sought to determine if deep learning could be utilized to distinguish normal OCT images from images from patients with Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD). Automated extraction of an OCT imaging database was linked to clinical endpoints from the EMR. OCT macula scans were obtained using Heidelberg Spectralis, and each OCT scan was linked to EMR clinical endpoints extracted from EPIC. The central 11 images were selected from each OCT scan of two cohorts of patients: normal and AMD. Cross-validation was performed using a random subset of patients. Area under receiver operator curves (auROC) were constructed at an independent image level, macular OCT level, and patient level. Of an extraction of 2.6 million OCT images linked to clinical datapoints from the EMR, 52,690 normal and 48,312 AMD macular OCT images were selected. A deep neural network was trained to categorize images as either normal or AMD. At the image level, an auROC of 92.78% with an accuracy of 87.63% was achieved. At the macula level, an auROC of 93.83% with an accuracy of 88.98% was achieved. At a patient level, an auROC of 97.45% with an accuracy of 93.45% was achieved. Peak sensitivity and specificity with optimal cutoffs were 92.64% and 93.69%, respectively. Deep learning techniques are effective for classifying OCT images, with implications for utilizing OCT in automated screening and computer-aided diagnosis tools.
label: AI

title: Scale Coding Bag of Deep Features for Human Attribute and Action Recognition
Abstract: Most approaches to human attribute and action recognition in still images rely on image representation where multi-scale local features are pooled across scales into a single, scale-invariant encoding. Both bag-of-words and the recently popular representations based on convolutional neural networks compute local features at multiple scales. However, these multi-scale convolutional features are pooled into a single scale-invariant representation. This paper argues that entirely scale-invariant image representations are sub-optimal and investigates approaches to scale coding within a Bag of Deep Features framework. The proposed approach explicitly encodes multi-scale information during the image encoding stage. Two strategies are introduced to explicitly encode multi-scale information in the final image representation.
