These techniques are validated on five datasets: Willow, PASCAL VOC 2010, PASCAL VOC 2012, Stanford-40, and Human Attributes (HAT-27). On all datasets, the proposed scale coding approaches outperform both the scale-invariant method and the standard deep features of the same network. Furthermore, combining these scale coding approaches with standard deep features consistently improves upon the state-of-the-art.
label: AI

title: Border-Peeling Clustering
Abstract: This paper presents a novel non-parametric clustering technique based on the concept that each latent cluster is composed of layers surrounding its core, where the external layers, or border points, implicitly separate the clusters. Unlike previous techniques, such as DBSCAN, where cluster cores are defined directly by their densities, this method reveals latent cores through a progressive peeling of border points. Analyzing the density of local neighborhoods allows identifying border points and associating them with points of inner layers. The peeling process adapts to local densities and characteristics to successfully separate adjacent clusters of potentially different densities. Extensive testing on large sets of labeled data, including high-dimensional datasets of deep features trained by a convolutional neural network, demonstrates the technique's competitiveness with other state-of-the-art non-parametric methods using a fixed set of parameters throughout the experiments.
label: AI

title: Temporal-Needle: A view and appearance invariant video descriptor
Abstract: The ability to detect similar actions across videos is highly beneficial for real-world applications in various fields. However, this task remains challenging for existing systems, as videos presenting the same action can be captured from significantly different viewing directions, performed by different actors and backgrounds, and under varying video qualities. Video descriptors play a crucial role in these systems. This work proposes the "temporal-needle" descriptor, which captures dynamic behavior while being invariant to viewpoint and appearance. The descriptor is computed using multiple temporal scales of the video and by computing self-similarity for every patch through time at each temporal scale. It is computed for every pixel in the video. However, to find similar actions across videos, only a small subset of statistically significant descriptors is considered, leading to more efficient identification of correspondences across videos. The descriptor allows for detecting the same behavior across videos in various scenarios. The paper demonstrates its use in tasks such as temporal and spatial alignment, action detection, and showcases its potential for unsupervised video clustering into categories. While this work focuses on videos captured with stationary cameras, the descriptor can be extended to handle moving cameras as well.
label: AI

title: The More You Know: Using Knowledge Graphs for Image Classification
Abstract: Humans possess the remarkable ability to acquire knowledge about the world and utilize that knowledge to reason about the visual world, a characteristic that sets them apart from modern learning-based computer vision algorithms. Humans can learn about the characteristics of objects and their relationships to acquire a wide variety of visual concepts, often with limited examples. This paper investigates the use of structured prior knowledge in the form of knowledge graphs and shows that incorporating this knowledge improves performance on image classification. Building upon recent work on end-to-end learning on graphs, the paper introduces the Graph Search Neural Network as an efficient method for integrating large knowledge graphs into a vision classification pipeline. Several experiments demonstrate that this method outperforms standard neural network baselines for multi-label classification.
label: AI

title: Fast-AT: Fast Automatic Thumbnail Generation using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Fast-AT is an automatic thumbnail generation system based on deep neural networks. It is a fully convolutional deep neural network that learns specific filters for thumbnails of different sizes and aspect ratios. During inference, the appropriate filter is selected based on the target thumbnail's dimensions. Unlike most previous work, Fast-AT does not rely on saliency but addresses the problem directly. It also eliminates the need for region search on the saliency map. The model generalizes to thumbnails of various sizes, including those with extreme aspect ratios, and can generate thumbnails in real-time. A dataset of over 70,000 thumbnail annotations was collected to train Fast-AT. The paper presents competitive results compared to existing techniques.
label: AI

title: Spectral video construction from RGB video: Application to Image Guided Neurosurgery
Abstract: Spectral imaging has gained significant interest in the field of medical imaging modalities. It provides a powerful tool for analyzing different organs and non-invasive tissues. As a result, extensive research has been conducted to explore its potential in biomedical applications. Observing spectral image information in real-time during surgery and monitoring temporal changes in organs and tissues is a demanding task. Current spectral imaging devices are insufficient for this task, lacking the required spatial and spectral resolution. A solution is to estimate the spectral video from RGB video and perform visualization using the most prominent spectral bands. This research proposes a framework for generating neurosurgery spectral video from RGB video. A spectral estimation technique is applied to each RGB video frame. The RGB video is captured using a digital camera connected to an operational microscope dedicated to neurosurgery. A database of neurosurgery spectral images is used to collect training data and evaluate the estimation accuracy. A searching technique identifies the best training set. Five different spectrum estimation techniques are experimented to identify the best method. While this framework is specifically developed for neurosurgery spectral video generation, the methodology outlined here is applicable to other similar research.
label: AI

title: Deep Function Machines: Generalized Neural Networks for Topological Layer Expression
Abstract: This paper proposes a generalization of deep neural networks called deep function machines (DFMs). DFMs operate on vector spaces of arbitrary (possibly infinite) dimension, and the paper shows that a family of DFMs is invariant to the dimension of input data; that is, the model's parameterization does not directly depend on the quality of the input (e.g., high-resolution images). This generalization leads to a new theory of universal approximation of bounded non-linear operators between function spaces. The paper suggests that DFMs provide an expressive framework for designing new neural network layer types with topological considerations. Finally, the paper introduces a novel architecture, RippLeNet, for resolution invariant computer vision, empirically achieving state-of-the-art invariance.
label: AI

title: Registering large volume serial-section electron microscopy image sets for neural circuit reconstruction using FFT signal whitening
Abstract: The detailed reconstruction of neural anatomy for connectomics studies requires a combination of high resolution and large three-dimensional data capture, provided by serial section electron microscopy (ssEM). Recent advancements in high-throughput ssEM imaging and improved tissue preparation methods now enable ssEM capture of complete specimen volumes up to cubic millimeter scale. The resulting multi-terabyte image sets span thousands of serial sections and must be precisely registered into coherent volumetric forms to trace and segment neural circuits. This paper introduces a Signal Whitening Fourier Transform Image Registration approach (SWiFT-IR) developed at the Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center and its application to align mouse and zebrafish brain datasets acquired using the wafer mapper ssEM imaging technology developed at Harvard University. Unlike other methods currently used for ssEM registration, SWiFT-IR modifies its spatial frequency response during image matching to maximize a signal-to-noise measure, serving as its primary indicator of alignment quality. This alignment signal is more robust to rapid variations in biological content and unavoidable data distortions than phase-only or standard Pearson correlation, enabling more precise alignment and statistical confidence. These improvements enable an iterative registration procedure based on projections through multiple sections rather than typical adjacent-pair matching methods. This projection approach, combined with known anatomical constraints and applied iteratively in a multi-resolution pyramid fashion, drives the alignment into a smooth form that accurately represents complex and widely varying anatomical content, such as full cross-section zebrafish data. |||
label: AI

title: Beam Search for Learning a Deep Convolutional Neural Network of 3D Shapes
Abstract: This paper presents a new approach for 3D shape recognition that addresses the challenge of limited training datasets. Instead of relying on ad hoc strategies, it formulates CNN learning as a beam search, aiming to find an optimal CNN architecture. By efficiently transferring parameter values between CNNs, the beam search effectively explores candidate architectures, resulting in a CNN that surpasses state-of-the-art performance on the ModelNet dataset.
label: AI

title: Detect, Replace, Refine: Deep Structured Prediction For Pixel Wise Labeling
Abstract: Pixel-wise image labeling poses a significant challenge due to the complex dependencies between input and output variables. Existing approaches, directly predicting labels or residual corrections, fall short. This paper proposes a novel architecture that decomposes the task into three steps: detection, replacement, and refinement. By employing this architecture, the proposed dense disparity estimation network achieves state-of-the-art results on the KITTI 2015 test dataset, outperforming prior methods by a significant margin.
label: AI

title: Attentive Explanations: Justifying Decisions and Pointing to the Evidence
Abstract: Deep models excel in visual decision-making but lack explainability. This paper introduces the Pointing and Justification (PJ-X) model, which provides natural language explanations and points to visual evidence for its decisions using an attention mechanism. Due to the absence of datasets with reference explanations, the authors collect two datasets: one for visual question answering with explanations and another for explaining human activities. The PJ-X model demonstrates promising performance on both justification and pointing tasks, outperforming prior models and ablations through both automatic and human evaluations.
label: AI

title: Super-resolution Reconstruction of SAR Image based on Non-Local Means Denoising Combined with BP Neural Network
Abstract: This paper presents a super-resolution method using back-propagation neural networks (BPNN) to overcome limitations of imaging devices in capturing high spatial resolution. The method utilizes Non-local means (NL-Means) and incorporates similar pixels as inputs to the BPNN, leveraging the self-similarity of images. Experimental results, evaluated using Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Equivalent Number of Look (ENL), show that incorporating similar pixels significantly enhances image quality.
label: AI

title: Linear feature detection algorithm for astronomical surveys - I. Algorithm description
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for detecting linear features in astronomical images, specifically designed for Big Data applications. The algorithm first removes stars and galaxies, enhances the lines, and employs a Hough algorithm for line detection. A false positive reduction step compares lines fitted to rectangles with those obtained directly from the image, enhancing accuracy. The algorithm's efficiency and applicability in astronomical surveys are discussed.
label: AI

title: Efficient phase retrieval based on dark fringe recognition with an ability of bypassing invalid fringes
Abstract: This paper tackles the noisy phase retrieval problem, aiming to recover a complex image signal from quadratic measurements. Inspired by dark fringes in measured images, the proposed approach recognizes and bypasses invalid fringes. By calculating multiplicative ratios between pixels, a more accurate relative phase ratio is achieved. The object phase image is then reconstructed with high precision, offering potential applications in X-ray crystallography, diffractive imaging, and more.
label: AI

title: UnrealStereo: Controlling Hazardous Factors to Analyze Stereo Vision
Abstract: Reliable stereo algorithms are essential for robotics, but textureless and specular regions pose a significant challenge. This paper introduces a synthetic image generation tool that enables controlled creation of hazardous regions. The tool utilizes a game engine (Unreal Engine 4) to produce a large dataset with automatically computed hazardous regions, allowing for rigorous testing of stereo algorithms. Observations from synthetic images are validated on real-world datasets like Middlebury and KITTI, providing a comprehensive evaluation framework.
label: AI

title: Harmonic Networks: Deep Translation and Rotation Equivariance
Abstract: This paper introduces Harmonic Networks (H-Nets), a novel CNN architecture that exhibits equivariance to both patch-wise translation and 360-degree rotation. By replacing regular filters with circular harmonics, H-Nets achieve this equivariance while maintaining a parameter-efficient and computationally efficient representation. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of H-Nets in achieving state-of-the-art classification on rotated-MNIST and competitive results on other benchmark challenges.
label: AI

title: Defining the Pose of any 3D Rigid Object and an Associated Distance
Abstract: This paper redefines pose as a distinguishable static state of an object, considering its symmetries. A frame-invariant metric is proposed for the pose space, valid for any rigid object and requiring no tuning. This metric is efficiently evaluated using a representation in a 12-dimensional Euclidean space. The practicality of this approach is demonstrated through an application of pose estimation using a Mean Shift procedure.
label: AI

title: Jamming in a lattice model of stochastically interacting agents with a field of view
Abstract: This paper studies the collective dynamics of interacting agents on a lattice with a weighted field of vision. The stochasticity of the system arises from agent interactions and is dependent on local density. The paper shows that this system exhibits a first-order jamming transition even at low densities. Furthermore, the critical jamming density is found to be strongly influenced by the field of vision.
label: AI

title: The Mehler-Fock Transform and some Applications in Texture Analysis and Color Processing
Abstract: This paper explores the application of harmonic analysis to investigate probability density functions on groups and homogeneous spaces, focusing on the Lorentz group SU(1,1) and the unit disk with hyperbolic geometry. The Mehler-Fock transform, the radial part of the Fourier transform on the disk, is highlighted, discussing its properties and applications in signal processing. Examples from low-level vision and color image processing illustrate the theory.
label: AI

title: Permutation-equivariant neural networks applied to dynamics prediction
Abstract: Convolutional layers excel at learning translation-invariant operations in image tasks. This paper introduces a permutation-invariant neural network layer analogous to convolutional layers, addressing the problem of learning operations invariant to input order in tasks with multiple entities. The paper demonstrates the layer's ability to predict the motion of interacting hard discs in 2D, highlighting its generalization to different numbers of objects.
label: AI

title: Astronomical image reconstruction with convolutional neural networks
Abstract: State-of-the-art methods in astronomical image reconstruction rely on computationally expensive optimization techniques. This paper explores the use of convolutional neural networks for image reconstruction, offering a computationally efficient and interpretable alternative. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the neural network approach is competitive with other state-of-the-art methods while maintaining linear complexity per pixel.
label: AI

title: Single Image Action Recognition using Semantic Body Part Actions
Abstract: This paper presents a novel single-image action recognition algorithm based on semantic body part actions. Unlike existing bottom-up methods, this approach divides the human body into parts and defines semantic actions for each part, leveraging their strong relationship to body actions. The proposed system utilizes a deep neural network to localize body parts, predict semantic part actions, and fuse them to recognize the entire body action. Experimental results on PASCAL VOC 2012 and Stanford-40 datasets demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Sparse Factorization Layers for Neural Networks with Limited Supervision
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) require vast amounts of labeled data, while dictionary learning, though effective at low-level tasks, struggles to scale. This paper introduces two new network layers based on dictionary learning: a sparse factorization layer and a convolutional sparse factorization layer. These layers can be incorporated into existing CNNs, trained end-to-end, and leverage semi-supervision. Experimental results show that networks with these layers outperform classical CNNs when labeled data is scarce and demonstrate performance improvements in certain tasks compared to CNNs without sparse factorization layers.
label: AI

title: Analysis of proposed PDE-based underwater image enhancement algorithms
Abstract: This paper presents an experimental analysis of underwater image enhancement algorithms based on partial differential equations (PDEs). The algorithms combine smoothing and enhancement processes within a unified framework, allowing for the incorporation of contrast enhancement algorithms like CLAHE. The CLAHE clip limit parameter is dynamically computed to control local enhancement, reducing noisy artifacts. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of these algorithms in performing illumination correction, color enhancement, contrast enhancement, and noise suppression, surpassing conventional approaches.
label: AI

title: Disentangling Space and Time in Video with Hierarchical Variational Auto-encoders
Abstract: This paper proposes a probabilistic approach for learning separable representations of object identity and pose information from unsupervised video data. The method leverages a deep generative model with a factored prior distribution that encodes temporal invariances in the hidden feature set. Learning is achieved through variational inference. Results on datasets of moving characters and rotating 3D objects demonstrate the model's ability to factor representations and achieve improved performance in transfer learning tasks.
label: AI

title: Finding Tiny Faces
Abstract: Detecting small objects remains a significant challenge in object recognition. This paper focuses on finding small faces and explores the roles of scale invariance, image resolution, and contextual reasoning. By training separate detectors for different scales and utilizing multi-task learning, the approach effectively addresses the challenges of recognizing small objects. The paper highlights the importance of context and introduces templates with large receptive fields. Furthermore, it explores ways to extrapolate networks tuned for limited scales to extreme ranges. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on face datasets like FDDB and WIDER FACE, significantly reducing errors compared to prior art.
label: AI

title: Multi-Dimensional Convergence in Future 5G Networks
Abstract: Future 5G services require high data rates, ubiquitous availability, low latency, and high reliability. The paper argues that a fragmented network view is inadequate and proposes a vision based on network convergence and application-centric approaches. It explores the expected 5G network requirements and examines ongoing standardization efforts. The paper introduces a novel interpretation of multi-dimensional convergence, leading to the exploration of node consolidation, converged network architectures, and optical-wireless integration. It discusses the role of ownership models and SDN in realizing the 5G vision and emphasizes the need for new business models aligned with the application-centric view.
label: AI

title: Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (SGAN), a novel generative model trained to invert the hierarchical representations of a bottom-up discriminative network. The model consists of a stack of GANs, each generating lower-level representations conditioned on higher-level ones. A representation discriminator is introduced at each hierarchy, guiding the generator's representation manifold to align with the discriminative network. The paper also introduces a conditional loss and an entropy loss to enhance the generative process. By training each stack independently and then end-to-end, SGAN demonstrates significant improvements in image quality compared to traditional GANs. |||
label: AI

title: Fast Patch-based Style Transfer of Arbitrary Style
Abstract: Artistic style transfer aims to reproduce the content of one image with the style of another. Existing methods either rely on expensive optimization procedures for any style image or efficient feedforward networks that only allow a limited number of pre-trained styles. This paper proposes a simpler optimization objective based on local matching, combining content structure and style textures in a single layer of the pretrained network. This approach exhibits desirable characteristics, including a simpler optimization landscape, intuitive parameter tuning, and consistent frame-by-frame performance on video. Furthermore, the paper trains an inverse network using 80,000 natural images and 80,000 paintings to approximate the optimization result, leading to an efficient artistic style transfer procedure that accommodates arbitrary content and style images.
label: AI

title: How do people explore virtual environments?
Abstract: Understanding how users explore immersive virtual environments is crucial for various applications, including virtual reality content design, compression algorithm development, and computational models of saliency and visual attention. While recent research has focused on modeling saliency in desktop viewing conditions, VR presents unique challenges due to stereoscopic vision and the complex interplay of head orientation, gaze, and kinematic constraints. To gain a deeper understanding of viewing behavior and saliency in VR, this study captured and analyzed gaze and head orientation data from 169 users exploring stereoscopic, static omni-directional panoramas, resulting in 1980 head and gaze trajectories across three different viewing conditions. The analysis reveals several important insights, including the existence of a specific fixation bias, which is utilized to adapt existing saliency predictors to immersive VR conditions. The data and analysis are further explored for other applications, including automatic alignment of VR video cuts, panorama thumbnails, panorama video synopsis, and saliency-based compression.
label: AI

title: Compressive Image Recovery Using Recurrent Generative Model
Abstract: Reconstructing signals from compressively sensed measurements is an ill-posed problem. This paper leverages the recurrent generative model, RIDE, as an image prior for compressive image reconstruction. Recurrent networks excel at modeling long-range dependencies in images, making them suitable for handling global multiplexing in reconstruction from compressive imaging. The paper performs MAP inference with RIDE using back-propagation to the inputs and the projected gradient method. To preserve texture in images effectively, an entropy thresholding based approach is introduced. The proposed approach demonstrates superior reconstructions compared to recent global reconstruction methods like D-AMP and TVAL3 on both simulated and real data.
label: AI

title: Observation of dynamics inside an unlabeled live cell using bright-field photon microscopy: Evaluation of organelles' trajectories
Abstract: This article presents an algorithm for evaluating organelle movements within unmodified live cells. Using a time-lapse image series obtained through wide-field bright-field photon transmission microscopy as input, the algorithm leverages the Rényi information entropy, specifically a variable called point information gain, to highlight intracellular organelle borders and localize their centers of mass with one-pixel precision.
label: AI

title: Spatial Pyramid Convolutional Neural Network for Social Event Detection in Static Image
Abstract: Social event detection in static images is a challenging yet valuable problem for various Internet of Things applications, including automatic photo organization, ads recommender systems, and image captioning. However, the presence of diverse objects, scenes, and people can make it ambiguous for systems to accurately determine the event depicted in an image. This paper proposes a spatial pyramid configuration of a convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier for social event detection in static images. By applying the spatial pyramid configuration to the CNN classifier, the classifier can observe image details more accurately. The USED dataset, consisting of two image sets (EiMM and SED), is utilized to evaluate the proposed method. The average accuracy of the system outperforms the baseline method by 15% and 2%, respectively.
label: AI

title: Learning to Hash-tag Videos with Tag2Vec
Abstract: User-provided tags or labels are valuable resources for semantic understanding of visual media, such as images and videos. Recently, hash-tags have gained significant popularity as a labeling mechanism on social media platforms. This paper investigates the problem of generating relevant and useful hash-tags for short video clips. While traditional data-driven approaches for tag enrichment and recommendation rely on direct visual similarity for label transfer and propagation, this paper proposes a direct, low-cost mapping from video to hash-tags using a two-step training process. First, a natural language processing (NLP) technique, skip-gram models with neural network training, is employed to learn a low-dimensional vector representation of hash-tags (Tag2Vec) using a corpus of 10 million hash-tags. Subsequently, an embedding function is trained to map video features to the low-dimensional Tag2vec space. This embedding is learned for 29 categories of short video clips with hash-tags. A query video without tag information can then be directly mapped to the vector space of tags using the learned embedding, and relevant tags can be retrieved through a simple nearest-neighbor search in the Tag2Vec space. The relevance of the suggested tags is validated qualitatively and quantitatively through a user study.
label: AI

title: Theory and Tools for the Conversion of Analog to Spiking Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown great potential in numerous real-world machine learning applications, but real-time inference in large CNNs remains a challenge. Previous work demonstrated that traditional CNNs can be converted into deep spiking neural networks (SNNs), achieving comparable accuracy while reducing latency and computational load due to their data-driven, event-based computing style. This paper provides a novel theory explaining the success of this conversion and derives several new tools for converting a larger and more powerful class of deep networks into SNNs. The paper identifies the main sources of approximation errors in previous conversion methods and proposes simple mechanisms to address these issues. Furthermore, the paper develops spiking implementations of common CNN operations, such as max-pooling, softmax, and batch-normalization, enabling almost loss-less conversion of arbitrary CNN architectures into the spiking domain. Empirical evaluation on the MNIST and CIFAR10 benchmarks using different network architectures leads to the best SNN results reported to date.
label: AI

title: A Video-Based Method for Objectively Rating Ataxia
Abstract: Many movement disorders, such as Parkinson's disease and ataxia, are visually assessed by clinicians using numerical disease rating scales. These tests are subjective, time-consuming, and require professional administration, posing challenges in settings lacking specialists or inconsistent evaluations by different clinicians. This paper presents an automated method for quantifying the severity of motion impairment in patients with ataxia using video recordings. The method analyzes videos of the finger-to-nose test, a common movement task used to assess ataxia progression during routine clinical checkups. Using neural network-based pose estimation and optical flow techniques, the motion of the patient's hand is tracked in the video recording. Features describing motion qualities like speed and performance variation are extracted. A supervised learning model is trained using labels provided by an expert clinician to predict severity according to the Brief Ataxia Rating Scale (BARS). The system's performance, in terms of mean error and correlation, is comparable to ataxia specialists, and its predictions remain within the range of inter-rater variability. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using computer vision and machine learning to produce consistent and clinically useful measures of motor impairment.
label: AI

title: Deep Convolutional Poses for Human Interaction Recognition in Monocular Videos
Abstract: Human interaction recognition is a challenging problem in computer vision with numerous important applications. With the advancement of deep models for human pose estimation, this work aims to verify the effectiveness of using human pose for human interaction recognition in monocular videos. The paper proposes a five-step method: detecting each person in the scene, tracking them, retrieving the human pose, extracting pose-based features, and finally recognizing the interaction using a classifier. The Two-Person interaction dataset was used to develop this methodology. Using a whole-sequence evaluation approach, the method achieved an average accuracy of 87.56% across all interactions. While Yun et al. achieved 91.10% using the same dataset, their methodology relied on a depth sensor for interaction recognition. The methodology developed in this paper demonstrates that an RGB camera can be as effective as depth cameras for recognizing interactions between two persons, leveraging recent advancements in deep models for human pose estimation.
label: AI

title: Neural Networks with Manifold Learning for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
Abstract: Widespread outreach programs using remote retinal imaging have proven to decrease the risk of diabetic retinopathy, the leading cause of blindness in the US. However, manual verification of image quality and disease level grading by trained human graders remains a bottleneck, limited by the scarcity of these resources. Computer-aided diagnosis of retinal images has gained significant attention in the machine learning community. This paper introduces a set of neural networks for diabetic retinopathy classification of fundus retinal images. The efficiency of the proposed classifiers is evaluated in combination with preprocessing and augmentation steps on a sample dataset. Experimental results show that neural networks combined with image preprocessing can enhance classification accuracy on the dataset. Moreover, the proposed models are scalable and can be utilized in large-scale datasets for diabetic retinopathy detection. These models can facilitate diagnosis and accelerate the detection process.
label: AI

title: Autoencoder-based holographic image restoration
Abstract: This paper proposes a holographic image restoration method using an autoencoder, an artificial neural network. Holographic reconstructed images are often contaminated by direct light, conjugate light, and speckle noise, making discrimination challenging. The paper demonstrates the restoration of reconstructed images from holograms recording page data in holographic memory and QR codes using the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Understanding the Impact of Precision Quantization on the Accuracy and Energy of Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks are gaining popularity due to their ability to generate state-of-the-art results in various computer vision and machine learning applications. However, these networks have become increasingly deep and complex to address challenging problems. Given the limitations in power budgets dedicated to these networks, low-power, low-memory solutions have gained importance in recent years. While numerous dedicated hardware solutions using different precisions have been proposed, a comprehensive study of different bit precisions and arithmetic in both inputs and network parameters is lacking. This work addresses this gap and performs a study of different bit-precisions in neural networks, ranging from floating-point to fixed-point, powers of two, and binary. The evaluation considers and analyzes the effect of precision scaling on both network accuracy and hardware metrics, including memory footprint, power and energy consumption, and design area. The paper also investigates training-time methodologies to compensate for accuracy reduction due to limited bit precision, demonstrating that precision scaling can deliver significant benefits in design metrics at the cost of modest decreases in network accuracy. Additionally, the paper proposes forfeiting a small portion of the benefits achieved with lower precisions to increase network size and accuracy. Experiments using three well-recognized networks and datasets demonstrate the generality of the findings. The trade-offs and benefits of using lower precisions in terms of energy and memory footprint are highlighted.
label: AI

title: Paying More Attention to Attention: Improving the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks via Attention Transfer
Abstract: Attention plays a crucial role in human visual experience. Recent research has demonstrated that attention can also significantly impact the performance of artificial neural networks in various tasks, such as computer vision and NLP. This paper shows that by defining attention for convolutional neural networks, a student CNN network's performance can be significantly improved by forcing it to mimic the attention maps of a powerful teacher network. Several novel methods for transferring attention are proposed, demonstrating consistent improvement across various datasets and convolutional neural network architectures. Code and models for the experiments are available at https://github.com/szagoruyko/attention-transfer.
label: AI

title: 3D fully convolutional networks for subcortical segmentation in MRI: A large-scale study
Abstract: This study investigates a 3D fully convolutional neural network (CNN) for subcortical brain structure segmentation in MRI. 3D CNN architectures have been generally avoided due to their computational and memory requirements during inference. This paper addresses the problem using small kernels, allowing for deeper architectures. The model incorporates both local and global context by embedding intermediate-layer outputs in the final prediction, encouraging consistency between features extracted at different scales and embedding fine-grained information directly in the segmentation process. The model is efficiently trained end-to-end on a graphics processing unit (GPU) in a single stage, leveraging the dense inference capabilities of fully CNNs. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on two publicly available datasets. First, the paper demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on the ISBR dataset. Then, a large-scale multi-site evaluation is performed over 1112 unregistered subject datasets acquired from 17 different sites (ABIDE dataset), with ages ranging from 7 to 64 years. The results show that the method is robust to various acquisition protocols, demographics, and clinical factors. The segmentations generated are highly consistent with a standard atlas-based approach while running significantly faster and avoiding registration/normalization steps, making it convenient for massive multi-site neuroanatomical imaging studies. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study of subcortical structure segmentation on such large-scale and heterogeneous data.
label: AI

title: Deep Supervised Hashing with Triplet Labels
Abstract: Hashing is a popular and powerful approximate nearest neighbor search technique for large-scale image retrieval. Most traditional hashing methods first represent images using off-the-shelf visual features and then produce hashing codes in a separate stage. However, off-the-shelf visual features may not be optimally compatible with the hash code learning procedure, leading to sub-optimal hash codes. Deep hashing methods have emerged to simultaneously learn image features and hash codes using deep neural networks, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional methods. While most deep hashing methods rely on supervised information in the form of pairwise labels or triplet labels, the state-of-the-art deep hashing method DPSH, based on pairwise labels, performs image feature learning and hash code learning simultaneously by maximizing the likelihood of pairwise similarities. Inspired by DPSH, this paper proposes a triplet label based deep hashing method that aims to maximize the likelihood of the given triplet labels. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms all baselines on CIFAR-10 and NUS-WIDE datasets, including the state-of-the-art DPSH and previous triplet label based deep hashing methods.
label: AI

title: Inverse Compositional Spatial Transformer Networks
Abstract: This paper establishes a theoretical connection between the classical Lucas & Kanade (LK) algorithm and Spatial Transformer Networks (STNs), which are gaining interest in the vision and learning communities due to their ability to combine alignment and classification within the same theoretical framework. Inspired by the Inverse Compositional (IC) variant of the LK algorithm, the paper presents Inverse Compositional Spatial Transformer Networks (IC-STNs). The paper demonstrates that IC-STNs can achieve better performance than conventional STNs with less model capacity, particularly showing superior performance in pure image alignment tasks and joint alignment/classification problems on real-world applications.
label: AI

title: Generalizable Features From Unsupervised Learning
Abstract: Humans learn a predictive model of the world and utilize it to reason about future events and the consequences of actions. Unlike most machine predictors, humans exhibit impressive generalization abilities to unseen scenarios and intelligent reasoning in these settings. One important aspect of this ability is physical intuition. This work explores the potential of unsupervised learning to find features that promote better generalization to settings outside the supervised training distribution. The task focuses on predicting the stability of towers of square blocks. The paper demonstrates that an unsupervised model trained to predict future frames of a video sequence of stable and unstable block configurations can yield features that support extrapolating stability prediction to block configurations outside the training set distribution.
label: AI

title: PoseAgent: Budget-Constrained 6D Object Pose Estimation via Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: State-of-the-art computer vision algorithms often achieve efficiency by making discrete choices about which hypotheses to explore next. This allows allocation of computational resources to promising candidates but makes these decisions non-differentiable. As a result, these algorithms are difficult to train end-to-end. This paper proposes to learn an efficient algorithm for the task of 6D object pose estimation. The system optimizes the parameters of an existing state-of-the-art pose estimation system using reinforcement learning, where the pose estimation system now becomes the stochastic policy parameterized by a CNN. The paper also presents an efficient training algorithm that significantly reduces computation time. Empirical results show that the learned pose estimation procedure makes better use of limited resources and improves upon the state-of-the-art on a challenging dataset. The approach enables differentiable end-to-end training of complex algorithmic pipelines and learns to make optimal use of a given computational budget.
label: AI

title: Hybrid Learning of Optical Flow and Next Frame Prediction to Boost Optical Flow in the Wild
Abstract: CNN-based optical flow estimation has gained recent attention due to its impressively high frame rates. While these networks perform well on synthetic datasets, they lag behind classical methods in real-world videos, as ground truth optical flow is not available for training on real data. This paper proposes boosting CNN-based optical flow estimation in real scenes using the freely available self-supervised task of next-frame prediction. The network is trained in a hybrid manner, receiving a mixture of synthetic and real videos. A sample-variant multi-tasking architecture enables the network to be trained on different tasks depending on the availability of ground truth. The paper also explores predicting "next-flow" instead of estimating the current flow, which intuitively aligns better with the next-frame prediction task and yields favorable results. The paper demonstrates improvement in optical flow estimation on the real-world KITTI benchmark. Additionally, optical flow is tested indirectly in an action classification scenario. As a side product of this work, the paper reports significant improvements over state-of-the-art in next-frame prediction.
label: AI

title: COCO-Stuff: Thing and Stuff Classes in Context
Abstract: Semantic classes can be categorized as either things (objects with well-defined shapes, e.g., car, person) or stuff (amorphous background regions, e.g., grass, sky). While extensive research focuses on thing classes, stuff classes have received less attention. However, stuff classes are important as they provide insights into various aspects of an image, including scene type, the likelihood and location of thing classes through contextual reasoning, and physical attributes, material types, and geometric properties of the scene. To comprehensively understand stuff and things in context, the paper introduces COCO-Stuff, which augments all 164K images of the COCO 2017 dataset with pixel-wise annotations for 91 stuff classes. An efficient stuff annotation protocol based on superpixels is introduced, leveraging the original thing annotations. The paper quantifies the speed versus quality trade-off of the protocol and explores the relationship between annotation time and boundary complexity. Further analysis using COCO-Stuff examines the importance of stuff and thing classes based on their surface cover and frequency of mention in image captions. The spatial relations between stuff and things are investigated, highlighting the rich contextual relationships that make the dataset unique. Finally, the performance of a modern semantic segmentation method on stuff and thing classes is evaluated to determine whether stuff is easier to segment than things. |||
label: AI

title: Segmentation of large images based on super-pixels and community detection in graphs
Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for image segmentation using super-pixels and graph-based community detection algorithms. By employing super-pixel pre-segmentation, the method efficiently reduces the number of graph nodes, enabling the processing of large images. Furthermore, community detection algorithms provide more accurate segmentation results compared to traditional spectral graph partitioning methods. The proposed approach is evaluated against two popular algorithms: Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher's graph-based method and Arbelaez's contour-based method. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more precise segmentation and exhibits faster processing speeds than both comparison methods.
label: AI

title: Analysis and Optimization of Loss Functions for Multiclass, Top-k, and Multilabel Classification
Abstract: The widespread adoption of top-k error as a performance measure for large-scale image classification benchmarks, such as ImageNet and Places, necessitates a deeper understanding of its properties. This paper explores two key aspects of top-k error. Firstly, it analyzes established and recently proposed single-label multiclass methods, including efficient optimization algorithms, revealing that softmax loss and smooth multiclass SVM exhibit surprisingly competitive top-k error performance across all k values. This observation is attributed to the analysis of multiclass top-k calibration. Secondly, the study utilizes top-k methods to investigate the transition from multiclass to multilabel learning. The findings suggest that effective multilabel classifiers can be obtained on the Pascal VOC dataset using single-label per image training, while a more significant gap exists between multiclass and multilabel methods on the MS COCO dataset. Additionally, the paper contributes efficient algorithms for training with top-k and multilabel loss functions.
label: AI

title: A Binary Convolutional Encoder-decoder Network for Real-time Natural Scene Text Processing
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel binary convolutional encoder-decoder network (B-CEDNet) for natural scene text processing (NSTP), addressing the limitations of existing solutions in terms of memory and run-time consumption. The proposed network converts a text image into a class-distinguished salience map, revealing categorical, spatial, and morphological information about characters. B-CEDNet can process multiple regions containing characters in a single forward operation and is trained with binary weights and feature maps, resulting in significant run-time speedup and memory reduction. Trained on over 200,000 synthetic scene text images, B-CEDNet achieves impressive pixel-wise accuracy on the ICDAR-03 and ICDAR-13 datasets. The network exhibits remarkable inference speed (4.59 ms) and a small size (2.14 MB), achieving up to 8x faster inference and 96% smaller memory footprint compared to its full-precision counterpart.
label: AI

title: VIBIKNet: Visual Bidirectional Kernelized Network for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: This paper proposes VIBIKNet, a novel model for visual question answering, combining Kernelized Convolutional Neural Networks (K-CNNs) and Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) units. VIBIKNet demonstrates an optimal balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, minimizing memory and time consumption. Its effectiveness is validated on the VQA challenge dataset, showcasing superior performance and speed compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Statistics of Visual Responses to Object Stimuli from Primate AIT Neurons to DNN Neurons
Abstract: This study investigates the response statistics and intrinsic dimensionality of object representations in deep neural networks (DNNs), comparing them with those of primate inferotemporal cortex (AIT). While DNNs have shown comparable performance to AIT in object recognition, their response characteristics differ significantly. Analysis of DNN neurons reveals distinct kurtosis and Pareto tail index values, indicating fundamental differences in single-neuron selectivity and population sparseness compared to IT neurons, except in certain specific cases. Increasing the number of neurons and stimuli can significantly alter these conclusions. The study further observes that as DNNs ascend through convolutional layers, single-neuron selectivity and population sparseness increase, suggesting that the final convolutional layer learns features for object representations, while fully-connected layers learn categorization features. Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of sufficient stimuli and neurons for obtaining stable dimensionality. This research represents the first analysis of DNN neuron response statistics in comparison to AIT neurons, providing insights into the discrepancies and potential outcomes of IT neurons with larger neuron and stimuli populations.
label: AI

title: Text-guided Attention Model for Image Captioning
Abstract: This paper introduces a text-guided attention model for image captioning, leveraging the interplay between visual attention and language comprehension. The model employs an exemplar-based learning approach to retrieve associated captions from training data, utilizing them to learn attention on visual features. This text-guided attention mechanism enhances image captioning by effectively distinguishing small or confusable objects, leading to more detailed and accurate scene descriptions. Validation on the MS-COCO Captioning benchmark demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in standard metrics.
label: AI

title: PIGMIL: Positive Instance Detection via Graph Updating for Multiple Instance Learning
Abstract: Positive instance detection, particularly within positive bags (true positive instances, TPIs), plays a crucial role in multiple instance learning (MIL), where only bag-level labels are available for classification. This paper proposes PIGMIL, a novel method for positive instance detection via graph updating in MIL, addressing the limitations of existing methods that ignore global similarity among positive instances and treat negative instances as independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.). PIGMIL constructs a consistent similarity and discrimination graph (CSDG) based on the global similarity among positive instances and robust discrimination of instances from negative instances, transforming TPI detection into a PCP updating problem. Efficiently approximated by updating CSDG using a random walk ranking algorithm and an instance updating strategy, PIGMIL effectively identifies TPIs and transforms bags into feature representation vectors for classifier training. Extensive experiments demonstrate PIGMIL's high precision in TPI detection and superior performance compared to traditional MIL methods.
label: AI

title: An Attention-Driven Approach of No-Reference Image Quality Assessment
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA), predicting perceptual quality scores without a reference image. The proposed method leverages three key concepts: visual attention, robust averaging, and multi-task learning. Visual attention is incorporated by considering fixation areas as containing crucial information for IQA. Robust averaging, supported by psychological studies, integrates multiple evidence to make a final perceptual judgment. Multi-task learning is employed to shape representation learning, resulting in a more generalized model. The NR-IQA process is modeled as a dynamic perception process where the model samples "informative" areas sequentially and aggregates information to learn a representation for predicting both image quality score and distortion type. Reinforcement learning, implemented using a deep network with policy gradient methods and trained through backpropagation, guides the learning of an optimal sampling policy for acquiring "task-informative" image regions. Experiments on the TID2008 dataset demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, while also showcasing the model's efficiency through its minimal use of fixations.
label: AI

title: On Choosing Training and Testing Data for Supervised Algorithms in Ground Penetrating Radar Data for Buried Threat Detection
Abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a widely used sensing modality for landmine and subsurface threat detection. This paper addresses the challenge of keypoint utilization in supervised GPR-based detection algorithms, which rely on labeled training examples. Keypoints are desirable locations for extracting patches of GPR data, but the optimal strategy for utilizing them remains unclear. The paper presents a taxonomy of existing keypoint utilization strategies and evaluates their effectiveness on a large dataset using diverse classifiers and features. Analysis of the results reveals that the choice of keypoint utilization strategy significantly impacts classifier performance. The paper proposes a new strategy, PatchSelect, which consistently outperforms other strategies across all experiments.
label: AI

title: A Novel Motion Detection Method Resistant to Severe Illumination Changes
Abstract: The increasing demand for motion detection in applications like video analysis and surveillance systems motivates the development of robust and accurate methods. Existing approaches struggle with challenges posed by illumination variations, occlusions, camouflage, burst physical motion, dynamic texture, and environmental changes. This paper proposes a novel per-pixel motion descriptor based on two complementary three-dimensional-discrete wavelet transform (3D-DWT) and three-dimensional wavelet leader techniques, addressing these challenges. The descriptor extracts a feature vector for each pixel using a wavelet-based motion descriptor, followed by clustering using algorithms like k-means or Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to existing motion detection approaches, particularly in challenging scenarios. Further details and results for different datasets are available online.
label: AI

title: Automated Inference on Sociopsychological Impressions of Attractive Female Faces
Abstract: This article, a continuation of earlier work, explores the potential of supervised machine learning in face-induced social computing and cognition. Building upon the success of face processing, analysis, and recognition in biometric-based identification, the study focuses on automated statistical inference of sociopsychological perceptions of female faces, controlling for race, attractiveness, age, and nationality. Empirical evidence suggests the feasibility of training machine learning algorithms using example face images characterized by internet users to predict perceptions of personality traits and demeanors.
label: AI

title: A probabilistic graphical model approach in 30 m land cover mapping with multiple data sources
Abstract: This research proposes a probabilistic graphical model (PGM) approach for high-accuracy land-cover mapping using multi-temporal Landsat and MODIS data. The method leverages independent classifiers applied to single-date Landsat 8 scenes and MODIS time-series data for probability estimation, constructing a PGM for each pixel in Landsat 8 data. Conditional probability distributions are calculated based on data quality and reliability, allowing for selective information utilization. The study uses two areas in China, Beijing City and a coastal region of Shandong province, for evaluation. Quantitative results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving significant improvements in overall accuracy compared to single-temporal Landsat image-based mapping. Incorporating MODIS data further enhances accuracy, highlighting the benefits of multi-source data integration. The method's key advantage lies in its applicability even when multi-temporal data cannot be stacked as a multi-layered image.
label: AI

title: A Fast Keypoint Based Hybrid Method for Copy Move Forgery Detection
Abstract: Copy move forgery detection, a prevalent research topic in image forensics, focuses on identifying manipulated regions in digital images. This paper proposes a hybrid approach using SURF for keypoint detection and BRISK for feature description, addressing the limitations of existing block-based and keypoint-based methods. The proposed method significantly outperforms previous approaches in terms of detection speed, while remaining invariant to post-processing operations like rotation, scaling, Gaussian noise addition, and JPEG compression.
label: AI

title: Multiple Instance Learning: A Survey of Problem Characteristics and Applications
Abstract: Multiple instance learning (MIL) is a weakly supervised learning paradigm where training instances are grouped into sets called bags, with labels assigned to the entire bag. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of MIL problem characteristics, which have not been formally identified and described previously. These characteristics are categorized into four groups: bag composition, data distribution, instance label ambiguity, and task to be performed. The paper reviews methods specialized for each category, analyzes their manifestation in key MIL application areas, and compares the performance of 16 state-of-the-art MIL methods on selected problem characteristics. The research provides insights into the influence of problem characteristics on MIL algorithms, recommendations for future benchmarking, and promising avenues for future research.
label: AI

title: Salient Object Detection with Convex Hull Overlap
Abstract: Salient object detection plays a crucial role in identifying important regions within a vision system. Convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods directly train their models with large-scale datasets, but the crucial features for saliency remain an open question. This paper introduces a novel bottom-up feature, convex hull overlap (CHO), combined with appearance contrast features, for salient object detection. CHO feature is a kind of enhanced Gestalt cue, drawing inspiration from psychological observations about the relationship between surroundedness and object overlap. The paper's contribution lies in its use of hand-crafted features for salient object detection, eliminating the need for training on large-scale datasets. Unlike previous works focused solely on appearance features, the CHO feature bridges the gap between spatial object covering and object saliency. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Towards an Automated Image De-fencing Algorithm Using Sparsity
Abstract: Traditional image de-fencing methods suffer from non-robust fence detection and limitations in processing dynamic scenes. This paper proposes an automatic de-fencing algorithm for images of dynamic scenes, dividing the problem into automated fence detection, motion estimation, and data fusion from multiple frames of a captured video. Fence detection is implemented using Gabor filters and a machine learning method. The fence removal problem is formulated within an optimization framework, modeling the degraded observations and solving the inverse problem using the split Bregman technique with a total variation regularization constraint.
label: AI

title: Generalized Deep Image to Image Regression
Abstract: This paper introduces a Deep Convolutional Neural Network architecture, the Recursively Branched Deconvolutional Network (RBDN), serving as a generic image-to-image regressor that can be trained end-to-end without additional machinery. RBDN leverages an efficient recursive branching scheme with extensive parameter sharing and learnable upsampling to create a cheap multi-context image representation early in the process. This multi-context representation undergoes a highly non-linear locality preserving transformation through subsequent convolutions/deconvolutions without spatial downsampling. RBDN is fully convolutional and can handle variable image sizes during inference. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of RBDN on three diverse tasks – relighting, denoising, and colorization – achieving comparable results to state-of-the-art methods without post-processing or task-specific modifications.
label: AI

title: StackGAN: Text to Photo-realistic Image Synthesis with Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Synthesizing high-quality images from text descriptions is a challenging task in computer vision with numerous applications. Existing text-to-image approaches often generate samples that capture the general meaning of the description but lack necessary details and vivid object representations. This paper proposes Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks (StackGAN) to generate 256x256 photo-realistic images conditioned on text descriptions. The approach decomposes the complex problem into manageable sub-problems through a sketch-refinement process. Stage-I GAN sketches the primitive shape and colors based on the text, producing low-resolution images. Stage-II GAN takes these results and the text as input to generate high-resolution images with photo-realistic details, rectifying defects in Stage-I and adding compelling details through refinement. To enhance image diversity and stabilize training, a novel Conditioning Augmentation technique is introduced, encouraging smoothness in the latent conditioning manifold. Extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in generating photo-realistic images conditioned on text descriptions.
label: AI

title: Co-localization with Category-Consistent Features and Geodesic Distance Propagation
Abstract: Co-localization, the problem of localizing objects of the same class using only images containing them, presents a challenge due to the absence of negative examples for informative supervision. This paper proposes a method based on clustering the feature space of a generically pre-trained CNN to identify category-consistent CNN features, those consistently and highly activated for a specific object category. These features' combined activation map is then propagated using superpixel geodesic distances for co-localization. Experiments on three benchmarks (PASCAL 2007, PASCAL-2012, and Object Discovery) demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. The method further demonstrates its ability to detect and localize truly unseen categories, achieving significantly higher accuracy than previous methods on six held-out ImageNet categories. Notably, this success is achieved without region proposals or object detectors and utilizes a CNN pre-trained solely on image classification tasks without fine-tuning.
label: AI

title: Automatic Lymphocyte Detection in H&E Images with Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Automatic lymphocyte detection in H&E images is a crucial first step in numerous tissue image analysis algorithms. This paper proposes a new deep neural network model for accurate and robust lymphocyte detection, extending the fully convolutional network with ideas from recent techniques like shortcut links. The model employs a novel training scheme incorporating prior knowledge about lymphocytes, efficiently utilizing limited free-form annotations from pathologists and supporting efficient fine-tuning. The training scheme enables self-improvement through error collection during real applications. Experiments demonstrate the model's effectiveness in images with diverse staining conditions and tissue types. |||
label: AI

title: Arch2030: A Vision of Computer Architecture Research over the Next 15 Years
Abstract: The rapid decline of Moore's Law and Dennard Scaling necessitates a new approach to ensure the continued progress of information technology.  The computer architecture community has been actively engaged in visioning exercises to address this challenge, culminating in the IEEE Rebooting Computing Initiative. This report aims to further this dialogue by engaging with the applications and device/circuit communities to understand their trends and vision. The goal is to identify opportunities where architecture research can bridge the gap between the application and device domains.
label: AI

title: Panoptic Studio: A Massively Multiview System for Social Interaction Capture
Abstract: To capture the 3D motion of people engaged in social interactions, the Panoptic Studio was developed. This system addresses the challenges of occlusion, subtle motion detection, human appearance variation, and the potential influence of markers on interaction behavior.  It uses 480 synchronized video streams as input to generate labeled, time-varying 3D structures of anatomical landmarks. The algorithm combines "weak" perceptual information from multiple views, progressively generating skeletal proposals and refining them temporally. This system and method are the first to reconstruct full body motion of multiple individuals without markers, showcasing the benefits of integrating perceptual analyses from diverse viewpoints.
label: AI

title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
Abstract: Feature pyramids are crucial for object detection at different scales. While deep learning object detectors have often avoided pyramid representations due to computational and memory constraints, this paper proposes a novel Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). This top-down architecture with lateral connections constructs semantic feature maps at various scales with minimal overhead.  FPN significantly enhances performance as a generic feature extractor, achieving state-of-the-art single-model results on the COCO detection benchmark. Its efficiency allows for real-time operation, making it a practical and accurate solution for multi-scale object detection.
label: AI

title: Understanding and Mapping Natural Beauty
Abstract: This paper presents a method for quantifying and predicting the scenicness of images, challenging the notion that natural beauty is solely subjective. Using a dataset of crowdsourced ratings for outdoor images from Great Britain, the approach explicitly accounts for the variance in human perceptions of scenicness. The results demonstrate that quantitative scenicness measures can improve semantic image understanding, content-aware image processing, and cross-view mapping, where overhead imagery can be used to compensate for the sparsity of ground-level images.
label: AI

title: Boundary-aware Instance Segmentation
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel object segment representation based on the distance transform of object masks, addressing the challenge of instance-level semantic segmentation. The proposed Object Mask Network (OMN) with a residual-deconvolution architecture infers this representation and decodes it into a final binary mask. This approach allows for mask prediction beyond the scope of bounding boxes, making it robust to inaccuracies in object candidate generation.  Integration into a Multitask Network Cascade framework leads to the Boundary-Aware Instance Segmentation (BAIS) network, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both object proposal generation and instance segmentation.
label: AI

title: Following Gaze Across Views
Abstract: This paper presents an approach for following gaze across different views, predicting the gaze direction of a person throughout a scene.  The VideoGaze dataset is introduced as a benchmark for both training and evaluating gaze prediction models. The model estimates a gaze location density in a second view given a person in a first view.  Key aspects of the model include the integration of saliency, gaze pose, and geometric relationships between views, all learned automatically without explicit supervision.  Experimental results demonstrate superior performance compared to baseline methods, suggesting the approach effectively follows gaze in everyday situations.
label: AI

title: ActionFlowNet: Learning Motion Representation for Action Recognition
Abstract: While convolutional neural networks (CNN) have made significant strides in visual recognition, action recognition models still rely on hand-crafted motion features for optimal performance. This paper introduces ActionFlowNet, a multitask learning model that directly learns from raw pixels to jointly estimate optical flow and recognize actions. This single-stream network captures both appearance and motion information, demonstrating the impact of optical flow quality on action recognition. The proposed model achieves a substantial improvement in accuracy compared to CNN-based action recognition models without external data or optical flow input. It also achieves competitive results with models trained on large-scale datasets like ImageNet and Sport-1M, demonstrating the effectiveness of exploiting motion information.
label: AI

title: Automatic Model Based Dataset Generation for Fast and Accurate Crop and Weeds Detection
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of selective weeding in agricultural robotics by proposing a novel approach for training detection and classification algorithms with minimal human intervention.  The method leverages procedurally generated synthetic datasets that randomize key environmental features such as crop and weed species, soil type, and lighting conditions.  Realistic views of an artificial agricultural scenario are generated by tuning model parameters and using real-world textures, enabling large-scale training data generation without manual annotation. The generated data can be used directly or as a supplement to real-world images.  Experiments using a deep learning-based image segmentation architecture confirm the effectiveness of the approach.
label: AI

title: A series of maximum entropy upper bounds of the differential entropy
Abstract: This paper presents a series of closed-form maximum entropy upper bounds for the differential entropy of a continuous univariate random variable and analyzes their properties. These generic bounds are applied to upper bound the differential entropy of Gaussian mixture models, requiring closed-form calculations of raw and absolute moments.  These calculations are also useful in statistical machine learning and information theory. Experiments demonstrate the tightness of the bounds.
label: AI

title: Facial Expression Recognition using Convolutional Neural Networks: State of the Art
Abstract: Automatic facial expression recognition has numerous applications in human-computer interaction and other fields.  This paper reviews recent advancements in image-based facial expression recognition using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), highlighting algorithmic differences and their impact on performance. Existing bottlenecks and future directions for research are identified.  The paper demonstrates that using more advanced CNN architectures significantly improves performance, achieving a 75.2% test accuracy on FER2013 dataset, surpassing previous works without relying on additional training data or face registration.
label: AI

title: Gesture-based Bootstrapping for Egocentric Hand Segmentation
Abstract: Accurate hand detection in images is crucial for understanding human activity in first-person point-of-view camera applications. This paper presents an interactive approach for learning a person-specific hand segmentation model that requires no manually labeled training data.  The approach leverages motion information to detect hand regions and then learns a personalized appearance model.  Two convolutional neural networks are employed: a gesture network for hand region detection and an appearance network for learning the person-specific model.  The appearance network's loss function incorporates the gesture network's confidence to mitigate errors. Experiments demonstrate robust performance across challenging datasets with diverse illumination and hand appearance variations.
label: AI

title: Fast Fourier single-pixel imaging using binary illumination
Abstract: Fourier single-pixel imaging (FSI) has proven its ability to reconstruct high-quality 2D and 3D images. The utilization of image sparsity in the Fourier domain enables high-resolution image reconstruction from fewer measurements. However, applying FSI to DMD-based high-speed imaging systems is challenging due to the binary nature of DMDs.  This paper proposes a DMD-based high-speed single-pixel imaging technique using binary Fourier patterns generated through upsampling and error diffusion dithering.  Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the technique in achieving high-quality static and real-time dynamic imaging, enabling high-speed imaging across a wide range of wavelengths.
label: AI

title: Exploiting 2D Floorplan for Building-scale Panorama RGBD Alignment
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for aligning panorama RGBD scans using a 2D floorplan image, addressing the need for dense RGBD sampling in conventional alignment techniques.  The approach formulates a Markov Random Field inference problem as a scan placement over the floorplan, utilizing multi-modal image correspondence cues between scans and the floorplan. A novel coverage potential is introduced to mitigate stacking bias.  Evaluations on large indoor spaces demonstrate the effectiveness of the system, presenting the first approach to utilize a 2D floorplan for building-scale 3D pointcloud alignment.
label: AI

title: Deep TEN: Texture Encoding Network
Abstract: This paper introduces a Deep Texture Encoding Network (Deep-TEN) with a novel Encoding Layer integrated into a convolutional network. This approach combines the entire dictionary learning and encoding pipeline into a single model, unlike current methods that use separate components.  Deep-TEN learns visual vocabularies directly from the loss function, enabling simultaneous learning of features, dictionaries, and encoding representation. The orderless representation is particularly valuable for material and texture recognition. The Encoding Layer generalizes robust encoders like VLAD and Fisher Vectors, discarding domain-specific information for easier feature transfer.  Joint training across multiple datasets results in increased recognition performance, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on benchmark databases.
label: AI

title: 3D Shape Segmentation with Projective Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a deep architecture for segmenting 3D objects into labeled semantic parts, combining image-based fully convolutional networks (FCNs) and surface-based conditional random fields (CRFs). The FCNs efficiently reason about 3D object parts from multiple views and scales, and their outputs are projected onto the 3D object surfaces.  The surface-based CRF integrates these projected outputs with geometric consistency cues for coherent segmentations. The end-to-end training of the architecture results in superior performance compared to existing methods on the ShapeNet benchmark.  Promising results are also demonstrated for noisy 3D shapes from consumer-grade depth cameras.
label: AI

title: Feedback Neural Network for Weakly Supervised Geo-Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a neural network architecture for weakly-supervised learning, addressing the challenge of expensive and subjective labeling in tasks like image semantic segmentation. The architecture suppresses irrelevant neuron activations to localize objects of interest using image-level categorical labels. The algorithm is applied to the task of transforming satellite images into maps of settlements and individual buildings, achieving superior performance and efficiency compared to baseline models.
label: AI

title: A Maximum A Posteriori Estimation Framework for Robust High Dynamic Range Video Synthesis
Abstract: High dynamic range (HDR) video synthesis from multiple low dynamic range (LDR) exposures poses challenges, particularly for accurate correspondence estimation between video frames. This paper proposes a statistical approach using maximum a posterior (MAP) estimation to avoid exact correspondence estimation. Under suitable statistical assumptions and prior choices, the problem is reduced to an optimization task involving foreground and background estimation.  Foreground is estimated using a multiscale adaptive kernel regression technique, implicitly capturing local structure and temporal motion.  Extensive experiments demonstrate the algorithm's superiority in generating high-quality HDR videos compared to existing methods, exhibiting a favorable complexity-performance trade-off.
label: AI

title: Joint Hand Detection and Rotation Estimation by Using CNN
Abstract: Hand detection is essential for tasks involving hand pose parsing and gesture understanding, crucial for robotics and human-computer interaction.  However, hand detection in uncontrolled environments is challenging due to wrist joint flexibility and cluttered backgrounds. This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach for simultaneous hand detection and in-plane rotation calibration. A context-aware proposal generation algorithm is used to ensure recall, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) that handles object rotation explicitly is designed to jointly solve detection and rotation estimation.  Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art detection models.
label: AI

title: Predicting Ground-Level Scene Layout from Aerial Imagery
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel strategy for learning semantically meaningful features from aerial imagery using ground imagery. The architecture extracts features from an aerial image using a convolutional neural network and applies an adaptive transformation to map these features to the ground-level perspective.  End-to-end learning minimizes the difference between the ground image's semantic segmentation and the prediction solely based on the aerial image.  The learned model can perform rough semantic labeling without additional training and achieve more accurate segmentation than baseline approaches.  The extracted features are also used for estimating ground image geolocation and geoorientation and for hallucinating a plausible ground-level panorama.
label: AI

title: Deep Supervision with Shape Concepts for Occlusion-Aware 3D Object Parsing
Abstract: Monocular 3D object parsing is highly desirable for tasks like occlusion reasoning and scene interpretation. This paper presents a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for localizing semantic parts in 2D images and 3D space while inferring their visibility states from a single RGB image. The network is regularized using domain knowledge through deep supervision of hidden layers, sequentially inferring concepts associated with the final task. Synthetic data is generated from 3D object CAD models to acquire large-scale training data with ground truth 3D shape and relevant concepts.
