The network achieves state-of-the-art performance on real image benchmarks for 2D and 3D keypoint localization and instance segmentation, demonstrating effective knowledge transfer from synthetic to real images with reduced overfitting. |||
label: AI

title: Domain knowledge assisted cyst segmentation in OCT retinal images
Abstract: 3D imaging techniques, particularly Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), are gaining prominence in retinal imaging due to their ability to highlight structures within sub-retinal layers.  However, the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in OCT images presents a challenge for automated cystoid structure detection and segmentation.  This research proposes a novel automated method inspired by biological processes for detecting and segmenting cysts in 3D OCT volumes. The method utilizes domain knowledge about cystoid structures and incorporates a Random Forests ensemble learning approach for classification. The unified approach achieves both detection and segmentation. The proposed method, with further enhancements, holds promise as a starting point for a more robust approach.  Validation against a training set achieved a mean Dice coefficient of 0.3893 with a standard deviation of 0.2987.
label: AI

title: A fuzzy approach for segmentation of touching characters
Abstract: The problem of accurately segmenting touching characters presents a significant challenge in pattern recognition.  Despite numerous proposed methods and algorithms, a definitive solution remains elusive.  This paper introduces a novel fuzzy logic-based method for segmenting touching characters. This method innovatively combines three features already explored in separate studies but not previously combined. The proposed strategy utilizes a three-input/one-output fuzzy inference system with fuzzy rules specifically optimized for segmenting touching characters in printed and handwritten Latin characters. The system's performance is illustrated through numerical examples demonstrating its ability to achieve reasonable accuracy in segmenting characters, even under challenging conditions. These numerical results suggest the method's adaptability to various character datasets through tuning of fuzzy sets and rules.
label: AI

title: FCNs in the Wild: Pixel-level Adversarial and Constraint-based Adaptation
Abstract: Fully convolutional models have proven successful in dense prediction for a wide range of visual tasks. Although these models perform well in supervised settings, their performance can degrade significantly under domain shifts, even those appearing minor to human observers. For instance, training on one city and testing on another with different geographic features or weather conditions can lead to substantial performance degradation due to pixel-level distribution shifts. This paper presents the first domain adaptive semantic segmentation method, introducing an unsupervised adversarial approach for pixel prediction problems. The method integrates both global and category-specific adaptation techniques. Global domain alignment is achieved through a novel semantic segmentation network utilizing fully convolutional domain adversarial learning. This initially adapted space enables category-specific adaptation through a generalization of constrained weak learning, explicitly transferring spatial layout from the source to the target domains. The approach outperforms baselines across diverse settings on multiple large-scale datasets, including adaptation across real city environments, synthetic sub-domains, simulated to real environments, and a novel large-scale dash-cam dataset.
label: AI

title: Learning Video Object Segmentation from Static Images
Abstract: Inspired by advancements in deep learning for instance segmentation and object tracking, this research introduces video object segmentation as a concept of guided instance segmentation. The proposed model operates on a per-frame basis, guided by the output of the previous frame towards the target object in the subsequent frame.  The research demonstrates that highly accurate object segmentation in videos can be achieved using a convolutional neural network (ConvNet) trained solely on static images. The key element of this approach is a combination of offline and online learning strategies, where offline learning refines the mask from the previous frame estimate, while online learning captures the appearance of the specific object instance.  The method can handle various types of input annotations, including bounding boxes and segments, and can incorporate multiple annotated frames, making it suitable for diverse applications.  The study achieves competitive results on three different datasets, independent of the type of input annotation.
label: AI

title: Progressive Tree-like Curvilinear Structure Reconstruction with Structured Ranking Learning and Graph Algorithm
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel tree-like curvilinear structure reconstruction algorithm based on supervised learning and graph theory. The algorithm analyzes image patches to extract local major orientations and rankings corresponding to the curvilinear structure.  Steerable filters are used to compute oriented gradient information for extracting local curvilinear features.  Structured Support Vector Machine is then employed for ordinal regression of input image patches, with the ordering based on shape similarity to latent curvilinear structures. Finally, the curvilinear structure is progressively reconstructed by searching for geodesic paths connecting remote vertices in the graph constructed from the structured output rankings. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's ability to accurately provide topological features of curvilinear structures using minimal pixels across various datasets.
label: AI

title: Scene Flow Estimation: A Survey
Abstract: This paper presents the first comprehensive review of scene flow estimation, analyzing and comparing methods, technical challenges, evaluation methodologies, and performance.  Existing algorithms are categorized based on scene representation, data source, and calculation scheme, with a comparative analysis of their respective advantages and disadvantages. Datasets and evaluation protocols are enumerated, and the performance of representative methods is presented. The paper concludes with a future vision, outlining key questions for further discussion.  This survey provides a general introduction and analysis of scene flow estimation.
label: AI

title: Multi-source Transfer Learning with Convolutional Neural Networks for Lung Pattern Analysis
Abstract: Early diagnosis of interstitial lung diseases is crucial for effective treatment, but even experienced physicians face challenges due to the similarity of clinical manifestations. Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have been developed to assist with diagnosis.  These systems typically rely on fixed-scale classifiers that scan CT images, recognize textural lung patterns, and generate pathology maps.  In a previous study, the authors proposed a method for classifying lung tissue patterns using a deep convolutional neural network (CNN), with an architecture specifically designed for this purpose.  This paper presents an improved method for training the proposed network by leveraging knowledge transfer from the similar domain of general texture classification. Six publicly available texture databases are used to pretrain networks with the proposed architecture, which are subsequently fine-tuned on lung tissue data. The resulting CNNs are combined in an ensemble, and their fused knowledge is compressed back to a network with the original architecture.  This approach resulted in an absolute performance increase of approximately 2% for the proposed CNN.  The results demonstrate the potential of transfer learning in medical image analysis, highlight the textural nature of the problem, and emphasize the importance of training methods alongside network architecture.
label: AI

title: From Motion Blur to Motion Flow: a Deep Learning Solution for Removing Heterogeneous Motion Blur
Abstract: Removing pixel-wise heterogeneous motion blur is a challenging task due to the ill-posed nature of the problem.  The prevailing solution involves estimating the blur kernel by incorporating a prior, but extensive research indicates the difficulty in identifying a prior that is sufficiently informative and general.  Instead of imposing a prior based on theoretical assumptions, this research proposes learning a prior directly from the data. Learning a prior over the latent image would necessitate modeling all possible image content. The key insight underlying this approach is that learning the motion flow instead allows the model to focus on the cause of the blur, regardless of the image content. This simplifies the learning task and eliminates the iterative process typically required for latent image priors. The proposed approach directly estimates the motion flow from the blurred image using a fully-convolutional deep neural network (FCN), and recovers the unblurred image from the estimated motion flow. The FCN represents the first universal end-to-end mapping from the blurred image to the dense motion flow.  To train the FCN, motion flows are simulated to generate synthetic blurred-image-motion-flow pairs, eliminating the need for human labeling. Extensive experiments on challenging realistic blurred images demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques.
label: AI

title: Imaging around corners with single-pixel detector by computational ghost imaging
Abstract: This research presents the design of a single-pixel camera capable of imaging around corners based on computational ghost imaging. This camera allows capturing images of objects when the camera cannot directly view them.  The imaging system utilizes the spatial resolution limitations of the bucket detector in a ghost imaging setup.  A series of experiments were conducted to validate the predictions. This camera holds potential for applications in imaging around corners or in similar environments where direct observation of the object is not possible.
label: AI

title: Filter sharing: Efficient learning of parameters for volumetric convolutions
Abstract: Typical convolutional neural networks (CNNs) involve millions of parameters and require extensive annotated data for training. In medical applications, where training data is scarce, these sophisticated machine learning models are challenging to train. This paper proposes a method to reduce the inherent complexity of CNNs during training by exploiting the significant redundancy observed in learned CNN filters. The method identifies a small set of filters and mixing coefficients to derive every filter in each convolutional layer during training, effectively reducing the number of parameters requiring training. The study focuses on 3D lung nodule segmentation in CT images, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in achieving good results with limited training examples.
label: AI

title: Predicting brain age with deep learning from raw imaging data results in a reliable and heritable biomarker
Abstract: Machine learning analysis of neuroimaging data can accurately predict chronological age in healthy individuals, and deviations from healthy brain aging have been linked to cognitive impairment and disease. This research aims to further establish "brain-predicted age" as a biomarker of individual differences in the brain aging process. The study utilizes a predictive modeling approach based on deep learning, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), applied to both preprocessed and raw T1-weighted MRI data.  The study first demonstrates the accuracy of CNN brain-predicted age using a large dataset of healthy adults (N = 2001).  Next, the heritability of brain-predicted age is investigated using a sample of monozygotic and dizygotic female twins (N = 62). Finally, the test-retest and multi-center reliability of brain-predicted age is examined using two samples (within-scanner N = 20; between-scanner N = 11).  CNN brain-predicted ages are generated and compared to a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) approach across all datasets.  Input data included gray matter (GM) or white matter (WM) volumetric maps generated by Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) or raw data. The study concludes that brain-predicted age represents an accurate, highly reliable, and genetically valid phenotype, with potential for use as a biomarker of brain aging. Moreover, age predictions can be accurately generated on raw T1-MRI data, significantly reducing computational time for new data, bringing the process closer to providing real-time information on brain health in clinical settings.
label: AI

title: Classification of Neurological Gait Disorders Using Multi-task Feature Learning
Abstract: As populations age, neurological impairments and musculoskeletal degeneration contribute to gait abnormalities, significantly impacting quality of life. Gait rehabilitative therapy is widely adopted to help patients maximize community participation and independence. To enhance the precision and efficiency of rehabilitative therapy, more objective methods based on sensory data are needed. This paper proposes an algorithmic framework for classifying gait disorders caused by stroke and Parkinson's Disease (PD) using ground contact force (GCF) data.  Multi-task feature learning (MTFL), an advanced machine learning method, is used to jointly train classification models of a subject's gait in three classes: post-stroke, PD, and healthy gait. Gait parameters related to mobility, balance, strength, and rhythm are utilized as features for classification. The MTFL models identify the most relevant features per disease, providing a more objective assessment and therapy progress tracking.  The methodology is evaluated using data from a human participant study, including five PD patients, three post-stroke patients, and three healthy subjects. Despite the diversity of abnormalities, the evaluation reveals that the proposed approach successfully distinguishes post-stroke and PD gait from healthy gait, as well as post-stroke from PD gait, with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) score of at least 0.96. The methodology also aids in selecting crucial gait features for a better understanding of the key characteristics that distinguish abnormal gaits and enables the design of personalized treatments.
label: AI

title: AGA: Attribute Guided Augmentation
Abstract: Data augmentation, the process of generating artificial samples to expand a training data corpus, is addressed in this paper. The authors propose attributed-guided augmentation (AGA), a method that learns a mapping to synthesize data where an attribute of a synthesized sample is at a desired value or strength. This approach is particularly useful when limited data with attribute annotations is available for learning, but a large external corpus of heavily annotated samples is accessible. Unlike previous works that primarily augment in the image space, AGA performs augmentation in the feature space. The method is implemented as a deep encoder-decoder architecture that learns the synthesis function in an end-to-end manner. The study demonstrates the utility of this approach in the context of (1) one-shot object recognition in a transfer-learning setting with no prior knowledge of new classes, and (2) object-based one-shot scene recognition.  Leveraging 3D depth and pose information from the SUN RGB-D dataset as external data, the experiments reveal that attribute-guided augmentation of high-level CNN features significantly improves one-shot recognition performance on both tasks.
label: AI

title: Query-adaptive Image Retrieval by Deep Weighted Hashing
Abstract: Hashing methods have gained significant interest for large-scale image retrieval. Deep hashing methods have achieved promising results by harnessing the powerful representation capabilities of deep networks. However, current deep hashing methods treat all hash bits equally. This approach has two major drawbacks:  (1) a large number of images share the same distance to a query image due to the discrete Hamming distance, a critical issue for image retrieval where fine-grained rankings are essential, and (2) different hash bits contribute differently to image retrieval, and treating them equally adversely affects retrieval accuracy. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the query-adaptive deep weighted hashing (QaDWH) approach, which enables fine-grained ranking for different queries using a weighted Hamming distance.  First, a novel deep hashing network is proposed to jointly learn hash codes and corresponding class-wise weights, allowing the learned weights to reflect the importance of different hash bits for different image classes.  Second, a query-adaptive image retrieval method is introduced, rapidly generating hash bit weights for different query images by fusing semantic probability and the learned class-wise weights.  Fine-grained image retrieval is then performed using the weighted Hamming distance, providing more accurate ranking compared to the traditional Hamming distance. Experiments on four widely used datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms eight state-of-the-art hashing methods.
label: AI

title: Contextual Visual Similarity
Abstract: Measuring visual similarity is crucial for image understanding. But what constitutes visual similarity? Most existing work assumes that images are similar if they contain the same object instance or category. However, the reasons behind image similarity are more complex. For example, from a category perspective, a black dog image is similar to a white dog image. However, in terms of color, a black dog image is more similar to a black horse image than the white dog image. This highlights the ambiguity of visual similarity, which can be clarified when given an explicit contextual perspective.  Based on this observation, this research proposes the concept of contextual visual similarity.  To illustrate, the concept is examined in the context of image search.  Instead of providing only a single image for image similarity search (e.g., Google image search), the proposed approach requires three images.  Given a query image, a second positive image (similar to the query), and a third negative image (dissimilar to the first two), a contextualized similarity search criteria is defined.  Specifically, feature weights are learned across all feature dimensions of each image, ensuring that the distance between the query image and the positive image is small, while their distances to the negative image are large after reweighting their features.  The learned feature weights encode the contextualized visual similarity specified by the user and can be applied for attribute-specific image search.  The study also demonstrates the usefulness of this contextualized similarity weighting scheme for various tasks, including answering visual analogy questions and unsupervised attribute discovery.
label: AI

title: An Efficient Algorithm for the Piecewise-Smooth Model with Approximately Explicit Solutions
Abstract: This paper presents an efficient approach to image segmentation that approximates the piecewise-smooth (PS) functional with explicit solutions. By imposing rational constraints on the initial conditions and final solutions of the PS functional, two novel formulations are proposed that can be approximated as explicit solutions to the evolution partial differential equations (PDEs) of the PS model, requiring the solution of only one PDE.  Furthermore, an energy term that regularizes the level set function to be a signed distance function is incorporated into the evolution formulation, eliminating the need for time-consuming re-initialization. Experiments on synthetic and real images demonstrate that the method is more efficient than both the PS model and the local binary fitting (LBF) model, while achieving similar segmentation accuracy to the LBF model.
label: AI

title: Complex Matrix Factorization for Face Recognition
Abstract: This work develops novel complex matrix factorization methods for face recognition: complex matrix factorization (CMF), sparse complex matrix factorization (SpaCMF), and graph complex matrix factorization (GraCMF).  After real-valued data is transformed into a complex field, the complex-valued matrix is decomposed into two matrices of bases and coefficients, derived from solutions to an optimization problem in the complex domain.  The generated objective function is a real-valued function of the reconstruction error, providing a parametric description.  Factorizing the matrix of complex entries directly transforms the constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one. Additionally, a complex vector space with N dimensions can be considered as a 2N-dimensional real vector space.  This allows for the utilization of all real analytic properties in the complex field.  The ability to exploit these characteristics motivates the development of a simpler framework that delivers improved recognition results. The effectiveness of this framework is further elucidated in later sections of the paper.
label: AI

title: Discrete Schroedinger Transform For Texture Recognition
Abstract: This work introduces a new procedure for extracting features from gray-level texture images based on the discrete Schroedinger transform.  This non-linear transform maps the image as the initial probability distribution of a wave function, which evolves over time according to the Schroedinger equation from Quantum Mechanics.  Features are extracted from statistical moments of the distribution measured at different times.  The proposed method is applied to the classification of three benchmark texture databases, comparing its performance to other well-known texture descriptors, such as textons, local binary patterns, multifractals, and others. The proposed method outperforms all other methods in terms of percentage of images correctly classified.  The method is further applied to plant species identification using scanned images of leaves, again demonstrating superior performance compared to other texture methods.  A test with images affected by Gaussian and "salt & pepper" noise is also conducted, with the Schroedinger descriptors achieving the best performance.
label: AI

title: Research on the Multiple Feature Fusion Image Retrieval Algorithm based on Texture Feature and Rough Set Theory
Abstract: The rapid growth of images containing complex information and content necessitates efficient and precise retrieval methods from large-scale image databases.  This paper proposes a multiple feature fusion image retrieval algorithm based on texture features and rough set theory, addressing the time-consuming nature of conventional approaches.  Unlike traditional methods that rely on single features or standards, this approach fuses different features through normalization operations.  Rough set theory enhances the robustness of the retrieval system when dealing with incomplete data warehouses. The wavelet Gabor function, known for its robustness, is used to improve the texture extraction paradigm.  Further optimization involves re-organizing extracted features through internal and external normalization, resulting in better combinations. Numerical experiments have validated the overall feasibility of this methodology, demonstrating improved accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art algorithms.
label: AI

title: DeMoN: Depth and Motion Network for Learning Monocular Stereo
Abstract: This paper frames structure from motion as a learning problem. It trains a convolutional network end-to-end to compute depth and camera motion from successive, unconstrained image pairs. The architecture consists of multiple stacked encoder-decoder networks, with an iterative network core capable of refining its own predictions. The network estimates not only depth and motion but also surface normals, optical flow between images, and confidence of the matching. A crucial aspect of the approach is a training loss based on spatial relative differences. Compared to traditional two-frame structure from motion methods, the results are more accurate and robust.  Unlike popular depth-from-single-image networks, DeMoN learns the concept of matching, enabling better generalization to structures not encountered during training. |||
label: AI

title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
Abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are neurodevelopmental conditions that significantly impact children and adults. Currently, diagnosis relies on expert evaluation using questionnaires and observation of behavioral markers, a process that is subjective, time-consuming, and costly. This paper proposes a novel methodology using automatic visual analysis of behavior to aid in the prediction of ADHD and ASD. The approach involves conducting questionnaires via a computer interface while recording participants with RGBD sensors. Unlike previous methods that focused on detecting specific behavioral markers, this system provides a fully automated end-to-end solution for directly predicting ADHD and ASD in adults. Leveraging state-of-the-art facial expression analysis based on Dynamic Deep Learning and 3D behavioral analysis, the system achieves impressive classification rates of 96% for Controls vs. Condition (ADHD/ASD) and 94% for Comorbid (ADHD+ASD) vs. ASD only. This innovative system holds potential for significant time savings in the diagnostic process for ADHD and ASD.
label: AI

title: Differential Angular Imaging for Material Recognition
Abstract: Material recognition for real-world outdoor surfaces is crucial for computer vision applications in unconstrained environments. Computational surface modeling for material recognition has evolved from reflectance modeling using controlled laboratory measurements to image-based representations derived from internet-mined images. This paper proposes a middle-ground approach that leverages both radiometric cues and flexible image capture for material recognition. The approach involves developing a framework for differential angular imaging, where small angular variations in image capture enhance appearance representation and improve recognition performance. A large-scale material database, Ground Terrain in Outdoor Scenes (GTOS), is constructed, featuring over 30,000 images across 40 outdoor ground terrain classes under diverse weather and lighting conditions. This paper introduces a novel material recognition approach called Differential Angular Imaging Network (DAIN) to fully exploit the GTOS dataset. DAIN utilizes a unique network architecture to extract material characteristics encoded in the angular and spatial gradients of their appearance. Empirical results demonstrate that DAIN surpasses single-view or coarsely quantized multiview images in recognition performance, highlighting the effectiveness of differential angular imaging for flexible, in-situ material recognition.
label: AI

title: Pano2Vid: Automatic Cinematography for Watching 360$^{\circ}$ Videos
Abstract: This paper introduces the novel task of Pano2Vid – automatic cinematography in panoramic 360° videos. Given a 360° video, the goal is to direct an imaginary camera to virtually capture natural-looking normal field-of-view (NFOV) video. By selecting "where to look" within the panorama at each time step, Pano2Vid aims to automate the selection of viewing content for both the videographer and the viewer. To achieve this, a dataset of 360° videos with human-edited NFOV camera trajectories is compiled for evaluation. The paper proposes AutoCam, a data-driven approach to solve the Pano2Vid task. AutoCam leverages NFOV web video to discriminatively identify space-time "glimpses" of interest at each time instant and employs dynamic programming to select optimal human-like camera trajectories. Experimental evaluation against several baselines using newly defined Pano2Vid performance measures demonstrates the effectiveness of AutoCam in generating informative videos that could plausibly be captured by human videographers.
label: AI

title: A Matrix Splitting Method for Composite Function Minimization
Abstract: Composite function minimization is a fundamental problem with widespread applications in computer vision and machine learning, encompassing bound constrained optimization and cardinality regularized optimization as special cases. This paper proposes and analyzes a novel Matrix Splitting Method (MSM) for minimizing composite functions. MSM can be viewed as a generalization of the classical Gauss-Seidel and Successive Over-Relaxation methods for solving linear systems. By incorporating a new Gaussian elimination procedure, MSM achieves state-of-the-art performance. For convex problems, the paper establishes the global convergence, convergence rate, and iteration complexity of MSM. For non-convex problems, global convergence is also proven. The effectiveness of MSM is validated on two specific applications: nonnegative matrix factorization and cardinality regularized sparse coding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MSM outperforms existing composite function minimization techniques in terms of efficiency and efficacy.
label: AI

title: Spatially Adaptive Computation Time for Residual Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning architecture based on Residual Networks that dynamically adjusts the number of executed layers for different image regions. This architecture is end-to-end trainable, deterministic, and problem-agnostic, making it applicable to various computer vision problems such as image classification, object detection, and image segmentation without modifications. Experimental results demonstrate that this model improves the computational efficiency of Residual Networks on the challenging ImageNet classification and COCO object detection datasets. Furthermore, the computation time maps are evaluated on the visual saliency dataset cat2000 and found to surprisingly correlate well with human eye fixation positions.
label: AI

title: Global Hypothesis Generation for 6D Object Pose Estimation
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenging task of estimating the 6D pose of a known 3D object from a single RGB-D image. Most modern approaches solve this task in three steps: compute local features, generate a pool of pose hypotheses, and select and refine a pose from the pool. This work focuses on the second step, hypothesis generation. While existing approaches rely on local reasoning techniques like RANSAC or Hough-voting, this paper demonstrates the benefit of global reasoning at this stage. A novel fully-connected Conditional Random Field (CRF) is formulated to output a small number of pose hypotheses. Despite the non-Gaussian potential functions of the CRF, a new and efficient two-step optimization procedure with optimality guarantees is presented. The global hypothesis generation procedure produces results surpassing state-of-the-art performance on the challenging "Occluded Object Dataset."
label: AI

title: Generalized Sinkhorn iterations for regularizing inverse problems using optimal mass transport
Abstract: The optimal mass transport problem provides a geometric framework for optimal allocation and has gained significant interest in applications such as signal processing, image processing, and computer vision. While it can be formulated as a linear programming problem, it becomes intractable for large problems due to the vast number of variables. To address this, a recent development utilizes an approximation with an entropic barrier term and solves the resulting optimization problem using Sinkhorn iterations. This paper extends this methodology to a class of inverse problems. The paper demonstrates that Sinkhorn-type iterations can be used to compute the proximal operator of the transport problem for large problems. A splitting framework is then employed to solve inverse problems incorporating the optimal mass transport cost for incorporating a priori information. The method is illustrated on problems in computerized tomography, particularly a limited-angle computerized tomography problem where a priori information compensates for missing measurements.
label: AI

title: Exploring the potential of combining time of flight and thermal infrared cameras for person detection
Abstract: Combining new, low-cost thermal infrared and time-of-flight range sensors presents novel opportunities. This position paper explores the possibilities of fusing data from these sensors for person detection. The proposed calibration approach differs from traditional stereo camera calibration in two key aspects. First, the spectral sensitivities of the two sensors differ significantly, with no overlapping sensitivity range. Second, their resolution is typically low, requiring special attention. Assuming the sensors' relative position is known but their orientation is unknown, the paper discusses typical measurement errors and proposes methods for compensation. The fused data enables increased accuracy and robustness in person detection without complex algorithms demanding high computational power and extensive training data.
label: AI

title: Process Monitoring of Extrusion Based 3D Printing via Laser Scanning
Abstract: Extrusion-based 3D Printing (E3DP) is an Additive Manufacturing (AM) technique that extrudes thermoplastic polymer to build components layerwise. AM typically involves long production times compared to mass production processes like Injection Molding. Failures in the AM process are often detected only after build completion, leading to part rejection and significant time and material loss due to dimensional inaccuracy or lack of mechanical performance. Integrating sensors to monitor and control process state-variables online offers a solution to improve the accuracy and robustness of manufacturing technology. By detecting and potentially compensating for errors early on, this approach reduces time and material loss. This paper describes the integration of a modular 2D laser triangulation scanner into an E3DP machine to analyze feedback signals. The compact size, achievable accuracy, and ability to capture geometrical 3D data make 2D laser triangulation scanners suitable for this application. The implemented system provides quantitative and qualitative information. The paper also presents initial steps towards developing a quality control loop for E3DP processes and discusses future opportunities.
label: AI

title: Embedded Line Scan Image Sensors: The Low Cost Alternative for High Speed Imaging
Abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, high-speed imaging line scan system. Replacing an expensive industrial line scan camera and illumination with a custom-built setup of inexpensive off-the-shelf components yields a measurement system with comparable quality at about 20 times lower cost. The system utilizes a low-cost linear (1D) image sensor, inexpensive optics including LED-based or LASER-based lighting, and an embedded platform for image processing. A step-by-step method for designing such a custom high-speed imaging system and selecting appropriate components is proposed. Simulations are developed to predict the final image quality obtained by the setup. The method is applied in a laboratory setting representing real-life scenarios. Results demonstrate the accuracy of the simulations and the ability of the low-cost line scan setup to acquire image quality comparable to high-end commercial vision systems at a fraction of the price.
label: AI

title: A Functional Regression approach to Facial Landmark Tracking
Abstract: Linear regression is a fundamental component in many face detection and tracking algorithms, typically used to predict shape displacements from image features through a linear mapping. This paper introduces a Functional Regression solution to the least squares problem, termed Continuous Regression, resulting in the first real-time incremental face tracker. Unlike prior work in Functional Regression that employed B-splines or Fourier series, the paper proposes approximating the input space by its first-order Taylor expansion, yielding a closed-form solution for the continuous domain of displacements. The continuous least squares problem is then extended to correlated variables, demonstrating the generalization of this approach. Continuous Regression is incorporated into the cascaded regression framework, highlighting its computational benefits for both training and testing. A fast approach for incremental learning within Cascaded Continuous Regression, coined iCCR, is presented, demonstrating its real-time face tracking capability by being 20 times faster than state-of-the-art methods. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first incremental face tracker to operate in real-time. iCCR achieves state-of-the-art performance on the 300-VW dataset, a recent large-scale benchmark for face tracking.
label: AI

title: Template Matching with Deformable Diversity Similarity
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel template matching measure called Deformable Diversity Similarity – based on the diversity of feature matches between a target image window and the template. The approach leverages both local appearance and geometric information for robust matching. The key contribution is a similarity measure that is robust to complex deformations, significant background clutter, and occlusions. Empirical evaluation on the most up-to-date benchmark demonstrates that this method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in detection accuracy while improving computational complexity.
label: AI

title: Saliency Driven Image Manipulation
Abstract: Have you ever taken a picture only to find an unimportant background object overly salient, or a team sports photo where your favorite player blends in? Wouldn't it be great to manipulate these pictures to attenuate distractors and enhance the desired subjects? This paper aims to manipulate images to control the saliency of objects. The proposed approach considers the internal color and saliency properties of the image and modifies the saliency map using an optimization framework that relies on patch-based manipulation using only patches from within the same image. This achieves realistic-looking results. Applications include object enhancement, distractor attenuation, and background decluttering. Comparing this method to previous ones shows significant improvement in both saliency manipulation and the realistic appearance of the resulting images.
label: AI

title: Fusion of Range and Thermal Images for Person Detection
Abstract: Detecting people in images is a challenging problem due to variations in pose, clothing, lighting, and other factors. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes a system based on fused range and thermal infrared images, which exhibit less variation and provide more meaningful information. The paper provides a brief introduction to the sensor technology and proposes a calibration method. Several data fusion algorithms are compared and evaluated on a simulated dataset. Initial experiments on real data are analyzed, highlighting measurement errors and associated challenges. The resulting fused data are utilized for efficient person detection in a fixed camera setup, and the system is extended to include person tracking.
label: AI

title: Deep Multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network for Dynamic Scene Deblurring
Abstract: Non-uniform blind deblurring for general dynamic scenes is a challenging computer vision problem, as blurs arise from multiple object motions, camera shake, and scene depth variation. Conventional energy optimization-based methods rely on simplified assumptions like partially uniform or locally linear blur kernels to remove these complicated motion blurs. Similarly, recent machine learning-based methods depend on synthetic blur datasets generated under these assumptions. This limits the effectiveness of conventional deblurring methods in removing blurs where the blur kernel is difficult to approximate or parameterize, such as object motion boundaries. This paper proposes a multi-scale convolutional neural network that restores sharp images in an end-to-end manner, handling blurs from various sources. A multi-scale loss function mimicking conventional coarse-to-fine approaches is introduced. Additionally, a new large-scale dataset is presented, providing pairs of realistic blurry images and corresponding ground truth sharp images obtained using a high-speed camera. Training the proposed model on this dataset empirically demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in dynamic scene deblurring, both qualitatively and quantitatively.
label: AI

title: Asynchronous approach in the plane: A deterministic polynomial algorithm
Abstract: This paper investigates the task of approach for two mobile agents with limited vision, moving asynchronously in a plane. The task involves bringing the agents within each other's range of vision in finite time. The agents execute the same deterministic algorithm and possess a compass indicating cardinal directions and a unit measure. However, they lack a shared global coordinate system (like GPS), cannot communicate, and have distinct labels. Each agent knows its label but not the other agent's label or initial position relative to its own. An agent's route is a sequence of segments traversed to achieve approach. The computation of each agent's route depends only on its algorithm and label. An adversary determines the agents' initial positions and controls their movement along each segment by arbitrarily varying their speeds. A deterministic approach algorithm always enables agents with distinct labels to solve the approach task regardless of the adversary's choices. The cost of algorithm execution is the total length of the routes traveled by the agents until approach is completed. Given an initial distance Δ separating the agents and a shortest label length l, both unknown to the agents, the paper explores the existence of a deterministic approach algorithm with a cost polynomial in Δ and l. The paper provides a positive answer to this question by designing such an algorithm.
label: AI

title: Consensus Based Medical Image Segmentation Using Semi-Supervised Learning And Graph Cuts
Abstract: Medical image segmentation requires consensus ground truth segmentations derived from multiple expert annotations. This paper proposes a novel approach to obtain consensus segmentations from experts using graph cuts (GC) and semi-supervised learning (SSL). Popular approaches utilize iterative Expectation Maximization (EM) to estimate the final annotation and quantify annotator performance. However, such techniques risk getting trapped in local minima. This paper introduces a self-consistency (SC) score to quantify annotator consistency using low-level image features. SSL is employed to predict missing annotations by considering global features and local image consistency. The SC score also serves as the penalty cost in a second-order Markov random field (MRF) cost function optimized using graph cuts to derive the final consensus label. Graph cut obtains a global maximum without an iterative procedure. Experimental results on synthetic images, real Crohn's disease patient data, and retinal images demonstrate that the final segmentation is accurate and more consistent than competing methods.

title: Re-identification of Humans in Crowds using Personal, Social and Environmental Constraints
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of human re-identification across non-overlapping cameras in crowded scenes. Re-identification in crowded scenes is challenging due to the large number of people, frequent occlusions, and variations in appearance caused by different camera properties and exposure. To solve this problem, the paper models multiple Personal, Social, and Environmental (PSE) constraints on human motion across cameras. Personal constraints include appearance and preferred speed, assumed to be consistent across cameras. Social influences (constraints) are quadratic in nature, occurring between pairs of individuals, and are modeled through grouping and collision avoidance. Environmental constraints capture transition probabilities between gates (entrances/exits) in different cameras, defined as multi-modal distributions of transition time and destination between all pairs of gates. These constraints are incorporated into an energy minimization framework for human re-identification. Assigning a one-to-one correspondence while modeling PSE constraints is NP-hard. The paper presents a stochastic local search algorithm to restrict the search space of hypotheses and obtain a one-to-one solution in the presence of linear and quadratic PSE constraints. Additionally, an alternative optimization using the Frank-Wolfe algorithm is presented, solving the convex approximation of the objective function with linear relaxation on binary variables, yielding an order of magnitude speedup over stochastic local search with a minor drop in performance. The approach is evaluated using Cumulative Matching Curves and one-to-one assignment on several thousand frames of Grand Central, PRID, and DukeMTMC datasets, achieving significantly better results compared to existing re-identification methods.
label: AI

title: Learning Localized Geometric Features Using 3D-CNN: An Application to Manufacturability Analysis of Drilled Holes
Abstract: 3D convolutional neural networks (3D-CNN) have been used for object recognition based on the voxelized shape of an object. This paper presents a 3D-CNN-based method to learn distinct local geometric features of interest within an object. In this context, the voxelized representation may not be sufficient to capture distinguishing information about these features. To enable efficient learning, the voxel data is augmented with surface normals of the object boundary. A 3D-CNN is then trained with this augmented data, and local features critical for decision-making are identified using 3D gradient-weighted class activation maps. An application of this feature identification framework is to recognize difficult-to-manufacture drilled hole features in a complex CAD geometry. The framework can be extended to identify difficult-to-manufacture features at multiple spatial scales, leading to a real-time decision support system for design for manufacturability.
label: AI

title: Mode Regularized Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract:
While Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) achieve state-of-the-art results on various generative tasks, they are known for being unstable and prone to missing modes. This paper argues that these issues are due to the specific functional shape of trained discriminators in high-dimensional spaces, which can easily lead to training stagnation or push probability mass in the wrong direction, towards higher concentration than the data generating distribution. The paper introduces several ways to regularize the objective function, which can significantly stabilize GAN training. These regularizers also promote fair distribution of probability mass across modes of the data generating distribution during the early training phases, providing a unified solution to the missing modes problem.

title: Richer Convolutional Features for Edge Detection
Abstract: We propose a novel edge detection method that leverages richer convolutional features (RCF). By incorporating multi-scale and multi-level information from convolutional features, our network achieves accurate image-to-image edge prediction. This is the first approach to utilize such rich convolutional features in computer vision tasks. We demonstrate superior results on various datasets, achieving an ODS F-measure of **.811** on the BSDS500 benchmark with a fast speed of **8** FPS. A faster version of our RCF achieves an ODS F-measure of **.806** at **30** FPS.
label: AI

title: Bottom-Up Top-Down Cues for Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: We introduce a novel weakly supervised approach for semantic segmentation, leveraging image-level labels and deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our method utilizes an Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework, focusing on initialization, latent posterior estimation, and parameter update. We demonstrate that saliency and attention maps serve as effective cues for initializing the EM algorithm, especially for simple images. By minimizing a combined loss function of softmax loss and KL divergence, we improve the robustness of the EM method to incorrect predictions. Extensive experiments highlight the simplicity, efficiency, and superior performance of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art results on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset.
label: AI

title: ExtremeWeather: A large-scale climate dataset for semi-supervised detection, localization, and understanding of extreme weather events
Abstract: Detecting and identifying extreme weather events within large-scale climate simulations is crucial for risk management, policy decision-making, and understanding the climate system. While supervised CNNs can classify known events effectively with abundant labeled data, existing datasets for various climate patterns are often incomplete, posing challenges for machine learning. We introduce a multichannel spatiotemporal CNN architecture for semi-supervised bounding box prediction and exploratory data analysis. This architecture leverages temporal information and unlabeled data to enhance the localization of extreme weather events, providing insights into the learned representations. We also introduce the ExtremeWeather dataset to facilitate research in this area and promote understanding and mitigation of climate change.
label: AI

title: Diverse Sampling for Self-Supervised Learning of Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: We present a novel method for learning category-level semantic segmentation solely from image-level classification tags. Our approach utilizes localization cues derived from classification-tasked convolutional networks to create a self-supervised learning process. This process automatically labels a sparse, diverse training set of points likely to belong to specific categories. Notably, our method is hyperparameter-free, modular, and allows for rapid training, achieving competitive results on the VOC 2012 segmentation benchmark. The modularity and fast training enable efficient addition of new classes for inference.
label: AI

title: Core Sampling Framework for Pixel Classification
Abstract: We introduce a novel core sampling framework for extracting contextual knowledge from Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) intermediate map responses. Our framework leverages activation maps from multiple layers as features for a separate neural network, employing transfer learning. This representation combines test data features with contextual knowledge gained from a pretrained network, enriching image understanding at the pixel level. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework using a pretrained VGG-16 model for segmentation on the BAERI and CAMVID datasets.
label: AI

title: On the Minimum Chordal Completion Polytope
Abstract: The minimum chordal completion problem (MCCP) aims to minimize the number of edges added to a graph to make it chordal. We propose a novel formulation for MCCP that avoids relying on perfect elimination orderings, as employed in previous work. Our approach introduces new families of facet-defining inequalities for cycle subgraphs and investigates the associated separation problems, highlighting the NP-hardness of separating certain key inequalities. We also establish general properties of the proposed polyhedra, demonstrating the adaptability of facets and inequalities for subgraphs and supergraphs. Numerical studies utilizing heuristic separation methods demonstrate the significant outperformance of our approach, solving numerous benchmark graphs to optimality for the first time.
label: AI

title: Learning Diverse Image Colorization
Abstract: Colorization, an inherently ambiguous problem, often produces a single most probable colorization, neglecting inherent diversity. Our goal is to model this diversity and generate multiple colorizations with long-scale spatial coordination. We utilize a variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn a low-dimensional embedding of color fields, incorporating loss terms that prevent blurry outputs and address uneven color distribution. We further develop a conditional model for the multi-modal distribution between gray-level images and color field embeddings, enabling diverse colorization through sampling. Our method outperforms standard conditional variational autoencoders (CVAE) and conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN) in generating diverse colorizations.
label: AI

title: Memory Efficient Multi-Scale Line Detector Architecture for Retinal Blood Vessel Segmentation
Abstract: We present a memory-efficient implementation of the Multi-Scale Line Detector (MSLD) algorithm for real-time retinal blood vessel detection in fundus images on a Zynq FPGA. Our architecture leverages FPGA parallelism to significantly reduce memory requirements, reuses computations, optimizes bit-width, and utilizes fully pipelined functional units for increased throughput. Compared to software implementations, our FPGA architecture achieves comparable accuracy while being 70 times faster for low-resolution images and 323 times faster for high-resolution images.
label: AI

title: Correlation Alignment for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
Abstract: We introduce CORrelation ALignment (CORAL), a simple yet effective method for unsupervised domain adaptation. CORAL aligns the second-order statistics of source and target distributions without requiring target labels. Unlike subspace manifold methods, CORAL aligns the original feature distributions, simplifying the process compared to other distribution matching techniques. CORAL demonstrates impressive performance on benchmark datasets. We present a linear transformation approach for aligning source features with target features, and for linear classifiers, we apply CORAL to the classifier weights, resulting in efficient CORAL-LDA. Finally, we extend CORAL to learn a nonlinear transformation for aligning correlations of layer activations in deep neural networks (DNNs), achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: FlowNet 2.0: Evolution of Optical Flow Estimation with Deep Networks
Abstract: FlowNet established optical flow estimation as a learnable problem, but its performance lagged behind traditional methods, particularly for small displacements and real-world data. We significantly advance end-to-end learning of optical flow, achieving substantial improvements in quality and speed. Our contributions include focusing on training data schedules, developing a stacked architecture with image warping using intermediate flow, and introducing a sub-network for small motions. FlowNet 2.0 maintains a similar speed as the original FlowNet while reducing estimation error by over 50%, achieving state-of-the-art performance with interactive frame rates. Faster variants enable optical flow computation at up to 140fps with accuracy matching the original FlowNet.
label: AI

title: Tag Prediction at Flickr: a View from the Darkroom
Abstract: Automated photo tagging has emerged as a key application of deep learning. While deep convolutional neural networks excel on standard datasets, real-world deployment necessitates addressing practical challenges. This paper outlines our efforts in developing a large-scale photo tagging system for Flickr photo search. We address crucial aspects, including tag selection relevant to users, developing lightweight high-performance models for tag prediction, and harnessing the power of noisy data for training. Our results demonstrate that training exclusively with noisy data yields performance comparable to the conventional approach of pre-training on clean data and fine-tuning. Moreover, models trained with user-generated data exhibit better fine-tuning results when a small amount of clean data is available, advocating for the use of user-generated data in large-scale systems.
label: AI

title: Knowing When to Look: Adaptive Attention via A Visual Sentinel for Image Captioning
Abstract: Attention-based neural encoder-decoder frameworks are widely employed in image captioning. However, most methods enforce visual attention for every generated word, even for non-visual words. We propose a novel adaptive attention model with a visual sentinel that decides whether to attend to the image or the sentinel at each time step. Our model dynamically chooses to attend to the image and its regions to extract meaningful information for sequential word generation. We achieve state-of-the-art results on the COCO and Flickr30K image captioning datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of our adaptive attention approach.
label: AI

title: Revisiting Winner Take All (WTA) Hashing for Sparse Datasets
Abstract: WTA (Winner Take All) hashing, commonly used in large-scale vision applications, leverages comparative reasoning for accuracy improvements. However, its discriminative power is limited by dataset sparsity. We identify this issue and propose a solution based on Densification, provably addressing the sparsity problem. Our experiments demonstrate that Densified WTA Hashing consistently and significantly outperforms Vanilla WTA in image classification and retrieval tasks.
label: AI

title: FLIC: Fast Linear Iterative Clustering with Active Search
Abstract: Simple Linear Iterative Clustering (SLIC) remains a popular over-segmentation tool due to its efficiency and simplicity. However, its boundary adaptation is suboptimal due to enforced spatial similarity, and its convergence rate is hindered by fixed search regions and separate assignment and update steps. We propose an alternative approach that overcomes these limitations. Each pixel actively searches for its corresponding segment with the help of neighboring pixels, enabling region coherence without compromising boundary adaptation. By jointly performing assignment and update steps, our method achieves high convergence rates. Extensive evaluations on the Berkeley segmentation benchmark demonstrate the superior performance of our approach across various metrics, with the lowest time cost among existing methods.
label: AI

title: In the transmission of information, the great potential of model-based coding with the SP theory of intelligence
Abstract: Model-based coding, originally proposed by John Pierce in 1961, holds immense potential for reducing information transmission volume without loss, particularly in large data and lossless communication. The advantage arises from both the transmitter and receiver possessing a grammar for the data type, enabling efficient transmission with minimal information exchange. Preliminary trials show that model-based coding significantly reduces information volume compared to traditional compression methods. Recent advancements in "SP theory of intelligence" and the "SP computer model" enable the realization of three crucial functions: unsupervised grammar learning, encoding by the transmitter, and decoding by the receiver. This opens doors for practical application in transmitting large datasets within reasonable timescales.
label: AI

title: Video Ladder Networks
Abstract: We introduce the Video Ladder Network (VLN) for efficient future video frame generation. VLN is an encoder-decoder model augmented with recurrent and feedforward lateral connections at all layers, forming lateral recurrent residual blocks. The recurrent connections enable the decoder to leverage temporal summaries generated from all encoder layers, alleviating the top layer's burden of modeling lower-level details. We extend VLN to incorporate ResNet-style residual blocks in the encoder and decoder, further enhancing prediction accuracy. VLN, trained in a self-supervised manner on the Moving MNIST dataset, achieves competitive results with a simple structure and fast inference.
label: AI

title: Deep Stereo Matching with Dense CRF Priors
Abstract: Stereo reconstruction from rectified images has been re-examined within the context of deep learning. Deep CNNs for obtaining patch-wise matching cost volumes have yielded state-of-the-art results on datasets like Middlebury and Kitti. Integrating this cost into traditional stereo pipelines significantly improves reconstruction quality. However, these pipelines often require hand-engineered post-processing steps for regularization and noise reduction. We demonstrate a holistic approach by training a fully end-to-end network that incorporates regularization through a densely connected Conditional Random Field (CRF) as a prior for inter-pixel interactions. Our approach outperforms alternative end-to-end networks and compares favorably to more hand-engineered methods on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
label: AI

title: Deep Neural Networks for No-Reference and Full-Reference Image Quality Assessment
Abstract: We present a deep neural network-based approach for image quality assessment (IQA). Our end-to-end network comprises ten convolutional layers, five pooling layers for feature extraction, and two fully connected layers for regression, making it significantly deeper than related IQA models. Notably, our network can be adapted for both no-reference (NR) and full-reference (FR) IQA settings and allows for joint learning of local quality and weights. Our approach is purely data-driven, relying solely on data and avoiding hand-crafted features or domain knowledge. Evaluated on the LIVE, CISQ, TID2013, and LIVE In the wild databases, our approach surpasses state-of-the-art NR and FR IQA methods. Cross-database evaluations demonstrate the network's high generalizability and robustness.
label: AI

title: Cluster-Wise Ratio Tests for Fast Camera Localization
Abstract: Feature point matching for camera localization faces scalability challenges. Even with locally unique feature descriptors associated with 3D scene points, similar or repeated features become prevalent with increased coverage. This leads to overly restrictive distance ratio-tests, rejecting many valid matches. We propose a coarse-to-fine strategy using conservative approximations of robust local ratio-tests computed efficiently through global approximate k-nearest neighbor search. These forward matches are treated as votes in camera pose space, prioritizing back-matching within candidate pose clusters and leveraging feature co-visibility from the 3D model camera pose graph. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art camera localization results on popular benchmarks, outperforming methods with complex data structures and restrictive pose assumptions. Diagnostic analyses on a challenging dataset confirm the approach's adaptability to large-scale image localization.
label: AI

title: MarioQA: Answering Questions by Watching Gameplay Videos
Abstract: We present a framework for analyzing VideoQA models using customizable synthetic datasets automatically generated from gameplay videos. Existing VideoQA models are often evaluated on datasets requiring high-level reasoning or accessible through single-frame inferences, hindering the assessment of model capacity and flexibility. We focus on understanding temporal relationships between video events, crucial for VideoQA problem-solving. Our framework leverages Super Mario Bros. gameplay videos to create a synthetic VideoQA dataset with varying levels of reasoning complexity. Using this dataset, we demonstrate the importance of well-constructed datasets for learning effective models and enhancing overall performance. |||
label: AI

title: Binary Subspace Coding for Query-by-Image Video Retrieval
Abstract: Query-by-image video retrieval (QBIVR) has recently gained significant research interest. However, existing methods often represent a video by aggregating or projecting all frames into a single data point, leading to potential information loss. This paper presents an efficient QBIVR framework for effective and efficient video search using image queries. The framework defines a similarity-preserving distance metric between an image and its orthogonal projection in the video subspace, which can be transformed into a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem. Additionally, two asymmetric hashing schemes are proposed to enhance the efficiency of solving the MIPS problem, bridging the domain gap between images and videos. The first approach, termed Inner-product Binary Coding (IBC), preserves the inner relationships of images and videos in a common Hamming space. To further improve retrieval efficiency, a Bilinear Binary Coding (BBC) approach is introduced, employing compact bilinear projections instead of a single large projection matrix. Extensive experiments on four real-world video datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches compared to state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Fine-grained Recurrent Neural Networks for Automatic Prostate Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
Abstract: Boundary incompleteness poses significant challenges for automatic prostate segmentation in ultrasound images. Shape priors can provide valuable guidance in estimating missing boundaries; however, traditional shape models often suffer from handcrafted descriptors and local information loss during the fitting process. This paper introduces a novel framework that seamlessly integrates feature extraction and shape prior exploration to estimate complete boundaries sequentially. The framework comprises three key modules: 1) Serialization of static 2D prostate ultrasound images into dynamic sequences, enabling sequential shape prior exploration and prostate shape prediction. Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are used to learn shape priors, effectively addressing boundary incompleteness. 2) A multi-view fusion strategy to merge shape predictions obtained from different perspectives, mitigating biases caused by varying serialization methods. 3) Integration of the RNN core into a multiscale Auto-Context scheme for successive refinement of the shape prediction map details. Extensive validation on challenging prostate ultrasound images demonstrates the framework's ability to bridge severe boundary incompleteness and achieve superior performance in prostate boundary delineation compared to advanced methods. The approach's generalizability allows for extension to other medical image segmentation tasks where boundary incompleteness is a significant challenge.
label: AI

title: Learning to Detect Multiple Photographic Defects
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of simultaneously detecting multiple photographic defects, aiming to identify the presence, severity, and potential locations of common defects related to color, noise, blur, and composition. Automatic detection of these defects can provide users with suggestions for photo improvement without manual correction attempts, and assist in selecting higher-quality photos while filtering out those with severe defects during photo curation and summarization. To investigate this problem, a large-scale dataset of user annotations on seven common photographic defects was collected, enabling algorithm evaluation based on consistency with human judgments. The new dataset allows the problem to be formulated as a multi-task learning problem, enabling training of a multi-column deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to simultaneously predict the severity of all defects. Unlike existing single-defect estimation methods that rely on low-level statistics and may fail on natural photographs, the proposed model understands image content and quality at a higher level. Experimental results demonstrate significantly higher consistency of the model's predictions with human judgments compared to low-level methods and baseline CNN models. The model also outperforms the average human performance from a user study.
label: AI

title: Automatic Event Detection for Signal-based Surveillance
Abstract: Signal-based surveillance systems, such as Closed Circuits Televisions (CCTV), are widely installed in public places to detect events of security interest and contribute to public safety. Despite these systems' reliance on human monitoring, a number of automatic techniques have been proposed for data analysis. This article provides an overview of automatic surveillance event detection techniques. Although popular in research, the problem remains challenging for real-world deployment. The challenges stem from both detection techniques, such as signal processing and machine learning, and experimental design factors, including data collection, evaluation protocols, and ground-truth annotation. The article concludes by suggesting that multi-disciplinary research is crucial to achieve a solution to this problem.
label: AI

title: AI Researchers, Video Games Are Your Friends!
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) researchers should consider video games as ideal testbeds for their work, while video game developers should explore AI for its potential to enable new game types. This chapter presents a compelling case for both propositions. It examines the benefits of video games for AI, highlighting how general video game playing serves as an ideal testbed for artificial general intelligence research. The chapter also explores the potential of AI for video games, envisioning future game experiences with significantly more advanced AI. This chapter is based on a keynote presentation at IJCCI 2015 and is written for a broad audience.
label: AI

title: Superpixels: An Evaluation of the State-of-the-Art
Abstract: Superpixels group perceptually similar pixels into visually meaningful entities, reducing the number of primitives for subsequent processing steps. These properties have led to widespread attention for superpixel algorithms since their introduction in 2003. Today, publicly available superpixel algorithms have become standard tools in low-level vision. However, the rapidly growing number of algorithms and varying experimental setups hindered the development of a unifying benchmark. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of 28 state-of-the-art superpixel algorithms using a benchmark designed for fair comparison and new insights relevant for applications. The paper explicitly discusses parameter optimization, the importance of strict connectivity enforcement, and extends well-known metrics to summarize algorithm performance independent of the number of generated superpixels, overcoming a major limitation of existing benchmarks. Additionally, the paper analyzes runtime, robustness against noise, blur, and affine transformations, implementation details, and visual quality aspects. Finally, an overall ranking of superpixel algorithms is presented, redefining the state-of-the-art and enabling researchers to easily select appropriate algorithms and implementations. The corresponding implementations are publicly available as part of the benchmark at davidstutz.de/projects/superpixel-benchmark/.
label: AI

title: Object Classification with Joint Projection and Low-rank Dictionary Learning
Abstract: For object classification systems, large intra-class variability due to factors such as lighting, occlusion, and corruption in limited sample sets presents significant challenges for real-world applications. Existing methods often fail when training samples are heavily occluded, corrupted, or exhibit significant illumination or viewpoint variations. Furthermore, most methods, especially deep learning-based ones, require large training sets to achieve satisfactory recognition performance. While using pre-trained networks on a generic large-scale dataset and fine-tuning them to the target dataset is a common practice, this approach may not be effective when the content of the base and target datasets significantly differs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a joint projection and low-rank dictionary learning method using dual graph constraints (JP-LRDL). The joint learning method learns features that enable better dictionary learning from data with large intra-class variability. Specifically, a structured class-specific dictionary is learned, and discrimination is further enhanced by imposing a graph constraint on the coding coefficients, maximizing intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Additionally, low-rank and structural incoherence constraints are enforced on sub-dictionaries to promote compactness, robustness to variations and outliers, and reduce redundancy. The introduction of a projection graph into the framework preserves the intrinsic structure of data while penalizing unfavorable relationships among training samples, significantly enhancing the discriminative ability of the projection matrix and making the method robust to small-sized and high-dimensional datasets.
label: AI

title: Towards the Limit of Network Quantization
Abstract: Network quantization is a network compression technique that reduces redundancy in deep neural networks by quantizing network parameter values, thereby saving storage space. This paper focuses on designing network quantization schemes that minimize performance loss due to quantization subject to a compression ratio constraint. An analysis of the quantitative relationship between quantization errors and the neural network loss function reveals that the Hessian-weighted distortion measure is locally the optimal objective function for optimizing network quantization. Based on this finding, Hessian-weighted k-means clustering is proposed for clustering network parameters for quantization. When optimal variable-length binary codes, such as Huffman codes, are employed for further compression, the network quantization problem can be related to the entropy-constrained scalar quantization (ECSQ) problem in information theory. Consequently, two ECSQ solutions for network quantization are proposed: uniform quantization and an iterative solution similar to Lloyd's algorithm. Experiments demonstrate that compression ratios of 51.25, 22.17, and 40.65 are achievable for LeNet, 32-layer ResNet, and AlexNet, respectively, using simple uniform quantization followed by Huffman coding.
label: AI

title: Explaining Radiological Emphysema Subtypes with Unsupervised Texture Prototypes: MESA COPD Study
Abstract: Pulmonary emphysema is traditionally classified into three subtypes based on distinct radiological appearances on computed tomography (CT) scans, aiding in the diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Automated texture-based quantification of emphysema subtypes has been successfully implemented using supervised learning of these three subtypes. This work demonstrates that unsupervised learning on a large heterogeneous database of CT scans can generate texture prototypes that are visually homogeneous, distinct, reproducible across subjects, and capable of accurately predicting the three standard radiological subtypes. These texture prototypes enable automated labeling of lung volumes, opening avenues for new interpretations of lung CT scans with finer subtyping of emphysema.
label: AI

title: ROAM: a Rich Object Appearance Model with Application to Rotoscoping
Abstract: Rotoscoping, the detailed delineation of scene elements throughout a video shot, is a laborious yet crucial task in professional post-production pipelines. While pixel-wise segmentation techniques can assist in this task, professional rotoscoping tools rely on parametric curves that provide artists with better interactive control over the definition, editing, and manipulation of segments of interest. Adhering to this prevalent rotoscoping paradigm, this paper proposes a novel framework for capturing and tracking the visual aspect of an arbitrary object in a scene, given an initial closed outline of the object. The model combines a collection of local foreground/background appearance models distributed along the outline, a global appearance model of the enclosed object, and a set of distinctive foreground landmarks. This rich appearance model enables simple initialization, efficient iterative optimization with exact minimization at each step, and online adaptation in videos. Qualitative and quantitative comparisons with tools based on dynamic segmentation with a closed curve or pixel-wise binary labeling demonstrate the framework's merit.
label: AI

title: Authoring image decompositions with generative models
Abstract: This paper extends traditional intrinsic image decompositions to incorporate additional layers beyond albedo and shading. Obtaining data for learning a multi-layer decomposition is challenging; therefore, the paper focuses on learning to decompose an image into layers that resemble specific characteristics by authoring generative models for each layer using proxy examples that represent ideal representations. For example, Mondrian images for albedo, rendered 3D primitives for shading, and material swatches for shading detail. The method generates image layers, one from each model, that explain the image. This approach relies on innovations in generative models for images. The paper introduces a Convolutional Variational Auto Encoder (conv-VAE), a novel VAE architecture capable of reconstructing high-fidelity images. This approach is general and does not require layers to have a physical interpretation.
label: AI

title: ArtTrack: Articulated Multi-person Tracking in the Wild
Abstract: This paper presents an approach for articulated tracking of multiple people in unconstrained videos. The starting point is a model resembling existing architectures for single-frame pose estimation but significantly faster. This is achieved in two ways: 1) Simplifying and sparsifying the body-part relationship graph and leveraging recent methods for faster inference. 2) Offloading a substantial portion of computation onto a feed-forward convolutional architecture that can detect and associate body joints of the same person even in cluttered environments. This model generates proposals for body joint locations and formulates articulated tracking as spatio-temporal grouping of these proposals. This allows for solving the association problem for all people in the scene jointly by propagating evidence from strong detections through time and enforcing constraints that each proposal can be assigned to only one person. Results are reported on a public MPII Human Pose benchmark and a new MPII Video Pose dataset of image sequences with multiple people. The model achieves state-of-the-art results while using a fraction of time and leverages temporal information to improve state-of-the-art performance in crowded scenes.
label: AI

title: ImageNet pre-trained models with batch normalization
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) pre-trained on ImageNet are the backbone of most state-of-the-art approaches. This paper presents a new set of pre-trained models with popular state-of-the-art architectures for the Caffe framework. The initial release includes Residual Networks (ResNets) with generation scripts, as well as batch-normalization variants of AlexNet and VGG19. All models outperform previous models with the same architecture.
