The models and training code are available at http://www.inf-cv.uni-jena.de/Research/CNN+Models.html and https://github.com/cvjena/cnn-models.
label: AI

title: On-Demand Learning for Deep Image Restoration
Abstract: Machine learning approaches to image restoration offer great promise; however, current methods risk training models that perform well only for a specific level of image corruption difficulty, such as a certain level of noise or blur. This paper examines the weaknesses of conventional "fixated" models and demonstrates the non-trivial nature of training general models to handle arbitrary levels of corruption. The paper proposes an on-demand learning algorithm for training image restoration models with deep convolutional neural networks. The key idea is to exploit a feedback mechanism to self-generate training instances where they are most needed, leading to models that generalize across difficulty levels. On four restoration tasks—image inpainting, pixel interpolation, image deblurring, and image denoising—and three diverse datasets, the approach consistently outperforms both the status quo training procedure and curriculum learning alternatives.
label: AI

title: Human-In-The-Loop Person Re-Identification
Abstract: Current person re-identification (re-id) methods assume that (1) pre-labeled training data is available for every camera pair, and (2) the gallery size for re-identification is moderate. These assumptions scale poorly to real-world applications when the camera network size increases and the gallery size becomes large. Human verification of automatic model-ranked re-id results becomes necessary. This work introduces a novel human-in-the-loop re-id model based on Human Verification Incremental Learning (HVIL), which does not require any pre-labeled training data to learn a model, making it readily scalable to new camera pairs. The HVIL model learns cumulatively from human feedback to provide instant improvement to re-id ranking for each probe on-the-fly, enabling the model to scale to large gallery sizes. Furthermore, a Regularized Metric Ensemble Learning (RMEL) model is formulated to combine a series of incrementally learned HVIL models into a single ensemble model for use when human feedback becomes unavailable.
label: AI

title: Highly Efficient Regression for Scalable Person Re-Identification
Abstract: Existing person re-identification (re-id) models struggle to scale to the large amounts of data required in real-world applications due to: (1) Complexity: They employ complex models for optimal performance, resulting in high computational costs for training at a large scale. (2) Inadaptability: Once trained, they are not suitable for incremental updates to incorporate new data. This work proposes a truly scalable solution to re-id by addressing both problems. Specifically, a Highly Efficient Regression (HER) model is formulated by embedding Fisher's criterion into a ridge regression model for very fast re-id model learning with scalable memory/storage usage. Notably, the HER model supports faster-than-real-time incremental model updates, enabling real-time active learning in re-id with human-in-the-loop. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this simple and fast model not only outperforms state-of-the-art re-id methods but is also more scalable to large data, offering additional benefits for active learning and reducing human labeling effort in re-id deployment.
label: AI

title: Classification With an Edge: Improving Semantic Image Segmentation with Boundary Detection
Abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end trainable deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) for semantic segmentation with built-in awareness of semantically meaningful boundaries. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental remote sensing task, and most state-of-the-art methods rely on DCNNs. Their success stems from deep networks' ability to learn contextual information over large windows (receptive fields). However, this comes at the cost of reduced effective spatial resolution, leading to blurry object boundaries. This paper proposes to counter this effect by combining semantic segmentation with semantically informed edge detection, making class boundaries explicit in the model. First, a comparatively simple, memory-efficient model is constructed by adding boundary detection to the SegNet encoder-decoder architecture. Second, boundary detection is included in FCN-type models, setting up a high-end classifier ensemble. The paper demonstrates that boundary detection significantly improves semantic segmentation with CNNs. The high-end ensemble achieves over 90% overall accuracy on the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark.
label: AI

title: Stereo image de-fencing using smartphones
Abstract: Conventional approaches to image de-fencing have been limited to using only image data from adjacent frames of captured video of an approximately static scene. This paper presents a method for harnessing disparity using a stereo pair of fenced images to detect fence pixels. Tourists and amateur photographers commonly carry smartphones/phablets that can capture short video sequences of fenced scenes. The paper models the formation of the occluded frames in the captured video and proposes an optimization framework to estimate the de-fenced image using the total variation prior to regularize the ill-posed problem.
label: AI

title: Message Passing Multi-Agent GANs
Abstract: Communication and intelligence sharing among agents are crucial for achieving Artificial General Intelligence. As a first step towards this challenge, this paper introduces a novel framework for image generation: Message Passing Multi-Agent Generative Adversarial Networks (MPM GANs). While GANs have proven effective for image generation and other tasks, they have been mostly limited to single generator-discriminator networks. This paper demonstrates the creation of multi-agent GANs that communicate through message passing to achieve better image generation. The objectives of the individual agents in this framework are twofold: a cooperation objective and a competing objective. The cooperation objective ensures that the message sharing mechanism guides other generators to generate better images than themselves, while the competing objective encourages each generator to outperform its counterparts. The messages shared by these GANs in various scenarios are analyzed and visualized. Quantitatively, the message sharing formulation serves as a regularizer for adversarial training. Qualitatively, the different generators capture distinct traits of the underlying data distribution.
label: AI

title: Point Pair Feature based Object Detection for Random Bin Picking
Abstract: Point pair features are a popular representation for free-form 3D object detection and pose estimation. This paper investigates their performance in an industrial random bin picking context. A new method for generating representative synthetic datasets is proposed, allowing for the examination of the influence of high clutter levels and the presence of self-similar features, typical in this application. The paper provides an overview of existing solutions, discussing their strengths and weaknesses. A simple heuristic method for drastically reducing computational complexity is introduced, resulting in improved robustness, speed, and accuracy compared to the naive approach. |||
label: AI

title: Panoramic Structure from Motion via Geometric Relationship Detection
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of Structure from Motion (SfM) for indoor panoramic image streams, a task notoriously challenging even for state-of-the-art methods due to the scarcity of textures and minimal parallax. The core idea is the fusion of single-view and multi-view reconstruction techniques through the detection of geometric relationships, specifically identifying coplanar 2D lines in 3D space. Rough geometric estimations, derived from an image-to-normal deep network, are sufficient for detecting these relationships. The discovered relationships provide precise geometric constraints within our line-based linear SfM formulation. A constrained linear least squares method is employed to reconstruct a 3D model and camera motions, followed by bundle adjustment. Our algorithm has been validated on challenging datasets, surpassing the performance of various state-of-the-art reconstruction techniques.
label: AI

title: Deep Image Category Discovery using a Transferred Similarity Function
Abstract: Automatically discovering image categories in unlabeled natural images is a key objective in unsupervised learning. However, this task is highly complex, and even humans rely on extensive prior knowledge to define visual categories. This paper leverages prior knowledge to facilitate the discovery of image categories. We introduce a novel end-to-end network that functions as a clustering network, mapping unlabeled images to categories. We propose that this network can be trained using contrastive loss, solely based on weak binary pairwise constraints. These binary constraints can be acquired from datasets in other domains and employed as transferred similarity functions, mimicking a simple knowledge transfer process. To demonstrate the concept, we first evaluate our approach on the MNIST dataset using predicted similarities trained on Omniglot, achieving a remarkable 99% accuracy, significantly outperforming clustering-based methods. Subsequently, we assess the discovery performance on Cifar-10, STL-10, and ImageNet, demonstrating both state-of-the-art accuracy and scalability to diverse large natural images.
label: AI

title: Cancerous Nuclei Detection and Scoring in Breast Cancer Histopathological Images
Abstract: Early detection and prognosis of breast cancer are achievable through histopathological grading of biopsy specimens. This research focuses on detecting and grading nuclear pleomorphism in histopathological breast cancer images. Our proposed method comprises three internal steps. Firstly, color unmixing of H&E is performed during preprocessing. Secondly, nuclei boundaries are extracted, incorporating the centers of cancerous nuclei detected by applying morphological operations and a Difference of Gaussian filter on the preprocessed image. Lastly, segmented nuclei are scored to determine one parameter of the Nottingham grading system for breast cancer. In this approach, features for nuclear pleomorphism scoring include nuclei area, chromatin density, contour regularity, and nucleoli presence. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm, achieving an accuracy of 86.6%, significantly advances the detection of cancerous nuclei compared to existing methods in the relevant literature.
label: AI

title: Turning an Urban Scene Video into a Cinemagraph
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm that transforms regular videos capturing urban scenes into high-quality endless animations known as Cinemagraphs. Traditionally, creating Cinemagraphs requires a static camera in a carefully configured scene. However, this task becomes challenging for regular videos with a moving camera and objects. Our approach initially warps an input video to the viewpoint of a reference camera. Based on the warped video, we propose effective temporal analysis algorithms to identify regions with static geometry and dynamic appearance, where geometric modeling is reliable and visually appealing animations can be generated. Finally, the algorithm applies a sequence of video processing techniques to produce a Cinemagraph movie. We have extensively tested our proposed approach on numerous challenging real scenes. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to automatically generate Cinemagraph animations from regular movies in the wild.
label: AI

title: Multi-way Particle Swarm Fusion
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel MAP inference framework for Markov Random Field (MRF) in parallel computing environments. This inference framework, named Swarm Fusion, is a natural generalization of the Fusion Move method. Each thread (in the context of multi-threading environments) maintains and updates a solution. At each iteration, a thread can generate an arbitrary number of solution proposals and concurrently retrieve an arbitrary number of solutions from other threads to perform multi-way fusion in updating its solution. This framework is highly versatile, encompassing popular existing inference techniques like alpha-expansion, fusion move, parallel alpha-expansion, and hierarchical fusion as special cases. We have evaluated the effectiveness of our approach against competing methods on three problems of varying complexity, namely the stereo, the optical flow, and the layered depthmap estimation problems.
label: AI

title: Deep Pyramidal Residual Networks with Separated Stochastic Depth
Abstract: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) achieve high accuracy in general object recognition. Notably, ResNet and its advancements have broken the lowest error rate records. This paper proposes a method to effectively combine two ResNet improvements, ResDrop and PyramidNet. Our analysis confirms that the proposed network surpasses conventional methods. On CIFAR-100, our proposed network achieved an error rate of 16.18%, outperforming PyramidNet (18.29%) and ResNeXt (17.31%).
label: AI

title: Deep Blur Mapping: Exploiting High-Level Semantics by Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: The human visual system excels at detecting local blur in visual images, but the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. Traditional blur definitions, such as reduction in high-frequency energy and loss of phase coherence at localized features, have fundamental limitations. For instance, they struggle to discriminate flat regions from blurred ones. We propose that high-level semantic information is crucial for successfully identifying local blur. Consequently, we employ deep neural networks, renowned for their ability to learn high-level features, and present the first end-to-end local blur mapping algorithm based on a fully convolutional network. Through an empirical analysis of various network architectures with different depths and design philosophies, we demonstrate that high-level features from deeper layers play a more significant role than low-level features from shallower layers in resolving challenging ambiguities for this task. We test the proposed method on a standard blur detection benchmark and show that it significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art (ODS F-score of 0.853). Furthermore, we explore the application of the generated blur maps in three domains: blur region segmentation, blur degree estimation, and blur magnification.
label: AI

title: Deep Multi-Modal Image Correspondence Learning
Abstract: Inferring correspondences between images from different modalities is a crucial perceptual ability that enables humans to understand and recognize cross-modal concepts. This paper focuses on a specific instance of this problem, involving matching photographs of building interiors with their corresponding floorplans. This poses a significant challenge due to the stylistic difference in appearance between a floorplan, a stylized architectural drawing, and a color photograph. Additionally, individual photographs capture only a portion of a floorplan (e.g., kitchen, bathroom, and living room). We propose utilizing various neural network architectures for this task, trained and evaluated on a novel large-scale dataset comprising 5 million floorplan images and 80 million associated photographs. Experimental evaluation reveals that our neural network architectures can identify visual cues leading to reliable matches across these distinct modalities. Notably, the trained networks even outperform human subjects in several challenging image matching scenarios. Our findings suggest that neural networks effectively handle perceptual tasks that require extensive reasoning, even for humans to solve.
label: AI

title: Deep Metric Learning via Facility Location
Abstract: Learning the representation and similarity metric in an end-to-end fashion with deep networks has yielded impressive results for clustering and retrieval. However, these recent approaches still suffer from performance degradation due to the local metric training procedure, which is unaware of the global structure of the embedding space. This paper proposes a global metric learning scheme for optimizing the deep metric embedding with the learnable clustering function and the clustering metric (NMI) within a novel structured prediction framework. Our experiments on CUB200-2011, Cars196, and Stanford online products datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on both clustering and retrieval tasks, measured using NMI and Recall@K evaluation metrics.
label: AI

title: DenseReg: Fully Convolutional Dense Shape Regression In-the-Wild
Abstract: This paper proposes learning a mapping from image pixels to a dense template grid using a fully convolutional network. We formulate this task as a regression problem and train our network using manually annotated facial landmarks "in-the-wild". These landmarks establish a dense correspondence field between a 3D object template and the input image, serving as the ground-truth for training our regression system. We demonstrate that combining ideas from semantic segmentation with regression networks yields a highly accurate "quantized regression" architecture. Our system, named DenseReg, enables the estimation of dense image-to-template correspondences in a fully convolutional manner. This network provides useful correspondence information independently, while when used as an initialization for Statistical Deformable Models, it significantly outperforms the current state-of-the-art on the challenging 300W benchmark for landmark localization. We thoroughly evaluate our method on various facial analysis tasks and provide qualitative results for dense human body correspondence. Our code is available at http://alpguler.com/DenseReg.html along with supplementary materials.
label: AI

title: Online Localization and Prediction of Actions and Interactions
Abstract: This paper presents a person-centric and online approach to the challenging problem of localizing and predicting actions and interactions in videos. Typically, localization or recognition is performed offline, where all frames in the video are processed together. This prevents timely localization and prediction of actions and interactions, a critical requirement for many tasks including surveillance and human-machine interaction. Our approach involves estimating human poses at each frame and training discriminative appearance models using the superpixels within the pose bounding boxes. As pose estimation per frame is inherently noisy, we calculate the conditional probability of pose hypotheses at the current time-step (frame) based on pose estimations in the current frame and their consistency with poses in previous frames. Subsequently, both superpixel and pose-based foreground likelihoods are utilized to infer the location of actors at each time instant through a Conditional Random Field. The issue of visual drift is addressed by updating appearance models and refining poses using motion smoothness on joint locations in an online manner. For online prediction of action (interaction) confidences, we propose an approach based on Structural SVM operating on short video segments. This approach is trained with the objective of increasing action or interaction confidence as time progresses. Finally, we quantify the performance of both detection and prediction together, analyzing how prediction accuracy varies as a function of observed action (interaction) at different detection performance levels. Our experiments on several datasets suggest that despite using only a few frames to localize actions (interactions) at each time instant, we achieve results competitive with state-of-the-art offline methods.
label: AI

title: Who is Mistaken?
Abstract: Recognizing when individuals hold false beliefs is crucial for understanding their actions. We introduce the novel problem of identifying instances where people in abstract scenes harbor incorrect beliefs. We present a dataset of scenes, each visually depicting an 8-frame story in which a character holds a mistaken belief. We then create a representation of characters' beliefs for two tasks in human action understanding: predicting who is mistaken and when they are mistaken. Experiments indicate that our method for identifying mistaken characters outperforms simple baselines in these tasks. Diagnostic analyses of our model suggest it learns important cues for recognizing mistaken beliefs, such as gaze. We believe models of people's beliefs will have numerous applications in action understanding, robotics, and healthcare.
label: AI

title: General models for rational cameras and the case of two-slit projections
Abstract: The rational camera model, recently introduced in [19], provides a general methodology for studying abstract nonlinear imaging systems and their multi-view geometry. This paper expands upon this framework to investigate "physical realizations" of rational cameras. Specifically, we provide an explicit account of the mapping between physical visual rays and image points (missing in the original description), enabling us to derive simple analytical expressions for direct and inverse projections. We also consider "primitive" camera models, which are orbits under the action of various projective transformations, leading to a general concept of intrinsic parameters. While the methodology is general, we illustrate it concretely through an in-depth study of two-slit cameras, modeled using pairs of linear projections. This simple analytical form allows us to describe models for the corresponding primitive cameras, introduce intrinsic parameters with clear geometric meaning, and define an epipolar tensor characterizing two-view correspondences. This, in turn, leads to novel algorithms for structure from motion and self-calibration.
label: AI

title: A method for the segmentation of images based on thresholding and applied to vesicular textures
Abstract: In image processing, segmentation involves partitioning an image into multiple sets of pixels, known as super-pixels. Each super-pixel is characterized by a label or parameter. We propose a method for determining super-pixels based on image thresholding. This approach is particularly useful for studying images exhibiting vesicular textures.
label: AI

title: Pyramid Scene Parsing Network
Abstract: Scene parsing poses significant challenges for unrestricted open vocabulary and diverse scenes. This paper exploits the capability of global context information through different-region-based context aggregation via our pyramid pooling module, along with the proposed pyramid scene parsing network (PSPNet). Our global prior representation effectively produces high-quality results for scene parsing, while PSPNet provides a superior framework for pixel-level prediction tasks. Our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on various datasets. It secured first place in the ImageNet scene parsing challenge 2016, the PASCAL VOC 2012 benchmark, and the Cityscapes benchmark. A single PSPNet achieves a new record of mIoU accuracy 85.4% on PASCAL VOC 2012 and an accuracy of 80.2% on Cityscapes.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning of Robotic Tasks without a Simulator using Strong and Weak Human Supervision
Abstract: We propose a scheme for training a computerized agent to perform complex human tasks, such as highway steering. This scheme is designed to mimic a natural learning process where a human instructor teaches a computerized trainee. The learning process consists of five elements: (i) unsupervised feature learning, (ii) supervised imitation learning, (iii) supervised reward induction, (iv) supervised safety module construction, and (v) reinforcement learning. We implemented the last four elements of the scheme using deep convolutional networks and successfully created a computerized agent capable of autonomous highway steering within the well-known racing game Assetto Corsa. We demonstrate that the use of the last four elements is crucial for effectively executing the steering task using vision alone, without access to driving simulator internals, and operating in wall-clock time. This is achieved through the introduction of a safety network, a novel approach for preventing catastrophic mistakes during the reinforcement learning stage.
label: AI

title: Multi-Label Image Classification with Regional Latent Semantic Dependencies
Abstract: Deep convolution neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated advanced performance in single-label image classification, and various advancements have been made to apply CNN methods to multi-label image classification, which requires annotating objects, attributes, scene categories, etc., in a single shot. Recent state-of-the-art approaches for multi-label image classification exploit label dependencies in an image at the global level, significantly improving labeling capabilities. However, predicting small objects and visual concepts remains challenging due to the limited discrimination of global visual features. This paper proposes a Regional Latent Semantic Dependencies model (RLSD) to address this problem. The utilized model includes a fully convolutional localization architecture to identify regions potentially containing multiple highly dependent labels. These localized regions are then sent to recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to characterize latent semantic dependencies at the regional level. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed model achieves the best performance compared to state-of-the-art models, particularly for predicting small objects occurring in images. Additionally, we set up an upper bound model (RLSD+ft-RPN) using bounding box coordinates during training. Experimental results indicate that our RLSD model can approach this upper bound without using bounding box annotations, making it more practical for real-world applications.
label: AI

title: End-to-end Learning of Driving Models from Large-scale Video Datasets
Abstract: Robust perception-action models should be learned from training data with diverse visual appearances and realistic behaviors. However, current approaches to deep visuomotor policy learning have been generally limited to in-situ models learned from a single vehicle or a simulation environment. We advocate learning a generic vehicle motion model from large-scale crowd-sourced video data and develop an end-to-end trainable architecture for predicting a distribution over future vehicle egomotion from instantaneous monocular camera observations and previous vehicle state. Our model incorporates a novel FCN-LSTM architecture, which can be learned from large-scale crowd-sourced vehicle action data, and leverages available scene segmentation side tasks to improve performance under a privileged learning paradigm.
label: AI

title: Joint Visual Denoising and Classification using Deep Learning
Abstract: Visual restoration and recognition are traditionally addressed in a pipeline fashion, i.e., denoising followed by classification. However, observing correlations between these tasks, for example, clearer images leading to better categorization and vice versa, we propose a joint framework for visual restoration and recognition of handwritten images, inspired by advancements in deep autoencoder and multi-modality learning. Our model is a 3-pathway deep architecture with a hidden-layer representation shared by multiple inputs and outputs, and each branch can be composed of a multi-layer deep model. Thus, visual restoration and classification can be unified using shared representation through non-linear mapping, and model parameters can be learned via backpropagation. Using MNIST and USPS data corrupted with structured noise, our proposed framework achieves at least 20% improvement in classification compared to separate pipelines, as well as clearer recovered images. The noise model and reproducible source code are available at {\\url{https://github.com/ganggit/jointmodel}}.
label: AI

title: Skin Cancer Detection and Tracking using Data Synthesis and Deep Learning
Abstract: Dense object detection and temporal tracking are essential across application domains ranging from people-tracking to the analysis of satellite imagery over time. The detection and tracking of malignant skin cancers and benign moles pose a particularly challenging problem due to the general uniformity of large skin patches, the fact that skin lesions vary little in appearance, and the relatively small amount of data available. We introduce a novel data synthesis technique that merges images of individual skin lesions with full-body images and heavily augments them to generate significant amounts of data. We construct a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based system, trained on this synthetic data, and demonstrate superior performance to traditional detection and tracking techniques. Additionally, we compare our system to humans trained with simple criteria. Our system is intended for potential clinical use to enhance the capabilities of healthcare providers. While domain-specific, we believe the methods invoked in this work will be useful in applying CNNs across domains that suffer from limited data availability. |||
label: AI

title: Word Recognition with Deep Conditional Random Fields
Abstract: Handwritten word recognition remains a key challenge in document analysis. Traditional methods rely on hand-crafted features, which struggle with new datasets. Deep learning, with its ability to learn features directly from raw data, has emerged as a promising solution. However, word recognition is inherently sequential, requiring the modeling of character relationships. This paper proposes the use of deep Conditional Random Fields (deep CRFs) for word recognition, integrating feature learning and sequence labeling into a unified framework. The deep structure is pre-trained using stacked restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) for feature learning and optimized with an online learning algorithm. Evaluations on two datasets demonstrate significant performance gains over existing methods. The source code is available at https://github.com/ganggit/deepCRFs.
label: AI

title: Algorithmic Songwriting with ALYSIA
Abstract: ALYSIA, an automated lyrical songwriting application, leverages a machine learning model based on Random Forests to predict pitch and rhythm. The paper outlines ALYSIA's success in predicting musical elements and describes its use in generating original pop songs that were subsequently recorded and produced. The authors conclude with a vision for the future of automated songwriting, envisioning both collaborative and autonomous systems.
label: AI

title: Learning to Segment Object Candidates via Recursive Neural Networks
Abstract: Object detection systems often rely on generating candidate object proposals to avoid exhaustive searches. This paper introduces a novel approach for segmenting object proposals using a deep architecture of recursive neural networks (ReNNs). ReNNs hierarchically group regions to detect object candidates across scales. Unlike traditional methods using fixed similarity measures for region merging, this approach adaptively learns the region merging similarity and objectness measure during hierarchical grouping. Guided by a structured loss, the ReNN model jointly optimizes the cross-region similarity metric with the region merging process and the objectness prediction. Randomness is introduced into the greedy search during inference to handle ambiguous region grouping. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, producing object proposals with high recall and accurate object boundaries, outperforming existing methods in both accuracy and efficiency.
label: AI

title: SqueezeDet: Unified, Small, Low Power Fully Convolutional Neural Networks for Real-Time Object Detection for Autonomous Driving
Abstract: Object detection is crucial for autonomous driving, demanding high accuracy, real-time inference, and small model size for embedded deployment. This paper introduces SqueezeDet, a fully convolutional neural network designed to meet these requirements. SqueezeDet utilizes convolutional layers for both feature extraction and output computation of bounding boxes and class probabilities. The single-pass detection pipeline ensures high speed, while the fully convolutional architecture results in a compact model with improved energy efficiency. Compared to previous baselines, SqueezeDet achieves comparable accuracy while being 30.4x smaller, 19.7x faster, and consuming 35.2x less energy. The code is open-sourced at https://github.com/BichenWuUCB/squeezeDet.
label: AI

title: Semi-Automated Annotation of Discrete States in Large Video Datasets
Abstract: This paper proposes a semi-automated annotation framework for video frames depicting an object with a finite number of discrete states. A Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is used to model both the object's behavior and its noisy observation through image processing. This approach simplifies the annotation process by reducing the need to label every frame to detecting state transitions. The framework's performance is evaluated on a driver gaze classification dataset with 16,000,000 images, fully annotated through 6,000 hours of manual labor. The framework achieves a 13x reduction in manual annotation for an average accuracy of 99.1%, and an 84x reduction for an average accuracy of 91.2%.
label: AI

title: Areas of Attention for Image Captioning
Abstract: This paper introduces "Areas of Attention," a novel attention-based model for automatic image captioning. This model captures the dependencies between image regions, caption words, and the state of an RNN language model using three pairwise interactions. Unlike previous approaches, this model allows direct association between caption words and image regions. During training, these associations are inferred from image-level captions, similar to weakly-supervised object detector training. This helps improve captioning by localizing the corresponding regions during testing. The paper explores different methods for generating attention areas: CNN activation grids, object proposals, and spatial transformers applied convolutionally. Spatial transformers yield the best results, enabling image-specific attention areas and joint training with the rest of the network. The combined attention mechanism and spatial transformer attention areas achieve state-of-the-art results on the MSCOCO dataset.
label: AI

title: Short-term traffic flow forecasting with spatial-temporal correlation in a hybrid deep learning framework
Abstract: Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Networks (RNNs), has achieved significant success in artificial intelligence. CNNs excel at visual tasks by leveraging spatial image and video properties, while RNNs, specifically long short-term memory methods (LSTMs), capture temporal correlations in time series data. Traffic flow data exhibits both spatial and temporal characteristics, but applications of CNNs and LSTMs in this domain are limited. This paper presents CLTFP, a novel deep architecture that combines CNNs and LSTMs for traffic flow forecasting. A 1-dimensional CNN captures spatial features, and two LSTMs mine short-term variability and periodicities. Feature-level fusion is performed to achieve short-term forecasting. CLTFP is compared to other forecasting methods on an open dataset, demonstrating significant advantages in traffic flow forecasting. Furthermore, CLTFP is analyzed from a Granger Causality perspective, revealing interesting properties.
label: AI

title: A Non-Local Means Approach for Gaussian Noise Removal from Images using a Modified Weighting Kernel
Abstract: Gaussian noise removal is crucial for improving image quality and enhancing post-processing algorithms like registration and segmentation. Many denoising methods utilize self-similarity or patch-based image processing. Non-Local Means (NLM), a patch-based filter, has gained popularity in recent years. This filter estimates noise-less signal values by calculating the Gaussian-weighted Euclidean distance between the patch under processing and other patches in the image. However, NLM is sensitive to outliers, assigning equal weights to symmetrically located pixels in the patch. This can lead to suboptimal denoising performance when noise introduces outliers within patches. This paper proposes a new weighting approach to modify the NLM filter's Gaussian kernel. This approach employs the geometric distance between image intensities to generate new weights for each pixel in a patch, reducing the impact of outliers on denoising performance. Experiments on standard images with varying noise levels demonstrate that this method outperforms other denoising filters.
label: AI

title: Mining Spatio-temporal Data on Industrialization from Historical Registries
Abstract: Despite the increasing availability of big data in various fields, historical data on socioenvironmental phenomena is often unavailable due to the lack of automated and scalable approaches for collection, digitization, and assembly. This paper presents a data-mining method for extracting tabulated, geocoded data from printed directories. While scanning and OCR can digitize text, they fail to capture the underlying data structure. The proposed pipeline integrates page layout analysis and OCR to extract tabular, geocoded data from structured text. The utility of this method is demonstrated by applying it to scanned manufacturing registries from Rhode Island, covering 41 years of industrial land use. The resulting spatio-temporal data enables socioenvironmental analyses of industrialization at a previously unattainable resolution. This analysis reveals strong evidence for the dispersion of manufacturing from the urban core of Providence along the Interstate 95 corridor.
label: AI

title: Ensembles of Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Ensembles are a popular technique for improving the performance of discriminative CNNs. Combining multiple networks trained with different initializations significantly enhances results. This paper explores the use of ensembles of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The unique nature of GANs enables novel ensemble construction methods. The first method leverages the fact that the generator network in the minimax game continues to evolve even after reaching optimality. This allows for self-ensembles, where models with varying training iterations are combined, offering faster training than traditional ensembles. The second method, called cascade GANs, redirects poorly modeled data from the first GAN to another GAN. Experiments on the CIFAR10 dataset show that ensembles of GANs generate model probability distributions that better represent the data distribution. These improved results are achieved with minimal additional computational cost.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning with Energy-efficient Binary Gradient Cameras
Abstract: Power consumption is a critical factor for deploying embedded computer vision systems. This paper explores the use of computational cameras that directly output binary gradient images to reduce power consumption allocated to image sensing. The accuracy of binary gradient cameras is evaluated for various computer vision tasks using deep learning, including object recognition, head pose regression, face detection, and gesture recognition. For certain applications, accuracy is comparable to or even surpasses traditional images. The paper also demonstrates the recovery of intensity information from binary spatial gradient images, beneficial for applications involving human observers. The findings, validated with a prototype binary gradient camera, highlight the potential of gradient-based computer vision systems.
label: AI

title: Food Image Recognition by Using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
Abstract: Food image recognition is a promising application of visual object recognition in computer vision. This study develops a small-scale dataset of 5822 images from ten categories and a five-layer CNN for image recognition. The bag-of-features (BoF) model coupled with a support vector machine (SVM) achieved an overall accuracy of 56%, while the CNN model significantly outperformed it with an accuracy of 74%. Data augmentation techniques based on geometric transformations were applied to increase the training image size, leading to a significant improvement in accuracy exceeding 90% and preventing overfitting. Further enhancements are anticipated by expanding the image collection and optimizing the network architecture and hyperparameters.
label: AI

title: Semi-supervised learning of deep metrics for stereo reconstruction
Abstract: Deep-learning metrics have demonstrated impressive performance for image patch matching in stereo reconstruction. However, training these metrics requires substantial labeled stereo images, which can be challenging or expensive to acquire for certain applications. This paper presents a novel semi-supervised method for learning deep metrics from unlabeled stereo images using coarse information about the scenes and optical system. This method alternates between optimizing the metric with stochastic gradient descent and applying stereo constraints for regularization. Experiments on reference datasets demonstrate that training without ground truth produces a metric with performance comparable to state-of-the-art baselines trained with ground truth. This approach addresses limitations of training sets, enables the use of larger training datasets, and allows tuning of deep metrics for specific stereo systems even without ground truth.
label: AI

title: End-to-end learning of brain tissue segmentation from imperfect labeling
Abstract: Segmenting a structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan is a crucial preprocessing step for analysis and inferences about tissue changes. Manual segmentation remains the gold standard but is expensive. Automatic approaches are computationally demanding, slow, and error-prone due to numerous potentially flawed intermediate steps. This paper introduces a deep learning model based on volumetric dilated convolutions, significantly reducing processing time and errors. Compared to competing models, the proposed model has fewer parameters, simplifying training and accelerating execution. Performance comparisons on a large dataset of unprocessed human brain volumes reveal the dilated network's superiority over state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, including up convolutional networks, even surpassing the ground truth used for training. The model's speed facilitates large-scale analyses and holds significant potential for clinical applications, allowing for rapid evaluation of test results.
label: AI

title: Commonly Uncommon: Semantic Sparsity in Situation Recognition
Abstract: Semantic sparsity is a common challenge in structured visual classification problems, particularly when the output space is complex and most possible predictions are rarely observed in the training set. This paper investigates semantic sparsity in situation recognition, which involves producing structured summaries of image content, including activities, objects, and object roles within activities. Empirical findings indicate that most object-role combinations are rare, leading to poor performance by existing state-of-the-art models. To address this, the paper introduces a novel tensor composition function that learns to share examples across role-noun combinations. Additionally, the training data is semantically augmented with automatically gathered examples of rarely observed outputs using web data. This tensor-based approach, integrated into a CRF-based structured prediction model, outperforms existing methods, achieving a relative improvement of 2.11% and 4.40% in top-5 verb and noun-role accuracy, respectively. Semantic augmentation with 5 million images further improves performance by 6.23% and 9.57% in top-5 verb and noun-role accuracy.
label: AI

title: Parameter Compression of Recurrent Neural Networks and Degradation of Short-term Memory
Abstract: The significant computational costs of deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments have fueled interest in model compression, aiming to reduce both arithmetic operations and storage memory. While techniques for compressing parameters in feed-forward and convolutional neural networks have been developed, the effect of parameter compression on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) remains less understood. Specifically, the extent of compressibility of recurrent parameters and its impact on short-term memory performance are unclear. This paper examines the effect of complexity reduction through singular value decomposition rank reduction on RNNs and minimal gated recurrent unit (MGRU) networks. The study demonstrates that considerable rank reduction is possible when compressing recurrent weights, even without fine-tuning. Furthermore, a perturbation model is proposed to analyze the impact of general perturbations, including compression, on RNN recurrent parameters. This model is tested on a noiseless memorization experiment, revealing that the effect of compression is dependent on the temporal coherence present in the data and task. This work provides insights for on-the-fly RNN compression in novel environments, facilitating the application of RNN compression in low-power devices.
label: AI

title: Procedural Generation of Videos to Train Deep Action Recognition Networks
Abstract: Deep learning for human action recognition in videos is making significant progress but is hindered by the dependency on expensive manual labeling of large video collections. This paper investigates the generation of synthetic training data for action recognition, which has shown promising results for other computer vision tasks. The paper proposes an interpretable parametric generative model of human action videos utilizing procedural generation and computer graphics techniques from modern game engines. This model generates a diverse, realistic, and physically plausible dataset of human action videos, called PHAV (Procedural Human Action Videos), containing 39,982 videos with over 1,000 examples for each of 35 action categories. The approach is not limited to existing motion capture sequences and procedurally defines 14 synthetic actions. A deep multi-task representation learning architecture is introduced to mix synthetic and real videos, even with differing action categories. Experiments on the UCF101 and HMDB51 benchmarks demonstrate that combining PHAV with small real-world datasets significantly enhances recognition performance, outperforming unsupervised generative models.
label: AI

title: Making the V in VQA Matter: Elevating the Role of Image Understanding in Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Problems at the intersection of vision and language are both challenging research topics and enable rich applications. However, the inherent structure of the world and biases in language often provide simpler signals for learning than visual modalities. This can lead models to ignore visual information, resulting in an inflated sense of their capabilities. This paper proposes to counter these language priors for the task of Visual Question Answering (VQA) and make vision matter. Specifically, the paper balances the popular VQA dataset by collecting complementary images such that each question is associated with a pair of similar images yielding different answers. This balanced dataset is larger than the original VQA dataset and is publicly available at www.visualqa.org as part of the VQA v2.0 challenge. Benchmarking state-of-the-art VQA models on the balanced dataset reveals significantly poorer performance, suggesting that these models have learned to exploit language priors. This provides concrete empirical evidence for a qualitative sense among practitioners. Furthermore, the data collection protocol for identifying complementary images enables the development of an interpretable model that provides explanations alongside answers. This model identifies an image similar to the original image but with a different answer to the same question, fostering trust in machine performance.
label: AI

title: Scribbler: Controlling Deep Image Synthesis with Sketch and Color
Abstract: Recent advancements in deep convolutional networks have yielded promising methods for generating realistic imagery. These methods bypass traditional computer graphics rendering and generate imagery at the pixel level by learning from large collections of photos. However, their limited utility arises from the difficulty of controlling network output. This paper proposes a deep adversarial image synthesis architecture conditioned on sketched boundaries and sparse color strokes for generating realistic cars, bedrooms, or faces. This approach enables a sketch-based image synthesis system where users can "scribble" on sketches to indicate desired object colors. The network then generates images that satisfy both color and sketch constraints. The feed-forward architecture allows real-time feedback on user edits. Comparisons with existing sketch-to-image synthesis methods demonstrate that this approach generates more realistic, diverse, and controllable outputs. The architecture is also effective for user-guided colorization of grayscale images.
label: AI

title: A Benchmark for Endoluminal Scene Segmentation of Colonoscopy Images
Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third leading cause of cancer death worldwide. Regular screening for polyps using colonoscopy is the standard approach to reduce CRC-related mortality. However, colonoscopy has limitations, including polyp miss-rate and the inability to visually assess polyp malignancy. To address these drawbacks, Decision Support Systems (DSS) are being developed to assist clinicians during colonoscopy. This paper introduces an extended benchmark of colonoscopy images, aiming to establish a strong benchmark for colonoscopy image analysis research. By training standard fully convolutional networks (FCNs) for semantic segmentation, new baselines are established on this dataset, significantly outperforming previous results in endoluminal scene segmentation without additional post-processing.
label: AI

title: Action Recognition with Dynamic Image Networks
Abstract: Dynamic images provide a compact representation of video data, especially useful for video analysis when combined with convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This method uses "rank pooling" to encode temporal information from videos, like RGB or optical flow sequences. A ranking machine learns the temporal evolution of the data, and its parameters are used for representation. Using a linear ranking machine results in an image representation, termed "dynamic" because it summarizes both appearance and video dynamics. This enables converting any video into an image, allowing the application of pre-trained CNN models designed for still images to video analysis. An efficient approximate rank pooling operator is introduced, significantly speeding up standard rank pooling algorithms and forming a new CNN layer. This layer extends dynamic image concept to dynamic feature maps. The effectiveness of this new representation is demonstrated on standard action recognition benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
label: AI

title: Identifying and Categorizing Anomalies in Retinal Imaging Data
Abstract: Anomaly detection in large-scale medical imaging data using healthy examples as a reference is proposed. The method aims to identify and categorize anomalies that deviate from the typical patterns observed in healthy data. A deep convolutional autoencoder trained on healthy retinal images learns a new feature representation. The distribution of healthy retinal patches is estimated using a one-class support vector machine, enabling the identification of pathologic regions in images without expert annotations. Subsequent clustering categorizes these findings into clinically relevant classes. The learned features outperform standard embedding approaches in a classification task.
label: AI

title: Voxelwise nonlinear regression toolbox for neuroimage analysis: Application to aging and neurodegenerative disease modeling
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel neuroimaging analysis toolbox capable of modeling nonlinear effects at the voxel level, addressing the limitations of linear model-based methods like the GLM. The toolbox's capabilities are illustrated with an example that reveals distinct nonlinear trajectories of Alzheimer's disease-related brain atrophy patterns across the entire disease spectrum. The open-source toolbox is accessible at https://github.com/imatge-upc/VNeAT.
label: AI

title: Centrog Feature technique for vehicle type recognition at day and night times
Abstract: This research presents a feature-based approach for recognizing vehicle types during both day and night. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier is applied to image histogram and CENTROG (CENsus Transformed histogRam Oriented Gradient) features for vehicle type classification. Thermal images are utilized for night-time experiments. Despite the challenges of low resolution, lack of color, and poor texture in thermal images, they provide the advantage of being unaffected by high-intensity light sources like vehicle headlights, which hinder regular image capture and analysis during night-time. CENTROG, which captures contour information crucial for shape-based categorization and is particularly effective with thermal images, is employed in the experiments. Experimental results comparing CENTROG with CENTRIST (CENsus TRansformed hISTogram) demonstrate that CENTROG achieves better recognition accuracy for both day and night-time vehicle type identification.
label: AI

title: Recognition of Text Image Using Multilayer Perceptron
Abstract: The paper focuses on the challenge of recognizing documents in both printed and handwritten formats. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a document image analysis technique that converts scanned digital images containing printed or handwritten text into editable machine-readable digital text. A neural network, a software simulation of the brain performing specific tasks, is designed to perform character recognition. This process involves converting printed text documents, such as books, papers, and magazines, into Unicode text. This is achieved by first scanning the documents using standard scanners to produce an image. Lines are then identified by an algorithm, followed by character boundary calculations within each line. The calculated boundaries allow for character isolation from the image, and subsequently, each character is classified using a basic backpropagation algorithm. The image characters consist of 30x20 pixels. The Backpropagation Neural Network is employed for efficient recognition, with errors corrected through backpropagation and rectified neuron values transmitted through feed-forward methods in the multi-layered network.
label: AI

title: SyncSpecCNN: Synchronized Spectral CNN for 3D Shape Segmentation
Abstract: This paper investigates semantic annotation on 3D models represented as shape graphs. A functional view is adopted to represent localized information on graphs, where annotations like part segments or keypoints are represented as 0-1 indicator vertex functions. Unlike images which are 2D grids, shape graphs have irregular and non-isomorphic structures. To predict vertex functions on shape graphs using convolutional neural networks, the paper leverages the spectral CNN method. This method facilitates weight sharing by parameterizing kernels in the spectral domain spanned by graph Laplacian eigenbases. Under this setting, the network, named SyncSpecCNN, tackles two key challenges: sharing coefficients and conducting multi-scale analysis in different parts of the graph for a single shape, and sharing information across related but different shapes represented by varying graphs. To address these challenges, spectral parameterization of dilated convolutional kernels and a spectral transformer network are introduced. The SyncSpecCNN is evaluated on various tasks, including 3D shape part segmentation and 3D keypoint prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance on all benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: Globally Consistent Multi-People Tracking using Motion Patterns
Abstract: Many advanced people tracking methods rely on independent detection in each frame, followed by grouping detections into short but reliable trajectory segments, which are then further grouped into complete trajectories. This grouping often involves local smoothness constraints, but rarely enforces more global trajectory constraints. This paper proposes an approach to impose global consistency by first inferring behavioral patterns from ground truth data and then using these patterns to guide the tracking algorithm. Integrating this approach with several state-of-the-art algorithms significantly enhances their performance. Additionally, an unsupervised scheme is presented, achieving similar improvements without requiring ground truth data.
label: AI

title: A Point Set Generation Network for 3D Object Reconstruction from a Single Image
Abstract: Generating 3D data using deep neural networks has become a prominent research area. While many existing methods rely on regular representations such as volumetric grids or image collections, these representations obscure the natural invariance of 3D shapes under geometric transformations and have other drawbacks. This paper tackles the problem of 3D reconstruction from a single image, generating a direct output form – point cloud coordinates. The inherent ambiguity in ground truth shapes for an input image presents a unique challenge.  Taking into account this unconventional output form and the ambiguity in ground truth, a novel and effective architecture, loss function, and learning paradigm are designed. The final solution is a conditional shape sampler capable of predicting multiple plausible 3D point clouds from an input image.  Experimental results demonstrate that the system not only outperforms state-of-the-art methods on single-image-based 3D reconstruction benchmarks but also shows strong performance for 3D shape completion and a promising ability to make multiple plausible predictions.
label: AI

title: Learning to Search on Manifolds for 3D Pose Estimation of Articulated Objects
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenging problem of 3D pose estimation for a diverse range of articulated objects from single depth images. A novel structured prediction approach is employed, where 3D poses are represented as skeletal models naturally operating on manifolds. Given an input depth image, the prediction of the most appropriate articulation of the underlying skeletal model is formulated as a sequential search for the optimal skeletal configuration. This is achieved by training convolutional neural networks end-to-end to sequentially predict joint locations by regressing a set of tangent vectors on the underlying manifolds. The approach is tested on various articulated objects including human hand, mouse, and fish benchmark datasets. Empirical results demonstrate highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods while operating in real-time (over 30 FPS).
label: AI

title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
Abstract: Point clouds are a significant type of geometric data structure. Due to their irregular format, many researchers transform them into regular 3D voxel grids or image collections. However, this process leads to unnecessarily voluminous data and introduces issues. This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture named PointNet that directly consumes point clouds and respects the permutation invariance of points in the input. PointNet provides a unified architecture for applications such as object classification, part segmentation, and scene semantic parsing. Despite its simplicity, PointNet is highly efficient and effective. Empirical results demonstrate strong performance, often exceeding or matching state-of-the-art methods. Theoretical analysis sheds light on the network's learning process and its robustness against input perturbation and corruption.
label: AI

title: Guided Open Vocabulary Image Captioning with Constrained Beam Search
Abstract: Existing image captioning models struggle to generalize to out-of-domain images containing novel scenes or objects. This limitation hinders their real-world applicability. This paper proposes a flexible approach enabling existing deep captioning architectures to leverage image taggers at test time without requiring retraining. The method uses constrained beam search to force the inclusion of selected tag words in the output and fixed, pretrained word embeddings to expand the vocabulary to previously unseen tag words. This approach achieves state-of-the-art results for out-of-domain captioning on MSCOCO, even improving in-domain captioning results. Surprisingly, the performance significantly surpasses approaches that incorporate the same tag predictions into the learning algorithm. The paper also demonstrates a significant improvement in the quality of generated ImageNet captions by leveraging ground-truth labels.
label: AI

title: Self-critical Sequence Training for Image Captioning
Abstract: Recent research has shown that policy-gradient methods for reinforcement learning can be used to train deep end-to-end systems directly on non-differentiable metrics for the task at hand. This paper focuses on optimizing image captioning systems using reinforcement learning and demonstrates significant performance gains by carefully optimizing these systems using the test metrics of the MSCOCO task. The systems are built using a new optimization approach called self-critical sequence training (SCST). SCST is a variant of the popular REINFORCE algorithm that, instead of estimating a "baseline" to normalize rewards and reduce variance, utilizes its own test-time inference algorithm's output for reward normalization. This approach eliminates the need for estimating the reward signal (as actor-critic methods do) and normalization (as REINFORCE algorithms typically do) while aligning the model with its test-time inference procedure. Empirically, directly optimizing the CIDEr metric with SCST and greedy decoding at test-time proves highly effective. The results on the MSCOCO evaluation server establish a new state-of-the-art on the task, improving the best CIDEr result from 104.9 to 114.7.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Learning posed as a Missing Data Problem
Abstract: This paper presents a zero-shot learning (ZSL) method that frames ZSL as a missing data problem instead of a missing label problem. Unlike most existing ZSL methods that focus on learning mapping functions from the image feature space to the label embedding space, this proposed method explores a simple yet effective transductive framework operating in reverse. The method estimates the data distribution of unseen classes in the image feature space by transferring knowledge from the label embedding space. Experiments show that this method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on two widely used datasets.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Human Action Detection by Action Matching
Abstract: This paper introduces a new unsupervised action detection task based on action matching. Given two long videos, the objective is to temporally detect all pairs of matching video segments. A pair of video segments are considered matched if they depict the same human action. This task is category-independent, meaning the specific action being performed is irrelevant, and no supervision is used to discover these video segments. Unsupervised action detection through action matching enables meaningful video alignment. This can be used to discover new action categories or as an action proposal technique within an action detection pipeline. Additionally, it serves as a useful pre-processing step for generating video highlights, especially from sports videos. The paper presents an effective and efficient method for unsupervised action detection. It utilizes an unsupervised temporal encoding method and exploits the temporal consistency of human actions to identify candidate action segments. The method is evaluated on three activity recognition benchmarks: the MPII Cooking activities dataset, the THUMOS15 action detection benchmark, and a new dataset called the IKEA dataset. On the MPII Cooking dataset, action segments are detected with a precision of 21.6% and a recall of 11.7% across 946 long video pairs and over 5000 ground truth action segments. Similarly, on the THUMOS dataset, 18.4% precision and 25.1% recall are achieved across 5094 ground truth action segment pairs.
label: AI

title: Breast Mass Classification from Mammograms using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Mammography is the most widely used method for breast cancer screening. Due to its largely manual nature, variability in mass appearance, and low signal-to-noise ratio, a significant number of breast masses are missed or misdiagnosed. This paper explores the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for direct classification of pre-segmented breast masses in mammograms as benign or malignant.  A combination of transfer learning, careful pre-processing, and data augmentation is used to overcome the limitations of limited training data. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on the DDSM dataset, surpassing human performance, and demonstrates the interpretability of the model.
label: AI

title: Object Detection via Aspect Ratio and Context Aware Region-based Convolutional Networks
Abstract: Jointly integrating aspect ratio and context has been extensively studied and shown to improve performance in traditional object detection systems like DPMs. However, this approach has largely been ignored in deep neural network-based detection systems. This paper presents a method for integrating a mixture of object models and region-based convolutional networks for accurate object detection. Each mixture component explicitly considers object aspect ratio and multi-scale contextual information: (i) it utilizes a mixture of tiling configurations in the RoI pooling to address warping artifacts caused by a single RoI pooling type (e.g., with equally-sized 7x7 cells) and respect the underlying object shapes better, and (ii) it incorporates contextual information at two scales by "looking both from the inside and outside of a RoI", including global context pooled from the whole image and local context pooled from the surroundings of a RoI. To facilitate accurate detection, a multi-stage detection scheme is proposed to integrate the mixture of object models, using the detection results of the previous stage as proposals for the current stage in both training and testing. The proposed method is named aspect ratio and context aware region-based convolutional network (ARC-R-CNN). In experiments, ARC-R-CNN demonstrates highly competitive results with Faster R-CNN and R-FCN on two datasets: PASCAL VOC and Microsoft COCO. It achieves significantly better mAP performance using high IoU thresholds on both datasets.
label: AI

title: Photorealistic Facial Texture Inference Using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a data-driven inference method capable of synthesizing a photorealistic texture map of a complete 3D face model from a partial 2D view of a person in the wild. After initial estimations of shape and low-frequency albedo, a high-frequency partial texture map without the shading component is computed for the visible face area. To extract fine appearance details from this incomplete input, a multi-scale detail analysis technique is introduced based on mid-layer feature correlations extracted from a deep convolutional neural network. The paper demonstrates that fitting a convex combination of feature correlations from a high-resolution face database can produce a semantically plausible facial detail description for the entire face. A complete and photorealistic texture map is then synthesized by iteratively optimizing for the reconstructed feature correlations. Using these high-resolution textures and a commercial rendering framework, high-fidelity 3D renderings are produced, visually comparable to those obtained using state-of-the-art multi-view face capture systems. Successful face reconstructions are demonstrated from a wide range of low-resolution input images, including those of historical figures. Extensive evaluations and a crowdsourced user study validate the realism of the results.
label: AI

title: A Visual Representation for Editing Face Images
Abstract: A novel approach for editing face images is proposed, enabling a wide range of applications, including face relighting, makeup transfer, and face detail editing. Face edits are based on a visual representation encompassing geometry, face segmentation, albedo, illumination, and detail map.  To recover this visual representation, geometry is first estimated using a morphable face model, followed by face image decomposition to recover the albedo. The geometry is then shaded using albedo and illumination. The residual between the shaded geometry and the input image generates the detail map, which carries high-frequency information inadequately or incorrectly captured by the shading process. Manipulating the detail map allows for face image editing while preserving reality and identity. The representation enables various applications. It allows direct manipulation of different illuminations. It also facilitates non-parametric makeup transfer while preserving the input face's distinctive identity features and non-parametric modifications to face appearance through detail transfer. For face relighting and detail editing, the method is evaluated through a user study and outperforms other methods. For makeup transfer, an online attractiveness evaluation system is used, showing the method's ability to reliably make people look younger and more attractive. Extensive qualitative comparisons to existing methods demonstrate significant improvements over previous techniques.
label: AI

title: Object-Centric Representation Learning from Unlabeled Videos
Abstract: Supervised (pre-)training currently delivers state-of-the-art performance for representation learning in visual recognition. However, it requires intensive manual annotations and limits the scope of data relevant for learning. This paper explores unsupervised feature learning from unlabeled video. A novel object-centric approach to temporal coherence is introduced, encouraging similar representations to be learned for object-like regions segmented from nearby frames. The framework relies on a Siamese-triplet network to train a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) representation.  Compared to existing temporal coherence methods, this approach offers the advantage of lightweight unlabeled video pre-processing (no tracking required) while still extracting object-level regions for learning invariances. Results on several standard datasets show that the method typically achieves substantial accuracy gains over competing unsupervised methods for image classification and retrieval tasks.
label: AI

title: FINN: A Framework for Fast, Scalable Binarized Neural Network Inference
Abstract: Research has demonstrated that convolutional neural networks contain significant redundancy, enabling high classification accuracy even when weights and activations are reduced from floating point to binary values. This paper presents FINN, a framework for constructing fast and flexible FPGA accelerators using a flexible heterogeneous streaming architecture. By utilizing a novel set of optimizations that enable efficient mapping of binarized neural networks to hardware, fully connected, convolutional, and pooling layers are implemented. Per-layer compute resources are tailored to user-defined throughput requirements. On a ZC706 embedded FPGA platform with less than 25 W total system power, the framework demonstrates up to 12.3 million image classifications per second with 0.31 µs latency on the MNIST dataset with 95.8% accuracy and 21906 image classifications per second with 283 µs latency on the CIFAR-10 and SVHN datasets with 80.1% and 94.9% accuracy, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these are the fastest classification rates reported to date on these benchmarks. |||
label: AI

title: 3D Bounding Box Estimation Using Deep Learning and Geometry
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for 3D object detection and pose estimation using a single image. Instead of directly regressing 3D orientation, our method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to estimate relatively stable 3D object properties. These estimates are then combined with geometric constraints from a 2D bounding box to produce a complete 3D bounding box. The network employs a hybrid discrete-continuous loss function for 3D orientation estimation, which significantly surpasses the L2 loss performance. It also estimates 3D object dimensions, which exhibit relatively low variance compared to alternatives and are often predictable for various object types. These estimates, combined with the geometric constraints on translation imposed by the 2D bounding box, enable robust and accurate 3D object pose recovery. We evaluate our method on the challenging KITTI object detection benchmark, both on the official metric of 3D orientation estimation and on the accuracy of the obtained 3D bounding boxes. Despite its conceptual simplicity, our method outperforms more complex and computationally expensive approaches that leverage semantic segmentation, instance-level segmentation, flat ground priors, and sub-category detection. Our discrete-continuous loss also achieves state-of-the-art results for 3D viewpoint estimation on the Pascal 3D+ dataset.
label: AI

title: In Teacher We Trust: Learning Compressed Models for Pedestrian Detection
Abstract: While large and complex deep convolutional neural networks are pushing the boundaries in various domains, many of their parameters are redundant. Knowledge Distillation allows learning smaller networks that mimic the outputs of larger ones. However, we show that standard Knowledge Distillation is ineffective for training small models for pedestrian detection. To address this, we introduce a higher-dimensional hint layer to enhance information flow. We further estimate the variance in the outputs of the large network and incorporate this uncertainty into a novel loss function. Finally, we aim to improve the small network's complexity without increasing its size by incorporating hand-designed features known to be effective for pedestrian detection. Through these strategies, we successfully train a model with 400 times fewer parameters than the large network, surpassing AlexNet's performance on the Caltech Pedestrian Dataset.
label: AI

title: Understanding image motion with group representations
Abstract: Motion is a crucial signal for agents navigating dynamic environments, but learning to represent motion from unlabeled video remains a challenging problem. We propose a motion model based on elementary group properties of transformations and use it to train a representation of image motion. Unlike most motion estimation methods that rely on pixel-level constraints, we use group properties to constrain the abstract representation of motion itself. We demonstrate that a deep neural network trained with this method captures motion in both synthetic 2D sequences and real-world sequences of vehicle motion, without requiring any labels. Networks trained to respect these constraints implicitly identify the image characteristics of motion in different sequence types. In the context of vehicle motion, this method extracts information useful for localization, tracking, and odometry. Our findings show that this representation is valuable for learning motion in situations where explicit labels are difficult to obtain.
label: AI

title: Efficient Pose and Cell Segmentation using Column Generation
Abstract: This paper tackles the problems of multi-person pose segmentation in natural images and instance segmentation in biological images with crowded cells. We formulate these distinct tasks as integer programs, where variables represent poses/cells. To optimize, we introduce a generic relaxation scheme for solving these combinatorial problems using a column generation formulation. The program for generating a column is solved via exact optimization of very small-scale integer programs. This approach enables efficient exploration of the spaces of poses and cells.
label: AI

title: TorontoCity: Seeing the World with a Million Eyes
Abstract: This paper introduces the TorontoCity benchmark, a large-scale dataset encompassing the entire Greater Toronto Area (GTA), covering 712.5 km² of land, 8439 km of road, and approximately 400,000 buildings. The benchmark provides diverse perspectives captured from airplanes, drones, and cars driving around the city. Manual labeling of such a massive dataset is impractical. We propose utilizing high-precision maps to generate ground truth. To achieve this, we develop algorithms that enable alignment of all data sources with the maps while requiring minimal human supervision. We have designed a wide variety of tasks, including building height estimation (reconstruction), road centerline and curb extraction, building instance segmentation, building contour extraction (reorganization), semantic labeling, and scene type classification (recognition). Our pilot study indicates that most of these tasks remain challenging for modern convolutional neural networks.
label: AI

title: Computerized Multiparametric MR image Analysis for Prostate Cancer Aggressiveness-Assessment
Abstract: We propose an automated method for detecting aggressive prostate cancer (CaP) (Gleason score >=7) based on a comprehensive analysis of the lesion and surrounding normal prostate tissue simultaneously captured in T2-weighted MR images, diffusion-weighted images (DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient maps (ADC). The proposed methodology was tested on a dataset of 79 patients (40 aggressive, 39 non-aggressive). We evaluated the performance of a wide range of popular quantitative imaging features on the characterization of aggressive versus non-aggressive CaP. Our results demonstrate that a group of 44 discriminative predictors among 1464 quantitative imaging features can effectively produce an area under the ROC curve of 0.73.
label: AI

title: Learning Shape Abstractions by Assembling Volumetric Primitives
Abstract: This paper presents a learning framework for abstracting complex shapes by learning to assemble objects using 3D volumetric primitives. Our framework generates simple and geometrically interpretable explanations of 3D objects, allowing us to automatically discover and exploit consistent structure in the data.
