We demonstrate that our method predicts shape representations that can be leveraged for consistent parsing across shape collections and constructing an interpretable shape similarity measure. We also explore applications for image-based prediction and shape manipulation.
label: AI

title: Anomaly Detection in Video Using Predictive Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Networks
Abstract: Automating the detection of anomalous events in long video sequences is challenging due to the ambiguity in defining such events. We address this problem by learning generative models that can identify anomalies in videos using limited supervision. We propose end-to-end trainable composite Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (Conv-LSTM) networks that predict the evolution of a video sequence from a small number of input frames. Regularity scores are derived from the reconstruction errors of a set of predictions. Abnormal video sequences yield lower regularity scores as they diverge further from the actual sequence over time. Our models utilize a composite structure and examine the effects of conditioning in learning more meaningful representations. The best model is chosen based on reconstruction and prediction accuracy. We evaluate the Conv-LSTM models both qualitatively and quantitatively, demonstrating competitive results on anomaly detection datasets. Conv-LSTM units prove to be effective tools for modeling and predicting video sequences.
label: AI

title: Temporal Attention-Gated Model for Robust Sequence Classification
Abstract: Traditional sequence classification techniques are designed for well-segmented sequences, which have been edited to remove noisy or irrelevant parts. Consequently, these methods are not readily applicable to noisy sequences typically encountered in real-world applications. This paper presents the Temporal Attention-Gated Model (TAGM), which integrates concepts from attention models and gated recurrent networks to handle noisy or unsegmented sequences effectively. We extend the concept of attention models to measure the relevance of each observation (time step) in a sequence. A novel gated recurrent network then learns the hidden representation for the final prediction. A key advantage of our approach is its interpretability, as the temporal attention weights provide meaningful values for the salience of each time step in the sequence. We demonstrate the benefits of our TAGM approach, both in terms of prediction accuracy and interpretability, on three distinct tasks: spoken digit recognition, text-based sentiment analysis, and visual event recognition.
label: AI

title: Playing Doom with SLAM-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Recent approaches to policy learning in 2D game domains have achieved success by directly mapping raw input images to actions. However, when applied to complex 3D environments, they often face challenges related to partial observability, combinatorial exploration spaces, path planning, and a scarcity of rewarding scenarios. Inspired by human cognition, which utilizes semantic concepts and abstractions (object categories, localization, etc.) for reasoning about the world, we build an agent-model that incorporates such abstractions into its policy-learning framework. We augment the raw image input to a Deep Q-Learning Network (DQN) by adding details of objects and structural elements encountered, along with the agent's localization. These components are automatically extracted and composed into a topological representation using on-the-fly object detection and 3D-scene reconstruction. We evaluate the efficacy of our approach in Doom, a 3D first-person combat game that exhibits many of the aforementioned challenges. Our augmented framework consistently learns better and more effective policies.
label: AI

title: Improved Image Captioning via Policy Gradient optimization of SPIDEr
Abstract: Current image captioning methods are typically trained using (penalized) maximum likelihood estimation. However, the log-likelihood score of a caption does not correlate well with human assessments of quality. Standard syntactic evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, METEOR, and ROUGE, also lack strong correlations. The newer SPICE and CIDEr metrics exhibit better correlations but have traditionally been difficult to optimize for. This paper presents a policy gradient (PG) method for directly optimizing a linear combination of SPICE and CIDEr (termed SPIDEr). The SPICE score ensures semantic faithfulness of our captions to the image, while the CIDEr score guarantees syntactic fluency. The proposed PG method improves upon the prior MIXER approach by utilizing Monte Carlo rollouts instead of mixing MLE training with PG. Our empirical findings show that our algorithm leads to easier optimization and improved results compared to MIXER. We demonstrate that using our PG method, we can optimize any of the metrics, including the proposed SPIDEr metric, resulting in image captions that are strongly preferred by human raters compared to captions generated by the same model but trained to optimize MLE or the COCO metrics.
label: AI

title: A Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Approach to Registration of CLARITY Images via Mutual Information
Abstract: CLARITY is a technique for converting biological tissues into translucent and porous hydrogel-tissue hybrids. This process facilitates interrogation with light sheet microscopy and penetration of molecular probes while avoiding physical slicing. This work develops a pipeline for registering CLARIfied mouse brains to an annotated brain atlas. Due to the novelty of this microscopy technique, using absolute intensity values to align these images to existing standard atlases is impractical. Therefore, we adopt a large deformation diffeomorphic approach for registering images via mutual information matching. Furthermore, we demonstrate how a cascaded multi-resolution approach can enhance registration quality while reducing algorithm run time. As acquired image volumes exceeded a terabyte in size, they were too large for processing on personal computers. Consequently, the NeuroData computational infrastructure was deployed for multi-resolution storage and visualization of these images and aligned annotations on the web.
label: AI

title: Global Minimum for a Finsler Elastica Minimal Path Approach
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel curvature-penalized minimal path model via an orientation-lifted Finsler metric and the Euler elastica curve. The original minimal path model computes the globally minimal geodesic by solving an Eikonal partial differential equation (PDE). However, this first-order model cannot penalize curvature, which is related to the path rigidity property in classical active contour models. To address this limitation, we present an Eikonal PDE-based Finsler elastica minimal path approach to minimize the curvature-penalized geodesic energy. We successfully introduce curvature penalization to the classical geodesic energy. The core idea is to interpret the Euler elastica bending energy through a novel Finsler elastica metric that incorporates a curvature penalty. This metric is non-Riemannian, anisotropic, and asymmetric, defined over an orientation-lifted space by adding orientation as an extra space dimension to the image domain. Through this orientation lifting, the proposed minimal path model benefits from both the curvature and orientation of the paths. Thanks to the fast marching method, the global minimum of the curvature-penalized geodesic energy can be computed efficiently. We introduce two anisotropic image data-driven speed functions computed using steerable filters. Based on these orientation-dependent speed functions, we can apply the proposed Finsler elastica minimal path model to applications like closed contour detection, perceptual grouping, and tubular structure extraction. Numerical experiments on both synthetic and real images demonstrate that these applications of our model achieve promising results.

title: Hippocampus Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Detection using a Combination of Shape-based Features and Spherical Harmonics Representation
Abstract: Most temporal lobe epilepsy detection approaches rely on hippocampus deformation and complex features, leading to intricate feature extraction and preprocessing tasks. This paper proposes a novel detection method based on shape-based features and spherical harmonics, enabling analysis of hippocampus shape anomaly and detection of asymmetry. This method consists of two main parts: (1) shape feature extraction and (2) image classification. For evaluation, we utilize the HFH database, publicly available in this field. Nine different geometry and 256 spherical harmonic features are introduced and then narrowed down to eighteen that significantly detect asymmetry in the hippocampus in a randomly selected subset of the dataset. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier is employed to classify the remaining images of the dataset into normal and epileptic images using our selected features. On a dataset of 25 images, 12 were used for feature extraction, and the remaining 13 for classification. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity of 84%, 100%, and 80%, respectively. Therefore, the proposed approach provides acceptable results and is straightforward, eliminating the need for complicated preprocessing steps compared to other methods.

title: A Theoretical Framework for Robustness of (Deep) Classifiers against Adversarial Examples
Abstract: Most machine learning classifiers, including deep neural networks, are vulnerable to adversarial examples. These inputs are typically generated by adding small but purposeful modifications that lead to incorrect outputs while remaining imperceptible to human eyes. This paper aims to contribute to a theoretical understanding of adversarial examples, not by introducing a single method, but by making theoretical steps towards fully understanding them. Using concepts from topology, our theoretical analysis reveals the key reasons why an adversarial example can fool a classifier ($f_1$) and includes its oracle ($f_2$, like human eyes) in this analysis. By investigating the topological relationship between two (pseudo)metric spaces corresponding to predictor $f_1$ and oracle $f_2$, we develop necessary and sufficient conditions to determine if $f_1$ is always robust (strong-robust) against adversarial examples according to $f_2$. Notably, our theorems indicate that a single unnecessary feature can render $f_1$ not strong-robust, highlighting the importance of proper feature representation learning for achieving classifiers that are both accurate and strong-robust.

title: Aggressive Quadrotor Flight through Narrow Gaps with Onboard Sensing and Computing using Active Vision
Abstract: We address one of the main challenges in autonomous quadrotor flight in complex environments: flight through narrow gaps. While previous works relied on off-board localization systems or accurate prior knowledge of the gap's position and orientation, we rely solely on onboard sensing and computing. We estimate the full state by fusing gap detection from a single onboard camera with an IMU. This problem presents two major challenges: (i) quadrotor pose uncertainty with respect to the gap increases quadratically with the distance from the gap; (ii) the quadrotor must actively control its orientation towards the gap to enable state estimation (i.e., active vision). We solve this problem by generating a trajectory that considers geometric, dynamic, and perception constraints. During the approach maneuver, the quadrotor always faces the gap to allow state estimation while respecting the vehicle dynamics. During traversal through the gap, the quadrotor's distance to the gap edges is maximized. Furthermore, we replan the trajectory during its execution to adapt to the varying uncertainty of the state estimate. We successfully evaluate and demonstrate our approach in numerous real experiments. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to achieve autonomous, aggressive flight through narrow gaps using only onboard sensing and computing without prior knowledge of the gap's pose.

title: An Evaluation of Models for Runtime Approximation in Link Discovery
Abstract: Time-efficient link discovery is crucial for realizing the vision of the Semantic Web. Some of the fastest link discovery approaches internally rely on planning to execute link specifications. Recent work has utilized linear models to estimate the runtime of the fastest planners. However, no other category of models has been explored for this purpose. This paper investigates non-linear runtime estimation functions for runtime estimation. Specifically, we study exponential and mixed models for estimating planner runtimes. We evaluate three different models for runtime on six datasets using 400 link specifications. Our findings indicate that exponential and mixed models achieve better fits when trained but are only preferable in certain cases. Our evaluation also shows that using better runtime approximation models has a positive impact on the overall execution of link specifications.

title: Video Captioning with Multi-Faceted Attention
Abstract: Video captioning has gained increasing interest due to its potential to improve accessibility and information retrieval. While existing methods utilize various visual features and model structures, they do not fully exploit relevant semantic information. We present an extensible approach that leverages several types of visual features and semantic attributes jointly. Our novel architecture builds on LSTMs for sentence generation, incorporating several attention layers and two multimodal layers. The attention mechanism automatically selects the most salient visual features or semantic attributes, and the multimodal layer generates overall representations for the input and outputs of the sentence generation component. Experimental results on the challenging MSVD and MSR-VTT datasets show that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, ground truth-based semantic attributes can further elevate the output quality to a near-human level.

title: Fully Convolutional Crowd Counting On Highly Congested Scenes
Abstract: This paper advances the state-of-the-art for crowd counting in high-density scenes by further exploring the concept of a fully convolutional crowd counting model introduced by (Zhang et al., 2016). Developing an accurate and robust crowd count estimator using computer vision techniques has attracted significant research interest in recent years. Applications for crowd counting systems exist in various domains, including city planning, retail, and public safety. Creating a highly generalized counting model deployable in any surveillance scenario with any camera perspective is a key research objective in this area. Techniques developed in the past generally performed poorly in highly congested scenes with thousands of people in the frame (Rodriguez et al., 2011). Our approach, inspired by the work of (Zhang et al., 2016), comprises the following contributions: (1) A training set augmentation scheme minimizing redundancy among training samples to improve model generalization and overall counting performance; (2) A deep, single-column, fully convolutional network (FCN) architecture; (3) A multi-scale averaging step during inference. The developed technique can analyze images of any resolution or aspect ratio and achieves state-of-the-art counting performance on the Shanghaitech Part B and UCF CC 50 datasets, as well as competitive performance on Shanghaitech Part A.
label: AI

title: Learning to Generate Images of Outdoor Scenes from Attributes and Semantic Layouts
Abstract: Automatic image synthesis research using deep networks has been rapidly growing, with networks becoming increasingly expressive. In recent years, we have seen images of digits, indoor scenes, birds, chairs, etc., being automatically generated. The expressive power of image generators has also been enhanced by introducing various conditioning variables, such as object names, sentences, bounding boxes, and key-point locations. This work proposes a novel deep conditional generative adversarial network architecture that leverages semantic layout and scene attributes integrated as conditioning variables. We show that our architecture can generate realistic outdoor scene images under different conditions, including day-night, sunny-foggy, with clear object boundaries. |||

title: Training Bit Fully Convolutional Network for Fast Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs) offer accurate per-pixel predictions for input images, finding use in applications such as semantic segmentation. However, conventional FCNs typically require extensive floating-point computations and substantial run-time memory, limiting their practical usability. We propose a method to train Bit Fully Convolutional Networks (BFCNs), a type of FCN with low bit-width weights and activations. Since most of the computationally intensive convolutions operate on low bit-width numbers, BFCNs can be accelerated through efficient bit-convolution implementations. On CPUs, the dot product operation between bit vectors can be reduced to bitwise operations and popcounts, significantly increasing throughput compared to 32-bit multiplications and additions.  To validate the efficacy of BFCNs, we conducted experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 semantic segmentation task and Cityscapes. Our BFCN with 1-bit weights and 2-bit activations, which executes 7.8x faster on CPUs or requires less than 1% of resources on FPGAs, achieves performance comparable to its 32-bit counterpart.

title: Learning in an Uncertain World: Representing Ambiguity Through Multiple Hypotheses
Abstract: Many prediction tasks involve inherent uncertainty. This uncertainty can stem from the task itself, as in future prediction where multiple outcomes are equally valid. It can also arise from data labeling, as seen in object detection where objects are often missed or in human pose estimation where occluded joints are assigned ambiguous values. This research focuses on a principled approach for handling such scenarios. We propose a framework that reformulates existing single-prediction models as multiple hypothesis prediction (MHP) models. This framework includes a meta loss and optimization procedure for training these models. To demonstrate our approach, we apply it to four diverse tasks: human pose estimation, future prediction, image classification, and segmentation. We find that MHP models consistently outperform their single-hypothesis counterparts and offer valuable insights into the variability of predictions.
label: AI

title: Flight Dynamics-based Recovery of a UAV Trajectory using Ground Cameras
Abstract: We introduce a novel method for estimating the 6-DOF trajectory of a flying object, such as a quadrotor UAV, within a 3D airspace monitored by multiple fixed ground cameras. Our method leverages a new structure from motion formulation for 3D reconstruction of a single moving point with known motion dynamics. Our key contribution is a novel bundle adjustment procedure that, in addition to optimizing camera poses, regularizes the point trajectory using a prior based on motion dynamics (specifically, flight dynamics). This approach further allows us to infer the underlying control input sent to the UAV's autopilot that determined its flight trajectory.  Our method does not require perfect single-view tracking or appearance matching across views. For robustness, we allow the tracker to generate multiple detections per frame in each video. The true detections and data association across videos are estimated using robust multi-view triangulation and subsequently refined during our bundle adjustment procedure. Quantitative evaluation on simulated data and real videos from indoor and outdoor scenes demonstrates the effectiveness of our method.

title: Monge's Optimal Transport Distance for Image Classification
Abstract: This paper focuses on a similarity measure, known as the Wasserstein distance, for comparing images. The Wasserstein distance arises from a partial differential equation (PDE) formulation of Monge's optimal transport problem. We present an efficient numerical solution method for solving Monge's problem. To illustrate the measure's discriminatory power in image comparison, we employ a 1-Nearest Neighbor (1-NN) machine learning algorithm. This demonstrates the potential benefits of the Wasserstein distance over traditional distance metrics and the Tangent Space distance, which performs well on the MNIST dataset. To our knowledge, the PDE formulation of the Wasserstein metric has not been previously applied to image comparison, nor has the Wasserstein distance been utilized within the 1-nearest neighbor architecture.

title: Adversarial Images for Variational Autoencoders
Abstract: We investigate adversarial attacks on autoencoders. We propose a procedure that distorts the input image to mislead the autoencoder into reconstructing a completely different target image. Our attack targets the internal latent representations, aiming to make the adversarial input produce an internal representation as similar as possible to the target's. We discover that autoencoders exhibit significantly higher robustness to this attack compared to classifiers. While some examples show tolerably small input distortion and reasonable similarity to the target image, there exists a quasi-linear trade-off between these objectives. We report results on MNIST and SVHN datasets and test both regular deterministic autoencoders, reaching similar conclusions in all cases. Finally, we show that the standard adversarial attack for classifiers, while simpler, also demonstrates a direct proportion between input distortion and misdirection in the output. However, this proportionality is obscured by the normalization of the output, which maps a linear layer into non-linear probabilities.

title: Perspective Transformer Nets: Learning Single-View 3D Object Reconstruction without 3D Supervision
Abstract: Understanding the 3D world is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. However, learning effective representations of 3D objects remains an open problem due to the high dimensionality of the data and numerous factors of variation involved. This work investigates the task of single-view 3D object reconstruction from a learning agent's perspective. We formulate the learning process as an interaction between 3D and 2D representations and propose an encoder-decoder network with a novel projection loss defined by the perspective transformation. Crucially, the projection loss enables unsupervised learning using 2D observations without explicit 3D supervision. We demonstrate the model's capability to generate 3D volumes from single 2D images through three sets of experiments: (1) learning from single-class objects, (2) learning from multi-class objects, and (3) testing on novel object classes. The results show superior performance and better generalization ability for 3D object reconstruction when the projection loss is included.

title: BASS Net: Band-Adaptive Spectral-Spatial Feature Learning Neural Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
Abstract: Deep learning-based landcover classification algorithms have recently emerged in the literature. When applied to hyperspectral images (HSI), they face challenges such as high dimensionality, spatial variability of spectral signatures, and limited labeled data. This article presents an end-to-end deep learning architecture that extracts band-specific spectral-spatial features and performs landcover classification. The architecture features fewer independent connection weights, requiring a smaller amount of training data. The method outperforms previously reported accuracies on popular hyperspectral image datasets.
label: AI

title: Towards Robust Deep Neural Networks with BANG
Abstract: Machine learning models, including state-of-the-art deep neural networks, are susceptible to small perturbations that can induce unexpected classification errors. This lack of robustness raises fundamental questions about their generalization properties and poses a significant concern for practical deployments. Since these perturbations can remain imperceptible, the resulting adversarial examples highlight an inherent inconsistency between vulnerable machine learning models and human perception. Some prior work characterizes this problem as a security issue. Despite the significance of the discovered instabilities and subsequent research, their underlying cause remains poorly understood, and no effective solution has been developed. In this paper, we present a novel theory to explain why this phenomenon exists in deep neural networks. Based on this theory, we introduce a simple, efficient, and effective training approach, Batch Adjusted Network Gradients (BANG), which substantially improves the robustness of machine learning models. While BANG does not rely on data augmentation or the use of adversarial images for training, the resulting classifiers are more resistant to adversarial perturbations while maintaining or even enhancing overall classification performance.
label: AI

title: RMPE: Regional Multi-person Pose Estimation
Abstract: Multi-person pose estimation in unconstrained environments poses significant challenges. While state-of-the-art human detectors exhibit good performance, small errors in localization and recognition are unavoidable. These errors can lead to failures in single-person pose estimators (SPPE), especially for methods that solely rely on human detection results. This paper proposes a novel regional multi-person pose estimation (RMPE) framework to facilitate pose estimation in the presence of inaccurate human bounding boxes. Our framework comprises three components: Symmetric Spatial Transformer Network (SSTN), Parametric Pose Non-Maximum-Suppression (NMS), and Pose-Guided Proposals Generator (PGPG). Our method effectively handles inaccurate bounding boxes and redundant detections, achieving a 17% increase in mAP over state-of-the-art methods on the MPII (multi-person) dataset. Our model and source code are publicly available.

title: CDVAE: Co-embedding Deep Variational Auto Encoder for Conditional Variational Generation
Abstract: Problems like predicting a new shading field (Y) for an image (X) are inherently ambiguous, as many distinct solutions can be considered good. Representing this ambiguity necessitates building a conditional model P(Y|X) of the prediction, conditioned on the image. Training such a model presents difficulties, as we usually lack training data containing diverse shadings for the same image. Consequently, we need different training examples to share data and produce effective models. This poses a danger we term "code space collapse"—the training procedure yields a model with a low loss score but poorly represents the conditional distribution. We demonstrate an improved method for building conditional models by leveraging a metric constraint on training data that prevents code space collapse. We showcase our model on two real-world tasks: image saturation adjustment and image relighting. We introduce quantitative metrics for evaluating ambiguous generation results. Our results surpass different strong baselines quantitatively and qualitatively.

title: A Novel Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm for Pattern Recognition with Convex Optimization
Abstract: Image pattern recognition constitutes a crucial area in digital image processing. An efficient pattern recognition algorithm should deliver accurate recognition while minimizing computational time. Among machine learning pattern recognition algorithms, the Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm (AFSA) is a swarm intelligence optimization algorithm that operates based on population and stochastic search. To achieve satisfactory results, numerous parameters must be adjusted in AFSA. Among these parameters, visual and step are particularly significant, as artificial fish primarily move based on these values. In standard AFSA, these parameters remain constant until algorithm termination. Larger values enhance the algorithm's global search capability, while smaller values improve its local search ability. In this paper, we empirically investigate the performance of AFSA and test different approaches to balance local and global exploration through adaptive modification of visual and step during algorithm execution. The proposed approaches are evaluated using four well-known benchmark functions. Experimental results show a substantial positive impact on the performance of AFSA. A convex optimization has been integrated into the proposed work to achieve ideal segmentation of the input image, which is an MR brain image.
label: AI

title: Video Scene Parsing with Predictive Feature Learning
Abstract: This research addresses the challenging video scene parsing problem by developing effective representation learning methods given limited parsing annotations. We contribute two novel methods that form a unified parsing framework: (1) **Predictive feature learning** from nearly unlimited unlabeled video data. Unlike existing methods that learn features from single-frame parsing, we learn spatiotemporal discriminative features by forcing a parsing network to predict future frames and their parsing maps (if available) using only historical frames. This enables the network to effectively capture video dynamics and temporal context, crucial for video scene parsing, without requiring extra manual annotations. (2) **Prediction steering parsing** architecture that effectively adapts the learned spatiotemporal features to scene parsing tasks and provides strong guidance for any off-the-shelf parsing model to achieve better video scene parsing performance. Extensive experiments on two challenging datasets, Cityscapes and Camvid, demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods by showing significant improvements over well-established baselines.
label: AI

title: Shape Completion using 3D-Encoder-Predictor CNNs and Shape Synthesis
Abstract: We introduce a data-driven approach to complete partial 3D shapes using a combination of volumetric deep neural networks and 3D shape synthesis. From a partially-scanned input shape, our method first infers a low-resolution but complete output. For this purpose, we present a 3D-Encoder-Predictor Network (3D-EPN) composed of 3D convolutional layers. The network is trained to predict and fill in missing data and operates on an implicit surface representation that encodes both known and unknown space. This enables us to predict global structure in unknown areas with high accuracy. We then correlate these intermediate results with 3D geometry from a shape database at test time. In a final step, we propose a patch-based 3D shape synthesis method that imposes the 3D geometry from these retrieved shapes as constraints on the coarsely-completed mesh. This synthesis process allows us to reconstruct fine-scale detail and generate high-resolution output while preserving the global mesh structure obtained by the 3D-EPN. Although our 3D-EPN outperforms existing completion methods, the primary contribution of our work lies in the combination of a data-driven shape predictor and analytic 3D shape synthesis. Our results showcase extensive evaluations on a newly-introduced shape completion benchmark for both real-world and synthetic data.
label: AI

title: Noise-Tolerant Life-Long Matrix Completion via Adaptive Sampling
Abstract: We investigate the problem of recovering an incomplete  m×n matrix of rank r with columns arriving online over time. This is known as the problem of life-long matrix completion and finds widespread application in recommendation systems, computer vision, system identification, and more. The challenge lies in designing provably robust algorithms that tolerate large amounts of noise with minimal sample complexity. This work presents algorithms that achieve strong guarantees under two realistic noise models. In bounded deterministic noise, an adversary can add any bounded yet unstructured noise to each column. For this problem, we introduce an algorithm that returns a matrix with a small error, with sample complexity nearly as small as the best prior results in the noiseless case. For sparse random noise, where corrupted columns are sparse and drawn randomly, we present an algorithm that exactly recovers a μ0-incoherent matrix with probability at least 1−δ, using a sample complexity as low as O(μ0rnlog(r/δ)). This result advances the state-of-the-art and matches the lower bound in a worst-case scenario. We also explore scenarios where the hidden matrix lies on a mixture of subspaces and show that the sample complexity can be even smaller. Our proposed algorithms demonstrate strong experimental performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
label: AI

title: Beyond standard benchmarks: Parameterizing performance evaluation in visual object tracking
Abstract: Object-to-camera motion generates diverse apparent motion patterns that significantly affect the performance of short-term visual trackers. Despite their crucial role in designing robust trackers, their influence is poorly explored in standard benchmarks due to weakly defined, biased, and overlapping attribute annotations. This paper proposes a departure from pre-recorded benchmarks with post-hoc annotations by presenting an approach that utilizes omnidirectional videos to generate realistic, consistently annotated, short-term tracking scenarios with precisely parameterized motion patterns. We have created an evaluation system, constructed a fully annotated dataset of omnidirectional videos, and developed generators for typical motion patterns. We provide an in-depth analysis of major tracking paradigms, complementing standard benchmarks and confirming the expressiveness of our evaluation approach.
label: AI

title: Texture Enhancement via High-Resolution Style Transfer for Single-Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: Recently, numerous deep-neural-network (DNN)-based approaches have been proposed for single-image super-resolution (SISR). Despite their promising results on major structural regions like edges and lines, they still struggle with limited performance on texture regions, which consist of highly complex and fine patterns. This limitation arises because during the acquisition of a low-resolution (LR) image via downsampling, these regions lose most of the high-frequency information necessary to represent texture details. This paper introduces a novel texture enhancement framework for SISR, effectively improving spatial resolution in texture regions, along with edges and lines. We call our method the high-resolution (HR) style transfer algorithm. Our framework consists of three steps: (i) generate an initial HR image from an interpolated LR image using an SISR algorithm, (ii) generate an HR style image from the initial HR image via downscaling and tiling, and (iii) combine the HR style image with the initial HR image through a customized style transfer algorithm. Here, the HR style image is obtained by downscaling the initial HR image and then repetitively tiling it into an image of the same size as the HR image. This downscaling and tiling process stems from the idea that texture regions often comprise small regions that appear similar but differ in scale. This process creates an HR style image rich in details, which can be used to restore high-frequency texture details back into the initial HR image via the style transfer algorithm. Experimental results on various texture datasets demonstrate that our proposed HR style transfer algorithm produces more visually pleasing results compared to competing methods.
label: AI

title: Plug & Play Generative Networks: Conditional Iterative Generation of Images in Latent Space
Abstract: Generating high-resolution, photo-realistic images has long been a goal in machine learning. Recently, Nguyen et al. (2016) presented an intriguing method for synthesizing novel images by performing gradient ascent in the latent space of a generator network to maximize the activations of one or multiple neurons in a separate classifier network. This paper extends this method by introducing an additional prior on the latent code, improving both sample quality and diversity. This leads to a state-of-the-art generative model that produces high-quality images at higher resolutions (227x227) than previous generative models, and it does so for all 1000 ImageNet categories. Additionally, we provide a unified probabilistic interpretation of related activation maximization methods and refer to this general class of models as "Plug and Play Generative Networks" (PPGNs). PPGNs consist of (1) a generator network G capable of drawing a wide range of image types and (2) a replaceable "condition" network C that instructs the generator what to draw. We demonstrate the generation of images conditioned on a class (when C is an ImageNet or MIT Places classification network) and also conditioned on a caption (when C is an image captioning network). Our method also improves the state of the art of Multifaceted Feature Visualization, which generates the set of synthetic inputs that activate a neuron to better understand deep neural network operations. Finally, we show that our model performs reasonably well at the task of image inpainting. While image models are used in this paper, the approach is modality-agnostic and can be applied to various data types.

title: An Artificial Agent for Robust Image Registration
Abstract: 3-D image registration, which involves aligning two or more images, is a crucial step in various medical applications, from diagnosis to therapy. Image registration is commonly performed by optimizing an image matching metric as a cost function. However, this task is challenging due to the non-convex nature of the matching metric over the plausible registration parameter space and insufficient approaches for robust optimization. As a result, current approaches are often customized to specific problems and sensitive to image quality and artifacts. This paper proposes a completely different approach to image registration, inspired by how experts perform the task. We first cast the image registration problem as a "strategy learning" process, where the goal is to find the optimal sequence of motion actions (e.g., up, down, etc.) that results in image alignment. Within this approach, an artificial agent is learned, modeled using deep convolutional neural networks, with 3D raw image data as input and the next optimal action as output. To address the dimensionality of the problem, we propose a greedy supervised approach for end-to-end training, coupled with attention-driven hierarchical strategy. The resulting registration approach inherently encodes both a data-driven matching metric and an optimal registration strategy (policy). We demonstrate, on two 3-D/3-D medical image registration examples with drastically different challenges, that the artificial agent outperforms several state-of-the-art registration methods by a large margin in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

title: Sync-DRAW: Automatic Video Generation using Deep Recurrent Attentive Architectures
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for video generation called Synchronized Deep Recurrent Attentive Writer (Sync-DRAW). Sync-DRAW can also perform text-to-video generation, which, to our knowledge, makes it the first approach of its kind. It combines a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a Recurrent Attention Mechanism in a novel way to create a temporally dependent sequence of frames that are gradually formed over time. The recurrent attention mechanism in Sync-DRAW attends to each individual frame of the video in synchronization, while the VAE learns a latent distribution for the entire video at the global level. Our experiments with Bouncing MNIST, KTH, and UCF-101 datasets suggest that Sync-DRAW effectively learns the spatial and temporal information of the videos and generates frames with high structural integrity. Additionally, it can generate videos from simple captions on these datasets (Accepted as oral paper in ACM-Multimedia 2017).

title: End-to-End Training of Hybrid CNN-CRF Models for Stereo
Abstract: We propose a novel and principled hybrid CNN+CRF model for stereo estimation. Our model enables the exploitation of the advantages of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and conditional random fields (CRFs) in a unified approach. The CNNs compute expressive features for matching and distinctive color edges, which are then used to calculate the unary and binary costs of the CRF. For inference, we apply a recently proposed highly parallel dual block descent algorithm that requires only a small fixed number of iterations to compute a high-quality approximate minimizer. As the main contribution of this paper, we propose a theoretically sound method based on the structured output support vector machine (SSVM) to train the hybrid CNN+CRF model on large-scale data end-to-end. Our trained models perform exceptionally well despite using shallow CNNs and without applying any post-processing to the final output of the CRF. We evaluate our combined models on challenging stereo benchmarks such as Middlebury 2014 and Kitti 2015 and also investigate the performance of each individual component. |||

title: POSEidon: Face-from-Depth for Driver Pose Estimation
Abstract: Fast and accurate head pose estimation from depth images is crucial for driver attention monitoring, particularly in challenging scenarios with varying illumination, occlusions, and extreme poses. This paper introduces POSEidon, a novel deep learning framework for head localization and pose estimation on depth images. POSEidon comprises three independent convolutional networks followed by a fusion layer designed to understand pose from depth. Additionally, a Face-from-Depth approach is proposed to recover facial appearance for enhanced head position and orientation comprehension. This method achieves impressive face reconstruction results. Evaluations on Biwi Kinect Head Pose, ICT-3DHP, and the new Pandora dataset demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art techniques, achieving real-time processing at over 30 frames per second.
label: AI

title: Effective Quantization Methods for Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Reducing the bit-widths of weights, activations, and gradients in neural networks can significantly shrink storage size and memory usage, enabling faster training and inference through bitwise operations. However, previous quantization attempts on RNNs have resulted in substantial performance degradation when using low bit-width weights and activations. This paper proposes methods to quantize the structure of gates and interlinks in LSTM and GRU cells, along with balanced quantization methods for weights to mitigate performance degradation. Experiments on PTB and IMDB datasets validate the effectiveness of these methods, achieving performances that match or surpass the previous state-of-the-art in quantized RNNs.
label: AI

title: Combining Data-driven and Model-driven Methods for Robust Facial Landmark Detection
Abstract: Facial landmark detection is a fundamental but challenging task in real-world computer vision applications. This paper presents an effective and robust approach combining data- and model-driven methods. A Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) is trained to generate response maps for all facial landmark points, leveraging holistic facial information for global landmark estimation. Subsequently, the maximum points in the response maps are fitted with a pre-trained Point Distribution Model (PDM), incorporating shape prior information to correct outlier locations. Finally, a weighted Regularized Landmark Mean-Shift (RLMS) is employed to iteratively refine the facial shape. This Estimation-Correction-Tuning process effectively combines the advantages of FCN's global robustness, PDM's outlier correction capability, and RLMS's non-parametric optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on challenging datasets such as 300W, AFLW, AFW, and COFW, achieving satisfactory detection results even in the presence of exaggerated expressions, large head poses, and partial occlusions.
label: AI

title: User Dependent Features in Online Signature Verification
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for online signature verification based on user-dependent feature selection and symbolic representation. Unlike existing methods that utilize the same features for all users, this approach leverages user-specific characteristics to select distinct features for each individual. Initially, all possible features are extracted for all users, and a feature selection method identifies user-dependent features. These selected features are clustered using the Fuzzy C-means algorithm. To preserve intra-class variation within each user, each cluster is represented by an interval-valued symbolic feature vector. A signature verification method based on this cluster-based symbolic representation is proposed. Extensive experiments on MCYT-100 User (DB1) and MCYT-330 User (DB2) online signature datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.
label: AI

title: Wider or Deeper: Revisiting the ResNet Model for Visual Recognition
Abstract: The trend towards increasingly deep neural networks is driven by the observation that deeper networks often lead to better performance. However, recent evidence suggests that simply increasing depth may not be the optimal approach, particularly considering other limitations. Research on deep residual networks has indicated that they might not operate as a single deep network but rather as an ensemble of numerous relatively shallow networks. This paper examines these issues, proposing a novel interpretation of the unravelled view of deep residual networks, which explains observed experimental behaviors. Based on this interpretation, a shallower architecture of residual networks is derived, significantly outperforming much deeper models like ResNet-200 on the ImageNet classification dataset. This performance is transferable to other domains, as demonstrated by a semantic segmentation approach that surpasses state-of-the-art results on PASCAL VOC, PASCAL Context, and Cityscapes datasets. This shallower architecture outperforms its comparators, including very deep ResNets, while being more efficient in memory use and sometimes also in training time. Code and models are available at https://github.com/itijyou/ademxapp.
label: AI

title: Active Deep Learning for Classification of Hyperspectral Images
Abstract: This paper investigates active deep learning classification of hyperspectral images. Deep learning has achieved success in various applications, but requires high-quality labeled samples to construct a deep learning network. Obtaining good labeled samples for hyperspectral images in remote sensing applications is expensive. This paper proposes an active learning algorithm based on weighted incremental dictionary learning for this purpose. The proposed algorithm selects training samples that maximize two selection criteria: representativeness and uncertainty. This algorithm efficiently trains a deep network by actively selecting training samples at each iteration. The proposed algorithm is applied for the classification of hyperspectral images and compared with other active learning-based classification algorithms. Results show that the proposed algorithm is efficient and effective in classifying hyperspectral images.
label: AI

title: Fast Supervised Discrete Hashing and its Analysis
Abstract: This paper introduces a learning-based supervised discrete hashing method. Binary hashing is widely used for large-scale image retrieval, video search, and document search due to the compact representation of binary codes, which are essential for data storage and efficient for query searches using bit-operations. The recently proposed Supervised Discrete Hashing (SDH) method effectively solves mixed-integer programming problems through alternating optimization and the Discrete Cyclic Coordinate descent (DCC) method. This paper demonstrates that the SDH model can be simplified without performance degradation based on preliminary experiments. This simplified model is termed "Fast SDH" (FSDH). The FSDH model is analyzed and a mathematically exact solution is provided. Unlike SDH, the FSDH model does not require an alternating optimization algorithm or depend on initial values. It is also easier to implement than Iterative Quantization (ITQ). Experimental results involving a large-scale database show that FSDH outperforms conventional SDH in terms of precision, recall, and computation time.

title: Speed/accuracy trade-offs for modern convolutional object detectors
Abstract: This paper serves as a guide for selecting an object detection architecture that balances speed, memory usage, and accuracy for specific applications and platforms. It explores various ways to trade accuracy for speed and memory in modern convolutional object detection systems. While numerous successful systems have been proposed, apples-to-apples comparisons are challenging due to differences in base feature extractors (e.g., VGG, Residual Networks), default image resolutions, and hardware/software platforms. This paper presents a unified implementation of Faster R-CNN, R-FCN, and SSD systems, viewed as "meta-architectures," and traces out the speed/accuracy trade-off curve created by using alternative feature extractors and varying critical parameters like image size within each meta-architecture. On one extreme, where speed and memory are paramount, a real-time detector is presented that can be deployed on mobile devices. On the opposite end, prioritizing accuracy, a detector achieving state-of-the-art performance on the COCO detection task is introduced.
label: AI

title: Deep Cuboid Detection: Beyond 2D Bounding Boxes
Abstract: This paper presents a Deep Cuboid Detector that takes a consumer-quality RGB image of a cluttered scene and localizes all 3D cuboids (box-like objects). Unlike classical approaches that fit a 3D model from low-level cues like corners, edges, and vanishing points, this paper proposes an end-to-end deep learning system for cuboid detection across various semantic categories (e.g., ovens, shipping boxes, furniture). Cuboids are localized using a 2D bounding box, and their corners are simultaneously localized, effectively producing a 3D interpretation of box-like objects. Keypoints are refined by iteratively pooling convolutional features, significantly improving the baseline method. The deep learning cuboid detector is trained end-to-end and is suitable for real-time applications in augmented reality (AR) and robotics.
label: AI

title: Modeling Relationships in Referential Expressions with Compositional Modular Networks
Abstract: People often describe entities in images using their relationships with other entities. For example, "the black cat sitting under the table" refers to both a "black cat" entity and its relationship with a "table" entity. Understanding these relationships is crucial for interpreting and grounding natural language expressions. Most prior work focuses on either grounding entire referential expressions holistically or localizing relationships based on a fixed set of categories. This paper presents a modular deep architecture capable of analyzing referential expressions into their component parts, identifying entities and relationships mentioned in the input expression and grounding them all in the scene. This approach, called Compositional Modular Networks (CMNs), is a novel architecture that learns linguistic analysis and visual inference end-to-end. CMNs are built around two types of neural modules that inspect local regions and pairwise interactions between regions. Evaluations on multiple referential expression datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches on all tasks.
label: AI

title: High-Resolution Image Inpainting using Multi-Scale Neural Patch Synthesis
Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning show promising potential for filling large holes in natural images with semantically plausible and context-aware details, impacting fundamental image manipulation tasks like object removal. While these learning-based methods excel at capturing high-level features compared to prior techniques, they are limited to very low-resolution inputs due to memory constraints and training difficulties. Even for slightly larger images, inpainted regions appear blurry, and unpleasant boundaries become visible. This paper proposes a multi-scale neural patch synthesis approach based on joint optimization of image content and texture constraints. This approach not only preserves contextual structures but also produces high-frequency details by matching and adapting patches with the most similar mid-layer feature correlations of a deep classification network. Evaluations on ImageNet and Paris Streetview datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art inpainting accuracy. The proposed approach generates sharper and more coherent results than previous methods, especially for high-resolution images.
label: AI

title: Sequential Person Recognition in Photo Albums with a Recurrent Network
Abstract: Recognizing the identities of people in everyday photos is still a challenging problem for machine vision due to non-frontal faces, changes in clothing, location, lighting, and similar factors. Recent studies have shown that rich relational information between people in the same photo can aid in identity recognition. This paper proposes modeling the relational information between people as a sequence prediction task. At the core of this work is a novel recurrent network architecture, where relational information between instance labels and appearance is modeled jointly. In addition to relational cues, scene context is incorporated into the sequence prediction model without additional cost. This approach provides a unified framework for modeling both contextual cues and visual appearance of person instances. The model is trained end-to-end with a sequence of annotated instances in a photo as input and a sequence of corresponding labels as targets. This simple yet elegant formulation achieves state-of-the-art performance on the newly released People In Photo Albums (PIPA) dataset.
label: AI

title: Semantic Facial Expression Editing using Autoencoded Flow
Abstract: Manipulating facial expressions in images, such as changing a smile to a neutral expression, is challenging due to the highly non-linear nature of expression changes and their dependence on facial appearance. This paper presents a fully automatic approach to face editing that combines the advantages of flow-based face manipulation with the generative capabilities of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). During training, the model learns to encode the flow from one expression to another over a low-dimensional latent space. At test time, expression editing can be achieved through simple latent vector arithmetic. The method is evaluated on two applications: 1) single-image facial expression editing, and 2) facial expression interpolation between two images. Results demonstrate that the method generates images of higher perceptual quality than previous VAE and flow-based methods.
label: AI

title: Attend in groups: a weakly-supervised deep learning framework for learning from web data
Abstract: Large-scale datasets have driven the rapid development of deep neural networks for visual recognition. However, annotating a massive dataset is expensive and time-consuming. Web images and their labels are much easier to obtain, but direct training on such automatically harvested images can lead to unsatisfactory performance due to noisy labels adversely affecting learned recognition models. This paper proposes an end-to-end weakly-supervised deep learning framework robust to label noise in Web images. The framework relies on two unified strategies -- random grouping and attention -- to effectively reduce the negative impact of noisy web image annotations. Random grouping stacks multiple images into a single training instance, increasing labeling accuracy at the instance level. Attention, on the other hand, suppresses noisy signals from both incorrectly labeled images and less discriminative image regions. Extensive experiments on two challenging datasets, including a newly collected fine-grained dataset with Web images of different car models, clearly demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed methods over competitive baselines.
label: AI

title: Machine Learning for Dental Image Analysis
Abstract: To study the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to dental imaging, AI technology was applied to classify a set of panoramic radiographs using (a) a convolutional neural network (CNN), a form of artificial neural network (ANN), (b) scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) algorithms, and (c) histogram of oriented gradients (HOG).

title: Efficient Likelihood Bayesian Constrained Local Model
Abstract: The constrained local model (CLM) proposes a paradigm where the locations of local landmark detectors are constrained to lie in a subspace spanned by a shape point distribution model (PDM). Fitting the model to an object involves two steps: (1) computing a response map for each landmark using local-texture detectors, representing the likelihood of the landmark's location, and (2) determining an optimal PDM by jointly maximizing all response maps while enforcing a global shape constraint. This global optimization can be considered a Bayesian inference problem, where the posterior distribution of shape and pose parameters can be inferred using maximum a posteriori (MAP). This paper presents a cascaded face-alignment approach using random-forest regressors to efficiently estimate the positions of each landmark as a likelihood term in the CLM model. From a CLM framework interpretation, this algorithm is named as an efficient likelihood Bayesian constrained local model (elBCLM). Furthermore, in each stage of the regressors, the PDM non-rigid parameters from the previous stage can serve as shape clues for training each stage regressors. Experimental results on benchmarks demonstrate that this approach achieves a 3 to 5 times speed-up compared to CLM models and improves fitting quality by around 10% compared to similar regression models.
label: AI

title: Photographic home styles in Congress: a computer vision approach
Abstract: While members of Congress now routinely communicate with constituents using images on various internet platforms, little is known about how images are used strategically in political communication. This is primarily due to computational limitations that have hindered large-scale, systematic analyses of image features. However, new developments in computer vision are making systematic image study feasible. This paper develops a framework for understanding visual political communication by extending Fenno's analysis of home style (Fenno 1978) to images, introducing "photographic" home styles. Using approximately 192,000 photographs collected from members of Congress' Facebook profiles, machine learning software with convolutional neural networks is built, and an image manipulation experiment is conducted to explore how the race of people members of Congress pose with shapes photographic home styles. Evidence is found that electoral pressures shape photographic home styles, demonstrating that Democratic and Republican members of Congress use images in very different ways.
label: AI

title: Learning a Discriminative Filter Bank within a CNN for Fine-grained Recognition
Abstract: Compared to earlier multistage frameworks using CNN features, recent end-to-end deep approaches for fine-grained recognition primarily enhance the mid-level learning capability of CNNs. Previous approaches achieve this by introducing an auxiliary network to infuse localization information into the main classification network or employing a sophisticated feature encoding method to capture higher-order feature statistics. This paper demonstrates that mid-level representation learning can be enhanced within the CNN framework by learning a bank of convolutional filters that capture class-specific discriminative patches without requiring extra part or bounding box annotations. This filter bank is well-structured, properly initialized, and discriminatively learned through a novel asymmetric multi-stream architecture with convolutional filter supervision and a non-random layer initialization. Experimental results show that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on three publicly available fine-grained recognition datasets (CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and FGVC-Aircraft). Ablation studies and visualizations are provided to understand the approach.
label: AI

title: Split-Brain Autoencoders: Unsupervised Learning by Cross-Channel Prediction
Abstract: This paper proposes split-brain autoencoders, a straightforward modification of the traditional autoencoder architecture, for unsupervised representation learning. The method introduces a split to the network, resulting in two disjoint sub-networks. Each sub-network is trained to perform a challenging task -- predicting one subset of the data channels from another. Together, the sub-networks extract features from the entire input signal. By forcing the network to solve cross-channel prediction tasks, a representation is induced within the network that transfers well to other, unseen tasks. This method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several large-scale transfer learning benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Measuring and modeling the perception of natural and unconstrained gaze in humans and machines
Abstract: Humans excel at interpreting the gaze direction of others in their surroundings. This ability is fundamental for engaging in joint visual attention, crucial for establishing social interactions. This paper investigates the accuracy of human gaze direction perception in lifelike scenes, where individuals can move their heads and eyes freely, and explores the sources of information underlying these perceptual processes. This question presents a challenge from both empirical and computational perspectives due to the complexity of visual input in real-life situations. The paper empirically measures human accuracy in perceiving the gaze direction of others in lifelike scenes and computationally studies the sources of information and representations underlying this cognitive capacity. Results show that humans perform better in face-to-face conditions compared to recorded conditions, and this advantage is not due to the availability of input dynamics. Furthermore, humans demonstrate good performance even when only the eyes-region is visible, rather than the whole face. A computational model that replicates the pattern of human performance is developed, including the finding that the eyes-region alone contains the required information for estimating both head orientation and direction of gaze. Consistent with neurophysiological findings on task-specific face regions in the brain, the learned computational representations reproduce perceptual effects like the Wollaston illusion when trained to estimate direction of gaze, but not when trained to recognize objects or faces. |||

title: Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation In The Wild Using Improved CNN Supervision
Abstract: This paper presents a CNN-based approach for 3D human body pose estimation from single RGB images, tackling the challenge of limited generalizability arising from the scarcity of publicly available 3D pose data. By leveraging existing 3D and 2D pose data, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on established benchmarks through feature transfer, while also generalizing to real-world scenes. Additionally, we introduce a new training dataset for human body pose estimation from monocular images of real humans, capturing ground truth using a multi-camera markerless motion capture system. This dataset offers greater diversity in pose, human appearance, clothing, occlusion, and viewpoints, enabling a wider scope of augmentation. We further contribute a new benchmark encompassing outdoor and indoor scenes, demonstrating that our 3D pose dataset surpasses existing annotated data in terms of real-world performance. This performance is further enhanced by incorporating transfer learning from 2D pose data. Overall, we advocate for the importance of combining transfer learning of representations with algorithmic and data contributions for robust general 3D body pose estimation.
label: AI

title: 3D Ultrasound image segmentation: A Survey
Abstract: This paper reviews three-dimensional ultrasound image segmentation methods, focusing on their applications and underlying concepts. While many two-dimensional image segmentation techniques have been mistakenly considered as three-dimensional approaches, we examine them as three-dimensional techniques. We specifically select studies that address medical three-dimensional ultrasound image segmentation using their proposed methods. We present and tabulate the evaluation methods and comparisons between these methods, considering evaluation techniques, interactivity, and robustness.

title: InterpoNet, A brain inspired neural network for optical flow dense interpolation
Abstract: Sparse-to-dense interpolation for optical flow is a fundamental step in many leading optical flow estimation algorithms. EpicFlow, the current state-of-the-art interpolation method, relies on a local average approach based on edge-aware geodesic distance. We propose a novel data-driven sparse-to-dense interpolation algorithm based on a fully convolutional network. Drawing inspiration from the filling-in process in the visual cortex, our learning process incorporates lateral dependencies between neurons and multi-layer supervision. We highlight the importance of image contours in the learning process. Our method demonstrates robustness and outperforms EpicFlow on competitive optical flow benchmarks, working with various underlying matching algorithms. This leads to state-of-the-art performance on the Sintel and KITTI 2012 benchmarks.
label: AI

title: On the Existence of Synchrostates in Multichannel EEG Signals during Face-perception Tasks
Abstract: Phase synchronization in multichannel EEG is recognized as a manifestation of functional brain connectivity. Traditional phase synchronization studies predominantly rely on time-averaged synchrony measures, neglecting the temporal evolution of phase differences. This paper introduces a new method to identify a small set of unique phase-synchronized patterns or "states" in multichannel EEG recordings, each "state" exhibiting stability on the order of milliseconds. These states are analyzed in typical and pathological subjects during face perception tasks. Our proposed methodology bridges the concepts of EEG microstates and phase synchronization in the time and frequency domains, respectively. We report analysis for four groups of children: typical, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), low anxiety, and high anxiety, totaling 44 subjects. Consistently, across all groups, we observe the existence of these states, termed "synchrostates", within specific cognition-related frequency bands (beta and gamma bands). However, the topographies of these synchrostates differ for different subject groups with varying pathological conditions. The inter-synchrostate switching follows a well-defined sequence, capturing the underlying inter-electrode phase relation dynamics in a stimulus- and person-centric manner. Our study is motivated by the well-established EEG microstate phenomenon, which exhibits stable potential maps across the scalp. Here, we report a similar observation of quasi-stable phase-synchronized states in multichannel EEG. The existence of synchrostates, coupled with their unique switching sequence characteristics, presents a potentially new field within contemporary EEG phase synchronization studies.

title: Computer Aided Detection of Oral Lesions on CT Images
Abstract: Oral lesions are significant findings on computed tomography (CT) images. This study proposes a fully automatic method for detecting oral lesions in the mandibular region from dental CT images. Two methods were developed to recognize two types of lesions: (1) Close border (CB) lesions and (2) Open border (OB) lesions, covering most lesion types found on CT images. For CB lesion detection, fifteen features were extracted from each initial lesion candidate, and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) neural network was used to classify suspicious regions. OB lesions were detected using a rule-based image processing method, eliminating the need for feature extraction or classification algorithms. The results were validated using a CT dataset of 52 patients, including 22 with abnormalities and 30 normal. Using a non-training dataset, the CB detection algorithm yielded 71% sensitivity with 0.31 false positives per patient. Furthermore, the OB detection algorithm achieved 100% sensitivity with 0.13 false positives per patient. These findings suggest that the proposed framework, consisting of two methods, has the potential for clinical application, assisting radiologists in improved diagnosis.

title: Gossip training for deep learning
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of accelerating the training of convolutional networks by exploring a distributed method adapted to stochastic gradient descent (SGD). The parallel optimization setup utilizes multiple threads, each applying independent gradient descents on a local variable. We introduce a novel approach for sharing information between threads, drawing inspiration from gossip algorithms and exhibiting favorable consensus convergence properties. Our method, dubbed GoSGD, offers the advantage of being fully asynchronous and decentralized. We compare GoSGD to the recent EASGD method on CIFAR-10, demonstrating encouraging results.
label: AI

title: Efficient Linear Programming for Dense CRFs
Abstract: The fully connected conditional random field (CRF) with Gaussian pairwise potentials has gained popularity and proven effective for multi-class semantic segmentation. While the energy of a dense CRF can be minimized accurately using a linear programming (LP) relaxation, the state-of-the-art algorithm is too slow for practical applications. To address this limitation, we introduce an efficient LP minimization algorithm for dense CRFs. We develop a proximal minimization framework, where the dual of each proximal problem is optimized through block coordinate descent. We demonstrate that each block of variables can be optimized efficiently. Specifically, for one block, the problem decomposes into significantly smaller subproblems, each defined over a single pixel. For the other block, the problem is optimized using conditional gradient descent, offering two advantages: 1) the conditional gradient can be computed linearly in time with the number of pixels and labels; and 2) the optimal step size can be calculated analytically. Our experiments on standard datasets provide compelling evidence that our approach outperforms all existing baselines, including the previous LP-based approach for dense CRFs.

title: Surveillance Video Parsing with Single Frame Supervision
Abstract: Surveillance video parsing, which segments video frames into various labels (e.g., face, pants, left-leg), has wide-ranging applications. However, pixel-wise annotation of all frames is tedious and inefficient. This paper develops a Single frame Video Parsing (SVP) method that requires only one labeled frame per video during the training stage. To parse a specific frame, the video segment preceding the frame is jointly considered. SVP (1) roughly parses frames within the video segment, (2) estimates the optical flow between frames, and (3) fuses the rough parsing results warped by optical flow to produce a refined parsing result. The three components of SVP, namely frame parsing, optical flow estimation, and temporal fusion, are integrated in an end-to-end manner. Experimental results on two surveillance video datasets demonstrate the superiority of SVP over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: A Large-scale Distributed Video Parsing and Evaluation Platform
Abstract: Visual surveillance systems have emerged as one of the largest data sources for Big Visual Data in the real world. Despite advancements in various visual recognition tasks and surveillance applications (e.g., pedestrian/vehicle detection, people/vehicle counting), existing video analysis systems struggle with scalability, expansibility, and error-proneness. Furthermore, few algorithms explore the unique values and characteristics of large-scale surveillance videos. To address these challenges in large-scale video analysis, we develop a scalable video parsing and evaluation platform by integrating advanced techniques for Big Data processing, including Spark Streaming, Kafka, and Hadoop Distributed Filesystem (HDFS). The system features a Web User Interface for collecting user satisfaction levels on recognition tasks, enabling performance evaluation of the entire system. Additionally, the highly extensible platform, operating on long-term surveillance videos, facilitates the development of more intelligent incremental algorithms to enhance the performance of diverse visual recognition tasks.
label: AI

title: Fast Face-swap Using Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of face swapping in images, where an input identity is transformed into a target identity while preserving pose, facial expression, and lighting. We leverage convolutional neural networks trained to capture the appearance of the target identity from an unstructured collection of their photographs. This approach is enabled by framing face swapping as a style transfer problem, where the goal is to render an image in the style of another. Building upon recent advancements in this field, we introduce a new loss function that empowers the network to produce highly photorealistic results. By combining neural networks with simple pre- and post-processing steps, we aim to achieve real-time face swapping with no user input.
label: AI

title: Occlusion-Aware Video Deblurring with a New Layered Blur Model
Abstract: This paper presents a deblurring method for scenes with occluding objects using a carefully designed layered blur model. Layered blur models are frequently employed in motion deblurring to handle locally varying blurs caused by object motions or depth variations in a scene. However, conventional models have limitations in representing layer interactions at occlusion boundaries. We address this limitation both theoretically and experimentally, proposing a new layered blur model that reflects the actual blur generation process. Based on this model, we develop an occlusion-aware deblurring method capable of estimating not only the clear foreground and background but also the object motion more accurately. We provide a novel analysis of the blur kernel at object boundaries, highlighting the distinctive characteristics of the blur kernel that cannot be captured by conventional blur models. Experimental results on synthetic and real blurred videos demonstrate that our method yields superior results, particularly at object boundaries.
label: AI

title: Predicting Human Eye Fixations via an LSTM-based Saliency Attentive Model
Abstract: Data-driven saliency has recently gained significant attention due to the use of Convolutional Neural Networks for predicting gaze fixations. In this paper, we move beyond standard saliency prediction approaches, where gaze maps are computed with a feed-forward network, and introduce a novel model that can predict accurate saliency maps by incorporating neural attentive mechanisms. The core of our solution is a Convolutional LSTM that focuses on the most salient regions of the input image to iteratively refine the predicted saliency map. Additionally, to address the center bias inherent in human eye fixations, our model can learn a set of prior maps generated using Gaussian functions. We show, through comprehensive evaluation, that our proposed architecture outperforms the current state-of-the-art on public saliency prediction datasets. We further investigate the contribution of each key component to demonstrate their robustness across various scenarios.
label: AI

title: Lens Distortion Rectification using Triangulation based Interpolation
Abstract: Nonlinear lens distortion rectification is a common initial step in image processing applications where the assumption of a linear camera model is essential. To rectify lens distortion, the forward distortion model needs to be known. However, many self-calibration methods estimate the inverse distortion model. In the literature, the inverse of the estimated model is approximated for image rectification, introducing additional error to the system. This paper proposes a novel distortion rectification method that directly utilizes the inverse distortion model. The method starts by mapping distorted pixels to the rectified image using the inverse distortion model. The resulting set of points with subpixel locations are triangulated. The pixel values of the rectified image are linearly interpolated based on this triangulation. This method is applicable to all camera calibration methods that estimate the inverse distortion model and performs well across a wide range of parameters.
label: AI

title: Is a picture worth a thousand words? A Deep Multi-Modal Fusion Architecture for Product Classification in e-commerce
Abstract: Precise and efficient product categorization is a major challenge in modern e-commerce. The high volume of new products uploaded daily and the dynamic nature of categories necessitate machine learning models that can reduce the cost and time required for human editors. This paper proposes a decision-level fusion approach for multi-modal product classification using text and image inputs. We train input-specific state-of-the-art deep neural networks for each input source, demonstrating the potential of combining them into a multi-modal architecture. We train a novel policy network that learns to choose between these networks. Finally, we show that our multi-modal network improves the top-1 accuracy compared to both individual networks on a real-world large-scale product classification dataset collected from Walmart.com. While we focus on image-text fusion, characteristic of e-commerce domains, our algorithms can be easily applied to other modalities like audio, video, physical sensors, etc.
