title: Deep Quantization: Encoding Convolutional Activations with Deep Generative Model
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven highly effective for visual recognition, where learning a universal representation from convolutional layer activations is a fundamental problem. This paper presents Fisher Vector encoding with Variational Auto-Encoder (FV-VAE), a novel deep architecture that quantizes local activations of convolutional layers within a deep generative model, training them in an end-to-end manner. To incorporate FV encoding strategies into deep generative models, we introduce the Variational Auto-Encoder model, which facilitates variational inference and learning in a neural network that can be readily optimized using standard stochastic gradient methods. Unlike traditional FV, which relies on parsimonious fitting of a discrete mixture model to data distribution, the proposed FV-VAE offers greater flexibility in representing the natural properties of data for improved generalization. Extensive experiments were conducted on three public datasets: UCF101, ActivityNet, and CUB-200-2011, in the context of video action recognition and fine-grained image classification. Superior results were reported compared to state-of-the-art representations. Notably, our proposed FV-VAE achieves the highest published accuracy of 94.2% on UCF101.
label: AI

title: Inertial-Based Scale Estimation for Structure from Motion on Mobile Devices
Abstract: Structure from motion algorithms inherently suffer from the limitation that reconstruction can only be determined up to an unknown scale factor. Modern mobile devices are equipped with an inertial measurement unit (IMU), which can be used to estimate the scale of the reconstruction. We propose a method that recovers the metric scale given inertial measurements and camera poses. This process also involves temporal and spatial alignment of the camera and the IMU, making our solution readily combinable with existing visual reconstruction software. Our method can handle noisy camera pose estimates, often caused by motion blur or rolling shutter artifacts, by employing a Rauch-Tung-Striebel (RTS) smoother. Furthermore, scale estimation is performed in the frequency domain, providing greater robustness to inaccurate sensor timestamps and noisy IMU samples compared to the previously used time domain representation. Unlike previous methods, our approach has no parameters that need to be tuned for optimal performance. Experiments demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and convergence speed of the scale estimate. The accuracy of the scale is approximately 1% from the ground truth, depending on the recording. We also showcase how our method can improve the scale accuracy of Project Tango's built-in motion tracking.
label: AI

title: Social Behavior Prediction from First Person Videos
Abstract: This paper presents a method to predict the future movements (location and gaze direction) of basketball players as a whole from their first-person videos. The predicted behaviors reflect individual physical spaces that afford the next actions while conforming to social behaviors by engaging in joint attention. Our key innovation is to use the 3D reconstruction of multiple first-person cameras to automatically annotate each other's visual semantics of social configurations. We leverage two learning signals uniquely embedded in first-person videos. Individually, a first-person video records the visual semantics of a spatial and social layout around a person, allowing association with past similar situations. Collectively, first-person videos follow joint attention, which can link individuals to a group. We learn the egocentric visual semantics of group movements using a Siamese neural network to retrieve future trajectories. We consolidate the retrieved trajectories from all players by maximizing a measure of social compatibility—the gaze alignment towards joint attention predicted by their social formation, where the dynamics of joint attention are learned by a long-term recurrent convolutional network. This enables us to characterize which social configuration is more plausible and predict future group trajectories.
label: AI

title: Easy-setup eye movement recording system for human-computer interaction
Abstract: Tracking human eye movements is expected to yield natural and convenient applications in human-computer interaction (HCI). To implement an effective eye-tracking system, eye movements must be recorded without imposing any restrictions on the user's behavior or causing discomfort. This paper describes an eye movement recording system that offers free-head, simple configuration. It does not require the user to wear anything on their head, allowing them to move freely. Instead of using a computer, the system utilizes a visual digital signal processor (DSP) camera to detect the position of the eye corner, the center of the pupil, and then calculate the eye movement. Evaluation tests reveal that the system's sampling rate can reach 300 Hz, with an accuracy of approximately 1.8 degrees/s.
label: AI

title: Material Recognition from Local Appearance in Global Context
Abstract: Recognizing materials has proven to be a challenging problem due to the wide variation in appearance within and between categories. Global image context, such as where the material is or what object it constitutes, can be crucial for material recognition. However, existing methods implicitly fuse materials and context by using large receptive fields as input (i.e., large image patches). Many recent material recognition methods treat materials as another set of labels, like objects. Materials, however, differ fundamentally from objects as they have no inherent shape or defined spatial extent. Approaches that ignore this can only leverage limited implicit context as it appears during training. Instead, we show that recognizing materials purely from their local appearance and integrating separately recognized global contextual cues, including objects and places, leads to superior dense, per-pixel material recognition. We achieve this by training a fully-convolutional material recognition network end-to-end with only material category supervision. We integrate object and place estimates into this network from independent CNNs. This approach avoids the need for an impractically large amount of training data to cover the product space of materials, objects, and scenes, while fully leveraging contextual cues for dense material recognition. Furthermore, we perform a detailed analysis of the effects of context granularity, spatial resolution, and the network level at which we introduce context. On a recently introduced comprehensive and diverse material database, we confirm that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly less training data compared to past methods.

title: Generating Holistic 3D Scene Abstractions for Text-based Image Retrieval
Abstract: Spatial relationships between objects provide valuable information for text-based image retrieval. As users are more likely to describe a scene from a real-world perspective, using 3D spatial relationships rather than 2D relationships that assume a particular viewing direction, one of the main challenges is inferring the 3D structure that bridges images with users' text descriptions. However, direct inference of 3D structure from images requires learning from large-scale annotated data. Since interactions between objects can be reduced to a limited set of atomic spatial relations in 3D, we study the possibility of inferring 3D structure from a text description rather than an image, applying physical relation models to synthesize holistic 3D abstract object layouts satisfying the spatial constraints present in a textual description. We present a generic framework for retrieving images from a textual description of a scene by matching images with these generated abstract object layouts. Images are ranked by matching object detection outputs (bounding boxes) to 2D layout candidates (also represented by bounding boxes) which are obtained by projecting the 3D scenes with sampled camera directions. We validate our approach using public indoor scene datasets and show that our method outperforms baselines built upon object occurrence histograms and learned 2D pairwise relations. |||

title: The One Hundred Layers Tiramisu: Fully Convolutional DenseNets for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: State-of-the-art semantic image segmentation methods rely heavily on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). These architectures typically consist of a downsampling path for extracting coarse semantic features, followed by an upsampling path to restore the input image resolution at the model's output. Optionally, a post-processing module (like Conditional Random Fields) can refine the model's predictions.  Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNets), a recent CNN architecture, have demonstrated excellent results in image classification tasks. DenseNets operate on the principle that direct connections between every layer in a feed-forward manner lead to improved accuracy and ease of training. This paper extends DenseNets to address the problem of semantic segmentation.  The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on urban scene benchmark datasets like CamVid and Gatech without requiring any post-processing module or pre-training. Furthermore, the model's intelligent construction significantly reduces the number of parameters compared to current best entries for these datasets. Code to reproduce the experiments is available at: https://github.com/SimJeg/FC-DenseNet/blob/master/train.py
label: AI

title: What Is Around The Camera?
Abstract: How much information about its surrounding environment can be gleaned from a single image? This paper investigates the retrieval of environmental information from a foreground object combined with its background (the visible portion of the environment). Assuming the foreground object isn't perfectly diffuse, it acts as a complexly shaped and imperfect mirror.  An additional challenge arises from the object's appearance, which conflates the light from the environment with the unknown materials it's composed of.  The proposed solution is a learning-based approach to predict the environment from multiple reflectance maps calculated from approximate surface normals. This method allows for joint modeling of environmental statistics and material properties. Trained on synthesized data, the system demonstrates its effectiveness with real-world data.  Interestingly, the analysis reveals that information from objects made of multiple materials often complements each other, leading to enhanced performance.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical Boundary-Aware Neural Encoder for Video Captioning
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have gained significant attention in video captioning due to their ability to encode input videos and generate corresponding descriptions. This paper presents a recurrent video encoding scheme capable of uncovering and leveraging the hierarchical structure within videos.  Unlike the traditional encoder-decoder approach where a video is encoded continuously by a recurrent layer, a novel LSTM cell is introduced. This cell can identify discontinuity points between frames or segments and dynamically adjust the temporal connections of the encoding layer accordingly.  Evaluations on three large-scale datasets (Montreal Video Annotation dataset, MPII Movie Description dataset, and Microsoft Video Description Corpus) show that this approach can discover appropriate hierarchical representations of input videos and improve the state-of-the-art results on movie description datasets.
label: AI

title: Gaze Embeddings for Zero-Shot Image Classification
Abstract: Zero-shot image classification using auxiliary information, such as attributes describing discriminative object properties, necessitates time-consuming annotation by domain experts. This paper proposes a method that leverages human gaze as auxiliary information, exploiting the natural ability of even non-expert users to judge class membership.  The proposed data collection paradigm involves a discrimination task to enhance the information content extracted from gaze data.  Discriminative descriptors are extracted from the data, and a compatibility function between image and gaze is learned using three novel gaze embeddings: Gaze Histograms (GH), Gaze Features with Grid (GFG), and Gaze Features with Sequence (GFS). Two new gaze-annotated datasets for fine-grained image classification are introduced, demonstrating that human gaze data is class discriminative, provides a competitive alternative to expert-annotated attributes, and surpasses other baselines in zero-shot image classification.
label: AI

title: Dense Prediction on Sequences with Time-Dilated Convolutions for Speech Recognition
Abstract: Pixelwise dense prediction in computer vision involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image. Convolutional neural networks excel in this task while remaining computationally efficient.  This paper extends these concepts to the problem of assigning a sequence of labels to a set of speech frames, a task known as framewise classification.  The paper highlights several advantages and insights offered by the dense prediction perspective of framewise classification, including computational efficiency and the ability to apply batch normalization.  Specific attention is paid to strided pooling in time, introducing an asymmetric dilated convolution, termed time-dilated convolution, for efficient and elegant implementation of pooling in time.  The paper presents results using time-dilated convolutions in a deep VGG-style CNN with batch normalization on the Hub5 Switchboard-2000 benchmark task.  A large n-gram language model achieves a 7.7% WER, representing the best single model single-pass performance reported to date.
label: AI

title: Multi-resolution Data Fusion for Super-Resolution Electron Microscopy
Abstract: Despite the rapid advancements in science, the total amount of data collected using electron microscopy (EM) remains surprisingly small, less than a cubic millimeter. Consequently, there's a significant demand for faster and lower-dosage imaging in materials and biological sciences while maintaining resolution. Traditional EM imaging, based on homogeneous raster-order scanning, severely limits the volume of high-resolution data that can be acquired, posing a fundamental obstacle to understanding physical processes like material deformation, crack propagation, and pyrolysis.  This paper introduces a novel multi-resolution data fusion (MDF) method for super-resolution computational EM.  This method combines innovative data acquisition with novel algorithmic techniques to dramatically improve the resolution/volume/speed trade-off. The key to this approach is to acquire the entire sample at low resolution while simultaneously collecting a small fraction of data at high resolution. These high-resolution measurements are then used to create a material-specific patch library within the "plug-and-play" framework to significantly enhance the super-resolution of the low-resolution data.  Results using FEI electron microscope data demonstrate super-resolution factors of 4x, 8x, and 16x while substantially maintaining high image quality and reducing dosage.
label: AI

title: ECO: Efficient Convolution Operators for Tracking
Abstract: Discriminative Correlation Filter (DCF)-based methods have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art in tracking. However, the pursuit of ever-increasing tracking performance has gradually diminished their characteristic speed and real-time capabilities. Additionally, the increasingly complex models with a massive number of trainable parameters introduce the risk of severe overfitting. This paper tackles the key causes behind the problems of computational complexity and overfitting, aiming to simultaneously improve both speed and performance.  The core DCF formulation is revisited and introduces: (i) a factorized convolution operator, drastically reducing the model's parameters; (ii) a compact generative model of the training sample distribution, significantly reducing memory and time complexity while providing better sample diversity; and (iii) a conservative model update strategy with improved robustness and reduced complexity.  Extensive experiments on four benchmarks (VOT2016, UAV123, OTB-2015, and TempleColor) demonstrate that when using expensive deep features, the proposed tracker achieves a 20-fold speedup and a 13.0% relative gain in Expected Average Overlap compared to the top-ranked method in the VOT2016 challenge.  Furthermore, the fast variant, using hand-crafted features, operates at 60 Hz on a single CPU while achieving 65.0% AUC on OTB-2015.
label: AI

title: Spatio-Temporal Movements in Team Sports: A Visualization approach using Motion Charts
Abstract: Analyzing player movements and studying their trajectories is crucial for teams seeking to improve their chances of winning or understanding their performance. State-of-the-art tracking systems now produce high-definition and high-frequency spatio-temporal traces of player trajectories, facilitating various research efforts to extract insights from these trajectories. Despite numerous methods borrowed from diverse disciplines (machine learning, network and complex systems, GIS, computer vision, statistics) to address team needs, a user-friendly and easy-to-use approach for visualizing spatio-temporal movements remains absent. This paper proposes the use of the gvisMotionChart function from the GoogleVis R package and presents and discusses results from a basketball case study.  The data pertains to a match played by an Italian team in the "C-gold" league on March 22nd, 2016. This case study demonstrates how such a visualization approach can be useful in supporting researchers during preliminary stages of their sports movement analysis and facilitate the interpretation of their results.
label: AI

title: Computational Mapping of the Ground Reflectivity with Laser Scanners
Abstract: This investigation focuses on the problem of mapping ground reflectivity using multiple laser scanners mounted on mobile robots/vehicles. The challenge arises because regions of the ground become populated with varying numbers of reflectivity measurements whose values depend on the observer and their perspective.  A novel automatic, data-driven computational mapping framework is proposed, specifically designed to preserve edge sharpness during map reconstruction and account for measurement variation sources.  This new formulation generates map-perspective gradients and applies subset selection fusion and de-noising operators through iterative algorithms that minimize an $\\ell_1$ sparse regularized least squares formulation. Reconstruction of the ground reflectivity is then performed based on Poisson's formulation, posed as an $\\ell_2$ term promoting consistency with the fused gradient of map-perspectives and a term ensuring equality constraints with reference measurement data.  Experiments conducted on Ford's fleet of autonomous vehicles demonstrate that this new framework outperforms existing methods. For instance, it achieves map enhancement (contrast enhancement), artifact removal, de-noising, and map-stitching without requiring additional reflectivity adjustments to calibrate sensors to specific mounting and robot/vehicle motion.
label: AI

title: Image Based Appraisal of Real Estate Properties
Abstract: Real estate appraisal, the process of estimating the price of real estate properties, is crucial for both buyers and sellers as the basis for negotiation and transactions. Traditionally, the repeat sales model has been widely adopted for real estate price estimation. However, it relies on the design and calculation of a complex economic-related index, making it challenging to estimate accurately. Today, real estate brokers provide easy access to detailed online information about properties to their clients.  This study focuses on estimating real estate prices using these large amounts of easily accessible data, particularly analyzing the predictive power of online house pictures, a key factor for online users making potential visiting decisions.  The development of robust computer vision algorithms enables the analysis of visual content.  This work employs a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to predict real estate prices using state-of-the-art visual features.  The experimental results demonstrate that the model outperforms several other state-of-the-art baseline algorithms in terms of both mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).
label: AI

title: Who's that Actor? Automatic Labelling of Actors in TV series starting from IMDB Images
Abstract: This work focuses on automating the labeling of actors in a TV series.  Instead of relying on transcripts and subtitles, as previously demonstrated, the paper explores a method starting from a set of example images of each main actor collected from the Internet Movie Database (IMDB). The problem then becomes one of domain adaptation: actors' IMDB photos are typically taken at award ceremonies and differ significantly from their appearances in TV series. Furthermore, within each series, there is considerable variation in actor appearance due to makeup, lighting, aging, etc.  To bridge this gap, a graph-matching based self-labeling algorithm, coined HSL (Hungarian Self Labeling), is proposed. Additionally, a new edge cost is introduced for this context, along with an extension more robust to outliers, where prototypical faces for each actor are selected based on a hierarchical clustering procedure.  Experiments conducted with 15 episodes from 3 different TV series demonstrate automatic annotation with an accuracy of 90% and above.
label: AI

title: Large-Scale Shape Retrieval with Sparse 3D Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper presents the performance evaluation results of S3DCNN, a Sparse 3D Convolutional Neural Network, on the large-scale 3D Shape benchmark ModelNet40. The impact of input shape voxel resolution on performance is measured.  The results show comparable classification and retrieval performance to state-of-the-art models, but with significantly lower computational costs during training and inference phases.  Furthermore, it's observed that the benefits of higher input resolution can be limited by the neural network's ability to generalize high-level features.
label: AI

title: Lazily Adapted Constant Kinky Inference for Nonparametric Regression and Model-Reference Adaptive Control
Abstract: Techniques known as Nonlinear Set Membership prediction, Lipschitz Interpolation, or Kinky Inference are machine learning approaches that utilize presupposed Lipschitz properties to compute inferences over unobserved function values. If a bound on the true best Lipschitz constant of the target function is known a priori, these methods offer convergence guarantees and bounds around predictions.  Considering a more general setting based on Hölder continuity relative to pseudo-metrics, an online method is proposed for estimating the Hölder constant online from function value observations potentially corrupted by bounded observational errors.  Utilizing this for computing adaptive parameters within a kinky inference rule gives rise to a nonparametric machine learning method.  Strong universal approximation guarantees are established for this method, demonstrating that the prediction rule can learn any continuous function in the limit of increasingly dense data to within a worst-case error bound depending on the level of observational uncertainty.  The method is applied in the context of nonparametric model-reference adaptive control (MRAC). Across a range of simulated aircraft roll-dynamics and performance metrics, the proposed approach outperforms recently proposed alternatives based on Gaussian processes and RBF-neural networks. For discrete-time systems, guarantees on the tracking success of the learning-based controllers are provided for both batch and online learning settings.
label: AI

title: Proceedings 29th and 30th Workshops on (Constraint) Logic Programming and 24th International Workshop on Functional and (Constraint) Logic Programming
Abstract: The Workshops on (Constraint) Logic Programming (WLP) are the annual meeting of the German Society of Logic Programming (Gesellschaft für Logische Programmierung e.V., GLP) and bring together researchers interested in logic programming, constraint programming, answer set programming, and related areas like databases and artificial intelligence (not only from Germany).  The International Workshops on Functional and (Constraint) Logic Programming (WFLP) aim to bring together researchers, students, and practitioners interested in functional programming, logic programming, and their integration.  The workshops have a tradition of co-location to foster the cross-fertilizing exchange of ideas and experiences among and between communities interested in the foundations, applications, and combinations of high-level, declarative programming languages and related areas.
label: AI

title: Cutting-off Redundant Repeating Generations for Neural Abstractive Summarization
Abstract: This paper addresses the reduction of redundant repeating generation often observed in RNN-based encoder-decoder models. The core idea is to jointly estimate the upper-bound frequency of each target vocabulary in the encoder and control the output words based on this estimation in the decoder.  The proposed method demonstrates significant improvement over a strong RNN-based encoder-decoder baseline and achieves its best results on an abstractive summarization benchmark.
label: AI

title: Simulated Tornado Optimization
Abstract: This paper proposes a swarm-based optimization algorithm inspired by the air currents of a tornado. Two main air currents, spiral and updraft, are mimicked. Spiral motion is designed for exploring new search areas, while updraft movements are deployed for exploiting promising candidate solutions.  Assigning only one search direction to each particle at each iteration leads to low computational complexity of the proposed algorithm compared to conventional algorithms.  Regardless of the step size parameters, the only parameter of the proposed algorithm, called tornado diameter, can be efficiently adjusted through randomization. Numerical results across six different benchmark cost functions indicate comparable and, in some cases, better performance of the proposed algorithm compared to other metaheuristics.
label: AI

title: Learning Weighted Association Rules in Human Phenotype Ontology
Abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a structured repository of concepts (HPO Terms) associated with one or more diseases. The association process is referred to as annotation.  The relevance and specificity of both HPO terms and annotations are evaluated using a measure defined as Information Content (IC).  Analyzing annotated data is a significant challenge in bioinformatics.  While various analysis approaches exist, the use of Association Rules (AR) can provide valuable knowledge and has been employed in some applications, such as improving annotation quality. However, traditional association rule algorithms do not consider the source of annotation or its importance, leading to the generation of candidate rules with low IC.  This paper presents HPO-Miner (Human Phenotype Ontology-based Weighted Association Rules), a methodology for extracting Weighted Association Rules. HPO-Miner can extract relevant rules from a biological perspective. A case study using HPO-Miner on publicly available HPO annotation datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of this methodology.
label: AI

title: p-DLA: A Predictive System Model for Onshore Oil and Gas Pipeline Dataset Classification and Monitoring - Part 1
Abstract: The rise in militant activity and rogue behavior in oil and gas regions worldwide has led to an increase in oil pipeline disturbances, resulting in substantial losses for multinational operators and the countries where such facilities exist.  However, this situation can be mitigated by implementing adequate predictive monitoring schemes.  This paper proposes, in its first part, an artificial intelligence predictive monitoring system capable of predictive classification and pattern recognition of pipeline datasets.  The predictive system is based on a highly sparse predictive Deviant Learning Algorithm (p-DLA) designed to synthesize a sequence of memory predictive clusters for eventual monitoring, control, and decision-making. The DLA (p-DLA) is compared with a popular machine learning algorithm, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), based on a temporal version of standard feed-forward back-propagation trained artificial neural networks (ANNs). The results of simulation studies show impressive results and validate the sparse memory predictive approach, which favors the sub-synthesis of a highly compressed and low-dimensional knowledge discovery and information prediction scheme.  It also demonstrates that the proposed new approach is competitive with a well-known and proven AI approach like the LSTM.
label: AI

title: Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Test Cases
Abstract: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is a problem with numerous applications, ranging from facial recognition to document clustering. However, due to the variety of algorithms solving NMF, the randomness involved in these algorithms, and the subjective nature of the problem, there is no clear "correct answer" to any particular NMF problem.  This makes testing new algorithms challenging. This paper suggests some test cases for NMF algorithms derived from matrices with enumerable exact non-negative factorizations and perturbations of these matrices. Three algorithms using widely divergent approaches to NMF all give similar solutions over these test cases, suggesting that these test cases could be used as test cases for implementations of existing NMF algorithms as well as potentially new NMF algorithms. This paper also describes how the proposed test cases could be used in practice.
label: AI

title: Digital Advertising Traffic Operation: Machine Learning for Process Discovery
Abstract: Managing the day-to-day trafficking, pacing, and optimization of digital and paid social campaigns is essential in a Web Advertising Traffic Operation.  Data analysts in Traffic Operation not only need to provide quick answers but also speak the language of Process Managers and visually display discovered process problems.  To resolve a growing number of complaints in the customer service process, weaknesses in the process itself must be identified and communicated to the department. Process Mining for CRM data allows for identifying unwanted loops and delays in the process.  This paper proposes a process discovery based on Machine Learning techniques to automatically discover variations and detect problems at a glance, enabling corrective measures to be taken.
label: AI

title: Deep Neural Networks to Enable Real-time Multimessenger Astrophysics
Abstract: Deep Filtering, a novel, highly scalable method for end-to-end time-series signal processing, significantly enhances the scientific reach of gravitational wave astronomy. Utilizing a system of two deep convolutional neural networks designed for classification and regression, Deep Filtering rapidly detects and estimates parameters of gravitational wave signals within highly noisy data streams. This approach employs a novel training scheme with progressively increasing noise levels, alongside a transfer learning procedure between the networks. Demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting and estimating parameters of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers, Deep Filtering surpasses conventional machine learning techniques and achieves comparable performance to matched filtering, while being several orders of magnitude faster. This enables real-time processing of raw big data with minimal resources and extends the range of detectable gravitational wave signals. Deep Filtering leverages recent advancements in artificial intelligence algorithms and hardware architectures, such as deep-learning-optimized GPUs, facilitating real-time searches for gravitational wave sources and their electromagnetic and astro-particle counterparts.
label: AI

title: Counterfactual Prediction with Deep Instrumental Variables Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a recipe for combining machine learning algorithms to solve causal effects in the presence of instrumental variables. By leveraging the success of deep learning architectures, which map from observables to outputs via multiple layers of latent representations, this Deep IV framework resolves into two prediction tasks. A first-stage network predicts treatment, while a second-stage network, incorporating integration over the conditional treatment distribution, utilizes a loss function. This framework imposes specific structure on the stochastic gradient descent routine used for training, yet remains general enough to benefit from off-the-shelf ML capabilities, avoiding extensive algorithm customization. Techniques for obtaining out-of-sample causal validation to prevent overfitting are outlined, along with schemes for both Bayesian and frequentist inference. The Bayesian approach employs a novel adaptation of dropout training, while the frequentist approach utilizes a data splitting routine.
label: AI

title: Fuzzy Constraints Linear Discriminant Analysis
Abstract: Fuzzy Constraint Linear Discriminant Analysis (FC-LDA) is a novel approach that minimizes misclassification error based on a modified perceptron criterion. FC-LDA effectively handles uncertainty near the decision boundary through a fuzzy linear programming approach with fuzzy resources. Its linear characteristics and ability to tolerate noisy data with varying degrees of tolerance result in low computational complexity. The effectiveness of FC-LDA is demonstrated through successful application to various problems, surpassing traditional LDA in classification tasks.
label: AI

title: When the map is better than the territory
Abstract: This paper explores the phenomenon of causal emergence, where the causal structure of a system can become more informative at a macroscale. Challenging the conventional understanding that macro descriptions are merely compressed representations, the paper draws upon information theory to demonstrate that some systems exhibit greater causal clarity at a higher level. This occurs when a macro model utilizes the full causal capacity of the system, which is analogous to Shannon's channel capacity concept. The paper argues that different causal models of a system capitalize on its causal capacity to varying degrees, with macroscale models potentially surpassing detailed microscopic models in informativeness and efficacy. This framework offers a general understanding of how the causal structure of certain systems cannot be fully captured by even the most detailed microscopic model.
label: AI

title: PrASP Report
Abstract: PrASP, a probabilistic inductive logic programming framework, integrates non-monotonic reasoning based on Answer Set Programming (ASP), probabilistic inference, and parameter learning. This research software distinguishes itself from traditional approaches by imposing minimal restrictions on probabilistic logic programs, enabling the use of both ASP and First-Order Logic syntax, along with the annotation of formulas with point probabilities and interval probabilities. PrASP provides a variety of use cases through a pipeline-like combination of widely configurable inference algorithms.
label: AI

title: Automatic Data Deformation Analysis on Evolving Folksonomy Driven Environment
Abstract: The Folksodriven framework empowers data scientists to define an ontology environment that effectively searches for buried patterns with predictive power for building predictive models. This is achieved through abstractions that isolate parameters of the predictive modeling process, focusing on pattern searching and feature set design. Utilizing folksonomies, the framework employs a new concept structure called "Folksodriven" to represent evolving knowledge. The study of transformational regulation of Folksodriven tags is crucial for adaptive folksonomy classifications in evolving environments, enabling Intelligent Systems to represent knowledge sharing. These tags categorize salient data points, facilitating their input into machine learning systems for data "featurization."
label: AI

title: A Joint Speaker-Listener-Reinforcer Model for Referring Expressions
Abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for referring expression comprehension and generation, encompassing three modules: speaker, listener, and reinforcer. The speaker generates referring expressions, the listener comprehends them, and the reinforcer introduces a reward function to guide the selection of more discriminative expressions. The listener-speaker modules are trained jointly in an end-to-end learning framework, allowing them to learn in mutual awareness while benefiting from the discriminative reinforcer's feedback. This unified framework and training methodology achieve state-of-the-art results in both comprehension and generation on three referring expression datasets.
label: AI

title: Adaptive Lambda Least-Squares Temporal Difference Learning
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of selecting the $\\lambda$ parameter in Temporal Difference (TD) learning, which controls the timescale of TD updates. The $\\lambda$ selection is formalized as a bias-variance trade-off, aiming to minimize the Mean Squared Value Error (MSVE). The paper proposes Leave-One-Trajectory-Out Cross-Validation (LOTO-CV) to search the space of $\\lambda$ values. While computationally expensive, LOTO-CV can be efficiently implemented for Least Squares TD (LSTD). The resulting algorithm, ALLSTD, is parameter-free and significantly faster than the naive LOTO-CV implementation, achieving comparable performance.
label: AI

title: Curiosity-Aware Bargaining
Abstract: This paper explores the concept of "curious" agents in automated negotiation, driven by the desire to collect information and improve their opponent models. Three extensions to the standard bargaining protocol are proposed using mechanism design, limiting information leakage and supporting an enhanced rationality model that considers exchanged information. These extensions are theoretically analyzed and experimentally evaluated, addressing the challenge of information leakage in opponent modeling within automated negotiation.
label: AI

title: Lifted Relational Algebra with Recursion and Connections to Modal Logic
Abstract: This paper introduces a new formalism for specifying and reasoning about problems involving heterogeneous "pieces of information," encompassing large data collections, decision procedures, and their interconnections. By extending Codd's relational algebra from operations on tables to operations on classes of structures with recursion, and incorporating information propagation, the formalism provides a framework for expressing unary negation and operations used in graph databases. The paper analyzes several reasoning tasks and establishes a connection between generalized query evaluation and temporal logic model checking. This development reveals a general correspondence between classical and modal logics, shedding new light on the computational properties of modal logics and related formalisms.
label: AI

title: A hybrid approach to supervised machine learning for algorithmic melody composition
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for composing monophonic melodies that emulate the style of a given sample of melodies, annotated with phrase information. Employing a hybrid approach, the algorithm combines parametric Markov models of higher order with a contour concept of phrases. This work builds upon Thayabaran Kathiresan's master thesis (2015). An online listening test demonstrates that integrating musically relevant context, such as count and planned melody contour, significantly improves the results compared to a pure Markov model.
label: AI

title: Deep neural heart rate variability analysis
Abstract: Despite the prevalence and limitations of blood tests for early cardiovascular disease detection, this paper presents a novel approach utilizing heart rate variability, a non-invasive and cost-effective alternative. By applying deep learning to heart beat interval classification, the paper introduces a differentiable hybrid architecture combining biological neuron models of cardiac dynamics (modified FitzHugh Nagumo neurons) and standard feed-forward neural networks. The model is evaluated on ECGs from patients with coronary artery disease and chest pain, demonstrating significant outperformance compared to traditional heart rate variability predictors. The model also approaches or surpasses the performance of clinical blood tests, based solely on 60 seconds of inter-beat intervals.
label: AI

title: From Virtual to Real World Visual Perception using Domain Adaptation -- The DPM as Example
Abstract: Supervised learning generally produces more accurate classifiers than unsupervised learning, highlighting the importance of annotated training data. However, annotating visual perception challenges, such as object localization, poses a significant bottleneck. This paper addresses this issue by advocating for the use of virtual worlds to automatically collect annotations with high precision. Recognizing the need for domain adaptation (DA) to bridge the gap between virtual and real-world data, the paper revisits the DA of a deformable part-based model (DPM) as an exemplifying case. Focusing on vehicle detection for driver assistance, the paper explores the influence of virtual-vs-real data on object appearance and the role of photo-realism in virtual worlds.
label: AI

title: On perfect clustering of high dimension, low sample size data
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenges of clustering algorithms in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) situations, where the concentration of pairwise distances negatively impacts performance. It introduces a dissimilarity measure based on the data cloud, called MADD, which leverages distance concentration to improve clustering performance. The paper provides theoretical and numerical results demonstrating the effectiveness of MADD for high-dimensional data. Additionally, it addresses the problem of estimating the number of clusters, showing that existing algorithms perform better with MADD instead of Euclidean distance. A new estimator based on penalized Dunn index is constructed and proven consistent in the HDLSS asymptotic regime. The paper analyzes simulated and real datasets to underscore the significance of MADD for cluster analysis of high-dimensional data.
label: AI

title: Sequence-to-point learning with neural networks for nonintrusive load monitoring
Abstract: Energy disaggregation, a single-channel blind source separation problem, aims to decompose the mains electricity consumption into appliance-wise readings. This paper presents sequence-to-point learning using convolutional neural networks to address the identifiability problem inherent in energy disaggregation. The proposed approach inputs a window of the mains data and outputs a single point of the target appliance. The paper demonstrates that convolutional neural networks inherently learn appliance signatures, reducing the identifiability problem. Applying these approaches to real-world household energy data, the paper showcases state-of-the-art performance, significantly improving standard error measures.
label: AI

title: Meta-Unsupervised-Learning: A supervised approach to unsupervised learning
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm for unsupervised learning by reducing it to supervised learning. Subjectivity in unsupervised decision-making is mitigated by leveraging knowledge acquired from prior supervised learning tasks, potentially heterogeneous. The versatility of this meta-unsupervised-learning framework is demonstrated through comprehensive expositions and experiments on clustering, outlier detection, and similarity prediction. Rigorous PAC-agnostic bounds are provided to establish theoretical foundations, and the framework's ability to circumvent Kleinberg's impossibility theorem for clustering is highlighted.
label: AI

title: Efficient iterative policy optimization
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of finding optimal policies within limited policy updates. It approximates the expected policy reward as a sequence of concave lower bounds, enabling efficient maximization and drastically reducing the number of updates required. The paper extends existing methods to handle negative rewards, allowing for the use of control variates.
label: AI

title: The formal-logical characterisation of lies, deception, and associated notions
Abstract: Defining dishonest notions in a formal manner is crucial for enabling intelligent agents to operate in untrustworthy environments. This review examines the literature on formal definitions based on modal logic and other approaches. Criteria from philosophical groundwork are applied to assess definitions for correctness and completeness. The review reveals that only a few definitions fully comply with these criteria, highlighting the missing steps towards successful application in real agent environments.
label: AI

title: FastMask: Segment Multi-scale Object Candidates in One Shot
Abstract: Objects exhibit varying scales in natural images, requiring object-centric tasks (e.g., object proposal) to be robust to scale variances. This paper presents FastMask, a novel segment proposal framework utilizing hierarchical features in deep convolutional neural networks to segment multi-scale objects in a single shot. FastMask is innovatively divided into three functional components: body, neck, and head. The paper proposes a weight-shared residual neck module and a scale-tolerant attentional head module for efficient one-shot inference. On the MS COCO benchmark, FastMask surpasses all state-of-the-art segment proposal methods in average recall while being 2-5 times faster. With a slight trade-off in accuracy, FastMask achieves near real-time object segmentation, demonstrating its potential for practical applications.
label: AI

title: Accelerated Convolutions for Efficient Multi-Scale Time to Contact Computation in Julia
Abstract: Convolutions are fundamental to applied mathematics, physics, and engineering, enabling efficient computation of tasks like numerical differentiation. Efficient convolution computation is critical for real-time artificial intelligence applications, such as machine vision. This paper explores the use of convolutions in fundamental machine vision applications and presents an accelerated n-dimensional convolution package in Julia, a high-performance computing language. The paper demonstrates the package's efficacy in solving the time to contact problem for machine vision, achieving an order of magnitude decrease in compute time and allocated memory compared to conventional methods. The package is integrated into the official Julia Package Manager for broader application in various scenarios. |||
label: AI

title: Multivariate mixture model for myocardium segmentation combining multi-source images
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for simultaneously segmenting multi-source images using the multivariate mixture model (MvMM) and maximum log-likelihood (LL) framework. The segmentation process involves texture classification, and the MvMM is employed to model the joint intensity distribution of the images. Specifically, the method is applied to myocardial segmentation by combining complementary texture information from multi-sequence (MS) cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images. Addressing the challenges of inter-image mis-registration and intra-image misalignment in MS CMR images, the MvMM is formulated with transformations that are integrated into the LL framework and optimized simultaneously with the segmentation parameters. This approach enables correction of inter- and intra-image misalignment by registering each slice of the MS CMR to a virtual common space, as well as delineating indistinguishable boundaries of myocardium containing pathologies. Experimental results demonstrate statistically significant improvements in segmentation performance compared to conventional methods, which can only segment each image individually. The proposed method exhibits enhanced robustness in incongruent data scenarios where some images may not fully cover the region of interest, and full coverage can be reconstructed by combining images from multiple sources.
label: AI

title: The Predictron: End-To-End Learning and Planning
Abstract: A key challenge in artificial intelligence is developing models that are effective in the context of planning. This paper introduces the predictron architecture, a fully abstract model represented by a Markov reward process, that can be rolled forward multiple "imagined" planning steps. Each forward pass of the predictron accumulates internal rewards and values over multiple planning depths. The predictron is trained end-to-end to ensure that these accumulated values accurately approximate the true value function. The paper applies the predictron to procedurally generated random mazes and a pool game simulator, demonstrating that it produces significantly more accurate predictions compared to traditional deep neural network architectures.
label: AI

title: Automated timetabling for small colleges and high schools using huge integer programs
Abstract: This paper presents an integer program to solve a highly constrained academic timetabling problem at the United States Merchant Marine Academy. The real-world case study results in an IP instance with approximately 170,000 rows and columns, which is solved to optimality in 4-24 hours using a commercial solver on a portable computer. Near-optimal feasible solutions are often found within 4-12 hours. The model is applicable to both high schools and small colleges seeking to deviate from group scheduling. The paper also addresses a necessary preprocessing student subgrouping problem, breaking up large groups of students into smaller groups to optimally fit them into classes with limited capacity.
label: AI

title: A Sparse Nonlinear Classifier Design Using AUC Optimization
Abstract: Area under the ROC curve (AUC) is a crucial performance metric for applications involving highly imbalanced data. Learning to maximize AUC performance is thus a significant research problem. By utilizing a max-margin based surrogate loss function, the AUC optimization problem can be approximated as a pairwise rankSVM learning problem. While batch learning methods for solving the kernelized version of this problem face scalability challenges and may not result in sparse classifiers, online or single-pass online learning algorithms have gained recent interest for designing classifiers that maximize AUC performance. However, the AUC performance of nonlinear classifiers designed using online methods may not be comparable to that of nonlinear classifiers designed using batch learning algorithms on many real-world datasets. Motivated by these observations, this paper proposes a scalable algorithm for maximizing AUC performance by greedily adding the required number of basis functions to the classifier model. The resulting sparse classifiers achieve faster inference. Experimental results indicate that the achievable level of sparsity can be an order of magnitude smaller than the Kernel RankSVM model without significantly affecting the AUC performance.
label: AI

title: Monte Carlo Sort for unreliable human comparisons
Abstract: Algorithms for sorting lists of real numbers into ascending order have been studied extensively for decades. These algorithms typically rely on a series of pairwise comparisons and operate entirely on chip. However, people routinely sort lists that depend on subjective or complex judgments that cannot be automated. Examples include marketing research, where surveys are used to understand customer preferences for products; the recruiting process, where interviewers rank potential employees; and sporting tournaments, where team rankings are inferred from a series of one-on-one matches. This paper develops a novel sorting algorithm where each pairwise comparison reflects a subjective human judgment about which element is bigger or better. The algorithm introduces a finite and large error rate to each judgment and considers the cost of each comparison to significantly exceed the cost of other computational steps. The algorithm must request the most informative sequence of comparisons from the user to identify the correct sorted list with minimal human input. The Discrete Adiabatic Monte Carlo approach leverages the gradual acquisition of information by tracking a set of plausible hypotheses that are updated after each additional comparison.
label: AI

title: Theory-guided Data Science: A New Paradigm for Scientific Discovery from Data
Abstract: Despite their success in commercial domains, data science models have limited applicability in scientific problems involving complex physical phenomena. Theory-guided data science (TGDS) is an emerging paradigm that aims to leverage scientific knowledge to improve the effectiveness of data science models in enabling scientific discovery. TGDS envisions introducing scientific consistency as an essential component for learning generalizable models. By producing scientifically interpretable models, TGDS aims to advance scientific understanding by discovering novel domain insights. The paradigm of TGDS has gained prominence in various scientific disciplines, including turbulence modeling, material discovery, quantum chemistry, biomedical science, biomarker discovery, climate science, and hydrology. This paper formally conceptualizes the TGDS paradigm and presents a taxonomy of research themes within TGDS. It describes several approaches for integrating domain knowledge in different research themes using illustrative examples from various disciplines. The paper also highlights promising avenues for novel research to realize the full potential of theory-guided data science.
label: AI

title: Artificial Intelligence Probes for Interstellar Exploration and Colonization
Abstract: A recurring topic in interstellar exploration and the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) is the role of artificial intelligence. Specifically, these are programs or devices capable of performing cognitive tasks previously associated with humans, such as image recognition, reasoning, decision-making, etc. Such systems are likely to play a crucial role in future deep space missions, notably interstellar exploration, where spacecraft need to act autonomously. This paper explores the drivers for an interstellar mission with a computation-heavy payload and provides an outline of a spacecraft and mission architecture that supports such a payload. Based on existing technologies and extrapolations of current trends, it demonstrates that AI spacecraft development and operation will be constrained and driven by three aspects: power requirements for the payload, power generation capabilities, and heat rejection capabilities. A likely mission architecture for such a probe is to enter an orbit close to the star to generate maximum power for computational activities and then prepare for further exploration activities. Considering current levels of increase in computational power, a payload with computational power similar to the human brain would have a mass of hundreds to dozens of tons in the 2050-2060 timeframe.
label: AI

title: Solving Combinatorial Optimization problems with Quantum inspired Evolutionary Algorithm Tuned using a Novel Heuristic Method
Abstract: Quantum inspired Evolutionary Algorithms (QEAs) were proposed over a decade ago and have been employed for solving a wide range of challenging search and optimization problems. Various modifications have been suggested to enhance the performance of canonical QEA. However, canonical QEA is one of the few evolutionary algorithms that uses a search operator with a relatively large number of parameters. It is well-established that the performance of evolutionary algorithms depends on the specific values of parameters for a given problem. The advantage of having a large number of parameters in an operator is that the search process can be made more powerful even with a single operator, eliminating the need for a combination of other operators for exploration and exploitation. However, tuning operators with a large number of parameters is complex and computationally expensive. This paper proposes a novel heuristic method for tuning parameters of canonical QEA. The tuned QEA outperforms canonical QEA on a class of discrete combinatorial optimization problems, validating the design of the proposed parameter tuning framework. The proposed framework can be used for tuning other algorithms with both large and small numbers of tunable parameters.
label: AI

title: Liquid Democracy: An Analysis in Binary Aggregation and Diffusion
Abstract: This paper analyzes liquid democracy (delegable proxy voting) from the perspectives of binary aggregation and binary diffusion models. The paper demonstrates how liquid democracy on binary issues can be embedded into the framework of binary aggregation with abstentions, enabling the transfer of known results about the latter, such as impossibility theorems, to the former. This embedding also clarifies the relationship between delegation cycles in liquid democracy and the probability of collective abstentions, as well as the issue of individual rationality in a delegable proxy voting setting. Furthermore, the paper shows how liquid democracy on binary issues can be modeled and analyzed as a specific process of dynamics of binary opinions on networks. These processes, called Boolean DeGroot processes, are a special case of the DeGroot stochastic model of opinion diffusion. The paper establishes the convergence conditions of such processes and demonstrates that they provide novel insights into how the effects of delegation cycles and individual rationality could be mitigated within liquid democracy. The study represents a first attempt to provide theoretical foundations for the delegable proxy features of the liquid democracy voting system. The analysis suggests recommendations for modifying the system to make it more resilient with respect to handling delegation cycles and inconsistent majorities.
