title: Geo-Location Based Access for Vehicular Communications: Analysis and Optimization via Stochastic Geometry
Abstract: Delivering broadcast messages among vehicles for safety purposes, a key component of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), requires an efficient Medium Access Control (MAC) that provides low average delay and high reliability. To this end, Geo-Location Based Access (GLOC) for vehicles has been proposed for Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications, aiming to maximize the distance of co-channel transmitters while maintaining low latency when accessing resources. This paper analyzes the delivery of periodic and non-periodic broadcast messages with GLOC, using stochastic geometry to account for path loss, fading, and the random locations of transmitting vehicles. Analytical results include the average interference, average Binary Rate (BR), capture probability (the probability of successful message transmission), and Energy Efficiency (EE). Mathematical analysis reveals interesting insights about system performance, which are validated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations. The analysis demonstrates that the capture probability is an increasing function with exponential dependence on the transmit power, and an arbitrarily high capture probability can be achieved as long as the number of access resources is sufficiently high. Finally, to facilitate system-level design of GLOC, the paper derives the optimal transmit power that maximizes EE subject to a given constraint in the capture probability.
label: AI

title: EnhanceNet: Single Image Super-Resolution Through Automated Texture Synthesis
Abstract: Single image super-resolution involves inferring a high-resolution image from a single low-resolution input. Traditionally, the performance of algorithms for this task is evaluated using pixel-wise reconstruction measures like peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), which have been shown to correlate poorly with human perception of image quality. As a result, algorithms minimizing these metrics often produce over-smoothed images that lack high-frequency textures and appear unnatural despite yielding high PSNR values. This paper proposes a novel application of automated texture synthesis combined with a perceptual loss, focusing on creating realistic textures rather than optimizing for pixel-accurate reproduction of ground truth images during training. By using feed-forward fully convolutional neural networks in an adversarial training setting, the paper achieves a significant boost in image quality at high magnification ratios. Extensive experiments on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, yielding state-of-the-art results in both quantitative and qualitative benchmarks.
label: AI

title: A Base Camp for Scaling AI
Abstract: Modern statistical machine learning (SML) methods share a major limitation with early AI approaches: there is no scalable way to adapt them to new domains. Human learning partially solves this by leveraging a rich, shared, and updateable world model. Achieving such scalability requires modularity, where updating part of the world model should not impact unrelated parts. This requires both "correctability" (errors can be corrected without introducing new ones) and "interpretability" (we can understand which components need correction). This paper explores two main ideas to achieve this: "Teacher Assisted Learning", which leverages crowdsourcing to learn language; and "Factored Dialog Learning", which factors the process of application development into roles where the language competencies needed are isolated, enabling non-experts to quickly create new applications. The paper tests these ideas in an "Automated Personal Assistant" (APA) setting with two scenarios: detecting user intent from a user-APA dialog; and creating a class of event reminder applications, where a non-expert "teacher" can create specific apps. For the intent detection task, a dataset of a thousand labeled utterances from user dialogs with Cortana is used. The approach matches state-of-the-art SML methods but provides full transparency, where the entire (editable) model can be summarized on a single human-readable page. For the reminder app task, small user studies verify the efficacy of the approach.
label: AI

title: Convergence Rates for Greedy Kaczmarz Algorithms, and Faster Randomized Kaczmarz Rules Using the Orthogonality Graph
Abstract: The Kaczmarz method is an iterative algorithm for solving systems of linear equalities and inequalities, which iteratively projects onto these constraints. Strohmer and Vershynin provided a non-asymptotic convergence rate analysis for this algorithm, leading to numerous extensions and generalizations of the Kaczmarz method. This paper explores greedy and approximate greedy selection rules, contrasting them with the randomized selection rule analyzed in previous work. The paper demonstrates that in some applications, the computational costs of greedy and random selection are comparable, and in many cases, greedy selection rules offer faster convergence rates than random selection rules. Additionally, the paper presents the first multi-step analysis of Kaczmarz methods for a particular greedy rule and proposes a provably-faster randomized selection rule for matrices with many pairwise-orthogonal rows.
label: AI

title: SampleRNN: An Unconditional End-to-End Neural Audio Generation Model
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel model for unconditional audio generation based on generating one audio sample at a time. The model combines memory-less modules, namely autoregressive multilayer perceptrons, and stateful recurrent neural networks in a hierarchical structure, enabling it to capture underlying sources of variations in temporal sequences over long time spans across three datasets of different nature. Human evaluation of the generated samples indicates that this model is preferred over competing models. The paper also analyzes how each component of the model contributes to the exhibited performance.
label: AI

title: Highway and Residual Networks learn Unrolled Iterative Estimation
Abstract: The past year witnessed the introduction of new architectures, such as Highway networks and Residual networks, which enabled the training of feedforward networks with dozens to hundreds of layers using simple gradient descent for the first time. While depth of representation has been suggested as a primary reason for their success, there are indications that these architectures defy the popular view of deep learning as a hierarchical computation of increasingly abstract features at each layer. This report argues that this view is incomplete and does not adequately explain several recent findings. The paper proposes an alternative viewpoint based on unrolled iterative estimation, where a group of successive layers iteratively refine their estimates of the same features instead of computing an entirely new representation. The paper demonstrates that this viewpoint directly leads to the construction of Highway and Residual networks. Finally, preliminary experiments are conducted to discuss the similarities and differences between the two architectures.
label: AI

title: Jointly Extracting Relations with Class Ties via Effective Deep Ranking
Abstract: Connections between relations in relation extraction, called class ties, are common. In distantly supervised scenarios, one entity tuple may have multiple relation facts. Exploiting class ties between relations of one entity tuple holds promise for distantly supervised relation extraction. However, previous models are not effective or ignore this property. This paper proposes to leverage class ties by performing joint relation extraction with a unified model that integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a general pairwise ranking framework, introducing three novel ranking loss functions. Additionally, the paper presents an effective method to mitigate the severe class imbalance problem from NR (not relation) for model training. Experiments on a widely used dataset show that leveraging class ties enhances extraction and demonstrates the effectiveness of the model in learning class ties. The model significantly outperforms baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
label: AI

title: Counting Answer Sets via Dynamic Programming
Abstract: While the solution counting problem for propositional satisfiability (#SAT) has received renewed attention in recent years, this research trend has not affected other AI solving paradigms like answer set programming (ASP). Although ASP solvers are designed to enumerate all solutions, and counting can therefore be easily done, the involved materialization of all solutions is a clear bottleneck for the counting problem of ASP (#ASP). This paper proposes dynamic programming-based #ASP algorithms that exploit the structure of the underlying (ground) ASP program. Experimental results for a prototype implementation show promise when compared to existing solvers.
label: AI

title: Quantum Learning with Noise and Decoherence: A Robust Quantum Neural Network
Abstract: Noise and decoherence pose significant obstacles to the implementation of large-scale quantum computing. Due to the no-cloning theorem, which states that we cannot make an exact copy of an arbitrary quantum state, simple redundancy does not work in a quantum context. Unwanted interactions with the environment can destroy coherence, compromising the quantum nature of the computation. The parallel and distributed nature of classical neural networks has made them successful in handling incomplete or damaged data. This work demonstrates that the model of a quantum neural network (QNN) is similarly robust to noise and decoherence. Furthermore, robustness to noise and decoherence is not only maintained but improved as the size of the system increases. Noise and decoherence can even be advantageous during training, as it helps correct for overfitting. The paper demonstrates this robustness using entanglement as a means for pattern storage in a qubit array. The results provide evidence that machine learning approaches can overcome otherwise intractable problems in quantum computing.
label: AI

title: Solving Set Optimization Problems by Cardinality Optimization via Weak Constraints with an Application to Argumentation
Abstract: Optimization, minimization or maximization, in the lattice of subsets is a frequent operation in Artificial Intelligence tasks. Examples include subset-minimal model-based diagnosis, nonmonotonic reasoning using circumscription, or preferred extensions in abstract argumentation. Finding the optimum among many admissible solutions is often more challenging than finding admissible solutions, considering both computational complexity and methodology. This paper addresses the computational complexity issue by presenting an effective method for finding subset-optimal solutions. The method is based on the relationship between cardinality-optimal and subset-optimal solutions, and the fact that many logic-based declarative programming systems provide constructs for finding cardinality-optimal solutions, such as maximum satisfiability (MaxSAT) or weak constraints in Answer Set Programming (ASP). Notably, every cardinality-optimal solution is also a subset-optimal one, and if the language allows for the addition of particular restricting constructs (both MaxSAT and ASP do), then all subset-optimal solutions can be found through an iterative computation of cardinality-optimal solutions. As a showcase, the paper explores the computation of preferred extensions of abstract argumentation frameworks using the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Role of Simplicity in Creative Behaviour: The Case of the Poietic Generator
Abstract: This paper proposes applying Simplicity Theory (ST) to model interest in creative situations. ST was designed to describe and predict interest in communication. The paper uses ST to derive a decision rule that is applied to a simplified version of a creative game, the Poietic Generator. The decision rule produces what can be considered an elementary form of creativity. This study serves as a proof of principle, suggesting that some creative actions may be motivated by the search for unexpected simplicity. |||
label: AI

title: The SP Theory of Intelligence as a Foundation for the Development of a General, Human-Level Thinking Machine
Abstract: This paper presents the "SP theory of intelligence" and its corresponding "SP computer model," which aims to simplify and integrate concepts within artificial intelligence and related fields. This model, inspired by the concept of "multiple alignment" from bioinformatics, aspires to become the "double helix" of intelligence, possessing a significance akin to DNA in biological sciences. The SP system exhibits strengths in representing diverse knowledge, exhibiting various aspects of intelligence (including unsupervised learning, natural language processing, pattern recognition, and diverse reasoning abilities), seamlessly integrating knowledge and intelligence, and possessing potential applications in various domains (including solving big data problems, developing human-level intelligence in robots, serving as an intelligent database, and aiding medical diagnosis).
label: AI

title: Non-Deterministic Policy Improvement Stabilizes Approximated Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This research explores a type of instability commonly observed in approximated reinforcement learning due to greedy policy improvement. The study demonstrates empirically that introducing non-deterministic policy improvement, which controls the stochasticity of improvements, can stabilize methods like LSPI. Furthermore, the paper highlights the role of a suitable representation of the value function in contributing to solution stability. The proposed approach is simple and adaptable to more advanced algorithms like deep reinforcement learning.
label: AI

title: Causal Effect Identification in Acyclic Directed Mixed Graphs and Gated Models
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel family of graphical models featuring a mix of directed, undirected, and bidirected edges, but without directed cycles. These models prove suitable for representing causal models with additive error terms. The research provides graphical criteria for identifying arbitrary causal effects in models with directed and undirected edges, as well as a criterion for identifying the causal effect of a single variable on the rest. Additionally, an exact algorithm is developed for learning these models from observational and interventional data using answer set programming. Finally, the paper introduces gated models for causal effect identification, a new family of graphical models that leverage context-specific independences to identify additional causal effects.
label: AI

title: Understanding Error Correction and its Role as Part of the Communication Channel in Environments composed of Self-Integrating Systems
Abstract: The increasing complexity of technical systems demands greater knowledge for their setup and maintenance, making evolution costly. Autonomic computing aims to equip these systems with self-healing capabilities, allowing system owners to provide partial and potentially inconsistent updates. Self-healing systems should adapt to these changes and restore functionality by autonomously identifying remaining adjustments to communications and functionalities. This is particularly crucial in the Internet of Things and Industrial Internet, where unexpected device combinations can be assembled to create novel functions. To achieve higher levels of self-integration, this paper proposes viewing self-integration as sophisticated error correcting communications. The paper explores an extended scope of error correction, emphasizing its role as an integral component of bidirectional communication channels within self-integrating, autonomic communication scenarios.
label: AI

title: Difficulty Adjustable and Scalable Constrained Multi-objective Test Problem Toolkit
Abstract: Multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) have witnessed substantial progress, but most are designed for unconstrained problems. However, many real-world problems involve constraints. To stimulate research in constrained multi-objective optimization, this paper proposes a classification scheme for problems, categorizing them based on difficulty levels reflecting challenges posed by real-world optimization problems. This scheme identifies three types of difficulty: feasibility-hardness, convergence-hardness, and diversity-hardness, characterizing constraint functions in constrained multi-objective optimization problems (CMOPs).  A general toolkit is then developed to construct difficulty-adjustable and scalable CMOPs (DAS-CMOPs or DAS-CMaOPs for more than three objectives) using parameterized constraint functions designed to capture the proposed difficulty types. The toolkit facilitates the creation of nine difficulty-adjustable and scalable CMOPs and nine CMaOPs. Experimental results reveal that MOEA/D-CDP mechanisms are more effective for convergence-hard DAS-CMOPs, while NSGA-II-CDP mechanisms excel in solving DAS-CMOPs with simultaneous diversity, feasibility, and convergence hardness. C-NSGA-III mechanisms show greater effectiveness for feasibility-hard CMaOPs, while C-MOEA/DD mechanisms perform better for CMaOPs with convergence-hardness. Notably, none of these algorithms solve these problems efficiently, encouraging further development of CMOEAs and CMaOEAs to address the suggested DAS-CMOPs and DAS-CMaOPs.
label: AI

title: A Survey of Deep Network Solutions for Learning Control in Robotics: From Reinforcement to Imitation
Abstract: Deep learning has become a powerful tool across diverse fields, achieving state-of-the-art results. This survey focuses specifically on deep learning solutions for learning control policies in robotics applications. The paper examines the two primary paradigms for learning control with deep networks: deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and imitation learning.  For DRL, the paper delves into traditional reinforcement learning algorithms, explaining their extensions to the deep context and effective mechanisms that can be incorporated. Representative works using DRL for solving navigation and manipulation tasks in robotics are then presented. The discussion extends to methods addressing the "reality gap" challenge of transferring DRL policies trained in simulation to real-world scenarios, along with a summary of robotics simulation platforms for conducting DRL research.  For imitation learning, the paper explores its three main categories (behavior cloning, inverse reinforcement learning, and generative adversarial imitation learning) by outlining their formulations and corresponding robotics applications. Finally, the paper highlights open challenges and research frontiers in this field.
label: AI

title: ARES: Adaptive Receding-Horizon Synthesis of Optimal Plans
Abstract: This paper introduces ARES, an efficient approximation algorithm for generating optimal plans (action sequences) that guide a Markov Decision Process (MDP) from an initial state to a state below a specified cost threshold.  ARES utilizes Particle Swarm Optimization with adaptive sizing for both the receding horizon and the particle swarm. Inspired by Importance Splitting, the horizon length and particle number are adjusted to ensure at least one particle reaches a "next-level state," where the cost decreases by a predefined delta from the previous state. The level relationship between states and the plans generated by ARES implicitly define a Lyapunov function and an optimal policy, respectively, which can be explicitly generated by applying ARES to all states of the MDP. The paper evaluates ARES statistically, assessing its success rate in generating optimal plans. ARES was motivated by exploring the optimality of V-formation flight in terms of energy conservation, clear view, and velocity alignment.  The algorithm successfully generates plans for flocks of 7 birds, reaching a V-formation in 95% of 8,000 random initial configurations within 63 seconds on average.  ARES can be adapted into a model-predictive controller (MPC) with an adaptive receding horizon and statistical convergence guarantees. The paper emphasizes the novel adaptive-sizing approach, which offers the first convergence guarantees in receding-horizon techniques.
label: AI

title: Boolean kernels for collaborative filtering in top-N item recommendation
Abstract: Many personalized recommendation problems rely on data consisting solely of positive interactions (implicit feedback) between users and items, a challenge known as One-Class Collaborative Filtering (OC-CF). While linear models often achieve top performance in OC-CF, efforts have focused on building more expressive representations for enhanced recommendations. Recent analyses reveal unique characteristics of collaborative filtering (CF) datasets, including high sparsity and a long-tailed distribution of ratings. This paper proposes a boolean kernel, called Disjunctive kernel, which is less expressive than the linear one but effectively alleviates the sparsity issue in CF contexts. The embedding of this kernel comprises all combinations of a specific arity d of the input variables, with combined features interpreted semantically as disjunctions of the input variables. Experiments on several CF datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of this proposed kernel.
label: AI

title: Stochastic Runtime Analysis of a Cross Entropy Algorithm for Traveling Salesman Problems
Abstract: This article analyzes the stochastic runtime of a Cross-Entropy Algorithm applied to two classes of traveling salesman problems. The algorithm shares key features with the Max-Min Ant System with iteration-best reinforcement. For simple instances with a {1,n}-valued distance function and a unique optimal solution, the paper proves a stochastic runtime of O(n^(6+ε)) with vertex-based random solution generation and O(n^(3+ε)ln n) with edge-based random solution generation for arbitrary ε ∈ (0,1). These runtimes closely align with the expected runtime for variants of the Max-Min Ant System with best-so-far reinforcement and are obtained for the stronger notion of stochastic runtime, ensuring an optimal solution within that time with an overwhelming probability that increases exponentially with problem size. For more complex instances with n vertices positioned on an m×m grid, the study derives a stochastic runtime of O(n^3 m^(5+ε)) with vertex-based solution generation and O(n^2 m^(5+ε)) for edge-based solution generation when the n vertices form a convex polygon. When k = O(1) vertices lie inside a convex polygon formed by the remaining n-k vertices, the paper obtains a stochastic runtime of O(n^4 m^(5+ε) + n^(6k-1) m^ε) with vertex-based solution generation and O(n^3 m^(5+ε) + n^(3k) m^ε) with edge-based solution generation. These runtimes outperform the expected runtime for the (μ+λ) EA reported in a recent article, again obtained for the stronger notion of stochastic runtime.
label: AI

title: EchoWear: Smartwatch Technology for Voice and Speech Treatments of Patients with Parkinson's Disease
Abstract: Approximately 90% of individuals with Parkinson's Disease (PD) experience impaired functional communication due to voice and speech disorders associated with dysarthria. These disorders are characterized by pitch monotony, reduced loudness, irregular speech rate, imprecise consonants, and voice quality changes. Speech-language pathologists (SLPs) employ intensive in-clinic speech treatments to improve speech intelligibility in PD patients, also prescribing home exercises for generalization of speech strategies. Despite the effectiveness of these therapies, patients struggle to adhere to prescribed exercise routines outside the clinic. To monitor compliance and accuracy of home exercises and in real-world communication situations, the paper introduces EchoWear, a smartwatch-based system for remote speech and voice exercise monitoring. A study involving six participants (three with PD and three healthy controls) compared EchoWear performance with high-quality audio equipment in a speech laboratory. Preliminary analysis suggests promising outcomes for using EchoWear in speech therapies for individuals with PD.
label: AI

title: AIVAT: A New Variance Reduction Technique for Agent Evaluation in Imperfect Information Games
Abstract: Evaluating agent performance in settings with stochastic outcomes and randomized strategies can be challenging with limited data. The variance of sampled outcomes may render Monte Carlo sampling inadequate, particularly in games like heads-up no-limit Texas hold'em poker.  In this paper, AIVAT, a low-variance, provably unbiased value assessment tool, is introduced. AIVAT utilizes an arbitrary heuristic estimate of state value and the explicit strategy of a subset of agents. Unlike existing techniques focusing on variance reduction from chance events or game-ending actions, AIVAT reduces variance from both nature's choices and players with known strategies. The resulting estimator in no-limit poker can reduce the number of hands required for statistical conclusions by more than a factor of 10.
label: AI

title: CLEVR: A Diagnostic Dataset for Compositional Language and Elementary Visual Reasoning
Abstract: Developing artificial intelligence systems capable of reasoning and answering questions about visual data necessitates diagnostic tests to analyze progress and identify shortcomings. Existing visual question answering benchmarks, while helpful, exhibit strong biases that models can exploit to answer questions without genuine reasoning. These benchmarks conflate multiple error sources, hindering the pinpointing of model weaknesses. This paper presents a diagnostic dataset designed to test a range of visual reasoning abilities. This dataset minimizes biases and includes detailed annotations describing the reasoning required for each question. The paper uses this dataset to analyze various modern visual reasoning systems, providing insights into their capabilities and limitations.
label: AI

title: Action-Driven Object Detection with Top-Down Visual Attentions
Abstract: A dominant paradigm in deep learning-based object detection relies on a "bottom-up" approach involving "passive" scoring of class-agnostic proposals. While efficient, these approaches lack holistic scene-level context analysis. This paper introduces an "action-driven" detection mechanism using a "top-down" visual attention model. Objects are localized by sequentially taking actions provided by the attention model, which, conditioned on an image region, directs actions towards a target object. Individual actions are weak, but their sequential ensemble converges a bounding box accurately to the object boundary. The attention model, called AttentionNet, is composed of a convolutional neural network.  The detection process utilizes only actions from a single AttentionNet without modules for object proposals or post-bounding-box regression.  Evaluation on PASCAL VOC and ILSVRC CLS-LOC datasets reveals state-of-the-art performance compared to bottom-up detection methods. The action-driven detection mechanism demonstrates a significant advantage in precise localization, outperforming Faster R-CNN by +7.1% on PASCAL VOC 2007 with an IoU threshold of 0.7 for positive detection.
label: AI

title: A Latent-class Model for Estimating Product-choice Probabilities from Clickstream Data
Abstract: This paper analyzes customer product-choice behavior based on the recency and frequency of their page views on e-commerce sites. The paper builds upon a previously devised optimization model for estimating product-choice probabilities that satisfy monotonicity, convexity, and concavity constraints with respect to recency and frequency. While this shape-restricted model exhibits high predictive performance even with limited training samples, its performance can be further enhanced by integrating product heterogeneity. To address this, the paper develops a novel latent-class shape-restricted model for estimating product-choice probabilities for each latent class of products. A tailored expectation-maximization algorithm for parameter estimation is also provided. Computational results demonstrate that the latent-class model achieves higher predictive performance than the previous shape-restricted model and common latent-class logistic regression.
label: AI

title: Neuro-symbolic EDA-based Optimisation using ILP-enhanced DBNs
Abstract: This paper explores solving discrete optimization problems using the estimation of distribution (EDA) approach through a novel combination of deep belief networks (DBNs) and inductive logic programming (ILP). DBNs are used to learn the structure of progressively better feasible solutions, while ILP facilitates the integration of domain-based background knowledge regarding solution goodness.  Recent work showed the effectiveness of ILP in incorporating domain knowledge into EDA scenarios. However, purely ILP-based EDA faces challenges with inefficient or complex sampling of successive populations. The proposed Neuro-symbolic EDA employs an ILP engine to construct a model for good solutions using domain-based background knowledge. These rules are introduced as Boolean features in the last hidden layer of DBNs used for EDA-based optimization. Incorporating logical ILP features requires adjustments during DBN training and sampling: DBNs need training with data for input layer units and some hidden layer units, and samples should be drawn from instances entailed by the logical model.  The viability of this approach is demonstrated on instances of two optimization problems: predicting optimal depth-of-win for the KRK endgame and jobshop scheduling. Results show that samples obtained with an ILP-assisted DBN consistently contain a significantly greater proportion of good solutions compared to those generated without ILP features. Additionally, on termination of distribution estimation, samples from the ILP-assisted DBN contain more near-optimal samples. These findings suggest the potential of ILP-constructed theories for integrating complex domain knowledge into deep models for estimation of distribution-based procedures.
label: AI

title: Parallelized Tensor Train Learning of Polynomial Classifiers
Abstract: Polynomial classifiers are well-established methods in pattern classification due to their ability to generate complex decision surfaces. However, multivariate polynomials become impractical for high-dimensional problems, limiting their application to kernels in support vector machines. This paper effectively overcomes the curse of dimensionality by employing the tensor train format to represent a polynomial classifier. Two learning algorithms are proposed, each involving optimization problems with low computational complexity. The paper demonstrates how regularization for overfitting prevention and parallelization for handling large training sets are incorporated into these methods.  The efficiency and efficacy of the tensor-based polynomial classifier are showcased on the USPS and MNIST datasets.
label: AI

title: Computational Complexity of Testing Proportional Justified Representation
Abstract: This paper examines a committee voting setting where each voter approves a subset of candidates, and a target number of candidates are selected based on these approvals.  Aziz et al. (2015) introduced two representation axioms: justified representation and extended justified representation. While the former can be tested and achieved in polynomial time, the latter is coNP-complete to test, and no polynomial-time algorithm is known to achieve it.  S{\\'a}nchez-Fern{\\'a}ndez et~al. (2016) proposed an intermediate property called proportional justified representation, which can be achieved using a polynomial-time algorithm.  The complexity of testing proportional justified representation remained an open problem. This paper resolves this by proving that testing proportional justified representation is coNP-complete. The paper complements this complexity result by demonstrating that the problem admits efficient algorithms when any of the following parameters are bounded: (1) number of voters, (2) number of candidates, (3) maximum number of candidates approved by a voter, and (4) maximum number of voters approving a given candidate.
label: AI

title: Learning Features by Watching Objects Move
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel and intuitive approach to unsupervised feature learning, drawing inspiration from the human visual system. It explores the potential of using low-level motion-based grouping cues to learn an effective visual representation. Unsupervised motion-based segmentation is applied to videos to obtain segments, which serve as "pseudo ground truth" for training a convolutional network to segment objects from single frames.  Given the importance of motion in human visual system development, this straightforward approach aims to surpass the effectiveness of cleverly designed "pretext" tasks studied in the literature. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this method. When applied to transfer learning for object detection, the resulting representation significantly outperforms previous unsupervised approaches across various settings, particularly when training data is scarce.
label: AI

title: Computing Human-Understandable Strategies
Abstract: Algorithms for equilibrium computation typically do not prioritize human comprehensibility of the computed strategies. For instance, the strategies of top poker agents are often represented as massive binary files. In many situations, strategies that are understandable and implementable by humans with their computational limitations and memory constraints are desirable.  This paper focuses on poker games where private information distributions can be arbitrary. A large training set of game instances and solutions is generated by randomly selecting information probabilities. Algorithms that learn from these instances to perform well in games with unseen information distributions are then presented. The study leads to the discovery of several new fundamental rules about poker strategy that can be easily implemented by humans.
label: AI

title: A Scalable Document-based Architecture for Text Analysis
Abstract:
Analyzing textual data presents significant challenges due to the vast volume generated daily. Text analysis faces issues such as the lack of structure in document datasets, the need for various preprocessing steps (stemming, lemmatization, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition), and performance and scaling limitations. Existing text analysis architectures offer partial solutions by providing restrictive data schemas, addressing only a single aspect of text preprocessing, or focusing on a specific task during performance optimization. This paper proposes a new generic text analysis architecture that addresses these shortcomings.  The architecture features flexible document structure, integrates multiple preprocessing techniques, and indexes textual datasets for efficient access.  The conceptual architecture is implemented using both relational and document-oriented databases. Experiments demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the document-oriented logical and physical implementation. 
|||
label: AI

title: A modified Physarum-inspired model for the user equilibrium traffic assignment problem
Abstract: A modified Physarum-inspired model is proposed for solving the user equilibrium traffic assignment problem in real traffic networks with two-way traffic and multiple origin-destination pairs. By decomposing traffic flux based on origin nodes, the model distinguishes traffic flux from different origin-destination pairs. The Physarum converges to equilibrium traffic flux when no shorter path can be found between each origin-destination pair. Numerical examples using the Sioux Falls network demonstrate the rationality and convergence properties of the proposed model.
label: AI

title: Improving Tweet Representations using Temporal and User Context
Abstract: This work presents a novel representation learning model for computing semantic representations of tweets accurately. The model leverages chronologically adjacent tweets ("context") from users' Twitter timelines and incorporates user-awareness by exploiting knowledge about the user's writing style and topics of interest. Empirical results show that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art models in predicting user profile attributes like spouse, education, and job.
label: AI

title: An Empirical Study of Adequate Vision Span for Attention-Based Neural Machine Translation
Abstract: This paper investigates the "vision span" of attention models in Neural Machine Translation, aiming to reduce computational complexity by dynamically reducing redundant score computations. The vision span refers to the window of encoder states considered by the attention model at each decoding step. Experiments on English-Japanese and German-English translation tasks demonstrate that the average window size can be reduced by over 50% with minimal loss in accuracy, indicating that conventional attention mechanisms perform significant redundant computations.
label: AI

title: Context and Interference Effects in the Combinations of Natural Concepts
Abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework for representing concepts and their combinations using the quantum formalism. The framework addresses the "conceptual combinations problem" in cognitive psychology, explaining deviations from classical structures in terms of quantum effects. Natural concepts exhibit interference when combined and demonstrate context-dependence, responsible for the over- and under-extension observed in membership judgments.
label: AI

title: Self-Correcting Models for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper explores the problem of model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) with imperfect environment models, where planning errors can lead to catastrophic failures. It analyzes Hallucinated Replay, a technique that trains the model to self-correct errors, improving MBRL with flawed models. The paper provides a novel error bound showing that a model's ability to self-correct is closely related to MBRL performance. This analysis inspires a novel MBRL algorithm for deterministic MDPs with performance guarantees robust to model limitations.
label: AI

title: A Hidden Absorbing Semi-Markov Model for Informatively Censored Temporal Data: Learning and Inference
Abstract: This paper introduces the Hidden Absorbing Semi-Markov Model (HASMM), a probabilistic model for capturing continuous-time physiological processes in electronic health records (EHR) data. Unlike existing models, HASMM accommodates irregularly sampled, temporally correlated, and informatively censored physiological data, describing non-stationary clinical state transitions. Learning is achieved through a novel forward-filtering backward-sampling Monte-Carlo EM algorithm that exploits knowledge of end-point clinical outcomes and implements the E-step by sequentially sampling patients' clinical states in reverse time. Real-time inferences are drawn via a forward-filtering algorithm, demonstrating the diagnostic and prognostic utility of HASMM in a critical care prognosis setting using a real-world dataset.
label: AI

title: Sample-efficient Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dialog Control
Abstract: Representing a dialog policy as a recurrent neural network (RNN) is attractive due to its handling of partial observability, latent state inference, and optimization with supervised learning (SL) or reinforcement learning (RL). This paper presents three methods for reducing the number of dialogs required to optimize an RNN-based dialog policy with RL. The key idea is to maintain a second RNN predicting the value of the current policy and apply experience replay to both networks. These methods reduce the number of dialogs/episodes by about a third compared to standard policy gradient methods.
label: AI

title: An Integrated Optimization + Learning Approach to Optimal Dynamic Pricing for the Retailer with Multi-type Customers in Smart Grids
Abstract: This paper addresses a realistic scenario in smart grids where an electricity retailer serves three customer types: customers with home energy management systems (C-HEMS), customers with smart meters (C-SM), and customers without smart meters (C-NONE). The paper proposes a two-level decision-making framework to support the retailer in making optimal day-ahead dynamic pricing decisions. The retailer, acting as the upper-level agent, announces electricity prices for the next 24 hours, while customers, acting as lower-level agents, schedule their energy usage accordingly. The framework models the price responsiveness of different customers and optimizes dynamic prices for the retailer to maximize profit subject to market constraints. This two-level model is tackled using genetic algorithms (GA) based distributed optimization methods, with simulation results confirming its feasibility and effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Graph-based Cyber Security Analysis of State Estimation in Smart Power Grid
Abstract: This paper introduces a graph-based framework for cyber-security analysis in power system state estimation, a crucial building block of the ICT system in smart grids. The graphical characterization of state estimation security provides intuitive visualization of complex problem structures and enables efficient graphical solution algorithms, which are useful for both defending and attacking the ICT system. The paper highlights promising future research directions on graph-based security analysis and its applications in smart power grids.
label: AI

title: EgoTransfer: Transferring Motion Across Egocentric and Exocentric Domains using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper explores the transfer of motion information between egocentric and exocentric camera perspectives, relevant for modeling mirror neurons in artificial systems. The research investigates the prediction of motion in one perspective based on observations from the other. Linear and nonlinear models are trained and evaluated in terms of retrieving egocentric/exocentric motion features. Experimental results demonstrate successful motion information transfer across the two views.
label: AI

title: The Dem@Care Experiments and Datasets: a Technical Report
Abstract: The Dem@Care project aims to develop a complete system providing personalized health services for individuals with dementia, medical professionals, and caregivers using multi-sensor technology. Multi-sensor data analysis and intelligent decision-making mechanisms enable accurate representation of the person's status and provide feedback to both the person and caregivers, enhancing clinical workflow. The paper outlines the project objectives, ethical principles, and datasets already created.
label: AI

title: A Comment on Argumentation
Abstract: This paper outlines a new theory of argumentation based on the theory of defaults and their meaning, building on the work of [GS16].
label: AI

title: Web-based Semantic Similarity for Emotion Recognition in Web Objects
Abstract: This project proposes a new approach for emotion recognition using web-based similarity measures (confidence, PMI, PMING). The approach aims to extract basic emotions from short sentences with emotional content by evaluating the semantic proximity between words and emotions from a psychological model (e.g., Plutchik, Ekman, Lovheim). The extraction process involves text preprocessing, automated query generation, HTML parsing, semantic proximity estimation, and emotion ranking. The core idea is that semantic similarity can be generalized based on the co-occurrence of concepts in search engine results, enabling the generalization of emotions. Results are compared with human evaluation and additional comparative tests are performed on ranking correlation and individual word emotion evaluation. Unlike sentiment analysis, this approach aims to recognize specific emotions rather than just positive/negative sentiment.
label: AI

title: Exploiting sparsity to build efficient kernel based collaborative filtering for top-N item recommendation
Abstract: The increasing availability of implicit feedback datasets has spurred the development of effective collaborative filtering techniques for top-N item recommendation with implicit feedback. This paper proposes a principled kernel-based collaborative filtering method using the linear kernel and its generalization to kernels of the dot product family. The paper investigates the factors influencing sparsity in the cosine kernel, revealing its dependence on dataset properties, particularly the long tail distribution. The proposed method achieves good results compared to state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of efficiency and effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Reinforcement Learning Using Quantum Boltzmann Machines
Abstract: This paper investigates whether quantum annealers with specific chip layouts can outperform classical computers in reinforcement learning tasks. It associates a transverse field Ising spin Hamiltonian with a deep Boltzmann machine (DBM) qubit layout and uses simulated quantum annealing (SQA) to simulate quantum sampling. A reinforcement learning algorithm is designed where visible nodes representing states and actions of an optimal policy are the first and last layers of the deep network. Simulations show that DBMs are trained more effectively than restricted Boltzmann machines (RBM) in the absence of a transverse field. The paper develops a framework for training the network as a quantum Boltzmann machine (QBM) in the presence of a transverse field for reinforcement learning, which also outperforms RBMs.
label: AI

title: Optimal Target Assignment and Path Finding for Teams of Agents
Abstract: This paper studies the TAPF (combined target-assignment and path-finding) problem for teams of agents in known terrain, generalizing anonymous and non-anonymous multi-agent path-finding problems. Each team is assigned the same number of targets as agents, with each agent needing to move to one target such that all targets are visited. The TAPF problem involves assigning agents to targets and planning collision-free paths to minimize makespan. The CBM (Conflict-Based Min-Cost-Flow) algorithm is presented, a hierarchical algorithm that solves TAPF instances optimally by combining ideas from anonymous and non-anonymous path-finding. On the low level, CBM uses a min-cost max-flow algorithm to assign agents and plan paths, while on the high level, it uses conflict-based search to resolve collisions between teams. CBM is proven to be correct, complete, and optimal, demonstrating scalability to large instances with dozens of teams and hundreds of agents.
label: AI

title: A User Simulator for Task-Completion Dialogues
Abstract: Despite widespread interest in reinforcement-learning for task-oriented dialogue systems, several obstacles hinder progress. This paper introduces a new publicly available simulation framework to address these challenges. The framework uses a simulator for the movie-booking domain, leveraging both rules and collected data, supporting two tasks: movie ticket booking and movie seeking. The simulator allows for training dialogue agents in an online fashion, providing an effective starting point for real-world deployment. The paper demonstrates several agents and details the procedure for adding and testing custom agents.
label: AI

title: An Alternative Softmax Operator for Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: The softmax operator, often used in sequential decision-making, acts as a combination of maximization and averaging. This paper addresses the limitations of the Boltzmann softmax operator, which is prone to misbehavior. It introduces a differentiable softmax operator that is a non-expansion, ensuring convergent behavior in learning and planning. A variant of the SARSA algorithm is presented that utilizes this new operator to compute a Boltzmann policy with a state-dependent temperature parameter. The algorithm is shown to be convergent and performs favorably in practice.
label: AI

title: Neuromorphic Deep Learning Machines
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of devising general and computationally efficient models of inference and learning compatible with the spatial and temporal constraints of the brain in neuromorphic computing. Inspired by deep neural networks, the paper proposes an event-driven random BP (eRBP) rule that uses error-modulated synaptic plasticity for learning deep representations. The rule requires only simple operations, making it suitable for implementation in digital or mixed-signal neuromorphic hardware. Results demonstrate that eRBP enables rapid learning of deep representations, achieving nearly identical classification accuracies compared to artificial neural network simulations on GPUs while being robust to neural and synaptic quantization.
label: AI

title: Supervised Quantum Learning without Measurements
Abstract: This paper presents a quantum machine learning algorithm for solving a class of problems encoded in quantum controlled unitary operations. The algorithm iterates a quantum time-delayed equation, introducing feedback in the dynamics and eliminating the need for intermediate measurements. The performance of the quantum algorithm is analyzed by comparing simulation results with classical machine learning methods. The use of time-delayed equations enhances the toolbox of quantum machine learning, enabling potential applications in quantum technologies. |||
label: AI

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Successor Features for Navigation across Similar Environments
Abstract: This paper explores robot navigation in maze-like environments, focusing on solutions that don't require localization, mapping, or planning. To address this challenge, the authors propose a reinforcement learning approach based on successor features. This method transfers knowledge from previously solved navigation tasks to new instances, significantly reducing learning time and enabling adaptability to changing environments. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulated and real-world experiments using a Robotino, outperforming traditional planning-based navigation methods.
label: AI

title: A correlation coefficient of belief functions
Abstract: Determining conflict levels in Dempster-Shafer evidence theory remains an unresolved issue. While correlation coefficients can quantify evidence similarity, existing approaches have limitations. This paper introduces a novel correlation coefficient with desirable properties, particularly its application in measuring conflict among belief functions. Numerical examples and comparisons highlight its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Machine Reading with Background Knowledge
Abstract: Natural language understanding is crucial for various AI applications, including voice assistants, computer vision, and robotics. Unlike many machine reading systems that rely solely on text, this paper presents two methods that integrate background knowledge to facilitate language understanding. The first method tackles prepositional phrase attachment ambiguity, utilizing background knowledge within a semi-supervised machine learning algorithm. This approach achieves state-of-the-art results on two datasets. The second method focuses on extracting relationships from compound nouns, significantly outperforming a baseline that lacks background knowledge.
label: AI

title: Multi-Agent Path Finding with Delay Probabilities
Abstract: This paper tackles the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) problem with imperfect plan execution. The authors propose a two-level approach for solving large MAPF instances, with the high-level search addressing agent collisions and the low-level search planning individual agent paths. The paper introduces the MAPF Problem with Delay Probabilities (MAPF-DP) and proposes robust plan-execution policies to ensure collision avoidance during execution. Two classes of decentralized robust policies are discussed, enabling collision-free execution for valid MAPF-DP plans. Finally, the paper presents a two-level MAPF-DP solver that generates valid MAPF-DP plans, minimizing expected makespans.
label: AI

title: A Survey of Inductive Biases for Factorial Representation-Learning
Abstract: Representation learning, a central focus in artificial intelligence, aims to discover useful data encodings that expose domain-relevant information. This paper explores factorial representations, which identify underlying independent causal factors of data variation. These representations are compact, faithful, and facilitate human interpretation. The paper surveys various constraints that encourage learning algorithms to discover factorial representations, categorizing them as unsupervised and supervised inductive biases. Unsupervised biases leverage environmental assumptions, while supervised biases rely on additional information connected to observations. The survey provides a framework for comparing models based on the strengths of their inductive biases.
label: AI

title: Neural Networks for Joint Sentence Classification in Medical Paper Abstracts
Abstract: Existing sentence classification models based on artificial neural networks often neglect sentence context, classifying them individually. This paper presents an ANN architecture that combines the strengths of traditional ANN models and structured prediction, enabling joint classification of subsequent sentences. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art results on two datasets for sequential sentence classification in medical abstracts.
label: AI

title: Separation of Concerns in Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper introduces a framework for solving single-agent tasks using multiple specialized agents, each focusing on different aspects of the task. This approach offers two advantages: training specialized agents on distinct subtasks and transferring knowledge by transferring trained agents. The framework generalizes traditional hierarchical decomposition, where a single agent controls the task until it completes its subtask. Empirical experiments on two domains illustrate the framework's effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Coupling Adaptive Batch Sizes with Learning Rates
Abstract: Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent is widely used for large-scale empirical risk minimization, such as training neural networks. This paper addresses the challenge of choosing an optimal batch size, which significantly impacts optimization behavior. The authors propose a method for dynamic batch size adaptation that estimates gradient variance and adjusts batch size proportionally to the objective function value. This eliminates the need for manual learning rate tuning. Experiments on image classification benchmarks demonstrate faster optimization convergence and simplified learning rate tuning.
label: AI

title: Adversarial Message Passing For Graphical Models
Abstract: Bayesian inference on structured models relies on inferring posterior distributions of hidden variables. However, inference in implicit models or complex posterior distributions poses challenges. This paper proposes a novel framework that treats Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) as a basis for likelihood-free inference in generative models, extending them to Bayesian posterior inference over factor graphs. The framework introduces local learning rules based on message passing, minimizing a global divergence criterion involving cooperating local adversaries. This allows for model composition and provides a unified inference and learning framework for adversarial learning. The paper highlights the ability to perform Bayesian inference on structured models using only sampling and discrimination, enabling the use of nonparametric variational families without explicit distributions.
label: AI

title: Ontohub: A semantic repository for heterogeneous ontologies
Abstract: Ontohub is a repository engine for managing distributed and heterogeneous ontologies. Its distributed nature facilitates collaboration and knowledge sharing among communities, while its heterogeneous nature allows integration of ontologies written in diverse languages. Ontohub supports a wide range of formal logical and ontology languages, modularity constructs, and inter-theory mappings, building upon the DOL language. Ontohub repositories are organized as Git repositories, leveraging the features of this version control system. Notably, Ontohub is the first repository engine to satisfy a significant number of requirements from the Open Ontology Repository (OOR) initiative, including an API for federation, logical inference, and axiom selection.
label: AI

title: TeKnowbase: Towards Construction of a Knowledge-base of Technical Concepts
Abstract: This paper describes the construction of TeKnowbase, a knowledge-base of technical concepts in computer science. Information is sourced from websites like Webopedia, Techtarget, Wikipedia, and online textbooks. The knowledge-base construction process is divided into two parts: acquiring entities and extracting relationships between them. The resulting knowledge-base comprises approximately 100,000 triples. An evaluation on a sample of triples reveals an accuracy exceeding 90%. Additionally, classification experiments on StackOverflow data using features from TeKnowbase demonstrate improved classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: Maintaining an Up-to-date Global Network View in SDN
Abstract: Maintaining an up-to-date global network view is crucial for intelligent SDN applications. This paper investigates two key factors influencing controller's network view and application performance: network state collection and network state distribution. The authors compare the impact of active and passive OpenFlow network state collection methods on an SDN load-balancing application. This comparison is conducted through simulation and evaluation of a load-balancing application on single and distributed controllers. The paper also examines the impact of network state collection on a state-distribution-aware load-balancing application and the influence of network scale on applications requiring a global network view. The findings reveal that both network state collection and distribution significantly affect SDN application performance, highlighting the need for effective management of network state information.
label: AI

title: Learning through Dialogue Interactions by Asking Questions
Abstract: A good dialogue agent should be able to both respond to questions and ask questions, learning from both types of interactions. This paper explores this concept by designing a movie domain simulator and synthetic tasks that allow such interactions between a learner and a teacher. The authors investigate how a learner benefits from asking questions in both offline and online reinforcement learning settings, demonstrating improvements in learning performance. Real-world experiments using Mechanical Turk validate the approach, representing a step towards developing interactive dialogue agents.
label: AI

title: Dynamical Kinds and their Discovery
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the possibility of classifying causal systems into kinds sharing a common structure without constructing an explicit dynamical model or using prior knowledge. This capability has significant practical applications in model development and validation and is theoretically relevant for inferring scientific laws from empirical data. The proposed algorithm is based on dynamical symmetry, an intervention that commutes with the system's time evolution. A dynamical kind is a class of systems sharing a set of dynamical symmetries. The algorithm classifies deterministic, time-dependent causal systems by comparing their exhibited symmetries. Simulations using noisy data from various nonlinear systems demonstrate the algorithm's ability to accurately sort systems into dynamical kinds. It is robust to sampling errors and fails gracefully with increasing dynamical similarity.
label: AI

title: Crowdsourced Outcome Determination in Prediction Markets
Abstract: Prediction markets are valuable tools for aggregating information about future events. To function, they require a trusted entity to verify the outcome. This paper introduces a mechanism for decentralized prediction markets where the outcome is determined by the votes of a group of arbiters. Despite potential conflicts of interest, the authors derive conditions for incentivizing truthful voting using funds raised from market fees and a peer prediction mechanism. The paper investigates parameter values suitable for real-world implementation.
label: AI

title: Graph Summarization Methods and Applications: A Survey
Abstract: With the increasing volume of stored time-oriented data, efficient methods are needed for handling, processing, and interpreting temporal data. Anomaly detection in time-oriented data is an important task in this context. This paper proposes a framework integrating the Knowledge-Based Temporal Abstraction (KBTA) method with temporal pattern mining for anomaly detection. The approach involves applying temporal pattern mining on a dataset of basic temporal abstraction, extracting patterns representing normal behavior. Abnormal time periods are identified by a significantly small number of normal patterns. The proposed approach is demonstrated using a real-world server dataset.
label: AI

title: Collaborative creativity with Monte-Carlo Tree Search and Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Model-based diagnosis often faces the challenge of identifying the real cause of a fault due to insufficient observations or measurements, leading to multiple possible candidates. Sequential diagnosis techniques address this by automatically generating a sequence of queries to an oracle. The answers provide information to restrict the search space by eliminating inconsistent diagnosis candidates. Existing methods often require generating unnecessary query candidates and rely heavily on expensive logical reasoners. This paper proposes efficient heuristic query search methods that eliminate the need for logical reasoning while guaranteeing optimality conditions, such as minimal cardinality or best understandability. These methods significantly improve performance and scalability, outperforming existing methods by orders of magnitude. |||
label: AI

title: Encapsulating models and approximate inference programs in probabilistic modules
Abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic module interface, which encapsulates complex probabilistic models with latent variables along with custom stochastic approximate inference techniques. The interface acts as a platform-agnostic abstraction layer, separating the model's internal workings from the host probabilistic inference system. It can be viewed as a stochastic generalization of the standard simulation and density interface used for probabilistic primitives. The paper demonstrates that sound approximate inference algorithms can be constructed for networks of probabilistic modules. It also shows that the interface can be implemented using learned stochastic inference networks, and MCMC and SMC approximate inference programs.
label: AI

title: Attentive Explanations: Justifying Decisions and Pointing to the Evidence
Abstract: Deep models are the standard in visual decision models due to their strong performance across a wide range of visual tasks. However, these models often lack transparency, making it difficult to understand their decision-making processes. In contrast, humans can easily justify their decisions using natural language and point to the visual evidence that led to their conclusions. This paper proposes the Pointing and Justification (PJ-X) model, which attempts to bridge this gap by enabling deep models to justify their decisions with sentences and point to relevant evidence. The model introspects its decision and explanation process using an attention mechanism. The authors recognize the lack of datasets with reference explanations for visual decision making and collect two datasets in two domains where explaining decisions is challenging. The first dataset extends the visual question answering task to include natural language explanations for the answers. The second focuses on explaining human activities, which is considered more complex than object classification. The PJ-X model is extensively evaluated on both justification and pointing tasks, comparing its performance to prior models and ablation studies using automatic and human evaluations.
label: AI

title: Imposing higher-level Structure in Polyphonic Music Generation using Convolutional Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Constraints
Abstract: This paper introduces a method for imposing higher-level structure on generated polyphonic music. It combines a Convolutional Restricted Boltzmann Machine (C-RBM) as a generative model with gradient descent constraint optimization to provide more control over the generation process. This approach enables the use of a "template" piece, extracting structural properties and transferring them as constraints to newly generated material. The sampling process is guided by Simulated Annealing to avoid local optima and find solutions that satisfy the constraints while maintaining stability with respect to the C-RBM. Results demonstrate the ability to control the higher-level self-similarity structure, meter, and tonal properties of the generated musical piece, while preserving local musical coherence.
label: AI

title: Real-time interactive sequence generation and control with Recurrent Neural Network ensembles
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), particularly Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) RNNs, are highly effective in learning and generating sequences. However, current generative RNN techniques lack real-time interactive control over the sequence generation process, limiting their suitability for live creative expression. This paper proposes a method for real-time continuous control and "steering" of sequence generation using an ensemble of RNNs and dynamically altering the mixture weights of the models. The method is demonstrated using character-based LSTM networks and a gestural interface, allowing users to "conduct" the generation of text.
label: AI

title: Retrieving sinusoids from nonuniformly sampled data using recursive formulation
Abstract: This paper proposes a heuristic procedure for decomposing both uniformly and nonuniformly sampled 1-D signals into a sparse set of sinusoids (SSS). The procedure relies on a novel recursive formulation of sinusoid (RFS) and regression with predictive least-squares (LS). An optimal SSS is found by Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) optimization of RFS parameters of near-optimal sinusoids, combined with common criteria for estimating the number of sinusoids embedded in noise. The procedure estimates both the cardinality and parameters of SSS. The algorithm can identify the RFS parameters of a sinusoid from a data sequence containing only a fraction of its cycle. In extreme cases, when the frequency of a sinusoid approaches zero, the algorithm can detect a linear trend in the data. Additionally, irregular sampling patterns allow the algorithm to correctly reconstruct under-sampled sinusoids. The parsimonious nature of the obtained models opens opportunities for using the proposed method in machine learning, expert systems, and intelligent systems requiring analysis and simple representation of 1-D signals. The algorithm's properties are evaluated on examples of irregularly sampled artificial signals in noise and compared with high accuracy frequency estimation algorithms based on linear prediction (LP) approach, particularly with respect to the Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB).
label: AI

title: Computational Intelligence: are you crazy? Since when has intelligence become computational?
Abstract: This paper argues that Computational Intelligence, an attempt to recreate human-like intelligence in a computer, is a dead-end pursuit. It claims that the goal is unattainable due to inherent inconsistencies and contradictions between the terms "computational" and "intelligence." "Computational" implies data processing capability, while "intelligence" suggests the ability to process information. The paper criticizes the lack of focus on the divergence between data and information in the research community. This indifference is attributed to Shannon's Information theory, which has dominated the scientific community since the early 1950s. However, the paper asserts that Shannon's theory is only applicable to specific cases of data communication and not to situations where information about the semantic properties of a message needs to be considered. It explores the consequences of overlooking these crucial issues, focusing on the nature of intelligence, semantic information, their interrelationship, and the impact of disregarding this relationship.
label: AI

title: Web-based Argumentation
Abstract: Assumption-Based Argumentation (ABA) is an argumentation framework that has been proposed in the late 20th century. However, there was no solver implemented in an easily setup programming language, nor was there any web-based interface, hindering public accessibility. This project aims to address this gap by implementing an ABA solver in Python, providing a user-friendly web interface for easier access. The project demonstrates the novelty of developing an ABA solver that computes conflict-free, stable, admissible, grounded, ideal, and complete semantics. The solver is accessible through an intuitive web interface that allows users to visualize the argument and dispute trees. Experiments were conducted to determine optimal configurations and compare the project with proxdd, a state-of-the-art ABA solver lacking a web interface and computing fewer semantics. The project's best configuration, utilizing "pickle" and tree caching techniques, achieved a lower average runtime compared to proxdd. While the project encountered more exceptions than proxdd, this might be due to the project computing more semantics and requiring additional resources. Overall, the project demonstrates comparable performance to proxdd. Future work includes computational complexity analysis, efficiency analysis of implemented algorithms, implementation of additional argumentation semantics, and usability testing of the web interface.
label: AI

title: Sparse Factorization Layers for Neural Networks with Limited Supervision
Abstract: While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have made significant progress in various vision problems, they heavily rely on large amounts of labeled training data. In contrast, dictionary learning, although effective for low-level vision tasks like denoising and inpainting, doesn't scale to the size of problems that CNNs handle. Recently, adapting dictionary learning methods for supervised tasks like classification and inverse problems has gained interest. This paper proposes two new network layers based on dictionary learning: a sparse factorization layer and a convolutional sparse factorization layer, analogous to fully-connected and convolutional layers, respectively. These layers can be integrated into existing CNNs, trained end-to-end using back-propagation, and leverage semi-supervision in ways traditional CNNs cannot. Experimental comparison with a baseline CNN shows that networks with either sparse factorization layer outperform classical CNNs when supervised data is limited. They also demonstrate performance improvements in certain tasks compared to CNNs without sparse factorization layers with the same number of parameters.
label: AI

title: An argumentative agent-based model of scientific inquiry
Abstract: This paper presents an agent-based model (ABM) of scientific inquiry designed to investigate the impact of different social networks on the efficiency of knowledge acquisition among scientists. The ABM serves as a computational tool for analyzing issues related to scientific methodology and science policy. Unlike existing ABMs of science, this model emphasizes the argumentative dynamics that underpin scientific practice. It utilizes abstract argumentation theory as the core design feature, helping to avoid problematic idealizations found in other ABMs and enhancing its relevance to actual scientific practice.
label: AI

title: Defensive Player Classification in the National Basketball Association
Abstract: The National Basketball Association (NBA) has expanded data gathering and invested heavily in new technologies to collect advanced player performance metrics. This expanded dataset enables analysts to utilize unique performance metrics in models to estimate and classify player performance. Instead of grouping players based on physical attributes and positions, analysts can now group players exhibiting similar playing styles based on these tracked metrics. Existing methods for player classification have typically used offensive metrics for clustering. While attempts have been made to classify players using past defensive metrics, the lack of quality metrics has yielded limited results. This paper proposes a classification method using newly introduced defensive metrics to identify distinct defensive positions for each player. Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) are applied to find the optimal number of clusters, as the number of player categories is unknown. The model identifies five different defensive player types.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning for Lane Keeping Assist
Abstract: Reinforcement learning is a promising AI paradigm for teaching machines through interactions with the environment and learning from their mistakes. However, its application in automotive domains has been limited. The recent resurgence of interest in this field is driven by the advancements in deep learning algorithms, enabling efficient representation learning of the environment. Inspired by Google DeepMind's successful applications of reinforcement learning in games, this paper proposes different methods for autonomous driving using deep reinforcement learning. The authors address the challenges of posing autonomous driving as a supervised learning problem due to its complex interactions with the environment, including other vehicles, pedestrians, and roadworks. They formulate two main categories of algorithms: 1) Discrete actions category, and 2) Continuous actions category. The discrete actions category employs the Deep Q-Network Algorithm (DQN), while the continuous actions category utilizes the Deep Deterministic Actor Critic Algorithm (DDAC). The performance of these algorithms is evaluated on TORCS, an open-source car simulator for racing. Simulation results demonstrate the learning of autonomous maneuvering in scenarios with complex road curvatures and simple interactions with other vehicles. The paper also examines the impact of restricted conditions imposed on the car during the learning phase on the convergence time for completing the learning process.
