title: Incorporating Human Domain Knowledge into Large Scale Cost Function Learning
Abstract: Recent advancements have demonstrated the ability of Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (FCN) to model cost functions for motion planning in the context of learning driving preferences from demonstration data of human drivers. While pure learning from demonstrations within the framework of Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) is promising, incorporating well-informed human priors into the learning process can further enhance its effectiveness. This paper achieves this by pretraining a model to regress to a manual cost function and refining it based on Maximum Entropy Deep Inverse Reinforcement Learning. Injecting prior knowledge through pretraining leads to higher robustness, visually distinct obstacle boundaries, and the ability to capture instances of obstacles that elude models solely trained on demonstration data. By exploiting these human priors, the resulting model can handle corner cases, such as stairs, slopes, and underpasses, that are rarely observed in the demonstration data.
label: AI

title: Towards Adaptive Training of Agent-based Sparring Partners for Fighter Pilots
Abstract: A key requirement for the current generation of artificial decision-makers is adaptability to unexpected situations. This paper addresses the scenario of an AI for aerial dog fighting, with tunable parameters governing its behavior, optimizing behavior with respect to an objective function evaluated and learned through simulations. Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian Process surrogate is employed to investigate the objective function. This method benefits from the Gaussian Process learning a global estimate of the true objective function, providing predicted outcomes and a statistical measure of confidence in unexplored areas. This model of the objective function is crucial for understanding potential outcomes within the decision space, which is vital for training and providing feedback to human pilots. However, standard Bayesian optimization doesn't consistently perform well or accurately model highly volatile objective functions. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel sampling technique called Hybrid Repeat/Multi-point Sampling. This technique enables the AI to learn optimal behaviors in highly uncertain environments. Notably, it not only improves optimization reliability but also creates a more comprehensive model of the entire objective surface, equipping the agent with enhanced abilities to predict performance in unexplored scenarios.
label: AI

title: Algorithms for Graph-Constrained Coalition Formation in the Real World
Abstract: Coalition formation typically involves the collaboration of multiple, heterogeneous agents to achieve both individual and collective goals. This paper focuses on a specific case known as Graph-Constrained Coalition Formation (GCCF), where a network connecting agents restricts coalition formation. This type of problem is relevant in real-world applications where agents might be connected by a communication network or trust only certain peers within their social network. This paper proposes a novel representation of the GCCF problem based on the concept of edge contraction, enabling the modeling of the search space as a rooted tree. An anytime solution algorithm (CFSS) is proposed, demonstrating high efficiency when applied to a general class of characteristic functions called $m+a$ functions. Furthermore, CFSS can be parallelized to solve GCCF efficiently using a non-redundant partition of the search space. CFSS is benchmarked on both synthetic and realistic scenarios, using a real-world dataset consisting of the energy consumption of a large number of households in the UK. Results show that, in the best case, the serial version of CFSS is 4 orders of magnitude faster than the state-of-the-art, while the parallel version is 9.44 times faster on a 12-core machine. CFSS is the first approach to provide anytime approximate solutions with quality guarantees for large systems of agents (more than 2700 agents).
label: AI

title: Application of Advanced Record Linkage Techniques for Complex Population Reconstruction
Abstract: Record linkage is the process of identifying records referring to the same entity from multiple databases, a challenging task given the lack of unique entity identifiers. Linkage relies on partially identifying attributes, such as names and addresses. Recent years have witnessed the development of novel techniques for linking data across diverse application areas, particularly complex data containing records about different entity types. Advanced approaches leveraging both similarities between record attributes and relationships between entities have been developed to identify clusters of matching records. This paper explores the novel problem of linking databases where the same entity can have different roles that change over time. It focuses on developing techniques for linking historical birth, death, marriage, and census records to reconstruct the covered population over several decades. Experimental evaluation on real Scottish data reveals that even with advanced linkage techniques considering group, relationship, and temporal aspects, achieving high-quality linkage from such complex data remains challenging.
label: AI

title: Millimeter Wave V2V Communications: Distributed Association and Beam Alignment
Abstract: Millimeter-wave bands have been proposed as a solution to accommodate the extreme bandwidth demands in vehicular communications, driven by the dissemination of sensory data for enhanced environmental awareness and improved safety. However, the literature lacks principled resource allocation schemes addressing the challenging radio conditions posed by the high mobility of vehicular scenarios. This paper proposes a novel framework blending Matching Theory and Swarm Intelligence for dynamically and efficiently pairing vehicles and optimizing transmission and reception beamwidths. The framework considers both Channel State Information (CSI) and Queue State Information (QSI) when establishing vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) links. Simulation results demonstrate the throughput performance, latency/reliability trade-offs, and comparison with baseline approaches. The proposed approach achieves performance gains in reliability and delay up to 25% for ultra-dense vehicular scenarios and on average 50% more paired vehicles compared to baselines. These results highlight the operational limits and feasibility of mmWave bands as a viable radio access solution for high-rate V2V communications in future scenarios.
