title: Stratified Knowledge Bases as Interpretable Probabilistic Models (Extended Abstract)
Abstract: This paper advocates for the use of stratified logical theories to represent probabilistic models. These encodings are argued to be more interpretable than those found in frameworks like Markov logic networks. This advantage enables domain experts to directly improve learned models by adding, removing, or modifying logical formulas.
label: AI

title: Team-maxmin equilibrium: efficiency bounds and algorithms
Abstract: The Team-maxmin equilibrium defines optimal strategies for a team of rational players with a shared goal, operating in strategic games against an adversary without the ability to correlate their strategies. This solution concept captures scenarios where an agent controls multiple non-communicating resources, analogous to team members. It is established that such equilibrium always exists and is unique (except in degenerate cases), making it a credible solution concept for real-world applications, particularly in security scenarios. However, the Team-maxmin equilibrium remains largely unexplored in the literature. This paper investigates the bounds of (in)efficiency of the Team-maxmin equilibrium in relation to Nash equilibria and Maxmin equilibria, where team members can employ correlated strategies. Additionally, the paper examines various algorithms for finding or approximating an equilibrium, discussing their theoretical guarantees and evaluating their performance using a standard testbed of game instances.
label: AI

title: Faster variational inducing input Gaussian process classification
Abstract: Gaussian processes (GP) provide a prior over functions and allow for the identification of complex regularities in data. GP's are widely employed for classification/regression problems and dimensionality reduction. This work focuses specifically on the classification problem. Conventional GP-classification methods exhibit computational complexity scaling cubically with the size of the training dataset, rendering them impractical for large-scale data. Several methods have been introduced to address this limitation, and this paper focuses on approaches based on inducing inputs. This technique utilizes variational inference to propose a particular lower bound for marginal likelihood (evidence). This bound is subsequently maximized with respect to the parameters of the Gaussian process's kernel function, effectively fitting the model to the data. The computational complexity of this method is O(nm^2), where m represents the number of inducing inputs used by the model, assumed to be significantly smaller than the dataset size n. A new evidence lower bound for GP-classification was recently introduced, enabling the use of stochastic optimization, making it suitable for large datasets. However, the new lower bound depends on O(m^2) variational parameters, making optimization challenging for large m. This work proposes a novel approach for training inducing input GP models for classification problems. By employing a quadratic approximation of several terms in the aforementioned evidence lower bound, analytical expressions for optimal values of most parameters in the optimization are obtained, significantly reducing the dimension of the optimization space. Experiments demonstrate comparable or superior results compared to existing methods. Notably, this method does not require manual setting of the learning rate, enhancing its practicality compared to existing approaches.

title: A Generalized Stochastic Variational Bayesian Hyperparameter Learning Framework for Sparse Spectrum Gaussian Process Regression
Abstract: While significant research has focused on scaling up sparse Gaussian process (GP) models based on inducing variables for large datasets, less attention has been paid to the other, less explored class of low-rank GP approximations that exploit the sparse spectral representation of a GP kernel. This paper presents an advancement in the state-of-the-art of sparse spectrum GP models to achieve competitive predictive performance for massive datasets. The proposed generalized framework of stochastic variational Bayesian sparse spectrum GP (sVBSSGP) models addresses their shortcomings by incorporating a Bayesian treatment of spectral frequencies to avoid overfitting, modeling these frequencies jointly in their variational distribution to enable their interaction a posteriori, and leveraging local data for boosting predictive performance. However, these structural improvements result in a variational lower bound that is intractable to optimize. To overcome this, a variational parameterization trick is employed to make it amenable to stochastic optimization. Interestingly, the resulting stochastic gradient has a linearly decomposable structure that can be exploited to refine the stochastic optimization method, ensuring constant time per iteration while maintaining its property of being an unbiased estimator of the exact gradient of the variational lower bound. Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate that sVBSSGP outperforms state-of-the-art stochastic implementations of sparse GP models.
label: AI

title: Monte Carlo Tableau Proof Search
Abstract: This study investigates the use of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to guide proof search in tableau calculi. The paper proposes several proof-state evaluation heuristics, some of which are learned from prior proofs. An implementation based on the leanCoP prover is presented. The system is trained and evaluated on a large suite of related problems from the Mizar proof assistant, demonstrating its ability to find new and distinct proofs.
label: AI

title: NCBO Ontology Recommender 2.0: An Enhanced Approach for Biomedical Ontology Recommendation
Abstract: Biomedical researchers leverage ontologies to annotate their data with ontology terms, enabling improved data integration and interoperability. However, the sheer number, variety, and complexity of current biomedical ontologies make it challenging for researchers to identify the appropriate ones for their specific needs. To address this challenge, the National Center for Biomedical Ontology (NCBO) introduced the Ontology Recommender in 2010, a service that suggests relevant ontologies based on input biomedical text corpus or keywords. This paper presents Ontology Recommender 2.0, a new version featuring a novel recommendation approach. It evaluates the relevance of an ontology to biomedical text data according to four criteria: (1) coverage of the input data, (2) community acceptance, (3) level of detail of classes covering the input data, and (4) specialization to the domain of the input data. Evaluation results show that the enhanced recommender provides higher-quality suggestions than its predecessor, offering better coverage, more detailed information, increased domain specialization, and greater community acceptance and usage. Additionally, it provides more explanatory information and recommends both individual ontologies and groups of ontologies. Customization options are available to cater to different scenarios. Ontology Recommender 2.0 combines the strengths of its predecessor with a range of adjustments and new features, improving its reliability and usefulness. It recommends over 500 biomedical ontologies from the NCBO BioPortal platform, where it is publicly available.
label: AI

title: Associative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: The paper proposes a higher-level associative memory for learning adversarial networks. The Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework comprises a discriminator and a generator network. The generator (G) maps white noise (z) to data samples, while the discriminator (D) maps data samples to a single scalar. G learns to map from high-level representation space to data space, while D learns the opposite. This paper argues that higher-level representation spaces need not follow a uniform probability distribution. It employs Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) as a higher-level associative memory, learning the probability distribution of high-level features generated by D. The associative memory samples its underlying probability distribution, and G learns to map these samples to data space. The proposed associative adversarial networks (AANs) are generative models at the higher levels of learning, utilizing adversarial non-stochastic models D and G to learn the mapping between data and higher-level representation spaces. Experiments demonstrate the potential of the proposed networks.
label: AI

title: Analysis of a Design Pattern for Teaching with Features and Labels
Abstract: This study examines the task of teaching a machine to classify objects using features and labels. It introduces the Error-Driven-Featuring design pattern for teaching using features and labels, where the teacher prefers to introduce features only when necessary. The paper analyzes the potential risks and benefits of this teaching pattern through the use of teaching protocols, illustrative examples, and by providing bounds on the effort required for an optimal machine teacher using a linear learning algorithm, the most prevalent type of learner in interactive machine learning systems. This analysis offers a deeper understanding of the trade-offs associated with different learning algorithms, the effort required for featuring (creating new features), and labeling (providing labels for objects).
label: AI

title: Answering Image Riddles using Vision and Reasoning through Probabilistic Soft Logic
Abstract: This work explores a genre of puzzles called "image riddles," which involve a set of images and a question. Solving these riddles requires both visual detection capabilities (including object and activity recognition) and knowledge-based or commonsense reasoning. The paper compiles a dataset of over 3,000 riddles, each consisting of four images and a ground truth answer. Annotations are validated through crowd-sourced evaluation. The paper defines an automatic evaluation metric to track future progress. This task shares similarities with common IQ tasks like analogy solving and sequence filling, often used to assess intelligence. The paper develops a Probabilistic Reasoning-based approach utilizing probabilistic commonsense knowledge to answer these riddles with reasonable accuracy. The approach is demonstrated through both automatic and human evaluations, achieving promising results for these riddles and establishing a strong baseline for future efforts. The entire dataset and related materials are publicly available on the ImageRiddle Website (http://bit.ly/22f9Ala).
label: AI

title: Generalized LR parsing and the shuffle operator
Abstract: This paper adapts Tomita's Generalized LR algorithm to languages generated by context-free grammars enriched with a shuffle operator. The adaptation involves extensions to the underlying handle-finding finite automaton, construction of parser tables, and necessary optimizations for building a deterministic parser. The system is motivated by an application in artificial intelligence plan recognition. The paper argues for the correctness of the system and discusses future extensions of this work.
label: AI

title: Towards a Mathematical Understanding of the Difficulty in Learning with Feedforward Neural Networks
Abstract: Training deep neural networks for solving machine learning problems presents a significant challenge, primarily due to the highly non-convex nature of its associated optimization problem. Recent advancements suggest that many training algorithms do not suffer from undesired local minima under certain conditions, leading to extensive efforts in seeking mathematical explanations for these observations. This work provides an alternative mathematical understanding of the challenge from a smooth optimization perspective. Assuming exact learning of finite samples, sufficient conditions are identified via a critical point analysis to ensure that any local minimum is also globally minimal. Furthermore, a state-of-the-art algorithm known as the Generalised Gauss-Newton (GGN) algorithm is rigorously revisited as an approximate Newton's algorithm, sharing the property of being locally quadratically convergent to a global minimum under the condition of exact learning.
label: AI

title: Nothing Else Matters: Model-Agnostic Explanations By Identifying Prediction Invariance
Abstract: At the heart of interpretable machine learning lies the question of whether humans can accurately predict a model's behavior. This question assumes three properties of the interpretable output: coverage, precision, and effort. Coverage refers to the frequency with which humans believe they can predict the model's behavior, precision to the accuracy of these predictions, and effort encompasses either the initial effort required to interpret the model or the effort needed to make predictions about its behavior. This work proposes anchor-LIME (aLIME), a model-agnostic technique that produces high-precision rule-based explanations with clearly defined coverage boundaries. aLIME is compared to linear LIME through simulated experiments, and its flexibility is demonstrated with qualitative examples from diverse domains and tasks.
label: AI

title: Navigational Rule Derivation: An algorithm to determine the effect of traffic signs on road networks
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm to construct a road network map enriched with traffic rules, such as one-way streets and forbidden turns, based on the interpretation of already detected and classified traffic signs. This algorithm aids in the automation of map creation for commercial navigation systems. The proposed solution involves simulating navigation along the road network, determining the visibility of signs and their impact on roads at each point of interest. The approach is tested on a small urban network, and various ways to generalize it for more complex environments are discussed.
label: AI

title: Learning to reinforcement learn
Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) systems have achieved superhuman performance in numerous challenging task domains in recent years. However, a major limitation of these applications is their requirement for massive amounts of training data. A critical current objective is to develop deep RL methods that can adapt rapidly to new tasks. This paper introduces a novel approach to this challenge, referred to as deep meta-reinforcement learning. Previous research has demonstrated that recurrent networks can support meta-learning in a fully supervised context. This work extends this approach to the RL setting, resulting in a system trained using one RL algorithm but whose recurrent dynamics implement a second, distinct RL procedure. This learned RL algorithm can differ from the original one in arbitrary ways. Importantly, because it is learned, it is configured to exploit structure within the training domain. These points are unpacked through a series of seven proof-of-concept experiments, each examining a key aspect of deep meta-RL. Prospects for extending and scaling up the approach are considered, along with potential implications for neuroscience.
label: AI

title: Fast Non-Parametric Tests of Relative Dependency and Similarity
Abstract: The paper introduces two novel non-parametric statistical hypothesis tests. The first test, termed the relative test of dependency, enables the determination of whether one source variable is significantly more dependent on a first target variable or a second. Dependence is measured using the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC). The second test, the relative test of similarity, determines which of two samples from arbitrary distributions is significantly closer to a reference sample of interest. The relative measure of similarity is based on the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). These tests are constructed by using the difference of HSIC statistics and MMD statistics, respectively, as their test statistics. The resulting tests are consistent, unbiased, and possess favorable convergence properties. The effectiveness of the relative dependency test is demonstrated on several real-world problems: identifying language groups from a multilingual parallel corpus and showing that tumor location is more dependent on gene expression than chromosome imbalance. The relative test of similarity's performance is also demonstrated across a broad selection of model comparison problems in deep generative models.
label: AI

title: Optimal Dynamic Coverage Infrastructure for Large-Scale Fleets of Reconnaissance UAVs
Abstract: Current state-of-the-art UAV activation relies solely on human operators for designing and adapting drone flight routes. Moreover, this is typically done on an individual level (one vehicle per operator), with a few exceptions of new systems comprising a small number of self-organizing swarms, manually guided by a human operator. Drone-based monitoring holds great importance in various civilian domains, including road safety, homeland security, and even environmental control. In the military context, efficiently detecting evading targets using a fleet of unmanned drones has a growing impact on modern armies' ability to engage in warfare, both in traditional symmetric conflicts and asymmetric ones. Whether it's a speeding driver, a polluting trailer, or a covert convoy, the fundamental challenge remains the same: how to maximize detection probability while using as few drones as possible. This paper proposes a novel approach for optimizing large-scale swarms of reconnaissance drones, capable of generating on-demand optimal coverage strategies for any given search scenario. Given an estimated cost of the threat's potential damages, the types of available monitoring drones, and their comparative performance, the proposed method generates an analytically provable strategy, specifying the optimal number and types of drones to be deployed to cost-effectively monitor a predefined region for targets maneuvering using a given road network. The model is demonstrated using a unique dataset of the Israeli transportation network, evaluating different drone deployment schemes.
label: AI

title: Study on Feature Subspace of Archetypal Emotions for Speech Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Feature subspace selection is a crucial aspect of speech emotion recognition. While most research focuses on finding a feature subspace representing all emotions, some studies indicate that features associated with different emotions are not identical. Consequently, traditional methods may struggle to distinguish certain emotions using a single global feature subspace. This work proposes a new divide-and-conquer approach to address this problem. Feature subspaces are constructed for all combinations of every two different emotions (emotion-pairs). Bi-classifiers are then trained on these feature subspaces individually. The final emotion recognition result is determined through voting and competition methods. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to traditional multi-classification methods.
label: AI

title: Learning to detect and localize many objects from few examples
Abstract: The current trend in object detection and localization involves learning predictions using high-capacity deep neural networks trained on massive amounts of annotated data, requiring significant processing power. This paper proposes a novel neural model that directly predicts bounding box coordinates. The unique aspect of this contribution lies in the local computations of predictions with a new form of local parameter sharing, keeping the overall number of trainable parameters low. Key components of the model include spatial 2D-LSTM recurrent layers that convey contextual information between image regions. The paper shows that this model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in applications where training data is less abundant than in classical natural image settings like Imagenet/Pascal VOC tasks. The focus is on detecting text in document images, but the method is not limited to this setting. The proposed model also facilitates the detection of multiple objects in a single image and can handle variable-sized inputs without resizing.
label: AI

title: Stream Packing for Asynchronous Multi-Context Systems using ASP
Abstract: When a processing unit relies on data from external streams, a challenge arises: the stream data may need rearrangement to enable the unit to perform its tasks. Upon arrival of new data, a decision must be made: is there sufficient information available to initiate processing, or should it wait for more data? Additionally, ensuring that the data conforms to the input specification of the processing step is crucial. In the case of multiple input streams, coordination is necessary to determine which data from which incoming stream should form the input for the next process instantiation. This work proposes a declarative approach as an interface between multiple streams and a processing unit. The concept involves specifying, via answer-set programming, how to arrange incoming data into packages suitable as input for subsequent processing. This approach is intended for use in asynchronous multi-context systems (aMCSs), a recently proposed framework for loosely coupling knowledge representation formalisms, enabling online reasoning in dynamic environments. Contexts in aMCSs process data streams from external sources and other contexts.
label: AI

title: Fictitious play for cooperative action selection in robot teams
Abstract: The paper presents a game-theoretic distributed decision-making approach for addressing the problem of control effort allocation in a robotic team, based on a novel variant of fictitious play. The proposed learning process allows robots to achieve their objectives by coordinating their actions to efficiently complete their tasks. Specifically, each robot in the team predicts the planned actions of other robots while making decisions to maximize its own expected reward, which depends on the reward for jointly successful task completion. Action selection is interpreted as an n-player cooperative game. The presented approach can be considered part of the Belief Desire Intention (BDI) framework, capable of addressing cooperative, legal, safe, considerate, and emphatic decisions by robots if their individual and group rewards are appropriately defined. Following theoretical analysis, the performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated in four simulation scenarios: a coordination game between two material handling robots, a warehouse patrolling task by a team of robots, a coordination mechanism between two robots carrying a heavy object on a corridor, and an example of coordination in a sensor network.
label: AI

title: Multimodal Transfer: A Hierarchical Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Fast Artistic Style Transfer
Abstract: Artistic style transfer using neural networks often struggles to capture fine textures and maintain accurate scale when applied to high-resolution images. This paper proposes a multimodal convolutional neural network that addresses this challenge by considering both color and luminance channels, and performing hierarchical stylization with multi-scale losses. The network achieves near real-time performance through efficient offline training and effectively captures both large-scale and subtle style cues, resulting in visually appealing outputs that closely resemble multiple desired artistic styles.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) aims to answer new questions about unseen images. Current methods require extensive training data, limiting their ability to perform Zero-Shot VQA, which involves answering questions beyond the scope of the training set. This paper proposes a new evaluation protocol for Zero-Shot VQA, highlighting limitations of existing approaches and evaluating various strategies based on pretrained word embeddings, object classifiers with semantic embeddings, and test-time image retrieval. The results serve as baselines for future research in Zero-Shot VQA and achieve state-of-the-art performance in standard VQA settings.
label: AI

title: Explicablility as Minimizing Distance from Expected Behavior
Abstract: Effective human-AI collaboration requires understanding how humans perceive AI agents' behavior. When AI agents generate plans without considering human perception, their actions can appear inexplicable. This paper addresses this issue by modeling plan explicability as the distance between an agent's plan and the human's expected plan. A regression model maps plan distances to explicability scores, and an anytime search algorithm uses this model as a heuristic to generate progressively more explicable plans. The effectiveness of this approach is evaluated in simulated autonomous car and physical robot domains.
label: AI

title: ProjE: Embedding Projection for Knowledge Graph Completion
Abstract: Knowledge graph completion aims to fill in missing information in knowledge graphs by learning low-dimensional embeddings of entities and edges. While complex feature engineering has improved existing models, this paper presents ProjE, a shared variable neural network model that outperforms state-of-the-art methods without relying on complex features. By learning joint embeddings and introducing subtle changes to the loss function, ProjE achieves a smaller parameter size than most existing methods and demonstrates superior performance on standard datasets. Additionally, a new fact-checking task showcases ProjE's ability to accurately determine the veracity of declarative statements.
label: AI

title: Composing Music with Grammar Argumented Neural Networks and Note-Level Encoding
Abstract: Generating aesthetically pleasing music with artificial intelligence is a long-standing goal. While LSTMs have shown promise in sequential learning, they struggle to generate natural-sounding music that conforms to music theory. This paper proposes a novel music composition method that combines LSTMs with music theory-motivated grammars. By encoding music theory tenets as grammar-augmented filters on training data, the model learns to generate music that inherits the naturalness of human compositions while adhering to music theory rules. The approach uses a note-level encoding scheme, allowing easy implementation of music theory grammars and emulating a musician's thinking pattern. While grammar rules are applied during training but not directly during music generation, the resulting music exhibits high incidences of diatonic scale notes, small pitch intervals, and chords, demonstrating the influence of music theory.
label: AI

title: PCT and Beyond: Towards a Computational Framework for `Intelligent' Communicative Systems
Abstract: The increasing interest in intelligent autonomous machines necessitates a comprehensive theory of intelligent communicative behavior for designing human-robot interaction systems. This chapter proposes a framework inspired by Perceptual Control Theory (PCT), incorporating recent advances in generative model-based solutions used in visual and auditory scene analysis. By extending PCT, the framework develops a symmetrical architecture for a needs-driven communicative agent, demonstrating that perception can be viewed as the simulation of behavior, mirroring the PCT principle of behavior as the control of perception.
label: AI

title: Neural Style Representations and the Large-Scale Classification of Artistic Style
Abstract: Artistic style classification is a crucial task in art history, used for grouping and classifying artwork. This paper investigates the effectiveness of a neural-style representation for classifying the artistic style of paintings. The study leverages the recent advancements in image analysis using convolutional neural networks and explores the potential of neural-style algorithms for style classification.
label: AI

title: Towards Interconnected Virtual Reality: Opportunities, Challenges and Enablers
Abstract: The emergence of augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) over wireless networks has ignited interest across academia, industry, and other sectors. Achieving an immersive VR experience requires addressing various challenges across multiple disciplines. This article emphasizes the importance of VR technology as a disruptive use case of 5G and beyond, highlighting the role of advancements in storage, fog/edge computing, computer vision, and artificial intelligence. The main requirements of wireless interconnected VR are outlined, followed by a discussion of key enablers, research avenues, and underlying grand challenges. Additionally, three VR case studies with numerical results under different configurations are presented. The article concludes by discussing the limitations of current networks and advocating for further theoretical development and innovation to make VR accessible to a wider audience.
label: AI

title: Driving CDCL Search
Abstract: The CDCL algorithm is widely adopted by state-of-the-art solvers for SAT, SMT, ASP, and other problems. Embedding domain-specific heuristics can significantly boost the performance of CDCL solvers, especially for large real-world problems. This paper proposes a general framework for designing and implementing new heuristics within CDCL implementations. The framework distills key ingredients that drive CDCL search and is implemented in an ASP solver, demonstrating its effectiveness on challenging industrial problems where existing methods struggle to find solutions.
label: AI

title: Variable Neighborhood Search Algorithms for the multi-depot dial-a-ride problem with heterogeneous vehicles and users
Abstract: This work presents a study on Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS) algorithms for multi-depot dial-a-ride problems, where patients need to be transported from pickup locations to delivery locations under various constraints. The problem involves heterogeneous vehicles, distributed depots, and heterogeneous patients, with the objective of minimizing the total routing cost while respecting time-window, ride-time, capacity, and route duration constraints. The study aims to determine the optimal algorithm configuration by comparing different initial solutions, neighborhoods, and local search procedures. Two different initial solution procedures, six neighborhood types, and five local search procedures are evaluated, along with an adjusting procedure to convert infeasible solutions into feasible ones. The VNS algorithms are tested on benchmark instances and real-world healthcare application instances.
label: AI

title: The Effects of Relative Importance of User Constraints in Cloud of Things Resource Discovery: A Case Study
Abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has created a need for efficient management of connected devices, data, and services. This paper explores the integration of Cloud Computing and IoT, known as Cloud of Things, and focuses on the challenge of resource discovery and reuse for smart objects. While existing approaches often rely on multi-criteria decision analysis algorithms, this paper examines the impact of user constraints on the final solution. The behavior of SAW, TOPSIS, and VIKOR multi-objective decision analysis algorithms is analyzed, evaluating the quality of the proposed solutions using the Pareto-optimality concept.
label: AI

title: An Analysis of Tournament Structure
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for analyzing tournament structures to determine the best suitable structure based on factors such as tournament cost, competitiveness development, and ranking precision. The method uses progress trees to identify potential throwaway matches and provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different tournament structures. The analysis concludes that single elimination is optimal for qualifying a single winner with high competitiveness, while double elimination with proper seeding is preferable for qualifying multiple winners. Round-robin offers reliable ranking precision for all participants but incurs high cost and lacks competitiveness development.
label: AI

title: A Way out of the Odyssey: Analyzing and Combining Recent Insights for LSTMs
Abstract: LSTMs have become a fundamental building block for deep natural language processing (NLP) models. This paper proposes and analyzes several augmentations and modifications to LSTM networks, resulting in improved performance for text classification datasets. The proposed modifications include Monte Carlo test-time model averaging, average pooling, residual connections, and four additional suggestions. The analysis demonstrates compounding improvements over traditional LSTMs, providing a simple, reliable, and high-quality baseline model for text classification.
label: AI

title: An integrated Graphical User Interface for Debugging Answer Set Programs
Abstract: Answer Set Programming (ASP) is a powerful knowledge representation and reasoning framework, used for industrial applications due to its simple syntax and high-performance solvers. Debugging is crucial for development, necessitating tools for non-ground answer set programs. This paper presents a new graphical debugging interface based on the DWASP approach, simplifying debugger interaction. The interface is integrated into ASPIDE, a rich IDE for answer set programs, turning it into a full-fledged IDE with debugging support.
label: AI

title: Deeply supervised salient object detection with short connections
Abstract: Saliency detection has significantly benefited from recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While semantic segmentation and saliency detection algorithms often rely on fully convolutional networks (FCNs), they struggle with the scale-space problem. This paper proposes a new saliency detection method that incorporates short connections into the skip-layer structures of the Holistically-Nested Edge Detector (HED) architecture. This framework generates rich multi-scale feature maps at each layer, enabling efficient segment detection. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on widely tested salient object detection benchmarks, surpassing existing algorithms in terms of efficiency, effectiveness, and simplicity.
label: AI

title: The NOESIS Network-Oriented Exploration, Simulation, and Induction System
Abstract: Network data mining has gained prominence due to its applicability to various problems. This paper introduces NOESIS, an open-source framework for network data mining that provides a comprehensive collection of network analysis techniques, including structural property analysis, community detection, link scoring, link prediction, and visualization algorithms. NOESIS features a complete graphical user interface that simplifies the use of these techniques and is designed using object-oriented principles and structured parallel programming. As a lightweight library with minimal dependencies and a permissive license, NOESIS can be easily integrated into other software projects.
label: AI

title: Prediction of Seasonal Temperature Using Soft Computing Techniques: Application in Benevento (Southern Italy) Area
Abstract: This work proposes the use of two soft computing methods, artificial neural networks (ANNs) and genetic programming (GP), for forecasting seasonal mean temperature. The study focuses on the area surrounding the town of Benevento in southern Italy. The methods are trained using data from meteorological stations in the region, demonstrating low error rates and providing explicit rule representations for temperature prediction. The GP approach offers an explicit formula that explains the forecast, further enhancing the understanding of the prediction model.
label: AI

title: #Exploration: A Study of Count-Based Exploration for Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Count-based exploration algorithms are known to perform well in tabular reinforcement learning (RL) for solving small discrete Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). However, their applicability to high-dimensional state spaces is limited due to the rarity of state occurrences. This paper presents a surprising finding that a simple generalization of count-based exploration can achieve near state-of-the-art performance on high-dimensional and/or continuous deep RL benchmarks. The approach involves mapping states to hash codes, using a hash table to count their occurrences, and computing a reward bonus based on the count values. The study demonstrates that simple hash functions can yield impressive results on challenging tasks, while learned hash codes can further enhance performance. The analysis reveals crucial aspects of effective hash functions, including appropriate granularity and encoding relevant information for solving the MDP. This exploration strategy provides a simple yet powerful baseline for solving complex MDPs.
label: AI

title: Recoverability of Joint Distribution from Missing Data
Abstract: Estimating probabilistic queries from observed data with missing values can be challenging, especially when the data are not missing at random (MAR). This paper presents an algorithm that systematically determines whether a joint probability is estimable from observed data with missing values, assuming a data-generation model represented as a Bayesian network. The model includes unobserved latent variables, capturing dependencies among variables and explicitly representing the missingness mechanisms. This approach significantly advances existing research by providing a framework for analyzing estimability in non-MAR scenarios.
label: AI

title: Causal Inference in Observational Data
Abstract: The increasing prevalence of multiple chronic diseases in aging populations necessitates comprehensive treatment strategies. Finding the optimal set of drugs for a combination of diseases poses a combinatorial pattern exploration challenge. While association rule mining is commonly used for such problems, its focus on associative rather than causal patterns makes it unsuitable for healthcare applications. This paper proposes a novel framework based on the Rubin-Neyman causal model for extracting causal rules from observational data, addressing common biases. The framework aims to identify subpopulations where effective intervention combinations exist and to find all intervention combinations within these subpopulations such that removing any intervention reduces treatment efficacy. The concept of closed intervention sets extends the quantification of single intervention effects to sets of concurrent interventions. The framework is evaluated using Electronic Health Records (EHR) data from a large cohort of Mayo Clinic patients, demonstrating the extraction of rich patterns that explain controversial findings in medical literature.
label: AI

title: Link Prediction using Embedded Knowledge Graphs
Abstract: Knowledge base completion aims to infer missing facts from existing ones. Current methods focus on exploring explicit paths within sequences of triples, often requiring human-designed sampling procedures due to the vast number of possible paths. We propose a novel approach, Embedded Knowledge Graph Network (EKGN), which utilizes an embedded knowledge graph trained end-to-end to optimize and compress the initial knowledge base. Through interactive lookup operations on this compressed representation, EKGN achieves state-of-the-art results on popular knowledge base completion benchmarks.
label: AI

title: When Saliency Meets Sentiment: Understanding How Image Content Invokes Emotion and Sentiment
Abstract: Sentiment analysis on social media is crucial for understanding social signals. As images are prevalent on these platforms, image sentiment analysis is gaining increasing attention. However, existing systems often fail to explain how visual content evokes sentiment. Psychological studies show that salient objects within an image often trigger emotions. This work investigates the fine-grained interaction between visual saliency and sentiment, analyzing images categorized by scene type (open-closed, natural-manmade, indoor-outdoor, face-noface). Our study explores the relationship between the sentiment of salient regions and the overall image sentiment using state-of-the-art saliency and sentiment classification algorithms. Results on a representative image emotion dataset reveal interesting correlations between saliency and sentiment in different scene types, shedding light on the mechanism of visual sentiment evocation.
label: AI

title: Google's Multilingual Neural Machine Translation System: Enabling Zero-Shot Translation
Abstract: This paper introduces a simple solution for multilingual Neural Machine Translation (NMT) using a single model. Instead of modifying the model architecture, we introduce an artificial token at the beginning of the input sentence to specify the target language. The rest of the model, including encoder, decoder, and attention, remains shared across all languages, utilizing a common wordpiece vocabulary. This approach allows for multilingual NMT with a single model without parameter increase, surpassing previous solutions in simplicity. Our method often improves translation quality for all language pairs, even while maintaining a constant number of parameters. On WMT'14 benchmarks, a single multilingual model achieves comparable performance for English-to-French and surpasses state-of-the-art results for English-to-German. Similarly, a single multilingual model outperforms state-of-the-art for French-to-English and German-to-English on WMT'14 and WMT'15 benchmarks respectively. Multilingual models of up to twelve language pairs demonstrate improved translation for individual pairs on production corpora. Notably, our models can learn to bridge language pairs unseen during training, highlighting the potential for transfer learning and zero-shot translation in neural translation. Further analysis suggests a universal interlingua representation within our models, showcasing interesting examples of language mixing.
label: AI

title: A Model-Predictive Motion Planner for the IARA Autonomous Car
Abstract: We present the Model-Predictive Motion Planner (MPMP) of the Intelligent Autonomous Robotic Automobile (IARA), a fully autonomous car. IARA uses a path planner to generate a path from its current location to a desired destination. Using this path, current position, a goal in the path, and a map, MPMP computes smooth trajectories from the current position to the goal within 50 milliseconds. MPMP calculates trajectory poses that closely follow the path while maintaining a safe distance from obstacles. Experiments demonstrate MPMP's ability to compute trajectories that precisely follow a human-generated path (average distance of 0.15 meters) while smoothly driving IARA at speeds up to 32.4 km/h (9 m/s).
label: AI

title: Learning-Theoretic Foundations of Algorithm Configuration for Combinatorial Partitioning Problems
Abstract: Max-cut, clustering, and other partitioning problems are NP-hard, motivating the development of approximation algorithms and heuristics. While worst-case analysis is common for comparing algorithms, it can be misleading if worst-case instances occur rarely. This necessitates optimization methods that find the best algorithm configuration for typical inputs. We address this problem for clustering, max-cut, and other partitioning problems like integer quadratic programming by designing efficient and sample-efficient learning algorithms. These algorithms learn from samples drawn from an application-specific distribution over problem instances and produce a partitioning algorithm with high expected performance. Our algorithms learn over common algorithm families: SDP rounding algorithms and agglomerative clustering algorithms with dynamic programming. We provide tight bounds on the pseudodimension of these algorithm classes, demonstrating that even for algorithms parameterized by a single parameter, the pseudo-dimension can be superconstant. This work contributes to algorithm configuration foundations and pushes the boundaries of learning theory by analyzing complex, multi-stage optimization procedures.
label: AI

title: Fast Task-Specific Target Detection via Graph Based Constraints Representation and Checking
Abstract: This paper presents a fast target detection framework for real-world robotics applications. Focusing on intelligent agents performing task-specific object detection, we propose the concept of early recognition, which influences the candidate proposal process for fast and reliable detection. To efficiently check target constraints, we introduce a novel policy to generate a sub-optimal checking order, proving its bounded time cost compared to the optimal sequence, which is computationally intractable. Experiments on rigid object and non-rigid body part detection scenarios validate our pipeline. To demonstrate its broad applicability, we showcase a human-robot interaction system based on our non-rigid body part detection.
label: AI

title: Zero-resource Machine Translation by Multimodal Encoder-decoder Network with Multimedia Pivot
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to build a neural machine translation system without supervised resources (i.e., no parallel corpora), leveraging multimodal embedded representations over texts and images. Based on the assumption that text documents are often accompanied by related multimedia information, we indirectly estimate the relevance between languages using multimedia as a "pivot." By projecting all modalities into a shared hidden space, samples belonging to similar semantic concepts converge regardless of their original space. This modality-agnostic representation bridges the gap between different modalities. With a decoder placed on top, our network flexibly outputs from any input modality. Notably, in testing, only source language texts are required for translation. Experiments on two benchmarks demonstrate the method's ability to achieve reasonable translation performance. We compared and investigated several implementations, finding that an end-to-end model optimizing both rank loss in multimodal encoders and cross-entropy loss in decoders performs best.
label: AI

title: Generative Models and Model Criticism via Optimized Maximum Mean Discrepancy
Abstract: This paper proposes a method to optimize the representation and distinguishability of samples from two probability distributions by maximizing the estimated power of a statistical test based on the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD). This optimized MMD is applied to unsupervised learning by generative adversarial networks (GAN), where a generator aims to produce realistic samples and a discriminator attempts to distinguish them from real data. The MMD serves two roles: as a discriminator, either directly on samples or their features, and as an evaluator of generative model performance by comparing generated samples against a reference dataset. The optimized MMD is particularly useful as it provides an interpretable indication of differences between model and data distributions, even in cases where individual samples are not easily distinguishable.
label: AI

title: An Evaluation of Information Sharing Parking Guidance Policies Using a Bayesian Approach
Abstract: Real-time parking occupancy information is essential for parking management systems to facilitate efficient parking. Advancements in connected and automated vehicle technologies enable sensor-equipped cars (probe cars) to detect and broadcast available parking spaces while driving through parking lots. This paper evaluates the impact of probe car market penetration on system performance and investigates various parking guidance policies to improve data acquisition. We use a simulation-based approach to implement four policies on an off-street parking lot, influencing probe car behavior by assigning parking spaces. This affects scanning routes and parking space occupancy estimations. Our final proposed policy is a near-optimal guidance strategy that maximizes the information gain of posteriors. Results suggest that an efficient information gathering policy can compensate for low penetration of connected and automated vehicles. We also highlight the trade-offs between maximizing information gain through exploration and improving assignment accuracy through exploitation. Our findings can assist urban policy makers in designing and managing smart parking systems.
label: AI

title: Fair and Throughput-Optimal Routing in Multi-Modal Underwater Networks
Abstract: While acoustic communications have been dominant underwater for years, other technologies based on optical and radio-frequency electro-magnetic waves are emerging. Each technology has advantages and disadvantages: acoustic signals achieve long ranges at kbit/s bit rates, while optical signals offer Mbit/s rates but only over short distances. This technological diversity can be leveraged by multi-modal systems that integrate different technologies and use intelligence to select the optimal one for any given situation. This paper addresses a fundamental aspect of this intelligence by proposing a novel routing protocol for networks of multi-modal nodes. The protocol makes distributed decisions about data flow over each link and technology, aiming to advance packets toward their destination. Our routing protocol prevents bottlenecks and ensures fair resource allocation to different nodes. Performance analysis through simulations and field experiments shows that the protocol successfully leverages all technologies for data delivery, even with imperfect topology information. Our simulation code is shared to facilitate reproducibility.
label: AI

title: Feature Engineering and Ensemble Modeling for Paper Acceptance Rank Prediction
Abstract: Measuring research impact and ranking academic achievement are important and challenging problems. An objective assessment of research institutions is valuable for students, parents, funding agencies, and attracts attention from government and industry. KDD Cup 2016 proposed the paper acceptance rank prediction task, where participants were asked to rank institutions based on the predicted number of accepted papers at the 8 top computer science conferences. Our approach involved a three-step feature engineering method, including basic feature definition, similar conference identification to enrich the feature set, and dimension reduction using PCA. We proposed three ranking models and ensemble methods for combining these models. Experiments verified the effectiveness of our approach, achieving second place overall in KDD Cup 2016.
label: AI

title: Weakly Learning to Match Experts in Online Community
Abstract: Finding users who can answer a given question on online question-and-answer (QA) platforms like Quora while ensuring their willingness to answer is a crucial challenge. The key is balancing the user's expertise with the question topic and their likelihood of responding positively to an invitation. This paper formally defines the problem and develops a weakly supervised factor graph (WeakFG) model to address it. The model explicitly captures expertise matching between questions and users. To model user willingness to answer, we incorporate social identity theory-based correlations into the WeakFG model. We validate the proposed model using two datasets: QA-Expert and Paper-Reviewer. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms (+1.5-10.7% by MAP) state-of-the-art algorithms for matching users with community questions. We also developed an online system to showcase the advantages of our approach.
label: AI

title: Growing Interpretable Part Graphs on ConvNets via Multi-Shot Learning
Abstract: This paper proposes a learning strategy to extract object-part concepts from a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN), aiming to explore explicit semantics hidden within CNN units and gradually build a semantically interpretable graphical model on the pre-trained CNN for hierarchical object understanding. Using part annotations on a small number of objects (e.g., 3-12), our method mines latent patterns from the pre-trained CNN and associates them with different semantic parts. These patterns are organized in a four-layer And-Or graph to clarify their internal semantic hierarchy. Guided by a small number of part annotations, our method achieves superior performance (13%-107% improvement) in part center prediction on PASCAL VOC and ImageNet datasets.
label: AI

title: SummaRuNNer: A Recurrent Neural Network based Sequence Model for Extractive Summarization of Documents
Abstract: We present SummaRuNNer, a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)-based sequence model for extractive summarization of documents, achieving performance comparable or better than state-of-the-art. Our model is highly interpretable, allowing visualization of predictions broken down by abstract features like information content, salience, and novelty. Another novel contribution is abstractive training of our extractive model, enabling training on human-generated summaries alone, eliminating the need for sentence-level extractive labels.
label: AI

title: Learning to Gather Information via Imitation
Abstract: The budgeted information gathering problem, where a robot with a fixed fuel budget must maximize information collected from the world, arises in autonomous exploration and inspection with mobile robots. While prior work investigated effective approximations, their performance depends heavily on the distribution of objects in the world. This paper proposes a novel data-driven imitation learning framework to address this issue. We present EXPLORE, an efficient algorithm that trains a policy on the target distribution to imitate a clairvoyant oracle that knows the world fully and computes non-myopic solutions to maximize information. Validation on 2D and 3D exploration problems demonstrates EXPLORE's ability to adapt to different object distributions. Our analysis provides theoretical insights into EXPLORE's behavior. This work paves the way for applying data-driven methods efficiently to information gathering.

title: Recognizing and Eliciting Weakly Single Crossing Profiles on Trees
Abstract: This paper introduces and studies the weakly single-crossing domain on trees, a generalization of the single-crossing domain in social choice theory. We present a polynomial-time algorithm for recognizing preference profiles belonging to this domain. We then develop an efficient elicitation algorithm for this domain that works even when preferences are accessed sequentially and the underlying single-crossing tree structure is unknown. We prove a matching lower bound on the query complexity of our elicitation algorithm when the number of voters is large compared to the number of candidates. We also prove a lower bound of Ω(m²log n) on the number of queries required for any algorithm to elicit a single crossing profile when random queries are allowed. This resolves an open question in an earlier paper and proves the optimality of their preference elicitation algorithm with random queries.

title: Commonsense Knowledge Enhanced Embeddings for Solving Pronoun Disambiguation Problems in Winograd Schema Challenge
Abstract: This paper proposes commonsense knowledge enhanced embeddings (KEE) to solve Pronoun Disambiguation Problems (PDP). The investigated PDP task is a complex coreference resolution problem requiring commonsense knowledge, a standard test set in the 2016 Winograd Schema Challenge. Traditional linguistic features used for coreference resolution (e.g., context and gender) are ineffective in this task. KEE models provide a general framework for utilizing commonsense knowledge to solve PDP problems. Since training data is unavailable for the PDP task, KEE models are used for unsupervised feature extraction. To evaluate KEE model effectiveness, we incorporate various commonsense knowledge bases (ConceptNet, WordNet, CauseCom) into the KEE training process. Applying these methods to the 2016 Winograd Schema Challenge achieved the best performance. Experiments on the standard PDP task indicate that KEE models can solve PDP problems with 66.7% accuracy, establishing a new state-of-the-art performance.

title: Entropic Causal Inference
Abstract: Identifying the causal direction between two discrete random variables using observational data is a challenging problem. Unlike previous work, we retain the most general functional model but assume simplicity of the unobserved exogenous variable in the true causal direction. We quantify simplicity using Rényi entropy. Our main result shows that, under natural assumptions, if the exogenous variable has low H0 entropy (cardinality) in the true direction, it must have high H0 entropy in the wrong direction. While estimating the minimum entropy exogenous variable is algorithmically hard, we show that finding the exogenous variable with minimum entropy is equivalent to the minimum joint entropy problem given n marginal distributions, known as the minimum entropy coupling problem. We propose an efficient greedy algorithm for the minimum entropy coupling problem, which provably finds a local optimum for n=2. This provides a greedy algorithm for finding the exogenous variable with minimum H1 (Shannon Entropy). Our greedy entropy-based causal inference algorithm performs similarly to state-of-the-art additive noise models on real datasets. An advantage of our approach is that it only utilizes distributions, not the values of random variables. This enables its application to both ordinal and categorical data, unlike additive noise models.

title: Leveraging Video Descriptions to Learn Video Question Answering
Abstract: This paper introduces a scalable approach to learn video-based question answering (QA) for answering free-form natural language questions about video content. Our approach automatically harvests a large number of videos and descriptions freely available online. Candidate QA pairs are then automatically generated from these descriptions, eliminating manual annotation. We train various video-based QA methods extended from MN (Sukhbaatar et al. 2015), VQA (Antol et al. 2015), SA (Yao et al. 2015), and SS (Venugopalan et al. 2015) using these candidate QA pairs. To handle imperfect candidate QA pairs, we propose a self-paced learning procedure to iteratively identify and mitigate their effects during training. Performance is evaluated on manually generated video-based QA pairs. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our self-paced learning procedure and show that the extended SS model outperforms various baselines.

title: A Review on Algorithms for Constraint-based Causal Discovery
Abstract: Causal discovery aims to mine causal relationships between variables from data, a crucial task in science. Over the past decades, significant progress has been made in this fundamental data mining paradigm. With the increasing availability of large and complex observational data, constraint-based approaches have gained significant interest and application due to their fast running speed and easy generalization to cases of causal insufficiency. This paper reviews constraint-based causal discovery algorithms. We discuss the learning paradigm of constraint-based approaches, survey state-of-the-art algorithms with detailed analysis, and summarize related open-source software packages and benchmark data repositories. Finally, we outline open problems in constraint-based causal discovery for future research. |||

title: Multilingual Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Cross-lingual Knowledge Alignment
Abstract: Recent research has highlighted the benefits of knowledge graph embeddings in completing monolingual knowledge graphs. However, the alignment of knowledge bases across different languages is crucial for constructing a coherent knowledge base and facilitating machine understanding of cross-lingual entity relationships. Due to the high cost and error-proneness of manual alignment, we introduce MTransE, a translation-based model for multilingual knowledge graph embeddings, offering a simple and automated solution. MTransE encodes entities and relations of each language in separate embedding spaces, providing transitions between embedding vectors to their cross-lingual counterparts while preserving monolingual embedding functionalities. We explore three techniques for representing cross-lingual transitions: axis calibration, translation vectors, and linear transformations, resulting in five MTransE variants using different loss functions. Our models can be trained on partially aligned graphs, requiring only a small portion of triples to be aligned with their cross-lingual counterparts. Experiments on cross-lingual entity matching and triple-wise alignment verification demonstrate promising results, with certain variants consistently outperforming others across different tasks. We also investigate how MTransE preserves key properties of its monolingual counterpart, TransE.

title: Reinforcement Learning in Rich-Observation MDPs using Spectral Methods
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in Markov decision processes (MDPs) with large state spaces poses significant challenges. The performance of standard RL algorithms degrades significantly as state space dimensionality increases. However, practical applications often involve large MDPs with underlying low-dimensional structures. This paper focuses on the setting of rich-observation Markov decision processes (ROMDPs), where a limited number of hidden states map injectively to observation states. Each observation state is generated by a single hidden state, with this mapping being unknown a priori. We introduce a spectral decomposition method to consistently learn this mapping, achieving low regret. This estimated mapping is integrated into an optimistic RL algorithm (UCRL), operating on the estimated hidden space. We derive finite-time regret bounds for our algorithm with weak dependence on the observed space dimensionality. Notably, our algorithm asymptotically achieves the same average regret as the oracle UCRL algorithm, which possesses prior knowledge of the mapping between hidden and observed spaces. Thus, we present an efficient spectral RL algorithm for ROMDPs.

title: Optimal incentives for collective intelligence
Abstract: Collective intelligence, where a group performs more effectively than any individual, depends heavily on diversity among its members. However, maintaining diversity is challenging due to social pressure to conform to peers. We investigate the role of incentives in preserving useful diversity through an evolutionary game-theoretic model of collective prediction. Our analysis reveals that market-based incentive systems lead to herding effects, reducing available information and hindering collective intelligence. To address this, we propose a new incentive scheme that rewards accurate minority predictions. This scheme promotes optimal diversity and collective predictive accuracy. We conclude that real-world systems should incentivize individuals who demonstrate accuracy when the majority opinion is incorrect.

title: A Connection between Generative Adversarial Networks, Inverse Reinforcement Learning, and Energy-Based Models
Abstract: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are a recent class of generative models where a generator is trained to optimize a cost function simultaneously learned by a discriminator. While cost function learning is relatively novel in generative modeling, it has long been explored in control and reinforcement learning (RL) domains, typically for imitation learning from demonstrations. In these fields, learning the cost function underlying observed behavior is known as inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) or inverse optimal control. Although the connection between cost learning in RL and generative modeling might seem superficial, this paper demonstrates a mathematical equivalence between certain IRL methods and GANs. Specifically, we show an equivalence between a sample-based algorithm for maximum entropy IRL and a GAN where the generator's density is evaluable and provided as an additional input to the discriminator. Interestingly, maximum entropy IRL is a special case of an energy-based model. We discuss the interpretation of GANs as an algorithm for training energy-based models, connecting this interpretation to recent work linking GANs and EBMs. By formally highlighting the connection between GANs, IRL, and EBMs, we aim to facilitate the transfer of ideas between these communities, particularly for developing more stable and scalable algorithms, a key challenge in all three domains.

title: Applying Chatbots to the Internet of Things: Opportunities and Architectural Elements
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is emerging as a pivotal technology shaping the future by connecting physical devices or "things" to the internet. This convergence presents opportunities for intersecting with other technological trends, enabling greater intelligence and efficiency. This paper focuses on integrating Intelligent Conversational Software Agents, or Chatbots, with IoT. While literature surveys have explored various IoT applications, features, underlying technologies, and challenges, Chatbots are gaining widespread adoption due to advancements in platform and framework development. The novelty of this paper lies in the specific integration of Chatbots into the IoT scenario. We analyze the shortcomings of existing IoT systems and propose solutions by incorporating chatbots. A general architecture is proposed for implementing such a system, outlining both commercial and open-source platforms and frameworks that facilitate implementation. We also address emerging challenges and potential future directions for this new integration.

title: Hierarchical Object Detection with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a method for performing hierarchical object detection in images guided by a deep reinforcement learning agent. The key idea is to concentrate on image areas with richer information and zoom in on them. We train an intelligent agent that, given an image window, can decide where to focus attention among five predefined region candidates (smaller windows). This procedure is iterated for hierarchical image analysis. We compare two candidate proposal strategies: with and without overlap. Additionally, our work compares two strategies for extracting features from a convolutional neural network for each region proposal: one that computes new feature maps for each proposal, and another that computes feature maps for the whole image and then generates crops for each proposal. Experiments indicate better results for the overlapping candidate proposal strategy and a performance loss for cropped image features due to reduced spatial resolution. While this loss seems inevitable when working with a large number of object candidates, the significantly reduced amount of region proposals generated by our reinforcement learning agent allows for extracting features for each location without sharing convolutional computation among regions.

title: Learning to Navigate in Complex Environments
Abstract: Learning to navigate in complex environments with dynamic elements is a crucial milestone in developing AI agents. This work formulates navigation as a reinforcement learning problem and demonstrates that data efficiency and task performance can be dramatically improved by utilizing auxiliary tasks leveraging multimodal sensory inputs. Specifically, we consider jointly learning the goal-driven reinforcement learning problem with auxiliary depth prediction and loop closure classification tasks. This approach can learn to navigate from raw sensory input in intricate 3D mazes, approaching human-level performance even when the goal location changes frequently. We provide detailed analysis of the agent's behavior, its ability to localize, and its network activity dynamics, showing that the agent implicitly learns key navigation abilities.

title: Show me the material evidence: Initial experiments on evaluating hypotheses from user-generated multimedia data
Abstract: Subjective questions, such as "does Neymar dive?" or "is Clinton lying?", are popular queries on web search engines, as evidenced by autocompletion suggestions on platforms like Google, Yahoo, and Bing. In the era of cognitive computing, these queries can be handled as hypotheses for evaluation beyond search. Our vision is to leverage unstructured data and metadata from rich user-generated multimedia often shared as evidence for or against hypotheses on social media platforms. This paper presents two preliminary experiments along these lines and discusses challenges for a cognitive computing system that collects material evidence from user-generated multimedia to aggregate it into a form of collective decision on the hypothesis.
label: AI

title: UTCNN: a Deep Learning Model of Stance Classificationon on Social Media Text
Abstract: Most neural network models for document classification on social media focus on text information to the neglect of other information on these platforms. This paper classifies post stance on social media channels and develops UTCNN, a neural network model that incorporates user tastes, topic tastes, and user comments on posts. UTCNN is applicable not only to social media texts but also to texts in forums and message boards. Experiments conducted on Chinese Facebook data and English online debate forum data show that UTCNN achieves a 0.755 macro-average f-score for supportive, neutral, and unsupportive stance classes on Facebook data, significantly outperforming models that omit user, topic, or comment information. This model design effectively mitigates the lack of data for the minor class without resorting to oversampling. Moreover, UTCNN yields a 0.842 accuracy on English online debate forum data, significantly outperforming results from previous work and other deep learning models, demonstrating UTCNN's robust performance regardless of language or platform.

title: Neural Networks Models for Entity Discovery and Linking
Abstract: This paper describes the USTC_NELSLIP systems submitted to the Trilingual Entity Detection and Linking (EDL) track in the 2016 TAC Knowledge Base Population (KBP) contests. We developed two systems for entity discovery and mention detection (MD): one using conditional RNNLM and the other using the attention-based encoder-decoder framework. The entity linking (EL) system comprises two modules: a rule-based candidate generation and a neural networks probability ranking model. Additionally, simple string matching rules are employed for NIL clustering. Ultimately, our best system achieved an F1 score of 0.624 in the end-to-end typed mention ceaf plus metric.

title: The Sum-Product Theorem: A Foundation for Learning Tractable Models
Abstract: Inference in expressive probabilistic models is generally intractable, making them challenging to learn and limiting their applicability. Sum-product networks are a class of deep models where, surprisingly, inference remains tractable even with an arbitrary number of hidden layers. This paper generalizes this result to a broader set of learning problems, encompassing all those where inference involves summing a function over a semiring. This includes satisfiability, constraint satisfaction, optimization, integration, and others. For summation to be tractable in any semiring, it is sufficient that the factors of every product have disjoint scopes. This unifies and extends numerous previous results in the literature. Enforcing this condition during learning ensures that the learned models are tractable. We illustrate the power and generality of this approach by applying it to a new type of structured prediction problem: learning a nonconvex function that can be globally optimized in polynomial time. Empirically, we demonstrate that this significantly outperforms the standard approach of learning without considering the cost of optimization.

title: Song From PI: A Musically Plausible Network for Pop Music Generation
Abstract: We present a novel framework for generating pop music. Our model is a hierarchical Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) where the layers and hierarchical structure encode our prior knowledge about pop music composition. Specifically, the bottom layers generate the melody, while higher levels produce drums and chords. Human studies show a strong preference for our generated music over that produced by a recent Google method. We further demonstrate two applications of our framework: neural dancing and karaoke, as well as neural story singing.
label: AI

title: Importance Sampling with Unequal Support
Abstract: Importance sampling is often employed in machine learning when training and testing data come from different distributions. This paper proposes a new variant of importance sampling that can reduce the variance of importance sampling-based estimates by orders of magnitude when the supports of the training and testing distributions differ. After motivating and presenting our new importance sampling estimator, we provide a detailed theoretical analysis characterizing both its bias and variance relative to the ordinary importance sampling estimator (in various settings, including cases where ordinary importance sampling is biased, while our new estimator is not, and vice versa). We conclude with an example of how our new importance sampling estimator can be used to improve estimates of the effectiveness of a new treatment policy for diabetes for an individual, using only data from when the individual used a previous treatment policy.

title: Why is it Difficult to Detect Sudden and Unexpected Epidemic Outbreaks in Twitter?
Abstract: Social media services like Twitter are valuable sources of information for decision support systems. Numerous studies have demonstrated this in the medical domain, where Twitter is considered a viable tool for public health officials to extract relevant information for early detection, management, and control of epidemic outbreaks. This is possible due to social media's inherent ability to transmit information faster than traditional channels. However, most current studies have limited their scope to detecting common and seasonal health recurring events (e.g., Influenza-like Illness), partially due to the noisy nature of Twitter data, which makes outbreak detection and management challenging. Within the European project M-Eco, we developed a Twitter-based Epidemic Intelligence (EI) system designed to handle a broader class of unexpected and aperiodic outbreaks. We addressed three key research challenges in this endeavor: 1) dynamic classification to manage the evolving terminology of Twitter messages, 2) alert generation to produce reliable outbreak alerts by analyzing noisy tweet time series, and 3) ranking and recommendation to support domain experts in better assessing generated alerts. This paper empirically evaluates our proposed approach to these challenges using real-world outbreak datasets and a large collection of tweets. We validate our solution with domain experts, describe our experiences, and provide a more realistic view of the benefits and issues of analyzing social media for public health.

title: XCSP3: An Integrated Format for Benchmarking Combinatorial Constrained Problems
Abstract: We propose a major revision of the XCSP 2.1 format, called XCSP3, to build integrated representations of combinatorial constrained problems. This new format can handle mono/multi optimization, various variable types, cost functions, reification, views, annotations, variable quantification, distributed, probabilistic, and qualitative reasoning. The format is compact, highly readable, and easily parsable. Notably, it captures the structure of problem models through the ability to declare arrays of variables and identify syntactic and semantic groups of constraints. The number of constraints is kept under control by introducing a limited set of basic constraint forms, and automatically generating variations through lifting, restriction, sliding, logical combination, and relaxation mechanisms. As a result, XCSP3 encompasses virtually all constraints found in major constraint solvers developed by the CP community. A website, developed alongside the format, hosts numerous models and series of instances. Users can perform sophisticated queries for selecting instances based on precise criteria. The objective of XCSP3 is to simplify the effort required to test and compare different algorithms by providing a common testbed of combinatorial constrained instances.

title: A stochastically verifiable autonomous control architecture with reasoning
Abstract: A new agent architecture called Limited Instruction Set Agent (LISA) is introduced for autonomous control. This architecture builds on previous implementations of AgentSpeak and is structurally simpler than its predecessors, aiming to facilitate design-time and run-time verification methods. We investigate and illustrate the process of abstracting the LISA system into two different types of discrete probabilistic models: DTMC and MDP. LISA provides a tool for complete modeling of the agent and environment for probabilistic verification. The agent program can be automatically compiled into a DTMC or MDP model for verification with Prism. The automatically generated Prism model can be used for both design-time and run-time verification. Run-time verification is investigated and illustrated in the LISA system as an internal modeling mechanism for predicting future outcomes.

title: Learning to Play Guess Who? and Inventing a Grounded Language as a Consequence
Abstract: Acquiring one's first language is an incredible feat, not easily replicated. Learning to communicate using only a few pictureless books, a corpus, would likely be impossible even for humans. Nevertheless, this is the dominant approach in most natural language processing today. As an alternative, we propose the use of situated interactions between agents as a driving force for communication, and the framework of Deep Recurrent Q-Networks for evolving a shared language grounded in the provided environment. We task the agents with interactive image search in the form of the game Guess Who?. The images from the game provide a non-trivial environment for the agents to discuss and a natural grounding for the concepts they decide to encode in their communication. Our experiments show that the agents learn not only to encode physical concepts in their words (grounding) but also to engage in multi-step dialogue, remembering the state of the dialogue from step to step.
