title: Mass-to-Light versus Color Relations for Dwarf Irregular Galaxies
Abstract: New relations between $UBV$ colors and mass-to-light ratios ($M/L$) are established for dwarf irregular (dIrr) galaxies using data from the LITTLE THINGS survey. Stellar mass density profiles were determined for 34 dIrr galaxies by fitting spectral energy distributions to multi-wavelength surface photometry. The resulting $M/L$ to color relations (MLCRs) are shallower than those observed in spiral galaxies. Further analysis across four metallicity bins reveals a steepening of the MLCR with increasing oxygen abundance, potentially attributed to increased line blanketing at higher metallicity. These MLCRs provide a valuable tool for estimating stellar masses in dIrr galaxies where other methods are unavailable.

title: A simulations approach for meta-analysis of genetic association studies based on additive genetic model
Abstract: Genetic association studies are becoming increasingly important in medical research, particularly in pharmacogenomics for personalized medicine. Meta-analysis of these studies is often employed to assess phenotypic differences between genotype groups. While analyzing summary statistics is valid for dominant or recessive genetic models, it leads to biased results for additive models. This paper demonstrates this bias through simulations and proposes an alternative strategy based on simulating data for individual studies. This approach proves to be superior to the strategy based on summary statistics, particularly for the additive genetic model.

title: A green program lifecycle supporting energy-efficient applications
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is expected to significantly increase global emissions due to the proliferation of internet-connected devices. While software systems do not directly consume energy, they heavily influence hardware energy consumption. Developers should consider the long-term energy implications of their systems and adopt green development lifecycles. This paper emphasizes the importance of energy-efficient software development and the need for methodologies and tools to identify and analyze energy hotspots early in the design process. The current lack of such tools and the limited awareness of developers regarding energy efficiency are discussed. The importance of optimizing energy consumption in smartphones and smart objects is also highlighted, emphasizing its impact on battery life and user experience.

title: Hardware for Machine Learning: Challenges and Opportunities
Abstract: Machine learning plays a crucial role in extracting valuable information from vast amounts of sensor data. While cloud-based processing is often preferred, local embedded processing near the sensor is often more desirable due to privacy, latency, and bandwidth constraints. However, embedded systems face stringent limitations on energy consumption, cost, and performance. This paper addresses these challenges through various hardware design approaches, including architecture optimization, hardware-friendly algorithms, mixed-signal circuits, and advanced technologies like memory and sensors. The challenges of data transformation into higher dimensional spaces and the associated energy consumption are discussed.

title: Partial $\ell_1$ optimization in random linear systems -- finite dimensions
Abstract: This paper complements previous research on the behavior of the partial $\\ell_1$ heuristic for solving underdetermined systems of linear equations. The paper focuses on finite dimensional scenarios, providing explicit performance characterizations for any given collection of systems and parameter dimensions. Two variants of the partial $\\ell_1$ are analyzed: the exact partial $\\ell_1$ and the hidden partial $\\ell_1$. The results build upon earlier research that established the phase-transition phenomenon and large deviations principles for the partial $\\ell_1$ in the asymptotic regime.

title: Understanding Error Correction and its Role as Part of the Communication Channel in Environments composed of Self-Integrating Systems
Abstract: The increasing complexity of technical systems necessitates advanced self-healing capabilities to enable system owners to provide partial or inconsistent updates. The paper discusses an extended scope of error correction, emphasizing its role as an integrated element of bidirectional communication channels in self-integrating, autonomic communication scenarios. This approach is particularly relevant in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial Internet, where unexpected device combinations may be assembled to create novel functionalities.

title: Survey of Promising Technologies for 5G Networks
Abstract: The 5G network, an enhancement of cellular networks, aims to provide ultra-high-speed connectivity. SDN provides a promising architecture that decouples control and data planes, supporting programmability and adaptability in dynamic network environments. The integration of cloud computing and SDN through IoT facilitates interaction between the physical and human worlds, enhancing the productivity of evolving technologies. This study presents a comprehensive overview of these enabling technologies for next-generation mobile systems and networks.

title: Performance analysis of smart digital signage system based on software-defined IoT and invisible image sensor communication
Abstract: The future of the interactive world hinges on the Internet of Things (IoT), where everything is interconnected and interactive. Software-defined networking (SDN), a new paradigm in networking, enables the creation of an IoT by controlling physical devices, data transmission, and data acquisition. Digital signage, a promising technology in this era of interconnectivity, connects users to the IoT network through device-to-device communication. This paper presents a novel prototype of a smart digital signage system based on software-defined IoT (SD-IoT) and invisible image sensor communication technology. The proposed SDN scheme offers flexibility and compatibility for an IoT network-based smart digital signage system, utilizing unused resources such as images and videos. Invisible communication enhances user engagement, enabling interactivity between the user and digital signage through smartphone camera communication. This approach has potential real-world applications due to the adaptability of SDN and the ubiquitous availability of displays and smartphones. A performance analysis compares the SD-IoT network to an internet protocol-based network, demonstrating the advantages of SD-IoT in terms of dynamic link allocation for user access. |||

title: Scaling limit of a self-avoiding walk interacting with spatial random permutations
Abstract: Nearest neighbor spatial random permutations are studied on the d-dimensional integer lattice. The energy of the system is proportional to the sum of cycle lengths, which can be interpreted as an ensemble of edge-weighted, mutually self-avoiding loops. The constant of proportionality, α, serves as the order parameter of the model. The authors demonstrate that even in a parameter regime where a single self-avoiding loop is known to be weakly space-filling, long cycles in spatial random permutations are still exponentially unlikely. They also embed a self-avoiding walk into a background of spatial random permutations, conditioned on it covering a macroscopic distance. For large values of α, where long cycles are improbable, the walk collapses to a straight line in the scaling limit, and bounds are provided on the fluctuations. To prove these results, the authors introduce the concepts of spatial strong Markov property and iterative sampling for spatial random permutations, which are of independent interest. They use these concepts to demonstrate exponential decay of correlations for large values of α in great generality.

title: Learning Motion Patterns in Videos
Abstract: The problem of detecting object motion, independent of camera motion, remains a challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach based on learning motion patterns from videos. The core of the approach is a fully convolutional network trained entirely on synthetic video sequences with ground-truth optical flow and motion segmentation. The encoder-decoder architecture learns a coarse representation of optical flow features and iteratively refines it to produce high-resolution motion labels. The labeling is further improved with an objectness map and a conditional random field, accounting for errors in optical flow and focusing on moving objects rather than static backgrounds. The output label for each pixel indicates whether it has undergone independent motion. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this learning framework in moving object segmentation, outperforming the top method on the DAVIS benchmark dataset by 5.6%. It also achieves state-of-the-art results on the Berkeley motion segmentation database.

title: Authentication Protocols for Internet of Things: A Comprehensive Survey
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of authentication protocols for the Internet of Things (IoT), examining over forty protocols developed for or applied in various IoT environments: machine-to-machine communications (M2M), Internet of Vehicles (IoV), Internet of Energy (IoE), and Internet of Sensors (IoS). The survey begins by reviewing existing literature on different aspects of IoT. It then analyzes threat models, countermeasures, and formal security verification techniques used in IoT authentication protocols. Furthermore, the paper provides a taxonomy and comparison of these protocols in five terms: network model, goals, main processes, computational complexity, and communication overhead. Based on the survey, the authors identify open issues and suggest future research directions.

title: Finite Blocklength Analysis of Energy Harvesting Channels
Abstract: The paper investigates the capacity of Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) and Discrete Memoryless Channels (DMC) in the finite blocklength regime when the transmitter harvests energy from the environment. This model can represent wireless sensor networks and the Internet of Things. A unifying framework is presented that applies to any energy harvesting channel, assuming an infinite energy buffer. Achievability and converse bounds on channel capacity are derived in the finite blocklength regime. Moderate deviation asymptotic bounds are also provided.

title: On the dark matter as a geometric effect in $f(\mathcal{R})$ gravity
Abstract: The paper examines the discrepancy between the observed rotational velocity curves of particles orbiting galactic centers and the expected curves, often attributed to dark matter. It specifically focuses on the $f(\mathcal{R})$ gravity model, where dark matter is proposed as a geometric effect. While a previous study claimed a form of $f(\mathcal{R})$ to explain dark matter, the authors demonstrate that this form is incorrect. Their calculations reveal a different form of $f(\mathcal{R})$ with a negative correction. They also demonstrate that an analytic solution for $f(\mathcal{R})$ cannot be obtained for all tangential velocity values, including observed values, if the radial component of the metric describing dark matter regions is not constant. Consequently, numerical solutions are required to develop an approximate model for dark matter in $f(\mathcal{R})$ gravity.

title: Random linear systems with sparse solutions -- asymptotics and large deviations
Abstract: This paper revisits the problem of solving underdetermined linear systems with sparse solutions using the ℓ1 optimization heuristic. It presents a collection of fundamental results related to the performance analysis of this heuristic in a statistical setting. The authors start by recalling classical phase transition results derived in previous work, characterizing the breaking points. They then complement these results by analyzing the behavior around these breaking points, focusing on large deviation properties. After providing a conceptual solution, they delve into a mathematically rigorous analysis, aiming for explicit solutions similar to those previously obtained. Surprisingly, the final large deviation ℓ1 characterizations are as elegant as the corresponding phase transition ones. The authors also present a corresponding set of large deviation results obtained through a high-dimensional geometry approach and demonstrate that the two approaches yield matching characterizations, as expected.

title: D-LITe: Building Internet of Things Choreographies
Abstract: The paper proposes a complete architecture for designing Internet of Things (IoT) applications, addressing the heterogeneity of object hardware, networks, and protocols. It introduces D-LITe, a solution that hides the complexity of low-level technologies by abstracting the hardware and focusing on object features. D-LITe provides universal access to object internal processing and computational power, utilizing a small virtual machine embedded in each object. Object features are discovered and programmed through the network, eliminating the need for physical access. The architecture incorporates the SALT language, which describes the logical behavior required to integrate user objects into an IoT application, leveraging REST communication. The paper argues that assembling these logical units into a global composition results in a service choreography, where each object contributes to a specific task, providing benefits over traditional service-based approaches.

title: A time-step approximation scheme for a viscous version of the Vlasov equation

By recognizing that the Vlasov equation can be viewed as an extension of Aubry-Mather theory in the space of probability measures (representing particle distributions), the authors show that Gomes and Valdinoci's theorem applies to the viscous Vlasov equation. This result recovers a theorem by Feng and Nguyen, but through a simpler and more elementary proof.

title: Structure in the Disk of epsilon Aurigae: Analysis of the ARCES and TripleSpec data obtained during the 2010 eclipse
Abstract: The paper explores the spectroscopic facets of the mass transfer stream during third contact in the epsilon Aurigae eclipse, utilizing high-resolution spectra obtained from the ARCES and TripleSpec instruments at Apache Point Observatory. The analysis of 116 epochs of data between 2009 and 2012, focused on high-eccentricity disk lines, reveals evidence of high-speed material associated with the mass transfer stream persisting between third and fourth contact. The interaction between the disk and stream is visualized using SHAPE software, while CLOUDY software is used to estimate the source of the enhanced He I 10830A absorption as a region with a density of 10/cm3 and a temperature of 20,000 K, consistent with a mid B type central star. The results support Van Rensbergen binary star evolutionary models for a 9+8 solar mass initial binary, evolving into a 2.3 and 14.11 solar mass end product after 35 Myr. The paper suggests that continued monitoring during the next eclipse will contribute to resolving remaining questions about this binary system.

title: Imposing higher-level Structure in Polyphonic Music Generation using Convolutional Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Constraints
Abstract: The paper introduces a method for incorporating higher-level structure into generated polyphonic music, combining a Convolutional Restricted Boltzmann Machine (C-RBM) as a generative model with gradient descent constraint optimization. This approach allows for the use of a "template" piece to extract structural properties and transfer them as constraints to the newly generated material. Simulated annealing is employed during the sampling process to avoid local optima and find solutions that satisfy the constraints while maintaining stability with respect to the C-RBM. Results demonstrate that this method enables control over higher-level self-similarity structure, meter, and tonal properties of the generated music, while preserving its local musical coherence.

title: Lightweight compression with encryption based on Asymmetric Numeral Systems
Abstract: Data compression and encryption are crucial for secure data storage and transmission, particularly for resource-constrained devices like sensors and implants. This paper examines Asymmetric Numeral Systems (ANS), an innovative entropy coding approach that offers compression comparable to arithmetic coding with the speed of Huffman coding, making it a viable alternative. ANS can be used for encryption by perturbing its coding tables, adding minimal overhead. The paper analyzes the security level of this approach and discusses its potential applications, including reducing cipher rounds on ANS-compressed data or eliminating the need for an additional encryption layer.

title: The Ethereum Scratch Off Puzzle

This paper applies provable security techniques to the algorithm description of CASPER, the new proof-of-stake consensus protocol being implemented in Ethereum. The analysis concludes that CASPER satisfies almost all security definitions, with room for improvement in one specific area.

title: Spatial Pyramid Convolutional Neural Network for Social Event Detection in Static Image

This configuration enhances the accuracy of the classifier by observing image details more accurately. The paper evaluates the proposed method using the USED dataset, consisting of EiMM and SED image sets. The results demonstrate a 15% and 2% improvement in average accuracy over the baseline method, respectively.

title: Are we close to put the anomalous perihelion precessions from Verlinde's emergent gravity to the test?
Abstract: The paper investigates the implications of Verlinde's emergent gravity scenario on planetary orbital motion, specifically focusing on an anomalous pericenter precession predicted by Liu and Prokopec. It shows that the magnitude of this precession for the inner planets of the Solar System would be comparable to the current accuracy in constraining deviations from their standard perihelion precessions, based on long data records spanning a century. Mars appears to be the most suitable target for testing the Verlinde-type precession, as recent planetary ephemerides indicate that non-standard precessions exceeding 0.02-0.11 milliarcseconds per century are not admissible, while the predicted precession is 0.09 milliarcseconds per century. Other astronomical and astrophysical scenarios, such as Earth's LAGEOS II satellite, the double pulsar system PSR J0737-3039A/B, and the S-stars orbiting Sgr A*, are deemed not viable due to the excessively small predicted effects.

title: Angular Momentum of Dwarf Galaxies
Abstract: The paper presents measurements of baryonic mass (Mb) and specific angular momentum (jb) for 14 rotating dwarf irregular (dIrr) galaxies from the LITTLE THINGS sample, utilizing 21cm kinematic data from the Very Large Array and stellar mass maps from the Spitzer Space Telescope. These measurements extend previous AM measurements by two orders of magnitude in Mb. The dwarf galaxies exhibit systematically higher jb values than expected from the jb~Mb^{2/3} scaling of spiral galaxies, suggesting a deviation from a scale-free galaxy formation scenario. This offset can be explained by decreasing baryon mass fractions (fM = Mb/Mdyn, where Mdyn is the dynamical mass) with decreasing Mb (for Mb < 10^{11} Msun). The paper finds that the sAM of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) alone is approximately 2.5 times higher than that of the stars. The M-j relation of HI is significantly steeper than that of the stars, attributed to the systematic variation of the HI fraction with Mb.

title: COCO-Stuff: Thing and Stuff Classes in Context

While research often focuses on "thing" classes, "stuff" classes play a crucial role in image understanding, providing information about scene type, contextual reasoning for "thing" classes, and physical attributes of the scene. To address this gap, the paper introduces COCO-Stuff, an extension of the COCO 2017 dataset with pixel-wise annotations for 91 stuff classes. The annotation protocol leverages existing "thing" annotations, offering a balance between speed and quality. The paper analyzes the importance of "stuff" and "thing" classes in terms of surface coverage and caption mentions, explores spatial relations between them, and evaluates the performance of a modern semantic segmentation method on both classes.

title: Cohen-Macaulay properties under the amalgamated construction
Abstract: The paper studies the Cohen-Macaulay property, a generalization of the usual Cohen-Macaulay property in the Noetherian case, for amalgamated rings. Given commutative rings with unity, A and B, a ring homomorphism f: A → B, and an ideal J of B, the amalgamation of A with B along J with respect to f is defined as the subring A ⋈^f J = {(a, f(a) + j) | a ∈ A and j ∈ J} of A × B. The authors investigate the Cohen-Macaulay property of this amalgamation ring, obtaining a generalization of the result that Nagata's idealization is Cohen-Macaulay.

title: Sterile neutrino searches at future $e^-e^+$, $pp$, and $e^-p$ colliders
Abstract: Sterile neutrinos, proposed as extensions to the Standard Model, are a potential explanation for the observed neutrino masses. The paper also discusses novel search channels and presents preliminary estimates of sensitivity for active-sterile mixings and heavy neutrino masses. It compares the performance of different collider types and highlights their complementarity.

title: Why Our Universe is Comprehensible

title: A microprocessor based on a two-dimensional semiconductor

title: A precise measure of avian magnetoreception based on quantum metrology
Abstract: The radical pair (RP) mechanism, a quantum model explaining the dynamics of spatially separated electron pairs, is a leading hypothesis for avian magnetoreception.  Unlike traditional approaches that measure sensitivity based on singlet yield (ΦS), this study introduces quantum Fisher information (QFI) as a precise measure of sensitivity in the avian compass. QFI represents the maximum information about the magnetic field's direction obtainable from the RP state.  The alignment of these results with experimental observations highlights QFI's crucial role in avian magnetoreception.  This framework, rooted in quantum metrology, enables the evaluation of potential measurement schemes for avian magnetoreception, revealing a direct link between singlet yield and specific measurement strategies.  By integrating quantum metrology, this research offers novel insights into avian magnetoreception, fostering a deeper connection between quantum information and biological functions.

title: Massive Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access for Cellular IoT: Potentials and Limitations
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) promises ubiquitous connectivity, becoming a dominant technological trend. This requires a significant departure from existing protocols, primarily designed for human-to-human (H2H) interactions. This article examines recent 3GPP solutions for enabling massive cellular IoT, focusing on random access strategies for M2M communications.  The analysis demonstrates the need for cellular networks to evolve to accommodate new device connectivity and communication patterns.  The article then proposes a massive non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique as a promising solution for supporting vast numbers of IoT devices within cellular networks.  The challenges and future research directions for implementing NOMA are also discussed.

title: Optimizing Governed Blockchains for Financial Process Authentications
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of governed blockchains, owned and controlled by organizations, that neither create cryptocurrencies nor rely on incentives for solving cryptographic puzzles.  These frameworks can leverage various technologies for their components, including cryptographic puzzles.  Owners of governed blockchains acquire puzzle solvers as controllable resources and employ a mathematical model to determine optimal parameters for the cryptographic puzzle mechanism and other blockchain components.  The paper illustrates this approach with a use case involving blockchains recording hashes of financial transaction data to enhance the trustworthiness of both transactions and audits.  Specifically, for Proof of Work as a cryptographic puzzle, a detailed mathematical model is developed to derive MINLP optimization problems for computing optimal Proof of Work configuration parameters.  These parameters balance conflicting aspects like availability, resiliency, security, and cost.  The paper demonstrates the utility of this "mining calculus" by solving instances of the optimization problem.  This experimental validation is further strengthened by statistical analysis confirming the validity of the random variables used in the mathematical model.  The authors hope this research facilitates the creation of domain-specific blockchains for applications such as trustworthy information in IoT systems and tailored enhancements of legacy financial services.

title: Multilingual Multiword Expressions
Abstract: This project aims to develop a semi-supervised approach for identifying Multiword Expressions (MWEs) in a multilingual context encompassing English and major Indian languages. MWEs are groups of words conveying a conventional or regional meaning, which, when literally translated, lose their inherent meaning. To automatically extract MWEs from a corpus, an extraction pipeline combining rule-based and statistical techniques was designed.  Due to the diverse nature of MWEs, different methods are employed to detect different types.  After initial POS tagging, the system applies regular expression filters to narrow the search space to specific patterns (e.g., reduplication, partial reduplication, compound nouns, compound verbs, conjunct verbs).  Matching word sequences undergo linguistic tests, including verb filtering, named entity filtering, and hyphenation filtering, to eliminate false positives. Candidate MWEs are then assessed for semantic relationships using Wordnet.  Wordnet is also utilized as a lexical database and lemmatisation tool for detecting partial reduplication.  Complex predicates are identified by analyzing constituent word features, while statistical methods are used to detect collocations. Finally, lexicographers manually examine the list of automatically extracted candidates to verify their validity as true MWEs and incorporate them into a multiword dictionary.

title: A General Age-Specific Mortality Model with An Example Indexed by Child or Child/Adult Mortality
Abstract: The majority of African countries and almost one-third of all countries rely on mortality models to infer complete age schedules of mortality, essential for population estimates, projections, and numerous tasks in demography and epidemiology. Models relating child mortality to mortality at other ages are particularly important because all countries have measures of child mortality.  This study aims to achieve three objectives: 1) Design a general model for age-specific mortality that provides a standard framework for relating covariates to mortality, 2) Calibrate the model using the relationship between child or child/adult mortality and mortality at other ages, and 3) Validate the calibrated model and compare its performance to existing models.  A general, parametrizable component model of mortality, based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD-Comp), is designed and calibrated to the relationship between child or child/adult mortality and mortality at other ages in the Human Mortality Database.  Cross-validation is employed for model validation, and the predictive performance is compared to the Log-Quad model, designed for the same purpose.  Prediction and cross-validation tests demonstrate that the child mortality-calibrated SVD-Comp model accurately represents observed mortality schedules in the Human Mortality Database, is robust to the selection of calibration schedules, and outperforms the Log-Quad model.  This research concludes that the child mortality-calibrated SVD-Comp model is a valuable tool for situations where child mortality data is available, but mortality at other ages is unknown.  Combined with previous work on an HIV prevalence-calibrated version of SVD-Comp, this research suggests that this approach is highly general and applicable for developing a wide range of additional useful models.

title: Towards Hierarchical Mobile Edge Computing: An Auction-Based Profit Maximization Approach

However, optimizing resource allocation in this three-tier network remains crucial for efficient delivery of computing, storage, and communication resources to users. This paper proposes a new hierarchical model by introducing the concept of field, shallow, and deep cloudlets, where the cloudlet tier itself is structured into three hierarchical levels based on the principle of LTE-Advanced backhaul networks.  This model utilizes a two-time scale approach, where computing resources are allocated through an auction-based profit maximization mechanism, followed by the allocation of communication resources to fulfill user QoS requirements.

title: Vocabulary and the Brain: Evidence from Neuroimaging Studies
Abstract: Research findings presented in this paper reveal a strong correlation between specific brain regions and vocabulary, including vocabulary acquisition. Semantic associations for vocabulary seem to be located near brain areas that vary according to the type of vocabulary, e.g., ventral temporal regions are important for words related to visually perceptible objects.  Semantic processing is believed to be closely associated with the angular gyrus (ANG). Phonological ability is strongly linked to the anterior surfaces of the supramarginal gyrus (SMG).  Pathways through the posterior SMG are thought to connect the anterior SMG and the ANG.  In vocabulary tasks, mediotemporal structures may be associated with long-term memory processing, with the left hippocampus and parahippocampal regions linked to long-term and working memory, respectively.  Precentral structures are associated with phonological retrieval.  Furthermore, numerous other brain regions are of interest in vocabulary tasks, particularly those involved in visual and auditory processing.  The study also highlights potential differences in brain anatomy attributed to the vocabulary demands of different languages.

title: Anticipating Moves to Prevent Botnet Generated DDoS Flooding Attacks
Abstract: Volumetric Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remain a persistent threat on the Internet, flooding targeted servers or network links with fake network traffic.  Despite numerous efforts to detect and mitigate DDoS attacks, attackers continually evolve their methods, circumventing existing countermeasures.  The rise of the Internet of Things and flexible communication technologies has led to a significant increase in the number of infected devices, further escalating the threat.  Leveraging device-to-device short-range wireless communication and other technologies, infected devices can coordinate sophisticated botnets, amplifying the intensity of DDoS attacks.  The new generation of botnets is even harder to detect due to their adaptive and dynamic behavior, often originating from mobile portable devices.  Furthermore, the geographically distributed nature of botnets results in a dramatic increase in DDoS traffic volume.  To address these evolving threats and the increasing volume of DDoS traffic, novel and intelligent-driven approaches are essential.  This paper advocates for proactive strategies to anticipate DDoS attack trends in their early stages.  The paper provides an overview of approaches for anticipating DDoS attack trends generated by botnets, discussing the advantages and open issues of each approach.

title: Proposal of Real Time Predictive Maintenance Platform with 3D Printer for Business Vehicles
Abstract: This paper proposes a maintenance platform for business vehicles that leverages IoT data to detect failure signs on the move, automatically orders repair parts using 3D printers, and delivers them to the designated location.  Recent advancements in IoT and 3D printer technologies have spurred increased application in manufacturing and maintenance sectors.  Specifically, in the air flight industry, various sensing data is collected during flight using IoT technologies, and 3D printers are employed for part creation.  The emergence of IoT platforms has facilitated the development and operation of IoT applications.  However, existing IoT platforms primarily focus on visualizing "thing" statuses through batch processing of collected sensing data, failing to adequately address the crucial factors of real-time analysis, automatic repair part ordering, and minimizing part stock cost. This paper specifically targets the maintenance of business vehicles such as airplanes or high-speed buses.  The proposed maintenance platform incorporates real-time analysis, automatic ordering of repair parts, and minimal part stock costs.  The platform collects data through a closed VPN, analyzes stream data using the online machine learning framework Jubatus to predict failures in real-time, coordinates with ERP or SCM systems via in-memory databases to order repair parts, and distributes repair part data to 3D printers for part creation near the destination.

title: Mean-field limits for large-scale random-access networks
Abstract: This paper establishes mean-field limits for large-scale random-access networks with buffer dynamics and arbitrary interference graphs. While saturated-buffer scenarios have been widely studied and provide useful throughput estimates for persistent sessions, they fail to capture buffer content fluctuations over time and offer no insight into delay performance for flows with intermittent packet arrivals.  To address this limitation, the paper explores random-access networks with buffer dynamics, where flows with empty buffers refrain from competing for the medium.  The presence of empty buffers creates a complex dynamic interaction between activity states and buffer contents, significantly complicating performance analysis. Therefore, the study focuses on a many-sources regime where the total number of nodes grows large, offering mathematical tractability and relevance to the densification of wireless networks as the Internet of Things emerges.  Exploiting time scale separation properties, the paper proves that the appropriately scaled buffer occupancy process converges to the solution of a deterministic initial-value problem and establishes the existence and uniqueness of the associated fixed point.  This approach simplifies the performance analysis of networks with a vast number of nodes to a low-dimensional fixed-point calculation.  For the case of a complete interference graph, the paper demonstrates asymptotic stability, provides a simple closed-form expression for the fixed point, and proves the interchangeability of the mean-field and steady-state limits.  This analysis yields asymptotically exact approximations for key performance metrics, including the stationary buffer content and packet delay distributions.  The methodological framework developed in this study readily extends to various model refinements, as illustrated by several examples.

title: When Students Choose to Use Event-B in their Software Engineering Projects
Abstract: Software engineering students often learn formal methods as part of their curriculum, but rarely apply these methods outside of dedicated modules.  In particular, students often build a significant application or system as part of their final project, where they are expected to demonstrate the application of previously learned concepts.  However, our experience indicates that the majority of students do not utilize formal methods in their project work.  This paper reports on feedback from the minority of students who did choose to employ formal methods in their projects, providing examples of instances where formal methods were beneficial and instances where they presented challenges.

title: Jolie Good Buildings: Internet of things for smart building infrastructure supporting concurrent apps utilizing distributed microservices
Abstract: A significant percentage of buildings, both residential and specialized, are expected to become increasingly "smart" in the future, driven by the substantial benefits offered by new technologies in terms of energy saving, safety, flexibility, and comfort.  However, no clear dominant standard frameworks currently exist at the hardware, software, or platform levels. This paper presents a prototype platform supporting multiple concurrent applications for smart buildings, utilizing an advanced sensor network and a distributed microservices architecture, centrally featuring the Jolie language. The architecture and benefits of the system are discussed, along with a prototype consisting of multiple nodes and a user interface deployed in a real-world academic building environment.  The results illustrate the promising nature of this approach, highlighting avenues for future work aimed at expanding its applicability to wider and larger-scale environments.

title: Multi-hop Communication in the Uplink for LPWANs
Abstract: Low-Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) have emerged as a promising communication technology for supporting Internet of Things (IoT) services, offering low power consumption, wide coverage range, low cost, and scalability.  However, most LPWAN solutions, such as SIGFOX or LoRaWAN, rely on star topology networks, where stations (STAs) transmit data directly to the gateway (GW), often leading to rapid battery depletion in STAs located far from the GW.  This paper analyzes the impact of multi-hop communication in the uplink on LPWANs energy consumption, allowing STAs to transmit data packets at lower power levels and higher data rates to closer parent STAs, thereby reducing their energy consumption.  To this end, the paper introduces the Distance-Ring Exponential Stations Generator (DRESG) framework, designed to evaluate the performance of the optimal-hop routing model, which establishes optimal routing connections in terms of energy efficiency, aiming to balance consumption among all STAs in the network.  Results demonstrate that enabling multi-hop connections significantly extends network lifetimes, reducing the bottleneck consumption in LPWANs with up to thousands of STAs. These findings suggest that multi-hop communication in the uplink is a promising routing alternative for extending the lifetime of LPWAN deployments.

title: On the Feasibility of Attribute-Based Encryption on Internet of Things Devices

This article explores the feasibility of implementing ABE on well-known IoT platforms, namely, Intel Galileo Gen 2, Intel Edison, Raspberry Pi 1 Model B, and Raspberry Pi Zero.  The study concludes that adopting ABE in the IoT is indeed feasible.

title: Heat Production of Non-Interacting Fermions Subjected to Electric Fields
Abstract: Electric resistance in conducting media is directly related to heat (or entropy) production in the presence of electric fields. This paper mathematically defines and analyzes heat production in free fermions within external potentials, utilizing Araki's relative entropy for states.  Specifically, the study investigates heat production in the non-autonomous C*-dynamical system obtained from the fermionic second quantization of a discrete Schrödinger operator with a bounded static potential in the presence of a time- and space-dependent electric field.  This represents a preliminary step towards a mathematical description of fermion transport properties based on thermal considerations.  This research program will be carried out in multiple papers. The regime of small and slowly varying electric fields is of particular importance in this context and is studied in this paper.  Tree-decay bounds for the n-point, n ∈ 2N, correlations of the many-fermion system are used to analyze this regime.  The paper verifies the first law of thermodynamics for the system under consideration, demonstrating that, for systems doing no work, the heat produced by the electromagnetic field is equivalent to the increase in internal energy resulting from the modification of the (infinite volume) state of the fermion system.  The identification of heat production with an energy increment is technically advantageous. The study initially focuses on non-interacting (or free) fermions, but the approach will be extended to weakly interacting fermions in future work.

title: Categories in control: applied PROPs
Abstract: Control theory utilizes "signal-flow diagrams" to depict processes involving real-valued functions of time, subject to operations such as addition, scalar multiplication, differentiation, integration, duplication, and deletion.  These diagrams can be viewed as string diagrams for the PROP FinRel_k, the strict version of the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces over the field of rational functions k = R(s) and linear relations, where the variable s acts as differentiation, and the monoidal structure is direct sum rather than the typical tensor product of vector spaces.  Control processes are also characterized by controllability and observability—whether the input can influence the process to any state and whether any state can be determined from subsequent outputs.  This paper provides a presentation of FinRel_k for any field k in terms of generators of the free PROP of signal-flow diagrams, along with equations that define the structure of FinRel_k. The "cap" and "cup" generators, absent when morphisms are linear maps, enable the modeling of feedback.  The relations indicate, among other things, that the 1-dimensional vector space k has two special commutative dagger-Frobenius structures, where the multiplication and unit of one structure and the comultiplication and counit of the other combine to form a bimonoid.  This type of structure, with tensor product replacing direct sum, is familiar from the "ZX-calculus" obeyed by a finite-dimensional Hilbert space with two mutually unbiased bases.  To address controllability and observability, the paper constructs the PROP Stateful_k and relates it back to the PROP of signal-flow diagrams.  This provides a graphical means of expressing controllability and observability for linear time-invariant processes.

title: Fast and Energy-Efficient CNN Inference on IoT Devices
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) exhibit remarkable performance in various machine learning tasks. title: An approximation result for a class of stochastic heat equations with colored noise
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that a broad class of stochastic heat equations can be approximated by systems of interacting stochastic differential equations.  As a consequence, the paper proves various comparison principles, extending earlier results. title: Throughput Efficient Large M2M Networks through Incremental Redundancy Combining
Abstract: This paper investigates the performance of incremental redundancy combining as a novel cooperative relaying protocol for large-scale Machine-to-Machine (M2M) networks with opportunistic relaying.  The nodes in the large M2M network are modeled using a Poisson Point Process, experience Rayleigh fading, and utilize slotted ALOHA as the Medium Access Control (MAC) protocol.  The progress rate density (PRD) of the M2M network is employed to quantify the performance of the proposed relaying protocol and compare it to conventional multihop relaying without cooperation.  The study shows that incremental redundancy combining in a large M2M network provides substantial throughput improvements over conventional relaying without cooperation across practical values of network parameters.

title: SC-DCNN: Highly-Scalable Deep Convolutional Neural Network using Stochastic Computing
Abstract: The recent advancement of the Internet of Things (IoT) has made implementing deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) on embedded/portable systems highly attractive.  Currently, executing software-based DCNNs requires high-performance server clusters, limiting their widespread deployment on mobile devices.  To address this challenge, significant research efforts have been dedicated to developing highly parallel and specialized DCNN hardware utilizing GPGPUs, FPGAs, and ASICs.  Stochastic Computing (SC), which represents numbers within [-1, 1] using bit-streams by counting the number of ones in the stream, holds considerable potential for implementing DCNNs with high scalability and an ultra-low hardware footprint.  SC allows multiplications and additions to be calculated using AND gates and multiplexers, leading to significant reductions in power/energy consumption and hardware footprint compared to conventional binary arithmetic implementations.  These substantial savings in power (energy) and hardware resources create ample design space for enhancing scalability and robustness in hardware DCNNs.  This paper presents the first comprehensive design and optimization framework for SC-based DCNNs (SC-DCNNs).  The paper first presents optimal designs for function blocks performing basic operations, including inner product, pooling, and activation functions.  It then proposes optimal designs for four types of combinations of basic function blocks, named feature extraction blocks, responsible for extracting features from input feature maps.  Additionally, weight storage methods are investigated to reduce area and power/energy consumption for storing weights.  Finally, the entire SC-DCNN implementation is optimized, carefully selecting feature extraction blocks to minimize area and power/energy consumption while maintaining high network accuracy. |||

title: A Socio-geographic Perspective on Human Activities in Social Media
Abstract: Location-based social media platforms provide valuable insights into the social and geographical aspects of human behavior. However, existing studies have primarily examined these aspects in isolation, neglecting the potential interplay between them. This study aims to bridge this gap by investigating the correlation between social connections and users' check-in locations from a socio-geographic perspective. We constructed three distinct types of networks: a people-people network, a location-location network, and a city-city network, using data from the former location-based social media platforms Brightkite and Gowalla in the U.S. These networks were built based on users' check-in locations and their friendship connections. Employing complexity science methods like power-law detection and head/tail breaks classification, we analyzed and visualized the data. Our analysis revealed heterogeneous check-in patterns at both individual and collective levels. We discovered that users' first or most frequent check-in locations effectively represent their spatial information. The constructed networks based on these locations exhibited significant heterogeneity, as indicated by their high ht-index. Importantly, we found a strong correlation between the node degree of the networks and the population at locations (with an R-square value of approximately 0.7) or cities (above 0.9). This correlation suggests a strong relationship between the geographic distribution of social media users and their online social connections.

title: Multiple Access Technologies for cellular M2M Communications: An Overview

We analyze the throughput efficiency of various multiple access techniques in both coordinated and uncoordinated scenarios. Our findings demonstrate that non-orthogonal multiple access outperforms orthogonal multiple access techniques in supporting a larger number of devices, particularly in uncoordinated scenarios. Additionally, we address the challenges and issues associated with implementing different multiple access techniques for M2M applications in cellular networks.

title: Fog Computing: A Taxonomy, Survey and Future Directions

title: Planetesimal collisions as a chondrule forming event
Abstract: Chondritic meteorites contain unique spherical materials known as chondrules – sub-millimeter-sized silicate grains that were once melted at high temperatures within the solar nebula. This study numerically investigates one of the potential chondrule formation processes, planetesimal collisions. Previous studies have shown that impact jetting, resulting from collisions between protoplanets and planetesimals, can generate chondrules with a mass equivalent to 1% of the impactor's mass when the impact velocity exceeds 2.5 km/s. Mineralogical data on chondrules suggests that undifferentiated planetesimals may be more suitable for chondrule-forming collisions than potentially differentiated protoplanets. We conducted simulations of planetesimal-planetesimal collisions using a shock physics code, revealing two key findings: Firstly, planetesimal-planetesimal collisions produce nearly the same amount of chondrules as protoplanet-planetesimal collisions (approximately 1%). Secondly, the amount of chondrule production increases with the impact velocity during collisions between two planetesimals. Our simulations also indicate that chondrule precursors can be ejected from deeper regions within larger targets (planetesimals or protoplanets) compared to smaller impactors (planetesimals). Therefore, the composition of targets plays a crucial role in fully accounting for the mineralogical data of currently sampled chondrules.

title: Multi-criteria IoT Resource Discovery: A Comparative Analysis
Abstract: The growing adoption of real-world objects embedded with sensors and connected globally through the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm fuels the expansion of ubiquitous and context-aware computing applications. The convergence of Cloud Computing and IoT, known as the Cloud of Things, is essential for managing the vast number of sensors and their data. One of the major challenges in the Cloud of Things is the context-aware search and selection of sensors. Typically, sensors need to be searched using two or more conflicting context properties. While existing approaches often employ multi-criteria decision analysis for sensor search and selection, they lack a comprehensive evaluation of the quality of the selection process. This paper analyzes the behavior and selection quality of three multi-objective decision methods: SAW, TOPSIS, and VIKOR, comparing them with Pareto-optimality solutions. The results provide insights into the performance of these algorithms, including their behavior, the number of optimal solutions, and redundancy.

title: The Effects of Relative Importance of User Constraints in Cloud of Things Resource Discovery: A Case Study
Abstract: The number of smart objects connected to the Internet has witnessed exponential growth in recent years, surpassing the number of services and applications available. The integration of Cloud Computing and IoT, known as the Cloud of Things, plays a crucial role in managing connected things, their data, and services. title: IoT Sentinel: Automated Device-Type Identification for Security Enforcement in IoT
Abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has raised significant concerns about the security of IoT devices. Numerous vendors are producing IP-connected devices for home and small office networks that often exhibit flawed security designs and implementations. These devices frequently lack mechanisms for firmware updates or patches, making them vulnerable to security threats. Securing networks where such vulnerable devices are present requires a brownfield approach: implementing necessary protection measures within the network to ensure the coexistence of potentially vulnerable devices without compromising the security of other devices on the same network. This paper presents IOT SENTINEL, a system that automatically identifies the types of devices connected to an IoT network and enforces rules to restrict communication from vulnerable devices, minimizing the impact of their compromise. We demonstrate that IOT SENTINEL effectively identifies device types with minimal performance overhead.

title: A study of conditional spreading sequences
Abstract: Every conditional spreading sequence can be decomposed into two well-behaved components: an unconditional part and a convex block homogeneous part. The latter component is equivalent to its convex block sequences. This decomposition allows us to prove several results concerning the structure of spaces with conditional spreading bases and establish connections to the theory of conditional spreading models. Notably, we demonstrate that the space $C(\\omega^\\omega)$ is universal for all spreading models, encompassing both conditional and unconditional spreading sequences as spreading models. Furthermore, every conditional spreading sequence can be generated as a spreading model by a sequence in a space that is quasi-reflexive of order one.

title: Collective navigation of complex networks: Participatory greedy routing
Abstract: Many networks facilitate the transfer of information or goods, requiring efficient navigation. As networks grow in size, navigating them effectively becomes increasingly challenging. The Internet, for example, faces significant scalability issues in information routing due to its rapid expansion, further accelerated by the rise of the Internet of Things. Efficient navigation in large networks like the Internet can be achieved if nodes or agents actively forward information based on hidden maps underlying these systems. However, in reality, most agents will decline to forward messages, incurring a cost and rendering navigation impossible. Can we design appropriate incentives to encourage participation and achieve global navigability? This paper presents an evolutionary game where agents share the value generated by successful delivery of information or goods. We demonstrate that global navigability can emerge but is also susceptible to complete breakdown. Moreover, we observe the system's tendency to self-organize into local clusters of agents who participate in navigation. This organizational principle can be exploited to promote the emergence of global navigability within the system.

title: Towards Information Privacy for the Internet of Things
Abstract: In an Internet of Things network, multiple sensors transmit information to a fusion center to infer a public hypothesis of interest. However, the same sensor information may be used by the fusion center to make inferences of a private nature that the sensors wish to protect. To model this, we adopt a decentralized hypothesis testing framework with binary public and private hypotheses. Each sensor makes a private observation and utilizes a local sensor decision rule or privacy mapping to independently summarize that observation without relying on information from other sensors. The local decision made by a sensor is then forwarded to the fusion center. Without assuming knowledge of the joint distribution of sensor observations and hypotheses, we employ a nonparametric learning approach to design local privacy mappings. We introduce the concept of an empirical normalized risk, providing a theoretical guarantee for the network to achieve information privacy for the private hypothesis with high probability when the number of training samples is large. We develop iterative optimization algorithms to determine an appropriate privacy threshold and the optimal sensor privacy mappings, demonstrating their convergence. Finally, we extend our approach to handle multiple private hypotheses. Numerical results on both synthetic and real datasets suggest that our proposed approach achieves low error rates for inferring the public hypothesis but high error rates for detecting the private hypothesis.

title: Not Only Horses Wear Blinkers: The Missing Perspectives in IS Research

However, do we consider the perspective from which we observe the phenomenon within our field of view? In the majority of mainstream Information Systems (IS) research, a single perspective dominates: organizations utilize IS and IT as tools for intervention within a context. The behavior of the phenomena is primarily observed from the viewpoint of these organizations. Is this viewpoint the only legitimate perspective for IS research to adopt? Even if it is, are clients' interests best served by IS research that solely adopts this perspective? This paper identifies alternative perspectives, highlighting the negative consequences of limiting our field of view and exploring the opportunities that arise from expanding our perspectives. We propose that these alternatives should be recognized as integral to the IS discipline rather than external to it.

title: Machine to Machine (M2M) Communications in Virtualized Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks

In the proposed framework, a hypervisor enables the virtualization of the physical vehicular network, abstracting and slicing it into multiple virtual networks based on different applications and quality of service (QoS) requirements of vehicles. Furthermore, the process of resource block (RB) selection and random access within each virtual vehicular network is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), maximizing the reward in terms of transmission capacity. The optimal policy for RB selection is derived using a dynamic programming approach. Extensive simulation results with various system parameters demonstrate the performance improvement achieved by the proposed scheme.

title: Anomaly Detection in Bitcoin Network Using Unsupervised Learning Methods
Abstract: Anomaly detection has been a subject of extensive research for a long time. Anomalies represent abnormal or unlikely occurrences. In financial networks, fraudulent activities and illegal actions often exhibit anomalous characteristics. Network members aim to detect anomalies as early as possible to prevent them from harming the network's community and integrity. Numerous Machine Learning techniques have been proposed to address this problem, with some promising results but no clear superior method. This paper focuses on anomaly detection specifically within the Bitcoin transaction network. Our objective is to identify the most suspicious users and transactions. In this context, anomalous behavior serves as a proxy for suspicious activity. To achieve this, we employ three unsupervised learning methods, including k-means clustering, Mahalanobis distance, and Unsupervised Support Vector Machine (SVM), on two graphs generated by the Bitcoin transaction network: one graph represents users as nodes, and the other represents transactions as nodes.

title: LITTLE THINGS in 3D: robust determination of the circular velocity of dwarf irregular galaxies
Abstract: Dwarf Irregular galaxies (dIrrs) are the smallest stellar systems with extended HI discs. Studying the kinematics of these discs provides a powerful tool for estimating the total matter distribution at these very small scales. This work investigates the HI kinematics of 17 galaxies extracted from the `Local Irregulars That Trace Luminosity Extremes, The HI Nearby Galaxy Survey' (LITTLE THINGS). Our approach differs significantly from previous studies in that we directly fit 3D models (two spatial dimensions plus one spectral dimension) using the software $^\\text{3D}$BAROLO, fully exploiting the information contained in the HI datacubes. For each galaxy, we derive the geometric parameters of the HI disc (inclination and position angle), the radial distribution of the surface density, the velocity-dispersion ($\\sigma_v$) profile, and the rotation curve. The circular velocity (V$_{\\text{c}}$), directly tracing the galactic potential, is then obtained by correcting the rotation curve for the asymmetric drift. As an initial application, we show that these dIrrs lie on a baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, consistent with observations at larger scales. The final products of this work are high-quality, ready-to-use kinematic data ($\\textrm{V}_\\textrm{c}$ and $\\sigma_v$) that we make publicly available. This data can be used to conduct dynamical studies and enhance our understanding of these low-mass galaxies.

title: Applying Chatbots to the Internet of Things: Opportunities and Architectural Elements

It offers opportunities for intersecting with other technological trends, further enhancing its intelligence and efficiency. This paper focuses on integrating Intelligent Conversational Software Agents, or Chatbots, with IoT. Literature surveys have explored various applications, features, underlying technologies, and known challenges of IoT. Chatbots are increasingly adopted due to significant advancements in the development of platforms and frameworks. This paper's novelty lies in its specific integration of Chatbots within the IoT scenario. We analyze the shortcomings of existing IoT systems and propose solutions by incorporating chatbots. A general architecture for implementing such a system is presented, along with relevant platforms and frameworks, both commercial and open source, enabling the implementation of such systems. title: Spatio-Temporal Waveform Design for Multi-user Massive MIMO Downlink with 1-bit Receivers
Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) refers to a high-density network of low-cost, low-bitrate terminals and sensors, where energy efficiency is a central feature. Since the power budget of traditional receiver chains is dominated by high-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), there is growing interest in deploying receiver architectures with reduced-bit or even 1-bit ADCs. This paper examines waveform design, optimization, and detection aspects of multi-user massive MIMO downlink where user terminals employ simple 1-bit ADCs with oversampling. To achieve a spectral efficiency exceeding 1 bit/s/Hz per real-dimension, we propose a two-stage precoding approach: a novel quantization precoder followed by maximum-ratio transmission (MRT) or zero-forcing (ZF) type spatial channel precoder, jointly forming the multi-user-multiantenna transmit waveform. The quantization precoder outputs are optimized under appropriate transmitter and receiver filter bandwidth constraints to provide controlled inter-symbol-interference (ISI), enabling unique symbol detection from 1-bit quantized observations using a low-complexity symbol detector in the absence of noise. An additional optimization constraint is imposed in the quantization precoder design to enhance robustness against noise and residual inter-user-interference (IUI). The spatial channel precoder aims to suppress IUI and provide high beamforming gains, ensuring good symbol-error rates (SERs) in the presence of noise and interference. Extensive numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed spatio-temporal precoder based multiantenna waveform design facilitates good multi-user link performance, despite the use of extremely simple 1-bit ADCs in the receivers, making it a potential enabling technology for future low-complexity IoT networks.

title: On the Shape of Things: From holography to elastica
Abstract: This paper delves into the question of how a manifold's shape is determined when immersed in another manifold, subject to the constraint of being an extremum of a specific functional. We consider a family of functionals that depend quadratically on the extrinsic curvatures and projections of the ambient curvatures. These functionals encompass various physical scenarios, ranging from holography to the study of membranes and elastica. We provide a detailed derivation of the equations of motion, known as the shape equations, focusing on the issue of gauge freedom in the choice of normal frame. We apply these equations to the specific case of holographic entanglement entropy in higher curvature three-dimensional gravity, uncovering new classes of entangling curves. Notably, we discuss the case of New Massive Gravity, demonstrating that non-geodesic entangling curves consistently exhibit a smaller on-shell value of the entropy functional. We then apply this formalism to compute the entanglement entropy for dual logarithmic CFTs. However, the correct value for entanglement entropy is obtained using geodesics. We conclude by discussing the significance of these equations in the context of classical elastica and commenting on terms that break gauge invariance.

title: Elastic properties of solid material with various arrangements of spherical voids

We focus on homogeneous solid materials with spherical, empty voids of equal size. The voids are arranged on crystalline lattices (SC, BCC, FCC, and HCP structure) or randomly, allowing for overlap to create connected voids. This approach covers the entire range of void fraction between 0.00 and 0.95, including closed-cell and open-cell structures. For each void arrangement and varying void fractions, the full stiffness tensor is computed. From this, the Young's modulus and Poisson ratios are derived for different orientations. Careful attention is paid to assessing and reducing the numerical uncertainty of the method. This allows for a reliable quantitative comparison of different void structures. Our findings demonstrate that the Young's modulus of FCC in the (1 1 1) plane differs from HCP in the (0 0 0 1) plane, despite their structural similarity. For a given void fraction, SC exhibits the highest and lowest Young's modulus depending on the direction. We observe a switch in elastic behavior for BCC at a critical void fraction, regarding the direction that maximizes Young's modulus. For certain crystalline void arrangements and specific directions, Poisson ratios between 0 and 1 are found, including values exceeding the bounds for isotropic materials. The full stiffness tensor for a range of void arrangements and void fractions is provided in the supplemental material for further investigations.

title: Energy Efficient Barring Factor Enabled Extended Access Barring for IoT Devices in LTE-Advanced

EAB-BB's optimal performance was analyzed in a recent study. However, the Barring Factor Enabled-Extended Access Barring (EAB-BF), an alternative mechanism considered during the standardization process, has not been analyzed. Due to the complexity involved in modeling EAB-BF, its analysis has been challenging. Moreover, the effect of these schemes on key network performance parameters, such as eNodeB energy consumption, has been overlooked. This paper, for the first time, presents a novel analytical model for EAB-BF to obtain its performance metrics. The results obtained from our analysis and simulations closely match. Furthermore, we develop an eNodeB energy consumption model to serve IoT RACH requests. We demonstrate that our analytical and energy consumption models can be combined to determine EAB-BF settings that minimize eNodeB energy consumption while providing optimal Quality of Service (QoS) performance. Our results show that EAB-BF outperforms EAB-BB in terms of optimal performance. Additionally, we find that all three 3GPP-proposed EAB-BF settings considered during standardization provide sub-optimal QoS to devices and result in excessive eNodeB energy consumption, significantly penalizing the network. title: A variational method for spectral functions

We propose a novel formulation of the GEVP in frequency space. Our approach involves applying the model-independent Backus-Gilbert method to a set of Euclidean two-point functions sharing common quantum numbers. A GEVP analysis in frequency space is then applied to a matrix of estimators, enabling us, among other things, to obtain specific linear combinations of the initial set of operators that optimally overlap with different local regions in frequency. We apply this method to lattice data from NRQCD. This approach holds promise for both vacuum physics and finite-temperature problems. |||

title: Disentangling the ISM phases of the dwarf galaxy NGC 4214 using [CII] SOFIA/GREAT observations
Abstract: The [CII] 158 µm fine-structure line is a dominant cooling line in the interstellar medium (ISM) and a crucial tracer of star formation. Recent velocity-resolved studies using Herschel/HIFI and SOFIA/GREAT have shown that the [CII] line can constrain the properties of the ISM phases in star-forming regions. The [CII] line is particularly important as a star formation tracer in low-metallicity environments where CO emission is weak due to the presence of significant amounts of CO-dark gas. NGC 4214, a nearby irregular dwarf galaxy, offers an excellent opportunity to study an actively star-forming ISM at low metallicity. We analyzed the spectrally resolved [CII] line profiles in three distinct regions at different evolutionary stages of NGC 4214, considering ancillary HI and CO data to investigate the origin of the [CII] line. Using SOFIA/GREAT [CII] 158 µm observations, HI data from THINGS, and CO(2-1) data from HERACLES, we decomposed the spectrally resolved [CII] line profiles into components associated with neutral atomic and molecular gas. This decomposition allowed us to infer gas masses traced by [CII] under different ISM conditions. Averaging over all regions, we found that approximately 46% of the [CII] emission is associated with the HI emission. However, we could only assign about 9% of the total [CII] emission to the cold neutral medium (CNM). We discovered that approximately 79% of the total molecular hydrogen mass is not traced by CO emission. On average, the fraction of CO-dark gas dominates the molecular gas mass budget. This fraction appears to depend on the evolutionary stage of the regions: it is highest in the region encompassing a super star cluster in NGC 4214, while it is lower in a more compact, more metal-rich region.

title: The Planckonions
Abstract: We consider a spherically symmetric stellar configuration with a density profile ρ(r) = c^2 / (8πGr^2). This configuration satisfies the Schwarzchild black hole condition 2GM / (c^2R) = 1 for every r = R. We refer to it as "Planckonion". The interesting feature of the Planckonion is its onion-like structure. The central sphere with a radius of the Planck length L_p = √(2ħG/c^3) contains one unit of the Planck mass M_p = √(cħ/2G). Subsequent spherical shells with radial width L_p each contain exactly one unit of M_p. We study this stellar configuration using the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation and demonstrate that the equation is satisfied if pressure P(r) = -ρ(r). From a geometrical perspective, the space component of the metric blows up at every point. The time component of the metric is zero inside the star, but only in the sense of a distribution (generalized function). Planckonions mimic some features of black holes but avoid the appearance of a central singularity due to the violation of null energy conditions.

title: Excited Random Walk in a Markovian Environment
Abstract: One-dimensional excited random walks have been extensively studied for bounded, i.i.d. cookie environments. In this case, many important properties of the walk, including transience or recurrence, positivity or non-positivity of the speed, and the limiting distribution of the walker's position, are all characterized by a single parameter δ, the total expected drift per site. The situation is less understood for the more general case of stationary ergodic environments. If all cookies are positive, the same threshold for transience versus recurrence holds, even if the cookie stacks are unbounded. However, it is unknown whether the threshold for transience versus recurrence extends to the case where cookies may be negative (even for bounded stacks), and there are simple counterexamples to show that the threshold for positivity of the speed does not. It is therefore natural to study the behavior of the model in the case of Markovian environments, which are intermediate between the i.i.d. and stationary ergodic cases. We demonstrate here that many of the important results from the i.i.d. setting, including the thresholds for transience and positivity of the speed, as well as the limiting distribution of the walker's position, extend to a large class of Markovian environments. No assumptions are made about the positivity of the cookies.

title: Multi-level Simulation of Internet of Things on Smart Territories

A two-level simulator is utilized, employing a coarse agent-based, adaptive parallel, and distributed simulation approach to model the general life of simulated entities. When needed, a finer-grained simulator (based on OMNeT++) is triggered on a restricted portion of the simulated area, enabling detailed consideration of wireless communication issues. This use case confirms that ad-hoc wireless networking technologies represent a crucial tool for deploying smart services in decentralized countrysides. Moreover, the performance evaluation confirms the viability of utilizing multi-level simulation for simulating large-scale IoT environments.

title: Emerging Wireless Technologies in the Internet of Things: a Comparative Study

title: Knowledge-infused and Consistent Complex Event Processing over Real-time and Persistent Streams
Abstract: Emerging applications in Internet of Things (IoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) present novel challenges to Big Data platforms for performing online analytics. Ubiquitous sensors from IoT deployments can generate data streams at high velocity, including information from a variety of domains, and accumulate to large volumes on disk. Complex Event Processing (CEP) is recognized as an important real-time computing paradigm for analyzing continuous data streams. However, existing CEP work is largely limited to relational query processing, exposing two distinctive gaps for query specification and execution: (1) infusing the relational query model with higher-level knowledge semantics, and (2) seamless query evaluation across temporal spaces spanning past, present, and future events. These gaps hinder accessible analytics over data streams with properties from different disciplines and restrict the ability to bridge the velocity (real-time) and volume (persistent) dimensions. This article introduces a Knowledge-infused CEP (X-CEP) framework that provides domain-aware knowledge query constructs along with temporal operators that allow end-to-end queries to span across real-time and persistent streams. We translate this query model into efficient query execution over online and offline data streams, proposing several optimizations to mitigate the overheads introduced by evaluating semantic predicates and accessing high-volume historic data streams. The proposed X-CEP query model and execution approaches are implemented in our prototype semantic CEP engine, SCEPter. We validate our query model using domain-aware CEP queries from a real-world Smart Power Grid application and experimentally analyze the benefits of our optimizations for executing these queries, using event streams from a campus-microgrid IoT deployment.

title: Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) for Internet of Things (IoT) Applications: Research Challenges and Future Trends

title: Ordinal Common-sense Inference

title: Conditioning a Brownian loop-soup cluster on a portion of its boundary

This result holds when l is discovered in a natural Markovian way, such as in the exploration procedures defined to construct Conformal Loop Ensembles as outer boundaries of loop-soup clusters. title: A local and operational framework for the foundations of physics

It can encode both classical and quantum (field) theories, implements spacetime locality in a manifest way, and incorporates the complete modern notion of measurement in the quantum case. Its mathematical content can be condensed into a set of axioms similar to those of Atiyah and Segal. This is supplemented by two basic rules for extracting probabilities or expectation values for measurement processes. The framework, called the positive formalism, is derived in three completely different ways. One derivation starts from first principles, one from classical field theory, and one from quantum field theory. The latter derivation arose previously in the program of the general boundary formulation of quantum theory. As in the convex operational framework, the difference between classical and quantum theories essentially arises from certain partially ordered vector spaces being either lattices or anti-lattices. If we add the ad hoc ingredient of imposing anti-lattice structures, the derivation from first principles can be seen as a reconstruction of quantum theory. Among other things, the positive formalism suggests a statistical approach to classical field theories with dynamical metric, provides a common ground for quantum information theory and quantum field theory, introduces a notion of local measurement into quantum field theory, and suggests a new perspective on quantum gravity by removing the incompatibility with general relativistic principles.

title: The Geometry of the Mappings by General Dirichlet Series

title: Tracing where IoT data are collected and aggregated

title: Things Bayes can't do
Abstract: The problem of forecasting conditional probabilities of the next event given the past is considered in a general probabilistic setting. We demonstrate that there are sets C for which such predictors exist, but none of them is a Bayesian predictor with a prior concentrated on C. In other words, there is a predictor with sublinear regret, but every Bayesian predictor must have linear regret. This negative finding contrasts sharply with previous results that establish the opposite for the case when one of the predictors in C achieves asymptotically vanishing error. In such a case, if there is a predictor that achieves asymptotically vanishing error for any measure in C, then there is a Bayesian predictor that also has this property and whose prior is concentrated on (a countable subset of) C.

title: Artificial Intelligence Safety and Cybersecurity: a Timeline of AI Failures

A single failure of a superintelligent system may cause a catastrophic event without a chance for recovery. The goal of cybersecurity is to reduce the number of successful attacks on the system; the goal of AI Safety is to ensure that zero attacks succeed in bypassing the safety mechanisms. Unfortunately, such a level of performance is unachievable. Every security system will eventually fail; there is no such thing as a 100% secure system.

Abstract: The widespread deployment of sensors and smart devices in urban infrastructures is motivating research in the area of the Internet of Things (IoT) to develop new services and improve citizens' quality of life.
