title: Relativistic Zitterbewegung in non-Hermitian photonic waveguide systems
Abstract: Zitterbewegung (ZB) is a phenomenon in relativistic quantum systems where the electron wave packet exhibits a trembling or oscillating behavior during its motion, caused by its interaction or coupling with the negative energy state. Direct observation of ZB in electronic systems is challenging due to the atomic scale wavelength of the electron. Photonic systems offer an alternative paradigm. The concept of pseudo parity-time (pseudo PT) symmetry is exploited to study ZB in non-Hermitian quantum systems implemented as an experimentally feasible optical waveguide array. The non-Hermitian Hamiltonian is realized through evanescent coupling among the waveguides to form a one-dimensional lattice with periodic modulations in gain and loss along the guiding direction. As the modulation frequency is changed, various phenomena are observed, including periodically suppressed ZB trembling, spatial energy localization, and Hermitian-like ZB oscillations. Phase diagrams are calculated indicating the emergence of different types of dynamical behaviors of the relativistic non-Hermitian quantum system in an experimentally justified parameter space. Numerical results and a physical analysis explain the distinct dynamical behaviors revealed by the phase diagrams. These findings provide a deeper understanding of both the relativistic ZB phenomenon and non-Hermitian pseudo-PT systems, with potential applications in controlling/harnessing light propagation in waveguide-based optical systems.

title: Massive spinons in $S=1/2$ spin chains: spinon-pair operator representation
Abstract: Spinons are generic excitations in one-dimensional spin systems, which can be massless or massive. The quantitative description of massive spinons poses a considerable challenge despite various variational approaches. A representation in terms of hopping and Bogoliubov spinon processes, referred to as "spinon-pair" operators and their combination, is shown to be possible. This representation is referred to as the second quantized form. Neglecting terms that change the number of spinons yields variational results. Treating the bilinear and quartic terms by continuous unitary transformations leads to significantly improved results. This provides proof-of-principle that systems displaying massive spinons as elementary excitations can be treated in second quantization based on the spinon-pair representation.

title: Reliable recovery of hierarchically sparse signals for Gaussian and Kronecker product measurements
Abstract: A solution to the problem of recovering a block sparse signal with sparse blocks from linear measurements is proposed and analyzed. Such problems arise naturally in the context of mobile communication, meeting the scalability and low complexity requirements of massive antenna systems and massive machine-type communication. A new variant of the Hard Thresholding Pursuit (HTP) algorithm, referred to as HiHTP, is introduced. Both a proof of convergence and a recovery guarantee for noisy Gaussian measurements are provided, exhibiting improved asymptotic scaling in terms of sampling complexity compared to the standard HTP algorithm. Hierarchically sparse signals and Kronecker product structured measurements arise together in various applications. The efficient reconstruction of hierarchically sparse signals from Kronecker product measurements using the HiHTP algorithm is established. Analytical results connecting the recovery conditions to generalized coherence measures are provided. Again, the recovery results show substantial improvement in the asymptotic sampling complexity scaling over the standard setting. Numerical experiments validate that HiHTP performs significantly better than HTP for hierarchically sparse signals.

title: Topological Weyl phase transition in Mo$_x$W$_{1-x}$Te$_2$
Abstract: Topological phases of matter exhibit phase transitions between distinct topological classes. These phase transitions are exotic, not falling within the traditional Ginzburg-Landau paradigm but instead associated with changes in bulk topological invariants and associated topological surface states. In the case of a Weyl semimetal, this phase transition is particularly unusual as it involves the creation of bulk chiral charges and the nucleation of topological Fermi arcs. A topological phase transition to a Weyl semimetal in MoxW1-xTe2 with changing composition x is imaged. Pump-probe ultrafast angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (pump-probe ARPES) directly observes the nucleation of a topological Fermi arc at xc ∼ 7%, revealing the critical point of a topological Weyl phase transition. For Mo dopings x < xc, no Fermi arc is observed, while for x > xc, the Fermi arc gradually extends as the bulk Weyl points separate. These results demonstrate the creation of magnetic monopoles in momentum space for the first time. This work opens the way to manipulating chiral charge and topological Fermi arcs in Weyl semimetals for transport experiments and device applications.

title: Purely flavor-changing Z' bosons and where they might hide
Abstract: Numerous ultraviolet completions of the Standard Model have extra U(1) gauge symmetries. The associated massive Z' gauge boson can mediate flavor-changing neutral current processes at tree level. A situation is considered where the Z' boson couples solely via flavor-changing interactions to quarks and leptons. In this scenario, the model parameter space is generally well constrained by existing flavor bounds. However, cancellation effects are argued to shelter islands in parameter space from strong flavor constraints, which can be probed by multipurpose collider experiments like ATLAS or CMS, as well as LHCb in upcoming LHC runs. In still allowed regions of parameter space, these scenarios may help to explain the current tension between theory and experiment of (g-2)μ, as well as a small anomaly in τ decays.

title: Functional Hypergraph Uncovers Novel Covariant Structures over Neurodevelopment
Abstract: Brain development during adolescence is characterized by significant changes in brain structure and function, leading to a stable network topology in adulthood. Most prior work has examined data through the lens of brain areas connected to one another in large-scale functional networks. A recently developed hypergraph approach, treating network connections (edges) rather than brain regions as the unit of interest, is applied to describe functional network topology from a fundamentally different perspective. Capitalizing on a sample of 780 youth imaged as part of the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort, this hypergraph representation of resting-state functional MRI data reveals three distinct classes of sub-networks (hyperedges): clusters, bridges, and stars, representing spatially distributed, bipartite, and focal architectures, respectively. Cluster hyperedges strongly resemble the functional modules of the brain, including somatomotor, visual, default mode, and salience systems. In contrast, star hyperedges represent highly localized subnetworks centered on a small set of regions, distributed across the entire cortex. Finally, bridge hyperedges link clusters and stars in a core-periphery organization. Notably, developmental changes within hyperedges are ordered in a similar core-periphery fashion, with the greatest developmental effects occurring in networked hyperedges within the functional core. These results highlight that the network organization of the human brain emerges across multiple scales and evolves substantially through the adolescent period.

title: A First Law of Entanglement Rates from Holography
Abstract: For a perturbation of the state of a Conformal Field Theory (CFT), the response of the entanglement entropy is governed by the "first law" of entanglement entropy, where the change in entanglement entropy is proportional to the change in energy. Whether such a first law holds for other types of perturbations, such as a change to the CFT Lagrangian, remains an open question. Holography is used to study the evolution in time t of entanglement entropy for a CFT driven by a t-linear source for a conserved U(1) current or marginal scalar operator. While the usual first law of entanglement entropy may be violated, a first law for the rates of change of entanglement entropy and energy is found to hold. More generally, it is proven that this first law for rates holds in holography for any asymptotically (d+1)-dimensional Anti-de Sitter metric perturbation whose t dependence first appears at order zd in the Fefferman-Graham expansion about the boundary at z=0. |||

title: Teechan: Payment Channels Using Trusted Execution Environments
Abstract:
Blockchain protocols face inherent limitations in terms of transaction throughput and latency. To address these challenges, off-chain payment channels have been proposed. While these channels offer advantages like low latency and high throughput, deploying them securely on the Bitcoin blockchain has proven difficult due to the need for protocol and ecosystem modifications. 

Teechan, a full-duplex payment channel framework that leverages trusted execution environments, addresses these limitations. Teechan can be deployed securely on the existing Bitcoin blockchain without requiring protocol changes. It offers several key benefits: 

(i) Increased transaction throughput and reduced latency compared to existing solutions.
(ii) Support for unlimited full-duplex payments as long as the channel's credit limit is not exceeded.
(iii) Single-message payment processing in any direction.
(iv) Maximum of two transactions on the blockchain per execution scenario.

The Teechan framework has been built and deployed using Intel SGX on the Bitcoin network. Experimental results indicate that Teechan can achieve a throughput of 2,480 transactions per second on a single channel with sub-millisecond latencies, excluding network delays.

title: Numerical evidence for bound secrecy from two-way post-processing in quantum key distribution
Abstract:
Bound secret information is classical information that possesses secrecy but prevents the extraction of that secrecy. While the existence of bound secrecy has been conjectured, concrete proof is currently lacking. This work presents analytical and numerical evidence supporting its existence. 

Specifically, the study focuses on two-way post-processing protocols within prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution, utilizing the well-known six-state signal states. These protocols currently exist for quantum bit-error rates (Q) below 27.6%. However, for Q values greater than or equal to 1/3, no such protocols are possible due to the data's compatibility with intercept-resend attacks. This leaves open the question of whether successful protocols exist in the interval between 27.6% and 1/3.

Prior research established a necessary condition for two-way post-processing protocols: breaking the symmetric extendability of the shared quantum state between Alice and Bob. Advantage distillation has been shown to break symmetric extendability up to the 27.6% lower bound. This work demonstrates that a generalized form of advantage distillation, involving one round of post-selection by Bob on a block of his data, is sufficient to break symmetric extendability. Furthermore, the study provides evidence that such generalized protocols cannot break symmetric extendability beyond 27.6%. This suggests that 27.6% represents an upper bound on two-way post-processing, indicating the existence of bound secrecy in the interval between 27.6% and 1/3.

title: Higher l^2-Betti numbers of universal quantum groups

title: Pot: Deterministic transactional execution
Abstract:
Pot, a novel system leveraging the concept of preordered transactions, enables deterministic multithreaded execution of programs utilizing Transactional Memory. Preordered transactions eliminate the root cause of nondeterminism in transactional execution by providing the illusion of deterministic serial order, unlike traditional transactions which execute nondeterministically and inconsistently across executions. 

Pot incorporates a new concurrency control protocol that utilizes the serialization order to distinguish between fast and speculative transaction execution modes, effectively mitigating the overhead of enforcing deterministic order. Two prototypes of Pot have been developed: one using Software Transactional Memory (STM) and another using off-the-shelf Hardware Transactional Memory (HTM). To the best of our knowledge, Pot is the first system to enable deterministic execution of programs using off-the-shelf HTM. 

Experimental evaluation demonstrates that Pot achieves deterministic execution of Transactional Memory programs with low overhead, sometimes even surpassing nondeterministic executions and significantly outperforming existing solutions.

title: Compression and reswelling of microgel particles after an osmotic shock

After an initial rapid compression, the particle slowly reswells to approximately its original size. Utilizing both a simple phenomenological model and a more elaborate poroelastic model, the study extracts crucial material properties from a single microfluidic experiment. These properties include the compressive modulus, gel permeability, and diffusivity of the osmolyte within the gel. The approach holds potential for applications in controlled release, chromatography, and responsive materials.

title: Impact of next-to-leading order contributions to CMB lensing
Abstract:
This Letter investigates the impact of lensing corrections on Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) temperature and polarization anisotropies beyond leading order, considering their implications for cosmological parameter estimation from current and future surveys. The analysis highlights the non-negligible influence of post-Born corrections, Large Scale Structure (LSS) effects, and polarization direction changes between emission at the source and detection at the observer, particularly for the determination of polarization spectra. 

These effects must be considered for accurate estimation of cosmological parameters sensitive to or derived from these spectra. The study specifically examines the impact of higher-order lensing on the determination of the tensor-to-scalar ratio (r) and the effective number of relativistic species (N_eff). The findings indicate that neglecting higher-order lensing terms can lead to misinterpretations, potentially attributing these corrections to a primordial tensor-to-scalar ratio of approximately 10⁻³. Furthermore, it results in a shift in the N_eff parameter by nearly two sigma when considering the accuracy level targeted by future S4 surveys.

title: Absolute Non-Violation of a Three-Setting Steering Inequality by Two-Qubit States
Abstract:
Steerability, a nonlocal characteristic of quantum states, lies between entanglement and Bell nonlocality. A quantum state is considered steerable if it violates a chosen steering inequality. While some states violate these inequalities, others can do so only under a global change of basis, meaning the state is transformed by a nonlocal unitary operation. Interestingly, certain states maintain their non-violation of the inequality under any global unitary operation. 

This work explores the effect of global unitary operations on the steering ability of two-qubit quantum states. The study characterizes such states using a necessary and sufficient condition on their spectrum. These states are also characterized in terms of analytical features of the set they belong to. 

The work further establishes a connection between steerability and quantum teleportation, deriving a result related to the optimal violation of the steering inequality. An analytical estimation of the size of non-violating states in terms of purity is also obtained. Notably, this purity-based estimation provides a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of the Bloch parameters of the state. Illustrations using signature classes of quantum states further underscore these observations.

title: The Globalization Theorem for the Curvature Dimension Condition
Abstract:
The Lott-Sturm-Villani Curvature-Dimension condition provides a synthetic framework for characterizing metric-measure spaces with Ricci-curvature bounded from below and dimension bounded from above. This work demonstrates that verifying this condition locally is sufficient. An essentially non-branching metric-measure space (X, d, m), where (supp m, d) forms a length-space and m(X) < ∞, satisfying the local Curvature-Dimension condition CD_loc(K, N) with parameters K ∈ R and N ∈ (1, ∞), also fulfills the global Curvature-Dimension condition CD(K, N). This signifies that the Curvature-Dimension condition enjoys the globalization (or local-to-global) property, resolving a long-standing open question in the theory.

The proof relies on establishing an equivalence between L¹ and L² optimal-transport-based interpolation. The challenge extends beyond technical aspects, with several novel conceptual contributions: 

(i) An explicit change-of-variables formula for densities of Wasserstein geodesics dependent on a second-order temporal derivative of associated Kantorovich potentials.
(ii) A surprising third-order theory for Kantorovich potentials, holding universally on any proper geodesic space.
(iii) A rigidity property of the change-of-variables formula, enabling bootstrapping of a-priori available regularity.

As a consequence, various variants of the Curvature-Dimension condition proposed throughout the years are shown to be equivalent in the above setting, unifying the theory.

title: On the length function of saturations of ideal powers
Abstract:
For an ideal I in a local ring (R, m), this work establishes that the integer-valued function ℓ_R(H⁰_m(R/I^(n+1))) exhibits polynomial behavior for sufficiently large n when either I is a principal ideal or I is generated by a subset of an almost p-standard system of parameters. 

Furthermore, the coefficients of this polynomial can be expressed in terms of the length of certain local cohomology modules and standard multiplicity when the ideal is either principal or generated by a subset of a standard system of parameters in a generalized Cohen-Macaulay ring. 

The study also provides an example of an ideal generated by a subset of a (general) system of parameters where the function ℓ_R(H⁰_m(R/I^(n+1))) does not exhibit polynomial behavior for n >> 0.

title: Disruption of sheetlike structures in Alfvénic turbulence by magnetic reconnection
Abstract:
This work proposes a mechanism by which intense, sheet-like structures formed by dynamically aligning Alfvénic turbulence are disrupted by magnetic reconnection at a scale λ_D, larger than the dissipation scale predicted by models of intermittent, dynamically aligning turbulence. 

The reconnection process unfolds in several stages: 

(i) A linear tearing mode with N magnetic islands grows and saturates.
(ii) The X-points between these islands collapse into secondary current sheets, leading to reconnection until the original structure is destroyed.

This effectively imposes an upper limit on the anisotropy of the structures within the perpendicular plane. Consequently, at scale λ_D, the turbulent dynamics change: 

(i) At scales larger than λ_D, the turbulence exhibits scale-dependent dynamic alignment and a spectral index approximately equal to -3/2.
(ii) At scales smaller than λ_D, turbulent structures undergo a succession of disruptions due to reconnection, limiting dynamic alignment, steepening the effective spectral index, and altering the final dissipation scale.

The scaling of λ_D with the Lundquist (magnetic Reynolds) number S_L_⊥ depends on the order of the statistics being considered and the specific model of intermittency. The transition between the two regimes in the energy spectrum is predicted at approximately λ_D ~ S_L_⊥⁻⁰.⁶. The spectral index below λ_D is bounded between -5/3 and -2.3. The final dissipation scale is at λ_η,∞ ~ S_L_⊥⁻³/⁴, aligning with the Kolmogorov scale found in turbulence theories without scale-dependent dynamic alignment.

title: Experimental setup for measuring the barocaloric effect in polymers: Application to natural rubber
Abstract:
Barocaloric materials offer a promising alternative to conventional vapor-compression refrigeration technologies. However, the barocaloric effect (σb-CE) remains underexplored for many material classes. Addressing this gap, this paper describes the development of a high-pressure experimental setup for measuring σb-CE in polymers. The setup enables simultaneous measurements of temperature, pressure, and strain during the barocaloric cycle. 

The system's functionality has been validated through basic experiments using natural rubber, demonstrating significant temperature variations associated with the σb-CE. Strain-temperature curves have also been obtained, allowing indirect measurements of the isothermal entropy change.

title: Luttinger liquids, Fermi liquids and fractional statistics
Abstract:
This study explores the reformulation of one-dimensional interacting fermion systems, described by Luttinger liquid theory in the low energy approximation, as systems of weakly interacting particles with fractional charge and statistics. 

The approach employs Landau's phenomenological approach to Fermi liquid theory, where quasiparticles are interpreted as adiabatically dressed fermions. Previous research established the fractional nature of the local charge carried by these excitations. This work focuses on the statistics of these quasiparticles, demonstrating that by changing momentum variables, the Landau parameters of the generalized Fermi fluid can be transformed to zero. This change in interaction is compensated by a modification of the entropy function, consistent with the interpretation of quasiparticles as satisfying generalized exclusion statistics.

title: Pressure dependence of dynamically screened Coulomb interactions in NiO: Effective Hubbard, Hund, intershell and intersite components
Abstract:
This work investigates the pressure dependence of effective Coulomb interaction parameters (Hubbard U) in paramagnetic NiO using the constrained random phase approximation (cRPA). Five different low-energy models are considered, ranging from the most comprehensive model treating both Ni-d and O-p states as correlated orbitals (dp-dp model) to the simplest two-orbital model involving only the eg states (eg-eg model). 

The results reveal that bare interactions exhibit minimal sensitivity to compression across all models. However, partially screened interaction parameters show an almost linear increase with compression, stemming from a significant weakening of screening effects upon compression. This counterintuitive trend is attributed to specific characteristic changes in the electronic structure of the system. 

The study also calculates nearest neighbor inter-site d-d interaction terms, revealing substantial enhancement due to compression. The findings for both experimental and highly compressed structures indicate that the frequency dependence of partially screened interactions cannot be disregarded in realistic modeling of NiO. 

Furthermore, the computed interaction parameters for antiferromagnetic NiO are found to be almost identical to their paramagnetic counterparts.

title: Degeneration of K3 surfaces with non-symplectic automorphisms

title: Invariant properties for Wronskian type determinants of classical and classical discrete orthogonal polynomials under an involution of sets of positive integers

This symmetry is linked to the existence of higher-order difference equations for the orthogonal polynomials with respect to specific Christoffel transforms of the classical discrete measures. title: Revisiting dark energy models using differential ages of galaxies
Abstract:
This work utilizes a test based on the differential ages of galaxies to distinguish between dark energy models. As proposed by Jimenez and Loeb, relative ages of galaxies can be used to constrain cosmological parameters. Following this approach, the study reconstructs H₀dt/dz and its derivative (H₀d²t/dz²) using a model-independent technique called non-parametric smoothing. 

H₀dt/dz represents the change in the age of an object as a function of redshift, directly linked to the Hubble parameter. For reconstruction, the most recent H(z) data is employed. 

The study calculates H₀dt/dz and its derivative for various models, including Phantom, Einstein de Sitter (EdS), ΛCDM, Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parametrization, Jassal-Bagla-Padmanabhan (JBP) parametrization, and Feng-Shen-Li-Li (FSLL) parametrization. The consistency of these models is then checked against the model-independent reconstruction results. 

The findings indicate that H₀dt/dz, as a tool, cannot distinguish between ΛCDM, CPL, JBP, and FSLL parametrizations. As expected, EdS and Phantom models show noticeable deviations from the reconstructed results. However, the derivative of H₀dt/dz for various dark energy models exhibits higher sensitivity at low redshifts. Notably, the FSLL model is inconsistent with the reconstructed results at redshifts less than 0.5, while the ΛCDM model aligns with the 3σ region of the reconstruction.

title: Planar photonic crystals for express analysis of liquids

The study reveals that different liquids exhibit distinct relationships between the inverse Q-factor and resonance frequency of the resonance peak, as well as the distance from the photonic crystal interface to the container with liquid. This dependence allows for one-to-one identification of the liquid. Thus, the study experimentally demonstrates the ability to perform express analysis of liquids in containers using a metamaterial based on two planar photonic crystals.

title: Insight into the Role of Oxygen in Phase-Change Material GeTe
Abstract:

However, the microscopic role of oxygen in the write-erase process, specifically the reversible phase transition between the crystalline and amorphous states of phase-change materials, remains unclear. 

This work investigates the role of oxygen in oxygen-doped GeTe at the atomic scale through ab initio total energy calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. The key finding is that after amorphization and subsequent re-crystallization simulated by ab initio molecular dynamics, oxygen pulls one Ge atom out of its lattice site, with both atoms residing in the interstitial region near the Te vacancy initially occupied by oxygen. This forms a "dumbbell-like" defect (O-VTe-Ge), contrasting with ab initio total energy calculations at 0 K which indicate oxygen's preference for substituting Te in crystalline GeTe. 

This specific defect configuration is found to be responsible for the slower crystallization speed and consequently improved data retention of oxygen-doped GeTe, aligning with recent experimental observations. Additionally, the study reveals that oxygen increases the effective mass of the carrier, leading to increased resistivity in GeTe. 

These results unveil the microscopic mechanism of oxygen-doping optimization in the phase-change material GeTe. The proposed mechanism can be applied to other oxygen-doped ternary chalcogenide phase-change materials.

title: Rotational and translational diffusion of anisotropic gold nanoparticles in liquid crystals controlled by varying surface anchoring
Abstract: We explore the translational and rotational diffusion of anisotropic gold nanoparticles dispersed within a nematic liquid crystal host. To understand the physical origins of these intricate diffusion properties, we compare them to the diffusion of prolate and oblate ellipsoidal particles in isotropic fluids and to the diffusion of shape-isotropic particles in nematic fluids. title: Critical Phenomena and Kibble-Zurek Scaling in the Long-Range Quantum Ising Chain

Applying a linear quench of the external field through the quantum critical point, we observe a power-law scaling of the defect density as a function of the total quench time. Notably, the defect density increases more slowly for longer-range models, leading to a twenty-five percent change in the critical exponent. Our research underscores the significance of such long-range interactions in both statics and dynamics, potentially indicating analogous phenomena in different dynamical systems or other models.

title: A dual cavity Fabry-Perot device for high precision Doppler measurements in astronomy

An optimized mounting geometry is suggested, minimizing fractional length changes to $\\Delta L/L \\approx 1.5\\times 10^{-12}$. title: Lyapunov spectrum of separated flows and its dependence on numerical discretization

title: Efficient Action Detection in Untrimmed Videos via Multi-Task Learning
Abstract: This research focuses on the joint learning of action recognition and temporal localization in long, untrimmed videos. title: Observation of the helicity-selection-rule suppressed decay of the $χ_{c2}$ charmonium state
Abstract: We analyze the decays of $\\chi_{c2}\\to K^{+}K^{-}\\pi^{0}$, $K_{S} K^{\\pm}\\pi^{\\mp}$ and $\\pi^{+}\\pi^{-}\\pi^{0}$ using data collected from the $\\psi(3686)$ samples at the Beijing Spectrometer (BESIII). For the first time, we measure the branching fractions of $\\chi_{c2}\\to K^{\\ast}\\overline{K}$, $\\chi_{c2}\\to a_{2}^{\\pm}(1320)\\pi^{\\mp}/a_{2}^{0}(1320)\\pi^{0}$ and $\\chi_{c2}\\to \\rho(770)^{\\pm}\\pi^{\\mp}$. Here, $K^{\\ast}\\overline{K}$ encompasses both $K^{\\ast\\pm}K^{\\mp}$ and $K^{\\ast 0}\\overline{K}{}^{0}+c.c.$, and $K^{\\ast}$ represents the resonances $K^{\\ast}(892)$, $K^{\\ast}_{2}(1430)$ and $K^{\\ast}_{3}(1780)$. Our observations reveal a strong violation of the helicity selection rule in $\\chi_{c2}$ decays into vector and pseudoscalar meson pairs. The measured branching fractions of $\\chi_{c2}\\to K^{\\ast}(892)\\overline{K}$ are significantly larger than the upper limit of $\\chi_{c2}\\to \\rho(770)^{\\pm}\\pi^{\\mp}$, representing the first direct observation of a substantial $U$-spin symmetry breaking effect in charmonium decays.

title: Globular Cluster Systems in Brightest Cluster Galaxies. III: Beyond Bimodality
Abstract: We present new deep photometry of the rich globular cluster (GC) systems surrounding the brightest cluster galaxies UGC 9799 (Abell 2052) and UGC 10143 (Abell 2147), obtained with the HST ACS and WFC3 cameras. For comparative purposes, we also present new reductions of similar HST/ACS data for the Coma supergiants NGC 4874 and 4889. All four galaxies possess extensive cluster populations (extending to the radial limits of our data, encompassing 12000 to 23000 clusters per galaxy). The metallicity distribution functions (MDFs) of the GCs can be effectively represented by a bimodal-Gaussian form, where the metal-rich and metal-poor modes are separated by ~0.8 dex. However, the internal dispersions of each mode are remarkably large, resulting in a very broad and nearly continuous total MDF spanning from [Fe/H] = -2.4 to Solar. Notably, there are significant differences between galaxies in the relative numbers of \emph{metal-rich} clusters, suggesting distinct histories of mergers with massive, gas-rich halos. Furthermore, the proportion of metal-poor GCs increases rapidly beyond projected radii R > 4 R_eff, highlighting the crucial role of accreted dwarf satellites in the outer halo. Comprehensive models for the formation of GCs within the hierarchical formation of their parent galaxies are necessary to trace the systematic change in the structure of the MDF with galaxy mass, transitioning from a distinctly bimodal form in smaller galaxies to the broad continuum observed in the largest systems.

title: Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA): Gas Fuelling of Spiral Galaxies in the Local Universe I. - The Effect of the Group Environment on Star Formation in Spiral Galaxies
Abstract: We quantify the impact of the galaxy group environment (spanning 12.5 < log(M_group/Msun) < 14.0) on the star formation rates of a morphologically-selected population of disk-dominated local Universe spiral galaxies (z < 0.13) with stellar masses log(M*/Msun) > 9.5. Within this population, while a small fraction of group satellites exhibit strong quenching, the group centrals and the vast majority of satellites show star formation rates indistinguishable from ungrouped "field" galaxies of the same M*, albeit with higher scatter, and for all M*. Modeling these results, we deduce that disk-dominated satellites continue to be characterized by rapid gas cycling into and out of their interstellar medium at rates comparable to those operating prior to infall. The ongoing fueling is likely sourced from the group intrahalo medium (IHM) on Mpc scales, rather than from the circum-galactic medium on 100kpc scales. Consequently, the color-density relation of the galaxy population as a whole appears to be primarily driven by a change in the mix of disk- and spheroid-dominated morphologies in the denser group environment compared to the field, rather than by a reduced propensity of the IHM in higher mass structures to cool and accrete onto galaxies. We further suggest that the inferred substantial accretion of IHM gas by satellite disk-dominated galaxies will lead to a progressive reduction in their specific angular momentum, representing an efficient secular mechanism to transform morphology from star-forming disk-dominated types to more passive spheroid-dominated types.

title: Analyzing the Largest Spectroscopic Dataset of Hydrogen-Poor Super-Luminous Supernovae
Abstract: Super-luminous supernovae (SLSNe) are exceptionally luminous explosions whose power sources and progenitors remain highly debated. Broad-lined SNe Ic (SNe Ic-bl) are the only type of SNe demonstrably linked to long-duration gamma ray bursts (GRBs). Comparing the spectral similarities and differences between the populations of hydrogen-poor SLSNe (SLSNe Ic) and hydrogen-poor stripped-envelope core-collapse SNe, particularly SNe Ic and SNe Ic-bl, provides crucial observational data for testing theoretical predictions based on various power source and progenitor models. This paper compiles published optical spectra of 32 SLSNe Ic, 21 SNe Ic-bl, and 17 SNe Ic, quantifies their spectral features, constructs average spectra, and systematically compares them using newly developed tools. Our analysis reveals that SLSNe Ic and SNe Ic-bl, including those associated with GRBs, have comparable widths for their spectral features and average absorption velocities at all phases. These findings strengthen the connection between SLSNe Ic and GRBs. Notably, SLSNe Ic exhibit average \\FeII absorption velocities of -15,000 +/- 2,600 \\kms~at 10 days after peak, which are significantly higher than those of SNe Ic by $\\sim7,000$ \\kms~on average. SLSNe Ic also display significantly broader \\FeII lines compared to SNe Ic. Furthermore, our results suggest that achieving such high absorption and width velocities in SLSNe Ic may be challenging to explain using the interaction model. Notably, none of the 13 SLSNe Ic with measured absorption velocities spanning over 10 days exhibit a convincing flat velocity-evolution, contradicting the one-dimensional magnetar model. Lastly, we compare SN 2011kl, the first SN linked to an ultra-long GRB, with the mean spectrum of SLSNe Ic and SNe Ic-bl.

title: Tidal Dissipation and Evolution of White Dwarfs Around Massive Black Holes: An Eccentric Path to Tidal Disruption
Abstract: A white dwarf (WD) captured into a high-eccentricity orbit around a massive black hole (MBH) may undergo numerous pericenter passages before experiencing tidal disruption. During these passages, the tidal potential of the MBH excites internal oscillations or waves in the WD. The dissipation of these oscillations can significantly influence the WD's physical properties before disruption. We calculate the amplitude of tidally excited gravity (buoyancy) waves in the WD as a function of pericenter distance and eccentricity for realistic WD models, assuming efficient dissipation of these outgoing gravity waves in the outer layers of the WD by nonlinear effects or radiative damping. We derive fitting formulas for tidal energy and angular momentum transfer rates, as well as the tidal heating rate. Our findings indicate that these dynamical tides are much weaker than gravitational radiation in driving the orbital decay of the WD-MBH binary. Additionally, they are inefficient in altering the WD spin during orbital evolution. Incorporating our calculated tidal dissipation rate into a MESA-based WD evolution code, we find that tidal heating can lead to appreciable brightening of the WD and may induce runaway fusion in the hydrogen envelope long before the WD undergoes tidal disruption.

title: Understanding Error Correction and its Role as Part of the Communication Channel in Environments composed of Self-Integrating Systems
Abstract: The increasing complexity of technical systems necessitates a corresponding increase in the knowledge required for their setup and maintenance, making evolution prohibitively expensive. In the domain of Autonomic Computing, technical systems should possess various self-healing capabilities, allowing system owners to provide only partial, potentially inconsistent updates. These self-healing or self-integrating systems should identify the remaining changes needed for communications and functionalities to accommodate updates while restoring function. This challenge becomes even more critical in the context of the Internet of Things and Industrial Internet, where previously unforeseen device combinations can be assembled to create unexpected new functionalities. To achieve higher levels of self-integration capabilities, we propose viewing self-integration as sophisticated error correcting communications. This paper discusses an extended scope of error correction, highlighting its role as an integrated element of bi-directional communication channels in self-integrating, autonomic communication scenarios.

title: Tensor perturbations during inflation in a spatially closed Universe
Abstract: In a previous study [17], we investigated the evolution of the background geometry and scalar perturbations within an inflationary, spatially closed Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) model characterized by constant positive spatial curvature and $\\mathbb S^3$ spatial topology. Due to spatial curvature, the early phase of slow-roll inflation is modified, resulting in suppression of power in the scalar power spectrum at large angular scales. This paper extends the analysis to include tensor perturbations. Our findings reveal that, similar to scalar perturbations, the tensor power spectrum also exhibits power suppression for long wavelength modes. The correction to the tensor spectrum is limited to very long wavelength modes, effectively maintaining the observable CMB B-mode polarization spectrum as in the standard scenario with flat spatial sections. However, as both the tensor and scalar power spectra are modified, scale-dependent corrections to the tensor-to-scalar ratio emerge, leading to violations of the standard slow-roll consistency relation.

title: Revisiting Primordial Black Holes Constraints from Ionization History
Abstract: Recent discoveries by the Advanced Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) of merging intermediate-mass black holes have attracted significant attention. Of particular interest is the possibility that these merger events could provide evidence for dark matter in the form of primordial black holes (PBHs). It has been argued that the presence of numerous black holes would impact the thermal and ionization history of the universe through their accretion of matter, leaving strong signatures in the Cosmic Microwave Background's (CMB) power spectra. These signatures would manifest as damping of anisotropies and alterations in low-$l$ polarization power. Generally, accretion is highly sensitive to the specific physics involved and the conditions of the early universe. This work adopts a minimalist approach to find constraints on PBHs, excluding model-dependent effects of nonlinear structure formation or transitions between different accretion models, which would amplify the impact. Additionally, we incorporate the relative velocity between dark matter and baryonic matter, including the effects of supersonic streaming at high redshift, which significantly reduce the constraining power. We also examine constraints on more astrophysically-motivated extended black hole mass functions and discuss how mergers might influence this distribution. Our findings place constraints on PBHs in the range $ \\approx 30 M_\\odot$, indicating that they cannot constitute more than 10\\% of the total dark matter content.

title: Obstructions to lifting cocycles on groupoids and the associated $C^*$-algebras
Abstract: Given a short exact sequence of locally compact abelian groups $0 \\to A \\to B \\to C \\to 0$ and a continuous $C$-valued $1$-cocycle $\\phi$ on a locally compact Hausdorff groupoid $\\Gamma$, we construct a twist of $\\Gamma$ by $A$ that is trivial if and only if $\\phi$ lifts. The cocycle determines a strongly continuous action of $\\widehat{C}$ into $\\operatorname{Aut} C^*(\\Gamma)$, and we prove that the $C^*$-algebra of the twist is isomorphic to the induced algebra of this action if $\\Gamma$ is amenable. We apply our results to a groupoid defined by a locally finite cover of a space $X$ and a cocycle provided by a Čech 1-cocycle with coefficients in the sheaf of germs of continuous $\\mathbb{T}$-valued functions. We prove that the $C^*$-algebra of the resulting twist is continuous trace and compute its Dixmier-Douady invariant.

title: Survey of Promising Technologies for 5G Networks
Abstract: As an enhancement of cellular networks, the future-generation 5G network can be considered an ultra-high-speed technology. The proposed 5G network might include all types of advanced dominant technologies to provide remarkable services. Consequently, new architectures and service management schemes for different applications of emerging technologies need to be recommended to address issues related to data traffic capacity, high data rates, and reliability for ensuring QoS. Cloud computing, Internet of things (IoT), and software-defined networking (SDN) have emerged as core technologies for the 5G network. Cloud-based services provide flexible and efficient solutions for information and communications technology by reducing the cost of investing in and managing information technology infrastructure. In terms of functionality, SDN offers a promising architecture that decouples control planes and data planes to support programmability, adaptability, and flexibility in ever-changing network architectures. However, IoT combines cloud computing and SDN to achieve greater productivity for evolving technologies in 5G by facilitating interaction between the physical and human world. This study provides a comprehensive vision on enabling technologies for the next generation of mobile systems and networks, primarily focusing on 5G mobile communications.

title: Neural Network Model Of The PXIE RFQ Cooling System and Resonant Frequency Response
Abstract: As part of the PIP-II Injector Experiment (PXIE) accelerator, a four-vane radio frequency quadrupole (RFQ) accelerates a 30-keV, 1-mA to 10-mA H- ion beam to 2.1 MeV. It is designed to operate at a frequency of 162.5 MHz with arbitrary duty factor, including continuous wave (CW) mode. The resonant frequency is controlled solely by a water-cooling system. We present an initial neural network model of the RFQ frequency response to changes in the cooling system and RF power conditions during pulsed operation. This neural network model will be used within a model predictive control scheme to regulate the resonant frequency of the RFQ.

title: Scaling limit of a self-avoiding walk interacting with spatial random permutations
Abstract: We examine nearest neighbor spatial random permutations on $\\mathbb{Z}^d$. In this scenario, the system's energy is proportional to the sum of all cycle lengths, and the system can be interpreted as an ensemble of edge-weighted, mutually self-avoiding loops. The constant of proportionality, $\\alpha$, serves as the order parameter of the model. Our first finding is that in a parameter regime of edge weights where a single self-avoiding loop is known to be weakly space-filling, long cycles of spatial random permutations remain exponentially unlikely. For our second result, we embed a self-avoiding walk into a background of spatial random permutations and condition it to cover a macroscopic distance. For large values of $\\alpha$ (where long cycles are highly unlikely), we demonstrate that this walk collapses to a straight line in the scaling limit, providing bounds on the fluctuations that are nearly sufficient for diffusive scaling. To prove our results, we develop the concepts of spatial strong Markov property and iterative sampling for spatial random permutations, which may be of independent interest. Among other applications, we use these concepts to demonstrate exponential decay of correlations for large values of $\\alpha$ in a highly general setting.

title: Two-Scale Oscillons
Abstract: Oscillons are spatially stationary, quasi-periodic solutions of nonlinear field theories observed in diverse settings, ranging from granular systems and low-temperature condensates to early universe cosmology. We describe a new class of oscillons where the spatial envelope can exhibit "off-center" maxima and pulsate on timescales much longer than the fundamental frequency. These solutions are exact solutions of the 1-D sine-Gordon equation, and we demonstrate numerically that similar solutions exist in up to three dimensions for a range of potentials. The dynamics of these solutions align with key properties of oscillons that may form after cosmological inflation in string-motivated monodromy scenarios.

title: A proof of concept for scale-adaptive parameterizations: the case of the Lorenz '96 model
Abstract: Constructing efficient and accurate parameterizations of sub-grid scale processes is a central focus in the numerical modeling of geophysical fluids. Using a modified version of the two-level Lorenz '96 model, we present a proof of concept for a scale-adaptive parameterization constructed using statistical mechanical arguments. By effectively employing the Ruelle response theory and the Mori-Zwanzig projection method, we explicitly derive a parameterization for the fast variables, translating into deterministic, stochastic, and non-Markovian contributions to the equations of motion of the variables of interest. We demonstrate that our approach is computationally parsimonious and highly flexible, being explicitly scale-adaptive. Moreover, we prove its competitiveness compared to empirical ad-hoc approaches. While the parameterization proposed here is universal and can be easily adapted analytically to changes in the parameters' values through simple rescaling, the parameterization constructed with the ad-hoc approach necessitates recomputation each time the system parameters are changed. The cost of the increased flexibility of our method lies in achieving lower accuracy in each individual case.

title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
Abstract: The prevailing method for training natural language systems involves exposing them to vast amounts of text. This passive learning approach is problematic if the goal is to develop interactive machines like conversational agents. This research proposes a framework for language learning that relies on multi-agent communication. This framework is studied in the context of referential games, where a sender and a receiver are presented with a pair of images. The sender is instructed to identify one image as the target and communicate this information to the receiver using a limited, predetermined vocabulary. The receiver must then rely on this message to identify the target. This interactive communication necessitates the development of a shared language. The study demonstrates that two networks with simple configurations are capable of learning to coordinate in the referential game. Further exploration focuses on modifying the game environment to ensure that the "word meanings" induced in the game accurately reflect the intuitive semantic properties of the images. Additionally, a simple strategy for grounding the agents' code in natural language is presented. These advancements are crucial steps toward developing machines capable of productive communication with humans.

title: Algebraic cutting equations
Abstract: Cutting equations are diagrammatic identities used to prove perturbative unitarity in quantum field theory. This paper presents algebraic, upgraded versions of these equations. Unlike their diagrammatic counterparts, these algebraic identities hold for propagators with arbitrary, nonvanishing widths. Notably, the cut propagators do not need to vanish off-shell. This new approach provides a framework for addressing unresolved issues in perturbative quantum field theory and serves as a tool for investigating perturbative unitarity in higher-derivative theories relevant to the problem of quantum gravity, such as the Lee-Wick models and the fakeon models.

title: The lattice of congruence lattices of algebras on a finite set
Abstract: The congruence lattices of all algebras defined on a fixed finite set A, ordered by inclusion, form a finite atomistic lattice, denoted as ℰ. This research describes the atoms and coatoms of this lattice. Since each meet-irreducible element of ℰ is determined by a single unary mapping on A, the study completely characterizes those determined by a permutation or an acyclic mapping on the set A. Utilizing these characterizations, several properties of the lattice ℰ are deduced. Notably, it is proven that ℰ is tolerance-simple whenever |A| ≥ 4.

title: Nanoindenting the Chelyabinsk meteorite to learn about impact deflection effects in asteroids
Abstract: The Chelyabinsk meteorite, a highly shocked, low-porosity, ordinary chondrite, is likely similar to S- or Q-type asteroids. Therefore, nanoindentation experiments on this meteorite provide valuable data for understanding the physical properties of near-Earth asteroids. Tests conducted at different length scales yield information about the local mechanical properties of the minerals composing the meteorite, including reduced Young's modulus, hardness, elastic recovery, and fracture toughness. These tests are also instrumental in comprehending the potential for deflecting threatening asteroids using a kinetic projectile. The study revealed that the variations in mechanical properties between different regions of the meteorite, which influence impact efficiency, are not due to compositional differences. A low mean particle size, attributed to repetitive shock, can enhance hardness, while low porosity promotes a higher momentum multiplication. Momentum multiplication, the ratio between the change in momentum of a target due to an impact and the momentum of the projectile, indicates impact efficiency; higher values imply more efficient impacts. In the Chelyabinsk meteorite, the properties of the light-colored lithology materials facilitate higher momentum multiplication values compared to other regions. Additionally, a low fracture toughness was observed in the shock-melt veins, which would promote material ejection after an impact, further enhancing momentum multiplication. These findings hold significant relevance given the growing interest in missions to test asteroid deflection, such as the Asteroid Impact and Deflection Assessment mission, a collaboration between the European Space Agency and NASA.

title: Computation of complex ion production due to cosmic rays during the Halloween sequence of GLEs on October-November 2003
Abstract: The potential impact of solar variability, leading to cosmic ray variations, on atmospheric physics and chemistry has been a subject of intense debate in recent years. According to several recent models, cosmic ray-induced atmospheric ionization plays a crucial role in various processes. Recent observations have indicated an apparent effect on minor constituents and aerosols over polar regions during major solar proton events. The ion production rate during ground-level enhancements is a superposition of contributions from cosmic rays of galactic and solar origin. Solar cycle 23 witnessed several strong ground-level enhancements. The period from the end of October to the beginning of November 2003 was characterized by significant cosmic ray variability, marked by a sequence of three ground-level enhancements. Additionally, multiple Forbush decreases occurred, suppressing galactic cosmic ray flux. Consequently, cosmic ray-induced ion production in the atmosphere and the corresponding ionization effects experienced dynamic changes. This research calculates the complex ion production due to cosmic rays during the Halloween sequence of ground-level enhancements in October-November 2003 and estimates the ionization effect. The spectral and angular characteristics of the solar protons, as well as their time evolution, are explicitly considered throughout the events. The ionization effect during this period is computed at several altitudes above sea level in regions with Rc ≤ 1 GV and Rc ≤ 2 GV.

title: Gauged Floreanini-Jackiw type chiral boson and its BRST quantization
Abstract: This study examines the gauged model of Siegel type chiral boson. An alternative quantization of the gauge symmetric action has been performed using a Lorentz gauge, with an attempt made to establish the equivalence between the gauge symmetric version of the extended phase space and the original gauge non-invariant version of the usual phase space.

title: MixedTrails: Bayesian hypothesis comparison on heterogeneous sequential data
Abstract: Sequential traces of user data are commonly observed both online and offline, such as sequences of visited websites or GPS-captured location sequences. However, understanding the factors behind the generation of this sequential data is a challenging task, particularly since the data generation is often heterogeneous. For instance, navigation behavior might change in different phases of browsing a website, or movement behavior may vary between user groups. This research addresses this challenge by proposing MixedTrails, a Bayesian approach for comparing the plausibility of hypotheses regarding the generative processes of heterogeneous sequence data. Each hypothesis is derived from existing literature, theory, or intuition, representing a belief about transition probabilities between a set of states that can vary between groups of observed transitions. For example, when attempting to understand human movement in a city and given some observed data, a hypothesis assuming tourists are more likely to move towards points of interest than locals can be demonstrated to be more plausible than a hypothesis assuming the opposite. MixedTrails incorporates such hypotheses as Bayesian priors in a generative mixed transition Markov chain model, comparing their plausibility using Bayes factors. The study discusses analytical and approximate inference methods for calculating marginal likelihoods for Bayes factors, provides guidance on interpreting the results, and illustrates the approach with several experiments on synthetic and empirical data from Wikipedia and Flickr. This work enables a novel type of analysis for studying sequential data in various application areas.

title: Correlation between battery material performance and cooperative electron-phonon interaction in LiCo$_y$Mn$_{2-y}$O$_{4}$
Abstract: Understanding the fundamental physics related to archetypal lithium battery materials, such as LiCo$_y$Mn$_{2-y}$O$_{4}$, is of paramount importance for designing high-capacity cathodes. This research investigates the relationship between electrochemical performance, activated-transport parameters, thermal expansion, and cooperativity of electron-phonon-interaction distortions in LiCo$_y$Mn$_{2-y}$O$_{4}$. The first-order cooperative-normal-mode transition, detected through the coefficient of thermal expansion, is found to disappear at a critical doping (y ∼ 0.16). Interestingly, for y ≥ 0.16, the resistivity remains relatively unchanged with doping, and the electrochemical capacity becomes constant over repeated cycling. This critical doping (y ∼ 0.16) results in the breakdown of the network of cooperative/coherent normal-mode distortions. This breakdown leads to the vanishing of the first-order transition, the establishment of hopping channels with lower resistance, and the enhancement of lithiation and delithiation of the battery, minimizing electrochemical capacity fading.

title: Search for transitions between states in redbacks and black widows using seven years of Fermi-LAT observations
Abstract: This research presents a systematic search for variability possibly related to transitions between states in redback and black widow systems, utilizing seven years of Fermi-Large Area Telescope (LAT) data. This phenomenology has previously been detected in two redback systems, PSR J1023+0038 and PSR J1227-4853, for which a dedicated study is presented here. The research reveals the existence of only one transition for each of these systems over the past seven years. Their spectra are determined, establishing high-energy cutoffs at a few GeV for the high gamma-ray state of PSR J1023+0038 and for both states of PSR J1227-4853. The surveying capabilities of the Fermi-LAT allow for the investigation of similar phenomenology in other sources. While no hint of state transitions was found for most of the studied pulsars, two black-widow systems, PSR J2234+0944 and PSR J1446-4701, exhibit apparent variability reminiscent of the transitions observed in PSR J1023+0038 and PSR J1227-4853. title: Supersymmetric partner potentials arising from nodeless half bound states
Abstract: A Half Bound State (HBS) ψ*(x) can be defined as a single, conditional, zero-energy, continuous solution of the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation for a scattering potential well V(x) (s.t. V(±∞) = 0). The non-normalizable and solitary HBS of a potential satisfies the Neumann boundary condition, where ψ'*(±∞) = 0. It can exhibit n (= 0, 1, 2, ...) number of nodes, indicating n number of bound states in V(x) below E = 0. This research demonstrates that starting with a nodeless HBS, one can construct a (supersymmetric) pair of finite potentials (well, double wells, well-barrier): V±(x), possessing no bound state and enclosing positive area on the x-axis. Conversely, their negative counterparts (-cV±(x)), c > 0, possess at least one bound state for any arbitrary positive value of c. Furthermore, cV±(x), c > 0, which binds positive area on the x-axis in accordance with Simon's theorem, can have at least one bound state only conditionally, such as when c > 1 or c >> 1.

title: Magnetothermopower and magnetoresistance of single Co-Ni/Cu multilayered nanowires
Abstract: This study investigates the magnetothermopower and magnetoresistance of single Co Ni/Cu multilayered nanowires with varying thicknesses of the Cu spacer. Assuming that non-diffusive thermopower contributions of the nanowire can be neglected, it was found that the magnetic field-induced changes in thermopower and resistivity are equivalent. The emphasis of this paper lies in the comparison of magnetoresistance and magnetothermopower results, revealing that the same correlation holds between the two sets of data for all samples, regardless of the relative importance of the giant magnetoresistance or anisotropic magnetoresistance contributions in the individual nanowires.

title: Supergravity Contributions to Inflation in models with non-minimal coupling to gravity
Abstract: This paper provides a systematic study of supergravity contributions relevant for inflationary model building in Jordan frame supergravity. In this framework, canonical kinetic terms in the Jordan frame lead to the separation of the Jordan frame scalar potential into a tree-level term and a supergravity contribution, which could potentially hinder sustained inflation. The research shows that if the vacuum energy driving inflation originates predominantly from the F-term of an auxiliary field (not the inflaton), the supergravity corrections to the Jordan frame scalar potential are generally suppressed. Furthermore, these supergravity contributions vanish entirely if the superpotential W disappears along the inflationary trajectory. Conversely, if the F-term associated with the inflaton dominates the vacuum energy, the supergravity contributions are typically comparable to the globally supersymmetric contributions. Additionally, the non-minimal coupling to gravity inherent to Jordan frame supergravity significantly impacts the inflationary model depending on the size and sign of this coupling. The phenomenology of representative inflationary models is discussed, highlighting the connection to the recently debated cosmological "attractor" models.

title: Sparsity Measure of a Network Graph: Gini Index
Abstract: This article examines the application of a popular sparsity measure, the Gini Index, to network graphs. A wide array of network graphs exhibits sparsity. However, the commonly employed measure of sparsity in network graphs is edge density, reflecting the proportion of the sum of the degrees of all nodes in the graph compared to the total possible degrees in the corresponding fully connected graph. Edge density, being a simple ratio, has limitations, primarily in the amount of information it accounts for in its definition. This research proposes a formulation for defining the sparsity of a network graph by generalizing the concept of the Gini Index, termed the sparsity index. The proposed index satisfies a majority of the six properties (Robin Hood, Scaling, Rising Tide, Cloning, Bill Gates, and Babies) commonly used to compare sparsity measures. A comparison between edge density and the sparsity index is drawn using appropriate examples to highlight the efficacy of the proposed index. It is theoretically demonstrated that the two measures follow a similar trend for a changing graph; as the edge density of a graph increases, its sparsity index decreases. Additionally, the paper analytically establishes a relationship between the sparsity index and the exponent term of a power law distribution, a distribution known to approximate the degree distribution of a wide variety of network graphs. Finally, the article emphasizes how the proposed index, along with the Gini Index, can reveal crucial properties of a network graph.

title: Analytic solution to variance optimization with no short-selling
Abstract: A large portfolio of independent returns is optimized under the variance risk measure with a ban on short positions. The no-short selling constraint acts as an asymmetric ℓ₁ regularizer, setting some portfolio weights to zero and keeping the out-of-sample estimator for the variance bounded, preventing the divergence present in the non-regularized case. However, the susceptibility, i.e., the sensitivity of the optimal portfolio weights to changes in the returns, diverges at a critical value r = 2. This signifies that a ban on short positions does not prevent the phase transition in the optimization problem, it merely shifts the critical point from its non-regularized value of r = 1 to 2. At r = 2, the out-of-sample estimator for the portfolio variance remains finite, while the estimated in-sample variance vanishes. Numerical simulations support the analytical results, showing perfect agreement for N/T < 2. Numerical experiments on finite-size samples of symmetrically distributed returns indicate that above this critical point, the probability of finding solutions with zero in-sample variance rapidly increases with increasing N, reaching one in the large N limit. However, these are not legitimate solutions of the optimization problem, as they are infinitely sensitive to any change in the input parameters, leading to wild fluctuations from sample to sample. The distribution of optimal weights over random samples is also calculated, revealing that the regularizer preferentially removes assets with large variances, aligning with natural expectations.

title: Dielectric Haloscopes to Search for Axion Dark Matter: Theoretical Foundations
Abstract: This research explores the underlying theory of dielectric haloscopes, a novel method for detecting dark matter axions. When an interface between different dielectric media is placed within a magnetic field, the oscillating axion field acts as a source of electromagnetic waves, which emerge in both directions perpendicular to the surface. The emission rate can be significantly enhanced by strategically placing multiple layers to achieve constructive interference and by utilizing a large transverse area. Starting from the axion-modified Maxwell equations, the efficiency of this new dielectric haloscope approach is calculated. This technique has the potential to explore the unexplored high-frequency range of 10-100 GHz (axion mass 40-400 μeV), where traditional cavity resonators struggle to achieve the required volume.

q\ d{\rm log} s) = A (q/q_{\rm br})^n s^m \, {\rm dex}^{-2}$ for $q > q_{\rm
br}$ and $dN_{\rm pl}/(d{\rm log} q\ d{\rm log} s) = A (q/q_{\rm br})^p s^m \,
{\rm dex}^{-2}$ for $q < q_{\rm br}$, where $q_{\rm br}$ is the mass ratio of

0.49_{-0.49}^{+0.47}$ and $p = 0.6^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$ for $q_{\rm br}\equiv
1.7\times 10^{-4}$. The unbroken power law model is disfavored with a $p$-value of 0.0022, which corresponds to a Bayes factor of 27 favoring the broken power-law model. These results suggest that cold Neptunes are likely to be the most common type of planets beyond the snow line.

title: Spectral dimension with deformed spacetime signature

title: Conditional Mutual Information and Quantum Steering

title: Quantizations of D=3 Lorentz symmetry

title: Smart Scheduling of Continuous Data-Intensive Workflows with Machine Learning Triggered Execution

These workflows are expressive, flexible, and scalable. However, this is not the most desirable behavior in numerous scenarios. To overcome this inefficiency, we introduce a novel workflow model for continuous and data-intensive processing, capable of relaxing triggering semantics based on the assessed impact of input data on changing the workflow output. To assess this impact, learn the correlation between input and output variation, and guarantee correctness within a given tolerated error constant, we rely on machine learning. The functionality of this workflow model is implemented in SmartFlux, a middleware framework effortlessly integrated with existing workflow managers. title: A stochastic model for directional changes of swimming bacteria

title: Fault Attacks on Encrypted General Purpose Compute Platforms

While encrypting RAM safeguards against passive eavesdropping, the level of protection it offers against an active adversary who can both read and modify RAM content remains unclear. While encryption prevents an adversary from viewing the plaintext or predicting system behavior based on changes, it is unclear if this is sufficient to thwart malicious actions. To investigate this, we developed a software-based memory encryption solution on a desktop system that mimics AMD's SME. We then demonstrated a proof-of-concept fault attack on this system, successfully extracting the private RSA key of a GnuPG user. title: A Revolutionary Rural Agricultural Participatory Sensing Approach Using Delay Tolerant Networks
Abstract: To deliver sustainable digital agro-advisory services to farmers, seamless information flow between farmers and experts/expert systems is essential. Queries generated by farmers, which may include multimedia data related to crop disease or pest attacks, need to be transmitted to experts for analysis. Subsequently, alerts or advice from the expert system must be communicated back to farmers within an acceptable time frame. However, in countries like India, network connectivity in many agricultural regions is extremely poor, making end-to-end communication between farmers and expert systems intermittent. This poses a significant challenge to providing timely agro-advisory services to farmers. This paper proposes a Delay Tolerant Network (DTN)-based relay application model that enables agro-advisory services to farmers located in areas with no or poor network connectivity. The proposed model utilizes Device to Device (D2D) communication and introduces mobile relay nodes that can carry queries (responses) between poor or no network zones and zones with reliable communication. The model's implementation is presented for tea farmers in West Bengal and Assam, with potential applications for various other agricultural sectors in the future.

title: Universal statistics of selected values
Abstract: Selection, the tendency of certain traits to become more frequent than others in a population under the influence of an agency (natural or artificial), is a fundamental principle in Darwinian evolution and numerous other natural and social phenomena. Despite its importance, a general theory of selection, analogous to the Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko theory of extreme events, has been lacking. Here, we introduce a probabilistic definition of selection and demonstrate that selected values converge towards a universal family of limiting distributions. The universality classes and scaling exponents are determined by the tail thickness of the random variable under selection. Our findings are supported by data from molecular biology, agriculture, and sport.

title: Drift Removal in Plant Electrical Signals via IIR Filtering Using Wavelet Energy
Abstract: Plant electrical signals often exhibit low-frequency drifts, with or without the application of external stimuli. Quantifying the randomness in plant signals in a stimulus-specific manner is hindered by the lack of knowledge regarding the vital frequency information in the actual biological response. This study designs an optimal Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filter that removes low-frequency drifts while preserving the frequency spectrum corresponding to the random component of unstimulated plant signals. The filter minimizes bias due to unknown artifacts and drifts. We utilize energy criteria of wavelet packet transform (WPT) for optimization-based tuning of the IIR filter parameters. This optimal filter ensures that the energy distribution of the pre-stimulus parts in different experiments overlaps, while the distributions under different stimuli change. This research may popularize plant signal processing as a separate field, complementing conventional bioelectrical signal processing paradigms.

title: Hyperspectral CNN Classification with Limited Training Samples
Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging sensors are gaining popularity in robotics applications, such as agriculture and mining, enabling per-pixel thematic classification of materials based on their unique spectral signatures. Convolutional neural networks have demonstrated remarkable performance in classification tasks but require substantial amounts of labeled training data. This data must adequately capture the variability expected in the environment. One of the major variations encountered outdoors with hyperspectral data is due to incident illumination, which can change in spectral shape and intensity depending on the scene geometry. For instance, regions occluded from sunlight have lower intensity and their incident irradiance skewed towards shorter wavelengths. This work introduces a data augmentation strategy based on relighting during the training of a hyperspectral convolutional neural network. This strategy enables training in outdoor environments using only a small labeled region, which need not represent the entire scene's geometric variability. This approach is particularly valuable for applications where acquiring large amounts of training data is laborious, hazardous, or difficult, such as labeling pixels within shadows. Radiometric normalization approaches for pre-processing hyperspectral data are analyzed, showing that methods based on raw pixel data are sufficient as input for the classifier. This eliminates the need for external hardware, such as calibration boards, which can restrict the application of hyperspectral sensors in robotics applications. Experiments to evaluate the classification system are conducted on two datasets captured from a field-based platform.

title: Skewness of citation impact data and covariates of citation distributions: A large-scale empirical analysis based on Web of Science data
Abstract: Using percentile shares, one can visualize and analyze the skewness in bibliometric data across disciplines and over time. The resulting figures provide an intuitive interpretation and are more suitable for detailed analysis of the effects of independent and control variables on distributions than regression analysis. We demonstrate this by using percentile shares to analyze so-called "factors influencing citation impact" (FICs; e.g., the impact factor of the publishing journal) across years and disciplines. The analysis includes all articles (n= 2,961,789) covered by WoS in 1990 (n= 637,301), 2000 (n= 919,485), and 2010 (n= 1,405,003). In 2010, nearly half of the citation impact is accounted for by the 10% most-frequently cited papers. The skewness is largest in the humanities (68.5% in the top-10% layer) and lowest in agricultural sciences (40.6%). Comparing the effects of different FICs (number of cited references, number of authors, number of pages, and JIF) on citation impact reveals that JIF has the strongest correlation with citation scores. However, the correlation between FICs and citation impact is lower when citations are normalized instead of using raw citation counts.

title: Understanding the Tracking Errors of Commodity Leveraged ETFs
Abstract: Commodity exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are a significant component of the rapidly growing ETF market. They have gained popularity in recent years as they provide investors access to a diverse range of commodities, from precious metals to building materials and from oil and gas to agricultural products. This article analyzes the tracking performance of commodity leveraged ETFs and discusses associated trading strategies. It is well-known that leveraged ETF returns deviate from their tracking targets over longer holding horizons due to the phenomenon of volatility decay. To address this, we construct a benchmark process that accounts for volatility decay and use it to examine the tracking performance of commodity leveraged ETFs. Our empirical data analysis reveals that many commodity leveraged ETFs underperform significantly against the benchmark, and we quantify this discrepancy using the novel concept of realized effective fee. Finally, we consider several trading strategies and evaluate their performance through backtesting using historical price data.

title: Understanding the Non-Convergence of Agricultural Futures via Stochastic Storage Costs and Timing Options
Abstract: This paper examines the market phenomenon of non-convergence between futures and spot prices in the grains market. We hypothesize that the positive basis observed at maturity arises from the futures holder's timing options to exercise the shipping certificate delivery item and subsequently liquidate the physical grain. Our proposed approach incorporates stochastic spot price and storage cost, and solves an optimal double stopping problem to determine the optimal strategies for exercising and liquidating the grain. Our new models for stochastic storage rates result in explicit no-arbitrage prices for the shipping certificate and associated futures contract. We calibrate our models to empirical futures data during periods of observed non-convergence and illustrate the premium generated by the shipping certificate.

title: Image Segmentation for Fruit Detection and Yield Estimation in Apple Orchards
Abstract: Ground vehicles equipped with monocular vision systems are valuable sources of high-resolution image data for precision agriculture applications in orchards. This paper presents an image processing framework for fruit detection and counting using orchard image data. A general-purpose image segmentation approach is employed, incorporating two feature learning algorithms: multi-scale Multi-Layered Perceptrons (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). These networks are extended by including contextual information about how the image data was captured (metadata), which correlates with some appearance variations and/or class distributions observed in the data. The pixel-wise fruit segmentation output is then processed using the Watershed Segmentation (WS) and Circular Hough Transform (CHT) algorithms to detect and count individual fruits. Experiments were conducted in a commercial apple orchard near Melbourne, Australia. The results demonstrate improved fruit segmentation performance with the inclusion of metadata on the previously benchmarked MLP network. This work is extended with CNNs, bringing agrovision closer to the state-of-the-art in computer vision. While metadata had a negligible influence on CNN performance, the best pixel-wise F1-score of 0.791 was achieved. The WS algorithm produced the best apple detection and counting results, with a detection F1-score of 0.858. Finally, image fruit counts were accumulated over multiple rows in the orchard and compared against post-harvest fruit counts obtained from a grading and counting machine. The count estimates using CNN and WS resulted in the best performance for this dataset, with a squared correlation coefficient of r2=0.826.

title: Deep Fruit Detection in Orchards
Abstract: An accurate and reliable image-based fruit detection system is crucial for supporting higher-level agriculture tasks such as yield mapping and robotic harvesting. This paper presents the application of a state-of-the-art object detection framework, Faster R-CNN, in the context of fruit detection in orchards, specifically for mangoes, almonds, and apples. Ablation studies are conducted to understand the practical deployment of the detection network, including the amount of training data required to capture dataset variability. Data augmentation techniques are shown to yield significant performance gains, resulting in a greater than two-fold reduction in the number of training images needed. In contrast, transferring knowledge between orchards contributed negligibly to performance gain compared to initializing the Deep Convolutional Neural Network directly from ImageNet features. Finally, to operate on orchard data containing between 100-1000 fruits per image, a tiling approach is introduced for the Faster R-CNN framework. The study achieved the best detection performance for these orchards relative to previous works, with an F1-score of >0.9 achieved for apples and mangoes.
