title: Scalable and Accurate Online Feature Selection for Big Data
Abstract: Feature selection is crucial in many big data applications. Two significant challenges are associated with big data:  1) Extremely high dimensionality (millions of features) that continues to grow; 2) The demand for highly scalable feature selection algorithms that operate online, allowing each feature to be processed sequentially. This paper presents SAOLA, a Scalable and Accurate OnLine Approach for feature selection.  Based on theoretical analysis of bounds on pairwise feature correlations, SAOLA utilizes novel pairwise comparison techniques and maintains a parsimonious model over time in an online fashion.  Furthermore, to handle arriving features in groups, we extend the SAOLA algorithm, proposing a new group-SAOLA algorithm for online group feature selection.  The group-SAOLA algorithm can maintain a set of feature groups that is sparse at both the group and individual feature levels simultaneously. An empirical study using a series of benchmark real datasets shows that our two algorithms, SAOLA and group-SAOLA, scale effectively on datasets with extremely high dimensionality and outperform state-of-the-art feature selection methods.

title: On Learning to Think: Algorithmic Information Theory for Novel Combinations of Reinforcement Learning Controllers and Recurrent Neural World Models
Abstract: This paper addresses the general problem of reinforcement learning (RL) in partially observable environments. In 2013, our large RL recurrent neural networks (RNNs) learned from scratch to drive simulated cars from high-dimensional video input. However, real brains are far more capable in many ways.  In particular, they learn a predictive model of their initially unknown environment, which they utilize for abstract (e.g., hierarchical) planning and reasoning.  Guided by algorithmic information theory, we describe RNN-based AIs (RNNAIs) designed to replicate this capability.  Such an RNNAI can be trained on an endless sequence of tasks, some provided by the user, while others are invented by the RNNAI itself in a curious, playful manner, to improve its RNN-based world model.  Unlike our previous model-building RNN-based RL machines dating back to 1990, the RNNAI learns to actively query its model for abstract reasoning, planning, and decision-making, essentially "learning to think."  The fundamental concepts presented in this report can be applied to numerous other scenarios where one RNN-like system exploits the algorithmic information content of another. These concepts are derived from a grant proposal submitted in Fall 2014 and also explain concepts such as "mirror neurons."  Experimental results will be described in separate papers.

title: Design of Kernels in Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Classification
Abstract: Despite the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification, our understanding of the relationship between convolutional kernel shapes and learned representations remains limited. In this work, we explore and leverage this relationship between kernel shapes, which define Receptive Fields (RFs) in CNNs, for learning feature representations and image classification.  To facilitate this, we propose a feature visualization method for visualizing pixel-wise classification score maps of learned features.  Motivated by our experimental results and observations reported in the literature for visual system modeling, we introduce a novel design of kernel shapes for learning representations in CNNs.  Experimentally, we achieve state-of-the-art classification performance compared to a baseline CNN model [28] by reducing the model's number of parameters and computational time using the ILSVRC-2012 dataset [24].  The proposed models also outperform state-of-the-art models employed on the CIFAR-10/100 datasets [12] for image classification.  Additionally, we analyzed the robustness of our proposed method to occlusion for classifying partially occluded images, comparing it to state-of-the-art methods.  Our results indicate the effectiveness of our approach. The code is available at github.com/minogame/caffe-qhconv.

title: Fine-Grained Classification via Mixture of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: We introduce a novel deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) system for fine-grained image classification, termed a mixture of DCNNs (MixDCNN).  Fine-grained image classification is characterized by significant intra-class variations and subtle inter-class variations.  To address these challenges, our proposed MixDCNN system partitions images into K subsets of similar images and learns an expert DCNN for each subset.  The outputs from each of the K DCNNs are combined to form a single classification decision.  In contrast to previous techniques, we provide a formulation for performing joint end-to-end training of the K DCNNs simultaneously.  Extensive experiments on three datasets using two network structures (AlexNet and GoogLeNet) demonstrate that the proposed MixDCNN system consistently outperforms other methods. It achieves a relative improvement of 12.7% and establishes state-of-the-art results on two datasets.

title: Non-adaptive Group Testing on Graphs
Abstract: Grebinski and Kucherov (1998) and Alon et al. (2004-2005) investigated the problem of learning a hidden graph for specific cases, such as Hamiltonian cycles, cliques, stars, and matchings. This problem finds application in domains like chemical reactions, molecular biology, and genome sequencing. This paper presents a generalization of this problem. Specifically, we consider a graph G and a subgraph H of G, assuming G contains exactly one defective subgraph isomorphic to H. The goal is to identify the defective subgraph by testing whether an induced subgraph contains an edge of the defective subgraph, minimizing the number of tests.  We present an upper bound for the number of tests required to find the defective subgraph by employing the symmetric and high-probability variation of Lovász Local Lemma.

title: Predicting diverse M-best protein contact maps
Abstract: Protein contacts hold vital information for protein structure and functional analysis, but predicting contacts from sequence information remains a challenging task.  Recent advances in evolutionary coupling (EC) analysis, predicting contacts by identifying co-evolved residues (or columns) in a multiple sequence alignment (MSA), have made progress due to improved statistical assessment techniques and high-throughput sequencing.  Existing EC analysis methods predict only a single contact map for a given protein, which may have limited accuracy, especially when the protein under prediction lacks a significant number of sequence homologs.  Similar to ab initio folding, which typically predicts several possible 3D models for a given protein sequence, this paper introduces a novel structure learning method that can predict a set of diverse contact maps for a given protein sequence.  The best solution within this set often exhibits significantly higher accuracy than the initial prediction.  Our experimental tests demonstrate that for many test proteins, the best out of 5 solutions generated by our method achieves an accuracy improvement of at least 0.1 compared to the initial solution when evaluating the top L/5 or L/10 (L being the sequence length) predicted long-range contacts, particularly for protein families with limited sequence homologs. Our best solutions also surpass the quality of those produced by the popular EC methods Evfold and PSICOV.

title: Asynchronous adaptive networks
Abstract: In a recent article [1], we reviewed advances related to adaptation, learning, and optimization across synchronous networks.  We discussed various distributed strategies enabling a collection of networked agents to interact locally in response to streaming data, continuously learning and adapting to track data and model drifts.  Under reasonable technical conditions on the data, the adaptive networks were shown to be mean-square stable in the slow adaptation regime, and their mean-square-error performance and convergence rate were characterized in terms of the network topology and data statistical moments [2].  Classical results for single-agent adaptation and learning were recovered as special cases.  Building upon the works [3]-[5], this chapter complements the exposition from [1] and extends the results to asynchronous networks.  The operation of this class of networks can be subject to various sources of uncertainties influencing their dynamic behavior, including randomly changing topologies, random link failures, random data arrival times, and agents turning on and off randomly.  In an asynchronous environment, agents may stop updating their solutions or sending/receiving information randomly and without coordination with other agents.  The presentation reveals that the mean-square-error performance of asynchronous networks remains largely unchanged compared to synchronous networks. These findings justify the remarkable resilience of cooperative networks in the face of random events.

title: Proximal gradient method for huberized support vector machine
Abstract: The Support Vector Machine (SVM) has found wide application in various classification problems.  The original SVM utilizes the hinge loss function, which is non-differentiable, making the problem challenging to solve, especially for regularized SVMs like those with ℓ₁-regularization. This paper investigates the Huberized SVM (HSVM), which employs a differentiable approximation of the hinge loss function. We first explore the use of the Proximal Gradient (PG) method for solving binary-class HSVM (B-HSVM) and then generalize it to multi-class HSVM (M-HSVM). Under strong convexity assumptions, we demonstrate linear convergence of our algorithm.  Furthermore, we present a finite convergence result regarding the solution's support, which enables further acceleration of the algorithm via a two-stage method.  Extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real datasets highlight the superiority of our methods over state-of-the-art methods for both binary- and multi-class SVMs.

title: Alternating direction method of multipliers for regularized multiclass support vector machines
Abstract: The support vector machine (SVM) was initially designed for binary classifications.  Significant effort has been dedicated to generalizing the binary SVM to multiclass SVM (MSVM), which are more complex problems.  Initially, MSVMs were solved by considering their dual formulations, which are quadratic programs solvable by standard second-order methods.  However, the duals of MSVMs with regularizers are usually more difficult to formulate and computationally expensive to solve.  This paper focuses on several regularized MSVMs and extends the alternating direction method of multiplier (ADMM) to these MSVMs.  Employing a splitting technique, all considered MSVMs are expressed as two-block convex programs, for which ADMM possesses global convergence guarantees.  Numerical experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate the high efficiency and accuracy of our algorithms. |||

title: Stability of similarity measurements for bipartite networks
Abstract: Similarity is a crucial metric in network analysis and machine learning algorithms, finding applications in various fields like personalized recommendations and socio-economic dynamics.  This study argues that a robust similarity measurement should exhibit stability even when faced with data loss.  The investigation analyzes fifteen similarity measurements across six bipartite networks by comparing similarity matrices derived from randomly divided data sets. The results classify the fifteen measurements into three distinct clusters based on their stability, revealing that measurements within the same cluster share similar mathematical definitions. Additionally, a novel top-$n$-stability method for personalized recommendation is developed. The research demonstrates that unstable similarities lead to inaccurate recommendations, whereas stable similarity measurements significantly enhance the performance of recommendation systems. This work introduces a new dimension for analyzing and evaluating similarity measurements, with potential applications in link prediction, clustering algorithms, community detection, and beyond.

title: Hierarchical Invariant Feature Learning with Marginalization for Person Re-Identification
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of matching pedestrians across multiple camera views, known as person re-identification.  Variations in lighting conditions, environment, and pose changes across camera views make re-identification a complex task. While existing methods focus on specific features or learning distance functions, this work proposes a hierarchical feature learning framework that learns invariant representations from labeled image pairs. The framework learns a mapping to ensure that extracted features remain consistent for images of the same individual across different camera views. To achieve robust representations and enhance generalization to unseen data, extensive training data is essential. Recognizing the scarcity of large person re-identification datasets, the paper introduces a hierarchical network that incorporates a marginalization technique, eliminating the need for explicit data augmentation.  The proposed approach outperforms baseline algorithms and popular metric learning techniques on publicly available datasets such as VIPeR, CUHK01, CAVIAR4REID, and iLIDS, achieving state-of-the-art results.

title: Aspect-based Opinion Summarization with Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper focuses on Aspect-based Opinion Summarization (AOS) of product reviews.  To enable real-world applications, an AOS system requires addressing two core subtasks: aspect extraction and sentiment classification. Existing approaches to aspect extraction, relying on linguistic analysis or topic modeling, may lack precision or suitability for specific products. This study proposes a more precise approach that directly maps each review sentence to pre-defined aspects. To handle aspect mapping and sentiment classification, two Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods are introduced: cascaded CNN and multitask CNN.  The cascaded CNN architecture employs multiple CNNs for aspect mapping at the first level and a single CNN for sentiment classification at the second level. In contrast, the multitask CNN utilizes multiple aspect CNNs and a sentiment CNN that share the same word embeddings. Experimental results demonstrate that both cascaded and multitask CNNs significantly outperform SVM-based methods, with multitask CNN generally performing better than cascaded CNN.

title: Coresets for Kinematic Data: From Theorems to Real-Time Systems
Abstract: A coreset is a semantic compression of a dataset with respect to a set of queries, guaranteeing that querying the coreset provides approximate answers to queries on the original dataset.  While coresets have revolutionized theoretical computer science for approximation algorithms and more recently, machine learning for "Big data", their real-time application at frame rates remains unexplored.  This paper proposes a framework to implement coreset-based systems capable of operating at dozens of frames per second. The work proves that any set of matrices whose sum is S can be represented by a positively weighted subset with the same center of mass and orientation as S, consisting of O(dr) matrices, where r is the rank of S. An efficient algorithm is presented to compute this core set in one pass over a potentially infinite stream of matrices.  By maintaining a coreset for a kinematic set of points, the framework enables running pose-estimation algorithms on the smaller coreset instead of the full set, achieving real-time performance on low-cost devices.  The paper illustrates this concept with a cost-effective IoT wireless system for tracking a quadcopter that guides guests to desired locations.  The research encourages the adoption of coresets in future systems and research beyond the theoretical community by providing extensive experimental results on both synthetic and real data, along with open-source code.

title: Machine Learning Sentiment Prediction based on Hybrid Document Representation
Abstract: Automated sentiment analysis and opinion mining involve extracting subjective information from text.  The surge in user-generated content on the web, particularly opinions on products and services expressed across various platforms, necessitates reliable automated sentiment extraction for commercial applications.  This paper presents a novel hybrid vectorization approach for textual resources that combines a weighted variant of the Word2Vec representation, a Bag-of-Words representation, and a vector of lexicon-based sentiment values. The proposed text representation approach is evaluated using various machine learning classification algorithms on a widely used sentiment detection dataset.  The hybrid vectorization method achieves higher classification accuracy than individual component methods and comparable performance with state-of-the-art sentiment detection methodologies.

title: Position paper: a general framework for applying machine learning techniques in operating room
Abstract: This position paper outlines a general framework for applying machine learning and pattern recognition techniques in healthcare. The focus is on developing an automated tool for monitoring and enhancing awareness within the operating room, specifically identifying human errors during laparoscopic surgical procedures.  The proposed framework comprises three layers, each implementing algorithms with increasing complexity and abstraction levels. The first layer preprocesses and aggregates raw data collected from sensors during surgical procedures. The processed data is then transferred to the second layer, which employs pattern recognition techniques to extract relevant features.  Finally, the third layer utilizes expert systems to make high-level decisions, representing the system's final output.

title: Non-judgemental Dynamic Fuel Cycle Benchmarking
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel fuel cycle benchmarking analysis methodology by coupling Gaussian process regression, a popular Machine Learning technique, with dynamic time warping, a technique widely used in speech recognition.  This combination generates figures-of-merit applicable to any time series metric studied in benchmarks. The figures-of-merit account for uncertainty in the metric, leverage information across the entire time domain, and do not require simulators to use a common time grid.  The paper defines a distance measure for comparing simulator performance for a specific metric and derives a contribution measure from the distance measure to rank the importance of fuel cycle metrics. The study warns against using standard signal processing techniques for error reduction, as Gaussian process regression itself effectively handles error reduction.

title: Sparse Coral Classification Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Autonomous repair of deep-sea coral reefs is a proposed solution to support the ocean ecosystem, which is vital for commercial fishing, tourism, and other species.  This idea involves using swarms of small autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm intelligence techniques to locate and replace broken coral fragments, promoting reef growth and habitat maintenance. This project focuses on developing machine vision algorithms to enable an underwater robot to locate a coral reef and a coral fragment on the seabed and pick it up.  While this specific problem lacks existing literature, related work on fish counting offers some insight. The technical challenges stem from the potential lack of water clarity, platform stabilization, and spurious artifacts. The paper proposes an efficient sparse classification for coral species using a supervised deep learning method called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The method combines Weber Local Descriptors (WLD), Phase Congruency (PC), and Zero Component Analysis (ZCA) Whitening for shape and texture feature extraction, serving as supplementary channels alongside spatial color channels in the coral input image.  The study also investigates state-of-the-art underwater preprocessing algorithms for image enhancement, color normalization, and color conversion adjustment.  The proposed coral classification method, implemented in MATLAB, is evaluated using two coral datasets: Moorea Labeled Corals from the University of California San Diego and Atlantic Deep Sea from Heriot-Watt University.

title: Computational Pathology: Challenges and Promises for Tissue Analysis
Abstract: Histological assessment of human tissue is a critical challenge in cancer detection and treatment.  Diverse data sources, ranging from tissue microarray data to gene expression, proteomics, and metabolomics, provide comprehensive insights into a patient's health. Medical doctors rely on data-driven automatic analysis tools to evaluate these information sources.  Methods for classification, grouping, segmentation of heterogeneous data sources, as well as regression of noisy dependencies and estimation of survival probabilities are integral to pathology diagnosis systems. This paper reviews the state-of-the-art in computational pathology workflows, analyzing their design and effectiveness, and discusses future research directions in this emerging field of medical informatics and diagnostic machine learning.

title: Write a Classifier: Predicting Visual Classifiers from Unstructured Text
Abstract: Humans typically learn by associating visual concepts with linguistic descriptions. For instance, teaching children about visual object categories often involves textual or spoken descriptions. This observation motivates the study of computationally modeling this learning process to develop visual classifiers. This work explores how to utilize purely textual descriptions of visual classes, without training images, to learn explicit visual classifiers. The paper proposes and investigates two baseline formulations based on regression and domain transfer, which predict a linear classifier.  A new constrained optimization formulation is introduced, combining a regression function and a knowledge transfer function with additional constraints to predict linear classifier parameters. The paper also presents generic kernelized models where a kernel classifier is predicted using the representer theorem, allowing the use of any two Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) kernel functions in the visual and text spaces, respectively.  Finally, a kernel function is proposed for unstructured text descriptions based on distributional semantics, offering advantages in this context and potential applications in other domains.  All studied models are applied to predict visual classifiers on two fine-grained and challenging categorization datasets (CU Birds and Flower Datasets). The results demonstrate the successful predictions of the final model over several designed baselines.

title: Event Specific Multimodal Pattern Mining with Image-Caption Pairs
Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework and algorithms for discovering image patch patterns from a large corpus of weakly supervised image-caption pairs generated from news events.  Current pattern mining techniques aim to find patterns that are representative and discriminative. However, this work emphasizes the importance of patterns that are human-recognizable and preferably have meaningful names. The paper introduces a multimodal pattern mining approach that leverages descriptive captions accompanying news images to learn semantically meaningful image patch patterns. These multimodal patterns are then named using words mined from the associated image captions for each pattern.  A novel evaluation framework demonstrates that the discovered patterns are significantly more semantically meaningful than those identified by existing vision-only pipelines. Additionally, the framework enables tagging discovered image patches with high accuracy without direct supervision.  The proposed methods discover named patterns beyond those covered by existing image datasets like ImageNet.  This research represents the first algorithm developed to automatically mine image patch patterns with strong semantic meaning specific to high-level news events and evaluate these patterns based on that criteria.

title: Autoencoding beyond pixels using a learned similarity metric
Abstract: This paper presents an autoencoder that leverages learned representations to improve similarity measurements in data space.  By combining a variational autoencoder with a generative adversarial network, the learned feature representations in the GAN discriminator are utilized as the basis for the VAE reconstruction objective. This approach replaces element-wise errors with feature-wise errors, better capturing the data distribution while offering invariance towards transformations like translation. The method is applied to images of faces, demonstrating superior performance compared to VAEs with element-wise similarity measures in terms of visual fidelity.  Furthermore, the research shows that the method learns an embedding where high-level abstract visual features (e.g., wearing glasses) can be modified using simple arithmetic operations.
label: AI

title: Learning Local Image Descriptors with Deep Siamese and Triplet Convolutional Networks by Minimising Global Loss Functions
Abstract: Recent advances in training deep convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) have led to the development of new methods for automatically learning local image descriptors.  State-of-the-art ConvNets for this task typically employ a siamese network trained by penalizing misclassification of pairs of local image patches.  Machine learning research suggests that replacing the siamese network with a triplet network can enhance classification accuracy in various problems. This paper proposes the use of triplet networks for local image descriptor learning, demonstrating its effectiveness for this specific task.  Moreover, the paper addresses the overfitting tendency of siamese and triplet networks trained with stochastic gradient descent by introducing a global loss that minimizes overall classification error in the training set. Using the UBC benchmark dataset, the study shows that the triplet network produces a more accurate embedding than the siamese network.  Further, the combination of triplet and global losses results in the most accurate embedding. Finally, the paper demonstrates that the central-surround siamese network trained with the global loss achieves the best performance on the UBC dataset.  Pre-trained models are available online at https://github.com/vijaykbg/deep-patchmatch.

title: Denoising and Completion of 3D Data via Multidimensional Dictionary Learning
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel dictionary learning algorithm for multidimensional data. Unlike traditional dictionary learning methods designed for vectors or matrices, the proposed algorithm, named KTSVD, learns a multidimensional dictionary directly through a novel algebraic approach for tensor factorization. This approach enables the definition of tensor-SVD, extending the K-SVD algorithm for 1-D data to K-TSVD for handling 2-D and 3-D data.  The algorithm, based on sparse coding using group-sparsity over multidimensional coefficient vectors, alternates between estimating a compact representation and dictionary learning. The paper analyzes the KTSVD algorithm and demonstrates its effectiveness in video completion and multispectral image denoising.
label: AI

title: Exploiting Local Structures with the Kronecker Layer in Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces a technique to reduce the number of parameters and computation time in convolutional neural networks.  The technique leverages the Kronecker product to exploit local structures within convolution and fully-connected layers.  Large weight matrices are replaced by combinations of multiple Kronecker products of smaller matrices. Similar to how the Kronecker product generalizes the outer product from vectors to matrices, this method generalizes the low-rank approximation method for convolutional neural networks.  The paper introduces combinations of different shapes of Kronecker products to enhance modeling capacity. Experiments on SVHN, scene text recognition, and ImageNet datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves significant speedup and parameter reduction with minimal accuracy loss. The computational efficiency of the Kronecker layer allows for the use of larger feature maps, resulting in state-of-the-art performance on SVHN (digit recognition) and CASIA-HWDB (handwritten Chinese character recognition) datasets.
label: AI

title: LIBSVX: A Supervoxel Library and Benchmark for Early Video Processing
Abstract: Supervoxel segmentation holds promise for early video analysis, similar to the role of superpixel segmentation in image analysis. However, the numerous supervoxel methods and lack of comparative studies make choosing the most appropriate method challenging. This research examines seven supervoxel algorithms, including both offline and streaming methods, based on desirable supervoxel characteristics: spatiotemporal uniformity, object/region boundary detection, region compression, and parsimony. A comprehensive suite of quality metrics is proposed to evaluate these characteristics. The study further evaluates the methods in a supervoxel classification task, serving as a proxy for high-level video analysis applications.  Six existing benchmark video datasets with diverse content types and dense human annotations are used for evaluation.  The findings conclusively identify the hierarchical graph-based (GBH), segmentation by weighted aggregation (SWA), and temporal superpixels (TSP) methods as top performers.  While all three methods exhibit high segmentation accuracy, they differ in other desirable features: GBH excels in object boundary capture, SWA offers the best potential for region compression, and TSP achieves the lowest undersegmentation error.

title: Actor-Action Semantic Segmentation with Grouping Process Models
Abstract: Actor-action semantic segmentation is a crucial step towards advanced video understanding problems, specifically determining what action is occurring, who is performing it, and where it takes place in space-time.  Current models for this problem are local, based on layered CRFs, and unable to capture long-range interactions of video parts. This paper proposes a new model that combines local labeling CRFs with a hierarchical supervoxel decomposition. Supervoxels provide cues for possible groupings of nodes at various scales in the CRFs, encouraging adaptive, high-order groups for more effective labeling. The model is dynamic, continuously exchanging information during inference: local CRFs influence active supervoxels in the hierarchy, and these active nodes influence CRF connectivity. The experimental results on a large-scale video dataset show a significant improvement over the state-of-the-art, demonstrating the effectiveness of the dynamic, bidirectional flow between labeling and grouping.
label: AI

title: Combined statistical and model based texture features for improved image classification
Abstract: This paper aims to improve the accuracy of texture classification by extracting texture features using five different methods and classifying the patterns using a naive Bayesian classifier.  Three statistical-based methods and two model-based methods are employed to extract texture features from eight distinct texture images. Their accuracy is then ranked based on individual and paired method use.  The accuracy significantly improves when model-based methods—Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) and fractional Brownian motion (fBm)—are used together for classification compared to using each method alone. This combination proves more effective than statistical methods.  Furthermore, combining GMRF with statistical methods such as Gray level co-occurrence (GLCM) and run-length (RLM) matrices improves the overall accuracy.

title: Robust Scene Text Recognition Using Sparse Coding based Features
Abstract: This paper proposes an effective scene text recognition method using sparse coding-based features, called Histograms of Sparse Codes (HSC) features.  For character detection, HSC features are used instead of Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) features.  HSC features are extracted by computing sparse codes with dictionaries learned from data using K-SVD and aggregating per-pixel sparse codes to form local histograms.  For word recognition, multiple cues, including character detection scores and geometric contexts, are integrated into an objective function. The final recognition results are obtained by searching for words that correspond to the maximum value of the objective function.  The parameters in the objective function are learned using the Minimum Classification Error (MCE) training method.  Experiments on challenging datasets demonstrate that the proposed HSC-based scene text recognition method outperforms HOG-based methods significantly and surpasses most state-of-the-art methods.

title: A framework for robust object multi-detection with a vote aggregation and a cascade filtering
Abstract: This paper presents a framework designed for multi-object detection purposes, specifically tailored for product search applications on market shelves. The framework utilizes a single feedback loop and a pattern resizing mechanism to showcase the effectiveness of state-of-the-art local features.  A high detection rate with a low false detection chance is achieved using only one pattern per object without manual parameter adjustments.  The method incorporates well-known local features and a basic matching process to create a reliable voting space. Further steps involve metric transformations, graphical vote space representation, a two-phase vote aggregation process, and a cascade of verifying filters. |||

title: Visually Indicated Sounds
Abstract: Sounds produced by objects when struck or scratched reveal information about their material properties and the actions causing them. We propose a new task: predicting the sound of an object struck, to understand physical interactions in visual scenes. Our algorithm generates sound from silent videos of object strikes, using a recurrent neural network to predict sound features from videos, and then producing a waveform from these features through an example-based synthesis process. We demonstrate the realism of our model's sound predictions by fooling participants in a "real or fake" psychophysical experiment, showing that the sounds convey significant information about material properties and physical interactions.

title: MRF-Based Multispectral Image Fusion Using an Adaptive Approach Based on Edge-Guided Interpolation
Abstract: Interpreting remote sensing images from diverse sensors can be challenging due to their inherent complexity. Pre-processing and elementary corrections are crucial for enhancing image perception, followed by main processing steps for precise analysis. Image fusion, a common approach, combines optical images with grayscale satellite images to improve observation. This paper explores the impact of interpolation methods on the quality of image fusion in Landsat-8 multispectral images. Traditional interpolation techniques like bi-linear (BL) and bi-cubic/cubic convolution (CC) are often used in image fusion, but we introduce a statistical, adaptive, and edge-guided interpolation method. Numerical simulations show that selecting the suitable interpolation technique in MRF-based images leads to higher quality results than classical interpolators.

title: Graph entropies in texture segmentation of images
Abstract: This study investigates the application of texture descriptors, derived from graph indices in quantitative graph theory, for texture-based image segmentation. The texture descriptors are computed from graphs encoding the local image structure, based on morphological amoebas as structuring elements. We focus on entropy-based graph indices and utilize them in a geodesic active contour framework for image segmentation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world images demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach. We also analyze the information encoded by selected entropy-based texture descriptors, indicating a potential relationship to fractal dimension measures, which have proven valuable in texture analysis.
label: AI

title: Outlier Detection In Large-scale Traffic Data By Naïve Bayes Method and Gaussian Mixture Model Method
Abstract: Detecting outliers in traffic data is crucial for effective traffic management, but manual analysis of large-scale datasets is time-consuming and challenging. This paper presents two automatic outlier detection methods: Kernel Smoothing Naive Bayes (NB) and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), for identifying hardware errors and abnormal traffic events in traffic data collected at a four-arm junction in Hong Kong. Traffic data, initially captured as video, is converted to spatial-temporal (ST) traffic signals using statistical analysis and subsequently projected to a 2D (x,y)-coordinate plane through Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimension reduction. The NB and GMM methods, assuming inlier data are normally distributed, are applied for outlier detection (OD). The kernel smooth NB method assumes the presence of kernel distributions in traffic data and employs Bayes' Theorem for OD, while the GMM method assumes a mixture of Gaussian distributions and utilizes confidence regions for OD. Experimental results show that the NB algorithm with Triangle kernel and GMM method achieve up to 93.78% and 94.50% accuracies, respectively.

title: Statistical and Computational Guarantees for the Baum-Welch Algorithm
Abstract: The Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is widely used in statistical modeling of discrete time series, with applications in various fields. Estimating an HMM from its observation process is typically addressed using the Baum-Welch algorithm, known to be susceptible to local optima. This paper provides a general characterization of the basin of attraction associated with any global optimum of the population likelihood, enabling us to provide non-asymptotic finite sample guarantees on the Baum-Welch updates. These guarantees ensure geometric convergence to a small ball of radius on the order of the minimax rate around a global optimum. We prove a linear rate of convergence for a hidden Markov mixture of two isotropic Gaussians with suitable mean separation and initialization. To our knowledge, these are the first rigorous local convergence guarantees to global optima for the Baum-Welch algorithm in a non-convex setting. Our theoretical results are complemented by numerical simulations that study the algorithm's convergence and illustrate the accuracy of our predictions.

title: Improving Facial Analysis and Performance Driven Animation through Disentangling Identity and Expression
Abstract: This paper presents techniques for enhancing performance-driven facial animation, emotion recognition, and facial key-point prediction using learned identity-invariant representations. Existing approaches often struggle when faced with new individuals or uncontrolled variations. By explicitly modeling identity-related variations separately from expression variations, we improve generalization to unseen individuals. A weakly-supervised approach is employed, using identity labels to learn separate factors of variation. Probabilistic modeling of these variations allows us to learn identity-invariant representations for expressions, which can then be used to identity-normalize various procedures. The widely used techniques of active appearance models and constrained local models are extended by replacing their underlying point distribution models with identity-expression factorized representations. Experimental results consistently demonstrate improved performance in emotion recognition, markerless performance-driven facial animation, and facial key-point tracking.

title: Data Driven Robust Image Guided Depth Map Restoration
Abstract: Depth maps captured by modern depth cameras often suffer from missing data, noise, and low resolution. This paper presents a robust method for high-quality restoration of degraded depth maps guided by the corresponding color image. We formulate the problem within an energy optimization framework, incorporating a novel robust data term and smoothness term. To accommodate both noise and inconsistency between depth discontinuities and color edges, both terms are modeled using a robust exponential error norm function. Iteratively Re-weighted Least Squares (IRLS) methods are employed to efficiently solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem. A data-driven adaptive parameter selection scheme is further developed to accurately determine the model parameter. The proposed approach preserves fine details and sharp depth discontinuities even for large upsampling factors. Experimental results on simulated and real datasets demonstrate the method's superior performance compared to recent state-of-the-art methods in handling heavy noise, preserving sharp depth discontinuities, and suppressing texture copy artifacts.

title: Part-Stacked CNN for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization
Abstract: In the context of fine-grained visual categorization, model interpretability is as crucial as achieving high classification accuracy. This paper proposes a novel Part-Stacked CNN architecture that explicitly explains the fine-grained recognition process by modeling subtle differences from object parts. Utilizing manually-labeled part annotations, the architecture consists of a fully convolutional network for object part localization and a two-stream classification network that simultaneously encodes object-level and part-level cues. Sharing strategies between multiple object parts ensure efficient computation, achieving 20 frames/sec during inference. Experimental results on the CUB-200-2011 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture in terms of both classification accuracy and model interpretability.

title: A Multiresolution Clinical Decision Support System Based on Fractal Model Design for Classification of Histological Brain Tumours
Abstract: Tissue texture exhibits heterogeneity and non-stationary characteristics, making a single-resolution approach insufficient for optimal classification. This paper proposes a clinical decision support system that exploits subband textural fractal characteristics for selecting the best bases in meningioma brain histopathological image classification. Each subband is analyzed using its fractal dimension instead of energy, offering less sensitivity to image intensity and abrupt texture changes. The most significant subband, best identifying texture discontinuities, is further decomposed, and its fractal characteristics represent the optimal feature vector for classification. The performance of the system was evaluated using support vector machine (SVM), Bayesian, and k-nearest neighbor (kNN) classifiers, employing a leave-one-patient-out method for validation. Our method outperformed classical energy-based selection approaches, achieving overall classification accuracies of 94.12%, 92.50%, and 79.70% for SVM, Bayesian, and kNN classifiers, respectively, compared to 86.31%, 83.19%, and 51.63% for the co-occurrence matrix, and 76.01%, 73.50%, and 50.69% for energy texture signatures. These results demonstrate the potential usefulness of this decision support system in complementing radiologists' diagnostic capabilities by discriminating higher-order statistical textural information.

title: Texture measures combination for improved meningioma classification of histopathological images
Abstract: This paper aims to provide an improved technique for assisting pathologists in accurately classifying meningioma tumors. The proposed technique, based on optimal texture measure combination, examines the separability of RGB color channels and selects the channel that best segments cell nuclei in histopathological images. The morphological gradient is applied to extract the region of interest for each subtype and eliminate noise. Meningioma texture features are extracted using four texture measures (two model-based and two statistical-based) and fused together in different combinations after excluding highly correlated features. A Bayesian classifier is then used for meningioma subtype discrimination. The combined Gaussian Markov random field and run-length matrix texture measures outperform all other combinations in characterizing meningioma tissue, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 92.50%, an improvement from 83.75%, the best accuracy achieved when using individual texture measures.

title: Assessment of texture measures susceptibility to noise in conventional and contrast enhanced computed tomography lung tumour images
Abstract: Noise is a major challenge in medical image texture analysis, potentially causing variability in disease diagnosis. This paper investigates the susceptibility of seven texture measurement methods (two wavelet, two model, and three statistical based) to subtle noise in computed tomography (CT) images. Features of lung tumors were extracted from two CT image datasets under filtered and noisy conditions. Noise analysis in the background region revealed Gaussian and Rayleigh distributions with varying mean and variance. Fisher distance was used to differentiate between the original extracted lung tumor region of interest (ROI) and its filtered and noisy versions. The wavelet packet (WP) and fractal dimension measures were found to be least affected, while Gaussian Markov random field, run-length, and co-occurrence matrices were most affected by noise. The study concludes that texture measures with fewer extracted features can reduce susceptibility to noise, with WP and the Gabor filter demonstrating stable performance in both filtered and noisy CT versions and for both datasets. Understanding the robustness of each texture measure in the presence of noise can guide physicians in choosing the appropriate feature extraction algorithm for more accurate diagnosis using an automated lung texture classification system.

title: A Combined Deep-Learning and Deformable-Model Approach to Fully Automatic Segmentation of the Left Ventricle in Cardiac MRI
Abstract: Segmenting the left ventricle (LV) from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets is crucial for calculating clinical indices like ventricular volume and ejection fraction. This work proposes a fully automatic LV segmentation tool using deep learning algorithms combined with deformable models. Convolutional networks are employed to automatically detect the LV chamber in MRI datasets, while stacked autoencoders infer the shape of the LV. The inferred shape is integrated into deformable models to enhance segmentation accuracy and robustness. Validation using 45 cardiac MR datasets from the MICCAI 2009 LV segmentation challenge demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Excellent agreement with ground truth was achieved, with validation metrics: percentage of good contours (96.69%), Dice metric (0.94), average perpendicular distance (1.81 mm), and conformity (0.86), outperforming other methods (79.2%-95.62%, 0.87-0.9, 1.76-2.97 mm, and 0.67-0.78, respectively).

title: Sparse Reconstruction of Compressive Sensing MRI using Cross-Domain Stochastically Fully Connected Conditional Random Fields
Abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a vital medical imaging technology for cancer screening and diagnosis. However, long acquisition times due to patient motion can affect image quality and cause patient discomfort. Compressive sensing strategies have been proven effective in reducing acquisition times by sparsely sampling the k-space during acquisition. However, this requires advanced reconstruction algorithms to produce high-quality images. This paper proposes a new reconstruction approach based on cross-domain stochastically fully connected conditional random fields (CD-SFCRF) for compressive sensing MRI. CD-SFCRF introduces constraints in both k-space and spatial domains within a stochastically fully connected graphical model to enhance reconstruction. Experimental results using T2-weighted (T2w) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) of the prostate show strong performance in preserving fine details and tissue structures in reconstructed images, even at low sampling rates.

title: Learning Transferrable Knowledge for Semantic Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Neural Network
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel weakly-supervised semantic segmentation algorithm based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) that leverages auxiliary segmentation annotations for different categories to guide segmentations on images with only image-level class labels. To facilitate knowledge transfer across categories, a decoupled encoder-decoder architecture with an attention model is designed. The model generates spatial highlights of each category using an attention model and subsequently generates foreground segmentation for each highlighted region using the decoder. Combining the attention model, the decoder trained with segmentation annotations from different categories can significantly improve the performance of weakly-supervised semantic segmentation. Experiments on the challenging PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset demonstrate substantially improved performance compared to state-of-the-art weakly-supervised techniques when our model is trained with annotations from 60 exclusive categories in the Microsoft COCO dataset.

title: Truncated Max-of-Convex Models
Abstract: Truncated convex models (TCM) are a special case of pairwise random fields widely used in computer vision. However, their limitations in capturing useful image statistics due to the restriction on potential order led to the development of truncated max-of-convex models (TMCM). TMCM generalizes TCM to high-order random fields, with an energy function consisting of unary and clique potentials. The unary potential has no form restrictions, while the clique potential is the sum of the m largest truncated convex distances over all label pairs in a clique. This approach encourages smoothness through the convex distance function and allows for discontinuities in labeling. TMCM's robustness towards clique definition errors is achieved by using m > 1. To minimize the energy function over all possible labelings, an efficient st-MINCUT based range expansion algorithm is designed. The algorithm's accuracy is demonstrated by establishing strong multiplicative bounds for several special cases. Experiments using synthetic and real datasets highlight the benefits of high-order TMCM over pairwise TCM and the superiority of the range expansion algorithm over other st-MINCUT based approaches.
