title: G-CNN: an Iterative Grid Based Object Detector
Abstract: We introduce G-CNN, an object detection technique based on CNNs that operates without proposal algorithms. G-CNN utilizes a multi-scale grid of fixed bounding boxes and trains a regressor to iteratively move and scale grid elements towards objects. Object detection is modeled as finding a path from a fixed grid to boxes tightly surrounding objects. G-CNN with around 180 boxes in a multi-scale grid performs comparably to Fast R-CNN, which uses approximately 2K bounding boxes generated using a proposal technique. This approach accelerates detection by eliminating the object proposal stage and reducing the number of boxes to be processed.
label: AI

title: Fast Acquisition for Quantitative MRI Maps: Sparse Recovery from Non-linear Measurements
Abstract: This work addresses the problem of estimating proton density and T1 maps from two partially sampled K-space scans while maintaining a total acquisition time similar to a single scan. Existing multiparametric nonlinear curve fitting techniques require a large number of echoes, leading to prolonged acquisition times. Our simulation results demonstrate accurate and robust results using only two partially sampled scans. We model PD and T1 maps as sparse in some transform domain. The PD map is recovered using standard Compressed Sensing based recovery techniques. Estimating the T1 map involves solving an analysis prior sparse recovery problem from nonlinear measurements. We propose a novel algorithm for analysis prior sparse recovery for nonlinear measurements. Comparison with the only existing technique based on matrix factorization from nonlinear measurements shows significantly superior results for our method.
label: AI

title: Adaptive Object Detection Using Adjacency and Zoom Prediction
Abstract: State-of-the-art object detection systems rely on accurate region proposals. Recent methods utilize neural network architectures to hypothesize promising object locations. While computationally efficient, these approaches rely on fixed image regions as anchors for predictions. This paper proposes a search strategy that adaptively directs computational resources to sub-regions likely to contain objects. Compared to methods based on fixed anchor locations, our approach naturally adapts to cases with sparse and small objects. The accuracy of our approach is comparable to the state-of-the-art Faster R-CNN while using two orders of magnitude fewer anchors on average. Code is publicly available.
label: AI

title: On the Automated Synthesis of Enterprise Integration Patterns to Adapt Choreography-based Distributed Systems
Abstract: The Future Internet is becoming a reality, offering large-scale computing environments with a virtually infinite number of available services. Modern service-oriented applications are increasingly built by reusing and assembling distributed services. Automatic composition and dynamic coordination of software services are key enablers for this vision. Service choreographies, an emerging Service Engineering (SE) approach, are used to compose and coordinate services in a distributed manner. When mismatching third-party services need to be composed, obtaining the distributed coordination and adaptation logic required to realize a choreography is a challenging task. This paper leverages previous work on automatic synthesis of choreography-based systems and describes preliminary steps towards utilizing Enterprise Integration Patterns to address a form of choreography adaptation.
label: AI

title: A Latent-Variable Lattice Model
Abstract: Markov random field (MRF) learning is computationally expensive and intractable. We focus on a subset of MRF frequently used in computer vision, characterized by three concepts: Lattice, Homogeneity, and Inertia, and propose a non-Markov model as an alternative. Our goal is robust learning from small datasets. Our learning algorithm employs vector quantization, achieving a time complexity of O(U log U) for a dataset of U pixels, significantly faster than general-purpose MRF.
label: AI

title: Recovering 6D Object Pose and Predicting Next-Best-View in the Crowd
Abstract: Object detection and 6D pose estimation in crowded scenes, with multiple object instances, severe occlusions, and distracting backgrounds, are crucial challenges in robotics and augmented reality. While single-shot 6D pose estimators using manually designed features struggle with these challenges, this work explores unsupervised feature learning and next-best-view estimation. We introduce a comprehensive framework for both single-shot 6D object pose estimation and next-best-view prediction based on Hough Forests, a state-of-the-art object pose estimator that combines classification and regression.  Instead of relying on manually designed features, we: (a) propose unsupervised feature learning from depth-invariant patches using a Sparse Autoencoder and (b) conduct an extensive evaluation of various state-of-the-art features. Leveraging the clustering in Hough Forest leaf nodes, we learn to estimate uncertainty reduction in different views, formulating the next-best-view selection problem.  To further enhance pose estimation, we introduce an improved joint registration and hypothesis verification module as a final refinement step to filter out false detections. We provide two new challenging datasets inspired by real-world scenarios: one focused on domestic environments and the other on bin-picking tasks commonly found in industrial settings. Our framework demonstrates significant performance improvements over existing methods on both public and our new datasets.
label: AI

title: Convolutional Architecture Exploration for Action Recognition and Image Classification
Abstract: This report explores a Caffe feature extraction pipeline for images extracted from videos in the UCF Sports Action dataset.  This dataset comprises 200 videos with 9 different sports activities (diving, golf, swinging, kicking, lifting, horseback riding, running, skateboarding, swinging, and walking) recorded in 720x480 resolution. We investigate the architecture and hyperparameters necessary for effective static analysis of action in videos and classification across various image datasets. Our results indicate that Caffe outperforms Overfeat in this context.
label: AI

title: A Deep Generative Deconvolutional Image Model
Abstract: This paper introduces a deep generative model for image representation and analysis, built upon a hierarchical convolutional dictionary-learning framework.  Stochastic unpooling is employed to connect consecutive layers in the model, enabling top-down image generation.  A Bayesian support vector machine is linked to the top-layer features, providing max-margin discrimination.  During testing, deep deconvolutional inference infers latent features, and the top-layer features are connected to the max-margin classifier for discrimination tasks. The model is trained efficiently using a Monte Carlo expectation-maximization (MCEM) algorithm, leveraging GPU acceleration for large-scale learning and fast testing.  Excellent results are obtained on benchmark datasets, including ImageNet, demonstrating the model's competitiveness with similarly sized convolutional neural networks.
label: AI

title: Plug-and-Play Priors for Bright Field Electron Tomography and Sparse Interpolation
Abstract: Many materials and biological samples in scientific imaging exhibit non-local repeating structures. These are studied using scanning electron microscopy and electron tomography. Sparse sampling of individual pixels in 2D image acquisition or sparse sampling of projection images with large tilt increments in tomography experiments allow for high-speed data acquisition and minimize sample damage from the electron beam. This paper presents an algorithm for electron tomographic reconstruction and sparse image interpolation that exploits non-local redundancy in images. We adapt a plug-and-play (P&P) prior framework to solve these imaging problems in a regularized inversion setting.  The P&P approach allows for the use of modern denoising algorithms as "prior models" for tomography and image interpolation.  We also present sufficient mathematical conditions for convergence of the P&P approach and use these insights to design a new non-local means denoising algorithm. We demonstrate that the algorithm produces higher quality reconstructions on both simulated and real electron microscope data, exhibiting improved convergence properties compared to other methods.
label: AI

title: Mid-level Representation for Visual Recognition
Abstract: Visual recognition, a fundamental challenge in AI, aims to understand the semantics of visual data. Mid-level representation has significantly shifted the paradigm in visual recognition by focusing on discovering and training a set of mid-level visual patterns (e.g., parts and attributes) to represent images and videos. These patterns can be extracted from images and videos using motion and appearance information of visual phenomena. This thesis focuses on employing mid-level representations for various high-level visual recognition tasks, specifically (i) image understanding and (ii) video understanding.  In image understanding, we concentrate on object detection/recognition, investigating the discovery and learning of mid-level patches for representing images within an object category. We employ discriminative patches in a subcategory-aware webly-supervised manner and analyze the outcomes of employing subcategory-based models for mitigating dataset bias.
label: AI

title: Do Less and Achieve More: Training CNNs for Action Recognition Utilizing Action Images from the Web
Abstract: Recent efforts have focused on collecting millions of videos for training CNN models for action recognition. However, creating such large-scale datasets requires substantial human effort, and training on millions of videos necessitates significant computational resources. In contrast, collecting action images from the web is much easier and training on images requires significantly less computation. Additionally, labeled web images tend to contain discriminative action poses, highlighting important parts of a video's temporal progression. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing web action images to train better CNN models for action recognition in videos. We collect 23.8K manually filtered images from the web depicting the 101 actions in the UCF101 action video dataset.  Our findings demonstrate that training with both web action images and videos results in significant performance improvements for CNN models. We then investigate the scalability of this approach by leveraging crawled web images (unfiltered) for UCF101 and ActivityNet. By replacing 16.2M video frames with 393K unfiltered images, we achieve comparable performance.
label: AI

title: SR-Clustering: Semantic Regularized Clustering for Egocentric Photo Streams Segmentation
Abstract: While wearable cameras are becoming increasingly popular, searching for relevant information within large, unstructured collections of egocentric images remains a tedious and time-consuming process. This paper tackles the problem of organizing egocentric photo streams acquired by a wearable camera into semantically meaningful segments. We first extract contextual and semantic information for each image using a Convolutional Neural Network approach.  Then, by integrating language processing, we define a vocabulary of concepts within a semantic space. Finally, by exploiting the temporal coherence in photo streams, images sharing contextual and semantic attributes are grouped together. The resulting temporal segmentation is well-suited for further analysis, ranging from activity and event recognition to semantic indexing and summarization. Experiments on a set of nearly 17,000 egocentric images demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Recent Advances in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: In recent years, deep learning has achieved remarkable performance on various tasks such as visual recognition, speech recognition, and natural language processing. Among different types of deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks have received extensive research attention.  The rapid growth in annotated data and advancements in graphics processing units have fueled swift progress in convolutional neural networks, leading to state-of-the-art results on diverse tasks. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of recent advances in convolutional neural networks. We delve into improvements across different aspects, including layer design, activation functions, loss functions, regularization, optimization, and fast computation. We also explore various applications of convolutional neural networks in computer vision, speech, and natural language processing.
label: AI

title: Cost-based Feature Transfer for Vehicle Occupant Classification
Abstract: Understanding human presence and interaction in vehicles is increasingly important for vehicle manufacturers for design and safety purposes. This paper presents a framework for occupant detection and occupant classification for automatic child locks and airbag suppression. The system operates on all passenger seats using a single overhead camera. We introduce a transfer learning technique to fully utilize training data from all seats while maintaining control over bias, essential for a system designed to penalize certain misclassifications more heavily than others. Our evaluation on a challenging dataset with both weighted and unweighted classifiers demonstrates the effectiveness of the transfer learning process.
label: AI

title: Implementation of deep learning algorithm for automatic detection of brain tumors using intraoperative IR-thermal mapping data
Abstract: Deep machine learning has proven effective for automatic delineation of tumor areas during intraoperative neuronavigation using active IR-mapping with the cold test. This approach uses a matrix IR-imager to remotely register the space-time distribution of surface temperature patterns, determined by the dynamics of local cerebral blood flow. This technique offers non-invasiveness, zero risks for patients and medical staff, low implementation and operational costs, and ease and speed of use. Traditional IR-diagnostic techniques have a major limitation: they rely on a diagnostician to determine tumor boundaries, introducing significant uncertainty and potential diagnosis errors that are difficult to control. This study demonstrates that implementing deep learning algorithms eliminates this drawback.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning with S-shaped Rectified Linear Activation Units
Abstract: Rectified linear activation units are essential components of state-of-the-art deep convolutional networks. This paper proposes a novel S-shaped rectified linear activation unit (SReLU) to learn both convex and non-convex functions, mimicking the multiple function forms observed in the Webner-Fechner and Stevens laws in psychophysics and neural sciences. SReLU consists of three piecewise linear functions defined by four learnable parameters.  SReLU is learned jointly with the training of the entire deep network through backpropagation. During training, we propose a "freezing" method to initialize SReLU in different layers. This method initially degenerates SReLU into a predefined leaky rectified linear unit for the first few training epochs before adaptively learning suitable initial values. SReLU can be universally used in existing deep networks with minimal additional parameters and computational cost. Experiments using two popular CNN architectures (Network in Network and GoogLeNet) on various benchmarks (CIFAR10, CIFAR100, MNIST, and ImageNet) demonstrate SReLU's significant improvement over other activation functions.
label: AI

title: Seeing through the Human Reporting Bias: Visual Classifiers from Noisy Human-Centric Labels
Abstract: Human annotators, when given choices for labeling an image, apply subjective judgments on what to ignore and what to mention, leading to "human-centric" annotations with inherent human reporting bias. Examples include image tags and keywords found on photo sharing sites or in datasets containing image captions. This paper explores the use of these noisy annotations for learning visually correct image classifiers. While these annotations lack consistent vocabulary and miss significant image information, we show that the noise exhibits structure and can be modeled. We propose an algorithm to decouple human reporting bias from the correct visually grounded labels. Our results are highly interpretable, distinguishing between "what's in the image" and "what's worth saying." We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness across various metrics and datasets, including MS COCO and Yahoo Flickr 100M.  Our findings show significant improvements over traditional algorithms for both image classification and image captioning, doubling the performance of existing methods in some cases.
label: AI

title: Multi-Instance Visual-Semantic Embedding
Abstract: Visual-semantic embedding models, which map images into a continuous semantic label space, have shown effectiveness for image classification and zero-shot learning. While several approaches have been proposed for single-label embedding tasks, handling images with multiple labels (a more general setting) remains an open problem due to the complex relationship between images and their labels. This paper presents a Multi-Instance visual-semantic Embedding (MIE) model for embedding images with either single or multiple labels.  Our model discovers and maps semantically meaningful image subregions to their corresponding labels.  We demonstrate the superiority of our method on two tasks: multi-label image annotation and zero-shot learning.
label: AI

title: Transformed Residual Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
Abstract: Product quantization (PQ) is a technique for fast nearest neighbor search, relying on exponentially reduced storage and computational complexities relative to the codebook size. Recent research has focused on employing advanced optimization strategies and exploring more effective models. Residual quantization (RQ) is an alternative approach that shares the same complexity benefits as PQ.  Beyond being a direct replacement for PQ, hybrids of PQ and RQ can yield further gains for approximate nearest neighbor search. This motivates us to propose a novel approach to optimizing RQ and related hybrid models. Recognizing the increase in general randomness in a residual space, we introduce a new strategy that jointly learns a local transformation per residual cluster with the aim of reducing overall quantization errors. We demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms both the original and optimized PQ on several large-scale benchmarks in terms of nearest neighbor search accuracy.
label: AI

title: Car Segmentation and Pose Estimation using 3D Object Models
Abstract: Image segmentation and 3D pose estimation are crucial components for scene understanding. However, state-of-the-art CRF-based models for image segmentation primarily rely on 2D object models to construct top-down high-order potentials. This paper introduces new top-down potentials for image segmentation and pose estimation based on the shape and volume of a 3D object model. We show that these complex top-down potentials can be efficiently decomposed into standard forms for inference in both segmentation and pose estimation tasks.  Experiments on a car dataset demonstrate that knowledge of segmentation improves pose estimation, and vice versa.
label: AI

title: Beyond Classification: Latent User Interests Profiling from Visual Contents Analysis
Abstract: User preference profiling is a key task in modern online social networks (OSN). With the rise of image-centric platforms like Pinterest, visual content has become a valuable data source for understanding user preferences. Traditional approaches typically treat visual content analysis as a general classification problem, assigning one or more labels to each image. This simplification overlooks the rich context and visual cues that significantly influence people's perception of images. This paper explores learning a user's latent visual preferences directly from image content. We propose a distance metric learning method based on Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to directly extract similarity information from visual content and use the derived distance metric to mine individual users' fine-grained visual preferences. Our preliminary experiments using data from 5,790 Pinterest users show that even within the same category, each user exhibits distinct and individually identifiable visual preferences that are consistent over time.  Our results highlight the untapped potential of finer-grained visual preference profiling for understanding users' preferences.
label: AI

title: GraphConnect: A Regularization Framework for Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks have proven highly successful in domains with large training sets, but their performance suffers from overfitting when the number of training samples is small. Prior methods for reducing overfitting, such as weight decay, Dropout, and DropConnect, are data-independent. This paper proposes a new data-dependent method, GraphConnect, motivated by the observation that data of interest lie close to a manifold. GraphConnect encourages the relationships between learned decisions to resemble a graph representing the manifold structure.  Essentially, GraphConnect is designed to learn attributes present in data samples, contrasting with weight decay, Dropout, and DropConnect, which simply aim to hinder fitting to random error or noise. Empirical Rademacher complexity is used to connect the generalization error of the neural network to spectral properties of the graph learned from the input data. This framework is used to demonstrate GraphConnect's superiority to weight decay. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets validate the theoretical analysis and show that GraphConnect significantly improves performance over weight decay when the number of training samples is small.
label: AI

title: Instance-Level Segmentation for Autonomous Driving with Deep Densely Connected MRFs
Abstract: This paper aims to provide pixel-wise instance-level labeling of a monocular image in the context of autonomous driving. Building upon recent work, we train a convolutional neural network to predict instance labeling in local image patches extracted exhaustively from an image. A simple Markov random field model using several heuristics was proposed to derive a globally consistent instance labeling of the image. In this paper, we formulate the global labeling problem using a novel densely connected Markov random field and show how to encode various intuitive potentials for efficient mean field inference. Our potentials encode compatibility between the global labeling and patch-level predictions, contrast-sensitive smoothness, and the fact that separate regions form different instances. Experiments on the challenging KITTI benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves a significant performance improvement over the baseline.
label: AI

title: Multilinear Subspace Clustering
Abstract: This paper presents a new model and algorithm for unsupervised clustering of 2-D data, such as images. We assume that the data comes from a union of multilinear subspaces (UOMS) model, a structured case of the well-studied union of subspaces (UOS) model. For segmentation under this model, we develop the Multilinear Subspace Clustering (MSC) algorithm and evaluate its performance on the YaleB and Olivetti image datasets. We show that MSC is highly competitive with existing algorithms employing the UOS model in terms of clustering performance while achieving improvements in computational complexity.
label: AI

title: Sparse Coding with Fast Image Alignment via Large Displacement Optical Flow
Abstract: Sparse representation-based classifiers have demonstrated outstanding accuracy and robustness in image classification tasks, even with intense noise and occlusion. However, their performance degrades significantly when test images are misaligned with dictionary atoms or when dictionary atoms themselves are misaligned. This occurs because the sparse linear representation assumption fails in such cases. This paper addresses the scenario where both training and test images are misaligned. We introduce a novel sparse coding framework that efficiently adapts dictionary atoms to the test image using large displacement optical flow. In our algorithm, each dictionary atom is automatically aligned with the input image, and the sparse code is then recovered using the adapted dictionary atoms.  A corresponding supervised dictionary learning algorithm is also developed for this framework. Experimental results on digit dataset recognition confirm the efficacy and robustness of our proposed algorithm. |||
label: AI

title: Deep Learning for Surface Material Classification Using Haptic And Visual Information
Abstract: A deep learning method is introduced for surface material classification using acceleration signals and corresponding image textures. This method employs a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) to automatically extract discriminative features from the combined input modalities. Experiments using the TUM surface material database demonstrate state-of-the-art classification accuracy, outperforming methods relying on hand-crafted features.
label: AI

title: Local and global gestalt laws: A neurally based spectral approach
Abstract: A mathematical model is presented that combines local and global Gestalt laws for figure-ground articulation. The model aligns with the functional architecture of the primary visual cortex (V1), particularly the local law of good continuity, which is represented using connectivity kernels derived from Lie group theory. These kernels, implementing long-range connectivity in V1, are based on solutions to different equations: Fokker-Planck, Sub-Riemannian Laplacian, and isotropic Laplacian. Global Gestalt constraints are incorporated via spectral analysis of the connectivity matrix, which can be implemented in V1 by mean field neural equations. This approach identifies perceptual units with the highest saliency by grouping local features. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the model on a variety of stimuli.
label: AI

title: Analysis of Vessel Connectivities in Retinal Images by Cortically Inspired Spectral Clustering
Abstract: This study proposes a contextual method based on the geometry of the primary visual cortex (V1) for analyzing retinal images and detecting signs of diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and hypertension. The method utilizes a connectivity kernel derived from the Fokker-Planck equation to address challenges at vessel junctions. Spectral clustering on a local affinity matrix, built using the connectivity kernel and intensity features, enables the hierarchical identification of vessels as individual perceptual units.
label: AI

title: Spatial Phase-Sweep: Increasing temporal resolution of transient imaging using a light source array
Abstract: This paper introduces "spatial phase-sweep," a technique for capturing transient images beyond the temporal resolution limitations of current electronics. This technique exploits the speed of light by using a linear array of light sources with spatial separation, resulting in a time shift and theoretically achieving 100 Gfps of transient imaging. A prototype and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the technique.
label: AI

title: Harnessing the Deep Net Object Models for Enhancing Human Action Recognition
Abstract: This study investigates the influence of objects in human action recognition with a large number of classes. The hypothesis is that interacting objects play a significant role in determining the action being performed. To address the limitation of spatio-temporal features in detecting non-moving objects, pre-trained object detectors are employed in every frame. Deep network models are used as object detectors, and various layers and encoding techniques are explored to extract rich feature vectors. This approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on HMDB51 and UCF101 datasets.
label: AI

title: Remote Health Coaching System and Human Motion Data Analysis for Physical Therapy with Microsoft Kinect
Abstract: This paper presents the latest advancements in computer vision technologies for physical therapy using accessible and affordable devices. A remote health coaching system built with Microsoft Kinect is introduced, and the data accuracy of Kinect is investigated. An outlier data removal algorithm is proposed based on data distribution. To extract kinematic parameters from noisy Kinect data, a kinematic filtering algorithm is developed using Unscented Kalman Filter and a human skeleton model. The proposed algorithm generates smooth kinematic parameters with reduced noise compared to raw motion data.
label: AI

title: Quantized Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Devices
Abstract: This paper proposes Quantized CNN, an efficient framework for speeding up computation and reducing storage and memory overhead of convolutional neural networks (CNN). Both filter kernels and weighting matrices are quantized to minimize estimation errors. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant speed-up (4~6x) and compression (15~20x) with minimal accuracy loss. This allows for accurate image classification on mobile devices within one second.
label: AI

title: Kernel principal component analysis network for image classification
Abstract: A deep learning network named Kernel Principal Component Analysis Network (KPCANet) is introduced to classify non-linear features with linear classifiers and improve classification accuracy. KPCANet maps data into a higher space using kernel principal component analysis to achieve linear separability. It then builds a two-layer network to extract principal components, which are finally classified using a linear classifier. Experiments show effectiveness in face, object, and handwriting digit recognition, outperforming Principal Component Analysis Network (PCANet). KPCANet is also invariant to illumination and robust to occlusion and slight deformations.
label: AI

title: Neutro-Connectedness Cut
Abstract: Interactive image segmentation is a challenging task. Existing methods suffer from sensitivity to initial ROI in ROI-based approaches and intensive interactions in seed-based approaches. This paper introduces a novel method called Neutro-Connectedness Cut (NC-Cut) to address these limitations. NC-Cut generalizes Neutro-Connectedness (NC) to be independent of object priors and model image topology with indeterminacy measurements. It excludes isolated background regions and enforces label consistency. By integrating pixel-wise appearance information and region-based NC properties, NC-Cut outperforms state-of-the-art interactive image segmentation methods.
label: AI

title: Multistage SFM: A Coarse-to-Fine Approach for 3D Reconstruction
Abstract: This paper proposes a multistage approach for structure from motion (SFM) reconstruction of large-scale 3D models from unorganized image collections. The approach overcomes the sequential nature of incremental SFM methods by first building a coarse 3D model using a fraction of features. Subsequent stages enrich the model by localizing remaining images and matching features, leveraging the coarse model's geometry for efficiency and parallelism. The method achieves comparable model quality to incremental SFM while being faster and parallel.
label: AI

title: Combining patch-based strategies and non-rigid registration-based label fusion methods
Abstract: A novel patch-based label fusion method is presented for automatic hippocampal segmentation in T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The method combines intensity-based and labeling-based similarity measures to select patches and calculate weights. This approach improves patch selection and weight robustness, leading to better segmentation results than other label fusion methods. Experiments on two databases demonstrate competitive performance in terms of Dice coefficients and computational efficiency.
label: AI

title: Poseidon: A System Architecture for Efficient GPU-based Deep Learning on Multiple Machines
Abstract: This paper proposes Poseidon, a scalable system architecture for distributed inter-machine communication in deep learning frameworks. It aims to accelerate deep neural network (DNN) training on clusters by enabling the efficient utilization of distributed GPUs. Poseidon features a hybrid architecture, a distributed wait-free backpropagation (DWBP) algorithm, and a structure-aware communication protocol (SACP) to minimize communication overheads. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art training speedup across multiple models and datasets, achieving significant improvements over single-machine training.
label: AI

title: Modeling Colors of Single Attribute Variations with Application to Food Appearance
Abstract: This paper investigates the intra-image color space of objects or scenes subject to a dominant single-source of variation. The analysis shows that quantized colors often lie on a planar subspace of RGB, with linear or polynomial curves effectively capturing color variations. The inter-image color sub-spaces are robust as long as drastic illumination changes are absent. The analysis is illustrated for discriminating between shading and reflectance changes, as well as for object detection, segmentation, and recognition using a single exemplar. The paper focuses on images of food items to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.
label: AI

title: Multiclass Classification of Cervical Cancer Tissues by Hidden Markov Model
Abstract: This paper presents a hidden Markov model based multiclass classification method for cervical cancer tissues. The model is validated on time series generated by medium refractive index fluctuations extracted from differential interference contrast images. The method shows promising results for multiclass classification with higher accuracy.
label: AI

title: Face Hallucination using Linear Models of Coupled Sparse Support
Abstract: Most face super-resolution methods assume similar local geometrical structure between low-resolution and high-resolution manifolds. This paper proposes a method that learns linear models based on the high-resolution manifold instead. It first derives a globally optimal estimate of the high-resolution patch from the low-resolution one, then uses sparse coding to find the support of the high-resolution manifold. Finally, a local projection model is learned using Multivariate Ridge Regression. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in terms of recognition and quality compared to other methods.
label: AI

title: Deformable Distributed Multiple Detector Fusion for Multi-Person Tracking
Abstract: This paper addresses fully automated multi-person tracking in complex environments with challenging occlusion and pose variations. The approach combines multiple detectors for different regions of interest (e.g., full-body and head) to improve detection accuracy. Detection outputs are grouped by bounding box location and depth information to address false positives. Deformable spatial relationships between detectors are learned to handle significant pose variations. Experiments on RGBD data from an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) show significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Can Pretrained Neural Networks Detect Anatomy?
Abstract: This paper presents two approaches for anatomy detection in medical imaging, where annotated data is scarce. The first approach utilizes a network pre-trained on a different domain with abundant data as a feature extractor, followed by a classifier trained on a small target dataset. The second approach uses a deep architecture trained with heavy augmentation and sophisticated regularization methods. The approaches are evaluated on a corpus of X-ray images.
label: AI

title: Domain Adaptation and Transfer Learning in StochasticNets
Abstract: This paper investigates the efficacy of transfer learning in StochasticNet frameworks, which utilize sparse connectivity to reduce the number of parameters and potentially relax training data requirements. Experimental results show a 7% improvement in StochasticNet performance when transfer learning is applied during training.
label: AI

title: Relay Backpropagation for Effective Learning of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of learning deeper convolutional neural networks. The authors propose a novel method called Relay Backpropagation to encourage the propagation of effective information through the network during training. This approach achieved first place in the ILSVRC 2015 Scene Classification Challenge and has been proven effective on various datasets and network architectures.
label: AI

title: Probabilistic Programming with Gaussian Process Memoization
Abstract: Gaussian Processes (GPs) are widely used in various fields, but their application can be complex due to the need for specifying and inferring over complex covariance functions. This paper presents gpmem, an interface that embeds GPs into higher-order probabilistic programming languages. gpmem takes an arbitrary real-valued computational process as input and returns a statistical emulator that improves with each invocation. The flexibility of gpmem is demonstrated through three applications: robust GP regression, discovering symbolic expressions from time-series data, and Bayesian optimization. These applications share a concise Python library and require minimal probabilistic code. |||
label: AI

title: Reconstruction of Enhanced Ultrasound Images From Compressed Measurements Using Simultaneous Direction Method of Multipliers
Abstract: High-resolution ultrasound image reconstruction from a limited number of measurements is a crucial aspect of ultrasound imaging, as it could improve both the frame rate and image resolution. Compressive deconvolution, a combination of compressed sensing and image deconvolution, offers a promising approach to address this challenging task. The compressive deconvolution model incorporates a 2D convolution operator representing the system point spread function, in addition to the compressive sampling matrix. This model highlights the importance of three key factors in determining the resolution of reconstructed ultrasound images from compressed measurements: the acquisition setup (i.e., the incoherence of the sampling matrix), image regularization (i.e., the sparsity prior), and the optimization technique. This paper focuses on the latter two aspects, proposing a novel simultaneous direction method of multipliers-based optimization scheme to invert the linear model. This scheme incorporates two regularization terms expressing the sparsity of the RF images in a given basis and the generalized Gaussian statistical assumption on tissue reflectivity functions. The method's performance is evaluated on both simulated and in vivo data.
label: AI

title: Large Scale Business Discovery from Street Level Imagery
Abstract: Search with local intent is gaining popularity due to the widespread use of mobile devices. However, creating and maintaining accurate listings of local businesses worldwide is a time-consuming and expensive process. This paper presents an approach for automatically discovering businesses visible in street-level imagery. Precise business storefront detection enables accurate geolocation of businesses and provides valuable input for business categorization, listing generation, and other applications. The large variety of business categories across different countries makes this a challenging problem, and manual annotation is not feasible due to the scale. We propose a MultiBox-based approach that directly outputs storefront bounding boxes from input image pixels. This end-to-end learning approach eliminates the need for hand modeling in both the proposal generation and post-processing phases, leveraging large labeled training datasets. Our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art detection techniques in terms of performance and run-time efficiency. Evaluation results demonstrate that our method achieves human-level accuracy in low-recall settings. We also provide an end-to-end evaluation of business discovery in real-world scenarios.
label: AI

title: Numerical Demultiplexing of Color Image Sensor Measurements via Non-linear Random Forest Modeling
Abstract: Simultaneous capture of imaging data at multiple wavelengths across the electromagnetic spectrum is a challenging task, requiring complex and costly multispectral image sensors. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for performing simultaneous multispectral imaging using conventional image sensors with color filter arrays through numerical demultiplexing of color image sensor measurements. A numerical forward model is constructed based on a comprehensive spectral characterization of the sensor, characterizing the formation of sensor measurements from light spectra hitting the sensor. A numerical demultiplexer is then learned using non-linear random forest modeling based on the forward model. With the learned numerical demultiplexer, one can demultiplex simultaneously acquired measurements made by the image sensor into reflectance intensities at discrete selectable wavelengths, resulting in a higher resolution reflectance spectrum. Simulation and real-world experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of this method for simultaneous multispectral imaging.

title: Ranking genetic factors related to age-related maculardegeneration by variable selection confidence sets
Abstract: Generalized linear models are widely used in case-control genetic studies to identify disease-associated risk factors, typically defined as DNA variants or single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Most existing literature focuses on selecting a unique best subset of SNPs based on statistical criteria. However, in the presence of significant noise, multiple biological pathways are often equally supported by a given dataset when dealing with complex genetic diseases. To address the ambiguity associated with SNP selection, we propose constructing a list of models called the variable selection confidence set (VSCS). The VSCS contains all well-supported SNP combinations at a user-specified confidence level. The VSCS extends the concept of confidence intervals to the variable selection setting, providing practitioners with new tools for variable selection beyond relying on a single model. Based on the VSCS, we introduce graphical and numerical statistics that measure the inclusion importance of an SNP based on its frequency in the most parsimonious VSCS models. This work is motivated by available case-control genetic data on age-related macular degeneration, a widespread complex disease and leading cause of vision loss.
label: AI

title: Multiregion Bilinear Convolutional Neural Networks for Person Re-Identification
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for person re-identification. As re-identification inherently involves embedding learning and non-rigid appearance description, our architecture is based on the deep bilinear convolutional network (Bilinear-CNN) recently proposed for fine-grained classification of highly non-rigid objects. While the original Bilinear-CNN architecture completely removes geometric information by performing orderless pooling in the final stages, we observe that a better embedding can be learned by performing bilinear pooling locally, where each pooling is confined to a predefined region. Our architecture represents a compromise between traditional convolutional networks and bilinear CNNs, striking a balance between rigid matching and completely ignoring spatial information. We validate the new architecture experimentally on three popular benchmark datasets (Market-1501, CUHK01, CUHK03), comparing it to baselines including Bilinear-CNN and prior art. The new architecture outperforms the baseline on all three datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results on two out of three. The code and pretrained models of the approach are available at https://github.com/madkn/MultiregionBilinearCNN-ReId.
label: AI

title: Shape and Spatially-Varying Reflectance Estimation From Virtual Exemplars
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating the shape of objects exhibiting spatially-varying reflectance under the photometric stereo setting, where multiple images of the object are obtained under a fixed viewpoint and varying illumination. Our technique leverages the assumption that the BRDF at each pixel lies in the non-negative span of a known BRDF dictionary. This assumption enables a per-pixel surface normal and BRDF estimation framework that is computationally efficient and requires no initialization, despite the underlying problem being non-convex. The estimation framework first solves for the surface normal at each pixel using a variant of example-based photometric stereo, employing an efficient multi-scale search strategy and subsequent refinement using gradient descent. Given the surface normal estimate, we solve for the spatially-varying BRDF by constraining the BRDF at each pixel to be in the span of the BRDF dictionary, using additional priors to further regularize the solution. Our approach stands out for its lack of iterative optimization techniques and the absence of the need for careful initialization, both of which are common challenges in most state-of-the-art techniques. We demonstrate the performance of our technique on a wide range of simulated and real scenes, outperforming competing methods.
label: AI

title: Blockout: Dynamic Model Selection for Hierarchical Deep Networks
Abstract: Most deep architectures for image classification, even those trained on a large number of diverse categories, learn shared image representations with a single model. However, intuitively, categories that are more similar should share more information than those that are very different. While hierarchical deep networks address this problem by learning separate features for subsets of related categories, current implementations require simplified models using fixed architectures specified via heuristic clustering methods. We propose Blockout, a method for regularization and model selection that simultaneously learns both the model architecture and parameters. As a generalization of Dropout, our approach introduces a novel parametrization of hierarchical architectures that enables structure learning via back-propagation. We evaluate Blockout on the CIFAR and ImageNet datasets, demonstrating improved classification accuracy, better regularization performance, faster training, and the clear emergence of hierarchical network structures.
label: AI

title: Fine-grained Categorization and Dataset Bootstrapping using Deep Metric Learning with Humans in the Loop
Abstract: Existing fine-grained visual categorization methods often face three challenges: lack of training data, a large number of fine-grained categories, and high intraclass versus low inter-class variance. This paper proposes a generic iterative framework for fine-grained categorization and dataset bootstrapping that addresses these challenges. Using deep metric learning with humans in the loop, we learn a low-dimensional feature embedding with anchor points on manifolds for each category. These anchor points capture intra-class variances while remaining discriminative between classes. In each round, images with high confidence scores from our model are sent to humans for labeling. By comparing with exemplar images, labelers mark each candidate image as either a "true positive" or a "false positive." True positives are added to our current dataset, and false positives are considered "hard negatives" for our metric learning model. The model is then retrained with an expanded dataset and hard negatives for the next round. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we bootstrap a fine-grained flower dataset with 620 categories from Instagram images. The proposed deep metric learning scheme is evaluated on both our dataset and the CUB-200-2001 Birds dataset. Experimental evaluations show significant performance gains using dataset bootstrapping and demonstrate state-of-the-art results achieved by the proposed deep metric learning methods.
label: AI

title: Effects of GIMP Retinex Filtering Evaluated by the Image Entropy
Abstract: GIMP Retinex filtering is a technique for enhancing images, particularly effective for improving foggy images. This filter has adjustable parameters that can be optimized to produce desired results. This paper considers maximizing image entropy as a criterion for optimizing filtering parameters. We use both Shannon entropy and a generalized entropy to evaluate the filter's performance.
label: AI

title: Multiple penalized principal curves: analysis and computation
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of finding the one-dimensional structure in a given dataset. In other words, we explore ways to approximate a given measure (data) by curves. We propose an objective functional whose minimizers represent a regularization of principal curves and introduce a new functional that allows for multiple curves. We prove the existence of minimizers and establish their basic properties. An efficient algorithm for obtaining (near) minimizers of the functional is developed. While both functionals used are nonconvex, we argue that enlarging the configuration space to allow for multiple curves leads to a simpler energy landscape with fewer undesirable (high-energy) local minima. Furthermore, the proposed approach can find the one-dimensional structure even in data with significant noise.
label: AI

title: Context Driven Label Fusion for segmentation of Subcutaneous and Visceral Fat in CT Volumes
Abstract: Quantification of adipose tissue (fat) from computed tomography (CT) scans is primarily conducted through manual or semi-automated image segmentation algorithms with limited efficacy. This paper proposes a completely unsupervised and automatic method for identifying adipose tissue and separating subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) from visceral adipose tissue (VAT) in the abdominal region. We introduce a three-phase pipeline consisting of (1) Initial boundary estimation using gradient points, (2) boundary refinement using Geometric Median Absolute Deviation and Appearance-based Local Outlier Scores, and (3) Context-driven label fusion using Conditional Random Fields (CRF) to obtain the final boundary between SAT and VAT. We evaluate the proposed method on 151 abdominal CT scans and achieve state-of-the-art 94% and 91% Dice similarity scores for SAT and VAT segmentation, respectively, as well as significant reduction in fat quantification error measure.
label: AI

title: On Deep Representation Learning from Noisy Web Images
Abstract: The ever-growing content of Web images represents a potential data source for scaling up deep neural networks, which have achieved significant success in the ImageNet classification challenge and related tasks. However, this prospect has not been validated on convolutional networks (convnets) due to their supervised regime. While unsupervised alternatives are generally not as good as convnets in generalizing learned models to new domains, we leverage convnets for semi-supervised representation learning. Our approach utilizes massive amounts of unlabeled and noisy Web images to train convnets as general feature detectors, despite challenges posed by data such as high levels of mislabeled data, outliers, and data biases. Extensive experiments are conducted at various data scales, with different network architectures and data reranking techniques. The learned representations are evaluated on nine public datasets of diverse topics. The best results obtained by our convnets, trained on 3.14 million Web images, outperform AlexNet trained on 1.2 million clean images of ILSVRC 2012 and approach the performance of VGG-16. These notable results suggest a cost-effective solution for practical deep learning applications and motivate further research in semi-supervised representation learning.
label: AI

title: Noise-Compensated, Bias-Corrected Diffusion Weighted Endorectal Magnetic Resonance Imaging via a Stochastically Fully-Connected Joint Conditional Random Field Model
Abstract: Diffusion weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MR) is a powerful tool in imaging-based prostate cancer screening and detection. Endorectal coils are commonly used in DW-MR imaging to improve the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the acquisition. However, this comes at the expense of significant intensity inhomogeneities (bias field) that worsen with increasing distance from the endorectal coil. Bias field can negatively impact the accuracy of various image analysis tasks, including prostate tumor localization, leading to increased inter- and intra-observer variability. Retrospective bias correction approaches are more efficient than prospective methods for correcting both scanner and anatomy-related bias fields in MR imaging. However, previously proposed retrospective bias field correction methods suffer from undesired noise amplification that can reduce the quality of the bias-corrected DW-MR image. We propose a unified data reconstruction approach that enables joint compensation of bias field and data noise in DW-MR imaging. The proposed noise-compensated, bias-corrected (NCBC) data reconstruction method leverages a novel stochastically fully connected joint conditional random field (SFC-JCRF) model to mitigate the effects of data noise and bias field in the reconstructed MR data. The proposed NCBC reconstruction method was tested on synthetic DW-MR data, physical DW-phantom, and real DW-MR data acquired using endorectal MR coil. Both qualitative and quantitative analysis demonstrate that the proposed NCBC method achieves improved image quality compared to other tested bias correction methods. As such, the proposed NCBC method may be a useful retrospective approach for improving the consistency of image interpretations.
label: AI

title: Semantic-enriched Visual Vocabulary Construction in a Weakly Supervised Context
Abstract: Content-based image classification is a prevalent learning task involving images. This task is challenging because the low-level features used to digitally describe images often capture little information about the semantics of the images. This paper addresses this challenge by enriching the semantic content of the image representation using external knowledge. Our work hypothesizes that creating a more semantically rich representation for images would lead to improved machine learning performances without modifying the learning algorithms themselves. The external semantic information is presented in the form of non-positional image labels, placing our work in a weakly supervised context. Two approaches are proposed: the first leverages the labels into the visual vocabulary construction algorithm, resulting in dedicated visual vocabularies. The second approach adds a filtering phase as a pre-processing step for vocabulary construction. Known positive and known negative sets are constructed, and features unlikely to be associated with the objects denoted by the labels are filtered. We apply our proposition to the task of content-based image classification and demonstrate that semantically enriching the image representation yields higher classification performances than the baseline representation.
label: AI

title: On non-iterative training of a neural classifier
Abstract: A recently discovered algorithm separates points in n-dimensions by planes in such a way that no two points remain unseparated by at least one plane. This paper shows that this algorithm enables two non-iterative and deterministic classification methods by a neural network for a large-dimensional feature space. To demonstrate the effectiveness of these methods, we apply them exhaustively to the classic pattern recognition problem: the Fisher-Anderson's IRIS flower data set, presenting the results. These methods are expected to be widely adopted for training neural networks for Deep Learning, not only due to their non-iterative and deterministic nature but also for their efficiency and speed. These methods are anticipated to supersede other iterative classification methods that rely on error minimization.
label: AI

title: Sparse Representation of a Blur Kernel for Blind Image Restoration
Abstract: Blind image restoration, a non-convex problem, involves restoring images from an unknown blur kernel. The performance of this restoration depends on the amount of prior information provided about the image and blur kernel, as well as the algorithm used for restoration. Prior information about images is often employed to restore the sharpness of the edges of an image. However, there is no consensus regarding what prior information to use in restoring from a blur kernel due to complex image blurring processes. This paper proposes modeling a blur kernel as a sparse linear combination of basic 2-D patterns. Our approach offers an advantage over existing blur kernel modeling methods due to its flexibility in customizing the dictionary design, making it well-suited for various applications. As a demonstration, we construct a dictionary formed by basic patterns derived from the Kronecker product of Gaussian sequences. We also compare our results with those derived by other state-of-the-art methods in terms of peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR).
label: AI

title: Instance-aware Semantic Segmentation via Multi-task Network Cascades
Abstract: Semantic segmentation research has witnessed rapid progress, but many leading methods are unable to identify object instances. This paper presents Multi-task Network Cascades for instance-aware semantic segmentation. Our model comprises three networks: one for differentiating instances, another for estimating masks, and a third for categorizing objects. These networks form a cascaded structure and are designed to share their convolutional features. We develop an algorithm for the non-trivial end-to-end training of this causal, cascaded structure. Our solution is a clean, single-step training framework and can be generalized to cascades with more stages. We demonstrate state-of-the-art instance-aware semantic segmentation accuracy on PASCAL VOC. Moreover, our method takes only 360ms to test an image using VGG-16, which is two orders of magnitude faster than previous systems for this challenging problem. As a byproduct, our method also achieves compelling object detection results that surpass the competitive Fast/Faster R-CNN systems. The method described in this paper is the foundation of our submissions to the MS COCO 2015 segmentation competition, where we won first place.
label: AI

title: We Are Humor Beings: Understanding and Predicting Visual Humor
Abstract: Humor is an integral part of human lives. Despite its profound impact, our understanding of humor remains incomplete. As interactions between humans and AI systems increase, it is essential to teach these systems to understand subtleties of human expressions, including humor. This work investigates the question: what content in a scene makes it funny? As a first step towards understanding visual humor, we analyze humor manifested in abstract scenes and design computational models for them. We collect two datasets of abstract scenes that facilitate the study of humor at both the scene-level and the object-level. We analyze the funny scenes and explore the different types of humor depicted in them via human studies. We model two tasks that we believe demonstrate an understanding of some aspects of visual humor. The tasks involve predicting the funniness of a scene and altering the funniness of a scene. Our models perform well quantitatively and qualitatively, as shown through human studies. Our datasets are publicly available.
label: AI

title: Passive Communication with Ambient Light
Abstract: This paper proposes a new communication system for illuminated areas, both indoors and outdoors. Light sources in our environments, such as light bulbs or even the sun, act as signal emitters. However, we do not modulate data at the light source. Instead, we propose that the environment itself modulates the ambient light signals. If mobile elements "wear" patterns consisting of distinctive reflecting surfaces, a single photodiode could decode the disturbed light signals to read passive information. Realizing this vision requires a deep understanding of a new type of communication channel. Many parameters can affect the performance of passive communication based on visible light: the size of reflective surfaces, the surrounding light intensity, the speed of mobile objects, and the field-of-view of the receiver, to name a few. This paper presents our vision for a passive communication channel with visible light, the design challenges, and the evaluation of an outdoor application where our receiver decodes information from a car moving at 18 km/h.
label: AI

title: Origami: A 803 GOp/s/W Convolutional Network Accelerator
Abstract: An increasing number of computer vision and image/video processing challenges are being addressed using deep convolutional neural networks, achieving state-of-the-art results in object recognition and detection, semantic segmentation, action recognition, optical flow, and super-resolution. Hardware acceleration of these algorithms is crucial for adopting these improvements in embedded and mobile computer vision systems. We present a new architecture, design, and implementation, as well as the first reported silicon measurements of such an accelerator, outperforming previous work in terms of power, area, and I/O efficiency. The manufactured device provides up to 196 GOp/s on 3.09 mm^2 of silicon in UMC 65nm technology and achieves a power efficiency of 803 GOp/s/W. The massively reduced bandwidth requirements make it the first architecture scalable to TOp/s performance.
label: AI

title: On the Relation between two Rotation Metrics
Abstract: Hartley and Kahl's "Global Optimization through Rotation Space Search" proposes a global optimization strategy for problems in geometric computer vision. Their method is based on a branch-and-bound algorithm that searches for optimal solutions in rotation space. A key element of their work is Lemma 2, which establishes a relationship between metrics for rotations represented by rotation matrices and axis-angle representation. This paper focuses on providing a proof for this relationship, building upon Rodrigues' Rotation Theorem for the composition of rotations in axis-angle representation.
label: AI

title: Watch-Bot: Unsupervised Learning for Reminding Humans of Forgotten Actions
Abstract: A robotic system is presented that uses a Kinect v2 RGB-D sensor to observe a human performing an activity. The system detects any forgotten steps and, if necessary, reminds the person using a laser pointer to indicate the related object. This simple setup can be easily adapted to any assistive robot.  The approach relies on a learning algorithm trained in an unsupervised setting, eliminating the need for human annotations. This makes it scalable and adaptable to diverse scenarios. The model learns the co-occurrence of actions and objects, as well as the temporal relationships between actions. These learned relationships enable the system to infer forgotten actions and associated objects. The results demonstrate improved performance in unsupervised action segmentation and action cluster assignment, alongside effective detection of forgotten actions in a challenging human activity RGB-D video dataset. Robotic experiments confirm the system's ability to successfully remind people of forgotten actions.
label: AI

title: Compressed Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Background Modeling
Abstract: This paper introduces the method of compressed dynamic mode decomposition (cDMD) for background modeling. Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is a regression technique that combines Fourier transforms and singular value decomposition, two leading data analysis methods. cDMD, inspired by compressed sensing and matrix sketching, reduces the computational load of processing high-resolution video. The core principle of cDMD is to perform the decomposition on a compressed matrix representation of the video feed, which is significantly smaller than the original data matrix. Consequently, the algorithm's complexity scales with the intrinsic rank of the matrix, not the size of the actual video data. The selection of optimal modes representing the background is formulated as a sparsity-constrained sparse coding problem. The results show that the quality of the resulting background model, quantified by the F-measure, Recall, and Precision, is highly competitive. A GPU-accelerated implementation is also presented, further enhancing the computational efficiency of the algorithm.
label: AI

title: Understanding Human-Centric Images: From Geometry to Fashion
Abstract: Understanding humans from photographs is a long-standing goal in computer vision. This thesis presents a hierarchical framework of tools that cover a wide range of topics, all aimed at understanding humans from monocular RGB images. This framework spans from low-level feature point descriptors to high-level fashion-aware conditional random fields models. The construction of these high-level models relies heavily on robust and reliable low and mid-level cues.  Two novel low-level keypoint descriptors are proposed: one based on the theory of heat diffusion on images and another utilizing a convolutional neural network to learn discriminative image patch representations. The thesis also introduces distinct low-level generative models for human pose representation, including a discrete model based on a directed acyclic graph and a continuous model that clusters poses on a Riemannian manifold.  Two 3D human pose estimation algorithms are proposed as mid-level cues: one estimating the 3D pose given a noisy 2D estimation and another simultaneously estimating both 2D and 3D poses. Finally, the thesis presents higher-level models built upon these low and mid-level cues for understanding humans from single images.  The focus is on two specific tasks related to fashion: semantic segmentation of clothing and predicting fashionability from images with metadata, ultimately aiming to provide fashion advice to users. Extensive results and comparisons to state-of-the-art methods are provided for all approaches, demonstrating significant improvements across the diverse tasks tackled.
label: AI

title: Learning Deep Features for Discriminative Localization
Abstract: This work revisits the global average pooling layer proposed in [13] and sheds light on its ability to enable convolutional neural networks to exhibit remarkable localization capabilities despite being trained on image-level labels. While previously considered a regularization technique, this research demonstrates that global average pooling actually builds a generic localizable deep representation applicable to various tasks. Despite the apparent simplicity of global average pooling, the achieved top-5 error for object localization on ILSVRC 2014 is 37.1%, strikingly close to the 34.2% top-5 error achieved by a fully supervised CNN approach. The study showcases the network's ability to localize discriminative image regions across diverse tasks, even without explicit training for these tasks.
label: AI

title: Inside-Outside Net: Detecting Objects in Context with Skip Pooling and Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Accurate visual recognition benefits greatly from contextual and multi-scale representations. This paper introduces the Inside-Outside Net (ION), an object detector that leverages information both inside and outside the region of interest. Contextual information outside the region of interest is integrated using spatial recurrent neural networks. Inside the region, skip pooling is employed to extract information at multiple scales and levels of abstraction. Through comprehensive experiments, the design space is evaluated, providing insights into key techniques. ION surpasses the state-of-the-art on the PASCAL VOC 2012 object detection dataset, achieving 76.4% mAP compared to the previous best of 73.9%. On the more challenging MS COCO dataset, the improvement is even more significant, from 19.7% to 33.1% mAP. In the 2015 MS COCO Detection Challenge, the ION model earned the Best Student Entry and achieved third place overall. These results strongly suggest that context and multi-scale representations enhance small object detection.
label: AI

title: Evaluation of Pose Tracking Accuracy in the First and Second Generations of Microsoft Kinect
Abstract: The Microsoft Kinect camera, with its skeletal tracking capabilities, has gained widespread adoption among researchers and commercial developers in various applications involving real-time human movement analysis. This paper evaluates the accuracy of the human kinematic motion data provided by the first and second generations of the Kinect system, comparing the results to an optical motion capture system. Motion data for 12 exercises was collected from 10 different subjects, using three different viewpoints. The accuracy of joint localization and bone length estimation of Kinect skeletons is reported in comparison to the motion capture system. The analysis also explores the distribution of joint localization offsets by fitting a mixture of Gaussian and uniform distribution models to identify outliers in the Kinect motion data. The findings demonstrate that Kinect 2 generally exhibits more robust and accurate human pose tracking compared to Kinect 1.
label: AI

title: A Person Re-Identification System For Mobile Devices
Abstract: Person re-identification, a critical security task, involves recognizing an individual across spatially disjoint sensors. Existing approaches can be computationally demanding and primarily rely on low-level cues extracted from RGB data, typically implemented on a PC for fixed sensor networks (e.g., traditional CCTV). This paper proposes a practical and efficient framework for mobile devices (e.g., smartphones and robots) where high-level semantic soft biometrics are extracted from RGB and depth data. Combining these cues aims to achieve robustness against noise, illumination variations, and minor clothing changes. This mobile approach is particularly valuable for identification in areas poorly covered by fixed sensors or for tasks requiring dynamic sensor positioning and direction adjustment. Preliminary results on the BIWI dataset are encouraging, and further evaluation and system demonstration are available on their website.
label: AI

title: Articulated Pose Estimation Using Hierarchical Exemplar-Based Models
Abstract: Exemplar-based models have achieved significant success in localizing parts of semi-rigid objects. However, their efficacy on highly articulated objects like humans remains unexplored. Inspired by hierarchical object representation and the recent application of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) to human pose estimation, this paper proposes a novel formulation that integrates both hierarchical exemplar-based models and DCNNs within the spatial terms. By assuming independence between exemplars at different levels in the hierarchy, more expressive spatial models are obtained. Additionally, stronger spatial constraints are achieved by inferring spatial relations between parts at the same level. This method strikes a balance between expressiveness and strength of spatial models, leading to effectiveness and generalizability, achieving state-of-the-art results on various benchmarks: Leeds Sports Dataset and CUB-200-2011.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Temporal Segmentation of Repetitive Human Actions Based on Kinematic Modeling and Frequency Analysis
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for temporal segmentation of human repetitive actions based on frequency analysis of kinematic parameters, zero-velocity crossing detection, and adaptive k-means clustering.  Since human motion data can be captured with varying modalities (e.g., optical motion capture systems vs. Microsoft Kinect), each having different temporal sampling rates and accuracies, a generic full-body kinematic model with an unscented Kalman filter is initially applied to convert the motion data into a unified representation robust to noise.  The most representative kinematic parameters are then extracted through primary frequency analysis. The sequences are segmented based on zero-velocity crossing of the selected parameters, followed by adaptive k-means clustering to identify the repetitive segments. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed algorithm's ability to robustly segment repetitive action sequences, regardless of whether the motion data is captured by a motion capture system or Microsoft Kinect.
label: AI

title: Deep Relative Attributes
Abstract: Visual attributes effectively describe images or scenes in a way that both humans and computers can understand. Relative attributes were introduced to establish a correspondence between images and compare the strength of each property across images. However, hand-crafted and engineered features have been used to learn increasingly complex models for relative attributes, limiting their applicability to more realistic scenarios.  This paper introduces a deep neural network architecture for relative attribute prediction.  A convolutional neural network (ConvNet) is used to learn features, including an additional ranking layer that learns to rank images based on these features. An appropriate ranking loss is adopted to train the entire network end-to-end. The proposed method outperforms baselines and state-of-the-art methods in relative attribute prediction on various coarse and fine-grained datasets.  Qualitative results, alongside visualizations of saliency maps, demonstrate the network's ability to learn effective features for each specific attribute. The source code for the proposed method is available at https://github.com/yassersouri/ghiaseddin.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning-Based Image Kernel for Inductive Transfer
Abstract: This paper proposes a method to classify images from target classes using a small number of training examples, based on transfer learning from non-target classes. Without utilizing additional information beyond class labels for samples from non-target classes, a Siamese net is trained to estimate the probability of two images belonging to the same class.  After post-processing, the Siamese net's output can be used to form a gram matrix of a Mercer kernel.  Combined with a support vector machine (SVM), this kernel achieves reasonable classification accuracy on target classes without any fine-tuning. When the Siamese net is partially fine-tuned using a small number of samples from the target classes, the resulting classifier surpasses state-of-the-art methods and other alternatives. The study shares insights into the class separation capabilities and learning process of this kernel on MNIST, Dogs vs. Cats, and CIFAR-10 datasets.
label: AI

title: Learning the Correction for Multi-Path Deviations in Time-of-Flight Cameras
Abstract: The Multipath effect in Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras remains a challenging problem that hinders further processing of 3D data information. Based on previous literature, this paper explores the potential of machine learning techniques to correct this effect. Two new datasets of ToF images were generated using the LuxRender ToF simulator, containing corners in multiple orientations and with different material properties. Corners were chosen for the scenes as multipath effects are most pronounced in these areas. This dataset was then used to construct a learning model that predicts real-valued corrections to the ToF data using Random Forests.  In the smaller dataset, the model successfully predicted real-valued corrections, significantly improving the quality of depth images by removing multipath bias.  The algorithm reduced the average per-pixel error from 19% to 3%, and the error variance decreased by an order of magnitude.
label: AI

title: Cross-dimensional Weighting for Aggregated Deep Convolutional Features
Abstract: This paper presents a simple and straightforward approach to creating powerful image representations through cross-dimensional weighting and aggregation of deep convolutional neural network layer outputs.  A generalized framework is introduced that encompasses a broad family of approaches, including cross-dimensional pooling and weighting steps.  Specific non-parametric schemes for both spatial- and channel-wise weighting are proposed to amplify the effect of highly active spatial responses while regulating burstiness effects.  Experiments on different public datasets for image search demonstrate that this approach surpasses the current state-of-the-art for methods based on pre-trained networks. An easy-to-use, open-source implementation that reproduces these results is also provided.
label: AI

title: Deep Tracking: Visual Tracking Using Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper investigates a discriminatively trained deep convolutional network for visual tracking. The tracker utilizes both motion and appearance features extracted from a pre-trained dual-stream deep convolution network.  The features extracted from this dual-stream network provide rich information about the target, resulting in competitive performance against state-of-the-art tracking methods on a visual tracking benchmark.
label: AI

title: Action Recognition with Image Based CNN Features
Abstract: Most human actions involve complex temporal compositions of simpler actions.  Action recognition tasks typically rely on complex handcrafted structures as features to represent the human action model. Convolutional Neural Nets (CNNs) have proven to be powerful tools that eliminate the need for designing handcrafted features.  Usually, the output of the last layer in a CNN (a layer before the classification layer, known as fc7) is used as a generic feature for images. This paper demonstrates that fc7 features alone are insufficient for achieving good performance in action recognition tasks when the network is trained only on images.  A novel feature structure is proposed on top of fc7 features to capture the temporal variation in a video.  To represent the temporal components necessary for capturing motion information, a hierarchical structure is introduced. This hierarchical model enables the capture of sub-actions from a complex action. Higher levels in the hierarchy provide a coarse representation of the action sequence, while lower levels capture fine action elements.  Furthermore, a method for extracting keyframes using binary coding of each frame in a video is introduced, enhancing the performance of the hierarchical model.
