Experiments on several action datasets show that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: RNN Fisher Vectors for Action Recognition and Image Annotation
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have achieved significant success in classifying and predicting sequences. This paper demonstrates that RNNs can be effectively used to encode sequences and provide effective representations. The methodology employed is based on Fisher Vectors, where RNNs serve as the generative probabilistic models, and partial derivatives are computed using backpropagation. State-of-the-art results are achieved in two central but distinct tasks that rely on sequences: video action recognition and image annotation.  The study also presents a surprising transfer learning result from the task of image annotation to the task of video action recognition.
label: AI

title: Improving Human Activity Recognition Through Ranking and Re-ranking
Abstract: This paper proposes two well-motivated ranking-based methods to enhance the performance of state-of-the-art human activity recognition systems.  First, as an improvement over the classic power normalization method, a parameter-free ranking technique called rank normalization (RaN) is introduced. RaN normalizes each dimension of the video features to address the sparse and bursty distribution problems of Fisher Vectors and VLAD. Second, inspired by curriculum learning, a training-free re-ranking technique called multi-class iterative re-ranking (MIR) is proposed. MIR captures relationships among action classes by separating easy and typical videos from difficult ones and re-ranking the prediction scores of classifiers accordingly. The paper demonstrates that these methods significantly improve the performance of state-of-the-art motion features on six real-world datasets.
label: AI

title: A New Approach of Gray Images Binarization with Threshold Methods
Abstract: This paper examines aspects of gray-level image binarization methods used in artificial vision systems, introducing a new approach for gray-level image binarization in artificial vision systems dedicated to industrial automation temporal thresholding.  The paper first outlines the limitations of using global optimum thresholding in gray-level image binarization.  Then, it presents aspects of the dynamic optimum thresholding method for gray-level image binarization.  Building upon classic methods of global and dynamic optimal thresholding of gray-level images, the concepts of temporal histogram and temporal thresholding are introduced. The paper concludes by exploring practical aspects of the temporal thresholding method in artificial vision applications for moving scenes in robotic automation, highlighting the influence of acquisition frequency on the method's results.
label: AI

title: Deep Feature Learning with Relative Distance Comparison for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Identifying the same individual across different scenes is a challenging task in intelligent video surveillance. The difficulty lies in preserving similarity for the same person despite significant appearance and structural variations while simultaneously discriminating between different individuals. This paper presents a scalable distance-driven feature learning framework based on deep neural networks for person re-identification, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing these challenges.  Specifically, given training images with class labels (person IDs), a large number of triplet units are generated, each containing three images: one person with a matched reference and a mismatched reference. Using these units as input, a convolutional neural network is built to generate layered representations, followed by an $L2$ distance metric.  Through parameter optimization, the framework maximizes the relative distance between the matched pair and the mismatched pair for each triplet unit.  The framework addresses the issue of cubic growth in the number of training triplets by proposing an effective triplet generation scheme and an optimized gradient descent algorithm, reducing computational load to depend primarily on the number of original images rather than the number of triplets.  The approach achieves promising results on several challenging databases, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. |||
label: AI

title: Robust Dictionary based Data Representation
Abstract: Linear data representation in real-world applications often faces challenges due to noise and outliers. This paper addresses the specific issue of "sample-specific" corruptions, where individual samples are heavily distorted. The proposed approach leverages the assumption that corrupted samples cannot be effectively represented by the underlying dictionary, while clean samples can be well represented.  By enforcing zero coefficients for corrupted samples, the representation quality of clean data is preserved. The paper presents a robust dictionary-based data representation method and its sparse representation version, which have significant implications for future applications.
label: AI

title: Randomized Low-Rank Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Motion Detection
Abstract: This paper presents a fast algorithm for computing a low-rank Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) of a matrix, representing the evolution of a spatial grid over time, such as data from a static video source. While DMD has found use in fluid mechanics, its application to motion detection and background subtraction in video streams has been limited. The paper thoroughly evaluates background subtraction using randomized DMD, comparing its performance to leading robust principal component analysis algorithms. The results demonstrate that randomized DMD is an efficient and powerful approach for background modeling, capable of processing high-resolution videos in real-time. The supplementary materials include Python implementations of the algorithms.
label: AI

title: Highly Dynamic Spectrum Management within Licensed Shared Access Regulatory Framework
Abstract: The fragmented nature of spectrum access models highlights the need for innovative solutions to efficiently share already available but underutilized spectrum. Licensed Shared Access (LSA) is a promising regulatory framework that enables more advanced spectrum sharing among a limited number of users while ensuring necessary interference protection. However, the practical benefits of LSA may be limited by the spatiotemporal availability of LSA bands. This paper advocates for a highly dynamic LSA architecture and explores its potential by reviewing market opportunities, discussing technology implementations, evaluating performance dynamics, and outlining the standardization landscape. The study is based on a comprehensive system-level evaluation framework specifically designed to assess highly dynamic LSA deployments.
label: AI

title: Neural Self Talk: Image Understanding via Continuous Questioning and Answering
Abstract: This paper investigates a method for continuous image content discovery by actively asking and answering image-based questions. The system comprises two key modules: Visual Question Generation (VQG) and Visual Question Answering (VQA). Both modules utilize Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for learning. VQG generates questions from images, while VQA answers questions based on images. The modules are jointly trained using a dataset containing images, questions, and their corresponding answers. The paper subjectively evaluates the "self-talk" process using Amazon Mechanical Turk, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Abstract: Deeper neural networks are notoriously difficult to train. This paper introduces a residual learning framework to simplify the training of significantly deeper networks. It re-frames layers as learning residual functions relative to the input, rather than learning unreferenced functions. Comprehensive empirical evidence demonstrates that these residual networks are easier to optimize and achieve higher accuracy with increased depth. The authors evaluate residual nets up to 152 layers on the ImageNet dataset, surpassing the complexity of VGG nets while achieving a 3.57% error rate. An ensemble of these residual nets secured the 1st place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification task. The paper also presents analyses on CIFAR-10 with 100 and 1000 layers. The depth of representations is crucial for many visual recognition tasks, leading to a 28% relative improvement on the COCO object detection dataset. These deep residual nets were instrumental in the authors' first-place wins in the ILSVRC & COCO 2015 competitions for ImageNet detection, localization, COCO detection, and segmentation.
label: AI

title: VRFP: On-the-fly Video Retrieval using Web Images and Fast Fisher Vector Products
Abstract: VRFP is a real-time video retrieval framework based on short text input queries that leverages weakly labeled training images retrieved from the web after the query is known. The retrieved web images representing the query and each database video are treated as unordered collections of images, represented by single Fisher Vectors built on CNN features. Experiments demonstrate the robustness of Fisher Vectors to noise in web images and their superior accuracy compared to other representations. While efficient for constructing query models, matching against the test set is slow due to the high dimensionality of Fisher Vectors. To address this, the paper presents a lossless algorithm that accelerates the inner product computation between high-dimensional Fisher Vectors. The algorithm reduces the expected number of multiplications quadratically with the sparsity of Fisher Vectors. This enables real-time construction and application of query models, and with a simple re-ranking scheme, VRFP outperforms state-of-the-art automatic retrieval methods on TRECVID MED13 (3.5%), MED14 (1.3%), and CCV datasets (5.2%). The paper also provides a direct comparison between zero-shot learning and on-the-fly retrieval paradigms for automatic video retrieval.
label: AI

title: 3D Reconstruction of Crime Scenes and Design Considerations for an Interactive Investigation Tool
Abstract: Crime Scene Investigation (CSI) is a systematic process involving the acquisition of physical evidence to shed light on the crime and identify the perpetrator. Capturing images and videos of the crime scene is crucial for analyzing digital evidence. This paper proposes a method for generating a 3D model of the crime scene using the acquired footage. The results demonstrate the feasibility of creating realistic reconstructions using advanced computer vision techniques. The paper discusses important design considerations and outlines key features for a powerful interactive CSI analysis tool.
label: AI

title: Enhanced image feature coverage: Key-point selection using genetic algorithms
Abstract: The distribution of image features significantly impacts the estimated homography in many vision algorithms. This paper introduces a Genetic Algorithm (GA) for selecting the optimal set of features that maximize image coverage, measured by a robust method based on spatial statistics. Statistical tests on two datasets show that the proposed metric achieves better coverage and improved homography accuracy compared to the original set of features. The new set exhibits similar performance in terms of homography accuracy while using fewer features, reducing the time required for descriptor calculation and matching.
label: AI

title: Evaluation of Object Detection Proposals Under Condition Variations
Abstract: Object detection is a fundamental task in many computer vision applications, making the evaluation of object detection quality essential. This paper introduces a novel object detection method combining Selective Search and EdgeBoxes. The three methods are evaluated under environmental variations, demonstrating the superior performance of the combination method under illumination and viewpoint variations.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning Algorithms with Applications to Video Analytics for A Smart City: A Survey
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable results in various fields, including computer vision, speech recognition, and natural language processing. It aims to learn hierarchical data representations using deep architecture models. Smart cities require automatic processing and analysis of large amounts of data, such as videos from distributed sensors. This paper provides a review of deep learning algorithms applied to video analytics in smart cities, focusing on object detection, tracking, face recognition, image classification, and scene labeling.
label: AI

title: Minimally Supervised Feature Selection for Classification (Master's Thesis, University Politehnica of Bucharest)
Abstract: This paper presents a robust and fast feature selection method designed to address the increasing number of features available today. The method aims to select the most representative features that are independent from each other but strong together. The paper proposes an algorithm requiring limited labeled data (as few as one labeled frame per class) and accommodating numerous unlabeled samples. The paper compares the supervised and unsupervised formulations with established methods like AdaBoost, SVM, Lasso, Elastic Net, and FoBa, showing that the proposed method is significantly faster with constant training time. The unsupervised approach outperforms all compared methods, particularly when the number of training shots is limited. The supervised approach also outperforms other methods, especially when the number of training samples is scarce. The algorithm requires a pool of positively correlated features for selection. The methods are evaluated on the Youtube-Objects video dataset and the MNIST digits dataset. The paper also explores transfer learning using features from the CIFAR10 dataset and ImageNet pre-trained models, demonstrating its effectiveness despite variations in datasets, including low-resolution images, high-resolution images with objects from different regions, and challenging videos with high intraclass variance.
label: AI

title: ShapeNet: An Information-Rich 3D Model Repository
Abstract: ShapeNet is a large-scale repository of 3D CAD models of objects, richly annotated with semantic information. It organizes models from various semantic categories under the WordNet taxonomy. ShapeNet provides multiple semantic annotations for each 3D model, including rigid alignments, parts, bilateral symmetry planes, physical sizes, keywords, and other planned annotations. These annotations are accessible through a public web-based interface to facilitate data visualization, data-driven geometric analysis, and provide a large-scale benchmark for research in computer graphics and vision. As of this report, ShapeNet indexes over 3,000,000 models, with 220,000 models classified into 3,135 categories (WordNet synsets). This report describes the ShapeNet project, detailing the available datasets and summarizing future plans.
label: AI

title: Get More With Less: Near Real-Time Image Clustering on Mobile Phones
Abstract: Machine learning algorithms, coupled with user data, hold the potential to revolutionize phone interactions. Their widespread adoption in app design testifies to this promise. However, computationally expensive segments of the learning pipeline, such as feature extraction and model training, are currently offloaded to the cloud, resulting in network dependence and underutilized mobile computing resources. This paper demonstrates that by combining distributed computing power across phones, judicious optimization choices, and contextual information, the entire end-to-end pipeline can be executed efficiently on phones at the network edge. The paper further shows that harnessing this combined power enables near real-time execution of computationally intensive pipelines. To illustrate this approach, the paper implements an end-to-end image processing pipeline, including feature extraction, vocabulary learning, vectorization, and image clustering, on a set of mobile phones. The results demonstrate a 75% improvement over the standard, unmodified pipeline running on phones, reducing the time to one minute under certain conditions. This research suggests the feasibility of fully distributed, infrastructure-less computing on networks of mobile phones, enabling a new class of mobile applications with reduced cloud reliance.
label: AI

title: Video captioning with recurrent networks based on frame- and video-level features and visual content classification
Abstract: This paper describes a system for generating textual descriptions of short video clips using recurrent neural networks (RNN), employed in the Large Scale Movie Description Challenge 2015 at ICCV 2015. The system builds on static image captioning systems with RNN-based language models, extending the framework to videos by incorporating both static image features and video-specific features. The paper investigates the utility of visual content classifiers as a source of additional information for caption generation. Experimental results demonstrate that combining keyframe-based features, dense trajectory video features, and content classifier outputs surpasses the performance of any individual feature type.
label: AI

title: Yet Another Statistical Analysis of Bob Ross Paintings
Abstract: This paper analyzes a sample of paintings by Bob Ross, focusing on the colorspace and luminosity values. Previous work examined qualitative themes in his paintings; this research extends that by analyzing color and luminosity data. The results highlight the subtle aesthetics of the average Ross painting, the common variations shared by his paintings, and the structure of relationships between each painting in the sample. The paper introduces renderings of the average paintings and "eigenross" components to identify and evaluate shared variance. All data and code are embedded within the document to encourage future research and, in the spirit of Bob Ross, teach others how to do so.
label: AI

title: MovieQA: Understanding Stories in Movies through Question-Answering
Abstract: The MovieQA dataset is introduced for evaluating automatic story comprehension from video and text. The dataset consists of 14,944 questions about 408 movies with high semantic diversity. Questions range from simple "Who" did "What" to "Whom," to "Why" and "How" certain events occurred. Each question is accompanied by five possible answers: one correct answer and four deceptive answers provided by human annotators. This dataset uniquely combines multiple information sources, including video clips, plots, subtitles, scripts, and DVS. The paper analyzes the data through various statistics and methods, demonstrating the challenges of question-answering with such open-ended semantics. The dataset is publicly available along with an evaluation benchmark to encourage research in this challenging domain.
label: AI

title: Embedding Label Structures for Fine-Grained Feature Representation
Abstract: Recent advancements in convolutional neural networks (CNN) have significantly improved fine-grained image classification, aiming to differentiate subtle differences among subordinate classes. However, prior research has rarely focused on learning fine-grained and structured feature representations that can locate similar images at different levels of relevance, such as discovering cars from the same make or model. This paper proposes two key contributions to address this challenge: 1) A multi-task learning framework is designed to effectively learn fine-grained feature representations by jointly optimizing both classification and similarity constraints. 2) To model multi-level relevance, label structures such as hierarchy or shared attributes are seamlessly embedded into the framework by generalizing the triplet loss. Extensive experiments conducted on three fine-grained datasets, including the Stanford car, car-333, and food datasets, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. It achieves competitive classification accuracy and significantly outperforms previous fine-grained feature representations for image retrieval at different levels of relevance.
label: AI

title: Affinity CNN: Learning Pixel-Centric Pairwise Relations for Figure/Ground Embedding
Abstract: Spectral embedding provides a framework for solving perceptual organization problems, including image segmentation and figure/ground organization. It clusters pixels into regions based on pairwise relationships described in an affinity matrix and orders pixels according to layer using a complex-valued extension. This paper trains a convolutional neural network (CNN) to directly predict the pairwise relationships defining the affinity matrix. Spectral embedding then resolves these predictions into a globally-consistent segmentation and figure/ground organization. Experiments demonstrate the advantages of this direct coupling compared to previous works using explicit intermediate stages like edge detection. The results suggest spectral embedding as a powerful alternative to CRF-based globalization schemes typically used with deep neural networks.
label: AI

title: Sensor Fusion of Camera, GPS and IMU using Fuzzy Adaptive Multiple Motion Models
Abstract: Tracking systems for Augmented Reality (AR) applications require both accuracy and frame rate. Accuracy depends on the performance of the pose estimation algorithm, which determines the user's position and orientation in the environment. Low-cost tracking devices often exhibit static errors during motion estimation. Frame rate relates to dynamic errors, caused by delays in motion estimation and image display. This paper investigates combining vision-based estimates with measurements from GPS and IMU sensors to improve tracking accuracy in outdoor environments. The paper utilizes Fuzzy Adaptive Multiple Models (FAMM) with a novel fuzzy rule-based approach to select the model that optimizes accuracy and convergence speed for the fusion filter. Results demonstrate that the developed tracking system is more accurate than a conventional GPS-IMU fusion approach due to camera estimates and fuzzy motion models. The paper also presents an application in the cultural heritage context.
label: AI

title: Perfect Recovery Conditions For Non-Negative Sparse Modeling
Abstract: Sparse modeling has been widely and successfully applied in various fields, such as computer vision, machine learning, and pattern recognition. Extensive research has explored theoretical limits and algorithm design for convex relaxations in sparse modeling. However, theoretical analyses on non-negative versions of sparse modeling are limited, either focusing on noiseless settings or specific statistical noise models like Gaussian noise. This paper investigates the performance of non-negative sparse modeling in a more general scenario with unknown arbitrary distortion, particularly focusing on non-negativity constrained and L1-penalized least squares. The paper provides an exact bound for recovering correct signal elements and proposes two conditions to guarantee this: minimum coefficient condition (MCC) and nonlinearity vs. subset coherence condition (NSCC). MCC defines the minimum weight for correct atoms in the signal, while NSCC defines the tolerable deviation from the linear model relative to the positive subset coherence (PSC), a novel "coherence" metric. The paper provides rigorous performance guarantees based on these conditions and experimentally verifies their predictive power in a hyperspectral data unmixing application. |||
label: AI

title: Window-Object Relationship Guided Representation Learning for Generic Object Detections
Abstract: Existing object detection methods simplify the relationship between candidate windows and ground truth bounding boxes using a thresholding approach. This simplification leads to information loss, particularly regarding relative location and size information. This paper proposes a representation learning pipeline that leverages the relationship between candidate windows and bounding boxes as supervision, improving the learned representation for object detection. This approach considers not only the target object but also surrounding objects of different categories, capturing diverse contexts and visual variations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, achieving a 6.4% improvement in mean average precision (mAP) on ILSVRC2014. Our single model achieves the best published result on the challenging ILSVRC2014 test dataset with 48.6% mAP, surpassing the state-of-the-art Fast RCNN by 3.3% in absolute mAP on PASCAL VOC.
label: AI

title: Fine-grained Image Classification by Exploring Bipartite-Graph Labels
Abstract: Can a fine-grained object recognition engine identify the specific restaurant and dish depicted in a food image? This ultra-fine grained image recognition task is crucial for applications like image-based search, but presents significant challenges due to the need to discern subtle differences between classes while dealing with limited training data. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing bipartite-graph labels (BGL) to exploit the rich relationships among object classes. We demonstrate how to integrate BGL into a convolutional neural network (CNN) framework, enabling optimization through back-propagation. The bipartite structure also ensures computational efficiency during inference. To facilitate research, we introduce a new food benchmark dataset comprising 37,885 food images collected from 6 restaurants and covering 975 menus. Experimental results on this new food dataset and three other datasets demonstrate the superiority of BGL compared to previous works in fine-grained object recognition. An online demo is available at http://www.f-zhou.com/fg_demo/.
label: AI

title: Deep Exemplar 2D-3D Detection by Adapting from Real to Rendered Views
Abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end convolutional neural network (CNN) for 2D-3D exemplar detection. We demonstrate that adapting features from natural images to better align with those of CAD rendered views is crucial for the success of our technique. We show that this adaptation can be learned by compositing rendered views of textured object models onto natural images. Our approach seamlessly integrates into a CNN detection pipeline, extending the accuracy and speed benefits of deep learning to 2D-3D exemplar detection. We evaluated our method on two tasks: instance detection (using the IKEA dataset) and object category detection (outperforming Aubry et al. for "chair" detection on a subset of the Pascal VOC dataset).
label: AI

title: Tracking Objects with Higher Order Interactions using Delayed Column Generation
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of multi-target tracking and data association in video by formulating it as the selection of high-quality tracks under the constraint that no two selected tracks are associated with the same detection. This objective corresponds to the classic NP-hard maximum-weight set packing (MWSP) problem, further complicated by the exponential growth of candidate tracks with the number of detections. We propose a relaxation of this combinatorial problem using a column generation formulation where the pricing problem is solved efficiently via dynamic programming to explore the track space. Row generation is employed to tighten the bound while preserving efficient inference in the pricing problem. We demonstrate the practical utility of this algorithm for tracking problems in natural and biological video datasets.
label: AI

title: Towards the Application of Linear Programming Methods For Multi-Camera Pose Estimation
Abstract: This paper introduces a separation-based optimization algorithm that minimizes reprojection error by optimizing variables separately, allowing for the use of nonlinear functions with three variables and a convex quadratic multivariable polynomial. By neglecting the inversion required for the nonlinear functions, we demonstrate how separation effectively eliminates matrix inversion.
label: AI

title: Is Hamming distance the only way for matching binary image feature descriptors?
Abstract: Conventional brute force matching of binary image feature descriptors relies on the Hamming distance. This paper explores the use of alternative metrics to investigate their potential to produce feature correspondences that yield more accurate homography matrices. Two statistical tests, ANOVA and McNemar's test, were employed for evaluation. Results indicate that the Jackard-Needham and Dice metrics can exhibit improved performance for certain descriptors. However, these performance differences were not found to be statistically significant.
label: AI

title: Computational Models for Multiview Dense Depth Maps of Dynamic Scene
Abstract: This paper reviews recent advancements in depth map generation for dynamic scenes and its corresponding computational models. The paper focuses on homogeneous ambiguity models in depth sensing, resolution models in depth processing, and consistency models in depth optimization. We also outline future research directions in depth map generation.
label: AI

title: Learning to Point and Count
Abstract: This paper presents the "point-and-count" problem as a test case for overcoming the "what-and-where" deadlock in object recognition. Unlike traditional detection problems, the goal is to identify key salient points for simultaneous object localization and counting. We propose two alternative approaches: one that counts first and then points, and another that reverses the process. These approaches differ in their prioritization of "what" and "where" information. We evaluate their performance on datasets containing multiple instances of the same class, highlighting their potential and synergies. Our findings reveal important insights into the complexity of this problem compared to classification, including strong data bias and the inability of state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks to handle object scales robustly.
label: AI

title: SSD: Single Shot MultiBox Detector
Abstract: This paper presents SSD (Single Shot MultiBox Detector), a method for object detection in images using a single deep neural network. SSD discretizes the output space of bounding boxes into a set of default boxes with varying aspect ratios and scales per feature map location. During prediction, the network generates scores for the presence of each object category in each default box and adjusts the box to better match the object shape. Furthermore, predictions from multiple feature maps with different resolutions are combined to handle objects of various sizes. SSD's simplicity compared to methods requiring object proposals eliminates proposal generation and subsequent pixel or feature resampling, encapsulating all computation within a single network. This simplifies training and integration into detection-based systems. Experimental results on PASCAL VOC, MS COCO, and ILSVRC datasets demonstrate SSD's comparable accuracy to methods using object proposals while being significantly faster. SSD also outperforms other single-stage methods, achieving higher accuracy even with smaller input image sizes. For a 300x300 input, SSD achieves 72.1% mAP on VOC2007 test at 58 FPS on a Nvidia Titan X, and for a 500x500 input, SSD reaches 75.1% mAP, surpassing a comparable Faster R-CNN model. Code is available at https://github.com/weiliu89/caffe/tree/ssd.
label: AI

title: Direct Intrinsics: Learning Albedo-Shading Decomposition by Convolutional Regression
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to intrinsic image decomposition, the task of separating a single image into albedo and shading components. Our method, termed direct intrinsics, learns a convolutional neural network (CNN) to directly predict output albedo and shading channels from an input RGB image patch. This approach deviates from classical techniques that rely on physically-motivated priors and graph-based inference algorithms. The large-scale synthetic ground-truth of the MPI Sintel dataset plays a crucial role in training direct intrinsics. We demonstrate results on both the synthetic images of Sintel and the real images of the classic MIT intrinsic image dataset. Using only RGB input, direct intrinsics outperforms all previous work on Sintel, including methods that rely on RGB+Depth input. Direct intrinsics also generalizes across modalities, producing reasonable decompositions on the real images of the MIT dataset. Our findings suggest that the combination of CNNs and synthetic training data is a promising technique for addressing classic problems in computer vision.
label: AI

title: Pseudo-Bayesian Robust PCA: Algorithms and Analyses
Abstract: Robust PCA, widely used in computer vision and other applications, aims to reduce the sensitivity of classical PCA to outliers. The fundamental idea is to decompose a data matrix into low-rank and sparse components, with the sparse component representing unwanted outliers. While the resulting optimization problem is typically NP-hard, convex relaxations offer a computationally efficient alternative with theoretical support. However, in practical settings, performance guarantees break down, leading to the development of various non-convex alternatives, including Bayesian-inspired models, to enhance estimation quality. Unfortunately, without additional a priori knowledge, these methods cannot significantly expand the operational range to enable exact principal subspace recovery. To address this limitation, we propose a novel pseudo-Bayesian algorithm that explicitly compensates for design weaknesses in existing non-convex approaches, resulting in state-of-the-art performance with a sound analytical foundation. Surprisingly, our algorithm can even outperform convex matrix completion despite the latter's access to perfect knowledge of uncorrupted entries.
label: AI

title: Simple Baseline for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: This paper describes a simple bag-of-words baseline for visual question answering. This baseline concatenates word features from the question and CNN features from the image to predict the answer. When evaluated on the challenging VQA dataset, it exhibits performance comparable to many recent approaches using recurrent neural networks. To investigate the model's strengths and weaknesses, we provide an interactive web demo and open-source code.
label: AI

title: A Large Dataset to Train Convolutional Networks for Disparity, Optical Flow, and Scene Flow Estimation
Abstract: Recent research has demonstrated that optical flow estimation can be formulated as a supervised learning task and successfully solved using convolutional networks. The training of FlowNet was enabled by a large synthetically generated dataset. This paper extends the concept of optical flow estimation via convolutional networks to disparity and scene flow estimation. To this end, we propose three synthetic stereo video datasets with sufficient realism, variation, and size for training large networks. Our datasets are the first large-scale datasets enabling training and evaluation of scene flow methods. In addition to the datasets, we present a convolutional network for real-time disparity estimation that achieves state-of-the-art results. By jointly training a flow and disparity estimation network, we demonstrate the first scene flow estimation using a convolutional network.
label: AI

title: In-situ multi-scattering tomography
Abstract: To reconstruct the three-dimensional (3D) volumetric distribution of matter within an object, images are captured from multiple directions and locations. Tomographic computations utilize these images to extract the distribution. In highly scattering media and constrained, natural irradiance scenarios, tomography must explicitly account for off-axis scattering. Furthermore, the tomographic model and recovery process must function in in-situ imaging settings, as encountered in medical imaging and ground-based atmospheric sensing. We formulate tomography that handles arbitrary orders of scattering using a Monte Carlo model, which is highly parallelizable in our formulation. This enables large-scale rendering and recovery of volumetric scenes with a large number of variables. We address stability and conditioning problems arising from in-situ radiative transfer (RT) modeling.
label: AI

title: Clustering by Deep Nearest Neighbor Descent (D-NND): A Density-based Parameter-Insensitive Clustering Method
Abstract: Most density-based clustering methods heavily rely on the accuracy of underlying density estimation. However, density estimation itself is a challenging problem, particularly regarding the determination of the kernel bandwidth. A large bandwidth can lead to over-smoothed density estimation, resulting in fewer density peaks than true clusters, while a small bandwidth can result in under-smoothed density estimation and the generation of spurious density peaks, known as "ripple noise". This paper proposes a density-based hierarchical clustering method called Deep Nearest Neighbor Descent (D-NND), which learns the underlying density structure layer by layer while capturing the cluster structure simultaneously. This approach significantly mitigates over-smoothed density estimation and reduces the negative effects of under-estimated cases. Overall, D-NND demonstrates strong capability in discovering the underlying cluster structure and exhibits remarkable reliability due to its insensitivity to parameters.
label: AI

title: Unification of Force and Substance
Abstract: Maxwell's mature presentation of his equations emphasized the unity of electromagnetism and mechanics, subsuming both as "dynamical systems". This intuition of unity has proven both fruitful, serving as a source of powerful concepts, and broadly inspiring. A key aspect of Maxwell's work is its use of redundant potentials and the associated requirement of gauge symmetry. These concepts have become central to our present understanding of fundamental physics but can appear formal and esoteric. This paper discusses two points: the physical significance of gauge invariance in broad terms and some tantalizing prospects for further unification based on this concept, visible on the horizon today. If these prospects are realized, Maxwell's vision of the unity of field and substance will reach a new level.
label: AI

title: On The Continuous Steering of the Scale of Tight Wavelet Frames
Abstract: Drawing inspiration from steerable wavelets, we present a general construction of adaptable tight wavelet frames, with a focus on scaling operations. The derived wavelets can be "dilated" through a process similar to steering steerable wavelets. The fundamental aspects of the construction remain the same: an admissible collection of Fourier multipliers is used to extend a tight wavelet frame, and the "scale" of the wavelets is adapted by scaling the multipliers. As an application, these wavelets can enhance frequency localization. Importantly, the localized frequency bands specified by this construction can be scaled efficiently using matrix multiplication.
label: AI

title: Visualizing Deep Convolutional Neural Networks Using Natural Pre-Images
Abstract: Image representations, ranging from SIFT and bag of visual words to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), are essential components of virtually all computer vision systems. However, our understanding of them remains limited. This paper investigates several landmark representations, both shallow and deep, using a variety of complementary visualization techniques. These visualizations are based on the concept of "natural pre-image", a natural-looking image whose representation exhibits a specific property. We study three such visualizations: inversion (reconstructing an image from its representation), activation maximization (searching for patterns that maximally stimulate a representation component), and caricaturization (exaggerating the visual patterns that a representation detects in an image). We formulate these as a regularized energy-minimization framework and demonstrate its generality and effectiveness. In particular, we show that this method can invert representations like HOG more accurately than recent alternatives while being applicable to CNNs. Our findings reveal that several layers in CNNs retain photographically accurate information about the image, with varying degrees of geometric and photometric invariance.
label: AI

title: Scalable domain adaptation of convolutional neural networks
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become a standard approach for solving a wide range of computer vision problems. Their success, besides significant theoretical and practical advancements in their design, is largely attributed to the availability of manually labeled visual resources, such as ImageNet. The creation of such datasets is laborious, and this paper focuses on alternatives to manual labeling. We hypothesize that new resources are crucial in domains not or weakly covered by ImageNet, such as tourism photographs. We first collect noisy Flickr images for tourist points of interest and apply automatic or weakly-supervised reranking techniques to reduce noise. We then learn domain-adapted models using a standard CNN architecture and compare them to a generic model obtained from ImageNet. Experimental validation is conducted using publicly available datasets, including Oxford5k, INRIA Holidays, and Div150Cred. Results demonstrate that low-cost domain adaptation improves results compared to using generic models and even surpasses strong non-CNN baselines like triangulation embedding.
label: AI

title: Hyperspectral Chemical Plume Detection Algorithms Based On Multidimensional Iterative Filtering Decomposition
Abstract: Chemicals released into the air pose significant risks to humans and the environment. Hyperspectral images can be used to identify chemical plumes, but the task can be challenging. Assuming prior knowledge of a chemical plume's frequency spectrum and its capture using a hyperspectral sensor, standard techniques like the matched filter or adaptive cosine estimator, combined with a suitable threshold value, can identify the plume's position. However, noise and sensor faults can hinder accurate identification of chemical pixels even in this seemingly simple scenario. This paper presents a post-processing tool that adaptively and data-drivenly improves the performance of any classification method in identifying plume boundaries. This is achieved using the Multidimensional Iterative Filtering (MIF) algorithm, a non-stationary signal decomposition method similar to the pioneering Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) method. Furthermore, we propose a pre-processing method based on MIF to decorrelate and mean-center a hyperspectral dataset. The Cosine Similarity measure, often unsuccessful in practice, becomes a successful and high-performing classifier when equipped with this pre-processing method. We provide examples of the proposed methods applied to real-life problems. |||

title: Fast Optimization Algorithm on Riemannian Manifolds and Its Application in Low-Rank Representation
Abstract: This paper presents a new first-order optimization algorithm (FOA) for optimizing composite functions on Riemannian manifolds.  The algorithm has been theoretically proven to achieve quadratic convergence.  FOA outperforms other first-order methods on Riemannian manifolds, as demonstrated by experiments in the matrix completion task.  A fast subspace pursuit method based on FOA, SP-RPRG(ALM), is proposed to solve the low-rank representation model using an augmented Lagrange method on the low-rank matrix variety.  Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that both FOA and SP-RPRG(ALM) achieve superior performance in terms of faster convergence and higher accuracy.
label: AI

title: Sparsifying Neural Network Connections for Face Recognition
Abstract: This paper explores the use of sparse convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) for face recognition.  The proposed approach involves iteratively sparsifying layers of a ConvNet and retraining the entire model using the initial weights learned in previous iterations.  Directly training a sparse ConvNet from scratch proved ineffective for face recognition, highlighting the importance of initializing sparser models with previously learned denser models.  A novel neural correlation-based weight selection criterion is introduced to effectively select informative connections from previously learned models in each iteration.  The sparse ConvNet model, with a moderate sparsity structure (26%-76% of weights in the dense model), significantly enhances the face recognition performance of the state-of-the-art DeepID2+ models while using only 12% of the original parameters.
label: AI

title: Recognition from Hand Cameras
Abstract: This paper investigates the use of a wrist-mounted camera system (HandCam) for recognizing hand activities. HandCam offers advantages over egocentric systems (HeadCam) by eliminating the need for hand detection and providing more consistent observation of hand activities. A deep-learning-based method is proposed for recognizing hand states (free vs. active hands, hand gestures, object categories) and discovering object categories using HandCam. A novel two-streams deep network is also introduced to leverage both HandCam and HeadCam. A synchronized HandCam and HeadCam dataset was collected, consisting of 20 videos captured across three scenes, for hand states recognition. Experiments show that HandCam consistently outperforms both a deep-learning-based HeadCam method (with estimated manipulation regions) and a dense-trajectory-based HeadCam method in all tasks.  The HandCam videos from different users can be aligned to improve free vs. active recognition accuracy (3.3% improvement) in across-scenes use cases.  Fine-tuning Convolutional Neural Networks consistently improves accuracy.  The two-streams deep network combining HandCam and HeadCam features achieves the best performance in four out of five tasks.  With more data, a joint HandCam and HeadCam system could robustly log hand states in daily life.

title: Fixation prediction with a combined model of bottom-up saliency and vanishing point
Abstract: To understand how humans perceive complex natural scenes and prioritize information for visual processing, this paper investigates the influence of vanishing points on human gaze.  While existing saliency models fall short of human performance, this study explores the cognitive factors guiding gaze.  The study shows that human gaze is attracted to vanishing point regions.  Eye movements of 10 observers were recorded across 532 images, with 319 containing vanishing points.  A combined model of traditional saliency and a vanishing point channel was constructed, demonstrating superior performance compared to state-of-the-art saliency models using three evaluation metrics.
label: AI

title: Rank Pooling for Action Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a function-based temporal pooling method for capturing the latent structure of video sequence data.  The method uses the parameters of a function fit to video data to create a new robust video representation.  Specifically, a pooling function is learned via ranking machines, where frame-level features are ranked chronologically.  This results in a representation that captures the video-wide temporal dynamics, suitable for action recognition.  The paper explores other parametric models for explaining temporal changes in videos.  The proposed functional pooling methods, particularly rank pooling, offer ease of interpretation and implementation, fast computation, and effectiveness in recognizing a wide variety of actions.  Evaluations on various benchmarks for generic action, fine-grained action, and gesture recognition demonstrate that rank pooling outperforms average pooling by 7-10% on average.  Rank pooling is compatible and complementary to appearance and local motion-based methods and features, such as improved trajectories and deep learning features.
label: AI

title: PatchBatch: a Batch Augmented Loss for Optical Flow
Abstract: This paper presents a novel deep learning-based pipeline for optical flow computation.  The method utilizes a Siamese CNN to independently and concurrently compute descriptors for both images in a pair.  The learned descriptors are then efficiently compared using the L2 norm, eliminating the need for patch pair network processing.  The success of the method relies on an innovative loss function that calculates higher moments of the loss distributions for each training batch.  Combined with an Approximate Nearest Neighbor patch matching method and a flow interpolation technique, this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the most challenging and competitive optical flow benchmarks.
label: AI

title: The Next Best Underwater View
Abstract: To capture high-resolution images of large, occlusion-prone scenes, a camera must move above and around the scene.  Scattering in participating media exacerbates visibility degradation due to geometric occlusions and distances.  Artificial lighting is often necessary in underwater environments and other media.  This work proposes optimizing camera and light source poses as they move, ensuring efficient surface scanning and high-quality descattered recovery.  The approach generalizes the next best view concept of robot vision to scattering media and cooperative movable lighting, extending descattering to optimally moving platforms.  The optimization criterion is information gain, based on information theory.  The method leverages the existence of a rough 3D model, which is commonly available underwater through sonar.  The principle is demonstrated in a scaled-down setup.
label: AI

title: Image reconstruction from dense binary pixels
Abstract: The dense binary pixel Gigavision camera, emulating a digital version of photographic film, offers promise for HDR imaging.  However, its output requires an image reconstruction process.  This paper formulates this problem as the minimization of a convex objective combining a maximum-likelihood term with a sparse synthesis prior.  MLNet, a novel feed-forward neural network, is presented, achieving acceptable output quality at a fixed complexity and demonstrating two orders of magnitude faster performance than iterative algorithms.  The paper presents state-of-the-art results in the abstract.
label: AI

title: Vanishing point attracts gaze in free-viewing and visual search tasks
Abstract: Two experiments were conducted to investigate the significance of the vanishing point (VP) in gaze guidance.  The first experiment recorded fixations of 10 observers freely viewing 532 images, with 319 containing VPs.  Results showed a significantly higher average number of fixations at a local region centered on the VP compared to random locations.  To address the confounding factor of saliency, a combined model of bottom-up saliency and VP was learned, demonstrating a significantly higher AUC score compared to the original saliency model and the VP-only model.  In the second experiment, 14 subjects searched for a target character placed on a 3x3 grid overlaying images, with some images containing a VP.  Subjects were significantly faster and more accurate when the target was located within the cell containing the VP.  These findings support the hypothesis that vanishing points, similar to faces, text, and gaze direction, attract attention in free-viewing and visual search.

title: A Restricted Visual Turing Test for Deep Scene and Event Understanding
Abstract: This paper presents a restricted visual Turing test (VTT) for evaluating story-line-based deep understanding in long-term and multi-camera videos.  Given videos of a scene and story-line-based queries, the task is to provide answers in binary form ("true/false" for polar queries) or natural language descriptions (for non-polar queries).  Queries can be view-based (answered from a specific camera view) or scene-centered (involving joint inference across cameras).  Story lines encompass spatial, temporal, and causal understanding of the videos.  The paper distinguishes this VTT from existing visual question answering and video captioning tasks.  A vision system is proposed for joint video and query parsing, integrating vision modules, a knowledge base, and a query engine.  The system provides unified interfaces for module reconfiguration.  A benchmark dataset and toolkit for ontology-guided story-line query generation are provided, comprising 93.5 hours of video from four locations and 3,426 queries split into 127 story lines.  A baseline implementation and result analyses are included.

title: Maximum Entropy Binary Encoding for Face Template Protection
Abstract: This paper introduces a framework for secure identification using deep neural networks, applied to template protection for face authentication.  Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed to learn a mapping from face images to maximum entropy binary (MEB) codes.  This mapping is robust enough to handle exact matching, yielding the same code for new samples of a user as the code assigned during training.  These codes are then hashed using a hash function conforming to the random oracle model (like SHA-512) to generate protected face templates.  The algorithm offers high template security, cancelability, and state-of-the-art matching performance without unrealistic assumptions.  Its efficacy is demonstrated on CMU-PIE, Extended Yale B, and Multi-PIE face databases.  High (~95%) genuine accept rates (GAR) are achieved at zero false accept rate (FAR) with up to 1024 bits of template security.
label: AI

title: A Shapley Value Solution to Game Theoretic-based Feature Reduction in False Alarm Detection
Abstract: False alarms are a major concern in intensive care units, leading to care disruption, sleep deprivation, and caregiver insensitivity.  While methods for suppressing false alarms through signal filtering and improved sensors have been proposed, significant intrinsic correlation among extracted features limits the performance of data mining techniques.  This paper proposes a model based on coalition game theory that considers inter-feature dependencies in determining salient predictors for false alarm, resulting in improved classification accuracy.  Simulations using PhysionNet's MIMIC II database demonstrate the superior performance of this method compared to existing approaches.
label: AI

title: Approximated and User Steerable tSNE for Progressive Visual Analytics
Abstract: Progressive Visual Analytics aims to enhance interactivity in existing analytics techniques through visualization and interaction with intermediate results.  Dimensionality reduction is a key method for data analysis, producing 2D embeddings for visualization and analysis.  t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (tSNE) is effective for visualizing high-dimensional data.  However, its slow initialization limits its application in Progressive Visual Analytics.  This paper introduces a controllable tSNE approximation (A-tSNE), trading off speed and accuracy to enable interactive data exploration.  Real-time visualization techniques, including a density-based solution and a Magic Lens, provide feedback on the approximation level.  Users can steer the approximation level during analysis by refining specific areas.  The effectiveness of the technique is demonstrated using various datasets in real-world research scenarios and for real-time analysis of high-dimensional streams.
label: AI

title: A Deep Structured Model with Radius-Margin Bound for 3D Human Activity Recognition
Abstract: Understanding human activity remains challenging even with recent advancements in 3D/depth sensors.  This paper investigates a novel deep structured model that adaptively decomposes activity instances into temporal parts using convolutional neural networks (CNNs).  The model advances traditional deep learning approaches by incorporating latent temporal structure into the deep model, accounting for large temporal variations in diverse human activities.  Latent variables decompose the input activity into temporally segmented sub-activities, which are then fed into parts (sub-networks) of the deep architecture.  A radius-margin bound is incorporated as a regularization term to improve generalization performance for classification.  A principled learning algorithm iteratively discovers optimal latent variables, updates classifiers based on generated features, and updates the parameters of multi-layer neural networks.  Experiments validate the approach on complex scenarios for human activity recognition, demonstrating superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Creation of a Deep Convolutional Auto-Encoder in Caffe
Abstract: This paper describes the development of a deep (stacked) convolutional auto-encoder within the Caffe deep learning framework.  Simple principles used to create the model are discussed.  The proposed convolutional auto-encoder lacks pooling/unpooling layers.  Experimental research shows comparable accuracy of dimensionality reduction compared to a classic auto-encoder using the MNIST dataset.
label: AI

title: Motion trails from time-lapse video
Abstract: Background subtraction, performed on an image sequence captured by a stationary camera, can detect moving foreground objects.  Various heuristics further improve the distinction between foreground and background.  The motion of each object is then emphasized by duplicating its positions as a motion trail.  These trails clarify spatial relationships between objects.  Adding motion trails to a video before high-speed previewing reduces the risk of overlooking transient events.
label: AI

title: Learning the Semantics of Manipulation Action
Abstract: This paper presents a formal computational framework for modeling manipulation actions, applicable to both observing and understanding human actions and executing them with robotic mechanisms.  The formalism, based on Combinatory Categorial Grammar, leads to semantics of manipulation action.  It aims to represent manipulation actions with syntax and semantics, where semantics use λ-calculus, enable probabilistic semantic parsing to learn λ-calculus representations from annotated action corpora, and develop a system that visually observes manipulation actions, understands their meaning, and reasons beyond observations using propositional logic and axiom schemata.  Experiments on a public manipulation action dataset validate the theoretical framework and implementation.
label: AI

title: ASIST: Automatic Semantically Invariant Scene Transformation
Abstract: This paper presents ASIST, a technique for transforming point clouds by replacing objects with their semantically equivalent counterparts.  Transformations of this type have applications in virtual reality, repair of fused scans, and robotics.  ASIST is based on a unified formulation of semantic labeling and object replacement, both achieved by minimizing a single objective.  Numerical tools are presented for efficiently solving this optimization problem.  The method is experimentally assessed on new datasets of synthetic and real point clouds, and compared to recent works on object replacement.
label: AI

title: Computational Imaging for VLBI Image Reconstruction
Abstract: Very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) is a technique for imaging celestial radio emissions using telescopes distributed across Earth.  Reconstructing images from fine angular resolution VLBI data is challenging due to sparsity and noise.  This paper presents a novel Bayesian approach for VLBI image reconstruction, called CHIRP.  Unlike other methods requiring parameter tuning, CHIRP produces good results under various settings, such as low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or extended emission.  The method's success is demonstrated on realistic synthetic experiments and publicly available real data.  The problem is presented in an accessible way for the community, and a dataset website is provided for controlled algorithm comparisons.
label: AI

title: Neuron's Eye View: Inferring Features of Complex Stimuli from Neural Responses
Abstract: Experiments studying neural encoding of stimuli at the individual neuron level typically focus on a small set of features (e.g., contrast and luminance for vision, pitch and intensity for sound) and create stimuli sets that systematically vary along these dimensions.  Analysis then relies on regression models, with experimenter-controlled features as predictors and neural responses as responses.  However, this approach requires prior knowledge of relevant features encoded by a neuron population.  For complex domains like social interaction or natural movement, the relevant feature space is poorly understood.  This paper presents a Bayesian model for exploratory data analysis that automatically identifies features in unstructured stimuli based solely on neuronal responses.  This model assumes that neuronal firing rates are sensitive to multiple discrete time-varying features tied to the stimulus, each with Markov or semi-Markov dynamics.  The model derives a fast variational Bayesian inference algorithm and shows its effectiveness in recovering hidden features in synthetic data and ground-truth stimulus features in a prototypical neural dataset.  The algorithm is applied to cluster neural responses, demonstrating successful recovery of features corresponding to monkeys and faces in an image set. |||
label: AI

title: Model Validation for Vision Systems via Graphics Simulation
Abstract: Rapid advances in computing, combined with the latest developments in computer graphics simulations, have facilitated the creation of vision systems and their training within virtual environments. However, a major hurdle remains in certifying the design and optimized parameters of these systems for real-world application. This paper delves into the fundamental question: which information transfer methodology better resembles real-world scenarios? Inspired by performance characterization methodologies established in the 1990s, we observe that insights derived from simulations can be either qualitative or quantitative, depending on the fidelity of the models used in the simulations and the nature of the questions posed by the experimenter. We adapt this methodology within the context of current graphics simulation tools to model data generation processes, enabling systematic performance characterization and trade-off analysis for vision system design, leading to qualitative and quantitative insights. Specifically, we examine invariance assumptions employed in vision algorithms for video surveillance settings as a case study and assess the extent to which these invariance assumptions deviate as a function of contextual variables in both graphics simulations and real-world data. As computer graphics rendering quality improves, we believe that systematically teasing apart the validity of model assumptions through graphics simulations can significantly assist in developing more principled approaches to vision system design and performance modeling.

title: Max-Pooling Dropout for Regularization of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Dropout has gained increasing popularity in deep learning. While dropout has proven effective in fully-connected layers of deep convolutional neural networks, its effect in pooling layers remains unclear. This paper demonstrates that max-pooling dropout is equivalent to randomly selecting activations based on a multinomial distribution during training. Based on this insight, we propose using probabilistic weighted pooling instead of the commonly used max-pooling as a form of model averaging at test time. Empirical evidence validates the superiority of probabilistic weighted pooling. We also compare max-pooling dropout and stochastic pooling, both of which introduce stochasticity based on multinomial distributions at the pooling stage.
label: AI

title: Sublabel-Accurate Relaxation of Nonconvex Energies
Abstract: We introduce a novel spatially continuous framework for convex relaxations based on functional lifting. Our method can be interpreted as a sublabel-accurate solution for multilabel problems. We demonstrate that previously proposed functional lifting methods optimize an energy that is linear between two labels, requiring (often infinitely) many labels for accurate approximation. In contrast, our proposed formulation utilizes a piecewise convex approximation, requiring significantly fewer labels. Compared to recent MRF-based approaches, our method is formulated in a spatially continuous setting, exhibiting less grid bias. Furthermore, our formulation represents the tightest possible convex relaxation in a local sense. It is easy to implement and allows efficient primal-dual optimization on GPUs. We showcase the effectiveness of our approach across various computer vision problems.
label: AI

title: Staple: Complementary Learners for Real-Time Tracking
Abstract: Correlation Filter-based trackers have recently achieved remarkable performance, demonstrating significant robustness to challenging situations involving motion blur and illumination changes. However, their reliance on the spatial layout of the tracked object makes them highly sensitive to deformation. Models based on color statistics offer complementary strengths: they effectively handle shape variations but struggle with inconsistent illumination throughout a sequence. Furthermore, color distributions alone can be insufficiently discriminative. This paper presents a simple tracker that combines complementary cues within a ridge regression framework, achieving faster performance than 80 FPS and surpassing not only all entries in the popular VOT14 competition but also recent and far more sophisticated trackers across multiple benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Toward a Taxonomy and Computational Models of Abnormalities in Images
Abstract: The human visual system possesses the ability to detect anomalous images and reason about their unusual aspects. This task has not received sufficient attention in computer vision. This paper investigates various types of atypicalities in images more comprehensively than previous studies. We introduce a novel dataset of abnormal images showcasing a wide range of atypicalities. Through human subject experiments, we aim to discover a coarse taxonomy of the reasons for abnormality. Our experiments reveal three primary categories of abnormality: object-centric, scene-centric, and contextual. Based on this taxonomy, we propose a comprehensive computational model capable of predicting all different types of abnormality in images, outperforming prior art in abnormality recognition.
label: AI

title: What can we learn about CNNs from a large scale controlled object dataset?
Abstract: Tolerance to image variations (e.g., translation, scale, pose, illumination) is a crucial desired property for any object recognition system, be it human or machine. Computer vision has witnessed a trend towards increasingly larger datasets, especially with the emergence of highly popular deep learning models. While these large-scale, real-world datasets are valuable for learning invariance to object inter- and intra-class shape variability, they are less effective for learning invariance to other parameters, forcing researchers to rely on alternative techniques for model training. This work introduces a large-scale synthetic dataset, freely and publicly available, to address fundamental questions regarding invariance and selectivity properties of convolutional neural networks. Our dataset consists of two parts: (a) objects captured on a turntable: 16 categories, 8 rotation angles, 11 cameras on a semicircular arch, 5 lighting conditions, 3 focus levels, various backgrounds (23.4 per instance) generating 1320 images per instance (over 20 million images in total), and (b) scenes: where a robot arm captures images of objects on a 1:160 scale scene. We investigate: 1) invariance and selectivity of different CNN layers, 2) knowledge transfer between object categories, 3) systematic or random image sampling for building a training set, 4) domain adaptation from synthetic to natural scenes, and 5) the order of knowledge delivery to CNNs. We explore how these analyses can guide the development of more efficient CNNs.
label: AI

title: Predicting and visualizing psychological attributions with a deep neural network
Abstract: Judgments about personality based on facial appearance play a significant role in social decision-making and are known to influence various aspects, from presidential elections to jury decisions. Recent research has shown that it is possible to predict perceptions of memorability, trustworthiness, intelligence, and other attributes from human face images. The most successful of these approaches require face images expertly annotated with key facial landmarks. We present a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model capable of performing the same task without the need for landmark features, significantly enhancing efficiency. The model exhibits high accuracy, surpassing human-level performance in some cases. Furthermore, we utilize a deconvolutional approach to visualize important features for the perception of 22 attributes and demonstrate a novel method for separately visualizing positive and negative features.

title: Prototypical Priors: From Improving Classification to Zero-Shot Learning
Abstract: Recent advancements in zero-shot learning leverage side information such as visual attributes or natural language semantics to define relationships between output visual classes and then use these relationships to draw inferences on unseen classes during testing. In a novel extension to this concept, we propose utilizing visual prototypical concepts as side information. While establishing a unique prototype for most real-world visual object categories can be challenging, categories like traffic signs, brand logos, flags, and even natural language characters possess readily available prototypical templates that can be leveraged for improved recognition performance. This work introduces a method to incorporate this prototypical information within a deep learning framework. Using prototypes as prior information, the deepnet pipeline learns input image projections into the prototypical embedding space, minimizing the final classification loss. Our experiments on two distinct datasets of traffic signs and brand logos demonstrate that prototypical embeddings incorporated into a conventional convolutional neural network enhance recognition performance. Notably, the recognition accuracy on the Belga logo dataset establishes a new state-of-the-art. In zero-shot learning scenarios, the same system can be directly deployed to draw inferences on unseen classes by simply adding the prototypical information for these new classes at test time. Unlike earlier approaches, testing on both seen and unseen classes is handled using the same pipeline, allowing the system to be tuned for a trade-off between seen and unseen class performance based on task requirements. Comparison with one of the latest works in the zero-shot learning domain yields top results on the two datasets mentioned above.
label: AI

title: Trending Chic: Analyzing the Influence of Social Media on Fashion Brands
Abstract: Social media platforms serve as popular venues for fashion brand marketing and advertising. The introduction of native advertising eliminates the need for banner ads, which hold minimal saliency and are unattractive to users. Through the use of images and subtle text overlays, brands can retain their audience even in a world of declining attention spans, offering significant creative potential. While various marketing strategies are often hypothesized, the subtle distinctions between different types of marketing strategies remain underexplored. This paper presents a qualitative analysis of the influence of social media platforms on distinct fashion brand marketing behaviors. We employ both linguistic and computer vision techniques, comparing and contrasting strategic idiosyncrasies. We also analyze brand audience retention and social engagement, providing suggestions for adapting advertising and marketing strategies across Twitter and Instagram.

title: Occlusion-Aware Human Pose Estimation with Mixtures of Sub-Trees
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of learning a model for human pose estimation as mixtures of compositional sub-trees in two layers of prediction. This involves estimating the pose of a sub-tree followed by identifying the relationships between sub-trees to handle occlusions between different parts. The mixtures of sub-trees are learned using both geometric and appearance distances. The Chow-Liu (CL) algorithm is recursively applied to determine the inter-relationships between nodes and build the structure of the sub-trees. These structures are then used to learn the latent parameters of the sub-trees, and inference is performed using a standard belief propagation technique. The proposed method handles occlusions during the inference process by identifying overlapping regions between different sub-trees and introducing a penalty term for overlapping parts. Experiments are conducted on three different datasets: the Leeds Sports, Image Parse, and UIUC People datasets. The results demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method to occlusions compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Simulations for Validation of Vision Systems
Abstract: As computer vision matures into a systems science and engineering discipline, there is a growing trend in leveraging the latest advancements in computer graphics simulations for performance evaluation, learning, and inference. However, the utility of graphics simulations for vision remains an open question, with seemingly contradicting perspectives in the literature. This paper contextualizes results from recent literature within the framework of performance characterization methodologies outlined in the 1990s, highlighting that insights derived from simulations can be either qualitative or quantitative, depending on the fidelity of the models used in the simulation and the nature of the questions posed by the experimenter. We describe a simulation platform incorporating the latest graphics advances and use it for systematic performance characterization and trade-off analysis for vision system design. We validate the utility of the platform by conducting a case study on a generative model-inspired vision hypothesis, the Rank-Order consistency model, in the context of global and local illumination changes, bad weather, and high-frequency noise. Our approach bridges the gap between alternative viewpoints, involving models with physics-based semantics and signal and perturbation semantics, confirming insights found in the literature on robust change detection.

title: Weighted Schatten $p$-Norm Minimization for Image Denoising and Background Subtraction
Abstract: Low-rank matrix approximation (LRMA), aiming to recover the underlying low-rank matrix from its degraded observation, finds widespread applications in computer vision. Recent LRMA methods rely on nuclear norm minimization (NNM) as a convex relaxation of the nonconvex rank minimization. However, NNM tends to over-shrink rank components and treats all components equally, limiting its flexibility in practical scenarios. We propose a more flexible model, namely the Weighted Schatten p-Norm Minimization (WSNM), generalizing NNM to Schatten p-norm minimization with weights assigned to different singular values. The proposed WSNM not only provides a better approximation to the original low-rank assumption but also considers the importance of different rank components. We analyze the solution of WSNM and prove that, under certain weight permutations, WSNM can be equivalently transformed into independent non-convex lp-norm subproblems, whose global optima can be efficiently solved using a generalized iterated shrinkage algorithm. We apply WSNM to typical low-level vision problems, such as image denoising and background subtraction. Extensive experimental results demonstrate, both qualitatively and quantitatively, that the proposed WSNM can more effectively remove noise and model complex and dynamic scenes compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Fast Low-Rank Matrix Learning with Nonconvex Regularization
Abstract: Low-rank modeling plays a crucial role in machine learning, computer vision, and social network analysis. While the matrix rank is often approximated by the convex nuclear norm, the use of nonconvex low-rank regularizers has demonstrated superior recovery performance. However, the resulting optimization problem is significantly more challenging. A very recent state-of-the-art approach utilizes the proximal gradient algorithm, requiring an expensive full SVD in each proximal step. This paper shows that, for many commonly used nonconvex low-rank regularizers, a cutoff can be derived to automatically threshold the singular values obtained from the proximal operator. This enables the efficient use of the power method to approximate the SVD. Additionally, the proximal operator can be reduced to that of a much smaller matrix projected onto this leading subspace. Convergence, with a rate of O(1/T) where T is the number of iterations, is guaranteed. Extensive experiments are conducted on matrix completion and robust principal component analysis. The proposed method achieves significant speedup compared to the state-of-the-art. Furthermore, the matrix solution obtained is more accurate and has a lower rank than that of the traditional nuclear norm regularizer.
