title: A Literature Survey of various Fingerprint De-noising Techniques to justify the need of a new De-noising model based upon Pixel Component Analysis
Abstract: Image preprocessing is an essential step in the field of image processing for biometric pattern recognition. This paper studies and reviews various classical and modern fingerprint image de-noising models. These models range widely from transform matrices using frequency, histogram model de-noising, de-noising by introducing Gabor filters and their types to enhance fingerprint images. The output efficiency of various proposed de-noising models is calculated based on SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) and MSE (mean square error rate). Our simulated experimental results indicate that incorporating the de-noising model based on Gabor filters within the domain of wavelets using a composite method only improves MSE (Mean Square Error). Improved MSE without significant improvement in SNR enhances fingerprint images only marginally, which is suboptimal in nature. Therefore, this research paper aims to develop an optimal de-noising model for fingerprint images, making biometric authentication more robust.
label: AI

title: The Indian Spontaneous Expression Database for Emotion Recognition
Abstract: Automatic recognition of spontaneous facial expressions poses a significant challenge in the field of affective computing. Attributes such as head rotation, face pose, illumination variation, and occlusion increase the complexity of recognizing spontaneous expressions in practical applications. Effective recognition of expressions heavily depends on the quality of the database used. Most well-known facial expression databases consist of posed expressions. However, there is a growing demand for spontaneous expression databases for the pragmatic implementation of facial expression recognition algorithms. This paper proposes and establishes a new facial expression database containing spontaneous expressions from both male and female participants of Indian origin. The database comprises 428 segmented video clips of spontaneous facial expressions from 50 participants. In our experiment, emotions were induced among participants using emotional videos, and their self-ratings for each experienced emotion were simultaneously collected. Facial expression clips were carefully annotated by four trained decoders, further validated by the nature of stimuli used and self-reported emotions. An extensive analysis of the database was conducted using several machine learning algorithms, and the results are provided for future reference. This spontaneous database will aid in the development and validation of algorithms for recognizing spontaneous expressions.

title: Innovation Pursuit: A New Approach to Subspace Clustering
Abstract: In subspace clustering, a group of data points belonging to a union of subspaces are assigned membership to their respective subspaces. This paper presents a novel approach, dubbed Innovation Pursuit (iPursuit), to the problem of subspace clustering using a new geometrical idea where subspaces are identified based on their relative novelties. We introduce two frameworks where the concept of innovation pursuit is employed to distinguish the subspaces. The first framework is based on an iterative method that finds the subspaces consecutively by solving a series of simple linear optimization problems. Each problem searches for a direction of innovation within the span of the data, potentially orthogonal to all subspaces except the one to be identified in a single step of the algorithm. We provide a detailed mathematical analysis establishing sufficient conditions for iPursuit to correctly cluster the data. The proposed approach can provably yield exact clustering even when subspaces have significant intersections. We demonstrate that the complexity of the iterative approach scales linearly with the number of data points and subspaces and quadratically with the dimension of the subspaces. The second framework integrates iPursuit with spectral clustering to yield a new variant of spectral-clustering-based algorithms. Numerical simulations with both real and synthetic data demonstrate that iPursuit can often outperform state-of-the-art subspace clustering algorithms, particularly for subspaces with significant intersections, and significantly improves the state-of-the-art result for subspace-segmentation-based face clustering.
label: AI

title: Compressive hyperspectral imaging via adaptive sampling and dictionary learning
Abstract: This paper proposes a new sampling strategy for hyperspectral signals based on dictionary learning and singular value decomposition (SVD). Specifically, we first learn a sparsifying dictionary from training spectral data using dictionary learning. We then perform an SVD on the dictionary and utilize the first few left singular vectors as the rows of the measurement matrix to obtain compressive measurements for reconstruction. The proposed method offers significant improvement over conventional compressive sensing approaches. The reconstruction performance is further enhanced by reconditioning the sensing matrix using matrix balancing. We also demonstrate the robustness of combining dictionary learning and SVD by applying them to different datasets.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Event Detection by Multimodal Distributional Semantic Embedding of Videos
Abstract: We introduce a novel zero-shot Event Detection method using Multi-modal Distributional Semantic embedding of videos. Our model embeds object and action concepts, along with other available modalities from videos, into a distributional semantic space. To our knowledge, this is the first Zero-Shot event detection model built upon distributional semantics and extends it in the following ways: (a) semantic embedding of multimodal information in videos (with a focus on visual modalities), (b) automatically determining the relevance of concepts/attributes to a free text query, potentially useful for other applications, and (c) retrieving videos based on free text event queries (e.g., "changing a vehicle tire") based on their content. We embed videos into a distributional semantic space and then measure the similarity between videos and event queries in a free text form. We validated our method on the large TRECVID MED (Multimedia Event Detection) challenge. Using only the event title as a query, our method outperformed the state-of-the-art, which utilizes extensive descriptions, by 12.6% to 13.5% with MAP metric and 0.73 to 0.83 with ROC-AUC metric. It is also an order of magnitude faster.

title: Actions ~ Transformations
Abstract: What defines an action like "kicking a ball"? We argue that the true meaning of an action lies in the transformation it brings to the environment. This paper proposes a novel representation for actions by modeling an action as a transformation that changes the state of the environment before the action occurs (precondition) to the state after the action (effect). Inspired by recent advancements in video representation using deep learning, we design a Siamese network that models the action as a transformation within a high-level feature space. We show that our model improves performance on standard action recognition datasets including UCF101 and HMDB51. More importantly, our approach generalizes beyond learned action categories and shows significant performance improvement on cross-category generalization on our new ACT dataset.

title: Active Learning for Delineation of Curvilinear Structures
Abstract: Many recent delineation techniques owe their increased effectiveness to path classification algorithms that enable distinguishing promising paths from others. The downside of this development is that they require annotated training data, which is tedious to produce. This paper proposes an Active Learning approach that significantly speeds up the annotation process. Unlike standard approaches, it leverages the specificities of the delineation problem. It operates on a graph and can reduce the training set size by up to 80% without compromising reconstruction quality. We will show that our approach outperforms conventional ones on various biomedical and natural image datasets, demonstrating its broad applicability.

title: Recognizing Semantic Features in Faces using Deep Learning
Abstract: Deep learning techniques offer a promising approach for automated interpretation of semantic information in human faces, eliminating the need for manual feature design. This thesis investigates the impact of various factors and hyperparameters on the performance of deep neural networks for semantic facial feature recognition, aiming to determine optimal network configurations. The study explores the system's effectiveness in recognizing diverse semantic features like emotions, age, gender, and ethnicity, analyzing the relationship between high-level concepts and low-level features. Additionally, the thesis proposes a novel method for generating 3D Active Appearance Models of faces from 2D images using a deep network.

title: MMSE Estimation for Poisson Noise Removal in Images
Abstract: This research introduces a novel patch-wise Poisson noise removal strategy that leverages the MMSE estimator for denoising each image patch. The proposed method employs k-d tree search and K-nearest neighbor graph analysis for fast and accurate MMSE estimator computation. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of this approach, particularly in low signal-to-noise ratio scenarios.

title: Continuous and Simultaneous Gesture and Posture Recognition for Commanding a Robotic Wheelchair; Towards Spotting the Signal Patterns
Abstract: This study presents a signal pattern recognition approach for continuous and simultaneous classification of hand postures and gestures, mapping them to steering commands for robotic wheelchair control. The methodology achieves 100% recognition accuracy on streaming signals, eliminating the need for human intervention in training dictionary construction. Subspace clustering techniques are used to identify the most representative state samples during training, and a successive decision tree structure reveals pattern boundaries on streaming signals. Collaborative and Block Sparse Representation based classification methods are employed for continuous gesture and posture recognition.

title: Double Sparse Multi-Frame Image Super Resolution
Abstract: Sparse coding-based image super-resolution algorithms have emerged, including those utilizing multi-frame super-resolution. This paper proposes a novel approach for multi-frame super-resolution based on sparse coding, addressing the challenges of accurate image registration and sparse coding optimization. The proposed method optimizes a single objective function, simultaneously addressing both problems. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.

title: The MegaFace Benchmark: 1 Million Faces for Recognition at Scale
Abstract: Recent face recognition advancements have achieved near-perfect performance on benchmarks like LFW. However, this paper emphasizes the need for evaluation at a million-scale, introducing the MegaFace dataset and challenge. The dataset includes one million photos of over 690K individuals, evaluating algorithm performance with increasing numbers of distractors in the gallery set. The paper analyzes identification and verification performance, explores the impact of pose and age, and compares results based on training data size. Experiments reveal significant performance differences between algorithms at the million scale, highlighting the ongoing challenges of age-invariant recognition and pose.
label: AI

title: Attribute2Image: Conditional Image Generation from Visual Attributes
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of generating images from visual attributes by modeling images as a composite of foreground and background. A layered generative model with disentangled latent variables is developed using a variational auto-encoder, enabling end-to-end learning. The model is evaluated on natural images of faces and birds, demonstrating the generation of realistic and diverse samples with disentangled representations. A general energy minimization algorithm facilitates posterior inference of latent variables given novel images, resulting in excellent quantitative and visual performance for attribute-conditioned image reconstruction and completion tasks.

title: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision
Abstract: Convolutional networks are fundamental to many state-of-the-art computer vision solutions. While deeper networks generally improve performance, computational efficiency remains a crucial factor for mobile vision and large-scale applications. This work investigates methods for scaling up networks by incorporating factorized convolutions and aggressive regularization, maximizing the utilization of added computation. The proposed methods demonstrate substantial performance improvements on the ILSVRC 2012 classification challenge, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy with a significantly lower computational cost and parameter count.

title: Labeling the Features Not the Samples: Efficient Video Classification with Minimal Supervision
Abstract: Effective visual recognition relies on efficient feature selection. This paper introduces a novel joint classifier learning and feature selection method that discovers sparse, compact representations from a vast pool of candidates, requiring minimal supervision. The method utilizes "feature signs," indicating the average strength of features for positive samples compared to negatives, which can be estimated using a single labeled training sample per class. These feature signs facilitate an unsupervised clustering formulation, allowing for incremental data incorporation without ground truth labels. The method exhibits low computational cost and high accuracy, particularly in scenarios with limited training data. Experiments on large-scale video recognition demonstrate superior speed and performance compared to existing feature selection approaches.

title: Efficient Edge Detection on Low-Cost FPGAs
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel edge detection architecture optimized for field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), aiming to enhance efficiency and reduce system cost and power dissipation in embedded applications like UAV control. The architecture leverages Sobel edge kernels, known for their separability and absence of multiplications. Edge intensities are calculated using a 4:2 compressor composed of custom-designed 3:2 compressors, while addition speed is improved through carry propagation chain breaking with look-ahead logic. The design exhibits a significant increase in speed and reduction in area compared to previous designs, contributing to cost reduction and power savings in edge detection systems.
label: AI

title: Loss Functions for Top-k Error: Analysis and Insights
Abstract: Recent advancements in computer vision tasks have resulted in benchmark datasets with a large number of classes, leading to increased ambiguity between class labels. This paper investigates the effectiveness of top-k performance evaluation in such scenarios, comparing established multiclass methods and their top-k performance from both practical and theoretical perspectives. The paper introduces novel top-k loss functions derived from softmax and multiclass SVM losses, accompanied by efficient optimization schemes. Experimental results on various datasets compare the proposed and established methods for top-k error optimization. The study reveals that softmax loss consistently achieves competitive top-k performance, while the new top-k losses offer further improvements for specific k values with faster training than softmax.

title: Accelerated graph-based nonlinear denoising filters
Abstract: Denoising filters like bilateral, guided, and total variation filters applied to images on general graphs often require repeated application for significant noise reduction. This paper introduces two acceleration techniques for iterative denoising: conjugate gradient method and Nesterov's acceleration. Numerical analysis demonstrates the efficiency of accelerated nonlinear filters for image denoising, achieving significant speed-up by reducing the number of iterations needed to reach a target peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).

title: On Optical Flow Models for Variational Motion Estimation
Abstract: This paper explores total variation-based regularization methods for motion estimation, particularly focusing on optical flow models. It provides an overview of different total variation regularization variants, combining them with higher-order models, and presents a unified computational optimization approach based on primal-dual methods. The paper also extends the models through Bregman iterations, offering an inverse problems perspective to variational optical flow models. The primary focus is on the quantitative evaluation of motion estimation, a challenging and often underestimated task. The paper discusses various quality measures for motion estimation and compares the effectiveness of different regularization approaches.

title: Towards Dropout Training for Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Dropout has gained popularity in deep learning, proving effective in fully-connected layers of convolutional neural networks. However, its impact on convolutional and pooling layers remains unclear. This paper demonstrates that max-pooling dropout is equivalent to randomly picking activation based on a multinomial distribution during training. Based on this insight, the paper advocates for probabilistic weighted pooling, replacing max-pooling, to act as model averaging at test time. Empirical evidence supports the superiority of probabilistic weighted pooling. The paper also explores the non-trivial effect of convolutional dropout, despite the reduced overfitting potential in convolutional architectures. By elaborately designing dropout training in both max-pooling and fully-connected layers, the paper achieves state-of-the-art performance on MNIST and competitive results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, outperforming other approaches without data augmentation. Finally, the paper compares max-pooling dropout and stochastic pooling, both introducing stochasticity based on multinomial distributions at the pooling stage.

title: Fast and High Quality Highlight Removal from A Single Image
Abstract: Specular reflection, a common occurrence in photography, can distort recorded colors. This paper proposes an analytical solution for highlight removal from single natural images, based on an L2 chromaticity definition and dichromatic model. The paper derives a normalized dichromatic model for pixels with identical diffuse color, representing projection coefficients in two orthogonal subspaces: one parallel to illumination and the other orthogonal to it. The illumination-orthogonal subspace, free from specular reflection, allows for robust clustering with adaptive cluster number determination. In the illumination-parallel subspace, a property called Pure Diffuse Pixels Distribution Rule (PDDR) helps map specular-influenced pixels to their diffuse components. The method is computationally efficient, involving minimal complex calculations, enabling fast highlight removal from high-resolution images. Experiments demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed approach in various challenging scenarios.
label: AI

title: Analyzing Classifiers: Fisher Vectors and Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Fisher Vector classifiers and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely used for image classification but are often considered "black box" predictors due to their non-linear transformations. This paper extends the Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) framework to Fisher Vector classifiers, utilizing it to analyze the reasoning behind complex classification models. The study quantifies the importance of context for classification, qualitatively compares DNNs and FV classifiers in terms of important image regions, and detects potential flaws and biases in data. All experiments are conducted on the PASCAL VOC 2007 dataset.

title: Implicit Sparse Code Hashing
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of converting high-dimensional image data into binary codes for efficient approximate nearest-neighbor search. Unlike existing unsupervised approaches, this method focuses on preserving image relationships through inner products of sparse codes rather than Euclidean distances. While the formulation avoids computing sparse codes, it still involves solving a complex eigenproblem for high-dimensional descriptors. To overcome this challenge, the paper utilizes column-sampling techniques and assumes a specific form of rotation matrix for subproblem decomposition. Experiments on challenging image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this method compared to state-of-the-art binary coding techniques.

title: Dynamic Parallel and Distributed Graph Cuts
Abstract: Graph-cuts are commonly used in computer vision, but optimization can be time-consuming for large graphs. To address this, Strandmark and Kahl introduced a splitting method for parallel computation, but this approach lacks a polynomial bound on iterations and may not converge due to multiple optimal sub-problem solutions. This paper introduces a merging method to address this non-convergence issue, merging adjacent sub-graphs that struggle to reach agreement on overlapping regions. Based on the pseudo-boolean representation of graph cuts, the merging method effectively reuses computed flows from sub-graphs. Combining splitting and merging, the paper proposes a dynamic parallel and distributed graph-cuts algorithm guaranteeing convergence to globally optimal solutions within a predefined number of iterations. This work provides a general framework for incorporating more sophisticated splitting and merging strategies to enhance performance, validated through extensive experimental results.

title: Sparseness Meets Deepness: 3D Human Pose Estimation from Monocular Video
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of 3D full-body human pose estimation from a monocular image sequence, considering two scenarios: known and unknown joint locations. For known locations, a novel approach integrates a sparsity-driven 3D geometric prior with temporal smoothness. For unknown locations, the approach is extended by treating joint locations as latent variables. A deep fully convolutional network is trained to predict uncertainty maps for 2D joint locations. 3D pose estimates are obtained through an Expectation-Maximization algorithm over the entire sequence, where 2D joint location uncertainties are marginalized out during inference. Empirical evaluation on the Human3.6M dataset demonstrates superior 3D pose estimation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. The approach also outperforms a 2D pose estimation baseline on the challenging PennAction dataset.

title: Proposed Approximate Dynamic Programming for Pathfinding under Visible Uncertainty
Abstract: Building upon previous work, this paper defines the safest-with-sight pathfinding problem, exploring its solution using techniques from measure-theoretic probability theory. A recursive definition is provided for the probability of an ideal pathfinder selecting an edge in an uncertain network, considering edge failure probabilities and vertex vision of edges through lines-of-sight. An approximate solution is proposed based on theoretical findings, utilizing techniques from approximate dynamic programming.

title: Full-density multi-scale account of structure and dynamics of macaque visual cortex
Abstract: This paper presents a multi-scale spiking network model of all vision-related areas of macaque cortex, representing each area with a full-scale microcircuit and area-specific architecture. The network connectivity integrates axonal tracing data from the CoCoMac database with recent quantitative tracing data, refined through dynamical constraints. Simulations reveal a stable asynchronous irregular ground state with heterogeneous activity across areas, layers, and populations. Large-scale interactions result in longer intrinsic time scales in higher visual areas compared to early ones. Activity propagation down the visual hierarchy aligns with experimental findings associated with visual imagery. Cortico-cortical interaction patterns match fMRI resting-state functional connectivity. The model bridges the gap between local and large-scale accounts of cortex, elucidating how detailed connectivity shapes cortical dynamics across multiple scales. |||

title: Behavior Discovery and Alignment of Articulated Object Classes from Unstructured Video
Abstract: We propose an automated system for organizing unstructured video collections of articulated objects (e.g., tigers, horses). Our system leverages recurring motion patterns to identify characteristic behaviors and recover pixel-to-pixel alignments across different instances of the object class. This system can be utilized for indexing and retrieval of video collections and serves as a platform for learning object class appearance and behaviors from internet videos. Traditional supervised methods are limited in their ability to utilize this wealth of data due to the requirement of extensive manual annotations. Our behavior discovery stage automatically identifies and clusters temporal video intervals, each representing a unique behavior. This stage relies on a novel motion representation based on the displacement of ordered pairs of trajectories. The alignment stage accurately aligns hundreds of instances of the object class, despite significant appearance variations. It employs a flexible Thin Plate Spline deformation model, which can vary over time. We evaluate our system rigorously using a new, fully annotated dataset. Our results demonstrate superior performance in behavior discovery compared to the state-of-the-art Improved DTF descriptor and outperform the popular SIFT Flow algorithm for spatial alignment.

title: Design of Kernels in Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Classification
Abstract: Despite the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification, the relationship between the shape of convolution kernels and learned representations remains unclear. This work explores and exploits the relationship between the shape of kernels, which define Receptive Fields (RFs) in CNNs, for learning feature representations and image classification. We introduce a feature visualization method to visualize pixel-wise classification score maps of learned features. Motivated by experimental results and observations reported in the literature regarding visual system modeling, we propose a novel design for kernel shapes to learn representations in CNNs. Our experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art classification performance compared to a baseline CNN model using the ILSVRC-2012 dataset, while reducing the number of parameters and computational time. The proposed models also outperform state-of-the-art models on the CIFAR-10/100 datasets for image classification. Additionally, we analyzed the robustness of our method to occlusion for classifying partially occluded images, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to existing approaches. The code is available on github.com/minogame/caffe-qhconv.

title: Fine-Grained Classification via Mixture of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: We present a novel deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) system called MixDCNN for fine-grained image classification. Fine-grained image classification is characterized by large intra-class variations and small inter-class variations. To address these challenges, MixDCNN partitions images into K subsets of similar images and learns an expert DCNN for each subset. The outputs from the K DCNNs are combined to form a single classification decision. Unlike previous techniques, our approach allows for joint end-to-end training of the K DCNNs simultaneously. Extensive experiments conducted on three datasets using two network structures (AlexNet and GoogLeNet) demonstrate that MixDCNN consistently outperforms other methods. It provides a relative improvement of 12.7% and achieves state-of-the-art results on two datasets.

title: Incidental Scene Text Understanding: Recent Progresses on ICDAR 2015 Robust Reading Competition Challenge 4
Abstract: Incidental texts, unlike focused texts present in natural images, exhibit greater diversity, variability, and complexity, posing significant challenges for scene text detection and recognition algorithms. The ICDAR 2015 Robust Reading Competition Challenge 4 was designed to assess the performance of existing methods on incidental texts and stimulate new ideas and solutions. This report provides a brief overview of our strategies for this challenging problem, comparing them to prior art in the field.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical Invariant Feature Learning with Marginalization for Person Re-Identification
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of matching pedestrians across multiple camera views, known as person re-identification. Re-identification is a challenging problem due to variations in lighting conditions, environment, and pose changes across camera views. Previous methods have addressed these challenges by designing specific features or learning a distance function. We propose a hierarchical feature learning framework that learns invariant representations from labeled image pairs. This framework learns a mapping that extracts features invariant for images belonging to the same individual across different views. To learn robust representations and achieve better generalization to unseen data, the system requires training with a large amount of data. However, most person re-identification datasets are small. Manually augmenting the dataset through partial corruption of input data introduces significant computational burden. We propose a hierarchical network incorporating a marginalization technique that leverages the benefits of training on large datasets without explicit augmentation. We compare our approach with baseline algorithms and popular linear and non-linear metric learning algorithms, demonstrating improved performance on challenging publicly available datasets: VIPeR, CUHK01, CAVIAR4REID, and iLIDS. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on these datasets.

title: Coresets for Kinematic Data: From Theorems to Real-Time Systems
Abstract: A coreset (or core-set) of a dataset is a semantic compression with respect to a set of queries, such that querying the (small) coreset provably yields an approximate answer to querying the original (full) dataset. Coresets have enabled breakthroughs in theoretical computer science for approximation algorithms and, more recently, in the machine learning community for learning "Big data." However, real-time systems that compute coresets at a rate of dozens of frames per second are currently unavailable. This paper presents a framework for developing such systems using coresets. We provide a proof of independent interest, demonstrating that any set of $n$ matrices in $\\mathbb{R}^{d\\times d}$ whose sum is $S$, has a positively weighted subset whose sum has the same center of mass (mean) and orientation (left+right singular vectors) as $S$, and consists of $O(dr)$ matrices (independent of $n$), where $r\\leq d$ is the rank of $S$. We provide an algorithm that computes this (core) set in one pass over a potentially infinite stream of matrices in $d^{O(1)}$ time per matrix insertion. By maintaining a coreset for a kinematic (moving) set of $n$ points, we can run pose-estimation algorithms such as Kabsch or PnP on the small coresets instead of the $n$ points in real-time using weak devices while obtaining the same results. This enabled us to implement a low-cost ($<\\$100$) IoT wireless system that tracks a toy (and harmless) quadcopter guiding guests to a desired room (in a hospital, mall, hotel, museum, etc.) without the need for additional human or remote control. Our framework encourages researchers outside the theoretical community to design and utilize coresets in future systems and papers. We provide extensive experimental results on both synthetic and real data, as well as a link to the open code of our system and algorithms.

title: Sparse Coral Classification Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Autonomous repair of deep-sea coral reefs is a recently proposed idea to support the oceans ecosystem, which is vital for commercial fishing, tourism, and other species. This idea involves using numerous small autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm intelligence techniques to locate and replace broken coral chunks, enabling re-growth and maintaining the habitat. This project aims to develop machine vision algorithms to enable an underwater robot to locate a coral reef and a coral chunk on the seabed, prompting the robot to pick it up. Although there is no existing literature on this specific problem, related work on fish counting may provide some insight. The technical challenges are primarily due to potential water clarity issues, platform stabilization, and spurious artifacts (rocks, fish, and crabs). We present an efficient sparse classification for coral species using a supervised deep learning method called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We compute Weber Local Descriptor (WLD), Phase Congruency (PC), and Zero Component Analysis (ZCA) Whitening to extract shape and texture feature descriptors. These descriptors are employed as supplementary channels (feature-based maps) in addition to basic spatial color channels (spatial-based maps) of the coral input image. We also experiment with state-of-the-art preprocessing underwater algorithms for image enhancement, color normalization, and color conversion adjustment. Our proposed coral classification method is developed on the MATLAB platform and evaluated using two different coral datasets: University of California San Diego's Moorea Labeled Corals, and Heriot-Watt University's Atlantic Deep Sea.

title: The Multiverse Loss for Robust Transfer Learning
Abstract: Deep learning techniques are renowned for supporting effective transfer learning. However, as we demonstrate, the transferred representations support only a few modes of separation, and much of its dimensionality is unutilized. This work proposes learning multiple orthogonal classifiers in the source domain. We prove that this leads to a reduced rank representation, which supports more discriminative directions. Interestingly, the softmax probabilities produced by the multiple classifiers are likely to be identical. Experimental results on CIFAR-100 and LFW further demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.
label: AI

title: On-line Recognition of Handwritten Mathematical Symbols
Abstract: Identifying the name of an unknown symbol is often difficult, but writing the symbol is straightforward. This bachelor's thesis presents multiple systems that utilize pen trajectory to classify handwritten symbols. Five preprocessing steps, one data augmentation algorithm, five features, and five variants for multilayer Perceptron training were evaluated using 166,898 recordings collected through two crowdsourcing projects. The evaluation results of these 21 experiments were used to create an optimized recognizer with a TOP1 error of less than 17.5% and a TOP3 error of 4.0%. This represents an improvement of 18.5% for the TOP1 error and 29.7% for the TOP3 error.

title: Sparseness helps: Sparsity Augmented Collaborative Representation for Classification
Abstract: Many classification approaches first represent a test sample using the training samples of all classes. This collaborative representation is then used to label the test sample. It was commonly believed that sparseness of the representation was key to the success of this classification scheme. However, more recent research suggests that collaboration, rather than sparseness, is the primary factor driving its effectiveness. This claim is attractive as it allows for the removal of the computationally expensive sparsity constraint on the representation. This paper first extends the analysis supporting this claim and then demonstrates that sparseness explicitly contributes to improved classification, indicating that it should not be completely ignored for computational gains. Inspired by this result, we augment a dense collaborative representation with a sparse representation and propose an efficient classification method leveraging the resulting representation. The augmented representation and classification method work together to achieve higher accuracy and lower computational time compared to state-of-the-art collaborative representation-based classification approaches. Experiments on benchmark face, object, and action databases demonstrate the efficacy of our approach.

title: MidRank: Learning to rank based on subsequences
Abstract: We present a supervised learning to rank algorithm that effectively orders images by exploiting the structure in image sequences. In supervised learning to rank literature, ranking is typically approached by analyzing pairs of images or by optimizing a list-wise surrogate loss function on full sequences. We propose MidRank, which learns from moderately sized sub-sequences. These sub-sequences contain useful structural ranking information leading to improved learnability during training and better generalization during testing. By leveraging sub-sequences, MidRank significantly improves ranking accuracy across an extensive array of image ranking applications and datasets.
label: AI

title: Sliding-Window Optimization on an Ambiguity-Clearness Graph for Multi-object Tracking
Abstract: Multi-object tracking remains challenging due to the frequent occurrence of occlusions and outliers. To address this problem, we propose an Approximation-Shrink Scheme for sequential optimization. This scheme introduces an Ambiguity-Clearness Graph to avoid conflicts and maintain sequence independence, as well as a sliding window optimization framework to constrain the size of the state space and guarantee convergence. Based on this window-wise framework, the states of targets are clustered in a self-organizing manner. We demonstrate that traditional online and batch tracking methods can be embraced by the window-wise framework. Experiments indicate that with only a small window, the optimization performance significantly surpasses online methods and approaches batch methods.

title: Applying deep learning to classify pornographic images and videos
Abstract: The proliferation of pornographic material, readily accessible online, poses a significant threat to children and minors. General social media networks are striving to isolate adult images and videos from standard content. Intelligent image analysis methods can assist in automatically detecting and isolating questionable images in media. Unfortunately, these methods require extensive expertise to design classifiers, often relying on popular computer vision feature descriptors. We propose building a classifier based on deep learning techniques. Convolutional neural networks consist of numerous layers for automatic feature extraction and classification. This approach simplifies system development, eliminating the need for hand-crafted features and classifiers. Our experiments demonstrate that this method is even more accurate than state-of-the-art methods on the latest benchmark dataset.
label: AI

title: Real-Time Depth Refinement for Specular Objects
Abstract: The introduction of consumer RGB-D scanners has significantly boosted research in 3D computer vision. However, the precision of existing depth scanners is insufficient for recovering fine details of scanned objects. While modern shading-based depth refinement methods have proven effective with Lambertian objects, they fail in the presence of specularities. We present a novel shape from shading framework addressing this issue and enhancing depth profiles for both diffuse and specular objects. We leverage the built-in monochromatic IR projector and IR images of RGB-D scanners, presenting a lighting model that accounts for specular regions in the input image. This model enables real-time depth map reconstruction. Both quantitative tests and visual evaluations demonstrate that our method produces state-of-the-art depth reconstruction results.
label: AI

title: Loss Functions for Neural Networks for Image Processing
Abstract: Neural networks are becoming central in various areas of computer vision and image processing, with different architectures proposed to solve specific problems. The impact of the loss layer in neural networks, however, has received limited attention in image processing. The default and virtually only choice is L2. This paper highlights alternative choices for image restoration. We demonstrate the importance of perceptually-motivated losses when the resulting image is evaluated by a human observer. We compare the performance of several losses and propose a novel, differentiable error function. We show that the quality of the results improves significantly with better loss functions, even when the network architecture remains unchanged.
label: AI

title: Structured learning of metric ensembles with application to person re-identification
Abstract: Matching individuals across non-overlapping camera networks, known as person re-identification, is a fundamentally challenging problem due to significant visual appearance changes caused by variations in viewpoints, lighting, and occlusion. Approaches in the literature can be categorized into two streams: The first stream focuses on developing reliable features against realistic conditions by combining several visual features in a pre-defined way. The second stream aims to learn a metric from training data to ensure strong inter-class differences and intra-class similarities. However, finding an optimal combination of visual features that is generic yet adaptive to different benchmarks remains an unsolved problem. Additionally, metric learning models are prone to overfitting due to the scarcity of training data in person re-identification. This paper proposes two effective structured learning-based approaches that explore the adaptive effects of visual features in recognizing persons across different benchmark datasets. Our framework is built on multiple low-level visual features with an optimal ensemble of their metrics. We formulate two optimization algorithms, CMCtriplet and CMCstruct, which directly optimize evaluation measures commonly used in person re-identification, known as the Cumulative Matching Characteristic (CMC) curve.

title: TennisVid2Text: Fine-grained Descriptions for Domain Specific Videos
Abstract: Automatically describing videos has always been fascinating. This work attempts to describe videos from a specific domain: broadcast videos of lawn tennis matches. Given a video shot from a tennis match, we aim to generate a textual commentary similar to what a human expert would write on a sports website. Unlike recent works focusing on generating short captions, we are interested in generating semantically richer descriptions. This requires detailed low-level analysis of the video content, particularly actions and interactions among subjects. We address this by limiting our domain to lawn tennis. Rich descriptions are generated by leveraging a large corpus of human-created descriptions harvested from the internet. We evaluate our method on a newly created tennis video dataset. Extensive analysis demonstrates that our approach addresses both semantic correctness and readability aspects involved in the task.
label: AI

title: Iterative Instance Segmentation
Abstract: Existing methods for pixel-wise labeling tasks typically disregard the underlying structure of labelings, often resulting in visually implausible predictions. While incorporating structure into the model should improve prediction quality, doing so is challenging. Manually specifying structural constraints can be impractical, and inference often becomes intractable even when structural constraints are provided. We sidestep this problem by reducing structured prediction to a sequence of unconstrained prediction problems. We demonstrate that this approach can automatically discover priors on shape, contiguity of region predictions, and smoothness of region contours from data without any a priori specification. On the instance segmentation task, this method outperforms the state-of-the-art, achieving a mean $\\mathrm{AP}^{r}$ of 63.6% at 50% overlap and 43.3% at 70% overlap.
label: AI

title: Distributed Machine Learning via Sufficient Factor Broadcasting
Abstract: Matrix-parametrized models, including multiclass logistic regression and sparse coding, are widely used in machine learning (ML) applications ranging from computer vision to computational biology. When these models are applied to large-scale ML problems with millions of samples and tens of thousands of classes, their parameter matrix can grow at an unexpected rate, resulting in high parameter synchronization costs that significantly slow down distributed learning. To address this issue, we propose a Sufficient Factor Broadcasting (SFB) computation model for efficient distributed learning of a large family of matrix-parameterized models. These models share the following property: the parameter update computed on each data sample is a rank-1 matrix, i.e., the outer product of two "sufficient factors" (SFs). By broadcasting the SFs among worker machines and reconstructing the update matrices locally at each worker, SFB improves communication efficiency - communication costs are linear in the parameter matrix's dimensions, rather than quadratic - without affecting computational correctness. We present a theoretical convergence analysis of SFB and empirically corroborate its efficiency on four different matrix-parametrized ML models.

title: An analysis of the factors affecting keypoint stability in scale-space
Abstract: The most popular image matching algorithm, SIFT, introduced by D. Lowe a decade ago, has proven sufficiently scale invariant to be used in numerous applications. However, in practice, scale invariance can be weakened by various sources of error inherent to the SIFT implementation, affecting the stability and accuracy of keypoint detection. The density of the sampling of the Gaussian scale-space and the level of blur in the input image are two such sources. This article presents a numerical analysis of their impact on the extracted keypoints' stability. This analysis has both methodological and practical implications for comparing feature detectors and improving SIFT. We demonstrate that even with a significantly oversampled scale-space, numerical errors prevent achieving perfect stability. Usual strategies for filtering out unstable detections are shown to be inefficient. We also prove that the effect of the error in the assumption on the initial blur is asymmetric, and the method is significantly degraded in the presence of aliasing or without a correct assumption on the camera blur. |||

title: An Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool in machine learning, particularly for image recognition tasks. CNNs, inspired by biological neural networks, offer a simplified approach to artificial intelligence due to their precise yet straightforward architecture. This document provides a brief overview of CNNs, highlighting recent research and advancements in developing these sophisticated image recognition models. It assumes familiarity with fundamental concepts of ANNs and machine learning.

title: Towards Automatic Image Editing: Learning to See another You
Abstract: Generating realistic images that resemble existing ones but with modified attributes presents a significant challenge in machine learning. This work focuses on generating similar images while altering specific attributes, such as facial features, while preserving other aspects and overall object appearance. The proposed approach utilizes a convolutional network that encodes the desired attribute information and merges it with the encoded image at the feature map level. Results on two face datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in disentangling attribute effects and achieving both qualitative and quantitative improvements in image generation.
label: AI

title: A Computational Model for Amodal Completion
Abstract: This paper introduces a computational model for inferring 3D scene structure from a 2D image, considering potential object occlusion. The model integrates global and local cues to reconstruct the complete disoccluded objects and their relative depth order. The method first computes multiple possible scene interpretations compatible with the input image. These interpretations are generated using a perceptually inspired object disocclusion method that minimizes Euler's elastica and incorporates contour relatability and object convexity. A Bayesian model then selects the most likely scene by considering global object complexity and the effort required to arrange objects in their relative positions within the 2D image. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through numerical experiments on synthetic and real images, showcasing its ability to reconstruct occluded objects and determine their perceptual ordering.
label: AI

title: The Scale-free Network of Passwords : Visualization and Estimation of Empirical Passwords
Abstract: This paper explores the characteristics of large-scale password datasets and their implications for security. By analyzing datasets from various sources like Yahoo, Phpbb, and 12306, the authors reveal the spatial structure of passwords, including community and clustering patterns. This analysis sheds light on password popularity based on frequency and degree of usage. Additionally, a model for statistical guessing attacks is proposed, providing insight into the "cracking curve" based on the data's topological space. The paper also establishes a lower bound for the minimum size of a dictionary required to compromise a given password set, demonstrating its equivalence to the NP-complete minimum dominating set problem.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised decoding of long-term, naturalistic human neural recordings with automated video and audio annotations
Abstract: This research proposes an unsupervised approach to decode neural states from human brain recordings obtained in a naturalistic setting. The study utilizes continuous long-term electrocorticographic (ECoG) data, combined with audio and video recordings, to identify distinct brain activity patterns associated with specific behaviors. By clustering high-dimensional ECoG recordings and annotating these clusters using automatically extracted speech and movement labels, the authors demonstrate the ability to discover behaviors like speaking, moving, and resting. This unsupervised approach represents a novel application of computer vision and speech processing techniques for natural ECoG decoding, providing a foundation for automated functional brain mapping in realistic environments.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Instance Segmentation
Abstract: Instance segmentation, the task of detecting and delineating individual objects in an image, is addressed by a novel end-to-end approach that learns to segment instances sequentially. The proposed model, based on a recurrent neural network, sequentially identifies and segments objects one at a time. A spatial memory component within the network keeps track of previously explained pixels, enabling occlusion handling. A principled loss function specifically designed for instance segmentation ensures accurate model training. Experimental results demonstrate that this method surpasses existing approaches on multiple person segmentation and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the Plant Phenotyping dataset for leaf counting.
label: AI

title: Exploring Person Context and Local Scene Context for Object Detection
Abstract: This paper investigates two approaches for incorporating context into object detection. The first focuses on objects commonly associated with people, such as fashion and sports accessories, while the second considers more general object detection and utilizes spatial relationships between objects and between objects and scenes. Both models effectively capture precise spatial relationships and leverage the appearance of contextual regions. Evaluation on the COCO dataset shows significant improvements (up to 5%) over CNN-based state-of-the-art detectors, particularly for challenging cases like small objects.
label: AI

title: Tracking Motion and Proxemics using Thermal-sensor Array
Abstract: Indoor tracking, with applications in various fields like education, health monitoring, and marketing, is traditionally reliant on intrusive image-based systems. This research explores the use of an 8x8 infrared sensor array for privacy-preserving tracking. By analyzing temperature readings from the array, the study aims to detect motion and model group proxemics. Approximately 902 scenes with different group configurations and walking directions were collected. Motion direction is inferred using cross-correlation analysis, while connected component analysis and support vector machine classification are employed to estimate the number of individuals in each scene.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Deep Feature Extraction for Remote Sensing Image Classification
Abstract: This paper investigates the application of convolutional networks for remote sensing data analysis, specifically targeting multi- and hyperspectral imagery. Addressing the challenges of high dimensionality and limited labeled data, the authors propose a greedy layer-wise unsupervised pre-training approach coupled with an efficient algorithm for sparse feature learning. This algorithm enforces both population and lifetime sparsity, resulting in powerful and discriminative feature representations. The effectiveness of these representations is illustrated in various scenarios, including aerial scene classification and land-cover classification from high-resolution multi- and hyperspectral images. The proposed approach outperforms traditional methods like PCA and kPCA, achieving state-of-the-art performance in aerial classification while being computationally efficient. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of both single-layer and deep convolutional networks, with deep architectures exhibiting superior performance by capturing increasing levels of abstraction and complexity within the feature hierarchy.
label: AI

title: Higher Order Conditional Random Fields in Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Semantic segmentation using deep learning is addressed by incorporating higher-order potentials into a Conditional Random Field (CRF) embedded within a convolutional neural network (CNN). Previous deep learning approaches have incorporated CRFs into CNNs, but have not utilized higher-order potentials, which can significantly enhance segmentation performance. This paper introduces two types of higher-order potentials based on object detections and superpixels, enabling inference with the differentiable mean field algorithm. As a result, all parameters of the richer CRF model can be learned end-to-end with the pixelwise CNN classifier. This approach achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance on the PASCAL VOC benchmark, demonstrating the effectiveness of trainable higher-order potentials in semantic segmentation.
label: AI

title: An open access repository of images on plant health to enable the development of mobile disease diagnostics
Abstract: To address the urgent need for increased food production to feed a growing global population, this paper presents a crowdsourcing initiative for developing mobile disease diagnostics using machine learning. The project releases over 50,000 expertly curated images of healthy and infected crop plant leaves through the PlantVillage platform. This dataset, along with the platform, serves as the foundation for ongoing crowdsourcing efforts aimed at leveraging computer vision approaches to combat yield losses caused by infectious diseases in crop plants.
label: AI

title: Pedestrian Detection Inspired by Appearance Constancy and Shape Symmetry
Abstract: Pedestrian detection, a crucial task in computer vision, requires features that balance discrimination and simplicity for efficient and accurate performance. This paper proposes two new types of non-neighboring features (NNF): side-inner difference features (SIDF) and symmetrical similarity features (SSF). SIDF captures the difference between background and pedestrian, as well as the difference between the pedestrian contour and its inner part, while SSF captures symmetrical similarities in pedestrian shape. These features, combined with traditional neighboring features, enhance pedestrian detection by reducing miss rate. Experimental results on INRIA and Caltech datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of this approach, outperforming existing methods without using CNNs and achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Caltech dataset.
label: AI

title: Learning to detect video events from zero or very few video examples
Abstract: This work focuses on high-level event detection in video, addressing the challenges of learning event detection from solely textual descriptions without positive video examples and leveraging limited positive samples alongside related videos. The authors propose a general learning framework and analyze the impact of different design choices within this framework. For learning from textual descriptions, an extension of the Support Vector Machine is employed to exploit related videos by assigning weights to different subsets of the videos. Experimental evaluations on the TRECVID MED 2014 video dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
label: AI

title: A Short Survey on Data Clustering Algorithms
Abstract: Clustering algorithms play a critical role in modern data analytics, finding applications in various domains like bioinformatics, speech recognition, and financial analysis. These algorithms divide data instances into subsets that maximize intra-subset similarity and inter-subset dissimilarity based on a defined similarity measure. This paper provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art clustering algorithms, covering design concepts, methodologies, different clustering paradigms, and advanced algorithms. The paper also examines existing clustering evaluation metrics and concludes with future insights and directions for the field.
label: AI

title: Calculate distance to object in the area where car, using video analysis
Abstract: This abstract describes a method for calculating the distance to an object in a car's field of view using video cameras installed on the vehicle. However, it lacks specific details about the implementation or algorithms used for distance estimation. Further information is required to understand the technical aspects of this method.
label: AI

title: PASCAL Boundaries: A Class-Agnostic Semantic Boundary Dataset
Abstract: This paper introduces the PASCAL Boundaries dataset, a large collection of over 10,000 images with ground-truth boundaries between 459 semantic classes, encompassing foreground objects and various background types. This dataset, 20 times larger than existing edge detection databases, addresses the ambiguities in current edge detection definitions. The authors also propose a novel deep network-based multi-scale semantic boundary detector (M-DSBD) and demonstrate its performance compared to models trained on edge detection. The dataset and proposed approach open new avenues for research in boundary detection.
label: AI

title: Video Tracking Using Learned Hierarchical Features
Abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical feature learning approach for visual object tracking. The method first learns features robust to diverse motion patterns from auxiliary video sequences using a two-layer convolutional neural network. Embedding temporal slowness constraint in the network architecture enhances the robustness of learned features to complex motion transformations. A domain adaptation module is then used to online adapt the pre-learned features to the specific target object in a given video sequence. This adaptation encompasses both layers of the deep feature learning module, incorporating appearance information of the target object. The resulting hierarchical features exhibit robustness to both complicated motion transformations and appearance changes, improving tracking performance significantly, particularly in challenging scenarios.
label: AI

title: Principal Basis Analysis in Sparse Representation
Abstract: This paper introduces a new signal analysis method called principal basis analysis (PBA), which can be interpreted as principal component analysis in sparse signal decomposition. PBA focuses on the reproducibility of components, a key characteristic of regularity in natural signals. The paper explains how to measure reproducibility and presents PBA, which selects components in a sparse representation of the signal that optimize reproducibility. This principal basis allows for effective extraction of underlying signal patterns from corrupted data. The method is illustrated with image denoising applications, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods in suppressing noise while preserving signal details.
label: AI

title: Context-aware CNNs for person head detection
Abstract: Person detection, a fundamental task in computer vision, remains challenging due to variations in camera viewpoints, human poses, lighting conditions, and occlusions. This paper focuses on detecting human heads in natural scenes, extending the local R-CNN object detector with contextual cues. The authors propose a Global CNN model trained to predict head positions and scales directly from the full image, leveraging person-scene relations. Additionally, a Pairwise CNN model, trained using a structured-output surrogate loss, explicitly models pairwise relationships between objects. These models are integrated into a joint CNN framework for improved head detection. To train and test the model, a large dataset of 369,846 human heads annotated in 224,740 movie frames is introduced. Evaluation demonstrates performance improvements compared to recent baselines on various datasets, along with enhancements in detection speed.
label: AI

title: Shape and Symmetry Induction for 3D Objects
Abstract: This paper explores the use of deep learning for recovering 3D object shape from a single viewpoint, crucial for tasks like grasping and navigation. The research repurposes object classification machinery to discover image cues relevant for inferring 3D shape, focusing on local prediction of surface normals and global detection of 3D reflection symmetry planes. This approach enables extrapolation of occluded surfaces from visible ones. The method demonstrates accurate 3D shape recovery for previously unseen object classes in both synthetic and real images, highlighting its potential for applications requiring 3D understanding of objects. |||
label: AI

title: Weakly Supervised Object Boundaries
Abstract: State-of-the-art learning-based boundary detection methods require extensive training data.  Annotating object boundaries is a costly process, therefore, there is a need to relax the requirement for meticulously annotated images to make both the training more affordable and to increase the amount of training data. This paper proposes a technique for generating weakly supervised annotations, demonstrating that bounding box annotations alone suffice to achieve high-quality object boundaries without using any object-specific boundary annotations. Using these weak supervision techniques, the authors achieve top performance in the object boundary detection task, significantly surpassing the performance of current fully supervised state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: LocNet: Improving Localization Accuracy for Object Detection
Abstract: A novel object localization methodology is proposed to boost the localization accuracy of state-of-the-art object detection systems.  Given a search region, the model aims to return the bounding box of the desired object within that region.  To achieve this, it relies on assigning conditional probabilities to each row and column of the region, where these probabilities provide useful information about the location of the object boundaries. This enables the accurate inference of the object bounding box under a simple probabilistic framework.  For implementing this localization model, a convolutional neural network architecture called LocNet is used.  The paper demonstrates that LocNet achieves significant improvement in mAP for high IoU thresholds on the PASCAL VOC2007 test set, and that it can be easily integrated with recent state-of-the-art object detection systems, boosting their performance.  Finally, the paper shows that this detection approach can achieve high accuracy even when given a set of sliding windows as input, proving its independence from box proposal methods.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Identification of Fixations, Saccades, and Smooth Pursuits
Abstract: Smooth pursuit eye movements provide valuable insights and information about a subject's behavior and health. In some situations, these movements can disrupt the performance of standard fixation/saccade classification algorithms.  Therefore, an automatic and efficient algorithm for identifying smooth pursuit eye movements is crucial for eye-tracking research involving dynamic stimuli. This paper introduces the Bayesian Decision Theory Identification (I-BDT) algorithm, a novel algorithm for ternary classification of eye movements.  I-BDT reliably separates fixations, saccades, and smooth pursuits in an online fashion, even for low-resolution eye trackers. The algorithm is evaluated on four datasets with different mixtures of eye movements, including fixations, saccades, and straight and circular smooth pursuits. Data was collected from six subjects at a sample rate of 30 Hz, totaling 24 evaluation datasets.  The algorithm consistently exhibits high performance across all datasets and movements relative to manual annotation by a domain expert. Compared to I-VDT, a state-of-the-art algorithm, the I-BDT algorithm shows a significant improvement. For algorithm implementation and annotated datasets, please contact the first author.
label: AI

title: Searching for Objects using Structure in Indoor Scenes
Abstract: To identify the location of objects belonging to a specific class, a typical passive computer vision system processes all regions within an image before outputting a limited number of regions.  However, it is possible to utilize scene structure to search for objects without processing the entire image. This paper proposes a search technique that sequentially processes image regions, prioritizing regions more likely to contain the target object. The problem is framed as a Markov decision process, and an imitation learning algorithm is used to learn a search strategy.  Scene structure is essential for search, and the authors focus on indoor scene images, which contain both unary scene context information and object-object context.  Experiments conducted on the NYU-depth v2 dataset demonstrate that unary scene context features alone can achieve high average precision while processing only 20-25% of the regions for classes like bed and sofa. The performance is further enhanced by incorporating object-object context features alongside the scene context features for classes like counter, lamp, pillow, and sofa.
label: AI

title: Mouse Pose Estimation From Depth Images
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenging problem of efficient mouse 3D pose estimation from static images, particularly single depth images. The authors introduce an approach to discriminatively train the split nodes of trees in a random forest to improve their performance in estimating 3D joint positions of mice. Their algorithm can be applied to different types of rodents and various depth cameras and imaging setups. The paper demonstrates that when a top-mounted depth camera is combined with a bottom-mounted color camera, the system can perform full-body pose estimation, including four limbs and paws.  Empirical examinations on synthesized and real-world depth images validate the applicability of this approach for mouse pose estimation, as well as the related task of part-based labeling of mice.
label: AI

title: Picking a Conveyor Clean by an Autonomously Learning Robot
Abstract: This paper presents a research picking prototype related to the company's industrial waste sorting application. The goal of the prototype is to be as autonomous as possible, with self-calibration and improvement of picking capabilities with minimal human intervention. The system learns to pick objects better based on feedback from a sensor in its gripper, and uses machine learning to choose the best proposal from a random sample generated by simple hard-coded geometric models.  The paper experimentally shows the system autonomously improving its picking performance by measuring the pick success rate as a function of time. It also demonstrates the system's ability to clear a conveyor belt, depositing 70 out of 80 objects from a difficult-to-manipulate pile of novel objects into the correct chute.  The paper discusses potential improvements and future directions for this research.
label: AI

title: Fine-Grain Annotation of Cricket Videos
Abstract: Human activity recognition is a fundamental problem in video understanding.  Even for specific categories of videos, such as sports, which contain a limited set of actions, action recognition remains challenging.  Sports videos, however, are often accompanied by detailed commentaries, which can be leveraged for weakly supervised action annotation.  This paper focuses on Cricket videos, addressing the challenge of temporal segmentation and annotation of actions with semantic descriptions. The solution consists of two stages. The first stage segments the video into "scenes" by utilizing scene category information extracted from the text commentary.  The second stage classifies video-shots and the corresponding phrases in the textual description into different categories.  Relevant phrases are then mapped to the video-shots.  The novel aspect of this work is the fine temporal scale at which semantic information is assigned to the video.  This approach enables the retrieval of specific actions lasting just a few seconds from several hours of video. The resulting large number of labeled exemplars, created without manual effort, can be used by machine learning algorithms to learn complex actions.
label: AI

title: DenseCap: Fully Convolutional Localization Networks for Dense Captioning
Abstract: This paper introduces the dense captioning task, requiring a computer vision system to localize and describe salient regions within images using natural language.  Dense captioning generalizes object detection (where descriptions consist of a single word) and Image Captioning (where one predicted region covers the entire image). To jointly address localization and description, the authors propose a Fully Convolutional Localization Network (FCLN) architecture.  FCLN processes an image with a single, efficient forward pass, requiring no external region proposals and enabling end-to-end training with a single optimization round.  The architecture consists of a Convolutional Network, a novel dense localization layer, and a Recurrent Neural Network language model for generating label sequences.  The network is evaluated on the Visual Genome dataset, containing 94,000 images and 4,100,000 region-grounded captions.  The authors observe improvements in both speed and accuracy over baseline approaches, in both generation and retrieval settings.
label: AI

title: Constrained Deep Metric Learning for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Person re-identification aims to identify a probe image within a given set of images captured from different camera views.  This task is challenging due to variations in pose, illumination, occlusion, and camera viewpoint.  Deep learning methods, particularly those utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have recently been applied in person re-identification due to their excellent feature extraction capabilities.  However, deep networks often suffer from overfitting problems in this context.  This paper proposes a novel CNN-based method for learning a discriminative metric with enhanced robustness to overfitting in person re-identification.  First, a novel deep architecture is built, where the Mahalanobis metric is learned with a weight constraint. This weight constraint regularizes the learning process, improving the generalization ability of the learned metric.  Second, the paper emphasizes the importance of intra-class sample pair selection, which has received limited attention.  To address large intra-class variations in pedestrian images, the authors propose a training strategy called moderate positive mining to prevent overfitting to extreme samples in intra-class pairs.  Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly surpasses the performance of state-of-the-art methods on several person re-identification benchmarks.
label: AI

title: The Limitations of Deep Learning in Adversarial Settings
Abstract: Deep learning excels at various machine learning tasks by leveraging large datasets and computationally efficient training algorithms. However, imperfections during the training phase of deep neural networks make them vulnerable to adversarial samples: inputs crafted by adversaries with the intention of causing misclassification.  This paper formalizes the space of adversaries against deep neural networks (DNNs) and introduces a new class of algorithms for crafting adversarial samples based on a precise understanding of the mapping between DNN inputs and outputs.  In an application to computer vision, the authors show that these algorithms can reliably produce samples correctly classified by humans but misclassified by a DNN with a 97% adversarial success rate, modifying only 4.02% of input features per sample on average.  The paper then evaluates the vulnerability of different sample classes to adversarial perturbations by defining a hardness measure.  Finally, it outlines preliminary work on defending against adversarial samples by defining a predictive measure of the distance between a benign input and a target classification.
label: AI

title: Constrained Structured Regression with Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become the dominant model in computer vision. Given sufficient training data, they can predict nearly any visual quantity. In discrete settings, such as classification, CNNs can not only predict a label but also estimate a confidence in the form of a probability distribution over the output space.  However, such a probability estimate is often missing in continuous regression tasks.  This paper presents a regression framework that models the output distribution of neural networks.  This output distribution enables the inference of the most likely labeling based on a set of physical or modeling constraints.  These constraints capture the intricate interplay between different input and output variables, complementing the output of a CNN. However, these constraints may not hold universally.  The framework allows for learning a confidence associated with the validity of each constraint, represented as a distribution of constraint satisfaction.  The authors evaluate their approach on the problem of intrinsic image decomposition, demonstrating that constrained structured regression significantly improves the state-of-the-art.
label: AI

title: Top-Down Learning for Structured Labeling with Convolutional Pseudoprior
Abstract: Current convolutional neural network (CNN) practice largely relies on bottom-up processing.  The role of top-down processes in CNNs for pattern analysis and visual inference is not well understood.  This paper proposes a new method for structured labeling by developing convolutional pseudo-prior (ConvPP) on ground-truth labels.  ConvPP exhibits several interesting properties: (1) compared to traditional machine learning algorithms like CRFs and Structural SVM, ConvPP automatically learns rich convolutional kernels to capture both short- and long-range contexts; (2) compared to cascade classifiers like Auto-Context, ConvPP avoids the iterative steps of learning a series of discriminative classifiers and automatically learns contextual configurations; (3) compared to recent approaches combining CNN models with CRFs and RNNs, ConvPP learns convolution in the labeling space with enhanced modeling capabilities and reduced manual specification; (4) compared to Bayesian models like MRFs, ConvPP leverages the representational power of convolution by automatically learning priors built on convolutional filters.  The task is achieved using pseudo-likelihood approximation to the prior under a novel fixed-point network structure, facilitating end-to-end learning.  The authors demonstrate state-of-the-art results on sequential labeling and image labeling benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Learning Visual Predictive Models of Physics for Playing Billiards
Abstract: The ability to plan and execute goal-specific actions in varied and unexpected settings is a fundamental requirement for intelligent agents. This paper investigates how an agent can be equipped with an internal model of the external world's dynamics and how it can utilize this model to plan novel actions by running multiple internal simulations ("visual imagination").  These models directly process raw visual input and employ a novel object-centric prediction formulation based on visual glimpses centered on objects (fixations) to enforce translational invariance of the learned physical laws.  The agent gathers training data through random interactions with a collection of different environments. The resulting model can then be used to plan goal-directed actions in previously unseen environments.  The authors demonstrate that their agent can accurately plan actions for playing a simulated billiards game, requiring the ability to push a ball into a target position or into collision with another ball.
label: AI

title: Where To Look: Focus Regions for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: This paper presents a method that learns to answer visual questions by selecting image regions relevant to the text-based query.  This method shows significant improvements in answering questions like "what color", requiring evaluation of a specific location, and "what room", requiring the selection of informative image regions.  The model is tested on the VQA dataset, the largest human-annotated visual question answering dataset to the authors' knowledge.
label: AI

title: Pushing the Boundaries of Boundary Detection using Deep Learning
