Abstract: This paper demonstrates that adapting Deep Convolutional Neural Network training to the task of boundary detection can result in significant improvements over the current state-of-the-art.  The contributions include a careful design of the loss function for boundary detection training, a multi-resolution architecture, and training with external data to enhance the detection accuracy.  When evaluated on the standard Berkeley Segmentation Dataset, the authors improve the optimal dataset scale F-measure from 0.780 to 0.808, while human performance is at 0.803.  Further improvement to 0.813 is achieved by combining deep learning with grouping, integrating the Normalized Cuts technique within a deep network.  The paper also examines the potential of this boundary detector in conjunction with semantic segmentation, showing clear improvements over existing systems.  This detector is fully integrated into the popular Caffe framework and can process a 320x420 image in under a second.
label: AI

title: CNNdroid: GPU-Accelerated Execution of Trained Deep Convolutional Neural Networks on Android
Abstract: Many mobile applications running on smartphones and wearable devices could benefit from the accuracy and scalability of deep CNN-based machine learning algorithms. However, performance and energy consumption limitations make executing computationally intensive algorithms on mobile devices prohibitive.  This paper presents CNNdroid, a GPU-accelerated library for executing trained deep CNNs on Android-based mobile devices.  Empirical evaluations show that CNNdroid achieves up to 60X speedup and 130X energy saving on current mobile devices.  The open-source CNNdroid library is available for download at https://github.com/ENCP/CNNdroid.
label: AI

title: Recombinator Networks: Learning Coarse-to-Fine Feature Aggregation
Abstract: Deep neural networks with alternating convolutional, max-pooling, and decimation layers are widely used in state-of-the-art computer vision architectures.  Max-pooling intentionally discards precise spatial information to create more robust features, typically organized as lower-resolution spatial feature maps.  While max-pooling derived features are well-suited for tasks like whole-image classification, they are less effective for tasks requiring precise localization, such as pixel-level prediction and segmentation.  Precise localization can be maintained by shallow convnets without pooling but at the expense of robustness.  This paper introduces Recombinator Networks, a model where coarse features inform finer features early in their formation, enabling finer features to utilize multiple layers of computation in deciding how to use coarse features.  The model is trained once, end-to-end, and outperforms summation-based architectures, reducing the error from the previous state-of-the-art on two facial keypoint datasets (AFW and AFLW) by 30% and surpassing the current state-of-the-art on 300W without using extra data. Performance is further improved by adding a denoising prediction model based on a novel convnet formulation.
label: AI

title: Node Specificity in Convolutional Deep Nets Depends on Receptive Field Position and Size
Abstract: In convolutional deep neural networks, receptive field (RF) size increases with hierarchical depth. When the RF size approaches full coverage of the input image, different RF positions result in RFs with varying specificity, as portions of the RF fall outside the input space.  This deviates from the convolutional concept of positional invariance and opens the possibility for complex forms of context specificity.
label: AI

title: Rendering refraction and reflection of eyeglasses for synthetic eye tracker images
Abstract: While real-world data is essential for evaluating the robustness of eye-tracking algorithms, simulated, synthetic eye images offer advantages in many applications.  They can generate labeled ground-truth data for appearance-based gaze estimation algorithms or enable the development of model-based gaze estimation techniques by demonstrating the influence of different model factors on gaze estimation error. This allows for simplification or extension of these factors.  This paper extends the generation of synthetic eye images by simulating refraction and reflection for eyeglasses. This allows testing of pupil and glint detection algorithms under various illumination and reflection conditions and enables the estimation of the error of gaze estimation routines in conjunction with different eyeglasses.  The paper demonstrates that polynomial function fitting calibration performs equally well with and without eyeglasses and shows how a geometrical eye model behaves when exposed to glasses.
label: AI

title: NetVLAD: CNN architecture for weakly supervised place recognition
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of large-scale visual place recognition, where the goal is to quickly and accurately recognize the location of a given query photograph.  The paper makes three key contributions: First, it develops a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture trainable end-to-end for the place recognition task.  The main component of this architecture, NetVLAD, is a new generalized VLAD layer inspired by the "Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors" image representation commonly used in image retrieval.  The layer is readily integrated into any CNN architecture and amenable to training via backpropagation. Second, the paper presents a training procedure, based on a new weakly supervised ranking loss, for learning the architecture's parameters end-to-end from images depicting the same places over time downloaded from Google Street View Time Machine.  Finally, the paper shows that the proposed architecture significantly outperforms non-learned image representations and off-the-shelf CNN descriptors on two challenging place recognition benchmarks.  It also demonstrates improvement over current state-of-the-art compact image representations on standard image retrieval benchmarks. |||
label: AI

title: Face Alignment Across Large Poses: A 3D Solution
Abstract: Face alignment, a crucial task in computer vision, involves fitting a face model to an image to extract facial features. However, current algorithms primarily focus on faces with small to medium poses (below 45 degrees), failing to align faces in larger poses (up to 90 degrees). This poses significant challenges: 1) landmark-based face models assume visibility of all landmarks, making them unsuitable for profile views, 2) facial appearance varies dramatically across large poses, and 3) landmark labelling in large poses is difficult due to invisible landmarks requiring estimation. This paper proposes a novel alignment framework, 3D Dense Face Alignment (3DDFA), which utilizes a dense 3D face model fitted to images via convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The paper also introduces a method for synthesizing large-scale training samples in profile views, addressing the data labelling challenge. Experiments on the challenging AFLW database demonstrate that 3DDFA significantly surpasses state-of-the-art methods in face alignment.
label: AI

title: Improving the performance of the linear systems solvers using CUDA
Abstract: Parallel computing offers substantial performance advantages for large-scale applications across various fields, including scientific computing, computer vision, databases, data mining, and economics. GPUs, high-performance many-core processors, enable exceptionally high FLOP rates. Since the inception of general purpose computing on GPUs, several programming models have emerged, notably CUDA from NVIDIA and Stream from AMD. CUDA, popular among C/C++ programmers, provides a powerful framework for general purpose computations on GPUs. Numerous applications ported to CUDA exhibit significant speedups compared to optimized CPU implementations. This paper presents an implementation of a library for solving linear systems using the CCUDA framework. Performance tests demonstrate that GPU utilization achieves speedups of approximately 80 times compared to a CPU implementation.
label: AI

title: DeePM: A Deep Part-Based Model for Object Detection and Semantic Part Localization
Abstract: This paper proposes a deep part-based model (DeePM) for symbiotic object detection and semantic part localization. DeePM utilizes semantic part annotations for 20 object categories on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, providing valuable information on object pose, occlusion, viewpoint, and functionality. DeePM is a latent graphical model built upon the state-of-the-art R-CNN framework, learning an explicit representation of the object-part configuration with flexible type sharing. For comparison, an end-to-end Object-Part (OP) R-CNN is also presented, which implicitly learns feature representation for joint mapping of image regions of interest (ROIs) to object and part bounding boxes. The proposed methods are evaluated for object and part detection performance on PASCAL VOC 2012, with DeePM consistently outperforming OP R-CNN in detecting objects and parts. Furthermore, DeePM demonstrates superior performance compared to Fast and Faster R-CNNs in object detection.
label: AI

title: What Happened to My Dog in That Network: Unraveling Top-down Generators in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Top-down information plays a crucial role in human perception, but its influence in many current deep networks, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), is limited. This work explores a method for incorporating top-down information directly into deep networks by learning and utilizing "generators" that represent the internal effects of three types of transformations (rotation, scaling, and translation) within the network. The learned generators can be used to transfer top-down information to novel settings via "feature flows" corresponding to the transformations. This paper explores three key aspects: 1) using generators to synthesize transformed images from unseen images, 2) "zero-shot learning" where learned generators enable accurate categorization of transformation amounts even for unseen transformations, and 3) (inside-CNN) "data augmentation" using learned generators to provide additional training data within the CNN.
label: AI

title: Multi-Scale Context Aggregation by Dilated Convolutions
Abstract: State-of-the-art semantic segmentation models are often adaptations of convolutional networks originally designed for image classification. However, dense prediction and image classification are fundamentally different tasks. This paper introduces a novel convolutional network module specifically designed for dense prediction. The module utilizes dilated convolutions to aggregate multi-scale contextual information without sacrificing resolution. This architecture leverages the fact that dilated convolutions allow exponential expansion of the receptive field without loss of resolution or coverage. The presented context module demonstrably enhances the accuracy of state-of-the-art semantic segmentation systems. The paper also investigates the adaptation of image classification networks to dense prediction and reveals that simplifying the adapted network can lead to increased accuracy.
label: AI

title: Adapting Deep Visuomotor Representations with Weak Pairwise Constraints
Abstract: Real-world robotics problems often occur in environments significantly different from the robot's training environment. Obtaining real-world experience for robotic control tasks is expensive, but data is readily available in instrumented environments or simulations. This paper proposes a novel domain adaptation approach for robot perception that adapts visual representations learned from large, easily obtainable source datasets (e.g., synthetic images) to real-world target domains, without requiring costly manual data annotation of real-world data before policy search. Supervised domain adaptation methods typically minimize cross-domain differences using aligned image pairs containing the same object or scene in both source and target domains, learning a domain-invariant representation. However, these methods require manual alignment of image pairs. Unsupervised adaptation methods rely on minimizing the discrepancy between feature distributions across domains. This paper proposes a powerful combination of both distribution and pairwise image alignment, eliminating the need for expensive annotation by using weakly aligned image pairs in the source and target domains. Focusing on adapting from simulation to real-world data using a PR2 robot, the paper evaluates the approach on a manipulation task and demonstrates that weakly paired images effectively compensate for domain shift, surpassing previous techniques and leading to improved robot performance in the real world.
label: AI

title: Multi-Volume High Resolution RGB-D Mapping with Dynamic Volume Placement
Abstract: This paper presents a novel RGB-D mapping system for generating 3D maps over extended regions with higher resolution than current methods. The system utilizes multiple, dynamically placed mapping volumes. It takes RGB-D frames as input and dynamically assigns multiple mapping volumes to the environment, seamlessly exchanging mapping volumes between the CPU and GPU. Mapping volumes are added or removed as needed, enabling spatially extended, high-resolution mapping. The system is designed to maximize resolution for volumetric methods while operating in an unbounded space.
label: AI

title: Auxiliary Image Regularization for Deep CNNs with Noisy Labels
Abstract: Precisely labeled datasets with sufficient samples are essential for training deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). However, many real-world datasets contain erroneous labels, significantly hindering the learning of highly accurate CNN models. This paper addresses the challenge of training a deep CNN model for image classification with mislabeled training samples, a prevalent issue in real image datasets with labels provided by amateur users. To tackle this problem, the paper proposes an auxiliary image regularization technique optimized by the stochastic Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. This technique automatically exploits mutual context information among training images, encouraging the model to select reliable images for robust learning. Comprehensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed regularized CNN model is resilient to label noise in training data.
label: AI

title: Visual Word2Vec (vis-w2v): Learning Visually Grounded Word Embeddings Using Abstract Scenes
Abstract: This paper introduces a model for learning visually grounded word embeddings (vis-w2v) to capture visual notions of semantic relatedness. While word embeddings trained using text have achieved great success, they fail to uncover semantic relatedness implicit in the visual world. For example, "eats" and "stares at" may appear unrelated in text but share visual semantics: people eating often stare at the food. Grounding diverse relations like "eats" and "stares at" in vision remains challenging despite recent advancements. Recognizing that visual grounding of words depends on semantics, not literal pixels, this paper utilizes abstract scenes created from clipart for visual grounding. The learned embeddings effectively capture fine-grained, visually grounded notions of semantic relatedness. The paper demonstrates improvements over text-only word embeddings (word2vec) on three tasks: common-sense assertion classification, visual paraphrasing, and text-based image retrieval. The code and datasets are publicly available online.
label: AI

title: Fine-grained pose prediction, normalization, and recognition
Abstract: Pose variation and subtle appearance differences present significant challenges for fine-grained classification. While deep networks have substantially improved general recognition, many fine-grained recognition approaches rely on anchoring networks to parts for enhanced accuracy. Identifying parts to establish correspondences mitigates pose variation, allowing features to be tuned for appearance. Existing methods have explored techniques for part localization and pose-normalized feature extraction. These methods often separate fine-grained recognition into stages, first localizing parts using hand-engineered and coarsely localized proposal features, and then separately learning deep descriptors centered on inferred part positions. This paper unifies these steps in an end-to-end trainable network supervised by keypoint locations and class labels. Part localization is achieved through a fully convolutional network, focusing the learning of feature representations for the fine-grained classification task. Experiments on the CUB200 dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, highlighting the continued importance of strong supervision.
label: AI

title: ReSeg: A Recurrent Neural Network-based Model for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a structured prediction architecture that leverages local generic features extracted by Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and the capacity of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to retrieve distant dependencies. The proposed architecture, called ReSeg, is based on the ReNet model for image classification. ReSeg modifies and extends ReNet to perform the more complex task of semantic segmentation. Each ReNet layer comprises four RNNs that sweep the image horizontally and vertically in both directions, encoding patches or activations and providing relevant global information. ReNet layers are stacked on top of pre-trained convolutional layers, benefiting from generic local features. Upsampling layers follow ReNet layers to recover the original image resolution in final predictions. The ReSeg architecture is efficient, flexible, and suitable for various semantic segmentation tasks. The paper evaluates ReSeg on several widely used semantic segmentation datasets, including Weizmann Horse, Oxford Flower, and CamVid, achieving state-of-the-art performance. The results demonstrate that ReSeg effectively handles semantic segmentation tasks and may have potential applications in other structured prediction problems. The source code and model hyperparameters are available on https://github.com/fvisin/reseg.
label: AI

title: SceneNet: Understanding Real World Indoor Scenes With Synthetic Data
Abstract: Scene understanding is a prerequisite for many high-level tasks in automated intelligent machines operating in real-world environments. Supervised learning has shown promise in this area, but highlights the need for vast amounts of supervised data; performance increases proportionally to the quantity of data used. However, collecting such data is prohibitively expensive due to manual labor requirements. This paper focuses on depth-based semantic per-pixel labeling as a scene understanding problem and explores the potential of computer graphics to generate virtually unlimited labeled data from synthetic 3D scenes. By carefully synthesizing training data with appropriate noise models, the paper demonstrates comparable performance to state-of-the-art RGBD systems on the NYUv2 dataset using only depth data as input. The paper sets a benchmark for depth-based segmentation on the SUN RGB-D dataset and offers a route to generating synthesized frame or video data, providing insights into factors influencing performance gains.
label: AI

title: Learning High-level Prior with Convolutional Neural Networks for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a convolutional neural network that incorporates high-level prior information for semantic image segmentation. Inspired by the human vision recognition system, the key design is a three-layer generative structure consisting of high-level coding, middle-level segmentation, and low-level image to introduce global prior for semantic segmentation. Based on this structure, the paper proposes a generative model called conditional variational auto-encoder (CVAE) that establishes connections between these three layers. These connections include an image encoder extracting high-level information from the image, a segmentation encoder extracting high-level information from segmentation, and a hybrid decoder outputting semantic segmentation from the high-level prior and input image. The paper theoretically derives semantic segmentation as an optimization problem parameterized by these connections. This optimization problem allows for leveraging state-of-the-art fully convolutional network structures for implementing the encoders and decoder. Experimental results on various representative datasets demonstrate superior performance for semantic segmentation.
label: AI

title: End-to-end Learning of Action Detection from Frame Glimpses in Videos
Abstract: This paper presents a fully end-to-end approach for action detection in videos that directly predicts the temporal bounds of actions. The intuition behind this approach is that action detection naturally involves observation and refinement: observing video moments and refining hypotheses about action occurrence. The model is formulated as a recurrent neural network-based agent interacting with a video over time. The agent observes video frames and makes decisions about where to look next and when to emit a prediction. Since backpropagation is insufficient in this non-differentiable setting, REINFORCE is used to learn the agent's decision policy. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on the THUMOS'14 and ActivityNet datasets while observing only a fraction (2% or less) of the video frames.
label: AI

title: Ask Me Anything: Free-form Visual Question Answering Based on Knowledge from External Sources
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for visual question answering that combines an internal representation of image content with information extracted from a general knowledge base to answer a broad range of image-based questions. This enables answering more complex questions than previously possible using neural network-based approaches. The method constructs a textual representation of the image's semantic content and merges it with textual information from a knowledge base to develop a deeper understanding of the scene. Priming a recurrent neural network with this combined information and the submitted question leads to a highly flexible visual question answering approach. This method can effectively answer questions phrased in natural language that refer to information not contained in the image itself. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the model on two publicly available datasets, Toronto COCO-QA and MS COCO-VQA, achieving the best reported results in both cases.
label: AI

title: Gradual DropIn of Layers to Train Very Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of dynamically growing a neural network during training. An initially untrainable deep network starts as a trainable shallow network, with newly added layers gradually incorporated during training, organically increasing the network's depth. This is achieved through a new layer called DropIn. The DropIn layer initially passes the output from a previous layer, effectively skipping over the newly added layers, and then progressively includes units from the new layers for both feedforward and backpropagation. The paper shows that deep networks, which are untrainable with conventional methods, can converge with DropIn layers interspersed in the architecture. Furthermore, DropIn provides regularization during training in a manner analogous to dropout. Experiments are conducted with the MNIST dataset and various expanded LeNet architectures, CIFAR-10 dataset with its architecture expanded from 3 to 11 layers, and ImageNet dataset with the AlexNet architecture expanded to 13 layers and the VGG 16-layer architecture.
label: AI

title: Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Localization in Crowded Scenes
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for real-time anomaly detection and localization in crowded scenes. Each video is defined as a set of non-overlapping cubic patches and described using two local and global descriptors. These descriptors capture video properties from different perspectives. By incorporating simple and cost-effective Gaussian classifiers, the method distinguishes normal activities from anomalies in videos. Local and global features are based on structural similarity between adjacent patches and features learned in an unsupervised manner using a sparse auto-encoder. Experimental results show that the algorithm is comparable to state-of-the-art procedures on UCSD ped2 and UMN benchmarks, but even more time-efficient. The experiments confirm that the system reliably detects and localizes anomalies as they occur in videos.
label: AI

title: Real-Time Anomalous Behavior Detection and Localization in Crowded Scenes
Abstract: This paper proposes an accurate and real-time anomaly detection and localization method in crowded scenes. The method introduces two descriptors for representing anomalous behavior in video. A video is considered as a set of cubic patches. Based on the low likelihood of anomaly occurrence and the redundancy of structures in normal patches in videos, two views (global and local) are considered for video modeling. The algorithm consists of two components: 1) representing patches using local and global descriptors and 2) modeling training patches using a new representation. Two Gaussian models are used for all training patches based on global and local descriptors. Local and global features are derived from structural similarity between adjacent patches and features learned in an unsupervised manner. A fusion strategy combines the two descriptors as the system output. Experimental results show that the algorithm performs comparably to state-of-the-art methods on various standard datasets but is even more time-efficient.
label: AI

title: Semantic Segmentation of Colon Glands with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks and Total Variation Segmentation
Abstract: Segmentation of histopathology sections is a crucial requirement in digital pathology. Due to the high variability of biological tissue, machine learning techniques have demonstrated superior performance compared to standard image processing methods. As part of the GlaS@MICCAI2015 colon gland segmentation challenge, this paper presents a learning-based algorithm to segment glands in tissue from benign and malignant colorectal cancer. Images are preprocessed according to the Hematoxylin-Eosin staining protocol, and two deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are trained as pixel classifiers. The CNN predictions are then regularized using figure-ground segmentation based on weighted total variation to produce the final segmentation result. On two test sets, the approach achieves a tissue classification accuracy of 98% and 94%, leveraging the system's inherent ability to distinguish between benign and malignant tissue.
label: AI

title: Screen Content Image Segmentation Using Sparse-Smooth Decomposition
Abstract: Sparse decomposition has found widespread applications in various fields, including signal compression, denoising, and document analysis. This paper utilizes sparse decomposition for image segmentation. The proposed algorithm separates the background and foreground using a sparse-smooth decomposition technique, where the smooth and sparse components correspond to the background and foreground, respectively. The algorithm is tested on several test images from HEVC test sequences and shows superior performance compared to other methods, such as hierarchical k-means clustering in DjVu. This segmentation algorithm can also be employed for text extraction, video compression, and medical image segmentation. |||
label: AI

title: Zoom Better to See Clearer: Human and Object Parsing with Hierarchical Auto-Zoom Net
Abstract: Parsing articulated objects, such as humans and animals, into their semantic parts (e.g., body, head, arms) from natural images is a challenging problem in computer vision. One major difficulty lies in the wide variation of object and part scales and locations within images. Even minor errors in scale and location estimation can significantly degrade the parsing output and lead to inaccurate boundary details. To address these challenges, we propose a "Hierarchical Auto-Zoom Net" (HAZN) for object part parsing. HAZN is a two-stage network, each stage consisting of a fully convolutional network (FCN) that performs two tasks: (1) predicting the locations and scales of object instances (first stage) or their parts (second stage); (2) estimating the part scores for predicted object instances or part regions. Our model can adaptively "zoom" (resize) predicted image regions to their correct scales, refining the parsing process. We conducted extensive experiments on the PASCAL part datasets for humans, horses, and cows. Our approach significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art for humans, achieving a 5% improvement in mean Intersection over Union (mIOU). It is particularly effective in segmenting small instances and parts. Similar improvements were observed for parsing cows and horses. Our strategy of first zooming into objects and then parts proves highly effective. It allows us to process different image regions at different scales adaptively, eliminating the need to waste computational resources scaling the entire image.
label: AI

title: Convex Sparse Spectral Clustering: Single-view to Multi-view
Abstract: Spectral Clustering (SC) is a widely used method for data clustering. It first finds a low-dimensional embedding of the data by calculating the eigenvectors of the normalized Laplacian matrix. It then performs k-means clustering on this embedding to obtain the final clustering results. In this work, we observe that, ideally, the product of the embedding matrix with its transpose should be block diagonal and therefore sparse. Based on this observation, we propose the Sparse Spectral Clustering (SSC) method, which extends SC by incorporating sparse regularization on this product. To address the computational challenges of the nonconvex SSC model, we propose a novel convex relaxation of SSC based on the convex hull of fixed-rank projection matrices. The convex SSC model can then be efficiently solved using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). Furthermore, we propose Pairwise Sparse Spectral Clustering (PSSC), which extends SSC to improve clustering performance by leveraging multi-view information from the data. Experimental comparisons with several baselines on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.
label: AI

title: Data-dependent Initializations of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have revolutionized computer vision, impacting nearly every visual task imaginable. Despite this, few researchers train their models from scratch. Most research builds upon a small set of ImageNet pre-trained models, fine-tuning or adapting these for specific tasks. This is largely due to the difficulty of properly initializing CNNs from scratch. Even small miscalibrations in initial weights can lead to vanishing or exploding gradients and poor convergence properties. In this work, we present a fast and simple data-dependent initialization procedure that sets network weights so that all units train at roughly the same rate, preventing vanishing or exploding gradients. Our initialization matches the performance of current state-of-the-art unsupervised or self-supervised pre-training methods on standard computer vision tasks, such as image classification and object detection. Notably, it is roughly three orders of magnitude faster. When combined with pre-training methods, our initialization significantly outperforms previous work, narrowing the gap between supervised and unsupervised pre-training.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised learning of object semantic parts from internal states of CNNs by population encoding
Abstract: We address the fundamental question of how object part representations can be extracted from the internal states of CNNs trained for high-level tasks like object classification. This work proposes a novel unsupervised method for learning semantic parts, offering new insights into the internal representations of CNNs. Our technique is based on the hypothesis that semantic parts are represented by populations of neurons rather than individual filters. We introduce a clustering technique to extract part representations, which we call Visual Concepts. We demonstrate that visual concepts are semantically coherent, representing semantic parts, and visually coherent, with corresponding image patches exhibiting strong visual similarity. Moreover, visual concepts provide comprehensive spatial coverage of object parts, unlike keypoint annotations, which typically capture only a few sparse parts. We treat each visual concept as a part detector and evaluate its performance on keypoint detection using the PASCAL3D+ dataset and on part detection using our newly annotated ImageNetPart dataset. The experiments demonstrate that visual concepts can effectively detect parts. Interestingly, we observe that some visual concepts respond to multiple semantic parts if these parts share visual similarity. Thus, visual concepts possess the essential properties of semantic meaning and detection capability. Our ImageNetPart dataset, with its rich part annotations covering the entire object, proves valuable for other part-related applications.
label: AI

title: TransCut: Transparent Object Segmentation from a Light-Field Image
Abstract: Segmenting transparent objects is highly beneficial for computer vision applications. However, their tendency to borrow texture from their background and exhibit similar appearances to their surroundings makes them difficult to handle with conventional image segmentation methods. We propose a method that overcomes these challenges by leveraging the consistency and distortion properties of light-field images. Graph-cut optimization is employed for pixel labeling. We utilize light-field linearity to estimate the likelihood of a pixel belonging to the transparent object or Lambertian background, and an occlusion detector is used to identify the occlusion boundary. We acquired a light-field dataset for transparent objects and employed it to evaluate our method. The results demonstrate the method's success in segmenting transparent objects from the background.
label: AI

title: Mapping Images to Sentiment Adjective Noun Pairs with Factorized Neural Nets
Abstract: We investigate the visual sentiment task of mapping an image to an adjective-noun pair (ANP), such as "cute baby." To capture the two-factor structure of ANP semantics and mitigate annotation noise and ambiguity, we propose a novel factorized CNN model. This model learns separate representations for adjectives and nouns but optimizes classification performance over their product. Our experiments on the publicly available SentiBank dataset demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms independent ANP classifiers on unseen ANPs and on retrieving images of novel ANPs. Furthermore, it outperforms image captioning models, which capture word semantics from co-occurrence in natural text. These latter models surprisingly struggle to capture the sentiment evoked by purely visual experiences. Our factorized ANP CNN not only trains better from noisy labels and generalizes better to new images but also expands the ANP vocabulary independently.
label: AI

title: Fidelity-Naturalness Evaluation of Single Image Super Resolution
Abstract: We delve into the problem of evaluating super-resolution methods. Traditional evaluation methods typically assess the quality of super-resolved images based on a single measure of their difference with the original high-resolution images. This paper proposes using both fidelity (difference with original images) and naturalness (human visual perception of super-resolved images) for evaluation. For fidelity evaluation, a new metric is introduced to address the bias problem present in traditional methods. For naturalness evaluation, we engage human participants to label their preference for super-resolution results using pairwise comparisons and examine the correlation between these human labels and the outputs of image quality assessment metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that our fidelity-naturalness approach surpasses the traditional evaluation method for super-resolution methods. This improvement can guide future research in single-image super-resolution.
label: AI

title: Ground-truth dataset and baseline evaluations for image base-detail separation algorithms
Abstract: Base-detail separation is a fundamental computer vision problem involving modeling a smooth base layer with coarse structures and a detail layer containing texture-like structures. One challenge in base estimation is preserving sharp boundaries between objects or parts to avoid halo artifacts. While many methods have been proposed to tackle this problem, there is no ground-truth dataset of real images for quantitative evaluation. We propose a procedure to construct such a dataset and provide two datasets: Pascal Base-Detail and Fashionista Base-Detail, containing 1000 and 250 images, respectively. Our assumption is that the base is piecewise smooth, and we label the appearance of each piece with a polynomial model. The pieces correspond to objects and object parts obtained from human annotations. Finally, we propose a method for evaluating methods using our base-detail ground-truth and compare the performances of seven state-of-the-art algorithms.
label: AI

title: An Immersive Telepresence System using RGB-D Sensors and Head Mounted Display
Abstract: We present a tele-immersive system that enables people to interact with each other in a virtual world using body gestures in addition to verbal communication. Beyond its obvious applications, including general online conversations and gaming, we hypothesize that our proposed system would be particularly beneficial for education by offering rich visual content and interactivity. One distinct feature is the integration of egocentric pose recognition, allowing participants to use their gestures to demonstrate and manipulate virtual objects simultaneously. This functionality empowers instructors to effectively and efficiently explain and illustrate complex concepts or sophisticated problems in an intuitive manner. The highly interactive and flexible environment can capture and sustain more student attention compared to traditional classroom settings, delivering a more engaging experience. Our primary focus is to investigate possible solutions for system design and implementation and devise strategies for fast, efficient computation suitable for visual data processing and network transmission. We detail the technique and experiments and provide quantitative performance results, demonstrating that our system can be run comfortably and reliably for various application scenarios. Our preliminary results are promising and demonstrate the potential for more compelling directions in cyberlearning.
label: AI

title: Learning visual groups from co-occurrences in space and time
Abstract: We propose a self-supervised framework that learns to group visual entities based on their rate of co-occurrence in space and time. To model statistical dependencies between entities, we set up a simple binary classification problem where the goal is to predict if two visual primitives occur in the same spatial or temporal context. We apply this framework to three domains: learning patch affinities from spatial adjacency in images, learning frame affinities from temporal adjacency in videos, and learning photo affinities from geospatial proximity in image collections. We demonstrate that in each case, the learned affinities uncover meaningful semantic groupings. From patch affinities, we generate object proposals that are competitive with state-of-the-art supervised methods. From frame affinities, we generate movie scene segmentations that correlate well with DVD chapter structure. Finally, from geospatial affinities, we learn groups that relate well to semantic place categories.
label: AI

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Noisy Data for Fine-Grained Recognition
Abstract: Current approaches for fine-grained recognition follow a two-step process: (1) recruiting experts to annotate a dataset of images, optionally collecting more structured data like part annotations and bounding boxes; (2) training a model using this data. To advance fine-grained recognition, we introduce an alternative approach that leverages freely available, noisy web data and simple, generic recognition methods. This approach offers advantages in both performance and scalability. We demonstrate its effectiveness on four fine-grained datasets, significantly surpassing the existing state-of-the-art without requiring any manual label collection. Furthermore, we present initial results for scaling to more than 10,000 fine-grained categories. Quantitatively, we achieve top-1 accuracies of 92.3% on CUB-200-2011, 85.4% on Birdsnap, 93.4% on FGVC-Aircraft, and 80.8% on Stanford Dogs without using their annotated training sets. We compare our approach to an active learning approach for expanding fine-grained datasets.
label: AI

title: Recognizing Activities of Daily Living with a Wrist-mounted Camera
Abstract: We present a novel dataset and a novel algorithm for recognizing activities of daily living (ADL) from a first-person wearable camera. Handled objects are crucial for egocentric ADL recognition. To examine objects related to users' actions separately from other objects in an environment, many previous works have focused on detecting handled objects in images captured from head-mounted and chest-mounted cameras. However, detecting handled objects is not always straightforward, as they tend to appear small in images and can be occluded by the user's body. We propose mounting a camera on the user's wrist. A wrist-mounted camera captures handled objects at a larger scale, eliminating the need for object detection. To compare a wrist-mounted camera with a head-mounted camera, we also develop a novel and publicly available dataset that includes videos and annotations of daily activities captured simultaneously by both cameras. Additionally, we propose a discriminative video representation that retains spatial and temporal information after encoding frame descriptors extracted by Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN).
label: AI

title: Images Don't Lie: Transferring Deep Visual Semantic Features to Large-Scale Multimodal Learning to Rank
Abstract: Search is at the core of modern e-commerce. Consequently, the task of automatically ranking search results (learning to rank) is a multibillion-dollar machine learning problem. Traditional models optimize over a handful of hand-constructed features based on the item's text. This paper introduces a multimodal learning-to-rank model that combines these traditional features with visual semantic features transferred from a deep convolutional neural network. In a large-scale experiment using data from the online marketplace Etsy, we verify that moving to a multimodal representation significantly improves ranking quality. We demonstrate how image features can capture fine-grained style information not available in a text-only representation. Additionally, we show concrete examples of how image information can successfully disentangle pairs of highly different items that are ranked similarly by a text-only model.
label: AI

title: Training CNNs with Low-Rank Filters for Efficient Image Classification
Abstract: We propose a new method for creating computationally efficient convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by employing low-rank representations of convolutional filters. Rather than approximating filters in previously trained networks with more efficient versions, we learn a set of small basis filters from scratch. During training, the network learns to combine these basis filters into more complex filters that are discriminative for image classification. To train such networks, a novel weight initialization scheme is used. This allows effective initialization of connection weights in convolutional layers composed of groups of differently shaped filters. We validate our approach by applying it to several existing CNN architectures and training these networks from scratch using the CIFAR, ILSVRC, and MIT Places datasets. Our results demonstrate similar or higher accuracy than conventional CNNs with significantly less compute. Applying our method to an improved version of VGG-11 network using global max-pooling, we achieve comparable validation accuracy with 41% less compute and only 24% of the original VGG-11 model parameters. Another variant of our method yields a 1 percentage point increase in accuracy over our improved VGG-11 model, achieving a top-5 center-crop validation accuracy of 89.7% while reducing computation by 16% relative to the original VGG-11 model. Applying our method to the GoogLeNet architecture for ILSVRC, we achieve comparable accuracy with 26% less compute and 41% fewer model parameters. Applying our method to a near state-of-the-art network for CIFAR, we achieve comparable accuracy with 46% less compute and 55% fewer parameters.
label: AI

title: Superpixel Convolutional Networks using Bilateral Inceptions
Abstract: This paper proposes a CNN architecture for semantic image segmentation. We introduce a new "bilateral inception" module that can be inserted into existing CNN architectures and performs bilateral filtering, at multiple feature scales, between superpixels in an image. The feature spaces for bilateral filtering and other module parameters are learned end-to-end using standard backpropagation techniques. The bilateral inception module addresses two key issues that arise with general CNN segmentation architectures. First, it propagates information between (super) pixels while respecting image edges, leveraging the structured information of the problem for improved results. Second, the layer recovers a full-resolution segmentation result from the lower-resolution solution of a CNN. In the experiments, we modify several existing CNN architectures by inserting our inception module between the last CNN (1x1 convolution) layers. Empirical results on three different datasets show reliable improvements not only compared to baseline networks but also compared to several dense-pixel prediction techniques like CRFs, while being competitive in terms of speed.
label: AI

title: Hand Pose Estimation through Semi-Supervised and Weakly-Supervised Learning
Abstract: We propose a method for hand pose estimation based on a deep regressor trained on two different types of input. Raw depth data is fused with an intermediate representation in the form of a segmentation of the hand into parts. This intermediate representation contains important topological information and provides useful cues for reasoning about joint locations. The mapping from raw depth to segmentation maps is learned in a semi/weakly supervised way from two different datasets: (i) a synthetic dataset created through a rendering pipeline including densely labeled ground truth (pixelwise segmentations); and (ii) a dataset with real images for which ground truth joint positions are available, but not dense segmentations. Loss for training on real images is generated from a patch-wise restoration process, which aligns tentative segmentation maps with a large dictionary of synthetic poses. The underlying premise is that the domain shift between synthetic and real data is smaller in the intermediate representation, where labels carry geometric and topological meaning, than in the raw input domain. Experiments on the NYU dataset demonstrate that the proposed training method reduces error on joints compared to direct regression of joints from depth data by 15.7%.
label: AI

title: Semantic Diversity versus Visual Diversity in Visual Dictionaries
Abstract: Visual dictionaries are a crucial component for image classification/retrieval systems based on the bag-of-visual-words (BoVW) model. Dictionaries are typically learned without supervision from a training set of images sampled from the collection of interest. However, for large, general-purpose, dynamic image collections (e.g., the Web), obtaining a representative sample in terms of semantic concepts is not straightforward. This paper evaluates the impact of semantics on dictionary quality, aiming to verify the importance of semantic diversity in relation to visual diversity for visual dictionaries. In the experiments, we vary the number of classes used for creating the dictionary and then compute different BoVW descriptors using multiple codebook sizes and different coding and pooling methods (standard BoVW and Fisher Vectors). Results for image classification show that as visual dictionaries are based on low-level visual appearances, visual diversity is more important than semantic diversity. Our conclusions open the opportunity to alleviate the burden of generating visual dictionaries as we only need a visually diverse set of images instead of the entire collection to create a good dictionary.
label: AI

title: Multi-view 3D Models from Single Images with a Convolutional Network
Abstract: We present a convolutional network capable of inferring a 3D representation of a previously unseen object given a single image of that object. Specifically, the network can predict an RGB image and a depth map of the object as seen from an arbitrary viewpoint. Several of these depth maps fused together yield a full point cloud of the object, which can be transformed into a surface mesh. The network is trained on renderings of synthetic 3D models of cars and chairs. It successfully handles objects on cluttered backgrounds and generates reasonable predictions for real images of cars.
label: AI

title: Direct Prediction of 3D Body Poses from Motion Compensated Sequences
Abstract: We propose an efficient approach to exploiting motion information from consecutive frames of a video sequence to recover the 3D pose of people. Previous approaches typically compute candidate poses in individual frames and then link them in a post-processing step to resolve ambiguities. In contrast, we directly regress from a spatio-temporal volume of bounding boxes to a 3D pose in the central frame. We further demonstrate that for this approach to reach its full potential, it is crucial to compensate for motion in consecutive frames so that the subject remains centered. This allows us to effectively overcome ambiguities and improve upon the state-of-the-art by a significant margin on the Human3.6m, HumanEva, and KTH Multiview Football 3D human pose estimation benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Top-k Multiclass SVM
Abstract: Class ambiguity is a common issue in image classification problems with a large number of classes. When classes are difficult to discriminate, it is sensible to allow k guesses and evaluate classifiers based on the top-k error instead of the standard zero-one loss. We propose top-k multiclass SVM as a direct method to optimize for top-k performance. Our generalization of the well-known multiclass SVM is based on a tight convex upper bound of the top-k error. We propose a fast optimization scheme based on an efficient projection onto the top-k simplex, which is of independent interest. Experiments on five datasets show consistent improvements in top-k accuracy compared to various baselines.
label: AI

title: Deep End2End Voxel2Voxel Prediction
Abstract: Deep learning methods have become highly effective for video analysis, excelling in video classification and detection. However, these networks often require extensive architecture searches, manual parameter adjustments, and complex pre- and post-processing, which can be time-consuming. This paper challenges these perceptions by introducing a deep 3D convolutional architecture that performs end-to-end voxel-level prediction, outputting a variable for each voxel in the video. Remarkably, this single architecture achieves competitive results on three diverse voxel-prediction tasks: video semantic segmentation, optical flow estimation, and video coloring. The networks, trained directly from raw video without preprocessing, generate outputs that require no post-processing, offering a more efficient alternative to traditional, computationally intensive methods in these video domains.
label: AI

title: Personalizing Human Video Pose Estimation
Abstract: A personalized ConvNet pose estimator is proposed, automatically adapting to individual appearances to enhance pose estimation in long videos. This method introduces several key contributions: (i) it utilizes a combination of image matching for temporally distant frames and dense optical flow for nearby frames to generate additional high-precision pose annotations from a few initial annotations; (ii) it develops an occlusion-aware self-evaluation model that identifies and rejects erroneous annotations; and (iii) it fine-tunes a ConvNet pose estimator using these high-quality annotations, personalizing it to focus on the target individual's distinctive features. This personalization significantly improves pose estimates compared to the original generic ConvNet. Outperforming state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, including a challenging YouTube video dataset, this approach demonstrates the effectiveness of training from automatically generated annotations for improving generic ConvNets.
label: AI

title: Stories in the Eye: Contextual Visual Interactions for Efficient Video to Language Translation
Abstract: Integrating visual and linguistic interpretations is a fundamental aspect of human intelligence. While image recognition systems are approaching human performance, understanding dynamic videos and translating them into natural language remains a significant challenge. Most vision-to-text approaches rely on pre-learned linguistic models. This paper proposes a method that learns to translate video content into language using solely visual cues, discovering the story played by the main actors through visual representations of objects and their interactions. The method employs a hierarchical approach, learning representations for recognizing subjects, actions, objects, their context, and their temporal interactions. It utilizes a three-stage process, incorporating features at the local, object-relationship, and spatiotemporal levels. This approach finds a coherent linguistic description of videos in the form of subject-verb-object based on the visual story learned from training data, without relying on a pre-existing language model. Demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on a large-scale dataset of YouTube clips, the method surpasses approaches that rely on complex, pre-learned linguistic knowledge.
label: AI

title: Tracklet Association by Online Target-Specific Metric Learning and Coherent Dynamics Estimation
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for tracklet (track fragment) association in long-term multi-person tracking, combining online target-specific metric learning and coherent dynamics estimation through network flow optimization. This framework aims to leverage appearance and motion cues to prevent identity switches during tracking and recover missed detections. The method learns and estimates target-specific metrics (appearance cue) and motion dynamics (motion cue) online, during the tracking process. It effectively handles situations where these cues fail to identify or track the target due to occlusions or object interactions. The weights of these tracking cues are dynamically adjusted to handle challenging scenarios like severe occlusions and object-to-object interactions. Evaluated on several public datasets, the method outperforms state-of-the-art tracking methods.
label: AI

title: Recurrent Semi-supervised Classification and Constrained Adversarial Generation with Motion Capture Data
Abstract: This work investigates recurrent encoder multi-decoder neural network architectures for semi-supervised sequence classification and reconstruction. The use of multiple reconstruction modules aids in generalization for classification tasks when limited labeled data is available, a common scenario in practice. These models provide high-level representations of motions, enabling clustering, searching, and faster labeling of new sequences. The paper also proposes a new realistic partitioning of a well-known motion-capture dataset for improved evaluations. It further explores a novel formulation for future-predicting decoders based on conditional recurrent generative adversarial networks, incorporating both soft and hard constraints derived from desired physical properties and animation goals. These constraints contribute to the stabilization of training recurrent adversarial architectures for animation generation.
label: AI

title: DeepCut: Joint Subset Partition and Labeling for Multi Person Pose Estimation
Abstract: This paper addresses the task of articulated human pose estimation for multiple people in real-world images. It introduces a novel approach that jointly solves detection and pose estimation, inferring the number of persons, identifying occluded body parts, and disambiguating body parts between individuals in close proximity. Unlike previous methods that first detect people and then estimate their pose, this joint formulation proposes a partitioning and labeling scheme for a set of body-part hypotheses generated by CNN-based part detectors. This formulation, an instance of an integer linear program, implicitly performs non-maximum suppression on the set of part candidates and groups them to form configurations of body parts, respecting geometric and appearance constraints. Experiments on four datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art results for both single and multi-person pose estimation. Models and code are available at http://pose.mpi-inf.mpg.de.
label: AI

title: Multi-Contrast MRI Reconstruction with Structure-Guided Total Variation
Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a versatile technique that allows different contrasts depending on acquisition parameters. However, acquiring multiple contrasts, such as T1 and T2 weighted images, can be time-consuming. This paper proposes two modifications of total variation that leverage structural a priori knowledge, reducing to standard total variation when no such knowledge is available. These modifications are based on (i) location and (ii) direction, and are solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers. The corresponding proximal operator is implemented as an extension of the fast gradient projection method on the dual problem for total variation. Testing on datasets of phantoms and real MRI images demonstrates that exploiting structural information from other contrasts yields better results than separate reconstructions with total variation, in terms of peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index. Utilizing directional information further improves image quality, resulting in well-defined edges compared to reconstructions solely using edge location information.
label: AI

title: Towards Arbitrary-View Face Alignment by Recommendation Trees
Abstract: Learning to simultaneously handle face alignment for arbitrary views, including frontal and profile views, poses significant challenges. These challenges stem from the complex appearance-shape relationships exhibited in different views and the varying landmark point sets due to self-occlusion and different landmark protocols. Existing methods often train multiple viewpoint-specific models and rely on head pose estimation for model selection, which can be susceptible to inaccurate pose estimation. This paper addresses this shortcoming by learning an Ensemble of Model Recommendation Trees (EMRT) that selects the optimal model configuration without prior head pose estimation. This unified framework seamlessly handles different viewpoints and landmark protocols, trained directly on landmark locations for superior performance on arbitrary-view face alignment. This is the first study to perform face alignment on the full AFLW dataset, encompassing faces of different views including profile view. State-of-the-art performances are also reported on MultiPIE and AFW datasets, containing both frontal and profile-view faces.
label: AI

title: TEMPO: Feature-Endowed Teichmüller Extremal Mappings of Point Clouds
Abstract: The use of 3D point clouds has become widespread in computer industry, necessitating the development of efficient analysis techniques, particularly in point cloud mapping. This paper introduces a discrete analogue of Teichmüller extremal mappings, which guarantee uniform conformality distortions, on point cloud surfaces. This analogue forms the basis for a novel method called TEMPO for computing Teichmüller extremal mappings between feature-endowed point clouds. The Teichmüller metric is introduced for evaluating point cloud dissimilarity using this method. The algorithm enables accurate recognition and classification of point clouds. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Crowd Behavior Analysis: A Review where Physics meets Biology
Abstract: Mass gatherings, despite their often spontaneous nature, can lead to crowd disasters. The significant increase in crowd-related fatalities in recent decades has spurred advancements in computer vision for proactive crowd surveillance. Studies on crowd behavior in computer vision resonate with principles from physics (complex systems) and biology (animal swarms), revealing surprising commonalities and contradictions. This survey provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art crowd behavior analysis methods from physics and biology-inspired perspectives. It offers insights and discussions for a broader understanding of the potential of combining physics and biology studies in computer vision.
label: AI

title: ElSe: Ellipse Selection for Robust Pupil Detection in Real-World Environments
Abstract: Fast and robust pupil detection is essential for video-based eye-tracking in real-world settings. Existing image-based pupil detection algorithms are often limited to laboratory conditions. Real-world scenarios pose challenges such as illumination changes, reflections, makeup, non-centered eye recording, and physiological variations. This paper proposes ElSe, a novel algorithm based on ellipse evaluation of a filtered edge image, aiming for a robust and resource-saving approach suitable for embedded architectures. The algorithm is evaluated against four state-of-the-art methods on a large dataset of over 93,000 hand-labeled images, including 55,000 new images contributed by this work. On average, the proposed method achieved a 14.53% improvement in detection rate compared to the best performing state-of-the-art method. Download: ftp://emmapupildata@messor.informatik.unituebingen.de (password: eyedata).
label: AI

title: Acceleration of the PDHGM on strongly convex subspaces
Abstract: This paper proposes several accelerated variants of the primal-dual method by Chambolle and Pock. Without requiring full strong convexity of the objective functions, these methods achieve acceleration on subspaces exhibiting strong convexity. This results in mixed rates, $O(1/N^2)$ with respect to initialization and $O(1/N)$ with respect to the dual sequence and the residual part of the primal sequence. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is demonstrated on image processing problems lacking strong convexity, such as total generalized variation denoising and total variation deblurring.
label: AI

title: A dense subgraph based algorithm for compact salient image region detection
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for graph-based saliency computation that leverages dense subgraphs to identify visually salient regions in an image. The model first generates a saliency map using random walks on a Markov chain. Subsequently, k-dense subgraphs are detected to enhance salient regions, as they provide richer information about local graph structure than simple centrality measures. The Markov chain is constructed using image intensity, color features, and region compactness. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method performs comparably to well-known algorithms in salient region detection.
label: AI

title: Compression of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Fast and Low Power Mobile Applications
Abstract: Despite the powerful CPUs and GPUs in high-end smartphones, running deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for complex tasks like ImageNet classification on mobile devices remains challenging. To deploy deep CNNs on mobile devices, this paper presents a simple and effective scheme for compressing the entire CNN, named one-shot whole network compression. This scheme involves three steps: (1) rank selection using variational Bayesian matrix factorization, (2) Tucker decomposition on the kernel tensor, and (3) fine-tuning to recover accuracy loss. Each step can be implemented using publicly available tools. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme by testing compressed CNNs (AlexNet, VGGS, GoogLeNet, and VGG-16) on a smartphone. Significant reductions in model size, runtime, and energy consumption are achieved with minimal accuracy loss. The paper also addresses the implementation issue of 1×1 convolution, a crucial operation in GoogLeNet's inception module and CNNs compressed using the proposed scheme.
label: AI

title: WIDER FACE: A Face Detection Benchmark
Abstract: Face detection is a widely studied topic in computer vision, greatly benefited by the availability of face detection benchmark datasets. However, a gap exists between current performance and real-world requirements. To address this, this paper introduces the WIDER FACE dataset, which is ten times larger than existing datasets. The dataset contains rich annotations, including occlusions, poses, event categories, and face bounding boxes. Faces in this dataset are extremely challenging due to large variations in scale, pose, and occlusion. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the WIDER FACE dataset as a training source for face detection. By benchmarking several detection systems, it provides an overview of state-of-the-art performance and proposes a solution for dealing with large-scale variations. Finally, it discusses common failure cases that require further investigation. The dataset is available for download at: mmlab.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/WIDERFace.
label: AI

title: Integrating Deep Features for Material Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for integrating features extracted using deep representations from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), each trained on a different image dataset of objects and materials, for material recognition. Given a set of representations from multiple pre-trained CNNs, the method first computes feature activations on images to select samples best represented by these features. It then measures feature uncertainty by calculating the entropy of class distributions for each sample set. Finally, it computes the contribution of each feature to class representation for feature selection and integration. Evaluated on three benchmark datasets for material recognition, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance by integrating deep features. The paper also introduces a new material dataset, EFMD, by extending the Flickr Material Database (FMD). Applying transfer learning to update learned CNN models using EFMD results in an accuracy of 84.0%+/-1.8% on the FMD dataset, nearing human performance at 84.9%.
label: AI

title: Bidirectional Warping of Active Appearance Model
Abstract: Active Appearance Model (AAM) is a widely used method for facial image analysis with applications in face identification and facial expression recognition. This paper proposes a new approach for AAM fitting based on image alignment called bidirectional warping. Previous methods warp either the input image or the appearance template. This approach proposes warping both the input image, using incremental affine transformation updates, and the appearance template, using an inverse compositional approach. Experimental results on the Multi-PIE face database demonstrate that the bidirectional approach outperforms state-of-the-art inverse compositional fitting approaches in extracting landmark points of faces with shape and pose variations.
label: AI

title: A Simple Hierarchical Pooling Data Structure for Loop Closure
Abstract: This paper proposes a data structure for large-scale loop closure applications, obtained by hierarchically averaging bag-of-word descriptors across a sequence of views. This method achieves average speedups ranging from 4 to 20 times on benchmark datasets. Despite its simplicity, it performs as well as sophisticated agglomerative schemes at a fraction of the cost with minimal performance loss.
label: AI

title: DOC: Deep OCclusion Estimation From a Single Image
Abstract: Recovering occlusion relationships between objects is a fundamental human visual ability that provides crucial information about the 3D world. This paper introduces a deep network architecture called DOC that operates on a single image, detecting object boundaries and estimating border ownership (which side of the boundary is foreground and which is background). Occlusion relations are represented by a binary edge map and an occlusion orientation variable, which is tangential to the boundary and indicates border ownership using a left-hand rule. The paper trains two related deep convolutional neural networks, called DOC, that exploit local and non-local image cues to estimate this representation and recover occlusion relations. A large-scale instance occlusion boundary dataset, called the PASCAL instance occlusion dataset (PIOD), is constructed using PASCAL VOC images. Containing 10,000 images, PIOD is two orders of magnitude larger than existing occlusion datasets for outdoor images. Testing two variants of DOC on PIOD and the BSDS occlusion dataset shows that they outperform state-of-the-art methods. Further experiments investigate different DOC settings and transfer learning between BSDS and PIOD, providing insights for future occlusion estimation research.
label: AI

title: Deep Metric Learning via Lifted Structured Feature Embedding
Abstract: Learning distance metrics between pairs of examples is crucial for learning and visual recognition. Leveraging the success of convolutional neural networks, recent works have shown promising results in discriminatively training networks to learn semantic feature embeddings where similar examples are mapped close together and dissimilar examples are mapped farther apart. This paper describes an algorithm that takes full advantage of training batches in neural network training by lifting the vector of pairwise distances within the batch to the matrix of pairwise distances. This enables the algorithm to learn state-of-the-art feature embeddings by optimizing a novel structured prediction objective on the lifted problem. The paper also introduces the Online Products dataset, consisting of 120,000 images of 23,000 online product classes for metric learning. Experiments on the CUB-200-2011, CARS196, and Online Products datasets demonstrate significant improvements over existing deep feature embedding methods for all embedding sizes using the GoogLeNet network. |||
label: AI

title: Learning to decompose for object detection and instance segmentation
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have revolutionized object detection and segmentation, but they often rely on pre- and post-processing steps, such as region proposals and non-maximum suppression (NMS), which increase computational complexity and sensitivity to hyperparameters. This work introduces a novel end-to-end trainable deep neural network architecture, combining convolutional and recurrent layers, that directly generates the correct number of object instances and their bounding boxes (or segmentation masks) from an image, eliminating the need for pre- or post-processing. The proposed architecture has been tested on detecting digits in multi-digit images synthesized using MNIST, segmenting digits in these images, and detecting cars in the KITTI benchmark dataset. The proposed approach outperforms a strong CNN baseline on the synthesized digits datasets and shows promising results on KITTI car detection.
label: AI

title: Learning Representations from EEG with Deep Recurrent-Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Modeling cognitive events from electroencephalogram (EEG) data presents a significant challenge due to inter- and intra-subject variability, as well as inherent noise. This paper proposes a novel approach for learning invariant representations from multi-channel EEG time-series, demonstrating its advantages in the context of mental load classification. The proposed method transforms EEG activities into a sequence of topology-preserving multi-spectral images, unlike standard EEG analysis techniques that ignore spatial information. A deep recurrent-convolutional network inspired by state-of-the-art video classification is then trained to learn robust representations from the image sequence. This approach effectively preserves the spatial, spectral, and temporal structure of EEG, leading to features that are less sensitive to variations and distortions. Empirical evaluation on the cognitive load classification task shows significant improvements in classification accuracy compared to current state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: Fast Metric Learning For Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Similarity metrics play a crucial role in many information retrieval and machine learning systems. This work proposes a method for learning a similarity metric from data equipped with a binary relation. By focusing solely on similarity constraints and initially disregarding features, the method learns target vectors for each instance using various appropriately designed loss functions. A regression model is then constructed to map novel feature vectors to the same target vector space, resulting in a feature extractor that computes vectors for which a predefined metric is a meaningful measure of similarity. Experiments on both multiclass and multi-label classification datasets demonstrate considerably faster convergence and higher accuracy on the majority of intrinsic evaluation tasks and all extrinsic evaluation tasks.
label: AI

title: A convnet for non-maximum suppression
Abstract: Non-maximum suppression (NMS) is a crucial component in virtually all state-of-the-art object detection pipelines. While other object detection components like features, classifiers, and proposal methods have been extensively researched, NMS has received surprisingly little attention. The current standard for NMS relies on greedy clustering with a fixed distance threshold, leading to a trade-off between recall and precision. This work proposes a convolutional neural network (ConvNet) designed to perform NMS on a given set of detections. Experiments on a synthetic setup and crowded pedestrian detection scenes demonstrate that the approach overcomes the intrinsic limitations of greedy NMS, achieving better recall and precision.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
Abstract: Supervised learning with convolutional networks (CNNs) has seen remarkable success in computer vision applications, while unsupervised learning with CNNs has received less attention. This paper aims to bridge the gap by introducing a class of CNNs called deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (DCGANs), which have specific architectural constraints, as potential candidates for unsupervised learning. Training on various image datasets, the paper presents convincing evidence that the deep convolutional adversarial pair learns a hierarchy of representations, from object parts to scenes, in both the generator and discriminator. The learned features are further utilized for novel tasks, demonstrating their applicability as general image representations.
label: AI

title: Delving Deeper into Convolutional Networks for Learning Video Representations
Abstract: This paper proposes an approach to learn spatio-temporal features in videos from intermediate visual representations called "percepts" using Gated-Recurrent-Unit Recurrent Networks (GRUs). The method utilizes percepts extracted from all levels of a deep convolutional network trained on the large ImageNet dataset. While high-level percepts provide highly discriminative information, they tend to have low spatial resolution. Low-level percepts, on the other hand, preserve a higher spatial resolution, enabling the modeling of finer motion patterns. To address the high dimensionality of video representations using low-level percepts and control the model's parameter count, a variant of the GRU model is introduced that leverages convolution operations to enforce sparse connectivity of the model units and share parameters across input spatial locations. The approach is empirically validated on both Human Action Recognition and Video Captioning tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on the YouTube2Text dataset using a simpler text-decoder model and without additional 3D CNN features.
label: AI

title: A Controller-Recognizer Framework: How necessary is recognition for control?
Abstract: Recent research has focused on developing active visual object recognizers, which actively seek information to classify objects, as opposed to passive recognizers that classify static images. This paper generalizes these end-to-end active visual recognizers into a controller-recognizer framework. A model in this framework comprises a controller, interacting with an external manipulator, and a recognizer that classifies visual input adjusted by the manipulator. Two representative examples, the recurrent attention model and spatial transformer network, are discussed. The paper observes that most existing end-to-end controller-recognizers tightly couple the controller and recognizer. The paper investigates whether this tight coupling is necessary and empirically explores a controller-recognizer model with a decoupled controller and recognizer. Experiments show that tight coupling is not always essential and decoupling allows the development of a generic, pretrained controller that can work with any subsequent recognizer.
label: AI

title: First Step toward Model-Free, Anonymous Object Tracking with Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a novel visual object tracking approach based on convolutional networks and recurrent networks. The proposed approach is distinct from existing filtering-based and tracking-by-detection methods, as it is explicitly trained offline to track anonymous objects in a noisy environment. The visual tracking model is end-to-end trainable, minimizing any adversarial effects arising from mismatches in object representation and between the true underlying dynamics and learning dynamics.
