Experiments on artificial video sequences with varying conditions, including the number of objects, noise levels, and shape variations, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed tracking approach in various scenarios.
label: AI

title: Deep Manifold Traversal: Changing Labels with Convolutional Features
Abstract: Many tasks in computer vision involve "label changing", where the goal is to semantically alter the appearance of an image or a subject to change its class membership. While successful task-specific methods have been developed for some label changing applications, a general-purpose method is lacking. This paper proposes deep manifold traversal, a method that addresses label changing in its most general form. The method first approximates the manifold of natural images and then morphs a test image along a traversal path away from a source class and towards a target class while remaining close to the manifold. The resulting algorithm is remarkably effective and versatile. It is entirely data-driven, requiring only example images from the desired source and target domains. Deep manifold traversal is demonstrated on diverse label changing tasks, including changing an individual's appearance (age and hair color), altering the season of an outdoor image, and transforming a city skyline towards nighttime.
label: AI

title: QBDC: Query by dropout committee for training deep supervised architecture
Abstract: While increasing the depth of neural networks typically improves performance, the size of their training databases must grow accordingly. This paper addresses the challenge of labeling a vast database by introducing an active learning strategy based on query by committee and dropout technique to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The strategy involves creating a committee of partial CNNs generated through batchwise dropout runs on the initial CNN. Evaluation on the MNIST benchmark demonstrates that selecting less than 30% of the annotated database is sufficient to achieve an error rate similar to using the full training set. The method's robustness against adversarial examples is also investigated.
label: AI

title: Learning to Generate Images with Perceptual Similarity Metrics
Abstract: Deep networks are increasingly being used in image synthesis tasks, such as generating images from textual descriptions and reconstructing an input image from a compact representation. Supervised training of image-synthesis networks typically relies on pixel-wise loss (PL) to measure the mismatch between a generated image and its target. This paper proposes using a loss function that is better aligned with human perceptual judgments of image quality: the multiscale structural-similarity score (MS-SSIM). MS-SSIM, being differentiable, can be easily incorporated into gradient-descent learning. The paper compares the effects of using MS-SSIM versus PL loss on training deterministic and stochastic autoencoders. Human judgments of image reconstruction quality reveal a consistent preference for images synthesized by MS-SSIM-optimized models over those generated by PL-optimized models, for both $\\ell_1$ and $\\ell_2$ distance measures. The effect of training objective on image encoding is further explored, demonstrating that perceptually-optimized representations yield better performance on image classification under certain conditions. The superiority of perceptually-optimized networks is also showcased in super-resolution imaging. Just as computer vision has advanced through convolutional architectures mimicking the mammalian visual system, the paper argues that significant progress can be made in image modeling through the use of training objectives that align with human perception characteristics.
label: AI

title: Feature-based Attention in Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven effective for image processing tasks, such as object recognition and classification. Recent advancements have incorporated concepts of attention, similar to those found in biology, with a focus on effective serial spatial processing. This paper introduces a simple procedure for applying feature-based attention (FBA) to CNNs and compares multiple implementation options. FBA is a top-down signal applied globally to an input image, aiding in detecting chosen objects in cluttered or noisy environments. The concept and implementation details of FBA are inspired by biological object- and feature-based attention. The implementations presented here enhance performance on challenging object detection tasks using a simple, fast procedure that does not require additional iterative training. Furthermore, the comparisons suggest that a proposed model of biological FBA, the "feature similarity gain model", is effective in improving performance.
label: AI

title: Geodesics of learned representations
Abstract: This paper introduces a new method for visualizing and refining the invariances of learned representations. It specifically examines a general form of invariance, linearization, where the action of a transformation is confined to a low-dimensional subspace. Given two reference images, typically differing by a transformation, the method synthesizes a sequence of images lying on a path between them, minimizing the length in the space of the representation, creating a "representational geodesic". If the transformation relating the two reference images is linearized by the representation, this sequence should follow the gradual evolution of the transformation. The method is applied to assess the invariance properties of a state-of-the-art image classification network. The generated geodesics for image pairs differing by translation, rotation, and dilation do not evolve according to their associated transformations. The method also suggests a remedy for these failures, and the modified representation demonstrates the ability to linearize a variety of geometric image transformations.
label: AI

title: Manifold Regularized Deep Neural Networks using Adversarial Examples
Abstract: Learning meaningful representations using deep neural networks requires efficient training schemes and well-structured networks. The method of stochastic gradient descent with momentum and dropout is one of the most popular training protocols. While more advanced methods like Maxout and Batch Normalization have been proposed, they still suffer from performance degradation caused by small perturbations, known as adversarial examples. To address this issue, this paper proposes manifold regularized networks (MRnet), which utilize a novel training objective function that minimizes the difference between multi-layer embedding results of samples and their adversarial counterparts. Experimental results demonstrate that MRnet is more resilient to adversarial examples and helps generalize representations on manifolds. Combining MRnet and dropout achieves competitive classification performances on three well-known benchmarks: MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Learning of Visual Structure using Predictive Generative Networks
Abstract: The ability to predict future states of the environment is a fundamental aspect of intelligence. Effective prediction requires an internal model of the world and an understanding of its dynamic rules. This paper explores the internal models developed by deep neural networks trained using a loss based on predicting future frames in synthetic video sequences, employing a CNN-LSTM-deCNN framework. The paper demonstrates that this architecture achieves excellent performance in visual sequence prediction tasks, including state-of-the-art performance in a standard "bouncing balls" dataset. Using a weighted mean-squared error and adversarial loss, the same architecture successfully extrapolates out-of-the-plane rotations of computer-generated faces. Notably, despite being trained end-to-end to predict only pixel-level information, the Predictive Generative Networks learn a representation of the latent structure of the underlying three-dimensional objects. This representation is naturally tolerant to object transformations and generalizes well to new tasks, such as static image classification. Models trained solely with a reconstruction loss fail to generalize as effectively. The paper argues that prediction can serve as a powerful unsupervised loss for learning rich internal representations of high-level object features.
label: AI

title: Efficient inference in occlusion-aware generative models of images
Abstract: This paper presents a generative model of images based on layering, where individual image layers are generated and then composited from front to back. This allows factoring the appearance of an image into the appearance of individual objects within the image and, for each object, factoring content from pose. Unlike previous work on layered models, the paper learns a shape prior for each object/layer, enabling the model to determine which object is in front by identifying consistent shapes, without relying on motion cues or labeled data. The paper shows that ordinary stochastic gradient variational bayes (SGVB), optimizing a fully differentiable lower-bound on the log-likelihood, is sufficient to learn an interpretable representation of images. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the model for inferring foreground and background objects in images.
label: AI

title: Order-Embeddings of Images and Language
Abstract: Hypernymy, textual entailment, and image captioning can be viewed as special cases of a single visual-semantic hierarchy spanning words, sentences, and images. This paper advocates for explicitly modeling the partial order structure of this hierarchy. To achieve this goal, the paper introduces a general method for learning ordered representations and demonstrates its application to various tasks involving images and language. The resulting representations improve performance compared to current approaches for hypernym prediction and image-caption retrieval.
label: AI

title: FRIST - Flipping and Rotation Invariant Sparsifying Transform Learning and Applications
Abstract: Features based on sparse representation, particularly using the synthesis dictionary model, have been widely exploited in signal processing and computer vision. However, synthesis dictionary learning typically involves NP-hard sparse coding and expensive learning steps. Recently, sparsifying transform learning has gained interest for its computational efficiency and optimal updates in alternating algorithms. This work develops a methodology for learning Flipping and Rotation Invariant Sparsifying Transforms, dubbed FRIST, to better represent natural images containing textures with various geometric directions. The proposed alternating FRIST learning algorithm involves efficient optimal updates. The paper provides a convergence guarantee and demonstrates the empirical convergence behavior of the FRIST learning approach. Preliminary experiments show promising performance of FRIST learning for sparse image representation, segmentation, denoising, robust inpainting, and compressed sensing-based magnetic resonance image reconstruction.
label: AI

title: How much data is needed to train a medical image deep learning system to achieve necessary high accuracy?
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have yielded impressive results in natural image classification systems. Coupled with the inherent characteristics of medical images that make them ideal for deep learning, applying such systems to medical image classification holds significant promise. However, the system's effectiveness and potential impact can be negated if it fails to achieve a target accuracy. This paper presents a study to determine the optimal size of the training data set required to achieve high classification accuracy with low variance in medical image classification systems. The CNN is applied to classify axial Computed Tomography (CT) images into six anatomical classes. The CNN is trained using six different training data set sizes (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 200), and the resulting system is tested with a total of 6000 CT images. All images were acquired from the Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). Using this data, the paper employs the learning curve approach to predict classification accuracy at a given training sample size. The research presents a general methodology for determining the necessary training data set size to achieve a specific target classification accuracy, which can be easily applied to other problems within such systems.
label: AI

title: Robust Classification by Pre-conditioned LASSO and Transductive Diffusion Component Analysis
Abstract: Modern machine learning-based recognition approaches rely on large-scale datasets with numerous labeled training images. However, collecting and annotating such datasets is inherently difficult and expensive. Therefore, there is a growing interest in automatic dataset collection methods that leverage the web. This paper addresses the challenge of outlier detection in web-collected datasets, which are often unreliable. The paper formulates outlier detection using Pre-conditioned LASSO and employs unsupervised transductive diffusion component analysis to integrate the topological structure of the data manifold, incorporating labeled and unlabeled instances, and reduce feature dimensionality. Synthetic experiments and results on two real-world classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework robustly detects outliers and improves classification. |||
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Deep Embedding for Clustering Analysis
Abstract: Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) is a novel method for learning feature representations and cluster assignments using deep neural networks. DEC maps data to a lower-dimensional feature space, iteratively optimizing a clustering objective. Experiments on image and text corpora show significant improvements over existing methods.
label: AI

title: face anti-spoofing based on color texture analysis
Abstract: Face spoofing detection has traditionally focused on analyzing luminance, neglecting potentially valuable chrominance information. This paper presents a new method using color texture analysis for face anti-spoofing. The proposed method leverages the joint color-texture information from luminance and chrominance channels using a color local binary pattern descriptor. Experiments on benchmark datasets, CASIA face anti-spoofing and Replay-Attack databases, demonstrate excellent results compared to existing approaches. Notably, inter-database evaluation reveals promising generalization capabilities.
label: AI

title: Why M Heads are Better than One: Training a Diverse Ensemble of Deep Networks
Abstract: This work addresses the problem of ensembling Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by rigorously evaluating various strategies. It explores different ensembling methods, including parameter sharing through TreeNets, a novel model family, and training under ensemble-aware and diversity-encouraging losses. Results show that TreeNets enhance ensemble performance and diverse ensembles can be trained end-to-end with unified loss, achieving significantly higher "oracle" accuracies than traditional ensembles.
label: AI

title: Spatio-temporal video autoencoder with differentiable memory
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel spatio-temporal video autoencoder based on a classic spatial image autoencoder and a nested temporal autoencoder. The temporal encoder employs a differentiable visual memory, composed of convolutional long short-term memory (LSTM) cells, to integrate changes over time. The temporal decoder utilizes a robust optical flow prediction module and an image sampler as a built-in feedback loop. The architecture, differentiable end-to-end, predicts optical flow based on current observation and LSTM memory state, applying it to the current frame for next frame generation. Minimizing the reconstruction error between the predicted and ground truth next frames trains the system to extract motion estimation features without supervision. The framework is demonstrated in weakly-supervised semantic segmentation of videos through label propagation using optical flow.
label: AI

title: Robust Convolutional Neural Networks under Adversarial Noise
Abstract: This research proposes a new feedforward CNN that enhances robustness against adversarial noise. The model incorporates stochastic additive noise to both the input image and CNN models. Convolution, max-pooling, and ReLU layers are modified to leverage the noise model. This feedforward model is parameterized by a mean and variance per pixel, simplifying computations and enabling scalability to deep architectures. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate superior performance compared to other methods, with significant improvements for difficult classification tasks or stronger adversarial noise.
label: AI

title: Foveation-based Mechanisms Alleviate Adversarial Examples
Abstract: This study investigates the mitigation of adversarial examples, visually imperceptible perturbations that cause Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to fail, using a foveation mechanism. The work revises the hypothesis that adversarial perturbations result from CNNs acting as linear classifiers, finding that CNNs act locally linearly to changes in image regions containing recognized objects, while behaving non-linearly in other regions. It shows that applying foveation to adversarial examples significantly reduces the effect of the perturbation, particularly when neural responses are linear. This is attributed to CNNs' robustness to scale and translation changes introduced by foveation, a property that doesn't generalize to transformations of the perturbation. Consequently, foveation leads to accuracy similar to the CNN without perturbation, even with adversarial noise considered during foveation.
label: AI

title: Density Modeling of Images using a Generalized Normalization Transformation
Abstract: This paper introduces a parametric nonlinear transformation suitable for Gaussianizing data from natural images. The transformation involves linear data transformation followed by component normalization using a pooled activity measure. The measure is computed by exponentiating a weighted sum of rectified and exponentiated components and a constant. The parameters are optimized over a database of natural images, directly minimizing the negentropy of responses. The optimized transformation significantly Gaussianizes the data, achieving lower mutual information between transformed components compared to alternative methods like ICA and radial Gaussianization. The transformation's differentiability and efficient inversion allow for a density model on images. Samples from this model exhibit visual similarity to natural image patches. Its application as a prior probability density for noise removal and its cascade capability for optimizing deep network architectures through Gaussianization are demonstrated.
label: AI

title: Faster method for Deep Belief Network based Object classification using DWT
Abstract: Training a Deep Belief Network (DBN) on large images requires multiple hidden layers with numerous hidden units, leading to longer training time and computational complexity. This paper proposes an integrated approach combining DBN with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to reduce training time and complexity. DWT-generated low-resolution images are used to train multiple DBNs, with their results combined using a weighted voting algorithm. This method demonstrates competent performance with faster execution compared to traditional DBNs.
label: AI

title: Asymmetrically Weighted CCA And Hierarchical Kernel Sentence Embedding For Image & Text Retrieval
Abstract: This work presents three contributions in canonical correlation analysis (CCA)-based multimodal retrieval for joint modeling of language and vision. Firstly, it demonstrates that asymmetric weighting of canonical weights, mapping from search to query space, improves retrieval performance. Secondly, a computationally efficient model selection method is devised, crucial for generalization and stability, within the Björck Golub algorithm for regularized CCA via spectral filtering. Finally, a Hierarchical Kernel Sentence Embedding (HKSE) is introduced, approximating Kernel CCA for a specific word distribution similarity kernel in a vector space. State-of-the-art results are achieved on MSCOCO and Flickr benchmarks when these techniques are combined.
label: AI

title: Convolutional Clustering for Unsupervised Learning
Abstract: Training deep neural networks requires a significant amount of labeled data, a daunting task. This research proposes an enhanced k-means clustering algorithm for training deep convolutional networks, reducing the number of correlated parameters in the form of similar filters. This "convolutional k-means clustering" algorithm improves test categorization accuracy. It is further shown that learning connections between layers of a deep convolutional neural network enhances its ability to train on smaller labeled datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's superiority to other unsupervised filter learning techniques, achieving a 74.1% test accuracy on STL-10 and 0.5% test error on MNIST.
label: AI

title: Multimodal sparse representation learning and applications
Abstract: Unsupervised methods have proven effective for discriminative tasks in single-modality settings. This paper introduces a multimodal framework for learning sparse representations that capture semantic correlations between modalities. The framework models relationships at a higher level by enforcing shared sparse representations, using joint dictionary learning for sparse coding. The joint representation allows for concision, cross-modal representations in case of missing modalities, and a union of cross-modal representations. The framework's effectiveness in image denoising, multimedia event detection and retrieval on TRECVID (audio-video), category classification on the Wikipedia dataset (image-text), and sentiment classification on PhotoTweet (image-text) is demonstrated.
label: AI

title: Towards Open Set Deep Networks
Abstract: Deep networks have achieved significant gains in visual recognition, leading to impactful academic and commercial applications. However, these networks are susceptible to "fooling" by images that humans wouldn't classify as belonging to a particular object class. The closed-set nature of deep networks compels them to choose from known classes, leading to such artifacts. Real-world recognition is open-set, requiring rejection of unknown classes at test time. This paper presents a methodology for adapting deep networks to open-set recognition by introducing a new model layer, OpenMax, which estimates the probability of an input being from an unknown class. The method adapts Meta-Recognition concepts to activation patterns in the penultimate layer of the network. OpenMax effectively rejects "fooling" and unrelated open-set images, reducing errors made by deep networks. The OpenMax concept is proven to provide bounded open space risk, formally providing an open-set recognition solution. Evaluation using pre-trained networks from the Caffe Model-zoo on ImageNet 2012 validation data, along with fooling and open-set images, shows significant improvement in open-set recognition accuracy compared to basic deep networks and deep networks with SoftMax probability thresholding.
label: AI

title: Automatically selecting inference algorithms for discrete energy minimisation
Abstract: Minimization of discrete energies defined over factors is a crucial problem in computer vision. Various MAP inference algorithms have been proposed, with different algorithms performing best on factor graph models (GMs) from different underlying problem classes. This paper proposes a technique to automatically select the best inference algorithm for a given GM, addressing the challenge of determining which algorithm will yield the lowest energy for a given model. The method is experimentally validated on an extended OpenGM2 benchmark containing diverse vision problems. Results show that the method selects an inference algorithm that achieves labelings with 96% of variables identical to those obtained by the best available algorithm.
label: AI

title: What Players do with the Ball: A Physically Constrained Interaction Modeling
Abstract: Tracking the ball is essential for video-based team sports analysis, but challenging due to low-resolution images, the ball's small size, speed-induced motion blur, and occlusion by players. This paper proposes a generic and principled approach for modeling the interaction between the ball and players while imposing physical constraints on the ball's trajectory. This approach, formulated as a Mixed Integer Program, demonstrates superior robustness and accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods on real-life volleyball, basketball, and soccer sequences.
label: AI

title: Coreset-Based Adaptive Tracking
Abstract: This research proposes a method for learning from streaming visual data using a compact, constant-size representation of all data seen until a given moment. This "coreset" representation, constructed using a parallelized algorithm, approximates a set with respect to squared distances to all other points in its ambient space. An adaptive object appearance model is learned from the coreset tree in constant time and logarithmic space, used for object tracking through detection. The method achieves excellent results on three standard datasets over 100 videos. The ability to efficiently summarize data makes it ideal for tracking in long videos with space and time constraints. This is demonstrated by outperforming various algorithms on the TLD dataset with 2685 frames on average. This coreset-based learning approach is applicable for both real-time learning of small, varied data and fast learning of big data.
label: AI

title: Quantitative Analysis of Particles Segregation
Abstract: Segregation, a common phenomenon with significant effects on material performance, currently lacks an automated, objective, quantitative indicator. This paper analyzes particle segregation by extracting particle edges from digital images and splitting the image into small rectangles of uniform shape. Statistical indices of edges in each rectangle are calculated, and segregation is evaluated based on differences between these indices. The results align with subjective evaluations and can be implemented as an automated system for materials quality control during production.
label: AI

title: Semi-supervised Learning for Convolutional Neural Networks via Online Graph Construction
Abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning heavily rely on labeled data. This research addresses the scarcity of labeled data by revisiting graph-based semi-supervised learning algorithms and proposing an online graph construction technique suitable for deep convolutional neural networks. An EM-like algorithm is employed for semi-supervised learning on deep neural networks, constructing a graph based on network output and utilizing it for loss calculation to update the network through backpropagation. This online approach outperforms conventional methods using static feature representations.
label: AI

title: Principled Parallel Mean-Field Inference for Discrete Random Fields
Abstract: Mean-field variational inference, a popular approach for inference in discrete random fields, often relies on coordinate descent, which can be impractical. This paper proposes a novel proximal gradient-based approach for optimizing the variational objective. This approach is naturally parallelizable and easy to implement, offering faster convergence and improved optima compared to traditional mean-field optimization techniques. The method is also less sensitive to parameter selection.
label: AI

title: Variable Rate Image Compression with Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: A significant portion of Internet traffic originates from mobile devices with small screens and limited bandwidth. Modern graphics-heavy websites use low-resolution thumbnails for initial page load to enhance responsiveness. This paper proposes a general framework for variable-rate image compression and a novel architecture based on convolutional and deconvolutional LSTM recurrent networks. The proposed model addresses the limitations of existing autoencoder neural networks for image compression. It requires only one training step, regardless of input image dimensions and desired compression rate. The networks are progressive, meaning that higher bit counts lead to more accurate image reconstruction. The proposed architecture is at least as efficient as a standard autoencoder for a given number of bits. On a benchmark of 32x32 thumbnails, LSTM-based approaches achieve better visual quality than JPEG, JPEG2000, and WebP, with a 10% or greater reduction in storage size.
label: AI

title: Learning Deep Structure-Preserving Image-Text Embeddings
Abstract: This paper presents a method for learning joint embeddings of images and text using a two-branch neural network with multiple layers of linear projections followed by nonlinearities. The network is trained using a large margin objective that combines cross-view ranking constraints with within-view neighborhood structure preservation constraints inspired by metric learning literature. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy for image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on Flickr30K and MSCOCO image-sentence datasets and shows promise for phrase localization on the Flickr30K Entities dataset. |||
label: AI

title: Structured Depth Prediction in Challenging Monocular Video Sequences
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of estimating depth from a monocular video sequence, especially in scenarios with non-translational camera motion and dynamic scenes, where traditional methods fail. The approach leverages depth information from a pool of known images and formulates monocular depth estimation as a discrete-continuous optimization problem. This problem is solved using particle belief propagation in a graphical model, with continuous variables representing superpixel depths and discrete variables capturing relationships between neighboring superpixels. To handle video sequences, the single-image model is extended to a two-frame model that incorporates short-range temporal consistency and dynamic object handling. A fully-connected pairwise CRF is then introduced to account for long-range spatio-temporal interactions throughout the video, demonstrating effectiveness in both indoor and outdoor environments.
label: AI

title: Convolutional neural networks with low-rank regularization
Abstract: Large convolutional neural networks (CNNs) excel in various computer vision applications, but their storage and computational demands hinder deployment on mobile devices. Tensor decompositions have been employed to accelerate CNNs, and this paper proposes a new algorithm for low-rank tensor decomposition to eliminate redundancy in convolution kernels. This algorithm finds the exact global optimizer of the decomposition, outperforming iterative methods.  The decomposition enables the training of low-rank constrained CNNs from scratch, surprisingly leading to significant speedup and sometimes even improved performance compared to non-constrained counterparts. On the CIFAR-10 dataset, the proposed low-rank NIN model achieves 91.31% accuracy (without data augmentation), exceeding state-of-the-art results.  The method's effectiveness has been validated on CIFAR-10 and ILSVRC12 datasets for various modern CNNs, including AlexNet, NIN, VGG, and GoogleNet, demonstrating substantial performance improvements with reduced computation time.  For example, the forward time of VGG-16 is halved while maintaining comparable performance. These findings suggest low-rank tensor decompositions are a valuable tool for accelerating large CNNs.
label: AI

title: Deep Learning for Tactile Understanding From Visual and Haptic Data
Abstract: Robots interacting with the physical world benefit from a fine-grained tactile understanding of objects and surfaces.  Furthermore, for certain tasks, robots may need to predict the haptic properties of an object before touching it.  To enable better tactile understanding, this paper proposes a method for classifying surfaces using haptic adjectives (e.g., compressible, smooth) based on both visual and physical interaction data.  Humans combine visual predictions and physical interaction feedback to predict haptic properties and interact with the world. Inspired by this cognitive pattern, a purely visual haptic prediction model is proposed and explored, allowing a robot to "feel" without physical interaction. The study also demonstrates that combining visual and physical interaction signals yields more accurate haptic classification. The proposed models utilize deep neural networks for learning features from physical interaction and visual observations, achieving better results than methods relying on hand-designed features despite limited domain-specific knowledge.
label: AI

title: Compact Bilinear Pooling
Abstract: Bilinear models have demonstrated impressive performance on a wide range of visual tasks, including semantic segmentation, fine-grained recognition, and face recognition. However, their high dimensionality (hundreds of thousands to millions) makes them impractical for subsequent analysis. This paper proposes two compact bilinear representations that retain the discriminative power of the full bilinear representation but have only a few thousand dimensions. These compact representations enable back-propagation of classification errors, facilitating end-to-end optimization of the visual recognition system. The compact bilinear representations are derived through a novel kernelized analysis of bilinear pooling, providing insights into its discriminative power and a foundation for further research in compact pooling methods.  Experiments illustrate the utility of the proposed representations for image classification and few-shot learning across multiple datasets.
label: AI

title: What Objective Does Self-paced Learning Indeed Optimize?
Abstract: Self-paced learning (SPL) is a methodology inspired by human/animal learning principles, with various implementations designed for computer vision and pattern recognition tasks.  Despite its empirical effectiveness, its theoretical understanding remains underdeveloped. This study aims to provide theoretical insights into the SPL scheme.  It is proven that the SPL solving strategy aligns with a majorization minimization algorithm implemented on a latent objective function.  Furthermore, the loss function within this latent objective exhibits a similar configuration to non-convex regularized penalty (NSPR) known in statistics and machine learning.  This connection reveals intrinsic relationships between SPL regimes and NSPR forms like SCAD, LOG, and EXP, providing a clear explanation for SPL's robustness. The study also analyzes SPL's easy loss prior embedding property, offering insights into the effectiveness mechanisms of previous SPL variations.  Additionally, a group-partial-order loss prior is designed, particularly beneficial for processing weakly labeled large-scale data. By applying SPL with this loss prior to the FCVID dataset (one of the largest manually annotated video datasets), the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance, supporting the theoretical arguments presented.
label: AI

title: A Hierarchical Deep Temporal Model for Group Activity Recognition
Abstract: Group activity recognition aims to infer the temporal dynamics of an entire activity based on the dynamics of the individual people representing it.  This paper proposes a deep model that captures these dynamics using LSTM (long-short term memory) models.  A two-stage deep temporal model for group activity recognition is presented.  The first stage employs an LSTM model to represent the action dynamics of individual people in a sequence, while the second stage uses another LSTM model to aggregate human-level information for complete activity understanding.  The model's effectiveness is evaluated on two datasets: the collective activity dataset and a new volleyball dataset.  Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves group activity recognition performance compared to baseline methods.
label: AI

title: Stochastic gradient method with accelerated stochastic dynamics
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel technique to implement stochastic gradient methods, advantageous for learning from large datasets, through accelerated stochastic dynamics.  Stochastic gradient methods rely on mini-batch learning to reduce computational cost when dealing with massive datasets.  Gaussian noise injection mitigates the stochasticity of the gradient, resulting in the stochastic Langevin gradient method, useful for Bayesian posterior sampling. However, the performance of this method hinges on the mixing rate of the stochastic dynamics.  This study proposes to enhance the mixing rate by violating the detailed balance condition. Recent studies have shown that violating this condition accelerates convergence to a stationary state and reduces correlation time between samplings. The violation of the detailed balance condition is implemented within the stochastic gradient Langevin method and tested on a simple model to demonstrate its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Active Object Localization with Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: This paper presents an active detection model for localizing objects in scenes. The model is class-specific, enabling an agent to focus attention on candidate regions for identifying the correct location of a target object.  This agent learns to deform a bounding box using simple transformation actions, aiming to pinpoint the most specific location of target objects using top-down reasoning.  The proposed localization agent is trained using deep reinforcement learning and evaluated on the Pascal VOC 2007 dataset.  Results show that agents guided by this model can localize a single instance of an object after analyzing only 11 to 25 regions in an image, achieving superior detection results compared to systems that do not employ object proposals for localization.
label: AI

title: ABC-CNN: An Attention Based Convolutional Neural Network for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel attention-based deep learning architecture for visual question answering (VQA).  Given an image and a related natural language question, VQA generates a natural language answer.  Accurate answer generation necessitates the model's attention to focus on regions corresponding to the question, as different questions inquire about attributes of different image regions.  An attention-based configurable convolutional neural network (ABC-CNN) is proposed to learn such question-guided attention.  ABC-CNN determines an attention map for an image-question pair by convolving the image feature map with configurable convolutional kernels derived from the question's semantics.  The ABC-CNN architecture is evaluated on three benchmark VQA datasets: Toronto COCO-QA, DAQUAR, and VQA dataset.  ABC-CNN achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on these datasets. The question-guided attention generated by ABC-CNN is also shown to effectively highlight regions relevant to the questions.
label: AI

title: Collecting and Annotating the Large Continuous Action Dataset
Abstract: This paper introduces a new dataset to support action-recognition research, distinct from previous datasets in several key ways. It is significantly larger, containing streaming video with long segments encompassing multiple action occurrences that often overlap in space and/or time.  All actions were filmed in the same background environment, minimizing background cues for action classification.  Five human annotators independently labeled the temporal extent of action occurrences and their classes, revealing a surprisingly low level of intercoder agreement.  Baseline experiments show that recent state-of-the-art methods perform poorly on this dataset, suggesting its challenging nature for advancing action-recognition research. This manuscript describes the novel content and characteristics of the LCA dataset, presents filming design decisions, and documents the novel annotation methods employed.
label: AI

title: Dense Human Body Correspondences Using Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning approach for finding dense correspondences between 3D scans of people.  The method only requires partial geometric information in the form of two depth maps or partial reconstructed surfaces, working for humans in arbitrary poses and with any clothing, without requiring similar viewpoints for the two individuals, and running in real time.  A deep convolutional neural network is used to train a feature descriptor on depth map pixels.  Rather than directly training the network to solve the shape correspondence problem, it is trained to solve a body region classification problem, modified to enhance the smoothness of the learned descriptors near region boundaries. This approach ensures that nearby points on the human body are close in feature space, enabling the computation of dense correspondences between the scans.  The method is validated on real and synthetic data for both clothed and unclothed humans, demonstrating more robust correspondences compared to unsupervised methods and greater accuracy than methods requiring full watertight 3D geometry.
label: AI

title: Particular object retrieval with integral max-pooling of CNN activations
Abstract: Image representation based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has emerged as an effective descriptor for image search, outperforming pre-CNN features as short-vector representations. However, these models are incompatible with geometry-aware re-ranking methods and are still outperformed by traditional image search systems on certain object retrieval benchmarks that rely on precise descriptor matching, geometric re-ranking, or query expansion. This work re-examines both retrieval stages, initial search and re-ranking, using the same primitive information derived from the CNN. Compact feature vectors are constructed to encode multiple image regions without requiring multiple inputs to the network.  Additionally, integral images are extended to handle max-pooling on convolutional layer activations, enabling efficient localization of matching objects.  The resulting bounding box is then used for image re-ranking. This approach significantly improves the existing CNN-based recognition pipeline, achieving results comparable to traditional methods on the challenging Oxford5k and Paris6k datasets for the first time.
label: AI

title: Eigenspectra optoacoustic tomography achieves quantitative blood oxygenation imaging deep in tissues
Abstract: Light propagating through tissue exhibits a location-dependent spectrum due to wavelength-dependent fluence attenuation by tissue optical properties, leading to spectral corruption.  Predicting spectral variations in light fluence within tissue is challenging due to limitations in resolving the spatial distribution of optical properties with high resolution or accuracy.  Spectral corruption has fundamentally limited the quantification accuracy of optical and optoacoustic methods, impeding the long-standing goal of imaging blood oxygen saturation (sO2) deep within tissues.  This study unveils a new principle governing light fluence in tissues, describing the wavelength dependence of light fluence as an affine function of a few reference base spectra, independent of the specific distribution of tissue optical properties. This discovery enables the introduction of a novel concept termed eigenspectra Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography (eMSOT) that effectively accounts for wavelength-dependent light attenuation without explicit knowledge of tissue optical properties.  eMSOT is validated in over 2000 simulations and through phantom and animal measurements.  Results show that eMSOT can quantitatively image tissue sO2, achieving up to a 10-fold improvement in accuracy over conventional spectral optoacoustic methods.  Furthermore, eMSOT can spatially resolve sO2 in muscle and tumor, revealing previously unattainable tissue physiology patterns.  The study also connects eMSOT readings to cancer hypoxia, finding congruency between eMSOT tumor sO2 images and tissue perfusion and hypoxia maps obtained through correlative histological analysis.
label: AI

title: From Pose to Activity: Surveying Datasets and Introducing CONVERSE
Abstract: This paper presents a review of publicly available datasets within the human action recognition community, highlighting the resurgence of pose-based methods and recent progress in understanding person-person interaction modeling.  Datasets are categorized based on key properties for use as benchmark datasets, including the number of class labels, ground truths provided, and application domain.  The level of abstraction of each dataset is also considered, grouping those presenting actions, interactions, and higher-level semantic activities.  The survey identifies key appearance and pose-based datasets, noting a trend towards simplistic, emphasized, or scripted action classes that are often readily defined by a stable set of sub-action gestures.  A clear lack of datasets providing closely related actions, those not implicitly identified through poses and gestures but rather a dynamic set of interactions, is highlighted.  Therefore, a novel dataset representing complex conversational interactions between two individuals through 3D pose is proposed. Eight pairwise interactions describing seven separate conversation-based scenarios were collected using two Kinect depth sensors.  The intention is to provide events constructed from numerous primitive actions, interactions, and motions over time, offering a set of subtle action classes more representative of the real world and posing a challenge to existing recognition methodologies.  This is believed to be one of the first datasets dedicated to conversational interaction classification using 3D pose features, and the accompanying papers demonstrate the feasibility of this task. The full dataset is publicly available at www.csvision.swansea.ac.uk/converse.
label: AI

title: Labeled pupils in the wild: A dataset for studying pupil detection in unconstrained environments
Abstract: This paper introduces Labelled Pupils in the Wild (LPW), a novel dataset of 66 high-quality, high-speed eye region videos for the development and evaluation of pupil detection algorithms.  The videos in this dataset were recorded from 22 participants in everyday locations at approximately 95 FPS using a state-of-the-art dark-pupil head-mounted eye tracker. The dataset covers individuals with diverse ethnicities, various everyday indoor and outdoor illumination environments, and natural gaze direction distributions. Participants wearing glasses, contact lenses, and makeup are also included.  Five state-of-the-art pupil detection algorithms are benchmarked on this dataset to assess their robustness and accuracy. The influence of image resolution, vision aids, and recording location (indoor, outdoor) on pupil detection performance is further investigated.  The evaluations provide valuable insights into the general pupil detection problem and identify key challenges for robust pupil detection on head-mounted eye trackers.
label: AI

title: Image Question Answering using Convolutional Neural Network with Dynamic Parameter Prediction
Abstract: This paper addresses the image question answering (ImageQA) problem by learning a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a dynamic parameter layer whose weights are adaptively determined based on questions.  A separate parameter prediction network, composed of a gated recurrent unit (GRU) taking a question as input and a fully-connected layer generating candidate weights, is employed for adaptive parameter prediction.  However, constructing a parameter prediction network for a large number of parameters in the fully-connected dynamic parameter layer of the CNN is challenging.  To mitigate this complexity, a hashing technique is incorporated, where the candidate weights from the parameter prediction network are selected using a predefined hash function to determine individual weights in the dynamic parameter layer.  The proposed network, a joint network combining the CNN for ImageQA and the parameter prediction network, is trained end-to-end through back-propagation, with weights initialized using a pre-trained CNN and GRU.  The proposed algorithm demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on all available public ImageQA benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Compositional Memory for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) has emerged as a captivating topic in computer vision. Many state-of-the-art methods utilize holistic visual features and language features within a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) module, neglecting the intricate interaction between them.  This coarse modeling hinders the exploration of finer-grained local features that contribute dynamically over time to question answering.  This paper addresses this fundamental problem by directly modeling the temporal dynamics between language and all possible local image patches.  As the question words are traversed sequentially, the proposed end-to-end approach explicitly fuses features associated with the words and those available at multiple local patches within an attention mechanism, further combining the fused information to generate dynamic messages called episodes.  These episodes are then fed to a standard question answering module along with contextual visual information and linguistic information. Motivated by recent practices in deep learning, auxiliary loss functions are used during training to enhance performance.  Experiments on two recent public datasets suggest that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches.  Notably, on the DARQUAR dataset, the state-of-the-art is advanced by 6%, and the approach is also evaluated on the latest MSCOCO-VQA dataset.
label: AI

title: Super-Resolution with Deep Convolutional Sufficient Statistics
Abstract: Inverse problems in image and audio, particularly super-resolution, can be viewed as high-dimensional structured prediction problems, where the goal is to characterize the conditional distribution of a high-resolution output given its low-resolution corrupted observation.  While point estimates achieve impressive performance for small scaling ratios, they suffer from the regression-to-the-mean problem due to their inability to capture the multi-modality of this conditional distribution.  Modeling high-dimensional image and audio distributions is challenging, requiring the ability to represent both complex geometrical structures and textured regions.  This paper proposes using a Gibbs distribution as the conditional model, where its sufficient statistics are provided by deep convolutional neural networks.  The features computed by the network are stable to local deformation and have reduced variance when the input is a stationary texture. These properties imply that the resulting sufficient statistics minimize the uncertainty of the target signals given the degraded observations while being highly informative.  The CNN filters are initialized using multiscale complex wavelets, and an algorithm for fine-tuning them by estimating the gradient of the conditional log-likelihood, bearing similarities with Generative Adversarial Networks, is proposed. The proposed approach is evaluated experimentally in the image super-resolution task, but its generalizability allows for its application in other challenging ill-posed problems such as audio bandwidth extension.
label: AI

title: A New Smooth Approximation to the Zero One Loss with a Probabilistic Interpretation
Abstract: This paper explores a novel smooth approximation of the zero-one loss for learning using a reformulation of the widely used logistic function.  The approach is based on the posterior mean of a novel generalized Beta-Bernoulli formulation, leading to a generalized logistic function that approximates the zero-one loss while retaining a probabilistic formulation with several beneficial properties.  This approach is easily generalized to kernel logistic regression and readily integrated into structured prediction methods.  Experiments are presented where models are learned using an optimization method combining gradient descent and coordinate descent with localized grid search to escape local minima. Experiments demonstrate improved optimization quality when meta-parameters are themselves optimized using a validation set.  The results show improved performance compared to widely used logistic and hinge loss methods across a range of problems, including standard UC Irvine and libSVM evaluation datasets, product review predictions, and a visual information extraction task. Notably, the approach: 1) is more robust to outliers compared to logistic and hinge losses; 2) surpasses comparable logistic and max margin models on larger-scale benchmark problems; 3) when combined with a Gaussian-Laplacian mixture prior on parameters, the kernelized version of this formulation yields sparser solutions than Support Vector Machine classifiers; and 4) when integrated into a probabilistic structured prediction technique, this approach provides more accurate probabilities, resulting in improved inference and enhanced information extraction performance.
label: AI

title: Competitive Multi-scale Convolution
Abstract: This paper introduces a new deep convolutional neural network (ConvNet) module that promotes competition among a set of multi-scale convolutional filters.  Inspired by the inception module, this new module replaces the original collaborative pooling stage (consisting of a concatenation of multi-scale filter outputs) with a competitive pooling represented by a maxout activation unit. This extension has two objectives: 1) selecting the maximum response among the multi-scale filters prevents filter co-adaptation and allows the formation of multiple sub-networks within the same model, facilitating the training of complex learning problems; and 2) the maxout unit reduces the dimensionality of the outputs from the multi-scale filters.  The study shows that using this proposed module in typical deep ConvNets produces classification results that are either better than or comparable to the state-of-the-art on benchmark datasets: MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN. |||
label: AI

title: Predicting distributions with Linearizing Belief Networks
Abstract: Conditional belief networks introduce stochastic binary variables into neural networks. Unlike traditional neural networks, belief networks can predict more than just the expected value of the output, $Y$, given the input, $X$. They can predict a distribution of outputs $Y$, which is useful when an input can produce multiple outputs whose average is not a valid answer. These networks are particularly useful for inverse problems like image prediction for denoising or text-to-speech. However, traditional sigmoid belief networks are difficult to train and are not suitable for continuous problems. This work introduces a new family of networks called linearizing belief nets (LBNs). An LBN decomposes into a deep linear network where each linear unit can be turned on or off by non-deterministic binary latent units. It is a universal approximator of real-valued conditional distributions and can be trained using gradient descent. Additionally, the linear pathways efficiently propagate continuous information and act as multiplicative skip-connections, which help optimization by reducing gradient diffusion. This results in a model that trains efficiently and surpasses current state-of-the-art performance in image denoising and facial expression generation using the Toronto Faces dataset.
label: AI

title: Learning Structured Inference Neural Networks with Label Relations
Abstract: Images of scenes contain various objects and numerous attributes, allowing for diverse levels of visual categorization. A single image can be labeled with fine-grained labels describing major components, coarse-grained labels representing high-level abstractions, or a set of labels revealing attributes. Such categorization at different concept layers can be modeled using label graphs encoding label information. This paper leverages this rich information using a cutting-edge deep learning framework, proposing a generic structured model that utilizes diverse label relationships to improve image classification performance. Our approach employs a novel stacked label prediction neural network, capturing both inter-level and intra-level label semantics. We evaluate our method on benchmark image datasets, and empirical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our model.
label: AI

title: Identifying the Absorption Bump with Deep Learning
Abstract: Interstellar dust grains, prevalent throughout the universe, offer significant insights into the formation and evolution of stars, planetary systems, and galaxies. They may even hold the building blocks of life. One of the most effective ways to analyze dust is through its interaction with light from background sources. Observed extinction curves and spectral features provide information about dust size and composition. The broad absorption bump at 2175 Angstrom is the most prominent feature in extinction curves. Traditionally, statistical methods are employed to detect the presence of this bump. These methods require extensive preprocessing and the coexistence of other reference features to mitigate noise effects. This paper presents an approach utilizing Deep Learning techniques to detect the broad absorption bump. We demonstrate the key steps for training selected models and present their results. The success of this Deep Learning-based method encourages us to generalize a common methodology for broader scientific discovery problems. We discuss our ongoing work to develop the DeepDis system for such applications.
label: AI

title: Return of Frustratingly Easy Domain Adaptation
Abstract: Unlike human learning, machine learning often struggles to adapt to changes between training (source) and testing (target) input distributions. Such domain shifts, common in practical scenarios, significantly hinder the performance of traditional machine learning methods. Supervised domain adaptation methods have been proposed for scenarios with labeled target data, some of which achieve excellent results despite their simplicity. However, in practice, the target domain is often unlabeled, requiring unsupervised adaptation. This paper introduces a simple, effective, and efficient method for unsupervised domain adaptation called CORrelation ALignment (CORAL). CORAL minimizes domain shift by aligning the second-order statistics of source and target distributions without needing any target labels. Despite its extraordinary simplicity (it can be implemented in four lines of Matlab code), CORAL demonstrates remarkable performance in extensive evaluations on standard benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: Learning Articulated Motion Models from Visual and Lingual Signals
Abstract: For robots to function effectively in homes and workplaces, they need to be able to manipulate the articulated objects common in human-designed environments. Previous research has focused on learning kinematic models that guide this manipulation from visual demonstrations. However, lingual signals, such as natural language descriptions and instructions, offer a complementary means of conveying knowledge about these manipulation models and are suitable for a wide range of interactions (e.g., remote manipulation). This paper presents a multimodal learning framework that integrates both visual and lingual information to estimate the structure and parameters defining kinematic models of articulated objects. The visual signal takes the form of an RGB-D image stream that opportunistically captures object motion in an unprepared scene. Accompanying natural language descriptions of the motion constitute the lingual signal. We introduce a probabilistic language model that uses word embeddings to associate lingual verbs with their corresponding kinematic structures. By leveraging the complementary nature of the visual and lingual inputs, our method infers correct kinematic structures for various multi-part objects, surpassing the capabilities of previous state-of-the-art, vision-only systems. We evaluate our multimodal learning framework on a dataset comprised of various household objects, demonstrating a 36% improvement in model accuracy compared to the vision-only baseline.
label: AI

title: Moral Lineage Tracing
Abstract: Lineage tracing, the tracking of living cells as they move and divide, is a central problem in biological image analysis. Solutions, called lineage forests, are crucial for understanding how the structure of multicellular organisms emerges. This paper proposes an integer linear program (ILP) whose feasible solutions define a decomposition of each image in a sequence into cells (segmentation) and a lineage forest of cells across images (tracing). Unlike previous formulations, we do not constrain the set of decompositions, except by contracting pixels to superpixels. The main challenge, as we show, is to enforce the morality of lineages, i.e., the constraint that cells do not merge. To enforce morality, we introduce path-cut inequalities. To find feasible solutions to the NP-hard ILP, with certified bounds to the global optimum, we define efficient separation procedures and apply them as part of a branch-and-cut algorithm. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by analyzing feasible solutions for real microscopy data in terms of bounds and runtime, and by comparing their weighted edit distance to ground truth lineage forests traced by humans.
label: AI

title: Learning Neural Network Architectures using Backpropagation
Abstract: Deep neural networks with millions of parameters are at the core of many state-of-the-art machine learning models today. However, recent studies have shown that models with significantly fewer parameters can perform equally well. This work introduces the problem of architecture-learning, i.e., learning the architecture of a neural network along with its weights. We introduce a new trainable parameter called tri-state ReLU, which facilitates the elimination of unnecessary neurons. We also propose a smooth regularizer that encourages a minimal total number of neurons after elimination. The resulting objective is differentiable and easy to optimize. We experimentally validate our method on both small and large networks, demonstrating its ability to learn models with significantly fewer parameters without compromising prediction accuracy.
label: AI

title: Deep multi-scale video prediction beyond mean square error
Abstract: Learning to predict future images from a video sequence involves constructing an internal representation that accurately models image evolution, and therefore, to some degree, its content and dynamics. This is why pixel-space video prediction can be viewed as a promising avenue for unsupervised feature learning. Additionally, while optical flow has been extensively studied in computer vision, future frame prediction is rarely explored. Nevertheless, many vision applications could benefit from knowledge of the next frames of videos without the complexity of tracking every pixel trajectory. This work trains a convolutional network to generate future frames given an input sequence. To address the inherent blurriness in predictions resulting from the standard Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function, we propose three complementary feature learning strategies: a multi-scale architecture, an adversarial training method, and an image gradient difference loss function. We compare our predictions to various published results based on recurrent neural networks on the UCF101 dataset.
label: AI

title: Structural-RNN: Deep Learning on Spatio-Temporal Graphs
Abstract: Deep Recurrent Neural Network architectures, while remarkably capable of modeling sequences, lack an intuitive high-level spatio-temporal structure. This is problematic for many computer vision problems that inherently have an underlying high-level structure and could benefit from it. Spatio-temporal graphs are a popular tool for imposing such high-level intuitions in the formulation of real-world problems. This paper proposes an approach for combining the power of high-level spatio-temporal graphs and the sequence learning success of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). We develop a scalable method for casting an arbitrary spatio-temporal graph as a rich RNN mixture that is feedforward, fully differentiable, and jointly trainable. The proposed method is generic and principled as it can be used to transform any spatio-temporal graph through a defined set of steps. Evaluations on a diverse set of problems, ranging from modeling human motion to object interactions, demonstrate significant improvements over the state-of-the-art. We anticipate this method to empower new approaches to problem formulation through high-level spatio-temporal graphs and Recurrent Neural Networks.
label: AI

title: Towards Predicting the Likeability of Fashion Images
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for ranking fashion images to identify those that are likely to be liked by more people. We collected two new datasets from image sharing websites (Pinterest and Polyvore). We represent fashion images based on attributes: semantic attributes and data-driven attributes. To learn semantic attributes from limited training data, we utilize an algorithm based on multi-task convolutional neural networks to share visual knowledge among different semantic attribute categories. To discover data-driven attributes unsupervisedly, we propose an algorithm that simultaneously discovers visual clusters and learns fashion-specific feature representations. Given attributes as representations, we propose to learn a ranking SPN (sum product networks) to rank pairs of fashion images. The proposed ranking SPN can capture the high-order correlations of the attributes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on our two newly collected datasets.
label: AI

title: Hierarchical Spatial Sum-Product Networks for Action Recognition in Still Images
Abstract: Recognizing actions from still images has recently gained popularity. This paper models an action class as a flexible number of spatial configurations of body parts by proposing a new spatial SPN (Sum-Product Networks). First, we discover a set of parts in image collections through unsupervised learning. Then, our new spatial SPN is applied to model the spatial relationship and high-order correlations of parts. To learn robust networks, we further develop a hierarchical spatial SPN method, which models pairwise spatial relationships between parts within sub-images and models the correlation of sub-images through extra SPN layers. Our method demonstrates effectiveness on two benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: Classifying and Segmenting Microscopy Images Using Convolutional Multiple Instance Learning
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance on both classification and segmentation tasks. However, applying CNNs to microscopy images is challenging due to the lack of datasets labeled at the single-cell level. We extend the application of CNNs to microscopy image classification and segmentation using multiple instance learning (MIL). We introduce the adaptive Noisy-AND MIL pooling function, a new MIL operator that is robust to outliers. Combining CNNs with MIL enables training CNNs using full-resolution microscopy images with global labels. Our approach leverages the similarity between the aggregation function used in MIL and pooling layers used in CNNs. We demonstrate that training MIL CNNs end-to-end outperforms several previous methods on both mammalian and yeast microscopy images without requiring any segmentation steps.
label: AI

title: Deep Compositional Captioning: Describing Novel Object Categories without Paired Training Data
Abstract: While recent deep neural network models have achieved promising results on the image captioning task, they rely heavily on the availability of corpora with paired image and sentence captions describing objects in context. This work introduces the Deep Compositional Captioner (DCC) to address the task of generating descriptions of novel objects that are not present in paired image-sentence datasets. Our method achieves this by leveraging large object recognition datasets and external text corpora and by transferring knowledge between semantically similar concepts. Existing deep caption models can only describe objects present in paired image-sentence corpora, despite being pre-trained with large object recognition datasets, namely ImageNet. In contrast, our model can compose sentences that describe novel objects and their interactions with other objects. We demonstrate our model's ability to describe novel concepts by empirically evaluating its performance on MSCOCO and show qualitative results on ImageNet images of objects for which no paired image-caption data exists. Further, we extend our approach to generate descriptions of objects in video clips. Our results demonstrate that DCC has distinct advantages over existing image and video captioning approaches for generating descriptions of new objects in context.
label: AI

title: Robust PCA via Nonconvex Rank Approximation
Abstract: Numerous applications in data mining and machine learning require recovering a matrix of minimal rank. Robust principal component analysis (RPCA) is a general framework for handling such problems. Nuclear norm-based convex surrogate of the rank function in RPCA has been extensively investigated. Under certain assumptions, it can recover the underlying true low-rank matrix with high probability. However, these assumptions may not hold in real-world applications. Since the nuclear norm approximates rank by adding all singular values together (essentially an $\\ell_1$-norm of the singular values), the resulting approximation error is not trivial, leading to a potentially biased matrix estimator. To seek a closer approximation and alleviate the aforementioned limitations of the nuclear norm, we propose a nonconvex rank approximation. This approximation to the matrix rank is tighter than the nuclear norm. To solve the associated nonconvex minimization problem, we develop an efficient augmented Lagrange multiplier-based optimization algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art algorithms in both accuracy and efficiency.
label: AI

title: Ask, Attend and Answer: Exploring Question-Guided Spatial Attention for Visual Question Answering
Abstract: We address the problem of Visual Question Answering (VQA), which requires joint image and language understanding to answer a question about a given photograph. Recent approaches have applied deep image captioning methods based on convolutional-recurrent networks to this problem, but have failed to model spatial inference. To address this, we propose a model called the Spatial Memory Network and apply it to the VQA task. Memory networks are recurrent neural networks with an explicit attention mechanism that selects specific parts of the information stored in memory. Our Spatial Memory Network stores neuron activations from different spatial regions of the image in its memory and uses the question to choose relevant regions for computing the answer, a process that constitutes a single "hop" in the network. We introduce a novel spatial attention architecture that aligns words with image patches in the first hop and achieve improved results by adding a second attention hop that considers the entire question to choose visual evidence based on the results of the first hop. To better understand the inference process learned by the network, we design synthetic questions that specifically require spatial inference and visualize the attention weights. We evaluate our model on two published visual question answering datasets, DAQUAR [1] and VQA [2], and obtain improved results compared to a strong deep baseline model (iBOWIMG) which concatenates image and question features to predict the answer [3].
label: AI

title: Learning Expressionlets via Universal Manifold Model for Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition
Abstract: Facial expression is a temporally dynamic event that can be decomposed into a set of muscle motions occurring in different facial regions over various time intervals. For dynamic expression recognition, two key issues, temporal alignment and semantics-aware dynamic representation, must be considered. This paper attempts to address both problems through manifold modeling of videos based on a novel mid-level representation, namely \textbf{expressionlet}. Specifically, our method comprises three key stages: 1) each expression video clip is characterized as a spatial-temporal manifold (STM) formed by dense low-level features; 2) a Universal Manifold Model (UMM) is learned over all low-level features and represented as a set of local modes to statistically unify all the STMs; 3) the local modes on each STM can be instantiated by fitting to UMM, and the corresponding expressionlet is constructed by modeling the variations in each local mode. With this strategy, expression videos are naturally aligned both spatially and temporally. To enhance discriminative power, the expressionlet-based STM representation is further processed with discriminant embedding. Our method is evaluated on four public expression databases, CK+, MMI, Oulu-CASIA, and FERA. In all cases, our method outperforms the known state-of-the-art by a significant margin.
label: AI

title: Visualizing and Understanding Deep Texture Representations
Abstract: Recent approaches have employed deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to construct texture representations. However, it remains unclear how these models represent texture and invariances to categorical variations. This work systematically evaluates recent CNN-based texture descriptors for recognition and attempts to understand the nature of invariances captured by these representations. First, we demonstrate that the recently proposed bilinear CNN model [25] is an excellent general-purpose texture descriptor and compares favorably to other CNN-based descriptors on various texture and scene recognition benchmarks. The model is translationally invariant and achieves better accuracy on the ImageNet dataset without requiring spatial jittering of data compared to corresponding models trained with spatial jittering. Based on recent work [13, 28], we propose a technique to visualize pre-images, providing a means for understanding categorical properties captured by these representations. Finally, we present preliminary results on how a unified parametric model of texture analysis and synthesis can be used for attribute-based image manipulation, e.g., to make an image more swirly, honeycombed, or knitted. The source code and additional visualizations are available at http://vis-www.cs.umass.edu/texture.
label: AI

title: Convolutional Models for Joint Object Categorization and Pose Estimation
Abstract: In the task of Object Recognition, there exists a dichotomy between the categorization of objects and estimating object pose. Object categorization requires a view-invariant representation, while object pose estimation necessitates a representation capable of capturing pose information across different object categories. With the rise of deep architectures, the primary focus has been on object category recognition. Deep learning methods have achieved widespread success in this task. In contrast, object pose regression using these approaches has received relatively less attention. This paper shows how deep architectures, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), can be adapted for simultaneous categorization and pose estimation of objects. We investigate and analyze the layers of various CNN models and extensively compare them with the goal of understanding how the layers of distributed representations in CNNs encode object pose information and how this contrasts with object category representations. We conduct extensive experiments on two recent large and challenging multi-view datasets. Our models achieve better than state-of-the-art performance on both datasets.
label: AI

title: Cross-scale predictive dictionaries
Abstract: Sparse representations using data dictionaries provide an efficient model, particularly for signals that lack alternate analytic sparsifying transformations. However, solving inverse problems with sparsifying dictionaries can be computationally expensive, especially when the dictionary under consideration has a large number of atoms. This paper incorporates additional structure into dictionary-based sparse representations for visual signals to enable speedups when solving sparse approximation problems. The specific structure we endow onto sparse models is that of multi-scale modeling, where the sparse representation at each scale is constrained by the sparse representation at coarser scales. We show that this cross-scale predictive model delivers significant speedups, often in the range of 10-60$\\times$, with little loss in accuracy for linear inverse problems associated with images, videos, and light fields.
label: AI

title: Nonlinear Local Metric Learning for Person Re-identification
Abstract: Person re-identification aims to match pedestrians observed from non-overlapping camera views. Feature descriptor and metric learning are two significant problems in person re-identification. A discriminative metric learning method should be capable of exploiting complex nonlinear transformations due to the large variations in feature space. This paper proposes a nonlinear local metric learning (NLML) method to enhance the state-of-the-art performance of person re-identification on public datasets. Motivated by the fact that local metric learning has been introduced to handle data that varies locally and deep neural networks have presented outstanding capability in exploiting the nonlinearity of samples, we utilize the merits of both local metric learning and deep neural networks to learn multiple sets of nonlinear transformations. By enforcing a margin between the distances of positive pedestrian image pairs and distances of negative pairs in the transformed feature subspace, discriminative information can be effectively exploited in the developed neural networks. Our experiments show that the proposed NLML method achieves state-of-the-art results on the widely used VIPeR, GRID, and CUHK 01 datasets. |||
label: AI

title: Adversarial Manipulation of Deep Representations
