Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) can be manipulated to produce adversarial images that appear visually similar to one image but have an internal representation that is remarkably similar to a different image from a different class. This phenomenon raises questions about the nature of DNN representations and the properties of natural images themselves.
label: AI

title: Yin and Yang: Balancing and Answering Binary Visual Questions
Abstract: The complex structure of language poses challenges for vision-and-language tasks, as language can provide a strong prior that leads to good superficial performance without deep understanding of the visual content. To address this issue, we focus on binary Visual Question Answering (VQA) on abstract scenes, formulating the problem as visual verification of concepts. We use abstract scenes to control language priors and highlight the importance of visual understanding. Our balanced dataset necessitates the use of visual reasoning, while our proposed approach matches state-of-the-art VQA performance on unbalanced datasets and outperforms it on the balanced dataset.
label: AI

title: Understanding learned CNN features through Filter Decoding with Substitution
Abstract: Understanding and visualizing the internal representations of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is crucial for both computer and human vision research. While early convolutional layers are easy to interpret, deeper layers become increasingly opaque. We propose a new approach based on filter substitution to reverse the encoding of a convolutional layer, allowing direct visualization of any CNN single neuron as a filter in the first layer, thereby providing insights into the image space.
label: AI

title: Joint Training of Generic CNN-CRF Models with Stochastic Optimization
Abstract: We introduce a novel end-to-end learning framework for CNN-CRF models, based on joint stochastic optimization of both CNN and CRF parameters. Our method is general, scalable, and easy to implement. It allows for arbitrary CNN and CRF architectures and potential functions, and its low memory footprint enables efficient parallelization on GPUs. The unified optimization approach simplifies potential hardware implementations. Our method demonstrates superior performance on the task of semantic labeling of body parts in depth images.
label: AI

title: Proposal Flow
Abstract: Finding image correspondences is challenging due to intra-class variations and scene layout changes. Semantic flow methods address these challenges by focusing on images depicting different instances of the same object or scene category. We introduce a novel approach called "proposal flow" that leverages object proposals to establish reliable correspondences. Unlike existing methods operating on pixels or local regions, proposal flow benefits from the repeatability of object proposals at multiple scales and utilizes local and geometric consistency constraints. Our experiments demonstrate that proposal flow significantly outperforms existing semantic flow methods in various settings.
label: AI

title: An Empirical Study of Recent Face Alignment Methods
Abstract: Recent advancements in face alignment have achieved impressive results on benchmark datasets like 300W. However, inconsistencies in experimental settings, evaluation metrics, and method descriptions hinder reproducibility and evaluation of relative merits. To address these issues, we introduce a new evaluation metric, AUC$_\\alpha$, which is less sensitive to large alignment errors. We extend the 300W database with more practical face detections, enabling fair comparisons. Our sensitivity analysis reveals the impact of face detection on alignment performance, and our study highlights important factors for achieving good performance. Our findings provide valuable insights for practical applications.
label: AI

title: Handcrafted Local Features are Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Image and video classification research has made significant progress using handcrafted local features and learning-based features. This paper highlights the structural similarities between these two approaches, showing how a unified view can lead to more efficient and effective features. We study the problem of designing efficient video feature learning algorithms for action recognition. We propose a two-stream Convolutional ISA (ConvISA) that leverages the convolution-pooling structure of handcrafted video features, combining greater modeling capacities with a cost-effective training algorithm. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
label: AI

title: Sample and Filter: Nonparametric Scene Parsing via Efficient Filtering
Abstract: Scene parsing has witnessed significant advancements using parametric models. However, these models struggle to incorporate new training data easily. Nonparametric approaches, while readily adaptable to new data, suffer from computational costs and often discard valuable information by filtering out most training images. We introduce a nonparametric approach to scene parsing that employs a sample-and-filter strategy. Our method samples labeled superpixels based on image similarity, leading to a balanced set of samples. We then formulate label transfer as an efficient filtering procedure, allowing us to utilize more labeled samples than existing techniques. Our experiments show the benefits of our approach on benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: Identification and Counting White Blood Cells and Red Blood Cells using Image Processing Case Study of Leukemia
Abstract: Leukemia diagnosis relies on complete blood counts to analyze white blood cells (WBC) and red blood cells (RBC). While manual counting is time-consuming and expensive, image processing techniques offer a potential solution. This study aims to identify Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia (ALL) and Acute Myeloid Leukemia type M3 (AML M3) using a Fuzzy Rule Based System based on WBC morphology. We extract characteristic parameters such as WBC area, nucleus, and granule ratio, using image processing algorithms like thresholding, Canny edge detection, and color identification filters. Our Fuzzy Rule Based System with the Sugeno method achieves 83.65% accuracy in identifying ALL, AML M3, and healthy cells.
label: AI

title: Performing Highly Accurate Predictions Through Convolutional Networks for Actual Telecommunication Challenges
Abstract: Deep learning, specifically convolutional networks trained with GPUs, has the potential to improve predictive models in telecommunication business environments. We focus on predicting customer churn, a challenging problem in telecommunication operators. Our model, WiseNet, consists of a convolutional network and a novel encoding method that transforms customer activity data and Call Detail Records (CDRs) into images. WiseNet outperforms traditional machine learning models with handcrafted features and eliminates the need for laborious feature engineering. Its generalization property allows for consistent results across different markets, highlighting its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Graph-based denoising for time-varying point clouds
Abstract: Noisy 3D point clouds are common in various applications, resulting from errors in 3D model construction or imprecise depth sensors. We introduce a technique that leverages graph structures derived from point cloud similarity information and convex optimization methods to denoise 3D point clouds. Our approach can be naturally extended to time-varying inputs such as 3D point cloud time series.
label: AI

title: Coarse-to-fine Face Alignment with Multi-Scale Local Patch Regression
Abstract: Facial landmark localization is crucial for face recognition and analysis. We present a coarse-to-fine pipeline using neural networks and sequential regression for accurate landmark prediction. Our system first utilizes a global convolutional network to generate an initial prediction. Subsequently, a pyramid of multi-scale local image patches is cropped and fed to a dedicated network for each landmark, refining the prediction. This iterative refinement process continues until convergence, resulting in highly accurate landmark localization. Our system achieves state-of-the-art performance on the 300-W dataset.
label: AI

title: Fast clustering for scalable statistical analysis on structured images
Abstract: Analyzing brain images for disease markers or behavioral differences is challenging due to small effect sizes and the need for large cohorts. The resulting data deluge poses significant challenges for traditional processing methods due to memory constraints. We propose a novel dimension reduction approach based on fast clustering, specifically designed for signals with strong spatial structure like anatomical and functional brain images. Our approach offers linear-time complexity, surpassing traditional quadratic-complexity variance-minimizing clustering schemes. Furthermore, it removes high-frequency noise, leading to improved subsequent estimations and more accurate models on large-scale problems, while significantly improving computational efficiency.
label: AI

title: Sherlock: Scalable Fact Learning in Images
Abstract: We explore scalable and uniform understanding of facts in images. Existing visual recognition systems typically model each fact type (objects, actions, interactions) differently. Our approach enables simultaneous modeling of an unbounded number of facts in a structured way. Training data comprises structured facts in images, including objects, attributes, actions, and interactions. We show that structured learning of visual facts leads to generalizable visual understanding. We investigate recent multiview learning methods and propose two learning representation models as baselines. Our experiments demonstrate the advantage of relating facts through structure, achieving superior performance on bidirectional fact retrieval.
label: AI

title: Deep learning is a good steganalysis tool when embedding key is reused for different images, even if there is a cover source-mismatch
Abstract: Most steganalysis approaches utilize a two-step learning methodology: feature extraction using Rich Models (RM) and classification using Ensemble Classifiers (EC). Recent research suggests that deep learning approaches that jointly learn and compute features are promising for steganalysis. We build upon this work, demonstrating that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Fully Connected Neural Networks (FNNs), when properly parameterized, outperform the conventional RM-EC combination. Our experiments highlight the effectiveness of CNNs and FNNs in steganalysis, achieving a significant reduction in classification error and demonstrating robustness to cover-source mismatch.
label: AI

title: Learning Mid-level Words on Riemannian Manifold for Action Recognition
Abstract: Human action recognition remains challenging due to diverse video data sources and large intra-class variations. We propose a novel representation approach based on constructing mid-level words in videos and encoding them on Riemannian manifolds. Our method first aligns densely extracted low-level features to create corresponding feature groups, modeled as mid-level words on Riemannian manifolds. We construct intrinsic Riemannian codebooks using K-Karcher-means clustering and Riemannian Gaussian Mixture Model, extending Euclidean encoding methods like BoVW, VLAD, and FV to the Riemannian domain. Our approach achieves competitive performance on action recognition and action similarity labeling tasks across various datasets.
label: AI

title: Heterogeneous Knowledge Transfer in Video Emotion Recognition, Attribution and Summarization
Abstract: Emotion plays a vital role in user-generated videos, but understanding emotions conveyed in these videos is challenging due to the complex and unstructured nature of content and the sparsity of emotion-expressing frames. We propose a novel framework for transferring knowledge from heterogeneous external sources (images and text) to facilitate video emotion understanding. Our framework learns a video encoding from an auxiliary emotional image dataset to improve supervised video emotion recognition and leverages an auxiliary textual corpus for zero-shot recognition of unseen emotion classes. This knowledge transfer enables emotion attribution and emotion-oriented summarization applications. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.
label: AI

title: Complete Dictionary Recovery over the Sphere II: Recovery by Riemannian Trust-region Method
Abstract: We investigate the problem of recovering a complete matrix $\mathbf A_0$ from $\mathbf Y \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ with $\mathbf Y = \mathbf A_0 \mathbf X_0$, where $\mathbf X_0$ is sufficiently sparse. This problem is fundamental to dictionary learning, which seeks sparse representations for input signals. We provide the first efficient algorithm that provably recovers $\mathbf A_0$ when $\mathbf X_0$ has $O(n)$ nonzeros per column under suitable probability model for $\mathbf X_0$. Our algorithmic pipeline involves solving a nonconvex optimization problem with a spherical constraint, which is naturally formulated in the language of manifold optimization. We leverage the geometric structure of the problem and describe a Riemannian trust region algorithm that provably converges to a local minimizer from arbitrary initializations. These minimizers provide excellent approximations to rows of $\mathbf X_0$, which can be further recovered through linear programming rounding and deflation.
label: AI

title: Separation Surfaces in the Spectral TV Domain for Texture Decomposition
Abstract: We introduce a novel notion of separation surfaces for image decomposition. These surfaces are embedded in the spectral total-variation (TV) three-dimensional domain and encode a spatially-varying separation scale, enabling effective separation of textures with gradually changing pattern-size, pattern-contrast, or illumination. The total variation spectral framework decomposes the image into a continuum of textural scales. A desired texture is found by fitting a surface to the local maximal responses in the spectral domain. This "Texture Stratum" defines an adaptive scale-range for each pixel, enabling natural and visually convincing texture attenuation or enhancement.
label: AI

title: Semi-Inner-Products for Convex Functionals and Their Use in Image Decomposition
Abstract: Semi-inner-products, as defined by Lumer, are extended to convex functionals, providing a Hilbert-space like structure to convex functionals in Banach spaces. We derive a general expression for semi-inner-products with respect to one homogeneous functional. This allows us to analyze total variation and higher-order functionals like total-generalized-variation (TGV). Using the semi-inner-product, we define an angle between functions. We demonstrate that in the one homogeneous case, the Bregman distance can be expressed in terms of this angle. We also derive properties of the semi-inner-product of nonlinear eigenfunctions induced by the functional. This construction provides a sufficient condition for perfect decomposition of two signals and suggests numerical measures for assessing when these conditions are approximately met. |||
label: AI

title: Uncovering Temporal Context for Video Question and Answering
Abstract: This work introduces Video Question Answering in the temporal domain, allowing us to infer past events, describe the present, and predict future happenings. We propose an encoder-decoder approach utilizing Recurrent Neural Networks to learn temporal structures within videos. A dual-channel ranking loss is implemented to answer multiple-choice questions.  We investigate methods for deeper understanding of video content by employing "fill-in-the-blank" question formats. A dataset comprising 109,895 video clips spanning over 1,000 hours was curated from TACoS, MPII-MD, and MEDTest 14 datasets, with 390,744 corresponding questions generated from annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate our approach significantly outperforms existing baselines.
label: AI

title: Deep Neural Network for Real-Time Autonomous Indoor Navigation
Abstract: Autonomous indoor navigation for Micro Aerial Vehicles (MAVs) poses significant challenges due to the limited precision of GPS in such environments. The inability of MAVs to carry heavy or energy-intensive sensors, such as range finders, further complicates the task. This paper presents a practical system where a quadcopter autonomously navigates indoor spaces and locates a specific target, a book bag, using only a single camera. A deep learning model, Convolutional Neural Network (ConvNet), is employed to learn a control strategy that mimics an expert pilot's decision-making process. We validate the system's performance through real-time experiments in diverse indoor locations. Visualization techniques are used to gain deeper insights into the trained network.
label: AI

title: Implementation and comparative quantitative assessment of different multispectral image pansharpening approches
Abstract: In remote sensing, images obtained from various Earth observation satellites often exhibit either high spatial resolution with low spectral resolution or vice versa. Pansharpening is a technique aimed at enhancing the spatial resolution of multispectral images. The challenge lies in achieving this improvement while preserving the spectral quality of the multispectral image. This paper examines and classifies various pansharpening algorithms based on their adopted approaches. Using the MATLAB image processing toolbox, several state-of-the-art pan-sharpening algorithms are implemented. The quality of the pansharpened images is assessed both visually and quantitatively.  Correlation coefficient (CC), Root mean square error (RMSE), Relative average spectral error (RASE), and Universal quality index (Q) indices are employed to measure spectral quality, while spatial-CC (SCC) is used for spatial quality assessment. The paper concludes with valuable observations.
label: AI

title: Sensory Polymorphism and Behavior: When Machine Vision Meets Monkey Eyes
Abstract: Polymorphism in the peripheral sensory system, such as congenital individual differences in photopigment configuration, plays a crucial role in diverse research fields, from evolutionary biology to engineering. This is due to its potential connection to cognitive and behavioral variability across individuals. However, a gap exists between the current understanding of sensory polymorphism and the behavioral variability resulting from potentially complex cognitive processes in natural environments. Linking peripheral sensor properties to behavior requires computational models of nervous processes that translate sensory representations into actions, based on quantitative data from physiological and behavioral studies. Recent research employing machine vision approaches is shedding light on the quantitative relationships between sensory polymorphisms and resulting behavioral variability. Achieving a convergent understanding of the functional impacts of sensory polymorphisms in realistic environments necessitates close collaboration between physiological, behavioral, and computational approaches. This paper aims to enhance such integrative research by providing an overview of recent advancements in these interdisciplinary approaches and suggesting effective strategies for their integration.
label: AI

title: Jointly Learning Non-negative Projection and Dictionary with Discriminative Graph Constraints for Classification
Abstract: Sparse coding with dictionary learning (DL) has demonstrated excellent classification performance. Despite the significant number of existing works, the optimal method for obtaining features on top of which dictionaries can be effectively learned remains an open question. Many prevalent DL methods directly utilize well-performing crafted features. While this strategy may work well empirically, it overlooks the inherent relationship between dictionaries and features. We propose a framework where features and dictionaries are jointly learned and optimized. This framework, dubbed joint non-negative projection and dictionary learning (JNPDL), enables interaction between the input features and the dictionaries. Non-negative projection results in discriminative parts-based object features, while DL seeks a more suitable representation. Discriminative graph constraints are further imposed to concurrently maximize intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Experiments on both image and image set classification demonstrate the superior performance of JNPDL, outperforming several state-of-the-art approaches.
label: AI

title: DeepFool: a simple and accurate method to fool deep neural networks
Abstract: State-of-the-art deep neural networks have achieved impressive results in numerous image classification tasks. However, these architectures have been shown to be susceptible to small, carefully crafted perturbations of the images. Despite the significance of this phenomenon, no effective methods have been proposed for accurately assessing the robustness of state-of-the-art deep classifiers to such perturbations on large-scale datasets. This paper addresses this gap by introducing the DeepFool algorithm to efficiently compute perturbations that mislead deep networks, thereby reliably quantifying the robustness of these classifiers. Extensive experimental results indicate that our approach surpasses recent methods in the task of computing adversarial perturbations and enhancing classifier robustness.
label: AI

title: Oracle performance for visual captioning
Abstract: The task of associating images and videos with natural language descriptions has garnered significant attention recently. Remarkable progress has been made in both developing novel algorithms and releasing new datasets.  The state-of-the-art results on some standard datasets have reached a point where further significant improvements are increasingly challenging. Instead of proposing new models, this work investigates the possibility of empirically establishing performance upper bounds on various visual captioning datasets without requiring additional data labeling effort or human evaluation.  It is assumed that visual captioning can be decomposed into two steps: from visual inputs to visual concepts and from visual concepts to natural language descriptions. An upper bound can be obtained by assuming the first step is perfect and only requiring training a conditional language model for the second step.  We demonstrate the construction of such bounds on MS-COCO, YouTube2Text, and LSMDC (a combination of M-VAD and MPII-MD). Surprisingly, despite the imperfect process used for visual concept extraction in the first step and the simplicity of the language model in the second step, we show that current state-of-the-art models fall short when compared to the learned upper bounds. Furthermore, with this bound, we quantify several important factors concerning image and video captioning: the number of visual concepts captured by different models, the trade-off between the amount of visual elements captured and their accuracy, and the intrinsic difficulty and advantages of different datasets.
label: AI

title: Accurate Image Super-Resolution Using Very Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a highly accurate single-image super-resolution (SR) method. Our method utilizes a very deep convolutional network inspired by VGG-net, which is known for its use in ImageNet classification. We observed that increasing the network depth significantly improves accuracy. Our final model uses 20 weight layers. By cascading small filters multiple times within a deep network structure, contextual information across large image regions is exploited efficiently. However, with very deep networks, convergence speed becomes a critical issue during training. We propose a simple yet effective training procedure. We learn residuals only and utilize extremely high learning rates (10^4 times higher than SRCNN), enabled by adjustable gradient clipping. Our proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, and visual improvements in our results are easily noticeable.
label: AI

title: Learning Fine-grained Features via a CNN Tree for Large-scale Classification
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance the discriminability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The key idea is to construct a tree structure that progressively learns fine-grained features to distinguish subsets of classes by learning features only among these classes.  These features are expected to be more discriminative compared to features learned for all classes. We develop a new algorithm for effectively learning the tree structure from a large number of classes. Experiments on large-scale image classification tasks demonstrate that our method can enhance the performance of a given basic CNN model. Our method is quite general and can potentially be used in conjunction with various other deep learning models.
label: AI

title: Efficient Training of Very Deep Neural Networks for Supervised Hashing
Abstract: This paper proposes the training of very deep neural networks (DNNs) for supervised learning of hash codes. Existing methods in this context train relatively "shallow" networks, limited by challenges arising from back propagation (e.g., vanishing gradients) and computational efficiency. We introduce a novel and efficient training algorithm inspired by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) that addresses some of these limitations. Our method decomposes the training process into independent layer-wise local updates through auxiliary variables. Empirically, we observe that our training algorithm consistently converges, and its computational complexity is linearly proportional to the number of edges in the networks. We successfully trained DNNs with 64 hidden layers and 1024 nodes per layer for supervised hashing in approximately 3 hours using a single GPU. Our proposed very deep supervised hashing (VDSH) method significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art on several benchmark datasets.
label: AI

title: Reversible Recursive Instance-level Object Segmentation
Abstract: This work presents a novel Reversible Recursive Instance-level Object Segmentation (R2-IOS) framework to address the challenging task of instance-level object segmentation. R2-IOS consists of a reversible proposal refinement sub-network that predicts bounding box offsets for refining object proposal locations and an instance-level segmentation sub-network that generates the foreground mask of the dominant object instance within each proposal. Through recursion, R2-IOS iteratively optimizes the two sub-networks during joint training. Refined object proposals and improved segmentation predictions are alternately fed into each other, progressively enhancing the network's capabilities. The reversible nature of the proposal refinement sub-network adaptively determines an optimal number of refinement iterations required for each proposal during both training and testing. Furthermore, to handle multiple overlapping instances within a proposal, an instance-aware denoising autoencoder is integrated into the segmentation sub-network to distinguish the dominant object from other distracting instances. Extensive experiments on the challenging PASCAL VOC 2012 benchmark clearly demonstrate the superiority of R2-IOS over other state-of-the-art methods. Notably, the AP^r over 20 classes at 0.5 IoU achieves 66.7%, significantly surpassing the results of 58.7% by PFN and 46.3% by Liu et al.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Learning via Joint Latent Similarity Embedding
Abstract: Zero-shot recognition (ZSR) tackles the problem of predicting class labels for target domain instances based on source domain side information (e.g., attributes) of unseen classes. We formulate ZSR as a binary prediction problem. Our resulting classifier is class-independent. It takes an arbitrary pair of source and target domain instances as input and predicts whether or not they belong to the same class, i.e., whether there is a match. We model the posterior probability of a match, as it is a sufficient statistic, and propose a latent probabilistic model in this context. We develop a joint discriminative learning framework based on dictionary learning to jointly learn the parameters of our model for both domains, ultimately leading to our class-independent classifier.  Many existing embedding methods can be viewed as special cases of our probabilistic model. In ZSR, our method exhibits a 4.90% improvement over the state-of-the-art in accuracy averaged across four benchmark datasets. We also adapt our ZSR method for zero-shot retrieval and demonstrate a 22.45% improvement in mean average precision (mAP).
label: AI

title: Sequential Optimization for Efficient High-Quality Object Proposal Generation
Abstract: Motivated by the need for a generic object proposal generation algorithm that achieves a good balance between object detection recall, proposal localization quality, and computational efficiency, we propose a novel object proposal algorithm, BING++. BING++ inherits the computational efficiency advantage of BING while significantly improving its proposal localization quality. At a high level, we formulate the problem of object proposal generation from a novel probabilistic perspective. Based on this perspective, BING++ enhances localization quality by employing edges and segments to estimate object boundaries and update the proposals sequentially. We propose an efficient parameter learning method by searching for approximate solutions in a quantized parameter space for complexity reduction. We demonstrate the generalization of BING++ with the same fixed parameters across different object classes and datasets. Empirically, BING++ can operate at half the speed of BING on CPU while significantly improving localization quality by 18.5% and 16.7% on the VOC2007 and Microsoft COCO datasets, respectively. Compared to other state-of-the-art approaches, BING++ achieves comparable performance but runs significantly faster.
label: AI

title: Semantic Object Parsing with Local-Global Long Short-Term Memory
Abstract: Semantic object parsing is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to understand objects in detail.  Incorporating multi-level contextual information is crucial for achieving this fine-grained pixel-level recognition. Prior methods often leverage contextual information through post-processing predicted confidence maps. In this work, we propose a novel deep Local-Global Long Short-Term Memory (LG-LSTM) architecture to seamlessly incorporate short-distance and long-distance spatial dependencies into feature learning across all pixel positions.  In each LG-LSTM layer, local guidance from neighboring positions and global guidance from the entire image are imposed on each position to better exploit complex local and global contextual information. Individual LSTMs for distinct spatial dimensions are also utilized to intrinsically capture various spatial layouts of semantic parts in the images, resulting in distinct hidden and memory cells for each position along each dimension. In our parsing approach, several LG-LSTM layers are stacked and appended to the intermediate convolutional layers to directly enhance visual features, allowing network parameters to be learned end-to-end. The long chains of sequential computation by stacked LG-LSTM layers also enable each pixel to sense a much larger region for inference, benefiting from the memorization of previous dependencies in all positions along all dimensions. Comprehensive evaluations on three public datasets demonstrate the significant superiority of our LG-LSTM over other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: This paper proposes an image super-resolution method (SR) using a deeply-recursive convolutional network (DRCN). Our network features a very deep recursive layer (up to 16 recursions). Increasing recursion depth can enhance performance without introducing new parameters for additional convolutions. While advantageous, learning a DRCN is very challenging using a standard gradient descent method due to exploding/vanishing gradients. To alleviate the difficulty of training, we propose two extensions: recursive-supervision and skip-connection. Our method significantly outperforms previous methods.
label: AI

title: Solving Jigsaw Puzzles with Linear Programming
Abstract: This paper presents a novel Linear Program (LP) based formulation for solving jigsaw puzzles. We frame jigsaw solving as a series of successive global convex relaxations of the standard NP-hard formulation, which can describe both jigsaws with pieces of unknown position and puzzles with unknown position and orientation. The primary contribution and strength of our approach lies in the LP assembly strategy. Unlike existing greedy methods, our LP solver exploits all pairwise matches simultaneously and computes the position of each piece/component globally.  The main advantages of our LP approach include: (i) reduced sensitivity to local minima compared to greedy approaches, as our successive approximations are global and convex, and (ii) increased robustness to the presence of mismatches in the pairwise matches due to the use of a weighted L1 penalty. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we test our algorithm on public jigsaw datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Transductive Zero-Shot Action Recognition by Word-Vector Embedding
Abstract: The number of categories for action recognition is growing rapidly, making it increasingly difficult to label sufficient training data for learning conventional models for all categories. Instead of collecting and exhaustively labeling ever-increasing data, a compelling alternative approach is zero-shot learning (ZSL).  To this end, this study constructs a mapping between visual features and a semantic descriptor of each action category, enabling the recognition of new categories without any visual training data. Existing ZSL studies primarily focus on still images and attribute-based semantic representations. In this work, we explore word-vectors as the shared semantic space to embed videos and category labels for ZSL action recognition. This is a more challenging problem than existing ZSL of still images and/or attributes, as the mapping between video spacetime features of actions and the semantic space is more complex and harder to learn for the purpose of generalizing across any cross-category domain shift. To address this generalization problem in ZSL action recognition, we investigate a series of synergistic strategies to improve upon the standard ZSL pipeline. Most of these strategies are transductive in nature, meaning they have access to testing data during the training phase.
label: AI

title: Robust Face Alignment Using a Mixture of Invariant Experts
Abstract: Face alignment, the task of identifying the locations of a set of facial landmark points in an image of a face, is crucial for numerous applications.  Face alignment presents particular challenges when there are large variations in pose (in-plane and out-of-plane rotations) and facial expression. To address this, we propose a cascade where each stage consists of a mixture of regression experts. Each expert learns a customized regression model specialized for a different subset of the joint space of pose and expressions. The system is invariant to a predefined class of transformations (e.g., affine) because the input is transformed to match each expert's prototype shape before regression is applied. We also introduce a method to incorporate deformation constraints within the discriminative alignment framework, enhancing the robustness of our algorithm. Our algorithm significantly outperforms previous methods on publicly available face alignment datasets.
label: AI

title: Symbol Grounding Association in Multimodal Sequences with Missing Elements
Abstract: This paper extends a symbolic association framework to handle missing elements in multimodal sequences. The broader scope of this work is the symbolic associations of object-word mappings, as they occur during language development in infants. In other words, two different representations of the same abstract concept can associate in both directions. This scenario has long been of interest to researchers in Artificial Intelligence, Psychology, and Neuroscience. This work expands a recent approach for multimodal sequences (visual and audio) to also address missing elements in one or both modalities. Our method uses two parallel Long Short-Term Memories (LSTMs) with a learning rule based on the EM algorithm. It aligns both LSTM outputs via Dynamic Time Warping (DTW). We propose an extra step for combination with the max operation to exploit common elements between both sequences. The rationale behind this is that the combination acts as a condition selector for choosing the best representation from both LSTMs.  We evaluated the proposed extension in the following scenarios: missing elements in one modality (visual or audio) and missing elements in both modalities (visual and sound). The performance of our extension achieves better results than the original model and similar results to individual LSTMs trained in each modality.
label: AI

title: Similarity-based Text Recognition by Deeply Supervised Siamese Network
Abstract: This paper introduces a new text recognition model based on measuring the visual similarity of text and predicting the content of unlabeled texts. First, a Siamese convolutional network is trained with deep supervision on a labeled training dataset. This network projects texts onto a similarity manifold. The Deeply Supervised Siamese network learns the visual similarity of texts. Then, a K-nearest neighbor classifier is used to predict unlabeled text based on the similarity distance to labeled texts. The model's performance is evaluated on three combined datasets of machine-print and handwritten text. We demonstrate that the model reduces the cost of human estimation by 50%-85%. The system's error is less than 0.5%. The proposed model surpasses conventional Siamese networks by identifying visually similar barely-readable and readable text, such as machine-printed and handwritten text, due to deep supervision. The results also show that the predicted labels are sometimes better than human labels, e.g., spelling correction. |||
label: AI

title: Deep Reflectance Maps
Abstract: Reconstructing an object's intrinsic properties, such as its shape, material, and illumination, from its image is a challenging problem due to its ill-posed nature. While significant progress has been made in inferring these properties from images alone, progress in an unconstrained setting remains limited. This paper presents a convolutional neural network architecture for estimating reflectance maps of specular materials under natural lighting conditions. The proposed architecture learns to directly predict a reflectance map from the image itself in an end-to-end fashion. The authors introduce an indirect scheme that first predicts surface orientation and then estimates the reflectance map using sparse data interpolation. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a new challenge called Specular MAterials on SHapes with complex IllumiNation (SMASHINg) using both synthetic and real images. The authors show that the proposed method can be applied to various image-based editing tasks on real images.
label: AI

title: Learning Dense Convolutional Embeddings for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: This paper presents a novel deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) architecture for learning pixel embeddings. The learned embeddings allow the network to infer whether two pixels belong to the same region based on their pairwise distances. Embeddings of pixels belonging to the same object are trained to be similar, while embeddings of pixels from different objects are trained to be dissimilar. Experimental results demonstrate that integrating this embedding network with a DCNN trained for semantic segmentation leads to significant improvements in per-pixel classification accuracy. These contributions are implemented as straightforward modifications to convolution routines in the popular Caffe deep learning framework, making them readily applicable to any task involving convolution layers.
label: AI

title: Standard methods for inexpensive pollen loads authentication by means of computer vision and machine learning
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for authenticating local bee pollen samples against fraudulent ones using image processing and machine learning techniques. The proposed approach does not require expensive equipment like advanced microscopes and can be used for preliminary fast rejection of unknown pollen types. The system efficiently rejects non-local pollen samples using inexpensive hardware, eliminating the need to send samples to a laboratory. The methods are based on color properties of bee pollen load images and the use of one-class classifiers, which are suitable for rejecting unknown pollen samples when limited data is available. The validation of the method is conducted by authenticating Spanish bee pollen types. Experimental results show that the proposed methods achieve an overall authentication accuracy of 94%. The paper concludes by illustrating user interaction with the developed application prototype through practical case studies.
label: AI

title: Learning to Assign Orientations to Feature Points
Abstract: This paper proposes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for assigning a canonical orientation to feature points based on image patches centered on those points. This method improves feature point matching compared to current state-of-the-art techniques and can be used in conjunction with any existing rotation-sensitive descriptors. To avoid the challenging task of manually defining a target orientation for training, the authors propose using Siamese networks, which implicitly learn the optimal orientations during training. They also introduce a novel activation function for neural networks that generalizes popular ReLU, maxout, and PReLU functions and performs better for this specific task. The effectiveness of the proposed method is extensively validated using four existing datasets, including two non-planar datasets and a dataset created by the authors. The results demonstrate that the method outperforms the state-of-the-art without requiring retraining for each dataset.
label: AI

title: Volume-based Semantic Labeling with Signed Distance Functions
Abstract: This paper bridges the gap between semantic segmentation and SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) by introducing a category label fusion technique. This technique enables the embedding of semantic information into dense maps created by volume-based SLAM algorithms like KinectFusion. The proposed approach is the first to provide semantically labeled dense reconstruction of the environment from a stream of RGB-D images. The effectiveness of the approach is validated using a publicly available semantically annotated RGB-D dataset. The validation is conducted using three different scenarios: employing ground truth labels, introducing synthetic noise to the annotations, and using a state-of-the-art semantic segmentation algorithm based on convolutional neural networks.
label: AI

title: An Adaptive Data Representation for Robust Point-Set Registration and Merging
Abstract: This paper presents a framework for rigid point-set registration and merging using a robust continuous data representation. The point-set representation is constructed by training a one-class support vector machine with a Gaussian radial basis function kernel and subsequently approximating the output function with a Gaussian mixture model. The framework leverages the representation's sparse parametrization and robustness to noise, outliers, and occlusions for efficient registration. The algorithm minimizes the L2 distance between support vector-parametrized Gaussian mixtures. In contrast to existing techniques like Iterative Closest Point and Gaussian mixture approaches, this method exhibits a wider region of convergence and is more robust to occlusions and missing data, as demonstrated through evaluation on various 2D and 3D datasets. The paper also presents a novel algorithm, GMMerge, for parsimoniously and equitably merging aligned mixture models, enabling the framework to be used for reconstruction and mapping.
label: AI

title: Spatial frequency processing in the central and peripheral visual field during scene viewing
Abstract: Visuospatial attention and gaze control rely on the interaction of foveal and peripheral visual processing. The foveal and peripheral regions of the visual field are differentially sensitive to different spatial frequency ranges. This paper investigates how selectively attenuating spatial frequencies in the central or peripheral visual field affects eye-movement behavior during real-world scene viewing. Two experiments were conducted using gaze-contingent low-pass or high-pass filters with varying filter levels (cutoff frequencies) or filter sizes. Compared to unfiltered control conditions, mean fixation durations increased most significantly with central high-pass and peripheral low-pass filtering. Increasing filter size prolonged fixation durations with peripheral filtering but not with central filtering. Increasing filter level prolonged fixation durations with low-pass filtering but not with high-pass filtering. These findings suggest that fixation durations are not always longer under conditions of increased processing difficulty. Saccade amplitudes largely adapted to processing difficulty, increasing with central filtering and decreasing with peripheral filtering. These effects were amplified with increasing filter size and filter level. Additionally, the study observed a trade-off between saccade timing and saccadic selection, as saccade amplitudes were modulated when fixation durations were unaffected by experimental manipulations. The authors conclude that interactions between perception and gaze control are highly sensitive to manipulations of input images, as long as residual information remains accessible for gaze control.
label: AI

title: Structure Inference Machines: Recurrent Neural Networks for Analyzing Relations in Group Activity Recognition
Abstract: Rich semantic relations are crucial for a variety of visual recognition problems, such as group activity recognition, which involves analyzing interactions and spatial relationships between people in a scene. While state-of-the-art recognition methods often rely on deep learning approaches for training complex classifiers to interpret images, bridging the gap between low-level concepts output by these methods and higher-level compositional scene understanding remains a challenge. Graphical models are a standard tool for addressing this challenge. This paper proposes a method to integrate graphical models and deep neural networks into a joint framework. Instead of using traditional inference methods, the authors use a sequential inference approach modeled by a recurrent neural network. Furthermore, the appropriate structure for inference is learned by imposing gates on edges between nodes. Empirical results on group activity recognition demonstrate the potential of this model to handle highly structured learning tasks.
label: AI

title: DISC: Deep Image Saliency Computing via Progressive Representation Learning
Abstract: Salient object detection has become increasingly important as a component or step in several pattern recognition and image processing tasks. While numerous powerful saliency models have been proposed, they often involve extensive feature (or model) engineering based on prior assumptions about the properties of objects and backgrounds. Inspired by the effectiveness of recent feature learning techniques, this paper presents a novel Deep Image Saliency Computing (DISC) framework for fine-grained image saliency computing. The DISC framework models image saliency from both coarse- and fine-level observations and utilizes deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn the saliency representation progressively. Specifically, the saliency model consists of two stacked CNNs. The first CNN generates a coarse-level saliency map based on the entire image as input, roughly identifying salient regions in the global context. The first CNN also integrates superpixel-based local context information to refine the coarse-level saliency map. Guided by this coarse saliency map, the second CNN focuses on local context to produce a fine-grained and accurate saliency map while preserving object details. For a test image, the two CNNs collaboratively perform saliency computing in one shot. The DISC framework effectively highlights objects of interest from complex backgrounds while preserving object details. Extensive experiments on several standard benchmarks demonstrate that DISC outperforms other state-of-the-art methods and generalizes well across datasets without additional training. The executable version of DISC is available online at: http://vision.sysu.edu.cn/projects/DISC.
label: AI

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning for Optical Character Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes an end-to-end recurrent encoder-decoder based sequence learning approach for printed text Optical Character Recognition (OCR). Unlike existing state-of-the-art OCR solutions that use connectionist temporal classification (CTC) output layers, the proposed approach makes minimal assumptions about the structure and length of the sequence. The two-step encoder-decoder approach first uses a recurrent encoder to read a variable-length printed text word image and encode it into a fixed-dimensional embedding. This fixed-dimensional embedding is then processed by the decoder structure, which converts it into a variable-length text output. The architecture achieves competitive performance compared to CTC output layers while operating in more natural settings. The learned deep word image embedding from the encoder can be used for printed text-based retrieval systems. The expressive fixed-dimensional embedding for any variable-length input makes retrieval tasks more efficient, which is not possible with other recurrent neural network architectures. The paper empirically investigates the expressiveness and learnability of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs) in the sequence-to-sequence learning regime by training the network for prediction tasks in segmentation-free printed text OCR. The utility of the proposed architecture for printed text is demonstrated through quantitative and qualitative evaluation of two tasks: word prediction and retrieval.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Learning of Edges
Abstract: Data-driven approaches for edge detection have proven effective and achieve top results on modern benchmarks. However, all current data-driven edge detectors require manual supervision for training, typically in the form of hand-labeled region segments or object boundaries. Human annotators mark semantically meaningful edges, which are then used for training. This paper investigates whether this form of strong, high-level supervision is truly necessary to learn accurate edge detection. The authors present a simple yet effective approach for training edge detectors without human supervision, utilizing motion and noisy semi-dense matches between frames. The method starts with rudimentary knowledge of edges (in the form of image gradients) and iteratively refines motion estimation and edge detection. Using a large corpus of video data, the authors demonstrate that edge detectors trained using this unsupervised scheme approach the performance of the same methods trained with full supervision (within 3-5%). They also show that using a deep network for the edge detector, this approach provides a novel pre-training scheme for object detection.
label: AI

title: Natural Language Object Retrieval
Abstract: This paper addresses the task of natural language object retrieval, which involves localizing a target object within a given image based on a natural language query. Natural language object retrieval differs from text-based image retrieval in that it incorporates spatial information about objects within the scene and global scene context. To address this challenge, the authors propose a novel Spatial Context Recurrent ConvNet (SCRC) model as a scoring function for candidate boxes in object retrieval. The SCRC model integrates spatial configurations and global scene-level contextual information into the network. The model processes query text, local image descriptors, spatial configurations, and global context features through a recurrent network. It outputs the probability of the query text conditioned on each candidate box as a score for the box, and can transfer visual-linguistic knowledge from the image captioning domain to this task. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively utilizes both local and global information, significantly outperforming previous baseline methods on different datasets and scenarios. The method can also leverage large-scale vision and language datasets for knowledge transfer.
label: AI

title: Adaptive Affinity Matrix for Unsupervised Metric Learning
Abstract: Spectral clustering is a popular clustering approach capable of handling challenging clustering problems. Most spectral clustering methods provide a nonlinear map from the data manifold to a subspace. However, only a limited amount of research focuses on explicit linear maps, which can be viewed as unsupervised distance metric learning. The selection of the affinity matrix significantly impacts unsupervised learning. While affinity learning has achieved considerable success in recent years, issues like noise reduction remain to be addressed. This paper proposes a novel method, dubbed Adaptive Affinity Matrix (AdaAM), to learn an adaptive affinity matrix and derive a distance metric from the affinity. The AdaAM assumes the affinity matrix to be positive semidefinite, capable of quantifying pairwise dissimilarity. The method optimizes the objective function as a spectral decomposition problem. The affinity matrix is derived from both the original data distribution and the widely-used heat kernel, providing an optimal representation of pairwise relationships on the manifold. Extensive experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of AdaAM.
label: AI

title: Deep Mean Maps
Abstract: The use of distributions and high-level features from deep architectures has become prevalent in modern computer vision. Both methodologies have achieved significant success in many computer vision tasks. However, there has been limited research on leveraging the power of these two methodologies jointly. This paper presents the Deep Mean Maps (DMMs) framework, a novel family of methods for non-parametrically representing distributions of features in convolutional neural network models. DMMs enable both classification of images using the distribution of top-level features and tuning of these features for performing this task. The paper shows how to implement DMMs using a special mean map layer composed of typical CNN operations, simplifying both forward and backward propagation. The efficacy of DMMs in analyzing distributional patterns in image data is illustrated through a synthetic data experiment. The paper also demonstrates that extending existing deep architectures with DMMs improves the performance of existing CNNs on several challenging real-world datasets.
label: AI

title: UA-DETRAC: A New Benchmark and Protocol for Multi-Object Detection and Tracking
Abstract: Recent years have witnessed the development of numerous effective multi-object tracking (MOT) methods due to their wide range of applications. Existing performance evaluations of MOT methods typically separate the object tracking step from the object detection step by using the same fixed object detection results for comparisons. This paper conducts a comprehensive quantitative study on the effects of object detection accuracy on overall MOT performance using the new large-scale University at Albany DETection and tRACking (UA-DETRAC) benchmark dataset. The UA-DETRAC dataset comprises 100 challenging video sequences captured from real-world traffic scenes (over 140,000 frames with rich annotations, including occlusion, weather, vehicle category, truncation, and vehicle bounding boxes) for object detection, object tracking, and MOT system evaluation. The authors evaluate complete MOT systems constructed from combinations of state-of-the-art object detection and object tracking methods. Their analysis reveals the complex effects of object detection accuracy on MOT system performance. Based on these observations, the paper proposes new evaluation tools and metrics for MOT systems that consider both object detection and object tracking for comprehensive analysis.
label: AI

title: Action Recognition using Visual Attention
Abstract: This paper proposes a soft attention-based model for action recognition in videos. The model utilizes multi-layered Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units, which are deep both spatially and temporally. The model learns to focus selectively on parts of video frames and classifies videos after taking a few glimpses. Essentially, the model learns which parts of the frames are relevant to the task at hand and assigns higher importance to them. The model is evaluated on the UCF-11 (YouTube Action), HMDB-51, and Hollywood2 datasets. The authors analyze how the model focuses its attention depending on the scene and the action being performed.
label: AI

title: Going Deeper in Facial Expression Recognition using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Automated Facial Expression Recognition (FER) remains a challenging and interesting problem. Despite efforts in developing various methods for FER, existing approaches traditionally lack generalizability when applied to unseen images or images captured in wild settings. Most existing approaches rely on engineered features (e.g., HOG, LBPH, and Gabor), where the classifier's hyperparameters are tuned to achieve optimal recognition accuracies across a single database or a small collection of similar databases. However, the results are not significant when applied to novel data. This paper proposes a deep neural network architecture to address the FER problem across multiple well-known standard face datasets. Specifically, the network consists of two convolutional layers, each followed by max pooling, and then four Inception layers. The network is a single-component architecture that takes registered facial images as input and classifies them into one of the six basic expressions or the neutral expression. The authors conducted comprehensive experiments on seven publicly available facial expression databases, namely MultiPIE, MMI, CK+, DISFA, FERA, SFEW, and FER2013. The results of the proposed architecture are comparable to or better than state-of-the-art methods and outperform traditional convolutional neural networks in both accuracy and training time.
label: AI

title: Basic Level Categorization Facilitates Visual Object Recognition
Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have led to significant progress in computer vision, especially for visual object recognition tasks. Feed-forward deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) automatically learn features useful for object classification, and these features have been shown to predict and decode neural representations in the ventral visual pathway of humans and monkeys. However, despite extensive research on optimizing CNNs, there has been limited research on linking CNNs with guiding principles from the human visual cortex. This paper proposes a network optimization strategy inspired by the developmental trajectory of children's visual object recognition capabilities and Bar (2003), who hypothesized that basic level information is carried in the fast magnocellular pathway through the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and then projected back to inferior temporal cortex (IT), where subordinate level categorization is achieved. The authors instantiate this idea by training a deep CNN to perform basic level object categorization first and then train it on subordinate level categorization. This idea is applied to training AlexNet (Krizhevsky et al., 2012) on the ILSVRC 2012 dataset, resulting in a top-5 accuracy increase from 80.13% to 82.14%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the method. The paper also shows that subsequent transfer learning on smaller datasets yields superior results.
label: AI

title: Deep Gaussian Conditional Random Field Network: A Model-based Deep Network for Discriminative Denoising
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep network architecture for image denoising based on a Gaussian Conditional Random Field (GCRF) model. Unlike existing discriminative denoising methods that train a separate model for each noise level, the proposed deep network explicitly models the input noise variance, making it capable of handling a range of noise levels. The deep network, referred to as the deep GCRF network, consists of two sub-networks: (i) a parameter generation network that generates pairwise potential parameters based on the noisy input image, and (ii) an inference network whose layers perform computations involved in an iterative GCRF inference procedure. The entire deep GCRF network (both parameter generation and inference networks) is trained discriminatively in an end-to-end fashion by maximizing the peak signal-to-noise ratio measure. Experiments on Berkeley segmentation and PASCAL VOC datasets show that the proposed deep GCRF network outperforms state-of-the-art image denoising approaches for various noise levels.
label: AI

title: Efficient non-greedy optimization of decision trees
Abstract: Decision trees and randomized forests are widely used in computer vision and machine learning. Standard algorithms for decision tree induction optimize split functions one node at a time using specific splitting criteria. This greedy procedure often leads to suboptimal trees. This paper presents an algorithm for optimizing split functions at all levels of the tree jointly with leaf parameters, based on a global objective. The authors show that finding optimal linear-combination (oblique) splits for decision trees is related to structured prediction with latent variables and formulate a convex-concave upper bound on the tree's empirical loss. The runtime for computing the gradient of the proposed surrogate objective with respect to each training exemplar is quadratic in the tree depth, making training deep trees feasible. Using stochastic gradient descent for optimization enables effective training with large datasets. Experiments on various classification benchmarks demonstrate that the resulting non-greedy decision trees outperform greedy decision tree baselines. |||
label: AI

title: Newtonian Image Understanding: Unfolding the Dynamics of Objects in Static Images
Abstract: This paper explores the challenging task of predicting the motion of objects in static images. The goal is to understand the object's behavior by inferring the forces acting on it and its long-term movement as a response to those forces. Directly estimating these forces and motions from a single image is a difficult problem. This work introduces Newtonian scenarios as an intermediary abstraction and proposes a Newtonian Neural Network ($N^3$) that maps a single image to a state within this scenario. Experimental results demonstrate the method's ability to reliably predict object dynamics from static images, providing insights into the predicted motion through velocity and force vectors. To foster further research, a new dataset called Visual Newtonian Dynamics (VIND) is introduced, consisting of 6806 videos and 4516 images, aligned with Newtonian scenarios and annotated with ground truth dynamics.
label: AI

title: Facial Landmark Detection with Tweaked Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: We introduce a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) design for facial landmark coordinate regression. By analyzing the intermediate features of a standard CNN trained for landmark detection, we observe that features extracted from later, more specialized layers capture rough landmark locations. This insight allows us to apply differential processing midway through the network, tailoring the processing based on facial alignment. The resulting Tweaked CNN model (TCNN) leverages the robustness of CNNs for landmark detection in an appearance-sensitive manner, without requiring multi-part or multi-scale models. Our results on standard face landmark detection and face verification benchmarks demonstrate that TCNN significantly outperforms previous approaches.
label: AI

title: Multimodal Skip-gram Using Convolutional Pseudowords
Abstract: This paper investigates the representational mapping across multimodal data, aiming to generate the semantic description of data in one modality from its raw representation in another modality. This mapping has broad applications, including image/video retrieval, object recognition, action/behavior recognition, and event understanding. To facilitate this mapping, we propose a simplified training objective for learning multimodal embeddings using the skip-gram architecture, introducing convolutional "pseudowords." These embeddings are formed by combining distributed word representations and image features from convolutional neural networks, projected into a shared multimodal space. We present extensive results on various word similarity benchmarks showcasing the promising representational properties of these embeddings.
label: AI

title: Human Curation and Convnets: Powering Item-to-Item Recommendations on Pinterest
Abstract: This paper introduces Pinterest Related Pins, an item-to-item recommendation system that integrates collaborative filtering with content-based ranking. We demonstrate the effectiveness of leveraging signals from user curation, the process of users organizing content, in conjunction with content-based ranking. Additionally, we show the efficacy of using visual features, such as image or object representations learned from convolutional neural networks, in enhancing user engagement in our recommendation system.
label: AI

title: LLNet: A Deep Autoencoder Approach to Natural Low-light Image Enhancement
Abstract: In surveillance, monitoring, and tactical reconnaissance, obtaining relevant visual information from dynamic environments and effectively processing such data are crucial for informed decision-making, which ultimately determines the success of operations. Camera sensors often face limitations in capturing clear images or videos without defects, especially in low-light environments. Many applications aim to enhance the brightness, contrast, and reduce noise in such images in real-time. This paper proposes a deep autoencoder-based approach to identify signal features from low-light images and adaptively brighten them without over-amplifying lighter areas, avoiding pixel saturation. We demonstrate that a variant of the stacked-sparse denoising autoencoder can learn to adaptively enhance and denoise images from synthetically darkened and noisy training data. This trained network can be effectively applied to naturally low-light environments and hardware-degraded images. Results showcase the significant credibility of deep learning-based approaches both visually and quantitatively compared to existing enhancing, denoising, and hybrid techniques.
label: AI

title: Automatic Inference of the Quantile Parameter
Abstract: Supervised learning is a prominent research area with diverse applications, including data analytics, computer vision, speech and audio processing, and image understanding. Most machine learning loss functions assume symmetric noise models and focus on estimating unknown function parameters. However, loss functions like quantile and quantile Huber generalize the symmetric $\\ell_1$ and Huber losses to the asymmetric setting, for a fixed quantile parameter. This paper proposes a method for jointly inferring both the quantile parameter and the unknown function parameters for the asymmetric quantile Huber and quantile losses. We investigate properties of the quantile Huber loss and implement a convexity certificate to check convexity in the quantile parameter. We prove that, when the loss is convex with respect to the function parameter, it is biconvex in both function and quantile parameters. We propose an algorithm for jointly estimating these parameters. Results with synthetic and real data demonstrate the approach's ability to automatically recover the quantile parameter corresponding to the noise while improving the recovery of function parameters. We extend gradient boosting machines with quantile losses to automatically estimate the quantile parameter at each iteration, highlighting the framework's potential.
label: AI

title: Representational Distance Learning for Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) offer valuable models of visual representational transformations. This paper introduces a method that allows a DNN (student) to learn from the internal representational spaces of a reference model (teacher), which can be another DNN or, potentially, a biological brain. The representational spaces of the student and teacher are characterized by representational distance matrices (RDMs). We propose representational distance learning (RDL), a stochastic gradient descent method that aims to make the student's RDMs approximate those of the teacher. We demonstrate that RDL is competitive with other transfer learning techniques on two benchmark datasets (MNIST and CIFAR-100), while allowing for architectural differences between student and teacher. By aligning the student's RDMs to those of the teacher, RDL significantly improves visual classification performance compared to baseline networks that do not use transfer learning. RDL could potentially enable combined supervised training of deep neural networks using task constraints (e.g., images and category labels) and constraints from brain-activity measurements, leading to models that replicate the internal representational spaces of biological brains.
label: AI

title: Learning Human Identity from Motion Patterns
Abstract: This paper presents a large-scale study investigating the ability of temporal deep neural networks to interpret natural human kinematics and introduces the first method for active biometric authentication using mobile inertial sensors. We have created a unique dataset of human movements collected passively from 1500 volunteers using their smartphones over several months. We compare various neural architectures for efficient learning of temporal multimodal data representations, propose an optimized shift-invariant dense convolutional mechanism (DCWRNN), and incorporate the discriminatively-trained dynamic features into a probabilistic generative framework that accounts for temporal characteristics. Our results demonstrate that human kinematics provide valuable information about user identity and can be integrated into multi-modal authentication systems.
label: AI

title: Sequential estimation of intrinsic activity and synaptic input in single neurons by particle filtering with optimal importance density
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of inferring the signals and parameters that cause neural activity. While the ultimate goal is to unravel the brain's connectivity, we focus on a microscopic view, studying single neurons potentially connected to a network of peers. The only available observations are noisy, sampled voltage traces obtained from intracellular recordings. We design algorithms and inference methods using stochastic filtering, enabling probabilistic interpretation and treatment of the problem. Using particle filtering, we reconstruct voltage traces and estimate the time course of auxiliary variables. By extending the algorithm through PMCMC methodology, we can estimate hidden physiological parameters, such as intrinsic conductances or reversal potentials. Finally, the method is applied to estimate synaptic conductances arriving at a target cell, reconstructing the synaptic excitatory/inhibitory input traces. Notably, these estimations achieve near-optimal performance even in spiking regimes.
label: AI

title: Feature Learning based Deep Supervised Hashing with Pairwise Labels
Abstract: Hashing has found widespread application in large-scale image retrieval in recent years. However, most existing hashing methods rely on hand-crafted features, which may not be optimally compatible with the hashing procedure. Deep hashing methods have emerged, enabling simultaneous feature learning and hash-code learning with deep neural networks, resulting in better performance than traditional methods using hand-crafted features. Most of these deep hashing methods are supervised, requiring triplet labels. For applications with pairwise labels, there have been no methods for simultaneous feature learning and hash-code learning. This paper proposes a novel deep hashing method called deep pairwise-supervised hashing (DPSH), which performs simultaneous feature learning and hash-code learning for applications with pairwise labels. Experiments on real datasets show that DPSH outperforms other methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance in image retrieval applications.
label: AI

title: When Naïve Bayes Nearest Neighbours Meet Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Since convolutional neural networks (CNNs) became the dominant learning paradigm in visual recognition, Naive Bayes Nearest Neighbour (NBNN)-based classifiers have lost prominence. This is primarily because (1) such algorithms cannot directly use CNN activations as input features; (2) they cannot be used as the final layer of CNN architectures for end-to-end training; and (3) they are generally not scalable and struggle with large datasets. This paper proposes a framework addressing all these limitations, bringing NBNNs back to the forefront. We solve the first issue by extracting CNN activations from local patches at multiple scale levels. We address the second and third issues simultaneously by proposing a scalable version of Naive Bayes Non-linear Learning (NBNL). Results obtained using pre-trained CNNs on standard scene and domain adaptation databases demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, opening new possibilities for NBNNs.
label: AI

title: Hand-Object Interaction and Precise Localization in Transitive Action Recognition
Abstract: Action recognition in still images has seen significant progress due to advancements in human pose estimation, object recognition, and stronger feature representations produced by deep neural networks. However, performance remains far from human capabilities in many cases. A major challenge lies in distinguishing between transitive actions where the overall actor pose is similar, requiring the recognition to rely on details of the grasp and object, which may be largely occluded. This paper demonstrates how recognition is improved by precisely localizing the action-object and extracting details of the object shape along with the actor-object interaction. To achieve this precise localization, we employ a coarse-to-fine approach that combines semantic segmentation and contextual features in successive stages. We focus on face-related actions, a set of actions that includes several currently challenging categories. Our approach shows an average relative improvement of 35% over the state-of-the-art and experimentally validates its effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Towards Vision-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Motion Control
Abstract: This paper introduces a machine learning-based system for controlling a robotic manipulator using only visual perception. For the first time, we demonstrate the ability to autonomously learn robot controllers solely from raw-pixel images without any prior knowledge of configuration. Building upon the success of recent deep reinforcement learning, we develop a system for learning target reaching with a three-joint robot manipulator using external visual observation. A Deep Q Network (DQN) successfully learned target reaching after training in simulation. While transferring the network to real hardware and real observation in a naive approach failed, experiments show that the network works when replacing camera images with synthetic images.
label: AI

title: ProNet: Learning to Propose Object-specific Boxes for Cascaded Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper aims to classify and locate objects accurately and efficiently without using bounding box annotations. This task is challenging as objects in the wild can appear at arbitrary locations and scales. We propose a novel classification architecture called ProNet, based on convolutional neural networks. It utilizes computationally efficient neural networks to propose image regions likely to contain objects and applies more powerful but slower networks on these proposed regions. The core building block is a multi-scale fully-convolutional network that assigns object confidence scores to boxes at different locations and scales. We show that these networks can be effectively trained using image-level annotations and can be connected into cascades or trees for efficient object classification. ProNet significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO datasets for object classification and point-based localization.
label: AI

title: Shearlet-Based Detection of Flame Fronts
Abstract: Identifying and characterizing flame fronts is a common task in computer-assisted analysis of data obtained from imaging techniques like planar laser-induced fluorescence (PLIF), laser Rayleigh scattering (LRS), or particle imaging velocimetry (PIV). This paper presents a novel edge and ridge (line) detection algorithm based on complex-valued wavelet-like analyzing functions, called complex shearlets, exhibiting several traits useful for flame front extraction. In addition to providing a unified approach for edge and ridge detection, our method inherently yields estimates of local tangent orientations and local curvatures. To assess its applicability for high-frequency recordings of combustion processes, the algorithm is applied to mock images with varying noise levels and real-world PLIF images of both OH and CH radicals. We compare the performance of the new complex shearlet-based measure to established edge and ridge detection techniques, including the Canny edge detector, another shearlet-based edge detector, and the phase congruency measure.
label: AI

title: Automatic Content-Aware Color and Tone Stylization
Abstract: This paper introduces a new technique for automatically generating diverse and visually compelling stylizations for a photograph in an unsupervised manner.
