title: Incorporating Knowledge into Structural Equation Models using Auxiliary Variables
Abstract: This paper extends graph-based identification methods by incorporating background knowledge in the form of non-zero parameter values. Such information could be obtained from prior randomized experiments, domain expertise, or even other identification techniques. To systematically incorporate this knowledge, the paper proposes the addition of auxiliary variables to the model, designed to cancel specific paths. This cancellation enables auxiliary variables to enhance conventional identification methods (e.g., single-door criterion, instrumental variables, half-trek criterion) and model testing (e.g., d-separation, over-identification). Moreover, the paper proposes an iterative approach involving alternating identification steps and adding auxiliary variables to improve the power of existing identification methods without requiring external knowledge. This method is operationalized for simple instrumental sets, a generalization of instrumental variables, and shown to identify at least as many models as the most general identification method for linear systems known to date. The paper further discusses the application of auxiliary variables to model testing and z-identification. |||

title: Traffic Sign Classification Using Deep Inception Based Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This work introduces a novel deep network for traffic sign classification that surpasses previous methods in performance on the GTSRB dataset. The network incorporates spatial transformer layers and a modified inception module designed to capture both local and global features, enabling precise classification even with deformed samples. Spatial transformer layers enhance the network's robustness to image transformations such as translation, rotation, and scaling. Unlike existing approaches relying on hand-crafted features, large parameter deep networks, and data augmentations, this method addresses the challenges of parameter explosion and data augmentation. It achieves state-of-the-art performance of 99.81% on the GTSRB dataset.

title: Detecting events and key actors in multi-person videos
Abstract: Multi-person event recognition in videos is a challenging task, especially when numerous individuals are present but only a subset contributes to the event. This paper proposes a model that learns to detect events while automatically attending to the responsible individuals, without requiring explicit annotations during training or testing. The model tracks people in videos and utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to represent track features. Time-varying attention weights are learned to combine these features at each time instant. The attended features are then processed using another RNN for event detection/classification. To address the limited size of video datasets with multiple people, a new basketball dataset comprising 257 games with 14K event annotations for 11 classes was collected. The model outperforms state-of-the-art methods for event classification and detection on this dataset. Additionally, the attention mechanism consistently localizes relevant players.

title: Spectral-Spatial Classification of Hyperspectral Image Using Autoencoders
Abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is a critical area in remote sensing. This paper presents a new framework for spectral-spatial feature extraction in HSI classification, introducing deep learning for the first time. The framework leverages the autoencoder model for feature extraction. The eligibility of autoencoders is verified by applying them to classical spectral information-based classification with varying depths. The framework then combines principal component analysis (PCA) on the spectral dimension with autoencoders on the spatial dimensions to extract spectral-spatial information for classification. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework achieves the highest classification accuracy among various methods, outperforming classical classifiers such as SVM and PCA-based SVM.

title: A disembodied developmental robotic agent called Samu Bátfai
Abstract: Samu, an experimental disembodied DevRob chatterbot, aims to engage in natural language conversations like humans. A key design feature is its interaction through a character terminal, crucial for both practical aspects like the Turing test and the study of fundamental principles in Developmental Robotics. This paper outlines the early development stages of a Q-learning prototype for Samu, using neural network approximators. Samu's initial task is to predict the next sentence in tales or conversations. The objective is to achieve results comparable to those obtained using classical Q lookup tables on small input samples, but with general function approximators. An experiment demonstrates significant improvement in Samu's learning when using LZW tree to reduce the number of possible Q-actions.

title: Visual Language Modeling on CNN Image Representations
Abstract: Measuring the naturalness of images is vital for generating realistic images and detecting unnatural regions. Naturalness evaluation can complement Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based features, which are known to be insensitive to naturalness. However, existing probabilistic image models struggle to capture the complex and abstract nature of perceived naturalness due to their reliance on raw pixels. This work proposes a novel method to evaluate naturalness based on the predictability of high-level features during eye movement. A variant of Recurrent Neural Network Language Models is built on pre-trained CNN representations to evaluate naturalness. The method is applied to two tasks: 1) generating more understandable images from image features using the method as a regularizer, and 2) producing unnaturalness maps that achieve state-of-the-art eye fixation prediction performance on well-studied datasets.

title: Enacting textual entailment and ontologies for automated essay grading in chemical domain
Abstract: This paper presents a system for automated essay grading using ontologies and textual entailment. Hypothesis extraction from a domain ontology guides the textual entailment process, which checks whether a hypothesis' truth follows from a given text. Textual entailment compares student answers to a model answer derived from the ontology. The solution is validated against various essays written by students in the chemistry domain.

title: An Efficient Multilinear Optimization Framework for Hypergraph Matching
Abstract: Hypergraph matching has emerged as a popular approach for solving correspondence problems in computer vision, allowing the integration of higher-order geometric information. Hypergraph matching can be formulated as a third-order optimization problem with assignment constraints, which is NP-hard. Previous work proposed an algorithm that lifts the third-order problem to a fourth-order problem, solving it through optimization of the corresponding multilinear form. This results in a tensor block coordinate ascent scheme that guarantees monotonic ascent in the original matching score function and achieves state-of-the-art performance in both matching score and accuracy. This paper demonstrates that the lifting step can be avoided, leading to a third-order scheme with the same guarantees and performance but twice as fast. Additionally, a homotopy type method is introduced to further improve performance.

title: Decomposition Bounds for Marginal MAP
Abstract: Marginal MAP inference involves making MAP predictions in systems with latent variables or missing information. It poses significant challenges compared to pure marginalization and MAP tasks, for which efficient and convergent variational algorithms exist, such as dual decomposition. This work generalizes dual decomposition to a generic power sum inference task, encompassing marginal MAP, pure marginalization, and MAP as special cases. The method is based on a block coordinate descent algorithm on a new convex decomposition bound, guaranteeing monotonic convergence and efficient parallelization. The approach is demonstrated on marginal MAP queries defined on real-world problems from the UAI approximate inference challenge, showing its superiority in speed and reliability over previous methods.

title: A fuzzy based conceptual framework for career counselling
Abstract: Career guidance for students, particularly in rural areas of India, presents a significant challenge. In the digital age, there is a need for an automated system that can analyze a student's capabilities, suggest suitable careers, and provide related information. This paper proposes a fuzzy-based conceptual framework to address this need. It comprises two parts: the first part analyzes a student's capabilities, and the second part suggests available courses and job aspects aligned with those capabilities. Student analysis considers marks in various subjects at the 10+2 level and vocational interests in different fields, using fuzzy sets. Fuzzy inference rules are framed to analyze abilities in engineering, medical, and hospitality fields as an example. The second part utilizes the composition of relations concept to suggest related courses and jobs.

title: Proceedings First International Workshop on Focusing
Abstract: This volume comprises the proceedings of WoF'15, the First International Workshop on Focusing, held on November 23rd, 2015 in Suva, Fiji. The workshop was a satellite event of LPAR-20, the 20th International Conferences on Logic for Programming, Artificial Intelligence and Reasoning. The program committee selected four papers for presentation at WoF'15, included in this volume. The program also featured an invited talk by Elaine Pimentel. Focusing is a proof search strategy that alternates two phases: an inversion phase applying invertible sequent rules exhaustively and a chaining phase selecting a formula and decomposing it maximally using non-invertible rules. Focusing is a recent development in computational logic, offering completeness for many logics and a foundation for their use in programming languages and rewriting calculi.

title: Proceedings Workshop on Models for Formal Analysis of Real Systems
Abstract: This volume contains the proceedings of MARS 2015, the first workshop on Models for Formal Analysis of Real Systems, held on November 23, 2015 in Suva, Fiji, as an affiliated workshop of LPAR 2015, the 20th International Conference on Logic for Programming, Artificial Intelligence and Reasoning. The workshop emphasizes modeling over verification, aiming to discuss lessons learned from applying formal methods to real systems. It explores questions like: 1) Formalism selection and rationale, 2) Abstractions made and their reasons, 3) Modeling of system characteristics, 4) Complications encountered during modeling, and 5) Measures taken to ensure model accuracy. The workshop invites papers presenting full models of real systems, encouraging alternative formal descriptions to foster the development of improved specification formalisms.

title: (Yet) Another Theoretical Model of Thinking
Abstract: This paper presents a theoretical, idealized model of the thinking process with the following characteristics: 1) ability to generate complex thought sequences and generalize to new inputs, 2) capacity to receive and maintain input information indefinitely for thought generation and later use, and 3) support for learning during execution. The model's core lies in the concept of internal consistency, where generated thoughts remain consistent with the input from which they are derived. Its merit, besides the ability to generate new thoughts internally, lies in its potential to enhance generalization during training. This is achieved by separating input information into parts handled by different processing components, with a focus mechanism to retrieve information for each. This modularized view, combined with the focus mechanism, aligns the model with computationally capable Turing machines. The paper constructively demonstrates that the model's computational complexity is at least, if not surpassing, that of a universal Turing machine.
label: AI

title: Learning Linguistic Biomarkers for Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment using Compound Skip-grams
Abstract: Predicting Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) remains a challenge due to existing diagnostic criteria relying on neuropsychological examinations. Automated Machine Learning (ML) models trained on verbal utterances of MCI patients can assist in diagnosis. Our model, utilizing skip-gram features, learned various linguistic biomarkers to differentiate between 19 MCI patients and 19 healthy controls from the DementiaBank language transcript clinical dataset. Results show that a model incorporating compound skip-grams achieves better AUC and can aid ML prediction with small MCI data samples.
label: AI

title: A Study of an Modeling Method of T-S fuzzy System Based on Moving Fuzzy Reasoning and Its Application
Abstract: To improve the effectiveness of fuzzy identification, a structure identification method based on moving rate is proposed for T-S fuzzy models. This method, called "T-S modeling (or T-S fuzzy identification method) based on moving rate," addresses shortcomings in existing fuzzy reasoning methods based on matching degree. The paper defines moving rates for s-type, z-type, and trapezoidal membership functions of T-S fuzzy models, highlighting differences between the proposed moving rate and existing matching degree. An identification method based on moving rate is then proposed for T-S models. The proposed method is applied to fuzzy modeling for precipitation forecast and security situation prediction. Test results demonstrate significant improvement in the effectiveness of fuzzy identification.
label: AI

title: A Winner-Take-All Approach to Emotional Neural Networks with Universal Approximation Property
Abstract: This paper introduces a brain-inspired winner-take-all emotional neural network (WTAENN) and proves its universal approximation property for the novel architecture. WTAENN is a single-layered feedforward neural network that benefits from excitatory, inhibitory, and expandatory neural connections, as well as winner-take-all (WTA) competition, mirroring the human brain's nervous system. WTA competition increases information capacity without adding hidden neurons. The universal approximation capability of this architecture is illustrated on example functions trained by a genetic algorithm and applied to various recent and benchmark problems like curve fitting, pattern recognition, classification, and prediction. Its performance is tested on twelve UCI classification datasets, a facial recognition problem, three real-world prediction problems (two chaotic time series of geomagnetic activity indices and wind farm power generation data), two synthetic case studies with constant and nonconstant noise variance, as well as k-selector and linear programming problems. Results indicate the general applicability and often superiority of the approach in terms of higher accuracy and lower model complexity, especially where low computational complexity is critical.
label: AI

title: Design of an Alarm System for Isfahan Ozone Level based on Artificial Intelligence Predictor Models
Abstract: Predicting ozone levels is a crucial task for air quality agencies in modern cities. This paper designs an ozone level alarm system (OLP) for Isfahan city and tests it using real-world data from 1-1-2000 to 7-6-2011. The system utilizes three inputs (solar ultraviolet (UV), total solar radiation (TSR), and total ozone (O3)) and a single output: the predicted O3 for the next day and alarm messages. An artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm is applied to determine the output based on the input variables. The paper compares AI models, including supervised brain emotional learning (BEL), adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), and artificial neural networks (ANNs), to identify the best model. Simulation of the proposed system demonstrates its effectiveness in predicting ozone levels in major cities.
label: AI

title: Review-Level Sentiment Classification with Sentence-Level Polarity Correction
Abstract: This paper proposes an effective technique to address the review-level sentiment classification problem using sentence-level polarity correction. The polarity correction technique considers the consistency of sentence polarities (positive and negative) within each product review before performing machine learning. Sentences with inconsistent polarities are removed, while those with consistent polarities are used to train state-of-the-art classifiers. The technique achieves superior results on various product review types and outperforms baseline models without correction. Experimental results show an average of 82% F-measure across four product review domains.
label: AI

title: Review of Person Re-identification Techniques
Abstract: Person re-identification across different surveillance cameras with disjoint fields of view is a significant and challenging area in intelligent video surveillance. While various methods have been developed, certain limitations and unresolved issues remain. Existing re-identification approaches typically extract feature vectors from segmented still images or video frames, applying different similarity or dissimilarity measures. Some methods employ simple constant metrics, while others utilize models to optimize metrics. Some approaches build models based on local color or texture information, while others leverage gait information. The primary goal of these approaches is to achieve high accuracy and low computational costs. This study summarizes recent developments in literature, discussing available person re-identification methods, highlighting their advantages and disadvantages, and comparing their performance.
label: AI

title: Combining Privileged Information to Improve Context-Aware Recommender Systems
Abstract: A recommender system is an information filtering technology that predicts user preference ratings for items (products, services, movies, etc.) or ranks items likely to interest the user. Context-aware recommender systems (CARS) learn and predict user preferences by incorporating contextual information into the recommendation process. A major challenge in CARS research is the lack of automatic methods to obtain contextual information. This paper proposes using contextual information from topic hierarchies of items (web pages) to improve CARS performance. Topic hierarchies are constructed using an extension of the LUPI-based Incremental Hierarchical Clustering method, considering three types of information: traditional bag-of-words (technical information) and the combination of named entities (privileged information I) with domain terms (privileged information II). The contextual information is evaluated in four CARS, assigning different weights to each information type. Empirical results demonstrate that topic hierarchies with the combined privileged information provide better recommendations.
label: AI

title: Robotics Technology in Mental Health Care
Abstract: This chapter explores the current and future use of robotics and intelligent sensing technology in mental health care. While the technology is nascent in this field, it offers potential as a valuable tool for practitioners. The chapter aims to provide a brief overview, discuss recent applications of robotics technology in mental health care practice, examine design and ethical considerations, and explore the potential of emerging technologies. |||
label: AI

title: Deep Kernel Learning
Abstract: Deep kernels combine the structural properties of deep learning with the flexibility of kernel methods. They transform inputs of a spectral mixture base kernel with a deep architecture, utilizing local kernel interpolation, inducing points, and efficient algebra for scalability. These closed-form kernels improve expressiveness and scalability, and can be used as replacements for standard kernels. Learning occurs through the marginal likelihood of a Gaussian process, with inference and learning cost linear in the number of training points, and constant cost per test point prediction. Experiments on diverse datasets, including one with 2 million examples, demonstrate improved performance compared to scalable Gaussian processes, flexible kernel learning models, and standalone deep architectures.
label: AI

title: Learning Optimized Or's of And's
Abstract: Or's of And's (OA) models are interpretable machine learning models consisting of a small number of disjunctions of conjunctions (disjunctive normal form). They represent a set of conditions that characterize specific data subsets. This work presents two optimization-based frameworks, Optimized OA (OOA) and its faster version, Optimized OA with Approximations (OOAx), for constructing OA models. Theoretical bounds on the properties of patterns in OA models are proven. OA models are demonstrated as a diagnostic screening tool for obstructive sleep apnea, achieving high accuracy with improved interpretability compared to other methods.
label: AI

title: Submodular Hamming Metrics
Abstract: This paper identifies a class of functions, positive polymatroids, that can define proper discrete metrics over binary vectors and are tractable to optimize. Exploiting submodularity, hardness results and approximation algorithms for optimization over these metrics are provided. Empirical studies showcase the effectiveness of these metrics and algorithms on both metric minimization (clustering) and maximization (diverse k-best lists) tasks.
label: AI

title: Towards a Better Understanding of Predict and Count Models
Abstract: This paper delves deeper into the connection between prediction-based word embedding models and count models based on pointwise mutual information, previously observed by Levy and Goldberg. It identifies key differences in optimization, namely predict models operating in low-dimensional spaces with heavy interaction between embedding vectors, and their fewer parameters reducing overfitting. Motivated by these insights, the paper introduces principled regularization for count models with closed-form solutions for L1 and L2 regularization. Finally, a new embedding model with a convex objective and improved intelligibility is proposed.
label: AI

title: Depth, balancing, and limits of the Elo model
Abstract: Computational complexity of games may not reflect human complexity. This paper investigates the depth of various games, extending it to a continuous measure. New depth results are provided, along with tools (given-first-move, pie rule, size extension) for increasing depth. These measures are used to analyze games and opening moves in Y, NoGo, Killall Go, and the effect of pie rules.
label: AI

title: An Action Language for Multi-Agent Domains: Foundations
Abstract: In multi-agent domains (MADs), actions can alter not only the world and an agent's knowledge about it, but also the knowledge and beliefs of other agents, creating a complex hierarchy of knowledge. This paper introduces an action language (mA+) designed to represent and reason about such knowledge manipulation scenarios in MADs. mA+ allows representation of various action types (world-altering, sensing, and communication) and incorporates dynamic awareness of action occurrences, impacting knowledge about the world and other agents' knowledge. The semantics of mA+ is based on pointed Kripke models, encoding agent knowledge and the real state of the world, and is defined by a transition function mapping actions and states to sets of states. The paper illustrates properties of action theories, including those guaranteeing finiteness of initial states and practical implementability. Finally, it connects mA+ to other formalisms addressing RAC in MADs.
label: AI

title: Thoughts on Massively Scalable Gaussian Processes
Abstract: This work significantly extends the KISS-GP approach for massively scalable Gaussian processes (MSGP). MSGP enables the use of Gaussian processes on billions of datapoints without requiring distributed inference or strong assumptions, reducing complexity to linear in the number of training points and constant per test point prediction. Key techniques include: 1) decomposing covariance matrices as Kronecker products of Toeplitz matrices approximated by circulant matrices, offering computational benefits over individual approaches; 2) local kernel interpolation and inducing points for arbitrary data inputs and constant test time predictions; 3) exploiting block-Toeplitz Toeplitz-block structure for fast inference and learning without multidimensional Kronecker structure; and 4) input space projections for modeling correlated inputs and high-dimensional data. The ability to handle a large number of inducing points allows for near-exact accuracy and large-scale kernel learning.
label: AI

title: Symmetry-invariant optimization in deep networks
Abstract: This paper investigates the complex forms of symmetry arising from scaling-based reparameterization of network weights in deep networks using max-pooling and sub-sampling layers. Two symmetry-invariant gradient-based weight updates for stochastic gradient descent are proposed. Empirical evidence on the MNIST dataset shows improved test performance without compromising computational efficiency. The paper also presents results of training with one of the proposed updates on an image segmentation problem.
label: AI

title: Adaptive information-theoretic bounded rational decision-making with parametric priors
Abstract: This work explores bounded rationality from an information-theoretic perspective, measuring information-processing costs using relative entropy between a posterior decision strategy and a fixed prior strategy. In the case of multiple environments, the problem is shown to be equivalent to the rate distortion problem in information theory. The optimal prior and posterior strategies can be computed using the Blahut-Arimoto algorithm, but this is challenging for continuous problems. This paper derives a sampling-based update rule for adapting prior behaviors, avoiding infeasible operations like computing partition sums. Simulations demonstrate a proof of concept for discrete action and environment domains. This approach offers a more realistic model of human decision-making processes.
label: AI

title: Computing sets of graded attribute implications with witnessed non-redundancy
Abstract: This paper extends previous work on sets of graded attribute implications with witnessed non-redundancy. Using finite residuated lattices for truth degrees and arbitrary idempotent truth-stressing linguistic hedges, an algorithm is introduced to transform any set of graded attribute implications into an equivalent non-redundant set with saturated consequents. This solves the open problem of general systems of pseudo-intents in formal concept analysis with graded attributes and linguistic hedges. Additionally, a polynomial-time procedure is presented for determining bases from complete sets of graded attribute implications.
label: AI

title: Radio SETI Observations of the Anomalous Star KIC 8462852
Abstract: This paper reports on a search for extraterrestrial intelligence signals from the star system KIC 8462852 using the Allen Telescope Array. No narrowband radio signals were detected at a level of 180-300 Jy in a 1 Hz channel, or medium band signals above 10 Jy in a 100 kHz channel.
label: AI

title: Achieving Sensor Fusion for Collaborative Multi-level Monitoring of Pipeline Infrastructures
Abstract: Large-scale monitoring systems enable efficient field-level data collection at high temporal and spatial resolutions, crucial for pipeline infrastructure applications requiring leak detection and security. This paper presents a multi-level system architecture for data collection and processing based on wireless sensor networks and unmanned aerial vehicles. Three sensor fusion methods (Kalman filtering, Fuzzy Sensor Validation and Fusion, and Consensus-based processing) are considered for intelligent data reduction and situational awareness, mitigating communication bottlenecks. Simulation and experimental results are presented.
label: AI

title: Train and Test Tightness of LP Relaxations in Structured Prediction
Abstract: Structured prediction, used in areas like computer vision and natural language processing, often involves approximate solvers due to complex scoring functions. This paper provides a theoretical explanation for the observed tightness of linear programming (LP) relaxations in real-world instances. It shows that learning with LP relaxed inference encourages integrality of training instances, and this tightness generalizes from training to test data.
label: AI

title: Learning in Auctions: Regret is Hard, Envy is Easy
Abstract: This paper investigates welfare guarantees of simple combinatorial auction formats like simultaneous second price auctions (SiSPAs), even when players use no-regret learning algorithms. It is shown that efficient no-regret algorithms are computationally intractable for SiSPAs. To address this, a novel concept of "no-envy learning" is introduced, based on Walrasian equilibrium. No-envy learning is shown to be efficiently implementable and results in approximately optimal welfare for bidders with various valuations. This work extends to other auction formats and is enabled by a novel Follow-The-Perturbed-Leader algorithm for settings with infinite experts and non-linear payoff functions.
label: AI

title: Co-Clustering Network-Constrained Trajectory Data
Abstract: Clustering moving object trajectories has been extensively studied in Euclidean space, but the problem of clustering trajectories restricted by road networks remains relatively unexplored. This paper models relations between trajectories and road segments as a bipartite graph, and proposes methods for clustering its vertices. The effectiveness of these approaches is demonstrated on synthetic data, showing their potential for inferring knowledge about flow dynamics and driver behavior using road networks.
label: AI

title: Algorithm Portfolios for Noisy Optimization
Abstract: This work focuses on portfolios of noisy optimization solvers, a set of solvers equipped with an algorithm selection tool for distributing computational power. It proposes an ad hoc portfolio algorithm dedicated to noisy optimization, mathematically proving its performance. Surprisingly, comparing solvers with some lag, i.e., recommending the best solver based on past performance, improves results. Additionally, a principled method for distributing computational power among solvers is presented.
label: AI

title: Learn on Source, Refine on Target:A Model Transfer Learning Framework with Random Forests
Abstract: This paper presents two novel model transfer-learning methods for refining decision forest models in a "target" domain using a training set sampled from a "source" domain. The first algorithm greedily searches for locally optimal modifications of tree structure, while the second adjusts parameters at decision nodes without altering structure. An ensemble combining both methods is also proposed. These methods demonstrate impressive experimental results across a range of problems.
label: AI

title: Understanding symmetries in deep networks
Abstract: Deep networks employing convolution, batch normalization, ReLU, max-pooling, and sub-sampling often exhibit scale invariance or symmetry in their weight space, hindering Euclidean gradient-based optimization. This paper proposes a solution by constraining filters to lie on the unit-norm manifold, reducing training to stochastic gradient descent updates on the manifold. Empirical evidence on the MNIST dataset shows improved test performance compared to batch normalization without compromising computational efficiency.
label: AI

title: Visualising interactive inferences with IDPD3
Abstract: Knowledge base systems require effective interpretation and interaction with end-users. This paper introduces IDPD3, a library for visualizing models of logic theories, an enhanced version of $ID^{P}_{Draw}$ that supports visualized interactive simulations.
label: AI

title: Bound Your Models! How to Make OWL an ASP Modeling Language
Abstract: This paper introduces bounded model semantics for the Web Ontology Language OWL, an intuitive and computationally advantageous alternative to classical semantics. It demonstrates that a translation into Answer Set Programming (ASP) allows for solving various bounded-model reasoning tasks, including satisfiability, axiom entailment, model extraction, and enumeration. This work facilitates harnessing advanced semantic web modeling environments for the logic programming community through an "off-label use" of OWL. |||
label: AI

title: A web-based IDE for IDP
Abstract: IDP, a knowledge base system rooted in first-order logic, is gaining traction but faces challenges in user accessibility.  To address this, we've developed an IDE using web technology, offering a modern interface that facilitates both online exploration and offline development of larger applications.
label: AI

title: Lowering the learning curve for declarative programming: a Python API for the IDP system
Abstract: Programmers may be reluctant to adopt declarative systems due to their learning curve.  This paper presents an API that seamlessly integrates the IDP Knowledge Base system into the Python programming language, providing a user-friendly approach to harnessing IDP's logical capabilities without requiring new syntax or semantics. This allows Python programmers to utilize IDP's declarative power within their existing codebase with minimal adjustments.
label: AI

title: SWISH: SWI-Prolog for Sharing
Abstract: Modern programming interfaces leverage web technology to enable cloud-based solutions, integration into tutorials, attractive result visualization, and collaborative development. SWISH, a web-based front-end for Prolog, exemplifies this trend by providing a public website that showcases SWI-Prolog for demonstration, experimentation, and education. SWISH is further integrated with the ClioPatria semantic web toolkit, facilitating collaborative program and query development within a dataset, and it's embedded within the "Learn Prolog Now!" online Prolog book.
label: AI

title: Finetuning Randomized Heuristic Search For 2D Path Planning: Finding The Best Input Parameters For R* Algorithm Through Series Of Experiments
Abstract: Path planning in Artificial Intelligence is often treated as a graph search problem, and R* is a cutting-edge algorithm specifically designed for this task.  The algorithm breaks down path-finding into a sequence of subtasks that are readily solvable using established methods like A*. The decomposition process relies on a parameterized random choice, making R*'s performance heavily reliant on its input parameters. Our work analyzes the relationship between R* parameters, their potential upper and lower bounds, and their influence on performance. Through extensive experimentation, we establish heuristic rules for parameter initialization to optimize algorithm performance.
label: AI

title: SAT as a game
Abstract: This paper introduces a playful representation of SAT, aiming to make propositional satisfiability more accessible for pedagogical purposes while potentially inspiring new search heuristics.
label: AI

title: A Pareto Optimal D* Search Algorithm for Multiobjective Path Planning
Abstract: Path planning is crucial in mobile robotics, providing collision-free routes for robots. While A* search guarantees optimal solutions, D* is commonly used for its dynamic replanning capabilities. However, traditional methods like A* and D* are not well-suited for multiobjective optimization (MOO) problems that consider multiple path planning objectives beyond distance. This paper presents D*-PO, a novel algorithm for optimal MOO path planning. D*-PO incorporates Pareto optimality into D*, ensuring non-dominated solution paths by calculating the Pareto front at each search step. Simulations simulating a Martian rover demonstrate D*-PO's superior performance compared to A* and D* for MOO path planning with five path costs.
label: AI

title: Toward an Efficient Multi-class Classification in an Open Universe
Abstract: Classification is a foundational task in machine learning and data mining. Existing methods focus on classifying unknown instances within a set of known training classes. However, real-world applications often involve open-set classification, where instances may not belong to any training class. To address this challenge, we introduce Galaxy-X, a novel multi-class classification approach for open-set recognition. Galaxy-X constructs a minimum bounding hyper-sphere for each training class, effectively separating instances resembling known classes from unknown ones. We introduce a novel evaluation procedure to assess open-set classification performance, and experimental results on benchmark datasets highlight Galaxy-X's efficiency in classifying both known and unknown instances.
label: AI

title: From random walks to distances on unweighted graphs
Abstract: Large unweighted directed graphs are commonly used to represent relationships between entities. A fundamental challenge in analyzing such networks is defining a suitable measure of similarity or dissimilarity between vertices. This paper introduces a class of techniques based on stochastic calculus for analyzing random walks on graphs. These techniques generalize results on the degeneracy of hitting times and analyze a metric based on the Laplace Transformed Hitting Time (LTHT). The LTHT metric provides a natural, well-behaved alternative to the expected hitting time. We establish a connection between hitting times of Brownian motion and analogous hitting times on graphs, demonstrating LTHT's consistency with underlying geometric graph metrics, its ability to preserve clustering tendencies, and its robustness against random non-geometric edge additions. Simulations and real-world data analyses validate the LTHT's theoretical predictions and its superiority over other metrics.
label: AI

title: Z Specification for the W3C Editor's Draft Core SHACL Semantics
Abstract: This paper formally defines the W3C Draft Core SHACL Semantics specification using the Z notation. This formalization process identified several quality issues in the draft and confirmed the well-foundedness of its recursive definitions. Further formal validation of the draft will require employing executable specification technology.
label: AI

title: Automatic Prosody Prediction for Chinese Speech Synthesis using BLSTM-RNN and Embedding Features
Abstract: Prosody plays a crucial role in the naturalness and intelligibility of speech. However, automatic prosodic boundary prediction for Chinese speech synthesis remains a significant challenge, with traditional CRF-based methods heavily reliant on feature engineering. This paper proposes using neural networks to directly predict prosodic boundary labels from Chinese characters without feature engineering. Experimental results demonstrate that stacking feed-forward and bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM) recurrent network layers outperforms the CRF-based method. Embedding features extracted from raw text further enhance performance.
label: AI

title: Optimized Mission Planning for Planetary Exploration Rovers
Abstract: Planetary surface exploration primarily relies on unmanned landing vehicles and rovers, demanding efficient mission planning through artificial intelligence and machine learning. This paper describes a coordinated approach utilizing both global navigation and metaheuristic optimization algorithms for safe and efficient mission planning. The goal is to determine the least-cost combination of a landing zone (LZ) and a global path plan, minimizing cost by avoiding terrain hazards for both the lander and rover. Computer vision methods identify craters, mounds, and rocks as obstacles. Multiple search methods for the rover's global path plan are investigated, and several combinatorial optimization algorithms are implemented to select the shortest distance path as the preferred mission plan. Simulations for a Google Lunar X Prize mission showcase an optimization scheme that leverages the A* search method for path planning and simulated annealing for selecting the ideal LZ-path-goal combination. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in minimizing hazard risk and enhancing mission efficiency. While specific to a lunar mission, the resulting architecture can be adapted to various planetary missions and rovers.
label: AI

title: Chaos of Protein Folding
Abstract: Protein folding, an NP-complete problem, has prompted the use of artificial intelligence tools like neural networks and genetic algorithms to predict the 3D shape of amino acid sequences. Underlying this effort is the assumption that the folding process is predictable. However, this assumption has not been proven or studied extensively. This paper analyzes the topological dynamics of protein folding, mathematically proving that protein folding in the 2D hydrophobic-hydrophilic (HP) square lattice model is chaotic according to Devaney's definition. Implications for both structure prediction and biology are discussed.
label: AI

title: Topological chaos and chaotic iterations. Application to Hash functions
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel concept of chaotic algorithms based on chaotic iterations.  Unlike previous studies on chaotic iterations, our focus lies not on stable states but on the unpredictable behaviors of these iterations.  By connecting chaotic iterations to Devaney's notion of topological chaos, we establish conditions ensuring that these algorithms exhibit topological chaos, leading to highly unpredictable outcomes.  After presenting the theoretical foundations, we explore practical aspects by demonstrating how these algorithms translate into computer programs that generate true topological chaos and proposing applications in the field of information security.
label: AI

title: Why Neurons Have Thousands of Synapses, A Theory of Sequence Memory in Neocortex
Abstract: Neocortical neurons possess thousands of excitatory synapses, making it a puzzle how neurons integrate input from so many synapses and what network behavior this facilitates.  Previous research suggested that non-linear properties of dendrites enable neurons to recognize multiple patterns.  This paper expands on this idea by demonstrating that a neuron with thousands of synapses arranged along active dendrites can accurately and robustly recognize hundreds of unique patterns of cellular activity, even in the presence of noise and variation.  We propose a neuron model where some recognized patterns trigger action potentials, defining the neuron's classic receptive field, while others serve as predictions, slightly depolarizing the neuron without immediately generating an action potential.  A network model based on these neurons demonstrates the network's ability to learn a robust model of time-based sequences.  Given the similarities of excitatory neurons throughout the neocortex and the importance of sequence memory in inference and behavior, we propose that this form of sequence memory is a universal property of neocortical tissue.  Cellular layers in the neocortex might implement variations of this sequence memory algorithm to achieve different aspects of inference and behavior.  The neuron and network models we introduce are robust across a wide range of parameters, as long as the network utilizes a sparse distributed code of cellular activations. The sequence capacity of the network scales linearly with the number of synapses on each neuron, highlighting the need for thousands of synapses to learn the numerous temporal patterns in sensory stimuli and motor sequences.
label: AI

title: Short-Term Plasticity and Long-Term Potentiation in Magnetic Tunnel Junctions: Towards Volatile Synapses
Abstract: Synaptic memory is widely considered the foundation of learning and cognition in humans. While non-volatile long-term plasticity changes have been implemented in nanoelectronic synapses for neuromorphic applications, recent neuroscience research reveals that biological synapses exhibit meta-stable volatile strengthening followed by long-term strengthening if the input stimulus frequency is sufficiently high. This "memory strengthening" and "memory decay" functionality holds potential for adaptive neuromorphic architectures. This paper demonstrates the close resemblance between the magnetization dynamics of a Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ) and the short-term plasticity and long-term potentiation observed in biological synapses.  We show that the frequency of the input stimulus, in addition to its magnitude and duration, plays a crucial role in determining long-term potentiation of the MTJ. Such MTJ synaptic memory arrays can be used to create compact, ultra-fast, and low-power intelligent neural systems.
label: AI

title: Learning Adversary Behavior in Security Games: A PAC Model Perspective
Abstract: Stackelberg Security Games (SSG) have emerged as a powerful tool for addressing diverse security challenges, from wildlife crime to urban crime. Machine learning techniques are increasingly employed to learn and predict adversary behavior based on data about defender-adversary interactions. This paper focuses on directly learning the adversary's response function. Utilizing the PAC model, we establish a strong theoretical foundation for learning in SSGs, providing theoretical answers to questions about the number of samples required to learn adversary behavior and utility guarantees when using the learned model for planning defender strategies. The paper explores practical questions like the amount of data needed to improve model accuracy and addresses the phenomenon where accurate prediction of adversary behavior may not be sufficient for identifying the optimal defender strategy.  This work presents four main contributions: (1) a PAC model for learning adversary response functions in SSGs; (2) PAC-model analysis of learning key bounded rationality models in SSGs; (3) a novel approach to adversary modeling based on a non-parametric class of response functions with PAC-model analysis; and (4) identification of conditions where computing the best defender strategy against the learned adversary behavior is indeed optimal. Real-world data from a Ugandan national park illustrates the benefits of our new adversary modeling approach and verifies the PAC model predictions.
label: AI

title: Learning Causal Graphs with Small Interventions
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of learning causal networks with interventions, where each intervention has a limited size within Pearl's Structural Equation Model with independent errors (SEM-IE). The objective is to minimize the number of experiments needed to discover the causal directions of all edges in a causal graph. Previous work focused on using separating systems for complete graphs. We prove that any deterministic adaptive algorithm must be a separating system to learn complete graphs in the worst-case scenario.  Furthermore, we introduce a novel separating system construction that approaches optimal size and is arguably simpler than previous work in combinatorics. We also develop a novel information theoretic lower bound on the number of interventions that applies generally, including randomized adaptive learning algorithms. For general chordal graphs, we derive worst-case lower bounds on the number of interventions. Based on observations about induced trees, we propose a new deterministic adaptive algorithm to learn directions on any chordal skeleton completely. Our scheme provides an $\alpha$-approximation algorithm, where $\alpha$ is the independence number of the graph. We also show that certain graph classes require a number of experiments close to the lower bound, while others require a number of experiments that is multiplicatively $\alpha$ away from our lower bound. Simulations show that our algorithm performs very close to the lower bound in most cases, significantly outperforming the approach based on separating systems for complete graphs when dealing with random chordal graphs.
label: AI

title: Quantum neural computation of entanglement is robust to noise and decoherence
Abstract: Previous research proposed an entanglement indicator for general multiqubit states, which can be "learned" by a quantum system acting as a neural network. This indicator is applicable to both pure and mixed states, and it need not be "close" to any specific state.  Moreover, as the system size increases, the amount of additional training required decreases.  This paper demonstrates that the indicator is stable to noise and decoherence.
label: AI

title: Latent Bayesian melding for integrating individual and population models
Abstract: Many statistical problems require different model types for population-level and individual-level behavior. This raises the question of how to integrate these models.  Methods like posterior regularization aim to match expectations between two models using generalized moment matching, but sometimes both models are best represented as latent variable models. This paper proposes latent Bayesian melding, inspired by averaging distributions over population statistics of both individual and population models under a logarithmic opinion pool framework. A case study on electricity disaggregation, a type of single-channel blind source separation problem, shows that latent Bayesian melding significantly improves prediction accuracy compared to an approach solely based on generalized moment matching.
label: AI

title: Turing's Red Flag
Abstract: In the future, we will need to address the impact of AI being mistaken for humans. Therefore, I propose that any autonomous system should be designed to minimize the likelihood of being mistaken for anything other than an autonomous system and should clearly identify itself at the beginning of any interaction with another agent.
label: AI

title: A Study of the Spatio-Temporal Correlations in Mobile Calls Networks
Abstract: The significant increase in data volume in companies necessitates the evolution of data analysis methods to meet these new demands. This paper presents a practical analysis of a large database from a telecommunication operator, focusing on segmenting a territory and characterizing areas based on mobile phone usage. The study utilizes call detail records collected over five months in France and proposes a two-stage analysis. The first stage groups source antennas with similar call distribution patterns to target antennas and vice versa, geographically projecting the results on a map of France. The second stage discretizes time into periods, identifying changes in call distribution patterns from clustered source antennas, enabling an analysis of temporal shifts in user behavior across the country.
label: AI

title: Highway Long Short-Term Memory RNNs for Distant Speech Recognition
Abstract: This work extends deep long short-term memory (DLSTM) recurrent neural networks by incorporating gated direct connections, called highway connections, between memory cells in adjacent layers. These connections facilitate unimpeded information flow across layers, mitigating the gradient vanishing problem encountered in deeper LSTMs. The paper also introduces latency-controlled bidirectional LSTMs (BLSTMs), which effectively utilize the entire history while managing latency. Efficient algorithms are proposed for training these novel networks using both frame and sequence discriminative criteria. Experiments on the AMI distant speech recognition (DSR) task demonstrate the ability to train deeper LSTMs and achieve improved performance through sequence training with highway LSTMs (HLSTMs). The novel model surpasses previous works with a Word Error Rate (WER) of 43.9/47.7% on the AMI (SDM) development and evaluation sets, significantly outperforming DNN and DLSTM baselines by 15.7% and 5.3% relative improvement, respectively.
label: AI

title: Robust Subspace Clustering via Tighter Rank Approximation
Abstract: The matrix rank minimization problem is generally NP-hard. While the nuclear norm is widely used as a substitute for the rank function, it approximates by adding all singular values, leading to potential errors heavily influenced by singular value magnitudes, limiting its effectiveness in practical applications. This paper introduces the arctangent function as a tighter approximation of the rank function, applying it to the challenging subspace clustering problem. An efficient optimization procedure based on the augmented Lagrange multipliers (ALM) method is developed for this nonconvex minimization problem. Extensive experiments on face clustering and motion segmentation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for rank approximation.

title: Sample Complexity of Episodic Fixed-Horizon Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Recent advancements in reinforcement learning for discounted infinite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) have yielded tight sample complexity bounds. However, real-world applications often involve interactive learning agents operating for fixed or bounded time periods, such as tutoring students for exams or handling customer service requests. Such scenarios are more appropriately modeled as episodic fixed-horizon MDPs, for which looser sample complexity bounds currently exist. This paper investigates the sample complexity in this setting, focusing on the number of episodes required for a specific performance guarantee with high probability (PAC guarantee). The paper presents an upper PAC bound of  $ \tilde{O}(\frac{|\mathcal{S}|^2 |\mathcal{A}| H^2}{\epsilon^2} \ln \frac{1}{\delta})$ and a lower PAC bound of $\tilde{\Omega}(\frac{|\mathcal{S}| |\mathcal{A}| H^2}{\epsilon^2} \ln \frac{1}{\delta + c})$. These bounds match up to log-terms and exhibit an additional linear dependency on the number of states $| \mathcal{S}|$. The lower bound is the first of its kind for this setting. The upper bound utilizes Bernstein's inequality to improve previous bounds for episodic finite-horizon MDPs, which had a time-horizon dependency of at least $H^3$.
label: AI

title: Fermi's paradox, extraterrestrial life and the future of humanity: a Bayesian analysis
Abstract: The Great Filter theory, addressing Fermi's Paradox, posits that the product $Npq$ is not a large number, where $N$ represents the number of potentially life-supporting planets in the observable universe, $p$ signifies the probability of a randomly chosen planet developing intelligent life comparable to present-day human civilization, and $q$ denotes the conditional probability of that civilization evolving into a technologically advanced supercivilization visible across the observable universe. While evidence suggests $N$ is vast, implying a small $pq$, Hanson (1998) and Bostrom (2008) argue that the discovery of extraterrestrial life would indicate a non-negligible $p$, leading to a very small $q$, potentially detrimental to humanity's prospects of universal colonization. This paper examines whether a Bayesian analysis supports this argument, finding that the conclusion hinges critically on the chosen prior distribution.
label: AI

title: My Reflections on the First Man vs. Machine No-Limit Texas Hold 'em Competition
Abstract: This article provides insights into the design, agent architecture, and lessons learned from the first human vs. computer no-limit Texas hold 'em competition, held from April 24 to May 8, 2015 at River's Casino in Pittsburgh, PA.
label: AI

title: Feature-Based Diversity Optimization for Problem Instance Classification
Abstract: Understanding the behavior of heuristic search methods, even simple ones like 2-OPT for the Traveling Salesperson problem (TSP), poses a challenge. This paper presents a general framework for constructing diverse sets of instances that are either hard or easy to solve for a given search heuristic. This diversity is achieved by employing an evolutionary algorithm to generate instances that are diverse with respect to various features of the underlying problem. Analysis of the constructed instance sets reveals that specific combinations of two or three features effectively classify TSP instances based on their difficulty for 2-OPT.
label: AI

title: Attention with Intention for a Neural Network Conversation Model
Abstract: Attention and intention play crucial roles in conversations and dialogue processes. This paper proposes a neural network-based approach for modeling these processes, consisting of three recurrent networks. The encoder network represents source-side sentences at the word level. The intention network models the dynamics of the intention process. The decoder network generates responses to the input from the source side, serving as a language model that depends on the intention and utilizes an attention mechanism to focus on specific source-side words when predicting symbols in the response. The model is trained end-to-end without labeled data. Experiments demonstrate the model's ability to generate natural responses to user inputs.
label: AI

title: Automatic Synthesis of Geometry Problems for an Intelligent Tutoring System
Abstract: This paper introduces GeoTutor, an intelligent tutoring system for Euclidean Geometry that automatically synthesizes proof problems and their solutions based on a given geometric figure and its associated properties. GeoTutor provides personalized practice problems tailored to address student deficiencies in the subject matter.
label: AI

title: Computing the Ramsey Number R(4,3,3) using Abstraction and Symmetry breaking
Abstract: The Ramsey number $R(4,3,3)$ is often considered the most likely to be determined soon. However, its exact value has remained elusive for almost 50 years. This paper presents a methodology based on abstraction and symmetry breaking, suitable for solving complex graph edge-coloring problems. This methodology is demonstrated by calculating the value $R(4,3,3) = 30$, requiring the computation of the previously unknown set $\mathcal{R}(3,3,3;13)$ comprising 78,892 Ramsey colorings.
label: AI

title: iCellular: Define Your Own Cellular Network Access on Commodity Smartphones
Abstract: Multi-carrier access holds promise for enhancing mobile network access quality. However, experiments reveal that network-controlled design limitations hinder the realization of its full potential. To address these limitations, the paper proposes iCellular, a system empowering users to define and intelligently select their own cellular network access from multiple carriers. iCellular leverages existing device-side mechanisms and standard cellular network procedures, but utilizes device intelligence for proactive and adaptive multi-carrier selection. It features adaptive monitoring for responsive selection and minimal service disruption, enhances carrier selection through online learning and runtime decision fault prevention, and is deployable on commodity phones without infrastructure or hardware changes. iCellular is implemented on Nexus 6 phones and tested using Google Project-Fi's multi-carrier access capabilities between T-Mobile and Sprint, two major US carriers. Experiments confirm iCellular's ability to improve user throughput by up to 3.74x (7x suspension reduction and 1.9x latency reduction) compared to state-of-the-art selection methods. Moreover, iCellular consistently identifies the best-quality carrier with negligible overhead on CPU, memory, and energy consumption.
label: AI

title: Learning Constructive Primitives for Online Level Generation and Real-time Content Adaptation in Super Mario Bros
Abstract: Procedural content generation (PCG) offers significant potential for game design and development by automating content creation. This paper proposes an alternative online content generation and adaptation approach for Super Mario Bros (SMB), inspired by recent learning-based PCG frameworks and existing PCG works. Unlike previous SMB-focused efforts, this approach utilizes the synergy between rule-based and learning-based methods to produce constructive primitives, creating high-quality and controllable game segments in SMB. This enables the generation of complete, high-quality game levels online by integrating relevant constructive primitives through controllable parameters related to geometric features and procedure-level properties. Adaptive content can also be generated in real time by dynamically selecting appropriate constructive primitives based on an adaptation criterion, such as dynamic difficulty adjustment (DDA). This approach exhibits desirable properties in terms of content quality assurance, generation efficiency, and controllability. Extensive simulation results demonstrate the approach's ability to generate controllable yet high-quality game levels online and adapt content for DDA in real time.
