title: Fast, simple and accurate handwritten digit classification by training shallow neural network classifiers with the 'extreme learning machine' algorithm
Abstract: Recent advancements in training deep neural network architectures have sparked renewed interest in their applications. Deep convolutional networks are now the preferred choice for complex tasks involving large datasets, such as image and speech recognition. However, this study demonstrates that shallow, non-convolutional neural networks, trained using the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) approach, can achieve error rates below 1% on the MNIST handwritten digit benchmark. This rapid training method (approximately 10 minutes) is significantly faster than traditional methods. Furthermore, adding distortions to the MNIST dataset, a common practice, further reduces error rates. The proposed methods also achieve error rates below 5.5% on the NORB image database. These results were achieved by introducing several enhancements to the standard ELM algorithm, which individually and collectively improve performance. A key innovation is the random receptive field sampling of the input, ensuring that each hidden unit operates on a randomly sized and positioned patch of each image. This method results in a sparse input weight matrix with approximately 90% of weights equal to zero. Combining these methods with a small number of iterations of a single-batch backpropagation method significantly reduces the number of hidden units required to achieve a desired performance level. These near-state-of-the-art results for MNIST and NORB highlight the ease of use and accuracy of the ELM algorithm for designing single-hidden-layer neural network classifiers. This suggests that ELM should be considered as a standalone method for simpler problems or as the final classification stage in deep neural networks for more complex tasks.
label: AI

title: Rigid and Non-rigid Shape Evolutions for Shape Alignment and Recovery in Images
Abstract: The accurate extraction of shapes from images is challenging due to variations in object shapes caused by rigid and non-rigid deformations, occluding foreground objects, and cluttered backgrounds. This work proposes a novel and general method for shape alignment and recovery using one example shape based on deterministic energy minimization. The approach leverages a general model of shape deformation to minimize active contour energies. Given a priori knowledge of the shape deformation, the corresponding curve evolution equation can be derived, known as the prior variation shape evolution (PVSE). The energy-minimizing PVSE is then derived for minimizing active contour energies. For shape recovery, a shape-preserving PVSE is employed to deform the shape while preserving its inherent characteristics. A theory of shape preservability for the PVSE is established to guide the selection of this shape-preserving PVSE. Experimental results validate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Metacarpal Bones Localization in X-ray Imagery Using Particle Filter Segmentation
Abstract: Statistical methods, such as sequential Monte Carlo methods, have been successfully applied to object detection, segmentation, and tracking in digital images. Building on this approach, Shape Particle Filters have been introduced for segmenting vertebrae, lungs, and hearts. This study presents a novel approach for segmenting metacarpal bones in X-ray images by combining a global shape model and a local appearance model. The global shape model is derived from annotated X-ray images of the metacarpal bones, while the local appearance model is constructed using a set of local features (Haar-like) in the neighborhood of each pixel. A probabilistic pixel classifier is then built using the random forest algorithm. To fit the shape model to a new image, a label probability map is extracted, and the optimal shape is obtained by maximizing the probability of each landmark using the Differential Evolution algorithm.
label: AI

title: Functional correspondence by matrix completion
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of finding dense intrinsic correspondence between manifolds using a recently introduced functional framework. The functional correspondence problem is formulated as a matrix completion problem incorporating manifold geometric structure and inducing functional localization using the L1 norm. Efficient numerical procedures for solving this problem are discussed. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art correspondence algorithms on non-rigid shape matching benchmarks, particularly in settings where only limited data is available.
label: AI

title: An NBDMMM Algorithm Based Framework for Allocation of Resources in Cloud
Abstract: Cloud computing has emerged as a significant technological advancement in the field of computing, providing on-demand access to computing resources such as networks, storage, computing capacity, and servers via an internet connection. These services are delivered on a pay-per-use basis, with costs determined by the amount of resource usage. The elastic nature of resource usage necessitates on-demand provisioning, which drives the entire cloud computing infrastructure. Maintaining these resources is a critical task that demands careful consideration. Infrastructure-level performance monitoring and enhancement are essential for optimal cloud operations. This paper proposes a framework for resource allocation in a cloud-based environment, leading to infrastructure-level performance enhancement in a cloud environment. The framework is divided into four stages: Stage 1 monitors infrastructure-level patterns of resource usage and cloud user behavior; Stage 2 reports monitoring activities to cloud service providers; Stage 3 applies the proposed Network Bandwidth Dependent DMMM algorithm; and Stage 4 allocates resources or provides services to cloud users, resulting in infrastructure-level performance enhancement and efficient resource management. Analysis of resource usage patterns is considered crucial for proper resource allocation by service providers. This paper utilizes Google cluster trace to access resource usage patterns in the cloud. Experiments conducted on the CloudSim simulation framework reveal that the NBDMMM algorithm significantly improves resource allocation in a virtualized cloud environment.
label: AI

title: Texture analysis by multi-resolution fractal descriptors
Abstract: This work introduces a novel texture descriptor based on fractal theory, leveraging Bouligand-Minkowski descriptors. The original image is recursively decomposed into four equal parts. At each recursion step, the average and deviation of Bouligand-Minkowski descriptors computed over each part are estimated. Entropy features are then extracted from both the average and deviation values. The proposed descriptors are obtained by concatenating these measures. The method is tested in a classification experiment using well-known datasets, Brodatz and Vistex. The results demonstrate that the proposed technique outperforms classical and state-of-the-art texture descriptors, such as Gabor wavelets and co-occurrence matrices.
label: AI

title: Detect2Rank : Combining Object Detectors Using Learning to Rank
Abstract: Object detection, a key area of research in computer vision, relies on various algorithms, each tailored to specific object appearance and imaging conditions. This lack of universality necessitates the development of methods for selecting and combining object detectors. This paper presents a framework for learning how to combine object detectors. The proposed method utilizes single detectors, such as DPM, CN, and EES, and exploits their correlations through high-level contextual features to generate a combined detection list. Experiments conducted on the PASCAL VOC07 and VOC10 datasets show that the proposed method significantly outperforms single object detectors, achieving improvements of 8.4% for DPM, 6.8% for CN, and 17.0% for EES on VOC07, and 6.5% for DPM, 5.5% for CN, and 16.2% for EES on VOC10.
label: AI

title: A Novel Feature Selection and Extraction Technique for Classification
Abstract: This paper introduces a versatile technique for feature selection and extraction called Class Dependent Features (CDFs). CDFs are used to improve classification accuracy while mitigating the curse of dimensionality by controlling computational expenses. To demonstrate the technique's generality, it is applied to handwritten digit recognition and text categorization.
label: AI

title: Improved texture image classification through the use of a corrosion-inspired cellular automaton
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of classifying synthetic and natural texture images by introducing a novel method that combines concepts from corrosion modeling and cellular automata. The core processes of metal pitting corrosion are identified and applied to texture images by incorporating the fundamental mechanisms of corrosion into the transition function of the cellular automaton. The surface morphology of the image is analyzed before and during the application of the cellular automaton's transition function. In each iteration, the cumulative mass of the corroded product is obtained to construct the attributes of the texture descriptor. Finally, this descriptor is used for image classification using Linear Discriminant Analysis. The method was evaluated on the well-known Brodatz and Vistex databases. To assess its robustness, the method's invariance to noise and rotation was tested using noise-added and rotated variants of the original databases. The results demonstrate the method's effectiveness for texture classification, achieving high success rates across all cases. This highlights the potential of employing methods inspired by natural phenomena in other fields.
label: AI

title: Sparkle Vision: Seeing the World through Random Specular Microfacets
Abstract: This paper investigates the problem of reproducing the world lighting from a single image of an object covered with random specular microfacets on its surface. These reflectors can be interpreted as a randomized mapping from the lighting to the image. Specular objects possess unique optical properties that distinguish them from both diffuse surfaces and smooth specular objects like metals, necessitating the design of a specialized imaging system to robustly and effectively photograph them. Simple yet reliable algorithms are presented for calibrating the proposed system and performing inference. Experiments validate the correctness of the model assumptions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed pipeline.
label: AI

title: Enhancing fractal descriptors on images by combining boundary and interior of Minkowski dilation
Abstract: This work proposes a novel method for obtaining fractal descriptors from gray-level texture images by combining information from interior and boundary measures of the Minkowski dilation applied to the texture surface. Initially, the image is transformed into a surface where the height of each point represents the gray intensity of the corresponding pixel in the image. This surface is then morphologically dilated using spheres of varying radii. For each radius, the volume and external area of the dilated structure are computed. The final descriptors are obtained by concatenating these measures and applying a canonical transform to reduce dimensionality. The proposed method enhances classical Bouligand-Minkowski fractal descriptors, which only consider volume information. By incorporating both volume and area, the proposed method provides richer descriptors, as confirmed by results on the classification of benchmark databases.
label: AI

title: Gabor wavelets combined with volumetric fractal dimension applied to texture analysis
Abstract: Texture analysis and classification remain significant challenges in computer vision and pattern recognition. Gabor wavelets have proven to be a valuable technique for characterizing distinctive texture patterns. However, most approaches used to extract descriptors from the Gabor magnitude space struggle to adequately represent the richness of detail within a single feature vector. This paper proposes a new method for enhancing the Gabor wavelets process by extracting a fractal signature from the magnitude spaces. Each signature is reduced using a canonical analysis function and concatenated to form the final feature vector. Experiments conducted on several texture image databases demonstrate the power and effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that this method outperforms earlier proposed methods, creating a more reliable technique for texture feature extraction.
label: AI

title: Joint Deep Learning for Car Detection
Abstract: Traditional object recognition approaches typically apply feature extraction, part deformation handling, occlusion handling, and classification sequentially and independently. Ouyang and Wang proposed a model for jointly learning all of these processes using a single deep neural network. This study utilizes and adapts their toolbox to apply it to car detection scenarios, where it had not been previously tested. Creating a single deep architecture from these components improves the interaction between them and can enhance the overall system performance. The approach is believed to have potential as a general-purpose object detection toolbox. The algorithm was tested on the UIUC car dataset, achieving an outstanding result with an accuracy of 97%. This significantly surpasses previously reported results, which reached up to 91%. The study emphasizes the potential benefits of using deep models over shallow ones, particularly when applied to larger datasets.
label: AI

title: Fractal descriptors based on the probability dimension: a texture analysis and classification approach
Abstract: This work introduces a novel technique for obtaining descriptors of gray-level texture images. The descriptors are generated by applying a multiscale transform to the fractal dimension of the image, estimated using the probability (Voss) method. The effectiveness of these descriptors is verified in a classification task using benchmark texture datasets. The results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method for describing and discriminating texture images.
label: AI

title: Brachiaria species identification using imaging techniques based on fractal descriptors
Abstract: Rapid and accurate methods for diagnosing and classifying forage species and/or cultivars have significant practical relevance in various fields, including scientific research and trade. This study focuses on identifying leaf samples of the fodder plant species Brachiaria. Samples were collected, scanned, and processed using artificial vision to create a database for subsequent classifications. The forage crops investigated include Brachiaria decumbens cv. IPEAN, Brachiaria ruziziensis Germain & Evrard, Brachiaria Brizantha (Hochst. ex. A. Rich.) Stapf, Brachiaria arrecta (Hack.) Stent., and Brachiaria spp. The images were analyzed using the fractal descriptors method, which extracts a set of measures from the fractal dimension values at different scales. These values serve as inputs for a state-of-the-art classifier, the Support Vector Machine, which discriminates the images based on their respective species.
label: AI

title: The three giri of Paradiso XXXIII
Abstract: This paper examines Dante's depiction of the tre giri ("three rings") of the Holy Trinity in Paradiso 33 of the Divine Comedy. It explores the myriad possibilities that Dante may have envisioned when describing his vision of God at this final stage of his journey. The analysis focuses on the features of shape, motion, size, color, and orientation that Dante details in his description of the Trinity. Drawing on mathematical tools from topology (specifically, knot theory) and combinatorics, the study analyzes all possible configurations of three intertwining circles. This is particularly compelling given Dante's description of the Trinity, where the round figures are arranged in a triangular format with rotational and reflective symmetry. Of the many possible link patterns, two particularly suggestive arrangements for the giri are identified: the Brunnian link and the (3,3)-torus link. These two patterns readily lend themselves to a Trinitarian model.
label: AI

title: Texture analysis using volume-radius fractal dimension
Abstract: Texture plays a crucial role in computer vision, providing information about pixel organization in different image regions. This paper proposes a novel approach for texture characterization based on complexity analysis. The proposed approach extends the concept of the Mass-radius fractal dimension, originally developed for shape analysis, to a set of coordinates in 3D space. This representation of the texture under analysis in a signature effectively characterizes different texture classes in terms of complexity. An experiment using images from the Brodatz album illustrates the method's performance.
label: AI

title: Multiple Object Recognition with Visual Attention
Abstract: This paper presents an attention-based model for recognizing multiple objects in images. The model is a deep recurrent neural network trained with reinforcement learning to focus on the most relevant regions of the input image. The model learns to both localize and recognize multiple objects despite being provided only class labels during training. The model is evaluated on the challenging task of transcribing house number sequences from Google Street View images. The results show that the model outperforms state-of-the-art convolutional networks in accuracy while using fewer parameters and less computation.
label: AI

title: Automatic Photo Adjustment Using Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Photo retouching empowers photographers to achieve dramatic visual impressions by artistically enhancing their photos through stylistic color and tone adjustments. However, this time-consuming and challenging task often requires advanced skills beyond the capabilities of casual photographers. While automated algorithms offer an appealing alternative to manual work, they face significant hurdles. Many photographic styles rely on subtle adjustments that depend on the image content and even its semantics. Furthermore, these adjustments are often spatially varying. Due to these characteristics, existing automatic algorithms are still limited and address only a subset of these challenges. Recent advances in deep machine learning have shown unique abilities to address complex problems that have resisted traditional machine algorithms for a long time. This motivated the exploration of deep learning in the context of photo editing. This paper explains how to formulate the automatic photo adjustment problem in a way suitable for this approach. It also introduces an image descriptor that accounts for the local semantics of an image. Experiments demonstrate that the deep learning formulation applied using these descriptors successfully captures sophisticated photographic styles. Notably, unlike previous techniques, it can model local adjustments that depend on the image semantics. Examples show that this yields results that are qualitatively and quantitatively better than previous work.
label: AI

title: Locating Tables in Scanned Documents for Reconstructing and Republishing (ICIAfS14)
Abstract: The pool of knowledge available to humanity depends on the source of learning resources, which can range from ancient printed documents to modern electronic materials. The rapid conversion of traditional library materials to digital form requires significant effort to maintain the format and appearance of electronic documents as closely as possible to their printed counterparts. Many printed documents contain not only characters and their formatting but also associated non-text objects, such as tables, charts, and graphical objects. Detecting and preserving the format of these objects while reproducing them is a challenging task. To address this issue, this paper proposes an algorithm using local thresholds for word space and line height to locate and extract all categories of tables from scanned document images. Experiments conducted on 298 documents demonstrate that the algorithm achieves an overall accuracy of approximately 75% in detecting tables from scanned document images. Since the algorithm does not completely depend on rule lines, it can detect all categories of tables across a range of scanned documents with varying font types, styles, and sizes to extract their formatting features. Furthermore, the algorithm can be adapted to locate tables in multi-column layouts with minor modifications to the layout analysis. Processing tables with their existing formatting features significantly aids in reproducing printed documents for reprinting and updating purposes. |||

title: A Fuzzy Based Model to Identify Printed Sinhala Characters (ICIAfS14)
Abstract: Sinhala character recognition is challenging due to the round shapes of the characters. Traditional techniques struggle to achieve high accuracy for this language. This paper presents a fuzzy inference system approach that leverages the unique round shape of Sinhala characters. The system uses distance and intersection measurements from the center of each letter to extract features. Experiments on 140 instances of letters resulted in an overall accuracy of 90.7%, outperforming similar systems.
label: AI

title: Transformation Properties of Learned Visual Representations
Abstract: When an object moves relative to an observer, the image captured by the observer changes. This paper explores the theory of group representations to understand how visual representations should transform under scene motions. It demonstrates that any linearly transforming representation is equivalent to a combination of irreducible representations.  The paper also establishes a relationship between irreducibility and statistical dependency, showing that under certain conditions, irreducible representations are decorrelated. To address partial observability caused by perspective projection, the paper proposes using a latent representation that transforms linearly. The concept is illustrated with a model that recognizes rotating NORB objects using a latent representation of the 3D rotation group SO(3).
label: AI

title: AltecOnDB: A Large-Vocabulary Arabic Online Handwriting Recognition Database
Abstract: Arabic handwriting recognition is a challenging task due to the complex morphology of the language and the ambiguity inherent in the writing system. Existing systems often struggle with large vocabularies and variations in writing styles. This paper introduces AltecOnDB, a large-scale online Arabic handwriting database designed to address these challenges. The database covers 98% of possible Arabic word combinations, includes complete sentences with digits and punctuation, and features data collected from over 1000 writers. This rich and comprehensive database, with data available at sentence, word, and character levels, can facilitate the development of more robust and accurate online Arabic handwriting recognition systems.
label: AI

title: An Effective Semi-supervised Divisive Clustering Algorithm
Abstract: Cluster analysis, a fundamental data analysis tool, is gaining renewed importance with the massive generation of data across various fields. This paper proposes a Semi-supervised Divisive Clustering algorithm (SDC) that effectively clusters data. SDC first organizes data points using a minimal spanning tree. This tree structure is then transitioned to an in-tree structure and divided into sub-trees under the supervision of labeled data.  The algorithm is fully automatic, non-iterative, parameter-free, and robust to noise. It can detect irregularly shaped clusters, handle high-dimensional data, and accommodate diverse attributes. SDC's effectiveness is demonstrated on multiple datasets.
label: AI

title: Symmetry in Image Registration and Deformation Modeling
Abstract: This paper explores the role of symmetry in diffeomorphic registration of various data types, including landmarks, curves, surfaces, images, and higher-order data. By leveraging symmetry, the infinite-dimensional problem of finding correspondences between objects can be reduced, leading to compact representations of shape and spatial structure. The paper provides a theoretical framework linking the registration problem to geometric mechanics. Symmetry also plays a role in reducing the problem to the Lie algebra using particle relabeling symmetry. This allows for expressing the equations of motion purely in terms of the Eulerian velocity field. The paper outlines recent applications of symmetry reduction in jet-matching and higher-order discrete approximations of image matching. These applications highlight the potential of symmetry reduction to develop novel approaches for registering complex data types.
label: AI

title: Higher-order Spatial Accuracy in Diffeomorphic Image Registration
Abstract: This paper introduces a method for discretizing a cost functional used in image registration problems by deriving Taylor expansions for the matching term. The discretized cost functionals allow for computing minima without spatial discretization error, and the optimal solutions correspond to minimal energy curves in the space of k-jets. The paper demonstrates that the solutions converge to the optimal solutions of the original cost functional as the number of particles increases, with a convergence rate of O(h^(d+k)), where h is a resolution parameter. The benefits of this approach compared to traditional particle methods are illustrated using synthetic examples and real images.
label: AI

title: STT-SNN: A Spin-Transfer-Torque Based Soft-Limiting Non-Linear Neuron for Low-Power Artificial Neural Networks
Abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are gaining popularity for vision, classification, and inference tasks. However, training and classification of large-scale ANNs require significant computational resources, leading to interest in post-CMOS devices for energy-efficient implementations. This paper proposes a spin-transfer-torque (STT) device based on Domain Wall Motion (DWM) magnetic strip for efficiently implementing a Soft-limiting Non-linear Neuron (SNN). Unlike previous spin-based neurons that could only implement hard-limiting transfer functions, the proposed STT-SNN exhibits a continuous resistance change with varying input current, enabling soft-limiting neuron transfer function implementation. Soft-limiting neurons are preferred over hard-limiting ones due to their improved modeling capacity, leading to higher network accuracy and lower complexity.  The paper also presents an ANN hardware design using the proposed STT-SNNs and Memristor Crossbar Arrays (MCA) as synapses. The ultra-low voltage operation of the magneto metallic STT-SNN enables the programmable MCA-synapses, allowing for analog-domain weighted summation of input voltages at ultra-low voltage. Simulations and evaluations using an ANN for character recognition show that STT-SNNs achieve significantly lower energy consumption compared to analog and digital CMOS neurons.
label: AI

title: Facial Expressions recognition Based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
Abstract: Facial expression recognition is a rapidly growing area of computer research with numerous applications. The task is challenging due to factors such as facial occlusions, shape, illumination, and color variations. This paper proposes a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) methodology for distinguishing facial expressions under various conditions.  The method relies on the Eigenfaces technique using standard database images, addressing the difficulty computers face in identifying facial features and expressions.
label: AI

title: Fusing Color and Texture Cues to Categorize the Fruit Diseases from Images
Abstract: Fruit diseases cause significant economic and production losses in agriculture. This paper presents an image processing-based method for classifying fruit diseases. The approach involves three main steps: K-Means clustering for defect segmentation, extraction and fusion of color and textural cues from the segmented image, and classification using a multi-class Support Vector Machine. The method is evaluated using apple diseases as a test case, including apple scab, apple blotch, apple rot, and healthy apples. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed fusion scheme effectively supports accurate detection and automatic classification of fruit diseases.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Feature Learning with C-SVDDNet
Abstract: This paper investigates feature representation learning from unlabeled data using a single-layer K-means network. While K-means networks are simple, effective, and scalable, they can be unreliable in the presence of noise. To address this issue, the paper proposes a Support Vector Data Description (SVDD)-based feature learning algorithm that describes the density and distribution of each K-means cluster with an SVDD ball for more robust feature representation. The paper introduces a new SVDD algorithm called C-SVDD that centers the SVDD ball towards the mode of local density of each cluster, enabling efficient solution as a linear programming problem.  To incorporate spatial information, the paper proposes a global representation using a variant of the SIFT descriptor. The architecture is extended with multiple receptive field scales and pooling sizes.  Extensive experiments on various object recognition benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed C-SVDDNet method achieves comparable or better performance than state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Learning of Proto-object Representations via Fixations on Low Resolution
Abstract: While previous eye fixation prediction research relied on integrating low-level features to form a saliency map, recent studies have highlighted the importance of proto-object representations. This paper presents a deep network-based framework demonstrating that proto-object representations can be learned from low-resolution image patches from fixation regions. The use of low-resolution inputs is justified by the parallel nature of proto-object computation, human object perception at low resolution, and the ability to predict fixations on higher-resolution images from lower-resolution fixations. The proposed computational model extracts multi-scale image patches from eye fixation datasets, resizes them to low resolution, and feeds them into a hierarchical network. Layer-wise unsupervised feature learning reveals the emergence of proto-objects representing different object shapes. Visualizations indicate that these features are selective to potential objects in the scene and their responses contribute to accurate eye fixation prediction.
label: AI

title: Denoising autoencoder with modulated lateral connections learns invariant representations of natural images
Abstract: This paper investigates the impact of lateral connections between encoder and decoder layers in denoising autoencoders (dAEs). Lateral connections allow higher layers to focus on invariant representations by relieving the pressure on these layers to carry detailed information. The paper demonstrates that abstract invariant features can be translated to detailed reconstructions when these features modulate the strength of the lateral connection. Three dAE structures with modulated and additive lateral connections, and without lateral connections, are compared using real-world images. The experiments show that modulated lateral connections: improve the accuracy of the probability model for inputs, lead to representations with increasing invariance towards higher layers, and support the formation of diverse invariant poolings.
label: AI

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for joint object detection and pose estimation: A comparative study
Abstract: This paper explores the application of convolutional neural networks for jointly detecting objects in images and estimating their 3D pose. The paper identifies different feature representations of oriented objects and energies that enable a network to learn these representations. The choice of representation is crucial as object pose has a continuous structure while its category is discrete. The paper evaluates different approaches on the Pascal3D+ benchmark using Average Viewpoint Precision. It demonstrates that a classification approach on discretized viewpoints achieves state-of-the-art performance for joint object detection and pose estimation, significantly outperforming existing baselines on this benchmark.
label: AI

title: Learning Compact Convolutional Neural Networks with Nested Dropout
Abstract: Nested dropout was proposed as a method for ordering representation units in autoencoders by their information content without compromising reconstruction cost. However, this technique has only been applied to fully-connected autoencoders in unsupervised settings. This paper investigates the impact of nested dropout on convolutional layers in a CNN trained using backpropagation, exploring whether nested dropout can determine the optimal representation size for desired accuracy, task, and data complexity.
label: AI

title: Fully Convolutional Multi-Class Multiple Instance Learning
Abstract: Multiple instance learning (MIL) can reduce the need for costly annotation in tasks like semantic segmentation by relaxing the level of supervision required. This paper proposes a novel MIL formulation for multi-class semantic segmentation learning using a fully convolutional network. The goal is to learn a segmentation model from weak image-level labels. The model is trained end-to-end to jointly optimize the representation while disambiguating the pixel-image label assignment.  Fully convolutional training accommodates inputs of any size, eliminates the need for object proposal pre-processing, and provides a pixelwise loss map for selecting latent instances. The paper's multi-class MIL loss leverages additional supervision from images with multiple labels. The approach is evaluated through preliminary experiments on the PASCAL VOC segmentation challenge.
label: AI

title: Learning Deep Object Detectors from 3D Models
Abstract: Crowdsourced 3D CAD models offer a readily available source of synthetic training images for various object categories. This paper shows that augmenting the training data of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) with such synthetic data can improve performance, especially when real data is limited or mismatched to the target domain. While freely available CAD models capture 3D shape, they often lack realistic texture, pose, and background. The paper investigates DCNN's ability to learn without these cues, revealing surprising findings.  The analysis shows that when DCNNs are fine-tuned on the target detection task, they exhibit significant invariance to missing low-level cues. However, when pre-trained on generic ImageNet classification, they learn better with simulated low-level cues. The paper demonstrates that the synthetic DCNN training approach outperforms previous methods on the PASCAL VOC2007 dataset in few-shot scenarios and improves performance in domain shift scenarios on the Office benchmark.
label: AI

title: Semantic Image Segmentation with Deep Convolutional Nets and Fully Connected CRFs
Abstract: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance in high-level vision tasks such as image classification and object detection. This paper integrates DCNNs and probabilistic graphical models to address the task of pixel-level classification, also known as semantic image segmentation. The paper highlights that responses at the final DCNN layer are insufficiently localized for accurate object segmentation due to the very invariance properties that make DCNNs suitable for high-level tasks. To overcome this localization issue, the paper combines responses at the final DCNN layer with a fully connected Conditional Random Field (CRF). The resulting "DeepLab" system is able to localize segment boundaries with higher accuracy than previous methods. The method sets a new state-of-the-art on the PASCAL VOC-2012 semantic image segmentation task, achieving 71.6% IOU accuracy on the test set.  The paper demonstrates how these results are obtained efficiently through careful network repurposing and a novel application of the 'hole' algorithm for dense computation of neural network responses.
label: AI

title: Clustering multi-way data: a novel algebraic approach
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for unsupervised clustering of two-way (matrix) data by combining Sparse Subspace Clustering (SSC) and the t-product. SSC groups data points from multiple subspaces, while the t-product provides matrix-like multiplication for third-order tensors. The algorithm builds an "affinity" between data points using sparse self-representation, leveraging the t-product for greater flexibility. SSC is a special case of this method. The t-product allows for treating three-way arrays as matrices whose elements are n-tuples.  The framework embeds 2-D data into a vector-space-like structure called a free module, which retains many properties of complex inner-product spaces.  This allows for theoretical guarantees on the algorithm.  The paper shows that compared to vector-space counterparts, SSmC achieves higher accuracy and requires less preprocessing for image clustering problems. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated on the Weizmann face database, the Extended Yale B Face database, and the MNIST handwritten digits database.
label: AI

title: Attention for Fine-Grained Categorization
Abstract: This paper extends the work of Ba et al. (2014) on recurrent neural models for attention to less constrained visual environments, specifically fine-grained categorization on the Stanford Dogs dataset. The paper uses an RNN with the same structure but substitutes a more powerful visual network and performs large-scale pre-training of the visual network. Most work in attention models focuses on simpler or more constrained visual environments, while this work presents results for fine-grained categorization surpassing the state-of-the-art GoogLeNet classification model. The model learns to direct high-resolution attention to discriminative regions without spatial supervision, such as bounding boxes, and can discriminate fine-grained dog breeds even when given only an initial low-resolution context image and glimpses at faces and fur patterns. The model's end-to-end training approach is an advantage over other detection and recognition pipelines with hand-engineered components. While the model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance, further work is needed to fully leverage the sequential input.
label: AI

title: Training deep neural networks with low precision multiplications
Abstract: Multipliers are the most resource-intensive operators in digital implementations of deep neural networks. This paper trains state-of-the-art Maxout networks on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN datasets using three different formats: floating point, fixed point, and dynamic fixed point. The impact of multiplication precision on final error after training is assessed for each dataset and format. The findings show that very low precision is sufficient not only for running trained networks but also for training them. For example, Maxout networks can be trained with 10-bit multiplications. |||
label: AI

title: Occlusion Edge Detection in RGB-D Frames using Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: Occlusion edges, indicating depth changes in a scene, are crucial for many vision and robotic applications. While these edges can be extracted from depth data, obtaining them directly from images and videos would be highly advantageous. We propose a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to identify occlusion edges in images and videos, using both RGB-D and RGB inputs. By employing CNNs, we avoid the need for hand-crafted features, enabling automated isolation of occlusion edges and differentiation from appearance edges. In addition to quantitative occlusion edge detection results, qualitative results demonstrate the trade-off between high-resolution analysis and frame-level computation time, which is critical for real-time robotics applications.
label: AI

title: Multi-modal Sensor Registration for Vehicle Perception via Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Simultaneous utilization of multiple sensor information is essential for an automated vehicle's perception of its surroundings. Spatio-temporal alignment, or registration, of this incoming data is often required for analysis. The persistence and reliability of multi-modal registration are therefore crucial for the stability of decision support systems processing the fused data. LiDAR-video systems, commonly employed in driverless cars, exemplify the importance of maintaining registration between LiDAR and video channels to shared physical features. We propose a deep learning method that analyzes multiple channels of heterogeneous data to detect misalignment between LiDAR-video inputs. We tested numerous variations on the Ford LiDAR-video driving test data set, and the results will be discussed. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first presentation of multi-modal deep convolutional neural networks for dynamic real-time LiDAR-video registration.
label: AI

title: Half-CNN: A General Framework for Whole-Image Regression
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in image classification. The classification model can also be applied at the image or patch level for other tasks, such as object detection and segmentation. This paper proposes a whole-image CNN regression model, achieved by removing the fully connected layer and training the network with continuous feature maps. This versatile regression framework can be adapted to numerous applications. We demonstrate its effectiveness through two tasks: simultaneous face detection and segmentation, and scene saliency prediction. The performance of our model is comparable to other methods in these fields, despite using a smaller network. Notably, our regression model, trained on corresponding image/feature map pairs, does not require uniform input size unlike the classification model. Our framework eliminates the need for classifier design, which often involves manual intervention in model development. Moreover, it retains a strong connection to the classification network, offering insights into CNN structures.
label: AI

title: Activity Identification and Local Linear Convergence of Douglas--Rachford/ADMM under Partial Smoothness
Abstract: Convex optimization has become ubiquitous across various quantitative disciplines, including variational image processing. Proximal splitting algorithms have gained popularity for solving such structured convex optimization problems. Within this class of algorithms, Douglas-Rachford (DR) and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) are designed to minimize the sum of two proper lower semi-continuous convex functions, whose proximity operators are easily computed. This work aims to understand the local convergence behavior of DR (resp. ADMM) when the involved functions (resp. their Legendre-Fenchel conjugates) exhibit partial smoothness. Specifically, we show that when both functions (resp. their conjugates) are partly smooth relative to their respective manifolds, DR (resp. ADMM) identifies these manifolds in finite time. Furthermore, when these manifolds are affine or linear, we prove that DR/ADMM converges linearly locally. When J and G are locally polyhedral, the optimal convergence radius is shown to be expressed in terms of the cosine of the Friedrichs angle between the tangent spaces of the identified manifolds. These findings are illustrated with concrete examples and supported by numerical experiments.
label: AI

title: Contour Detection Using Cost-Sensitive Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Contour detection is addressed as a per-pixel classification problem for edge point identification. To facilitate this process, we leverage DenseNet, an efficient implementation of multiscale convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to extract informative feature vectors for each pixel. An SVM classifier is then used to accomplish contour detection. The key challenge lies in adapting a pre-trained per-image CNN model for generating per-pixel image features. We propose to base our approach on the DenseNet architecture to achieve pixel-wise fine-tuning, and then employ a cost-sensitive strategy to further improve learning with a small dataset of edge and non-edge image patches. In our contour detection experiments, we examine the effectiveness of combining per-pixel features from different CNN layers and achieve comparable performance to the state-of-the-art on BSDS500.
label: AI

title: Object Detectors Emerge in Deep Scene CNNs
Abstract: Recent advancements in visual processing architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and the availability of large labeled image databases (e.g., ImageNet, Places) have significantly accelerated progress in computer vision. A crucial aspect for continued advancement is understanding the representations learned by the inner layers of these deep architectures. Here we demonstrate that object detectors emerge naturally during the training of CNNs for scene classification. Since scenes are composed of objects, the CNN for scene classification automatically discovers meaningful object detectors, representative of the learned scene categories. With object detectors emerging as a byproduct of learning to recognize scenes, our work shows that the same network can perform both scene recognition and object localization in a single forward pass, without explicit training on object concepts.
label: AI

title: A New Way to Factorize Linear Cameras
Abstract: This work details the implementation of factorizing 3x4 projection matrices of linear cameras into their left matrix factors and 4x4 homogeneous central (also parallel for infinite center cases) projection factors. Any full row rank 3x4 real matrix can be factored into such basic matrices, which we refer to as LC factors. This factorization is further extended to multiple view midpoint triangulation, applicable to both pinhole and affine camera cases, based on these camera factorizations.
label: AI

title: Learning Activation Functions to Improve Deep Neural Networks
Abstract: Artificial neural networks typically employ a fixed, non-linear activation function at each neuron. We propose a novel form of piecewise linear activation function that is learned independently for each neuron using gradient descent. This adaptive activation function enables us to outperform deep neural network architectures composed of static rectified linear units, achieving state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10 (7.51%), CIFAR-100 (30.83%), and a benchmark from high-energy physics involving Higgs boson decay modes.
label: AI

title: A Stable Multi-Scale Kernel for Topological Machine Learning
Abstract: Topological data analysis offers a wealth of valuable information for studying vision problems. However, a theoretical connection to popular kernel-based learning techniques, such as kernel SVMs or kernel PCA, remains elusive. This work establishes such a connection by designing a multi-scale kernel for persistence diagrams, a stable representation summarizing topological features in data. We demonstrate the positive definiteness of this kernel and prove its stability with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance. Experiments on two benchmark datasets for 3D shape classification/retrieval and texture recognition show significant performance gains of the proposed method compared to an alternative approach based on persistence landscapes.
label: AI

title: Extraction of Salient Sentences from Labelled Documents
Abstract: We present a hierarchical convolutional document model with an architecture designed to support introspection of the document structure. This model allows us to leverage visualization techniques from the computer vision literature to identify and extract topic-relevant sentences. Additionally, we introduce a new scalable evaluation technique for automatic sentence extraction systems, eliminating the need for time-consuming human annotation of validation data.
label: AI

title: Learning the nonlinear geometry of high-dimensional data: Models and algorithms
Abstract: Modern information processing relies on the principle that high-dimensional data lies close to low-dimensional geometric structures. This paper revisits the problem of data-driven learning of these geometric structures, proposing two novel nonlinear geometric models for data representing "related" objects or phenomena. The first model, termed the metric-constrained union-of-subspaces (MC-UoS) model, bridges the gap between the subspace model and the union-of-subspaces model. The second model, suitable for data drawn from a mixture of nonlinear manifolds, generalizes the kernel subspace model and is named the metric-constrained kernel union-of-subspaces (MC-KUoS) model. The main contributions of this paper include: first, the motivation and formalization of MC-UoS and MC-KUoS learning; second, the development of algorithms for efficiently learning an MC-UoS or an MC-KUoS underlying data of interest; third, the extension of these algorithms to handle missing data; and lastly, the presentation of numerical experiments involving both synthetic and real data, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed geometric models and learning algorithms compared to existing approaches. These experiments also clarify the connections between this work and the literature on (subspace and kernel k-means) clustering.
label: AI

title: Striving for Simplicity: The All Convolutional Net
Abstract: Most contemporary convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used for object recognition share similar principles: alternating convolution and max-pooling layers followed by a limited number of fully connected layers. We re-evaluate the state of the art for object recognition from small images using convolutional networks, questioning the necessity of various components within the pipeline. We find that max-pooling can be replaced with a convolutional layer with increased stride without compromising accuracy on multiple image recognition benchmarks. Based on this finding, and building upon other recent work on simple network structures, we propose a new architecture that consists solely of convolutional layers and achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance on several object recognition datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet). To analyze the network, we introduce a new variant of the "deconvolution approach" for visualizing features learned by CNNs, applicable to a broader range of network structures compared to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Mixture of Parts Revisited: Expressive Part Interactions for Pose Estimation
Abstract: Part-based models with restrictive tree-structured interactions for the Human Pose Estimation problem fail to account for many part interactions. Two prominent examples of such unhandled interactions are self-occlusion among parts and confusion in localizing non-adjacent symmetric parts. By efficiently addressing self-occlusion, we significantly improve the performance of the basic Mixture of Parts model, particularly for uncommon poses. Through a combination of two complementary trees, we mitigate confusion in symmetric limb localization, enhancing performance across all parts, albeit at the cost of doubling the running time. Finally, we demonstrate that combining both solutions improves the overall results. We report results equivalent to the state-of-the-art on two standard datasets, achieved in significantly less time than the best performing part-based model due to the preserved tree-structured interactions and part-level modeling of the base Mixture of Parts model.
label: AI

title: Bi-directional Shape Correspondences (BSC): A Novel Technique for 2-d Shape Warping in Quadratic Time?
Abstract: We propose Bidirectional Shape Correspondence (BSC) as a potential improvement upon the well-known shape contexts (SC) framework. Our proposals stem from the observation that the SC framework enforces a one-to-one correspondence between sample points, leading to two potential drawbacks. First, this limitation prevents the framework from benefiting from advantageous many-to-many matching between points on the two shapes being compared. Second, this necessitates the use of the Hungarian algorithm, which unfortunately requires cubic time. While the dynamic-space-warping dynamic programming algorithm offers a standard solution to the first problem, it demands quintic time for general multi-contour shapes, and w times quadratic time for single-contour shapes, even after an heuristic search window of width w has been selected. Therefore, in this work, we propose a simple method for computing "many-to-many" correspondences for the class of all 2-D shapes in quadratic time. Our approach explicitly allows each point on the first shape to choose a best match on the second shape, and vice versa. We also introduce the use of data-clustering techniques to address the outliers problem, which, from another perspective, can be viewed as autonomous, rather than pre-computed, sampling of shape boundary.
label: AI

title: SENNS: Sparse Extraction Neural NetworkS for Feature Extraction
Abstract: Drawing inspiration from optimization theory, artificial neural networks (ANN), graph embeddings, and sparse representations, I present a novel technique called SENNS (Sparse Extraction Neural NetworkS) to address the feature extraction problem. This method leverages (preferably deep) ANNs to project input attribute vectors to an output space where pairwise distances are maximized for vectors belonging to different classes but minimized for those belonging to the same class, while simultaneously enforcing sparsity on the ANN outputs. The resulting vectors from the projection can then be used as features in any desired classifier. Mathematically, I formulate this method as the minimization of an objective function, which can be interpreted, in the ANN output space, as a negative factor of the sum of the squares of pairwise distances between output vectors belonging to different classes, added to a positive factor of the sum of squares of pairwise distances between output vectors belonging to the same classes, plus sparsity and weight decay terms. To derive an algorithm for minimizing the objective function via gradient descent, I utilize the multivariate version of the chain rule to obtain the partial derivatives of the function with respect to ANN weights and biases. I find that each required partial derivative can be expressed as a sum of six terms. Notably, four of these six terms can be computed using the standard backpropagation algorithm; the fifth can be computed through a slight modification of the standard backpropagation algorithm; while the sixth can be calculated via simple arithmetic. Finally, I propose experiments on the ARABASE Arabic corpora of digits and letters, the CMU PIE database of faces, the MNIST digits database, and other standard machine learning databases.
label: AI

title: Deep Captioning with Multimodal Recurrent Neural Networks (m-RNN)
Abstract: This paper presents a multimodal Recurrent Neural Network (m-RNN) model for generating novel image captions. The model directly models the probability distribution of generating a word given preceding words and an image. Image captions are generated by sampling from this distribution. The model comprises two sub-networks: a deep recurrent neural network for sentences and a deep convolutional network for images. These two sub-networks interact within a multimodal layer to form the complete m-RNN model. The effectiveness of our model is validated on four benchmark datasets (IAPR TC-12, Flickr 8K, Flickr 30K, and MS COCO). Our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we apply the m-RNN model to retrieval tasks for retrieving images or sentences, achieving significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods that directly optimize the ranking objective function for retrieval. The project page for this work is: www.stat.ucla.edu/~junhua.mao/m-RNN.html.
label: AI

title: Visualizing and Comparing Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved comparable error rates to well-trained humans on the ILSVRC2014 image classification task. To further improve performance, the complexity of CNNs is continuously increasing with deeper and larger architectures. While CNNs have demonstrated promising external classification behavior, understanding their internal workings remains limited. This work aims to gain insights into the internal workings of CNNs by probing their internal representations in two comprehensive aspects: visualizing patches in the representation spaces constructed by different layers and visualizing visual information retained in each layer. We further compare CNNs with varying depths, highlighting the advantages of deeper architectures.
label: AI

title: The local low-dimensionality of natural images
Abstract: We introduce a novel statistical model for photographic images, where the local responses of a bank of linear filters are described as jointly Gaussian, with zero mean and a covariance that varies slowly across spatial positions. We optimize filter sets to minimize the nuclear norms of matrices of their local activations (i.e., the sum of the singular values), promoting a flexible form of sparsity that is not tied to any specific dictionary or coordinate system. Filters optimized under this objective exhibit orientation and bandpass characteristics, and their responses display significant local correlation. We demonstrate that images can be reconstructed almost perfectly using solely estimates of the local filter response covariances, with minimal visual or MSE degradation from low-rank approximations of these covariances. This representation holds significant promise for applications such as denoising, compression, and texture representation, and may serve as a useful substrate for hierarchical decompositions.
label: AI

title: Deep metric learning using Triplet network
Abstract: Deep learning has emerged as a successful set of models for learning useful semantic representations of data. However, these representations are predominantly learned implicitly as part of a classification task. This paper proposes the triplet network model, designed to learn useful representations through distance comparisons. A similar model was introduced by Wang et al. (2014), specifically tailored for learning a ranking for image information retrieval. Here, we demonstrate, using various datasets, that our model learns a better representation than its immediate competitor, the Siamese network. We also discuss potential future use as a framework for unsupervised learning.
label: AI

title: Permutohedral Lattice CNNs
Abstract: This paper presents a convolutional layer capable of processing sparse input features. For image recognition problems, this enables efficient filtering of signals that do not lie on a dense grid (like pixel position) but rather on more general features (such as color values). The presented algorithm utilizes the permutohedral lattice data structure. The permutohedral lattice was introduced to efficiently implement a bilateral filter, a commonly used image processing operation. Its application allows for a generalization of the convolution type found in current (spatial) convolutional network architectures. |||
label: AI

title: In Search of the Real Inductive Bias: On the Role of Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
Abstract: Experiments reveal that a novel form of capacity control, distinct from network size, plays a crucial role in learning multilayer feed-forward networks. Drawing parallels with matrix factorization, we propose that this mechanism represents an inductive bias that sheds light on the workings of deep learning.
label: AI

title: Visual Scene Representations: Contrast, Scaling and Occlusion
Abstract: Representations, defined as approximations of minimal sufficient statistics that are maximal invariants to nuisance factors, are investigated for visual data subject to scaling and occlusion of line-of-sight. Analytical expressions for these representations are derived, revealing a connection, under specific assumptions, to commonly used computer vision features. This link elucidates the implicit conditions underlying these descriptors and suggests avenues for their improvement and generalization. This novel interpretation establishes connections to classical theories of sampling, hypothesis testing, and group invariance.
label: AI

title: Video (language) modeling: a baseline for generative models of natural videos
Abstract: We introduce a robust baseline model for unsupervised feature learning using video data. By learning to predict missing or extrapolate future frames from an input sequence, the model uncovers both spatial and temporal correlations, facilitating the representation of complex deformations and motion patterns. Inspired by the language modeling literature, our models are adapted to the visual domain by quantizing the space of image patches into a large dictionary. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach on both filling and generation tasks. Notably, we present the first evidence that such a model, trained on natural videos, can predict non-trivial motions over short video sequences.
label: AI

title: Automatic Discovery and Optimization of Parts for Image Classification
Abstract: Part-based representations have proven highly effective for image classification. Traditionally, learning these models has been treated as a two-stage problem. The first stage involves discovering informative parts using heuristics that promote part distinctiveness and diversity, followed by training classifiers on the vector of part responses. In this paper, we unify these stages by jointly learning image classifiers and a set of shared parts. An initial pool of parts is generated through random sampling and L1/L2 regularization is employed to select a suitable subset. All steps are driven by the same objective, namely the classification loss on a training set, eliminating the need for engineered heuristics. Additionally, we introduce the concept of "negative parts", intended as parts negatively correlated with one or more classes. These negative parts complement parts discovered by other methods, which solely focus on positive correlations.
label: AI

title: An Analysis of Unsupervised Pre-training in Light of Recent Advances
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks excel at object recognition due to recent advancements like rectified linear units (ReLUs), data augmentation, dropout, and large labeled datasets. While unsupervised data has been proposed as an avenue for performance enhancement, it is not employed by state-of-the-art methods, prompting the question: Is unsupervised pre-training still beneficial given recent advances? If so, under what circumstances? We address this question in three parts: 1) We develop an unsupervised method incorporating ReLUs and contemporary unsupervised regularization techniques. 2) We analyze the benefits of unsupervised pre-training compared to data augmentation and dropout on CIFAR-10 while varying the ratio of unsupervised to supervised samples. 3) We validate our findings on STL-10. Our findings reveal that unsupervised pre-training, as anticipated, proves advantageous when the ratio of unsupervised to supervised samples is high, but surprisingly, hinders performance when this ratio is low. Furthermore, we achieve near state-of-the-art performance on STL-10 using unsupervised pre-training with additional color augmentation.
label: AI

title: Training Deep Neural Networks on Noisy Labels with Bootstrapping
Abstract: Current cutting-edge deep learning systems for visual object recognition and detection rely solely on supervised training with regularization techniques such as dropout to prevent overfitting. Performance hinges critically on the availability of labeled examples, with labels assumed to be unambiguous and accurate. However, this assumption often fails to hold. For instance, in recognition, class labels may be missing; in detection, objects within the image may not be localized; and in general, labeling can be subjective. In this paper, we propose a generic approach for handling noisy and incomplete labeling by incorporating a notion of consistency into the prediction objective. We consider a prediction consistent if the same prediction is made given similar percepts, where similarity is measured between deep network features computed from the input data. Experimental results demonstrate the substantial robustness of our approach to label noise on diverse datasets. On MNIST handwritten digits, we show robustness to label corruption. On the Toronto Face Database, our model effectively handles subjective labels in emotion recognition, achieving state-of-the-art results and benefiting from unlabeled face images without requiring any method modification. On the ILSVRC2014 detection challenge data, we demonstrate the applicability of our approach to very deep networks, high-resolution images, and structured outputs, leading to improved scalable detection.
label: AI

title: Discovering Hidden Factors of Variation in Deep Networks
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success due to its ability to learn useful features for tasks like classification. However, less attention has been paid to learning factors of variation beyond the classification signal. By augmenting autoencoders with simple regularization terms during training, we demonstrate that standard deep architectures can discover and explicitly represent factors of variation beyond those relevant for categorization. We introduce a cross-covariance penalty (XCov) as a method to disentangle factors such as handwriting style for digits and subject identity in faces. We validate this approach on the MNIST handwritten digit database, the Toronto Faces Database (TFD), and the Multi-PIE dataset by generating manipulated instances of the data. Moreover, we demonstrate the ability of these deep networks to extrapolate "hidden" variation in the supervised signal.
label: AI

title: Visual Instance Retrieval with Deep Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the suitability of convolutional network (ConvNet) based image representations for visual instance retrieval. Beyond the choice of convolutional layers, we propose an efficient pipeline leveraging multi-scale schemes to extract local features, explicitly accounting for geometric invariance, i.e., positions, scales, and spatial consistency. Our experiments using five standard image retrieval datasets demonstrate that generic ConvNet image representations can outperform other state-of-the-art methods when extracted appropriately.
label: AI

title: Self-informed neural network structure learning
Abstract: We address the problem of large-scale, multi-label visual recognition with a vast number of potential classes. We propose a method for augmenting a trained neural network classifier with auxiliary capacity, designed to significantly enhance an already high-performing model while minimally impacting its computational footprint. By leveraging the network's predictions as a descriptor for assessing visual similarity, we define a partitioning of the label space into groups of visually similar entities. We then augment the network with auxiliary hidden layer pathways connected solely to these groups of label units. We report a substantial improvement in mean average precision on a large-scale object recognition task with the augmented model, while increasing the number of multiply-adds by less than 3%.
label: AI

title: Speeding-up Convolutional Neural Networks Using Fine-tuned CP-Decomposition
Abstract: We propose a simple two-step approach for accelerating convolution layers within large convolutional neural networks, based on tensor decomposition and discriminative fine-tuning. Given a layer, we employ non-linear least squares to compute a low-rank CP-decomposition of the 4D convolution kernel tensor into a sum of a small number of rank-one tensors. In the second step, this decomposition replaces the original convolutional layer with a sequence of four convolutional layers with small kernels. After this replacement, the entire network is fine-tuned on the training data using standard backpropagation. We evaluate this approach on two CNNs and demonstrate its competitiveness with previous methods, achieving higher CPU speedups at the cost of lower accuracy drops for the smaller network. Specifically, for the 36-class character classification CNN, our approach yields an 8.5x CPU speedup of the entire network with only a minor accuracy drop (1% from 91% to 90%). For the standard ImageNet architecture (AlexNet), the approach accelerates the second convolution layer by a factor of 4x at the cost of a 1% increase in overall top-5 classification error.
label: AI

title: Fracking Deep Convolutional Image Descriptors
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for learning local image descriptors in a discriminative manner. We explore a Siamese architecture of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), employing a Hinge embedding loss on the L2 distance between descriptors. Since a Siamese architecture utilizes pairs rather than single image patches for training, there exists a large number of positive samples and an exponential number of negative samples. We propose to explore this space using stochastic sampling of the training set, coupled with an aggressive mining strategy over both positive and negative samples, which we term "fracking". We conduct a thorough evaluation of the architecture hyper-parameters and demonstrate significant performance gains compared to both standard CNN learning strategies, handcrafted image descriptors like SIFT, and state-of-the-art learned descriptors: up to 2.5x vs SIFT and 1.5x vs the state-of-the-art in terms of the area under the curve (AUC) of the Precision-Recall curve.

title: Score Function Features for Discriminative Learning
Abstract: Feature learning forms the foundation for tackling challenging learning problems in domains such as speech, computer vision, and natural language processing. In this paper, we introduce a novel class of matrix and tensor-valued features, which can be pre-trained using unlabeled samples. We present efficient algorithms for extracting discriminative information, given these pre-trained features and labeled samples for any related task. Our class of features is based on higher-order score functions, capturing local variations in the probability density function of the input. We establish a theoretical framework to characterize the nature of discriminative information that can be extracted from score-function features when used in conjunction with labeled samples. We employ efficient spectral decomposition algorithms (on matrices and tensors) for extracting discriminative components. The advantage of using tensor-valued features lies in their ability to extract richer discriminative information in the form of overcomplete representations. Thus, we present a novel framework for employing generative models of the input for discriminative learning.

title: Cauchy Principal Component Analysis
Abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), widely used in machine learning, text mining, and computer vision, is vulnerable to noise of large magnitude when based on a Gaussian noise model. PCA methods relying on Laplace noise assumptions cannot effectively handle dense noise. In this paper, we propose Cauchy Principal Component Analysis (Cauchy PCA), a simple yet highly effective PCA method robust to various types of noise. We utilize the Cauchy distribution to model noise and derive Cauchy PCA under the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) framework with low-rank constraint. Our method can robustly estimate the low-rank matrix regardless of the noise characteristics, be it large or small, dense or sparse. We analyze the robustness of Cauchy PCA from a robust statistics perspective and present an efficient singular value projection optimization method. Experimental results on both simulated data and real applications demonstrate the robustness of Cauchy PCA to diverse noise patterns.

title: Pooled Motion Features for First-Person Videos
Abstract: This paper presents a novel feature representation for first-person videos. In first-person video understanding (e.g., activity recognition), capturing both overall scene dynamics (i.e., egomotion) and salient local motion observed in videos is crucial. We describe a representation framework based on time series pooling, designed to abstract short-term/long-term changes in feature descriptor elements. The core idea is to track how descriptor values evolve over time and summarize them to represent motion in the activity video. The framework is general, handling any type of per-frame feature descriptors, including conventional motion descriptors like histogram of optical flows (HOF) as well as appearance descriptors from more recent convolutional neural networks (CNN). Our experimental results confirm that our approach significantly outperforms previous feature representations, including bag-of-visual-words and improved Fisher vector (IFV), when using identical underlying feature descriptors. We also verify that our feature representation outperforms existing state-of-the-art features like local spatio-temporal features and Improved Trajectory Features (originally developed for third-person videos) when handling first-person videos. Multiple first-person activity datasets were tested under various settings to corroborate these findings.

title: Learning to Segment Moving Objects in Videos
Abstract: We segment moving objects in videos by ranking spatio-temporal segment proposals based on their "moving objectness": the likelihood of containing a moving object. In each video frame, we compute segment proposals using multiple figure-ground segmentations on per-frame motion boundaries. These proposals are then ranked using a Moving Objectness Detector trained on image and motion fields to detect moving objects and discard over/under segmentations or background portions of the scene. The top-ranked segments are extended into spatio-temporal tubes using random walkers on motion affinities of dense point trajectories. Our final tube ranking consistently outperforms previous segmentation methods in the two largest video segmentation benchmarks currently available, regardless of the number of proposals. Furthermore, our per-frame moving object proposals enhance the detection rate by up to 7% compared to previous state-of-the-art static proposal methods.

title: Simplified firefly algorithm for 2D image key-points search
Abstract: Human eyes initially search the field of view for points or areas possessing specific properties to identify an object. These properties are then used to recognize an image or object. This process can be used as a model for developing computer algorithms for image identification. This paper proposes the idea of applying the simplified firefly algorithm to search for key areas within 2D images. The proposed version of the firefly algorithm is evaluated on a set of input test images. Research results are presented and discussed to demonstrate the efficiency of this evolutionary computation method.

title: Py3DFreeHandUS: a library for voxel-array reconstruction using Ultrasonography and attitude sensors
Abstract: In medical imaging, there is a growing demand for real-time images with high quality for large anatomical structures. To address this need, we have developed a library that can replace, for specific clinical applications, more robust systems like Computer Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Our python library Py3DFreeHandUS is a package for processing data acquired simultaneously by ultra-sonographic systems (US) and marker-based optoelectronic systems. Specifically, US data enables visualization of subcutaneous body structures, while the optoelectronic system collects the 3D position in space for reflective objects, known as markers. Combining these two measurement devices allows us to reconstruct the real 3D morphology of body structures such as muscles, with significant clinical implications. This research work explores the different steps involved in obtaining a relevant 3D dataset, including system calibration procedures and quality assessment of the reconstruction.

title: Generative Modeling of Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be a powerful tool for discriminative learning. Recently, researchers have begun to investigate the generative aspects of CNNs to gain a deeper understanding of their learned representations and how to further improve them. This paper explores generative modeling of CNNs. The main contributions include: 1) We construct a generative model for the CNN in the form of exponential tilting of a reference distribution. 2) We propose a generative gradient for pre-training CNNs using a non-parametric importance sampling scheme, which is fundamentally different from the commonly used discriminative gradient, yet possesses the same computational architecture and cost. 3) We introduce a generative visualization method for CNNs by sampling from an explicit parametric image distribution. This visualization method can directly generate synthetic samples for any given node in a trained CNN using the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm, without requiring any additional hold-out images. Experiments on the challenging ImageNet benchmark show that the proposed generative gradient pre-training consistently improves the performance of CNNs, and the generative visualization method produces meaningful and varied samples of synthetic images from a large-scale deep CNN.
