title: Non-parametric PSF estimation from celestial transit solar images using blind deconvolution
Abstract: Context: Characterizing instrumental effects in astronomical imaging is crucial for extracting accurate physical information from observations. The measured image in a real optical instrument is typically represented by the convolution of an ideal image with a Point Spread Function (PSF). Additionally, the image acquisition process is contaminated by other noise sources (read-out, photon-counting). The problem of simultaneously estimating both the PSF and a denoised image is known as blind deconvolution and is ill-posed. Aims: We propose a blind deconvolution scheme that relies on image regularization. Unlike most methods presented in the literature, our method does not assume a parametric model of the PSF and can therefore be applied to any telescope. Methods: Our scheme utilizes a wavelet analysis prior model on the image and makes weak assumptions about the PSF. We exploit observations from a celestial transit, where the occulting body can be assumed to be a black disk. These constraints enable us to retain meaningful solutions for the filter and the image, eliminating trivial, translated, and interchanged solutions. Under an additive Gaussian noise assumption, they also enforce noise cancellation and prevent reconstruction artifacts by promoting the whiteness of the residual between the blurred observations and the cleaned data. Results: Our method is applied to synthetic and experimental data. The PSF is estimated for the SECCHI/EUVI instrument using the 2007 Lunar transit, and for SDO/AIA using the 2012 Venus transit. Results demonstrate that the proposed non-parametric blind deconvolution method can estimate the core of the PSF with comparable quality to parametric methods reported in the literature. Furthermore, incorporating these parametric estimations into the acquisition model yields a PSF that outperforms both parametric and non-parametric methods.

title: Automated Objective Surgical Skill Assessment in the Operating Room Using Unstructured Tool Motion
Abstract: Prior research on surgical skill assessment using intraoperative tool motion in the operating room (OR) has focused on highly structured surgical tasks like cholecystectomy. Moreover, these methods primarily considered generic motion metrics such as time and number of movements, which provide limited instructive value. In this paper, we developed and evaluated an automated approach for surgical skill assessment of nasal septoplasty in the OR. The obstructed field of view and highly unstructured nature of septoplasty hinder trainees from efficiently learning the procedure. We propose a descriptive structure of septoplasty encompassing two activity types: 1) brushing activity directed away from the septal plane, characterizing the consistency of the surgeon's wrist motion, and 2) activity along the septal plane, characterizing the surgeon's coverage pattern. We derived features related to these two activity types that classify a surgeon's level of training with an average accuracy of about 72%. The developed features provide surgeons with personalized, actionable feedback regarding their tool motion. |||

title: Data Representation using the Weyl Transform
Abstract: The Weyl transform provides a robust framework for data representation. Its coefficients correlate with the Walsh-Hadamard transform of multiscale autocorrelations, highlighting dyadic periodicity in signals as distinct features.  The Weyl transform exhibits significant symmetry under multiscale transformations, enabling compact yet discriminative representations through coefficient pooling. Its effectiveness is demonstrated in textured image classification.
label: AI

title: Semantic Part Segmentation using Compositional Model combining Shape and Appearance
Abstract: This paper tackles the challenging problem of semantic part segmentation for animals, where parts often share similar appearance and exhibit highly variable shapes. To overcome these challenges, the authors propose a mixture of compositional models to represent object and part boundaries, integrating edge, appearance, and semantic cues. They introduce a novel algorithm to learn this mixture for specific animal classes under diverse poses and viewpoints. Efficient inference is facilitated by a linear complexity algorithm utilizing dynamic programming. The method is evaluated on horses and cows using a newly annotated Pascal VOC 2010 dataset with pixelwise part labels, demonstrating effectiveness.
label: AI

title: Compressing Deep Convolutional Networks using Vector Quantization
Abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become the leading method for object recognition, achieving record-breaking performance in image classification and object detection. However, the vast number of parameters in deep CNNs creates a substantial storage burden, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained hardware. To address this, the paper explores information-theoretical vector quantization for compressing CNN parameters.  Vector quantization, particularly k-means clustering and product quantization, effectively compresses dense connected layers, achieving a good balance between model size and recognition accuracy.  The approach enables 16-24 times compression of the network with only 1% loss of accuracy on the ImageNet 1000-category classification task.

title: Fractional Max-Pooling
Abstract: Convolutional networks often employ spatial pooling, typically alpha times alpha max-pooling with alpha=2.  Max-pooling reduces hidden layer sizes by a factor of alpha, introducing translational and elastic distortion invariance. However, alternating convolutional layers with max-pooling can limit performance due to rapid size reduction and disjoint pooling regions. This paper introduces a fractional version of max-pooling where alpha can take non-integer values, allowing for stochastic construction of pooling regions. This fractional max-pooling reduces overfitting across various datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-100 without requiring dropout.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Learning of Spatiotemporally Coherent Metrics
Abstract: This research explores unsupervised feature learning from temporally coherent video data for image classification and detection tasks.  Leveraging the assumption that adjacent video frames contain semantically similar information, the authors train a convolutional pooling auto-encoder regularized by slowness and sparsity.  They establish a connection between slow feature learning and metric learning, demonstrating that the trained encoder can define a more temporally and semantically coherent metric for video data.
label: AI

title: Deep Structured Output Learning for Unconstrained Text Recognition
Abstract: The paper introduces a representation suitable for unconstrained word recognition in natural images, addressing the challenge of variable lexicons and word lengths.  It proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture incorporating a Conditional Random Field (CRF) graphical model, processing the entire word image as a single input.  The CRF unaries are provided by a CNN predicting characters at each position, while higher-order terms are generated by another CNN detecting N-grams.  Joint optimization of the model (CRF, character predictor, N-gram predictor) through backpropagation of the structured output loss enables multi-task learning, trained entirely on synthetic data. The resulting model surpasses character prediction alone on real-world text recognition benchmarks, setting a new standard for lexicon-independent systems. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in lexicon-constrained scenarios as well.  Generalization is demonstrated by experiments with random alphanumeric strings, showcasing its effectiveness even without a visual language model.

title: Minimizing the Number of Matching Queries for Object Retrieval
Abstract: To improve the efficiency of interest-point based object retrieval, researchers have focused on optimizing kNN-based feature matching. However, high-dimensional image features and the vast number of features stored in databases pose challenges. This paper proposes a complementary approach to indexing for faster retrieval by querying only the most promising keypoint descriptors, leading to linear runtime improvements. To mitigate the loss of query precision caused by reducing kNN queries, an image-level correspondence generation stage is introduced, independent of the underlying indexing structure.  Evaluation on various datasets using SIFT and binary descriptors demonstrates that reducing queried descriptors does not necessarily impact result quality, provided adequate measures are taken to increase query recall and MAP.

title: Contour Detection Using Contrast Formulas in the Framework of Logarithmic Models
Abstract: This paper leverages a new logarithmic model of image representation for edge detection. The model provides formulas for calculating the "contrast of a pixel," effectively producing a "contrast" image that corresponds to the "contour" or edge image.  This approach preserves the range of values and achieves high-quality contours for both high and low luminosity regions. The results are compared with those obtained using classical edge detection operators.

title: Image Enhancement Using a Generalization of Homographic Function
Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for gray-level image enhancement using point transforms.  A generalization of the homographic function is employed to define the transform function, leading to enhanced image quality.

title: Image enhancement using the mean dynamic range maximization with logarithmic operations
Abstract: This paper utilizes a logarithmic model for gray-level image enhancement. After introducing the model, the paper presents a new formula for mean dynamic range.  Two image transforms are proposed: one optimizes the mean dynamic range using logarithmic addition, while the other addresses positive and negative values using logarithmic scalar multiplication.  The results obtained through dynamic range optimization are compared with those achieved using classical enhancement methods like gamma correction and histogram equalization.

title: Gray Level Image Enhancement Using Polygonal Functions
Abstract: This paper proposes a gray-level image enhancement method based on point transforms, specifically employing interpolation functions represented by polygonal lines.  The interpolation nodes of these functions are determined based on the statistics of gray levels within the image.

title: Gray level image enhancement using the Bernstein polynomials
Abstract: This paper introduces an image enhancement method based on point operations using piecewise linear functions. The interpolation nodes for these functions are calculated utilizing Bernstein polynomials, leading to improved image quality.

title: Image Dynamic Range Enhancement in the Context of Logarithmic Models
Abstract: This paper addresses the question of whether a privileged representative exists for images captured under varying illumination or aperture settings, exploring the context of logarithmic image models.  The authors introduce two image transforms: one for optimal dynamic range enhancement and the other for mean dynamic range enhancement. Experimental results showcase the effectiveness of these transforms.

title: Decomposition-Based Domain Adaptation for Real-World Font Recognition
Abstract: The paper proposes a domain adaptation framework to address the mismatch between synthetic training data and real-world testing data, specifically focusing on font style recognition.  Due to the difficulty in obtaining real-world labeled font images, a large synthetic training corpus is leveraged to obtain effective features for classification.  This is achieved using a Stacked Convolutional Auto-Encoder adaptation technique, incorporating unlabeled real-world text images along with preprocessed synthetic data. The DeepFont method achieves over 80% accuracy (top-5) on a new large-scale labeled real-world dataset.

title: Towards Open World Recognition
Abstract: With advancements in classification models and computational power, visual recognition systems have found widespread applications. However, real-world recognition faces challenges such as dynamic datasets, continuous detection of novel categories, and the need for robust performance in the presence of unseen categories. This paper introduces the concept of Open World recognition, formally defining the problem and proving that thresholding sums of monotonically decreasing distance functions in linearly transformed feature space can balance open space risk and empirical risk. The paper extends existing open world recognition algorithms, presents an evaluation protocol, and introduces the Nearest Non-Outlier (NNO) algorithm for efficient model evolution. NNO incrementally adds categories, detects outliers, and manages open space risk. Experiments on ImageNet demonstrate the effectiveness of NNO on large-scale visual recognition tasks.

title: DeepID-Net: Deformable Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Object Detection
Abstract: This paper introduces deformable deep convolutional neural networks for generic object detection.  The proposed architecture includes a new deformation constrained pooling (def-pooling) layer that models object part deformations with geometric constraints and penalties. A novel pre-training strategy is introduced to learn feature representations suitable for object detection with strong generalization capabilities.  By varying network structures, training strategies, and key components in the detection pipeline, a diverse set of models is generated, significantly improving model averaging effectiveness.  The approach surpasses the state-of-the-art RCNN in terms of mean averaged precision on the ILSVRC2014 detection test set, achieving 50.3% compared to RCNN's 31%. It also outperforms the ILSVRC2014 winner, GoogLeNet, by 6.1%.  Detailed component-wise analysis through extensive experimental evaluation provides a comprehensive understanding of the deep learning object detection pipeline.

title: High Frequency Content based Stimulus for Perceptual Sharpness Assessment in Natural Images
Abstract: This paper proposes a blind approach to evaluating perceptual sharpness in natural images. While existing literature emphasizes various visual cues for sharpness detection, the authors focus on high-frequency content and local standard deviation as strong features for quantifying perceived sharpness.  Sharp image transitions are characterized by high-frequency content, while unsharp areas exhibit uniform intensity.  The approach leverages convolution with a high-pass filter to identify high-frequency content, using the resulting values as stimulus.  Local standard deviation is then used to weight the stimulus, incorporating the contribution of local contrast to form a sharpness map.  This sharpness map highlights sharper regions and enables the calculation of a perceived sharpness score.  The method's advantages lie in its simplicity, relying only on visual cues, and its ability to perform blind evaluation without training.  Experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in quantifying sharpness both within and across images, as well as in assessing blur-induced perceptual degradation.

title: Full-reference image quality assessment by combining global and local distortion measures
Abstract: Full-reference image quality assessment (FR-IQA) techniques compare a reference image and a distorted test image to predict the perceptual quality of the test image using an objective score.  FR-IQA evaluation relies on comparing objective scores with subjective scores obtained from human observers.  The paper argues that human visual system (HVS) processing involves both top-down (goal-driven search for local distortions) and bottom-up (spontaneous visual functions) mechanisms.  Based on this, the paper proposes that objective scores should be derived from a combination of local and global distortion measures.  Local distortion is calculated using gradient and contrast information, while global distortion is assessed using saliency map dissimilarity based on a bottom-up saliency model.  The proposed approach's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on six benchmark databases, showing competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods and achieving an overall performance improvement.

title: The Affine Transforms for Image Enhancement in the Context of Logarithmic Models
Abstract: The logarithmic model offers valuable tools for image processing.  This paper introduces an image enhancement method employing an affine transformation with logarithmic operations: addition and scalar multiplication.  Criteria for automatically determining processing parameters are defined using mean and variance calculated through logarithmic operations.

title: A Mathematical Model for Logarithmic Image Processing
Abstract: This paper introduces a new logarithmic mathematical model for image processing.  The gray-level set is represented by the bounded interval (-1, 1).  The paper defines two operations: addition <+> and real scalar multiplication <x>.  These operations transform the gray-level set into a real vector space.  Furthermore, a scalar product (.|.) and a norm ||.|| are introduced, converting the space into an Euclidean space of gray levels.  The paper extends these operations and functions for color images. Finally, the impact of various simple operations on an image is illustrated. |||

title: Color Image Enhancement In the Framework of Logarithmic Models
Abstract: This paper introduces a logarithmic mathematical model for color image processing. It uses the cube (-1,1)x(-1,1)x(-1,1) to represent the color space and defines addition and real scalar multiplication operations, turning the color space into a real vector space. By defining the scalar product and norm, the model becomes a (logarithmic) Euclidean space. The paper demonstrates the application of this model for color image enhancement and presents experimental results.

title: An Algebraical Model for Gray Level Images
Abstract: This paper presents a new algebraic model for gray level images, suitable for digital image processing. This model is particularly useful for images captured in improper light conditions (very low or high light levels). The vector space structure allows the illustration of image features by modifying contrast and luminosity. The proposed structure can also be applied for image enhancement. The general approach is illustrated with experimental results demonstrating image enhancement.

title: Iranian cashes recognition using mobile
Abstract: In today's economic societies, cash transactions are an integral part of daily life. People use cash for various purposes including shopping, services, entertainment, and banking. The frequent interaction with cash and the need to identify its monetary value poses a significant challenge for visually impaired individuals. This paper proposes a mobile phone-based approach to identify the monetary value of cash in images using image processing and machine vision techniques. While the developed approach is fast, it can recognize the value of cash with an average accuracy of approximately 95%. It can also overcome various challenges such as rotation, scaling, collisions, illumination changes, perspective, and others.

title: Are We Ready for Driver-less Vehicles? Security vs. Privacy- A Social Perspective
Abstract: Autonomous vehicles are currently one of the most discussed technologies in the Robotics Research Community. Despite significant technological advancements in recent years, a fully autonomous car remains a distant reality. This article explores the existing systems and discusses the potential of computer vision-based driving compared to LiDAR-based systems. It delves into privacy violations that might arise from autonomous driving, examining both technical and legal perspectives. Evidence and arguments suggest a negative correlation between efficient and accurate constraint satisfaction problem solutions in autonomous cars and user privacy preservation. This presents a difficult trade-off, as both safety and privacy are crucial considerations. The unavoidable need to address safety concerns creates significant privacy issues with potential adverse social and political implications.

title: A Robust Regression Approach for Background/Foreground Segmentation
Abstract: Background/foreground segmentation is a crucial process in image and video processing, with numerous applications. This paper proposes a segmentation algorithm specifically designed for text and line extraction in screen content. The algorithm leverages the fact that the background in each block typically varies smoothly and can be modeled well by a linear combination of smoothly varying basis functions. In contrast, foreground text and graphics introduce sharp discontinuities. The algorithm distinguishes between background and foreground pixels by attempting to fit pixel values in the block to a smooth function using a robust regression method. Pixels fitting well are considered background, while outlier pixels are considered foreground. This algorithm has been extensively tested on various images from HEVC standard test sequences for screen content coding, demonstrating superior performance compared to other methods, such as the k-means clustering-based segmentation algorithm in DjVu. This background/foreground segmentation can be applied in diverse applications including text extraction, separate coding of background and foreground for compression of screen content and mixed content documents, principle line extraction from palmprint images, and crease detection in fingerprint images.

title: IceCube-Gen2: A Vision for the Future of Neutrino Astronomy in Antarctica
Abstract: The recent observation of an astrophysical flux of neutrinos by the IceCube neutrino observatory marks a significant milestone in the burgeoning field of neutrino astronomy. The observed diffuse neutrino flux suggests a much higher level of hadronic activity in the non-thermal universe than previously believed, indicating promising opportunities for future discovery with larger neutrino observatories. This document outlines a vision for a substantial expansion of the current IceCube detector, named IceCube-Gen2. The goal is to instrument a $10\\,\\mathrm{km}^3$ volume of clear glacial ice at the South Pole, leading to significant increases in the astrophysical neutrino sample for all flavors. A detector of this scale would offer a rich physics program, aiming to identify the sources of astrophysical neutrinos, discover GZK neutrinos, and become a leading observatory in future multi-messenger astronomy programs.

title: Locally Scale-Invariant Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (ConvNets) have demonstrated remarkable performance on various visual classification tasks. However, most datasets, excluding ImageNet, are meticulously designed with objects well-aligned at similar scales. As data variation increases, the feature learning problem becomes more challenging, requiring models to learn invariances to specific appearance changes. Recent ImageNet results show that ConvNets can learn such invariances, producing highly discriminative features with sufficient data. This paper explores the potential for achieving greater discriminative features with fewer parameters and less data by incorporating invariances into the learning process. The paper presents a simple model that enables ConvNets to learn features in a locally scale-invariant manner without increasing the number of model parameters. Experiments on a modified MNIST dataset demonstrate that when faced with scale variation, building in scale-invariance allows ConvNets to learn more discriminative features with reduced overfitting.

title: Random Forests Can Hash
Abstract: Hash codes provide an efficient data representation, essential for managing the ever-increasing data volumes. This paper introduces a random forest semantic hashing scheme with information-theoretic code aggregation. It demonstrates, for the first time, how random forest, a technique renowned for its classification success along with deep learning, can be extended to large-scale retrieval. Traditional random forest fails to enforce consistency in hashes generated from each tree for the same class data, i.e., it does not preserve the underlying similarity, and lacks a principled approach for code aggregation across trees. The paper starts with a simple hashing scheme, where independently trained random trees in a forest act as hashing functions. It proposes a subspace model as the splitting function, demonstrating its ability to enforce hash consistency in a tree for data belonging to the same class. The paper also introduces an information-theoretic approach for aggregating individual tree codes into a single hash code, producing near-optimal unique hashes for each class. Experiments on large-scale public datasets showcase the proposed approach's significant outperformance over state-of-the-art hashing methods for retrieval tasks.

title: The Dirichlet-Bohr radius
Abstract: Let $\\Omega(n)$ denote the number of prime divisors of $n \\in \\mathbb{N}$ (counted with multiplicities). For $x\\in \\mathbb{N}$, define the Dirichlet-Bohr radius $L(x)$ as the optimal $r>0$ such that for every finite Dirichlet polynomial $\\sum_{n \\leq x} a_n n^{-s}$, the following inequality holds: $$ \\sum_{n \\leq x} |a_n|\nr^{\\Omega(n)} \\leq \\sup_{t\\in \\mathbb{R}} \\big|\\sum_{n \\leq x} a_n\nn^{-it}\\big|\\,. $$ This paper proves that the asymptotically correct order of $L(x)$ is $ (\\log x)^{1/4}x^{-1/8} $. Inspired by Bohr's vision, the proof establishes a connection between estimating $L(x)$ and classical Bohr radii for holomorphic functions in multiple variables. Furthermore, the paper proposes a general framework for translating various results on Bohr radii into results on Dirichlet-Bohr radii, and vice versa.

title: Efficient GPU Implementation for Single Block Orthogonal Dictionary Learning
Abstract: Dictionary training for sparse representations involves handling large datasets and complex algorithms, leading to computationally demanding implementations. SBO is an iterative dictionary learning algorithm based on constructing unions of orthonormal bases via singular value decomposition, representing each data item using a single best-fit orthobase. This paper presents a GPGPU approach for implementing SBO in OpenCL. It provides a lock-free solution ensuring full GPU utilization by adopting the map-reduce model for the sparse-coding stage and utilizing the Partitioned Global Address Space (PGAS) model for parallel dictionary updates. The resulting implementation achieves a favorable trade-off between algorithm complexity and data representation quality compared to PAK-SVD, the standard overcomplete dictionary learning approach. Numerical results demonstrate significant acceleration of the dictionary learning process.
label: AI

title: Discovering beautiful attributes for aesthetic image analysis
Abstract: Aesthetic image analysis involves studying and evaluating the aesthetic qualities of images. Current computational approaches to aesthetic image analysis either prioritize accuracy or interpretability. To achieve both accuracy and human interpretability, this paper advocates for the use of learned and nameable visual attributes as mid-level features. To this end, the paper proposes a method for automatically discovering and learning the visual appearance of attributes using the AVA database, which contains over 250,000 images with aesthetic scores and textual comments provided by photography enthusiasts. The paper provides a detailed analysis of these annotations and the context in which they were given. It then describes how these key components of AVA - images, scores, and comments - can be effectively leveraged to learn visual attributes. Finally, the paper demonstrates the successful application of these learned attributes in three areas: aesthetic quality prediction, image tagging, and retrieval.
label: AI

title: Boltzmann-Machine Learning of Prior Distributions of Binarized Natural Images
Abstract: Prior distributions of binarized natural images are learned using a Boltzmann machine. This study reveals a structure with two sublattices in the interactions. The nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor interactions exhibit distinct values, reflecting the unique characteristics of the three sets of images processed. Additionally, a longer-range, yet rapidly decaying, ferromagnetic interaction is observed in all cases at a larger spatial scale. The characteristic length scale of the interactions is universally up to approximately four lattice spacings $\\xi \\approx 4$. These results are obtained using the mean-field method, effectively reducing the computational time required for the Boltzmann machine. An improved mean-field method called the Bethe approximation yields the same results, as does the Monte Carlo method for small-size images. These findings reinforce the validity of the analysis and results. The paper also discusses relations to criticality, frustration, and simple-cell receptive fields.

title: Translating Videos to Natural Language Using Deep Recurrent Neural Networks
Abstract: Solving the visual symbol grounding problem has been a long-standing goal in artificial intelligence. Recent advancements in deep learning for natural language grounding in static images have brought the field closer to this goal. This paper proposes a unified deep neural network with both convolutional and recurrent structure to translate videos directly into sentences. Due to the scarcity of described video datasets and the limitations of existing methods applied to toy domains with small vocabularies, the proposed method leverages knowledge transfer from 1.2M+ images with category labels and 100,000+ images with captions. This allows for the creation of sentence descriptions of open-domain videos with large vocabularies. The approach is compared to recent work using language generation metrics, subject, verb, and object prediction accuracy, and human evaluation.
label: AI

title: Finding a sparse vector in a subspace: Linear sparsity using alternating directions
Abstract: Is it possible to find the sparsest vector (direction) within a generic subspace $\\mathcal{S} \\subseteq \\mathbb{R}^p$ with $\\mathrm{dim}(\\mathcal{S})= n < p$? This problem, a homogeneous variant of the sparse recovery problem, connects to sparse dictionary learning, sparse PCA, and various other problems in signal processing and machine learning. This paper focuses on a **planted sparse model** for the subspace, where the target sparse vector is embedded within an otherwise random subspace. Simple convex heuristics for this planted recovery problem provably break down when the fraction of nonzero entries in the target sparse vector significantly exceeds $O(1/\\sqrt{n})$. In contrast, the paper presents a relatively simple nonconvex approach based on alternating directions, which provably succeeds even when the fraction of nonzero entries is $\\Omega(1)$. This is, to the best of our knowledge, the first practical algorithm to achieve linear scaling under the planted sparse model. Empirically, the proposed algorithm also proves successful in more challenging data models, such as sparse dictionary learning.
label: AI

title: MatConvNet - Convolutional Neural Networks for MATLAB
Abstract: MatConvNet is a MATLAB implementation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The toolbox prioritizes simplicity and flexibility, exposing the building blocks of CNNs as user-friendly MATLAB functions. These functions include routines for computing linear convolutions with filter banks, feature pooling, and more. MatConvNet enables rapid prototyping of new CNN architectures while supporting efficient computation on CPU and GPU, facilitating the training of complex models on large datasets such as ImageNet ILSVRC. This document provides an overview of CNNs, their implementation in MatConvNet, and technical details of each computational block within the toolbox.

title: Highly Efficient Forward and Backward Propagation of Convolutional Neural Networks for Pixelwise Classification
Abstract: This paper presents highly efficient algorithms for performing forward and backward propagation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for pixelwise classification on images. In pixelwise classification tasks, such as image segmentation and object detection, surrounding image patches are fed into CNN for predicting the classes of centered pixels via forward propagation and for updating CNN parameters via backward propagation. However, forward and backward propagation were originally designed for whole-image classification. Directly applying them to pixelwise classification in a patch-by-patch scanning manner is highly inefficient due to significant overlaps between surrounding patches, resulting in redundant computation. The proposed algorithms eliminate all redundant computation in convolution and pooling on images by introducing novel d-regularly sparse kernels. This approach generates identical results to patch-by-patch scanning. Convolution and pooling operations with these kernels enable continuous memory access and efficient execution on GPUs. A fraction of patches of interest can be selected from each training image for backward propagation by applying a mask to the error map at the last CNN layer. The computational complexity remains constant with respect to the number of patches sampled from the image. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithms achieve over 1500 times faster forward and backward propagation compared to conventional patch-by-patch scanning. The speedup increases with the size of images and patches.

title: CITlab ARGUS for Arabic Handwriting

title: CITlab ARGUS for historical data tables

title: Automatic video scene segmentation based on spatial-temporal clues and rhythm
Abstract: With rapidly increasing computing power and data storage capacity, the potential for large digital video libraries is growing exponentially. Therefore, providing a convenient and efficient environment for video storage and retrieval, particularly for content-based searching similar to traditional text-based database systems, has become a primary focus of recent research efforts. This paper proposes a new automatic video scene segmentation method that leverages two key video features: spatial-temporal relationships and shot rhythm. title: Fixed Point Algorithm Based on Quasi-Newton Method for Convex Minimization Problem with Application to Image Deblurring
Abstract: Solving optimization problems with objective functions consisting of the sum of two convex functions has gained considerable interest in the context of image processing. This paper focuses on the scenario where a non-differentiable convex function, such as the total variation (TV) norm, is included in the objective function. Many variational models established in image processing exhibit this characteristic. The paper proposes a fast fixed-point algorithm based on the quasi-Newton method for solving this class of problems, and applies it to TV-based image deblurring. The novel method is derived from the quasi-Newton method and fixed-point algorithms based on the proximity operator, which have been extensively investigated recently. Utilizing the non-expansion property of the proximity operator, the paper further investigates the global convergence of the proposed algorithm. Numerical experiments on image deblurring problems with additive or multiplicative noise demonstrate the algorithm's superior computational efficiency compared to recently developed fixed-point algorithms. |||

title: Inexact Alternating Direction Method Based on Newton descent algorithm with Application to Poisson Image Deblurring
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of recovering images degraded by linear operators and Poisson noise, a critical task in astronomical and biomedical imaging. This approach is inspired by alternating direction minimization algorithms and Newton's method, aiming for a faster convergence rate. title: Combining the Best of Graphical Models and ConvNets for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: A two-module approach to semantic segmentation is presented, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graphical models. title: First order algorithms in variational image processing
Abstract: Variational methods in imaging have emerged as a versatile tool for tasks like denoising, deblurring, inpainting, segmentation, and optical flow estimation. These methods typically involve minimizing a functional that comprises a data fidelity term and a regularization functional. While the data fidelity term is often smooth and convex, most successful techniques utilize nonsmooth and convex regularization functionals, such as total variation and generalizations thereof. This paper provides an overview of methods currently developed for solving such variational problems, highlighting the use of splitting algorithms due to the specific structure of the minimized functional. It discusses recent results and computational studies comparing different methods and illustrating their success in applications.

title: A Study of Sindhi Related and Arabic Script Adapted languages Recognition

title: The application of the Bayes Ying Yang harmony based GMMs in on-line signature verification
Abstract: This paper presents a Bayes Ying Yang (BYY) harmony-based approach for non-linear signature verification using Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs). title: Descriptor Ensemble: An Unsupervised Approach to Descriptor Fusion in the Homography Space
Abstract: This paper introduces an unsupervised approach to feature matching that fuses various local descriptors in the space of homographies. Recognizing the smooth variation of homographies for correct feature correspondences across the spatial domain, the proposed method leverages the unsupervised nature of feature matching to select a good descriptor for each feature point. By integrating different descriptors in the homography space, both geometric coherence and spatial continuity among correspondences are considered through geodesic distances. This allows for mutual verification across descriptors, highlighting correct correspondences with high consistency. Subsequently, one-class SVM is applied to identify these correct correspondences, boosting the performance of feature matching. The approach's effectiveness is demonstrated through comprehensive comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches on four benchmarks of image matching.

title: A survey of modern optical character recognition techniques
Abstract: This report examines recent advancements in digital document recognition, particularly focusing on printed document imagery. title: Oriented Edge Forests for Boundary Detection
Abstract: This paper presents a simple and efficient model for boundary detection using a random forest classifier. The model combines efficient clustering of training examples based on local edge orientations and scale-dependent calibration of individual tree output probabilities. This approach outperforms published results on the challenging BSDS500 boundary detection benchmark and demonstrates significant advantages in terms of memory requirements and training time compared to structured forest models.

title: Optimizing Over Radial Kernels on Compact Manifolds
Abstract: This paper tackles the problem of optimizing over all possible positive definite radial kernels on Riemannian manifolds for classification. While kernel methods on Riemannian manifolds are becoming increasingly popular in computer vision, the number of known positive definite kernels remains limited, and most kernels require parameter tuning. The paper demonstrates that positive definite radial kernels on the unit n-sphere, the Grassmann manifold, and Kendall's shape manifold can be expressed in a simple form with parameters automatically optimized within a support vector machine framework. The benefits of this kernel learning algorithm are showcased on object, face, action, and shape recognition tasks.

title: A Framework for Shape Analysis via Hilbert Space Embedding
Abstract: This paper proposes a framework for 2D shape analysis using positive definite kernels defined on Kendall's shape manifold. Recognizing the nonlinearity of different shape representations, the proposed approach maps shapes onto Kendall's shape manifold to a high-dimensional Hilbert space where Euclidean geometry applies. This mapping is facilitated by a novel kernel on the manifold, proven to be positive definite. This kernel extends kernel-based algorithms developed for Euclidean spaces, such as SVM, MKL, and kernel PCA, to the shape manifold. The approach's effectiveness is demonstrated on shape classification, clustering, and retrieval tasks.

title: Kernel Methods on the Riemannian Manifold of Symmetric Positive Definite Matrices
Abstract: Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) matrices have become popular for encoding image information, with the geometry of the Riemannian manifold of SPD matrices proving crucial for many algorithms. However, existing methods often approximate the manifold locally with its tangent plane. This paper introduces a family of provably positive definite kernels on the Riemannian manifold of SPD matrices, inspired by kernel methods, mapping SPD matrices to a high-dimensional Hilbert space. These kernels leverage different metrics on the manifold, extending kernel-based algorithms developed for Euclidean spaces to the Riemannian manifold. The benefits of the approach are demonstrated on pedestrian detection, object categorization, texture analysis, 2D motion segmentation, and Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) segmentation.

title: Representing Data by a Mixture of Activated Simplices
Abstract: This paper introduces a new model that represents data as a mixture of simplices, geometric structures generalizing triangles. The paper provides a simple geometric understanding for learning simplicial structure efficiently, requiring data to be unit normalized. Under this restriction, building a model with simplices amounts to constructing a convex hull inside the sphere whose boundary facets are close to the data. These boundary facets are termed Activated Simplices. The dimensions of individual activated simplices are learned from the data, allowing for modeling of inhomogeneous data sources. The simplicial structure is bounded, suitable for modeling data with constraints. The method provides good reconstruction and regularization, supports nearest neighbor classification, and allows for realistic generative models. Its effectiveness is demonstrated on benchmark datasets, including 3D poses and digits.

title: An Experimental Evaluation of Machine-to-Machine Coordination Middleware: Extended Version
Abstract: The Internet-of-Things (IoT) vision encompasses seamless discovery, configuration, and interoperability of networked devices across various settings. As these applications become increasingly critical, middleware handling Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication and coordination must address fault tolerance and complexity while respecting resource constraints. This report focuses on configuration management and coordination of services in a M2M scenario. It compares two approaches: ZooKeeper, offering file-system abstraction and fault-tolerance, and the Devices Profile for Web Services (DPWS) stack with replicated services based on the Raft consensus protocol. The report shows that DPWS offers adequate performance for targeted applications while providing greater flexibility.

title: Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent on the Grassmannian for Robust Low-Rank Subspace Recovery and Clustering
Abstract: This paper presents GASG21 (Grassmannian Adaptive Stochastic Gradient for L2,1 norm minimization), an adaptive stochastic gradient algorithm for robustly recovering the low-rank subspace from a large matrix. In the presence of column outliers, the batch mode matrix L2,1 norm minimization with rank constraint problem is reformulated as a stochastic optimization approach constrained on the Grassmann manifold. Each observed data vector updates the low-rank subspace by taking a gradient step along the geodesic of the Grassmannian. To accelerate convergence, the algorithm adaptively tunes the step-size based on consecutive gradients. The paper demonstrates that with proper initialization, the K-subspaces extension, K-GASG21, robustly clusters corrupted data vectors into a union of subspaces. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real data showcase the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithms even with heavy column outliers corruption.

title: An Automatic Seeded Region Growing for 2D Biomedical Image Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes an automatic seeded region growing algorithm for cellular image segmentation. The algorithm first extracts Regions of Interest (ROIs) from the preprocessed image and automatically selects initial seeds based on these ROIs. The most representative seeds are then selected using a machine learning algorithm, followed by segmentation of the cellular image into regions corresponding to each seed. The aim of this approach is to automatically extract ROIs from cellular images, overcoming challenges such as explosion, under-segmentation, and over-segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's ability to improve segmented images and reduce noise compared to existing methods.

title: CITlab ARGUS for historical handwritten documents

The core algorithms of the system are based on multi-dimensional recurrent neural networks (MDRNN) and connectionist temporal classification (CTC). title: Region segmentation for sparse decompositions: better brain parcellations from rest fMRI
Abstract: Functional Magnetic Resonance Images (fMRI) acquired during resting-state provide insights into the brain's functional organization by measuring correlations between brain areas. Independent component analysis is the standard approach for estimating spatial components from weakly structured data like brain signal time courses. However, even with sophisticated priors, the results may not be sparse and often fail to separate spatial components into distinct brain regions. This work presents post-processing techniques that automatically sparsify brain maps and separate regions using geometric operations. The techniques are compared based on faithfulness to data and stability metrics, highlighting the superior stability of random walker segmentation over other threshold-based approaches.

title: Machine Learning for Neuroimaging with Scikit-Learn
Abstract: Statistical machine learning methods are increasingly employed for neuroimaging data analysis due to their ability to model high-dimensional datasets. Supervised learning is typically used in decoding or encoding settings to relate brain images to behavioral or clinical observations, while unsupervised learning can uncover hidden structures in images or identify sub-populations in large cohorts. This paper illustrates how scikit-learn, a Python machine learning library, can be used to perform key analysis steps in various functional neuroimaging applications.  Scikit-learn provides a comprehensive set of supervised and unsupervised statistical learning algorithms, offering a versatile tool for brain studies.

title: Edge Preserving Multi-Modal Registration Based On Gradient Intensity Self-Similarity
Abstract: Image registration is a challenging task in medical imaging, with accurate edge registration playing a crucial role in various clinical applications. The Modality Independent Neighbourhood Descriptor (MIND) demonstrates state-of-the-art alignment based on image self-similarity. However, it exhibits limitations in edge registration. This paper proposes a new registration method that incorporates gradient intensity and the MIND self-similarity metric. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of this method for edge registration tasks while maintaining MIND's performance for other image features and textures.

title: Towards Deep Neural Network Architectures Robust to Adversarial Examples
Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are highly vulnerable to adversarial examples, small well-designed perturbations at the input layer that can lead to misclassification. This paper examines the structure of adversarial examples and explores network topology, pre-processing, and training strategies to enhance DNN robustness. Experiments assess the removability of adversarial examples by introducing noise and pre-processing with denoising autoencoders (DAEs). While DAEs effectively reduce adversarial noise, stacking them with DNNs leads to new attacks with even smaller distortions. The paper proposes Deep Contractive Network, a model with a new end-to-end training procedure incorporating a smoothness penalty. This approach significantly increases robustness to adversarial examples without compromising performance. |||

title: An active search strategy for efficient object class detection
Abstract: This paper presents an active search strategy for object class detection that significantly reduces the number of classifier evaluations while maintaining high detection accuracy. The method exploits context and classifier scores to guide the search, enabling efficient exploration of the image and focusing on promising areas. Experiments on the SUN2012 dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves similar detection accuracy to evaluating all windows independently, but with a 9x reduction in evaluations.

title: Compact Compositional Models
Abstract: This paper explores the composition of experts for learning compact and interpretable representations from binary data. The authors argue that competitive interactions between experts are crucial for low-dimensional representations and propose a new composition rule that discourages experts from focusing on similar structures and penalizes opposing votes. They introduce a novel sequential initialization procedure based on oversimplification and correction. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach enables the learning of intuitive models.

title: A Novel Adaptive Possibilistic Clustering Algorithm
Abstract: The paper introduces an adaptive possibilistic c-means clustering algorithm, called Adaptive Possibilistic c-means. This algorithm automatically adapts all its parameters during execution, starting with an overestimate of the number of clusters. title: High-level numerical simulations of noise in CCD and CMOS photosensors: review and tutorial

The model incorporates photo-response non-uniformity, photon shot noise, dark current noise, offset noise, source follower noise, sense node reset noise, and quantization noise. title: EgoSampling: Fast-Forward and Stereo for Egocentric Videos

The method minimizes an energy function to obtain an optimal frame sampling strategy, resulting in more stable fast-forwarding. title: Road Detection by One-Class Color Classification: Dataset and Experiments

title: Deep Domain Confusion: Maximizing for Domain Invariance

title: Multi-Atlas Segmentation of Biomedical Images: A Survey
Abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive survey of multi-atlas segmentation (MAS), a widely used image segmentation technique in biomedical applications. title: Object Recognition Using Deep Neural Networks: A Survey

title: Candidate Constrained CRFs for Loss-Aware Structured Prediction

title: Memory vectors for similarity search in high-dimensional spaces
Abstract: This paper presents an indexing architecture for storing and searching high-dimensional vectors, drawing inspiration from statistical signal processing and decision theory. title: Object-centric Sampling for Fine-grained Image Classification

title: Road Detection via On--line Label Transfer

title: Real-Time Grasp Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks

title: Multi-Platform Generative Development of Component & Connector Systems using Model and Code Libraries

title: Cancer Detection with Multiple Radiologists via Soft Multiple Instance Logistic Regression and $L_1$ Regularization

title: Score Function Features for Discriminative Learning: Matrix and Tensor Framework
Abstract: This paper explores feature learning using a novel class of matrix and tensor-valued features, which can be pre-trained using unlabeled samples. title: Image quality assessment measure based on natural image statistics in the Tetrolet domain
Abstract: This paper presents a reduced reference (RR) image quality measure based on natural image statistics modeling. title: HyperSpectral classification with adaptively weighted L1-norm regularization and spatial postprocessing

title: Real-Time System of Hand Detection And Gesture Recognition In Cyber Presence Interactive System For E-Learning
Abstract: The advancements in multimedia technologies, coupled with the growth of the Internet and democratization of high bandwidth, have made E-learning a reality for learners in virtual classrooms distributed geographically. title: When Computer Vision Gazes at Cognition
Abstract: Joint attention, a fundamental and early-developing form of social interaction, relies on our ability to discern the objects that other people are looking at. While studies have shown that individuals can accurately identify whether another person is looking directly at them or away, little is known about our ability to discriminate third-party gaze directed towards objects that are further away, especially in unconstrained situations where the observer can move their head and eyes freely. This paper addresses this question by investigating both human psychophysics and a cognitively motivated computer vision model, capable of detecting the 3D direction of gaze from 2D face images. The combined analysis reveals several interesting findings: (1) Human accuracy in discriminating targets 8-10 degrees of visual angle apart is approximately 40% in a free-looking gaze task; (2) The ability to interpret gaze from different observers varies significantly; (3) This variability can be captured by the computational model; (4) Human performance significantly surpasses the current model. These results demonstrate the remarkable accuracy of human joint attention, given the computational challenges of the natural looking task. However, the gap between human and model performance, alongside the variability of gaze interpretation across different observers, calls for further exploration of the underlying mechanisms utilized by humans for this complex task.

title: Actions and Attributes from Wholes and Parts
Abstract: This paper investigates the importance of parts for action and attribute classification tasks. A part-based approach is developed by leveraging convolutional network features inspired by recent advances in computer vision. The part detectors are a deep version of poselets and capture parts of the human body under various poses. For action and attribute classification, holistic convolutional neural networks are trained and demonstrate that the addition of parts leads to superior performance for both tasks. Furthermore, the effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated by replacing an oracle person detector (the default in current evaluation protocols for both tasks) with a state-of-the-art person detection system.

title: Web image annotation by diffusion maps manifold learning algorithm
Abstract: Automatic image annotation, a challenging problem in machine vision, aims to automatically predict keywords for images captured in real-world scenarios. Many methods rely on visual features to calculate similarities between image samples, but these approaches are computationally expensive and require a large number of training samples to be stored in memory. To alleviate this burden, various techniques have been developed to reduce the number of features in a dataset. Manifold learning, a popular approach for nonlinear dimensionality reduction, is investigated in this paper. The Diffusion maps manifold learning method is employed to reduce the dimensionality of visual features. Extensive experiments and analysis on the NUS-WIDE-LITE web image dataset, utilizing different visual features, demonstrate the effective application of this manifold learning dimensionality reduction method for image annotation.

title: An Approach for Reducing Outliers of Non Local Means Image Denoising Filter
Abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive approach for non-local means (NLM) image filtering, named non-local adaptive clipped means (NLACM), to reduce the impact of outliers and improve denoising quality compared to traditional NLM. Outliers are typically neglected by computing the mean within a range defined by the mean and standard deviation. In NLACM, the median within the defined range is calculated based on statistical estimations of the neighborhood region of a pixel to be denoised. As the parameters of the range are independent of any additional input and rely on local intensity values, the approach is adaptive. Experimental results for NLACM demonstrate better estimation of true intensity from noisy neighborhood observations compared to NLM at high noise levels. The technique was verified for speckle noise reduction and tested on ultrasound (US) images of the lumbar spine, which serve as guidance for injection therapy in the treatment of lumbar radiculopathy. The proposed image denoising approach is believed to be novel and its efficiency is well justified through its superior performance in image restoration.

title: Linear optical demonstration of quantum speed-up with a single qudit
Abstract: Quantum algorithms play a significant role in quantum computation, not only for their potential to solve classically intractable problems but also for their contribution to understanding quantum physics. However, the origin of the power of quantum algorithms remains an open question. Non-classical correlation is considered the most plausible answer. This paper experimentally realizes a quantum speed-up algorithm on a four-level system using linear optical elements and demonstrates that even a single qudit is sufficient for designing an oracle-based algorithm that solves a model problem twice as fast as any classical algorithm. This algorithm can be generalized to higher-dimensional qudits with the same two-to-one speed-up ratio.

title: Nearest Descent, In-Tree, and Clustering
Abstract: This paper presents a physically inspired graph-theoretical clustering method that organizes data points into an attractive graph called In-Tree using a physically inspired rule known as Nearest Descent (ND). The ND rule selects the nearest node in the descending direction of potential as the parent node for each node, differing from the classical Gradient Descent or Steepest Descent. The constructed In-Tree is an excellent candidate for clustering due to its unique features and properties. The original clustering problem in the In-Tree is simplified to removing a limited number of undesirable edges from the graph. Importantly, these undesirable edges are easily identifiable in the In-Tree, either automatically or interactively, in contrast to the commonly used Minimal Spanning Tree and k-nearest-neighbor graph. The cluster number in the proposed method can be easily determined based on intermediate plots, and cluster assignment for each node is achieved by quickly searching for its root node in each sub-graph (also an In-Tree). The proposed method is extensively evaluated on both synthetic and real-world datasets. It is a density-based method but demonstrates significant differences and advantages compared to traditional methods. It is simple, efficient, reliable, and applicable to diverse datasets with varying shapes, attributes, and high dimensionality.

title: Bayesian Image Restoration for Poisson Corrupted Image using a Latent Variational Method with Gaussian MRF
Abstract: This paper addresses image restoration with a Poisson noise channel within a Bayesian framework. Poisson randomness can occur during the observation of low-contrast objects in imaging. This noise observation is often challenging to analyze theoretically. The formulation interprets the observation through the Poisson noise channel as a likelihood and estimates its bound using a Gaussian function with a latent variable method. A Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) is then introduced as the prior for the Bayesian approach, resulting in a Gaussian posterior distribution. The latent parameters in the likelihood and the hyperparameter in the GMRF prior are treated as hidden parameters, prompting the development of an algorithm to infer them using the expectation maximization (EM) framework with loopy belief propagation (LBP). Computer simulations confirm the algorithm's effectiveness and compare it to other image restoration frameworks.

title: Visual Causal Feature Learning
Abstract: This paper provides a rigorous definition of the visual cause of behavior that is broadly applicable to visually driven behavior in humans, animals, neurons, robots, and other perceiving systems. This framework generalizes standard accounts of causal learning to situations where causal variables need to be constructed from micro-variables. The Causal Coarsening Theorem is proven, enabling causal knowledge acquisition from observational data with minimal experimental effort. This theorem connects to standard inference techniques in machine learning that identify image features that correlate with, but may not cause, the target behavior. An active learning scheme is proposed to learn a manipulator function that performs optimal manipulations on the image to automatically identify the visual cause of a target behavior. Experiments based on both synthetic and real data illustrate the inference and learning algorithms.

title: Deep Visual-Semantic Alignments for Generating Image Descriptions
Abstract: This paper presents a model for generating natural language descriptions of images and their regions. The approach utilizes datasets of images and their sentence descriptions to learn about the inter-modal correspondences between language and visual data. The alignment model is based on a novel combination of Convolutional Neural Networks over image regions, bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks over sentences, and a structured objective that aligns the two modalities through a multimodal embedding. A Multimodal Recurrent Neural Network architecture is described that uses the inferred alignments to generate novel descriptions of image regions. The alignment model achieves state-of-the-art results in retrieval experiments on Flickr8K, Flickr30K, and MSCOCO datasets. The generated descriptions significantly outperform retrieval baselines for both full images and a new dataset of region-level annotations.

title: Adjusted least squares fitting of algebraic hypersurfaces
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of fitting a set of points in Euclidean space using an algebraic hypersurface. It assumes that points on a true hypersurface, described by a polynomial equation, are corrupted by zero-mean independent Gaussian noise. The goal is to estimate the coefficients of the true polynomial equation. The adjusted least squares estimator accounts for the bias present in the ordinary least squares estimator. This estimator is based on constructing a quasi-Hankel matrix, which is a bias-corrected matrix of moments. For cases with unknown noise variance, the estimator is defined as a solution to a polynomial eigenvalue problem. The paper presents new results on the invariance properties of the adjusted least squares estimator and an improved algorithm for computing the estimator for an arbitrary set of monomials in the polynomial equation.

title: Generalized Singular Value Thresholding
Abstract: This work investigates the Generalized Singular Value Thresholding (GSVT) operator Prox_{g}^{σ}(⋅), which minimizes the sum of a nonconvex function g defined on the singular values of X and the squared Frobenius norm of the difference between X and B. The paper proves that GSVT can be obtained by applying the proximal operator of g (denoted as Prox_g(⋅)) on the singular values, as Prox_g(⋅) is monotone when g is lower bounded. A general solver is proposed for finding Prox_g(b) for any b≥0, provided that the nonconvex function g satisfies certain conditions. This solver is applicable to many popular nonconvex surrogate functions such as the lp-norm (0<p<1) or the l0-norm. GSVT significantly generalizes the known Singular Value Thresholding (SVT), a fundamental subroutine in many convex low-rank minimization methods. The nonconvex low-rank minimization problem can be solved by using GSVT instead of SVT.

title: Risk Estimation Without Using Stein's Lemma -- Application to Image Denoising
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of image denoising in additive white noise without imposing restrictive assumptions on its statistical distribution. In recent literature, specific noise distributions have been considered, leading to the development of corresponding optimal denoising techniques. One successful approach for denoising relies on the concept of unbiased risk estimation, which provides a useful substitute for the mean-square error. For additive white Gaussian noise contamination, the risk estimation procedure relies on Stein's lemma. Advanced wavelet-based denoising techniques, which are essentially nonlinear, have been developed with the help of this lemma. The paper demonstrates that for linear, shift-invariant denoisers, unbiased risk estimates of the mean-square error can be obtained without using Stein's lemma. This leads to an unbiased risk estimator that is agnostic to the statistical distribution of the noise. As a proof of concept, the new methodology is used to optimize the parameters of a simple Gaussian smoother. By locally adapting the parameters of the Gaussian smoother, a shift-variant smoother is obtained. This smoother exhibits denoising performance, quantified by peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) improvement, that is competitive with much more sophisticated methods reported in the literature. The proposed solution exhibits significant parallelism, which is exploited in a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) implementation.

title: Subspace based low rank and joint sparse matrix recovery
Abstract: This paper focuses on the recovery of a low-rank and jointly sparse matrix from undersampled measurements of its columns. This problem is highly relevant in the recovery of dynamic MRI data with high spatio-temporal resolution, where each column of the matrix corresponds to a frame in the image time series. The matrix is highly low-rank due to the strong correlation between frames. Similarly, the non-zero locations of the matrix in appropriate transform/frame domains (e.g., wavelet, gradient) are roughly the same across different frames. The superset of the support can be safely assumed to be jointly sparse. Unlike the classical multiple measurement vector (MMV) setup that measures all snapshots using the same matrix, this approach measures each snapshot using a different measurement matrix. It is shown that this approach reduces the total number of measurements, especially when the rank of the matrix is much smaller than its sparsity. Experiments in the context of dynamic imaging show that this approach is highly beneficial in achieving free-breathing cardiac MRI.

title: Learning Multi-target Tracking with Quadratic Object Interactions
Abstract: This paper describes a model for multi-target tracking based on associating collections of candidate detections across video frames. To model pairwise interactions between different tracks, such as suppression of overlapping tracks and contextual cues about co-occurrence of different objects, a standard min-cost flow objective is augmented with quadratic terms between detection variables. The model parameters are learned using structured prediction and a loss function that approximates the multi-target tracking accuracy. Two approaches are evaluated for finding an optimal set of tracks under the model objective: an LP relaxation and a novel greedy extension to dynamic programming that handles pairwise interactions. The greedy algorithm achieves performance equivalent to the LP relaxation while being 2-7x faster than a commercial solver. The resulting model with learned parameters surpasses existing methods across several categories on the KITTI tracking benchmark.
label: AI

title: CoMIC: Good features for detection and matching at object boundaries
Abstract: Feature or interest points typically rely on information aggregation in 2D patches, which becomes unstable at object boundaries when objects move against significantly varying backgrounds. Level or iso-intensity curves are much more stable under such conditions, especially the longer ones. This paper identifies stable portions on long iso-curves and detects corners on them. The iso-curve associated with a corner is used to discard portions from the background and improve matching. These CoMIC (Corners on Maximally-stable Iso-intensity Curves) points yield superior results at object boundary regions compared to state-of-the-art detectors, while performing comparably at interior regions. This is demonstrated in exhaustive matching experiments for both boundary and non-boundary regions in applications such as stereo and point tracking for structure from motion in video sequences.

title: Background Modelling using Octree Color Quantization
Abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm for detecting foreground objects in a video based on the assumption that the most frequently occurring color in a video or a region of a video represents the background. Detecting foreground objects is complex due to factors like swaying trees, moving background objects, and lighting changes. Many existing solutions rely heavily on expensive floating-point operations to address these complexities. This paper utilizes a data structure called an Octree, which is implemented using only binary operations. Traditionally, octrees were used for color quantization, but this paper uses it to store the most frequently occurring colors in a video. For the initial frames of the video, an Octree is constructed using all colors in each frame. The trees are then pruned by removing nodes below a certain height, and the leaf nodes are assigned a color dependent on the topological path from that node to its parent. Two leaf nodes in different octrees with the same topological path to the root represent the same color. These individual trees are then merged into a single tree, retaining only nodes with the most common topological path to the root among all trees. The colors represented by the leaf nodes in the resulting tree are the most frequently occurring colors in the initial video frames. Any color in an incoming frame that is not close to any of the colors represented by the leaf nodes of the merged tree is considered part of a foreground object. Since an Octree is constructed using binary operations, it is significantly faster compared to other leading algorithms.
label: AI

title: Person Re-identification by Saliency Learning
Abstract: Human eyes can recognize person identities based on small salient regions, indicating that human saliency is distinctive and reliable for pedestrian matching across disjoint camera views. However, this valuable information is often overlooked when computing similarities of pedestrian images using existing approaches. Inspired by user study results on human perception of human saliency, this paper proposes a novel perspective for person re-identification based on learning human saliency and matching saliency distribution. The proposed saliency learning and matching framework consists of four steps: (1) To address misalignment caused by drastic viewpoint changes and pose variations, adjacency-constrained patch matching is applied to build dense correspondence between image pairs. (2) Two alternative methods, K-Nearest Neighbors and One-class SVM, are proposed to estimate a saliency score for each image patch, highlighting distinctive features without using identity labels in the training procedure. (3) Saliency matching is proposed based on patch matching. Matching patches with inconsistent saliency incurs a penalty, and images of the same identity are recognized by minimizing the saliency matching cost. (4) Saliency matching is tightly integrated with patch matching in a unified structural RankSVM learning framework. The effectiveness of this approach is validated on the VIPeR and CUHK01 datasets. The proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art person re-identification methods on both datasets. |||

title: Deep Neural Networks are Easily Fooled: High Confidence Predictions for Unrecognizable Images
Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are increasingly achieving state-of-the-art performance in various pattern recognition tasks, particularly in visual classification. Although DNNs now exhibit near-human performance in image classification, discrepancies between human and computer vision persist.  Recent research revealed that imperceptible modifications to an image can drastically alter a DNN's classification, for example, misidentifying a lion as a library. This study further demonstrates that generating images indistinguishable from random noise can lead DNNs to confidently identify these images as recognizable objects with a 99.99% certainty, such as labeling random noise as a lion. This phenomenon is achieved by utilizing evolutionary algorithms or gradient ascent to discover images that DNNs, trained on datasets like ImageNet or MNIST, classify with high confidence as belonging to specific classes. The study identifies these images as "fooling images" (more broadly, fooling examples), highlighting the presence of intriguing distinctions between human vision and current DNNs, and prompting further exploration of the generality of DNN computer vision.

title: A higher homotopic extension of persistent (co)homology
Abstract: This article presents a unique structure with homological properties within the framework of persistent (co)homology. By assuming that the filtration of a simplicial set embedded in a finite-dimensional vector space induces a multiplicative filtration on the dg algebra defined by the simplicial cochains complex, we utilize a result by T. Kadeishvili to construct a unique (up to noncanonical equivalence) A_infinity-algebra structure on the complete persistent cohomology of the filtered simplicial (or topological) set. We then introduce a (pseudo)metric defined on the set of all (generalized) barcodes (encompassing all cohomological degrees) enriched with the previously mentioned A_infinity-algebra structure. This metric refines the conventional bottleneck metric and remains independent of the specific A_infinity-algebra structure chosen (among those equivalent). We believe this distance metric warrants attention in topological data analysis as it can effectively distinguish diverse linking or folding patterns, as exemplified by the Borromean rings. Additionally, we provide a concise proof of a result establishing a relationship between the barcode structure in persistent homology and cohomology. This result was previously observed under restricted assumptions in a recent article by V. de Silva, D. Morozov, and M. Vejdemo-Johansson, which our work does not require.

title: Reading Text in the Wild with Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces an end-to-end system for text spotting, a task that involves localizing and recognizing text in natural scene images, and text-based image retrieval. The system leverages a region proposal mechanism for detection and deep convolutional neural networks for recognition. Our pipeline employs a novel combination of complementary proposal generation techniques to maximize recall, followed by a rapid filtering stage to enhance precision. For recognition and ranking of proposals, we train extensive convolutional neural networks to perform word recognition on the entire proposal region simultaneously, departing from traditional character classifier-based systems. Notably, these networks are exclusively trained on synthetic text data generated by a synthetic text generation engine, eliminating the need for human-labeled data. Analysis of the stages in our pipeline demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across all stages. We conducted rigorous experiments on various standard end-to-end text spotting benchmarks and text-based image retrieval datasets, achieving significant improvements over all previous methods. Finally, we showcase a real-world application of our text spotting system that enables instant text-based searches of thousands of hours of news footage.

title: Image Data Compression for Covariance and Histogram Descriptors
Abstract: Covariance and histogram image descriptors provide an effective means of capturing image information. Both descriptors excel when used in conjunction with specialized distance metrics. For covariance descriptors, these metrics assess distances along the non-Euclidean Riemannian manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices. Conversely, for histogram descriptors, the Earth Mover's Distance quantifies the optimal transport between two histograms. While these distance metrics offer greater precision, their computational expense makes them impractical for many applications, particularly those involving datasets with even a few thousand examples. This paper presents two methods for compressing covariance and histogram datasets, resulting in only marginal increases in test error for k-nearest neighbor classification. Specifically, we demonstrate that datasets can be reduced to 16% and in some cases as little as 2% of their original size while achieving comparable test error to kNN classification on the full training set. Notably, the compressed set is learned in a supervised manner, potentially surpassing the performance of the full dataset while requiring significantly less storage space and drastically reducing test-time computation.
