title: A statistical reduced-reference method for color image quality assessment
Abstract: Although color is a fundamental feature of human visual perception, it has been largely unexplored in reduced-reference (RR) image quality assessment (IQA) schemes. This paper proposes a natural scene statistic (NSS) method that efficiently utilizes this information. It is based on the statistical deviation between the steerable pyramid coefficients of the reference color image and the degraded one. We propose and analyze the multivariate generalized Gaussian distribution (MGGD) to model the underlying statistics. To quantify degradation, we develop and evaluate two measures based on the Geodesic distance between two MGGDs and on the closed-form Kullback-Leibler divergence. We conducted an extensive evaluation of both metrics in various color spaces (RGB, HSV, CIELAB, and YCrCb) using the TID 2008 benchmark and the FRTV Phase I validation process. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in achieving good consistency with human visual perception. Moreover, the best configuration is obtained with the CIELAB color space associated with the KLD deviation measure.
label: AI

title: An Egocentric Look at Video Photographer Identity
Abstract: Egocentric cameras are being worn by an increasing number of users, including many security forces worldwide. GoPro cameras have already penetrated the mass market, reporting substantial sales growth annually. As head-worn cameras do not capture the photographer, it may seem that the photographer's anonymity is preserved even when the video is publicly distributed. This paper shows that camera motion, which can be computed from the egocentric video, provides unique identity information. The photographer can be reliably recognized from a few seconds of video captured while walking. The proposed method achieves over 90% recognition accuracy in cases where the random success rate is only 3%. Applications include theft prevention by locking the camera when not worn by its rightful owner. Searching video sharing services (e.g., YouTube) for egocentric videos shot by a specific photographer may also become possible. It is important to note that sharing egocentric videos can compromise anonymity, even when the face is not visible.
label: AI

title: Large-scale Binary Quadratic Optimization Using Semidefinite Relaxation and Applications
Abstract: A novel SDP formulation for binary quadratic programs (BQPs) is presented, which offers a tighter relaxation bound compared to spectral methods while maintaining a similar level of computational complexity. This new formulation enables efficient and scalable dual optimization, comparable to spectral methods. Two solvers, quasi-Newton and smoothing Newton methods, are proposed for the dual problem, offering significant efficiency gains over standard interior-point methods. The smoothing Newton solver outperforms the quasi-Newton solver for dense or medium-sized problems, while the quasi-Newton solver proves more efficient for large sparse or structured problems. The potential of this SDP formulation for solving large-scale BQPs is demonstrated through experiments on computer vision applications such as clustering, image segmentation, co-segmentation, and registration.
label: AI

title: The Treasure beneath Convolutional Layers: Cross-convolutional-layer Pooling for Image Classification
Abstract: This paper argues that convolutional layer activations, when appropriately utilized, can be transformed into a powerful image representation, offering advantages over fully-connected layer activations.  This is achieved through a novel technique called cross-convolutional-layer pooling.  This method extracts subarrays of feature maps from one convolutional layer as local features and pools these features guided by feature maps from the successive convolutional layer. Compared to existing methods using DCNNs for local feature extraction, this approach significantly reduces the computational cost by requiring fewer DCNN forward computations.  Moreover, it mitigates the domain mismatch issue often encountered when applying fully-connected layer activations to local regions. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by achieving comparable or superior performance to fully-connected layer based image representations across four popular visual classification tasks, while incurring substantially lower computational cost.
label: AI

title: Bi-objective Optimization for Robust RGB-D Visual Odometry
Abstract: A novel bi-objective optimization formulation is introduced for robust RGB-D visual odometry. Two methods for solving this formulation are investigated: the weighted sum method, combining objective functions into a single one, and the bounded objective method, optimizing one objective while bounding the other through a constraint. Experimental results on the TUM RGB-D dataset demonstrate the superiority of the new bi-objective optimization formulation over existing RGB-D odometry methods.  The new formulation yields more accurate motion estimates and enhances robustness when textural or structural features in the image sequence are lacking.
label: AI

title: $Υ$-DB: A system for data-driven hypothesis management and analytics
Abstract: $\\Upsilon$-DB, a system for deterministic scientific hypotheses management and analytics, introduces the concept of scientific hypotheses as uncertain and probabilistic data. It addresses key technical challenges through a design-by-synthesis pipeline, processing hypotheses from XML-based extraction to encoding as uncertain and probabilistic U-relational data, culminating in conditioning based on observations. This demo showcases the core innovative features of a prototype $\\Upsilon$-DB system, using use-case scenarios in computational science. Hypotheses are extracted from a web-based model repository and evaluated (rated/ranked) as probabilistic data.
label: AI

title: 3D-Assisted Image Feature Synthesis for Novel Views of an Object
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of view-invariant image comparison by synthesizing new features for different views of the same object, given a single input image. This is achieved by introducing an aligned set of 3D models belonging to the same class as the input object.  By analyzing the correlation of image patches between different views of the 3D models, surrogates (patches in one view whose features predict well the features of a patch in another view) are identified. For each patch in the desired novel view, surrogates from the observed view of the given image are found. Using a linear combination of the corresponding patches from the 3D model views, these surrogates are predicted, and the learned coefficients are transferred on a per-patch basis to synthesize the features of the patch in the novel view. This process creates multi-view feature sets for all views of the latent object, enabling view-invariant comparisons by calculating the $L^2$ distances between features of corresponding views.  The theoretical and empirical analysis of the feature synthesis process, as well as the evaluation of the proposed view-agnostic distance (VAD) in fine-grained image retrieval and classification tasks, demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.
label: AI

title: Fisher Vectors Derived from Hybrid Gaussian-Laplacian Mixture Models for Image Annotation
Abstract: Traditional object recognition pipelines rely on densely sampled descriptors, pooled into high-dimensional non-linear representations before being passed to a classifier. Fisher Vectors have emerged as leading representations in this context, typically calculated as gradients of the log-likelihood of descriptors with respect to the parameters of a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). This paper proposes two alternative Mixture Models, motivated by the assumption that different distributions are suitable for different datasets.  The first model, a Laplacian Mixture Model (LMM), is based on the Laplacian distribution, while the second, a Hybrid Gaussian-Laplacian Mixture Model (HGLMM), utilizes a weighted geometric mean of Gaussian and Laplacian distributions.  The Expectation-Maximization algorithm for the HGLMM model exhibits an interesting property: each dimension in each component is dynamically assigned as either a Gaussian or Laplacian.  Experiments utilizing the new Fisher Vectors derived from HGLMMs demonstrate state-of-the-art results for image annotation and image search by a sentence tasks.
label: AI

title: Edge direction matrixes-based local binar patterns descriptor for shape pattern recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel combinative descriptor for shape and texture image recognition, integrating the strengths of Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and edge direction matrixes (EDMS). LBP excels in encoding both global and local information with scaling invariance, while EDMS provides a global invariant descriptor using first and second-order relationships. This combination leverages the individual advantages of both descriptors, addressing their weaknesses and achieving improved recognition capabilities.  The proposed descriptor is compared to state-of-the-art combinative methods based on Gray-Level Co-occurrence matrix (GLCM with EDMS), LBP, and moment invariants, using four benchmark datasets: MPEG-7 CE-Shape-1, KTH-TIPS image, Enghlishfnt, and Arabic calligraphy.  Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the introduced descriptor over GLCM with EDMS, LBP, moment invariants, and other well-known descriptors like Scale Invariant Feature Transform.
label: AI

title: Understanding Deep Image Representations by Inverting Them
Abstract: Image representations, from traditional methods like SIFT and Bag of Visual Words to modern Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), are fundamental to image understanding systems. Despite their importance, our understanding of these representations remains limited. This paper explores the visual information encoded in representations by investigating the possibility of reconstructing the original image from its representation.  A general framework for inverting representations is introduced, enabling more accurate inversion of representations like HOG and SIFT compared to existing methods, while also being applicable to CNNs. This framework is utilized to study the inverse of recent state-of-the-art CNN image representations for the first time. The findings reveal that several layers in CNNs retain photographically accurate information about the image, with varying degrees of geometric and photometric invariance.
label: AI

title: Open-source code for manifold-based 3D rotation recovery of X-ray scattering patterns
Abstract: Single particle 3D imaging using ultrashort X-ray laser pulses relies on collecting and combining information from 2D scattering patterns of an object at different orientations.  Due to limitations in typical sample-delivery schemes, orientation information must be estimated after the experiment. This paper presents an open-source code for the most rigorous technique reported in this context.  Practical issues and proposed solutions are discussed.
label: AI

title: Behaviour Trees for Evolutionary Robotics
Abstract: This paper presents the first application of the Behaviour Tree framework to a real robotic platform using the Evolutionary Robotics methodology. This framework improves the intelligibility of emergent robotic behavior compared to traditional Neural Network formulations, making it easier to comprehend and manually adapt when transitioning from simulation to real-world scenarios. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through real-world flight tests with the 20-gram DelFly Explorer flapping wing Micro Air Vehicle equipped with a 4-gram onboard stereo vision system.  The experiments show that the DelFly can autonomously search for and fly through a window using only its onboard sensors and processing. The optimized behavior achieved an 88% success rate in simulation, with a corresponding real-world performance of 54% after user adaptation.  Although this leaves room for improvement, it surpasses the 46% success rate of a tuned user-defined controller.
label: AI

title: Universality of Sea Wave Growth and Its Physical Roots
Abstract: Modern studies of wind-driven sea waves typically focus on wind forcing, neglecting the impact of resonant nonlinear wave interactions. This paper argues that these interactions are dominant and proposes a simple relationship between instant wave steepness and time or fetch of wave development expressed in wave periods or lengths. This relationship is independent of wind speed and relies on asymptotic theory. The validity of this proposed law is supported by numerical simulations, in situ measurements of growing wind seas, and wind wave tank experiments. The implications of this new perspective on sea wave physics are discussed in the context of conventional wave modeling and forecasting approaches.
label: AI

title: Patents used by NPE as an Open Information System in Web 2.0 - Two mini case studies
Abstract: This paper examines the complexities of Information Systems surrounding patents, advocating for a creative and unconventional perspective that goes beyond basic patent functionalities.  The authors highlight how patent information can be leveraged for research, guiding the development of new patents, the invalidation of existing ones, and the creation of value-added information with links to other Information Systems.  While traditional R&D relies on heavy investments, patent information offers an alternative and powerful tool for technology transfer, innovation, and creativity. Academic research on patents, even without a primary focus on financial revenue, can be considered a form of "Non Practicing Entities" (NPE) activity, often referred to as "Patent Trolls." The paper explores the controversy surrounding the term "patent troll" and provides two case studies illustrating the effective use of patent information in emerging countries: the pharmaceutical industry in Brazil and the oil industry in Algeria.
label: AI

title: Real time Detection of Lane Markers in Urban Streets
Abstract: This paper presents a robust and real-time approach for detecting lane markers in urban streets. The method generates a top view of the road, applies selective oriented Gaussian filters for noise reduction, and utilizes RANSAC line fitting to provide initial estimates for a new and fast RANSAC algorithm that fits Bezier Splines. A post-processing step further refines the results. This algorithm can detect all lanes in still images of the street under various conditions, achieving comparable results to previous techniques while operating at a rate of 50 Hz.
label: AI

title: Post-acquisition image based compensation for thickness variation in microscopy section series
Abstract: Serial section Microscopy, an established method for volumetric anatomy reconstruction, is crucial for reconstructing the synaptic connectivity of entire animal brains. This paper addresses the challenge of limited precision in section thickness during the removal of ultrathin layers from the specimen block. A novel method is introduced to estimate the relative z-position of each individual section based on signal change across the section series.  Initial experiments demonstrate promising results on both serial section Transmission Electron Microscopy (ssTEM) data and Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM) series. The solution is made available as Open Source plugins for the TrakEM2 software and the ImageJ distribution Fiji.
label: AI

title: Image Classification and Retrieval from User-Supplied Tags
Abstract: This paper proposes a direct learning approach for image classification using user-supplied tags, eliminating the need for filtering. These tags, readily available online, provide insights into image categories that are important to users and relevant for image classification.  The approach complements conventional manual annotation methods, which are expensive. The paper analyzes the Flickr 100 Million Image dataset, revealing valuable insights into the statistics of user-supplied tags. A large-scale robust classification algorithm is introduced to handle the inherent noise in tags, along with a calibration procedure to improve predictions of objective annotations.  The paper demonstrates that freely available, user-supplied tags can achieve comparable or superior results to large databases of costly manual annotations.
label: AI

title: An Automated Images-to-Graphs Framework for High Resolution Connectomics
Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing a map of neuronal connectivity, a crucial task in neuroscience.  Recent advancements in high-throughput serial section electron microscopy (EM) have enabled the generation of massive 3D image volumes of nanoscale brain tissue. This high resolution allows for direct observation of individual neurons and their synaptic connections.  Manually tracing each neuronal process at this scale is an overwhelming task, prompting the development of automated image processing modules.  This paper presents the first fully automated images-to-graphs pipeline, a system that directly produces a brain graph from an imaged volume of neural tissue without human intervention.  A metric for assessing the quality of output graphs is developed to evaluate performance and select optimal parameters and methods.  The paper evaluates a set of algorithms and parameters, identifying the best available brain graph based on the assessment metric. Finally, a reference end-to-end version of the pipeline is deployed on a large, publicly available dataset, providing a baseline for community analysis, future algorithm development, and testing.  All code and data derivatives are made publicly available to facilitate further research.
label: AI

title: Design, Implementation and Simulation of a Cloud Computing System for Enhancing Real-time Video Services by using VANET and Onboard Navigation Systems
Abstract: This paper proposes a design for novel and experimental cloud computing systems aimed at enhancing computational, communicational, and analytical capabilities of road navigation services. The proposed system merges multiple technologies, including vision-based embedded navigation systems, prominent Cloud Computing Systems (CCSs), and Vehicular Ad-hoc NETwork (VANET).  The paper presents initial investigations describing the design of a global generic system, which has been experimented with in various scenarios of video-based road services.  The associated architecture has been implemented on a small-scale simulator of an in-vehicle embedded system and tested in a simulated road service scenario to aid law enforcement. This service involves real-time recognition and tracking of individuals and vehicles remotely connected to moving cars. The paper demonstrates the potential of the system for efficiently enhancing and diversifying real-time video services in road environments.
label: AI

title: Similarity- based approach for outlier detection
Abstract: This paper introduces a new approach for outlier detection based on the concept of object proximity. The core principle is that normal points share similar characteristics with several neighbors.  Therefore, a point is not an outlier if it exhibits a high degree of proximity and has multiple neighbors. The effectiveness of this approach is illustrated using real datasets.
label: AI

title: Non-Verbal Communication Analysis in Victim-Offender Mediations
Abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive ambient intelligence framework for semi-automatic analysis of non-verbal communication applied to the restorative justice field. It proposes the use of computer vision and social signal processing technologies in real-world scenarios of Victim-Offender Mediations, analyzing multi-modal audio-RGB-depth data.  Behavioral indicators defining communicative cues are derived from psychology and observational methodology. The methodology is tested on data captured in real Victim-Offender Mediation sessions in Catalonia, with ground truth annotations based on expert opinions. Utilizing state-of-the-art binary classification approaches, the system achieves recognition accuracies of 86% for predicting satisfaction and 79% for predicting agreement and receptivity.  A regression strategy yields a mean deviation of 0.5 to 0.7 in the range of [1-5] for the computed social signals.
label: AI

title: Deep convolutional filter banks for texture recognition and segmentation
Abstract: Research in texture recognition commonly focuses on material recognition in uncluttered conditions, an assumption rarely met in real-world applications. This paper presents a first study of material and describable texture attribute recognition in cluttered environments, utilizing a new dataset derived from the OpenSurface texture repository.  Motivated by the challenges posed by this problem, a novel texture descriptor, D-CNN, is proposed.  D-CNN is obtained through Fisher Vector pooling of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) filter bank. D-CNN significantly surpasses the state-of-the-art in texture, material, and scene recognition, achieving 82.3% accuracy on the Flickr material dataset and 81.1% accuracy on the MIT indoor scenes dataset, representing absolute gains of over 10% compared to existing approaches. D-CNN readily transfers across domains without requiring feature adaptation, unlike methods relying on the fully-connected layers of CNNs. Moreover, D-CNN seamlessly incorporates multi-scale information and describes regions of arbitrary shapes and sizes.  The approach is particularly adept at localizing stuff categories and achieves state-of-the-art results on the MSRC segmentation dataset, along with promising results in recognizing materials and surface attributes in clutter on the OpenSurfaces dataset. |||
label: AI

title: The Digital Humanities Unveiled: Perceptions Held by Art Historians and Computer Scientists about Computer Vision Technology
Abstract: Computer scientists are generally familiar with the achievements of computer vision technology in art history, but this knowledge is less prevalent and often misunderstood among scholars in the humanities. To understand this disconnect, we examined the social, philosophical, and practical concerns raised by the digitization of the humanities, specifically focusing on the use of computer vision technology in art analysis. Our insights are based on two surveys conducted in August 2014, which explored the perceptions of computer scientists and art historians regarding this technology. This paper discusses the development of these surveys, their results, and the major philosophical conclusions drawn from our research in this area.
label: AI

title: Beyond Gaussian Pyramid: Multi-skip Feature Stacking for Action Recognition
Abstract: Most cutting-edge action feature extractors utilize differential operators, which function as highpass filters and tend to suppress low-frequency action information. This suppression introduces bias to the extracted features and creates poorly conditioned feature matrices. While the Gaussian Pyramid has been used as a feature enhancement technique, encoding scale-invariant characteristics into the feature space to address this attenuation, its core convolutional smoothing operation limits its ability to generate new features at coarser scales. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel feature enhancement technique called Multi-skIp Feature Stacking (MIFS), which stacks features extracted using a family of differential filters parameterized with multiple time skips. This approach encodes shift-invariance into the frequency space and compensates for information lost through the use of differential operators by recovering information at coarse scales. This recovered information enables matching actions at different speeds and ranges of motion. We mathematically demonstrate that MIFS exponentially enhances the learnability of differential-based features. Feature matrices produced by MIFS exhibit significantly smaller conditional numbers and variances compared to conventional methods. Experimental results demonstrate significantly improved performance on challenging action recognition and event detection tasks. Notably, our method surpasses the state-of-the-art on the Hollywood2, UCF101, and UCF50 datasets and achieves comparable performance to the state-of-the-art on the HMDB51 and Olympics Sports datasets. MIFS can also serve as a speedup strategy for feature extraction with minimal or no accuracy compromise.
label: AI

title: Persistent Evidence of Local Image Properties in Generic ConvNets
Abstract: Supervised training of a convolutional network for object classification aims to explicitly utilize information related to the object class while disregarding any auxiliary information associated with image capture or variations within the object class. However, despite this objective, analysis of earlier layers in the network reveals that this ideal separation doesn't always hold true in practice. Surprisingly, strong spatial information remains implicitly present. This paper investigates this phenomenon, particularly focusing on the image representation at the first fully connected layer, a global image descriptor known for its effectiveness in various visual recognition tasks. Through empirical analysis, we demonstrate evidence for this finding across four distinct tasks: 2D landmark detection, 2D object keypoints prediction, estimation of input image RGB values, and recovery of semantic labels for each pixel. Our investigation utilizes a simple framework based on ridge regression, consistently applied across these tasks. The results consistently support our insight. Such spatial information proves valuable for accurately computing landmark correspondences and has the potential to improve the training of convolutional nets for classification purposes.
label: AI

title: The Joint Center for Energy Storage Research: A New Paradigm for Battery Research and Development
Abstract: The Joint Center for Energy Storage Research (JCESR) strives for transformative advancements in transportation and the electricity grid through the development of next-generation, high-performance, low-cost electricity storage solutions. To achieve this vision, JCESR introduces a novel paradigm for battery research: integrating discovery science, battery design, research prototyping, and manufacturing collaboration within a single, highly interactive organization. This integrated approach aims to accelerate the pace of discovery and innovation, significantly reducing the time from conceptualization to commercialization. JCESR applies this new paradigm exclusively to beyond-lithium-ion batteries, a vast, unexplored frontier ripe for exploration. This review outlines JCESR's motivation, vision, mission, intended legacies, and accomplishments during its first year of operation.
label: AI

title: The Application of Two-level Attention Models in Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Fine-grained Image Classification
Abstract: Fine-grained classification presents unique challenges due to the need to discriminate categories based on subtle and localized differences. Variations in pose, scale, or rotation often exacerbate these challenges. Most fine-grained classification systems follow a pipeline that involves identifying foreground objects or object parts ("where") to extract discriminative features ("what"). This paper proposes utilizing visual attention within a deep neural network to address the fine-grained classification task. Our pipeline integrates three types of attention: bottom-up attention for proposing candidate patches, object-level top-down attention for selecting relevant patches specific to an object, and part-level top-down attention for localizing discriminative parts. By combining these attentions, we train domain-specific deep nets, enhancing both the "what" and "where" aspects. Importantly, our approach avoids the use of costly annotations like bounding boxes or part information during end-to-end training. This weak supervision constraint promotes the generalizability of our work. We have validated the effectiveness of our method on subsets of the ILSVRC2012 and CUB200_2011 datasets, achieving significant improvements and the highest accuracy under the weakest supervision condition. Our performance is competitive with other methods that rely on additional annotations.
label: AI

title: Encoding High Dimensional Local Features by Sparse Coding Based Fisher Vectors
Abstract: Fisher vector coding (FVC), derived from the gradient vector of a generative model of local features, has emerged as an effective coding method for image classification. While most FVC implementations employ the Gaussian mixture model (GMM) to characterize the generation process of local features, this choice has proven sufficient for traditional low-dimensional local features, such as SIFT. Typically, satisfactory performance can be achieved with only a few hundred Gaussian distributions. However, the same number of Gaussians is insufficient to model the feature space spanned by higher-dimensional local features, which have gained popularity recently. Simply increasing the number of Gaussians to enhance modeling capacity for high-dimensional features proves inefficient and computationally impractical. In this paper, we propose a model where each local feature is drawn from a Gaussian distribution with a mean vector sampled from a subspace. With certain approximations, this model can be transformed into a sparse coding procedure, and the learning/inference problems can be readily solved using standard sparse coding methods. By calculating the gradient vector of this proposed model, we derive a new Fisher vector encoding strategy, dubbed Sparse Coding based Fisher Vector Coding (SCFVC). Furthermore, we utilize the recently developed Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) descriptor as a high-dimensional local feature and implement image classification using our proposed SCFVC. Our experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method not only significantly outperforms the traditional GMM-based Fisher vector encoding but also achieves state-of-the-art performance in generic object recognition, indoor scene, and fine-grained image classification problems.
label: AI

title: Multiple object tracking with context awareness
Abstract: Multiple people tracking is a critical problem in numerous applications, including surveillance, animation, car navigation, and as a crucial input for tasks such as activity recognition. In crowded environments, occlusions and false detections are prevalent, posing significant challenges to tracking, despite substantial advancements in recent years. Tracking is typically divided into two steps: detection, involving the localization of pedestrians within the image, and data association, connecting detections across frames to form complete trajectories. Traditional approaches for data association aim to develop more complex formulations, shifting focus towards optimization techniques to solve them. However, these approaches still rely heavily on basic information, such as the distance between detections. This thesis focuses on the data association task and argues that contextual information, particularly social context and spatial context derived from different views, has not been fully exploited by the tracking community.
label: AI

title: Deep Convolutional Neural Fields for Depth Estimation from a Single Image
Abstract: This work addresses the problem of depth estimation from a single monocular image, a challenging task due to the absence of reliable depth cues like stereo correspondences or motion information. Previous efforts have focused on exploiting geometric priors or incorporating additional information sources, all utilizing hand-crafted features. Recent advancements have shown that features extracted from deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are setting new records in various vision applications. Given the continuous nature of depth values, depth estimations can be naturally formulated as a continuous conditional random field (CRF) learning problem. Therefore, this paper presents a deep convolutional neural field model for depth estimation from a single image, aiming to leverage the combined capabilities of deep CNNs and continuous CRFs. Specifically, we propose a deep structured learning scheme that learns the unary and pairwise potentials of continuous CRFs within a unified deep CNN framework. This method can be applied to depth estimation of general scenes without requiring geometric priors or additional injected information. In our case, the integral of the partition function can be analytically calculated, allowing for exact log-likelihood optimization. Furthermore, solving the MAP problem for predicting depths of a new image is highly efficient due to the existence of closed-form solutions. We experimentally demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art depth estimation methods on both indoor and outdoor scene datasets.
label: AI

title: Mid-level Deep Pattern Mining
Abstract: Mid-level visual element discovery aims to identify clusters of image patches that are both representative and discriminative. This work investigates this problem from the perspective of pattern mining while leveraging the recently popularized Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We observe that activations extracted from the first fully-connected layer of CNNs for an image patch possess two desirable properties that enable seamless integration with pattern mining. Patterns are then discovered from a vast number of CNN activations of image patches through well-established association rule mining techniques. Interestingly, when we retrieve and visualize image patches with the same pattern, they exhibit not only visual similarity but also semantic consistency. We apply our approach to scene and object classification tasks, demonstrating that it outperforms all previous works on mid-level visual element discovery by a substantial margin, using significantly fewer elements. Our approach also surpasses or matches recent works utilizing CNNs for these tasks. The source code of the complete system is available online.
label: AI

title: Scale-Invariant Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Despite achieving near-human performance in various computer vision tasks, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have limited tolerance for scale variations. The conventional practice involves first increasing the model size and then training it with data augmentation using extensive scale-jittering. In this paper, we introduce a scale-invariant convolutional neural network (SiCNN), a model designed to incorporate multi-scale feature extraction and classification into the network structure. SiCNN utilizes a multi-column architecture, with each column specializing in a particular scale. Unlike previous multi-column strategies, these columns share the same set of filter parameters through scale transformations among them. This design effectively handles scale variations without increasing the model size. Experimental results demonstrate that SiCNN detects features at various scales, and the classification results exhibit robust performance against object scale variations.
label: AI

title: On the mathematic modeling of non-parametric curves based on cubic Bézier curves
Abstract: Bézier splines are widely used in various systems for curve and surface designs. In general, a Bézier spline can be defined using Bézier curve segments, and each segment can be fitted to any number of control points. The number of control points determines the degree of the Bézier polynomial. This paper presents a method for determining control points for Bézier curves that approximate segments of an obtained image outline (non-parametric curve), leveraging the properties of cubic Bézier curves. Our proposed method is a technique for control point determination that offers generality and reduces the error in Bézier curve approximation. The primary advantage of our proposed method is its higher accuracy and compression rate compared to previous methods. The cubic Bézier spline is constructed from cubic Bézier curve segments. Experimental results are provided to demonstrate the performance of our proposed algorithm, comparing it to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Iteratively Reweighted Graph Cut for Multi-label MRFs with Non-convex Priors
Abstract: Multi-label MRFs with non-convex priors, despite being highly effective in computer vision, are notoriously difficult to optimize. To address this challenge, we introduce an algorithm that iteratively approximates the original energy with an appropriately weighted surrogate energy that is easier to minimize. Our algorithm guarantees a decrease in the original energy at each iteration. Specifically, we consider scenarios where the global minimizer of the weighted surrogate energy can be obtained through a multi-label graph cut algorithm, demonstrating that our algorithm can handle a wide range of non-convex priors. We showcase the benefits of our method over state-of-the-art MRF energy minimization techniques on stereo and inpainting problems.
label: AI

title: Vision and Learning for Deliberative Monocular Cluttered Flight
Abstract: Cameras offer a rich source of information while being passive, inexpensive, and lightweight, making them ideal for small and medium Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). This work presents the first implementation of receding horizon control, widely used in ground vehicles, utilizing monocular vision as the sole sensing mode for autonomous UAV flight in dense clutter. We achieve feasibility on UAVs through several key contributions: novel coupling of perception and control via relevant and diverse, multiple interpretations of the scene around the robot, leveraging recent advances in machine learning to showcase anytime budgeted cost-sensitive feature selection, and fast non-linear regression for monocular depth prediction. We demonstrate the efficacy of our novel pipeline through real-world experiments spanning over 2 kilometers through dense trees with a quadrotor constructed from off-the-shelf components. Furthermore, our pipeline is designed to integrate information from other modalities, such as stereo and lidar, if available.
label: AI

title: Detection of Non-Stationary Photometric Perturbations on Projection Screens
Abstract: Interfaces based on projection screens have gained significant popularity in recent years, primarily due to their ability to provide large screen size and resolution, as well as stereo-vision capabilities. This work introduces a localized method for real-time detection of non-stationary photometric perturbations in projected images using computer vision techniques. The method is based on computing differences between the images in the projector's frame buffer and the corresponding images on the projection screen observed by the camera. It exhibits robustness against spatial variations in the light intensity emitted by the projector on the projection surface and also demonstrates robustness against stationary photometric perturbations caused by external factors. Furthermore, we describe the experiments conducted to validate the reliability of this method.
label: AI

title: From Image-level to Pixel-level Labeling with Convolutional Networks
Abstract: We aim to infer object segmentation by leveraging solely object class information and considering minimal priors on the object segmentation task. This problem can be viewed as a form of weakly supervised segmentation task and naturally aligns with the Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) framework. Each training image is known to contain (or not) at least one pixel corresponding to the image class label, and the segmentation task can be reformulated as inferring the pixels belonging to the object's class (given an image and its object class). We propose a Convolutional Neural Network-based model that is constrained during training to assign greater weight to pixels crucial for image classification. We demonstrate that at test time, the model has effectively learned to discriminate the correct pixels, achieving excellent performance on an existing segmentation benchmark by adding only a few smoothing priors. Our system is trained using a subset of the Imagenet dataset, and segmentation experiments are performed on the challenging Pascal VOC dataset without fine-tuning the model on Pascal VOC. Our model significantly surpasses the state-of-the-art results in weakly supervised object segmentation, achieving a substantial margin. We also compare the performance of our model with state-of-the-art fully-supervised segmentation approaches.
label: AI

title: Low-Rank and Sparse Matrix Decomposition with a-priori knowledge for Dynamic 3D MRI reconstruction
Abstract: Recent studies have shown that incorporating prior knowledge significantly enhances the performance of basic compressive sensing-based approaches. We have successfully exploited this concept for recovering a matrix as a summation of a Low-rank and a Sparse component from compressive measurements. When applied to the real-time reconstruction of 4D Cardiac MR image sequences from highly undersampled $k$-space data, our proposed method achieves superior reconstruction quality compared to other state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Virtual View Networks for Object Reconstruction
Abstract: All that structure from motion algorithms "see" are sets of 2D points. We demonstrate that these impoverished views of the world can be simulated for the purpose of reconstructing objects in challenging settings, such as from a single image or a few widely spaced images, by recognizing the object and utilizing a collection of images of other objects from the same class. We synthesize virtual views by calculating geodesics on novel networks connecting objects with similar viewpoints and introduce techniques to enhance the specificity and robustness of factorization-based object reconstruction in this context. We report accurate object shape reconstruction from a single image on the challenging PASCAL VOC data, suggesting a significant expansion in the potential application domain of rigid structure-from-motion techniques.
label: AI

title: Category-Specific Object Reconstruction from a Single Image
Abstract: Object reconstruction from a single image in real-world scenarios is a problem where we can make progress and obtain meaningful results today. This is the core message of this paper, which introduces an automated pipeline that takes pixels as inputs and produces 3D surfaces of various rigid categories from images of realistic scenes. At the heart of our approach are deformable 3D models that can be learned from 2D annotations available in existing object detection datasets. These models can be driven by noisy automatic object segmentations and are complemented by a bottom-up module for recovering high-frequency shape details. We conduct a comprehensive quantitative analysis and ablation study of our approach using the recently introduced PASCAL 3D+ dataset, showcasing very encouraging automatic reconstructions on PASCAL VOC.
label: AI

title: Viewpoints and Keypoints
Abstract: We characterize the problem of pose estimation for rigid objects in terms of determining the viewpoint to explain coarse pose and keypoint prediction to capture the finer details. We address both these tasks in two distinct settings: the constrained setting with known bounding boxes and the more challenging detection setting where the goal is to simultaneously detect and accurately estimate the pose of objects. We present Convolutional Neural Network-based architectures for these tasks and demonstrate that leveraging viewpoint estimates can significantly improve local appearance-based keypoint predictions. Beyond achieving substantial improvements over the state-of-the-art in these tasks, we analyze the error modes and the effect of object characteristics on performance to guide future research efforts towards this goal.
label: AI

title: Finding Action Tubes
Abstract: We address the problem of action detection in videos. Inspired by recent advancements in object detection from 2D images, we construct action models using rich feature hierarchies derived from shape and kinematic cues. We integrate appearance and motion in two ways. First, starting from image region proposals, we select those that are motion salient and thus more likely to contain the action. This leads to a significant reduction in the number of regions being processed, enabling faster computations. Second, we extract spatio-temporal feature representations to build robust classifiers using Convolutional Neural Networks. We link our predictions to produce detections consistent over time, referred to as action tubes. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms other techniques in the task of action detection. |||
label: AI

title: Learning to Generate Chairs, Tables and Cars with Convolutional Networks
Abstract: We propose a method for generating images of objects using "up-convolutional" neural networks. These networks are trained on rendered 3D models of chairs, tables, and cars. Our experiments demonstrate that the networks not only memorize all images but also learn a meaningful representation of 3D models, allowing them to assess similarities between models, interpolate between views, extrapolate new views, and even create new objects by recombining existing training instances or combining different object classes. Furthermore, we show that these generative networks can be used to find correspondences between different objects in the dataset, outperforming existing approaches on this task.
label: AI

title: Understanding image representations by measuring their equivariance and equivalence
Abstract: Despite the significance of image representations like histograms of oriented gradients and deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), our theoretical understanding remains limited. To address this gap, we investigate three key mathematical properties of representations: equivariance, invariance, and equivalence. Equivariance explores how transformations of the input image are encoded by the representation, with invariance being a special case where a transformation has no effect. Equivalence examines whether two representations, such as different parameterizations of a CNN, capture the same visual information. We propose several empirical methods to establish these properties, including the introduction of transformation and stitching layers in CNNs. These methods are then applied to popular representations, revealing insightful aspects of their structure, including clarifying at which layers in a CNN certain geometric invariances are achieved. While the paper's focus is theoretical, we also demonstrate direct applications to structured-output regression.

title: Assessment of algorithms for mitosis detection in breast cancer histopathology images
Abstract: Mitosis counting, traditionally performed by manually counting mitotic figures in hematoxylin and eosin-stained histology sections, is a critical prognostic marker for breast tumors. However, this method is laborious, subjective, and prone to low inter-observer agreement. With the increasing adoption of whole slide images in pathology labs, automated image analysis has emerged as a potential solution. This paper presents the results of the Assessment of Mitosis Detection Algorithms 2013 (AMIDA13) challenge. The challenge utilized a dataset of 12 training and 11 testing subjects, with over a thousand annotated mitotic figures from multiple observers. The paper provides concise descriptions and results of the evaluation of eleven methods. The top-performing method achieved an error rate comparable to the inter-observer agreement among pathologists.
label: AI

title: Hypercolumns for Object Segmentation and Fine-grained Localization
Abstract: Object recognition algorithms based on convolutional networks (CNNs) typically utilize the output of the last layer as the feature representation. However, this layer's information might be too coarse for precise localization. Conversely, earlier layers may excel in localization but lack semantic understanding. To leverage the strengths of both worlds, we introduce the hypercolumn, a pixel descriptor composed of the activations of all CNN units above that pixel. Using hypercolumns as pixel descriptors, we demonstrate results on three fine-grained localization tasks: simultaneous detection and segmentation, where we improve the state-of-the-art from 49.7 mean AP^r to 60.0; keypoint localization, achieving a 3.3 point improvement over previous work; and part labeling, showing a 6.6 point gain over a strong baseline.
label: AI

title: Visual Sentiment Prediction with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Images have become a prevalent form of media for users to express their emotions on online social networks. While sentiment analysis of textual data has received significant attention, research on analyzing sentiment in image data remains limited. This work introduces a novel visual sentiment prediction framework that utilizes deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image understanding. The proposed sentiment prediction framework performs transfer learning from a CNN with millions of parameters, pre-trained on large-scale data for object recognition. Experiments conducted on two real-world datasets from Twitter and Tumblr demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed visual sentiment analysis framework.
label: AI

title: CIDEr: Consensus-based Image Description Evaluation
Abstract: Automatically generating a sentence to describe an image has been a longstanding challenge in computer vision and natural language processing. Recent advancements in object detection, attribute classification, action recognition, and other areas have reignited interest in this field. However, evaluating the quality of generated descriptions remains challenging. We propose a novel paradigm for evaluating image descriptions based on human consensus. This paradigm consists of three key components: a new triplet-based method for collecting human annotations to measure consensus, a novel automated metric (CIDEr) that captures consensus, and two new datasets: PASCAL-50S and ABSTRACT-50S, containing 50 sentences describing each image. Our simple metric outperforms existing metrics in capturing human judgment of consensus across sentences generated from various sources. We evaluate five state-of-the-art image description approaches using this new protocol and establish a benchmark for future comparisons. A version of CIDEr, named CIDEr-D, is available on the MS COCO evaluation server for systematic evaluation and benchmarking.
label: AI

title: An algorithm for improving Non-Local Means operators via low-rank approximation
Abstract: We present a method for enhancing a Non Local Means operator by computing its low-rank approximation. This low-rank operator is constructed by applying a filter to the spectrum of the original Non Local Means operator. The resulting operator is less sensitive to noise while preserving crucial properties of the original operator. The method is efficiently implemented using Chebyshev polynomials and demonstrated on the application of natural image denoising. For this application, we provide a comprehensive comparison of our method with leading denoising techniques.
label: AI

title: Learning a Recurrent Visual Representation for Image Caption Generation
Abstract: This paper explores the bi-directional mapping between images and their sentence-based descriptions. We propose learning this mapping using a recurrent neural network. Unlike previous approaches that map both sentences and images to a common embedding, our method enables the generation of novel sentences given an image. The same model also allows us to reconstruct the visual features associated with an image given its textual description. We utilize a novel recurrent visual memory that automatically learns to retain long-term visual concepts, assisting in both sentence generation and visual feature reconstruction. We evaluate our approach on various tasks, including sentence generation, sentence retrieval, and image retrieval. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results in generating novel image descriptions. Compared to human-generated captions, our automatically generated captions are preferred by humans over 19.8% of the time. Results on image and sentence retrieval tasks are better than or comparable to state-of-the-art methods using similar visual features.
label: AI

title: Maximum Likelihood Directed Enumeration Method in Piecewise-Regular Object Recognition
Abstract: We investigate the problem of classifying composite objects (images, speech signals) with a limited number of models per class. Specifically, we focus on improving recognition performance for medium-sized databases (thousands of classes). The heuristic nature of fast approximate nearest-neighbor methods, widely used in this task, poses a challenge. While their efficiency can be rigorously proven using the theory of algorithms only for simple similarity measures and artificially generated tasks, this paper proposes an alternative, statistically optimal greedy algorithm. At each step of this algorithm, the joint density (likelihood) of distances to previously checked models is estimated for each class. The next model to check is selected from the class with the maximal likelihood. This likelihood is estimated based on the asymptotic properties of the Kullback-Leibler information discrimination and a mathematical model of a piecewise-regular object with a distribution of each regular segment of exponential type. Experimental results in face recognition using the FERET dataset demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms not only brute force and the baseline (directed enumeration method) but also approximate nearest-neighbor methods from the FLANN and NonMetricSpaceLib libraries (randomized kd-tree, composite index, perm-sort).

title: Affordances Provide a Fundamental Categorization Principle for Visual Scenes
Abstract: How do we visually recognize a kitchen as a kitchen? Our understanding of how we conceptualize and categorize different visual environments is limited. Traditional models of visual perception propose that scene categorization is achieved through the recognition of a scene's objects, but these models fail to account for evidence suggesting that human observers are relatively insensitive to local details in an image. Psychologists have long theorized that affordances, or the actionable possibilities of a stimulus, are crucial to its perception. To what extent are scene categories formed based on similar affordances? Using a large-scale experiment with hundreds of scene categories, we demonstrate that the activities afforded by a visual scene provide a fundamental categorization principle. Affordance-based similarity explained the majority of the structure in human scene categorization patterns, outperforming alternative similarities based on objects or visual features. When all models were combined, affordances provided the majority of the predictive power in the combined model, with nearly half of the total explained variance captured solely by affordances. These findings challenge existing models of high-level visual perception and provide immediately testable hypotheses for the functional organization of the human perceptual system.
label: AI

title: Visual Noise from Natural Scene Statistics Reveals Human Scene Category Representations
Abstract: Our perceptions are influenced by both bottom-up information entering our eyes and top-down expectations of what we will see. While bottom-up visual processing has been extensively studied, our understanding of top-down signals remains limited. This paper introduces REVEAL (Representations Envisioned Via Evolutionary Algorithm), a method for visualizing an observer's internal representation of a complex, real-world scene, allowing us, for the first time, to visualize top-down information in an observer's mind. REVEAL utilizes two key innovations to address this high-dimensional problem: visual noise sampled from natural image statistics and a computer algorithm that collaborates with human observers to efficiently obtain a solution. In this work, we visualize observers' internal representations of a visual scene category (street) using an experiment where observers view naturalistic visual noise and work with the algorithm to externalize their internal representation. Since no scene information was provided, observers had to rely on their internal knowledge of the target, matching it with the visual features in the noise. Reconstructed images were matched with images of real-world street scenes to enhance visualization. Critically, we show that the visualized mental images can predict rapid scene detection performance, as each observer exhibited faster and more accurate responses to detecting real-world images that were most similar to their reconstructed street templates. These results demonstrate the feasibility of visualizing previously unobservable mental representations of real-world stimuli. More broadly, REVEAL provides a general method for objectively examining the content of previously private, subjective mental experiences.
label: AI

title: ConceptLearner: Discovering Visual Concepts from Weakly Labeled Image Collections
Abstract: Discovering visual knowledge from weakly labeled data is crucial for scaling up computer vision recognition systems, as acquiring fully labeled data for a large number of concept categories is expensive. This paper proposes ConceptLearner, a scalable approach for discovering visual concepts from weakly labeled image collections. Thousands of visual concept detectors are learned automatically, without human intervention for additional annotation. We demonstrate that these learned detectors can accurately recognize concepts at the image level and detect concepts at the image region level. Under domain-specific supervision, we further evaluate the learned concepts for scene recognition on the SUN database and for object detection on Pascal VOC 2007. ConceptLearner shows promising performance compared to fully supervised and weakly supervised methods.
label: AI

title: Fashion Apparel Detection: The Role of Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Pose-dependent Priors
Abstract: This work introduces and addresses a new computer vision task, fashion item detection, aiming to detect various fashion items a person in an image is wearing or carrying. The types of fashion items considered include hats, glasses, bags, pants, shoes, and so on. Detecting fashion items can serve as a crucial first step for various e-commerce applications in the fashion industry. Our method is based on a state-of-the-art object detection method pipeline that combines object proposal methods with a deep convolutional neural network. As the locations of fashion items are strongly correlated with body joint positions, we incorporate contextual information from body poses to enhance detection performance. Through experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: End-to-End Integration of a Convolutional Network, Deformable Parts Model and Non-Maximum Suppression
Abstract: Deformable Parts Models (DPMs) and Convolutional Networks (ConvNets) have achieved notable performance in object detection, each excelling in complementary areas. DPMs are adept at modeling object composition and fine-grained spatial relationships between parts, while ConvNets excel at generating powerful image features through discriminative training directly on pixels. This paper proposes a novel model that combines these two approaches, leveraging the advantages of each. We train this model using a new structured loss function that considers all bounding boxes within an image, rather than isolated object instances. This integration allows the non-maximal suppression (NMS) operation, previously treated as a separate post-processing stage, to be incorporated into the model. This enables discriminative training of our combined ConvNet + DPM + NMS model in an end-to-end manner. We evaluate our system on PASCAL VOC 2007 and 2011 datasets, achieving competitive results on both benchmarks.
label: AI

title: Efficient Media Retrieval from Non-Cooperative Queries
Abstract: Text is ubiquitous in the artificial world and readily available when it comes to book titles and author names. Utilizing images from the book cover set of the Stanford Mobile Visual Search dataset, along with additional book covers and metadata from openlibrary.org, we construct a large-scale book cover retrieval dataset, including 100K distractor covers and title and author strings for each. Since our query images are poorly conditioned for clean text extraction, we propose a method for extracting matching noisy and erroneous OCR readings and matching them against clean author and book title strings in a standard document look-up problem setup. Finally, we demonstrate how to use this text-matching as a feature in conjunction with popular retrieval features like VLAD, employing a simple learning setup to achieve significant improvements in retrieval accuracy over both VLAD and text alone.
label: AI

title: Sparse distributed localized gradient fused features of objects
Abstract: The sparse, hierarchical, and modular processing of natural signals is related to humans' ability to recognize objects with high accuracy. This study reports a sparse feature processing and encoding method that improves the recognition performance of an automated object recognition system. Randomly distributed localized gradient-enhanced features are selected before employing aggregate functions for representation, where we utilize a modular and hierarchical approach to detect object features. These object features are combined with a minimum distance classifier, resulting in object recognition system accuracies of 93% using the Amsterdam library of object images (ALOI) database, 92% using the Columbia object image library (COIL)-100 database, and 69% using the PASCAL visual object challenge 2007 database. The object recognition performance demonstrates robustness to variations in noise, object scaling, and object shifts. Finally, a comparison with eight existing object recognition methods indicates that our new method improves recognition accuracy by 10% with ALOI, 8% with the COIL-100 database, and 10% with the PASCAL visual object challenge 2007 database.
label: AI

title: A Pooling Approach to Modelling Spatial Relations for Image Retrieval and Annotation
Abstract: Over the past two decades, we have witnessed significant progress in modeling visual object classes, scenes, and attributes, contributing significantly to automated image understanding. Surprisingly, however, little progress has been made on incorporating a spatial representation and reasoning into the inference process. This work proposes a pooling interpretation of spatial relations and demonstrates how it improves image retrieval and annotation tasks involving spatial language. Due to the complexity of spatial language, we advocate for a learning-based approach that acquires a representation of spatial relations by learning parameters of the pooling operator. We show improvements over previous work on two datasets and two different tasks, as well as provide additional insights on a new dataset with an explicit focus on spatial relations.
label: AI

title: Attentional Neural Network: Feature Selection Using Cognitive Feedback
Abstract: Attentional Neural Networks (ANNs) are a novel framework that integrates top-down cognitive bias and bottom-up feature extraction within a single coherent architecture. The top-down influence is particularly effective when dealing with high noise or challenging segmentation problems. Our system is modular and extensible. It is also easy to train and inexpensive to run while accommodating complex behaviors. We achieve classification accuracy that surpasses or is competitive with state-of-the-art results on the MNIST variation dataset, and successfully disentangle overlaid digits with high success rates. We view this general-purpose framework as an essential foundation for a larger system emulating the cognitive abilities of the entire brain.
label: AI

title: SIRF: Simultaneous Image Registration and Fusion in A Unified Framework
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for image fusion involving a high-resolution panchromatic image and a low-resolution multispectral image at the same geographical location. The fusion is formulated as a convex optimization problem that minimizes a linear combination of a least-squares fitting term and a dynamic gradient sparsity regularizer. The former preserves accurate spectral information from the multispectral image, while the latter maintains sharp edges from the high-resolution panchromatic image. We propose simultaneously registering the two images during the fusion process, naturally achieved through the dynamic gradient sparsity property. An efficient algorithm is then devised to solve the optimization problem, achieving linear computational complexity in the size of the output image in each iteration. We compare our method against seven state-of-the-art image fusion methods on multispectral image datasets from four satellites. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms others in terms of both spatial and spectral qualities. We also show that our method can produce high-quality products from coarsely registered real-world datasets. Finally, a MATLAB implementation is provided to facilitate future research.

title: Fast Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares Algorithms for Analysis-Based Sparsity Reconstruction
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for analysis-based sparsity reconstruction. It solves the generalized problem through structured sparsity regularization with an orthogonal basis and total variation regularization. The proposed algorithm is based on the iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS) model, further accelerated by the preconditioned conjugate gradient method. The convergence rate of the proposed algorithm is nearly the same as that of traditional IRLS algorithms, exhibiting exponential speed. Moreover, with the specifically designed preconditioner, the computational cost per iteration is significantly reduced compared to traditional IRLS algorithms, enabling our approach to handle large-scale problems. Besides its fast convergence, our method is readily applicable to standard sparsity, group sparsity, overlapping group sparsity, and TV-based problems. Experiments are conducted on a practical application: compressive sensing magnetic resonance imaging. Extensive results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance over 14 state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of both accuracy and computational cost.
label: AI

title: Salient Object Detection: A Survey
Abstract: Salient object detection, the process of identifying and outlining important objects in images, has gained significant attention within computer vision. Despite numerous models and applications, a comprehensive understanding of the field's progress and challenges remains elusive. This paper aims to offer a comprehensive review of recent advancements in salient object detection, situating it within related fields such as generic scene segmentation, object proposal generation, and saliency for fixation prediction. Covering 228 publications, this review delves into the historical roots, key concepts, and tasks, as well as core techniques, modeling trends, datasets, and evaluation metrics. Furthermore, it addresses open problems like evaluation metrics and dataset bias in model performance, and proposes promising directions for future research.
label: AI

title: Designing Deep Networks for Surface Normal Estimation
Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for learning visual representations. This paper investigates the application of CNNs for surface normal prediction from single images. By drawing inspiration from decades of research in 3D scene understanding, a novel CNN architecture is proposed for the task of surface normal estimation. The proposed architecture incorporates several constraints, including man-made and Manhattan world assumptions, along with meaningful intermediate representations such as room layout and edge labels. This approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in surface normal estimation, demonstrating robustness and achieving excellent results on other datasets without the need for fine-tuning.
label: AI

title: From Captions to Visual Concepts and Back
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for automatically generating image descriptions by integrating visual detectors, language models, and multimodal similarity models trained directly from a dataset of image captions. Multiple instance learning is employed to train visual detectors for words commonly found in captions, encompassing various parts of speech like nouns, verbs, and adjectives. The outputs from these word detectors act as conditional inputs to a maximum-entropy language model, which learns from over 400,000 image descriptions to capture word usage statistics. Global semantics are captured by re-ranking caption candidates using sentence-level features and a deep multimodal similarity model. The proposed system achieves state-of-the-art performance on the official Microsoft COCO benchmark, achieving a BLEU-4 score of 29.1%. Human evaluation on a held-out test set reveals that the generated captions have equal or better quality than those written by humans in 34% of cases.
label: AI

title: A Unified Semantic Embedding: Relating Taxonomies and Attributes
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for learning a discriminative yet semantic space for object categorization, where auxiliary semantic entities like supercategories and attributes are also embedded. Unlike previous methods that treated these entities as side information, this approach explicitly embeds them into the same space as categories, enabling the representation of a category as a linear combination of its components. By leveraging this unified semantic model, the method ensures that each category is represented by a supercategory combined with a sparse combination of attributes, further employing exclusive regularization to learn discriminative composition.
label: AI

title: Low-level Vision by Consensus in a Spatial Hierarchy of Regions
Abstract: This paper presents a multi-scale framework for low-level vision, focused on estimating physical scene values from image data, such as depth from stereo image pairs. The framework utilizes a dense, overlapping set of image regions at multiple scales and employs a "local model," like a slanted-plane model for stereo disparity, which is expected to be valid piecewise across the visual field. Estimation is formulated as an optimization problem over a dichotomous mixture of variables, simultaneously determining inlier regions with respect to the local model (binary variables) and their corresponding coordinates in the local model space (continuous variables). The multi-scale hierarchical organization of regions enables efficient and parallel optimization, with distributed computational units iteratively performing calculations and sharing information through sparse connections between parents and children. The framework exhibits strong performance on a standard benchmark for binocular stereo, generating a distributional scene representation suitable for integration with higher-level reasoning and other low-level cues.
label: AI

title: Towards Scene Understanding with Detailed 3D Object Representations
Abstract: Current approaches to semantic image and scene understanding typically rely on simplistic object representations like 2D or 3D bounding boxes. While these coarse models provide robustness and enable reliable object detection, they discard crucial information about objects' 3D shape and pose, hindering their suitability for higher-level reasoning. This paper proposes a scene understanding approach based on a high-resolution object representation, where an object class, specifically cars, is modeled as a deformable 3D wireframe. This wireframe allows for fine-grained modeling at the level of individual vertices and faces, further augmented with vertex-level occlusion information and embedded into a common coordinate frame to infer and exploit object-object interactions. From a single view, the system jointly estimates the shapes and poses of multiple objects in a common 3D frame. A ground plane in this frame is estimated through consensus among different objects, significantly stabilizing monocular 3D pose estimation. The detailed object class model, combined with the explicit 3D scene model, facilitates the inference of part-level occlusions between modeled objects, as well as occlusions by unmodeled scene elements. The effectiveness of this detailed object class model for scene understanding is demonstrated through systematic evaluation on the challenging KITTI street scene dataset. Experiments reveal that the model's ability to leverage image evidence at the part level improves monocular 3D pose estimation in terms of both location and continuous viewpoint.
label: AI

title: Unsupervised Neural Architecture for Saliency Detection: Extended Version
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture for visual saliency detection, inspired by neurophysiologically plausible mechanisms for extracting salient regions. The model draws inspiration from recent findings in neurophysiology, aiming to simulate the bottom-up processes of human selective attention. Two types of features are analyzed: color and direction of maximum variance. These features are processed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), implemented through normalized Hebbian learning and waves of spikes. The performance of the model is evaluated through a psychological experiment, demonstrating good agreement between simulation results and experimental findings.
label: AI

title: Predicting Depth, Surface Normals and Semantic Labels with a Common Multi-Scale Convolutional Architecture
Abstract: This paper presents a single basic architecture capable of tackling three distinct computer vision tasks: depth prediction, surface normal estimation, and semantic labeling. A multiscale convolutional network is employed, easily adaptable to each task through minimal modifications, enabling direct regression from the input image to the output map. The method progressively refines predictions through a sequence of scales, capturing intricate image details without relying on superpixels or low-level segmentation. State-of-the-art performance is achieved on benchmarks for all three tasks.
label: AI

title: Structured Hough Voting for Vision-based Highway Border Detection
Abstract: This paper proposes a vision-based highway border detection algorithm utilizing structured Hough voting. The approach leverages the geometric relationship between highway road borders and lane markings, employing a strategy where trained road border and lane marking detectors are triggered, followed by Hough voting to generate corresponding border and lane marking detections. As the initial triggered detectors often yield a large number of positives, traditional frame-wise Hough voting may fail to produce robust border and lane marking results. Consequently, the problem is formulated as a joint detection-and-tracking problem within the structured Hough voting model, where tracking leverages inter-frame structural information to stabilize detection results. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed structured Hough voting model compared to baseline methods.
label: AI

title: AlexU-Word: A New Dataset for Isolated-Word Closed-Vocabulary Offline Arabic Handwriting Recognition
Abstract: This paper introduces the first phase of a novel dataset for offline Arabic handwriting recognition, aiming to collect a large dataset of isolated Arabic words encompassing all alphabet letters in all possible shapes using a small number of simple words. The ultimate goal is to compile a vast dataset of segmented letter images, facilitating the development and evaluation of Arabic handwriting recognition systems based on segmented letter recognition. The current version of the dataset comprises 25,114 samples of 109 unique Arabic words, covering all possible shapes of all alphabet letters, collected from 907 writers. In its current form, the dataset is suitable for closed-vocabulary word recognition. Evaluation of several window-based descriptors and classifiers on this task achieved an accuracy of 92.16% using a SIFT-based descriptor and Artificial Neural Network (ANN).
label: AI

title: TILDE: A Temporally Invariant Learned DEtector
Abstract: This paper introduces a learning-based approach for detecting repeatable keypoints under significant imaging changes due to weather and lighting conditions, factors that pose significant challenges for state-of-the-art keypoint detectors. The method initially identifies good keypoint candidates within multiple training images captured from the same viewpoint. Subsequently, a regressor is trained to predict a score map, where maxima correspond to these keypoints, enabling their identification through simple non-maximum suppression. Since standard datasets for testing the influence of these changes are lacking, a new dataset has been created and will be made publicly available. The proposed method demonstrates significant outperformance compared to state-of-the-art methods in challenging conditions, while maintaining state-of-the-art performance on the untrained Oxford dataset.
label: AI

title: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator
Abstract: Automatically describing the content of an image is a fundamental problem in artificial intelligence, bridging computer vision and natural language processing. This paper presents a generative model based on a deep recurrent architecture, combining recent advancements in computer vision and machine translation for generating natural sentences describing images. The model is trained to maximize the likelihood of the target description sentence given the training image. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate the model's accuracy and the fluency of the language it learns solely from image descriptions. The model often exhibits high accuracy, verified both qualitatively and quantitatively. For instance, while the current state-of-the-art BLEU-1 score on the Pascal dataset is 25, this approach achieves 59, approaching human performance at 69. Significant BLEU-1 score improvements are also observed on Flickr30k (from 56 to 66) and SBU (from 19 to 28). On the recently released COCO dataset, the model achieves a BLEU-4 score of 27.7, setting the current state-of-the-art.
