title: Joint cross-domain classification and subspace learning for unsupervised adaptation
Abstract: Domain adaptation aims to transfer knowledge acquired in a source domain to a new, different, but related target domain. In the unsupervised scenario, where no labeled target data are available, various approaches have been proposed for classification tasks. While much research focuses on finding a domain-invariant representation, leaving the prediction function definition for a later stage, this paper proposes a method for jointly learning both. Specifically, it learns the source subspace that best aligns with the target subspace while simultaneously minimizing a regularized misclassification loss. An alternating optimization technique based on stochastic sub-gradient descent is employed to solve the learning problem, demonstrating its effectiveness across several domain adaptation tasks.
label: AI

title: Fully Convolutional Neural Networks for Crowd Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes a fast fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) for crowd segmentation. By replacing fully connected layers in CNNs with 1x1 convolution kernels, FCNNs process entire images as inputs and directly output segmentation maps through a single forward propagation pass. This approach retains translation invariance like patch-by-patch scanning while significantly reducing computational cost. Once trained, FCNNs can process input images of arbitrary sizes without warping them to a fixed size. These attractive properties make it extensible to other general image segmentation problems. Based on FCNN, a multi-stage deep learning framework is proposed to integrate appearance and motion cues for crowd segmentation. Both appearance filters and motion filters are pre-trained stage-by-stage and then jointly optimized. Various combination methods are investigated. The effectiveness of the proposed approach and its component-wise analysis are evaluated on two crowd segmentation datasets created by the authors, encompassing image frames from 235 and 11 scenes, respectively. These datasets, currently the largest for crowd segmentation, will be made publicly available.
label: AI

title: A Nonparametric Bayesian Approach Toward Stacked Convolutional Independent Component Analysis
Abstract: Unsupervised feature learning algorithms based on convolutional formulations of independent components analysis (ICA) have yielded state-of-the-art results in several action recognition benchmarks. However, existing approaches lack the ability to automatically infer the number of latent components (features) from the data in an unsupervised manner. This limitation significantly burdens researchers and practitioners, who must resort to tedious cross-validation procedures to find the optimal number of latent features. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a convolutional nonparametric Bayesian sparse ICA architecture for overcomplete feature learning from high-dimensional data. The method utilizes an Indian buffet process prior to facilitate inference of the appropriate number of latent features under a hybrid variational inference algorithm, scalable to massive datasets. As shown, the model can be naturally applied to obtain deep unsupervised hierarchical feature extractors by greedily stacking successive model layers, similar to existing approaches. Furthermore, inference for this model is entirely heuristics-free, eliminating the need for tedious parameter tuning, a major challenge in most deep learning approaches. The method is evaluated on several action recognition benchmarks, highlighting its advantages over state-of-the-art methods.
label: AI

title: Automatic Subspace Learning via Principal Coefficients Embedding
Abstract: This paper addresses two key challenges in unsupervised subspace learning: 1) automatic identification of the feature dimension of the learned subspace (automatic subspace learning), and 2) learning the underlying subspace in the presence of Gaussian noise (robust subspace learning). The proposed method, called principal coefficients embedding (PCE), simultaneously solves these problems. For a given dataset  D  ∈  ℝ  m×n  , PCE recovers a clean dataset  D  0  ∈  ℝ  m×n  from  D  and concurrently learns a global reconstruction relation  C  ∈  ℝ  n×n  of  D  0  . By preserving  C  in an  m'  -dimensional space, the method obtains a projection matrix that captures the latent manifold structure of  D  0  , where  m'  ≪  m  is automatically determined by the rank of  C  with theoretical guarantees. PCE offers three advantages: 1) automatic feature dimension determination even when data are sampled from a union of multiple linear subspaces in the presence of Gaussian noise, 2) robustness to non-Gaussian noise (e.g., random pixel corruption) and real disguises despite the objective function considering only Gaussian noise, and 3) a closed-form solution enabling fast computation. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the superiority of PCE on various databases in terms of classification accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

title: Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Networks for Visual Recognition and Description
Abstract: Models based on deep convolutional networks have dominated recent image interpretation tasks. This paper explores the effectiveness of recurrent, or "temporally deep," models for tasks involving sequences, both visual and otherwise. A novel recurrent convolutional architecture suitable for large-scale visual learning is developed, fully trainable end-to-end, and its value is demonstrated on benchmark video recognition tasks, image description and retrieval problems, and video narration challenges. Unlike existing models that assume a fixed spatio-temporal receptive field or simple temporal averaging for sequential processing, recurrent convolutional models are "doubly deep" in that they can be compositional in spatial and temporal "layers." This architecture may be advantageous when target concepts are complex or training data is limited. Learning long-term dependencies becomes possible with the incorporation of nonlinearities into the network state updates. Long-term RNN models are attractive because they directly map variable-length inputs (e.g., video frames) to variable-length outputs (e.g., natural language text) and can model complex temporal dynamics while being optimized using backpropagation. These recurrent long-term models are directly connected to modern visual convnet models, enabling joint training to simultaneously learn temporal dynamics and convolutional perceptual representations. The results demonstrate the distinct advantages of these models over state-of-the-art recognition or generation models, which are separately defined and/or optimized.
label: AI

title: A Latent Clothing Attribute Approach for Human Pose Estimation
Abstract: Human pose estimation (HPE), a fundamental technique crucial for various vision tasks like image parsing, action recognition, and clothing retrieval, has been extensively investigated in recent years. Accurate and reliable human pose estimation benefits significantly from utilizing clothing attributes. However, most prior approaches require manual annotation of these attributes, incurring substantial cost. This paper proposes and explores a *latent* clothing attribute approach for HPE. Unlike previous methods, this approach models clothing attributes as latent variables, eliminating the need for explicit labeling. Inference of these latent variables is achieved using the framework of latent structured support vector machines (LSSVM). The LSSVM model is trained using an *alternating direction* strategy: in each iteration, one type of variable (e.g., human pose or clothing attribute) is fixed while the other is optimized. Extensive experiments on two real-world benchmarks demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of the proposed approach.

title: Ten Years of Pedestrian Detection, What Have We Learned?
Abstract: Analyzing individual research papers can obscure the broader picture. This paper delves into the remarkable progress made over the past decade in pedestrian detection by examining the main ideas explored in the 40+ detectors currently included in the Caltech pedestrian detection benchmark. The analysis reveals three distinct families of approaches, all achieving comparable detection quality. Building upon this analysis, the paper investigates the complementarity of the most promising ideas by combining multiple published strategies. This newly developed decision forest detector achieves the current best known performance on the challenging Caltech-USA dataset.
label: AI

title: Combining contextual and local edges for line segment extraction in cluttered images
Abstract: Automatic line segment extraction methods typically assume that line segments are pronounced, thin, infrequent, non-intersecting, and free from noise and clutter. As these assumptions often fail in real-world scenarios, many line segments are missed or fragmented. In severe cases, extraction can fail entirely, particularly for methods relying on the Hough Transform. This paper proposes a method to address these issues. The key aspect is the combination of thresholded image derivatives obtained using filters with large and small footprints, referred to as contextual and local edges, respectively. Contextual edges are robust to noise and are used to select valid local edges, those that share the same type (dark-to-bright transition or vice-versa) as contextual edges. If the distance between valid local edges does not exceed a maximum threshold, connectivity is enforced by marking them and the intervening pixels as edge points. This process generates connected edge maps that are robust and well-localized. A powerful two-sample statistical test is employed to compute contextual edges, which are introduced briefly as they are unfamiliar to the image processing community. Experiments with synthetic and real images demonstrate the method's effectiveness in extracting complete segments of all lengths and widths in various situations where current methods fail. |||

title: Efficient Object Localization Using Convolutional Networks
Abstract: Deep convolutional networks (ConvNets) have significantly advanced the field of human-body pose estimation. However, traditional ConvNet architectures rely on pooling and sub-sampling layers, which, while reducing computational requirements and promoting invariance, also compromise localization accuracy. This work introduces a novel architecture featuring an efficient "position refinement" model trained to estimate joint offset locations within small image regions. This refinement model is jointly trained in a cascade with a state-of-the-art ConvNet model, achieving enhanced accuracy in human joint location estimation. Our detector's variance approaches that of human annotations on the FLIC dataset, surpassing all existing methods on the MPII-human-pose dataset.
label: AI

title: Efficient and Accurate Approximations of Nonlinear Convolutional Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to accelerate the test-time computation of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), focusing on nonlinear units rather than approximating linear filters or responses. Our approach minimizes the reconstruction error of nonlinear responses subject to a low-rank constraint, reducing filter complexity. An effective solution for this constrained nonlinear optimization problem is developed, along with an algorithm to reduce accumulated error when approximating multiple layers. We demonstrate a 4x whole-model speedup on a large ImageNet-trained network, with a mere 0.9% increase in top-5 error rate. Our accelerated model achieves comparable speed to "AlexNet" while exhibiting 4.7% higher accuracy.
label: AI

title: Revisiting Kernelized Locality-Sensitive Hashing for Improved Large-Scale Image Retrieval
Abstract: This paper presents a novel perspective on kernelized locality-sensitive hashing (KLSH), a widely used technique for approximate nearest-neighbor searches in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). By viewing the KLSH algorithm in an appropriately projected space, we eliminate conceptual difficulties present in existing interpretations, provide the first formal retrieval performance bounds for KLSH, and unveil two techniques for boosting its empirical performance. Evaluating these extensions on large-scale benchmark image retrieval datasets, we demonstrate a recall performance improvement of at least 12%, and often significantly higher, compared to the standard KLSH method.
label: AI

title: Definition of Visual Speech Element and Research on a Method of Extracting Feature Vector for Korean Lip-Reading
Abstract: This paper introduces the concept of visemes (visual speech elements) and outlines a method for extracting visual feature vectors. We define 10 visemes based on vowel analysis of Korean utterances and propose a method for extracting 20-dimensional visual feature vectors, incorporating both static and dynamic features. Finally, we evaluate the efficiency of word recognition based on 3-viseme Hidden Markov Models (HMMs).
label: AI

title: Anisotropic Agglomerative Adaptive Mean-Shift
Abstract: Mean Shift, commonly used for mode detection and clustering, faces challenges due to assumptions of isotropicity and homoscedasticity. This paper introduces an adaptive Mean Shift methodology that enables full anisotropic clustering through unsupervised local bandwidth selection. Bandwidth matrices evolve naturally, adapting locally through agglomeration and guiding further agglomeration. This online methodology is practical and effective for low-dimensional feature spaces, preserving detail and clustering salience. Unlike conventional Mean Shift methods that critically depend on per-instance bandwidth choices or rely on inflexible offline methods, our approach alleviates this issue through its adaptive design, with a default form generally performing well. Nonetheless, the methodology allows for effective fine-tuning of results.
label: AI

title: Deep Deconvolutional Networks for Scene Parsing
Abstract: Scene parsing, a fundamental and challenging problem in computer vision, requires labeling each pixel in an image with its corresponding category. Traditionally tackled using hand-engineered features derived from color information, recent advancements have employed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically learn feature hierarchies, achieving record performance. These approaches typically involve post-processing techniques like superpixels to produce final labeling. This paper proposes a novel network architecture that combines deep deconvolutional neural networks with CNNs. Our experiments show that deconvolutional neural networks excel at learning higher-order image structure beyond edge primitives compared to CNNs. This new architecture is utilized for multi-patch training, which effectively learns spatial priors from scenes. Our approach yields state-of-the-art performance on four scene parsing datasets: Stanford Background, SIFT Flow, CamVid, and KITTI. Furthermore, our system features a fully automated end-to-end training system that eliminates the need for post-processing.
label: AI

title: GASP : Geometric Association with Surface Patches
Abstract: A fundamental challenge in sensory processing tasks for perception and robotics is establishing data associations across different views. This paper presents a robust solution for determining potentially dense surface patch (superpixel) associations using only range information. Our approach involves decomposing a view into regularized surface patches, representing them as sequences expressing geometry invariantly over their superpixel neighborhoods as uniquely consistent partial orderings. These representations are matched using an optimal sequence comparison metric based on the Damerau-Levenshtein distance, enabling robust association with quadratic complexity (in contrast to NP-complete joint matching formulations). Our approach is capable of performing under wide baselines, heavy rotations, partial overlaps, significant occlusions, and sensor noise. This technique does not require any priors, including motion or scene structure assumptions, and is invulnerable to ambiguities related to textureless or aliased content. We demonstrate promising qualitative and quantitative results under diverse settings, comparing our method with popular approaches based on range as well as RGB-D data.
label: AI

title: 6 Seconds of Sound and Vision: Creativity in Micro-Videos
Abstract: The notion of creativity, distinct from concepts like beauty or interestingness, has not been studied from the perspective of automatic multimedia content analysis. The emergence of short online videos shared on social media platforms, or micro-videos, provides a new medium for creative expression. This paper investigates creative micro-videos to understand features that contribute to their creativity and addresses the problem of automatically detecting creative content. Defining creative videos as those that are novel and possess aesthetic value, we conducted a crowdsourcing experiment to create a dataset of over 3,800 micro-videos labeled as creative and non-creative. We propose a set of computational features mapped to the components of our creativity definition and conduct an analysis to determine which features correlate most strongly with creative videos. Finally, we evaluate a supervised approach for automatic creative video detection, achieving promising results that highlight the necessity of modeling both aesthetic value and novelty for optimal classification accuracy.
label: AI

title: A Faster Method for Tracking and Scoring Videos Corresponding to Sentences
Abstract: Prior work introduced the sentence tracker, a method for scoring how well a sentence describes a video clip or vice versa. This paper presents an improved method for optimizing the same cost function employed by this prior work, reducing space complexity from exponential in sentence length to polynomial. This new method achieves qualitatively identical results in time polynomial in sentence length, replacing the original exponential time complexity. As this method is plug-compatible with the previous one, it can be used for the same applications: video retrieval with sentential queries, generating sentential video descriptions, and focusing tracker attention with a sentence. Moreover, this allows these applications to scale with significantly larger numbers of object detections, word meanings modeled with HMMs with significantly larger numbers of states, and significantly longer sentences, without significant degradation in result quality.
label: AI

title: Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation
Abstract: Convolutional networks are powerful visual models that generate hierarchies of features. This paper demonstrates that convolutional networks alone, trained end-to-end from pixels to pixels, surpass state-of-the-art performance in semantic segmentation. Our key insight lies in building "fully convolutional" networks that handle arbitrary input sizes and produce correspondingly sized outputs with efficient inference and learning. We define and detail the space of fully convolutional networks, explain their application to spatially dense prediction tasks, and draw connections to prior models. We adapt contemporary classification networks (AlexNet, the VGG net, and GoogLeNet) into fully convolutional networks and transfer their learned representations by fine-tuning for the segmentation task. We then define a novel architecture that combines semantic information from a deep, coarse layer with appearance information from a shallow, fine layer to produce accurate and detailed segmentations. Our fully convolutional network achieves state-of-the-art segmentation of PASCAL VOC (20% relative improvement to 62.2% mean IU on 2012), NYUDv2, and SIFT Flow, while inference takes one-third of a second for a typical image.

title: Sparse And Low Rank Decomposition Based Batch Image Alignment for Speckle Reduction of retinal OCT Images
Abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is an emerging biomedical imaging technique with applications in ophthalmology, dermatology, coronary imaging, and more. Due to its underlying physics, OCT images often exhibit a granular pattern known as speckle noise, hindering interpretation. This paper utilizes a sparse and low-rank decomposition method for speckle reduction in retinal OCT images. This technique operates on input data comprising multiple B-scans of the same location. The next step involves batch alignment of the images using a sparse and low-rank decomposition-based technique. Finally, the denoised image is generated by median filtering the low-rank component of the processed data. Simultaneous decomposition and alignment of the images result in superior performance compared to simple registration-based methods commonly used for noise reduction in OCT images.
label: AI

title: A Discriminative CNN Video Representation for Event Detection
Abstract: This paper proposes a discriminative video representation for event detection on large-scale video datasets when limited hardware resources are available. Focusing on leveraging deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to advance event detection, where only frame-level static descriptors can be extracted by existing CNN toolkits, this paper makes two contributions to CNN video representation inference. First, while average pooling and max pooling have been standard approaches for aggregating frame-level static features, we demonstrate that performance can be significantly improved by employing an appropriate encoding method. Second, we propose using a set of latent concept descriptors as the frame descriptor, enriching visual information while maintaining computational affordability. Integrating these two contributions results in state-of-the-art performance in event detection on the largest video datasets. Compared to improved Dense Trajectories, recognized as the best video representation for event detection, our new representation improves Mean Average Precision (mAP) from 27.6% to 36.8% for the TRECVID MEDTest 14 dataset and from 34.0% to 44.6% for the TRECVID MEDTest 13 dataset. This work forms the core of the winning solution of our CMU-Informedia team in the TRECVID MED 2014 competition.

title: A convex formulation for hyperspectral image superresolution via subspace-based regularization
Abstract: Hyperspectral remote sensing images (HSIs) typically exhibit high spectral resolution and low spatial resolution, while multispectral images (MSIs) possess low spectral and high spatial resolutions. The problem of inferring images that combine the high spectral and spatial resolutions of HSIs and MSIs, respectively, is a data fusion problem that has garnered significant research attention due to the increasing availability of HSIs and MSIs from the same geographical area. This paper formulates this problem as the minimization of a convex objective function comprising two quadratic data-fitting terms and an edge-preserving regularizer. The data-fitting terms account for blur, different resolutions, and additive noise. The regularizer, a form of vector Total Variation, promotes piecewise-smooth solutions with discontinuities aligned across the hyperspectral bands. The downsampling operator accounting for different spatial resolutions, the non-quadratic and non-smooth nature of the regularizer, and the vast size of the HSI to be estimated present a challenging optimization problem. We address these challenges by leveraging the fact that HSIs generally "live" in a low-dimensional subspace and tailoring the Split Augmented Lagrangian Shrinkage Algorithm (SALSA), an instance of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), to this optimization problem through convenient variable splitting. The spatial blur and the spectral linear operators associated with the HSI and MSI acquisition processes are also estimated, resulting in an effective algorithm that outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, as demonstrated in experiments with simulated and real-life data.

title: Deep Belief Network Training Improvement Using Elite Samples Minimizing Free Energy
Abstract: Deep architectures are becoming increasingly popular in machine learning. Deep Belief Networks (DBNs) are deep architectures that utilize stacks of Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) to create a powerful generative model using training data. This paper presents an improvement on a commonly used method for training RBMs. The new method utilizes free energy as a criterion to obtain elite samples from the generative model. We argue that these samples can more accurately compute the gradient of the log probability of training data. Our results demonstrate an error rate of 0.99% on the MNIST test set, outperforming the method presented in the original DBN paper (1.25% error rate) and general classification methods like SVM (1.4% error rate) and KNN (1.6% error rate). In another test using the ISOLET dataset, letter classification error dropped to 3.59% compared to 5.59% achieved in previous studies using this dataset. The implemented method is available online at "http://ceit.aut.ac.ir/~keyvanrad/DeeBNet Toolbox.html".

title: Predictive Encoding of Contextual Relationships for Perceptual Inference, Interpolation and Prediction
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel neurally-inspired model that learns to encode the global relationship context of visual events across time and space, using this contextual information to modulate the analysis-by-synthesis process within a predictive coding framework. The model learns latent contextual representations by maximizing the predictability of visual events based on local and global contextual information through both top-down and bottom-up processes. Unlike standard predictive coding models, the prediction error in this model updates the contextual representation without altering the feedforward input for the next layer, aligning more closely with neurophysiological observations. We demonstrate the model's computational feasibility by showcasing its abilities in several aspects. Our model surpasses the performance of gated Boltzmann machines (GBMs) in estimating contextual information. It can also interpolate missing events or predict future events in image sequences while simultaneously estimating contextual information. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of prediction accuracy across various tasks and possesses the ability to interpolate missing frames, a function lacking in GBMs.

title: Gaze Stabilization for Humanoid Robots: a Comprehensive Framework
Abstract: Gaze stabilization is a crucial requirement for humanoid robots. Previous research in this area has focused on integrating inertial and visual information, neglecting the contribution of the robot's own movement knowledge. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for gaze stabilization in humanoid robots, concentrating on compensating for disturbances induced in cameras due to self-generated movements. We employ two separate signals for stabilization: (1) an anticipatory term derived from the velocity commands sent to the joints during autonomous robot movement; (2) a feedback term from the onboard gyroscope, compensating for unpredictable external disturbances. We provide the mathematical formulation for deriving the forward and differential kinematics of the stereo system's fixation point. Finally, we test our method on the iCub robot. Our results show that stabilization consistently reduces residual optical flow during robot movement and in the presence of external disturbances. We also demonstrate the critical role of proper integration of neck degrees of freedom in achieving accurate stabilization.

title: Window-Based Descriptors for Arabic Handwritten Alphabet Recognition: A Comparative Study on a Novel Dataset
Abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of window-based descriptors for Arabic handwritten alphabet recognition, providing a detailed experimental evaluation of different descriptors with several classifiers. The objective is to assess the performance of various window-based descriptors on the problem of Arabic letter recognition. Our experiments clearly show that these descriptors perform exceptionally well. Furthermore, we introduce a novel spatial pyramid partitioning scheme that enhances recognition accuracy for most descriptors. Additionally, we present a novel dataset for Arabic handwritten isolated alphabet letters, serving as a benchmark for future research.

title: A Comparative Study of Techniques of Distant Reconstruction of Displacement Fields by using DISTRESS Simulator
Abstract: Reconstruction and monitoring of displacement and strain fields are critical in engineering. This paper analyzes remote and non-obtrusive strain measurement methods based on photogrammetry and Digital Image Correlation (DIC). The method involves covering the photographed surface with a pattern of speckles and comparing images taken before and after deformation. This study provides a comprehensive literature review and comparative analysis of photogrammetric solutions. The analysis is conducted using a specially developed Digital Image Synthesizer To Reconstruct Strain in Solids (DISTRESS) Simulator to generate synthetic images of displacement and stress fields, investigating the intrinsic accuracy of existing DIC variants. We examined Basic DIC and a commercial software, VIC 2D, both based on displacement field reconstruction with post-processing strain determination through numerical differentiation. We also investigated Extended DIC, where the strain field is determined independently of the displacement field. While Basic DIC and VIC 2D are faster, Extended DIC delivers the highest accuracy in strain reconstruction. The speckle pattern plays a crucial role in achieving high DIC accuracy. Increasing subset size for DIC does not significantly improve accuracy, while the smallest subset size depends on the speckle pattern and size. Increasing the overall image size provides more detail but does not significantly improve accuracy, while substantially increasing computational cost.

title: Person Re-identification Based on Color Histogram and Spatial Configuration of Dominant Color Regions
Abstract: Person re-identification, determining if a person of interest has been observed in a network of video surveillance cameras, poses a significant challenge. Human appearance captured by different cameras varies due to differences in illumination, pose, viewpoint, and camera parameters. This paper proposes a novel method for person re-identification based on the dominant color histogram and spatial configuration of dominant color regions on human body parts. The dominant color histogram and spatial configuration of dominant color regions based on the dominant color descriptor (DCD) exhibit robustness to changes in illumination, pose, and viewpoint. We evaluate our proposed method using benchmark video datasets. Experimental results using the cumulative matching characteristic (CMC) curve demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach for person re-identification.

title: Amoeba Techniques for Shape and Texture Analysis
Abstract: Morphological amoebas are image-adaptive structuring elements for morphological and other local image filters introduced by Lerallut et al. Their construction involves combining spatial distance with contrast information into an image-dependent metric. Amoeba filters exhibit interesting parallels to image filtering methods based on partial differential equations (PDEs), as confirmed by asymptotic equivalence results. In computing amoebas, graph structures are generated that contain information about local image texture. This paper reviews and summarizes the work of the author and his coauthors on morphological amoebas, particularly their relationships with PDE filters and texture analysis. It presents some extensions and points towards future research directions in this area. |||

title: Sparse Modeling for Image and Vision Processing
Abstract: Sparse models have garnered significant interest in various disciplines, including statistics, machine learning, and signal processing. This monograph provides a comprehensive overview of sparse modeling techniques, specifically focusing on their application to visual recognition and image processing. The emphasis lies on learning data-adapted dictionaries, leading to compact representations with proven efficacy across multiple domains.

title: Multi-modal Image Registration for Correlative Microscopy
Abstract: Correlative microscopy, a technique combining light microscopy with high-resolution electron microscopy and other modalities, presents unique challenges for image registration. This report presents two registration methods specifically designed for correlative microscopy. The first method relies on fiducial beads, generating landmarks for similarity transformation computation and subsequent refinement. The second method draws inspiration from image analogies, integrating sparse representation models to transfer images between different modalities. This approach transforms a multi-modal registration problem into a mono-modal one, achieving promising results when tested on TEM and confocal microscopy images.
label: AI

title: On Coarse Graining of Information and Its Application to Pattern Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes a method for classifying observations into distinct categories using finite mixture models. The component densities for the mixture model are derived using the maximum entropy method and conservation of Pythagorean means, resulting in distributions belonging to the Pythagorean family. The paper also explores parameter estimation for the model and discusses the determination of the number of categories.
label: AI

title: Part Detector Discovery in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Fine-grained object classification methods often rely on precise localization of object parts to extract discriminative features. However, part localization is a challenging task due to variations in appearance and pose. This paper presents a novel approach, "part detector discovery" (PDD), which utilizes pre-trained convolutional neural networks to achieve robust and efficient object part localization without requiring dataset-specific training. PDD analyzes the gradient maps of network outputs to identify activation centers related to semantic parts or bounding boxes. This method achieves outstanding performance on the CUB200-2011 dataset, enabling joint detection and classification without relying on ground-truth parts during training.

title: Collecting Image Description Datasets using Crowdsourcing
Abstract: This paper introduces two new image datasets with human-generated descriptions. Both datasets, collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk, provide significantly more descriptions per image compared to existing datasets. One dataset is based on the UIUC Pascal Sentence Dataset, while the other utilizes the Abstract Scenes dataset, consisting of images composed from clipart objects. The paper details the interfaces used for data collection, analyzes dataset properties, and presents example descriptions from both datasets.

title: 3D Shape Estimation from 2D Landmarks: A Convex Relaxation Approach
Abstract: Estimating the 3D shape of an object from a single image with 2D landmarks presents a challenging reconstruction problem. Confining the unknown 3D shape within a shape space built from existing shapes is a common approach to mitigate ambiguity. However, jointly estimating shape and camera-pose parameters requires solving a nonconvex optimization problem, leading to initialization-dependent solutions. This paper proposes a convex formulation to address this issue, developing an efficient algorithm to solve the resulting convex program. The proposed method exhibits exact recovery properties, demonstrating advantages over alternative methods and applicability in human pose and car shape estimation.
label: AI

title: Computational Baby Learning
Abstract: Inspired by the human ability to learn new visual concepts from limited positive examples, this paper proposes a computational model for slightly-supervised object detection. The model incorporates prior knowledge through a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), utilizes exemplar learning for initial concept detection, and incorporates video contexts for further learning. By simulating interaction with the real world, the model tracks diverse instances in unlabeled videos, refining the concept detector iteratively. Experimental results on Pascal VOC object detection datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving state-of-the-art performance with limited training samples.
label: AI

title: Unifying Visual-Semantic Embeddings with Multimodal Neural Language Models
Abstract: Drawing on recent advances in multimodal learning and machine translation, this paper introduces an encoder-decoder pipeline that learns a joint embedding space for images and text, along with a novel language model for decoding representations from this space. The pipeline effectively unifies joint image-text embedding models with multimodal neural language models. The structure-content neural language model disentangles sentence structure and content, conditioned on encoder representations. This enables image and sentence ranking, as well as novel description generation. Using LSTMs for sentence encoding, the model achieves state-of-the-art performance on Flickr8K and Flickr30K without using object detections. The learned embedding space captures multimodal regularities, as demonstrated by vector space arithmetic, allowing the model to perform tasks like adding "red" to "image of a blue car" to obtain representations near images of red cars.
label: AI

title: Infinite Object Coating in the Amoebot Model
Abstract: Programmable matter refers to materials with the ability to change physical properties based on user input or autonomous sensing, enabling applications in smart materials, autonomous monitoring and repair, and minimally invasive surgery. This paper introduces the Amoebot model, a novel framework inspired by amoeba behavior for modeling self-organizing particles and facilitating rigorous algorithmic research in programmable matter. The paper presents an algorithm for coating an infinite object within this model, proving its correctness and work-optimality.
label: AI

title: An Improved Tracking using IMU and Vision Fusion for Mobile Augmented Reality Applications
Abstract: Mobile Augmented Reality (MAR) is becoming increasingly prevalent as a cyber-physical system application, with accurate and robust registration and tracking crucial for operating in unprepared environments. This paper presents results and insights gained during the development of a prototype MAR system for vehicle damage assessment. The novelty lies in integrating different components and modules with enhancements towards a complete working system, addressing the challenges of marker-less tracking and sensor fusion for tele-interactive applications involving large distances.
label: AI

title: Zero-Aliasing Correlation Filters for Object Recognition
Abstract: Correlation filters (CFs) are a class of classifiers widely used for object localization and tracking. Traditionally, CFs are designed in the frequency domain using the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) for efficient correlation computation. However, existing CF designs overlook the fact that DFT multiplication in the frequency domain corresponds to circular correlation in the time/spatial domain. This paper introduces new zero-aliasing constraints that eliminate this aliasing problem, ensuring optimization criteria accurately reflect the intended linear correlation. The proposed design significantly improves previous CFs, with experimental results showcasing its benefits across diverse datasets. Code for the CFs and their zero-aliasing versions is made available online.
label: AI

title: Applications of sampling Kantorovich operators to thermographic images for seismic engineering
Abstract: This paper explores applications of the multivariate sampling Kantorovich operators ($S_w$) to seismic engineering. The mathematical theory of these operators, both in the space of continuous functions and in Orlicz spaces, demonstrates their ability to approximate and reconstruct multivariate signals, including images. A mathematical algorithm is developed using MATLAB and matrix calculus for reconstructing thermographic images, enabling the simulation of structural behavior under seismic action. The paper analyzes a real-world case study, comparing the behavior of the building under seismic action using various models.
label: AI

title: Two maximum entropy based algorithms for running quantile estimation in non-stationary data streams
Abstract: Estimating the quantile of a distribution is essential for many computer vision and signal processing applications, particularly in semi-automatic surveillance systems that detect abnormalities in CCTV footage using statistical models. This paper addresses the challenge of estimating the running quantile of a data stream with limited memory. It highlights the limitations of existing approaches for non-stationary streams, introduces a novel principle for storage space utilization, and presents two new algorithms that exploit this principle. Comprehensive evaluation on synthetic data and real-world surveillance streams demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed algorithms compared to existing methods, achieving significantly lower estimate errors even with reduced memory.
label: AI

title: Abnormal Object Recognition: A Comprehensive Study
Abstract: Humans tend to describe images by highlighting what they find interesting, often focusing on abnormalities or deviations from typicalities. This paper introduces abnormality detection as a recognition problem, showcasing how to model typicalities and identify meaningful deviations from prototypical category properties. The proposed model can recognize abnormalities and explain the reasons behind them. The paper introduces an abnormality detection dataset and presents results demonstrating the model's ability to reason about abnormalities.
label: AI

title: Stacked Quantizers for Compositional Vector Compression
Abstract: Additive Quantization (AQ), a generalization of Product Quantization (PQ), utilizes non-independent codebooks to compress vectors into binary codes. While offering improved accuracy, AQ suffers from NP-hard optimal encoding. This paper observes that both PQ and AQ lie on extremes of codebook dependence-independence and proposes an intermediate approach exploiting a hierarchical structure in codebooks. This method achieves comparable or lower quantization error than AQ, while being significantly faster. The paper performs a complexity analysis of PQ, AQ, and the proposed method, evaluating its performance on standard benchmarks and datasets with features extracted from state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks.
label: AI

title: Fast Mesh-Based Medical Image Registration
Abstract: This paper presents a fast triangular mesh-based registration method for image alignment. The template image is triangulated using a content-adaptive mesh generation algorithm, and spline interpolation is used to interpolate pixel values at mesh nodes for both images. The energy functional needed for registration is minimized by discretizing the distance measure and regularization term using a mesh-based approach. The resulting sparse system of linear equations, due to its smaller size compared to pixel-wise registration, can be solved directly. Experimental results demonstrate faster registration compared to pixel-based curvature registration, achieving significant speedup using a fast DCT solver.
label: AI

title: Parallax Effect Free Mosaicing of Underwater Video Sequence Based on Texture Features
Abstract: This paper proposes a feature-based technique for constructing mosaic images from underwater video sequences, which often suffer from parallax distortion due to light propagation properties. Existing mosaicing tools and underwater image mosaicing techniques often result in artifacts like blurring, ghosting, and seams due to parallax. This approach minimizes parallax effects by incorporating efficient local alignment after global registration. Centre Symmetric Local Binary Pattern (CS-LBP) descriptors are used to extract texture features and find correspondences, which are then used to estimate homography through RANSAC. Colour alignment preprocessing based on colour distribution adjustment enhances global registration accuracy. To reduce computational cost, frames with minimal overlap are selected for mosaicing. This approach effectively minimizes parallax effects in the final mosaic constructed from underwater video sequences.
