title: Compositional Structure Learning for Action Understanding
Abstract: The focus of the action understanding literature has predominantly been on classification. However, numerous applications, such as mobile robotics and video search, necessitate richer action understanding, encompassing solutions for classification, localization, and detection. This paper proposes a compositional model that leverages a novel mid-level representation called compositional trajectories and a locally articulated spatiotemporal deformable parts model (LALSDPM) for comprehensive action understanding. Our method excels in capturing the variable structure of dynamic human activity over a long range. First, compositional trajectories capture long-ranging, frequently co-occurring groups of trajectories in space-time and represent them in discriminative hierarchies, separating human motion from camera motion. Second, LASTDPM learns a structured model with multi-layer deformable parts to capture multiple levels of articulated motion. We implement our methods and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across all three problems: action detection, localization, and recognition.

title: Attentive monitoring of multiple video streams driven by a Bayesian foraging strategy
Abstract: This paper explores the problem of deploying attention to subsets of video streams to collate the most relevant data and information related to a given task. We formalize this monitoring problem as a foraging problem. We propose a probabilistic framework to model the observer's attentive behavior as the behavior of a forager. The forager, at every moment, focuses its attention on the most informative stream/camera, detects interesting objects or activities, or switches to a more profitable stream. The approach proposed here is suitable for multi-stream video summarization. Moreover, it can serve as a preliminary step for more sophisticated video surveillance, such as activity and behavior analysis. Experimental results obtained on the UCR Videoweb Activities Dataset, a publicly available dataset, illustrate the utility of the proposed technique.

title: Mobility Enhancement for Elderly
Abstract: Loss of mobility is a common handicap affecting senior citizens, hindering their ease of movement for activities such as outdoor visits, movement in hospitals, social outings, and essential daily in-house routine functions. Relying on servants or domestic help and simple wheelchairs is not only costly in the long run but also forces senior citizens to be reliant on others, diminishing their dignity. To provide a dignified life, the mobility obtained must be at the complete discretion, will, and control of the senior citizen. This can only be achieved through a reasonably sophisticated and versatile wheelchair, offering enhanced vision and hearing through man-machine interfaces, and sensor-aided navigation and control. Senior citizens often have poor vision, making visual judgment difficult and necessitating the use of artificial intelligence in visual image analysis and guided navigation systems. This project focuses on two important mobility enhancement features: audio command and vision-aided obstacle detection and navigation. We have implemented a speech recognition algorithm using a template of stored words to identify voice commands given by the user, freeing up a hand for operating a joystick or mouse control. We have also developed a novel appearance-based obstacle detection system using stereo-vision cameras that estimates the distance of the nearest obstacle to the wheelchair and takes appropriate action. This helps the user make better route judgments and navigate obstacles. The main challenge in this project is navigating in unknown or unfamiliar environments while avoiding obstacles.

title: Learning to Rank Binary Codes
Abstract: Binary codes have been extensively used in vision problems as a compact feature representation to achieve both space and time advantages. Various methods have been proposed to learn data-dependent hash functions that map a feature vector to a binary code. However, significant data information is inevitably lost during the binarization step, leading to ambiguity in measuring sample similarity using Hamming distance. Additionally, the learned hash functions cannot be modified after training, making them unable to adapt to new data outside the training dataset. To address these issues, we propose a flexible bitwise weight learning framework based on binary codes obtained from state-of-the-art hashing methods and incorporate the learned weights into weighted Hamming distance computation. We then formulate the proposed framework as a ranking problem and utilize the Ranking SVM model for offline weight learning. The framework is further extended to an online mode that updates the weights each time new data arrives, making it scalable to large and dynamic datasets. Extensive experimental results demonstrate significant performance gains of using binary codes with bitwise weighting in image retrieval tasks. Notably, the online weight learning achieves comparable accuracy to its offline counterpart, making our approach practical for real-world applications.
label: AI

title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Supervised Learning of Brain Connectivity Measures Extracted from Synchrostates
Abstract: Objective: This paper investigates the presence of autism using functional brain connectivity measures derived from electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings of children during face perception tasks. Approach: Phase synchronized patterns from 128-channel EEG signals are obtained for typical children and children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The phase synchronized states, or synchrostates, temporally switch amongst themselves as an underlying process for completing a particular cognitive task. We used 12 subjects in each group (ASD and typical) to analyze their EEG while processing fearful, happy, and neutral faces. The minimal and maximally occurring synchrostates for each subject are selected for extracting brain connectivity features, which are then used to classify between these two groups of subjects. Among different supervised learning techniques, we explored discriminant analysis and support vector machines, both with polynomial kernels, for the classification task. Main Results: Leave-one-out cross-validation of the classification algorithm yields 94.7% accuracy as the best performance, with corresponding sensitivity and specificity values of 85.7% and 100%, respectively. Significance: The proposed method achieves high classification accuracies and outperforms other contemporary research results. The effectiveness of the proposed method for classifying autistic and typical children suggests its potential for use on a larger population to validate its clinical applicability.

title: Remote sensing image classification exploiting multiple kernel learning
Abstract: We propose a strategy for land use classification that exploits Multiple Kernel Learning (MKL) to automatically determine a suitable combination of a set of features without requiring any heuristic knowledge about the classification task. We present a novel procedure that enables MKL to achieve good performance even with small training sets. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Building pattern recognition applications with the SPARE library
Abstract: This paper introduces the SPARE C++ library, an open-source software tool designed for building pattern recognition and soft computing systems. The library adheres to the principle of generality: most of the implemented algorithms can process user-defined input data types transparently, such as labeled graphs and sequences of objects, as well as standard numeric vectors. We present a high-level overview of the SPARE library characteristics, focusing on the practical possibility of constructing pattern recognition systems for various input data types. As a proof of concept, we discuss two application instances involving clustering of real-valued multidimensional sequences and classification of labeled graphs.
label: AI

title: Supervised mid-level features for word image representation
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of learning word image representations: given a cropped image of a word, we aim to find a descriptive, robust, and compact fixed-length representation. Machine learning techniques can then utilize these representations to generate models useful for word retrieval or recognition tasks. While many works have focused on the machine learning aspect after a global representation is produced, little research has been devoted to the construction of these base image representations. Most works directly use standard coding and aggregation techniques on top of standard computer vision features like SIFT or HOG. We propose learning local mid-level features suitable for constructing word image representations. These features are learned by leveraging character bounding box annotations on a small set of training images. Unlike other approaches that use character bounding box information, our approach does not rely on explicitly detecting individual characters at testing time. These local mid-level features can then be aggregated to produce a global word image signature. When paired with the recent word attributes framework of Almazán et al., we achieve results comparable to or better than the state-of-the-art on matching and recognition tasks using global descriptors of only 96 dimensions.

title: The brain as a trigger system
Abstract: There are significant analogies between the issues related to real-time event selection in High Energy Physics (HEP) and those faced by the human visual system. The visual system must rapidly extract the most important elements of the external world from a large flux of information for survival purposes. A rapid and reliable detection of visual stimuli is crucial for triggering autonomic responses to emotive stimuli, initiating adaptive behaviors, and orienting towards potentially interesting or dangerous stimuli. The speed of visual processing can be as fast as 20 ms, approximately 20 times the duration of the elementary information exchanges by the action potential. The limitations to the brain's capacity to process visual information, imposed by intrinsic energetic costs of neuronal activity and ecological limits to the size of the skull, necessitate strong data reduction at an early stage by creating a compact summary of relevant information, the so-called "primal sketch," to be handled by further levels of processing. This is quite similar to the problem in experimental HEP of providing fast data reduction at a reasonable monetary cost and with a practical device size. As a result of a joint effort of HEP physicists and practicing vision scientists, we recently proposed that not only are the problems similar, but the solutions adopted in the two cases also have strong similarities, and their parallel study can shed light on each other. Modeling the visual system as a trigger processor leads to a deeper understanding and even very specific predictions of its functionality. Conversely, the insights gained from this new approach to vision can lead to new ideas for enhancing the capabilities of artificial vision systems, and HEP trigger systems as well.

title: Dense 3D Face Correspondence
Abstract: We present an algorithm that automatically establishes dense correspondences between a large number of 3D faces. Starting from automatically detected sparse correspondences on the outer boundary of 3D faces, the algorithm triangulates existing correspondences and expands them iteratively by matching points of distinctive surface curvature along the triangle edges. After exhausting keypoint matches, further correspondences are established by generating evenly distributed points within triangles by evolving level set geodesic curves from the centroids of large triangles. A deformable model (K3DM) is constructed from the densely corresponded faces, and an algorithm is proposed for morphing the K3DM to fit unseen faces. This algorithm iterates between rigid alignment of an unseen face followed by regularized morphing of the deformable model. We have extensively evaluated the proposed algorithms on synthetic data and real 3D faces from the FRGCv2, Bosphorus, BU3DFE, and UND Ear databases using quantitative and qualitative benchmarks. Our algorithm achieved dense correspondences with a mean localization error of 1.28mm on synthetic faces and detected 14 anthropometric landmarks on unseen real faces from the FRGCv2 database with 3mm precision. Furthermore, our deformable model fitting algorithm achieved 98.5% face recognition accuracy on the FRGCv2 and 98.6% on the Bosphorus database. Our dense model is also able to generalize to unseen datasets. |||

title: Bayesian estimation of the multifractality parameter for image texture using a Whittle approximation
Abstract: Multifractal analysis, a valuable tool for signal and image processing, faces challenges in accurately estimating multifractal parameters for image texture. This is largely attributed to the limitations of current estimation procedures, which rely on linear regressions across frequency scales of the 2D dyadic wavelet transform. The non-Gaussian nature and intricate dependence structure of multifractal processes make model development for parameter estimation difficult. We propose a Bayesian procedure to overcome these difficulties. Our procedure is novel in three ways:  First, we construct a generic semi-parametric statistical model for the logarithm of wavelet leaders. Second, we develop Bayesian estimators associated with this model and the parameter values permitted by multifractal theory. Third, we employ a suitable Whittle approximation within the Bayesian model, enabling the previously infeasible evaluation of the posterior distribution. We numerically evaluate performance across various 2D multifractal processes, image sizes, and process parameters. Our procedure significantly outperforms current benchmarks in terms of estimation performance and its ability to distinguish between the two most common multifractal process models. The performance gains are particularly pronounced for smaller image sizes, enabling for the first time the analysis of image patches as small as 64x64 pixels.
label: AI

title: Olfactory Signal Processing
Abstract: Olfaction, the sense of smell, has received considerably less attention from a signal processing perspective than audition and vision. This paper presents a signal processing paradigm for olfactory signals based on recent scientific discoveries, including the psychophysics concept of olfactory white. We outline a framework for predicting the perception of odorant compounds from their physicochemical features, establishing a foundation for subsequent processing tasks. Formulations for odor cancellation and food steganography are detailed, with real-world empirical examples provided. The paper also discusses adaptive filtering and other olfactory signal processing tasks at a high level.
label: AI

title: Large Vocabulary Arabic Online Handwriting Recognition System
Abstract: Arabic handwriting, characterized by its consonantal and cursive nature, presents unique challenges for analysis. The obligatory dots/strokes placed above or below most letters, often written with a delay, further complicate the process. Due to ambiguities and diverse writing styles, recognition systems typically rely on a lexicon of possible words. While small lexicons prioritize accuracy, large lexicons necessitate both speed and accuracy. The rich morphology and syntax of Arabic create a large lexicon, demanding a practical online handwriting recognition system that can handle this complexity with acceptable performance. This paper introduces a fully-fledged Hidden Markov Model (HMM) based system for Arabic online handwriting recognition that addresses key challenges associated with recognizing the Arabic script. A novel preprocessing technique for handling delayed strokes is presented. Advanced modeling techniques are employed to build a recognition system from training data, providing a more detailed representation of differences between writing units, minimizing variations between writers, and improving feature space representation. System results are enhanced through a post-processing step with a higher order language model and cross-word HMM models. The system's performance is evaluated using two databases, encompassing small and large lexicons. Our system outperforms state-of-the-art systems for the small lexicon database and demonstrates promising results in terms of accuracy and time when handling large lexicons. The models can be adapted for specific writers to achieve even better results.
label: AI

title: KCRC-LCD: Discriminative Kernel Collaborative Representation with Locality Constrained Dictionary for Visual Categorization
Abstract: This paper explores the image classification problem through kernel collaborative representation classification with locality constrained dictionary (KCRC-LCD). We propose a kernel collaborative representation classification (KCRC) approach that leverages kernel methods to enhance the discrimination ability of collaborative representation classification (CRC). To construct a locality constrained dictionary (LCD) for KCRC, we measure the similarity between the query and atoms within the global dictionary. Various similarity measure approaches in LCD are discussed, and a simple yet effective unified similarity measure is presented, demonstrating its superiority through experiments. LCD offers several benefits: First, LCD integrates seamlessly into the KCRC framework, allowing its similarity measure to be kernelized, theoretically connecting CRC and LCD under kernel methods. Second, KCRC-LCD exhibits improved scalability in handling both training set size and feature dimension. Examples show that KCRC perfectly classifies data with specific distributions, while conventional CRC fails completely. Comprehensive experiments conducted on various public datasets indicate that KCRC-LCD serves as a robust discriminative classifier with exceptional performance and scalability, rivaling or exceeding other state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Randomized Structural Sparsity via Constrained Block Subsampling for Improved Sensitivity of Discriminative Voxel Identification
Abstract: This paper focuses on voxel selection for functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) brain data, aiming to identify a more complete set of potentially correlated discriminative voxels to enhance the interpretation of discovered potential biomarkers. The primary challenge lies in the extremely high dimensionality of the voxel space and limited training samples, leading to unreliable feature selection. Stability selection, while gaining traction due to its finite sample control of false discoveries and transparent regularization principle, fails to explicitly utilize the correlation property or structural information of discriminative features, resulting in high false negative rates. This means many relevant, potentially correlated discriminative voxels are missed. To address this, we propose a new variant of stability selection called "randomized structural sparsity", incorporating the concept of structural sparsity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the method's superiority in controlling for false negatives while retaining the control of false positives inherited from stability selection.

title: Learning visual biases from human imagination
Abstract: While the human visual system excels at recognizing concepts under challenging conditions, it still exhibits certain biases. This paper investigates the possibility of extracting these biases and transferring them to a machine recognition system. We introduce a novel method, inspired by established tools in human psychophysics, to estimate the biases the human visual system might use for recognition, but within computer vision feature spaces. Our experiments yield surprising results, suggesting that classifiers from the human visual system can be successfully transferred to a machine. As these classifiers appear to capture beneficial biases in the human visual system, we propose an SVM formulation that constrains the orientation of the SVM hyperplane to align with the bias from the human visual system. Our findings indicate that transferring this human bias to machines could improve object recognition systems' generalization across datasets and enhance performance when limited training data is available.

title: Reconstructive Sparse Code Transfer for Contour Detection and Semantic Labeling
Abstract: We frame the task of predicting semantic labeling as a sparse reconstruction procedure that applies a target-specific learned transfer function to a generic deep sparse code representation of an image. This strategy involves two distinct training stages. First, we learn a set of generic dictionaries optimized for sparse coding of image patches in an unsupervised manner. A multilayer representation is trained via recursive sparse dictionary learning on pooled codes output by earlier layers. Second, we encode all training images using the generic dictionaries and learn a transfer function that optimizes the reconstruction of patches extracted from annotated ground-truth given the sparse codes of their corresponding image patches. At test time, we encode a novel image using the generic dictionaries and reconstruct it using the transfer function. The output reconstruction represents a semantic labeling of the test image. Applying this strategy to contour detection, we demonstrate performance that rivals state-of-the-art systems. Unlike most prior work, our approach eliminates the need for hand-designed features or filters. To illustrate general applicability, we also present initial results on semantic part labeling of human faces. The effectiveness of our approach opens new avenues for research on deep sparse representations. Our classifiers utilize this representation in a novel way. Instead of operating on nodes in the deepest layer, they attach to nodes along a slice through multiple layers of the network to make predictions about local patches. Our flexible combination of a generatively learned sparse representation with discriminatively trained transfer classifiers extends the concept of sparse reconstruction to encompass arbitrary semantic labeling tasks.

title: Graph-Sparse LDA: A Topic Model with Structured Sparsity
Abstract: Originally designed for text modeling, topic modeling has become a powerful tool for uncovering latent structure in various domains, including medicine, finance, and vision. The model's goals vary depending on the application: in some cases, the discovered topics are used for prediction or other downstream tasks, while in others, the topic content itself holds intrinsic scientific value. Despite the use of modern sparse techniques, the discovered topics can be difficult to interpret due to the high dimensionality of the underlying space. To enhance topic interpretability, we introduce Graph-Sparse LDA, a hierarchical topic model that leverages knowledge of relationships between words (e.g., as encoded by an ontology). In our model, topics are summarized by a few latent concept-words from the underlying graph that explain the observed words. Graph-Sparse LDA recovers sparse, interpretable summaries on two real-world biomedical datasets while achieving state-of-the-art prediction performance.
label: AI

title: A Gesture Recognition System for Detecting Behavioral Patterns of ADHD
Abstract: We present an application of gesture recognition using an extension of Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to recognize behavioral patterns of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). We propose extending DTW by incorporating one-class classifiers to capture the variability of a gesture category, enabling alignment between a gesture sample and a gesture class. We model the set of gesture samples for a particular gesture category using either GMMs or an approximation of Convex Hulls. This introduces a theoretical contribution to classical warping paths in DTW by including local modeling of intra-class gesture variability. This methodology is applied in a clinical context to detect a group of ADHD behavioral patterns defined by psychology/psychiatry experts, providing support to clinicians during the diagnosis process. The proposed methodology is tested on a novel multi-modal dataset (RGB plus Depth) of ADHD children recordings with behavioral patterns. Compared to standard state-of-the-art approaches in the DTW context, our method yields satisfactory results.

title: MKL-RT: Multiple Kernel Learning for Ratio-trace Problems via Convex Optimization
Abstract: In recent years, automatic kernel (or feature) selection or combination based on multiple kernel learning (MKL) approaches has garnered significant attention from various research communities. While MKL has been extensively studied within the context of support vector machines (SVM), its application to ratio-trace problems remains relatively unexplored. This paper demonstrates that MKL can be formulated as a convex optimization problem for a general class of ratio-trace problems, encompassing many popular algorithms used in various computer vision applications. We also provide an optimization procedure that is guaranteed to converge to the global optimum of the proposed optimization problem. Experimentally, we show that the proposed MKL approach, referred to as MKL-RT, can effectively select features for discriminative dimensionality reduction and cross-modal retrieval. Furthermore, the proposed convex MKL-RT approach outperforms the recently proposed non-convex MKL-DR approach.
label: AI

title: Improve CAPTCHA's Security Using Gaussian Blur Filter
Abstract: Securing webservers against unwanted and automated registrations has become a major concern. To prevent these fraudulent registrations, many websites utilize CAPTCHAs. Among the various types of CAPTCHAs, OCR-Based or visual CAPTCHAs are highly prevalent. Visual CAPTCHAs are essentially images containing a sequence of characters. To resist OCR programs, most visual CAPTCHAs employ common implementations such as character wrapping, random character placement and rotation, etc. This paper applies the Gaussian Blur filter, an image transformation, to visual CAPTCHAs to reduce their readability by OCR programs. Our findings indicate that this technique renders CAPTCHAs nearly unreadable for OCR programs while maintaining high readability for human users.
label: AI

title: The HAWKwood Database
Abstract: We present a database of wood pile images designed as a benchmark for evaluating the performance of wood pile detection and surveying algorithms. The database is categorized into six distinct categories suitable for different types of algorithms. Images of both real and synthetic scenes are included, comprising a total of 7655 images divided into 354 datasets. Depending on the category, datasets may include ground truth data or forestry-specific measurements that can be used for algorithm comparison.
label: AI

title: Implicit segmentation of Kannada characters in offline handwriting recognition using hidden Markov models
Abstract: This paper describes a method for classifying handwritten Kannada characters using Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). Kannada script is agglutinative, where simple shapes are joined horizontally to form characters. This results in a large number of characters, making classification challenging. Character segmentation plays a crucial role in reducing the number of classes. Explicit segmentation techniques struggle when overlapping shapes are present, which is common in handwritten text. We utilize HMMs to leverage the agglutinative nature of Kannada script, enabling implicit segmentation of characters alongside recognition. All experiments are conducted on the Chars74k dataset, containing 657 handwritten characters collected from multiple users. Gradient-based features are extracted from individual characters and used to train character HMMs. The use of implicit segmentation at the character level resulted in a 10% improvement in performance. This system also outperformed an existing system tested on the same dataset by approximately 16%. Analysis based on learning curves indicates that increasing training data could further improve accuracy. Accordingly, we collected additional data, achieving a 4% improvement with six additional samples.

title: Super-resolution method using sparse regularization for point-spread function recovery
Abstract: Large-scale spatial surveys, such as the upcoming ESA Euclid mission, may result in undersampled images due to the size of optical sensors. Therefore, super-resolution (SR) methods can be employed to recover aliased frequencies prior to further analysis. This is particularly relevant for point-source images, which provide direct measurements of the instrument point-spread function (PSF). We introduce SPRITE (SParse Recovery of InsTrumental rEsponse), an SR algorithm that utilizes a sparse analysis prior. We demonstrate that this prior offers significant improvements over existing methods, especially for low SNR PSFs.
label: AI

title: On the Covariance of ICP-based Scan-matching Techniques
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of estimating the covariance of roto-translations computed by the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm. This problem is relevant for localizing mobile robots and vehicles equipped with depth-sensing cameras (e.g., Kinect) or Lidar (e.g., Velodyne). While previous literature offers closed-form formulas for covariance based on the fact that ICP's solution minimizes a linear least-squares problem, this paper highlights the need for caution. The rematching step of the algorithm is not explicitly accounted for, and applying this approach to the point-to-point version of ICP leads to completely erroneous covariances. We then provide a formal mathematical proof demonstrating the validity of the approach for the point-to-plane version of ICP, confirming the intuition and experimental results of practitioners.
label: AI

title: Unified mobile public health care system (UMPHCS) for underdeveloped countries
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel smartphone-based system for healthcare monitoring and diagnosis, specifically designed to enhance public healthcare systems in remote, rural, and underserved areas of developing countries. Our all-in-one system digitizes health monitoring and diagnostic devices, enabling each device to function as a minimal "plug and play" sensor module within the overall system, significantly reducing costs. The user-friendly smartphone application for operating the entire system minimizes the need for skilled and trained personnel, making it an ideal toolbox for government health workers in remote rural areas.

title: Online Tracking of Skin Colour Regions Against a Complex Background
Abstract: Tracking human activity online against a complex background presents a significant challenge for many applications. This paper develops a robust technique for localizing skin color regions from unconstrained image frames. A simple and fast segmentation algorithm is used to train a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for skin color detection. Stepper motors are synchronized with the MLP to track the movement of the skin color regions.

title: A two-pass fuzzy-geno approach to pattern classification
Abstract: This work extends the fuzzy approach to 2-D shape recognition by refining initial or coarse classification decisions under a two-pass approach. In this approach, an unknown pattern is classified by refining possible classification decisions obtained through coarse classification. To build a fuzzy model of a pattern class, horizontal and vertical fuzzy partitions on the sample images of the class are optimized using a genetic algorithm. Coarse classification decisions about an unknown pattern are made by comparing its fuzzy representation with models of all pattern classes using a specially designed similarity measure. These coarse decisions are then refined in the second pass to obtain the final classification decision. Optimized horizontal and vertical fuzzy partitions are created on specific regions of the image frame for each group of similar pattern classes. Experiments show that this technique improves the overall recognition rate from 86.2% in the first pass to 90.4% after the second pass, with 500 training samples of handwritten digits.

title: Online interpretation of numeric sign language using 2-d skeletal model
Abstract: Gesturing is a natural mode of human communication. Gestures can convey basic meaning along with additional information layered over that meaning. Sign language, a structured and globally recognized communication medium for the deaf and mute, provides a prime example of communicative gestures. This paper proposes an online recognition scheme to interpret standard numeric sign language, comprising 10 basic hand symbols. A web camera captures real-time hand movements as input to the system. The basic meaning of the hand gesture is extracted from the input data frame by analyzing the shape of the hand, considering its orientation, movement, and location as fixed. The input hand shape is processed to identify the palm structure, fingertips, their relative positions, and the presence of an extended thumb. A 2-dimensional skeletal model is generated from the acquired shape information to represent and subsequently interpret the basic meaning of the hand gesture.
label: AI

title: Shape and Color Object Tracking for Real-Time Robotic Navigation
Abstract: This paper presents a real-time approach for detecting and tracking single-colored balls. The approach consists of two main phases. In an offline calibration phase, the camera's intrinsic parameters and radial distortion are estimated, and a classification of colors is learned from a sample image of colored balls. The second phase consists of four steps: (1) color segmentation of the input image based on the offline classification, (2) robust estimation of circle parameters, (3) refinement of circle parameters, and (4) ball tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach offers a good compromise between real-time navigation suitability and robustness to occlusions, background congestion, and color interference in the scene. |||

title: Detection of Salient Regions in Crowded Scenes
Abstract: The proliferation of surveillance cameras coupled with limited human operators poses a significant challenge in effectively monitoring vast video streams. Detecting anomalies in real-time necessitates an automated approach that can pinpoint regions requiring immediate attention. This paper presents a novel framework that leverages temporal variations in crowd scene flow fields to automatically identify salient regions. The proposed method analyzes the motion dynamics within the scene using stability theory, identifying areas with high motion variability as salient regions. These regions often correspond to unstable flow, occlusions, bottlenecks, entries, and exits. Experimental results on publicly available crowd scenes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting these crucial areas.

title: High Order Structure Descriptors for Scene Images
Abstract: Scene images often exhibit intricate structural arrangements that play a crucial role in scene representation. This paper proposes a novel approach that utilizes higher-order structure statistics (TOSS and FOSS) to encode these structural patterns. By analyzing radial and normal slices of TOSS and FOSS, the authors derive two new high-order structure features: TOSF and FOSF. The method then divides the scene image into non-overlapping sub-regions and calculates the proposed higher-order structural features for each region. These features are subsequently used to classify the scene using an SVM classifier. Experimental results show that higher-order structure statistics effectively capture image structure information and their spatial envelopes exhibit strong discriminative ability.
label: AI

title: Efficient Image Categorization with Sparse Fisher Vector
Abstract: Fisher vectors (FV) are renowned for their effectiveness in object recognition but suffer from the drawbacks of dense, high-dimensional features and computationally intensive processing. This paper introduces a novel representation called Sparse Fisher Vector (SFV) to mitigate these limitations. The proposed method incorporates a locality strategy to accelerate the Fisher coding step, enabling efficient image categorization. By analyzing the relationship between the coding and pooling steps, the authors provide a theoretical explanation for SFV's effectiveness. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SFV significantly accelerates the process compared to FV while preserving categorization performance. Moreover, SFV effectively maintains representation consistency for similar local features.

title: An exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning
Abstract: Deep learning has achieved groundbreaking results in various machine learning tasks, including computer vision, speech recognition, and natural language processing. However, understanding the theoretical underpinnings of its success remains an open question. This paper explores the connection between deep learning and the renormalization group (RG), a powerful technique in theoretical physics. The authors demonstrate an exact mapping between the variational renormalization group and deep learning architectures based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs). Using the nearest-neighbor Ising model as an example, the paper illustrates how deep learning algorithms may employ a generalized RG-like scheme to learn relevant features from data. This finding suggests that deep learning's success stems from its ability to extract relevant features across different length scales, mirroring the principle of RG.
label: AI

title: Crowd Saliency Detection via Global Similarity Structure
Abstract: Crowd scenes, especially those with a large number of individuals, can be challenging for CCTV operators to monitor effectively, often leading to missed events. This paper proposes an unsupervised framework to automatically identify and localize salient regions within crowd scenes. The method extracts low-level features from crowd motion fields and transforms them into a global similarity structure representation. This representation allows the discovery of intrinsic manifold patterns in motion dynamics that are not readily apparent in the low-level representation. The framework then ranks the global similarity structure to identify a set of extrema, which are subsequently used to detect salient regions. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying salient regions exhibiting crowding, local irregular motion, and unique motion areas.
label: AI

title: Enhanced Random Forest with Image/Patch-Level Learning for Image Understanding
Abstract: Visual codebooks, a critical component of image understanding frameworks using the Bag-of-Words model representation, play a crucial role in image classification. Random forests (RF) are widely used as a tree-structured discriminative codebook. However, RF performance can be hampered by inaccurate local patch label assignments. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a novel approach to update RF codebook learning using soft class labels, estimated from a pLSA model based on a feedback scheme. The proposed feedback scheme operates on both image and patch levels, unlike existing RF codebook learning methods that typically focus on either level. Experiments on 15-Scene and C-Pascal datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving image understanding performance.
label: AI

title: A Fusion Approach for Efficient Human Skin Detection
Abstract: Reliable human skin detection, adaptable to diverse skin tones and illumination conditions, is essential for accurate skin segmentation. While existing methods have achieved some success, they often suffer from false skin detection and struggle with ethnic variations. Moreover, these methods tend to be computationally expensive. This paper introduces a novel skin detection approach that combines a smoothed 2D histogram and Gaussian model to achieve robust skin detection in color images. The method employs an eye detector to refine the skin model for specific individuals, reducing computational costs and improving accuracy. The proposed approach eliminates the need for training and demonstrates improved accuracy despite variations in ethnicity and illumination. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first method to utilize a fusion strategy for this purpose. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations on three standard public datasets, along with comparisons to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Zero-Shot Object Recognition System based on Topic Model
Abstract: Traditional object recognition systems rely on complete, manually labeled training data. This paper explores zero-shot learning, where the classifier is trained without access to training samples for specific object categories. The proposed approach leverages topic models and hierarchical class concepts to achieve zero-shot learning. The method eliminates the need for cumbersome human annotation, commonly associated with attribute-based classification. Experimental results on four public datasets demonstrate comparable performance to state-of-the-art algorithms when unseen classes are involved in the classification task.
label: AI

title: Refined Particle Swarm Intelligence Method for Abrupt Motion Tracking
Abstract: Conventional tracking solutions often struggle with abrupt motion due to their reliance on smooth motion assumptions or accurate motion models. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel abrupt motion tracker based on swarm intelligence, termed SwaTrack. Unlike existing swarm-based filtering methods, SwaTrack introduces an optimized swarm-based sampling strategy to balance exploration and exploitation of the search space for the optimal proposal distribution. Additionally, the proposed Dynamic Acceleration Parameters (DAP) dynamically tune the mean and variance of the distribution for sampling. This innovative approach combines these strategies within the PSO framework to effectively handle abrupt motion, a feat not previously achieved by existing methods. Both quantitative and qualitative experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in tracking abrupt motions.
label: AI

title: Scene Image is Non-Mutually Exclusive - A Fuzzy Qualitative Scene Understanding
Abstract: Ambiguity and uncertainty are inherent in many real-world decision-making processes, often leading to variations in decisions when the same problem is posed to different individuals. This subjective nature of human decision-making, influenced by factors like experience, age, and background, also poses a challenge for scene understanding in computer vision. Traditional methods typically assume scene images are mutually exclusive and focus on binary classification tasks. This paper challenges this assumption, demonstrating that scene images are often non-mutually exclusive. The authors propose the Fuzzy Qualitative Rank Classifier (FQRC) to handle this non-exclusive nature, providing a ranking interpretation rather than a binary decision. Evaluations using large and challenging public scene datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in modeling the non-mutually exclusive nature of scene images.
label: AI

title: A graph Laplacian regularization for hyperspectral data unmixing
Abstract: This paper introduces graph Laplacian regularization into the hyperspectral unmixing formulation. The proposed approach leverages a graph representation of the hyperspectral image, where each node represents a pixel's spectrum and edges connect spectrally and spatially similar pixels. This graph framework encourages smoothness in the estimated abundance maps and collaborative estimation between homogeneous image areas. The resulting convex optimization problem is solved using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). The paper addresses computational complexity concerns and proposes Graph-cut methods to reduce computational burden. Simulations on synthetic data demonstrate the effectiveness of graph Laplacian regularization compared to other traditional regularizations for hyperspectral unmixing.

title: Computing Topology Preservation of RBF Transformations for Landmark-Based Image Registration
Abstract: Topology preservation is a critical aspect of image registration, ensuring that the transformation maintains spatial relationships between features. In landmark-based image registration, if the displacement of one landmark exceeds that of its neighbors, topology violations can occur. This paper analyzes the topology preservation properties of Radial Basis Functions (RBFs), commonly used to model deformations in image registration. Specifically, the authors focus on Matérn functions, widely used in statistical literature, to solve the landmark-based image registration problem. The paper presents the topology preservation properties of RBFs in one landmark and four landmark models, respectively. Numerical results comparing three types of Matérn transformations with Gaussian, Wendland's, and Wu's functions demonstrate the effectiveness of Matérn functions in preserving topology.
label: AI

title: Single Image Super Resolution via Manifold Approximation
Abstract: Image super-resolution, a crucial research area aimed at overcoming the limitations of physical acquisition systems and supporting high-resolution displays, has seen significant advancements in recent years. This paper builds upon a previous work that proposed a single image super-resolution approach based on linear manifold approximation of the high-resolution image-patch space. The current work analyzes each tangent subspace as a point in a Grassmann manifold, enabling the computation of geodesic pairwise distances between these subspaces. The authors develop a min-max algorithm to select an optimal subset of tangent subspaces, reducing computational costs without compromising image quality. Further computational efficiency is achieved through hierarchical clustering of the optimal subset based on Grassmann manifold distances. Finally, the paper analytically proves the validity of the proposed Grassmann-distance based clustering. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate the viability of the proposed framework.
label: AI

title: Tag Relevance Fusion for Social Image Retrieval
Abstract: Social tagging, being inherently subjective, necessitates accurate measurement of tag relevance to the visual content of social-networked images, crucial for effective image retrieval. Recognizing the limitations of single relevance measurements, this paper introduces tag relevance fusion as an extension to tag relevance estimation methods. The authors conduct a systematic study of tag relevance fusion in early and late stages, encompassing both supervised and unsupervised settings. Experiments on a large present-day benchmark set reveal that tag relevance fusion improves image retrieval performance. Moreover, unsupervised tag relevance fusion proves to be as effective as supervised methods without requiring training. This finding suggests the potential of tag relevance fusion for real-world deployment.
label: AI

title: Tree-Structure Bayesian Compressive Sensing for Video
Abstract: This paper proposes a Bayesian compressive sensing framework for video reconstruction using the Color Coded Aperture Compressive Temporal Imaging (CACTI) system. Exploiting the three-dimensional (3D) tree structure of wavelet and Discrete Cosine Transformation (DCT) coefficients, the authors derive a Bayesian compressive sensing inversion algorithm to reconstruct color video frames from a single monochromatic compressive measurement. The algorithm reconstructs up to 22 color video frames. Both simulated and real datasets are used to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm.
label: AI

title: Direct Processing of Document Images in Compressed Domain
Abstract: The exponential growth of big data in the digital age necessitates efficient methods for storing and transmitting data, particularly for documents like fax documents, invoices, and receipts. Traditional approaches involve compressing these documents for efficiency but require decompression for processing, introducing computational overhead. This paper explores the possibility of directly processing compressed images without decompression. The research summarizes methods for performing various operations, including feature extraction, text-line, word and character segmentation, document block segmentation, and font size detection, directly on run-length compressed documents. Feature extraction methods are demonstrated for extracting conventional features, such as projection profile, run-histogram, and entropy, directly from the compressed data. Document segmentation involves extracting compressed segments of text-lines, words, and characters using vertical and horizontal projection profile features. The paper also explores segmenting a block of interest from the compressed document for characterization, finding applications in real-time processing of bank checks, challans, etc. Finally, an application for detecting font size at the text line level is investigated. All proposed algorithms are validated experimentally using a comprehensive dataset of compressed documents.
label: AI

title: Challenge IEEE-ISBI/TCB : Application of Covariance matrices and wavelet marginals
Abstract: This short memo describes an approach for the IEEE-ISBI Bone Texture Characterization challenge. The proposed method focuses on utilizing covariance matrices and wavelet marginals within an SVM classifier to characterize bone texture.
label: AI

title: A unified approach for multi-object triangulation, tracking and camera calibration
Abstract: Object triangulation, 3-D object tracking, feature correspondence, and camera calibration are fundamental problems in estimation from camera networks. This paper addresses these problems within a unified Bayesian framework for joint multi-object tracking and sensor registration. Given the challenges of using standard filtering approaches for state estimation from cameras, the authors exploit an alternative parameterization called disparity space. The disparity space-based approach for triangulation and object tracking is shown to be more effective than non-linear versions of the Kalman filter and particle filtering for non-rectified cameras. The approach for feature correspondence is based on the Probability Hypothesis Density (PHD) filter, inheriting the ability to update without explicit measurement association, initiate new targets, and discriminate between target and clutter. This PHD filtering approach forms the basis of a camera calibration method from static or moving objects. Results are demonstrated on simulated data.
label: AI

title: Genetic Stereo Matching Algorithm with Fuzzy Fitness
Abstract: This paper presents a genetic stereo matching algorithm with a fuzzy evaluation function. The proposed algorithm introduces a new encoding scheme where a chromosome represents a disparity matrix. Evolution is guided by a fuzzy fitness function capable of handling noise and uncertain camera measurements, utilizing classical evolutionary operators. The algorithm produces accurate dense disparity maps in a reasonable computational time, suitable for real-time applications as demonstrated by experimental results.
label: AI

title: Bayesian Robust Tensor Factorization for Incomplete Multiway Data
Abstract: This paper proposes a generative model for robust tensor factorization in the presence of both missing data and outliers. The objective is to infer the underlying low-CP-rank tensor capturing global information and a sparse tensor capturing local information (considered outliers), thus providing a robust predictive distribution over missing entries. The low-CP-rank tensor is modeled by multilinear interactions between latent factors, with column sparsity enforced by a hierarchical prior. The sparse tensor is modeled by a hierarchical view of the Student-$t$ distribution, associating an individual hyperparameter with each element. An efficient closed-form variational inference is developed for model learning under a fully Bayesian treatment, effectively preventing overfitting and scaling linearly with data size. The method automatically performs model selection and adapts sparsity-inducing priors to various outlier types, optimizing the trade-off between low-rank approximation and sparse representation. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art algorithms. |||

title: Recognition of cDNA microarray image Using Feedforward artificial neural network
Abstract: The complementary DNA (cDNA) sequence is considered to be the magic biometric technique for personal identification. This paper introduces a new method for cDNA recognition based on an artificial neural network (ANN). Microarray imaging is used to simultaneously identify thousands of genes. The location of the spots in a cDNA microarray has been segmented. Accurate localization and segmentation of a spot are crucial for precise intensity measurement, leading to more accurate gene expression measurements. The segmented cDNA microarray image is resized and used as input for the proposed artificial neural network. The network is trained for matching and recognition. Recognition results are presented for galleries of cDNA sequences. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed matching technique for processing cDNA sequences. A comparison with previous results reveals that the proposed technique exhibits effective matching performance.
label: AI

title: Automatic Training Data Synthesis for Handwriting Recognition Using the Structural Crossing-Over Technique
Abstract: This paper presents a novel technique called "Structural Crossing-Over" for synthesizing qualified data to train machine learning-based handwriting recognition systems. This approach offers a wider variety of training data patterns compared to existing methods like elastic distortion and tangent-based affine transformation. Pairs of training characters are selected, analyzed based on their similar and different structures, and then crossed over to generate new characters. Experiments were conducted to compare the performance of tangent-based affine transformation and the proposed approach in terms of the variety of generated characters and recognition error rates. The standard MNIST corpus, consisting of 60,000 training characters and 10,000 test characters, was used in these experiments. The proposed technique synthesized 60,000 characters from 1,000 characters and used this data to train and test a benchmark handwriting recognition system that utilizes Histogram of Gradient (HOG) features and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the recognizer. The experimental results yielded an error rate of 8.06%. This significantly outperforms both tangent-based affine transformation and the original MNIST training data, which resulted in error rates of 11.74% and 16.55%, respectively.

title: Introducing SLAMBench, a performance and accuracy benchmarking methodology for SLAM
Abstract: Real-time dense computer vision and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) offer immense potential for advanced scene modeling, tracking, and real-world environmental interaction in various robotic applications. However, their demanding computational requirements pose challenges for deployment on mass-market embedded platforms. Current trends in low-cost, low-power processing favor massive parallelism and heterogeneity, making it difficult for robotics and vision researchers to implement their algorithms in a performance-portable manner. This paper introduces SLAMBench, a publicly available software framework designed to facilitate quantitative, comparable, and verifiable experimental research. This framework serves as a starting point for investigating performance, accuracy, and energy consumption trade-offs within a dense RGB-D SLAM system. SLAMBench provides a KinectFusion implementation in C++, OpenMP, OpenCL, and CUDA, leveraging the ICL-NUIM dataset of synthetic RGB-D sequences with ground truth trajectory and scene information. This dataset enables reliable accuracy comparison of different implementations and algorithms. The paper presents an analysis and breakdown of the constituent algorithmic elements of KinectFusion, and experimentally investigates their execution time on various multicore and GPU-accelerated platforms. Furthermore, the paper examines energy efficiency for different configuration alternatives on a popular embedded platform.
label: AI

title: Deep Representations for Iris, Face, and Fingerprint Spoofing Detection
Abstract: Biometric systems have significantly enhanced person identification and authentication, playing a pivotal role in personal, national, and global security. However, these systems can be deceived (or "spoofed"), and despite recent advancements in spoofing detection, current solutions often rely on domain knowledge, specific biometric reading systems, and attack types. This research assumes very limited knowledge about biometric spoofing at the sensor level to develop robust spoofing detection systems for iris, face, and fingerprint modalities. Two deep learning approaches are employed. The first approach involves learning suitable convolutional network architectures for each domain, while the second focuses on learning network weights through backpropagation. Nine biometric spoofing benchmarks are considered, each containing real and fake samples for a specific biometric modality and attack type. Deep representations are learned for each benchmark by combining and contrasting the two learning approaches. This strategy not only provides a better understanding of the interplay between these approaches but also creates systems that surpass the best-known results in eight out of the nine benchmarks. The findings strongly suggest that spoofing detection systems based on convolutional networks are resilient to known attacks and potentially adaptable, with minimal effort, to image-based attacks that are yet to emerge.
label: AI

title: Builders Instead of Consumers: Training Astronomers in Instrumentation & Observation
Abstract: The astronomy community has clearly articulated its shared scientific vision in the Astro2010 decadal survey. However, the cost and scarcity of telescope resources make hands-on learning crucial for students and early career researchers extremely challenging. To foster a deep understanding, creativity, and experience in the field, dedicated resources are needed, both present and future. McDonald Observatory offers a clear model and a long history of successfully training the next generation of instrument builders and observers. Supporting and sustaining small to medium-range local resources like McDonald is essential for the successful growth of the astronomy field.
label: AI

title: A Convex Approach to Consensus on SO(n)
Abstract: This paper introduces several novel algorithms for achieving consensus over the special orthogonal group. By employing a convex relaxation of the space of rotation matrices, consensus over rotation elements is reduced to solving a convex problem with a unique global solution. The consensus protocol is then implemented as a distributed optimization using dual decomposition and semi and fully distributed variants of the alternating direction method of multipliers technique. All methods offer strong convergence guarantees. The convex relaxation is demonstrated to be exact at all iterations of the dual decomposition-based method and exact once consensus is reached in the case of the alternating direction method of multipliers. Additionally, analytic or efficient solutions are provided for each iteration of these distributed computation schemes, allowing consensus to be achieved without any online optimization. Examples in satellite attitude alignment involving up to 100 agents, an estimation problem from computer vision, and a rotation averaging problem on SO(6) validate the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Mumford-Shah and Potts Regularization for Manifold-Valued Data with Applications to DTI and Q-Ball Imaging
Abstract: Mumford-Shah and Potts functionals are powerful variational models for regularization widely used in signal and image processing. Typical applications include edge-preserving denoising and segmentation. Due to their non-smooth and non-convex nature, these functionals pose computational challenges even for scalar data. The problem becomes even more complex for manifold-valued data as typical features of vector spaces are not available. This paper proposes algorithms for Mumford-Shah and Potts regularization of manifold-valued signals and images. For univariate problems, solvers are derived based on dynamic programming combined with convex optimization techniques for manifold-valued data. For the class of Cartan-Hadamard manifolds (including the data space in diffusion tensor imaging), the algorithms are shown to compute global minimizers for any starting point. For multivariate Mumford-Shah and Potts problems (for image regularization), a splitting into suitable subproblems is proposed, which can be solved exactly using techniques developed for the corresponding univariate problems. The proposed method does not require any a priori restrictions on the edge set and avoids discretization of the data space. The method is applied to diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and Q-ball imaging. Using the DTI model, a segmentation of the corpus callosum is obtained.
label: AI

title: Quantum Structure in Cognition and the Foundations of Human Reasoning
Abstract: Traditional cognitive science relies on classical logic and probability theory. This foundation has been challenged by various findings in experimental psychology regarding human decision-making. The formalism of quantum theory offers an efficient means of modeling these classically problematic situations. This paper builds upon a successful quantum-theoretic approach to modeling concept combinations to formulate a unifying explanatory hypothesis. In this hypothesis, human reasoning is viewed as the superposition of two processes: conceptual reasoning, characterized by the emergence of new conceptuality, and logical reasoning, founded on an algebraic calculus of the logical type. However, in most cognitive processes, conceptual reasoning dominates logical reasoning. From this perspective, observed deviations from classical logical reasoning should not be interpreted as biases but rather as natural expressions of emergence in its deepest form.
label: AI

title: Workshop Notes of the 6th International Workshop on Acquisition, Representation and Reasoning about Context with Logic (ARCOE-Logic 2014)
Abstract: ARCOE-Logic 2014, the 6th International Workshop on Acquisition, Representation, and Reasoning about Context with Logic, was held in conjunction with the 19th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Knowledge Management (EKAW 2014) on November 25, 2014, in Linköping, Sweden. These notes contain the five papers accepted and presented at the workshop.

title: A note about the generalisation of the C-tests
Abstract: This exploratory note investigates the concept of a performance measure for all tasks when using a weighting scheme based on a difficulty function. This difficulty function depends on the complexity of the (acceptable) solution for the task, instead of a universal distribution over tasks or an adaptive test. The resulting aggregations and decompositions can be retrospectively viewed as the natural and trivial interactive generalization of C-tests.
label: AI

title: Understanding and Designing Complex Systems: Response to "A framework for optimal high-level descriptions in science and engineering---preliminary report"
Abstract: This commentary recounts recent history surrounding the development of compact models of nonlinear, complex processes and the identification of their relevant macroscopic patterns or "macrostates." It provides a synopsis of computational mechanics, predictive rate-distortion theory, and the role of information measures in monitoring model complexity and predictive performance. Computational mechanics offers a method for extracting the optimal minimal predictive model for a given process. Rate-distortion theory provides methods for systematically approximating such models. The commentary concludes by discussing future prospects for developing a general framework that automatically discovers optimal compact models. As a response to the manuscript cited in the title, this brief commentary clarifies potentially misleading claims about its state space compression method and places it within a broader historical context.
label: AI

title: Persian Sentiment Analyzer: A Framework based on a Novel Feature Selection Method
Abstract: In recent years, with the exponential growth of digital content on the internet and in databases, sentiment analysis has garnered increasing attention from researchers in information retrieval and natural language processing. Sentiment analysis aims to use automated tools to detect subjective information from reviews. Feature selection presents a major challenge in sentiment analysis. Feature selection is commonly used as the initial stage of analysis and classification tasks to reduce dimensionality, improve speed, and eliminate irrelevant and redundant features. While there has been limited research on feature selection in sentiment analysis, particularly for Persian sentiment analysis, this paper addresses the problem of sentiment classification using different feature selection methods for online customer reviews in the Persian language. Three challenges in Persian text analysis include the use of a wide variety of declensional suffixes, varying word spacing, and the prevalence of informal or colloquial words. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a model for sentiment classification of Persian review documents. The model is based on lemmatization and feature selection and employs the Naive Bayes algorithm for classification. The performance of the model is evaluated on a manually gathered collection of cellphone reviews, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.
label: AI

title: Context-Aware Analytics in MOM Applications
Abstract: Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) systems are complex due to their integration of data from heterogeneous systems within the automation pyramid. Context-aware analytics are crucial to address the dynamics of these systems, which influence data generation and hinder comparability of analytics, especially predictive models (e.g., predictive maintenance). Concept drift affects the application of these models in the future. Recent research has increasingly focused on data integration using semantic context models. Manual construction of such context models is a complex and error-prone task. This paper proposes a challenge: applying combinations of knowledge extraction techniques in the domain of analytics within MOM. This encompasses data integration across Product Life-cycle Management (PLM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES). The paper outlines motivations, technological challenges, and benefits of context-aware analytics that leverage and consider the interconnectedness of semantic context data. An example scenario illustrates the need for distribution and effective change tracking of context information.
label: AI

title: Different Types of Conflicting Knowledge in AmI Environments
Abstract: This paper characterizes various types of conflicts that can occur in complex distributed multi-agent scenarios, such as those found in Ambient Intelligence (AmI) environments. The paper argues that these conflicts should be resolved in a suitable order and with appropriate strategies for each individual conflict type. It calls for further research to transform conflict resolution in AmI environments and similar multi-agent domains into a more coordinated and agreed-upon process.
label: AI

title: Adding Context to Knowledge and Action Bases
Abstract: Knowledge and Action Bases (KABs) have recently emerged as a formal framework for capturing the dynamics of systems that manipulate Description Logic (DL) Knowledge Bases (KBs) through action execution. This work enhances the KAB setting by incorporating contextual information using different context dimensions. Context is determined by the environment using context-changing actions that utilize the current state of the KB and the current context. Context also influences the set of TBox assertions relevant at each time point, which must be considered when processing queries over the KAB. This paper extends previous results on verification of rich temporal properties expressed in mu-calculus, which were established for standard KABs, to this enriched setting. Specifically, it shows that under a run-boundedness condition, verification remains decidable.
label: AI

title: Knowledge Propagation in Contextualized Knowledge Repositories: an Experimental Evaluation
Abstract: The growing interest in representing context-dependent knowledge on the Semantic Web has led to the development of several logic-based solutions. To address this need, the authors have presented the Description Logic-based Contextualized Knowledge Repository (CKR) framework. CKR is not only a theoretical framework but has also been implemented effectively using state-of-the-art tools for managing Semantic Web data. Inference within and across contexts has been realized through forward SPARQL-based rules over different RDF named graphs. This paper presents the first evaluation results for the CKR implementation. The first experiment studies its scalability with respect to different reasoning regimes. The second experiment analyzes the effects of knowledge propagation on the computation of inferences.
label: AI

title: Reasoning for Improved Sensor Data Interpretation in a Smart Home
Abstract: This paper proposes an ontological representation and reasoning paradigm for interpreting time-series signals from sensors observing a smart environment. The focus is on annotating a set of unintuitive and complex gas sensor data. The ontology, inspired by the SSN ontology (Semantic Sensor Network), represents both sensor data and contextual information. The interpretation process is primarily handled by an incremental ASP solver, which receives as input a logic program generated from the ontology's contents. Contextual information, along with high-level domain knowledge provided in the ontology, is used to infer explanations (answer sets) for changes in ambient air detected by the gas sensors.
label: AI

title: Polyphonic Music Generation by Modeling Temporal Dependencies Using a RNN-DBN
Abstract: This paper presents a generic technique for modeling temporal dependencies and sequences using a combination of a recurrent neural network (RNN) and a Deep Belief Network (DBN). The proposed technique, RNN-DBN, merges the memory state of the RNN, which provides temporal information, with a multi-layer DBN that enables high-level data representation. This combination makes RNN-DBNs ideal for sequence generation. Furthermore, the use of a DBN alongside the RNN allows for significantly more complex data representation than a Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM). The technique is applied to the task of polyphonic music generation.
label: AI

title: Interactive Visual Exploration of Halos in Large Scale Cosmology Simulation
Abstract: Halos are fundamental elements in cosmological simulations, forming from small clumps into increasingly larger objects. The processes of halo birth and merging are crucial for understanding the evolution of large-scale cosmological structures. This paper presents a visual analysis system designed for interactive identification and exploration of the evolution histories of thousands of halos. The system features an intelligent structure-aware selection method that allows users to efficiently define regions of interest in 3D space using 2D hand-drawn lasso input. Data mining of the merger tree files then identifies the exact information of halos within this 3D region. To avoid visual clutter, all halos are projected onto a 2D space using a Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) method. Through a linked view of the 3D and 2D visualizations, users can interactively explore these halos, including tracing their paths and evolution history trees.
label: AI

title: The Computational Theory of Intelligence: Data Aggregation
Abstract: This paper expands upon the concepts presented in a previous work, which proposed an information-theoretic approach to intelligence in the computational sense. The paper examines data and meme aggregation and analyzes the effects of limited resources on the resulting meme amplitudes. |||

title: The Computational Theory of Intelligence: Information Entropy
Abstract: This paper explores computational intelligence from an information theoretic perspective, proposing a probabilistic framework where intelligence is viewed as an entropy minimization process at the local level. This new scheme is illustrated with a data-driven clustering example and its potential applications are discussed.
label: AI

title: Converting Instance Checking to Subsumption: A Rethink for Object Queries over Practical Ontologies
Abstract: Efficiently querying Description Logic (DL) ontologies is crucial for many data-intensive DL applications. Instance checking, a fundamental service for answering object queries over DL ontologies, can be implemented using the most specific concept (MSC) method, which transforms instance checking into subsumption problems. However, for large and complex ontologies, this method becomes inefficient due to the generation of large MSCs leading to intractable reasoning. This paper proposes a revised MSC method for DL SHI that generates simpler and smaller concepts, sufficient for answering a given query. The independence between computed MSCs allows for scalability by enabling distributed and parallelized computations. Empirical evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the revised MSC method and its significant efficiency in answering object queries.
label: AI

title: Decision-theoretic rough sets-based three-way approximations of interval-valued fuzzy sets
Abstract: Interval-valued fuzzy sets are common in practical scenarios. This paper introduces shadowed sets as a means of interpreting and understanding these sets, providing an analytical solution for determining the pair of thresholds by balancing uncertainty within the shadowed set framework. Additionally, the paper constructs errors-based three-way approximations of interval-valued fuzzy sets and presents an alternative decision-theoretic approach for calculating thresholds by transforming interval-valued loss functions into single-valued functions, minimizing decision costs. Furthermore, it explores the computation of errors-based three-way approximations using interval-valued loss functions and illustrates how to make decisions for objects with interval-valued membership grades using these loss functions.
