title: RoboBrain: Large-Scale Knowledge Engine for Robots
Abstract: This paper introduces a knowledge engine that learns and shares knowledge representations, enabling robots to perform various tasks. This engine addresses the challenge of handling diverse data modalities, including symbols, natural language, haptic senses, robot trajectories, visual features, and more. The knowledge stored in the engine originates from multiple sources, including physical interactions during task execution, knowledge bases from the internet, and learned representations from various robotics research groups. The paper discusses technical aspects and challenges related to modeling knowledge correctness, inferring latent information, and formulating robotic tasks as queries to the knowledge engine. The system architecture and its support for user and robot interaction are described. Finally, the paper demonstrates the engine's use in three important research areas: grounding natural language, perception, and planning, which are fundamental building blocks for many robotic tasks. This collaborative knowledge engine is called RoboBrain.

title: Problem Theory
Abstract: The Turing machine, as conceived by Turing, models human calculations. This implies that we can compute anything a Turing machine can compute, making us Turing complete. The paper investigates the reason behind our Turing completeness, asking why our brains implement the functionality of a universal Turing machine. The paper argues that Turing completeness is a product of evolution and requires an evolutionary explanation, not merely a mathematical one. The paper introduces a mathematical theory of problems, assuming that solving more problems provides more survival opportunities. It builds a problem theory by fusing set and computing theories and constructs a series of resolvers, each defined by its computing capacity. The resolvers exhibit a property where all problems solved by a resolver are also solved by the next resolver in the series under certain conditions. The final condition is to be Turing complete. This series defines a resolvers hierarchy, serving as a framework for the evolution of cognition. The answer to the question of why we are Turing complete is: to solve most problems. The problem theory also defines adaptation, perception, and learning, revealing three ways to resolve any problem: routine, trial, and analogy. Importantly, the theory demonstrates how problems can be used to ground mathematics and computing on biology.

title: Neutrosophic information in the framework of multi-valued representation
Abstract: This paper presents steps for multi-valued representation of neutrosophic information within the framework of multi-valued logics. The approach utilizes the logical values: true, false, neutral, unknown, and saturated. It provides calculus formulae for neutrosophic features: truth, falsity, neutrality, ignorance, under-definedness, over-definedness, saturation, and entropy. The paper also defines net truth, definedness, and neutrosophic score.

title: SmartPacket: Re-Distributing the Routing Intelligence among Network Components in SDNs
Abstract: This work introduces a new region-based, multipath-enabled packet routing approach called SmartPacket Routing. The proposed approach decentralizes decision-making by distributing intelligence across various network elements, including the packets themselves, providing a decentralized solution for Software-Defined Networks (SDNs). This approach aims to improve efficiency, scalability, and reduce the environmental footprint of ever-growing networks. The paper proposes a region-based representation of the network topology, which is used to describe routing actions along possible paths for a packet flow. A region stack, representing a partial or full regional path of a packet, is introduced, and the Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of the packet or its associated flow are considered in the packet header. This enables QoS-aware routing at the region level without requiring a centralized controller.

title: Fuzzy human motion analysis: A review
Abstract: Human Motion Analysis (HMA) is a rapidly growing research area driven by real-world applications such as video surveillance, sports analysis, and healthcare monitoring. However, these applications often face high levels of uncertainties, affecting their operations. The paper reviews fuzzy set-oriented approaches for HMA, exploring how fuzzy sets can improve HMA and outlining future perspectives. This comprehensive survey provides a classification of human motion into three levels: Low-Level (LoL), Mid-Level (MiL), and High-Level (HiL) HMA.

title: A CSP implementation of the bigraph embedding problem
Abstract: A crucial problem for bigraphs and bigraphical reactive systems is bigraph embedding, which is more informative than bigraph matching as it tracks the correspondence between redex (guest) components within the agent (host). This paper presents an algorithm for computing embeddings based on a reduction to a constraint satisfaction problem. This algorithm, proven to be sound and complete, has been successfully implemented in LibBig, a library for manipulating bigraphical reactive systems. LibBig can be used for implementing a wide range of tools and can be adapted to various extensions of bigraphs.

title: Chases and Escapes, and Optimization Problems
Abstract: The paper proposes a new approach for solving combinatorial optimization problems by utilizing the mechanism of chases and escapes, which has a long history in mathematics. In addition to the commonly used steepest descent and neighboring search, the approach involves playing a chase and escape game on the "landscape" of the cost function. A concrete algorithm for the Traveling Salesman Problem is created. Preliminary tests suggest the potential for this new fusion of chases and escapes into combinatorial optimization search.

title: Canonical Logic Programs are Succinctly Incomparable with Propositional Formulas
Abstract: Canonical (logic) programs (CP) refer to normal logic programs augmented with the connective $not\\ not$. This paper investigates whether CP are succinctly incomparable with propositional formulas (PF). The main result demonstrates that the PARITY problem, which can be represented polynomially in PF but only has exponential representations in CP, separates PF from CP. This implies that an exponential size blowup is generally unavoidable when translating a set of formulas in PF into an equivalent program in CP without introducing new variables. Since Lifschitz and Razborov showed that there is also a problem separating CP from PF (assuming $\\mathsf{P}\\nsubseteq \\mathsf{NC^1/poly}$), it follows that CP and PF are indeed succinctly incomparable. From a computational theory perspective, this result can be viewed as the separation of two models of computation, identifying a language in $\\mathsf{NC^1/poly}$ that is not in the set of languages computable by polynomial size CP programs.

title: Lifted Probabilistic Inference for Asymmetric Graphical Models
Abstract: Lifted probabilistic inference algorithms have been successfully applied to numerous symmetric graphical models. However, the majority of real-world graphical models are asymmetric, even in relational representations when evidence is given. Existing work often attempts to make models symmetric to apply lifted inference algorithms, but this approach has limitations. All existing over-symmetric approximations require relational representations like Markov logic networks. Additionally, induced symmetries can significantly alter the distribution, leading to biased probability estimates. This paper presents a framework for probabilistic sampling-based inference that uses induced approximate symmetries to propose steps in a Metropolis-Hastings style Markov chain. This framework improves probability estimates while remaining unbiased. Experiments demonstrate the approach's superior performance compared to existing Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms.

title: Bits from Biology for Computational Intelligence
Abstract: Computational intelligence is broadly defined as biologically-inspired computing, often drawing inspiration from neural systems. This article explores the use of information theory to analyze neural systems, obtaining constraints that help identify the algorithms executed by such systems and the information they represent. Information-theoretically identified algorithms and representations can guide the design of biologically inspired computing systems (BICS). The paper covers necessary introductions to information theory and the estimation of information-theoretic quantities from neural data. It then examines how information about the environment is encoded in a system and discusses methodological developments on the amount of information each agent carries about the environment uniquely, redundantly, or synergistically with others. Finally, the framework of local information dynamics is introduced, decomposing information processing into component processes of information storage, transfer, and modification locally in space and time. The paper concludes by discussing example applications of these measures to neural data and other complex systems.

title: A Clearer Picture of Blind Deconvolution
Abstract: Blind deconvolution is the problem of recovering a sharp image and a blur kernel from a noisy blurry image. Recent research has focused on understanding the fundamental mechanisms for solving blind deconvolution. Although effective algorithms have been developed, theoretical findings offer contrasting views on why these approaches work. While alternating energy minimization algorithms have shown experimental convergence to the desired solution, it has been proven that these algorithms should fail to converge, and a Variational Bayes approach is recommended. To address this conundrum, recent work suggested that a good image and blur prior is crucial for successful blind deconvolution. However, this analysis did not apply to algorithms based on total variation regularization. This manuscript provides analysis and experiments to shed light on blind deconvolution. The analysis reveals the reason behind the effectiveness of total variation-based algorithms. The paper also introduces an implementation of this algorithm and shows its robustness and state-of-the-art performance despite its simplicity.

title: Heuristic for Network Coverage Optimization Applied in Finding Organizational Change Agents
Abstract: This paper compares different methods for selecting change agents within a network analysis paradigm and proposes a novel algorithm. All methods are evaluated against a network coverage measure that calculates how many network members can be directly reached by selected nodes. Analysis of an organizational network demonstrates that the proposed algorithm provides better network coverage compared to other methods while selecting well-connected, influential opinion leaders as change agents.

title: Solving Games with Functional Regret Estimation
Abstract: The paper proposes a novel online learning method for minimizing regret in large extensive-form games. The approach learns a function approximator online to estimate the regret for choosing a particular action. A no-regret algorithm uses these estimates in place of the true regrets to define a sequence of policies. The paper proves the approach sound by providing a bound relating the function approximation quality and the algorithm's regret. A corollary indicates that the method converges to a Nash equilibrium in self-play if the regrets are ultimately realizable by the function approximator. The technique is a principled generalization of existing work on abstraction in large games, where both the abstraction and the equilibrium are learned during self-play. Empirical demonstrations show that the method achieves higher-quality strategies than state-of-the-art abstraction techniques with the same resources.

title: Probability Theory without Bayes' Rule
Abstract: Within the Kolmogorov theory of probability, Bayes' rule enables statistical inference by relating conditional probabilities to unconditional probabilities. However, this paper demonstrates the existence of a continuous set of alternative inference rules that yield the same results and may have computational or practical advantages for certain problems. The paper formulates generalized axioms for probability theory, where the reverse conditional probability distribution P(B|A) is not specified by the forward conditional probability distribution P(A|B) and the marginals P(A) and P(B). To perform statistical inference, an additional "inference axiom" is required to relate P(B|A) to P(A|B), P(A), and P(B). The paper shows that when Bayes' rule is chosen as the inference axiom, the axioms are equivalent to the classical Kolmogorov axioms. It then derives consistency conditions on the inference axiom, characterizing the set of all possible rules for inference. The set of "first-order" inference axioms, where P(B|A) depends on the first power of P(A|B), is found to be a 1-simplex with Bayes' rule at one of the extreme points. The paper investigates the other extreme point, the "inversion rule," in depth.
label: AI

title: Elections with Few Voters: Candidate Control Can Be Easy
Abstract: This paper investigates the computational complexity of candidate control in elections with few voters. It examines the parameterized complexity of candidate control with respect to the number of voters as a parameter. The paper considers both the standard scenario of adding and deleting candidates (asking whether a candidate can become a winner or be precluded from winning by adding or deleting few candidates) and a combinatorial scenario where adding/deleting a candidate automatically implies adding or deleting a whole group of candidates. Considering several fundamental voting rules, the results demonstrate that the parameterized complexity of candidate control with the number of voters as the parameter is much more varied than in settings with many voters.
label: AI

title: Two Gaussian Approaches to Black-Box Optomization
Abstract: This paper outlines several strategies for utilizing Gaussian processes as surrogate models for the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES). |||
label: AI

title: Large-scale Binary Quadratic Optimization Using Semidefinite Relaxation and Applications
Abstract: Binary quadratic programs (BQPs) are widely used in computer vision to solve problems such as image segmentation, pixel labelling, and scene parsing. While cuts-based methods are effective for submodular problems, solving general nonsubmodular problems requires relaxation techniques like spectral methods and semidefinite programming (SDP). Spectral relaxation is simple but has a loose bound, while SDP has a tighter bound but is computationally expensive for large-scale problems. This paper presents a new SDP formulation for BQPs with a similar relaxation bound to conventional SDP formulations. This new formulation leads to a more efficient and scalable dual optimization approach, with complexity comparable to spectral methods. Two solvers, quasi-Newton and smoothing Newton, are proposed for the dual problem, both significantly more efficient than standard interior-point methods. The smoothing Newton solver outperforms the quasi-Newton solver for dense or medium-sized problems, while the quasi-Newton solver is more suitable for large sparse or structured problems. Experiments on computer vision applications, including clustering, image segmentation, co-segmentation, and registration, demonstrate the potential of this SDP formulation for solving large-scale BQPs.
label: AI

title: On the analysis of set-based fuzzy quantified reasoning using classical syllogistics
Abstract: Syllogism is a deductive reasoning method involving quantified statements. The classical Aristotelian framework uses three crisp term sets and four linguistic quantifiers, focusing on the linguistic properties of the quantifiers. Fuzzy approaches for defining approximate syllogisms have been proposed, using cardinality calculus. This paper analyzes fuzzy syllogistic models proposed by Zadeh and Dubois et al., comparing their behavior with the classical Aristotelian framework. The goal is to identify which of the 24 classical valid syllogistic reasoning patterns are specific crisp cases of these fuzzy approaches. This analysis helps assess whether these approaches can be considered plausible extensions of the classical crisp syllogism or a basis for a general approach to approximate syllogism.
label: AI

title: Unweighted Stochastic Local Search can be Effective for Random CSP Benchmarks
Abstract: This paper introduces ULSA, a novel stochastic local search algorithm designed for solving random binary constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). ULSA significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms on a widely studied benchmark suite of random CSPs. Unlike previous methods, ULSA is a simple, unweighted method that avoids dynamic weight or penalty adaptation. Notably, ULSA sets new records by achieving solutions satisfying 99 out of 100 variables in the challenging frb100-40 benchmark instance.
label: AI

title: Pattern Decomposition with Complex Combinatorial Constraints: Application to Materials Discovery
Abstract: Identifying crucial components or factors within large, noisy datasets is a critical problem in machine learning and data mining. Motivated by a pattern decomposition problem in materials discovery, aiming to discover new materials for renewable energy applications, this paper introduces CombiFD, a framework for factor-based pattern decomposition that allows incorporating a-priori knowledge as constraints, including complex combinatorial constraints. The paper proposes a new pattern decomposition algorithm, AMIQO, based on solving a sequence of (mixed-integer) quadratic programs. This approach significantly surpasses the state-of-the-art on the materials discovery problem, scaling to larger datasets and producing more precise and physically meaningful decompositions. The effectiveness of this approach for enforcing background knowledge is also demonstrated in other application domains.
label: AI

title: Behaviour Trees for Evolutionary Robotics
Abstract: Evolutionary Robotics enables robots with limited sensors and processing to handle complex tasks through sensory-motor coordination. This paper presents the first application of the Behavior Tree framework to a real robotic platform using the Evolutionary Robotics methodology. This framework enhances the intelligibility of emergent robotic behavior compared to the traditional Neural Network formulation. This improved comprehension facilitates manual adaptation when bridging the reality gap from simulation to reality. The paper demonstrates this functionality through real-world flight tests with the DelFly Explorer flapping wing Micro Air Vehicle, equipped with a 4-gram onboard stereo vision system. Experiments show that the DelFly can autonomously search for and fly through a window using only its onboard sensors and processing. While the optimized behavior achieves an 88% success rate in simulation, real-world performance is 54% after user adaptation. This, while requiring further improvement, surpasses the 46% success rate of a tuned user-defined controller.
label: AI

title: A model-free control strategy for an experimental greenhouse with an application to fault accommodation
Abstract: Developing mathematical models for agricultural greenhouses and regulating them with advanced controllers pose significant challenges due to strong perturbations, such as meteorological variations. This paper proposes a new model-free control approach and corresponding intelligent controllers, eliminating the need for a precise model. This easy-to-implement approach, recently introduced and successful in various engineering domains, is tested on a real greenhouse. Comparisons with Boolean controllers demonstrate excellent climate control, allowing straightforward reference modification, and efficient fault accommodation concerning actuators.
label: AI

title: A Fuzzy Syllogistic Reasoning Schema for Generalized Quantifiers
Abstract: This paper introduces a new approximate syllogistic reasoning schema that expands upon existing approaches in two key ways: (i) it considers a wider range of quantifiers, including logical, absolute, proportional, comparative, and exception quantifiers from the Theory of Generalized Quantifiers, and similarity quantifiers from statistics; and (ii) it allows for an arbitrary number of premises within the reasoning process. The paper also proposes a systematic reasoning procedure that interprets the syllogism as an equivalent mathematical optimization problem, where the premises define the constraints of the search space for the quantifier in the conclusion.
label: AI

title: Real time Detection of Lane Markers in Urban Streets
Abstract: This paper presents a robust and real-time approach to lane marker detection in urban streets. The method involves generating a top view of the road, filtering using selective oriented Gaussian filters, and employing RANSAC line fitting to provide initial guesses for a new, fast RANSAC algorithm for fitting Bézier Splines. A post-processing step further refines the results. This algorithm can detect all lanes in still images of the street under various conditions, operating at a rate of 50 Hz and achieving comparable results to previous techniques.
label: AI

title: Designing Socially Intelligent Virtual Companions
Abstract: Virtual companions interacting in socially complex environments require a wide range of social skills. Displaying curiosity is crucial for enhancing a companion's believability and subtly influencing user activities over time. Curiosity represents a drive to learn and is a powerful motivator for active learning. Existing research has paid limited attention to curiosity. This paper enriches the social skills of a virtual companion by integrating curiosity into its mental model. A curious companion residing in a Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) is proposed to stimulate user curiosity. The model is developed based on multidisciplinary considerations. A preliminary field study demonstrates the effectiveness of this curious companion.
label: AI

title: Efficient Algorithms for Bayesian Network Parameter Learning from Incomplete Data
Abstract: This paper presents an efficient family of algorithms for learning the parameters of a Bayesian network from incomplete data. Unlike traditional approaches like EM and gradient methods, this approach is non-iterative, provides closed-form parameter estimates, and eliminates the need for inference in a Bayesian network. This approach delivers consistent parameter estimates for missing data problems that are MCAR, MAR, and, in some cases, MNAR. Empirically, the method is significantly faster than EM due to its lack of inference requirement. Given sufficient data, it learns parameters that can be orders of magnitude more accurate.
label: AI

title: Non-Verbal Communication Analysis in Victim-Offender Mediations
Abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive ambient intelligence framework for semi-automatic analysis of non-verbal communication applied to the restorative justice field. The framework utilizes computer vision and social signal processing technologies in real scenarios of Victim-Offender Mediations, extracting features from multi-modal audio-RGB-depth data. Behavioral indicators defining communicative cues, derived from psychology and observational methodology, are computed. The methodology is tested on data collected during real-world Victim-Offender Mediation sessions in Catalonia in collaboration with the regional government. Ground truth is established through expert opinions when annotating observed social responses. Using state-of-the-art binary classification approaches, the system achieves recognition accuracies of 86% for predicting satisfaction and 79% for predicting both agreement and receptivity. A regression strategy results in a mean deviation of 0.5 to 0.7 in the range [1-5] for the computed social signals.
label: AI

title: Some Reflections on the Set-based and the Conditional-based Interpretations of Statements in Syllogistic Reasoning
Abstract: This paper explores two interpretations of syllogistic statements: the set-based interpretation, which assumes quantified statements and syllogisms describe quantity relationships between sets, and the conditional interpretation, which assumes that quantified propositions describe conditional propositions and the strength of the links between antecedent and consequent. The paper compares both interpretations concerning three key aspects: existential import, singular statements, and non-proportional quantifiers, analyzing their impact on the further development of this type of reasoning.
label: AI

title: Hypotheses of neural code and the information model of the neuron-detector
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of neural code solving. Based on formulated hypotheses, an information model of a neuron-detector, a fundamental element of an artificial neural network (ANN), is proposed. The paper critiques the connectionist paradigm of ANN building and suggests a new presentation paradigm for ANN building and neuroelement (NE) learning. The suggested model's adequacy is supported by its compatibility with contemporary propositions in neuropsychology and neurophysiology.
label: AI

title: HCRS: A hybrid clothes recommender system based on user ratings and product features
Abstract: Online clothes-selling businesses have gained immense popularity due to convenience and competitive pricing. Websites like Yintai.com, Vancl.com, and Shop.vipshop.com offer a vast selection of clothes, but the challenge for online shoppers lies in finding the right product. This paper proposes a collaborative clothes recommender system that aims to simplify online shopping. A unique feature of this system is its ability to recommend clothes based on both user ratings and clothing attributes. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed recommender effectively meets user needs.
label: AI

title: Detecting fraudulent activity in a cloud using privacy-friendly data aggregates
Abstract: The increasing reliance on cloud services by users and companies necessitates perfect performance and transparency regarding any issues. Achieving this presents significant challenges as user activities in the cloud can impact overall server performance and affect other resources. This paper explores the identification of potentially fraudulent activities, including illegal activities like DDoS attacks and undesired activities like Bitcoin mining, which consume significant power, shorten hardware lifespan, and potentially slow down other users. This research focuses on detecting these activities using non-intrusive, privacy-friendly billing data. Using OpenStack as an example, with data from Telemetry (the component responsible for measuring resource usage for billing), the paper demonstrates the efficiency of this method, discusses improvements, and highlights its advantages and disadvantages.
label: AI

title: A Greedy, Flexible Algorithm to Learn an Optimal Bayesian Network Structure
Abstract: This paper presents a novel heuristic algorithm for exact Bayesian network (BN) structure discovery using decomposable scoring functions. This algorithm offers an alternative approach to BN structure discovery compared to previously used methods like Dynamic Programming (DP) and Branch and Bound, aiming to reduce the search space and identify the optimal structure. The proposed algorithm exhibits a degree of flexibility, allowing it to be more or less greedy. Increased greediness enhances speed but reduces optimality. This algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of runtime while ensuring a near-optimal structure, sacrificing less than one percent of the optimal score for a significantly faster execution, making it suitable for large datasets.
label: AI

title: Rational Deployment of Multiple Heuristics in IDA*
Abstract: Recent advances in metareasoning for search have proven beneficial in enhancing numerous search algorithms. This paper applies rational metareasoning to IDA* when multiple admissible heuristics are available. The basic approach of taking the maximum of the heuristics is improved by incorporating lazy evaluation, resulting in a variant known as Lazy IDA*. This paper introduces a rational version of lazy IDA* that decides whether to compute more expensive heuristics or bypass them based on a myopic expected regret estimate. Empirical evaluation in various domains supports the theoretical results and shows that rational lazy IDA* is a state-of-the-art heuristic combination method.
label: AI

title: On the Feasibility of Social Network-based Pollution Sensing in ITSs
Abstract: Intense vehicular traffic is a global societal problem significantly impacting quality of life. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) can play a crucial role in mitigating this problem by reducing pollution levels and their negative effects. ITS aims to control traffic flows, measure traffic states, and provide routes minimizing pollution. While significant research has focused on measuring and enforcing traffic states, limited attention has been paid to the potential of social network analysis. Social networks offer direct feedback from people and can provide valuable information. This paper investigates the feasibility of integrating pollution-related social network feeds into ITS operations. It focuses on assessing the reliability of such information by analyzing over 1,500,000 posts and pollution data from on-the-field sensors over a year.
label: AI

title: Solving the Periodic Timetabling Problem using a Genetic Algorithm
Abstract: In railway operations, timetables determine departure and arrival times for trains or other rolling stock at stations or specific points within the rail network. These timetables are created to meet commercial requirements for passenger and freight traffic while adhering to safety, capacity constraints, and regulations associated with the railway network, rolling stock, and legislation. The complexity and time-consuming nature of timetable generation, due to the number of trains and schedules, often requires several months. This paper focuses on generating periodic timetables, where trains operate in a recurrent pattern. The paper proposes a constraint-based model suitable for this type of problem and introduces a genetic algorithm that enables rapid generation of feasible periodic timetables. Two case studies, one involving a portion of the Netherlands rail network and the other a large part of the Nord-pas-de-Calais regional rail network, are presented and solved using the proposed algorithm. The results are discussed in detail.
label: AI

title: Towards a Consistent, Sound and Complete Conceptual Knowledge
Abstract: Knowledge is only valuable if it is sound, consistent, and complete. This principle applies to conceptual knowledge, which represents knowledge about concepts and their relationships. Regardless of the format used, conceptual knowledge must be consistent, sound, and complete to be practically useful. This paper emphasizes the importance of consistency, soundness, and completeness in conceptual knowledge development.
label: AI

title: On the High-dimensional Power of Linear-time Kernel Two-Sample Testing under Mean-difference Alternatives
Abstract: Nonparametric two-sample testing determines if two distributions differ based on samples, without making parametric assumptions. Existing tests focus on either general alternatives, where the difference between distributions is unknown, or specific alternatives like a difference in means. This paper explicitly analyzes the power of a popular nonparametric test, the Maximum Mean Discrepancy statistic, designed for general alternatives, under a mean-shift alternative in high-dimensional settings. The power of the test is derived for scenarios where both the dimension and sample size can grow infinitely, and the two distributions differ only in their means. It is shown that if the signal-to-noise ratio remains constant, the test's power approaches one as the sample size grows faster than the dimension. This is the first explicit power derivation for a general nonparametric test in high dimensions, and it also demonstrates how tests designed for general alternatives perform when confronted with simpler ones.
label: AI

title: Diversifying Sparsity Using Variational Determinantal Point Processes
Abstract: A novel diverse feature selection method based on determinantal point processes (DPPs) is proposed, enabling flexible definition of diversity based on feature covariance or side information. This approach is integrated into Bayesian sparse regression, employing a DPP as a variational approximation to the true spike and slab posterior distribution. The proposed method generalizes and extends mean-field approximation, benefiting from the efficient sampling properties of DPPs. The motivating application is in bioinformatics, where the goal is to identify a diverse set of genes predicting tumor type, with diversity defined by a gene-gene interaction network. The method also demonstrates potential in spatial statistics. In both cases, the proposed method yields more diverse feature sets than traditional sparse methods without compromising accuracy.
label: AI

title: Discrete Bayesian Networks: The Exact Posterior Marginal Distributions
Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of evaluating the marginal probability of a query variable in a Bayesian network, potentially conditioned on evidence variables. First, the "border algorithm" is introduced, which converts a Bayesian network into a directed chain. This algorithm is then used as a framework for a detailed analysis of the "revised polytree algorithm" for polytrees. Finally, a novel "parentless polytree method" is presented, which converts any Bayesian network into a polytree when combined with the border algorithm. This conversion allows for inference complexity to be independent of the network size, with linear dependence only on the number of evidence and query variables. All quantities presented have probabilistic interpretations.
label: AI

title: Logics of Temporal-Epistemic Actions
Abstract: This paper presents Dynamic Epistemic Temporal Logic, a framework for reasoning about operations on multi-agent Kripke models containing a designated temporal relation. These operations are extensions of "action models" from Dynamic Epistemic Logic. "Temporal action models" can be used to define informational actions that modify the temporal structure of a model, along with agents' knowledge and beliefs about this structure, including their beliefs about time. This approach extends action model-style operations from atemporal Kripke models to temporal ones, allowing actions to control the flow of time. Examples illustrate the interpretation of extended action models' effects on temporal Kripke models. The paper further examines the preservation of epistemic-temporal properties under temporal action model-induced operations, provides axiomatizations for two theories of temporal action models, and connects this approach to previous work on time in Dynamic Epistemic Logic.
label: AI

title: Enhanced Multi-Parameter Cognitive Architecture for Future Wireless Communications
Abstract: Mitola's original concept of cognitive radio (CR) aimed at full cognition across all environmental parameters, including physical layer, MAC layer, application layer, and extracted information from reasoning. However, due to implementation challenges, a simplified definition emerged, focusing on spectrum occupancy detection. This paper proposes a new cognitive architecture for future cellular networks, aiming at multiple parameters beyond the "on/off" status of licensed users, moving closer to "full cognition." The architecture is presented in detailed stages, and three representative examples based on recent research demonstrate its feasibility and validity.
label: AI

title: Code Drones
Abstract: The paper proposes and explores the "Code Drones" paradigm, where software artifacts like classes are intelligent and socially active entities. In this paradigm, humanized artifacts take the lead in collaborating with other intelligent software artifacts and humans to create automated software engineering solutions for development and maintenance challenges. These challenges include API migration, reuse, documentation, testing, patching, and refactoring. The implications of having social and intelligent software artifacts that guide their own self-improvement are discussed.
label: AI

title: Falling Rule Lists
Abstract: Falling rule lists are classification models consisting of ordered lists of if-then rules where the order determines which example is classified by each rule, and the estimated probability of success decreases monotonically down the list. Inspired by healthcare applications, where patients are stratified into risk sets, this paper presents a Bayesian framework for learning falling rule lists without relying on traditional greedy decision tree learning methods.
label: AI

title: Learning a Recurrent Visual Representation for Image Caption Generation
Abstract: This paper explores the bi-directional mapping between images and their sentence-based descriptions using a recurrent neural network. Unlike previous approaches that map both sentences and images to a common embedding, this method allows for the generation of novel sentences given an image. The same model can also reconstruct visual features associated with an image based on its description. A novel recurrent visual memory is used to learn and remember long-term visual concepts for sentence generation and visual feature reconstruction. The approach is evaluated on sentence generation, sentence retrieval, and image retrieval tasks. State-of-the-art results are achieved for novel image description generation, with automatically generated captions preferred over human-generated ones in 19.8% of cases. The results are comparable to or better than state-of-the-art methods on image and sentence retrieval tasks using similar visual features.
label: AI

title: Justifying Answer Sets using Argumentation
Abstract: Answer sets are plain sets of literals lacking structure to explain why certain literals are included. This paper demonstrates how argumentation theory can justify the presence or absence of a literal in an answer set. Two justification methods are introduced, both based on the correspondence between answer sets of a logic program and stable extensions of the Assumption-Based Argumentation (ABA) framework. Attack Trees justify literals using arguments and attacks between them, while ABA-Based Answer Set Justifications express the same structure using literals and their relationships. Notably, an ABA-Based Answer Set Justification corresponds to an admissible fragment of the answer set, and an Attack Tree corresponds to an admissible fragment of the stable extension associated with the answer set.
label: AI

title: Recommending the Most Encompassing Opposing and Endorsing Arguments in Debates
Abstract: Arguments are essential objects in DirectDemocracyP2P, where they are associated with signatures for petitions or debated decisions. This paper addresses two problems: recommending the best justification of a given type to a new voter and recommending a compact list of justifications subsuming the majority of known arguments for or against an issue. Solutions based on weighted bipartite graphs are investigated.
label: AI

title: Stable Model Counting and Its Application in Probabilistic Logic Programming
Abstract: Model counting involves computing the number of models satisfying a propositional theory. It has applications in probabilistic logic programming, where the goal is to compute the probability of given queries being true. This paper demonstrates that for problems involving inductive definitions, such as reachability in a graph, translating logic programs to SAT can be expensive for inference tasks. Direct implementation of stable model semantics offers a more efficient solution. Two implementation techniques based on unfounded set detection are presented, extending a propositional model counter to a stable model counter. Experiments show that this approach outperforms a state-of-the-art probabilistic logic programming solver in terms of running time and space requirements, enabling the solution of larger problem instances.
label: AI

title: Stochastic Block Transition Models for Dynamic Networks
Abstract: This paper proposes a stochastic block transition model (SBTM) for dynamic networks, inspired by the stochastic block model (SBM) for static networks. Unlike most existing dynamic network models, the SBTM does not make a hidden Markov assumption on edge-level dynamics, allowing edge presence or absence to directly influence future edge probabilities while retaining the SBM's interpretability. An approximate inference procedure for the SBTM is derived, demonstrating its superior performance in reproducing edge durations in real social network data.
label: AI

title: ConceptLearner: Discovering Visual Concepts from Weakly Labeled Image Collections
Abstract: Discovering visual knowledge from weakly labeled data is crucial for scaling up computer vision recognition systems, as fully labeled data is expensive to obtain. This paper proposes ConceptLearner, a scalable approach to discover visual concepts from weakly labeled image collections. Thousands of visual concept detectors are learned automatically without human intervention for additional annotation. The learned detectors are applied to recognize concepts at the image level and detect concepts at the image region level accurately. Under domain-specific supervision, the learned concepts are evaluated for scene recognition and object detection, showing promising performance compared to fully supervised and weakly supervised methods.
label: AI

title: Compress and Control
Abstract: This paper presents a new information-theoretic policy evaluation technique for reinforcement learning. This technique converts any compression or density model into a corresponding estimate of value. Under appropriate stationarity and ergodicity conditions, a sufficiently powerful model results in a consistent value function estimator. The paper studies the technique's behavior in Atari 2600 video games, where suboptimal modeling is necessary. Despite using limited models, the technique provides accurate value estimates for effective on-policy control. The paper highlights the technique's potential for scaling to large problems.
label: AI

title: Genetic Algorithms in Wireless Networking: Techniques, Applications, and Issues
Abstract: Wireless access technology is becoming increasingly common due to its ease of operation and installation. The design of wireless networks is challenging due to highly dynamic environments, making parameter optimization complex. Modern wireless networking standards rely on machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms due to dynamic and often unknown operating conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of the applications of genetic algorithms (GAs) in wireless networks, covering common GA models, configuration, and a broad range of GA techniques. Open research issues and future work directions are identified. This paper is the first to focus specifically on the applications of GAs in wireless networks.
label: AI

title: Ontology Module Extraction via Datalog Reasoning
Abstract: Module extraction, the task of computing a small fragment of an ontology that preserves entailments over a given signature, has various applications. While extracting modules of minimal size is computationally hard, practical techniques rely on approximations that capture relevant entailments but are not guaranteed to be minimal. Existing approximations preserve all second-order entailments, which can be unnecessarily strong and lead to large modules. This paper proposes a novel approach where module extraction is reduced to a datalog reasoning problem. This approach generalizes existing approximations and allows for tailoring to specific kinds of entailments, resulting in significantly smaller modules. Evaluation on widely-used ontologies shows promising results.
label: AI

title: Sparse distributed localized gradient fused features of objects
Abstract: The sparse, hierarchical, and modular processing of natural signals is linked to humans' ability to recognize objects accurately. This paper proposes a sparse feature processing and encoding method for improved object recognition performance. Randomly distributed localized gradient enhanced features are selected before employing aggregate functions for representation, using a modular and hierarchical approach to detect object features. These features are combined with a minimum distance classifier, resulting in high object recognition accuracies on benchmark datasets. The performance is shown to be robust to noise, object scaling, and object shifts. Compared to other object recognition methods, the proposed method achieves significant accuracy improvements.
label: AI

title: Existential Rule Languages with Finite Chase: Complexity and Expressiveness
Abstract: Finite chase, or chase termination, is a crucial condition for the decidability of existential rule languages. This paper proposes a novel approach for classifying rule languages with finite chase, naturally defining a family of decidable rule languages that extend existing ones. The complexity of these languages is studied, demonstrating that while they are tractable for data complexity, their combined complexity can be arbitrarily high. It is shown that rule languages with finite chase extending weakly acyclic languages have the same expressiveness as the weakly acyclic one, while languages with higher combined complexity are generally more succinct than those with lower combined complexity.
label: AI

title: Salient Object Detection: A Survey
Abstract: Salient object detection, the task of detecting and segmenting salient objects from natural scenes, has gained significant attention in computer vision. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent progress in salient object detection, situating it within related areas like generic scene segmentation, object proposal generation, and saliency for fixation prediction. Covering 228 publications, the paper surveys the roots, key concepts, core techniques, modeling trends, datasets, and evaluation metrics for salient object detection. Open problems, including evaluation metrics and dataset bias in model performance, are discussed, and future research directions are suggested.
label: AI

title: Introduction to astroML: Machine Learning for Astrophysics
Abstract: Astronomy and astrophysics are experiencing a surge in data volume due to advancements in detectors, telescopes, and computers. This paper describes astroML, an initiative using Python and scikit-learn to develop a compendium of machine learning tools designed for the statistical needs of astronomy students and surveys. astroML is presented with example applications enabled by this package.
label: AI

title: A Unified View of Large-scale Zero-sum Equilibrium Computation
Abstract: The task of computing approximate Nash equilibria in extensive-form games with many players has garnered significant attention, particularly due to the Annual Computer Poker Competition. Two distinct approaches emerged shortly after its inception: one based on no-regret online learning, the other employing a sophisticated gradient method applied to a convex-concave saddle-point formulation. While these approaches have progressed independently, this paper aims to bridge the gap by dissecting and unifying these two perspectives.
label: AI

title: Linguistic Descriptions for Automatic Generation of Textual Short-Term Weather Forecasts on Real Prediction Data
Abstract: This paper presents GALiWeather, an application that automatically generates textual short-term weather forecasts for every municipality in Galicia, Spain. Leveraging real data from the Galician Meteorology Agency (MeteoGalicia), GALiWeather innovatively combines computational and perceptual techniques with natural language generation (NLG) capabilities. It extracts relevant information from weather forecasts, encodes it using linguistic variables and temporal references, and then translates these descriptions into natural language text using an NLG system. The generated forecasts have been validated by a MeteoGalicia expert using a quality assessment methodology, ensuring both content accuracy and textual correctness.  GALiWeather is set to be released as a public service, offering custom forecasts to a wide audience.
label: AI

title: Cognitive Systems and Question Answering
Abstract: This paper provides an overview of cognitive computing, using the field of natural language question answering as an example. It highlights the specific challenges associated with this field and presents the LogAnswer system as a successful demonstration of how these challenges can be overcome. LogAnswer is a representative system within the field of natural language question answering.
label: AI

title: Automated Reasoning in Deontic Logic
Abstract: Deontic logic, a well-established branch of mathematical logic and philosophy, has been extensively studied for diverse application domains such as argumentation theory, legal reasoning, and multi-agent systems. This paper demonstrates how standard deontic logic can be systematically transformed into description logic and DL-clauses, enabling processing by Hyper, a high-performance theorem prover that utilizes a hypertableau calculus. Two use cases, one from multi-agent research and the other from normative system development, are investigated to illustrate this transformation.
label: AI

title: Toward a Universal Cortical Algorithm: Examining Hierarchical Temporal Memory in Light of Frontal Cortical Function
Abstract: A growing body of evidence suggests the existence of a common algorithm underlying information processing throughout the cerebral cortex. This paper reviews several hypothesized features of this algorithm, including sparse distributed representation, Bayesian inference, hierarchical organization with alternating template matching and pooling layers, temporal slowness, and predictive coding. Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM), a family of learning algorithms and related theories of cortical function, embodies these principles. While HTM has primarily been applied to perceptual tasks typical of the posterior cortex, this paper examines its compatibility with frontal cortical functions. By integrating various models of frontal cortical function, the paper proposes that functions like attention, working memory, and action selection rely largely on the same fundamental algorithms as posterior functions, with the notable additions of a mechanism for active representation maintenance and multiple cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical loops for adaptive gating of communication between frontal cortex regions. The paper reviews computational models of this system and discusses how HTM can contribute to understanding frontal cortical function and the implications for its future development.
label: AI

title: Can we build a conscious machine?
Abstract: The underlying physiological mechanisms responsible for generating conscious states remain elusive. To advance our understanding of consciousness, we need to experimentally design a system that evolves in a manner analogous to the human brain. Recent research demonstrates that the multiscale nature of the evolving human brain can be achieved by reprogramming human cells. This paper proposes a hybrid system incorporating an evolving brain equipped with digital computers that maintain homeostasis and provide essential nutrients and oxygen for brain growth. The evolving brain's structure will be shaped through controlled spatial organization of various cell types, following a specific program. This evolving brain can then be trained using substitutional reality to learn and experience real-world scenes. Neuroelectrodynamics reveals that meaningful information in the brain is electrically (wirelessly) read and written rapidly at the molecular (protein) level during action potential and synaptic activity. As training progresses, meaningful information accumulates and becomes electrically integrated within the brain. This gradual process of training is predicted to trigger a tipping point for conscious experience to emerge in the hybrid system.
label: AI

title: Aggregating partial rankings with applications to peer grading in massive online open courses
Abstract: This paper explores the potential of ordinal peer grading for evaluating students in massive open online courses (MOOCs). In this grading scheme, each student receives a few assignments (from other students) to rank.  A global ranking (potentially translated into numerical scores) is then generated by combining individual rankings. This innovative application of social choice concepts presents a crucial problem: how to distribute assignments effectively so that individual rankings can be seamlessly merged into a global ranking that accurately reflects the students' relative performance. The main theoretical result suggests that using simple assignment distribution methods, where each student ranks only k assignments, a Borda-like aggregation method can recover a 1-O(1/k) fraction of the true ranking when students accurately rank their assigned work. Experimental results further strengthen this analysis and demonstrate the robustness of this method even when students exhibit imperfect grading abilities. The findings provide strong evidence that ordinal peer grading is a highly effective and scalable evaluation solution for MOOCs.
label: AI

title: Relations World: A Possibilistic Graphical Model
Abstract: This paper explores the use of a "possibilistic graphical model" as the foundation for a world model that drives a dialog system. As a first step, the paper presents a system that utilizes text-based dialog to construct a model of the user's family relations. The system leverages its world model to infer relational triples, learn to recover from upstream coreference resolution errors and ambiguities, and learn context-dependent paraphrase models. The paper also delves into some theoretical aspects of the underlying graphical model.
label: AI

title: A Note on Systematic Conflict Generation in CA-EN-type Causal Structures
Abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive, systematic overview of potential conflict generation within CA-EN-like causal structures. For simplicity, only the outermost level of graphs is considered. The paper focuses on the localization of the "conflict area", diagnostic preferences, and the basis for systematic conflict generation. A notion of {\\em Potential Conflict Structure} ({\\em PCS}), a foundational tool for identifying potential conflicts, is proposed and its use is discussed.
label: AI

title: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator
Abstract: Automatically describing the content of an image is a fundamental challenge in artificial intelligence, bridging computer vision and natural language processing. This paper presents a generative model based on a deep recurrent architecture, combining recent advancements in computer vision and machine translation, to generate natural sentences describing images. The model is trained to maximize the likelihood of the target description sentence given the training image. Experiments conducted on various datasets demonstrate the model's accuracy and the fluency of the language it learns solely from image descriptions. The model achieves significant accuracy, both qualitatively and quantitatively. For example, while the current state-of-the-art BLEU-1 score on the Pascal dataset is 25, the proposed approach achieves 59, comparable to human performance at 69. The paper also reports BLEU-1 score improvements on Flickr30k (from 56 to 66) and SBU (from 19 to 28). Notably, on the newly released COCO dataset, the model achieves a BLEU-4 score of 27.7, establishing a new state-of-the-art.
label: AI

title: Verification of Relational Multiagent Systems with Data Types (Extended Version)
Abstract: This paper investigates the extension of relational multiagent systems (RMASs), where agents manipulate full-fledged relational databases equipped with data types and facets with domain-specific, rigid relations (such as total orders). The focus is on design-time verification of RMASs against rich first-order temporal properties expressed in a variant of first-order mu-calculus with quantification across states. Building upon previous decidability results under the "state-bounded" assumption, where each state holds a bounded number of data objects, the paper recasts this condition, demonstrating decidability in the presence of dense, linear orders and facets defined on top of them. The approach is based on constructing a finite-state, sound and complete abstraction of the original system, where dense linear orders are reformulated as non-rigid relations operating on the active domain of the system only. The paper also proves undecidability when including a data type equipped with the successor relation.
label: AI

title: Parallel Gaussian Process Regression for Big Data: Low-Rank Representation Meets Markov Approximation
Abstract: The expressive power of Gaussian process (GP) models comes at the cost of poor scalability with increasing data size. This paper introduces a low-rank-cum-Markov approximation (LMA) of the GP model, leveraging the dual computational advantages of combining a low-rank approximate representation of the full-rank GP with a Markov approximation of the resulting residual process. The Markov approximation is guaranteed to be closest in the Kullback-Leibler distance criterion subject to specific constraints and is significantly more refined than existing sparse GP models due to its more relaxed conditional independence assumption, especially with larger datasets. Consequently, the LMA method can trade off between the support set size and the order of the Markov property to: (a) achieve lower computational cost than sparse GP models while maintaining comparable predictive performance, and (b) accurately represent features/patterns of any scale. Notably, varying the Markov order produces a spectrum of LMAs, with PIC approximation and full-rank GP at the two extremes. The LMA method is amenable to parallelization on multiple machines/cores, further enhancing its scalability. Empirical evaluation on three real-world datasets using up to 32 computing nodes demonstrates that the centralized and parallel LMA methods are significantly more time-efficient and scalable than state-of-the-art sparse and full-rank GP regression methods while achieving comparable predictive performance.
label: AI

title: FGPGA: An Efficient Genetic Approach for Producing Feasible Graph Partitions
Abstract: Graph partitioning, a well-studied problem in parallel computing, finds applications in diverse fields such as distributed computing, social network analysis, data mining, and more. This paper introduces FGPGA, an efficient genetic approach for generating feasible graph partitions. The method considers the heterogeneity and capacity constraints of the partitions to ensure balanced partitioning. FGPGA has numerous applications in mobile cloud computing, enabling feasible deployment of software applications on more resourceful cloud infrastructure instead of mobile devices. The proposed approach is lightweight, making it suitable for cloud architectures. Feasibility of the generated partitions is ensured by preventing the generation of oversized partitions during initialization and search. Tested on standard benchmark datasets, FGPGA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of partition quality and solution feasibility.
label: AI

title: Influence Functions for Machine Learning: Nonparametric Estimators for Entropies, Divergences and Mutual Informations
Abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes estimators for statistical functionals of one or more distributions under nonparametric assumptions. The estimators are based on the theory of influence functions, a concept from semiparametric statistics. The paper demonstrates that estimators based on either data-splitting or a leave-one-out technique achieve fast rates of convergence and exhibit other favorable theoretical properties. The framework is applied to derive estimators for several popular information-theoretic quantities, and empirical evaluation highlights the advantages of this approach over existing estimators.
label: AI

title: HIPAD - A Hybrid Interior-Point Alternating Direction algorithm for knowledge-based SVM and feature selection
Abstract: This paper addresses classification tasks in the regime of limited labeled training data in high-dimensional feature spaces, where specific expert knowledge is also available. A new hybrid optimization algorithm is proposed, which solves the elastic-net support vector machine (SVM) using an alternating direction method of multipliers in the first phase, followed by an interior-point method for the classical SVM in the second phase. Both SVM formulations are adapted to incorporate knowledge. The algorithm tackles the challenges of automatic feature selection, high optimization accuracy, and algorithmic flexibility to leverage prior knowledge. Its effectiveness and efficiency are demonstrated through comparisons with existing methods on synthetic and real-world data.
label: AI

title: ROSS User's Guide and Reference Manual (Version 1.0)
Abstract: The ROSS method is a novel approach in the field of knowledge representation, proving valuable for various artificial intelligence and natural language understanding representation and reasoning tasks. (ROSS stands for "Representation", "Ontology", "Structure", "Star" language).  ROSS is a physical symbol-based representational scheme. It provides a complex model for the declarative representation of physical structure and for representing processes and causality. From a metaphysical standpoint, the ROSS view of external reality involves a 4D model, where discrete, single-time-point, unit-sized locations with states constitute the basis for all objects, processes, and aspects that can be modeled.  ROSS includes a language called "Star" for specifying ontology classes. It also incorporates a formal scheme known as the "instance model". Instance models are used in the domain of natural language meaning representation to represent situations. This document provides a comprehensive specification of the ROSS method.
label: AI

title: Introduction to ROSS: A New Representational Scheme
Abstract: ROSS ("Representation, Ontology, Structure, Star") is introduced as a new method for knowledge representation, emphasizing representational constructs for physical structure. The ROSS representational scheme includes a language called "Star" for specifying ontology classes.  It also incorporates a formal scheme known as the "instance model". Instance models are used in the domain of natural language meaning representation to represent situations. This paper provides both the rationale and the philosophical background for the ROSS method.
label: AI

title: Using Description Logics for RDF Constraint Checking and Closed-World Recognition
Abstract: RDF and Description Logics operate in an open-world setting where the absence of information is not interpreted as information about absence. However, Description Logic axioms can be interpreted in a closed-world setting, enabling their use for both constraint checking and closed-world recognition against information sources. When information sources are expressed in well-behaved RDF or RDFS (i.e., RDF graphs interpreted under the RDF or RDFS semantics), this constraint checking and closed-world recognition is straightforward. Furthermore, this constraint checking can be implemented as SPARQL querying, allowing for efficient execution.
label: AI

title: Diversity Handling In Evolutionary Landscape
Abstract: The search ability of an Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) relies on the variation among individuals within the population. Maintaining an optimal level of diversity in the EA population is crucial to prevent premature convergence to suboptimal solutions and ensure ongoing search progress. A clearer understanding of population diversity, particularly in the context of evolutionary search and premature convergence, is key to designing efficient EAs. This paper first presents a comprehensive analysis of EA population diversity issues. It then investigates a counter-niching EA technique that introduces and maintains constructive diversity within the population. The proposed approach utilizes informed genetic operations to explore promising, but unexplored or under-explored areas of the search space, while discouraging premature local convergence. Simulation runs on standard benchmark test functions using a Genetic Algorithm (GA) implementation demonstrate promising results.
label: AI

title: Resolution of Difficult Pronouns Using the ROSS Method
Abstract: This paper describes a new natural language understanding method for disambiguating challenging pronouns. Difficult pronouns require a level of world or domain knowledge for anaphoral or other types of resolution. Resolving these pronouns may necessitate a prior inference step applied to the situation represented by the natural language text. The paper outlines a general method encompassing entity resolution and pronoun resolution. An extension to this method incorporates inference as an embedded commonsense reasoning mechanism.  Both the general method and the embedded method utilize features of the ROSS representational scheme, specifically ROSS ontology classes and the ROSS situation model. The overall method provides a working solution for resolving the following Winograd schemas: a) trophy and suitcase, b) person lifts person, c) person pays detective, and d) councilmen and demonstrators. |||
label: AI

title: Association Rule Based Flexible Machine Learning Module for Embedded System Platforms like Android
Abstract: Smartphones have become increasingly popular in recent years, and their utility is expected to grow further with the addition of new features. Integrating machine learning with mobile computing can enable smartphones to become "intelligent" devices, capable of proactively understanding and fulfilling user needs based on their environment and context. This paper explores methods and applications for integrating machine learning and context-aware computing on the Android platform to enhance user utility. A Machine Learning (ML) module is proposed to be incorporated into the basic Android architecture, offering two main functionalities:  This paper outlines three architectures, each incorporating the ML module at a different level within the Android architecture. The advantages and disadvantages of each architecture are analyzed, and several potential applications for the proposed system are discussed.
label: AI

title: Automatic Generation of Alternative Starting Positions for Simple Traditional Board Games
Abstract: Simple board games like Tic-Tac-Toe and CONNECT-4 play a crucial role in developing mathematical, logical, emotional, and social skills. This paper addresses the challenge of generating targeted starting positions for these games. This can facilitate new approaches for guiding novice players towards mastery and lead to the discovery of interesting game variations. The proposed approach generates starting states of varying difficulty levels for player 1 in a two-player board game. The method utilizes symbolic techniques and iterative simulations to efficiently search the vast state space. Experimental results demonstrate the discovery of states with varying difficulty levels for several simple grid-based board games, including standard game variants like 4x4 Tic-Tac-Toe. This opens up new game possibilities that have never been explored before, as the default starting state is often heavily biased.
label: AI

title: How to Scale Up Kernel Methods to Be As Good As Deep Neural Nets
Abstract: Kernel methods have often faced a significant obstacle due to their computational complexity, limiting their applicability to large-scale learning problems. This paper argues that this barrier can be effectively overcome. The authors develop methods to scale up kernel models to effectively address large-scale learning problems, which were previously accessible only to deep learning architectures. Building on the seminal work by Rahimi and Recht on approximating kernel functions using features derived from random projections, the paper advances the state-of-the-art by proposing methods for efficiently training models with hundreds of millions of parameters and learning optimal representations from multiple kernels. Extensive empirical studies conducted on problems from image recognition and automatic speech recognition demonstrate that the performance of the proposed kernel models matches that of well-engineered deep neural nets (DNNs). This represents the first direct comparison between these two methods on large-scale problems. The kernel methods proposed in this paper offer several attractive properties, including training with convex optimization, comparable training costs to DNNs, and significantly reduced total cost due to fewer hyperparameters requiring tuning for model selection. This contrastive study sheds light on fundamental questions about learning good representations.
label: AI

title: Sample-targeted clinical trial adaptation
Abstract: Clinical trial adaptation involves adjustments to the trial protocol after its initiation. The primary objective is to enhance the efficiency of introducing new medical interventions to patients by reducing the cost and time associated with evaluating their safety and efficacy. This paper proposes a novel method for achieving this goal while minimizing the risk of distorting the trial's outcome. Unlike previous approaches, this method focuses on trial adaptation by sample size adjustment. The paper utilizes a recently proposed stratification framework based on collected auxiliary data. It demonstrates that this information, along with the primary measured variables, can be used to make a probabilistically informed decision about the specific subgroup from which a sample should be removed. Experiments on simulated data illustrate the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed method.
label: AI

title: Learning Fuzzy Controllers in Mobile Robotics with Embedded Preprocessing
Abstract: The automatic design of controllers for mobile robots typically involves two stages: preprocessing sensorial data into high-level, meaningful variables, and utilizing a machine learning technique to map these high-level variables to control commands sent to the robot. This paper describes an algorithm that integrates the preprocessing stage into the learning stage, enabling the creation of controllers directly from raw sensorial data without expert knowledge. To address the high dimensionality of sensorial data, the approach utilizes Quantified Fuzzy Rules (QFRs). QFRs transform low-level input variables into high-level input variables, reducing dimensionality through summarization. The proposed learning algorithm, called Iterative Quantified Fuzzy Rule Learning (IQFRL), is based on genetic programming. IQFRL can learn rules with different structures and manage linguistic variables with multiple granularities. The algorithm was tested by implementing wall-following behavior in realistic simulated environments of varying complexity and on a Pioneer 3-AT robot in real-world scenarios. The results demonstrate superior and statistically significant performance compared to several well-known learning algorithms combined with various data preprocessing techniques. Additionally, three real-world applications where IQFRL plays a central role are presented: path and object tracking with static and moving obstacle avoidance.
label: AI

title: Optimal Cost Almost-sure Reachability in POMDPs
Abstract: This paper investigates partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with a set of target states, where each transition incurs an integer cost. The optimization objective is to minimize the expected total cost until the target set is reached, ensuring that the target set is reached with probability 1. The paper proves that approximating the optimal cost is undecidable for integer costs. For positive costs, the paper establishes matching lower and upper bounds for the optimal cost, revealing that the bound is double exponential. Additionally, the paper demonstrates that the problem of approximating the optimal cost is decidable and presents approximation algorithms based on existing algorithms for POMDPs with finite-horizon objectives. While the worst-case running time of the proposed algorithm is double exponential, it includes efficient stopping criteria and demonstrates good performance experimentally on many examples of interest.
label: AI

title: Integrating Fuzzy and Ant Colony System for Fuzzy Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows
Abstract: This paper focuses on fuzzy Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) with uncertain travel time. Credibility theory is used to model the problem, specifying a preference index for the desired probability that travel times to reach customers fall within their time windows. An integrated fuzzy and ant colony system-based evolutionary algorithm is proposed to solve the problem while satisfying constraints. Computational results for benchmark problems with short and long time horizons demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness. Comparisons between different preference indexes are provided to assist users in making appropriate decisions.
label: AI

title: An Approach to Model Checking of Multi-agent Data Analysis
Abstract: This paper presents an approach for verifying a multi-agent data analysis algorithm. It achieves correct simulation of the multi-agent system using a finite integer model and employs the model checking tool SPIN for verification. Agent protocols are written in Promela language, and properties of the multi-agent data analysis system are expressed in LTL logic. The paper describes the execution of several experiments with SPIN and the model.
label: AI

title: A Hybrid Approach to Finding Relevant Social Media Content for Complex Domain Specific Information Needs
Abstract: While contemporary semantic search systems aim to improve traditional keyword-based search, they often fall short when addressing complex domain-specific information needs. The domain of prescription drug abuse, for instance, requires knowledge of both ontological concepts and "intelligible constructs" not typically modeled in ontologies. These intelligible constructs convey essential information like intensity, frequency, interval, dosage, and sentiments, crucial for meeting the holistic needs of information seekers. This paper introduces a hybrid approach to domain-specific information retrieval (or knowledge-aware search) that integrates ontology-driven query interpretation with synonym-based query expansion and domain-specific rules to facilitate search in social media. The framework is based on a context-free grammar (CFG) that defines the query language of constructs interpretable by the search system. The grammar provides two levels of semantic interpretation: a top-level CFG for retrieving diverse textual patterns belonging to broad templates and a low-level CFG for interpreting specific expressions within those patterns. These low-level expressions represent concepts from four categories of data: ontological concepts, concepts in lexicons (emotions and sentiments), lexico-ontology concepts (side effects and routes of administration), and domain-specific expressions derived through rules. This approach is embodied in a novel Semantic Web platform called PREDOSE, developed for prescription drug abuse epidemiology.
label: AI

title: Scalable Link Prediction in Dynamic Networks via Non-Negative Matrix Factorization
Abstract: This paper proposes a scalable temporal latent space model for link prediction in dynamic social networks, where the goal is to predict links over time based on a sequence of previous graph snapshots. The model assumes that each user resides in an unobserved latent space, and interactions are more likely to form between similar users in this latent space representation. The model further allows each user to gradually shift its position in the latent space as the network structure evolves over time. A global optimization algorithm with a quadratic convergence rate is presented to effectively infer the temporal latent space. Two alternative optimization algorithms with local and incremental updates are also proposed, enabling the model to scale to larger networks without compromising prediction accuracy. Empirical evaluations on real-world dynamic networks demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms existing approaches for temporal link prediction in terms of scalability and predictive power.
label: AI

title: Jamming Bandits
Abstract: This paper investigates the ability of an intelligent jammer to learn and adapt to unknown environments in an electronic warfare scenario. The authors answer this question in the affirmative by developing a cognitive jammer that adaptively and optimally disrupts communication between a victim transmitter-receiver pair. The problem is formalized using a novel multi-armed bandit framework, where the jammer can select various physical layer parameters, such as signaling scheme, power level, and on-off/pulsing duration, to achieve power-efficient jamming strategies. The paper presents novel online learning algorithms to maximize jamming efficacy against static transmitter-receiver pairs and proves that the learning algorithm converges to the optimal jamming strategy in terms of error rate inflicted on the victim and energy used. Importantly, the rate of convergence to the optimal jamming strategy is proven to be sub-linear, demonstrating fast learning compared to existing reinforcement learning algorithms. This rapid learning is crucial in dynamically changing wireless environments. The performance of the proposed bandit-based learning algorithm is also characterized against multiple static and adaptive transmitter-receiver pairs.
label: AI

title: Handling owl:sameAs via Rewriting
Abstract: Rewriting is widely used to optimize owl:sameAs reasoning in materialization-based OWL 2 RL systems. This paper investigates issues related to the correctness and efficiency of rewriting, presenting an algorithm that guarantees correctness, improves efficiency, and can be effectively parallelized. An evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach can reduce reasoning times on practical data sets by orders of magnitude.
label: AI
