title: Building the Observer into the System: Toward a Realistic Description of Human Interaction with the World
Abstract: Human beings do not perceive the world from an external perspective but are fully immersed in it. However, scientific approaches often provide the observer with a "god's eye" perspective and significant a priori knowledge. Inspired by W. Ross Ashby's statement about the theory of the Black Box, this paper presents an alternative picture of the world as a black box to which the observer is coupled. Within this framework, the paper proves purely-classical analogs of the "no-go" theorems of quantum theory. Focusing on identifying macroscopic objects like laboratory apparatus or other observers, the paper shows that the standard quantum formalism of superposition is necessary to adequately represent the classical information an observer can obtain. The paper connects these results to supporting considerations from evolutionary biology, cognitive and developmental psychology, and artificial intelligence.
label: AI

title: Membership Function Assignment for Elements of Single OWL Ontology
Abstract: This paper explores the idea of assigning membership functions to elements in an OWL (Web Ontology Language) ontology to subsequently generate fuzzy rules from this ontology. While membership function assignment for OWL ontology elements has been partially described, it typically involves merging several OWL ontologies from the same domain into a single ontology. This paper presents a method for assigning membership functions to OWL ontology elements when only one ontology is available. The generated fuzzy rules are essential for supplementing the SWES (Semantic Web Expert System) knowledge base. SWES is an expert system capable of extracting knowledge from OWL ontologies found on the web and acting as a universal expert for the user.
label: AI

title: On Sparse Discretization for Graphical Games
Abstract: This paper focuses on discretization schemes for representing and computing approximate Nash equilibria, primarily within the context of graphical games, while briefly touching on normal-form and poly-matrix games. The main technical contribution is a representation theorem that informally states that to represent every exact Nash equilibrium using a nearby approximate Nash equilibrium on a grid over mixed strategies, a uniform discretization size linear in the inverse of the approximation quality and natural game-representation parameters is sufficient. For graphical games, under natural conditions, the discretization is logarithmic in the game-representation size, a substantial improvement over the linear dependency previously required. The paper has five additional objectives: to highlight the role of constraint networks in AI in simplifying the derivation and analysis of algorithms for computing approximate Nash equilibria; to summarize the state-of-the-art in computing approximate Nash equilibria with a focus on graphical games; to clarify the distinction between sparse-discretization and sparse-support techniques; to illustrate and advocate for the mathematical simplicity of the representation theorem's formal proof; and to list and discuss important open problems, particularly focusing on graphical-game generalizations.
label: AI

title: Logical Limitations to Machine Ethics with Consequences to Lethal Autonomous Weapons
Abstract: Lethal Autonomous Weapons (LAWs) hold the potential to revolutionize warfare while raising numerous ethical and legal concerns. The paper explores fundamental limitations to the moral behavior of intelligent machines through a series of "Gedankenexperiments." By refining and sharpening variations of the Trolley Problem, the authors construct an artificial yet fully deterministic situation where a robot faces two choices: one morally preferable to the other. However, based on the undecidability of the Halting problem, the robot provably cannot algorithmically decide which choice to make. The considerations presented have surprising implications for the question of responsibility and liability for an autonomous system's actions, leading to specific technical recommendations.
label: AI

title: Exploiting Parallelism for Hard Problems in Abstract Argumentation: Technical Report
Abstract: Abstract argumentation framework (\\AFname) is a unifying framework encompassing various nonmonotonic reasoning approaches, logic programming, and computational argumentation. However, efficient approaches for most decision and enumeration problems associated with \\AFname are lacking, potentially limiting the efficacy of argumentation-based approaches in real-world domains. This paper presents an algorithm for enumerating the preferred extensions of abstract argumentation frameworks that leverages parallel computation. The algorithm utilizes the SCC-recursive semantics definition schema, where extensions are defined at the level of specific sub-frameworks. The algorithm demonstrates significant performance improvements in large frameworks, both in terms of the number of solutions found and speedup.
label: AI

title: Warranty Cost Estimation Using Bayesian Network
Abstract: All multi-component product manufacturing companies face the challenge of estimating warranty costs. Failure rate analysis of components plays a crucial role in this problem. Traditionally, past failure data of components has been the primary source of information for failure rate analysis. However, this analysis can be enhanced by fusing additional information, such as symptoms observed during after-sale service, geographical information (hilly or plains areas), and data from tele-diagnostic analytics. This paper proposes an approach that learns dependencies between part failures and symptoms gleaned from diverse information sources to predict the expected number of failures with improved accuracy. The paper also outlines how to compute the optimal warranty period. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly enhance warranty cost estimates.
label: AI

title: Inferring User Preferences by Probabilistic Logical Reasoning over Social Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces a framework for inferring the latent attitudes or preferences of users by performing probabilistic first-order logical reasoning over the social network graph. The method answers questions about Twitter users, such as "Does this user like sushi?" or "Is this user a New York Knicks fan?" by building a probabilistic model that reasons over user attributes (location, gender) and the social network (friends, spouse), using inferences like homophily (e.g., I am more likely to like sushi if my spouse or friends like sushi, I am more likely to like the Knicks if I live in New York). The algorithm leverages distant supervision, semi-supervised data harvesting, and vector space models to extract user attributes (spouse, education, location) and preferences (likes and dislikes) from text. These extracted propositions are then fed into a probabilistic reasoner, either Markov Logic or Probabilistic Soft Logic. Experiments show that probabilistic logical reasoning significantly improves the performance of attribute and relation extraction and achieves an F-score of 0.791 in predicting user likes or dislikes, outperforming two strong baselines.
label: AI

title: Bounding the Probability of Causation in Mediation Analysis
Abstract: Given empirical evidence for the dependence of an outcome variable on an exposure variable, typically only bounds for the "probability of causation" can be provided in the case of an individual who developed the outcome after being exposed. This paper shows how these bounds can be adapted or improved when further information becomes available. In addition to reviewing existing work on this topic, the paper provides a new analysis for the case where a mediating variable can be observed. Specifically, the paper demonstrates how the probability of causation can be bounded when there is no direct effect and no confounding. |||
label: AI

title: Answering Conjunctive Queries over $\mathcal{EL}$ Knowledge Bases with Transitive and Reflexive Roles
Abstract: Answering conjunctive queries (CQs) over EL knowledge bases (KBs) with complex role inclusions is a PSPACE-hard problem, but it becomes tractable for acyclic CQs and ELH KBs. The complexity landscape for CQ answering is further refined by considering the presence of reflexive and transitive roles. This paper presents a practical NP algorithm for answering CQs over ELHO^s KBs, a logic encompassing all of OWL 2 EL, but with complex role inclusions limited to role transitivity. The algorithm's preliminary evaluation suggests its suitability for practical applications. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that CQ answering over EL KBs becomes NP-hard even for a restricted class of arborescent acyclic queries in the presence of either transitive or reflexive roles. Finally, it shows that answering arborescent CQs over ELHO KBs is tractable, while answering acyclic CQs remains NP-hard.
label: AI

title: Comparative Study of View Update Algorithms in Rational Choice Theory
Abstract: Knowledge base dynamics, a crucial component of any autonomous system capable of incorporating new information, has interesting connections with kernel change via hitting set and abduction. This approach integrates standard techniques for efficient query answering and integrity checking. The generation of hitting sets is achieved through a hyper tableaux calculus and magic set, focusing on minimality. The paper provides a comparative study of view update algorithms in a rational approach, addressing the challenges of integrating new information into existing knowledge bases.
label: AI

title: Similarity Learning for High-Dimensional Sparse Data
Abstract: Similarity learning methods are often challenged by high dimensionality in data. This paper presents a novel method to efficiently learn similarity measures from high-dimensional sparse data. It parameterizes the similarity measure as a convex combination of rank-one matrices with specific sparsity structures. Parameters are optimized using an approximate Frank-Wolfe procedure to maximize satisfaction of relative similarity constraints on the training data. The algorithm greedily incorporates feature pairs into the similarity measure, controlling the number of active features and reducing overfitting. The method enjoys appealing convergence guarantees and its time and memory complexity depend on data sparsity rather than feature space dimensionality. Experiments on real-world high-dimensional datasets demonstrate its potential for classification, dimensionality reduction, and data exploration.
label: AI

title: Modeling Word Relatedness in Latent Dirichlet Allocation
Abstract: Standard LDA models neglect word correlation due to independent topic assignment for each word. This paper introduces Word Related Latent Dirichlet Allocation (WR-LDA), incorporating word correlation into LDA topic models. WR-LDA enables capabilities absent in standard LDA, such as estimating infrequent words and multi-language topic modeling. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of WR-LDA compared to standard LDA.
label: AI

title: Zero-Aliasing Correlation Filters for Object Recognition
Abstract: Correlation filters (CFs) are widely used in object localization and tracking due to their efficiency. Traditionally, CFs have been designed in the frequency domain using the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). This paper addresses the issue of circular correlation in the time/spatial domain, which is a consequence of DFT multiplication. The paper introduces zero-aliasing constraints that eliminate this aliasing problem, ensuring that the optimization criterion corresponds to linear correlation rather than circular correlation. This reformulation leads to significantly improved CF designs. The benefits of the new CF design approach are demonstrated with several important CFs, and experimental results on diverse datasets are presented. Computational challenges associated with these CFs are also addressed.
label: AI

title: Estimating Fire Weather Indices via Semantic Reasoning over Wireless Sensor Network Data Streams
Abstract: Wildfires in Australia pose significant risks, and fire weather indices play a vital role in warning systems and resource allocation. Existing fire weather index calculation systems are limited by low spatial and temporal resolution. This paper proposes a standardized approach using semantic web technologies to overcome these limitations by leveraging high-resolution data from localized wireless sensor networks. The paper describes the ontologies, semantic reasoning, and Semantic Fire Weather Index (SFWI) system developed to enable domain experts to specify and adapt rules for index calculation. A web-based mapping interface is also presented, allowing users to visualize temporal variations in fire weather indices within specific regions. The evaluation results demonstrate the system's superiority in accuracy, precision, and query performance compared to existing methods.
label: AI

title: Efficient Estimation of Mutual Information for Strongly Dependent Variables
Abstract: Nonparametric mutual information (MI) estimators based on k-nearest-neighbor graphs require an exponentially increasing sample size with the true MI. This paper highlights this shortcoming and introduces a new estimator that is robust to local non-uniformity, performs well with limited data, and captures relationship strengths over multiple orders of magnitude. The paper demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed estimator on both synthetic and real-world data.
label: AI

title: Azhary: An Arabic Lexical Ontology
Abstract: Arabic, a widely spoken language with significant cultural and religious importance, lacks a comprehensive semantic lexicon for researchers. This paper introduces Azhary, a lexical ontology for the Arabic language. Azhary organizes Arabic words into synsets (sets of synonyms) and records various relationships between words, including synonym, antonym, hypernym, hyponym, meronym, holonym, and association relations. The ontology contains 26,195 words in 13,328 synsets and has been developed and contrasted against AWN, the most widely available Arabic lexical ontology.
label: AI

title: Hardware and Software manual for Evolution of Oil Droplets in a Chemo-Robotic Platform
Abstract: This manual outlines a fully automated liquid handling robot for physically-embodied evolution within a chemical oil-droplet system. The robot, based on the REPRAP3D printer system, creates droplets by mixing chemicals and placing them in a petri dish. Droplet behavior is then analyzed using image recognition software after being recorded by a camera. This manual accompanies the open access publication in Nature Communications DOI: 10.1038/ncomms6571.

title: A Novel Uncertainty Parameter SR (Signal To Residual Spectrum Ratio) Evaluation Approach For Speech Enhancement
Abstract: Hearing impaired individuals often rely on hearing aids equipped with speech enhancement algorithms. This paper addresses the challenge of noise power spectrum estimation for non-stationary environments in single-channel speech enhancement systems. It introduces a novel evaluation approach based on the Signal to Residual spectrum ratio (SR) to enhance intelligibility, quality, and reduce listener fatigue. The proposed method estimates and updates noise based on dividing the original signal into three parts: pure speech, quasi speech, and non-speech frames, using multiple threshold conditions. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the SR and LLR (Log Likelihood Ratio) parameters in controlling distortions and compares the proposed method with the Weighted Average Technique (WAT).

title: Pervasive Healthcare-A Comprehensive Survey of Tools and Techniques
Abstract: Pervasive healthcare aims to provide continuous monitoring of vital signs using health sensors, communication protocols, and context-aware applications. This paper presents a comprehensive review of common disorders addressed by pervasive healthcare, classified by patient age groups. It discusses hardware and software tools and techniques for detecting and treating these disorders. The paper also includes a detailed tabular classification of significant research articles in pervasive healthcare.

title: Variational Tempering
Abstract: Variational inference (VI) combined with data subsampling enables approximate posterior inference over large datasets, but suffers from poor local optima. This paper formulates a deterministic annealing approach for conditionally conjugate exponential family models, using a decreasing temperature parameter to deform the objective during optimization. The paper then introduces variational tempering, an algorithm that introduces a temperature latent variable to the model, resulting in adaptive annealing schedules. Finally, local variational tempering, which assigns a latent temperature to each data point, allows for dynamic annealing across data. All proposed approaches achieve improved predictive likelihoods on held-out data compared to traditional VI.
label: AI

title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
Abstract: Generative Adversarial Nets (GANs) are a novel method for training generative models. This paper introduces the conditional version of GANs, which can generate data conditioned on a specific input. The model is demonstrated by generating MNIST digits conditioned on class labels. The paper also explores the potential of conditional GANs for learning multi-modal models and image tagging applications, where it generates descriptive tags that are not part of training labels.
label: AI

title: Submodular meets Structured: Finding Diverse Subsets in Exponentially-Large Structured Item Sets
Abstract: Robust prediction methods often search for diverse high-quality candidate solutions in domains like computer vision and natural language processing, especially in structured prediction problems where the solution space is exponentially large. This paper investigates greedy algorithms for finding diverse subsets of solutions in structured-output spaces by drawing connections between submodular functions and high-order potentials (HOPs) in graphical models. The paper shows that when marginal gains of submodular diversity functions allow structured representations, efficient approximate maximization is possible by reducing the greedy augmentation step to inference in a factor graph with appropriately constructed HOPs. The benefits, tradeoffs, and significantly improved proposals achieved through this approach are discussed.
label: AI

title: The Limitations of Standardized Science Tests as Benchmarks for Artificial Intelligence Research: Position Paper
Abstract: Standardized tests for elementary science, such as SAT and Regents tests, are not effective benchmarks for measuring progress in AI understanding of basic science. This position paper argues that these tests are designed to assess human-specific challenges, which differ significantly from AI challenges. The paper analyzes the Physics subject SAT and the New York State Regents Science test, highlighting their shortcomings as AI benchmarks. The paper concludes that more appropriate collections of exam-style problems could be assembled and that alternative benchmarks beyond exam-style problems are preferable.

title: Scalable Parallel Numerical CSP Solver
Abstract: This paper presents a parallel solver for numerical constraint satisfaction problems (NCSPs) that scales on a number of cores. The proposed method employs worker solvers on available cores, with simultaneous cooperation for search space distribution and balancing. The experiments achieved up to 119-fold speedup using 256 cores of a parallel computer.
label: AI

title: The Spaces of Data, Information, and Knowledge
Abstract: The paper explores the concept of knowledge discovery from data. It defines the data space D of a dataset X and explains how functions and relations are defined over D. The information space I is constructed by interpreting variables, functions, and explicit relations over D within a specific domain Δ. The knowledge space K is then built as the product of two spaces, KT and KP. KT is derived from I using induction and deduction principles to generalize and generate relations, while KP represents methods and their operational instructions valid in KT. The paper concludes that knowledge discovery involves mining domain objects and relations, applying induction and deduction principles to generate propositions, synthesizing and modeling information to generate specifications, and validating propositions and specifications. This understanding enables the development of efficient approaches for automated knowledge discovery from simple data.
label: AI

title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: This book-length article analyzes the ethical implications of artificial intelligence (AI), combining peer-reviewed papers and new material. It explores mathematical descriptions of AI behavior and discusses potential unintended consequences and design strategies to avoid them. The article advocates for utility-maximizing agents and the avoidance of infinite sets in agent definitions. It demonstrates techniques for preventing agent self-delusion and perverse instantiation, and argues that agents can avoid unintended instrumental actions by accurately learning human values. The article defines a self-modeling agent framework and shows its effectiveness in addressing problems of resource limits, prediction by other agents, and inconsistencies between utility functions and definitions. It also discusses the future of AI, its political implications, and its potential for understanding the universe and our place in it.

title: An Intelligent Personal Robot Assistant
Abstract: The development of humanoid robots presents new challenges for human-machine interaction communication. This paper proposes a system to develop a robot capable of receiving commands, engaging in natural language conversations, and providing expert advice in specific areas. Notably, the robot can display emotions through facial expressions, speech, and gestures, making the interaction process more comprehensive and compelling.
label: AI

title: Learning of Agent Capability Models with Applications in Multi-agent Planning
Abstract: Efficient collaboration among agents requires accurate models of each other. This paper introduces a novel representation for agent models based on capability models, which offers several advantages over MDP-based and action-based models. Capability models can be efficiently learnt online using Bayesian learning and are robust to high degrees of incompleteness in plan execution traces. The paper demonstrates that capability models can abstract useful information from incomplete traces, making them suitable for applications like robot learning from human observations. Capability models also provide flexible action abstraction in multi-agent planning, although the synthesized plan is incomplete and abstract.
label: AI

title: Enhancing software module reusability using port plug-ins: an experiment with the iCub robot
Abstract: Developing reusable software components of high quality is a challenging task that necessitates careful design to achieve a balance between potential reuse, functionalities, and ease of implementation. Extendibility is a crucial property for software, contributing to reduced development costs and enhanced reusability. This work introduces an approach to improve component reusability by extending their functionalities using plug-ins at the connection points (ports). Application-specific functionalities like data monitoring and arbitration can be implemented using conventional scripting languages and integrated into the ports of components. The main advantage of this approach is its ability to avoid introducing application-specific modifications to existing components, minimizing development time and promoting the creation of simpler, more reusable components. Additionally, this approach reduces communication and deployment overhead, as extra functionalities can be added without the need for additional modules.
label: AI

title: Modeling Transitivity in Complex Networks
Abstract: Transitivity plays a significant role in the high clustering coefficient observed in real-world networks. However, existing models for transitivity suffer from shortcomings, including their limitation to specific graph classes (e.g., bipartite graphs), lack of analytical justification for the high clustering coefficient, and significantly lower clustering coefficients compared to real-world networks. This paper proposes a new model for complex networks based on incorporating transitivity into scale-free models. The model is theoretically analyzed, providing analytical arguments for its various properties. Notably, a lower bound on the clustering coefficient of the model is calculated, independent of the network size, mirroring real-world networks. Beyond theoretical analysis, the model's main properties are empirically evaluated, demonstrating its ability to accurately simulate real-world networks from diverse domains with varying specifications.
label: AI

title: Tied Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis for Speech Recognition
Abstract: Acoustic models employing probabilistic linear discriminant analysis (PLDA) capture correlations within feature vectors using subspaces, avoiding significant expansion of the model. This enables the use of high-dimensional and correlated feature spaces without requiring the estimation of numerous high-dimensional covariance matrices. This letter extends the recently introduced PLDA mixture model for speech recognition through a tied PLDA approach, better controlling model size to prevent overfitting. Experiments using the Switchboard corpus, with both mel frequency cepstral coefficient features and bottleneck features derived from a deep neural network, were conducted. Tied PLDA achieved reductions in word error rate compared to the PLDA mixture model, subspace Gaussian mixture models, and deep neural networks.
label: AI

title: Approximate Counting in SMT and Value Estimation for Probabilistic Programs
Abstract: Model counting for logical theories (#SMT) is a well-known computationally challenging problem, encompassing tasks such as counting satisfying assignments to Boolean formulas and computing the volume of a polytope. In the context of satisfiability modulo theories (SMT), there is a growing need for model counting solvers, driven by various application domains such as quantitative information flow and static analysis of probabilistic programs. This paper presents a reduction from an approximate version of #SMT to SMT. Focusing on the theories of integer arithmetic and linear real arithmetic, model counting algorithms are proposed that provide approximate solutions with formal bounds on the approximation error. These algorithms operate in polynomial time and make a polynomial number of queries to the SMT solver for the underlying theory, leveraging the sophisticated heuristics implemented within modern SMT solvers. The algorithms have been implemented and used to solve the value problem for a model of loop-free probabilistic programs with nondeterminism.
label: AI

title: Affective Facial Expression Processing via Simulation: A Probabilistic Model
Abstract: Understanding the mental state of others is a crucial skill for intelligent agents and robots operating within social environments. However, the mental processes involved in "mind-reading" are complex. Simulation Theory, supported by extensive neuropsychological research, offers one explanation for these processes. Determining the optimal computational model or theory for simulation-style emotion detection remains a challenge. This work utilizes Simulation Theory and neuroscience findings on Mirror-Neuron Systems as the foundation for a novel computational model for handling affective facial expressions. The model is based on a probabilistic mapping of observations from multiple identities onto a single fixed identity ("internal transcoding of external stimuli") and then onto a latent space ("phenomenological response"). Along with the proposed architecture, promising preliminary results are presented.
label: AI

title: Distributed Submodular Maximization
Abstract: Many large-scale machine learning problems, including clustering, non-parametric learning, and kernel machines, require the selection of a small yet representative subset from a large dataset. These problems can often be reduced to maximizing a submodular set function subject to various constraints. Traditional submodular optimization approaches necessitate centralized access to the complete dataset, which is impractical for truly large-scale problems. This paper explores submodular function maximization in a distributed manner. A simple, two-stage protocol, GreeDi, is developed that is easily implementable using MapReduce-style computations. The approach is theoretically analyzed, demonstrating that under certain natural conditions, performance close to the centralized approach can be achieved. The paper begins with monotone submodular maximization subject to a cardinality constraint, then extends this approach to obtain approximation guarantees for (not necessarily monotone) submodular maximization subject to more general constraints, including matroid or knapsack constraints. Extensive experiments showcase the effectiveness of this approach on various applications, including sparse Gaussian process inference and exemplar-based clustering on tens of millions of examples using Hadoop.

title: Modelling serendipity in a computational context
Abstract: Serendipity refers to a creative process that unfolds within a context, involving the active participation of a creative agent, but not entirely under their control. While a system cannot be made to perform serendipitously on demand, we argue that its serendipity potential can be enhanced through appropriate system architecture and design choices. A unified description of serendipitous occurrences is distilled from historical theories of serendipity and creativity, resulting in a framework with six phases: perception, attention, interest, explanation, bridge, and valuation. This framework is used to organize a survey of literature in cognitive science, philosophy, and computing, leading to practical definitions of the six phases and heuristics for implementation. The resulting model is used to evaluate the serendipity potential of four existing systems developed by others and two systems previously developed by two of the authors. Most existing research on serendipity in computing focuses on serendipity as a service. This work connects theories of serendipity to the development of autonomous systems and computational creativity practice. We argue that serendipity is not teleologically blind and outline representative directions for future applications of the model. The study concludes that equipping computational systems with the potential for serendipity is feasible and could be beneficial in various computational creativity/AI applications, particularly those designed to operate responsively in real-world contexts.

title: GC-SROIQ(C) : Expressive Constraint Modelling and Grounded Circumscription for SROIQ
Abstract: Advancements in semantic web technologies have spurred the ontological encoding of knowledge from diverse domains. However, modeling many practical domains demands more expressive representation schemes than what standard description logics (DLs) support. This paper extends the DL SROIQ with constraint networks and grounded circumscription. Constraint modeling finds applications in embedding ontologies with temporal or spatial information, while grounded circumscription enables defeasible inference and closed-world reasoning. The paper addresses limitations of existing constraint modeling approaches by introducing expressive constructs. Grounded circumscription facilitates concept and role minimization and is decidable for DL. A general and intuitive algorithm for the framework of grounded circumscription is provided, applicable to a wide range of logics. The resulting logic, GC-SROIQ(C), is presented, along with a tableau decision procedure for it.
label: AI

title: NESTA, The NICTA Energy System Test Case Archive
Abstract: In recent years, the power systems research community has witnessed a surge in work applying operations research techniques to challenging power network optimization problems. Regardless of the application, these works rely on power system test cases for evaluation and validation. However, many well-established power system test cases were developed as far back as the 1960s with the aim of testing AC power flow algorithms. The suitability of these power flow test cases for power system optimization studies remains uncertain. This report comprehensively surveys all publicly available AC transmission system test cases, to the best of our knowledge, and assesses their suitability for optimization tasks. The survey reveals that many traditional test cases lack key network operation constraints, such as line thermal limits and generator capability curves. To incorporate these missing constraints, data-driven models are developed from various publicly available data sources. The resulting extended test cases form a comprehensive archive, NESTA, for the evaluation and validation of power system optimization algorithms.

title: On the read-once property of branching programs and CNFs of bounded treewidth
Abstract: This paper proves a space lower bound of $n^{\\Omega(k)}$ for non-deterministic (syntactic) read-once branching programs (nrobps) on functions expressible as CNFs with treewidth at most $k$ of their primal graphs. This lower bound eliminates the possibility of fixed-parameter space complexity of nrobps parameterized by $k$. The lower bound for nrobps is used to obtain a quasi-polynomial separation between Free Binary Decision Diagrams and Decision Decomposable Negation Normal Forms, essentially matching the existing upper bound introduced by Beame et al. and thus proving the tightness of the latter.

title: A Heuristic Method for Solving the Problem of Partitioning Graphs with Supply and Demand
Abstract: This paper presents a greedy algorithm for solving the problem of maximum partitioning of graphs with supply and demand (MPGSD). The algorithm aims to solve the MPGSD for large graphs within a reasonable time limit by employing a two-stage greedy algorithm, with two corresponding types of heuristics. The obtained solutions are further improved by applying a computationally inexpensive, hill-climbing-like, greedy correction procedure. Numerical experiments analyze different heuristic functions for each stage of the greedy algorithm, demonstrating that their performance is highly dependent on the specific instance's properties. Tests show that by exploring a relatively small number of solutions generated by combining different heuristic functions and applying the proposed correction procedure, solutions within a few percent of the optimal ones can be found.
label: AI

title: A Multi-Heuristic Approach for Solving the Pre-Marshalling Problem
Abstract: Minimizing the number of reshuffling operations at maritime container terminals involves the Pre-Marshalling Problem (PMP) as a crucial aspect. Based on an analysis of existing solution approaches, new heuristics are developed that utilize specific properties of problem instances of the PMP. The performance of these heuristics is shown to be highly dependent on these properties. A new method is introduced that exploits a greedy heuristic of four stages, where several different heuristics can be applied at each stage. Instead of relying on randomization to improve heuristic performance, solutions are generated repetitively by using a combination of different heuristics for each stage. This approach ensures that only a small number of solutions are generated, minimizing undesirable properties compared to simple randomization. Experiments demonstrate that this deterministic algorithm significantly outperforms the original nondeterministic method in terms of solution quality, with a much lower number of generated solutions.

title: Synthetic Cognitive Development: where intelligence comes from
Abstract: The human cognitive system serves as a remarkable example of a general intelligent system with capabilities extending beyond a specific problem domain. Evidently, general cognitive competences arise from a prolonged and intricate process of cognitive development. Consequently, understanding the emergence of intelligent behavior hinges on comprehending this process. This paper develops the theoretical foundations for a model that generalizes the process of cognitive development. The model aims to provide a realistic scheme for synthesizing scalable cognitive systems with an open-ended range of capabilities. Major concepts and theories of human cognitive development are introduced and briefly explored, focusing on the enactive approach to cognition and the concept of sense-making. The initial scheme of human cognitive development is then generalized by introducing the philosophy of individuation and the abstract mechanism of transduction. The theory of individuation provides the foundation for the necessary paradigmatic shift from cognitive systems as given products to cognitive development as a formative process of self-organization. The conceptual model is specified as a scalable scheme of networks of agents. The mechanisms of individuation are formulated in context-independent information-theoretical terms. Finally, the paper discusses two concrete aspects of the generative model: mechanisms of transduction and value-modulating systems. These topics serve as further research directions towards a computationally realizable model.
label: AI

title: Surrogate Search As a Way to Combat Harmful Effects of Ill-behaved Evaluation Functions
Abstract: Recent research has revealed that cost-based satisficing search with A* often encounters difficulties. While "workarounds" have been proposed to mitigate the problem, a concerted effort to pinpoint its origin has been lacking. This paper argues that the root of this problem lies in the fact that most planners aiming to optimize cost also utilize cost-based evaluation functions (i.e., f(n) is a cost estimate). It is shown that cost-based evaluation functions become ill-behaved when there is a wide variance in action costs, a common occurrence in planning domains. The general solution to this issue is what we call "surrogate search," where a surrogate evaluation function that does not directly track the cost objective and is resistant to cost-variance is used. Compelling choices for surrogate evaluation functions based on size rather than cost are discussed. Of particular practical interest is a cost-sensitive version of a size-based evaluation function, where the heuristic estimates the size of cheap paths, as it offers attractive quality vs. speed tradeoffs.
label: AI

title: How Many Workers to Ask? Adaptive Exploration for Collecting High Quality Labels
Abstract: Crowdsourcing has become a part of the information retrieval toolbox as a cost-effective and rapid mechanism for obtaining labels for system development and evaluation. Successful deployment of crowdsourcing at scale involves adjusting numerous variables, with a crucial one being the number of workers needed per human intelligence task (HIT). This paper focuses on the crowdsourcing task of learning the answer to simple multiple-choice HITs, representative of many relevance experiments. Obtaining statistically significant results often necessitates asking multiple workers to answer the same HIT. A stopping rule is an algorithm that, given a HIT, decides for any given set of worker answers whether the system should stop and output an answer or iterate and ask one more worker. Knowing the historical performance of a worker in the form of a quality score can be beneficial in this scenario. This paper investigates how to devise better stopping rules given such quality scores. Adaptive exploration is suggested as a promising approach for scalable and automatic creation of ground truth. A data analysis is conducted on an industrial crowdsourcing platform, and the observations from this analysis are used to design new stopping rules that utilize workers' quality scores in a non-trivial manner. A simulation based on a real-world workload shows that the proposed algorithm performs better than more naive approaches.
label: AI

title: A Comparison of learning algorithms on the Arcade Learning Environment
Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents have traditionally been evaluated on small, toy problems. Advancements in computing power and the advent of the Arcade Learning Environment have made it possible to evaluate algorithms on diverse and challenging problems within a consistent framework. This paper discusses some challenges posed by the arcade learning environment that do not manifest in simpler environments. A comparison of model-free, linear learning algorithms is then provided on this challenging problem set.
label: AI

title: An Ensemble-based System for Microaneurysm Detection and Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
Abstract: Reliable microaneurysm detection in digital fundus images remains an open issue in medical image processing. This paper proposes an ensemble-based framework to enhance microaneurysm detection. Unlike the well-known approach of considering the output of multiple classifiers, this framework proposes a combination of internal components of microaneurysm detectors, namely preprocessing methods and candidate extractors. The approach has been evaluated for microaneurysm detection in an online competition, where it currently ranks first, as well as on two other databases. Since microaneurysm detection is crucial in diabetic retinopathy grading, the proposed method was also tested for this task on the publicly available Messidor database, achieving a promising AUC of 0.90 with 0.01 uncertainty in a "DR/non-DR" classification based on the presence or absence of microaneurysms.

title: Managing shop floor systems Using RFID in the Middle East
Abstract: The controllability of a factory is highly dependent on the capability of a given enterprise planning system to interact with the shop floor, as well as the ability of authorized users to review operation plans and the status of any sales order on the shop floor. This paper introduces the concept of E-manufacturing, a method for improving factory controllability by connecting the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system to the shop floor control (SFC) system through the internet. Integrating business systems and plant systems reduces decision cycle times, increases plant productivity, eliminates human intervention for improved accuracy, and accelerates data availability. This paper presents the findings of a project funded by the Egyptian Ministry of Scientific Research and Technology. The project's overall objective is to bridge the gap between R&D and manufacturing to address the immediate technological needs of Egyptian industry and economy, building national technology expertise. This is achieved by developing an E-Manufacturing system using state-of-the-art RFID technology. The specific objective is to create an end product for Egyptian industry that manages real-time interaction with back-end ERP systems to correct delays on the shop floor, improving real-time operation, reducing costs, and enabling real-time visibility through intelligent use of RFID. The end product is a fully functioning system tested in the factory of the manufacturing partner MOBICA. This report outlines the logical and technical structure, as well as technology constraints to be considered in such systems, and the implementation stages of the project.

title: Tasks that Require, or can Benefit from, Matching Blank Nodes
Abstract: In various domains and cases, we observe the creation and usage of information elements that are unnamed. These elements lack a name or may have a name that is not externally referable (usually meaningless and not persistent over time). This paper discusses why we will never fully escape the problem of constructing mappings between such unnamed elements in information systems. Since unnamed elements are common in the context of the Semantic Web and Linked Data as blank nodes, the paper describes scenarios that can benefit from methods that compute mappings between these unnamed elements. For each scenario, the corresponding blank node matching problem is formally defined. Based on this analysis, a more general formulation of the problem is sought, which can guide required technological advancements. Finally, the paper discusses methods to realize blank node matching, existing implementations, and identifies open issues and challenges.

title: Training for Fast Sequential Prediction Using Dynamic Feature Selection
Abstract: This paper presents paired learning and inference algorithms for significantly reducing computation and increasing the speed of vector dot products in classifiers that are at the heart of many natural language processing (NLP) components. This is achieved by partitioning features into a sequence of templates ordered such that high confidence can often be reached using only a small fraction of all features. Parameter estimation is arranged to maximize accuracy and early confidence in this sequence. Experiments in left-to-right part-of-speech tagging on WSJ demonstrate that accuracy above 97% can be preserved with a five-fold reduction in runtime. |||

title: Towards Learning Object Affordance Priors from Technical Texts
Abstract: Artificial assistants often lack common sense knowledge, potentially leading to naive and dangerous actions. This paper proposes a new approach to understanding the abilities of entities by analyzing semantic relations in non-figurative texts. The method focuses on extracting "X can Y" relations by examining the co-occurrence of grammatical instances of subjects, verbs, and objects. This approach could provide insights into the usual modalities (passive or active) of entities and their affordance estimates. The paper outlines the concept, potential applications, limitations, and possible feature and learning frameworks for this approach.
label: AI

title: Efficient Decision-Making by Volume-Conserving Physical Object
Abstract: By demonstrating that any physical object, when coupled with suitable operations, can provide a sophisticated decision-making capability, this paper introduces a novel method for finding the most profitable option from a set of stochastic reward-giving options. This method involves physically manipulating the object in a way reminiscent of a tug-of-war, with movements mirroring the fluctuations of a rigid body. Analytical calculations validate the higher efficiency of this approach compared to conventional algorithms.
label: AI

title: Do Artificial Reinforcement-Learning Agents Matter Morally?
Abstract: Artificial reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful technique in artificial intelligence that trains agents to perform various tasks. Striking parallels exist between RL in computer science and reward/punishment learning in human and animal brains. This paper argues that current RL agents possess a small but non-zero degree of ethical importance, particularly in light of theories suggesting varying degrees of sentience based on mind complexity. Even for binary views on consciousness, the possibility of RL programs having morally relevant experiences should not be disregarded. Although not a top ethical priority today, RL programs may become more significant as the technology is increasingly applied in various fields. The paper encourages discussion among scientists, philosophers, and citizens about our ethical responsibilities to minimize harm to these powerless agents.
label: AI

title: A Semantic Web of Know-How: Linked Data for Community-Centric Tasks
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for representing community know-how on the Semantic Web. Community-generated procedural knowledge, typically presented as natural language instructions or videos, lacks semantic structure. This absence hinders the development of many useful applications, including automated know-how discovery and integration. Analyzing the characteristics of community know-how, the paper argues that existing knowledge representation frameworks are insufficient. It presents a new framework for representing the semantic structure of community know-how and demonstrates its feasibility through a concrete implementation. This implementation includes a method for automatically acquiring procedural knowledge for real-world tasks.
label: AI

title: Towards a Visual Turing Challenge
Abstract: As language and visual understanding by machines advance rapidly, there is a growing interest in holistic architectures that seamlessly combine both modalities in a joint learning and inference process. This trend facilitates tackling more challenging and open tasks, reviving the AI dream of creating machines capable of passing the Turing test in open domains. However, quantifying performance in these open tasks becomes increasingly complex. This paper explores the challenges of defining such tasks and evaluating algorithms on them. It discusses potential solutions found in the literature, exemplified through a recently presented question-answering dataset based on real-world indoor images. The paper argues that, while carefully curated datasets have achieved success, we need to move beyond them and rely on "social consensus" to create suitable benchmarks. Addressing the ambiguity inherent in output spaces is a crucial challenge for making quantifiable progress in this area.
label: AI

title: Reasoning for ALCQ extended with a flexible meta-modelling hierarchy
Abstract: Motivated by a real-world case study requiring integration and connection of existing ontologies through meta-modeling, this paper introduces the Description Logic ALCQM. This extension of ALCQ incorporates statements that equate individuals to concepts in a knowledge base, allowing concepts to be individuals of other concepts (meta-concepts), which can themselves be individuals of further concepts (meta meta-concepts), and so on. The paper defines a tableau algorithm for checking the consistency of an ontology in ALCQM and proves its correctness.
label: AI

title: Using synchronous Boolean networks to model several phenomena of collective behavior
Abstract: This paper presents an approach for modeling and analyzing phenomena of collective behavior in multi-agent systems transitioning between states at discrete time moments. The behavior of individual agents is categorized as conforming if their opinion at a given time aligns with the opinions of other agents at the previous time. Each agent makes a decision from a set of two choices (action or inaction). The approach models collective behavior using synchronous Boolean networks with agents categorized as instigators (acting at every time moment), loyalists (never acting), and simple agents (neither instigators nor loyalists). The paper investigates two combinatorial problems: finding an arrangement of instigators to transition the network from a majority of inactive simple agents to a majority of active agents, and finding an arrangement of loyalists to revert the network to a state with a majority of inactive agents. These problems are also studied for networks exhibiting anticonforming behavior, where simple agents act contrary to the conforming pattern. The paper presents theoretical results regarding the behavior of collectives with conforming or anticonforming agents and solves the problems computationally for randomly generated networks with hundreds of vertices. The combinatorial problems are reduced to the Boolean satisfiability problem (SAT) and solved using modern SAT solvers.
label: AI

title: Resource Allocation Optimization for Delay-Sensitive Traffic in Fronthaul Constrained Cloud Radio Access Networks
Abstract: Cloud radio access networks (C-RANs) offer operators high spectral and energy efficiency, low expenditures, and intelligent centralized system structures. This paper presents a hybrid coordinated multi-point transmission (H-CoMP) scheme for downlink transmission in C-RANs, allowing flexible trade-offs between cooperation gains and fronthaul consumption. The paper formulates the problem of queue-aware power and rate allocation with fronthaul consumption constraints for delay-sensitive traffic as an infinite horizon constrained partially observed Markov decision process (POMDP). This formulation considers both urgent queue state information (QSI) and imperfect channel state information at transmitters (CSIT). To address the curse of dimensionality in the equivalent Bellman equation, the paper utilizes linear approximation of post-decision value functions. A stochastic gradient algorithm is presented to allocate queue-aware power and transmission rate with H-CoMP, robust against unpredictable traffic arrivals and CSIT uncertainties. An online learning algorithm is proposed to estimate the per-queue post-decision value functions and update Lagrange multipliers, significantly reducing computing complexity. Simulation results demonstrate performance gains achieved through the proposed stochastic gradient algorithms and confirm the asymptotic convergence of the online learning algorithm.
label: AI

title: A Statistical Decision-Theoretic Framework for Social Choice
Abstract: This paper adopts a statistical decision-theoretic viewpoint on social choice, focusing on decisions made on behalf of a system of agents. Within this framework, a statistical ranking model, a decision space, and a loss function on (parameter, decision) pairs are provided. Social choice mechanisms are formulated as decision rules minimizing expected loss. This approach offers a general framework for designing and analyzing new social choice mechanisms. The paper compares Bayesian estimators, minimizing Bayesian expected loss, for the Mallows model and the Condorcet model, alongside the Kemeny rule. The analysis considers various normative properties, computational complexity, and asymptotic behavior. The paper shows that the Bayesian estimator for the Condorcet model satisfies desired properties like anonymity, neutrality, and monotonicity, can be computed in polynomial time, and exhibits asymptotic differences from the other two rules when data is generated from the Condorcet model for a specific ground truth parameter.
label: AI

title: Efficient optimisation of structures using tabu search
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for optimizing structures using a Tabu search (TS) method. TS is a metaheuristic guiding local search methods towards a globally optimal solution using flexible memory cycles with varying time spans. The paper presents results for the well-established ten-bar truss problem, comparing them to published results. In the first example, a truss is optimized to minimize mass, with results compared to those obtained using an alternative TS implementation. The second example addresses a multi-objective problem, combining objectives into a single objective function value through game theory. The results demonstrate that the TS method can solve structural optimization problems as efficiently as other numerical optimization approaches.
label: AI

title: A mutli-thread tabu search algorithm
Abstract: This paper describes a novel refinement to a Tabu search algorithm designed to enhance search robustness when tackling complex problems. This approach employs two Tabu searches running in parallel. Each thread has its own short-term memory to escape local optima, but they share an intermediate-term memory, allowing information exchange. Results are presented for unconstrained and constrained numerical functions, as well as a problem in hydraulic circuit optimization. Simulation of hydraulic circuit performance is achieved by linking the optimization algorithm to the commercial simulation package Bathfp.
label: AI

title: Generalized Product of Experts for Automatic and Principled Fusion of Gaussian Process Predictions
Abstract: This work proposes a generalized product of experts (gPoE) framework for combining predictions from multiple probabilistic models. Four key properties are identified as crucial for scalability, expressiveness, and robustness in learning and inference with multiple models. Through analysis and experiments, the paper demonstrates that gPoE of Gaussian processes (GP) possess these qualities, surpassing other existing combination schemes. The resulting GP-gPoE is highly scalable due to parallel learning of individual GP experts, expressive as the combination of experts depends on the input, provides a valid probabilistic model with natural interpretation, and is robust to unreliable predictions from individual experts.
label: AI

title: Worlds beyond our own
Abstract: This paper offers a popular account of current research on extra-solar planetary systems (exoplanets), providing a brief overview of the techniques employed. It discusses the question of habitability and the possibility of finding intelligent life elsewhere in the Milky Way. Finally, the paper explores the less-explored territory of exomoons.
label: AI

title: Trend Filtering on Graphs
Abstract: This paper introduces a family of adaptive estimators on graphs, based on penalizing the $\\ell_1$ norm of discrete graph differences. This generalizes the idea of trend filtering, used for univariate nonparametric regression, to graphs. Similar to the univariate case, graph trend filtering exhibits local adaptivity unmatched by traditional $\\ell_2$-based graph smoothers. It is defined by a convex minimization problem readily solved by efficient algorithms like ADMM or Newton methods. The paper showcases the advantages of graph trend filtering through examples and theory.
label: AI

title: Consensus Message Passing for Layered Graphical Models
Abstract: Generative models offer a powerful framework for probabilistic reasoning, but their application has been hindered by inference difficulties, particularly in computer vision. This paper addresses this challenge by introducing a modification to message passing algorithms, specifically Expectation Propagation (EP) and Variational Message Passing (VMP). This modification learns to exploit the layered structure of vision models by passing "consensus" messages that guide inference towards better solutions. Experiments on various problems show that this approach significantly improves inference accuracy compared to standard EP and VMP, as well as competitive bottom-up conditional models.
label: AI

title: Maximally Informative Hierarchical Representations of High-Dimensional Data
Abstract: This paper presents bounds on the informativeness of a set of probabilistic functions representing input variables. These bounds are extended to hierarchical representations, quantifying the contribution of each layer to capturing information from the original data. The special form of these bounds facilitates a simple, bottom-up optimization procedure to construct maximally informative hierarchical representations. This optimization exhibits linear computational complexity and constant sample complexity in the number of variables. This approach establishes a new, principled, and practical method for unsupervised learning of deep representations. The paper demonstrates its effectiveness on both synthetic and real-world data.
label: AI

title: Internalizing Null Extraterrestrial "Signals": An Astrobiological App for a Technological Society
Abstract: The search for life in the Universe has the beneficial outcome of highlighting our own problems on Earth. The lack of contact with alien beings to date may be a null "signal," pointing humankind towards a sustainable future. Astrobiology surprisingly has practical applications to human society, clarifying the energetic essence of complex systems throughout the Universe, including technological intelligence, which relies heavily on energy. The "message" conveyed by this "signal" suggests that only solar energy can power our civilization going forward without harming the environment while robustly driving the economy. The null "signals" from extraterrestrials also offer a solution to the Fermi paradox, suggesting that a principle of cosmic selection may limit galactic civilizations in both space and time. Advanced life-forms that wisely adopt the energy of their parent star are more likely to survive.
label: AI

title: An Unsupervised Ensemble-based Markov Random Field Approach to Microscope Cell Image Segmentation
Abstract: This paper proposes an unsupervised image segmentation approach using Markov Random Fields, based on the idea of Bit Plane Slicing. The method utilizes bit planes as initial labelings for an ensemble of segmentations. Pixelwise voting then produces a robust segmentation, as demonstrated on microscope cell images. The approach was tested on a publicly available database, showing competitiveness with other methods and manual segmentation.
label: AI

title: Can Collimated Extraterrestrial Signals be Intercepted?
Abstract: The Optical Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (OSETI) aims to detect collimated, narrowband pulses of electromagnetic radiation, which could be intentional signals directed at Earth or unintentional signals between star systems intersecting the Solar System. This paper explores the likelihood of intercepting such unintentional signals and investigates constraints on the frequency of intelligent civilizations based on interception. Monte Carlo simulations of interstellar communications between civilizations in the Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ) using collimated beams were conducted to measure the frequency of interceptions. The interception rate increases linearly with the fraction of communicating civilizations and as the cube of the beam opening angle, exceeding theoretical expectations due to the geometry of the GHZ. For an annular GHZ containing 10,000 civilizations, interceptions are unlikely unless beams are relatively uncollimated. The results suggest that optical SETI is more likely to find intentionally directed signals than accidental interceptions of collimated communications. Civilizations seeking to establish a communication network might use weakly collimated beams to facilitate interception, balancing cost optimization with contact encouragement. Future SETI searches should consider both narrow-beam pulses directed at Earth and weakly collimated pulses.
