title: The probatilistic Quantifier Fuzzification Mechanism FA: A theoretical analysis
Abstract: This work analyzes the behavior of the FA quantifier fuzzification mechanism. The paper proves the mechanism's solid theoretical behavior, surpassing most models in the literature. The underlying probabilistic interpretation is shown to have interesting consequences.
label: AI

title: Analysis of Named Entity Recognition and Linking for Tweets
Abstract: Applying natural language processing to extract information from tweets is a challenging task due to their short, noisy, and dynamic nature. Traditional information extraction pipelines, which involve language identification, tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and disambiguation, face difficulties with these unique characteristics. This paper introduces a new Twitter entity disambiguation dataset and conducts an empirical analysis of named entity recognition and disambiguation on this dataset. The study examines the robustness of state-of-the-art systems in handling noisy text, identifies major sources of error, and pinpoints areas that require further investigation to enhance performance.
label: AI

title: XML Information Retrieval:An overview
Abstract: Information retrieval (IR) systems face significant challenges in locating and extracting relevant information from the vast amount of online data. As XML has become a widely adopted standard for web content, these challenges are amplified for XML-based IR. While initial efforts focused on adapting traditional IR strategies to the XML format, more recent research has developed novel IR techniques specifically tailored for XML. Despite advancements in specific constrained domains, existing IR systems still struggle to effectively handle the complexity of the information space. This article provides an overview of previous research in XML IR and highlights the remaining gaps.
label: AI

title: Estimating the intrinsic dimension in fMRI space via dataset fractal analysis - Counting the `cpu cores' of the human brain
Abstract: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) is a valuable tool for studying brain activity and its localization. This study investigates the level of parallelism in the human brain during complex cognitive tasks by analyzing fMRI data. Using a data-driven approach, the fMRI signal is treated as a multi-dimensional data space, and its "complexity" is analyzed through fractal analysis and blind-source separation (BSS) methods. The study employs Independent Component Analysis (ICA) and fractal analysis on both simulated and real fMRI datasets to estimate the intrinsic dimensionality of brain activity. These findings provide data-driven evidence about the number of independent brain processes operating simultaneously during visual and visuo-motor tasks. While the exact number of parallel processes is not a fixed threshold but rather a continuous range, the study demonstrates that a specific activation level corresponds to a quantifiable number of parallel processes, or the equivalent of "CPU cores" in the human brain.
label: AI

title: Towards a General Framework for Actual Causation Using CP-logic
Abstract: Since Pearl's seminal work on establishing a formal language for causality, the topic has gained significant attention in both philosophy and artificial intelligence research. One of the most hotly debated areas in this context is the concept of actual causation, which focuses on specific, rather than general, causal claims. The pursuit of a formal definition for actual causation has led to a contentious debate marked by ambiguities and confusion. This research addresses two key objectives. Firstly, it aims to provide a clear framework for comparing competing definitions of actual causation. Secondly, it seeks to enhance these definitions to broaden their applicability to a wider range of instances, including non-deterministic ones. The study achieves these goals by introducing a general, abstract definition of actual causation formulated within the expressive language of CP-logic (Causal Probabilistic logic). It then demonstrates how three recent definitions by Ned Hall, originally formulated for structural models, and a new definition formulated for CP-logic, can be viewed as instantiations of this abstract definition, enabling them to handle a wider array of examples.
label: AI

title: Parameterizing the semantics of fuzzy attribute implications by systems of isotone Galois connections
Abstract: This paper delves into the semantics of fuzzy if-then rules, known as fuzzy attribute implications, parameterized by systems of isotone Galois connections. These rules express dependencies between fuzzy attributes in object-attribute incidence data. The proposed parameterizations are general and encompass previous approaches based on linguistic hedges as special cases. The paper formalizes these general parameterizations, introduces both bivalent and graded notions of semantic entailment for fuzzy attribute implications, and provides characterizations in terms of least models and complete axiomatization. Additionally, it characterizes bases of fuzzy attribute implications derived from data.
label: AI

title: A World of Views: A World of Interacting Post-human Intelligences
Abstract: Speculating about the nature of a being hundreds or thousands of times more intelligent than the brightest human ever born is a daunting task. Such an entity would be so radically different from us that it might not even be recognizable as human. Similarly, imagining a machine with such intelligence requires an immense leap of the imagination. The concept of Technological Singularity, where artificial intelligence surpasses human intelligence and rapidly self-augments beyond that point, embodies an event that is impossible to fully comprehend or predict. This event, often symbolized by the mathematical concept of singularity, represents a significant disruption with far-reaching consequences that defy our ability to grasp conceptually or even metaphorically.
label: AI

title: The Quantum Nature of Identity in Human Thought: Bose-Einstein Statistics for Conceptual Indistinguishability
Abstract: Experimental evidence suggests that humans combine concepts in ways that contradict the rules of classical logic and probability theory. However, mathematical models inspired by quantum theory align with data on concept combination. This paper investigates a novel type of concept combination where a number is combined with a noun, such as "Eleven Animals." The study aims to explore "conceptual identity" and the impact of "indistinguishability" on the mechanisms of concept combination. In the phrase "Eleven Animals," the "animals" are considered identical and indistinguishable. Experiments conducted on human subjects reveal significant deviations from the predictions of classical statistical theories, particularly with respect to Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics. This deviation resembles the divergence of quantum mechanical from classical mechanical statistics due to the indistinguishability of microscopic quantum particles, suggesting the presence of Bose-Einstein statistics. The paper also presents preliminary evidence supporting this phenomenon in a web-based study.
label: AI

title: On the Complexity of Optimization Problems based on Compiled NNF Representations
Abstract: Optimization is a critical task in numerous applications. When the set of feasible solutions is of combinatorial nature and implicitly defined by a set of constraints, optimization is typically NP-hard. However, in many scenarios, the set of feasible solutions remains constant and independent of user requests. In such cases, compiling the set of constraints during an off-line phase can simplify the generation of a non-dominated, feasible solution that meets the user's requirements and preferences, which are only known at the on-line step. This paper focuses on propositional constraints, considering subsets of the NNF language analyzed in Darwiche and Marquis' knowledge compilation map. It examines various families of representations for objective functions over propositional variables, including linear pseudo-Boolean functions and more sophisticated ones. The complexity of generating an optimal solution is determined for each combination of constraint language and objective function family, taking into account the compilation of constraints and optimality with respect to a function from the chosen family.
label: AI

title: Augmenting Ordered Binary Decision Diagrams with Conjunctive Decomposition
Abstract: This paper proposes a generalization of OBDD (Ordered Binary Decision Diagram) called OBDD[$\\wedge$] by incorporating conjunctive decomposition. By imposing reducedness and a finest $\\wedge$-decomposition bounded by integer $i$ ($\\wedge_{\\widehat{i}}$-decomposition) on OBDD[$\\wedge$], a family of canonical languages called ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{i}}$] is identified, where ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{0}}$] is equivalent to ROBDD. The paper demonstrates that the succinctness of ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{i}}$] increases strictly as $i$ increases. A new time-efficiency criterion called rapidity is introduced, which reflects the preference for exponential operations if they enable exponential succinctness gains. The paper shows that the rapidity of each operation on ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{i}}$] increases as $i$ increases, with some operations (e.g., conjoining) exhibiting strict increases in rapidity. Empirical results demonstrate that the size of ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{i}}$] is typically not larger than that of the equivalent ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{i+1}}$]; conjoining two ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{1}}$]s is more efficient than conjoining two ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{0}}$]s in most cases (despite the former being NP-hard and the latter in P); and the space-efficiency of ROBDD[$\\wedge_{\\widehat{\\infty}}$] is comparable to that of d-DNNF and another canonical generalization of ROBDD called SDD.
label: AI

title: StegExpose - A Tool for Detecting LSB Steganography
Abstract: Steganalysis tools are essential for forensic analysts to save time and provide new avenues of attack. StegExpose is a real-world solution designed to analyze images for LSB (Least Significant Bit) steganography in bulk using proven attacks in a time-efficient manner. StegExpose leverages the combined power of steganalytic methods to generate even more accurate results, making it a valuable tool for detecting hidden information within images.
label: AI

title: Partial Optimality by Pruning for MAP-Inference with General Graphical Models
Abstract: The energy minimization problem for undirected graphical models, also known as the MAP-inference problem for Markov random fields, is NP-hard in general. This paper introduces a novel polynomial time algorithm to obtain a part of the optimal non-relaxed integral solution to this problem. The algorithm initializes with variables taking integral values from the solution of a convex relaxation of the MAP-inference problem and iteratively prunes those that do not satisfy the partial optimality criterion. The study demonstrates that the pruning strategy is theoretically optimal in a specific sense. Empirical results show that the method outperforms previous approaches in terms of the number of persistently labeled variables. The method is highly general, applicable to models with arbitrary factors of any order and compatible with any solver for the considered relaxed problem. The runtime is determined by the runtime of the convex relaxation solver for the MAP-inference problem.
label: AI

title: Effect of noise in intelligent cellular decision making
Abstract: Similar to complex multicellular neural networks controlling the human brain, even single cells exhibit intelligent decision-making capabilities in classifying and associating external stimuli. This phenomenon is attributed to gene regulatory networks functioning as perceptrons, simple intelligent schemes well-known from studies in artificial intelligence. This paper investigates the role of genetic noise in intelligent decision making at the genetic level and demonstrates that noise can play a constructive role in helping cells make informed decisions. The study uses a simple genetic classifier capable of classifying two external stimuli to illustrate this principle.
label: AI

title: Justifying and Improving Meta-Agent Conflict-Based Search
Abstract: Meta-Agent Conflict-Based Search (MA-CBS) is a recently proposed algorithm for the multi-agent pathfinding problem. As an extension of Conflict-Based Search (CBS), MA-CBS automatically merges conflicting agents into meta-agents when the number of conflicts surpasses a certain threshold. However, the decision to merge agents relies on an empirically chosen fixed threshold, with the optimal threshold varying based on the domain and number of agents. The nature of this dependence is not fully understood. This paper provides a justification for using a fixed threshold based on the analysis of a model problem. Following this justification, the study introduces new decision policies for the MA-CBS algorithm, significantly enhancing its performance. These improved variants are evaluated on various problem sets to highlight different algorithmic aspects.
label: AI

title: The Lovelace 2.0 Test of Artificial Creativity and Intelligence
Abstract: Observing that the creation of certain artistic artifacts requires intelligence, this paper presents the Lovelace 2.0 Test of creativity as an alternative to the Turing Test for determining whether an agent is intelligent. Building on prior tests of creativity, the Lovelace 2.0 Test provides a means of directly comparing the relative intelligence of different agents.
label: AI

title: Log-Optimal Portfolio Selection Using the Blackwell Approachability Theorem
Abstract: This paper presents a method for constructing the log-optimal portfolio based on well-calibrated forecasts of market values. Dawid's notion of calibration and the Blackwell approachability theorem are employed to compute well-calibrated forecasts. The portfolio is then selected using this "artificial" probability distribution of market values. The resulting portfolio performs asymptotically at least as well as any stationary portfolio that redistributes investments at each round using a continuous function of side information. Unlike traditional mathematical finance theory, this approach does not rely on stochastic assumptions about market values.
label: AI

title: A Parallel and Efficient Algorithm for Learning to Match
Abstract: Many tasks in data mining and related fields can be formalized as matching between objects in two heterogeneous domains, including collaborative filtering, link prediction, image tagging, and web search. Machine learning techniques, referred to as learning-to-match in this paper, have been successfully applied to these problems. Feature-based matrix factorization, a class of state-of-the-art learning-to-match methods, extends matrix factorization by incorporating auxiliary features into the model. However, scaling these algorithms to real-world problems is challenging, and simple parallelization strategies fail due to complex cross-talking patterns between sub-tasks. This paper addresses this challenge with a novel parallel and efficient algorithm for feature-based matrix factorization. The proposed algorithm, based on coordinate descent, can handle hundreds of millions of instances and features on a single machine. The key to this algorithm is an iterative relaxation of the objective function to facilitate parallel updates of parameters, while guaranteeing convergence on minimizing the original objective function. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method on a wide range of matching problems, significantly improving efficiency over baselines while maintaining accuracy.
label: AI

title: Towards a Model Theory for Distributed Representations
Abstract: Distributed representations (such as those based on embeddings) and discrete representations (such as those based on logic) possess complementary strengths. This paper explores one approach for combining these two representation types. It presents a model theory/semantics for first-order logic based on vectors of real numbers. The paper describes the model theory, discusses interesting properties of such a system, and presents a simple approach to query answering.
label: AI

title: Generalized Compression Dictionary Distance as Universal Similarity Measure
Abstract: This paper introduces a new similarity measure based on information-theoretic measures that outperforms Normalized Compression Distance for clustering problems while inheriting the valuable properties of conditional Kolmogorov complexity. The study shows that Normalized Compression Dictionary Size and Normalized Compression Dictionary Entropy are computationally more efficient, eliminating the need for compression itself. Additionally, they scale linearly with exponential vector size growth and are content-independent. The paper demonstrates that normalized compression dictionary distance is compressor-independent when limited to lossless compressors, enabling optimizations and implementation speed improvements for real-time and big data applications. The introduced measure is applicable for various machine learning tasks, including parameter-free unsupervised clustering, supervised learning (classification and regression), feature selection, and big data problems, offering significant speed increases.
label: AI

title: Investigation of A Collective Decision Making System of Different Neighbourhood-Size Based on Hyper-Geometric Distribution
Abstract: The study of collective decision-making systems has become a central focus of Swarm-Intelligence related research in recent years. A key challenge in modeling such systems is developing macroscopic stochastic equations from their microscopic models. This report investigates the behavior of a collective decision-making system with specific microscopic rules resembling chemical reactions, using different group sizes. The study aims to derive a generalized analytical model of a collective-decision system using hyper-geometric distribution.
label: AI

title: Improvement of PSO algorithm by memory based gradient search - application in inventory management
Abstract: Effective and robust nonlinear optimization is crucial for advanced inventory management in complex supply chains, due to the stochastic nature of supply and demand variations. Applying estimated gradients can accelerate the convergence of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, but traditional gradient calculation is not applicable to stochastic and uncertain systems. This paper proposes a memory-based algorithm that utilizes stored and shared past function evaluations of particles instead of generating new simulated samples to estimate gradients through local weighted least squares regression. The performance of the resulting regional gradient-based PSO is verified using benchmark problems and a complex application example where optimal reorder points for a supply chain are determined. |||
label: AI

title: The Tomaco Hybrid Matching Framework for SAWSDL Semantic Web Services
Abstract: This research aims to address the challenge of retrieving web services, also known as service selection, discovery, or matching. It proposes a novel hybrid matching algorithm for SAWSDL, combining logic-based strategies and syntactic text-similarity measures on semantic annotations and textual descriptions. This algorithm, called Tomaco, was evaluated in the S3 contest environment and achieved high rankings, particularly for early recall levels.  Additionally, the research presents the Tomaco web application, designed to promote the adoption of Semantic Web Service technologies and algorithms by providing a user-friendly platform. Tomaco integrates various configurable matching algorithms, enabling the discovery of both existing and user-contributed service collections and ontologies, effectively functioning as a service registry.

title: Mobility Enhancement for Elderly
Abstract: Loss of mobility is a significant challenge for senior citizens, limiting their independence and quality of life. Current solutions, such as domestic help and basic wheelchairs, often fall short in providing dignified and self-sufficient mobility. This project proposes a sophisticated wheelchair equipped with enhanced vision and hearing capabilities, sensor-aided navigation and control, and a user-friendly interface. Specifically, it integrates speech recognition and vision-aided obstacle detection systems. The speech recognition component allows users to control the wheelchair using voice commands, freeing their hands for other tasks. The vision-aided obstacle detection system uses stereo cameras to estimate distances to obstacles, enabling safer navigation and improved route planning. This project focuses on addressing the challenge of navigating unfamiliar environments by incorporating these advanced features, offering senior citizens greater independence and mobility.
label: AI

title: Where do goals come from? A Generic Approach to Autonomous Goal-System Development
Abstract: Goals serve as agents' intentions, providing a structured framework for organizing behavior based on simplified representations of complex world states. This paper explores how agents can develop goals autonomously, proposing a comprehensive conceptual and computational account of this longstanding problem. It argues that goals should be viewed as high-level abstractions of lower-level intention mechanisms, such as rewards and values. The paper emphasizes the importance of integrating goal detection alongside the agent's own actions' effects. The proposed computational learning formulation, Latent Goal Analysis, demonstrates that any reward or value function can be explained by goals and self-detection as underlying mechanisms. This approach is validated through practical reinforcement learning problems, showcasing the effectiveness of learned goals in dimensionality reduction. Additionally, the paper investigates a developmental scenario where task-unspecific rewards, induced by visual saliency, lead to the emergence of self and goal representations, enabling goal-directed reaching behavior.

title: Certified Connection Tableaux Proofs for HOL Light and TPTP
Abstract: Recent advancements in automated theorem proving have seen the Metis prover, based on ordered paramodulation and model elimination, replace earlier built-in methods in HOL4 and Isabelle/HOL. However, in the annual CASC competition, the leanCoP system, utilizing connection tableaux, has consistently outperformed Metis. This paper demonstrates the integration of leanCoP's core algorithm within HOLLight, leveraging its minimalist design to create a simple and efficient proof system. This integration facilitates the extension of the MESON proof reconstruction mechanism to connection tableaux proofs, enabling leanCoP to produce certified proofs within HOLLight. The paper compares the performance of this direct Prolog stack implementation with the continuation passing implementation of MESON, revealing the strengths and weaknesses of each approach on core HOLLight goals. The resulting prover can also be used as a general-purpose TPTP prover, and its performance is compared against the resolution-based Metis on TPTP and other relevant datasets.
label: AI

title: Interactive Error Correction in Implicative Theories
Abstract: This study investigates errors that may arise in implicative theories derived from binary data. Two distinct classes of errors are identified, and two approaches based on Formal Concept Analysis are proposed to detect them. The first approach utilizes the cardinality minimal (canonical or Duquenne-Guigues) implication base, while the second method checks for possible errors in polynomial time by computing closures of subsets of attributes. Both approaches are interactive, relying on user feedback to validate or invalidate certain implications. The paper presents and discusses the results of computer experiments conducted to evaluate the proposed methods.
label: AI

title: Learning Vague Concepts for the Semantic Web
Abstract: Ontologies, powerful tools for structuring knowledge, are extensively researched for their ability to organize and represent information. Updating ontology content or enhancing interoperability with other ontologies presents significant challenges. This paper focuses on the presence of vague concepts, prevalent in natural language, within the framework of formal ontologies. It adopts a framework where vagueness is represented through numerical restrictions that can be automatically adjusted. Recognizing that updating vague concepts can lead to inconsistent sets of axioms, the paper proposes and implements a method for detecting and repairing such inconsistencies in a localized manner.
label: AI

title: Dense 3D Face Correspondence
Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm capable of automatically establishing dense correspondences between a large number of 3D faces. Starting with automatically detected sparse correspondences on the outer boundary of 3D faces, the algorithm triangulates existing correspondences and expands them iteratively. This expansion is achieved by matching points with distinct surface curvature along triangle edges. After exhausting keypoint matches, further correspondences are generated by distributing points within triangles using evolving level set geodesic curves originating from the centroids of large triangles. A deformable model, K3DM, is constructed from the dense corresponded faces, and an algorithm is proposed for morphing the K3DM to fit unseen faces. This morphing algorithm iteratively aligns an unseen face with the model, followed by regularized morphing of the deformable model. The algorithm's performance is extensively evaluated on synthetic and real 3D faces from multiple databases using both quantitative and qualitative benchmarks. Results demonstrate the algorithm's ability to achieve dense correspondences with low localization error, detect anthropometric landmarks with high precision, and achieve high face recognition accuracy on various datasets.
label: AI

title: The upgrade of the LHCb trigger system
Abstract: The LHCb experiment, operating at a luminosity of $2\\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ during LHC Run 3, faces significant challenges due to the limitations of its current readout and hardware Level-0 trigger, especially for fully hadronic final states. To maintain high signal efficiency, the upgraded LHCb detector will implement two innovative concepts: a triggerless readout and a full software trigger. This upgrade aims to address the limitations imposed by the high luminosity environment and ensure efficient data processing for future experiments.
label: AI

title: Semantic Gateway as a Service architecture for IoT Interoperability
Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to play a crucial role in the future of the internet, connecting sensors and devices that record physical observations to internet applications and services. However, the IoT faces challenges related to the fragmentation of proprietary systems and lack of interoperability. This paper proposes a gateway and Semantic Web enabled IoT architecture to address these challenges, promoting interoperability between different systems. The Semantic Gateway as Service (SGS) facilitates translation between messaging protocols such as XMPP, CoAP, and MQTT using a multi-protocol proxy architecture. Leveraging widely accepted standards, such as the W3C's Semantic Sensor Network (SSN) ontology for semantic annotations of sensor data, enables semantic interoperability between messages and supports semantic reasoning to derive actionable knowledge from low-level sensor data.
label: AI

title: Learning to Execute
Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) with Long Short-Term Memory units (LSTM) are widely used for their expressiveness and ease of training. This paper investigates the expressiveness and learnability of LSTMs in the sequence-to-sequence regime by training them to evaluate short computer programs, a domain traditionally considered too complex for neural networks. The research focuses on a simple class of programs that can be evaluated with a single left-to-right pass using constant memory. The study demonstrates that LSTMs can effectively learn to map character-level representations of these programs to their correct outputs. The paper highlights the importance of curriculum learning and introduces a novel variant that significantly enhances the performance of the networks. This improved curriculum proves particularly impactful on an addition problem, enabling the training of an LSTM to add two 9-digit numbers with 99% accuracy.
label: AI

title: Domain-Independent Optimistic Initialization for Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: In Reinforcement Learning (RL), optimistic initialization of value functions is often used to encourage exploration. However, this approach can be domain-dependent, requiring knowledge of the scale of rewards and a constant norm in the feature representation. This paper proposes a simple approach that performs optimistic initialization with less dependence on specific domain characteristics, providing a more robust and generalizable method for exploration in RL.
label: AI

title: Partial Force Control of Constrained Floating-Base Robots
Abstract: Controlling legged robots poses a significant challenge due to their multiple rigid contact points with the environment. This paper presents a method for controlling both the motion and a subset of contact forces of a floating-base robot. A novel formulation of the lexicographic optimization problem, commonly encountered in multitask motion/force control frameworks, is derived. The structure of the problem's constraints, stemming from the robot's dynamics, allows for a sparse analytical solution, leading to a reduced computational complexity equivalent to inverse-dynamics based approaches. This method preserves the flexibility of optimization-based control frameworks while reducing computational cost. Simulations conducted on a 23-degree-of-freedom humanoid robot demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving various multi-contact behaviors. Comparisons with other state-of-the-art control techniques highlight the benefits of this controller, particularly in eliminating force/torque discontinuities.

title: Informatic error-disturbance relation in the qubit case
Abstract: In 1927, Heisenberg first proposed the tradeoff between measurement error and disturbance on a complementary observable. While quantum uncertainty relations quantify unavoidable uncertainty in the measuring process, this paper explores the error-disturbance relationship from an information viewpoint. It investigates the amount of information that can be obtained during two sequential measurements, rather than focusing solely on uncertainty. To maximize information gain, the paper proposes a strategy involving cloning the unknown state for the "intelligent" prior apparatus and performing a swapping operation for the posterior one. The concept of a coarse-grained random access code is introduced, where information causality is exploited as a physical principle to derive an upper bound for information gain. Finally, the paper conjectures the information gain of measuring the position and momentum of a quantum object using this coarse-grained approach.
label: AI

title: Model the System from Adversary Viewpoint: Threats Identification and Modeling
Abstract: Security attacks are often difficult to understand due to their complex and often unfriendly descriptions, hindering security experts and analysts in developing clear and comprehensive security specifications. This paper introduces a security attack meta-model for the SysML-Sec framework, aimed at improving threat identification and modeling by explicitly representing security concerns using knowledge representation techniques. The proposed meta-model facilitates the specification of security concerns through ontological concepts, defining the semantics of security artifacts and represented using SysML-Sec diagrams. This meta-model further enables the representation of relationships between these concepts, facilitating reasoning about knowledge introduced by system designers and security experts within the graphical environment of the SysML-Sec framework.
label: AI

title: USBcat - Towards an Intrusion Surveillance Toolset
Abstract: This paper presents an intrusion surveillance framework designed to empower analysts with the ability to investigate and monitor cyber-attacks covertly. Recognizing the importance of understanding an adversary's techniques and objectives in countering espionage-motivated cyber-attacks, the framework enables security investigators to conduct both live and stealthy counter-intelligence operations. By observing the behavior and communications of intruders, investigators can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the attacker's identity, objectives, capabilities, and infiltration methods, surpassing the limitations of current technologies. The research focused on developing an extensible framework for covert malware investigation, including the design and implementation of a Universal Serial Bus (USB) Mass Storage Device (MSD) based covert channel for remote command and control of the framework. The framework's effectiveness is validated through design, implementation, and testing.
label: AI

title: Optimal Adaptive Random Multiaccess in Energy Harvesting Wireless Sensor Networks
Abstract: Wireless sensors, integrating rechargeable batteries and energy-harvesting (EH) devices, enable long-term, autonomous operation, necessitating intelligent energy management to mitigate the impact of energy outages. This work examines a network of EH wireless sensors reporting packets with random utility values to a fusion center (FC) over a shared wireless channel. Decentralized access schemes are designed where each node locally decides to transmit or discard a packet based on its utility, energy level, and EH process state, aiming to maximize the average long-term aggregate utility of packets received at the FC. Due to the problem's non-convex structure, an approximate optimization approach is developed using a game-theoretic formulation. Nodes do not behave strategically but rather attempt to maximize a common network utility based on their individual policies. The symmetric Nash equilibrium (SNE) is characterized, proving its uniqueness and showing that it is a local maximum of the original problem. An algorithm for computing the SNE is presented, along with a heuristic scheme that is optimal for large battery capacity. Numerical results demonstrate that the SNE typically achieves near-optimal performance, within 3% of the optimal policy, with significantly reduced complexity. The paper identifies and analyzes two operational regimes of EH-networks: an energy-limited scenario with scarce energy and an underutilized channel, and a network-limited scenario with abundant energy where the shared wireless channel becomes the bottleneck.

title: Softwaretechnische Absicherung intelligenter Systeme im Fahrzeug
Abstract: This article discusses software engineering techniques crucial for ensuring the quality of intelligent, software-intensive systems in vehicles. Quality assurance for intelligent software is achieved through a combination of modern software engineering methods. Architecture and design patterns for securing software components are complemented by testing concepts and frameworks for validating specifications and assessing the robustness of implementations. These patterns represent proven and established solutions for specific problem classes, such as reliability and efficient execution.
label: AI

title: Online interpretation of numeric sign language using 2-d skeletal model
Abstract: Gesturing is a natural form of human communication, with gestures conveying both basic meanings and additional layers of information. Sign language, a prominent example of communicative gestures, is a highly structured communication medium widely accepted worldwide for deaf and dumb individuals. This paper proposes an online recognition scheme for interpreting the standard numeric sign language, comprising 10 basic hand symbols. A web camera captures real-time hand movements as input to the system, and the basic meaning of the hand gesture is extracted by analyzing hand shape, orientation, movement, and location. The input hand shape is processed to identify the palm structure, fingertips, their relative positions, and the presence of an extended thumb. A 2-dimensional skeletal model is generated based on this shape information to represent and interpret the basic meaning of the hand gesture.
label: AI

title: Memory Networks
Abstract: This paper introduces a new class of learning models called memory networks, designed to perform reasoning using inference components combined with a long-term memory component. These models learn to jointly use these components for prediction. The long-term memory can be both read and written to, facilitating knowledge storage and retrieval. The paper investigates memory networks in the context of question answering (QA), where the long-term memory acts as a dynamic knowledge base, and the output is a textual response. The models are evaluated on a large-scale QA task and a smaller, more complex toy task generated from a simulated world. In the latter, the paper demonstrates the reasoning power of these models by chaining multiple supporting sentences to answer questions requiring an understanding of verb intension.
label: AI

title: Multi-Agent Shape Formation and Tracking Inspired from a Social Foraging Dynamics
Abstract: The principle of Swarm Intelligence has found widespread application in information control and automated tracking using multi-agent systems. This article proposes an elegant and effective method for generating geometric patterns by search agents, inspired by foraging dynamics. Starting from a random initial orientation, the article investigates how foraging dynamics can be modified to achieve agent convergence on the desired pattern with near-uniform density. Guided by these modified dynamics, agents can also track a moving point by continuously circulating around it. The paper provides an analytical treatment supported by computer simulation results to gain a deeper understanding of the system's convergence behavior.
label: AI

title: Presence-absence reasoning for evolutionary phenotypes
Abstract:
Phenotype data is often described in detail in scientific literature, using natural language. However, researchers who want to synthesize or integrate this data across multiple studies or fields face challenges. They need to abstract detailed observations to construct phenotypic concepts common across datasets. This abstraction can be difficult, as it requires inferring information not explicitly stated in the original publications. 

For example, a phenotype describing the length of a manual digit implies the organism has a hand and forelimb, even if these features are not explicitly mentioned. To address this issue, the Phenoscape project uses a pipeline of OWL axiom generation and reasoning steps to infer taxon-specific presence/absence of anatomical entities from anatomical phenotypes. This method allows researchers to link genotype to phenotype and construct synthetic morphological supermatrices for comparative analysis.
label: AI

title: Refined Particle Swarm Intelligence Method for Abrupt Motion Tracking
Abstract: Conventional tracking methods struggle to handle abrupt motion due to their reliance on assumptions of smooth motion or accurate motion models. To address this challenge, we introduce SwaTrack, a novel abrupt motion tracker based on swarm intelligence. SwaTrack utilizes an optimized swarm-based sampling strategy to balance exploration and exploitation of the search space, seeking the optimal proposal distribution. It also incorporates Dynamic Acceleration Parameters (DAP) for on-the-fly tuning of the distribution's mean and variance during sampling. This unique combination of strategies within the PSO framework allows SwaTrack to effectively track abrupt motions, a feat not achieved by existing methods.
label: AI

title: Scene Image is Non-Mutually Exclusive - A Fuzzy Qualitative Scene Understanding
Abstract: Many real-world decision-making processes involve ambiguity or uncertainty. This often leads to variations in decisions even when the same problem is presented to different individuals. Research in psychology and metaphysics has shown that human decision-making is subjective, influenced by factors such as experience, age, and background. Scene understanding, a computer vision problem, falls into this category. Traditional methods simplify the problem by assuming scene images are mutually exclusive, focusing on binary classification. However, scene images are not mutually exclusive.  We propose the Fuzzy Qualitative Rank Classifier (FQRC) to address this challenge, offering a ranking interpretation instead of a binary decision. Evaluation using large and challenging public scene datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of FQRC in modeling non-mutually exclusive scene images.
label: AI

title: eTutor: Online Learning for Personalized Education
Abstract: Recent advances in information technology and artificial intelligence have led to the emergence of web-based education systems as viable alternatives to traditional classroom settings. These systems have gained popularity due to their ability to make education accessible to a wide demographic, as exemplified by MOOCs. However, existing systems lack personalization, despite the potential it offers in web-based education. This paper introduces a systematic approach to designing a personalized web-based education system. Personalizing education is challenging, as it requires adapting teaching and training methods to individual student contexts, identifying optimal methods for each context, and adapting these methods online based on student feedback. Our proposed system, e-Tutor, addresses these challenges by learning how to adapt the teaching methodology to maximize student performance in the final exam while minimizing learning time and reducing dropouts.  The efficiency of this approach is illustrated using a real-world eTutor platform for remedial training in Digital Signal Processing (DSP).
label: AI

title: DISARM: A Social Distributed Agent Reputation Model based on Defeasible Logic
Abstract: Intelligent agents operating in open environments face inherent risks, making it challenging to determine whom to trust for interaction.  As intelligent agents become increasingly integrated with Semantic Web technology, enabling them to act on behalf of users with minimal human intervention, their ability to perform assigned tasks comes under scrutiny. Trust and reputation models based on interaction trust or witness reputation have been proposed. However, these models often rely on a centralized authority, which raises concerns regarding trustworthiness and robustness. Distributed models, while more complex, offer personalized estimations based on individual agent preferences. This article introduces DISARM, a novel distributed reputation model that treats multi-agent systems (MASs) as social networks, allowing agents to establish and maintain relationships, mitigating the drawbacks of common distributed approaches. DISARM is grounded in defeasible logic, capturing how intelligent agents, similar to humans, draw conclusions from incomplete and potentially conflicting information. An evaluation demonstrating the usability of the proposed model is provided.
label: AI

title: Machine Learning Techniques in Cognitive Radio Networks
Abstract: Cognitive radio is an intelligent radio system capable of dynamic programming and configuration to fully utilize unused frequency resources allocated to licensed users. It empowers radio devices with the ability to learn and adapt their transmission to the external radio environment, demonstrating a level of intelligence for monitoring, learning, and making informed decisions. This paper reviews examples of how machine learning techniques are being employed in cognitive radio networks to realize this intelligent radio functionality.
label: AI

title: Relational Linear Programs
Abstract: We introduce relational linear programming (RLP), a simple framework for integrating linear programs (LPs) and logic programs. An RLP is a declarative LP template that defines the objective and constraints using the logical concepts of objects, relations, and quantified variables. This relational representation allows expressing the LP objective and constraints for a varying number of individuals and relations without explicit enumeration. In conjunction with a logical knowledge base (a logic program composed of logical facts and rules), it induces a ground LP, which is solved using lifted linear programming. This approach leverages symmetries within the ground LP to potentially reduce its dimensionality before solving using standard LP solvers. Unlike mainstream LP template languages like AMPL, which combines declarative and imperative programming styles, RLP's relational nature facilitates a more intuitive representation of optimization problems within relational domains. The effectiveness of RLP is demonstrated through empirical experiments on approximate inference in Markov logic networks, solving Markov decision processes, and performing collective inference using LP support vector machines.
label: AI

title: Realizing RCC8 networks using convex regions
Abstract: RCC8, a popular fragment of the region connection calculus, enables the expression of qualitative spatial relations between regions, including adjacency, overlap, and parthood. While RCC8 is inherently dimensionless, its application has largely been confined to reasoning about two-dimensional or three-dimensional physical space. This paper focuses on conceptual spaces, which are typically high-dimensional Euclidean spaces representing the meaning of natural language concepts using convex regions. The aim is to analyze how restricting to convex regions influences the realizability of RCC8 relation networks. We identify all possible restrictions on the set of RCC8 base relations to guarantee consistent networks can be convexly realized in 1D, 2D, 3D, and 4D. Surprisingly, disallowing the 'partially overlaps' relation allows all consistent atomic RCC8 networks to be convexly realized in 4D. Similarly, excluding refinements of the 'part of' relation enables the convex realization of all consistent atomic RCC8 relations in 3D. We further demonstrate that any consistent RCC8 network with 2n+1 variables can be realized using convex regions in the n-dimensional Euclidean space.
label: AI

title: Recognition of cDNA microarray image Using Feedforward artificial neural network
Abstract: The complementary DNA (cDNA) sequence is considered a powerful biometric technique for personal identification. This paper introduces a new method for cDNA recognition based on artificial neural networks (ANNs). Microarray imaging, which allows for the simultaneous identification of thousands of genes, is utilized. We segment the location of spots in a cDNA microarray, as precise localization and segmentation are crucial for accurate intensity measurement and gene expression quantification. The segmented cDNA microarray image is then resized and used as input for the proposed ANN. The ANN is trained for matching and recognition, and results are presented for cDNA sequence galleries. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed matching technique for processing cDNA sequences.  Comparisons with previous methods confirm the superior matching performance of the proposed approach.
label: AI

title: Automatic Training Data Synthesis for Handwriting Recognition Using the Structural Crossing-Over Technique
Abstract: This paper introduces a novel technique called "Structural Crossing-Over" for synthesizing qualified data to train machine learning-based handwriting recognition systems. This technique can generate a wider variety of patterns in training data compared to existing methods like elastic distortion and tangent-based affine transformation. Pairs of training characters are selected, analyzed for similarities and differences in their structures, and then crossed over to generate new characters. Experiments compare the performances of tangent-based affine transformation and the proposed approach in terms of generated character variety and recognition error rates. The standard MNIST corpus, including 60,000 training characters and 10,000 test characters, is used in the experiments. The proposed technique synthesizes 60,000 characters from 1,000 characters, which are then used to train and test a benchmark handwriting recognition system employing Histogram of Gradient (HOG) features and Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the recognizer.  The experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in performance with an error rate of 8.06%, outperforming tangent-based affine transformation (11.74%) and the original MNIST training data (16.55%).
label: AI

title: Committment-Based Data-Aware Multi-Agent-Contexts Systems
Abstract: Communication and interaction among agents have been extensively studied for years. Commitment-based communication, where agents are seen as debtors committing to creditors to achieve a desired outcome (possibly under certain conditions), is now well-established. The DACMAS (Data-Aware Commitment-based MAS) approach extends commitment-related approaches from a propositional to a first-order setting by adopting the DRL-Lite Description Logic. Notably, DACMASs provide simple forms of inter-agent event-based communication, alongside commitments. However, the ability to acquire knowledge from contexts external to the MAS, such as non-agent entities, is missing. Managed MCSs (Managed Multi-Context Systems) address this by enabling knowledge exchange among knowledge bases, but not agents. This paper proposes the DACmMCMASs (Data-Aware Commitment-based managed Multi-Context MAS) approach to develop a commitment-based first-order agent system that can interact with heterogeneous external information sources. The paper shows that DACmMCMASs retain the desirable formal properties of the original approaches.
label: AI

title: An improved multimodal PSO method based on electrostatic interaction using n- nearest-neighbor local search
Abstract: This paper presents an improved multimodal optimization (MMO) algorithm called LSEPSO. LSEPSO combines the Electrostatic Particle Swarm Optimization (EPSO) algorithm with a local search method and incorporates modifications to enhance its global and local optima finding abilities. The algorithm utilizes a modified local search to improve the particle's personal best, employing n-nearest-neighbor instead of the nearest-neighbor approach.  This involves creating n new points between each particle and its n nearest particles to identify a potential alternative for the particle's personal best.  This method prevents particle attenuation and ensures that particles don't simply follow their neighbors.  Testing on benchmark functions demonstrates the improved algorithm's effectiveness in solving MMO problems, outperforming other algorithms.
label: AI

title: Supervised learning Methods for Bangla Web Document Categorization
Abstract: This paper examines the application of machine learning approaches, specifically four supervised learning methods—Decision Tree (C 4.5), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—for categorizing Bangla web documents. This involves automatically sorting documents into categories from a predefined set. While numerous methods have been applied to English text categorization, relatively few studies have focused on Bangla language text categorization.  The paper analyzes the efficiency of these four methods for categorizing Bangla documents. To validate the approach, a Bangla corpus from various websites was developed and used as examples in the experiment. Empirical results show that all four methods achieve satisfactory performance, with SVM demonstrating good results for high-dimensional and relatively noisy document feature vectors.
label: AI

title: Analysis of corporate environmental reports using statistical techniques and data mining
Abstract: Measuring the effectiveness of corporate environmental reports, often highly qualitative and minimally regulated, is a challenging task, particularly when comparisons are required. This study employs data mining techniques to overcome physical verification problems and further explore effectiveness by performing exploratory analysis and structural equation modeling to identify significant linkages between selected variables. A sample of 539 reports from various countries is obtained from an international directory for statistical analysis, including One-way ANOVA (Analysis of Variance), MDA (Multivariate Discriminant Analysis), and SEM (Structural Equation Modeling).  The results highlight significant differences in environmental reporting practices across industries.  Furthermore, exploratory factors like stakeholder involvement, organizational strategy, and industry-specific factors prove significant.  The study's key finding is the correlation between the results and the conceptual framework of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI).
label: AI

title: Ontology-based Representation and Reasoning on Process Models: A Logic Programming Approach
Abstract: This paper proposes a framework grounded in Logic Programming for representing and reasoning about business processes from both procedural and ontological perspectives. The goals are threefold: (1) define a logical language and formal semantics for process models enriched with ontology-based annotations; (2) provide an effective inference mechanism supporting the combination of reasoning services addressing the structural definition of a process model, its behavior, and the domain knowledge associated with participating business entities; (3) implement this theoretical framework into a process modeling and reasoning platform. To achieve these goals, a process ontology is defined, covering a relevant fragment of the popular BPMN modeling notation.  The behavioral semantics of a process is defined as a state transition system using an approach similar to the Fluent Calculus, allowing for the specification of state changes in terms of preconditions and effects of activity enactment.  The paper demonstrates how procedural process knowledge can be seamlessly integrated with domain knowledge expressed using the OWL 2 RL rule-based ontology language. The proposed framework provides a range of reasoning services, including CTL model checking, which can be performed using standard Logic Programming inference engines through a goal-oriented, efficient, sound, and complete evaluation procedure. A software environment implementing the proposed framework is also presented, along with experimental evaluation results showcasing the viability of the approach.
label: AI

title: Mobile Agent Systems, Recent Security Threats and Counter Measures
Abstract: Mobile agent technology offers a dynamically evolving computing paradigm where programs, in the form of software agents, can suspend execution on a host computer, transfer themselves to another agent-enabled host on the network, and resume execution on the new host. The use of mobile code dates back to the 1960s, with remote job entry systems.  Today's mobile agents range from simple distributed objects to highly organized intelligent softwares.  This rapid evolution has introduced critical security concerns, prompting research to address these challenges. The goal is to establish trusted mobile agent systems that can be readily deployed and widely adopted. This paper provides an overview of the latest threats facing the designers of agent platforms and developers of agent-based applications.  The paper also identifies security objectives and measures to counter identified threats and achieve those objectives.
label: AI

title: Top Rank Optimization in Linear Time
Abstract: Bipartite ranking aims to learn a real-valued ranking function that prioritizes positive instances over negative instances. Recent bipartite ranking efforts focus on optimizing ranking accuracy at the top of the ranked list. Existing approaches either optimize task-specific metrics or extend ranking loss by emphasizing errors associated with top-ranked instances, resulting in high computational costs that scale super-linearly with the number of training instances. We propose TopPush, a highly efficient approach for optimizing accuracy at the top, with computational complexity linear in the number of training instances. A novel analysis bounds the generalization error for the top-ranked instances for this approach. Empirical studies demonstrate TopPush's competitiveness with state-of-the-art approaches while being 10-100 times faster.
label: AI

title: An Aerial Image Recognition Framework using Discrimination and Redundancy Quality Measure
Abstract: Aerial image categorization plays a vital role in remote sensing and artificial intelligence. This paper introduces a new aerial image categorization framework that organizes local patches of each aerial image into multiple discriminative subgraphs.  These subgraphs reflect both geometric properties and color distributions within an aerial image.  First, each aerial image is decomposed into a collection of regions based on their color intensities.  Then, a region connected graph (RCG) is constructed, modeling the connections between spatially neighboring regions to encode the spatial context of the aerial image.  Second, a subgraph mining technique is applied to uncover frequent structures within the RCGs derived from training aerial images.  From these frequent structures, a set of refined structures is selected, emphasizing high discriminative power and low redundancy.  Finally, for a new aerial image, its sub-RCGs corresponding to the refined structures are extracted and quantized into a discriminative vector for SVM classification.  Thorough experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and visualized mined subgraphs reveal the discriminative topologies of each aerial image.
label: AI

title: Bayesian regression and Bitcoin
Abstract: This paper explores the use of Bayesian regression for predicting Bitcoin price variation. Bayesian regression leverages empirical data to perform Bayesian inference. We apply Bayesian regression to the "latent source model," which was introduced by Chen, Nikolov, and Shah (2013) and Bresler, Chen, and Shah (2014) for binary classification.  While they demonstrated the theoretical and empirical efficacy of this method for binary classification, we adapt it to predict the real-valued quantity of Bitcoin price. Based on this price prediction method, a simple Bitcoin trading strategy is devised.  When tested against real data, the strategy successfully nearly doubled the investment in under 60 days.
label: AI

title: On the Computational Efficiency of Training Neural Networks
Abstract: Training neural networks is known to be computationally challenging.  However, in practice, modern neural networks are trained efficiently using SGD and various tricks, including different activation functions (e.g., ReLU), over-specification (training networks larger than needed), and regularization.  This paper revisits the computational complexity of training neural networks from a modern perspective. It presents both positive and negative results, some of which yield new provably efficient and practical algorithms for training specific types of neural networks.
label: AI

title: Gamma Processes, Stick-Breaking, and Variational Inference
Abstract: While numerous Bayesian nonparametric models in machine learning have centered on the Dirichlet process, beta process, or their variants, the gamma process has recently gained prominence as a valuable nonparametric prior in its own right. Current inference schemes for models involving the gamma process are confined to MCMC-based methods, which limits their scalability. This paper presents a variational inference framework for models incorporating gamma process priors. Our approach relies on a novel stick-breaking constructive definition of the gamma process. We prove the correctness of this stick-breaking process using the characterization of the gamma process as a completely random measure (CRM), and explicitly derive the rate measure of our construction employing Poisson process machinery. Additionally, we derive error bounds on the truncation of the infinite process required for variational inference, analogous to the truncation analyses for other nonparametric models based on the Dirichlet and beta processes. Our representation is then utilized to derive a variational inference algorithm for a particular Bayesian nonparametric latent structure formulation known as the infinite Gamma-Poisson model, where the latent variables are drawn from a gamma process prior with Poisson likelihoods. Finally, we present results for our algorithms on nonnegative matrix factorization tasks using document corpora and demonstrate that our approach compares favorably to both sampling-based techniques and variational methods based on beta-Bernoulli priors.
label: AI

title: Experimental Realization of Quantum Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Machines have the potential to exhibit artificial intelligence akin to human beings due to specific algorithms or software. These machines can learn knowledge from human instruction and perform tasks based on that knowledge. In practical learning scenarios, the data is often extremely complex and extensive, leading to classical learning machines requiring substantial computational resources. Quantum machine learning algorithms, on the other hand, can achieve exponential speedup compared to classical machines by leveraging quantum parallelism. This paper showcases a quantum machine learning algorithm implemented on a four-qubit NMR test bench to address an optical character recognition problem, also known as handwriting recognition. The quantum machine learns standard character fonts and then recognizes handwritten characters from a set containing two candidates. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first realization of artificial intelligence on a quantum processor. Given the widespread importance of artificial intelligence and its immense computational resource consumption, quantum speedup would be highly advantageous in tackling the challenges posed by Big Data.
label: AI

title: Tight Regret Bounds for Stochastic Combinatorial Semi-Bandits
Abstract: A stochastic combinatorial semi-bandit constitutes an online learning problem where, at each step, a learning agent selects a subset of ground items subject to constraints. The agent then observes stochastic weights of these items and receives their sum as a payoff. This paper provides a complete solution to the problem of computationally and sample efficient learning in stochastic combinatorial semi-bandits. Specifically, we analyze a UCB-like algorithm for solving the problem, which is known to be computationally efficient. We prove upper bounds of O(KL(1/Δ)log n) and O(√KLnlog n) on its n-step regret, where L is the number of ground items, K is the maximum number of chosen items, and Δ is the gap between the expected returns of the optimal and best suboptimal solutions. The gap-dependent bound is tight up to a constant factor, while the gap-free bound is tight up to a polylogarithmic factor.
label: AI

title: HD-CNN: Hierarchical Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Large Scale Visual Recognition
Abstract: In image classification, visual separability between different object categories is highly uneven, with some categories being more difficult to distinguish than others. These challenging categories necessitate more dedicated classifiers. However, existing deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are trained as flat N-way classifiers, and limited efforts have been made to leverage the hierarchical structure of categories. This paper introduces hierarchical deep CNNs (HD-CNNs) by embedding deep CNNs into a category hierarchy. An HD-CNN separates easy classes using a coarse category classifier while distinguishing difficult classes using fine category classifiers. During HD-CNN training, component-wise pretraining is followed by global fine-tuning with a multinomial logistic loss regularized by a coarse category consistency term. Additionally, conditional executions of fine category classifiers and layer parameter compression enhance the scalability of HD-CNNs for large-scale visual recognition. We achieve state-of-the-art results on both CIFAR100 and large-scale ImageNet 1000-class benchmark datasets. In our experiments, we construct three different HD-CNNs, which reduce the top-1 error of standard CNNs by 2.65%, 3.1%, and 1.1%, respectively.

title: Algebraic Semantics of Proto-Transitive Rough Sets
Abstract: Rough sets over generalized transitive relations, like proto-transitive ones, were first explored by the present author in 2012. Subsequently, the approximation of proto-transitive relations by other relations was investigated, and the relationship with rough approximations was developed to construct semantics capable of handling fragments of structure. It was also proven that the difference of approximations induced by some approximate relations does not necessarily induce rough structures. In this research, we develop distinct semantics of proto-transitive rough sets (PRAX) after characterizing the structure of rough objects. We also establish a theory of dependence for general rough sets and utilize it to internalize the Nelson-algebra-based approximate semantics developed earlier. The theory of rough dependence, initially introduced by the present author, is further extended in the process. This monograph is relatively self-contained and includes proofs and extensions of object representations that were not part of previous papers.
label: AI

title: Design Mining Interacting Wind Turbines
Abstract: An initial study of surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms used to design vertical-axis wind turbines was recently presented, where candidate prototypes were evaluated under fan-generated wind conditions after being physically instantiated by a 3D printer. Unlike other approaches, such as computational fluid dynamics simulations, no mathematical formulations were used and no model assumptions were made. This paper expands on that work by exploring alternative surrogate modeling and evolutionary techniques. The accuracy of various modeling algorithms used to estimate the fitness of evaluated individuals from the initial experiments is compared. The impact of temporally windowing surrogate model training samples is investigated. A surrogate-assisted approach based on an enhanced local search is introduced, and alternative coevolution collaboration schemes are examined.
label: AI

title: Stochastic Discriminative EM
Abstract: Stochastic discriminative EM (sdEM) is an online-EM-type algorithm for discriminative training of probabilistic generative models belonging to the exponential family. This work introduces and justifies this algorithm as a stochastic natural gradient descent method, i.e., a method that accounts for the information geometry in the parameter space of the statistical model. We demonstrate how this learning algorithm can be employed to train probabilistic generative models by minimizing different discriminative loss functions, such as the negative conditional log-likelihood and the Hinge loss. The resulting models trained by sdEM are always generative (i.e., they define a joint probability distribution) and, consequently, allow for handling missing data and latent variables in a principled manner, both during learning and prediction. The performance of this method is illustrated by several text classification problems where a multinomial naive Bayes and a latent Dirichlet allocation-based classifier are learned using various discriminative loss functions.
label: AI

title: Generating functionals for computational intelligence: the Fisher information as an objective function for self-limiting Hebbian learning rules
Abstract: Generating functionals can guide the evolution of a dynamical system and provide a potential route for handling the complexity of neural networks, relevant for computational intelligence. We propose and explore a novel objective function that allows us to obtain plasticity rules for the afferent synaptic weights. The adaptation rules are Hebbian, self-limiting, and result from minimizing the Fisher information with respect to the synaptic flux. We perform a series of simulations examining the behavior of these new learning rules under various circumstances. The vector of synaptic weights aligns with the principal direction of input activities whenever one exists. A linear discrimination is performed when two or more principal directions are present. Directions characterized by bimodal firing-rate distributions, exhibiting a negative excess kurtosis, are preferred. We observe robust performance and complete homeostatic adaptation of the synaptic weights as a by-product of synaptic flux minimization. This self-limiting behavior enables stable online learning for arbitrary durations. The neuron acquires new information when the statistics of input activities change at a certain point in the simulation, demonstrating resilience to unlearning previously acquired knowledge. Learning is rapid when starting with randomly drawn synaptic weights and significantly slower when the synaptic weights are already fully adapted.
label: AI

title: Recognition of Handwritten Bangla Basic Characters and Digits using Convex Hull based Feature Set
Abstract: In addressing the problem of recognizing handwritten character patterns with varying shapes and sizes, selecting an appropriate feature set is crucial for achieving high recognition performance. This research evaluates the performance of the convex hull-based feature set, comprising 125 features computed over different bay attributes of the convex hull of a pattern, for effectively recognizing isolated handwritten Bangla basic characters and digits. Experiments using a database of 10,000 samples yielded a maximum recognition rate of 76.86% for handwritten Bangla characters. For Bangla numerals, a maximum success rate of 99.45% was achieved using a database of 12,000 samples. This work validates the usefulness of a novel feature set for recognizing handwritten Bangla basic characters and numerals.
label: AI

title: PinView: Implicit Feedback in Content-Based Image Retrieval
Abstract: This paper describes PinView, a content-based image retrieval system that leverages implicit relevance feedback gathered during a search session. PinView incorporates several novel methods to infer user intent. From relevance feedback, such as eye movements or pointer clicks, and visual features of images, PinView learns a similarity metric between images that is dependent on the user's current interests. It then retrieves images using a specialized online learning algorithm that balances the trade-off between exploring new images and exploiting the inferred user interests. We have integrated PinView into the content-based image retrieval system PicSOM, enabling the application of PinView to real-world image databases. With these new algorithms, PinView outperforms the original PicSOM, and in online experiments with real users, the combination of implicit and explicit feedback yields the best results.
label: AI

title: Risk Dynamics in Trade Networks
Abstract: We introduce a novel framework to model interactions among agents seeking to trade to minimize their risk with respect to some future outcome. We quantify this risk using the concept of risk measures from finance and introduce a class of trade dynamics that enable agents to trade contracts contingent upon the future outcome. We then demonstrate that these trade dynamics precisely correspond to a variant of randomized coordinate descent. By extending the analysis of these coordinate descent methods to account for our more organic setting, we are able to establish convergence rates for highly general trade dynamics, proving that the market or network converges to a unique steady state. Applying these results to prediction markets, we expand on recent findings by adding convergence rates and general aggregation properties. Finally, we illustrate the generality of our framework by applying it to agent interactions on a scale-free network.
label: AI

title: The Universe of Minds
Abstract: This paper aims to describe the space of possible mind designs by first equating all minds to software. It then proves some interesting properties of the mind design space, such as the infinitude of minds, the size and representation complexity of minds. A survey of mind design taxonomies is followed by a proposal for a new field of investigation dedicated to the study of minds, intellectology, and a list of open problems for this new field is presented.
label: AI

title: A Multi-World Approach to Question Answering about Real-World Scenes based on Uncertain Input
Abstract: We propose a method for automatically answering questions about images by combining recent advances from natural language processing and computer vision. We integrate discrete reasoning with uncertain predictions using a multi-world approach that represents uncertainty about the perceived world within a Bayesian framework. Our approach can handle human questions of high complexity about realistic scenes and provides a range of answers, including counts, object classes, instances, and lists of them. The system is directly trained from question-answer pairs. We establish a first benchmark for this task that can be viewed as a modern attempt at a visual Turing test.
label: AI

title: Coupling Top-down and Bottom-up Methods for 3D Human Pose and Shape Estimation from Monocular Image Sequences
Abstract: Until recently, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) focused on acquiring behavioral information of targets and their activities. The continuous evolution of intelligence gathering for human-centric activities has shifted the focus to humans, particularly inferring their innate characteristics—size, shapes, and physiology. These bio-signatures extracted from surveillance sensors can be used to deduce age, ethnicity, gender, and actions, and further characterize human actions in unseen scenarios. However, recovering the pose and shape of humans in such monocular videos is inherently an ill-posed problem, marked by frequent depth and view-based ambiguities due to self-occlusion, foreshortening, and misalignment. The likelihood function often yields a highly multimodal posterior that is difficult to propagate, even using the most advanced particle filtering (PF) algorithms. Motivated by the recent success of discriminative approaches to efficiently predict 3D poses directly from 2D images, we present several principled approaches to integrate predictive cues using learned regression models to maintain the multimodality of the posterior during tracking. Additionally, these learned priors can be actively adapted to the test data using a likelihood-based feedback mechanism. Estimated 3D poses are then used to fit a 3D human shape model to each frame independently for inferring anthropometric bio-signatures. The proposed system is fully automated, robust to noisy test data, and capable of swiftly recovering from tracking failures even after encountering significant errors. We evaluate the system on a large number of monocular human motion sequences.
label: AI

title: Integrating active sensing into reactive synthesis with temporal logic constraints under partial observations
Abstract: We introduce the notion of online reactive planning with sensing actions for systems with temporal logic constraints in partially observable and dynamic environments. With incomplete information about the dynamic environment, reactive controller synthesis amounts to solving a two-player game with partial observations, which has impractically high computational complexity. To mitigate this computational burden, online replanning via sensing actions avoids solving the strategy in the reactive system under partial observations. Instead, we only solve for a strategy that ensures a given temporal logic specification can be satisfied if the system had complete observations of its environment. This strategy is then transformed into one that makes control decisions based on the observed sequence of states (of the interacting system and its environment). When the system encounters a belief—a set including all possible hypotheses the system has for the current state—for which the observation-based strategy is undefined, a sequence of sensing actions are triggered, chosen by an active sensing strategy, to reduce uncertainty in the system's belief. We demonstrate that by alternating between the observation-based strategy and the active sensing strategy, under a mild technical assumption of the set of sensors in the system, the given temporal logic specification can be satisfied with probability 1.

title: Dynamic Control and Optimization of Distributed Energy Resources in a Microgrid
Abstract: As we transition towards a power grid increasingly reliant on renewable resources like solar and wind, the intelligent control of distributed energy resources (DERs) including photovoltaic (PV) arrays, controllable loads, energy storage, and plug-in electric vehicles (EVs) will be crucial for realizing a power grid that can handle both the variability and unpredictability of renewable energy sources as well as increasing system complexity. Achieving such a decentralized and dynamic infrastructure requires the ability to solve large-scale problems in real-time with hundreds of thousands of DERs simultaneously online. Due to the scale of the optimization problem, we employ an iterative distributed algorithm previously developed in our group to operate each DER independently and autonomously within this environment. The algorithm is deployed within a framework that allows the microgrid to dynamically adapt to changes in the operating environment. Specifically, we consider a commercial site equipped with on-site PV generation, partially curtailable load, EV charge stations, and a battery electric storage (BES) unit. The site operates as a small microgrid that can participate in the wholesale market on the power grid. We report results for simulations using real data that demonstrate the ability of the optimization framework to respond dynamically in real-time to external conditions while maintaining the functional requirements of all DERs.
